d171c920f0a0ce69396ea4b61c8f466dd1f1cb2f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified, fine-grained framework for characterizing and quantifying subpopulation shift, enabling systematic analysis across multiple domains and shift types. The benchmark will be the most comprehensive to date for subpopulation shift, covering more algorithms and datasets than prior work. The study will reveal that current algorithms only address certain shift types, expose fundamental trade-offs between worst-group accuracy and other key metrics, and demonstrate that simple model selection criteria can be effective without group annotations. The work will also provide new insights into the distinct roles of representation and classifier learning under subpopulation shift, and highlight the limitations of existing evaluation metrics.

d1776e0a3d8c39a3c264c8fdecbca5b626426065.title: How Does Information Bottleneck Help Deep Learning?
d1776e0a3d8c39a3c264c8fdecbca5b626426065.research_question: How does the concept of the information bottleneck relate to generalization errors in deep learning, and can controlling the information bottleneck provide a rigorous theoretical foundation for improved generalization in neural networks across various architectures and learning settings?
d1776e0a3d8c39a3c264c8fdecbca5b626426065.hypothesis: Controlling the information bottleneck, specifically by minimizing the mutual information between input and intermediate representations while maximizing task-relevant information, will lead to improved generalization in deep neural networks. Furthermore, a rigorous mathematical relationship exists between information bottleneck measures and generalization error, providing tighter bounds than those based on traditional complexity measures.
d1776e0a3d8c39a3c264c8fdecbca5b626426065.proposed_method: A new theoretical framework will be developed to mathematically relate the information bottleneck—quantified as the mutual information between input data and hidden representations—to generalization error in deep neural networks. The approach will derive novel generalization bounds that scale with the degree of information bottleneck, specifically using conditional mutual information I(X;Z|Y) and the mutual information between the encoder and the training dataset I(ϕ;S), rather than traditional complexity measures like VC dimension or parameter count. The methodology will address both scenarios where the encoder is fixed and independent of training data (e.g., transfer learning) and where the encoder is learned from the data, providing rigorous sample complexity bounds in both cases. Extensions will be made to handle both discrete and continuous input domains, including cases where mutual information may be infinite, by introducing binning and other estimation techniques.
d1776e0a3d8c39a3c264c8fdecbca5b626426065.experiment_details: Comprehensive empirical experiments will be conducted across a range of neural network architectures (e.g., MLPs, ResNets) and learning settings (e.g., supervised, transfer learning) using datasets such as clustered 2D synthetic data, MNIST, FashionMNIST, and CIFAR-10. Experiments will involve training hundreds of models with varying architectures, hyperparameters, and random seeds, and will measure generalization gaps between training and test losses. Mutual information at various network layers will be estimated using both sampling-based and upper-bound estimators, including kernel density estimation and binning methods. Baseline metrics such as parameter count and weight norms will be compared against the proposed information bottleneck-based metrics. Evaluation will focus on the correlation between these metrics and generalization gaps, using statistical measures such as Pearson and Spearman correlation coefficients.
d1776e0a3d8c39a3c264c8fdecbca5b626426065.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides the first rigorous and valid sample complexity bounds for deep learning generalization that directly scale with the degree of information bottleneck, rather than with traditional complexity measures. The theoretical results improve upon prior conjectures by replacing exponential dependencies with linear ones and introducing conditional mutual information as a tighter and more relevant bound. The framework unifies and extends previous empirical and theoretical work, offering a foundation for both explicit and implicit regularization via information bottlenecks. The empirical findings demonstrate that combining representation compression and model compression yields superior predictors of generalization, outperforming previous metrics. The approach also resolves issues of arbitrariness in mutual information estimation and extends to cases with infinite mutual information through practical estimation techniques.

d17a3e9f34125ba6454e365ffe403ce8a91f2632.title: SGD and Hogwild! Convergence Without the Bounded Gradients Assumption
d17a3e9f34125ba6454e365ffe403ce8a91f2632.research_question: Can stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and asynchronous parallel SGD (Hogwild!) be shown to converge under more relaxed conditions, specifically without assuming uniformly bounded stochastic gradients, in strongly convex and non-convex stochastic optimization problems commonly arising in machine learning?
d17a3e9f34125ba6454e365ffe403ce8a91f2632.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that convergence of SGD and Hogwild! can be established under the assumption of Lipschitz continuity of individual function realizations, without the need for bounded stochastic gradients, and that sublinear convergence rates can be achieved with diminishing step sizes even in the presence of inconsistent memory reads and writes.
d17a3e9f34125ba6454e365ffe403ce8a91f2632.proposed_method: A new analytical framework will be developed for the convergence analysis of stochastic gradient algorithms in the strongly convex setting, relying on the Lipschitz continuity of individual stochastic function realizations but not requiring any uniform bound on the stochastic gradients. The approach introduces a general recursion for vector updates, encompassing both standard SGD and asynchronous parallel SGD (Hogwild!) as special cases. The analysis will consider both consistent and inconsistent reads/writes to shared memory, modeling delays via a parameter τ, and will derive sufficient conditions for almost sure convergence and explicit sublinear convergence rates. The methodology will also be extended to non-convex settings where only the expected objective is strongly convex, and will provide explicit step size schedules that are less restrictive than previous analyses.
d17a3e9f34125ba6454e365ffe403ce8a91f2632.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard machine learning tasks formulated as regularized empirical risk minimization, specifically using ℓ2-regularized logistic regression. Benchmark datasets such as ijcnn1 (n = 91,701) and covtype (n = 406,709) from the LIBSVM repository will be used. The experimental setup will involve varying the delay parameter τ and the fraction of gradient coordinates updated per iteration, simulating both single-core and parallel asynchronous scenarios. Evaluation metrics will include training loss and convergence rate, measured in terms of both epochs and the number of coordinate updates. Multiple runs (e.g., 10) will be averaged to assess expected convergence behavior, and step sizes will be chosen according to the theoretical analysis.
d17a3e9f34125ba6454e365ffe403ce8a91f2632.novelty_claims: The proposed framework eliminates the need for the classical bounded gradient assumption in the convergence analysis of SGD and Hogwild!, replacing it with the more realistic and broadly applicable assumption of Lipschitz continuity of individual loss realizations. It provides the first convergence guarantees for Hogwild! with diminishing step sizes and inconsistent memory access, and extends these results to non-convex settings. The analysis yields less restrictive conditions on step size selection, allowing larger initial step sizes and improved convergence rates compared to prior work. Additionally, the framework offers new theoretical insights into the effect of memory delays and parallelization on convergence, supported by experimental validation.

d18362341e4d7ffdbc94fef984fb686950f928b3.title: Anti-Backdoor Learning: Training Clean Models on Poisoned Data
d18362341e4d7ffdbc94fef984fb686950f928b3.research_question: Is it possible to train deep neural network models that are robust to backdoor attacks directly on potentially poisoned datasets, without prior knowledge of the proportion or distribution of poisoned data?
d18362341e4d7ffdbc94fef984fb686950f928b3.hypothesis: A two-stage anti-backdoor learning approach that exploits the faster learning dynamics and target-class dependency of backdoor examples can enable the training of clean, robust models on poisoned data, achieving performance comparable to models trained on clean data while significantly reducing attack success rates.
d18362341e4d7ffdbc94fef984fb686950f928b3.proposed_method: The proposed approach, Anti-Backdoor Learning (ABL), introduces a two-stage training process. In the early training stage, a local gradient ascent (LGA) mechanism is applied to each training example, maintaining its loss around a predefined threshold. This amplifies the loss gap between clean and backdoor examples, enabling the isolation of a small subset of likely backdoor examples based on their rapid loss convergence. In the later training stage, a global gradient ascent (GGA) is performed on the isolated backdoor subset to break the correlation between the backdoor trigger and the target class, effectively unlearning the backdoor. The method does not require prior knowledge of the poisoning rate or distribution, and the isolation rate for backdoor examples is set to be much smaller than the actual poisoning rate. Key hyperparameters, such as the loss threshold and turning epoch between stages, are tuned to maximize separation and defense efficacy.
d18362341e4d7ffdbc94fef984fb686950f928b3.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three benchmark datasets: CIFAR-10, GTSRB, and an ImageNet subset, using model architectures such as WideResNet-16-1 and ResNet-34. The method is evaluated against 10 state-of-the-art backdoor attacks, including both dirty-label and clean-label attacks, as well as feature-space attacks. Baseline comparisons include Fine-Pruning (FP), Mode Connectivity Repair (MCR), and Neural Attention Distillation (NAD). Evaluation metrics include Attack Success Rate (ASR) on backdoor test sets and Clean Accuracy (CA) on clean test sets. The experimental setup explores various poisoning rates (up to 70%), isolation rates, and turning epochs, and includes ablation studies and comparisons with alternative isolation and unlearning strategies.
d18362341e4d7ffdbc94fef984fb686950f928b3.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first principled anti-backdoor learning scheme capable of training clean models directly on poisoned data, without altering the data or requiring knowledge of the poisoning rate. The method leverages two fundamental weaknesses of backdoor attacks—faster learning dynamics and target-class dependency—to isolate and unlearn backdoor correlations. Extensive empirical results demonstrate that the approach achieves state-of-the-art robustness against a wide range of backdoor attacks while maintaining high clean accuracy, even under high poisoning rates. The framework opens a new research direction for robust and secure machine learning in untrusted data environments.

d1a596b5dce1ff183a763cdd1610a95f7f05e170.title: COptiDICE: Offline Constrained Reinforcement Learning via Stationary Distribution Correction Estimation
d1a596b5dce1ff183a763cdd1610a95f7f05e170.research_question: How can an agent learn a policy that maximizes expected return while satisfying cost constraints, using only a fixed offline dataset, in environments where direct interaction is costly or risky and safety constraints must be enforced?
d1a596b5dce1ff183a763cdd1610a95f7f05e170.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that optimizing policies in the space of stationary distributions, combined with explicit estimation and constraint of the upper bound of cost values, will yield policies that are both reward-maximizing and robustly satisfy cost constraints in the offline reinforcement learning setting.
d1a596b5dce1ff183a763cdd1610a95f7f05e170.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a novel offline constrained reinforcement learning algorithm that operates in the space of state-action stationary distributions. The approach formulates the constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP) as a convex optimization problem with f-divergence regularization to penalize distributional shift from the offline dataset. The method estimates stationary distribution corrections between the target and dataset distributions, and incorporates a cost upper bound constraint, computed efficiently via a minimization problem inspired by off-policy confidence interval estimation. Policy extraction is performed using importance-weighted behavioral cloning for continuous action spaces, and all optimization variables (including Lagrange multipliers and value functions) are parameterized with neural networks for scalability. Joint optimization is performed over the policy, value function, cost upper bound estimator, and Lagrange multipliers to ensure both reward maximization and robust constraint satisfaction.
d1a596b5dce1ff183a763cdd1610a95f7f05e170.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both randomly generated tabular CMDPs and continuous control tasks from the Real-World RL (RWRL) suite, where safety constraints are present. In the tabular setting, various numbers of trajectories and both constraint-satisfying and constraint-violating data-collection policies will be used to generate offline datasets, with 10,000 runs per configuration. Baselines will include behavior cloning (BC), a maximum-likelihood estimation CMDP solver, and a constrained variant of SPIBB. For continuous control, datasets will be constructed by mixing constraint-satisfying and constraint-violating trajectories, and comparisons will be made against BC, a state-of-the-art unconstrained offline RL algorithm (CRR), and a constrained variant of CRR. Evaluation metrics will include normalized reward performance and average cost, with results averaged over multiple runs and standard errors reported. Hyperparameters controlling the degree of cost-conservativeness will be varied to assess robustness.
d1a596b5dce1ff183a763cdd1610a95f7f05e170.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a single convex minimization framework for offline constrained RL by operating directly in the stationary distribution space, avoiding the instability of triple actor-critic-Lagrange optimization. It innovatively constrains the upper bound of cost values, estimated efficiently using distribution correction techniques, to achieve robust constraint satisfaction. The method leverages recent advances in off-policy confidence interval estimation to provide conservative cost estimates, and demonstrates improved trade-offs between reward maximization and constraint satisfaction compared to existing baselines. Additionally, the approach is scalable to continuous action spaces via neural network parameterization and importance-weighted behavioral cloning.

d1c33172c2ffbc038f0598f3ac56bb04af79c904.title: An Edit Friendly DDPM Noise Space: Inversion and Manipulations
d1c33172c2ffbc038f0598f3ac56bb04af79c904.research_question: How can the noise space of denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) be restructured or inverted to enable more effective and flexible editing of real images, particularly for tasks such as text-guided manipulation, color changes, and spatial transformations, without requiring model fine-tuning or intervention in attention maps?
d1c33172c2ffbc038f0598f3ac56bb04af79c904.hypothesis: An alternative, edit-friendly latent noise space for DDPMs can be constructed such that extracted noise maps allow for perfect reconstruction of a given image and enable diverse, semantically meaningful manipulations (e.g., via text or spatial edits), outperforming native DDPM and DDIM inversion approaches in terms of editability, fidelity, and diversity.
d1c33172c2ffbc038f0598f3ac56bb04af79c904.proposed_method: A new inversion method for DDPMs will be developed to extract a sequence of noise maps from any given image, real or synthetic, such that these maps are not distributed as in regular DDPM sampling but are specifically structured to be more amenable to editing. The approach constructs auxiliary image sequences directly from the input image using a modified stochastic process, where noise vectors are sampled independently and used to generate intermediate images, resulting in noise maps with higher variance and negative correlation across timesteps. This inversion is non-iterative, requires no optimization, and can be applied to both unconditional and conditional (e.g., text-guided) diffusion models. The extracted noise maps will allow for perfect image reconstruction and, when fixed, will enable semantic changes via prompt modification while preserving image structure. The method is designed to be easily integrated into existing diffusion-based editing pipelines.
d1c33172c2ffbc038f0598f3ac56bb04af79c904.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on real image editing tasks, including text-guided manipulations, color changes, and spatial transformations. Datasets will include a modified ImageNet-R-TI2I set (with 48 images and 212 image-text pairs) and a modified Zero-Shot I2I set (60 image-text pairs across four classes). The method will be evaluated using Stable Diffusion in latent space (512x512x3 images, 64x64x4 latent space), with 100 inference steps and classifier-free guidance. Baselines for comparison will include Plug-and-Play (PnP), EDICT, null-text inversion, CycleDiffusion, DDIM inversion, and Prompt-to-Prompt (P2P), both standalone and integrated with the proposed inversion. Evaluation metrics will include LPIPS for structure preservation, CLIP score for text compliance, editing time, and qualitative assessments of fidelity and diversity. Parameter sweeps will be performed to analyze trade-offs between fidelity and edit strength.
d1c33172c2ffbc038f0598f3ac56bb04af79c904.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a fundamentally different inversion process for DDPMs that constructs an edit-friendly noise space, enabling perfect image reconstruction and diverse, structure-preserving edits without model fine-tuning or attention map modification. The approach allows for stochastic, diverse editing outputs and is significantly faster than optimization-based methods. It is compatible with a wide range of diffusion-based editing algorithms, improving their fidelity and diversity. The method demonstrates superior performance in both quantitative and qualitative evaluations compared to existing DDIM and DDPM inversion techniques.

d1f974089f205d24517634c98df92fc1b0e4ad69.title: A Variational Perspective on Solving Inverse Problems with Diffusion Models
d1f974089f205d24517634c98df92fc1b0e4ad69.research_question: How can a universal and efficient framework be developed for solving a wide range of inverse problems in imaging using diffusion models, without requiring retraining for each individual task?
d1f974089f205d24517634c98df92fc1b0e4ad69.hypothesis: A variational inference-based approach, leveraging pretrained diffusion models as priors and incorporating a principled weighting mechanism for denoisers at different timesteps, will enable accurate, efficient, and tunable solutions to both linear and nonlinear inverse problems, outperforming existing sampling-based diffusion methods.
d1f974089f205d24517634c98df92fc1b0e4ad69.proposed_method: A variational framework is proposed for solving inverse problems by approximating the posterior distribution of data given measurements using pretrained denoising diffusion models as priors. The approach formulates the inference as a KL divergence minimization between a variational Gaussian distribution and the true posterior, resulting in a loss function that combines measurement matching (reconstruction) and a score-matching regularization term derived from the diffusion prior. The regularization is implemented as an ensemble over denoisers at different diffusion timesteps, each imposing structural constraints from high-level semantics to fine details. A novel weighting mechanism based on the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at each timestep is introduced to balance the contribution of each denoiser, and sampling is cast as a stochastic optimization problem, allowing the use of first-order optimizers such as Adam. The method, termed RED-diff, is designed to be lightweight, memory-efficient, and compatible with off-the-shelf optimizers, facilitating fast and tunable sampling.
d1f974089f205d24517634c98df92fc1b0e4ad69.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a 1,000-sample subset of the ImageNet validation dataset for a variety of linear and nonlinear image restoration tasks, including inpainting, phase retrieval, high dynamic range (HDR) reconstruction, and deblurring. The pretrained unconditional guided diffusion model (256x256 ImageNet) will serve as the prior. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art methods such as DPS, ΠGDM, and DDRM, with hyperparameters tuned for optimal performance. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, Kernel Inception Distance (KID), LPIPS, and top-1 classifier accuracy using a pretrained ResNet50. The experimental setup will utilize uniform timestep spacing, Adam optimizer with 1,000 steps, and batch processing on an NVIDIA RTX6000 Ada GPU. Ablations will be performed to investigate the impact of denoiser weighting mechanisms and timestep sampling strategies.
d1f974089f205d24517634c98df92fc1b0e4ad69.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled variational inference perspective for solving general inverse problems with diffusion models, addressing the limitations of prior score-approximation-based methods. It establishes a novel connection to the regularization-by-denoising (RED) framework, enabling the use of the entire diffusion trajectory for regularization and allowing sampling to be treated as stochastic optimization. The SNR-based weighting mechanism for denoisers at different timesteps is a new contribution that improves regularization and sample quality. The method achieves superior image fidelity, perceptual quality, and computational efficiency compared to state-of-the-art alternatives, and provides a flexible, tunable, and memory-efficient solution for a broad class of inverse problems.

d212c555293b81f845b3c99af4e922b0fcdb4290.title: Unifying Unsupervised Graph-Level Anomaly Detection and Out-of-Distribution Detection: A Benchmark
d212c555293b81f845b3c99af4e922b0fcdb4290.research_question: How can unsupervised graph-level anomaly detection (GLAD) and unsupervised graph-level out-of-distribution (GLOD) detection be unified under a generalized evaluation framework, and how do state-of-the-art methods perform across diverse anomaly and OOD detection scenarios in graph data?
d212c555293b81f845b3c99af4e922b0fcdb4290.hypothesis: Unsupervised GLAD and GLOD share fundamental objectives and can be effectively unified under a generalized graph-level OOD detection framework, enabling comprehensive and fair evaluation of existing methods across a wide range of scenarios. Furthermore, end-to-end methods are expected to outperform two-step approaches in both effectiveness and efficiency.
d212c555293b81f845b3c99af4e922b0fcdb4290.proposed_method: A unified benchmark, termed UB-GOLD, will be developed to comprehensively evaluate unsupervised GLAD and GLOD methods under the concept of generalized graph-level OOD detection. The benchmark will encompass 35 datasets spanning four practical scenarios: intrinsic anomaly, class-based anomaly, inter-dataset shift, and intra-dataset shift. Eighteen representative methods, including both two-step (graph kernel/self-supervised learning with detector) and end-to-end (GNN-based GLAD and GLOD) approaches, will be systematically compared. The framework will support multiple evaluation tasks, including general anomaly/OOD detection, near-far OOD detection, and robustness analysis under data perturbation. The evaluation module will provide comprehensive metrics and facilitate multi-dimensional analysis of effectiveness, OOD sensitivity, robustness, and computational efficiency.
d212c555293b81f845b3c99af4e922b0fcdb4290.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 35 datasets, each mapped to one of four detection scenarios, with standardized splits ensuring that only normal/ID samples are present in training and anomaly/OOD samples in testing. Eighteen methods, covering two-step (e.g., PK-SVM, WL-iF, IG-SVM, GCL-iF) and end-to-end (e.g., OCGIN, SIGNET, GOOD-D, GraphDE) approaches, will be evaluated. Metrics will include AUROC, AUPRC, and FPR95, with performance averaged over five runs per method-dataset pair. Random hyperparameter search will be performed to ensure fair comparison. Additional experiments will assess OOD sensitivity (near vs. far OOD), robustness to training set contamination (0-30% OOD in training), and computational efficiency (time and memory usage on CPU/GPU).
d212c555293b81f845b3c99af4e922b0fcdb4290.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark is the first to unify unsupervised GLAD and GLOD under a generalized graph-level OOD detection framework, enabling direct and fair comparison across both tasks. UB-GOLD offers a comprehensive suite of datasets, tasks, and evaluation metrics, supporting multi-dimensional analysis of methods' effectiveness, OOD sensitivity spectrum, robustness, and efficiency. The open-source codebase facilitates reproducible research and rapid experimentation. The benchmark highlights critical gaps in current methods, such as the challenge of near-OOD detection and robustness to noisy training data, and provides actionable insights and future research directions for the community.

d212fa27f5868f0fd106e1a7bba908fd47da0816.title: MotionGPT: Human Motion as a Foreign Language
d212fa27f5868f0fd106e1a7bba908fd47da0816.research_question: Can a unified pre-trained model be developed to jointly handle human motion and language, enabling diverse motion-relevant tasks such as text-to-motion generation, motion captioning, motion prediction, and motion completion through prompt-based instructions?
d212fa27f5868f0fd106e1a7bba908fd47da0816.hypothesis: A unified motion-language model that treats human motion as a foreign language and leverages large language models, combined with discrete motion tokenization and prompt-based instruction tuning, will outperform or match state-of-the-art methods across multiple human motion tasks.
d212fa27f5868f0fd106e1a7bba908fd47da0816.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves developing a unified motion-language framework that treats human motion as a foreign language. First, a motion tokenizer based on a Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQ-VAE) is trained to discretize 3D human motion sequences into motion tokens, creating a motion vocabulary analogous to word tokens in language models. These motion tokens are combined with text tokens to form a unified vocabulary, enabling joint modeling of motion and language using a transformer-based language model (such as T5). The training pipeline consists of three stages: (1) training the motion tokenizer to create the motion codebook, (2) motion-language pre-training using both unsupervised (masked token prediction) and supervised (paired text-motion translation) objectives, and (3) instruction tuning on a multi-task dataset with diverse prompt-based instructions for various motion tasks. The model is designed to flexibly generate or interpret both motion and language outputs, depending on the input prompt.
d212fa27f5868f0fd106e1a7bba908fd47da0816.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark datasets including HumanML3D and KIT for text-to-motion and motion-to-text tasks, as well as AMASS for motion prediction and completion. The evaluation will utilize metrics such as Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for motion quality, Diversity (DIV) for motion diversity, Average Displacement Error (ADE) and Final Displacement Error (FDE) for motion prediction, and linguistic metrics (BLEU, Cider, Rouge, BertScore) for captioning. Baselines will include state-of-the-art models such as MDM, T2M-GPT, TM2T, MLD, and MotionDiffuse. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by adopting consistent motion representations and following established protocols. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of model size and instruction tuning.
d212fa27f5868f0fd106e1a7bba908fd47da0816.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to treat human motion as a foreign language, enabling the use of large pre-trained language models for motion tasks. It introduces a unified motion-language vocabulary, allowing a single model to flexibly handle diverse tasks such as text-to-motion, motion captioning, motion prediction, and motion in-between via prompt-based instructions. The approach leverages instruction tuning to enhance generalization to unseen tasks and demonstrates competitive or superior performance across multiple benchmarks, establishing a new paradigm for multimodal motion-language modeling.

d22231359a3731fa9be45929615ee8d6a76b7b6e.title: Inverse Problem Sampling in Latent Space Using Sequential Monte Carlo
d22231359a3731fa9be45929615ee8d6a76b7b6e.research_question: How can inverse problems in image processing, particularly those involving complex and nonlinear degradation operators, be more effectively solved using generative models, especially in the latent space of diffusion models?
d22231359a3731fa9be45929615ee8d6a76b7b6e.hypothesis: Introducing auxiliary observations at each diffusion timestep and leveraging sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) sampling in the latent space of diffusion models will enable more accurate and perceptually realistic solutions to inverse problems, outperforming existing methods, particularly in challenging tasks such as inpainting.
d22231359a3731fa9be45929615ee8d6a76b7b6e.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed Latent Diffusion Sequential Monte Carlo (LD-SMC), is developed for solving inverse problems in the latent space of diffusion models. The approach augments the generative model with auxiliary observations at each diffusion timestep, generated via a known corruption operator applied to the decoded latent variables. Posterior inference over all latent variables is performed using a blocked Gibbs sampling scheme, where SMC is employed to sample from an approximate sequence of target distributions tailored for diffusion models. The method introduces new proposal distributions and a weighting scheme for SMC, leveraging both the auxiliary observations and the corrupted measurement to guide the sampling process. Initialization of the latent variables is achieved by solving an optimization problem that aligns the corrupted observation with the output of the autoencoder-decoder pipeline, ensuring efficient convergence and effective use of the auxiliary labels.
d22231359a3731fa9be45929615ee8d6a76b7b6e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard image datasets, including ImageNet and FFHQ, using pre-trained latent diffusion models (LDMs) and the DDIM sampler. The evaluation covers a variety of inverse problem tasks: box inpainting, free-form inpainting, Gaussian deblurring, and 8x super-resolution. Baseline methods include adaptations of DPS, TDS, ReSample, PSLD, PFLD, and LatentDAPS, all evaluated under the same experimental setup for fairness. Metrics for evaluation focus on both perceptual quality (FID, NIQE, LPIPS) and distortion (PSNR, SSIM), with grid search over method-specific hyperparameters to optimize FID. The number of SMC particles and the influence of auxiliary labels are varied to analyze trade-offs between perceptual quality and reconstruction fidelity.
d22231359a3731fa9be45929615ee8d6a76b7b6e.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to combine auxiliary observations at each diffusion timestep with SMC sampling in the latent space of diffusion models, enabling effective posterior inference even with nonlinear corruption operators and autoencoder-based latent spaces. It introduces new proposal distributions and weighting schemes specifically designed for the latent diffusion setting, and provides theoretical guarantees of asymptotic accuracy. Empirical results demonstrate significant improvements in perceptual quality, especially in challenging inverse problems such as inpainting, compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

d24b4f34197df0257390b57f02537e6ce3284f2e.title: Universal Guidance for Diffusion Models
d24b4f34197df0257390b57f02537e6ce3284f2e.research_question: How can diffusion models be universally guided by arbitrary modalities and external functions, without the need for retraining or modifying the underlying diffusion model, to enable controlled image generation across diverse tasks and constraints?
d24b4f34197df0257390b57f02537e6ce3284f2e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a universal guidance algorithm can be developed to enable any pre-trained diffusion model to be controlled by arbitrary, differentiable guidance functions—including segmentation, face recognition, object detection, and classifier signals—without retraining or fine-tuning the diffusion model, by modifying the sampling procedure to close the domain gap between noisy and clean images.
d24b4f34197df0257390b57f02537e6ce3284f2e.proposed_method: A universal guidance algorithm will be developed that augments the sampling process of pre-trained diffusion models to incorporate feedback from arbitrary, differentiable guidance functions. The approach consists of three main components: forward universal guidance, which computes guidance gradients on denoised image predictions at each diffusion step; backward universal guidance, which performs gradient-based optimization in the clean image space to enforce constraints and then maps the result back to the noisy latent space; and per-step self-recurrence, which injects additional noise and repeats the guidance step multiple times at each diffusion timestep to improve image fidelity and constraint satisfaction. The method allows for multiple guidance functions to be combined and used simultaneously, and does not require any modification or retraining of the diffusion model or the guidance networks. Guidance strength and the number of recurrence steps are tunable hyperparameters, and the method is compatible with both conditional and unconditional diffusion models.
d24b4f34197df0257390b57f02537e6ce3284f2e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both text-conditional diffusion models (e.g., Stable Diffusion) and unconditional diffusion models trained on ImageNet. The proposed universal guidance algorithm will be evaluated across a variety of guidance modalities, including CLIP-based text/image similarity, segmentation maps, face recognition embeddings, object detection outputs, and style transfer via reference images. Baselines will include standard conditional diffusion models and prior guided diffusion methods. Evaluation metrics will include qualitative assessment of image fidelity, alignment with guidance constraints (e.g., segmentation overlap, identity similarity, object localization accuracy), and quantitative measures such as classification accuracy and similarity scores. Experimental setups will involve varying guidance strengths, recurrence steps, and combinations of multiple guidance functions to assess flexibility and robustness.
d24b4f34197df0257390b57f02537e6ce3284f2e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a universal, plug-and-play guidance framework that enables any pre-trained diffusion model to be controlled by arbitrary, differentiable external functions without retraining or fine-tuning. The approach closes the domain gap between noisy and clean images by evaluating guidance on denoised predictions, incorporates both forward and backward guidance for improved constraint satisfaction, and introduces per-step self-recurrence to enhance image realism. The method supports simultaneous use of multiple guidance modalities and demonstrates effectiveness across diverse tasks, representing a significant advance in the flexibility and applicability of diffusion models for controlled image generation.

d25cd021507c1a1bfbec89cf980d4920df1073c2.title: Hardware-aligned Hierarchical Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-term Memory Access
d25cd021507c1a1bfbec89cf980d4920df1073c2.research_question: How can recurrent neural network-based language models be enhanced to achieve efficient, scalable, and flexible long-term memory access for long-context modeling, while maintaining strong length generalization and computational efficiency?
d25cd021507c1a1bfbec89cf980d4920df1073c2.hypothesis: A hierarchical sparse attention mechanism, when integrated with RNN-based architectures and aligned with hardware-efficient design, will enable efficient long-range random access to memory, improve length generalization, and maintain or improve performance on long-context tasks, all while preserving or enhancing computational and memory efficiency.
d25cd021507c1a1bfbec89cf980d4920df1073c2.proposed_method: A novel Hierarchical Sparse Attention (HSA) mechanism will be developed to augment RNN-based language models, such as Mamba, for efficient long-term memory access. HSA will divide input sequences into chunks, select the top-k most relevant chunks for each token using a two-stage attention process, and hierarchically aggregate information. The first stage will apply attention within each chunk to capture fine-grained token-level information, while the second stage will aggregate across selected chunks using learned token-to-chunk relevance scores, optimized end-to-end. To ensure practical scalability, a hardware-aligned kernel implementation will be designed, leveraging parallel computation and efficient memory management (including CPU-GPU offloading and shared chunk selection) to minimize memory footprint and maximize throughput. The resulting architecture, termed RAMba, will integrate HSA into specific layers of Mamba, offloading token-level key-value caches to CPU memory and maintaining compact chunk-level representations on GPU for efficient chunk selection and inference.
d25cd021507c1a1bfbec89cf980d4920df1073c2.experiment_details: Comprehensive experiments will be conducted on long-range language modeling and downstream tasks. Models will be pre-trained from scratch on a 60-billion-token subset of the Pile dataset, with a context length of 4K tokens, and evaluated for extrapolation to much longer contexts (up to 64M tokens). Baselines will include Transformer models (with full attention), Mamba-2, and variants with sliding window attention (SWA), Native Sparse Attention (NSA), and other sparse attention mechanisms. Evaluation datasets will include PG19, ArXiv-math, and Code for language modeling, as well as LongBenchV2 and RULER synthetic tasks for retrieval and reasoning. Downstream tasks such as summarization (XSUM, CNN) and QA (SQuaD, HotpotQA, QuALITY) will also be included. Metrics will include perplexity, retrieval accuracy, and task-specific scores (e.g., ROUGE, EM/F1, accuracy). Ablations will assess the impact of memory reset, chunk encoder presence, and chunk selection strategies. Efficiency will be measured via runtime, memory footprint, and throughput across varying sequence lengths and model sizes, with and without memory offloading.
d25cd021507c1a1bfbec89cf980d4920df1073c2.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a two-stage hierarchical sparse attention mechanism that enables end-to-end learning of token-to-chunk relevance, improving chunk selection accuracy and length generalization far beyond pre-training context lengths. The hardware-aligned kernel design allows for efficient parallel computation and near-constant memory usage during inference, even with extremely long contexts. RAMba, the resulting architecture, is the first Mamba-based model to achieve perfect accuracy on passkey retrieval tasks with contexts up to 64 million tokens, and demonstrates superior performance and efficiency compared to both Transformer and prior sparse attention baselines. The approach also provides a practical solution for scalable, permanent memory in language models.

d279d184011c6fe35075c27286473976ff56a00a.title: Closed-form merging of parameter-efficient modules for Federated Continual Learning
d279d184011c6fe35075c27286473976ff56a00a.research_question: How can parameter-efficient modules be effectively merged in federated continual learning settings to produce a unified model that preserves performance across clients and tasks, while maintaining efficiency and privacy?
d279d184011c6fe35075c27286473976ff56a00a.hypothesis: A closed-form solution for merging low-rank adaptation (LoRA) modules, combined with an alternating optimization strategy, will yield a unified model that aligns the responses of all learned modules, achieves state-of-the-art performance in federated class-incremental learning, and improves efficiency and privacy compared to existing methods.
d279d184011c6fe35075c27286473976ff56a00a.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a closed-form merging framework for parameter-efficient LoRA modules in federated continual learning. The approach formulates the merging problem as an objective to match the responses of all learned modules, leading to a system with infinitely many solutions for the low-rank matrices A and B. To resolve this, an alternating optimization strategy is employed: in each communication round, one matrix (either A or B) is fixed and shared across clients, while the other is trained and then merged in closed form using derived equations. Clients transmit only the diagonal of the Gram matrix (X X^T) and the updated low-rank matrix to the server, ensuring privacy and reducing communication overhead. At the end of each task, task-specific residuals are merged across tasks using a closed-form regression mean, resulting in a final model that generalizes across both clients and tasks.
d279d184011c6fe35075c27286473976ff56a00a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of vision and language datasets, including CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, Cars-196, CUB-200, EuroSAT, and the Out-Of-Scope intent classification dataset. Each dataset is partitioned into incremental tasks and distributed across multiple clients (typically 10), with varying degrees of data heterogeneity controlled by Dirichlet distribution parameters (β). The proposed method will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines from continual learning, federated learning, and model merging literature, including EWC, LwF, L2P, CODA-Prompt, FisherAvg, RegMean, CCVR, FedProto, TARGET, PILoRA, and TIES-Merging. Evaluation metrics include Final Average Accuracy (FAA), with experiments repeated over multiple seeds for statistical robustness. Implementation details specify the use of pre-trained ViT-B/16 and T5-small backbones, fixed numbers of communication rounds and epochs, and standardized data augmentations and hyperparameters.
d279d184011c6fe35075c27286473976ff56a00a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first closed-form solution for merging LoRA modules in federated continual learning, resolving the indeterminacy of previous formulations through an alternating optimization strategy. The method ensures privacy by transmitting only the diagonal of the Gram matrix, improves communication efficiency by sending only one low-rank matrix per round, and achieves faster convergence than existing baselines. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across a range of datasets and distribution scenarios, with ablation studies confirming the effectiveness of each component. The methodology is generalizable and can be extended to other parameter-efficient fine-tuning modules.

d28254a00141c4b83ade90af10ec432665a6ccdb.title: Eliminating Oversaturation and Artifacts of High Guidance Scales in Diffusion Models
d28254a00141c4b83ade90af10ec432665a6ccdb.research_question: How can the oversaturation and artifacts caused by high guidance scales in classifier-free guidance (CFG) for diffusion models be eliminated while preserving or improving image quality and alignment with input conditions?
d28254a00141c4b83ade90af10ec432665a6ccdb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that decomposing the CFG update into parallel and orthogonal components with respect to the conditional model prediction, and selectively down-weighting the parallel component, combined with rescaling and a reverse momentum term, will allow the use of higher guidance scales in diffusion models without causing oversaturation or artifacts, while maintaining or improving generation quality and alignment.
d28254a00141c4b83ade90af10ec432665a6ccdb.proposed_method: A novel guidance method, termed adaptive projected guidance (APG), will be developed for diffusion models. The approach involves decomposing the CFG update direction at each sampling step into parallel and orthogonal components relative to the conditional model prediction. The parallel component, which is responsible for oversaturation, will be down-weighted using a tunable hyperparameter, while the orthogonal component, which enhances image quality, will be retained. Additionally, the update direction will be rescaled to constrain its norm within a fixed radius, preventing large drifts during sampling. A reverse momentum term will be introduced, which negatively weights the average of previous updates, encouraging diversity and further reducing artifacts. The method will be implemented to operate directly on denoised predictions, ensuring compatibility with various diffusion model architectures and prediction types.
d28254a00141c4b83ade90af10ec432665a6ccdb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both text-to-image and class-conditional image generation tasks using state-of-the-art diffusion models, including Stable Diffusion (XL and 2.1), EDM2, DiT-XL/2, and Stable Diffusion 3. The evaluation will utilize standard pretrained checkpoints and default diffusion samplers to ensure consistency. Baseline comparisons will include standard CFG, CFGRescale, and other recent diversity-boosting methods. Evaluation metrics will comprise Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for overall quality and diversity, precision and recall for sample quality and distribution coverage, and custom color metrics such as mean saturation (from HSV conversion) and RMS contrast. Additional experiments will test compatibility with distilled models (e.g., SDXL-Lightning) and ablation studies will assess the contribution of each APG component. Computational overhead will be measured to confirm practical efficiency.
d28254a00141c4b83ade90af10ec432665a6ccdb.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first explicit decomposition of the CFG update into parallel and orthogonal components, identifying the parallel component as the source of oversaturation. By selectively down-weighting this component and incorporating rescaling and a novel reverse momentum term, the approach enables the use of higher guidance scales without the typical artifacts or loss of quality. APG is designed as a plug-and-play, computationally efficient alternative to CFG, compatible with a wide range of diffusion models and samplers. The method claims superior performance in FID, recall, and saturation metrics while maintaining precision, and demonstrates improved diversity and text rendering consistency in generated images.

d28aebd3c71def61a020373c1f76452590939426.title: Black-Box Dataset Ownership Verification via Backdoor Watermarking
d28aebd3c71def61a020373c1f76452590939426.research_question: How can ownership of released datasets be verified in black-box settings to detect and prevent unauthorized use, particularly when only model queries are available and no access to model parameters or training details is possible?
d28aebd3c71def61a020373c1f76452590939426.hypothesis: Embedding external patterns via poison-only backdoor attacks into datasets enables effective, stealthy, and harmless watermarking, such that ownership can be verified through hypothesis-test-guided black-box queries to suspicious models.
d28aebd3c71def61a020373c1f76452590939426.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework is proposed for dataset ownership verification in black-box settings, consisting of two main components: dataset watermarking and dataset verification. For watermarking, poison-only backdoor attacks (such as BadNets, blended attacks, word/sentence-level triggers in NLP, and graph backdoor attacks) are used to inject specific trigger patterns into a small subset of the released dataset, associating them with a target label while preserving high benign accuracy. The verification phase employs hypothesis-test-guided statistical tests (pairwise t-tests for probability-available scenarios and Wilcoxon tests for label-only scenarios) to determine if a suspicious model exhibits the backdoor behavior when queried with watermarked samples. The approach is designed to be stealthy (low poisoning rate, natural triggers), distinctive (high watermark success rate), and harmless (minimal impact on benign accuracy), and includes theoretical analysis to relate watermark success rate, sample size, and verification confidence.
d28aebd3c71def61a020373c1f76452590939426.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple benchmark datasets across image classification (CIFAR-10, ImageNet), natural language processing (IMDB, DBpedia), and graph recognition (COLLAB, REDDIT-MULTI-5K) tasks. For each domain, representative DNN architectures (e.g., ResNet, VGG, LSTM, WordCNN, GIN, GraphSAGE) will be used. The datasets will be watermarked using various backdoor attack methods with different triggers and poisoning rates. Suspicious models will be trained on both benign and watermarked datasets, and verification will be performed under three scenarios: independent trigger, independent model, and actual dataset stealing. Evaluation metrics include benign accuracy, watermark success rate, verification confidence (ΔP), and p-value from statistical tests. Ablation studies will assess the impact of poisoning rate and sample size, and robustness to fine-tuning will be evaluated.
d28aebd3c71def61a020373c1f76452590939426.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to address dataset ownership verification in black-box settings using backdoor watermarking, enabling dataset owners to detect unauthorized use without access to model internals. The method is generalizable across multiple data modalities (images, text, graphs), supports both probability-available and label-only black-box scenarios, and provides formal theoretical guarantees on verification confidence. The framework achieves high effectiveness, stealthiness, and minimal impact on dataset utility, and demonstrates strong empirical performance and robustness across diverse tasks.

d293299a18e1daa706ce603abce02b9df8f0ca7a.title: Nerfstudio: A Modular Framework for Neural Radiance Field Development
d293299a18e1daa706ce603abce02b9df8f0ca7a.research_question: How can the development, evaluation, and deployment of Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) methods be streamlined and made more accessible for both researchers and practitioners, particularly when working with real-world data and diverse application requirements?
d293299a18e1daa706ce603abce02b9df8f0ca7a.hypothesis: A modular, extensible, and user-friendly framework with real-time visualization and comprehensive data handling will significantly accelerate NeRF research and facilitate broader adoption and innovation, enabling efficient experimentation, qualitative assessment, and integration of new techniques.
d293299a18e1daa706ce603abce02b9df8f0ca7a.proposed_method: A modular Python-based framework will be developed for NeRF research, built around plug-and-play components such as data parsers, ray generators, samplers, encoders, fields, and renderers. The framework will support multiple input data pipelines, including images and videos from various sources (e.g., mobile apps, photogrammetry software), and allow for flexible integration of new NeRF techniques and architectures. An interactive real-time web viewer will be implemented to enable qualitative evaluation during both training and inference, supporting remote and local GPU environments. The framework will provide streamlined workflows for processing real-world data, optimizing camera poses, and exporting results in various formats (e.g., video, point clouds, meshes). The modular design will facilitate rapid prototyping, ablation studies, and community-driven extension.
d293299a18e1daa706ce603abce02b9df8f0ca7a.experiment_details: Experiments will include benchmarking the default NeRF-based method (Nerfacto) against state-of-the-art baselines such as Mip-NeRF-360 using both public datasets (e.g., Mip-NeRF-360’s 7 scenes) and a newly curated NerfstudioDataset of 10 real-world scenes captured with mobile phones and mirrorless cameras. Evaluation protocols will involve splitting data into training and held-out sets, with metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS computed on novel views. Ablation studies will be conducted by systematically disabling or modifying components (e.g., pose optimization, appearance embeddings, scene contraction) to assess their impact on both quantitative metrics and qualitative renderings, leveraging the real-time viewer for in-depth analysis. The framework’s extensibility will be demonstrated by integrating components from multiple recent NeRF papers and supporting export to downstream 3D tools.
d293299a18e1daa706ce603abce02b9df8f0ca7a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a highly modular and extensible architecture for NeRF development, enabling seamless integration of components from diverse NeRF methods. It provides an end-to-end workflow for real-world data, including user-friendly data ingestion, pose optimization, and export capabilities. The real-time web-based visualization tool offers interactive qualitative assessment during training and inference, addressing limitations of traditional quantitative metrics. The framework consolidates best practices and innovations from the NeRF literature into a unified, open-source platform, facilitating reproducible research, rapid experimentation, and community-driven development.

d2cbe11a0120e7654706816333c3a7785851280b.title: Multi-agent Contracts
d2cbe11a0120e7654706816333c3a7785851280b.research_question: How can computationally efficient algorithms be developed for designing optimal or near-optimal linear contracts in single-principal multi-agent settings, particularly when the principal's reward function belongs to various classes within the complement-free hierarchy?
d2cbe11a0120e7654706816333c3a7785851280b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that for certain structured reward functions, such as submodular and XOS, constant-factor approximation algorithms for optimal linear contract design are achievable in polynomial time using value and/or demand oracles, while for broader classes like subadditive functions, no polynomial-time algorithm can achieve better than a polynomially bounded approximation.
d2cbe11a0120e7654706816333c3a7785851280b.proposed_method: The proposed approach focuses on the multi-agent hidden-action principal-agent problem, where each agent chooses whether to exert costly effort, and the principal's expected reward is determined by a set function over the subset of agents exerting effort. The methodology restricts attention to linear contracts, which pay each agent a fixed fraction of the realized reward. The contract design problem is formulated as maximizing the principal's expected utility, subject to incentive compatibility constraints for all agents. For submodular and XOS reward functions, the method leverages value and demand oracles to define agent-specific 'prices' and uses a novel scaling property of XOS functions to select incentivized agent sets. The approach involves constructing demand sets based on these prices and, if necessary, scaling down sets to maintain sufficient marginal contributions, ensuring constant-factor approximation to the optimal utility.
d2cbe11a0120e7654706816333c3a7785851280b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets that instantiate various classes of reward functions (additive, submodular, XOS, and subadditive) over sets of agents with randomly assigned costs. The proposed algorithms will be evaluated against known baselines, such as single-agent optimal contracts and naive greedy selection, using approximation ratio (relative to the optimal utility) as the primary evaluation metric. Both value and demand oracle models will be simulated, and the computational complexity as well as achieved utility will be measured for varying numbers of agents and reward function structures. Hardness results will be demonstrated by constructing specific subadditive functions where the gap between achievable and optimal utility is provably large.
d2cbe11a0120e7654706816333c3a7785851280b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel algorithmic framework for multi-agent contract design that achieves constant-factor approximations for submodular and XOS reward functions using oracular access. A key innovation is the unconventional use of agent-specific prices and demand queries, combined with a new scaling property for XOS functions and their marginals, which may have independent interest in combinatorial optimization. The work also establishes a sharp computational separation between XOS/submodular and subadditive reward functions, showing that even functions close to submodular can exhibit polynomial hardness gaps in contract design, a phenomenon not observed in related domains such as combinatorial auctions.

d2e00bb58b53be546016cbe52df80a148b812624.title: Near-Optimal Policy Optimization for Correlated Equilibrium in General-Sum Markov Games
d2e00bb58b53be546016cbe52df80a148b812624.research_question: How can policy optimization algorithms be designed to efficiently compute correlated equilibria in multi-player general-sum Markov games, and what are the achievable convergence rates under oracle access to reward and transition functions?
d2e00bb58b53be546016cbe52df80a148b812624.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that an uncoupled, single-loop policy optimization algorithm, leveraging smooth value updates and optimistic follow-the-regularized-leader (OFTRL) with log barrier regularization, can achieve a near-optimal convergence rate of O~(1/T) to correlated equilibrium in general-sum Markov games, surpassing prior state-of-the-art rates.
d2e00bb58b53be546016cbe52df80a148b812624.proposed_method: A new policy optimization algorithm will be developed for multi-player general-sum Markov games, combining two core components: (i) smooth value updates for stability and efficient propagation of value information, and (ii) an optimistic follow-the-regularized-leader (OFTRL) policy update step using a log barrier regularizer to ensure low swap regret. The method will operate in a decentralized, uncoupled manner, allowing each agent to update its policy independently based only on local information and oracle access to reward and transition functions. The algorithm will maintain value functions for each player and update policies using weighted regret minimization, with the log barrier regularizer providing strong theoretical guarantees for convergence. The approach will be analyzed for both Q-value and V-value update variants, with a focus on the latter for compactness and scalability in multi-agent settings.
d2e00bb58b53be546016cbe52df80a148b812624.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in simulated multi-player general-sum Markov games, assuming oracle access to reward and transition functions. The proposed algorithm will be evaluated against existing baselines, including V-learning and prior OFTRL-based methods, with convergence rates to correlated equilibrium and coarse correlated equilibrium as primary metrics. Evaluation will focus on the rate of decrease of the equilibrium gap (CEGap) as a function of the number of episodes T, and the dependence on the number of agents, horizon, and action set size. Additional metrics such as per-state and weighted swap regret will be tracked. The experimental setup will include varying the number of agents, action space sizes, and horizon lengths to assess scalability and robustness.
d2e00bb58b53be546016cbe52df80a148b812624.novelty_claims: The proposed method claims a significant improvement in convergence rates, achieving a near-optimal O~(1/T) rate to correlated equilibrium in general-sum Markov games, which is a substantial advance over previous best-known rates of O~(T^{-1/2}) and O~(T^{-3/4}). The algorithm is uncoupled, decentralized, and single-loop, making it practical for multi-agent systems. The use of smooth value updates in conjunction with OFTRL and log barrier regularization is novel in this context, enabling both computational efficiency and strong theoretical guarantees. The method also provides a scalable approach that avoids the curse of dimensionality associated with Q-value updates in multi-agent settings.

d2f395e032864af365978559b1751d658d8137f4.title: Sample Efficiency of Data Augmentation Consistency Regularization
d2f395e032864af365978559b1751d658d8137f4.research_question: How do different algorithmic approaches to utilizing augmented data affect sample efficiency and generalization in supervised learning, particularly in the context of data augmentation consistency regularization versus empirical risk minimization on augmented data?
d2f395e032864af365978559b1751d658d8137f4.hypothesis: Data augmentation consistency (DAC) regularization is intrinsically more sample-efficient and yields better generalization than empirical risk minimization on augmented data (DA-ERM), even when augmentations are misspecified or limited in number.
d2f395e032864af365978559b1751d658d8137f4.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to compare data augmentation consistency (DAC) regularization and empirical risk minimization on augmented data (DA-ERM). The approach begins with a formal analysis in the linear regression setting, focusing on label-invariant augmentations, and extends to cases where augmentations may alter the label distribution (misspecified augmentations). The analysis will be further generalized to non-linear models, including two-layer neural networks and deep neural network (DNN)-based classifiers, using expansion-based augmentations. The DAC regularization will be implemented as a penalty enforcing similarity between the model's representations or predictions on original and augmented samples, controlled by a regularization parameter. Theoretical results will be derived to quantify generalization bounds and sample efficiency, with special attention to the effects of augmentation strength, number, and misspecification.
d2f395e032864af365978559b1751d658d8137f4.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on the CIFAR-100 dataset, using a subset of 10,000 labeled samples (100 per class) for training and the standard test set for evaluation. Data augmentations will be generated using RandAugment, with the number of augmentations per sample varied systematically (e.g., 1, 3, 7, 15). The primary comparison will be between DAC regularization (with varying regularization strengths) and DA-ERM, using the same neural network architecture (WideResNet-28-2) and identical training settings (optimizer, learning rate schedule, etc.) for both methods. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy, reported as mean and standard deviation over five independent runs. Additional experiments will investigate the effect of the number and strength of augmentations, as well as the impact of augmentation-induced label misspecification.
d2f395e032864af365978559b1751d658d8137f4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified theoretical and empirical framework for directly comparing DAC regularization and DA-ERM under identical conditions, providing the first rigorous sample efficiency analysis of these approaches. Theoretical contributions include new generalization bounds for both linear and non-linear models under various augmentation regimes, including label-invariant and misspecified augmentations. The dimension reduction perspective on DAC is formalized and extended to complex models and classification settings. Empirical results are designed to provide clean, apples-to-apples comparisons without confounding factors, demonstrating the superior efficacy and robustness of DAC regularization, especially with limited or strong augmentations.

d2f8d3bd5cdddf1f3d607714f21deaab019a87cb.title: Graph Inductive Biases in Transformers without Message Passing
d2f8d3bd5cdddf1f3d607714f21deaab019a87cb.research_question: How can graph inductive biases be effectively incorporated into Transformer architectures for graph data, without relying on explicit message-passing modules, to improve performance across both small and large graph datasets?
d2f8d3bd5cdddf1f3d607714f21deaab019a87cb.hypothesis: A Transformer-based architecture for graphs that integrates graph inductive biases through learned relative positional encodings, a flexible attention mechanism, and degree information—without explicit message passing—will achieve state-of-the-art performance across a variety of graph learning tasks and dataset scales.
d2f8d3bd5cdddf1f3d607714f21deaab019a87cb.proposed_method: A novel Graph Transformer architecture, termed GRIT (Graph Inductive bias Transformer), will be developed to incorporate graph inductive biases without explicit message-passing modules. The method will utilize learned relative positional encodings initialized with relative random walk probabilities (RRWP), which are theoretically shown to capture shortest path distances and general classes of graph propagation matrices. A flexible attention mechanism will be designed to jointly update both node and node-pair representations, allowing the model to learn and update positional encodings dynamically. Additionally, degree information will be injected into each layer using adaptive degree scalers, and batch normalization will be employed instead of layer normalization to preserve degree information. The architecture will be theoretically justified for its expressivity and empirically validated through ablation and synthetic experiments.
d2f8d3bd5cdddf1f3d607714f21deaab019a87cb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of graph learning benchmarks, including five datasets from BenchmarkingGNNs (ZINC, MNIST, CIFAR10, PATTERN, CLUSTER), two from the Long-Range Graph Benchmark (Peptides-func, Peptides-struct), the large-scale ZINC-full dataset, and the PCQM4Mv2 molecular regression dataset. The proposed method will be compared against a comprehensive suite of baselines: popular message-passing neural networks (GCN, GIN, GAT, GatedGCN, PNA), higher-order GNNs (δ-2-GNN, CIN), positional encoding enhanced GNNs (SignNet), and state-of-the-art Graph Transformers (Graphormer, SAN, GPS, TokenGT, EGT, Graphormer-URPE, Graphormer-GD). Evaluation metrics will include mean absolute error (MAE) for regression tasks and accuracy or average precision for classification tasks. Experiments will also include ablation studies to assess the impact of each architectural component, sensitivity analysis on the order of random walk positional encodings, and synthetic tasks to test the attention mechanism's ability to emulate various graph propagation matrices.
d2f8d3bd5cdddf1f3d607714f21deaab019a87cb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a Graph Transformer that incorporates graph inductive biases without explicit message-passing, bridging the performance gap between message-passing-based and non-message-passing-based methods across dataset sizes. The use of learned relative positional encodings initialized with random walk probabilities is theoretically and empirically shown to be more expressive than shortest path distance encodings. The flexible attention mechanism jointly updates node and node-pair representations, enabling the model to learn a broad class of graph propagations. The integration of degree information with batch normalization preserves critical structural information. The method achieves state-of-the-art results on a wide range of graph benchmarks, demonstrating the effectiveness of graph inductive biases in Transformers without message passing.

d2fd115e9d6be6d18430a9a05b2556a2773b96e6.title: Scalable First-order Method for Certifying Optimal k-Sparse GLMs
d2fd115e9d6be6d18430a9a05b2556a2773b96e6.research_question: How can optimality certificates for k-sparse generalized linear models (GLMs) be efficiently and scalably computed, especially in high-dimensional settings with highly correlated features, where existing methods for lower-bound computation in branch-and-bound frameworks are computationally intensive or slow to converge?
d2fd115e9d6be6d18430a9a05b2556a2773b96e6.hypothesis: A first-order proximal gradient algorithm, leveraging a perspective relaxation and a customized pooled-adjacent-violators algorithm (PAVA) for efficient proximal operator computation, will enable scalable and efficient certification of optimality for k-sparse GLMs, outperforming existing convex relaxation and mixed-integer programming methods in both speed and scalability.
d2fd115e9d6be6d18430a9a05b2556a2773b96e6.proposed_method: The proposed approach will reformulate the k-sparse GLM optimization problem using a perspective relaxation, resulting in a composite convex objective amenable to first-order optimization. A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm (FISTA) will be employed as the core solver, with a novel, customized PAVA designed to compute the proximal operator of the non-smooth component exactly in log-linear time, thus eliminating the need for expensive second-order cone programs. The method will incorporate a value-based restart strategy to empirically achieve linear convergence and will be designed for efficient GPU acceleration by relying primarily on matrix-vector multiplications. Safe lower bounds will be computed at each branch-and-bound node using duality, ensuring effective pruning and optimality certification.
d2fd115e9d6be6d18430a9a05b2556a2773b96e6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including high-dimensional regression and classification tasks (e.g., n, p up to 16,000). Baselines will include state-of-the-art commercial and open-source SOCP solvers such as Gurobi, MOSEK, SCS, and Clarabel, interfaced via CVXPY. Evaluation metrics will include runtime, optimality gap, and scalability (problem size handled). The efficiency of the customized PAVA for proximal operator evaluation will be benchmarked against direct SOCP-based approaches. The effectiveness of the proposed FISTA-based method for lower-bound computation and overall branch-and-bound performance will be assessed, including GPU acceleration. Empirical convergence rates (primal, dual, and primal-dual gap) will be tracked, and early termination criteria will be tested for practical efficiency.
d2fd115e9d6be6d18430a9a05b2556a2773b96e6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first scalable first-order method for certifying optimality of k-sparse GLMs using a perspective relaxation, with a proximal operator computed exactly in log-linear time via a customized PAVA. The approach achieves substantial speedups (1-2 orders of magnitude) in lower-bound computation compared to existing methods, enables GPU acceleration, and empirically demonstrates linear convergence with a simple restart strategy. This framework allows for efficient optimality certification on large-scale problems previously intractable for commercial MIP solvers, and provides a practical, high-performance component for integration into next-generation MIP solvers.

d3135733aa39dec20ce72aa138589dda27c8406d.title: Learn to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering
d3135733aa39dec20ce72aa138589dda27c8406d.research_question: Can large language models be enhanced to perform reliable and interpretable multimodal science question answering by generating explicit, human-like chains of thought, and how does access to explanations and lectures affect their reasoning and data efficiency?
d3135733aa39dec20ce72aa138589dda27c8406d.hypothesis: Incorporating explicit chain-of-thought reasoning, in the form of generated lectures and explanations, into large language models will improve their accuracy, interpretability, and data efficiency for multimodal science question answering tasks.
d3135733aa39dec20ce72aa138589dda27c8406d.proposed_method: A large-scale multimodal science question answering benchmark, SCIENCEQA, will be constructed, containing over 21,000 multiple-choice questions spanning natural, social, and language sciences, each annotated with multimodal context (images, text), lectures, and detailed explanations. Two main approaches will be developed: (1) fine-tuning large language models (e.g., UnifiedQA) to generate not only the answer but also a lecture and explanation as a chain-of-thought; (2) employing few-shot prompting of large language models (e.g., GPT-3) with in-context examples that include both answers and their corresponding lectures and explanations. The models will be trained to output a structured response comprising the answer, a general lecture (background knowledge), and a specific explanation (reasoning path), thereby mimicking human multi-hop reasoning.
d3135733aa39dec20ce72aa138589dda27c8406d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the SCIENCEQA dataset, which is split into training, validation, and test sets (60:20:20). Baseline models will include heuristic (random, human), state-of-the-art VQA models, and large language models in zero-shot, few-shot, and fine-tuned settings. Evaluation will measure question answering accuracy, as well as the quality of generated explanations using automatic metrics (BLEU, ROUGE-L, semantic similarity) and human judgments (relevance, correctness, completeness). Ablation studies will assess the impact of different input modalities and prompt types, and upper-bound experiments will provide models with gold explanations to measure maximal potential gains. Data efficiency will be analyzed by varying the amount of training data.
d3135733aa39dec20ce72aa138589dda27c8406d.novelty_claims: The proposed work introduces the first large-scale, multimodal science question answering dataset with rich domain diversity and detailed, grounded lectures and explanations for each answer. It pioneers the systematic study of chain-of-thought generation in multimodal scientific reasoning, demonstrating that explicit reasoning steps improve both performance and interpretability of large language models. The research also quantifies the impact of explanations on data efficiency and establishes new benchmarks for interpretable, multimodal question answering.

d318e0169f649656c71f02a1f84194a734fe1962.title: Reward Design with Language Models
d318e0169f649656c71f02a1f84194a734fe1962.research_question: Can reinforcement learning agents be effectively trained to align with diverse and potentially hard-to-specify human objectives by leveraging large language models as proxy reward functions, using only natural language prompts and minimal user-provided examples or descriptions?
d318e0169f649656c71f02a1f84194a734fe1962.hypothesis: Large language models, when prompted with a small number of user-provided examples or natural language descriptions, can serve as effective proxy reward functions for reinforcement learning agents, enabling the agents to learn behaviors aligned with user objectives even in the absence of explicit or easily specified reward functions.
d318e0169f649656c71f02a1f84194a734fe1962.proposed_method: A general reinforcement learning framework is developed in which a large language model (LLM), such as GPT-3, is prompted with a concatenation of (1) a task description, (2) a user-specified objective (either as a few examples or a natural language description), (3) a textual representation of an RL episode's outcome, and (4) a question asking whether the outcome satisfies the user’s objective. The LLM's output is parsed into a reward signal (typically binary) using a handcrafted, task-specific parser. This reward signal replaces the traditional reward function in the RL training loop. The RL agent updates its policy based on these LLM-derived rewards, and the process is repeated for each episode. The framework is agnostic to the underlying RL algorithm and can be applied to both single-step and multi-step tasks.
d318e0169f649656c71f02a1f84194a734fe1962.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three domains: the Ultimatum Game (single-step, few-shot prompting), normal-form Matrix Games (single-step, zero-shot prompting), and the DEALORNODEAL negotiation task (multi-step, few-shot prompting). In each domain, ground truth user objectives are defined (e.g., fairness thresholds, solution concepts, negotiation styles), and prompts are constructed accordingly. Baselines include supervised learning models trained on the same examples, RL agents trained with ground truth reward functions, and, for zero-shot settings, a NoObjective baseline where the LLM is prompted without user objectives. Evaluation metrics include labeling accuracy (agreement between LLM-provided rewards and ground truth), RL agent accuracy (alignment of learned policy with user objectives), and, in the negotiation task, qualitative measures such as advantage, diversity, and agreement rate. A pilot user study is also conducted in the negotiation domain, where human users provide their own examples and rate agent alignment.
d318e0169f649656c71f02a1f84194a734fe1962.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the use of large language models as proxy reward functions for reinforcement learning, enabling intuitive and efficient reward design via natural language prompts and minimal user input. The method is shown to be data-efficient, requiring far fewer examples than supervised learning baselines, and is robust across both few-shot and zero-shot settings. The approach generalizes to new user objectives, supports complex multi-step tasks, and demonstrates superior alignment with user-specified objectives compared to traditional reward design or supervised learning. A pilot user study further validates the framework's effectiveness in producing agents aligned with diverse, user-defined objectives.

d31afa9013658209ad3b2b6b1f360efa27aee4c6.title: Diffusion Models are Secretly Exchangeable: Parallelizing DDPMs via Autospeculation
