d31afa9013658209ad3b2b6b1f360efa27aee4c6.research_question: How can inference in denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) be parallelized to achieve significant speedup without sacrificing sample quality, and what fundamental properties of diffusion processes can be leveraged to enable such parallelization?
d31afa9013658209ad3b2b6b1f360efa27aee4c6.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a hidden exchangeability property in the increments of DDPMs, when appropriately reparametrized, allows for the adaptation of speculative decoding techniques to diffusion models, enabling error-free parallelization and substantial theoretical and empirical speedup in inference.
d31afa9013658209ad3b2b6b1f360efa27aee4c6.proposed_method: A novel inference framework, Autospeculative Decoding (ASD), is developed for DDPMs by exploiting a hidden exchangeability property in the increments of the diffusion process. Under an appropriate transformation, the increments of the DDPM process become exchangeable, meaning their joint distribution is invariant under permutation. ASD adapts speculative decoding—originally designed for autoregressive models—to the diffusion setting without requiring any auxiliary draft models. At each inference step, ASD generates speculative samples for future denoising steps using the main diffusion model itself, then verifies these speculations in parallel via a rejection sampling mechanism tailored for Gaussian transitions. The method ensures that the output samples are identically distributed to those from the sequential DDPM process, maintaining sample quality while enabling parallel execution.
d31afa9013658209ad3b2b6b1f360efa27aee4c6.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a range of generative modeling tasks, including image generation with both latent and pixel-space diffusion models (e.g., Stable Diffusion-v2, LSUN Church) and robot control tasks using diffusion policies (e.g., Robomimic suite). ASD is evaluated for both algorithmic speedup (reduction in neural network calls) and wall-clock speedup (actual runtime reduction), with parallelization implemented via multi-GPU setups or batching, depending on model size. Baselines include standard sequential DDPM inference and, where relevant, other parallelization or acceleration techniques. Evaluation metrics include CLIP score and FID for image quality, and task success rates for robot control, ensuring that acceleration does not degrade sample fidelity. Empirical results demonstrate 1.8-4× wall-clock speedup and up to 7× algorithmic speedup, with no loss in output quality.
d31afa9013658209ad3b2b6b1f360efa27aee4c6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach uncovers and exploits a previously unrecognized exchangeability property in DDPM increments, enabling the first error-free, theoretically guaranteed parallelization of DDPM inference without restrictive assumptions on the score function. ASD achieves a provable O~(K1/3) parallel runtime speedup over K-step sequential DDPM, surpassing prior methods that either required auxiliary models, imposed strong smoothness assumptions, or introduced approximation errors. The method bridges performance optimization techniques between autoregressive and diffusion models, and demonstrates practical, high-fidelity acceleration across diverse domains.

d32a0fdd974badf6bf5529e11c6776fe5ed88d00.title: Leveraging sparse and shared feature activations for disentangled representation learning
d32a0fdd974badf6bf5529e11c6776fe5ed88d00.research_question: How can meaningful and disentangled representations be learned from high-dimensional data using knowledge from multiple supervised tasks, in a way that supports robust generalization to out-of-distribution and few-shot scenarios, without direct supervision on the underlying factors of variation?
d32a0fdd974badf6bf5529e11c6776fe5ed88d00.hypothesis: Disentangled representations that generalize well to new tasks and domains can be learned by enforcing sparse sufficiency and minimality constraints on feature activations across a diverse set of supervised tasks, even without direct observation of the underlying factors of variation.
d32a0fdd974badf6bf5529e11c6776fe5ed88d00.proposed_method: A meta-learning framework will be developed in which a shared backbone network learns feature representations across a distribution of supervised classification tasks, each defined as a C-way classification problem. For each task, a task-specific linear classification head is trained using a support set, while the backbone is updated using query set samples. Two regularizers are incorporated into the training objective: an L1 sparsity penalty to ensure that each task activates only a sparse subset of features (sparse sufficiency), and an entropy-based feature sharing penalty to encourage maximal sharing of features across tasks (minimality). The overall optimization is formulated as a bi-level problem, with the inner loop fitting the linear heads and the outer loop updating the backbone via implicit differentiation. Tasks are generated by randomly sampling class subsets from the training data, and the regularization strengths are controlled by hyperparameters α and β.
d32a0fdd974badf6bf5529e11c6776fe5ed88d00.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic benchmarks such as DSprites, 3DShapes, SmallNorb, and Cars will be used to quantitatively assess disentanglement using metrics like DCI, leveraging ground-truth factors of variation. Real-world evaluations will include domain generalization and distribution shift benchmarks such as PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, Waterbirds, CivilComments, and Camelyon17, covering both image and text modalities. Baselines for comparison will include ERM, IRM, CORAL, GroupDRO, and other state-of-the-art domain generalization and meta-learning methods. Evaluation metrics will include in-distribution and out-of-distribution accuracy, worst-group accuracy, and disentanglement metrics where applicable. Few-shot transfer learning scenarios will be tested by fitting linear heads with limited labeled samples from new domains, and results will be averaged over multiple random draws for statistical robustness.
d32a0fdd974badf6bf5529e11c6776fe5ed88d00.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled method for learning disentangled representations from real-world data by leveraging a distribution of supervised tasks, without requiring direct supervision on the factors of variation. The combination of sparse sufficiency and minimality regularizers within a meta-learning framework is claimed to yield representations that are both interpretable and robust to distribution shifts, outperforming existing baselines in domain generalization and few-shot transfer settings. Theoretical analysis is provided to support the identifiability of the approach under reasonable assumptions, and empirical results demonstrate improved disentanglement and generalization compared to prior methods.

d339b1ec6d4365abdc13ce36631b72482cfa10a8.title: Variational Linearized Laplace Approximation for Bayesian Deep Learning
d339b1ec6d4365abdc13ce36631b72482cfa10a8.research_question: How can scalable and efficient uncertainty estimation be achieved for large deep neural networks (DNNs) in Bayesian deep learning, particularly when computing predictive distributions that accurately reflect model confidence, without incurring prohibitive computational costs?
d339b1ec6d4365abdc13ce36631b72482cfa10a8.hypothesis: A variational sparse Gaussian Process (GP) approximation based on the dual RKHS formulation, which anchors the predictive mean to a pre-trained DNN, will enable efficient and accurate uncertainty estimation for large DNNs, outperforming existing scalable Laplace-based methods in both predictive quality and computational efficiency.
d339b1ec6d4365abdc13ce36631b72482cfa10a8.proposed_method: A new method, Variational Linearized Laplace Approximation (VaLLA), is developed to approximate the Linearized Laplace Approximation (LLA) for Bayesian deep learning. VaLLA interprets the LLA predictive distribution as a Gaussian Process and employs a variational sparse GP using inducing points, leveraging the dual RKHS representation to ensure the predictive mean matches that of the pre-trained DNN. The method decouples the mean and covariance inducing points, allowing the predictive variance to be efficiently approximated while preserving the original DNN's predictions. Optimization is performed via stochastic mini-batch training, with the variational parameters for the covariance found by maximizing an objective based on α-divergences, supporting early stopping and validation-based hyperparameter tuning. The approach achieves sub-linear training time with respect to dataset size, and the computational cost is independent of the number of training points.
d339b1ec6d4365abdc13ce36631b72482cfa10a8.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both regression and classification tasks, including large-scale datasets such as Year, Airline, and Taxi for regression, and MNIST, FMNIST, and CIFAR10 with various ResNet architectures for classification. The proposed method is compared against several baselines: accelerated LLA (ELLA, using Nyström approximation), Kronecker-factored and diagonal GGN approximations, sample-then-optimize LLA, mean-field variational inference, SNGP, and GP-Subset. Evaluation metrics include negative log-likelihood (NLL), continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), centered quantile metric (CQM), accuracy (ACC), expected calibration error (ECE), Brier score, and out-of-distribution AUC. Experimental setups involve using pre-trained DNNs, fixing the predictive mean, and optimizing variational parameters for the covariance, with early stopping based on validation sets to prevent overfitting. The number of inducing points is varied, and computational time is measured to assess scalability.
d339b1ec6d4365abdc13ce36631b72482cfa10a8.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel variational sparse GP approximation for LLA that retains the predictive mean of the pre-trained DNN, enabling accurate uncertainty quantification without additional prediction error. Unlike previous scalable LLA variants, VaLLA achieves sub-linear training cost with respect to dataset size and computational cost independent of the number of training points. The dual RKHS formulation allows for efficient stochastic optimization and flexible hyperparameter tuning. VaLLA demonstrates superior or comparable predictive distribution quality and computational efficiency compared to state-of-the-art scalable LLA methods, including ELLA and sample-then-optimize approaches, and provides robust predictive distributions even in large-scale settings.

d358ec5922838452c269cf09accc57bf3354bafe.title: Testing the Limits of Fine-Tuning for Improving Visual Cognition in Vision Language Models
d358ec5922838452c269cf09accc57bf3354bafe.research_question: Can fine-tuning vision-language models (VLMs) on specific visual cognition tasks improve their performance and alignment with human behavior, and does such fine-tuning enable robust generalization to new tasks, domains, or visual characteristics beyond the fine-tuning distribution?
d358ec5922838452c269cf09accc57bf3354bafe.hypothesis: Fine-tuning VLMs on task-specific data will improve their performance and alignment with human judgments on the fine-tuned task, but may not enable robust generalization to tasks with different visual characteristics or cognitive domains.
d358ec5922838452c269cf09accc57bf3354bafe.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted by fine-tuning large-scale vision-language models (VLMs), such as Qwen2-VL and Llama3.2, on datasets designed for two cognitive domains: intuitive physics and causal reasoning. Datasets will be generated using a virtual environment (ThreeDWorld) to create block towers and pyramids with varying properties, ensuring controlled evaluation of both within-domain and cross-domain generalization. Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) with QLoRA will be employed, where only low-rank adapter layers are trained while the main model weights remain fixed, reducing computational overhead and risk of catastrophic forgetting. The models will be prompted with structured queries to elicit binary (Yes/No) responses regarding the stability or causal properties of block configurations, and will be fine-tuned both on ground truth labels and on human judgment data. Multiple seeds and data splits will be used to ensure robustness and reproducibility.
d358ec5922838452c269cf09accc57bf3354bafe.experiment_details: Experiments will involve fine-tuning models on one domain (e.g., intuitive physics with towers of 2–4 blocks) and evaluating them on a variety of test sets: (1) held-out samples from the same distribution, (2) out-of-distribution samples with different block counts (e.g., 5–7 blocks), (3) images with different visual characteristics (e.g., real block towers from Lerer et al., 2016), and (4) tasks from a different cognitive domain (e.g., causal reasoning). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on binary classification tasks and Cohen’s kappa for alignment with human judgments. Baselines will include zero-shot performance of the pre-trained models and comparison to human participant data collected via online experiments. All experiments will be repeated with three different random seeds, and results will be averaged for statistical robustness.
d358ec5922838452c269cf09accc57bf3354bafe.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a comprehensive, systematic framework for testing the limits of task-specific fine-tuning in VLMs across multiple cognitive domains and visual environments. It leverages controlled synthetic datasets and human behavioral data to rigorously evaluate both performance and human alignment, and uniquely examines not only in-domain improvements but also the ability to generalize across domains, visual characteristics, and task types. The methodology combines parameter-efficient fine-tuning with detailed behavioral alignment analysis, providing new insights into the brittleness and boundaries of current VLM adaptation strategies for human-like visual cognition.

d364f8cb20daf958ebca53a807e79082eff98e78.title: Bigger, Better, Faster: Human-level Atari with human-level efficiency
d364f8cb20daf958ebca53a807e79082eff98e78.research_question: How can deep reinforcement learning agents achieve human-level or super-human performance on the Atari 100K benchmark with sample efficiency and computational efficiency comparable to or better than human-level gameplay, and what design choices enable scalable and efficient value-based RL in low-data regimes?
d364f8cb20daf958ebca53a807e79082eff98e78.hypothesis: Scaling the neural network capacity of value-based RL agents, combined with targeted algorithmic modifications such as periodic network resets, adaptive update horizons, increased discount factors, weight decay, and the removal of certain exploration mechanisms, will enable model-free RL agents to achieve super-human performance on the Atari 100K benchmark with human-level sample efficiency and improved computational efficiency.
d364f8cb20daf958ebca53a807e79082eff98e78.proposed_method: A new value-based RL agent, termed BBF, will be developed by scaling up the neural network architecture used for value estimation, specifically employing a 15-layer Impala-based ResNet with a 4× width increase per layer. The agent will incorporate periodic 'hard' resets of the convolutional layers, moving parameters 50% toward random initialization to counter overfitting and enable higher replay ratios. An adaptive n-step update horizon will be used, exponentially decreasing from 10 to 3 over the first 10K gradient steps after each reset, and the discount factor will be increased from 0.97 to 0.997 on a similar schedule to prioritize delayed rewards. Weight decay will be applied via the AdamW optimizer to further regularize training, and the self-supervised SPR loss will be retained to enhance representation learning. NoisyNets will be removed to reduce computational overhead and variance. An exponential moving average target network will be used for stability during training and action selection.
d364f8cb20daf958ebca53a807e79082eff98e78.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Atari 100K benchmark, which consists of 26 diverse Atari 2600 games, limiting agents to 100,000 environment steps (approximately two hours of gameplay). The agent's performance will be evaluated using the interquartile mean (IQM) of human-normalized scores across all games and seeds, as well as the optimality gap metric. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art model-free and model-based agents such as SR-SPR, SPR, DrQ, DER, EfficientZero, and IRIS. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of each component (e.g., network size, reset strength, replay ratio, weight decay, n-step schedule, discount factor, self-supervision, and target networks). Additional validation will be performed on the full suite of 55 ALE games, including those not present in Atari 100K, and with/without sticky actions to assess generalization and robustness. Computational efficiency will be measured in terms of GPU-hours and compared to other agents.
d364f8cb20daf958ebca53a807e79082eff98e78.novelty_claims: The proposed approach claims a significant advancement in sample-efficient, model-free deep RL by demonstrating that large-scale value networks, when combined with carefully selected algorithmic modifications, can achieve super-human performance on the Atari 100K benchmark with human-level efficiency. The method introduces a combination of aggressive network resets, adaptive update horizons, increased discount factors, and weight decay to enable stable and efficient training at high replay ratios. The removal of NoisyNets for computational savings and the demonstration of generalization to unseen games and sticky actions further contribute to the novelty. The approach sets a new milestone for computational efficiency, outperforming both model-free and model-based baselines in terms of GPU-hours required for training, and provides actionable insights for scaling value-based RL in sample-constrained settings.

d39ad86d4617e069d89b6d62c760c2ba268a2b85.title: Continuous PDE Dynamics Forecasting with Implicit Neural Representations
d39ad86d4617e069d89b6d62c760c2ba268a2b85.research_question: How can data-driven methods be developed to forecast the temporal evolution of physical phenomena governed by partial differential equations (PDEs) in a way that is continuous in both space and time, robust to changes in spatial and temporal discretization, and able to generalize to new observation grids, resolutions, and extrapolation scenarios?
d39ad86d4617e069d89b6d62c760c2ba268a2b85.hypothesis: A model that leverages implicit neural representations (INRs) to embed spatial observations into a latent space and employs a learned continuous-time ordinary differential equation (ODE) for temporal evolution will enable accurate, flexible, and generalizable forecasting of PDE dynamics at arbitrary spatiotemporal locations, even when trained on sparse or irregular grids.
d39ad86d4617e069d89b6d62c760c2ba268a2b85.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a framework that models PDE dynamics using a combination of implicit neural representations and latent ODEs. Spatial observations at any given time are embedded into a low-dimensional latent vector via an encoder based on auto-decoding, which is flexible to arbitrary and irregular spatial grids. The temporal evolution of this latent vector is governed by a learned ODE, providing continuous-time dynamics. A decoder, implemented as a hypernetwork-conditioned INR (specifically, a FourierNet with amplitude modulation for space-time separation), maps the latent vector back to a spatial function at any desired time and location. The method is trained in two stages: first, the decoder and latent vectors are optimized via auto-decoding; second, the latent ODE parameters are learned to model the temporal flow in latent space. This architecture allows for independent and flexible treatment of space and time, enabling forecasting at unseen spatial locations and times beyond the training horizon.
d39ad86d4617e069d89b6d62c760c2ba268a2b85.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of multi-dimensional PDE systems representative of real-world physical processes, such as those encountered in climate modeling and fluid dynamics. The evaluation will consider scenarios involving generalization to new initial conditions, extrapolation to new spatial grids and resolutions, prediction at unobserved spatial and temporal locations, and adaptation to irregular or manifold-based domains. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art neural PDE forecasters, such as CNN-based, GNN-based, neural operator (e.g., FNO, GNO, DeepONet), and INR-based models. Evaluation metrics will include standard forecasting accuracy measures (e.g., mean squared error) on both interpolation and extrapolation tasks, with detailed ablation studies to assess the impact of each architectural component. The experimental setup will ensure that training and test grids differ, and that extrapolation beyond the training time horizon is required.
d39ad86d4617e069d89b6d62c760c2ba268a2b85.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first data-driven model to combine continuous-time latent dynamics with space-continuous implicit neural representations, enabling forecasting at arbitrary spatiotemporal locations and generalization to new grids, resolutions, and domains. The approach introduces a novel amplitude modulation parameterization for INRs, achieving effective space-time separation and improved efficiency. Unlike prior methods, the framework is robust to changes in spatial and temporal discretization, supports learning from sparse or irregular grids, and can extrapolate both in time and space. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and versatility across a range of challenging PDE forecasting scenarios.

d3aa244f42c598d58d055c177b2ca1fdc1a172ad.title: Adapting Neural Link Predictors for Data-Efficient Complex Query Answering
d3aa244f42c598d58d055c177b2ca1fdc1a172ad.research_question: How can neural link predictors be adapted for data-efficient and interpretable complex query answering over incomplete knowledge graphs, including queries with logical negations, while maintaining or improving predictive accuracy and parameter efficiency?
d3aa244f42c598d58d055c177b2ca1fdc1a172ad.hypothesis: A parameter-efficient adaptation layer that calibrates neural link prediction scores for complex query answering will enable accurate, interpretable, and data-efficient reasoning over a broad class of logical queries, including those with atomic negations, without the need for retraining or fine-tuning the underlying link predictor.
d3aa244f42c598d58d055c177b2ca1fdc1a172ad.proposed_method: A lightweight adaptation model, termed CQDA, will be developed to calibrate the scores produced by a frozen neural link predictor for the task of complex query answering. The adaptation function will be implemented as an affine transformation with a small number of learnable parameters, optionally conditioned on the representations of predicates and entities involved in each atomic query. This adaptation layer will be trained end-to-end on the downstream complex query answering task using a cross-entropy loss over query-answer pairs, while the underlying link predictor remains fixed. The method will extend the compositional query decomposition framework by enabling reasoning over queries with conjunctions, disjunctions, and atomic negations, using fuzzy logic t-norms and t-conorms for score aggregation. The approach will ensure monotonicity and interpretability of intermediate scores, and will support efficient combinatorial optimization for variable assignment during query answering.
d3aa244f42c598d58d055c177b2ca1fdc1a172ad.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three benchmark knowledge graph datasets: FB15K, FB15K-237, and NELL995. The evaluation will use a suite of first-order logic queries with various structures, including queries with conjunction, disjunction, and atomic negation, as defined in prior work. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as GQE, Query2Box, BetaE, ConE, GNN-QE, and previous CQD variants. Evaluation metrics will include Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) on hard queries, which require non-trivial reasoning. The adaptation layer will be trained using only a subset (≤30%) of available complex query types, and additional experiments will assess data efficiency by training with as little as 1% of complex queries. Hyperparameters will be selected based on validation MRR, and ablation studies will analyze the impact of adaptation layer design and parameterization.
d3aa244f42c598d58d055c177b2ca1fdc1a172ad.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a parameter-efficient adaptation layer that calibrates neural link prediction scores for complex query answering, enabling support for queries with atomic negations, which was previously not possible with link predictors. The approach achieves competitive or superior predictive accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods while using significantly less training data and model parameters. The method preserves the interpretability and compositionality of intermediate reasoning steps, generalizes to unseen query types, and demonstrates robustness in out-of-distribution evaluations. This framework allows for efficient transfer of pre-trained neural link predictors to complex query answering tasks without the need for resource-intensive retraining.

d3b071c61992078d6cb77377621cf80f620136b4.title: BackdoorBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Backdoor Learning
d3b071c61992078d6cb77377621cf80f620136b4.research_question: How can a comprehensive, standardized, and extensible benchmark be established to enable thorough, reproducible, and fair evaluation of backdoor attacks and defenses in deep neural networks across diverse settings, models, and datasets?
d3b071c61992078d6cb77377621cf80f620136b4.hypothesis: A modular, extensible benchmarking framework that systematically implements and evaluates state-of-the-art backdoor attacks and defenses across multiple models, datasets, and poisoning ratios will provide more reliable, comparable, and insightful assessments of backdoor learning methods, revealing nuanced interactions and guiding future research.
d3b071c61992078d6cb77377621cf80f620136b4.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, BackdoorBench, will be developed with a modular codebase encompassing implementations of eight state-of-the-art backdoor attack algorithms and nine state-of-the-art defense algorithms. The framework will include distinct modules for data input, attack generation (covering both data poisoning and training controllable threat models), defense application (spanning pre-training, in-training, and post-training stages), and evaluation/analysis. Standardized protocols will be established to ensure fair and reproducible experimental procedures, covering all steps from data preprocessing, attack insertion, defense deployment, to result analysis. The evaluation module will provide multiple metrics, including clean accuracy, attack success rate, and robust accuracy, and will be augmented with advanced analysis tools such as t-SNE, Grad-CAM, Shapley value maps, frequency saliency maps, and neuron activation analysis to facilitate deeper understanding of backdoor behaviors.
d3b071c61992078d6cb77377621cf80f620136b4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by exhaustively evaluating every pair of eight attack methods and nine defense methods, across five poisoning ratios (0.1%, 0.5%, 1%, 5%, 10%), four widely used datasets (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, GTSRB, TinyImageNet), and five neural network architectures (PreAct-ResNet18, VGG-19, EfficientNet-B3, MobileNetV3-Large, DenseNet-161). Each attack-defense pair will be assessed using the standardized protocol, resulting in up to 8,000 evaluation pairs. Baseline comparisons will include classic and advanced attack/defense methods, and all models will be trained from scratch without additional training tricks to ensure fair comparisons. Evaluation metrics will include clean accuracy (C-Acc), attack success rate (ASR), and robust accuracy (R-Acc), with additional analyses performed using the provided visualization and interpretability tools.
d3b071c61992078d6cb77377621cf80f620136b4.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces the first extensible, modular, and standardized codebase for backdoor learning that covers a wide spectrum of threat models, attack/defense strategies, and evaluation metrics. It enables comprehensive, reproducible, and fair comparisons across 8,000 attack-defense pairs, providing unprecedented scale and depth of analysis. The benchmark offers new perspectives on the effects of poisoning ratio, model architecture, and dataset characteristics, and integrates advanced analysis tools for interpretability. This resource is expected to accelerate progress in backdoor learning research, facilitate the development of more robust methods, and inspire exploration of intrinsic properties of backdoor vulnerabilities.

d4032b47c1e5b9c51df5e3c4e33fea72761ff5da.title: EffiBench: Benchmarking the Efficiency of Automatically Generated Code
d4032b47c1e5b9c51df5e3c4e33fea72761ff5da.research_question: How can the efficiency of automatically generated code, in terms of execution time and memory usage, be systematically benchmarked and compared across a diverse set of code generation models?
d4032b47c1e5b9c51df5e3c4e33fea72761ff5da.hypothesis: Automatically generated code from large language models is generally less efficient than human-written canonical solutions, especially for efficiency-critical coding tasks.
d4032b47c1e5b9c51df5e3c4e33fea72761ff5da.proposed_method: A new benchmark, EFFIBENCH, will be constructed to evaluate the efficiency of code generated by large language models (LLMs). The benchmark will consist of 1,000 efficiency-critical coding problems sourced from LeetCode, each paired with an executable, human-written canonical solution that achieves state-of-the-art efficiency. A test case generator will be developed to produce extensive and diverse test cases for each problem, enabling comprehensive evaluation under various computational loads. The evaluation framework will include automated metrics for execution time, normalized execution time, maximum memory usage, normalized maximum memory usage, total memory usage, and normalized total memory usage. The benchmarking system will be implemented to execute and measure generated code in a controlled environment, with scripts and a public server provided for reproducible evaluation.
d4032b47c1e5b9c51df5e3c4e33fea72761ff5da.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by generating code for each EFFIBENCH problem using a wide range of LLMs, including both open-source and closed-source models (e.g., CodeLlama, StarCoder, GPT-4, Claude-3). Only code that passes all correctness test cases will be evaluated for efficiency. Each model's performance will be assessed using the provided test cases (100 per problem by default), and efficiency metrics will be computed relative to the canonical solutions. Baselines will include the human-written canonical solutions, and results will be compared across models using metrics such as normalized execution time and memory usage. Evaluations will be run on a standardized hardware environment (e.g., Intel Xeon Platinum CPU, NVIDIA A100 GPUs, 2.0 TiB RAM) to ensure comparability.
d4032b47c1e5b9c51df5e3c4e33fea72761ff5da.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark is the first to systematically evaluate the efficiency (not just correctness) of LLM-generated code across a large and diverse set of efficiency-critical problems. EFFIBENCH provides canonical solutions optimized for efficiency, a scalable test case generator, and a comprehensive set of efficiency metrics. The framework enables fair and reproducible comparison of code efficiency across models and tasks, and includes a public server for community use. This approach addresses a significant gap in current code generation evaluation, emphasizing the importance of green computing and sustainable software development.

d4177489596748e43aa571f59556097f2cc4c8be.title: GPTFUZZER: Red Teaming Large Language Models with Auto-Generated Jailbreak Prompts
d4177489596748e43aa571f59556097f2cc4c8be.research_question: How can the process of red-teaming large language models (LLMs) be automated to efficiently and comprehensively generate jailbreak prompts that test and expose vulnerabilities in LLM safety mechanisms across a variety of models and harmful queries?
d4177489596748e43aa571f59556097f2cc4c8be.hypothesis: Automating the generation of jailbreak prompts using a black-box fuzzing framework, which leverages human-written seeds, LLM-driven mutation operators, and an automated judgment model, will produce more effective and diverse jailbreak prompts than manual approaches, resulting in higher attack success rates across both commercial and open-source LLMs.
d4177489596748e43aa571f59556097f2cc4c8be.proposed_method: A black-box fuzzing framework, inspired by AFL, will be developed to automate the generation of jailbreak prompts for LLMs. The process begins with the collection of human-written jailbreak templates, which serve as initial seeds. In each iteration, a seed selection strategy—balancing efficiency and diversity, such as a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-based approach—selects a template from the pool. Specialized mutation operators, implemented via LLMs, generate new templates through operations such as generate, crossover, expand, shorten, and rephrase, ensuring syntactic and semantic validity. The mutated template is combined with a harmful question and submitted to the target LLM. An automated judgment model, based on a fine-tuned RoBERTa classifier, evaluates the LLM's response to determine if the attack was successful. Successful jailbreak templates are retained and added to the seed pool, while unsuccessful ones are discarded, and the process iterates until a stopping criterion is met.
d4177489596748e43aa571f59556097f2cc4c8be.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of commercial and open-source LLMs, including ChatGPT, Llama-2, and Vicuna, using a dataset of 100 harmful questions sourced from open datasets. The initial seed set will consist of 77 human-written jailbreak templates, filtered for generalizability and single-turn applicability. Attack Success Rate (ASR) will serve as the primary evaluation metric, with both top-1 and top-5 ASR variants calculated. Baselines for comparison will include manual prompt engineering, random and round-robin seed selection, and alternative judgment models such as rule-based methods, moderation APIs, and LLM-based labeling. The experiments will also assess the transferability of generated jailbreaks to unseen models (e.g., Bard, Claude-2, PaLM2) and the impact of different seed selection and mutation strategies. All experiments will be run on a high-performance server with multiple GPUs, and the entire codebase will be made publicly available for reproducibility.
d4177489596748e43aa571f59556097f2cc4c8be.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first automated, black-box fuzzing system for generating jailbreak prompts targeting LLMs, eliminating the scalability and coverage limitations of manual prompt engineering. Key innovations include the integration of LLM-driven mutation operators for natural language prompt generation, a novel MCTS-based seed selection strategy to balance exploration and exploitation, and an efficient, fine-tuned RoBERTa judgment model for automated attack success evaluation. The framework demonstrates the ability to consistently outperform human-crafted templates, achieving high attack success rates even on well-aligned models, and exhibits strong transferability to unseen LLMs. This approach provides a scalable, adaptable, and comprehensive tool for red-teaming LLMs and advancing research in LLM safety.

d47170ed5ddaa2edf16e3b58a214e1c196b37d4d.title: SPD: Sync-Point Drop for efficient tensor parallelism of Large Language Models
d47170ed5ddaa2edf16e3b58a214e1c196b37d4d.research_question: How can communication overheads in distributed inference of large language models be reduced to improve scalability and latency, while minimizing loss in model accuracy?
d47170ed5ddaa2edf16e3b58a214e1c196b37d4d.hypothesis: Selective removal of synchronization points in tensor parallelism, combined with block-wise sensitivity analysis and tailored optimization strategies, can significantly reduce communication overhead and inference latency with minimal accuracy degradation in large language models.
d47170ed5ddaa2edf16e3b58a214e1c196b37d4d.proposed_method: A novel optimization technique, Sync-Point Drop (SPD), is introduced to selectively eliminate synchronization (sync) points in the self-attention outputs of transformer blocks during tensor parallel inference. The method begins by designing specialized transformer block architectures that minimize information loss when sync-points are dropped, with separate designs for blocks with and without bias in linear layers. SPD is applied in a block-wise manner, guided by a sensitivity analysis that measures the impact of sync-point removal on model performance (using perplexity as a metric). Blocks are classified into in-sensitive, sensitive, and extremely sensitive categories. For in-sensitive blocks, sync-points are dropped directly (zero-shot). Sensitive blocks undergo block-to-block distillation to recover accuracy, while extremely sensitive blocks receive additional SPD-aware attention head grouping and matching to ensure functional diversity and minimize information loss. The approach includes reordering of attention heads and MLP partitions to maintain architectural integrity after sync-point removal.
d47170ed5ddaa2edf16e3b58a214e1c196b37d4d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on multiple large language models, including LLaMA2 (7B, 13B, 70B) and OPT (6.7B, 13B, 30B, 66B), using distributed inference across 4 or 8 Nvidia A100-80G GPUs under both high (300GB/s) and low (10GB/s) bandwidth interconnect settings. Calibration data is sampled from WikiText2 for sensitivity measurement and distillation, and evaluation is performed on a suite of zero-shot tasks (ARC, HellaSwag, LAMBADA, PIQA, SciQ, WinoGrande) and MMLU, with results averaged across tasks. Baselines include standard tensor parallelism (TP) with all sync-points, and SPD is compared at various levels of block coverage. Evaluation metrics include inference latency (time to first token), accuracy on zero-shot tasks, and perplexity for sensitivity analysis. Hyperparameters for distillation and sensitivity thresholds are tuned for each model size, and both single-node and multi-node distributed setups are tested.
d47170ed5ddaa2edf16e3b58a214e1c196b37d4d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first block-wise sensitivity-driven approach for selectively dropping synchronization points in tensor parallelism, with novel block designs that minimize information loss. The multi-tiered strategy—combining zero-shot dropping, block-to-block distillation, and SPD-aware attention head grouping—enables significant reductions in inference latency (up to 20%) with less than 1% accuracy regression on large models such as LLaMA2-70B. The approach provides a scalable and generalizable solution for distributed inference in large language models, outperforming prior work that only optimizes communication operations without addressing the underlying model architecture.

d476d3bfdc014b02561c08f49aa7d37adcbac154.title: EffoVPR: Effective Foundation Model Utilization for Visual Place Recognition
d476d3bfdc014b02561c08f49aa7d37adcbac154.research_question: How can foundation models be effectively leveraged for visual place recognition (VPR) to achieve robust, generalizable, and memory-efficient performance across diverse and challenging real-world scenarios, without relying on complex external pooling mechanisms or extensive fine-tuning?
d476d3bfdc014b02561c08f49aa7d37adcbac154.hypothesis: Utilizing internal self-attention features of a foundation model, specifically Vision Transformers (ViT) pre-trained with DINOv2, enables the extraction of both global and local descriptors that, when combined with a novel re-ranking strategy, can achieve state-of-the-art VPR performance with highly compact feature representations, even in zero-shot settings.
d476d3bfdc014b02561c08f49aa7d37adcbac154.proposed_method: The proposed approach employs a ViT backbone initialized with DINOv2 pre-trained weights, fine-tuned for VPR using a classification loss on the [CLS] token, with classes defined by spatial cells to promote viewpoint invariance. Global image descriptors are obtained directly from the [CLS] token of the penultimate transformer layer, enabling efficient retrieval with reduced feature dimensionality via a linear projection. For re-ranking, local features are extracted from intermediate self-attention layers: keypoints are selected based on attention scores between patch tokens and the [CLS] token, and descriptors are derived from the Value facet of the self-attention matrix. Candidate matches are scored using mutual nearest neighbor (MNN) matching of these local descriptors, filtered by fixed similarity thresholds, to robustly re-rank top-K global retrievals. The method is designed to be effective both in zero-shot (no fine-tuning) and fine-tuned scenarios, and does not require additional pooling layers, adapters, or spatial verification.
d476d3bfdc014b02561c08f49aa7d37adcbac154.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 20 diverse VPR benchmarks, including Pitts30k, Tokyo24/7, MSLS-val/challenge, Nordland, AmsterTime, SF-XL, SF-Occlusion, SF-Night, and SVOX (Night/Rain), covering urban, seasonal, day/night, and occlusion challenges. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art single- and two-stage VPR methods, including those using external pooling (NetVLAD, GeM, VLAD, SALAD, BoQ) and recent DINOv2-based approaches (AnyLoc, SelaVPR, CricaVPR). Evaluation will use Recall@K (K=1,5,10) with a 25-meter localization threshold (or ±10 frames for Nordland), and feature compactness (dimensionality) will be systematically varied (e.g., 128D, 256D, 1024D). Both zero-shot and fine-tuned variants will be assessed, and ablation studies will analyze the impact of self-attention layer selection, thresholding, and number of re-ranked candidates.
d476d3bfdc014b02561c08f49aa7d37adcbac154.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel use of internal self-attention features from a foundation model for both global pooling and local descriptor extraction, eliminating the need for external pooling layers or adapters. A new re-ranking strategy based on mutual nearest neighbor matching of attention-based local descriptors is developed, effective even in zero-shot settings. The approach achieves state-of-the-art performance with highly compact global features (as low as 128D), demonstrating superior robustness to occlusion, illumination, and seasonal changes, and strong generalization across diverse datasets. The method also offers significant memory and computational efficiency, making it suitable for large-scale, real-time VPR applications.

d479efb49f3aae2ab1b3a0b89755a5a7af40fdf2.title: Sharper Convergence Guarantees for Asynchronous SGD for Distributed and Federated Learning
d479efb49f3aae2ab1b3a0b89755a5a7af40fdf2.research_question: How can the convergence rates of asynchronous stochastic gradient descent (SGD) be improved for distributed and federated learning settings, particularly under heterogeneous data and varying computation/communication delays among workers?
d479efb49f3aae2ab1b3a0b89755a5a7af40fdf2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging average delay and concurrency, rather than maximum delay, and by introducing a delay-adaptive learning rate scheme, asynchronous SGD can achieve faster and more robust convergence rates in both homogeneous and heterogeneous distributed learning environments.
d479efb49f3aae2ab1b3a0b89755a5a7af40fdf2.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves a detailed theoretical and algorithmic study of asynchronous SGD in distributed and federated learning scenarios. First, a refined convergence analysis will be conducted, focusing on the impact of average delay and concurrency (number of parallel workers) rather than the traditionally used maximum delay. A standard asynchronous SGD algorithm will be used, where workers compute stochastic gradients in parallel at their own pace and send updates to a central server without synchronization. The method will introduce a simple delay-adaptive learning rate schedule, where the step size for each update is adjusted based on the observed delay, eliminating the need for extra hyperparameter tuning or additional communication. The analysis will be extended to both homogeneous (i.i.d. data) and heterogeneous (non-i.i.d. data) settings, with theoretical guarantees provided for each case.
d479efb49f3aae2ab1b3a0b89755a5a7af40fdf2.experiment_details: Experiments will be designed to evaluate the convergence rates of the proposed asynchronous SGD algorithms under various delay patterns and data heterogeneity scenarios. Synthetic and real-world distributed/federated learning datasets will be used, simulating different worker speeds and communication delays. Baseline methods will include standard asynchronous SGD with constant step sizes, synchronous mini-batch SGD, and recent delay-adaptive algorithms. Evaluation metrics will focus on the number of iterations and wall-clock time required to reach an 5-stationary point, as well as robustness to straggler nodes. Key experimental setups will include varying the number of workers, the distribution of delays, and the degree of data heterogeneity across clients.
d479efb49f3aae2ab1b3a0b89755a5a7af40fdf2.novelty_claims: The proposal claims several innovations: (1) a tighter convergence rate for asynchronous SGD that depends on the average delay and concurrency, rather than the maximum delay, which is more reflective of practical distributed systems; (2) a simple delay-adaptive step size scheme that achieves convergence rates depending only on the average delay, without requiring additional hyperparameter tuning or communication; (3) theoretical results showing that asynchronous SGD can always outperform mini-batch SGD regardless of delay patterns; and (4) improved convergence guarantees for heterogeneous objectives, with weaker dependence on maximum delay and explicit characterization of the effect of client-specific average delays.

d47b83c622e9e6c00329775ea46f6d90e294e4c3.title: Efficient mapping of phase diagrams with conditional Boltzmann Generators
d47b83c622e9e6c00329775ea46f6d90e294e4c3.research_question: How can phase diagrams of materials be efficiently and accurately mapped across a wide range of thermodynamic states, such as temperature and pressure, using machine learning approaches to overcome the computational challenges of traditional free energy estimation methods?
d47b83c622e9e6c00329775ea46f6d90e294e4c3.hypothesis: A single deep generative model, specifically a conditional Boltzmann Generator based on normalizing flows conditioned on thermodynamic variables, can be trained using samples from one reference state to generate equilibrium samples across the entire phase diagram, enabling accurate and efficient computation of free energy differences and phase boundaries while significantly reducing the number of required simulations.
d47b83c622e9e6c00329775ea46f6d90e294e4c3.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a conditional Boltzmann Generator (BG) framework utilizing normalizing flows conditioned on temperature and pressure to map equilibrium distributions from a single reference thermodynamic state to a continuum of target states. The approach involves sampling atomic configurations and volumes at a reference state using molecular dynamics (MD) in the NPT ensemble, then training a conditional normalizing flow to transform these samples to approximate equilibrium distributions at arbitrary target (T, P) values. The flow architecture includes a permutation-equivariant transformer-based coupling layer to handle both solid and liquid phases, and an affine transformation for isotropic box scaling. Training is performed by minimizing a conditional Kullback-Leibler divergence loss, using energy-based objectives and importance weighting to ensure accurate reweighting of generated samples for free energy estimation.
d47b83c622e9e6c00329775ea46f6d90e294e4c3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a Lennard-Jones system consisting of 180 particles, with the goal of predicting the solid-liquid coexistence line across a range of temperatures and pressures. The method will be benchmarked against state-of-the-art free energy estimation techniques such as MBAR and traditional targeted free energy perturbation (TFEP), using reference systems like the Einstein crystal for solids and the Uhlenbeck-Ford model for liquids. Evaluation metrics will include the accuracy of predicted coexistence lines, the number of energy evaluations required, and the effective sample size (ESS) of generated samples. The experimental setup will involve training the conditional BG on MD samples from a single reference state and assessing its performance in generating equilibrium samples and computing free energy differences at multiple target states.
d47b83c622e9e6c00329775ea46f6d90e294e4c3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a single conditional Boltzmann Generator capable of mapping equilibrium distributions across the entire phase diagram from only one reference state, eliminating the need for multiple simulations at each thermodynamic point. The method leverages a permutation-equivariant, transformer-based normalizing flow architecture conditioned on temperature and pressure, enabling unified treatment of both solid and liquid phases. This framework allows for efficient, continuous conditioning over thermodynamic variables and significantly reduces computational cost compared to traditional free energy methods, while achieving high accuracy in phase boundary prediction.

d494727306a375e524c4c4c8cc1a2dc1845cc4b7.title: Towards Vision-Language Mechanistic Interpretability: A Causal Tracing Tool for BLIP
d494727306a375e524c4c4c8cc1a2dc1845cc4b7.research_question: How can mechanistic interpretability techniques, particularly causal mediation analysis, be adapted and applied to vision-language models to understand the neural mechanisms underlying image-conditioned text generation tasks such as visual question answering?
d494727306a375e524c4c4c8cc1a2dc1845cc4b7.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that adapting causal tracing methods to vision-language models will enable the identification of specific neural mechanisms responsible for image-conditioned text generation, and that certain layers or components within the model will exhibit higher causal relevance for task performance.
d494727306a375e524c4c4c8cc1a2dc1845cc4b7.proposed_method: A causal tracing framework will be developed for vision-language models, specifically targeting the BLIP architecture. The method involves corrupting image embeddings by injecting Gaussian noise into all image patch embeddings before they are fed into the question encoder. Three types of model runs will be conducted: a clean run (with uncorrupted embeddings), a corrupted run (with noisy embeddings), and an intervention run where individual intermediate states (layer outputs for specific tokens) from the clean run are patched into the corrupted run. The causal relevance of each state is quantified by measuring the improvement in the probability of the correct answer after patching, normalized by the difference between clean and corrupted runs. This process is repeated for all layers and tokens in both the question encoder and answer decoder to generate a comprehensive causal relevance map.
d494727306a375e524c4c4c8cc1a2dc1845cc4b7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the COCO-QA dataset, which contains over 123,000 images and associated visual question answering pairs, focusing on one-word answers in categories such as color identification, location identification, and object counting. The model's zero-shot performance will be evaluated on each category, with a particular emphasis on the color identification subset due to its higher baseline accuracy. Baselines include clean and corrupted runs without intervention. Evaluation metrics will include the probability difference of the correct answer before and after intervention (Γ), visualized as heatmaps across model layers and tokens. The effect of varying the noise factor (ν) in the image embedding corruption process will also be systematically analyzed to determine its impact on causal relevance and model restoration.
d494727306a375e524c4c4c8cc1a2dc1845cc4b7.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first causal tracing tool specifically adapted for vision-language models, enabling mechanistic interpretability in multimodal settings. The approach extends causal mediation analysis beyond unimodal language models and provides a systematic method to localize task-relevant computations within the BLIP architecture. The open-source release of the tool and planned visualizer will facilitate further research in vision-language mechanistic interpretability.

d4af12327385260116dfd68ed1ec6d0602d26d1f.title: Improving CLIP Training with Language Rewrites
d4af12327385260116dfd68ed1ec6d0602d26d1f.research_question: How can the training of contrastive language-image pre-training (CLIP) models be improved by incorporating augmentation strategies for language inputs, and what impact does this have on the transferability and robustness of learned visual representations across diverse datasets and tasks?
d4af12327385260116dfd68ed1ec6d0602d26d1f.hypothesis: Introducing diverse, semantically consistent language augmentations during CLIP training will improve the transfer performance and generalization of vision-language models without incurring additional computational or memory overhead during training.
d4af12327385260116dfd68ed1ec6d0602d26d1f.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed that augments the text side of image-text pairs used in CLIP training by generating multiple diverse rewrites of each caption. These rewrites will be produced using large language models (LLMs) with in-context learning (ICL), specifically leveraging open-source models such as LLaMA. Meta input-output pairs for rewriting will be constructed using a combination of chatbot outputs (e.g., ChatGPT, Bard), human annotators, and multi-caption datasets like MS-COCO. For each image-text pair, four distinct rewrites will be generated, each reflecting different sentence structures and vocabularies while preserving core semantics. During CLIP training, the text input for each image will be randomly sampled from the set of original and rewritten captions, thus introducing text augmentation in parallel with standard image augmentations. An extension of the method will also be explored, where each image is paired with all its augmented captions in a multi-positive contrastive loss.
d4af12327385260116dfd68ed1ec6d0602d26d1f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale image-text datasets including CC3M, CC12M, RedCaps, and LAION-400M, covering a range of data sizes and distributions. Models will be trained using various Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures (e.g., ViT-B/16, ViT-B/32, ViT-L/16) with consistent batch sizes and optimizer settings as in standard CLIP training. Evaluation will include zero-shot, few-shot, and linear probing classification on ImageNet and 15 common downstream datasets such as Food101, SUN397, and FGVCAircraft. Baselines will include vanilla CLIP, SLIP, and other text augmentation strategies like EDA and back translation. Performance will be measured using top-1 accuracy for zero-shot and few-shot settings, and linear probe accuracy, with ablation studies on augmentation sources, number of augmentations, and backbone architectures.
d4af12327385260116dfd68ed1ec6d0602d26d1f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically introduce diverse, sentence-level language augmentations into CLIP training using LLM-based rewrites, bridging the augmentation asymmetry between image and text modalities. Unlike prior text augmentation methods that operate at the word level or use back translation, this method leverages the generative capabilities of LLMs to produce richer and more varied text inputs. The framework is scalable, incurs no additional training overhead, and is compatible with existing CLIP-based methods. Experimental results demonstrate substantial improvements in transfer performance across datasets and tasks, and the method generalizes to other vision-language frameworks and scales with dataset and model size.

d4c60620570801a231a7756f931dda1740288fb9.title: Looped Transformers as Programmable Computers
d4c60620570801a231a7756f931dda1740288fb9.research_question: Can transformer networks, when configured with specific weights and placed in a loop, be programmed to emulate general-purpose computation and execute complex algorithmic tasks using a fixed, shallow architecture?
d4c60620570801a231a7756f931dda1740288fb9.hypothesis: Transformer architectures, when looped and programmed via their input sequences, can emulate the functionality of a universal computer, including iterative algorithms, with a constant number of layers regardless of program length.
d4c60620570801a231a7756f931dda1740288fb9.proposed_method: A framework will be developed in which transformer networks are programmed by hardcoding their weights and running them in a loop, allowing the output to be fed back as input for iterative computation. The input sequence will be structured to act as a punchcard, containing both instructions (commands) and memory slots for data, as well as a scratchpad for intermediate results. Specialized transformer blocks will be constructed to emulate basic computing operations, such as reading/writing memory, non-linear function application, program counters, and conditional branching. These blocks will be assembled to implement a flexible single-instruction set computer (FLEQ), capable of executing programs written in a generalized SUBLEQ-like instruction set, where each instruction can perform a range of operations (e.g., matrix multiplication, non-linear functions) and control flow. The architecture will utilize positional encodings for pointers and counters, and will leverage the attention mechanism to perform data movement and function application within a bounded number of layers.
d4c60620570801a231a7756f931dda1740288fb9.experiment_details: Experiments will involve constructing explicit looped transformer models with up to 13 layers and varying numbers of attention heads, each hardcoded to emulate specific algorithmic tasks. The framework will be evaluated by programming the transformer to execute a variety of functions at inference time, including a basic calculator, a linear algebra library (matrix transpose, multiplication, inversion, power iteration), and an in-context learning algorithm implementing backpropagation for neural networks. The input sequence will encode both the program and the data, and the transformer’s ability to correctly execute these tasks will be assessed. Evaluation will focus on correctness of computation, generality of the approach (ability to implement arbitrary iterative algorithms), and the minimal network size required for each task. No external datasets are specified, as the focus is on algorithmic emulation rather than data-driven learning.
d4c60620570801a231a7756f931dda1740288fb9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach demonstrates that shallow, looped transformer networks can emulate general-purpose computation, including iterative and non-linear algorithms, with a constant number of layers independent of program length. The method enables the execution of arbitrary programs by encoding instructions and memory in the input sequence, leveraging the attention mechanism for flexible data movement and function application. This framework expands the known computational capabilities of transformers, showing that even small models can act as universal computers when appropriately programmed, and provides explicit constructions and minimal network sizes for a range of algorithmic tasks.

d4d224d10b64a1cbb6c11986a4c44e052cf7d64f.title: Score Regularized Policy Optimization through Diffusion Behavior
d4d224d10b64a1cbb6c11986a4c44e052cf7d64f.research_question: Can the generative capabilities of diffusion models be fully leveraged for behavior regularization in offline reinforcement learning, while eliminating the computational inefficiencies associated with iterative diffusion sampling during both training and evaluation?
d4d224d10b64a1cbb6c11986a4c44e052cf7d64f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a deterministic inference policy can be extracted by directly regularizing the policy gradient with the score function of a pretrained diffusion behavior model, thereby achieving efficient and effective behavior regularization without requiring diffusion sampling.
d4d224d10b64a1cbb6c11986a4c44e052cf7d64f.proposed_method: A novel offline reinforcement learning algorithm, Score Regularized Policy Optimization (SRPO), is proposed. The approach begins by pretraining a conditional diffusion model to represent the behavior policy and estimate its score function. Implicit Q-learning is employed to train the critic network independently. Policy extraction is performed by regularizing the policy gradient using the score function estimated by the pretrained diffusion model, rather than relying on sample-based KL divergence estimation. The method introduces an ensemble of score approximations at different diffusion times to exploit the generative capacity of the diffusion model, and incorporates a baseline subtraction technique to reduce gradient estimation variance. The surrogate objective integrates these components, enabling efficient optimization of a deterministic policy that remains close to the behavior distribution.
d4d224d10b64a1cbb6c11986a4c44e052cf7d64f.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the D4RL benchmark suite, including locomotion (HalfCheetah, Hopper, Walker2d) and AntMaze tasks, with datasets such as medium, medium-expert, and medium-replay. The proposed method is compared against a range of baselines, including BEAR, TD3+BC, IQL, SfBC, Diffuser, Diffusion-QL, QGPO, and IDQL. Evaluation metrics include normalized return as suggested by D4RL, as well as computational efficiency metrics such as action sampling speed and FLOPS. All experiments are run under consistent hardware and software environments, and results are averaged across multiple random seeds. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of surrogate objective weighting, baseline subtraction, and temperature coefficient settings.
d4d224d10b64a1cbb6c11986a4c44e052cf7d64f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new policy optimization framework that regularizes policy gradients using the score function of a pretrained diffusion model, eliminating the need for computationally expensive diffusion sampling during both training and evaluation. The method leverages ensembling across diffusion times and baseline subtraction to enhance training stability and performance. This results in a significant boost in computational efficiency—action sampling is over 25 times faster than existing diffusion-based methods—while maintaining or surpassing state-of-the-art performance on standard offline RL benchmarks. The approach is particularly well-suited for computationally sensitive domains such as robotics.

d4f53b1c3f232f9a7828dd1ddad4d2dad123936f.title: Score identity Distillation: Exponentially Fast Distillation of Pretrained Diffusion Models for One-Step Generation
d4f53b1c3f232f9a7828dd1ddad4d2dad123936f.research_question: How can the generative capabilities of pretrained diffusion models be distilled into a single-step generator without access to real data, while maintaining or surpassing the generation quality of the original multi-step diffusion models?
d4f53b1c3f232f9a7828dd1ddad4d2dad123936f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging score-related identities and a model-based score-matching loss, it is possible to distill the knowledge of a pretrained diffusion model into a single-step generator that achieves generation quality comparable to or better than the original teacher model, without requiring real data or iterative reverse diffusion.
d4f53b1c3f232f9a7828dd1ddad4d2dad123936f.proposed_method: The proposed method, Score identity Distillation (SiD), introduces a data-free distillation framework that reformulates the forward diffusion process as a semi-implicit distribution. Three key score-related identities are derived and fused to construct a novel loss mechanism based on model-based score-matching (a variant of Fisher divergence). This loss aligns the scores of the diffused generator distribution and the pretrained teacher diffusion model at various noise levels, using only the generator's own synthesized images. The approach employs alternating optimization: a generator network is trained to minimize the score-matching loss, while a score network is updated to estimate the score of the generator distribution. Monte Carlo estimation and neural network approximations are used to handle intractable expectations, and the loss is weighted and scheduled according to the noise level. The method eliminates the need for real data or reverse diffusion-based sampling during distillation, enabling rapid, single-step generation.
d4f53b1c3f232f9a7828dd1ddad4d2dad123936f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four benchmark datasets: CIFAR-10 (32x32, both conditional and unconditional), ImageNet 64x64, FFHQ 64x64, and AFHQ-v2 64x64. The VP-EDM checkpoints will serve as the teacher diffusion models. The proposed SiD generator will be compared against a wide range of baselines, including multi-step diffusion models, GANs, and state-of-the-art distillation methods (both data-free and data-dependent). Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), and, for ImageNet, Precision and Recall. The setup will use a consistent number of generated samples (e.g., 50k) for FID calculation, and experiments will track FID reduction as a function of the number of synthesized images processed during distillation. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of key parameters such as the loss weighting coefficient (alpha) and batch size.
d4f53b1c3f232f9a7828dd1ddad4d2dad123936f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to achieve data-free, single-step distillation of pretrained diffusion models that matches or surpasses the teacher model's generation quality. The method introduces a novel loss mechanism based on three fused score identities and model-based score-matching, enabling efficient and effective distillation without access to real data or iterative reverse diffusion. The approach demonstrates exponentially fast reduction in FID during distillation and sets new benchmarks for efficiency and effectiveness in diffusion model distillation. Unlike prior methods, SiD does not require auxiliary losses, access to training data, or GAN-based components, and is applicable to a wide range of pretrained diffusion models.

d51cbf9c5c9e6f8bdac93d5dca38f61e2ad33f35.title: Tighter Information-Theoretic Generalization Bounds from Supersamples
d51cbf9c5c9e6f8bdac93d5dca38f61e2ad33f35.research_question: How can information-theoretic generalization bounds for learning algorithms be made tighter and more practical to compute in the supersample (conditional mutual information) setting, and how do these new bounds compare to existing approaches in terms of tracking generalization behavior for modern machine learning models?
d51cbf9c5c9e6f8bdac93d5dca38f61e2ad33f35.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by projecting loss pairs to lower-dimensional statistics (such as loss differences) and correlating them with Rademacher sequences, new information-theoretic generalization bounds can be derived that are both tighter and easier to measure than existing bounds in the supersample setting.
d51cbf9c5c9e6f8bdac93d5dca38f61e2ad33f35.proposed_method: The proposed methodology develops several novel information-theoretic generalization bounds within the supersample (conditional mutual information) framework. The approach begins by replacing the traditional loss pair with the loss difference, leading to new disintegrated conditional mutual information (CMI) and unconditional mutual information (MI) bounds. These bounds are further refined using communication-theoretic perspectives, interpreting the MI term as the achievable rate over a memoryless channel. To address both standard and weighted generalization errors, the method introduces bounds based on correlating losses with Rademacher sequences and their shifted variants, enabling the derivation of square-root and fast-rate bounds. Additional bounds are constructed using variance and sharpness-based arguments, as well as a novel Wasserstein distance-based bound. All bounds are formulated to be easy to measure, often involving only one-dimensional random variables, and are applicable to both bounded and unbounded loss functions.
d51cbf9c5c9e6f8bdac93d5dca38f61e2ad33f35.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real datasets. For synthetic data, Gaussian datasets will be generated for binary and multi-class classification tasks, with both separable (interpolating) and non-separable settings. Linear classifiers and neural networks (e.g., 4-layer CNNs and fine-tuned ResNet-50) will be trained on datasets such as MNIST and CIFAR10. Empirical risk minimization (ERM) and stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) will be used as learning algorithms. The proposed bounds will be compared against established baselines, including the binary KL bound and previous CMI/e-CMI/f-CMI bounds. Evaluation metrics will include the empirical generalization error and the tightness of each bound, with results averaged over multiple runs to ensure statistical significance. Additional comparisons will be made between variance-based, sharpness-based, and Wasserstein-based bounds.
d51cbf9c5c9e6f8bdac93d5dca38f61e2ad33f35.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces several innovations: (1) new disintegrated CMI and unconditional MI bounds based on loss differences, which are provably tighter and easier to measure than previous bounds in the supersample setting; (2) a communication-theoretic interpretation that connects generalization error to channel capacity in the interpolating regime; (3) the use of Rademacher correlation to derive both square-root and fast-rate bounds, including variance and sharpness-based extensions; (4) a novel Wasserstein distance-based generalization bound; and (5) comprehensive empirical validation demonstrating that these new bounds more closely track the generalization dynamics of both linear and deep models, outperforming the tightest existing information-theoretic bounds, especially in regimes with small or zero training error.

d53662e70b0aa4bee963751a41985b550ec96fbd.title: Causal Structure Discovery between Clusters of Nodes Induced by Latent Factors
d53662e70b0aa4bee963751a41985b550ec96fbd.research_question: How can the causal structure among clusters of observed variables, which are influenced by latent factors, be accurately discovered in the presence of latent confounders and under realistic structural assumptions?
d53662e70b0aa4bee963751a41985b550ec96fbd.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under a set of structural and faithfulness assumptions, a constraint-based algorithm leveraging algebraic constraints in the covariance matrix (such as tetrad constraints) can consistently and efficiently recover both the clustering of observed variables and the causal structure among latent and observed nodes, even when latent variables are not exogenous.
d53662e70b0aa4bee963751a41985b550ec96fbd.proposed_method: A novel three-stage constraint-based algorithm is proposed for causal structure discovery in latent factor causal models (LFCMs). In the first stage, clusters of observed variables sharing the same latent parent are identified by testing for vanishing tetrads (2x2 subdeterminants of the covariance matrix) and constructing a graph where edges indicate indistinguishable tetrad structure, followed by clique extraction to form clusters. The second stage merges clusters as needed by further vanishing tetrad tests to ensure all nodes with the same latent parent are grouped together, preserving an ordering among clusters. In the third stage, the algorithm learns the directed acyclic graph (DAG) structure over both latent and observed nodes by testing conditional independence (via partial correlations) between observed nodes and latent variables, using the previously identified clustering and ordering. Multiple hypothesis testing procedures, such as Sidak or max-T adjustments, are employed to control false discovery rates in the presence of multiple simultaneous tests. The method is designed to be consistent under genericity and faithfulness assumptions and is computationally efficient relative to existing causal discovery methods.
d53662e70b0aa4bee963751a41985b550ec96fbd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both synthetic and semi-synthetic settings. In the synthetic setting, random DAGs with latent and observed nodes are generated according to the LFCM assumptions, with parameters sampled to avoid trivial variance structures and ensure realistic difficulty. The algorithm's ability to recover the ground truth clustering and causal edges will be evaluated using metrics such as true positive and false positive rates for cluster assignments and edge recovery. Baselines will include existing methods such as FOFC and BPC, which also leverage covariance constraints but do not employ the proposed multiple hypothesis testing or relax the exogeneity assumption. In the semi-synthetic setting, real biological data (e.g., protein mass spectrometry data with known ground truth networks) will be modified to fit the LFCM assumptions, and the method's accuracy in recovering known clusters and edges will be assessed. Evaluation metrics will include clustering accuracy (e.g., pairwise precision/recall) and edge recovery accuracy, and experiments will be performed across a range of sample sizes and significance thresholds.
d53662e70b0aa4bee963751a41985b550ec96fbd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new class of latent factor causal models (LFCMs) that allow for non-exogenous latent variables and enforce a bipartite structure with unique cluster and triple-child assumptions, motivated by biological systems such as gene regulatory networks. The algorithm is the first to provide a consistent, constraint-based method for recovering both clusters and the full causal structure over observed and latent nodes without requiring the measurement assumption or non-Gaussianity. The use of multiple hypothesis testing for tetrad constraints and the staged clustering and merging process are novel, enabling high accuracy in cluster and edge recovery even at low sample sizes. The method achieves superior performance compared to existing baselines and is computationally efficient, with polynomial complexity under reasonable assumptions.

d53fe76bd2795a19ddf52d012917782f6f6f2c1e.title: Griffin: Mixing Gated Linear Recurrences with Local Attention for Efficient Language Models
d53fe76bd2795a19ddf52d012917782f6f6f2c1e.research_question: Can a hybrid language model architecture that combines gated linear recurrences with local attention achieve efficient scaling, hardware efficiency, and competitive performance compared to Transformer-based models for long-context language modeling?
d53fe76bd2795a19ddf52d012917782f6f6f2c1e.hypothesis: A hybrid model that interleaves gated linear recurrent units with local attention blocks will match or exceed the performance and efficiency of state-of-the-art Transformer architectures, particularly in long-sequence modeling and inference throughput, while requiring fewer training tokens.
d53fe76bd2795a19ddf52d012917782f6f6f2c1e.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a novel Real-Gated Linear Recurrent Unit (RG-LRU) as the core of a new recurrent block, which is then integrated into two model families: Hawk (pure RNN) and Griffin (a hybrid combining recurrent blocks with local attention). The RG-LRU layer incorporates gating mechanisms inspired by LSTMs and GRUs, but uses a diagonal recurrent weight and element-wise operations for stability and efficiency. In the Griffin architecture, model layers alternate between RG-LRU-based recurrent blocks and local (sliding-window) attention blocks, leveraging the strengths of both recurrence (for long-range dependencies) and attention (for recent context). The model backbone consists of stacked residual blocks, each containing RMSNorm, a gated MLP block with GeLU activations, and a temporal-mixing block (either RG-LRU or local attention). Model parallelism and custom kernel implementations are employed to maximize hardware efficiency, particularly on TPU-v3.
d53fe76bd2795a19ddf52d012917782f6f6f2c1e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the MassiveText dataset, previously used for large-scale language model training, with model sizes ranging from 100M to 14B parameters. Training will use the AdamW optimizer and hyperparameters scaled according to Chinchilla scaling laws. Baselines will include a Multi-Query Attention (MQA) Transformer and external models such as Mamba and Llama-2. Evaluation will cover both held-out validation loss scaling and downstream tasks (MMLU, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, ARC-E, ARC-C) using character-normalized accuracy and absolute accuracy where appropriate. Inference speed will be assessed via latency and throughput metrics over varying sequence lengths and batch sizes. Additional experiments will probe long-context extrapolation and copying/retrieval capabilities, comparing performance on sequences longer than those seen during training.
d53fe76bd2795a19ddf52d012917782f6f6f2c1e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new gated linear recurrent unit (RG-LRU) that combines the stability and efficiency of linear recurrences with gating mechanisms for enhanced memory and expressivity. The Griffin architecture is a novel hybrid that mixes recurrent blocks with local attention, enabling efficient scaling to long sequences and high hardware throughput. The approach achieves competitive or superior performance to leading Transformer models with significantly fewer training tokens, and demonstrates improved inference efficiency and extrapolation to longer contexts.
