Custom sharding and kernel implementations further enable efficient distributed training and inference on modern accelerators.

d544dd9a6ba9ea5f2c1217bc554cf7fded732fbf.title: Anti-DreamBooth: Protecting users from personalized text-to-image synthesis
d544dd9a6ba9ea5f2c1217bc554cf7fded732fbf.research_question: How can individuals be proactively protected from the malicious use of personalized text-to-image synthesis models, such as DreamBooth, which can generate harmful or fake images of specific persons using only a few reference images?
d544dd9a6ba9ea5f2c1217bc554cf7fded732fbf.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that adding carefully crafted, imperceptible adversarial noise to users' images before publication can effectively disrupt the ability of personalized text-to-image synthesis models, such as DreamBooth, to generate high-quality or recognizable images of the target individual, even under varying attack conditions.
d544dd9a6ba9ea5f2c1217bc554cf7fded732fbf.proposed_method: A defense framework is proposed that injects subtle, adversarial perturbations into each user's image prior to public release, with the goal of disrupting the training and output quality of any personalized text-to-image generator (e.g., DreamBooth) that uses these images as reference. The method formulates the problem as a bi-level optimization, where the adversarial noise is optimized to maximize the reconstruction loss of a surrogate DreamBooth model, thereby degrading its ability to learn the target identity. Two main algorithms are developed: (1) Fully-trained Surrogate Model Guidance (FSMG), which uses a fixed surrogate DreamBooth model trained on a clean subset to guide the perturbation optimization via Projected Gradient Descent (PGD); and (2) Alternating Surrogate and Perturbation Learning (ASPL), which alternates between finetuning a surrogate model on clean data and optimizing perturbations on the current image set, better mimicking the attacker's training process. Both untargeted and targeted variants are considered, and ensemble approaches are explored for robustness against unknown model versions.
d544dd9a6ba9ea5f2c1217bc554cf7fded732fbf.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two large-scale facial datasets, CelebA-HQ and VGGFace2, each containing hundreds of identities with sufficient images per subject. For each identity, images are split into reference, protection, and extra clean sets. The defense methods are evaluated by training DreamBooth models on protected (perturbed) images and generating outputs using both seen and novel prompts. Evaluation metrics include Face Detection Failure Rate (FDFR), Identity Score Matching (ISM) using ArcFace embeddings, SER-FQA (face image quality), and BRISQUE (general image quality). Baselines include no defense, targeted and untargeted variants, and standard image preprocessing (e.g., Gaussian blur, JPEG compression). Additional experiments assess robustness to model, term, and prompt mismatches, as well as to alternative personalization methods (Textual Inversion, LoRA), and real-world black-box services.
d544dd9a6ba9ea5f2c1217bc554cf7fded732fbf.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to proactively defend against malicious personalized text-to-image synthesis, specifically targeting the DreamBooth finetuning process with adversarial image cloaking. Unlike prior work focused on GAN-based DeepFakes or artistic mimicry, this approach addresses the unique challenges of diffusion-based models and instance-level personalization. The method introduces new bi-level optimization algorithms (FSMG, ASPL) tailored to the diffusion and DreamBooth setting, demonstrates effectiveness across multiple datasets and adverse conditions (model/prompt mismatch, partial clean image leakage), and shows robustness against alternative personalization techniques and common image preprocessing. The defense is shown to significantly degrade the quality and identity preservation of generated images, providing a practical tool for user protection.

d55a2440b56181e2b04e274aa7a809f58c6b0c0c.title: Explaining Time Series Predictions with Dynamic Masks
d55a2440b56181e2b04e274aa7a809f58c6b0c0c.research_question: How can the predictions of machine learning models for multivariate time series data be explained in a way that accounts for temporal dependencies, parsimony, and legibility, and how can such explanations be quantitatively evaluated?
d55a2440b56181e2b04e274aa7a809f58c6b0c0c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a perturbation-based dynamic masking approach, which produces instance-wise importance scores for each feature at each time step and incorporates temporal context, parsimony, and legibility, will provide more accurate and interpretable explanations of time series model predictions compared to existing saliency methods.
d55a2440b56181e2b04e274aa7a809f58c6b0c0c.proposed_method: A novel perturbation-based framework, termed dynamic masks (Dynamask), is proposed to generate instance-wise feature importance scores for each time step in multivariate time series data. The method constructs a mask matrix of the same shape as the input, where each element represents the importance of a specific feature at a specific time. Perturbation operators are defined to dynamically alter input features based on their temporal neighbors, allowing the mask to capture temporal dependencies. The mask is optimized by minimizing a loss function that balances the fidelity of the perturbed prediction to the original model output, a parsimony regularization term that encourages sparsity and near-binary masks, and a temporal continuity term that discourages abrupt changes in saliency over time. Information-theoretic metrics, such as mask information and mask entropy, are introduced to quantitatively assess the sharpness and legibility of the resulting explanations.
d55a2440b56181e2b04e274aa7a809f58c6b0c0c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic experiments include white-box regression tasks with known salient features and hidden Markov model-based classification tasks with known state-dependent feature saliency, allowing for precise evaluation of feature importance identification. Real-world experiments will use the MIMIC-III clinical dataset to predict patient mortality with a recurrent neural network, where the quality of explanations is assessed by measuring the impact of perturbing salient features on model predictions. Baselines for comparison include Feature Occlusion, Feature Permutation, Integrated Gradients, Shapley Value Sampling, Augmented Feature Occlusion, FIT, RETAIN, DeepLIFT, LIME, and GradSHAP. Evaluation metrics include area under the precision and recall curves (AUP, AUR), mask information and entropy, cross-entropy shift, accuracy of perturbed predictions, AUROC, and AUPRC. Experimental setups are designed to test the method's ability to identify salient features, maintain parsimony, and provide legible explanations.
d55a2440b56181e2b04e274aa7a809f58c6b0c0c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first saliency method to rigorously address temporal context, parsimony, and legibility in multivariate time series explanations. It introduces dynamic perturbation operators that leverage temporal structure, a parsimony-driven regularization scheme for mask optimization, and information-theoretic metrics for explanation quality assessment. The method is model-agnostic, modular, and applicable as a plug-in to a wide range of machine learning models, offering improved identification of feature importance over time and enhanced transparency in domains such as medicine and finance.

d58c92fed5069840ab18fcac9f538358645d2260.title: Making Sense of Dependence: Efficient Black-box Explanations Using Dependence Measure
d58c92fed5069840ab18fcac9f538358645d2260.research_question: How can efficient and faithful black-box attribution methods be developed for explaining the predictions of complex machine learning models, including both image classification and object detection, while also enabling the assessment of interactions between input regions?
d58c92fed5069840ab18fcac9f538358645d2260.hypothesis: A black-box attribution method based on the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC) can provide efficient, faithful, and interpretable explanations for model predictions, and can be extended to assess not only the importance of individual input regions but also their pairwise interactions.
d58c92fed5069840ab18fcac9f538358645d2260.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a black-box attribution framework that leverages the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC), a dependence measure based on Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces (RKHS), to quantify the relationship between input image regions (patches) and model outputs. The method involves generating random binary masks to perturb input images, applying these masks to create perturbed samples, and measuring the dependence between each patch's perturbation and the model output using HSIC. An efficient estimator for HSIC is utilized, requiring only O(p^2) operations for p samples, and the process is vectorized for computational efficiency. Additionally, a novel kernel is introduced to enable an ANOVA-like orthogonal decomposition of HSIC, allowing for the quantification of not only the main effects of individual patches but also the interactions between pairs of patches. The method is implemented using Latin Hypercube Sampling for mask generation and bilinear upsampling for attribution map visualization.
d58c92fed5069840ab18fcac9f538358645d2260.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification tasks using the ImageNet (ILSVRC-2012) dataset with multiple neural network architectures, including MobileNet, ResNet50, EfficientNet, and VGG16. The method will be compared to state-of-the-art black-box (e.g., RISE, Sobol, LIME, KernelSHAP) and white-box (e.g., Saliency, Integrated Gradients, GradCAM++) attribution methods. Evaluation metrics will include Deletion, Insertion, and µFidelity, which assess the faithfulness of the explanations. Execution time and sample efficiency will also be measured. Additional experiments will extend the method to object detection tasks on the COCO dataset using YOLOv4, and the ability to explain pairwise patch interactions will be qualitatively and quantitatively evaluated.
d58c92fed5069840ab18fcac9f538358645d2260.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first efficient black-box attribution approach based on HSIC, significantly reducing computational cost compared to existing black-box methods while matching or surpassing their fidelity. The approach bridges the efficiency gap between black-box and white-box attribution techniques. Furthermore, the introduction of a new kernel enables an ANOVA-like orthogonal decomposition of HSIC, allowing for the explicit evaluation of pairwise interactions between input regions, which is not possible with traditional attribution methods. The method is also demonstrated to be versatile, applicable to both classification and object detection models.

d59523889679aee15992c4bf6e52b134186d07d3.title: The Geometry of Truth: Emergent Linear Structure in Large Language Model Representations of True/False Datasets
d59523889679aee15992c4bf6e52b134186d07d3.research_question: Do large language models (LLMs) develop unified, abstract internal representations of the truth or falsehood of factual statements, and can these representations be identified, visualized, and causally manipulated across diverse datasets and model scales?
d59523889679aee15992c4bf6e52b134186d07d3.hypothesis: At sufficient scale, LLMs linearly encode the truth or falsehood of factual statements in specific hidden states, and these representations generalize across structurally and topically diverse inputs. Furthermore, simple difference-in-mean probes can identify directions in activation space that are causally implicated in model outputs regarding truthfulness.
d59523889679aee15992c4bf6e52b134186d07d3.proposed_method: The proposed research will curate high-quality datasets of simple, unambiguous true/false statements, including both curated and uncurated sources, as well as nonfactual 'likely' datasets to control for text plausibility. Principal component analysis (PCA) will be used to visualize the geometry of LLM activations for true and false statements, focusing on specific hidden states localized via patching experiments. Linear probes—including logistic regression, mass-mean (difference-in-mean) probes, and contrast-consistent search—will be trained to classify truthfulness from these activations. To assess causality, interventions will be performed by shifting hidden states along probe-identified directions, measuring the effect on model outputs when labeling statements as true or false.
d59523889679aee15992c4bf6e52b134186d07d3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on LLaMA-2 models of varying sizes (7B, 13B, 70B parameters). Datasets will include templates such as 'The city of [city] is in [country].', negated versions, comparative statements, and factual claims from prior work, with both curated (simple, unambiguous) and uncurated (diverse, potentially ambiguous) sets. Baselines will include few-shot prompting and oracle logistic regression on test data. Probes will be evaluated on their classification accuracy both in-distribution and out-of-distribution, as well as their causal efficacy via normalized indirect effect (NIE) metrics when interventions are applied to hidden states. The effect of training on both statements and their logical opposites will be systematically studied to assess generalization and disentanglement from confounding features.
d59523889679aee15992c4bf6e52b134186d07d3.novelty_claims: This research introduces a comprehensive framework for identifying and causally testing linear truth representations in LLMs, including the use of mass-mean probing as a simple, optimization-free alternative to traditional linear probes. The approach systematically localizes truth-relevant hidden states, visualizes emergent linear structure, and demonstrates that at scale, LLMs develop abstract, generalizable truth directions. The research also provides evidence that these directions are more causally implicated in model outputs than those found by other probing techniques, and that training on statements and their opposites improves generalization by mitigating confounding features.

d5bf014858a47b73224c3ed97b7db9d406b9c82c.title: A Blackbox Approach to Best of Both Worlds in Bandits and Beyond
d5bf014858a47b73224c3ed97b7db9d406b9c82c.research_question: Can a general, black-box reduction framework be developed for online learning algorithms that achieves near-optimal regret in both adversarial and stochastic regimes across a wide range of bandit and decision-making problems, including linear bandits, contextual bandits, graph bandits, and tabular Markov decision processes?
d5bf014858a47b73224c3ed97b7db9d406b9c82c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a general reduction approach can be constructed, which, when applied to standard Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL) and Online Mirror Descent (OMD) algorithms, yields algorithms that achieve best-of-both-worlds regret guarantees—specifically, O(log(T)) regret in the stochastic regime and Õ(√T) regret in the adversarial regime—without the need for problem-specific potentials or parameter tuning.
d5bf014858a47b73224c3ed97b7db9d406b9c82c.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves designing a general reduction procedure that transforms any base online learning algorithm satisfying a local self-bounding (LSB) condition into an algorithm with best-of-both-worlds guarantees. The reduction operates in epochs, dynamically selecting candidate actions and monitoring empirical draws to trigger restarts, ensuring adaptation to the environment's hardness. Two main reduction strategies are developed: (1) a direct reduction from LSB algorithms, which is applicable when such algorithms exist for the problem class, and (2) a more general reduction leveraging importance-weighting-stable (iw-stable) algorithms combined via a Corral-style meta-algorithm, allowing the construction of LSB algorithms from standard FTRL/OMD bases. These reductions are instantiated for various settings, including linear and contextual bandits, by adapting existing algorithms (e.g., logdet-FTRL, EXP2, EXP4) to satisfy the required stability properties. The framework is further extended to handle graph feedback and tabular MDPs, and supports data-dependent (first- and second-order) regret bounds.
d5bf014858a47b73224c3ed97b7db9d406b9c82c.experiment_details: The experimental evaluation will consist of rigorous theoretical analysis and empirical simulations across multiple online learning settings. Regret bounds will be established for the proposed algorithms in the adversarial, stochastic, and corrupted stochastic regimes. Key benchmarks include linear bandits, contextual bandits, graph bandits (with both strongly and weakly observable feedback graphs), and tabular MDPs. Baseline comparisons will be made against state-of-the-art best-of-both-worlds algorithms and standard FTRL/OMD approaches, with evaluation metrics focusing on cumulative regret, dependence on problem parameters (e.g., dimension, number of arms, graph complexity), and adaptation to corruption. Experiments will utilize both synthetic and standard benchmark datasets, and ablation studies will assess the impact of different reduction components and stability conditions.
d5bf014858a47b73224c3ed97b7db9d406b9c82c.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first general, black-box reduction framework that enables the construction of best-of-both-worlds algorithms from a wide family of FTRL and OMD algorithms, eliminating the need for problem-specific potential functions and manual parameter tuning. The approach provides the first algorithms for linear bandits and tabular MDPs that achieve optimal O(log(T)) regret in the stochastic regime and optimal adversarial regret, as well as the first best-of-both-worlds algorithms for bandits with graph feedback and expert advice with optimal stochastic guarantees. The reduction framework is broadly applicable, modular, and extends to data-dependent regret bounds, significantly advancing the robustness and generality of online learning algorithms.

d5d7b26dbdf09737878644530b226a79c9f43bfb.title: LlamaFactory: Unified Efficient Fine-Tuning of 100+ Language Models
d5d7b26dbdf09737878644530b226a79c9f43bfb.research_question: How can the process of fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) be unified and made more efficient across a wide variety of models and tasks, enabling scalable, resource-efficient, and user-friendly adaptation to downstream applications?
d5d7b26dbdf09737878644530b226a79c9f43bfb.hypothesis: A modular, unified framework that integrates state-of-the-art efficient fine-tuning techniques and provides both command-line and web-based interfaces will significantly lower the technical barriers, resource requirements, and integration costs for fine-tuning a wide range of LLMs, while maintaining or improving adaptation quality on downstream tasks.
d5d7b26dbdf09737878644530b226a79c9f43bfb.proposed_method: A unified framework will be developed that modularizes the fine-tuning process for LLMs into three main components: Model Loader, Data Worker, and Trainer. The Model Loader will support dynamic model initialization, patching for advanced attention mechanisms, quantization (including 8-bit and 4-bit), and automatic adapter attachment for parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods. The Data Worker will standardize diverse datasets into a unified format, support efficient dataset loading, alignment, merging, and pre-processing, and enable seamless integration of various data structures. The Trainer will incorporate a suite of efficient optimization and computation techniques, such as LoRA, QLoRA, GaLore, BAdam, mixed precision, activation checkpointing, and distributed training via DeepSpeed. An intuitive web interface (LLAMABOARD) will be provided for codeless configuration, monitoring, and evaluation of fine-tuning runs, supporting multiple languages and real-time feedback.
d5d7b26dbdf09737878644530b226a79c9f43bfb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple LLMs, including Gemma-2B, Llama2-7B, Llama2-13B, and others, using the PubMed corpus for language modeling and representative text generation tasks such as CNN/DM, XSum, and AdGen. Fine-tuning will be performed using various efficient methods (full-tuning, freeze-tuning, GaLore, LoRA, QLoRA), and evaluated in terms of memory usage, throughput (tokens/sec), and perplexity on the training corpus. For downstream tasks, models will be fine-tuned and evaluated using ROUGE scores on held-out test sets. Baselines will include pre-trained models and full-tuning, with comparisons made against state-of-the-art parameter-efficient methods. All experiments will utilize consistent hyperparameters, activation checkpointing, and be run on high-memory GPUs (e.g., NVIDIA A100 40GB).
d5d7b26dbdf09737878644530b226a79c9f43bfb.novelty_claims: The proposed framework will be the first to unify over a dozen state-of-the-art efficient fine-tuning techniques and support fine-tuning for over 100 LLMs through a single, modular system. It will minimize dependencies between models, datasets, and training methods, enabling rapid integration and scalability. The approach will introduce model-sharing RLHF, allowing reinforcement learning from human feedback on consumer devices with a single pre-trained model. The web interface will democratize LLM fine-tuning by providing a no-code, multilingual, and real-time monitoring environment. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior efficiency (lower memory footprint, higher throughput) and competitive or improved adaptation quality compared to existing frameworks.

d5d8ca1fe4696ad75820a036c622d292f1b3e22b.title: Approximately Solving Mean Field Games via Entropy-Regularized Deep Reinforcement Learning
d5d8ca1fe4696ad75820a036c622d292f1b3e22b.research_question: How can approximate Nash equilibria be efficiently computed in discrete-time, finite mean field games, especially when standard assumptions such as contractivity and uniqueness of the mean field equilibrium operator do not hold, and how can these methods be extended to high-dimensional or otherwise intractable settings?
d5d8ca1fe4696ad75820a036c622d292f1b3e22b.hypothesis: Introducing entropy regularization and Boltzmann policies into the fixed point iteration for mean field games will guarantee convergence to approximate fixed points, even in cases where standard fixed point methods fail due to non-contractivity, thereby enabling the computation of approximate Nash equilibria in otherwise intractable multi-agent settings.
d5d8ca1fe4696ad75820a036c622d292f1b3e22b.proposed_method: The proposed methodology formulates discrete-time, finite mean field games (MFGs) and demonstrates that standard fixed point iteration fails due to non-contractivity of the equilibrium operator in most practical cases. To address this, the method incorporates entropy regularization into the policy optimization step, leading to the use of softmax (Boltzmann) policies parameterized by a temperature parameter η. The approach defines two related fixed point operators: one based on relative entropy regularization (η-RelEnt MFE) and one based on Boltzmann policies (η-Boltzmann MFE). For each, the agent's policy is updated using a soft Bellman recursion or softmax over action-value functions, with a prior policy as a baseline. Theoretical analysis is provided to show that for sufficiently high temperature, the regularized operators become contractive, guaranteeing convergence to an approximate equilibrium. Additionally, a prior descent strategy is proposed, where the prior policy is iteratively refined to further improve exploitability and equilibrium quality. For high-dimensional problems, deep reinforcement learning (specifically DQN) is used to approximate the value functions and policies, with particle-based simulations to estimate mean field distributions.
d5d8ca1fe4696ad75820a036c622d292f1b3e22b.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a range of environments, including low-dimensional toy problems (e.g., Left-Right, Rock-Paper-Scissors, SIS epidemic model) and a high-dimensional Taxi environment. For tractable problems, exact computation of policies and mean fields is performed, while for high-dimensional cases, deep Q-learning (DQN) is used to approximate optimal policies, with particle-based simulations for mean field estimation. The main evaluation metric is exploitability, defined as the difference in expected reward between the current policy and the best response policy, which directly measures the quality of the approximate Nash equilibrium. Baselines include standard fixed point iteration, fictitious play, and uniform prior policies. The experiments systematically vary the entropy regularization temperature parameter and examine convergence, exploitability, and the effect of prior descent. Results are averaged over multiple seeds and iterations, and both deterministic and stochastic evaluations are reported depending on the environment.
d5d8ca1fe4696ad75820a036c622d292f1b3e22b.novelty_claims: The proposal claims several innovations: (1) a theoretical and empirical demonstration that standard fixed point iteration fails in most finite MFGs due to non-contractivity; (2) the introduction of entropy regularization and Boltzmann policies into the fixed point iteration, which provably guarantee convergence to approximate equilibria for sufficiently high temperature; (3) the development of a prior descent technique to iteratively improve equilibrium quality; (4) the extension of these methods to high-dimensional problems using deep reinforcement learning and particle-based simulations; and (5) comprehensive empirical evaluation showing superior exploitability and convergence properties compared to existing methods such as fictitious play and standard fixed point iteration, thus enabling practical computation of approximate Nash equilibria in settings previously considered intractable.

d5e0ee741e953d857263f70787449e4a57fc1c8d.title: Post-Training Quantization on Diffusion Models
d5e0ee741e953d857263f70787449e4a57fc1c8d.research_question: How can post-training quantization techniques be effectively adapted to accelerate denoising diffusion models, given their unique multi-time-step structure and the challenges of training-free model compression?
d5e0ee741e953d857263f70787449e4a57fc1c8d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a diffusion-model-specific post-training quantization approach, which accounts for the time-varying output distributions of the noise estimation network and employs a tailored calibration dataset and metric, can quantize pre-trained diffusion models to low-bit precision (e.g., 8-bit) without significant loss in generative performance, and may even improve efficiency and quality.
d5e0ee741e953d857263f70787449e4a57fc1c8d.proposed_method: A novel post-training quantization (PTQ) framework, specifically designed for diffusion models, will be developed. The approach will focus on quantizing the noise estimation network in a training-free manner, avoiding the need for retraining or access to original training data. Key steps include: (1) identifying and quantizing the most computation-intensive operations (primarily convolution and fully-connected layers) while preserving full-precision for sensitive functions such as SiLU and softmax; (2) devising a Normally Distributed Time-step Calibration (NDTC) method, which generates calibration samples by sampling time-steps from a skewed normal distribution to better capture the distributional discrepancies across the denoising process; and (3) calibrating quantization parameters using the mean squared error (MSE) metric between full-precision and quantized activations, as MSE is empirically found to yield the best results. The method is designed to be plug-and-play, enabling integration with existing fast-sampling diffusion model variants.
d5e0ee741e953d857263f70787449e4a57fc1c8d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard generative modeling benchmarks, including CIFAR-10 (32x32) and ImageNet (64x64) datasets. Both DDPM (4000 steps) and DDIM (100 and 250 steps) samplers will be evaluated. The quantized models will be compared against their full-precision counterparts using metrics such as Inception Score (IS), Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), and sFID. Baselines will include traditional PTQ methods, naive calibration strategies, and state-of-the-art fast-sampling diffusion methods. Calibration will be performed using 1024 samples generated via the proposed NDTC method, and model performance will be assessed by generating 10,000 samples per configuration. The plug-and-play nature of the method will be validated by applying it to both standard and accelerated diffusion samplers.
d5e0ee741e953d857263f70787449e4a57fc1c8d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic study of post-training quantization for diffusion models, addressing the unique challenge of time-dependent output distributions in the noise estimation network. The NDTC calibration strategy is specifically designed to handle the multi-time-step structure of diffusion models, leading to effective low-bit quantization without retraining. The approach is both training-free and data-agnostic, enabling direct quantization of pre-trained models, and can be seamlessly integrated with existing fast-sampling methods. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate that 8-bit quantized diffusion models can match or even surpass the performance of full-precision models, establishing a new paradigm for efficient deployment of generative diffusion models.

d6045d2ccc9c09ca1671348de86d07da6bc28eea.title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems
d6045d2ccc9c09ca1671348de86d07da6bc28eea.research_question: How can the robustness and accuracy of large language models on multi-step grade school math word problems be improved, particularly given their sensitivity to small errors and the limitations of current generative approaches?
d6045d2ccc9c09ca1671348de86d07da6bc28eea.hypothesis: Training dedicated verifier models to judge the correctness of generated solutions and using them to select among multiple candidate completions will significantly improve performance on multi-step math word problems compared to standard finetuning, and will scale more effectively with increased data.
d6045d2ccc9c09ca1671348de86d07da6bc28eea.proposed_method: A two-stage framework is proposed: first, a large language model (generator) is finetuned on a curated dataset of grade school math word problems and their natural language solutions. The generator is then used to sample multiple candidate solutions for each problem. A separate verifier model is trained to predict the correctness of these candidate solutions, using labels based solely on whether the final answer matches the ground truth. The verifier is trained either at the token or solution level, and may include an auxiliary language modeling objective to improve generalization. At inference, the system generates a set of candidate solutions per problem, ranks them using the verifier, and selects the highest-scoring solution as the final answer. Optionally, majority voting among top-ranked solutions can be used to further increase robustness.
d6045d2ccc9c09ca1671348de86d07da6bc28eea.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted primarily on the GSM8K dataset, which contains 8.5K high-quality, linguistically diverse grade school math word problems with natural language solutions. The dataset is split into 7.5K training and 1K test problems. Baseline comparisons will include standard finetuning of GPT-3 family models (6B and 175B parameters) and the proposed verification approach. Evaluation metrics will focus on the solve rate (percentage of problems correctly answered), with both single-sample and multi-sample (test@N) settings. Ablation studies will examine the effect of model size, number of candidate solutions, verifier training objectives, and the use of auxiliary objectives. Additional experiments will explore the impact of test-time compute, such as varying the number of candidate completions and the use of majority voting.
d6045d2ccc9c09ca1671348de86d07da6bc28eea.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel application of verifier models to the domain of mathematical reasoning in natural language, demonstrating that verification can yield performance gains comparable to a 30x increase in model size. The approach leverages a new, high-quality dataset (GSM8K) specifically designed to probe informal reasoning in language models. The method also systematically explores the scaling properties of verification versus finetuning, and provides empirical evidence that verifiers generalize better with increased data. The use of natural language solutions, token-level verification, and auxiliary language modeling objectives further distinguish this approach from prior work.

d627537b4abc4aa69d0200d38915c9f438e72c02.title: Speculative Prefill: Turbocharging TTFT with Lightweight and Training-Free Token Importance Estimation
d627537b4abc4aa69d0200d38915c9f438e72c02.research_question: How can time-to-first-token (TTFT) latency in large language model (LLM) inference be significantly reduced for both long and medium context queries, without requiring additional training or fine-tuning, while maintaining high output quality?
d627537b4abc4aa69d0200d38915c9f438e72c02.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a lightweight, training-free framework leveraging a secondary model to estimate and select contextually important tokens can substantially reduce TTFT and improve maximal queries-per-second (QPS) in LLM inference, with minimal impact on output quality.
d627537b4abc4aa69d0200d38915c9f438e72c02.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed Speculative Prefill (SPECPREFILL), will be developed to accelerate the prefill phase of LLM inference. The approach involves deploying a lightweight speculator model—typically a smaller LLM from the same family—which, given a prompt, computes attention scores to estimate the importance of each token. Key steps include aggregating attention scores (using max-mean strategies), denoising via chunk selection and pooling, and restoring original positional information for the selected tokens. Only the most contextually important tokens, as determined by the speculator, along with their positional encodings, are forwarded to the main, larger LLM for processing. The method is designed to be training-free, requiring no fine-tuning or adaptation, and can be seamlessly integrated with existing inference engines and techniques such as quantization, key-value (KV) cache eviction, and speculative decoding.
d627537b4abc4aa69d0200d38915c9f438e72c02.experiment_details: Comprehensive experiments will be conducted using both real and synthetic datasets. Downstream tasks will be drawn from LongBench (covering single- and multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, code completion, and synthetic context probing via RULER), as well as standard short-context benchmarks (Generative MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, MBPP, ArcChallenge, GPQA). The main models evaluated will include Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (BF16) and Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct-FP8, with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct serving as the speculator. Baselines will include the vanilla Llama models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) at sentence level, LLMLingua (context compression), and MInference (sparse attention optimization). Evaluation metrics will include TTFT, QPS, accuracy, and latency under varying token keep rates and batch sizes. Experiments will be run on multi-GPU systems (e.g., 8x NVIDIA H100/H200), and ablation studies will assess the impact of various design choices (e.g., look-ahead, chunking).
d627537b4abc4aa69d0200d38915c9f438e72c02.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a conceptually simple, training-free, and highly efficient framework for reducing TTFT in LLM inference by leveraging a lightweight speculator model for token importance estimation. Unlike prior approaches, this method does not require any fine-tuning, model adaptation, or explicit context-question separation, and can be deployed with minimal code changes. It is the first to demonstrate substantial TTFT and QPS improvements (up to 7.66× TTFT reduction and 7× QPS increase) for very large models (e.g., Llama-3.1-405B) in real-world server-client settings, while maintaining high output quality. The approach is orthogonal and complementary to existing acceleration techniques such as quantization and speculative decoding, and can be combined with them for further gains. Additionally, the method is shown to be robust across a wide range of tasks and context lengths, and in some cases, even improves output quality by removing noisy or redundant prompt tokens.

d62a029b1f0c51bbd760a18edcd8825f06c7e056.title: DBLoss: Decomposition-based Loss Function for Time Series Forecasting
d62a029b1f0c51bbd760a18edcd8825f06c7e056.research_question: How can time series forecasting models be improved to more accurately capture seasonality and trend components within the forecasting horizon, beyond what is achievable with standard loss functions such as Mean Squared Error (MSE)?
d62a029b1f0c51bbd760a18edcd8825f06c7e056.hypothesis: Explicitly decomposing both predictions and ground truth into trend and seasonal components within the loss function, and optimizing their errors separately with appropriate weighting, will improve the ability of forecasting models to capture these patterns and enhance both predictive accuracy and generalization.
d62a029b1f0c51bbd760a18edcd8825f06c7e056.proposed_method: A new loss function, termed Decomposition-Based Loss (DBLoss), will be developed for time series forecasting tasks. The method first generates model predictions using any deep learning backbone. Both the predicted and ground truth sequences are then decomposed into seasonal and trend components using an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) decomposition module. Separate losses are computed for the seasonal and trend components, and these losses are combined via a weighted sum, with a tunable parameter to balance their contributions. To address scale differences, a scale alignment mechanism is introduced, adaptively adjusting the trend loss based on the relative magnitudes of the two components. The final loss is used to optimize the forecasting model, encouraging it to learn both seasonality and trend more effectively.
d62a029b1f0c51bbd760a18edcd8825f06c7e056.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on eight widely-used real-world time series forecasting benchmarks: ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, ETTm2, Solar, Weather, Electricity, and Traffic. The proposed loss will be evaluated across multiple deep learning backbones, including iTransformer, Amplifier, PatchTST, DLinear, and four foundation models (CALF, UniTS, TTM, GPT4TS). Standard evaluation metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) will be used. Forecasting horizons of 96, 192, 336, and 720 will be considered. Baseline results will be obtained using the original loss functions (e.g., MSE), and only the loss function will be replaced with DBLoss for fair comparison. Additional experiments will include zero-shot generalization and few-shot fine-tuning settings to assess robustness and transferability. All experiments will be run in a unified benchmark environment with consistent hyperparameters and hardware.
d62a029b1f0c51bbd760a18edcd8825f06c7e056.novelty_claims: The proposed loss function introduces a novel approach by decomposing both predictions and ground truth into trend and seasonal components within the forecasting horizon and optimizing their errors separately. Unlike prior loss functions that focus on shape, dependency, or patch-based structures, this method directly targets the inductive biases of seasonality and trend in the loss computation. DBLoss is model-agnostic, incurs negligible computational overhead, and can be seamlessly integrated with any deep learning forecasting model. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this approach consistently improves performance over state-of-the-art models and loss functions, enhances generalization to unseen datasets, and provides a new perspective for loss function design in time series forecasting.

d6819eebb479ee6e9955227c2d87ee9228b63cb0.title: Sparsing Law: Towards Large Language Models with Greater Activation Sparsity
d6819eebb479ee6e9955227c2d87ee9228b63cb0.research_question: How can activation sparsity in large language models be measured more accurately, what factors influence activation sparsity during model architecture design and training, and how can more sparsely activated and efficient large language models be constructed?
d6819eebb479ee6e9955227c2d87ee9228b63cb0.hypothesis: Greater activation sparsity in large language models can be achieved and measured accurately through improved metrics, specific architectural choices, and training strategies, leading to more efficient models without significant performance degradation.
d6819eebb479ee6e9955227c2d87ee9228b63cb0.proposed_method: A generalizable and performance-friendly metric, CETT-PPL-1%, will be developed to measure activation sparsity in large language models. This metric will use a binary search to tune the CETT (Cumulative Error of Tail Truncation) hyperparameter such that the increase in perplexity (PPL) on validation data does not exceed 1% compared to the dense baseline, ensuring negligible performance loss. The method will systematically identify weakly-contributed neurons in each feed-forward network layer by adaptively setting layer-wise activation thresholds, applicable across various activation functions. The approach will also explore the impact of activation function selection (e.g., ReLU vs. SiLU), width-depth ratio, and pre-training data amount on activation sparsity, and will propose architectural and training guidelines to maximize sparsity while maintaining model stability.
d6819eebb479ee6e9955227c2d87ee9228b63cb0.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training and evaluating large language models ranging from 0.1B to 2.4B parameters using architectures based on µP Transformer with gated FFNs and µP parametrization for stability. Models will be pre-trained on large-scale datasets, including subsets of The Pile, Wikipedia, code, math, and Chinese corpora, with varying activation functions (ReLU, SiLU) and width-depth ratios. Activation sparsity will be measured using CETT-PPL-1% and compared to other metrics such as Top-k and FAT-ε. Baselines will include dense models and models with alternative sparsity metrics. Evaluation will be performed on commonsense reasoning and reading comprehension benchmarks, using metrics such as perplexity and downstream task accuracy. Additional experiments will assess the impact of architectural choices and training data scale on sparsity, and decoding speed will be benchmarked using PowerInfer and llama.cpp to quantify efficiency gains.
d6819eebb479ee6e9955227c2d87ee9228b63cb0.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces CETT-PPL-1%, a novel, generalizable metric for accurately measuring activation sparsity with minimal performance degradation. It presents the first comprehensive quantitative study of activation sparsity's influential factors, including activation function, width-depth ratio, and pre-training data scale, and establishes empirical scaling laws for sparsity in large language models. The approach demonstrates that ReLU activation, increased training data, and optimized width-depth ratios can yield highly sparse and efficient models, validated by training a 2.4B parameter model achieving over 93% sparsity and a 4.1× inference speedup. The findings provide actionable guidelines for designing and pre-training large language models with greater activation sparsity, enabling practical efficiency improvements.

d6837b60f100b40c5ee2284fbee3134a904c0603.title: Generative Inbetweening: Adapting Image-to-Video Models for Keyframe Interpolation
d6837b60f100b40c5ee2284fbee3134a904c0603.research_question: How can high-quality, temporally coherent video sequences be generated to interpolate between two given keyframes, leveraging existing large-scale image-to-video diffusion models without requiring extensive retraining from scratch?
d6837b60f100b40c5ee2284fbee3134a904c0603.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that adapting a pre-trained image-to-video diffusion model through lightweight fine-tuning and a dual-directional sampling process can enable effective keyframe interpolation, producing videos with coherent motion between distant frames, outperforming both traditional frame interpolation and existing diffusion-based methods.
d6837b60f100b40c5ee2284fbee3134a904c0603.proposed_method: The proposed approach adapts a pre-trained image-to-video diffusion model, such as Stable Video Diffusion (SVD), for keyframe interpolation by introducing a lightweight fine-tuning technique. This technique specifically fine-tunes the value and output projection matrices in the temporal self-attention layers, using 180-degree rotated attention maps to reverse the learned motion-time association, thereby enabling backward motion generation from a single input frame. During inference, a dual-directional diffusion sampling process is employed: the original model generates forward motion from the first keyframe, while the fine-tuned model generates backward motion from the second keyframe. At each sampling step, the intermediate noise predictions from both directions are fused (typically via averaging), ensuring forward-backward motion consistency and producing a video that starts and ends with the provided frames. The process includes per-step recurrence, where Gaussian noise is re-injected and denoising is repeated multiple times at each step to enhance fusion quality.
d6837b60f100b40c5ee2284fbee3134a904c0603.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two high-resolution (1080p) datasets: the DAVIS dataset (117 keyframe pairs) and a curated Pexels dataset (106 keyframe pairs), both featuring dynamic scenes and large object motions. The method is compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including FILM (a flow-based frame interpolation method), TRF (a recent SVD-based bounded video generation approach), and DynamiCrafter (a large-scale image-to-video model with keyframing). Evaluation metrics include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Fréchet Video Distance (FVD), which assess the similarity between generated and ground-truth videos. The experimental setup utilizes a small training set of 100 SVD-generated videos for fine-tuning, with training performed on 4 A100 GPUs for approximately 15,000 iterations and a batch size of 4. Sampling uses 50 steps and default SVD parameters.
d6837b60f100b40c5ee2284fbee3134a904c0603.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel, lightweight fine-tuning strategy that adapts only a small subset of parameters in the temporal self-attention layers, enabling backward motion generation without full model retraining. The approach leverages 180-degree rotation of attention maps to reverse motion-time association, facilitating dual-directional sampling that fuses forward and backward motion predictions for consistent in-between video generation. This dual-directional fusion ensures coherent motion paths between distant keyframes, addressing limitations of both traditional frame interpolation and prior diffusion-based methods. The method achieves superior quantitative and qualitative results on challenging datasets, demonstrating improved motion coherence and video quality with minimal computational overhead.

d6a7261a98f5029abce173dbe41af6afe52367aa.title: Hierarchical Sliced Wasserstein Distance
d6a7261a98f5029abce173dbe41af6afe52367aa.research_question: How can the computational and memory efficiency of Wasserstein distance-based metrics be improved for high-dimensional, low-support settings, such as those encountered in deep learning applications, without sacrificing generative or statistical performance?
d6a7261a98f5029abce173dbe41af6afe52367aa.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a hierarchical projection strategy, which constructs final projections as random linear combinations of a smaller set of bottleneck projections, can significantly reduce computational and memory costs in estimating Wasserstein-type distances while maintaining or improving performance in generative modeling tasks.
d6a7261a98f5029abce173dbe41af6afe52367aa.proposed_method: A novel metric, the Hierarchical Sliced Wasserstein (HSW) distance, will be developed by introducing the Hierarchical Radon Transform (HRT). The HRT is constructed by recursively applying variants of the Radon Transform, specifically composing Partial Radon Transform (PRT) and Overparameterized Radon Transform (ORT). In practice, two probability measures are first projected into k bottleneck one-dimensional projections using random directions, where k is much smaller than the total number of final projections L. The final L projections are then formed as random linear combinations of these k bottleneck projections, with the mixing coefficients sampled from a uniform distribution on the unit hypersphere. The HSW distance is defined as the average Wasserstein distance between the projected measures over these hierarchical projections. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to prove the injectivity of HRT, the metricity of HSW, and to characterize its computational, projection, and sample complexities.
d6a7261a98f5029abce173dbe41af6afe52367aa.experiment_details: Experiments will focus on deep generative modeling using standard benchmark image datasets such as CIFAR10 (32x32), CelebA (64x64), and TinyImageNet (64x64). The proposed HSW distance will be compared to conventional Sliced Wasserstein (SW) distance in the context of mini-batch training with high-dimensional feature spaces (e.g., d=8192, batch size=128). Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS), as well as computational and memory complexity and wall-clock time. Ablation studies will be performed to analyze the effect of varying the number of bottleneck projections k and final projections L. Baselines will include SW with varying numbers of projections, and additional comparisons will be made to Max-SW and Max-HSW variants. Each experiment will be repeated multiple times to report mean and standard deviation of results.
d6a7261a98f5029abce173dbe41af6afe52367aa.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the Hierarchical Radon Transform (HRT) and the Hierarchical Sliced Wasserstein (HSW) distance, both of which are novel constructs not previously explored in the literature. The method provides a provably injective and metric-preserving hierarchical projection framework that enables efficient computation and memory usage in high-dimensional, low-support settings. Theoretical contributions include proofs of metricity, injectivity, and favorable sample complexity. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that HSW achieves comparable or superior generative quality and faster convergence than conventional SW, with significantly reduced computational and memory requirements. The approach also offers a new perspective on the geometry of projection manifolds for Wasserstein-type distances.

d6a7ff47580d6eb47b35f77a7c831cabcbb21120.title: Commonsense Knowledge Editing Based on Free-Text in LLMs
d6a7ff47580d6eb47b35f77a7c831cabcbb21120.research_question: How can large language models be effectively edited to update or correct commonsense knowledge that is expressed in free-text form, rather than structured triples or entities?
d6a7ff47580d6eb47b35f77a7c831cabcbb21120.hypothesis: Commonsense knowledge in large language models is dispersed across MLP and Attention layers, and a dynamics-aware, layer-specific editing method will enable more effective and precise editing of free-text commonsense knowledge than existing approaches.
d6a7ff47580d6eb47b35f77a7c831cabcbb21120.proposed_method: A new methodology will be developed that first localizes commonsense knowledge within large language models by analyzing the distribution of knowledge across MLP and Attention layers using a Knowledge Localization for Free-Text (KLFT) method. This involves causal tracing and semantic similarity evaluation to identify which layers and hidden states contribute most to the storage and recall of free-text commonsense knowledge. Building on these findings, a Dynamics-aware Editing Method (DEM) will be introduced, which employs a Dynamics-aware Module to dynamically select the most relevant layers for editing based on cosine similarity of input/output hidden states. The Knowledge Editing Module then updates both MLP and Attention weights in the selected layers using an optimization objective that balances retention of existing knowledge and insertion of new target knowledge, leveraging incremental weight updates derived from target answer representations. The editing process is designed to handle multi-token, free-text knowledge, and includes mechanisms for both generalization and specificity.
d6a7ff47580d6eb47b35f77a7c831cabcbb21120.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large language models such as GPT-J (6B) and LLaMA-2 (7B), using a newly constructed Commonsense Knowledge Editing Benchmark (CKEBench) dataset derived from the ATOMIC commonsense database. CKEBench contains 15,600 samples spanning 23 relationship types and is specifically designed for free-text knowledge editing. Baseline methods for comparison will include Fine-Tuning, MEND, MEMIT, and PMET. Evaluation metrics will include Score, Efficiency, Generalization, Specificity, Fluency, Consistency, and a dedicated Commonsense indicator, with GPT-4 used to assess semantic similarity between generated and target texts. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of the Dynamics-aware module and the separate editing of MLP and Attention layers.
d6a7ff47580d6eb47b35f77a7c831cabcbb21120.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first benchmark (CKEBench) specifically for editing commonsense knowledge in free-text form. It pioneers a KLFT method for localizing dispersed commonsense knowledge in LLMs and demonstrates that such knowledge is not stored locally but is distributed across MLP and Attention layers. The proposed DEM is the first dynamics-aware, layer-specific editing approach designed for multi-token, free-text knowledge, enabling more precise and effective editing than prior methods focused on structured triples or fixed-layer edits. Substantial improvements over state-of-the-art baselines are claimed in both overall editing efficacy and commonsense-specific metrics.

d6b5452d5dfc0bdc3e571166ebafc1d86a544bd0.title: Do as We Do, Not as You Think: the Conformity of Large Language Models
d6b5452d5dfc0bdc3e571166ebafc1d86a544bd0.research_question: How does conformity manifest in large language model (LLM)-driven multi-agent systems, what factors influence its emergence, and what strategies can be developed to mitigate conformity in collaborative AI environments?
d6b5452d5dfc0bdc3e571166ebafc1d86a544bd0.hypothesis: LLM-driven multi-agent systems exhibit measurable conformity behaviors analogous to human group dynamics, and these behaviors are influenced by both intrinsic model properties and extrinsic contextual variables. Furthermore, targeted interventions such as persona enhancement and reflection mechanisms can reduce conformity and promote independent decision-making.
d6b5452d5dfc0bdc3e571166ebafc1d86a544bd0.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted using a newly developed benchmark, BENCHFORM, designed to probe conformity in LLM-based multi-agent collaborations. BENCHFORM will consist of reasoning-intensive tasks derived from the BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) dataset, encompassing both logical/analytical and language/contextual questions. Five distinct interaction protocols will be implemented to simulate various social dynamics, including baseline (Raw), Correct Guidance, Wrong Guidance, Trust, and Doubt, thereby enabling the study of both short-term and long-term group interactions. Quantitative metrics such as conformity rate and independence rate will be defined to assess the impact of group influence on agent decision-making. Additionally, ablation studies will be performed to analyze the effects of interaction time and majority size, and behavioral studies will be conducted to understand how agents rationalize their conformity. Finally, two mitigation strategies—empowered persona prompts and reflection mechanisms—will be developed and evaluated to reduce conformity effects.
d6b5452d5dfc0bdc3e571166ebafc1d86a544bd0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on BENCHFORM using 11 representative LLMs, including both proprietary (e.g., GPT-3.5, GPT-4o) and open-source models (e.g., Llama3, Llama3.1, Gemma2, Qwen2 series). Each model will be evaluated across all five interaction protocols, with up to 300 samples per task type and a total of 3,299 multiple-choice questions. Baseline performance will be established using the Raw protocol, and comparative analysis will be performed under the other protocols to measure changes in accuracy, conformity rate, and independence rate. Ablation studies will vary the number of discussion rounds and the majority size to assess their effects on conformity. Behavioral studies will involve qualitative analysis of agent responses to probe self-awareness and rationalization of conformity. The efficacy of mitigation strategies will be quantified by comparing conformity and independence rates before and after the application of persona and reflection prompts.
d6b5452d5dfc0bdc3e571166ebafc1d86a544bd0.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces BENCHFORM, the first benchmark specifically designed to study conformity in LLM-driven multi-agent systems, featuring reasoning-intensive tasks and interaction protocols inspired by social psychology. It establishes new quantitative metrics for measuring conformity and independence in collaborative AI settings. The methodology enables comprehensive analysis of both intrinsic and extrinsic factors influencing conformity, including model size, interaction duration, and group majority effects. The proposal further pioneers prompt-based mitigation strategies—empowered persona and reflection mechanisms—to reduce conformity, providing actionable insights for developing more robust and ethically-aligned collaborative AI systems.

d6ba4475a263418033d270e80ff431747388f38b.title: MOBO-OSD: Batch Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization via Orthogonal Search Directions
d6ba4475a263418033d270e80ff431747388f38b.research_question: How can multi-objective Bayesian optimization be improved to efficiently generate a diverse set of Pareto optimal solutions, with broad coverage of the objective space, under limited evaluation budgets and in both sequential and batch optimization settings?
d6ba4475a263418033d270e80ff431747388f38b.hypothesis: A multi-objective Bayesian optimization framework that generates candidate solutions by solving constrained optimization subproblems along orthogonal search directions, defined with respect to an approximated convex hull of individual objective minima, and further enriches solution diversity through local Pareto front estimation, will achieve superior Pareto front diversity and hypervolume performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, while remaining scalable to problems with many objectives and supporting efficient batch optimization.
d6ba4475a263418033d270e80ff431747388f38b.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a batch multi-objective Bayesian optimization framework that constructs an approximated convex hull of individual objective minima (CHIM) using boundary points derived from observed data. A set of well-distributed orthogonal search directions (OSDs) is generated with respect to this approximated CHIM, leveraging the Riesz s-Energy method to ensure diversity. For each OSD, a constrained optimization subproblem is solved using the posterior mean and confidence bounds from Gaussian process surrogates, seeking candidate solutions that are close to the OSD and maximize a scalar parameter representing progress along the direction. To further enhance the density of Pareto optimal candidates, a Pareto Front Estimation (PFE) technique is applied, locally exploring the neighborhood of each OSD-derived candidate using first-order approximations and random perturbations. Batch selection of solutions for evaluation is performed using the Hypervolume Improvement acquisition function, with the Kriging Believer strategy and constraints to ensure diversity across exploration spaces.
d6ba4475a263418033d270e80ff431747388f38b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five synthetic and four real-world multi-objective benchmark problems, with the number of objectives ranging from two to six. The synthetic benchmarks include DTLZ2 (with 2, 3, and 4 objectives), ZDT1, and VLMOP2, while the real-world tasks are drawn from the RE problem suite (Speed Reducer, Car Side Design, Marine Design, and Water Planning). The proposed method will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines: qParEGO, USeMO, DGEMO, PDBO, JES, qEHVI, NSGA-II, and NBI. Evaluation will be based on the logarithmic hypervolume difference between the observed Pareto front and the maximum hypervolume, with results averaged over 10 independent runs. Both sequential (batch size 1) and batch (batch sizes 4, 8, 10) optimization settings will be tested, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of key parameters and components.
d6ba4475a263418033d270e80ff431747388f38b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel use of orthogonal search directions defined with respect to an approximated convex hull of objective minima for candidate generation in multi-objective Bayesian optimization. The integration of a Pareto Front Estimation technique enables local exploration around candidate solutions, enhancing Pareto front coverage without excessive computational cost. The method is designed to be scalable to an arbitrary number of objectives and supports efficient batch optimization via a diversity-aware batch selection strategy. Empirical results demonstrate consistent outperformance over state-of-the-art baselines in both sequential and batch settings, across a wide range of benchmark problems.

d6cd7acbb7f919ee8111b45e8027094460dc3c7d.title: WMCopier: Forging Invisible Image Watermarks on Arbitrary Images
d6cd7acbb7f919ee8111b45e8027094460dc3c7d.research_question: How can invisible image watermarking systems be compromised in practical, real-world settings where attackers have no access to the watermarking algorithm or embedding process, and what are the limitations and defenses against such forgery attacks?
d6cd7acbb7f919ee8111b45e8027094460dc3c7d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a diffusion model trained solely on watermarked images can learn the underlying watermark distribution and, through a carefully designed inversion and refinement process, can inject convincing, undetectable watermarks into arbitrary images, even without knowledge of the watermarking scheme.
d6cd7acbb7f919ee8111b45e8027094460dc3c7d.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a three-stage attack pipeline for forging invisible watermarks onto arbitrary images in a no-box setting. First, an unconditional diffusion model is trained on a collection of watermarked images to estimate the target watermark distribution. Next, a shallow inversion strategy is employed: a clean image is mapped to its latent representation via DDIM inversion up to an early timestep, and then denoised using the trained diffusion model, effectively injecting the watermark signal while preserving semantic content. Finally, a refinement procedure is applied, jointly optimizing for image fidelity and conformity to the watermark distribution using a gradient-based update that balances semantic similarity and watermark detectability. This process leverages the score function from the diffusion model to ensure the forged image lies within the high-probability region of the watermarked distribution.
d6cd7acbb7f919ee8111b45e8027094460dc3c7d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using both AI-generated images (DiffusionDB) and real photographs (MS-COCO, ImageNet, CelebA-HQ) to simulate real-world forgery scenarios. The method is evaluated against four watermarking schemes: three open-source post-processing methods (DWT-DCT, HiDDeN, RivaGAN), one in-processing method (Stable Signature), and a closed-source deployed system (Amazon's watermarking API). Baselines include a heuristic no-box method (Yang et al.) and a black-box method (Wang et al.). Evaluation metrics include Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) for visual fidelity, bit accuracy for watermark extraction, and false positive rate (FPR) at calibrated thresholds. The impact of attack parameters, dataset size, and defense strategies (multi-message watermarking) is systematically analyzed, including ablation studies and robustness tests under common image distortions.
d6cd7acbb7f919ee8111b45e8027094460dc3c7d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first no-box watermark forgery attack based on diffusion models, capable of forging watermarks without any knowledge of the underlying scheme or access to the embedding process. It develops a novel shallow inversion and refinement procedure that jointly optimizes for image quality and watermark conformity. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art forgery success rates and visual fidelity across both open-source and real-world deployed watermarking systems, including Amazon's. Additionally, the research provides the first comprehensive analysis of defense strategies against such attacks, offering actionable insights for the design of more robust watermarking systems.

d6d0fd994f37b630f35945736b5e1bb198148404.title: Time Travel in LLMs: Tracing Data Contamination in Large Language Models
d6d0fd994f37b630f35945736b5e1bb198148404.research_question: How can data contamination in large language models (LLMs) be automatically detected at both the instance and partition levels, especially when access to pre-training data is unavailable and computational resources are limited?
d6d0fd994f37b630f35945736b5e1bb198148404.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a method leveraging guided instruction prompts, overlap metrics (such as ROUGE-L and BLEURT), and few-shot in-context learning with a powerful LLM (e.g., GPT-4) can accurately and efficiently detect data contamination in LLMs at both the instance and partition levels, even without access to pre-training data.
d6d0fd994f37b630f35945736b5e1bb198148404.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a two-stage framework for detecting data contamination in LLMs. First, guided instruction prompts are constructed by including the dataset name, partition type, and a random-length initial segment of a reference instance (plus label if relevant), and the LLM is tasked with completing the instance. Two main approaches are then used for contamination detection: (1) Overlap-based detection, where the generated completions under guided and general (non-specific) instructions are compared using ROUGE-L and BLEURT scores; a statistically significant increase in overlap under guided instruction indicates contamination. (2) Few-shot in-context learning (ICL) with GPT-4, where the model is prompted with examples of exact and near-exact matches to classify new completions; a partition is flagged as contaminated if at least one exact or two near-exact matches are found. This process is applied to small random samples from each dataset partition, enabling efficient evaluation.
d6d0fd994f37b630f35945736b5e1bb198148404.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven diverse NLP datasets (IMDB, AG News, Yelp Full Reviews, SAMSum, XSum, WNLI, RTE) covering classification, summarization, and natural language inference tasks. Both training and test/validation splits will be sampled, with 10 random instances per split. The LLMs under investigation are GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 (specific API versions), and the methods will be compared to a baseline approach (ChatGPT-Cheat?) that prompts the model to reproduce dataset instances. Evaluation metrics include BLEURT and ROUGE-L for overlap, as well as human expert annotation for exact and near-exact matches. The primary baseline is human annotation, and the main experimental setup involves deterministic prompting (temperature zero, capped completion length) to ensure reproducibility.
d6d0fd994f37b630f35945736b5e1bb198148404.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a robust, inexpensive, and scalable method for detecting data contamination in LLMs without requiring access to pre-training data or significant computational resources. The approach combines guided instruction prompting with both statistical overlap metrics and advanced few-shot ICL evaluation, enabling detection at both the instance and partition levels. The method is validated across multiple datasets and LLMs, demonstrating high accuracy (92–100%) and outperforming prior contamination detection strategies, particularly in closed-source and resource-constrained scenarios.

d6d40e778032fd06ea5a4127cb3c6722f3165a33.title: A Unified Continual Learning Framework with General Parameter-Efficient Tuning
d6d40e778032fd06ea5a4127cb3c6722f3165a33.research_question: How can a unified continual learning framework be developed that enables robust, memory-free adaptation of pre-trained models to novel tasks using general parameter-efficient tuning methods, across diverse architectures and tasks?
d6d40e778032fd06ea5a4127cb3c6722f3165a33.hypothesis: A unified continual learning framework that incorporates general parameter-efficient tuning (PET) methods, with mechanisms for adaptation speed calibration, knowledge accumulation, and expert ensemble, will achieve superior incremental learning performance and robustness compared to existing prompt-based or task-specific PET approaches.
d6d40e778032fd06ea5a4127cb3c6722f3165a33.proposed_method: The proposed framework, Learning-Accumulation-Ensemble (LAE), is designed to reshape any parameter-efficient tuning (PET) method for continual learning. First, an online PET module is attached to a frozen pre-trained model and adapted to new tasks, with a novel adaptation speed calibration mechanism that aligns the learning dynamics of different PET modules (e.g., Adapter, LoRA, Prefix) using gradient analysis and learnable scaling parameters. Second, knowledge from the online PET module is accumulated into an offline PET module via an exponential moving average, integrating multi-task knowledge without retaining old data or explicit task-specific modules. Third, during inference, predictions from both online (novel task expert) and offline (historical task expert) PET modules are ensembled using an energy-based selection mechanism, normalizing outputs to ensure robust task-agnostic prediction. The framework is architecture-agnostic and supports various PET modules as long as they are compatible with the underlying pre-trained model.
d6d40e778032fd06ea5a4127cb3c6722f3165a33.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on class-incremental learning settings using CIFAR100 and ImageNet-R benchmarks, with models pre-trained on ImageNet21k. The datasets will be split into 10 tasks (10 classes per task for CIFAR100, 20 for ImageNet-R), and the framework will be evaluated using last incremental accuracy (A_10) and average incremental accuracy (Ā_10). Baselines will include state-of-the-art prompt-based continual learning methods (e.g., L2P, DualPrompt, ESN), as well as naive sequential fine-tuning and joint fine-tuning. The proposed method will be tested with multiple PET modules (Adapter, LoRA, Prefix) and on different architectures (ViT-B/16, Swin-B, ConvNeXt-B). Ablation studies will analyze the impact of adaptation speed calibration, accumulation, ensemble strategy, PET module size and position, and architectural generalization. All experiments will be repeated with different class orders and reported with mean and standard deviation.
d6d40e778032fd06ea5a4127cb3c6722f3165a33.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to unify general parameter-efficient tuning methods for continual learning, extending beyond prompt-based approaches and supporting diverse architectures. Key innovations include a novel adaptation speed calibration mechanism for PET modules, a memory-free accumulation of multi-task knowledge via an offline PET module, and an energy-based ensemble of online and offline experts for robust inference. The approach eliminates the need for task-specific parameter selection and demonstrates superior performance and robustness in long-term continual learning scenarios, outperforming prior state-of-the-art methods on multiple benchmarks.

d6e8af411ae267aa4cd31e36c027dc6f624f9d65.title: DEAR: Disentangled Environment and Agent Representations for Reinforcement Learning without Reconstruction
d6e8af411ae267aa4cd31e36c027dc6f624f9d65.research_question: How can the incorporation of explicit agent knowledge, such as segmentation masks, improve the sample efficiency and robustness of reinforcement learning algorithms for visual control tasks in complex and dynamic environments?
d6e8af411ae267aa4cd31e36c027dc6f624f9d65.hypothesis: Explicitly disentangling agent and environment representations in the latent space, using agent segmentation masks as supervision and enforcing feature separation constraints, will improve sample efficiency and robustness of visual reinforcement learning without requiring reconstruction of visual observations.
d6e8af411ae267aa4cd31e36c027dc6f624f9d65.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that leverages agent segmentation masks as supervision to explicitly disentangle agent and environment representations in the latent space of a visual encoder. The method will use an encoder to process input images, splitting the resulting latent vector into agent-specific and environment-specific components. The agent component will be supervised by a decoder trained to reconstruct the agent mask using a binary cross-entropy loss, while a feature separation constraint (cosine similarity minimization) will be applied to enforce orthogonality between agent and environment representations. These disentangled representations will be concatenated and used as input to the reinforcement learning policy. The auxiliary losses for mask reconstruction and disentanglement will be combined with the standard RL objective, and gradient flow will be managed to ensure stable learning.
d6e8af411ae267aa4cd31e36c027dc6f624f9d65.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two challenging benchmarks: the Distracting DeepMind Control Suite (including Walker-walk, Ball-in-the-cup, and Finger-spin tasks with randomized backgrounds) and Franka Kitchen manipulation tasks (light switch and kettle tasks with sparse rewards). The agent will receive RGB images and agent masks as inputs, with masks generated from the simulator or perturbed to simulate noise and approximation. Baselines for comparison will include DrQ-v2 (data-augmented RL), TED (temporal disentanglement), and SEAR (supervised agent-environment disentanglement with reconstruction). Evaluation metrics will include average total reward, sample efficiency (convergence speed), latent cosine similarity between agent and environment representations, and robustness to noisy/approximate masks. Ablation studies will be performed on auxiliary loss coefficients and mask quality. All experiments will use consistent hyperparameters, with additional tuning for new loss coefficients introduced by the proposed method.
d6e8af411ae267aa4cd31e36c027dc6f624f9d65.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a disentanglement framework for agent and environment representations in visual reinforcement learning that does not require reconstruction of the full observation, reducing model complexity and training time. The method leverages agent segmentation masks as direct supervision to learn interpretable and orthogonal latent features, improving sample efficiency and robustness compared to prior methods. The approach demonstrates superior or comparable performance to state-of-the-art baselines, with enhanced interpretability and robustness to noisy or approximate agent masks, and requires fewer parameters than previous reconstruction-based disentanglement methods.

d6eeb2898bd9bd34744194ef543062dda6c4531a.title: Scissorhands: Exploiting the Persistence of Importance Hypothesis for LLM KV Cache Compression at Test Time
d6eeb2898bd9bd34744194ef543062dda6c4531a.research_question: How can memory usage for key-value (KV) cache during inference in large language models (LLMs) be significantly reduced without compromising model quality or requiring model retraining, especially as context window sizes and batch sizes increase?
d6eeb2898bd9bd34744194ef543062dda6c4531a.hypothesis: Only pivotal tokens—those that have had substantial influence at one step—will significantly influence future generations in LLM inference, enabling the prediction and retention of only important tokens in the KV cache for efficient memory usage.
d6eeb2898bd9bd34744194ef543062dda6c4531a.proposed_method: A novel KV cache compression framework, SCISSORHANDS, will be developed to maintain the memory usage of the KV cache under a fixed budget during LLM inference, without any model fine-tuning. The method will monitor attention scores over a configurable history window to identify and retain only the most influential (pivotal) tokens, while non-influential tokens are periodically dropped from the cache. The approach will use an efficient algorithm inspired by reservoir sampling and least-recently-used (LRU) cache replacement, ensuring that recent tokens are always kept and that the cache size never exceeds the predetermined memory budget. The method will be compatible with quantization techniques, such as 4-bit quantization, for further memory savings.
d6eeb2898bd9bd34744194ef543062dda6c4531a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of LLMs, including OPT-6B, OPT-13B, OPT-30B, and OPT-66B, using both language modeling datasets (e.g., C4) and multiple few-shot downstream tasks (Hellaswag, MathQA, PIQA, Winogrande). The evaluation will compare SCISSORHANDS against standard inference using the original KV cache, measuring metrics such as perplexity for language modeling and accuracy for downstream tasks. Experiments will be run on NVIDIA A100 GPUs, and the impact of different compression ratios (up to 5× reduction) will be assessed. Baseline comparisons will include the original model and the combination of SCISSORHANDS with 4-bit quantization. Additional ablations will analyze attention score fidelity and the effect of compression on model outputs.
