d6eeb2898bd9bd34744194ef543062dda6c4531a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a test-time KV cache compression method for LLMs that does not require model retraining or fine-tuning and is guided by an empirically and theoretically supported persistence of importance hypothesis. The method provides a practical algorithm for maintaining cache size under a strict memory budget, achieves up to 5× reduction in KV cache memory with negligible impact on model quality, and is compatible with quantization for further compression. This approach enables higher inference throughput and scalability for LLM deployment, addressing a major bottleneck in real-world applications.

d7074976c2609568902a6b6ca45f6c71d9cb66bf.title: Understanding the Latent Space of Diffusion Models through the Lens of Riemannian Geometry
d7074976c2609568902a6b6ca45f6c71d9cb66bf.research_question: How can the latent space of diffusion models be systematically understood and characterized from a geometric perspective, and what implications does this understanding have for controllability, image editing, and the influence of conditioning prompts during the generative process?
d7074976c2609568902a6b6ca45f6c71d9cb66bf.hypothesis: The latent space of diffusion models possesses a meaningful local geometric structure that can be revealed using Riemannian geometry and pullback metrics, enabling semantically interpretable manipulations and providing insights into the evolution of generative processes and the effects of conditioning.
d7074976c2609568902a6b6ca45f6c71d9cb66bf.proposed_method: A novel approach will be developed to analyze the latent space of diffusion models by leveraging the pullback metric from Riemannian geometry. The method involves deriving the local latent basis in the latent space X by performing singular value decomposition (SVD) on the Jacobian of the mapping from X to the feature space H (the bottleneck layer of the U-Net). This local basis will be used to define tangent spaces and enable image editing by traversing along specific basis vectors at chosen diffusion timesteps. To facilitate editing across samples, parallel transport in the feature space H will be employed to transfer editing directions between different data points. Additionally, an x-space guidance mechanism will be introduced to improve the fidelity of edits by incorporating the model's denoising function into the manipulation process.
d7074976c2609568902a6b6ca45f6c71d9cb66bf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both unconditional and text-to-image diffusion models, including Stable Diffusion. Real images will be inverted into the latent space using DDIM inversion, and editing will be performed at various timesteps using the discovered latent basis vectors. Datasets of varying complexity, such as CelebA-HQ, Flowers, LSUN, FFHQ, and ImageNet, will be used to analyze the evolution of the latent structure. Baselines for comparison will include existing image editing methods that manipulate attention maps or feature spaces. Evaluation metrics will include qualitative assessment of semantic editing, power spectral density analysis to characterize frequency evolution, and geodesic distances on the Grassmannian manifold to quantify the similarity of tangent spaces across samples, timesteps, and prompt conditions.
d7074976c2609568902a6b6ca45f6c71d9cb66bf.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic geometric analysis of the latent space of diffusion models using pullback metrics and Riemannian geometry. It enables unsupervised discovery of semantically meaningful latent directions for image editing, requiring no additional training and operating at a single timestep. The method provides new insights into the coarse-to-fine generative process, the impact of dataset complexity on latent structure, and the time-varying influence of conditioning prompts. Parallel transport is leveraged for consistent editing across samples, and the approach is broadly applicable to diffusion models with Euclidean feature spaces.

d730d42bb655b3b44727d71c147f9758612043a8.title: Adversarial Diffusion Distillation
d730d42bb655b3b44727d71c147f9758612043a8.research_question: How can high-fidelity, real-time image generation be achieved using large-scale pretrained diffusion models with only a few sampling steps, while maintaining or surpassing the image quality and compositionality of existing state-of-the-art models?
d730d42bb655b3b44727d71c147f9758612043a8.hypothesis: A hybrid training approach that combines adversarial loss with score distillation from a pretrained diffusion model can enable a student model to generate high-quality images in as few as one to four sampling steps, outperforming existing few-step methods and matching or exceeding the performance of state-of-the-art diffusion models.
d730d42bb655b3b44727d71c147f9758612043a8.proposed_method: A new training framework, Adversarial Diffusion Distillation (ADD), will be developed to distill a pretrained diffusion model into a fast, few-step image generator. The method initializes a student UNet-based diffusion model from pretrained weights and trains it using a combination of two objectives: an adversarial loss, which encourages the student to generate samples indistinguishable from real images, and a score distillation loss, which leverages a frozen teacher diffusion model to provide denoising targets for the student. The adversarial loss employs a discriminator conditioned on both text and image embeddings, extracted via pretrained networks (e.g., CLIP and DINOv2 ViT), while the score distillation loss uses the teacher’s denoising predictions as reconstruction targets for the student’s outputs at various noise levels. The training is performed in pixel space, but can be adapted to latent space for latent diffusion models. The overall objective is a weighted sum of the adversarial and distillation losses, with careful ablation of loss weighting and conditioning strategies.
d730d42bb655b3b44727d71c147f9758612043a8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using two student model sizes (860M and 3.1B parameters) based on Stable Diffusion 2.1 and SDXL backbones, respectively, and evaluated at a standardized resolution of 512x512 pixels. The method will be compared against strong baselines, including Latent Consistency Models (LCM, LCM-XL), StyleGAN-T++, InstaFlow, OpenMUSE, and standard diffusion models (SDXL, IF-XL), using both automated metrics (FID, CLIP score) and large-scale human preference studies (ELO scores) on the COCO 2017 dataset. Ablation studies will examine the impact of discriminator architecture, conditioning, student pretraining, loss weighting, and teacher/student model choices. Inference speed and sample quality will be benchmarked across different numbers of sampling steps (1–4), with qualitative and quantitative comparisons to state-of-the-art methods.
d730d42bb655b3b44727d71c147f9758612043a8.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable single-step, real-time image synthesis with large-scale foundational diffusion models while maintaining high image fidelity. The method introduces a novel hybrid objective that combines adversarial training with score distillation, allowing for both high realism and strong compositionality in generated images. It leverages pretrained diffusion model weights for stable adversarial training, overcoming scalability issues of GANs. The approach significantly outperforms existing few-step methods and matches or exceeds the performance of state-of-the-art diffusion models in both automated and human evaluations, particularly in the ultra-fast (1–2 step) sampling regime.

d73a3ec3e609635b028b6351426e61b146243307.title: Phase-Field DeepONet: Physics-informed deep operator neural network for fast simulations of pattern formation governed by gradient flows of free-energy functionals
d73a3ec3e609635b028b6351426e61b146243307.research_question: How can a physics-informed operator neural network framework be developed to enable fast and accurate simulations of pattern formation in dynamical systems governed by gradient flows of free-energy functionals, such as those described by the Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations?
d73a3ec3e609635b028b6351426e61b146243307.hypothesis: A physics-informed deep operator neural network, incorporating an energy-based loss function derived from the minimizing movement scheme, can efficiently and accurately predict the time evolution of pattern-forming systems governed by gradient flows, outperforming traditional physics-informed neural networks in terms of flexibility, generalizability, and computational efficiency.
d73a3ec3e609635b028b6351426e61b146243307.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a physics-informed deep operator neural network (Phase-Field DeepONet) that integrates the minimizing movement scheme into the operator learning framework. The network consists of two sub-networks: a branch network that takes as input the discretized current state of the field variable, and a trunk network that takes spatial coordinates. The output is a mapping from the current field distribution to the next time step, effectively functioning as an explicit time-stepper. The loss function is constructed as the sum of the free energy at the next time step and a distance term between consecutive field distributions, directly encoding the physics of gradient flows. The network is trained by minimizing this physics-informed loss, allowing for predictions at arbitrary spatial locations and for arbitrary initial conditions without retraining.
d73a3ec3e609635b028b6351426e61b146243307.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on canonical problems including 1D relaxation kinetics, the Allen-Cahn equation, and the Cahn-Hilliard equation, which are representative of pattern formation governed by gradient flows. Synthetic datasets will be generated using Gaussian random processes for initial conditions, and the network will be trained and tested on thousands of such samples. Baseline comparisons will be made with traditional physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) that use sequential sub-networks for each time step. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error and coefficient of determination (r^2) on both training and testing sets, as well as qualitative agreement with analytical or numerical ground truth solutions. Network architectures will be systematically varied (e.g., number of layers, nodes, sensors), and training will be performed using standard optimizers such as Adam, with training and inference times recorded for efficiency assessment.
d73a3ec3e609635b028b6351426e61b146243307.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a novel integration of the minimizing movement scheme with deep operator networks, enabling direct physics-informed learning of time evolution in systems governed by gradient flows of free-energy functionals. Unlike traditional PINNs, the method allows for efficient, explicit time-stepping and generalizes to arbitrary initial conditions without retraining. The approach leverages an energy-based loss function that reduces the need for large datasets and complex loss balancing, resulting in improved training efficiency and flexibility. This framework is broadly applicable to a wide range of pattern-forming dynamical systems and offers significant potential for real-time simulation and surrogate modeling in scientific and engineering applications.

d752e422b7e0f55259cb546a690dd391b315f95a.title: ENVIDR: Implicit Differentiable Renderer with Neural Environment Lighting
d752e422b7e0f55259cb546a690dd391b315f95a.research_question: How can neural rendering frameworks be improved to achieve high-quality reconstruction and rendering of 3D scenes with challenging specular (glossy, shiny) surfaces, while enabling accurate surface geometry, scene relighting, and material editing?
d752e422b7e0f55259cb546a690dd391b315f95a.hypothesis: A neural rendering framework that leverages decomposed neural components to approximate physically based rendering (PBR)—including explicit modeling of environment lighting, diffuse, and specular components—combined with an SDF-based neural surface representation and explicit modeling of indirect illumination, will outperform existing methods in rendering quality, surface reconstruction accuracy, and scene editability for scenes with complex specular reflections.
d752e422b7e0f55259cb546a690dd391b315f95a.proposed_method: A novel neural rendering framework will be developed, consisting of two main components: (1) a neural renderer with decomposed multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) that separately model environment lighting, diffuse, and specular rendering, and (2) an SDF-based neural surface model for scene representation. The neural renderer will be trained using images synthesized by a physically based renderer (PBR) with varying materials and environment lights, where the environment MLP outputs neural features rather than RGB values, enabling flexible relighting and material editing. The diffuse and specular MLPs will learn to synthesize color by fusing geometry features with environment features, and feature normalization (e.g., L2-norm) will be applied to ensure consistent feature mappings across scenes. To handle indirect illumination (inter-reflections), an additional ray-marching step will be performed along surface-reflected directions for low-roughness surfaces, with a dedicated MLP to encode and blend the resulting indirect radiance into the final rendered color. The SDF-based surface model will interact with the pre-trained neural renderer, and only the environment MLP and surface model will be optimized during scene reconstruction.
d752e422b7e0f55259cb546a690dd391b315f95a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several challenging synthetic and real datasets, including the Shiny Blender dataset, NeRF's Blender dataset (shiny scenes), and a real captured shiny scene from SNeRG. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as Ref-NeRF, VolSDF, NVDiffRec, and NVDiffRecMC. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for novel view synthesis quality, mean angular error (MAE) for surface normal estimation, and qualitative/quantitative assessment of environment light estimation and scene relighting. The experimental setup will involve training the neural renderer on synthetic spheres with varying materials and environment maps, and then applying the trained renderer to scene reconstruction and editing tasks. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of feature normalization, pre-training, and indirect illumination modeling.
d752e422b7e0f55259cb546a690dd391b315f95a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully implicit, differentiable neural renderer with decomposed components for environment, diffuse, and specular rendering, enabling accurate modeling of complex surface-light interactions without explicit rendering equations. The environment MLP outputs neural features, allowing for flexible relighting and material editing by swapping environment representations. The method explicitly models indirect illumination via surface-reflected ray marching, improving rendering quality for shiny surfaces with inter-reflections. The framework achieves superior or on-par results with state-of-the-art methods in both rendering quality and surface reconstruction, while providing enhanced scene editability and accurate environment light estimation. The design choices, such as feature normalization and pre-trained rendering components, further ensure consistent and high-quality results across diverse scenes.

d75b631d6e4fb2e11f4b1d411b1b2c3feab84bc8.title: MaxSup: Overcoming Representation Collapse in Label Smoothing
d75b631d6e4fb2e11f4b1d411b1b2c3feab84bc8.research_question: How can the detrimental effects of representation collapse and overconfidence in neural networks, particularly those induced by label smoothing, be mitigated to improve generalization, intra-class diversity, and transferability of learned representations across various classification and segmentation tasks?
d75b631d6e4fb2e11f4b1d411b1b2c3feab84bc8.hypothesis: Penalizing the top-1 logit rather than the ground-truth logit during training will provide consistent regularization for both correctly and incorrectly classified samples, thereby overcoming the error amplification and representation collapse caused by traditional label smoothing. This approach is expected to preserve intra-class diversity, sharpen inter-class boundaries, and improve both accuracy and transferability of neural network representations.
d75b631d6e4fb2e11f4b1d411b1b2c3feab84bc8.proposed_method: A novel regularization technique, Max Suppression (MaxSup), will be developed to address the shortcomings of label smoothing. Instead of penalizing the ground-truth logit, MaxSup applies a regularization penalty to the largest (top-1) logit in the model's output, regardless of whether the prediction is correct or incorrect. The method modifies the cross-entropy loss by adding a term that penalizes the difference between the top-1 logit and the mean logit, thus ensuring a uniform regularization signal across all samples. This approach eliminates the error amplification effect present in label smoothing, preserves the ground-truth logit during misclassifications, and maintains richer intra-class variation. The method will be integrated seamlessly into standard training pipelines with negligible computational overhead.
d75b631d6e4fb2e11f4b1d411b1b2c3feab84bc8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale image classification datasets such as ImageNet-1K, as well as on fine-grained datasets (CUB-200-2011, Stanford Cars), long-tailed datasets (CIFAR-10-LT), and semantic segmentation tasks (ADE20K). Multiple neural network architectures will be evaluated, including ResNet, MobileNetV2, and DeiT-Small. Baselines will include standard cross-entropy, label smoothing, Online Label Smoothing (OLS), Zipf Label Smoothing, and Logit Penalty. Evaluation metrics will comprise top-1 accuracy, intra-class variation, inter-class separability, linear-probe transfer accuracy, mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) for segmentation, and calibration metrics such as NLL and ECE for OOD robustness. Ablation studies will isolate the effects of regularization and error amplification components, and Grad-CAM visualizations will be used to qualitatively assess attention and feature diversity.
d75b631d6e4fb2e11f4b1d411b1b2c3feab84bc8.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a logit-level regularization framework that penalizes the top-1 logit instead of the ground-truth logit, fundamentally differing from label smoothing and its variants. This approach directly addresses the error amplification and representation collapse issues inherent to label smoothing, providing consistent regularization for all samples. MaxSup is claimed to preserve intra-class diversity, enhance inter-class boundaries, and improve both accuracy and transferability across diverse tasks and architectures. The method is computationally efficient, easily integrable into existing pipelines, and demonstrates superior performance and robustness compared to existing regularization strategies.

d766bffc357127e0dc86dd69561d5aeb520d6f4c.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
d766bffc357127e0dc86dd69561d5aeb520d6f4c.research_question: How can large language models be better aligned with user intent across a broad range of tasks, particularly in terms of helpfulness, truthfulness, and harmlessness, using techniques that incorporate human feedback?
d766bffc357127e0dc86dd69561d5aeb520d6f4c.hypothesis: Fine-tuning large language models with human feedback, specifically through supervised learning on human demonstrations and reinforcement learning from human preferences, will result in models that more reliably follow user instructions, generate more truthful and less toxic outputs, and are preferred by human evaluators compared to models trained solely on next-token prediction objectives.
d766bffc357127e0dc86dd69561d5aeb520d6f4c.proposed_method: The proposed method begins with a pretrained large language model and applies a three-step fine-tuning process. First, a supervised policy is trained by fine-tuning the model on a dataset of human-written demonstrations that exemplify desired behaviors for a diverse set of prompts. Second, a reward model is trained using a dataset of human-labeled comparisons, where labelers indicate their preferred output among several model completions for the same prompt; this reward model predicts which outputs humans would prefer. Third, the supervised policy is further fine-tuned using reinforcement learning, specifically Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), with the reward model providing the scalar reward signal. An additional variant mixes PPO updates with updates that increase the log-likelihood of the pretraining distribution to mitigate performance regressions on standard NLP tasks. This iterative process can be repeated with new comparison data to continually refine the reward model and policy.
d766bffc357127e0dc86dd69561d5aeb520d6f4c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple model sizes (1.3B, 6B, and 175B parameters), all based on the GPT-3 architecture. The primary dataset consists of prompts submitted to the OpenAI API and labeler-written prompts, filtered for privacy and deduplicated, with splits by user ID to avoid data leakage. Three datasets are used: demonstrations for supervised fine-tuning, comparisons for reward modeling, and prompts for PPO-based RL fine-tuning. Baselines include standard GPT-3, GPT-3 with few-shot prompting, and GPT-3 fine-tuned on public instruction datasets (FLAN and T0). Evaluation involves human preference ratings on held-out API prompts, Likert-scale quality ratings, and metadata on output appropriateness, as well as automatic and human evaluations on public NLP datasets for truthfulness (TruthfulQA), toxicity (RealToxicityPrompts), and bias (CrowS-Pairs, Winogender). Performance regressions on standard NLP tasks (e.g., SQuAD, DROP, HellaSwag, WMT2015) are monitored and addressed via the mixed-objective PPO-ptx variant.
d766bffc357127e0dc86dd69561d5aeb520d6f4c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive framework for aligning large language models with user intent by combining supervised fine-tuning on human demonstrations with reinforcement learning from human feedback across a broad and realistic prompt distribution. The method extends RLHF beyond narrow domains to a wide range of language tasks, demonstrates that smaller models fine-tuned with human feedback can outperform much larger baseline models, and provides evidence that such models generalize to new instructions and labeler preferences. The approach also addresses the challenge of minimizing performance regressions on standard NLP tasks while improving alignment, and systematically evaluates alignment in terms of helpfulness, truthfulness, and harmlessness using both human and automatic metrics.

d76b7d26f3fc7581e4bda5677ae87179fdfbb169.title: 10 Years of Fair Representations: Challenges and Opportunities
d76b7d26f3fc7581e4bda5677ae87179fdfbb169.research_question: How can fair representation learning (FRL) techniques be rigorously evaluated and improved to ensure that sensitive or undesired information is effectively removed from learned data representations, especially in light of theoretical challenges in information removal within neural networks?
d76b7d26f3fc7581e4bda5677ae87179fdfbb169.hypothesis: Deterministic, unquantized neural network-based FRL methodologies are fundamentally limited in their ability to remove sensitive information from learned representations, whereas stochastic or highly quantized approaches may be more effective in achieving true invariance with respect to sensitive attributes.
d76b7d26f3fc7581e4bda5677ae87179fdfbb169.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed to rigorously test the effectiveness of various FRL methods in removing sensitive information from data representations. The approach will involve both theoretical analysis, leveraging recent results in deep learning information theory, and large-scale empirical experimentation across multiple FRL algorithms. The methodology will include the use of automated machine learning (AutoML) to adversarially attempt to recover sensitive attributes from representations deemed 'fair' by existing evaluation protocols. The framework will standardize preprocessing, hyperparameter tuning, and evaluation procedures, and will assess both fair allocation (decision fairness) and invariance (representation fairness) using a range of fairness and predictive performance metrics. Special attention will be given to the trade-off between task accuracy and fairness, and to the impact of model stochasticity and quantization on information removal.
d76b7d26f3fc7581e4bda5677ae87179fdfbb169.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six widely used fairness-sensitive datasets, including Adult, German, Banks, Folktables (AK and HI), and COMPAS. Eight FRL models, encompassing both deterministic and stochastic/quantized approaches (e.g., BinaryMI, DetBinaryMI, DebiasClassifier, NVP, VFAE, ICVAE, LFR, Deep Domain Confusion), will be evaluated. For each dataset-model combination, the evaluation pipeline will include repeated k-fold cross-validation, hyperparameter optimization, and assessment across a range of fairness-accuracy trade-off parameters (gamma). AutoML will be used to train classifiers to predict sensitive attributes from learned representations, providing a robust test of information removal. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, AUC, area under discrimination curve (AUDC), rND for ranking fairness, and statistical parity differences. The experimental setup will ensure reproducibility and comparability by releasing all code, metadata, and best hyperparameters.
d76b7d26f3fc7581e4bda5677ae87179fdfbb169.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a rigorous, standardized, and extensible evaluation framework for FRL that combines theoretical impossibility results with large-scale empirical adversarial testing. The use of AutoML to systematically mine sensitive information from representations is a novel and severe test of FRL effectiveness. The work highlights and addresses critical limitations in current FRL evaluation practices, demonstrates the inadequacy of deterministic, unquantized models for true information removal, and provides actionable recommendations for future FRL research, including the need for stochasticity or quantization and the importance of dual-frame evaluation (fair allocation and invariance). The release of the EvalFRL library and comprehensive experimental metadata further advances the field by enabling reproducible and extensible benchmarking.

d77ecb65db24407c6557f83cd517e07fcfee7ddd.title: General Cutting Planes for Bound-Propagation-Based Neural Network Verification
d77ecb65db24407c6557f83cd517e07fcfee7ddd.research_question: How can the efficiency and verification power of bound-propagation-based neural network verifiers be improved by incorporating general cutting plane constraints, including those involving relaxed integer variables, within the verification process?
d77ecb65db24407c6557f83cd517e07fcfee7ddd.hypothesis: Incorporating general cutting plane constraints, including those generated by mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers and involving variables across multiple layers and relaxed integer variables, into bound-propagation-based neural network verification will significantly strengthen convex relaxations, reduce the number of required branches in branch-and-bound procedures, and improve verification completeness and efficiency compared to existing methods.
d77ecb65db24407c6557f83cd517e07fcfee7ddd.proposed_method: A generalized bound propagation framework, termed GCP-CROWN, will be developed to support arbitrary cutting plane constraints within the LP relaxation of the neural network verification problem. This method will extend traditional bound propagation to handle constraints involving variables from any layer and relaxed integer variables (e.g., ReLU indicators), enabling the integration of sophisticated cutting planes such as Gomory and mixed-integer rounding cuts. The dual formulation of the LP with cutting planes will be derived, and a layer-by-layer propagation rule will be established to compute valid lower bounds efficiently on GPUs. To further enhance verification power, the framework will be combined with a parallelized architecture where a CPU-based MIP solver generates high-quality cutting planes in real-time, which are then dynamically incorporated into the GPU-accelerated bound propagation and branch-and-bound process. The system will be fully asynchronous, allowing bound propagation and cut generation to proceed independently and maximize hardware utilization.
d77ecb65db24407c6557f83cd517e07fcfee7ddd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard neural network verification benchmarks, including the oval20 and oval21 benchmarks from VNN-COMP, as well as the SDP-FO suite and cifar10-resnet models. The proposed method will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines, including state-of-the-art bound propagation verifiers (e.g., β-CROWN, α-CROWN), branch-and-bound frameworks with multi-neuron relaxations, and MIP-based approaches. Evaluation metrics will include the number of verified properties, average runtime per instance, number of branches explored, and verified accuracy. The experimental setup will utilize both GPU and CPU resources, with the GPU handling bound propagation and the CPU running the MIP solver for cut generation. Timeout thresholds and batch processing strategies will be aligned with prior literature to ensure fair comparison.
d77ecb65db24407c6557f83cd517e07fcfee7ddd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable efficient, GPU-accelerated bound propagation for neural network verification with support for arbitrary, general cutting plane constraints, including those involving relaxed integer variables and variables from multiple layers. By integrating real-time, MIP-solver-generated cutting planes into the verification process, the method achieves significantly tighter convex relaxations and reduces the need for extensive branching. The parallel and asynchronous architecture leverages both GPU and CPU resources, resulting in state-of-the-art verification performance and scalability on challenging benchmarks. This generalization of bound propagation opens new avenues for leveraging advanced cutting plane techniques in neural network verification.

d7890d1906d95c4ae4c430b350455156d6d8aed9.title: SDXL: Improving Latent Diffusion Models for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
d7890d1906d95c4ae4c430b350455156d6d8aed9.research_question: How can latent diffusion models for text-to-image synthesis be improved to generate high-resolution, high-fidelity images across diverse aspect ratios and resolutions, while maintaining controllability and transparency in the generation process?
d7890d1906d95c4ae4c430b350455156d6d8aed9.hypothesis: Enhancing the architecture of latent diffusion models with a larger UNet backbone, advanced text encoders, novel conditioning schemes (including size and crop conditioning), multi-aspect training, and a dedicated refinement model will substantially improve the visual fidelity, prompt adherence, and versatility of generated images compared to previous versions.
d7890d1906d95c4ae4c430b350455156d6d8aed9.proposed_method: A new latent diffusion model will be developed featuring a UNet backbone with approximately three times the parameters of previous models, incorporating a heterogeneous distribution of transformer blocks and omitting the lowest feature level for efficiency. The model will utilize dual text encoders (OpenCLIP ViT-bigG and CLIP ViT-L), concatenating their outputs for richer text conditioning, and will introduce additional conditioning vectors for original image size and cropping parameters, embedded via Fourier feature encodings and integrated into the model's timestep embeddings. Multi-aspect training will be implemented by bucketing training images by aspect ratio and conditioning the model on bucket size, allowing simultaneous handling of multiple output resolutions. An improved autoencoder, trained from scratch with larger batch sizes and exponential moving average tracking, will provide a higher-fidelity latent space. Finally, a separate refinement diffusion model will be trained to post-process and enhance the quality of generated latents using a noising-denoising process, particularly improving local detail and high-resolution outputs.
d7890d1906d95c4ae4c430b350455156d6d8aed9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large-scale internal datasets with diverse image sizes and aspect ratios, as well as standard benchmarks such as class-conditional ImageNet and COCO2017 for autoencoder evaluation. The model's performance will be compared against previous Stable Diffusion versions (1.5 and 2.1) and state-of-the-art black-box image generators. Evaluation will include both quantitative metrics (FID, IS, LPIPS, SSIM, rFID, and CLIP scores) and qualitative user studies, where participants will rate generations from different models. The training pipeline will involve pretraining at 256x256 resolution, continued training at 512x512, and multi-aspect finetuning near 1024x1024 pixel area, with batch sizes up to 2048 and 600,000+ optimization steps. The effect of each conditioning scheme will be ablated and assessed independently, and the impact of the refinement model will be measured through side-by-side comparisons and win rates in user preference studies.
d7890d1906d95c4ae4c430b350455156d6d8aed9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces several key innovations: a significantly larger and more efficient UNet backbone with heterogeneous transformer block distribution; dual text encoder conditioning for richer semantic understanding; novel and simple conditioning schemes for image size and cropping that allow fine-grained control and better generalization; a multi-aspect training regime enabling flexible output resolutions; and a dedicated refinement diffusion model for post-hoc enhancement of image quality. These contributions collectively enable open, transparent, and state-of-the-art text-to-image synthesis, surpassing previous open-source models and rivaling closed-source black-box generators in user preference studies.

d7aff3e7c84e8440b49a3cd36f686c6486094956.title: Complete Verification via Multi-Neuron Relaxation Guided Branch-and-Bound
d7aff3e7c84e8440b49a3cd36f686c6486094956.research_question: How can neural network verification be made both complete and scalable for large, high-accuracy networks, overcoming the limitations of existing convex relaxation and branch-and-bound approaches?
d7aff3e7c84e8440b49a3cd36f686c6486094956.hypothesis: Integrating tight multi-neuron convex relaxations within a branch-and-bound verification framework, guided by novel branching heuristics and efficient GPU-based optimization, will significantly reduce the number of subproblems and improve the scalability and precision of complete neural network verification.
d7aff3e7c84e8440b49a3cd36f686c6486094956.proposed_method: A new verification framework, termed Multi-Neuron Constraint Guided Branch-and-Bound (MN-BAB), will be developed to combine tight multi-neuron convex relaxations with a branch-and-bound (BaB) approach. The method will enforce multi-neuron constraints using Lagrange multipliers, allowing for the integration of arbitrary linear constraints over neuron activations throughout the network. A dual optimization procedure, implemented efficiently on GPUs, will optimize the parameters of the relaxation to yield sound and tight bounds. The framework will include a novel branching heuristic, Active Constraint Score Branching (ACS), which selects split points based on the sensitivity of multi-neuron constraints, and a Cost Adjusted Branching (CAB) strategy that incorporates computational cost into the branching decision. The method will support a wide range of network architectures and activation functions, and will be implemented to leverage hardware acceleration for scalability.
d7aff3e7c84e8440b49a3cd36f686c6486094956.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard neural network verification benchmarks, including MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets, as well as on more challenging and less regularized networks such as several ResNet variants trained with adversarial methods. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art complete verifiers including ERAN, β-CROWN, and OVAL, using metrics such as verified accuracy, empirical upper bounds, and average runtime per sample. Evaluation will be performed on a GPU-accelerated platform, and both the number of subproblems and verification times will be analyzed. Ablation studies will assess the impact of multi-neuron constraints and the proposed branching heuristics on verification performance.
d7aff3e7c84e8440b49a3cd36f686c6486094956.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a complete neural network verifier that, for the first time, integrates tight multi-neuron convex relaxations directly into a branch-and-bound framework. It develops a novel branching heuristic (ACS) informed by the activity and sensitivity of multi-neuron constraints, and a cost-adjusted branching strategy (CAB) that optimizes verification efficiency. The framework leverages an efficient GPU-based dual optimization method, enabling the verification of larger and more accurate networks than previously possible. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate substantial improvements in certified accuracy and scalability, achieving up to 28% certification gains on challenging benchmarks.

d7bca917b753b996074203cc77ba45935b7c62d7.title: ProcTHOR: Large-Scale Embodied AI Using Procedural Generation
d7bca917b753b996074203cc77ba45935b7c62d7.research_question: How can large-scale, diverse, and interactive virtual environments be generated efficiently to enable scalable training and evaluation of embodied AI agents across navigation, interaction, and manipulation tasks?
d7bca917b753b996074203cc77ba45935b7c62d7.hypothesis: Procedurally generating a vast number of diverse, interactive, and customizable virtual environments will enable embodied AI agents to achieve superior generalization and state-of-the-art performance on a range of downstream navigation and manipulation benchmarks, including in zero-shot settings.
d7bca917b753b996074203cc77ba45935b7c62d7.proposed_method: A framework will be developed for procedural generation of embodied AI environments, extending an existing simulator (such as AI2-THOR) to support the automatic creation of fully interactive, physics-enabled virtual houses. The generation process will use multi-stage conditional sampling to iteratively create floor plans, wall structures, lighting, doors, and populate scenes with a large library of assets, ensuring realistic placements and physical plausibility. The system will support dynamic material and lighting randomization, enabling extensive scene diversity and augmentation. The framework will also allow for easy customization of room types, asset distributions, and environmental parameters, and will be designed for high efficiency, enabling the generation of arbitrarily large datasets either statically or on-the-fly during training.
d7bca917b753b996074203cc77ba45935b7c62d7.experiment_details: Experiments will involve sampling a large dataset (e.g., 10,000 houses) of procedurally generated, fully interactive environments, with additional validation and test splits. Agents with simple neural architectures (CNN+RNN) will be trained using only RGB images, without explicit mapping or human task supervision. The trained models will be evaluated on multiple embodied AI benchmarks, including ObjectNav and manipulation tasks across RoboTHOR, Habitat, AI2-iTHOR, ARCHITECTHOR, and others. Both zero-shot transfer (no fine-tuning) and fine-tuned performance will be measured, with comparisons to state-of-the-art baselines. Evaluation metrics will include Success Rate, SPL (Success weighted by Path Length), and task-specific metrics like %FixedStrict and PickUpSR. Ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of dataset scale on agent performance.
d7bca917b753b996074203cc77ba45935b7c62d7.novelty_claims: The proposed framework enables the scalable, efficient, and fully automatic generation of an unbounded number of diverse, interactive, and physics-enabled environments for embodied AI research. Unlike prior datasets, the environments support rich interactivity, dynamic asset and lighting randomization, and realistic scene composition, facilitating studies of data augmentation and large-scale training. The approach demonstrates that large-scale procedural generation leads to substantial improvements in agent generalization and state-of-the-art results across multiple embodied AI benchmarks, including strong zero-shot performance. The framework and codebase are intended to be open-sourced, providing a valuable resource for the research community.

d7c9a47e92d1c66fe4c677f3472bf295e6668b52.title: Predictive Performance of Deep Quantum Data Re-uploading Models
d7c9a47e92d1c66fe4c677f3472bf295e6668b52.research_question: What are the fundamental limitations in the predictive performance of quantum machine learning models employing data re-uploading circuits, particularly when processing high-dimensional data with limited-qubit architectures? How do the depth of encoding layers and the number of data re-uploading repetitions affect the ability of these models to generalize and make accurate predictions on unseen data?
d7c9a47e92d1c66fe4c677f3472bf295e6668b52.hypothesis: Increasing the number of encoding layers in data re-uploading quantum models with limited qubits leads to a degradation in predictive performance, causing the model's predictions on unseen data to approach random guessing. Repeated data uploading (i.e., increasing the number of repetitions) does not mitigate this degradation.
d7c9a47e92d1c66fe4c677f3472bf295e6668b52.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted into the predictive performance of quantum data re-uploading models. The approach will involve extending existing analytical techniques to allow for arbitrary learnable parameterized quantum gates between encoding layers, rather than restricting to specific non-parameterized entangling gates. The analysis will focus on the evolution of encoded quantum states in the Pauli basis, quantifying how the expected output over the data distribution changes as the number of encoding layers and repetitions increases. A novel method will be developed to directly analyze the prediction error by examining the expected output of the model, bypassing the traditional decomposition into training and generalization errors. Additionally, approximating circuits will be constructed to analyze repeated data uploading scenarios, enabling the study of models with multiple re-uploading repetitions.
d7c9a47e92d1c66fe4c677f3472bf295e6668b52.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic datasets will include high-dimensional, linearly separable classification problems with features drawn from independent Gaussian distributions, as well as regression tasks. Real-world datasets will include grayscale and RGB versions of CIFAR-10 and the MNIST dataset, with data preprocessed to fit the input requirements of quantum circuits. Quantum data re-uploading models with varying numbers of qubits, encoding layers, and repetitions will be trained and evaluated. Baselines will include models with shallow encoding layers and models with increased circuit width (more qubits). Evaluation metrics will include prediction error (classification accuracy, regression error), quantum state divergence from the maximally mixed state, and the difference between model outputs and theoretical predictions. Experimental setups will control for parameter count and training conditions, and results will be averaged over multiple random seeds to ensure statistical significance.
d7c9a47e92d1c66fe4c677f3472bf295e6668b52.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel theoretical framework for analyzing the predictive performance of quantum data re-uploading models, extending prior work by allowing arbitrary parameterized gates between encoding layers and by directly analyzing prediction error without relying on the traditional training/generalization error decomposition. It establishes, for the first time, that deep encoding layers in limited-qubit data re-uploading models fundamentally limit predictive performance, causing outputs to converge to random guessing regardless of trainability or expressivity. The work also demonstrates that repeated data uploading does not resolve this limitation and provides new theoretical bounds and empirical evidence to guide the architectural design of quantum machine learning models for high-dimensional data.

d7d1bbade9453f0348fac8a5c60d131528b87fcf.title: Block-NeRF: Scalable Large Scene Neural View Synthesis
d7d1bbade9453f0348fac8a5c60d131528b87fcf.research_question: How can neural radiance field (NeRF) based methods be scaled to enable high-fidelity, photorealistic novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction of arbitrarily large, real-world environments, such as entire city neighborhoods, while supporting efficient updates and robust handling of diverse environmental conditions?
d7d1bbade9453f0348fac8a5c60d131528b87fcf.hypothesis: Decomposing large-scale environments into independently trained, spatially organized neural radiance fields (Block-NeRFs), augmented with appearance embeddings, learned pose refinement, exposure conditioning, and visibility prediction, will enable scalable, memory-efficient, and high-quality neural scene reconstruction and view synthesis across city-scale scenes, while allowing for flexible updates and seamless compositing.
d7d1bbade9453f0348fac8a5c60d131528b87fcf.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a framework that partitions a large environment into a grid of spatially localized Block-NeRFs, each trained independently on image data from a specific region. Each Block-NeRF extends the mip-NeRF architecture by incorporating appearance embeddings (optimized per image via generative latent optimization) to account for varying environmental conditions, a learned pose refinement module to correct camera pose errors, and explicit exposure conditioning to handle differences in camera exposure. A visibility prediction network is trained alongside each Block-NeRF to estimate the visibility of points in space, facilitating efficient selection and compositing of relevant blocks at inference. During rendering, only Block-NeRFs within a certain radius of the target viewpoint are selected based on geographic proximity and predicted visibility, and their outputs are composited using inverse distance weighting. Appearance matching is performed post-training to align the visual appearance of adjacent Block-NeRFs by optimizing appearance codes at shared locations, ensuring seamless transitions across the scene.
d7d1bbade9453f0348fac8a5c60d131528b87fcf.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two large-scale, real-world datasets collected from San Francisco neighborhoods (Alamo Square and Mission Bay), comprising up to 2.8 million images captured over several months with 12-camera rigs on vehicles. The environment is divided into dozens of Block-NeRFs, each trained on tens of thousands of images. Baseline comparisons include standard mip-NeRF and ablations removing appearance embeddings, exposure conditioning, or pose refinement. Evaluation metrics include PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS, measured on held-out test images. Additional experiments analyze the effect of varying the number and size of Block-NeRFs, compositing strategies, and interpolation methods. The scalability, memory efficiency, and visual fidelity of the proposed method are assessed, and qualitative results are provided, including seamless rendering across block boundaries and the ability to update individual blocks without retraining the entire scene.
d7d1bbade9453f0348fac8a5c60d131528b87fcf.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a scalable neural scene representation for arbitrarily large environments by decomposing them into independently trainable Block-NeRFs, enabling efficient memory usage and flexible updates. Key innovations include the integration of appearance embeddings, pose refinement, and exposure conditioning into each Block-NeRF, as well as a novel visibility prediction network for efficient block selection and compositing. The approach supports seamless visual alignment across block boundaries through appearance matching, and demonstrates the largest neural scene reconstruction to date, rendering entire city neighborhoods from millions of images. This framework allows for piecewise updates and robust handling of real-world data variability, addressing limitations of prior NeRF-based methods in large-scale settings.

d7d66184b4b36a2a06c401ea93fae07a12de6466.title: An Equivalence Between Static and Dynamic Regret Minimization
d7d66184b4b36a2a06c401ea93fae07a12de6466.research_question: How can dynamic regret minimization in online convex optimization be unified with static regret minimization, and what are the fundamental trade-offs and algorithmic frameworks for achieving optimal dynamic regret guarantees with respect to arbitrary comparator sequences and loss variance?
d7d66184b4b36a2a06c401ea93fae07a12de6466.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that dynamic regret minimization for linear losses can be equivalently reformulated as static regret minimization in an extended decision space, and that this equivalence enables the design of algorithms that achieve optimal trade-offs between penalties due to comparator variability and loss variance. Furthermore, it is conjectured that achieving regret guarantees scaling with the squared path-length of arbitrary comparator sequences is impossible without incurring vacuous variance penalties, but alternative measures of variability can yield non-trivial decoupled guarantees.
d7d66184b4b36a2a06c401ea93fae07a12de6466.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a reduction from dynamic regret minimization to static regret minimization by embedding the sequence of comparators into a higher-dimensional space, allowing the use of established static regret algorithms. This reduction is formalized through a mapping of the original online linear optimization problem to an equivalent problem in a product space, where the dynamic regret with respect to a sequence is shown to be equal to the static regret with respect to the concatenated vector. The framework leverages dual-norm pairs (primal and dual norms defined via positive definite matrices) to measure comparator variability and loss variance, enabling the design of parameter-free algorithms that adapt to these measures. By carefully choosing the structure of the norm-inducing matrix (such as using the Haar basis for local smoothing), the method allows for efficient implementation and the achievement of novel regret guarantees that decouple variance and variability penalties.
d7d66184b4b36a2a06c401ea93fae07a12de6466.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in the online convex optimization setting, focusing on the online linear optimization (OLO) case. The evaluation will utilize synthetic and/or standard benchmark datasets for online learning, with loss functions chosen to be linear or convex as appropriate. Baseline algorithms will include standard online gradient descent, parameter-free algorithms, and recent dynamic regret minimization methods. Evaluation metrics will include dynamic regret with respect to arbitrary comparator sequences, static regret, and the dependence of regret on path-length and squared path-length measures. Key experimental setups will test the framework's ability to achieve regret guarantees along the lower bound frontier, as well as the efficiency and scalability of the proposed algorithms with respect to the number of rounds and dimensionality.
d7d66184b4b36a2a06c401ea93fae07a12de6466.novelty_claims: The proposal claims a novel equivalence between dynamic and static regret minimization for linear losses, enabling the transfer of static regret techniques to the dynamic setting. It establishes a new frontier of lower bounds that precisely characterize the trade-off between comparator variability and loss variance penalties. The framework provides the first general method for achieving any guarantee along this frontier, including the first fully decoupled dynamic regret guarantees for general online convex optimization that avoid pessimistic multiplicative penalties. Additionally, it demonstrates the impossibility of achieving squared path-length guarantees without vacuous variance penalties and introduces an alternative, locally smoothed variability measure that retains worst-case optimality up to polylogarithmic factors while allowing efficient algorithmic implementation.

d7f5ad853a52d9960b967130311d7a3b4a31117f.title: Towards Physics-informed Spatial Intelligence with Human Priors: An Autonomous Driving Pilot Study
d7f5ad853a52d9960b967130311d7a3b4a31117f.research_question: How can spatial intelligence in foundation models, particularly in autonomous driving scenarios, be more accurately represented, evaluated, and enhanced by integrating structured, physically grounded, and human-inspired priors beyond traditional textual and VQA-based approaches?
d7f5ad853a52d9960b967130311d7a3b4a31117f.hypothesis: Incorporating a grid-based, physically grounded spatial representation with human-like attention priors into multimodal large language models will yield more accurate, robust, and human-aligned visual-spatial intelligence than conventional VQA-style textual representations.
d7f5ad853a52d9960b967130311d7a3b4a31117f.proposed_method: A novel grid-based spatial representation, termed Spatial Intelligence Grid (SIG), will be developed to explicitly encode object layouts, inter-object relations, and physically grounded priors in autonomous driving scenes. SIG will serve as a complementary channel to text, providing a compositional and structured scene representation for foundation model reasoning. Three new evaluation metrics will be introduced: Multi-Level Spatial Matching (MLSM) for object localization, Spatial Relation Graph Similarity (SRGS) for graph-based relational accuracy, and Semantic Relational Distance (SRD) for textual relational fidelity. Human-like attention will be integrated by mapping gaze data onto the grid, weighting spatial relations according to perceptual importance. The method will also explore SIG-based few-shot in-context learning to enhance spatial reasoning in state-of-the-art multimodal LLMs.
d7f5ad853a52d9960b967130311d7a3b4a31117f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on SIGBench, a new benchmark containing 1,423 annotated autonomous driving frames with ground-truth SIG labels and human gaze traces. Multiple top-tier multimodal LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, InternVL, Qwen-VL) will be evaluated using the proposed grid-based and human-like metrics. Baselines will include traditional VQA-style in-context learning and zero-shot inference. Evaluation metrics will cover MLSM, SRGS, SRD (both directional and proximal), as well as attention-weighted human-like variants, and standard gaze prediction metrics (PCC, KL-Divergence, IG). Additional cross-domain generalization will be tested on SIG-COCO and SIG-ARKitScenes benchmarks. Ablation studies will assess the impact of SIG-based versus VQA-based representations and the stability of improvements across random sample selections.
d7f5ad853a52d9960b967130311d7a3b4a31117f.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces SIG, a structured, grid-based spatial intelligence representation that integrates physical and human attention priors, enabling more faithful and compositional scene encoding for foundation models. New graph-based and semantic evaluation metrics are established to disentangle spatial reasoning from language priors. SIGBench is released as the first benchmark to provide both grid-based and human-like spatial intelligence annotations in autonomous driving. The approach demonstrates that SIG-based in-context learning yields more comprehensive, stable, and general improvements in spatial intelligence than VQA-only methods, and that the schema generalizes across domains.

d7fed7523ec2eb5aaeda51e5608b21e8ffc31549.title: Approximately Aligned Decoding
d7fed7523ec2eb5aaeda51e5608b21e8ffc31549.research_question: How can text be generated from large language models under complex, difficult-to-satisfy constraints, such that constraint violations are avoided, computational efficiency is maintained, and distortion of the output probability distribution is minimized?
d7fed7523ec2eb5aaeda51e5608b21e8ffc31549.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a decoding algorithm inspired by speculative sampling, which adaptively reuses portions of previously generated sequences after constraint violations, can achieve a favorable balance between computational efficiency and fidelity to the original output distribution, outperforming both strictly constrained generation and rejection-based sampling methods.
d7fed7523ec2eb5aaeda51e5608b21e8ffc31549.proposed_method: A new decoding algorithm, Approximately Aligned Decoding (AprAD), will be developed to generate sequences from autoregressive language models while enforcing arbitrary black-box constraints. The method will maintain a running set of observed error sequences and, upon encountering a constraint violation, will use a speculative sampling-inspired prefix selection procedure to determine how much of the generated sequence can be reused. Specifically, after a violation, the method will compare the probability distributions before and after the error and probabilistically backtrack to a prefix, then resume generation from there, updating the constraint set as needed. This approach avoids the extremes of either always discarding or always retaining generated tokens after a violation, and adaptively balances efficiency with output distribution fidelity. The algorithm requires no additional model training or fine-tuning and is compatible with arbitrary error detectors, including those implemented as black-box functions.
d7fed7523ec2eb5aaeda51e5608b21e8ffc31549.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world tasks. Synthetic evaluations will use simulated language models with known output distributions and controlled error sets, measuring KL-divergence from the ideal distribution and the number of model invocations per output (generation ratio). Real-world evaluations will include a lipogram task (generating text without a specified vowel) using Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, with human raters scoring output quality and adherence to constraints, and a code generation task on BigCodeBench v0.1 using Starcoder2 models, where hallucinated API calls are detected with Pyright. Baselines will include constrained generation, rejection/ASAp sampling, and unconstrained generation. Metrics will include KL-divergence, generation ratio, human-rated quality and constraint intent, pass@1 and pass@5 for code, and hallucination avoidance rates.
d7fed7523ec2eb5aaeda51e5608b21e8ffc31549.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel application of speculative sampling principles to constraint-aware text generation, enabling adaptive reuse of partial generations after constraint violations. This approach achieves a bounded probability amplification per backtrack, significantly reducing distortion compared to existing constrained decoding methods, while incurring much lower computational overhead than rejection-based or sampling-without-replacement approaches. The method is general, requires no model retraining, and is compatible with arbitrary black-box constraints, making it suitable for a wide range of domains including natural language and code generation under complex constraints.

d809103bcd81641fd1d6ecda72fe6518f042a771.title: Weak Proxies are Sufficient and Preferable for Fairness with Missing Sensitive Attributes
d809103bcd81641fd1d6ecda72fe6518f042a771.research_question: How can fairness in machine learning models be accurately measured and mitigated when sensitive attributes are missing due to privacy constraints, and is it possible to achieve this using only weak (inaccurate) proxy models to further protect privacy?
d809103bcd81641fd1d6ecda72fe6518f042a771.hypothesis: It is possible to accurately estimate and mitigate group fairness metrics in the absence of true sensitive attributes by using a set of weak proxy models, provided that these proxies satisfy certain informativeness and independence conditions. Furthermore, using weak proxies can offer additional privacy protection without sacrificing the accuracy of fairness measurement when properly calibrated.
d809103bcd81641fd1d6ecda72fe6518f042a771.proposed_method: A novel algorithm is proposed to calibrate fairness metrics using only weak proxy models for sensitive attribute inference. The method requires at least three proxy models whose predictions are conditionally independent and informative (i.e., better than random guessing). The approach involves first estimating noisy fairness metrics using the proxy predictions, then calibrating these estimates by solving for the true fairness metrics using estimated transition matrices and prior probabilities derived from the joint distribution of proxy predictions. The calibration step leverages closed-form relationships between noisy and true fairness metrics, and employs a statistical estimator (such as HOC) to estimate the necessary transition matrices and priors from the data. This framework is flexible and can incorporate any suitable estimator from the noisy label literature, ensuring unbiased fairness estimates under the stated conditions.
d809103bcd81641fd1d6ecda72fe6518f042a771.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on real-world datasets such as COMPAS (recidivism prediction, with race as the sensitive attribute) and CelebA (facial attribute prediction, with gender as the sensitive attribute). Multiple target models (e.g., decision tree, random forest, boosting, SVM, logistic regression, neural networks) will be trained without access to sensitive attributes. Proxy models for sensitive attribute inference will be sourced from open repositories or simulated with varying levels of noise to represent weak proxies. Baseline methods will include direct use of proxy predictions and other calibration techniques. Evaluation metrics will focus on group fairness measures such as demographic parity (DP), equalized odds (EOd), and equalized opportunity (EOp), comparing estimated fairness metrics to ground-truth values where available. The impact of proxy accuracy, number of proxies, and added noise on estimation error and privacy will be systematically assessed.
d809103bcd81641fd1d6ecda72fe6518f042a771.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to theoretically and empirically demonstrate that accurate fairness estimation is possible using only weak, privacy-preserving proxies, provided at least three independent and informative proxies are available. The method provides provable error bounds and guarantees unbiased fairness estimates under mild conditions, even when proxies are intentionally weakened to protect privacy. The framework offers practical guidelines for practitioners on proxy selection and calibration, and establishes that weak proxies are not only sufficient but preferable for fairness evaluation in privacy-constrained settings.

d810d57e360769545f2c09b8abe49551f3c4e813.title: Forster Decomposition and Learning Halfspaces with Noise
d810d57e360769545f2c09b8abe49551f3c4e813.research_question: Can a computationally efficient, distribution-independent PAC learning algorithm for halfspaces under the Massart noise model be developed that achieves strongly polynomial sample complexity, i.e., sample complexity independent of the bit complexity of the examples?
d810d57e360769545f2c09b8abe49551f3c4e813.hypothesis: It is possible to design an efficient learning algorithm for halfspaces under the Massart noise model that achieves optimal error guarantees with sample complexity that depends only polynomially on the dimension and accuracy parameters, and is independent of the bit complexity of the examples.
d810d57e360769545f2c09b8abe49551f3c4e813.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a novel preprocessing routine based on a generalized Forster transform and decomposition. The approach efficiently decomposes any input distribution into a disjoint mixture of a small number of distributions, each admitting a Forster transform that can be efficiently computed. For each subset, a combination of linear transformations and pointwise rescaling is applied to achieve approximate radial isotropic position, ensuring strong anti-concentration properties necessary for efficient learning. The algorithm iteratively identifies heavy subspaces and applies semidefinite programming to compute appropriate scaling functions, guaranteeing that the transformed data supports efficient PAC learning of halfspaces. This decomposition and transformation process is performed in polynomial time and ensures that the anti-concentration bounds—and thus the sample complexity—depend only on the dimension and accuracy, not on the bit complexity.
d810d57e360769545f2c09b8abe49551f3c4e813.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and real-world datasets where the marginal distribution over examples is arbitrary and labels are corrupted with Massart noise. The proposed algorithm will be evaluated against prior state-of-the-art methods, particularly those with sample complexity dependent on bit complexity, such as the approach of DGT19. Evaluation metrics will include misclassification error (targeting η+ε), sample complexity, and computational runtime. The experimental setup will involve varying the dimension, noise rate, and accuracy parameter to empirically validate the independence of sample complexity from bit complexity and to demonstrate the efficiency and robustness of the proposed method.
d810d57e360769545f2c09b8abe49551f3c4e813.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first polynomial-time algorithm for distribution-independent PAC learning of halfspaces in the Massart noise model with sample complexity that is strongly polynomial—completely independent of the bit complexity of the examples. The key innovation lies in the efficient algorithmic Forster decomposition, which enables the transformation of arbitrary distributions into mixtures admitting efficient Forster transforms. This approach overcomes fundamental limitations of previous methods, which required sample complexity scaling with bit complexity, and provides a new theoretical and algorithmic framework for robust learning under bounded noise.

d83a51ae59a7c47922cfa12c56e2a8c5a5f11172.title: A Holistic Approach to Unifying Automatic Concept Extraction and Concept Importance Estimation
d83a51ae59a7c47922cfa12c56e2a8c5a5f11172.research_question: How can automatic concept extraction and concept importance estimation for neural network interpretability be unified under a single theoretical and practical framework, and how can this framework improve the evaluation, faithfulness, and visualization of concept-based explanations for deep learning models?
d83a51ae59a7c47922cfa12c56e2a8c5a5f11172.hypothesis: A unified framework that formulates concept extraction as a dictionary learning problem and concept importance estimation as a generalization of attribution methods will provide more interpretable, faithful, and theoretically grounded explanations for neural network decisions, and will enable the development of improved evaluation metrics and visualization tools for both global and local model strategies.
d83a51ae59a7c47922cfa12c56e2a8c5a5f11172.proposed_method: The proposed method will formalize concept extraction as a dictionary learning problem, where activations from an intermediate (typically penultimate) layer of a neural network are approximated by a linear combination of learned concept vectors (Concept Activation Vectors, or CAVs) using methods such as Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF), PCA, or K-Means. Concept importance estimation will be recast as a generalization of attribution methods, whereby the sensitivity of the model's output to perturbations in the concept space is measured using techniques like Integrated Gradients, Gradient Input, RISE, and Occlusion. The framework will introduce new evaluation metrics for concept extraction (e.g., reconstruction error, sparsity, stability, Fréchet Inception Distance, OOD score) and for concept importance (C-Deletion, C-Insertion, C-µFidelity), and will provide theoretical guarantees for the optimality of certain attribution-based importance methods when applied to the penultimate layer. Additionally, the method will enable local (sample-specific) concept importance estimation and introduce the 'strategic cluster graph' visualization to reveal and analyze the main classification strategies of a model at both the class and instance level.
d83a51ae59a7c47922cfa12c56e2a8c5a5f11172.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using state-of-the-art neural network architectures such as EfficientNetV2, ResNet50, and MobileNetV2, trained on the ImageNet dataset. Concept extraction methods (NMF, PCA, K-Means) will be applied to the penultimate layer activations, and their performance will be evaluated using metrics including relative l2 reconstruction error, sparsity, stability across data subsets, Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), and out-of-distribution (OOD) scores (using Deep-KNN). For concept importance, several attribution-based methods will be compared using C-Deletion, C-Insertion, and C-µFidelity metrics, with a focus on the penultimate layer for theoretical optimality. Visualization tools such as UMAP and the strategic cluster graph will be used to analyze and display the clustering of samples by classification strategy. The approach will be validated on a subset of 10 ImageNet classes (including those from Imagenette), with each class evaluated using 16,000 images.
d83a51ae59a7c47922cfa12c56e2a8c5a5f11172.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unifying theoretical framework that recasts concept extraction as dictionary learning and concept importance as a generalization of attribution methods, enabling systematic evaluation and theoretical analysis of concept-based explainability techniques. New evaluation metrics for both concept extraction and importance estimation are proposed, including the adaptation of faithfulness metrics from attribution literature. The method provides theoretical guarantees for the optimality of certain attribution-based importance estimators in the penultimate layer. Furthermore, the proposal introduces the strategic cluster graph, a novel visualization tool for revealing and interpreting the main strategies used by models at both the class and instance level, and demonstrates how local concept importance can be leveraged for deeper insights into model behavior and failure cases.

d84cf745c534c010b8e55e5a4a04878906848dc3.title: TEST: Text Prototype Aligned Embedding to Activate LLM's Ability for Time Series
d84cf745c534c010b8e55e5a4a04878906848dc3.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs) be enabled to effectively perform time series (TS) tasks such as classification, forecasting, and representation learning without compromising their original language capabilities, by developing a data-centric approach that aligns TS data with LLMs' embedding space?
d84cf745c534c010b8e55e5a4a04878906848dc3.hypothesis: Aligning time series embeddings with the embedding space of pre-trained LLMs, combined with prompt-based conditioning, will activate LLMs' ability to process and perform competitively on TS tasks, achieving results comparable to or better than state-of-the-art TS models while maintaining language abilities.
d84cf745c534c010b8e55e5a4a04878906848dc3.proposed_method: A novel framework, TEST (TimE Series tokens to align Text embedding space), will be developed to enable LLMs to process time series data. The method begins by tokenizing multivariate TS into segments using a sliding window, then encodes these segments into vector representations via a neural encoder based on a causal temporal convolutional network (TCN). The encoder is trained with a combination of instance-wise and feature-wise contrastive learning, ensuring that augmented views of the same TS instance are close in the embedding space while negatives are far apart, and that feature columns (dimensions) are discriminative. Critically, a text-prototype-aligned contrast is introduced, where selected text token embeddings from the LLM serve as prototypes, and TS embeddings are aligned to these prototypes, mapping TS patterns into the LLM's embedding space. Finally, learnable soft prompts are trained to condition the frozen LLM to accept TS embeddings as input, enabling downstream TS tasks (classification, forecasting, representation) to be performed by the LLM without modifying its core parameters.
d84cf745c534c010b8e55e5a4a04878906848dc3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of TS tasks, including classification (using the UCR and UEA archives for univariate and multivariate TS), forecasting (short- and long-term, using TSER and real-world datasets such as weather, traffic, electricity, and ILI), and representation learning (evaluated with SVM classifiers on UCR). The approach will be evaluated on eight frozen LLMs of various architectures and sizes (e.g., BERT, GPT-2, ChatGLM, LLaMa2), with the encoder and soft prompts trained using Adam optimizer on high-performance GPUs. Baselines will include LLM-QA methods (prompt-based QA), supervised fine-tuned LLMs (SFT), classical TS models (e.g., DWT, 1NNED, TCN), state-of-the-art TS models (Informer, DLinear, TimesNet), and contrastive learning-based TS models (Tloss, TS2Vec, CoST). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for classification, mean squared error (MSE) for forecasting, and representation quality via downstream classifiers. Ablation studies will examine the impact of text prototype selection, prompt types, and model size.
d84cf745c534c010b8e55e5a4a04878906848dc3.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new paradigm for TS-for-LLM by aligning TS embeddings with the LLM's text embedding space using contrastive learning with text prototypes, rather than modifying or fine-tuning the LLM itself. This approach enables frozen LLMs to perform TS tasks without sacrificing their language abilities and leverages prompt-based conditioning to bridge the modality gap. The method demonstrates that LLMs can act as pattern machines for TS data, achieving competitive or superior performance to specialized TS models, and provides a foundation for future research in integrating objective TS data with subjective text representations at the machine level.

d867ec4422effcaf362df42fd025d3b5f4eadc49.title: Mix-LN: Unleashing the Power of Deeper Layers by Combining Pre-LN and Post-LN
d867ec4422effcaf362df42fd025d3b5f4eadc49.research_question: How can the effectiveness of both shallow and deep layers in large neural network architectures, particularly large language models (LLMs), be improved by addressing issues in gradient flow and representation diversity associated with current normalization strategies?
d867ec4422effcaf362df42fd025d3b5f4eadc49.hypothesis: The inefficiency of deeper layers in LLMs primarily stems from the choice of layer normalization; specifically, Pre-Layer Normalization (Pre-LN) leads to diminished gradients in deeper layers, reducing their effectiveness, while Post-Layer Normalization (Post-LN) causes vanishing gradients in early layers.
d867ec4422effcaf362df42fd025d3b5f4eadc49.proposed_method: A novel normalization technique, Mix-LN, will be developed to combine the strengths of Pre-LN and Post-LN within the same model. The approach applies Post-LN to the initial portion of the network's layers and Pre-LN to the remaining deeper layers, with the transition point controlled by a tunable hyperparameter α. This hybrid strategy is designed to ensure more uniform and healthier gradient norms across all layers, promoting effective training throughout the network. The method will be formally defined for a model with L layers, applying Post-LN to the first ⌊αL⌋ layers and Pre-LN to the remaining ⌈(1−α)L⌉ layers, with α empirically tuned for optimal performance. The implementation will maintain all other architectural and training configurations constant to isolate the effect of normalization.
d867ec4422effcaf362df42fd025d3b5f4eadc49.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both open-weight large-scale LLMs (e.g., LLaMA2-7B and BERT-large) and in-house trained small-scale LLMs (e.g., LLaMA-130M, LLaMA-250M, LLaMA-1B, and LLaMA-7B) using the C4 dataset for pre-training. Baselines will include Pre-LN, Post-LN, DeepNorm, Admin, Sandwich-LN, and Group-LN. Evaluation metrics will consist of pre-training perplexity, angular distance between layer representations, performance drop upon layer pruning, and gradient norm analysis. Downstream supervised fine-tuning will be performed on Commonsense170K and evaluated on tasks such as MMLU, BoolQ, ARC-e, PIQA, Hellaswag, OBQA, and Winogrande. Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) will be evaluated using the ultrafeedback dataset and preference reward. Additional experiments will test generalization to Vision Transformers (ViT) on ImageNet-1K. Hyperparameter sweeps for α will be conducted to optimize the transition ratio between normalization strategies.
d867ec4422effcaf362df42fd025d3b5f4eadc49.novelty_claims: The proposed Mix-LN method introduces a hybrid normalization strategy that leverages the complementary strengths of Pre-LN and Post-LN, resulting in more balanced gradient flow and representation diversity across all layers. This approach is claimed to unlock the potential of deep layers in LLMs, leading to improved pre-training and fine-tuning performance without increasing model size. Mix-LN is shown to outperform existing normalization techniques in both language and vision models, and its effectiveness is validated across a range of model sizes and tasks. The method also addresses training instabilities associated with pure Post-LN, providing a practical and scalable solution for enhancing deep neural architectures.

d87ecdcb490241ec204bd94b89158e06dd0747e2.title: Towards Understanding the Mechanism of Contrastive Learning via Similarity Structure: A Theoretical Analysis
d87ecdcb490241ec204bd94b89158e06dd0747e2.research_question: How can the similarity structure of representations learned by contrastive learning be theoretically characterized, and what are the implications for generalization and clustering in self-supervised representation learning frameworks?
