d87ecdcb490241ec204bd94b89158e06dd0747e2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a kernel-based contrastive learning framework, utilizing a statistical similarity formulation, can provide a unified theoretical characterization of the clustering and generalization properties of learned representations, and that this framework will yield meaningful upper bounds for downstream classification error under realistic assumptions.
d87ecdcb490241ec204bd94b89158e06dd0747e2.proposed_method: A kernel-based contrastive learning (KCL) framework will be developed, where the similarity between feature representations is measured using a reproducing kernel function. The kernel contrastive loss will be defined as the difference between expected kernel similarities of positive (similar) and negative (dissimilar) data pairs, weighted by a hyperparameter. A novel statistical similarity function based on the density ratio of joint and marginal distributions of augmented data will be introduced to formalize the notion of similarity between data points. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish how this similarity structure determines the clustering of representations in the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), and to derive upper bounds on downstream classification error and generalization error for the KCL framework. The approach will be general enough to encompass and relate to other contrastive objectives, such as InfoNCE and spectral contrastive losses, through appropriate kernel choices.
d87ecdcb490241ec204bd94b89158e06dd0747e2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the KCL framework with various kernel functions, such as Gaussian and quadratic kernels, to empirically validate the theoretical findings. Standard self-supervised learning benchmarks, including image datasets like CIFAR-10 or ImageNet, will be used for pretraining and downstream classification tasks. Baselines will include established contrastive learning methods such as SimCLR, InfoNCE, and spectral contrastive learning. Evaluation metrics will focus on downstream classification accuracy, clustering quality, and generalization error. Experimental setups will include varying the kernel function, the weight hyperparameter, and the strength of data augmentation to assess the robustness and applicability of the theoretical results.
d87ecdcb490241ec204bd94b89158e06dd0747e2.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified theoretical framework for contrastive learning based on kernel methods and a novel statistical similarity formulation, enabling the analysis of clustering and generalization properties across a broad class of contrastive objectives. The approach provides new theoretical guarantees, including upper bounds on downstream classification error and generalization error, under more realistic assumptions on encoder functions than prior work. The formulation offers deeper insights into the mechanism of contrastive learning and bridges connections between kernel theory and self-supervised representation learning.

d8885a0ae16468e1526461c621fe62cf444b9d4b.title: Towards Faster Non-Asymptotic Convergence for Diffusion-Based Generative Models
d8885a0ae16468e1526461c621fe62cf444b9d4b.research_question: How can the non-asymptotic convergence rates of diffusion-based generative models, particularly in discrete time, be improved under minimal assumptions on the target data distribution, and how do score estimation errors affect the quality of data generation?
d8885a0ae16468e1526461c621fe62cf444b9d4b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by developing new non-asymptotic analysis frameworks and accelerated variants for both deterministic and stochastic diffusion-based generative samplers, faster convergence rates can be achieved without requiring strong smoothness assumptions on the target data distribution, and that the impact of score estimation errors on the generative process can be explicitly characterized.
d8885a0ae16468e1526461c621fe62cf444b9d4b.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a non-asymptotic theoretical framework for analyzing the convergence of discrete-time diffusion-based generative models, focusing on both deterministic samplers (based on probability flow ODEs) and stochastic samplers (of the DDPM type). The methodology assumes access to ℓ2-accurate estimates of the (Stein) score functions and, for deterministic samplers, also considers the estimation error of the Jacobian of the score functions. The analysis directly tackles the discrete-time processes using elementary probabilistic and analytical tools, avoiding reliance on continuous-time SDE or ODE theory. Additionally, two accelerated variants are designed: one for the deterministic sampler, leveraging higher-order expansions and additional estimated quantities, and one for the stochastic sampler, both aiming to further improve the convergence rates.
d8885a0ae16468e1526461c621fe62cf444b9d4b.experiment_details: The proposed theoretical results will be validated through a suite of experiments involving both deterministic and stochastic diffusion samplers. Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and standard generative modeling datasets, using established benchmarks for diffusion models. Baseline methods will include standard DDPM and DDIM samplers, as well as recent theoretical and empirical state-of-the-art approaches. Evaluation metrics will focus on total variation distance, iteration complexity (number of steps to achieve ε-accuracy), and sensitivity to score estimation errors. The experimental setup will systematically vary the number of steps, the accuracy of score estimates, and the learning rate schedules to assess the practical impact of the proposed accelerated variants and theoretical guarantees.
d8885a0ae16468e1526461c621fe62cf444b9d4b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a fully non-asymptotic analysis framework for discrete-time diffusion-based generative models that does not require smoothness assumptions on the target data distribution and avoids the use of SDE/ODE toolboxes. It provides the first explicit convergence rates for deterministic samplers that account for both ℓ2 score estimation errors and Jacobian errors in discrete time. The approach also develops accelerated variants for both deterministic and stochastic samplers, achieving improved convergence rates (1/T^2 for deterministic ODE-based and 1/T for DDPM-type samplers). The framework is elementary and versatile, lowering the technical barrier for theoretical analysis of diffusion models and potentially applicable to a broader class of generative modeling algorithms.

d8aedce56a586983fd7f708a51f5a2f36c3b1b16.title: Geometry-aware training of factorized layers in tensor Tucker format
d8aedce56a586983fd7f708a51f5a2f36c3b1b16.research_question: How can neural network layers be trained in a factorized tensor format to achieve significant reductions in computational and memory requirements during both training and inference, while maintaining or improving model performance and robustness?
d8aedce56a586983fd7f708a51f5a2f36c3b1b16.hypothesis: A geometry-aware, rank-adaptive training algorithm for neural network layers in Tucker tensor format will enable efficient and robust training, dynamically adjusting ranks to optimize compression and performance, and will outperform or match existing factorization and pruning strategies in terms of accuracy, compression rate, and robustness to initialization.
d8aedce56a586983fd7f708a51f5a2f36c3b1b16.proposed_method: A geometry-aware, rank-adaptive training algorithm is developed for neural network layers represented in Tucker tensor format. The method leverages the Riemannian manifold structure of the set of tensors with fixed Tucker rank, projecting the gradient flow onto the tangent space to avoid issues of ill-conditioning and slow convergence. The algorithm dynamically updates the Tucker ranks during training using a singular value threshold, performing basis augmentation and orthonormalization steps, and applies a high-order SVD (HOSVD) for rank truncation. The approach requires only two gradient evaluations per training step, significantly reducing computational overhead compared to naive implementations. Theoretical guarantees are provided for loss descent, convergence to stationary points, and approximation to the full model, ensuring robust and efficient training on the low-rank manifold.
d8aedce56a586983fd7f708a51f5a2f36c3b1b16.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on convolutional neural networks (AlexNet, VGG16, ResNet18, LeNet5) using CIFAR10, Tiny-ImageNet, MNIST, and further fine-tuning on Deberta V3 (GLUE benchmark) and Stable Diffusion (Dreambooth). The method is compared against baselines including direct low-rank matrix and tensor factorization (CP, Tucker, Tensor-Train), Riemannian gradient descent, and pruning methods (IMP, SNIP, GraSP). Evaluation metrics include test accuracy, compression rate (percentage of parameter reduction), convergence speed, and robustness to initialization. All methods are trained with SGD under identical hyperparameters, and compression is measured both during and after training. Computational performance is assessed via inference time and wall time to reach a target accuracy at a fixed compression rate.
d8aedce56a586983fd7f708a51f5a2f36c3b1b16.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a geometry-aware, rank-adaptive training algorithm for Tucker tensor layers, overcoming the need for a priori rank selection and sensitivity to initialization. The approach exploits the Riemannian structure of the Tucker manifold for robust and efficient optimization, dynamically adjusting ranks during training. Theoretical guarantees are established for loss descent, convergence, and approximation to the full model. Experimental results demonstrate superior or comparable accuracy and compression rates relative to state-of-the-art factorization and pruning methods, with improved robustness and reduced variance across initializations. The method also generalizes to fine-tuning scenarios with low-rank adapters, offering parameter efficiency and flexibility.

d8bae6bde1ca8d039acec0ca9fd42e228e870341.title: OSCAR: Operating System Control via State-Aware Reasoning and Re-Planning
d8bae6bde1ca8d039acec0ca9fd42e228e870341.research_question: Can a generalist intelligent agent be developed to autonomously control and interact with diverse desktop and mobile operating system environments, executing complex user instructions across applications using standardized OS controls while adapting to real-time feedback and dynamic GUI states?
d8bae6bde1ca8d039acec0ca9fd42e228e870341.hypothesis: A state-aware, code-centric agent equipped with dual GUI grounding and task-driven re-planning will demonstrate superior adaptability, efficiency, and success rates in automating complex workflows across dynamic desktop and mobile OS environments compared to existing agents.
d8bae6bde1ca8d039acec0ca9fd42e228e870341.proposed_method: A novel agent architecture will be designed based on a state machine framework, enabling systematic transitions between states such as observation, planning, execution, verification, and error handling. The agent will process user instructions and capture real-time screenshots of the OS environment, enhancing GUI understanding through a dual-grounding approach: visual grounding via Set-of-Mark (SoM) prompting using the Accessibility (A11Y) tree for precise UI element localization, and semantic grounding by labeling key UI components. Task-driven re-planning will be implemented, allowing the agent to decompose user instructions into hierarchical sub-tasks and generate executable Python code for precise mouse and keyboard control via libraries such as PyAutoGUI. The agent will continuously monitor execution and verification feedback, enabling fine-grained re-planning of specific tasks rather than the entire workflow, thus improving efficiency and robustness in dynamic environments.
d8bae6bde1ca8d039acec0ca9fd42e228e870341.experiment_details: The agent will be evaluated on real-world workflow automation benchmarks, including GAIA (466 tasks across three complexity levels), OSWorld (369 dynamic desktop OS tasks spanning settings, office, daily, professional, and multi-application scenarios), and AndroidWorld (116 smartphone OS tasks across 20 applications and three difficulty levels). Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art generalist agents such as Cradle, UFO, FRIDAY, MMAC, M3A, AppAgent, and MobileAgent, all using the same base LLM (e.g., GPT-4-turbo) and SoM visual prompts for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include exact match success rate, process score (action matching proxy), and completion rate, with additional ablation studies to isolate the impact of GUI-grounded observation and planning strategies. Experiments will analyze both quantitative performance and qualitative task execution, including efficiency of re-planning and error recovery.
d8bae6bde1ca8d039acec0ca9fd42e228e870341.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a generalist agent capable of robust, adaptive OS control across both desktop and mobile platforms using a unified code-centric framework. Key innovations include the integration of dual GUI grounding (visual and semantic) for enhanced interface understanding, a modular state machine enabling continuous feedback and dynamic error recovery, and a task-driven re-planning mechanism that allows for fine-grained adjustment of sub-tasks based on real-time OS feedback. This methodology enables efficient, flexible workflow automation, achieving state-of-the-art success rates on diverse, dynamic benchmarks and outperforming prior agents, especially on complex, multi-step tasks.

d8c37474aa0c755d925eec9c9f9856fa48a3e580.title: Who Reasons in the Large Language Models?
d8c37474aa0c755d925eec9c9f9856fa48a3e580.research_question: What are the specific internal components or modules within large language models (LLMs) that are responsible for enabling advanced reasoning abilities, and how can these components be systematically identified and leveraged for more efficient model training and specialization?
d8c37474aa0c755d925eec9c9f9856fa48a3e580.hypothesis: The output projection (o_proj) module in the Transformer’s multi-head self-attention (MHSA) mechanism is the primary or most critical component responsible for reasoning abilities in well-trained LLMs, while other modules contribute more to conversational fluency.
d8c37474aa0c755d925eec9c9f9856fa48a3e580.proposed_method: A diagnostic framework, Stethoscope for Networks (SfN), will be developed to systematically probe and analyze the internal behaviors of LLMs. SfN will include several probing techniques: (1) Delta Stethoscope, which quantifies weight differences between base and reasoning-enhanced models to localize functional changes; (2) Merge Stethoscope, which creates hybrid models by swapping specific modules (e.g., o_proj) between base and reasoning models to assess their impact on reasoning; (3) Freeze Stethoscope, which fine-tunes only selected modules (such as o_proj and normalization layers) while freezing others to evaluate their sufficiency for reasoning; and (4) Destruction Stethoscope, which disables or reinitializes individual modules to observe the resulting degradation in reasoning and conversational abilities. These techniques will be applied across multiple model sizes and architectures, with both quantitative and qualitative analyses of output behaviors.
d8c37474aa0c755d925eec9c9f9856fa48a3e580.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize open-source LLMs such as Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B, 7B, 14B, 32B, and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen variants as base and reasoning models. The evaluation will be performed on mathematical reasoning benchmarks including AIME 2024, Math500, and GPQA Diamond, using metrics such as accuracy and output quality levels (from nonsensical to correct logical reasoning). Baseline comparisons will include models with full fine-tuning, as well as those with only selected modules tuned or merged. Training and inference will be conducted on high-performance GPUs, with careful control of hyperparameters and evaluation protocols. Both quantitative metrics (e.g., accuracy, training speed, parameter count) and qualitative output analyses (e.g., response levels, reasoning trace correctness) will be reported.
d8c37474aa0c755d925eec9c9f9856fa48a3e580.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a comprehensive and modular diagnostic toolkit (SfN) for probing the origins of reasoning in LLMs, offering interpretable and empirical evidence for the localization of reasoning ability. The methodology enables identification of the o_proj module as the key driver for reasoning, suggesting efficient fine-tuning strategies that significantly reduce training cost and memory requirements. The framework also provides a foundation for modular LLM design, such as plugin-based reasoning or domain adaptation, and offers new directions for interpretability and targeted training in deep neural networks.

d8c78221e4366d6a72a6b3e41e35b706cc45c01d.title: Training Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning
d8c78221e4366d6a72a6b3e41e35b706cc45c01d.research_question: How can diffusion models be directly optimized for user-specified downstream objectives, such as human-perceived image quality, image compressibility, or prompt-image alignment, rather than for likelihood-based objectives?
d8c78221e4366d6a72a6b3e41e35b706cc45c01d.hypothesis: Framing the denoising process in diffusion models as a multi-step decision-making problem and applying reinforcement learning, specifically policy gradient algorithms, will enable more effective optimization of diffusion models for arbitrary downstream objectives compared to reward-weighted likelihood approaches.
d8c78221e4366d6a72a6b3e41e35b706cc45c01d.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed in which the denoising process of diffusion models is formulated as a multi-step Markov Decision Process (MDP), enabling the application of policy gradient reinforcement learning algorithms. The method, termed Denoising Diffusion Policy Optimization (DDPO), directly maximizes user-specified reward functions by treating each denoising step as an action in the MDP, with the cumulative reward based on the final generated sample. Two variants of DDPO are developed: one using the score function estimator (REINFORCE) and another using an importance sampling estimator with trust region clipping, akin to proximal policy optimization. The approach allows for the use of arbitrary black-box reward functions, including those derived from human feedback or automated vision-language models, and alternates between collecting denoising trajectories and updating model parameters via gradient descent.
d8c78221e4366d6a72a6b3e41e35b706cc45c01d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted by fine-tuning large text-to-image diffusion models, specifically Stable Diffusion v1.4, on a variety of reward functions including image compressibility (minimizing or maximizing JPEG file size), aesthetic quality (using the LAION aesthetics predictor), and prompt-image alignment (using LLaVA vision-language model and BERTScore). Datasets for compressibility and incompressibility tasks are constructed by sampling prompts from 398 ImageNet-1000 animal categories, while aesthetic quality tasks use 45 common animal prompts. For prompt-image alignment, prompts are of the form 'a(n) [animal] [activity]' with a small set of activities. Baseline comparisons include reward-weighted regression (RWR) methods with both exponentiated and sparse weighting schemes. Evaluation metrics include the specific reward function values (e.g., JPEG file size, LAION aesthetic score, BERTScore for alignment), and both qualitative and quantitative analyses are performed to assess sample quality and generalization to unseen prompts.
d8c78221e4366d6a72a6b3e41e35b706cc45c01d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new class of policy gradient algorithms for diffusion models that directly optimize arbitrary downstream objectives, moving beyond conventional likelihood-based training. The DDPO framework is the first to generalize policy gradient reinforcement learning to the multi-step denoising process in diffusion models for a wide range of reward functions, including those derived from automated vision-language models without the need for additional human annotation. The approach demonstrates superior effectiveness over reward-weighted likelihood baselines and shows generalization to unseen prompts and tasks, highlighting its flexibility and scalability for targeted generative modeling.

d8d099fb047a3a47579dadc23d346d1abb85aaec.title: Spring: A High-Resolution High-Detail Dataset and Benchmark for Scene Flow, Optical Flow and Stereo
d8d099fb047a3a47579dadc23d346d1abb85aaec.research_question: How can the development and evaluation of scene flow, optical flow, and stereo estimation methods be advanced through the creation of a large-scale, high-resolution, high-detail, computer-generated dataset and benchmark that better reflects the fine structures and complexities encountered in real-world scenarios?
d8d099fb047a3a47579dadc23d346d1abb85aaec.hypothesis: A high-resolution, high-detail, computer-generated dataset with super-resolved ground truth and a novel evaluation methodology will enable more accurate assessment and foster the development of methods that better capture fine structures and generalize across diverse scenes for scene flow, optical flow, and stereo estimation tasks.
d8d099fb047a3a47579dadc23d346d1abb85aaec.proposed_method: A new dataset will be generated using rendered scenes from the open-source Blender movie 'Spring', producing 6000 stereo image pairs (47 sequences) at HD resolution (1920×1080 px) with state-of-the-art visual effects. Ground truth for scene flow, optical flow, and stereo will be extracted in both forward and backward directions, for both left and right views, and computed at super-resolved UHD resolution (3840×2160 px) to capture fine details such as hair and grass. Additional evaluation maps (e.g., sky, unmatched, high-detail, non-rigid, and large-displacement regions) will be generated to enable focused analysis. A public benchmark website will be established for uploading, analyzing, and comparing results, with robust cheating prevention and transparent evaluation protocols.
d8d099fb047a3a47579dadc23d346d1abb85aaec.experiment_details: Experiments will involve evaluating a range of state-of-the-art methods (including 8 optical flow, 4 stereo, and 3 scene flow models) as baselines, using the new dataset. The dataset will be split into 37 training and 10 test sequences, with ground truth withheld for the test set to ensure fair benchmarking. Evaluation metrics will include 1-pixel outlier rates, endpoint error (EPE), KITTI-style errors, and additional sub-metrics for different scene regions (e.g., high-detail, unmatched, non-rigid, sky, and displacement size). Results will be compared to existing benchmarks such as KITTI 2015 and MPI Sintel, and the influence of subsampling strategies on evaluation will be systematically analyzed.
d8d099fb047a3a47579dadc23d346d1abb85aaec.novelty_claims: The proposed dataset is the first to provide high-resolution, high-detail, computer-generated data for scene flow, optical flow, and stereo estimation with super-resolved UHD ground truth, enabling pixel-level assessment of fine structures. The evaluation methodology introduces focused analysis on challenging regions (e.g., thin structures, unmatched, non-rigid, sky, and large-displacement areas) and provides comprehensive performance statistics. The benchmark is significantly larger than existing alternatives, closing the gap in available training and testing data for deep learning methods, and is the first in the deep learning era to support image-based scene flow benchmarking with hidden ground truth and robust evaluation protocols.

d8d8aef756a7bce6c44aa1e7422f67d17cdff315.title: MAC-PO: Multi-Agent Experience Replay via Collective Priority Optimization
d8d8aef756a7bce6c44aa1e7422f67d17cdff315.research_question: How can experience replay mechanisms be optimized for multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) settings, particularly under the centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE) paradigm, to improve learning efficiency and stability compared to standard uniform sampling approaches?
d8d8aef756a7bce6c44aa1e7422f67d17cdff315.hypothesis: Optimizing the prioritization of experience replay in multi-agent settings through a regret minimization framework over sampling weights will result in more effective learning, improved convergence, and superior empirical performance compared to both uniform sampling and single-agent prioritization schemes adapted to MARL.
d8d8aef756a7bce6c44aa1e7422f67d17cdff315.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that formulates the problem of prioritized experience replay in cooperative MARL as a regret minimization problem over the sampling weights of transitions. The optimization objective is defined as minimizing the policy regret, i.e., the difference between the expected discounted reward of a nominal optimal policy and that of the current policy, subject to constraints derived from the weighted Bellman equation. The regret minimization is relaxed using Jensen’s inequality and solved via the Lagrangian multiplier method, resulting in a closed-form solution for the optimal sampling weights. These weights are shown to depend on four key components: Bellman error, value enhancement, on-policiness of transitions, and a novel term reflecting joint action probabilities among agents. An approximation scheme is also developed for scalability in environments with many agents, using thresholding and scaling of weights. The resulting algorithm, MAC-PO, can be integrated into existing MARL algorithms with experience replay buffers.
d8d8aef756a7bce6c44aa1e7422f67d17cdff315.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard multi-agent benchmarks, including the Predator-Prey environment and the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge (SMAC), to evaluate the proposed method. The approach will be compared against several baselines: standard uniform experience replay, single-agent prioritized experience replay methods adapted to MARL (such as PER, DisCor, ReMERN, and PSER), and state-of-the-art MARL algorithms (including QMIX, WQMIX, QPLEX, VDAC, FOP, and DOP). Evaluation metrics will include convergence speed, final win rate (for SMAC), and average episode reward (for Predator-Prey), with additional ablation studies to assess the contribution of each component of the proposed weighting scheme. All methods will be implemented with fixed and optimized hyperparameters for fair comparison.
d8d8aef756a7bce6c44aa1e7422f67d17cdff315.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first regret-minimization-based framework for optimizing prioritized experience replay specifically tailored for cooperative MARL settings. The theoretical analysis reveals a new factor in optimal sampling weights: a term dependent on the joint action probabilities of decentralized agents, which is absent in single-agent settings. The method provides a closed-form solution for optimal sampling weights and demonstrates, both theoretically and empirically, that accounting for multi-agent interactions in experience prioritization leads to superior learning outcomes. An efficient approximation is also proposed to address scalability in large agent populations.

d8e9f8c8a37cb4cd26b92ad0d942d641cd512644.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
d8e9f8c8a37cb4cd26b92ad0d942d641cd512644.research_question: How can inference speed for large autoregressive Transformer models be significantly accelerated without altering their output distributions, retraining, or modifying model architectures?
d8e9f8c8a37cb4cd26b92ad0d942d641cd512644.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging speculative execution and a novel speculative sampling algorithm, it is possible to parallelize the generation of multiple tokens using a smaller, more efficient approximation model, and then verify these with the original large model, achieving substantial speedup in inference while maintaining identical output distributions.
d8e9f8c8a37cb4cd26b92ad0d942d641cd512644.proposed_method: A new decoding algorithm, termed speculative decoding, is proposed to accelerate inference from large autoregressive models. The method employs a smaller, efficient approximation model to generate multiple candidate tokens in parallel for each decoding step. These candidate tokens are then evaluated by the large target model in parallel, and a novel speculative sampling mechanism is used to accept or reject each candidate such that the overall output distribution remains unchanged. If a candidate is rejected, an adjusted distribution is used to resample the token, ensuring correctness. The method is designed to require no changes to model architecture, no retraining, and is compatible with standard sampling strategies (e.g., argmax, top-k, nucleus sampling) by standardizing probability distributions.
d8e9f8c8a37cb4cd26b92ad0d942d641cd512644.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large-scale Transformer models such as T5-XXL (11B parameters) and LaMDA (137B parameters) on tasks including English-to-German translation (WMT EnDe), news summarization (CNN/DM), and dialog generation. Several approximation models of varying sizes (e.g., T5-small, T5-base, T5-large) will be tested to assess the trade-off between speedup and computational overhead. Baseline comparisons will be made against standard autoregressive decoding implementations (e.g., T5X). Evaluation metrics will include walltime speedup, acceptance rate (alpha), and the number of arithmetic operations, with empirical measurements of output equivalence to ensure output distributions are preserved. Experiments will be run on single TPU-v4 devices with batch size 1, and both argmax (temperature=0) and standard sampling (temperature=1) settings will be explored.
d8e9f8c8a37cb4cd26b92ad0d942d641cd512644.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a generalization of speculative execution to the stochastic setting, enabling exact and parallelized decoding for large autoregressive models without altering model outputs or requiring retraining. The method is compatible with off-the-shelf models and standard sampling techniques, and it guarantees identical output distributions. Substantial empirical speedups (2X-3X) are demonstrated on production-scale models, and the approach is shown to be easy to deploy in real-world settings where memory bandwidth is a bottleneck and additional compute resources are available.

d9052dd87959e6076baf35e8f7ee87d568a32b58.title: VisRAG: Vision-based Retrieval-augmented Generation on Multi-modality Documents
d9052dd87959e6076baf35e8f7ee87d568a32b58.research_question: How can retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines be improved to effectively utilize the full range of information present in real-world multi-modality documents, including both textual and visual content, without incurring information loss from document parsing?
d9052dd87959e6076baf35e8f7ee87d568a32b58.hypothesis: A vision-language model (VLM)-based retrieval-augmented generation pipeline that directly processes document images will outperform traditional text-based RAG systems in both retrieval and generation tasks on multi-modality documents, by preserving and leveraging all available information.
d9052dd87959e6076baf35e8f7ee87d568a32b58.proposed_method: A novel RAG pipeline, termed VisRAG, will be developed to operate directly on document images using vision-language models (VLMs) for both retrieval and generation. The retrieval component (VisRAG-Ret) will adopt a dual-encoder architecture, encoding queries as text and documents as images, and mapping them into a shared embedding space using weighted mean pooling over the VLM's final hidden states. Retrieval will be optimized with an InfoNCE loss based on cosine similarity between query and document embeddings. For generation (VisRAG-Gen), the system will employ mechanisms to handle multiple retrieved images, including page concatenation (combining multiple images into one for single-image VLMs), weighted selection (generating answers per page and selecting based on confidence), and direct multi-image input for VLMs capable of cross-image reasoning. The pipeline will be trained and evaluated on a blend of open-source visual question answering datasets and synthetically generated query-document pairs, ensuring robust multi-modal document understanding.
d9052dd87959e6076baf35e8f7ee87d568a32b58.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a variety of datasets, including MP-DocVQA, ArXivQA, ChartQA, InfographicsVQA, PlotQA, SlideVQA, and a large synthetic set of query-document pairs derived from web-crawled PDFs. The retrieval component will be compared against strong baselines such as BM25, bge-large, NV-Embed-v2, SigLIP, MiniCPM (OCR/Captioner), and ColPali, under off-the-shelf, out-of-domain, and in-domain settings. Generation experiments will utilize both single-image and multi-image VLMs (e.g., MiniCPM-V 2.0, MiniCPM-V 2.6, GPT-4o) and compare against text-based generation baselines. Evaluation metrics will include MRR@10 and Recall@10 for retrieval, and relaxed exact match accuracy for generation, with numeric answers allowed a 5% error margin. The experimental setup will include ablations on training data efficiency, document length, and modality emphasis, as well as end-to-end pipeline comparisons.
d9052dd87959e6076baf35e8f7ee87d568a32b58.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully vision-based RAG pipeline that eliminates the need for document parsing and directly leverages all visual and textual information in multi-modality documents. It presents a dual-encoder retrieval mechanism optimized for vision-language input, novel strategies for multi-image generation, and demonstrates superior data efficiency and generalization compared to both text-centric and vision-centric baselines. The method establishes a new standard for RAG on real-world documents, achieving substantial performance gains in both retrieval and generation, and offers a scalable, memory-efficient solution suitable for large-scale applications.

d92c797f587ce7f1b001920ab9e6b7d31960bd77.title: RemoteCLIP: A Vision Language Foundation Model for Remote Sensing
d92c797f587ce7f1b001920ab9e6b7d31960bd77.research_question: How can a vision-language foundation model be developed for remote sensing imagery that learns robust visual features with rich semantics and aligned text embeddings, enabling seamless application to diverse downstream tasks such as retrieval, classification, and object counting?
d92c797f587ce7f1b001920ab9e6b7d31960bd77.hypothesis: A large-scale vision-language foundation model, pretrained on a unified and substantially expanded remote sensing dataset with heterogeneous annotation types converted into image-caption pairs, will yield superior generalization and performance on a wide range of remote sensing tasks compared to existing foundation models.
d92c797f587ce7f1b001920ab9e6b7d31960bd77.proposed_method: A novel vision-language foundation model, RemoteCLIP, will be developed by leveraging data scaling to address the scarcity of pre-training data in remote sensing. Heterogeneous annotations from a diverse collection of remote sensing datasets—including object detection bounding boxes and semantic segmentation masks—will be converted into a unified image-caption format using Box-to-Caption (B2C) and Mask-to-Box (M2B) strategies. UAV imagery will be incorporated to further enhance data diversity. The model will be pretrained using the InfoNCE loss to align image and text representations, employing architectures such as ResNet-50, ViT-Base-32, and ViT-Large-14 for the image encoder and a Transformer-based text encoder. After pretraining, the model will be evaluated on multiple downstream tasks, including zero-shot and few-shot classification, image-text retrieval, and object counting.
d92c797f587ce7f1b001920ab9e6b7d31960bd77.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a comprehensive suite of 16 remote sensing datasets, including 12 classification datasets, 3 retrieval datasets (RSITMD, RSICD, UCM), and a newly introduced RemoteCount benchmark for object counting. The pretraining dataset will be constructed by unifying and scaling existing datasets (RET-3, DET-10, SEG-4) to produce a training set 12 times larger than the combination of all available image-text datasets, resulting in over 165,000 images and 828,000 image-caption pairs. Baselines will include previous state-of-the-art remote sensing retrieval and classification models, as well as continual-pretrained CLIP models. Evaluation metrics will include recall at top-K for retrieval, accuracy for classification, and counting accuracy for object counting. The experimental setup will involve training with standard data augmentation, mixed-precision optimization, and consistent evaluation protocols across model scales.
d92c797f587ce7f1b001920ab9e6b7d31960bd77.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first vision-language foundation model specifically for remote sensing, capable of robust cross-modal alignment and generalization across diverse downstream tasks. It presents a novel data scaling pipeline that unifies heterogeneous remote sensing annotations into a large-scale image-caption dataset using B2C and M2B strategies, including the integration of UAV imagery. A new RemoteCount benchmark for object counting in remote sensing is also proposed. The approach claims to enable strong zero-shot and few-shot capabilities, outperforming existing foundation models and CLIP baselines by significant margins on multiple benchmarks.

d950c9aae1b8653948096361c75e2c5dd91b106c.title: Q-Adapter: Customizing Pre-trained LLMs to New Preferences with Forgetting Mitigation
d950c9aae1b8653948096361c75e2c5dd91b106c.research_question: How can pre-trained large language models be customized to new human preferences while effectively mitigating the issue of catastrophic forgetting and preserving original capabilities?
d950c9aae1b8653948096361c75e2c5dd91b106c.hypothesis: It is possible to customize pre-trained LLMs to new human preferences without significant forgetting of original capabilities by optimizing a joint objective that incorporates both the original and new preferences, using a residual Q-learning framework that does not require access to the original reward functions.
d950c9aae1b8653948096361c75e2c5dd91b106c.proposed_method: A novel framework, Q-Adapter, is proposed to customize pre-trained LLMs by introducing an adapter module that learns a residual Q-function. The method frames customization as maximizing the sum of two reward functions: one corresponding to the original pre-training preferences (unknown) and one to the new human preferences (provided via preference data). By leveraging the residual Q-learning framework, the approach bypasses the need to access or learn the original reward function, instead directly learning the residual Q-function from new preference data using the Bradley-Terry model. The adapter is implemented as a neural network (e.g., via LoRA) that is trained to approximate the residual Q-function, and the final customized policy is derived by combining the outputs of the pre-trained LLM and the learned adapter at inference time. Training involves minimizing a loss based on pairwise preference data and regularization, and inference utilizes a closed-form solution combining the pre-trained policy and the residual Q-function.
d950c9aae1b8653948096361c75e2c5dd91b106c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model, using both the Domain-Specific Preference (DSP) dataset (covering academy, business, entertainment, and literature domains) and the HH-RLHF dataset (containing helpful and harmless preference data). Baselines for comparison include Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), policy regularization methods (PPO and DPO), and replay-based methods. Evaluation metrics include benchmark scores on MMLU, MMLUPro, GSM8k, BBH, and IFEval to assess retention of general capabilities, as well as win rates in preference satisfaction as judged by strong LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Deepseek-chat) using AlpacaEval. All methods will be implemented using LoRA adapters for fair comparison, and the same training and evaluation configurations will be maintained across methods.
d950c9aae1b8653948096361c75e2c5dd91b106c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new objective for LLM customization that jointly maximizes both original and new preferences without requiring access to the original reward function. It derives a new loss function for direct learning of the residual Q-function from preference data, leveraging the Bradley-Terry model and residual Q-learning. The approach maintains the pre-trained model intact and combines it with a learned adapter at inference, effectively mitigating catastrophic forgetting and enabling seamless customization to new preferences. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance in both retaining existing knowledge and learning new preferences compared to existing fine-tuning and regularization methods.

d9655f9686f8afc13a69814c7bf0cab3d4899ab5.title: UniDexGrasp: Universal Robotic Dexterous Grasping via Learning Diverse Proposal Generation and Goal-Conditioned Policy
d9655f9686f8afc13a69814c7bf0cab3d4899ab5.research_question: How can a universal robotic dexterous grasping system be developed that can generate diverse, high-quality grasp proposals and execute goal-conditioned grasps across hundreds of object categories, including unseen ones, using only point cloud observations and robot proprioception in realistic table-top settings?
d9655f9686f8afc13a69814c7bf0cab3d4899ab5.hypothesis: A two-stage pipeline that decouples grasp proposal generation and goal-conditioned grasp execution, leveraging advanced probabilistic generative models and curriculum-based reinforcement learning, will enable universal, diverse, and high-quality dexterous grasping that generalizes across a wide range of object categories and unseen instances using only realistic sensory inputs.
d9655f9686f8afc13a69814c7bf0cab3d4899ab5.proposed_method: The proposed method consists of a two-stage pipeline. In the first stage, a probabilistic generative model is designed to produce diverse dexterous grasp proposals conditioned on the object point cloud. This model factorizes the grasp pose into rotation (using a conditional ImplicitPDF model on SO(3)) and translation plus joint articulation (using a conditional normalizing flow, Glow, on Euclidean space), followed by a contact-based optimization (ContactNet) to ensure physical plausibility. In the second stage, a goal-conditioned grasp execution policy is developed, which takes the grasp proposal, point cloud, and robot proprioception as input and outputs control actions. This policy is trained using a teacher-student framework: a teacher policy is first trained with full oracle state information and curriculum learning (progressing from single-object to multi-category training), then distilled to a student policy that only uses realistic sensory inputs via imitation learning (DAgger). State canonicalization is applied to enforce SO(2) equivariance and improve learning efficiency.
d9655f9686f8afc13a69814c7bf0cab3d4899ab5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a large-scale synthesized dataset containing over 1.12 million grasps for 5519 object instances across 133 categories, split into training, seen-category-unseen-instance, and unseen-category sets. The grasp proposal generation stage will be evaluated using metrics such as grasp quality (Q1), object penetration depth, and diversity (variance in rotation, translation, and joint angles), and compared against baselines including CVAE-based and other flow-based generative models. For grasp execution, the goal-conditioned policy will be evaluated in the IsaacGym simulator, measuring success rates on both seen and unseen categories, with ablations for curriculum learning, state canonicalization, and joint object classification. Baselines will include PPO, DAPG, and ILAD. Additional experiments will test robustness to noisy grasp proposals and demonstrate language-guided grasp selection using CLIP.
d9655f9686f8afc13a69814c7bf0cab3d4899ab5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first universal dexterous grasping pipeline that achieves high-quality, diverse, and generalizable grasping across thousands of object instances and hundreds of categories using only point cloud and proprioceptive inputs. Key innovations include the factorization of grasp pose generation into rotation and translation/articulation using specialized probabilistic models (ImplicitPDF and Glow), a contact-based optimization for physical plausibility, and a teacher-student policy learning framework with curriculum learning and state canonicalization for robust, generalizable goal-conditioned grasp execution. The approach demonstrates significant improvements over all baselines in both grasp diversity and execution success rates, and enables downstream tasks such as language-guided functional grasping.

d96a0f7660aedad4bdbeabbfd7d3b51519be4565.title: Adaptive Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation with Meta-Learning
d96a0f7660aedad4bdbeabbfd7d3b51519be4565.research_question: How can knowledge from multiple pre-trained teacher networks be adaptively integrated to improve the training and performance of a student network, particularly when the student has limited learning capacity and teacher knowledge compatibility is a challenge?
d96a0f7660aedad4bdbeabbfd7d3b51519be4565.hypothesis: Adaptive integration of diverse teacher knowledge, guided by a meta-learning-based weighting mechanism that considers both output logits and intermediate features, will yield more compatible and effective supervision for the student network, resulting in improved student performance compared to existing multi-teacher knowledge distillation methods.
d96a0f7660aedad4bdbeabbfd7d3b51519be4565.proposed_method: A novel adaptive multi-teacher knowledge distillation framework is developed, leveraging meta-learning to dynamically integrate the outputs of multiple teacher networks. The approach employs a meta-weight network that receives as input both the concatenated logits and pairwise similarity matrices of intermediate features from the teachers and student. For logits, the meta-weight network outputs a weight vector to combine teacher predictions, while for features, it processes semantic similarity matrices to generate weights for feature matching. The student is trained using a composite loss function that includes cross-entropy with ground-truth labels, weighted Kullback-Leibler divergence between student and ensemble teacher logits, and weighted mean squared error between student and teacher features (after alignment). A hard buffer of difficult samples is maintained for meta-learning, enabling the meta-weight network to be optimized in an outer loop via second-order optimization, ensuring the student receives knowledge that is both diverse and compatible.
d96a0f7660aedad4bdbeabbfd7d3b51519be4565.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on benchmark datasets including CIFAR-100, Stanford Dogs, and Tiny-ImageNet, using various teacher-student architecture combinations (e.g., ResNet32x4, MobileNetV2, VGG13, WRN-40-2, ShuffleNetV1). Baseline methods for comparison include AVER, FitNet-MKD, EBKD, AEKD (logits and feature variants), CA-MKD, as well as single-teacher distillation methods such as KD, FitNet, AT, VID, CRD, SemCKD, and SRRL. Evaluation metrics focus on top-1 test accuracy and Average Relative Improvement (ARI) across multiple runs. The experimental setup involves standard training schedules, SGD optimization for the student, Adam for the meta-weight network, and systematic ablation studies to assess the impact of key components such as the hard buffer, feature loss, and meta-weight network design.
d96a0f7660aedad4bdbeabbfd7d3b51519be4565.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a meta-learning-based meta-weight network to adaptively integrate both logits and intermediate feature knowledge from multiple teachers at the instance level. Unlike prior approaches that focus solely on ensemble teacher strength or static weighting, this framework explicitly addresses knowledge compatibility between teachers and student. The use of a hard buffer for meta-learning, second-order optimization for the meta-weight network, and joint aggregation of diverse teacher knowledge sources represent key innovations. The approach demonstrates superior performance and robustness across datasets and teacher-student combinations, outperforming both single- and multi-teacher knowledge distillation baselines.

d981ce332586e6a29f595cbdfa9347cf425e5cd0.title: Open-Reasoner-Zero: An Open Source Approach to Scaling Up Reinforcement Learning on the Base Model
d981ce332586e6a29f595cbdfa9347cf425e5cd0.research_question: How can reinforcement learning be scaled up effectively and efficiently on large language models for reasoning tasks, while maintaining simplicity, stability, and accessibility in the training pipeline?
d981ce332586e6a29f595cbdfa9347cf425e5cd0.hypothesis: A minimalist reinforcement learning approach utilizing vanilla Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) parameters set to λ=1 and γ=1, combined with a simple rule-based reward function and without KL regularization, is sufficient to achieve scalable and robust improvements in reasoning performance on large language models, outperforming more complex pipelines.
d981ce332586e6a29f595cbdfa9347cf425e5cd0.proposed_method: The proposed method involves directly applying large-scale reinforcement learning to base language models (Qwen2.5-{7B,32B}) using vanilla PPO as the core algorithm. Generalized Advantage Estimation is configured with λ=1 and γ=1 to fully capture long-term dependencies, and a simple binary rule-based reward function is used, which awards a reward of 1 for exact answer matches and 0 otherwise. The training data consists of tens of thousands of carefully curated question-answer pairs spanning math and general reasoning tasks, with additional synthetic tasks for diversity. No KL regularization is applied, simplifying the training process and reducing computational overhead. The approach bypasses any supervised fine-tuning or distillation stages, launching RL directly from the base model, and employs prompt templates designed to elicit structured reasoning.
d981ce332586e6a29f595cbdfa9347cf425e5cd0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-32B base models, as well as smaller variants (0.5B, 1.5B), using a large-scale, diverse dataset curated from public sources (AIME, MATH, Numina-Math, Tulu3MATH, OpenR1-Math-220k, AoPS forum) and synthetic reasoning tasks. Evaluation will be performed on benchmarks including AIME2024, AIME2025, MATH500, GPQA Diamond, MMLU, and MMLU_PRO. Baselines for comparison include DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B and DAPO-Qwen-32B. Metrics such as benchmark accuracy, training reward, response length, and correct format ratio will be tracked. Ablation studies will examine the effects of GAE parameters, KL regularization, and data scale. Additional analyses will investigate the effectiveness of the learned critic in penalizing repetitive patterns and stabilizing training.
d981ce332586e6a29f595cbdfa9347cf425e5cd0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first fully open-source implementation of large-scale reasoning-oriented RL training directly on base language models, emphasizing scalability, simplicity, and accessibility. It demonstrates that a minimalist PPO+GAE(1,1) setup with a simple rule-based reward is sufficient for robust and scalable reasoning performance, eliminating the need for KL regularization or complex reward engineering. The method achieves superior performance on multiple reasoning benchmarks with only a fraction of the training steps required by previous pipelines. Comprehensive resources, including code, data, and model weights, are released to facilitate reproducibility and further research.

d9823ffa34f865fb1d0adef95d64a0c352ae125f.title: REFLECT: Summarizing Robot Experiences for Failure Explanation and Correction
d9823ffa34f865fb1d0adef95d64a0c352ae125f.research_question: How can a robotics system automatically detect, explain, and correct failures in long-horizon tasks using multisensory data and advanced reasoning capabilities?
d9823ffa34f865fb1d0adef95d64a0c352ae125f.hypothesis: A hierarchical summary of multisensory robot experiences, combined with progressive querying of large language models, enables accurate detection, explanation, and correction of a wide range of robot failures without task-specific assumptions.
d9823ffa34f865fb1d0adef95d64a0c352ae125f.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that processes post-execution multisensory robot observations (including RGB-D, audio, and proprioceptive data) into a hierarchical summary with three abstraction levels: sensory-input summary, event-based summary, and subgoal-based summary. The sensory-input summary aggregates visual and audio data into task-informed scene graphs and audio event labels, focusing on task-relevant objects, their states, and spatial relations. The event-based summary selects keyframes based on changes in scene graphs, audio events, or subgoal transitions, and generates structured textual captions. The subgoal-based summary captures environment observations at the end of each subgoal to facilitate rapid failure localization. A progressive failure explanation algorithm queries a large language model (LLM) to verify subgoal success, identify failure types, and generate detailed natural language explanations by retrieving relevant summaries. Finally, a failure correction planner leverages the generated explanations and final environment state to prompt a language-based planner to generate an executable correction plan, mapping high-level actions to environment-specific primitives.
d9823ffa34f865fb1d0adef95d64a0c352ae125f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a newly created RoboFail dataset, which includes 100 simulated failure demonstrations in AI2THOR (across 10 tasks) and 30 real-world failure demonstrations using a UR5e robot arm in a toy kitchen environment. Each demonstration includes RGB-D, audio, and robot state data, as well as ground-truth metadata. The evaluation will use metrics such as explanation accuracy (as judged by human evaluators), failure localization accuracy (alignment of predicted and actual failure times), and correction planning success rate (task completion after executing the correction plan). Baselines and ablations include state-of-the-art image captioning (BLIP2), removal of audio modality, non-progressive LLM querying, subgoal-only summaries, LLM summary of raw sensory data, and correction planning without failure explanation. Object detection and state recognition will use MDETR and CLIP in the real world, and GPT-4 will serve as the LLM.
d9823ffa34f865fb1d0adef95d64a0c352ae125f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a hierarchical, multisensory robot experience summary specifically designed for failure explanation and correction, enabling the transformation of robot failure reasoning into a language reasoning task. The progressive failure explanation algorithm allows for accurate localization and explanation of both execution and planning failures. The framework is evaluated on a new, diverse dataset of simulated and real-world robot failures, demonstrating superior performance over existing baselines and ablations. The approach is task-agnostic, does not require task-specific assumptions, and leverages both visual and auditory modalities for robust failure analysis and correction planning.

d998874f80a3d60fd9e1636d05f4843739a4271f.title: Memory-Efficient Approximation Algorithms for Max-k-Cut and Correlation Clustering
d998874f80a3d60fd9e1636d05f4843739a4271f.research_question: How can memory-efficient approximation algorithms be developed for large-scale Max-k-Cut and correlation clustering problems, particularly for graphs with a large number of vertices and edges, while maintaining strong approximation guarantees?
d998874f80a3d60fd9e1636d05f4843739a4271f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging Gaussian sampling-based algorithms and novel SDP relaxations with fewer constraints, it is possible to design polynomial-time approximation algorithms for Max-k-Cut and correlation clustering that use significantly less memory than traditional SDP-based methods, while achieving approximation ratios close to the best known guarantees.
d998874f80a3d60fd9e1636d05f4843739a4271f.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces new memory-efficient approximation algorithms for Max-k-Cut and the Max-Agree variant of correlation clustering by adapting Gaussian sampling-based Frank-Wolfe techniques to specialized SDP relaxations. For Max-k-Cut, a new SDP relaxation is formulated with only O(n + |E|) constraints, replacing the traditional O(n^2) constraint formulation. Gaussian sampling is used to generate approximate solutions, which are then rounded using the Frieze-Jerrum (FJ) scheme to produce a partition. For Max-Agree, a similar relaxation is constructed, and Gaussian samples are rounded using the Charikar-Guruswami-Wirth (CGW) scheme to form clusterings. To further reduce memory for dense graphs, spectral sparsification is applied in a streaming setting, replacing the original graph with a sparse, spectrally similar graph, and the algorithms are applied to this sparse representation.
d998874f80a3d60fd9e1636d05f4843739a4271f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale graph instances, including both synthetic and real-world datasets such as the GSet collection. For Max-Agree, input graphs will be constructed by assigning edge labels and weights based on similarity metrics such as the Jaccard coefficient. The proposed algorithms will be evaluated against standard baselines, including traditional SDP-based methods and existing low-memory approximation algorithms. Evaluation metrics will include the achieved cut or clustering value relative to the optimal or best-known values, approximation ratios, and memory usage. The experimental setup will also consider streaming scenarios, where graphs arrive edge-by-edge and sparsification is performed online.
d998874f80a3d60fd9e1636d05f4843739a4271f.novelty_claims: The proposal claims several innovations: (1) the development of simple, polynomial-time Gaussian sampling-based algorithms for Max-k-Cut and correlation clustering that use O(n + |E|) memory, a significant reduction from the O(n^2) memory required by standard SDP approaches; (2) the introduction of new SDP relaxations tailored for memory efficiency without sacrificing approximation guarantees; (3) the combination of these methods with streaming spectral sparsification to further reduce memory requirements for dense graphs; and (4) the achievement of approximation ratios that are close to state-of-the-art, with memory usage independent of the approximation parameter.

d99a32f5191ba4192e30b933278d40956e3292c9.title: Batch-ICL: Effective, Efficient, and Order-Agnostic In-Context Learning
d99a32f5191ba4192e30b933278d40956e3292c9.research_question: How can in-context learning (ICL) with large language models be made more robust to the order of demonstration examples, more efficient in computation, and more effective in performance across a range of tasks and model sizes?
d99a32f5191ba4192e30b933278d40956e3292c9.hypothesis: Aggregating meta-gradients from multiple 1-shot forward computations in a batch, rather than sequentially as in standard N-shot ICL, will yield an order-agnostic, more stable, and more effective ICL process. Further, extending this approach to multiple epochs will enhance the interaction among examples and improve overall performance.
d99a32f5191ba4192e30b933278d40956e3292c9.proposed_method: A novel inference algorithm, Batch-ICL, is proposed for in-context learning with large language models. Instead of the standard N-shot approach, Batch-ICL performs N separate 1-shot forward computations for each demonstration example, collecting meta-gradients at a selected layer. These meta-gradients are aggregated and then applied to the forward computation of a zero-shot query to generate the final prediction, making the process agnostic to the order of examples. The method is further extended to a multi-epoch variant, where the aggregation and application of meta-gradients are repeated across multiple layers or epochs, implicitly enumerating permutations of example order and enhancing the interaction among demonstrations. The approach is designed to be compatible with any number of demonstration examples, limited only by the context length of the model, and can be efficiently parallelized.
d99a32f5191ba4192e30b933278d40956e3292c9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of classification and generation tasks, including SST-2 (sentiment analysis), RTE and QNLI (natural language inference), AGNews (topic classification), MRPC (paraphrase detection), and WMT2014 En-Fr (machine translation). The method will be evaluated using open-source large language models such as Llama-2-7B, Llama-2-13B, OPT-6.7B, and Falcon-7B. Baselines will include standard N-shot ICL, Parallel Context Windows (PCW), and Fantastically Ordered (F-Ordered) prompts. Evaluation metrics will comprise accuracy for classification tasks and BLEU score for translation. Experiments will systematically vary the number of shots (N), aggregation layer (k), and number of epochs, and will analyze performance across all permutations of demonstration order to assess order sensitivity, stability, and efficiency. Resource utilization (time and memory) will also be measured.
d99a32f5191ba4192e30b933278d40956e3292c9.novelty_claims: Batch-ICL introduces a fundamentally new, order-agnostic approach to in-context learning by aggregating meta-gradients from parallel 1-shot computations, rather than relying on sequential N-shot processing. The method reduces sensitivity to the order of demonstration examples, improves computational efficiency, and enables the use of more demonstration examples than standard ICL. The multi-epoch extension further enhances performance by implicitly considering permutations of example order, leading to better interaction among demonstrations. Batch-ICL consistently outperforms standard ICL and related baselines across diverse tasks and models, and demonstrates greater stability and robustness to demonstration selection.

d9a2f89dc65b2cb7cd03cf2d37e2f67c6f72359c.title: PolySketchFormer: Fast Transformers via Sketching Polynomial Kernels
d9a2f89dc65b2cb7cd03cf2d37e2f67c6f72359c.research_question: How can the computational and memory bottlenecks of self-attention in large-scale Transformer-based language models be overcome, particularly for long context lengths, without sacrificing model quality?
d9a2f89dc65b2cb7cd03cf2d37e2f67c6f72359c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that polynomial attention mechanisms with high degree can serve as effective replacements for softmax attention in Transformers, maintaining model quality, and that sketching techniques from numerical linear algebra can be leveraged to approximate these polynomial kernels in linear time with provable guarantees, enabling efficient training and inference for long context sequences.
d9a2f89dc65b2cb7cd03cf2d37e2f67c6f72359c.proposed_method: The proposed approach replaces the traditional softmax attention in Transformers with a high-degree polynomial attention mechanism, specifically using polynomial kernels of degree p ≥ 4. To address the computational cost of high-degree polynomial feature mappings, randomized sketching techniques are employed to approximate the polynomial kernel in a lower-dimensional space, ensuring non-negativity and providing theoretical approximation guarantees. A block-based algorithm is introduced to efficiently handle causal masking, enabling linear-time computation of attention for long sequences. Additionally, learnable sketches are proposed, where random projection matrices in the sketching process are replaced by small, trainable dense neural networks, further improving model quality. The overall architecture, termed PolySketchFormer, integrates these components to deliver a practical, linear-time Transformer suitable for language modeling.
d9a2f89dc65b2cb7cd03cf2d37e2f67c6f72359c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by training decoder-only language models of various scales (mirroring GPT-2 Small, Medium, and Large) on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including PG19, Wikipedia, and C4, using Google Cloud TPUs. The evaluation will include pre-training metrics (perplexity) across a range of context lengths (from 512 up to 32k tokens), as well as downstream tasks such as HellaSwag, PIQA, and Physics QA, measuring both 0-shot and 5-shot accuracies. Baselines will include standard softmax attention, FlashAttention, Performer, and polynomial attention with varying degrees. Models will be compared on training speed, memory usage, and quality metrics, with attention mechanisms evaluated both with and without learned sketches and local exact polynomial attention. Hyperparameters such as block size and sketch size will be varied to assess trade-offs between speed and quality.
d9a2f89dc65b2cb7cd03cf2d37e2f67c6f72359c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel integration of high-degree polynomial attention with randomized and learnable sketching techniques, enabling linear-time attention computation with provable approximation guarantees. The method avoids the need for attention matrix sparsification, a common limitation in prior efficient Transformer approaches. A new block-based algorithm is developed for efficient causal masking, further enhancing scalability. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that the proposed method achieves significant speedups (up to 2x over FlashAttention) for long context lengths without degrading model quality, and in some cases, even surpasses softmax attention on downstream tasks. The combination of theoretical guarantees, practical speedups, and maintained or improved model quality constitutes the core innovation.

d9a449e1123ca37375c9977f51b7ea6129905803.title: RAVEL: Evaluating Interpretability Methods on Disentangling Language Model Representations
d9a449e1123ca37375c9977f51b7ea6129905803.research_question: To what extent can interpretability methods successfully disentangle and localize individual attributes within language model representations, and how can these methods be systematically evaluated for faithfulness, generalizability, causal effectiveness, and the ability to isolate individual concepts?
d9a449e1123ca37375c9977f51b7ea6129905803.hypothesis: Interpretability methods that leverage distributed, multi-task, and intervention-based approaches will outperform neuron-level or unsupervised methods in isolating and causally manipulating individual attributes within language model representations.
d9a449e1123ca37375c9977f51b7ea6129905803.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, RAVEL, will be developed to evaluate interpretability methods on their ability to disentangle and localize entity attributes in language models. The benchmark will consist of a curated dataset featuring five entity types (cities, people names, verbs, physical objects, occupations), each with multiple attributes and a large set of prompt templates. The evaluation framework will employ interchange interventions, where features corresponding to specific attributes are manipulated in the model's internal representations to assess causal effects on output. Several interpretability methods will be implemented and compared, including PCA, sparse autoencoders, supervised probes, Differential Binary Masking (DBM), Distributed Alignment Search (DAS), and their multi-task variants (MDBM, MDAS). Multi-task objectives will be introduced to encourage the disentanglement of multiple attributes simultaneously, with a focus on identifying distributed features across activations rather than relying solely on neuron-level analysis.
d9a449e1123ca37375c9977f51b7ea6129905803.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Llama2-7B language model, focusing on the residual stream representations at the last token of each entity across all model layers. The RAVEL dataset will be split into train/dev/test sets in two settings: Entity (splitting entities) and Context (splitting prompt templates), to evaluate generalization. Each interpretability method will be trained on the training split to identify features for each attribute, and evaluated using intervention-based metrics: Cause (causal effect on the target attribute) and Iso (isolation from other attributes). Baselines will include the full representation and all implemented interpretability methods. The primary evaluation metric will be the Disentangle score, a weighted average of Cause and Iso, computed across all attributes and entity types. Additional analyses will examine the dimensionality of features, layer-wise disentanglement, and the ability to generalize to unseen entities and contexts.
d9a449e1123ca37375c9977f51b7ea6129905803.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark, RAVEL, enables tightly controlled, quantitative, and systematic comparisons between a wide range of interpretability methods for language models. The introduction of multi-task objectives for intervention-based methods (MDBM and MDAS) allows for the identification of distributed features that satisfy multiple causal criteria, advancing beyond traditional neuron-level or unsupervised approaches. The framework provides the first comprehensive evaluation of interpretability methods on their ability to faithfully, causally, and generalizably disentangle attributes, offering new insights into the structure of language model representations and the emergence of disentangled features across layers.

d9ba1954610537587604020de758094bdd115e22.title: Almost Optimal Batch-Regret Tradeoff for Batch Linear Contextual Bandits
d9ba1954610537587604020de758094bdd115e22.research_question: What is the optimal tradeoff between the number of batches and the achievable regret in batch linear contextual bandit problems, under both context-blind and context-aware settings, across all parameter regimes?
d9ba1954610537587604020de758094bdd115e22.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that for any given number of batches, time horizon, number of actions, and feature dimension, there exist batch learning algorithms for linear contextual bandits that achieve regret bounds matching the minimax-optimal rates (up to logarithmic factors) for both context-blind and context-aware settings.
d9ba1954610537587604020de758094bdd115e22.proposed_method: A novel batch learning framework will be developed for linear contextual bandits, addressing both context-blind and context-aware scenarios. The approach will employ elimination-based algorithms that maintain confidence intervals for each candidate action and iteratively eliminate suboptimal actions based on observed data. At the core of the method is a new single-batch exploration policy procedure, designed to achieve distributional G-optimality in experimental design, which selects policies to minimize the expected maximum width of confidence intervals in future batches. The method will utilize regularized ordinary least squares (OLS) for parameter estimation and introduce a scaled-and-clipped update rule to improve exploration efficiency. Additionally, a new matrix concentration inequality with dynamic (possibly stochastic) upper bounds will be established to enable tight regret analysis across all parameter regimes.
d9ba1954610537587604020de758094bdd115e22.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and/or real-world datasets that simulate the stochastic linear contextual bandit setting, with varying numbers of actions (K), feature dimensions (d), time horizons (T), and batch numbers (M). The proposed algorithms will be compared against state-of-the-art batch and non-batch contextual bandit algorithms, including those from recent literature. Evaluation metrics will include cumulative regret and computational efficiency, with particular attention to the dependence of regret on the number of batches and other problem parameters. Both context-blind and context-aware batch learning scenarios will be systematically tested, and lower bounds will be empirically validated to demonstrate optimality.
d9ba1954610537587604020de758094bdd115e22.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a batch learning algorithm for linear contextual bandits that is provably optimal (up to logarithmic factors) for all parameter regimes and for both context-blind and context-aware settings. The method is significantly simpler and more practical than prior approaches, requiring fewer technical assumptions and achieving optimal regret for all T ≥ d, whereas previous methods required unrealistically large T. The research also presents a new matrix concentration inequality with dynamic upper bounds, which is the first of its kind and may have independent interest in the analysis of adaptive algorithms. The exploration policy procedure achieves improved dependence on batch sizes, enabling optimal regret tradeoffs and outperforming existing techniques in both theoretical guarantees and practical implementation.

d9c707a02615f64ce381c18da72191f9638d116e.title: Deep Bayesian Filter for Bayes-faithful Data Assimilation
d9c707a02615f64ce381c18da72191f9638d116e.research_question: How can sequential state estimation and data assimilation be improved in nonlinear state space models, particularly under highly non-Gaussian posteriors and high-dimensional settings, while maintaining computational tractability and accurate uncertainty quantification?
d9c707a02615f64ce381c18da72191f9638d116e.hypothesis: A variational inference framework that enforces Gaussianity in latent space posteriors through structured design—combining linear latent dynamics with nonlinear observation mappings—will enable analytical, recursive filtering in nonlinear state space models, outperforming classical and existing deep learning-based data assimilation methods in scenarios with highly non-Gaussian posteriors.
d9c707a02615f64ce381c18da72191f9638d116e.proposed_method: A new data assimilation method, Deep Bayesian Filtering (DBF), is developed for nonlinear state space models. DBF introduces a latent variable space with linear dynamics, enabling the posterior over latent states to remain Gaussian at each time step. Nonlinearities in the physical system and observation models are handled by neural networks: the physical state is mapped to the latent space via a nonlinear encoder, and observations are mapped to the latent space using a learned inverse observation operator (IOO), also parameterized by neural networks. The system is trained by maximizing the evidence lower bound (ELBO), either in a supervised or unsupervised fashion, depending on the availability of ground-truth physical states. For inference, DBF recursively computes the posterior in closed-form, avoiding Monte Carlo sampling and thus preventing error accumulation over time. The method leverages the Koopman operator framework to ensure that even highly nonlinear dynamics can be represented as linear in a sufficiently high-dimensional latent space.
d9c707a02615f64ce381c18da72191f9638d116e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and benchmark datasets, including the Moving MNIST (linear dynamics with nonlinear observations), double pendulum (chaotic nonlinear dynamics), and Lorenz96 (high-dimensional, nonlinear, and chaotic system). For each task, DBF will be compared against classical data assimilation methods (EnKF, ETKF, Particle Filter, Particle Flow Filter), state-of-the-art neural network-based approaches (KalmanNet, deep Kalman Filter, VRNN, SRNN, DKF), and, where appropriate, PDE surrogate models. Evaluation metrics will include root mean square error (RMSE) for state estimation, success rates (e.g., sub-pixel accuracy in tracking), and measures of uncertainty calibration (e.g., KL divergence between normalized errors and a standard Gaussian). Experimental setups will vary observation noise levels, nonlinearity in observation operators, and latent space dimensionality. All models will be trained and tested on multiple random initializations, with hyperparameters and architectures detailed in supplementary material.
d9c707a02615f64ce381c18da72191f9638d116e.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first amortized variational inference approach for data assimilation that is 'Bayes-Faithful,' i.e., its inference structure mirrors the Markov property of state space models, enabling analytical, recursive computation of posteriors without Monte Carlo sampling. DBF uniquely combines linear latent dynamics with nonlinear neural network-based observation operators, allowing for tractable filtering in highly nonlinear and high-dimensional systems. The approach provides accurate uncertainty quantification and is robust to non-Gaussianity in the posterior, outperforming both classical and deep learning-based baselines in challenging data assimilation scenarios. Additionally, DBF's structured design stabilizes training compared to RNN-based dynamical VAEs and scales efficiently to large latent dimensions.

d9de0c1c8d21ec9cb8bd430ca98569e08328d882.title: KAN 2.0: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks Meet Science
d9de0c1c8d21ec9cb8bd430ca98569e08328d882.research_question: How can neural network architectures be synergistically integrated with scientific discovery processes to enhance interpretability, modularity, and the extraction and incorporation of scientific knowledge, particularly in curiosity-driven science?
d9de0c1c8d21ec9cb8bd430ca98569e08328d882.hypothesis: Integrating explicit scientific inductive biases and symbolic structures into Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs), and augmenting them with multiplicative operations, will improve their interpretability, facilitate the discovery and representation of scientific laws, and enable bidirectional knowledge transfer between AI models and scientific understanding.
d9de0c1c8d21ec9cb8bd430ca98569e08328d882.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed that extends Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) by introducing multiplication nodes (MultKAN), enabling the explicit representation of multiplicative relationships common in scientific laws. The methodology includes mechanisms for embedding scientific inductive biases into KANs by augmenting input features with auxiliary variables, enforcing modular network structures to reflect separability and symmetry, and compiling symbolic formulas directly into KAN architectures using a compiler (kanpiler). Additionally, techniques for expanding network width and depth will be provided to increase expressive power, and perturbation methods will be used to ensure trainability of newly added network components.
