Tools will be developed for extracting scientific knowledge from trained KANs, including attribution-based feature importance scoring, modularity analysis (both anatomical and functional), and symbolic regression for formula discovery.
d9de0c1c8d21ec9cb8bd430ca98569e08328d882.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of scientific discovery tasks, including the identification of conserved quantities, Lagrangians, symmetries, and constitutive laws. Datasets will include both synthetic functions (e.g., Feynman equations, parity and majority voting tasks) and real-world scientific datasets. Baseline comparisons will involve standard Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) and original KANs without multiplicative enhancements. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE) for regression accuracy, interpretability as measured by the clarity of extracted symbolic formulas and modular structures, and feature attribution accuracy. Experimental setups will involve ablation studies on the impact of auxiliary variables, modularity enforcement, and symbolic compilation, as well as visual and quantitative analysis of the extracted scientific knowledge.
d9de0c1c8d21ec9cb8bd430ca98569e08328d882.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a bidirectional synergy between neural network architectures (KANs) and scientific discovery, enabling both the embedding of scientific knowledge into AI models and the extraction of interpretable scientific insights from them. Key innovations include the explicit incorporation of multiplicative operations into KANs (MultKAN), a compiler for converting symbolic formulas into neural architectures, and new methods for enforcing and extracting modularity and feature importance. The framework advances the interpretability and scientific utility of neural networks, supporting curiosity-driven science and enabling the discovery of symbolic laws and modular structures directly from data.

d9ef08a1a0d231d01ce805c61230995877c606d3.title: Grammar-Aligned Decoding
d9ef08a1a0d231d01ce805c61230995877c606d3.research_question: How can language model decoding be improved to generate outputs that are both guaranteed to satisfy complex structural constraints (such as context-free grammars) and remain faithful to the original probability distribution of the language model?
d9ef08a1a0d231d01ce805c61230995877c606d3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that an adaptive sampling algorithm, which iteratively refines estimates of future grammaticality using observed samples, can produce outputs that are both grammatical and unbiased with respect to the language model's distribution, outperforming existing grammar-constrained decoding methods in distributional fidelity.
d9ef08a1a0d231d01ce805c61230995877c606d3.proposed_method: A novel decoding algorithm, Adaptive Sampling with Approximate Expected Futures (ASAp), will be developed to address the problem of grammar-aligned decoding. The method operates by initially using grammar-constrained decoding (GCD) to mask out tokens that would lead to ungrammatical outputs, then iteratively refines an overapproximation of the expected future grammaticality (EFG) for each prefix based on observed samples. After each sample, the algorithm updates EFG estimates by back-propagating the probability mass of grammatical and ungrammatical continuations, thereby tightening the approximation. Sampling is performed autoregressively, with the probability of each next token reweighted by the current EFG estimate, and the process is repeated over multiple iterations, converging to the true constrained distribution. The approach is general and can be applied on top of any structured decoding method, but will be evaluated specifically for context-free grammar constraints.
d9ef08a1a0d231d01ce805c61230995877c606d3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three structured prediction tasks: syntax-guided program synthesis (SyGuS) with string linear integer arithmetic (SLIA) and bit-vector invariant generation (INV-BV), and constituency parsing (CP). For each task, a set of benchmarks will be selected (e.g., 15 SLIA, 15 INV-BV, and 6 CP problems), and prompts will include several in-context examples along with the grammar constraint. The open-source Mistral-7B language model will be used for generation. Both ASAp and standard GCD will be run for 2,000 iterations per benchmark, and the empirical distributions of generated outputs will be compared to the ideal grammar-aligned distribution using Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence. Additional metrics include the empirical expectation of solution correctness and the rate of convergence to the target distribution. Correctness of generated programs or parses will also be measured against the task specifications.
d9ef08a1a0d231d01ce805c61230995877c606d3.novelty_claims: The proposed research formalizes the problem of grammar-aligned decoding and identifies a fundamental bias in existing constrained decoding approaches. It introduces the first adaptive algorithm (ASAp) that provably converges to the grammar-aligned distribution, ensuring both grammaticality and faithfulness to the language model's learned distribution. The method provides a flexible trade-off between efficiency and accuracy, and is the first to use iterative refinement of expected future grammaticality estimates for unbiased constrained sampling. The approach is generalizable to any structured constraint expressible via grammars.

d9fc4a4179ba964a6c5f69e7be7deffc14a434e4.title: DriveAdapter: Breaking the Coupling Barrier of Perception and Planning in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
d9fc4a4179ba964a6c5f69e7be7deffc14a434e4.research_question: How can the coupling between perception and planning in end-to-end autonomous driving systems be effectively decoupled to improve driving performance, efficiency, and interpretability, while mitigating issues such as causal confusion and imperfect perception or planning modules?
d9fc4a4179ba964a6c5f69e7be7deffc14a434e4.hypothesis: Decoupling perception and planning by directly leveraging a frozen, reinforcement learning-trained teacher model for planning, while employing adapters with feature alignment and action-guided objectives to bridge the distribution gap between predicted and privileged inputs, will yield superior driving performance and robustness compared to traditional behavior cloning-based teacher-student paradigms.
d9fc4a4179ba964a6c5f69e7be7deffc14a434e4.proposed_method: A new framework, DriveAdapter, will be developed to decouple perception and planning in end-to-end autonomous driving. The perception module (student) will process raw sensor data (multi-camera images and LiDAR) to generate bird’s-eye-view (BEV) semantic segmentation, which serves as the input to a frozen planning module (teacher) trained via reinforcement learning on privileged information. Between the student and teacher, a series of learnable adapter modules will be inserted after each block of the teacher model. These adapters will receive both the predicted BEV segmentation and raw BEV features, and will be trained with feature alignment objectives to match the distribution of ground-truth privileged inputs. To address the imperfections of the teacher model, a masked feature alignment loss and an action-guided loss will be introduced, allowing the adapters to selectively learn from hand-crafted rule-based interventions and backpropagate action losses when the teacher is overridden by rules. The entire system will remain end-to-end differentiable, and the adapters will be implemented as CNNs or MLPs depending on the feature dimensionality.
d9fc4a4179ba964a6c5f69e7be7deffc14a434e4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the CARLA simulator, with data collected from four cameras and one LiDAR sensor, and ground-truth privileged information for training. The primary teacher model will be Roach (a reinforcement learning-based planner) with additional rule-based overrides for safety-critical scenarios. The evaluation will be performed on two public closed-loop simulation benchmarks: Town05 Long and Longest6, which include challenging urban driving scenarios and long-tail events. Baselines will include state-of-the-art end-to-end driving models such as Transfuser, LAV, TCP, MILE, and others, with both behavior cloning and teacher-student paradigms. Evaluation metrics will include Driving Score (DS), Route Completion (RC), and Infraction Score (IS), as defined in the CARLA benchmark. Ablation studies will be conducted to analyze the impact of feature alignment loss, action-guided loss, adapter placement, and learning targets (e.g., BEV segmentation vs. intermediate features). Additional experiments will explore the effect of training data scale and the interpretability of intermediate representations.
d9fc4a4179ba964a6c5f69e7be7deffc14a434e4.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first thorough exploration of a fully decoupled paradigm for end-to-end autonomous driving, where planning is handled entirely by a frozen, expert teacher model and perception is learned independently. The use of adapters with feature alignment and action-guided objectives to bridge the distribution gap between predicted and privileged inputs is novel in this context. The approach provides a more interpretable intermediate representation (BEV segmentation), enables leveraging recent advances in BEV perception, and explicitly addresses both imperfect perception and planning modules. The proposed method is expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance on challenging closed-loop driving benchmarks, while offering new insights into the design of modular, robust, and explainable end-to-end driving systems.

d9ffb44ee3c8ec0b6692df8a90451384c1edd89b.title: Likelihood-Based Diffusion Language Models
d9ffb44ee3c8ec0b6692df8a90451384c1edd89b.research_question: Can diffusion-based language models, when trained with likelihood-based objectives and appropriate algorithmic improvements, achieve competitive or superior likelihood performance compared to established autoregressive language models on standard language modeling benchmarks?
d9ffb44ee3c8ec0b6692df8a90451384c1edd89b.hypothesis: Likelihood-based diffusion language models, equipped with methodological enhancements and trained at scale, can outperform small but widely-used autoregressive models in terms of likelihood on standard benchmarks, while also supporting fluent and controllable text generation.
d9ffb44ee3c8ec0b6692df8a90451384c1edd89b.proposed_method: A novel framework for likelihood-based diffusion language modeling, termed Plaid (Perplexity-based LAnguage Inverse Diffusion), will be developed. The method maps discrete text sequences into a continuous embedding space and applies a variational diffusion process, adding Gaussian noise to embeddings and learning a reverse generative process via a denoising neural network. Key algorithmic components include jointly learned embeddings, categorical reparameterization to avoid memorization of embeddings, an analytically computed output prior to ease the modeling burden, a learned conditional likelihood model for more flexible output distributions, and self-conditioning to improve denoising performance. The noise schedule will be parameterized as a neural network and optimized via gradient descent, and all components will be ablated to validate their contributions. The framework will leverage Transformer architectures, with careful design choices for embedding dimension, sequence length, and stochastic sequence truncation to improve generalization.
d9ffb44ee3c8ec0b6692df8a90451384c1edd89b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale language modeling datasets, including OpenWebText2 for pretraining and standard benchmarks such as Penn Treebank, enwik8, text8, WikiText2, WikiText103, and the One Billion Word corpus for evaluation. The proposed Plaid models will be compared against autoregressive baselines, notably various sizes of GPT-2, using log-likelihood (bits per character or perplexity) as the primary evaluation metric. Compute-matched ablation studies will assess the impact of each algorithmic component, and scaling law analyses will be performed to determine compute-optimal training regimes. Human evaluation of sample quality will be conducted via crowdworker preference tests, and zero-shot control capabilities will be demonstrated using classifier-guidance-based token control during generation.
d9ffb44ee3c8ec0b6692df8a90451384c1edd89b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first likelihood-based diffusion language modeling framework capable of outperforming a widely-used autoregressive model (GPT-2 124M) in likelihood on standard benchmarks. It presents several methodological innovations, including a principled variational objective for diffusion models over text, joint optimization of embeddings, categorical reparameterization for efficient denoising, an analytically derived output prior, and a learned conditional likelihood model. The work also provides the first comprehensive scaling law analysis for diffusion language models, establishing compute-optimal training regimes distinct from those of autoregressive models. Additionally, the framework supports zero-shot conditional generation via token-level classifier guidance, enabling diverse and controllable text generation without explicit conditioning during training.

da053e2a4ba1b244940c8f2cad5dcdf0d730f85f.title: DoRA: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation
da053e2a4ba1b244940c8f2cad5dcdf0d730f85f.research_question: How can the learning capacity and stability of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods for large pre-trained models be improved to more closely resemble full fine-tuning, while maintaining low inference overhead and parameter efficiency across diverse tasks and architectures?
da053e2a4ba1b244940c8f2cad5dcdf0d730f85f.hypothesis: Decomposing pre-trained model weights into magnitude and direction components, and applying low-rank adaptation specifically to the directional component while fine-tuning the magnitude, will yield a learning pattern and capacity closer to full fine-tuning than existing PEFT methods such as LoRA, without introducing additional inference latency.
da053e2a4ba1b244940c8f2cad5dcdf0d730f85f.proposed_method: A new parameter-efficient fine-tuning framework, Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation (DoRA), will be developed. The method begins by decomposing each pre-trained weight matrix into two components: a magnitude vector and a directional matrix, using vector-wise norms. During fine-tuning, the magnitude component is made trainable, while the directional component is updated via a low-rank adaptation mechanism (e.g., LoRA or its variants). The low-rank adaptation is applied only to the direction, reducing the number of trainable parameters and simplifying the optimization landscape. Both components are initialized from the pre-trained weights, and after training, the adapted weights can be merged back into the original model structure, ensuring no extra inference cost. The approach also includes a memory-efficient training variant by detaching the normalization term from the gradient graph, further reducing training overhead.
da053e2a4ba1b244940c8f2cad5dcdf0d730f85f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of downstream tasks, including commonsense reasoning (using LLaMA-7B/13B, LLaMA2-7B, and LLaMA3-8B), multi-modal tasks (using VL-BART and LLaVA), and instruction tuning (with LLaMA and Alpaca datasets). Baselines will include full fine-tuning, LoRA, VeRA, and other PEFT methods such as adapters and prompt tuning. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on standard benchmarks (e.g., BoolQ, PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, VQAv2, GQA, NLVR2, COCO Caption, TVQA, How2QA, TVC, YC2C), as well as MT-Bench scores for instruction tuning and exact match for math reasoning tasks. The experimental setup will control for the number of trainable parameters, use identical hyperparameters where possible, and include ablation studies on rank, training sample size, and tuning granularity. Additional experiments will assess compatibility with quantized backbones (QLoRA/ QDoRA) and text-to-image generation (DreamBooth/SDXL).
da053e2a4ba1b244940c8f2cad5dcdf0d730f85f.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel weight decomposition analysis that uncovers fundamental differences between full fine-tuning and PEFT methods, leading to a new adaptation strategy that separates magnitude and direction updates. By applying low-rank adaptation exclusively to the direction component, the approach achieves a learning pattern more closely resembling full fine-tuning, resulting in improved accuracy and stability over LoRA and other PEFT baselines. The method maintains parameter efficiency and incurs no additional inference cost, and is compatible with existing LoRA variants and quantized training pipelines. The framework also demonstrates robustness to low-rank settings and reduced training data, and enables fine-grained control over tuning granularity, offering a costless and memory-efficient alternative to current PEFT approaches.

da20329f34b10521ad98bdc9cd4c27de3f6a8d52.title: Hyperbolic Sliced-Wasserstein via Geodesic and Horospherical Projections
da20329f34b10521ad98bdc9cd4c27de3f6a8d52.research_question: How can efficient and theoretically sound discrepancies for comparing probability distributions be developed for data embedded in hyperbolic spaces, particularly for applications where hierarchical or non-Euclidean geometry is relevant?
da20329f34b10521ad98bdc9cd4c27de3f6a8d52.hypothesis: Novel sliced-Wasserstein discrepancies, constructed via geodesic and horospherical projections intrinsic to hyperbolic geometry, will provide computationally efficient, theoretically grounded, and empirically effective tools for comparing distributions in hyperbolic spaces, outperforming existing Euclidean-based or naïve extensions in both accuracy and efficiency.
da20329f34b10521ad98bdc9cd4c27de3f6a8d52.proposed_method: A new family of sliced-Wasserstein discrepancies is proposed for probability distributions supported on hyperbolic spaces, specifically leveraging the Lorentz and Poincaré ball models. The methodology involves projecting distributions onto geodesics passing through the origin, using either geodesic projections (shortest path) or horospherical projections (level sets of the Busemann function), and then computing the Wasserstein distance in one dimension using closed-form solutions. The approach defines two main variants: Geodesic Hyperbolic Sliced-Wasserstein (GHSW) and Horospherical Hyperbolic Sliced-Wasserstein (HHSW), each with explicit algorithms for projection and coordinate computation. Monte Carlo integration is used to approximate the integral over projection directions, and the method is designed to inherit computational efficiency and sample complexity properties similar to Euclidean sliced-Wasserstein, while being intrinsic to hyperbolic geometry.
da20329f34b10521ad98bdc9cd4c27de3f6a8d52.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic experiments include comparing the proposed discrepancies (GHSW, HHSW) to standard Wasserstein, Sinkhorn, and Euclidean sliced-Wasserstein (SW) distances between wrapped normal distributions on hyperbolic spaces, analyzing their scaling, convergence, and numerical stability. Gradient flow experiments will demonstrate the ability of the proposed methods to fit distributions via Riemannian optimization. Real-world tasks include image classification using hyperbolic embeddings, where the proposed discrepancies are used to regularize or fit priors in the latent space, with evaluation on datasets such as CIFAR10 and CIFAR100. Baselines include Euclidean SW, Wasserstein, and Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) with Laplacian kernels. Performance will be measured in terms of accuracy, convergence speed, and computational runtime, with detailed ablation on the number of projections and the effect of distance from the origin.
da20329f34b10521ad98bdc9cd4c27de3f6a8d52.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first intrinsic hyperbolic sliced-Wasserstein discrepancies based on geodesic and horospherical projections, providing closed-form projection and coordinate formulas for both Lorentz and Poincaré ball models. The approach establishes connections to hyperbolic Radon transforms and demonstrates that the new discrepancies are computationally efficient, with sample and projection complexity independent of ambient dimension. Empirical results suggest superior numerical stability and convergence properties over existing methods, especially for distributions far from the origin in hyperbolic space. The framework is broadly applicable to tasks requiring comparison of distributions in non-Euclidean geometries.

da2fe6cd385194b0274d04d04ee72e8caf3854d4.title: Learning Universal Policies via Text-Guided Video Generation
da2fe6cd385194b0274d04d04ee72e8caf3854d4.research_question: How can a universal policy be developed that enables agents to solve a wide variety of tasks across diverse environments, leveraging natural language instructions and visual observations as universal interfaces for planning and control?
da2fe6cd385194b0274d04d04ee72e8caf3854d4.hypothesis: Formulating sequential decision making as a text-conditioned video generation problem, where a planner synthesizes future frames based on a text-encoded goal and an initial observation, will enable combinatorial generalization, multi-task learning, and effective transfer to novel tasks and environments, surpassing traditional policy learning approaches.
da2fe6cd385194b0274d04d04ee72e8caf3854d4.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that casts policy generation as a text-conditioned video generation task. The approach employs a diffusion-based video generator that, given an initial observation frame and a natural language goal description, synthesizes a sequence of future frames representing a planned trajectory. To translate these visual plans into executable actions, a task-specific inverse dynamics model is trained to infer action sequences from the generated video frames. The video generation process is enhanced by conditioning on the initial frame throughout the trajectory, enforcing temporal consistency via tiling, and employing a hierarchical planning strategy that generates coarse-to-fine plans through temporal super-resolution. The system is designed to be adaptable at test time by incorporating additional constraints into the video generation process, allowing for flexible and steerable planning.
da2fe6cd385194b0274d04d04ee72e8caf3854d4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across simulated and real-world robotic environments to evaluate combinatorial generalization, multi-task learning, and transfer capabilities. Datasets will include large-scale internet video-text pairs, simulated robot manipulation demonstrations, and real-world robot datasets such as Bridge. Baselines for comparison will include transformer-based behavior cloning agents (using both state and image observations), trajectory transformers, and action-space diffusion models. Evaluation metrics will comprise task completion accuracy, CLIP scores, Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Fréchet Video Distance (FVD), and a learned success classifier for control-specific tasks. Experiments will be designed to test performance on both seen and novel language instructions, multi-task generalization, and the impact of internet-scale pretraining on real-world transfer.
da2fe6cd385194b0274d04d04ee72e8caf3854d4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a universal policy framework that leverages text-conditioned video generation as a planning mechanism, enabling generalization across diverse environments with different state and action spaces. By using videos and language as universal interfaces, the method bypasses the need for reward engineering and environment-specific state representations. The integration of hierarchical video diffusion, temporal consistency enforcement, and inverse dynamics for action extraction represents a novel combination for policy learning. Additionally, the framework enables leveraging internet-scale video and language data for knowledge transfer, facilitating the synthesis of realistic and adaptable plans for novel tasks and real-world robots.

da40e92fc04ef8bd5895b4ea8e829d85273c08b0.title: A Hierarchical 3D Gaussian Representation for Real-Time Rendering of Very Large Datasets
da40e92fc04ef8bd5895b4ea8e829d85273c08b0.research_question: How can real-time rendering of extremely large 3D scenes, captured from thousands of images over kilometer-scale trajectories, be achieved with high visual quality and efficient resource usage?
da40e92fc04ef8bd5895b4ea8e829d85273c08b0.hypothesis: A hierarchical 3D Gaussian representation, combined with a divide-and-conquer training approach and optimized level-of-detail (LOD) selection, will enable real-time rendering of very large datasets while preserving visual quality and allowing scalable resource usage.
da40e92fc04ef8bd5895b4ea8e829d85273c08b0.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a hierarchical framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), enabling efficient level-of-detail rendering of massive scenes. The scene is first subdivided into manageable chunks, each trained independently using an adapted 3DGS optimization that accounts for sparse and large-scale data. For each chunk, a tree-based hierarchy is constructed, merging 3D Gaussian primitives into interior nodes using geometric and appearance-based criteria, and supporting efficient cut selection and smooth transitions between LODs. The method further optimizes the attributes of intermediate nodes in the hierarchy, using a full-resolution, multi-granularity training regime that preserves high-frequency details and enables robust anti-aliasing. After per-chunk optimization, hierarchies are consolidated into a global structure, with redundant nodes pruned and cross-chunk consistency enforced, enabling real-time LOD-based rendering of the entire scene.
da40e92fc04ef8bd5895b4ea8e829d85273c08b0.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on four large-scale datasets, including three newly captured urban and campus scenes (ranging from 5,800 to 38,000 images and up to 7 km in trajectory) and one provided by Wayve. Scenes are subdivided into 4 to 46 chunks, each processed independently and then consolidated. Baseline comparisons include Mip-NeRF360, Instant-NGP, F2-NeRF, Mega-NeRF, and the original 3DGS, with all methods evaluated on single-chunk subsets for fairness. Evaluation metrics include PSNR, LPIPS, and SSIM, measured on held-out test images, and real-time rendering performance (FPS) is reported on an NVIDIA A6000 GPU. Additional ablation studies assess the impact of hierarchy optimization, LOD selection, and chunk-based processing. Qualitative results are supported by free-viewpoint navigation videos, and the method's scalability and resource efficiency are demonstrated by parallel chunk training and real-time rendering of kilometer-scale scenes.
da40e92fc04ef8bd5895b4ea8e829d85273c08b0.novelty_claims: The method introduces the first hierarchical 3D Gaussian representation supporting dynamic level-of-detail rendering for extremely large scenes. It enables divide-and-conquer training and parallel processing of scene chunks, scalable to tens of thousands of images and multi-kilometer trajectories. The approach includes a novel hierarchy construction and optimization scheme that preserves high-frequency details at all levels, robust anti-aliasing, and smooth LOD transitions. The solution is the first to demonstrate real-time rendering of radiance fields at this scale, with resource-adaptive behavior and compatibility with affordable consumer capture rigs. Planned public release of code and large-scale datasets further contributes to the field.

da555d3b44dba5a29f47c35affb666e8954b2305.title: LoLCATs: On Low-Rank Linearizing of Large Language Models
da555d3b44dba5a29f47c35affb666e8954b2305.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be efficiently linearized to achieve subquadratic attention mechanisms while preserving model quality, minimizing parameter and token update requirements, and scaling to very large model sizes?
da555d3b44dba5a29f47c35affb666e8954b2305.hypothesis: By explicitly training linear attention mechanisms to approximate softmax attention outputs via attention transfer, followed by minimal low-rank adaptation (LoRA), it is possible to efficiently linearize LLMs with minimal loss in quality, significant reductions in computational and memory requirements, and scalability to very large models.
da555d3b44dba5a29f47c35affb666e8954b2305.proposed_method: The proposed method, LoLCATs (Low-rank Linear Conversion via Attention Transfer), consists of a two-step framework. First, each softmax attention layer in a pretrained LLM is replaced with a parameterized linear attention analog, trained to closely approximate the original softmax attention outputs using a mean squared error (MSE) loss on the attention outputs (attention transfer). The feature maps for linear attention are learnable and can be hybridized with sliding window attention to improve approximation quality. Second, after swapping in the trained linear attention layers, only low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is applied to the new attention projections, updating a small fraction of parameters to recover any residual quality loss via next-token prediction. For large models, attention transfer is performed in a block-wise fashion, training small groups of layers independently to manage memory and computational costs. The entire process is designed to be highly parameter- and token-efficient, requiring only a small subset of the model's parameters and a modest number of training tokens.
da555d3b44dba5a29f47c35affb666e8954b2305.experiment_details: Experiments will linearize strong base LLMs such as Llama 3 8B, Mistral 7B, and scale up to Llama 3.1 70B and 405B. The attention transfer step will be trained on a small, cleaned Alpaca dataset (50K samples, ~40M tokens), with evaluation on standard zero-shot and few-shot LM Evaluation Harness tasks, including PiQA, ARC-e, ARC-c, HellaSwag, Winogrande, and MMLU (5-shot). Baselines will include prior linearization methods (e.g., SUPRA, Mamba, Hedgehog), pretrained subquadratic models (RWKV, Mamba, Griffin, StripedHyena, Zamba), and original Transformer models. Evaluation metrics will include validation perplexity, accuracy on LM Eval tasks, and resource efficiency (parameter and token updates, memory, and training time). Generation throughput and memory usage will also be benchmarked against FlashAttention-2. Ablation studies will assess the impact of attention transfer, hybrid attention architectures, and block-wise training.
da555d3b44dba5a29f47c35affb666e8954b2305.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a simple yet highly effective two-step linearization framework that achieves state-of-the-art quality for linearized LLMs with orders-of-magnitude improvements in parameter and token efficiency. It is the first method to successfully linearize LLMs at the 70B and 405B scale, closing the quality gap with original Transformers by over 77% on challenging benchmarks. The method uniquely combines explicit attention output matching (attention transfer) with minimal low-rank adaptation, and introduces hybrid linear + sliding window attention layers for improved expressivity. Block-wise attention transfer enables practical scalability to very large models, and the method achieves substantial improvements in generation throughput and memory efficiency compared to both prior linearization approaches and standard Transformer inference.

da55dae285d8a71752accb00cb4ce1b41bc647eb.title: Measuring and Enhancing Trustworthiness of LLMs in RAG through Grounded Attributions and Learning to Refuse
da55dae285d8a71752accb00cb4ce1b41bc647eb.research_question: How can the trustworthiness of large language models (LLMs) in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems be effectively measured and enhanced, particularly with respect to grounding responses in retrieved documents and learning to refuse when information is insufficient?
da55dae285d8a71752accb00cb4ce1b41bc647eb.hypothesis: Aligning LLMs using a dataset that explicitly targets grounding errors and refusal behaviors, and optimizing with direct preference optimization, will significantly improve their trustworthiness in RAG settings as measured by a holistic metric that accounts for answer correctness, citation groundedness, and refusal capability.
da55dae285d8a71752accb00cb4ce1b41bc647eb.proposed_method: A new holistic metric, TRUST-SCORE, will be developed to evaluate LLMs in RAG by measuring grounded refusals, answer correctness, and grounded citations, thus isolating LLM performance from retriever quality. To enhance LLM trustworthiness, an alignment method called TRUST-ALIGN will be introduced. TRUST-ALIGN involves constructing a 19K-sample alignment dataset containing diverse question-document pairs, each annotated with positive (grounded or correct refusal) and negative (hallucinated or inappropriate) responses, covering multiple hallucination types such as inaccurate answers, over-responsiveness, excessive refusal, over-citation, and improper citation. The alignment dataset will be curated by collecting high-quality questions, retrieving relevant and irrelevant documents, generating positive responses with gold claims and citations (using models like GPT-4), and mining hard negative responses from fine-tuned LLMs exhibiting hallucinations. The final model alignment will be performed using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) on the constructed dataset.
da55dae285d8a71752accb00cb4ce1b41bc647eb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard RAG evaluation datasets, including ASQA, QAMPARI, and ELI5, with additional out-of-domain evaluation on ExpertQA. The evaluation will use the TRUST-SCORE metric, which aggregates F1 scores for grounded refusals, answer correctness, and citation groundedness. Baselines will include prompting-based methods (ICL), post-hoc citation and attribution frameworks (PostCite, PostAttr), self-retrieval approaches (Self-RAG), and fine-grained attribution models (FRONT). Both open-weight model families (LLaMA, Qwen, Phi3.5) and closed-source models (GPT-4, Claude-3.5) will be compared, with models evaluated before and after TRUST-ALIGN alignment. Key experimental factors include ablation studies on hallucination types, comparison of DPO versus SFT training, and analysis of parametric knowledge reliance. Evaluation metrics will include TRUST-SCORE and its components, as well as responsiveness and out-of-domain generalization.
da55dae285d8a71752accb00cb4ce1b41bc647eb.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces TRUST-SCORE, a holistic and consolidated metric that comprehensively evaluates LLM trustworthiness in RAG by isolating LLM performance from retriever influence and jointly measuring answer correctness, citation groundedness, and refusal capability. TRUST-ALIGN is a novel alignment approach that systematically targets multiple hallucination types and refusal behaviors via a curated preference dataset and DPO, enabling substantial improvements in groundedness and trustworthiness across diverse model families and sizes. The approach is claimed to outperform leading baselines in nearly all configurations, generalize across domains, and close the performance gap with major closed-source models.

da90a5ea13e02ca9c4a92f18560afb7478cc269e.title: Long-Tail Learning with Foundation Model: Heavy Fine-Tuning Hurts
da90a5ea13e02ca9c4a92f18560afb7478cc269e.research_question: How can long-tail learning performance be improved when leveraging foundation models, and what is the impact of fine-tuning strategies on head and tail class accuracy in highly imbalanced datasets?
da90a5ea13e02ca9c4a92f18560afb7478cc269e.hypothesis: Heavy fine-tuning of foundation models leads to performance deterioration on tail classes due to distributional inconsistencies, whereas lightweight fine-tuning can achieve better generalization and balanced accuracy across head and tail classes.
da90a5ea13e02ca9c4a92f18560afb7478cc269e.proposed_method: A new long-tail learning framework, LIghtweight Fine-Tuning (LIFT), will be developed to address class imbalance by adaptively fine-tuning only a small proportion of the foundation model's parameters. The method will employ structured lightweight fine-tuning strategies, such as masking a subset of weights or integrating parameter-efficient modules (e.g., adapters, prompt tuning, LoRA), to optimize feature representations while preserving intra-class distributions. LIFT will introduce a semantic-aware classifier initialization using textual prompts from the foundation model's text encoder, ensuring robust starting points for optimization. The approach will further incorporate a cosine classifier with logit-adjusted loss to mitigate class imbalance, and employ test-time ensembling by aggregating predictions from perturbed input versions to enhance generalization.
da90a5ea13e02ca9c4a92f18560afb7478cc269e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard long-tail benchmarks, including ImageNet-LT, Places-LT, iNaturalist2018, and CIFAR-100-LT, covering a range of class imbalance scenarios. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, such as full fine-tuning, classifier-only fine-tuning, and other lightweight adaptation techniques (BitFit, Adapter, VPT, LoRA, AdaptFormer). Evaluation metrics will include overall accuracy, as well as accuracy on head, medium, and tail class splits. The experimental setup will control for the number of learnable parameters, training epochs, and the use of external data, with LIFT targeting convergence in fewer than 20 epochs and minimal parameter updates.
da90a5ea13e02ca9c4a92f18560afb7478cc269e.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a systematic analysis of fine-tuning granularity in foundation models for long-tail learning, revealing that heavy fine-tuning can harm tail class performance. LIFT offers a versatile, low-complexity, and accurate approach that achieves state-of-the-art results with significantly reduced computational cost and training time, without requiring external data. Key innovations include adaptive lightweight fine-tuning, semantic-aware classifier initialization leveraging text encoders, and a robust test-time ensembling strategy. The method demonstrates superior performance and efficiency across multiple challenging long-tail datasets.

daaedabad8e668131cb35b6c64553aa627ce580a.title: Navigation-Guided Sparse Scene Representation for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
daaedabad8e668131cb35b6c64553aa627ce580a.research_question: How can end-to-end autonomous driving systems efficiently and effectively represent critical scene information for planning, without relying on expensive supervised perception tasks or dense scene representations?
daaedabad8e668131cb35b6c64553aa627ce580a.hypothesis: A sparse, navigation-guided scene representation using a minimal set of learned tokens, combined with temporal self-supervision, can provide sufficient and efficient scene understanding for end-to-end autonomous driving, outperforming traditional dense or task-specific supervised approaches in both accuracy and computational efficiency.
daaedabad8e668131cb35b6c64553aa627ce580a.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that constructs a sparse scene representation for end-to-end autonomous driving by extracting a small set (e.g., 16) of navigation-guided tokens from dense BEV (Bird's Eye View) features. The method will use a Scenes TokenLearner module, which incorporates navigation commands via a Squeeze-and-Excitation layer to generate navigation-aware BEV features, and then applies spatial attention to compress these into sparse scene tokens. These tokens will serve as the sole input for trajectory planning, replacing traditional dense or task-specific queries. Temporal context will be leveraged through a Future Feature Predictor, which predicts future BEV features based on current scene tokens and planned trajectories, enabling self-supervised learning by aligning predicted and actual future scenes. The overall training objective will combine imitation loss for trajectory prediction and BEV reconstruction loss for scene representation, enabling fully end-to-end, annotation-free learning.
daaedabad8e668131cb35b6c64553aa627ce580a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the nuScenes dataset for open-loop evaluation, using displacement (L2) error and collision rate as primary metrics, with results reported at 1s, 2s, and 3s horizons and both AVG and MAX evaluation protocols. Baselines will include state-of-the-art E2EAD models such as UniAD, VAD-Base, PARA-Drive, GenAD, UAD, LAW, and SparseDrive, with comparisons on both accuracy and inference speed. Closed-loop evaluations will be performed on the CARLA Town05 Long benchmark, using Route Completion, Infraction Score, and Driving Score as metrics. Implementation will use ResNet-50 or ResNet-34 backbones, with BEV features at 100x100 resolution and scene tokens of size 16x256. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the number of scene queries, navigation guidance, and the temporal enhancement module.
daaedabad8e668131cb35b6c64553aa627ce580a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach eliminates the need for any supervised perception sub-tasks or auxiliary annotations, instead learning a sparse, navigation-guided scene representation with as few as 16 tokens. This method introduces a human-inspired attention mechanism that adaptively focuses on navigation-relevant scene elements, drastically reducing computational cost and improving interpretability. The integration of a temporal self-supervision module for future scene prediction further enhances scene understanding without additional labels. The framework claims state-of-the-art performance in both open-loop and closed-loop settings, with significant improvements in accuracy, collision avoidance, and real-time efficiency over existing methods.

dab57fb5af4d1a7bb6d7c2e95827a9e1697d4705.title: Gradient Variance Reveals Failure Modes in Flow-Based Generative Models
dab57fb5af4d1a7bb6d7c2e95827a9e1697d4705.research_question: How does the variance of gradients during training reveal failure modes such as memorization and lack of generalization in flow-based generative models, particularly under deterministic versus stochastic training regimes?
dab57fb5af4d1a7bb6d7c2e95827a9e1697d4705.hypothesis: Deterministic training regimes in flow-based generative models, especially those employing straight-path objectives, induce low gradient variance that leads to memorization of arbitrary training pairings and stagnation, whereas introducing stochasticity (e.g., noise in interpolants) increases gradient variance and promotes generalization toward optimal transport solutions.
dab57fb5af4d1a7bb6d7c2e95827a9e1697d4705.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to analyze the relationship between gradient variance and the quality of learned vector fields in flow-based generative models. The study will focus on both deterministic and stochastic training regimes, examining how the choice of interpolants (noiseless vs. noisy) and pairings (optimal, random, or adversarial) affects the loss landscape and the tendency to memorize training data. Analytical derivations will be performed for Gaussian-to-Gaussian transport, including closed-form expressions for optimal and non-optimal vector fields, and their representability by neural architectures. The methodology will be extended to general finite datasets, with formal proofs characterizing when and why memorization occurs, and how noise disrupts this effect. Empirical experiments will validate theoretical claims by measuring gradient variance, transport error, and memorization across different settings.
dab57fb5af4d1a7bb6d7c2e95827a9e1697d4705.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets (Gaussian and Gaussian mixtures) and the CelebA image dataset. For Gaussian-to-Gaussian transport, both low (d=3) and high (d=50) dimensional settings will be used. Models will be trained using Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) with both deterministic (noiseless) and stochastic (noisy) interpolants. Baselines will include optimal transport pairings, random pairings, and adversarially shuffled pairings. Evaluation metrics will comprise log-likelihood, Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), Sinkhorn distance, and L2 error to both true OT targets and memorized pairings. Additional experiments will simulate iterative rectified flows (e.g., 1-ReFlow) to assess the reinforcement of memorization. Multiple seeds and held-out test sets will be used to ensure statistical robustness, and confidence intervals will be reported where appropriate.
dab57fb5af4d1a7bb6d7c2e95827a9e1697d4705.novelty_claims: The proposed research will provide the first comprehensive theoretical and empirical characterization of how gradient variance exposes memorization and stagnation in flow-based generative models trained with deterministic objectives. It will formally prove that deterministic training regimes can lead to exact memorization of training pairings, even when interpolant lines intersect, and that introducing stochasticity in interpolants breaks this effect and restores generalization. The work will challenge prevailing assumptions about the sufficiency of rectification steps in rectified flows, demonstrate the limitations of standard neural parameterizations for optimal transport, and establish gradient variance as a diagnostic tool for identifying suboptimal learning dynamics in generative modeling.

dad15404d372a23b4b3bf9a63b3124693df3c85e.title: A Time Series is Worth 64 Words: Long-term Forecasting with Transformers
dad15404d372a23b4b3bf9a63b3124693df3c85e.research_question: How can Transformer-based models be designed to improve long-term forecasting and self-supervised representation learning for multivariate time series data, while addressing computational efficiency and the ability to capture local semantic information?
dad15404d372a23b4b3bf9a63b3124693df3c85e.hypothesis: Segmenting time series into subseries-level patches and employing a channel-independent Transformer architecture will significantly enhance forecasting accuracy, computational efficiency, and representation learning capabilities compared to existing state-of-the-art models.
dad15404d372a23b4b3bf9a63b3124693df3c85e.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a channel-independent patch time series Transformer (PatchTST) for multivariate time series forecasting and representation learning. Each multivariate time series is decomposed into univariate channels, which are independently processed using a shared Transformer backbone. Input sequences are segmented into patches (subseries-level groups of time steps), which serve as input tokens to the Transformer, reducing the number of tokens and thus the computational and memory complexity quadratically. Instance normalization is applied to each channel before patching, and the patches are projected into a latent space with positional encodings. For self-supervised representation learning, a masked autoencoder strategy is used, where a subset of patches is randomly masked and the model is trained to reconstruct them, enabling the extraction of high-level representations. The model uses mean squared error (MSE) loss for both supervised forecasting and self-supervised reconstruction tasks.
dad15404d372a23b4b3bf9a63b3124693df3c85e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on eight widely used multivariate time series datasets, including Weather, Traffic, Electricity, ILI, and four ETT datasets (ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, ETTm2), each with varying numbers of features and time steps. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art Transformer-based models (FEDformer, Autoformer, Informer, Pyraformer, LogTrans) and a leading non-Transformer model (DLinear). Evaluation metrics will be mean squared error (MSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) for forecasting tasks. Both supervised and self-supervised (masked patch reconstruction) settings will be tested, with ablation studies on patching and channel-independence, as well as transfer learning experiments where models pre-trained on one dataset are fine-tuned on others. The experimental setup will include varying look-back windows and patch configurations to assess scalability and effectiveness.
dad15404d372a23b4b3bf9a63b3124693df3c85e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces two key innovations: (1) patching of time series into subseries-level tokens, which enables the model to capture local semantic information and attend to longer historical contexts with reduced computational cost; and (2) a channel-independent Transformer design, allowing each univariate time series to be processed independently with shared weights, improving both efficiency and forecasting accuracy. The approach demonstrates superior performance over existing baselines in both supervised and self-supervised settings, achieves state-of-the-art results in transfer learning for time series, and provides a scalable foundation for future Transformer-based time series models.

dae169a0fbea50239a87321a3a7ea43c01f31289.title: Predictive Multiplicity in Probabilistic Classification
dae169a0fbea50239a87321a3a7ea43c01f31289.research_question: To what extent do predictions from probabilistic classification models vary across multiple, near-optimal models for a given prediction task, and how can this variation be systematically measured and reported?
dae169a0fbea50239a87321a3a7ea43c01f31289.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that significant predictive multiplicity exists in probabilistic classification tasks, such that near-optimal models can assign substantially different risk estimates to the same individuals, and that this multiplicity is influenced by dataset characteristics such as separability, outliers, and majority-minority structure.
dae169a0fbea50239a87321a3a7ea43c01f31289.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to measure predictive multiplicity in probabilistic classification. This framework will introduce quantitative measures such as the Viable Prediction Range, ambiguity, and discrepancy, which capture the variation in risk estimates assigned by sets of near-optimal models. Optimization-based algorithms, including mixed-integer non-linear programming (MINLP) and outer-approximation methods, will be employed to efficiently and reliably compute these measures for convex empirical risk minimization problems, such as logistic regression with convex regularization. The methodology will allow users to specify what constitutes 'competing' models (via a near-optimality threshold on performance metrics such as loss or AUC) and what constitutes 'conflicting' predictions (via a user-defined deviation threshold). The approach will be applicable to any convex loss function and will be illustrated using logistic regression.
dae169a0fbea50239a87321a3a7ea43c01f31289.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets to analyze the prevalence and characteristics of predictive multiplicity. Synthetic datasets will be used to systematically vary properties such as class separability, outlier position, and majority-minority group structure, allowing for controlled studies of their impact on predictive multiplicity. Real-world experiments will be performed on seven risk assessment datasets from domains such as medicine, lending, and criminal justice. Evaluation metrics will include the Viable Prediction Range, ambiguity, and discrepancy, computed for sets of models within specified near-optimality thresholds (e.g., within 1% or 5% of baseline loss or AUC). Baselines will include standard empirical risk minimization models, and the impact of multiplicity will be analyzed across subgroups (e.g., by class or demographic group) to assess fairness implications.
dae169a0fbea50239a87321a3a7ea43c01f31289.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic framework for measuring predictive multiplicity in probabilistic classification, extending previous work on model multiplicity beyond binary predictions to risk estimates. It provides novel, optimization-based algorithms for efficiently computing multiplicity measures in convex settings, allowing for flexible specification of near-optimality and conflict thresholds. The research also presents the first empirical analysis of how dataset characteristics such as separability, outlier proximity, and group structure influence predictive multiplicity, and demonstrates the disparate impact of multiplicity on marginalized groups. The framework enables more transparent and accountable reporting of model uncertainty in high-stakes decision-making contexts.

db26827a859ab3d63c84d151e6c2356c68560480.title: SCLIP: Rethinking Self-Attention for Dense Vision-Language Inference
db26827a859ab3d63c84d151e6c2356c68560480.research_question: How can vision-language models, specifically CLIP, be adapted to achieve effective zero-shot and open-vocabulary semantic segmentation for dense prediction tasks without extensive fine-tuning or additional parameters?
db26827a859ab3d63c84d151e6c2356c68560480.hypothesis: Modifying the self-attention mechanism in CLIP to better preserve spatial covariant features will resolve spatial misalignment issues and significantly improve its performance on dense prediction tasks such as semantic segmentation, even without additional training or parameters.
db26827a859ab3d63c84d151e6c2356c68560480.proposed_method: A novel adaptation of the CLIP model is proposed by introducing Correlative Self-Attention (CSA) in place of the standard self-attention mechanism within the vision encoder. The CSA mechanism computes attention scores based on pairwise correlations between local visual tokens, using a single projection matrix and leveraging both query-to-query and key-to-key similarities. This architectural change encourages spatially covariant features, allowing each local token to attend more to itself and to semantically similar positions, thus enhancing feature localization and semantic consistency in dense predictions. The adaptation is implemented by replacing the last transformer block's self-attention in a pretrained CLIP ViT-Base/16 encoder with the CSA module, reusing existing projection weights, and requiring no additional parameters or fine-tuning. The approach is designed to be training-free and robust, not relying on post-processing techniques for spatial continuity.
db26827a859ab3d63c84d151e6c2356c68560480.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on eight semantic segmentation benchmarks, including PASCAL VOC 2012, PASCAL Context, Cityscapes, ADE20k, COCO-Stuff, and COCO-Object, as well as variants with and without background categories. The evaluation protocol involves resizing input images to a shorter side of 336 (or 560 for Cityscapes), using sliding window inference, and aligning dense visual features with text embeddings from the CLIP language encoder. Baselines for comparison include original CLIP, MaskCLIP, GroupViT, ReCo, TCL, SegCLIP, and OVSegmentor, with and without post-processing strategies like PAMR. The primary evaluation metric is mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) across all datasets. Experimental setup avoids heavy post-processing to fairly assess the inherent capabilities of the proposed method.
db26827a859ab3d63c84d151e6c2356c68560480.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a minimal yet highly effective architectural modification to CLIP, enabling training-free, parameter-free adaptation for dense prediction tasks. The Correlative Self-Attention mechanism is claimed to resolve spatial misalignment in CLIP, facilitating spatially covariant feature representations crucial for semantic segmentation. The approach achieves substantial improvements in zero-shot mIoU over strong baselines and state-of-the-art methods, validating the transferability of vision-language models to dense prediction without fine-tuning. The method demonstrates that weakly-supervised pretraining with language guidance can serve as a strong foundation for a wide range of downstream vision tasks.

db2aae1bd6e71e7c23716d0eb50d12aa72a0f0f2.title: Driving Into the Future: Multiview Visual Forecasting and Planning with World Model for Autonomous Driving
db2aae1bd6e71e7c23716d0eb50d12aa72a0f0f2.research_question: How can a multiview visual world model be developed to enable high-fidelity forecasting and planning for autonomous driving, improving safety, robustness, and controllability in both standard and out-of-distribution scenarios?
db2aae1bd6e71e7c23716d0eb50d12aa72a0f0f2.hypothesis: A multiview world model that jointly models spatial and temporal dependencies across multiple camera views, augmented with a unified conditional interface and factorized generation for consistency, will enable more accurate visual forecasting and safer, more robust planning for autonomous vehicles, especially in complex and out-of-distribution driving scenarios.
db2aae1bd6e71e7c23716d0eb50d12aa72a0f0f2.proposed_method: A novel multiview world model, Drive-WM, will be constructed using a latent video diffusion framework adapted for high-resolution, multiview video generation. The approach will introduce temporal encoding layers to capture temporal dependencies and multiview encoding layers to facilitate information exchange across camera views, ensuring consistent structure and style. To further enhance multiview consistency, the joint modeling will be factorized such that reference views are generated jointly and stitched views are conditioned on reference views in an autoregressive manner. A unified condition interface will be designed to flexibly incorporate heterogeneous inputs such as images, text, 3D layouts, and ego actions, enabling controllable and context-aware video generation. The world model will be integrated into a tree-based planning pipeline, where imagined futures are evaluated using image-based reward functions derived from perception models and non-vectorized cues, guiding the selection of optimal driving trajectories.
db2aae1bd6e71e7c23716d0eb50d12aa72a0f0f2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the nuScenes dataset, utilizing its six-camera surround-view video and diverse driving scenarios. The model will be trained on the training split and evaluated on the validation split, with images resized to 384x192 and initialized from Stable Diffusion checkpoints. Baselines for comparison will include prior single-view and multiview image/video generation methods (e.g., BEVGen, MagicDrive, DriveGAN, DriveDreamer, BEVControl, LayoutDiffusion, GLIGEN). Evaluation metrics will include FID and FVD for video quality, a novel Key Points Matching (KPM) score for multiview consistency, and controllability metrics such as mAP for 3D object detection and mIoU for segmentation. Planning performance will be assessed using open-loop metrics such as L2 trajectory error and collision rate, with additional experiments on out-of-distribution scenarios and counterfactual event generation. Ablation studies will examine the impact of unified condition interfaces, temporal/view layers, and factorized generation.
db2aae1bd6e71e7c23716d0eb50d12aa72a0f0f2.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first multiview world model capable of generating high-quality, controllable, and consistent multiview videos for autonomous driving. The factorized generation approach significantly enhances spatial consistency across views, addressing a key challenge in multiview video synthesis. The unified conditional interface allows seamless integration of diverse contextual information, improving controllability and flexibility. The integration of the world model into end-to-end planning pipelines enables comprehensive evaluation of imagined futures, leading to safer and more robust autonomous driving, particularly in out-of-distribution and counterfactual scenarios. A novel multiview consistency metric (KPM) is also introduced for quantitative evaluation.

db32da8f3b075d566a73512f4ccc2c95449c75a1.title: MaxMin-RLHF: Alignment with Diverse Human Preferences
db32da8f3b075d566a73512f4ccc2c95449c75a1.research_question: How can language models be aligned with the diverse preferences of human users, rather than being biased toward majority groups or a single aggregated reward signal?
db32da8f3b075d566a73512f4ccc2c95449c75a1.hypothesis: A max-min alignment approach that learns a mixture of reward models for different human sub-populations and optimizes for the minimum utility across these groups will achieve more equitable and effective alignment with diverse human preferences than single-reward RLHF.
db32da8f3b075d566a73512f4ccc2c95449c75a1.proposed_method: A novel alignment framework is proposed that models human preference diversity by learning a mixture of reward functions, each corresponding to a distinct human sub-population. The reward functions are learned via an Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm, which clusters users based on their feedback and iteratively updates the parameters of each group's reward model using maximum likelihood estimation. Once the mixture of reward models is established, a max-min RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) policy optimization is performed, where the policy is updated to maximize the minimum expected reward across all sub-population-specific reward models, inspired by the Egalitarian principle from social choice theory. The policy optimization employs PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) updates, and the overall objective includes a KL-regularization term to control deviation from a reference policy.
db32da8f3b075d566a73512f4ccc2c95449c75a1.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both small-scale (GPT-2) and large-scale (Tulu2-7B) language models. For small-scale experiments, the IMDB movie review dataset is used, with synthetic preference splits to simulate majority and minority user groups (e.g., sentiment vs. conciseness preferences). The models are evaluated on their ability to generate responses that satisfy both majority and minority preferences, using metrics such as sentiment score and conciseness. For large-scale experiments, datasets with simulated user groups and diverse preferences are constructed, and pairwise preference data is collected using GPT-4 as a simulated annotator. Baselines include single-reward RLHF models trained on datasets with varying group ratios (e.g., 1:1, 2:1, 6:1, 10:1 majority:minority). Evaluation metrics include test accuracy on group-specific preferences and pairwise win rates on held-out sets, with performance compared across both majority and minority groups.
db32da8f3b075d566a73512f4ccc2c95449c75a1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first formal impossibility result for aligning language models with diverse human preferences using single-reward RLHF, both theoretically and empirically. It presents a new max-min RLHF framework that explicitly models and optimizes for diversity in human feedback, rather than aggregating all preferences into a single reward. The method leverages an EM-based approach to learn a mixture of reward models and applies a max-min policy optimization objective to ensure equitable alignment across sub-populations. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that this approach achieves more socially fair and effective alignment than existing single-reward RLHF methods, particularly in the presence of minority user groups.

db36d71a93f0da577db779dc65672fe7d4c18ccf.title: Energy-Guided Diffusion Sampling for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning
db36d71a93f0da577db779dc65672fe7d4c18ccf.research_question: How can offline data be leveraged to improve the efficiency and safety of reinforcement learning in scenarios where online data acquisition is expensive, while mitigating the challenges of data distribution shift and compounding errors during online fine-tuning?
db36d71a93f0da577db779dc65672fe7d4c18ccf.hypothesis: Integrating a diffusion model guided by energy functions to generate synthetic samples aligned with the online data distribution will reduce suboptimality and improve empirical performance in offline-to-online reinforcement learning compared to methods that directly reuse offline data or rely solely on online data.
db36d71a93f0da577db779dc65672fe7d4c18ccf.proposed_method: A novel framework, Energy-guided Diffusion Sampling (EDIS), is proposed to address the distribution shift between offline and online data in reinforcement learning. The approach employs a diffusion model trained on the offline dataset to extract prior knowledge, and introduces three energy functions that guide the sampling process to align generated samples with the online state distribution, the current policy's action distribution, and the environment's transition dynamics. The energy functions are learned via contrastive energy prediction using InfoNCE losses, where positive and negative samples are carefully constructed from recent online data and the denoiser's outputs. During online fine-tuning, the diffusion model, guided by the learned energy functions, generates synthetic samples that are used to augment the online dataset, thereby reducing distribution shift and compounding errors. The method is designed to be plug-and-play, allowing integration with existing offline-to-online RL algorithms.
db36d71a93f0da577db779dc65672fe7d4c18ccf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard RL benchmarks from the D4RL suite, including MuJoCo Locomotion, AntMaze Navigation, and Adroit Manipulation environments. The proposed EDIS framework will be implemented on top of baseline offline-to-online RL algorithms such as Cal-QL and IQL. Performance will be evaluated after a fixed number of online fine-tuning steps (e.g., 0.2M steps following 1M offline pre-training), with results averaged over five random seeds. Baselines will include the original algorithms without EDIS, as well as traditional model-based augmentation methods using MLP and diffusion models for transition modeling. Evaluation metrics will consist of normalized return scores, divergence measures (e.g., JS divergence for state distribution, mean squared error for actions and transitions), and ablation studies on the impact of individual energy functions.
db36d71a93f0da577db779dc65672fe7d4c18ccf.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new approach for sample generation in offline-to-online RL by using energy-guided diffusion models to directly generate synthetic samples aligned with the online data distribution. Unlike prior methods that replay offline data or use model-based rollouts, this approach mitigates distribution shift and compounding errors by leveraging energy functions to guide the generative process. Theoretical analysis demonstrates improved suboptimality bounds compared to existing methods, and empirical results show substantial performance gains (e.g., 20% average improvement) across multiple challenging RL benchmarks. The framework is general and can be seamlessly integrated with a variety of existing offline-to-online RL algorithms.

db4ab91d5675c37795e719e997a2827d3d83cd45.title: Towards Reasoning in Large Language Models: A Survey
db4ab91d5675c37795e719e997a2827d3d83cd45.research_question: To what extent are large language models (LLMs) capable of reasoning, and how can their reasoning abilities be effectively improved, elicited, and evaluated across a variety of tasks and benchmarks?
db4ab91d5675c37795e719e997a2827d3d83cd45.hypothesis: Large language models, when equipped with appropriate techniques such as chain-of-thought prompting, rationale engineering, problem decomposition, and hybrid training methods, can exhibit emergent reasoning abilities that approach or mimic certain aspects of human reasoning, but their true reasoning capabilities remain limited and require further enhancement and rigorous evaluation.
db4ab91d5675c37795e719e997a2827d3d83cd45.proposed_method: A comprehensive research program will be established to systematically investigate and improve reasoning in large language models. The approach will involve developing and refining prompting techniques such as chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, rationale engineering (including refinement, exploration, and verification), and problem decomposition strategies. Hybrid methods that combine reasoning-enhanced pretraining or finetuning with advanced prompting will be explored to simultaneously improve model parameters and reasoning utilization. Bootstrapping and self-improving mechanisms will be implemented, enabling models to iteratively refine their own reasoning outputs. The methodology will also include the design of new benchmarks and evaluation metrics that directly assess the quality and validity of reasoning steps, rather than relying solely on end-task accuracy.
db4ab91d5675c37795e719e997a2827d3d83cd45.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of reasoning benchmarks, including arithmetic reasoning datasets (e.g., GSM8K, MathQA, SVAMP), commonsense reasoning tasks (e.g., CSQA, StrategyQA, ARC), symbolic reasoning tasks (e.g., Last Letter Concatenation, CoinFlip), and large-scale multi-task suites such as BIG-bench. Additional synthetic and formal evaluation datasets (e.g., PrOntoQA, FOLIO, ROSCOE) will be used to analyze step-by-step reasoning quality. Baseline comparisons will include standard prompting, fully supervised finetuning, and existing state-of-the-art LLMs. Evaluation metrics will encompass end-task accuracy, semantic alignment, logical inference, and coherence of generated rationales. Experiments will also analyze the effects of model scale, prompt design, rationale diversity, and training data composition on reasoning performance and generalization.
db4ab91d5675c37795e719e997a2827d3d83cd45.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified and systematic investigation into reasoning in LLMs, integrating multiple advanced prompting and training techniques with novel evaluation frameworks that directly assess reasoning steps. The approach aims to move beyond end-task accuracy by developing interpretable, step-wise metrics and synthetic benchmarks for formal reasoning analysis. The research also explores self-improving and bootstrapping mechanisms for reasoning, and addresses the limitations of current benchmarks by proposing more realistic and challenging tasks. This comprehensive methodology is expected to yield new insights into the emergent properties of reasoning in LLMs and inform the design of models and training regimes that better approximate human-like reasoning.

db4cf9f6a653d5c15973e836c800ea47743251ae.title: Prompt Injection attack against LLM-integrated Applications
db4cf9f6a653d5c15973e836c800ea47743251ae.research_question: What are the vulnerabilities and risks associated with prompt injection attacks in real-world LLM-integrated applications, and how can a systematic, black-box attack methodology be developed to assess and exploit these vulnerabilities across diverse application scenarios?
db4cf9f6a653d5c15973e836c800ea47743251ae.hypothesis: A systematic, black-box prompt injection attack methodology, inspired by traditional web injection techniques and leveraging dynamic context inference, can effectively identify and exploit prompt injection vulnerabilities in a wide range of LLM-integrated applications, even in the absence of internal system knowledge.
db4cf9f6a653d5c15973e836c800ea47743251ae.proposed_method: A novel black-box prompt injection attack framework, HOUYI, will be developed to systematically analyze and exploit vulnerabilities in LLM-integrated applications. The methodology consists of three core phases: (1) Context Inference, where the system interacts with the target application to infer its internal prompt structure and input-output relationships using a custom LLM; (2) Payload Generation, which constructs injection prompts composed of three components—a Framework Component that mimics normal user interaction, a Separator Component that disrupts the semantic connection between preset prompts and user input, and a Disruptor Component containing the malicious payload; and (3) Feedback-driven Iterative Refinement, where the effectiveness of each attack is evaluated and the prompt components are dynamically adjusted to maximize success. The approach leverages generative LLMs for both context analysis and prompt construction, and incorporates strategies inspired by SQL/XSS injection, language switching, and semantic manipulation to bypass application-specific defenses.
db4cf9f6a653d5c15973e836c800ea47743251ae.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 36 real-world LLM-integrated applications, selected for their diversity in domain and architecture, and verified for LLM integration and accessibility. Five distinct exploit scenarios will be tested per application, including prompt leaking, code generation, content manipulation, spam generation, and information gathering. Each attack will be executed five times to account for LLM output variability, and results will be manually verified for success. Baseline comparisons will include existing prompt injection techniques (direct injection, escape characters, context ignoring) applied to a subset of applications. Evaluation metrics will include attack success rate per scenario, number of vulnerable applications detected, and qualitative analysis of application-specific defenses and failure cases. Responsible disclosure protocols will be followed for all identified vulnerabilities.
db4cf9f6a653d5c15973e836c800ea47743251ae.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic, black-box prompt injection attack methodology tailored for LLM-integrated applications, drawing direct inspiration from traditional web injection attacks. Key innovations include a dynamic context inference phase that does not require internal system access, a modular prompt construction strategy that adapts to application-specific contexts, and an iterative feedback mechanism for optimizing attack efficacy. The approach demonstrates high versatility and effectiveness across diverse real-world applications, revealing previously unknown vulnerabilities and providing actionable insights for both attackers and defenders in the LLM application ecosystem.

db5cb5354d8c1ff9cccf2a1c9ef5c218c9323cc1.title: TimeXer: Empowering Transformers for Time Series Forecasting with Exogenous Variables
db5cb5354d8c1ff9cccf2a1c9ef5c218c9323cc1.research_question: How can time series forecasting models be enhanced to effectively utilize exogenous variables, capturing both intra-series temporal dependencies and inter-series correlations, in order to improve forecasting accuracy and robustness in real-world scenarios where exogenous data may be irregular, misaligned, or incomplete?
db5cb5354d8c1ff9cccf2a1c9ef5c218c9323cc1.hypothesis: A Transformer-based forecasting model that separately embeds endogenous and exogenous variables—using patch-wise representations for endogenous and variate-wise representations for exogenous variables, bridged by a learnable global token and leveraging both self-attention and cross-attention—will enable more accurate and robust forecasting of endogenous variables, especially in the presence of irregular, misaligned, or heterogeneous exogenous data.
db5cb5354d8c1ff9cccf2a1c9ef5c218c9323cc1.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that empowers the canonical Transformer architecture for time series forecasting with exogenous variables, without requiring architectural modifications. Endogenous variables will be embedded using patch-wise representations, where the time series is divided into non-overlapping patches and each patch is projected into a temporal token. Exogenous variables will be embedded at the variate level, with each exogenous series mapped to a single variate token, allowing the model to handle arbitrary irregularities such as missing values, misaligned timestamps, and frequency mismatches. A learnable global token will be introduced for each endogenous variable, serving as a bridge to aggregate and propagate information between endogenous temporal patches and exogenous variate tokens. The model will employ patch-wise self-attention to capture temporal dependencies within the endogenous series, and variate-wise cross-attention to integrate relevant information from exogenous variables into the endogenous representation. The final prediction will be generated via a linear projection of the output embeddings, and the model will be trained using squared loss (L2) between predictions and ground truth.
db5cb5354d8c1ff9cccf2a1c9ef5c218c9323cc1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on twelve real-world time series forecasting benchmarks, including five short-term electricity price forecasting datasets (EPF) with exogenous variables and seven public long-term multivariate forecasting datasets. The model will be compared against a comprehensive set of state-of-the-art baselines, including Transformer-based models (iTransformer, PatchTST, Crossformer, Autoformer), CNN-based models (TimesNet, SCINet), linear models (RLinear, DLinear), and advanced exogenous-variable forecasters (TiDE, TFT, NBEATSx). Evaluation metrics will include Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). Experimental setups will follow standard protocols for each dataset, with input and prediction lengths specified according to established benchmarks. Additional experiments will assess the model's robustness to missing values, scalability to large datasets, and adaptability to mismatched look-back lengths between endogenous and exogenous series. Ablation studies will be performed to analyze the contributions of embedding strategies and attention mechanisms.
db5cb5354d8c1ff9cccf2a1c9ef5c218c9323cc1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified Transformer-based framework that explicitly models exogenous and endogenous variables at different granularities, using patch-wise and variate-wise embeddings, respectively. The design of a learnable global token as a bridge between endogenous and exogenous information is novel and enables effective integration of causal and contextual information. The method is general, requiring no architectural changes to the canonical Transformer, and is robust to practical challenges such as missing values, temporal misalignment, frequency mismatch, and series heterogeneity. The framework demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across diverse benchmarks, and exhibits notable scalability and efficiency advantages over existing methods.

db614435aac0b9d9c26ff3d2c4e7453bcecc91eb.title: UniRelight: Learning Joint Decomposition and Synthesis for Video Relighting
db614435aac0b9d9c26ff3d2c4e7453bcecc91eb.research_question: How can video relighting be achieved from a single image or video input, with high visual fidelity and temporal consistency, while generalizing robustly across diverse real-world scenes and complex lighting conditions, despite the scarcity of paired multi-illumination data?
