db614435aac0b9d9c26ff3d2c4e7453bcecc91eb.hypothesis: Jointly modeling scene intrinsic decomposition (e.g., albedo estimation) and relighting synthesis within a single generative diffusion framework enables improved generalization, higher visual fidelity, and better temporal consistency in video relighting, compared to two-stage or end-to-end models trained with limited paired data.
db614435aac0b9d9c26ff3d2c4e7453bcecc91eb.proposed_method: A generative video relighting framework will be developed by fine-tuning a transformer-based video diffusion model (DiT) to jointly predict both the albedo and the relit appearance of an input image or video under a target lighting condition. The method encodes the input video, albedo, and relit video into a shared latent space using a pre-trained VAE, concatenating these latents along the temporal dimension to enable cross-modal self-attention and information exchange. Lighting conditions are encoded using multiple complementary representations (LDR panorama, normalized log-intensity, and directional encoding) and concatenated with the relit video latent. A binary condition mask is attached to each frame to indicate conditioning or prediction targets, allowing the model to flexibly handle partial supervision. The model is trained with a denoising score matching objective, optimizing for both relit video and albedo reconstruction, and incorporates classifier-free guidance by randomly dropping conditioning inputs during training.
db614435aac0b9d9c26ff3d2c4e7453bcecc91eb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a combination of a large-scale synthetic video dataset (with 108k videos rendered from 3D scenes with diverse objects, materials, and lighting), the MIT multi-illumination dataset (real-world indoor scenes with 25 lighting conditions), and 150k real-world video clips auto-labeled with albedo maps. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art relighting and intrinsic decomposition methods such as DiLightNet, NeuralGaffer, DiffusionRenderer (with and without Cosmos backbone), and IntrinsicImageDiffusion. Evaluation metrics will comprise PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for both relighting and albedo estimation, with additional user studies to assess perceptual quality. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of joint modeling and the use of real-world auto-labeled data. The SyntheticScenes dataset (unseen during training) and the MIT multi-illumination test set will serve as primary benchmarks, with qualitative and quantitative analyses performed on both indoor and in-the-wild scenes.
db614435aac0b9d9c26ff3d2c4e7453bcecc91eb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a joint generative modeling framework that simultaneously predicts albedo and relit video in a single pass, leveraging cross-modal self-attention for improved scene understanding and generalization. Unlike prior two-stage pipelines, the method avoids explicit G-buffer estimation, reducing error accumulation and enabling the modeling of complex visual effects such as shadows, reflections, transparency, and subsurface scattering. The training strategy uniquely combines fully supervised synthetic data, multi-illumination real-world data, and large-scale auto-labeled real-world videos, significantly enhancing generalization to unseen domains. The approach claims state-of-the-art performance in both visual fidelity and temporal consistency for video relighting, as well as competitive results in intrinsic decomposition.

db633c6b1c286c0386f0078d8a2e6224e03a6227.title: Mistral 7B
db633c6b1c286c0386f0078d8a2e6224e03a6227.research_question: How can a language model with a relatively small parameter count achieve high performance and efficiency across a wide range of natural language processing tasks, including reasoning, mathematics, and code generation, while maintaining practical inference costs and adaptability for real-world applications?
db633c6b1c286c0386f0078d8a2e6224e03a6227.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that incorporating advanced attention mechanisms, such as grouped-query attention (GQA) and sliding window attention (SWA), into a compact transformer-based language model will enable superior performance and efficiency compared to larger open models, without sacrificing versatility or adaptability.
db633c6b1c286c0386f0078d8a2e6224e03a6227.proposed_method: A 7-billion-parameter transformer-based language model will be developed, integrating grouped-query attention (GQA) to accelerate inference and reduce memory requirements, and sliding window attention (SWA) to efficiently handle long sequences with reduced computational cost. The architecture will feature 32 layers, a hidden dimension of 14336, 32 attention heads, and a context length of 8192 tokens, with a window size of 4096 for SWA. A rolling buffer cache will be implemented to further optimize memory usage during inference, and pre-fill with chunking will be used to efficiently process long prompts. The model will be pre-trained on large-scale text corpora and subsequently fine-tuned on instruction-following datasets to enhance generalization and usability for conversational agents.
db633c6b1c286c0386f0078d8a2e6224e03a6227.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the model on a comprehensive suite of benchmarks, including commonsense reasoning (Hellaswag, Winogrande, PIQA, SIQA, OpenbookQA, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, CommonsenseQA), world knowledge (NaturalQuestions, TriviaQA), reading comprehension (BoolQ, QuAC), mathematics (GSM8K, MATH), code generation (HumanEval, MBPP), and aggregated tasks (MMLU, BBH, AGI Eval). Baselines will include Llama 2 (7B and 13B), Llama 1 (34B), and Code-Llama 7B. Evaluation metrics will be task-specific accuracy or pass rates, and all models will be re-evaluated using a unified pipeline to ensure fair comparison. Additional experiments will assess instruction-following performance (MT-Bench, Chatbot Arena) and safety/guardrail enforcement using curated prompt sets, with both automated and human preference evaluations.
db633c6b1c286c0386f0078d8a2e6224e03a6227.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the use of grouped-query attention and sliding window attention in a compact 7B-parameter model, achieving performance that surpasses larger open models (up to 34B parameters) on key benchmarks. The model demonstrates state-of-the-art efficiency, enabling higher throughput and lower memory usage without compromising quality. The architecture supports efficient fine-tuning and robust instruction-following capabilities, and includes mechanisms for enforcing output guardrails and content moderation. The combination of these innovations results in a highly efficient, adaptable, and high-performing language model suitable for a wide range of real-world applications.

db6965ab7ae91e7c81d5dc606861159f83bfd3a4.title: Vector Quantized Models for Planning
db6965ab7ae91e7c81d5dc606861159f83bfd3a4.research_question: How can model-based planning in reinforcement learning be extended to effectively handle stochastic and partially-observable environments, particularly those with large action and observation spaces?
db6965ab7ae91e7c81d5dc606861159f83bfd3a4.hypothesis: Discrete autoencoder-based abstractions of state and action spaces, when combined with a modified Monte Carlo Tree Search algorithm, will enable effective planning in stochastic and partially-observable environments, outperforming existing model-based RL approaches such as MuZero in these settings.
db6965ab7ae91e7c81d5dc606861159f83bfd3a4.proposed_method: A novel planning framework is developed that leverages Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs) to encode sequences of observations and actions into discrete latent variables. The method involves a two-stage training process: first, a state VQVAE is trained to encode future observations into discrete latent variables, and second, a transition model is trained to model the dynamics over these discrete codes. Planning is performed using a stochastic variant of Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) that branches over both agent actions and the discrete latent variables representing possible environment responses. Several variants of the planning path are proposed, including hybrid approaches that interleave actions and latent codes, and pure latent approaches that plan entirely in the discrete latent space. The framework supports planning in environments with partial observability and stochastic transitions by allowing the search to consider multiple possible future outcomes.
db6965ab7ae91e7c81d5dc606861159f83bfd3a4.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in two main domains: a stochastic interpretation of chess (single-player chess, where the opponent is considered part of the environment) and DeepMind Lab, a visually complex 3D environment with partial observability and stochasticity. In chess, models are trained offline using large datasets of human games (MillionBase and FICS Elo>2000), and evaluated by playing against Stockfish, imitation agents, and MuZero baselines, with win/draw rates and performance under varying simulation budgets as metrics. In DeepMind Lab, a large dataset of agent-collected episodes is used to train the models, and evaluation focuses on long-range trajectory prediction using the Mean Best Reconstruction Error (MBRE) metric, comparing the proposed approach to deterministic LSTM and sequential VAE baselines. Key experimental setups include ablation of planning path variants, analysis of simulation budget effects, and assessment of scalability to high-dimensional observations.
db6965ab7ae91e7c81d5dc606861159f83bfd3a4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach generalizes MuZero-style planning to stochastic and partially-observable environments by planning over discrete latent variables learned via VQVAEs, rather than relying on deterministic models or full state observability. The method introduces a stochastic MCTS that can branch over both actions and latent variables, enabling effective planning in environments with large action spaces and uncertain dynamics. The framework supports abstraction in both time and action, allowing for flexible planning horizons and granularity. Empirical results demonstrate superior performance to offline MuZero in stochastic chess and strong predictive capabilities in visually complex, partially-observed environments, highlighting the approach's scalability and generality.

db8b335f5286f9173e4d2315044575f6af9ded68.title: Geometry Informed Tokenization of Molecules for Language Model Generation
db8b335f5286f9173e4d2315044575f6af9ded68.research_question: How can language models be effectively applied to the generation of three-dimensional molecular structures, ensuring geometric invariance and atomic fidelity, and how do such approaches compare to existing state-of-the-art methods in both unconditional and controllable molecule generation tasks?
db8b335f5286f9173e4d2315044575f6af9ded68.hypothesis: A tokenization method that converts 3D molecular geometries into SE(3)-invariant one-dimensional discrete sequences will enable language models to generate valid, diverse, and chemically accurate 3D molecules, outperforming or matching current state-of-the-art generative models, particularly in tasks requiring conditional property control.
db8b335f5286f9173e4d2315044575f6af9ded68.proposed_method: A geometry-informed tokenization framework, Geo2Seq, will be developed to transform 3D molecular structures into SE(3)-invariant 1D discrete sequences suitable for language model processing. The method involves two main steps: (1) canonical labeling of molecular graphs to ensure a unique, isomorphism-invariant node ordering, and (2) conversion of atomic Cartesian coordinates into spherical coordinates relative to an equivariant global frame, ensuring SE(3)-invariance. Each atom is represented by a vector containing its type and spherical coordinates, and all such vectors are concatenated in canonical order to form the sequence. Numerical values are discretized to a fixed precision to enable tokenization, and the resulting vocabulary includes atom types and quantized geometric tokens. The approach is designed to be model-agnostic, allowing integration with various language model architectures.
db8b335f5286f9173e4d2315044575f6af9ded68.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the QM9 and GEOM-DRUGS datasets, which provide diverse 3D molecular structures and properties. Both unconditional (random) and controllable (conditional on molecular properties) generation tasks will be evaluated. Language models such as GPT and Mamba will be trained on Geo2Seq tokenized sequences using next-token prediction objectives. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art 3D molecule generation methods such as E-NFs, G-SchNet, EDM, GDM, EDM-Bridge, and GEOLDM. Evaluation metrics will include atom stability, molecule stability, validity (successful conversion to SMILES), uniqueness, and mean absolute error (MAE) for property-controlled generation. Standardized data splits and hyperparameter settings will be used to ensure fair comparison, and model performance will be assessed over multiple runs.
db8b335f5286f9173e4d2315044575f6af9ded68.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first comprehensive SE(3)-invariant tokenization scheme for 3D molecular geometries, enabling direct application of language models to 3D molecule generation. Geo2Seq provides a bijective mapping between 3D molecular structures and discrete sequences, preserving both geometric and atomic information with minimal information loss. The method is model-agnostic, allowing flexible integration with different language model architectures. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate superior or competitive performance compared to leading diffusion-based and autoregressive 3D generative models, especially in controllable generation tasks, thereby establishing the feasibility and advantages of language models for 3D molecular design.

db916693bc6f0b858b290b5963c8f012f8e8bccd.title: Robustifying State-space Models for Long Sequences via Approximate Diagonalization
db916693bc6f0b858b290b5963c8f012f8e8bccd.research_question: How can state-space models be made more robust and accurate for long-range sequence modeling, particularly in the presence of ill-posed diagonalization problems and input perturbations, while maintaining computational efficiency?
db916693bc6f0b858b290b5963c8f012f8e8bccd.hypothesis: Introducing a backward-stable, perturb-then-diagonalize (PTD) methodology for approximately diagonalizing non-normal matrices in state-space models will improve robustness to input perturbations and potentially enhance accuracy on long-range sequence tasks compared to existing diagonal or diagonal-plus-low-rank initializations.
db916693bc6f0b858b290b5963c8f012f8e8bccd.proposed_method: A new methodology, termed 'perturb-then-diagonalize' (PTD), will be developed to address ill-posed diagonalization problems in state-space models. The approach involves adding a small, carefully chosen perturbation matrix to the original (e.g., HiPPO) state matrix, thereby regularizing the diagonalization problem and making it backward stable. The perturbed matrix is then diagonalized, and the resulting eigenbasis is used to initialize the state-space model. The perturbation matrix will be optimized to balance the condition number of the eigenbasis and the magnitude of the perturbation, formulated as a constrained optimization problem. This method will be instantiated in new S4-PTD and S5-PTD models, which retain the computational efficiency and channel communication benefits of diagonal models while achieving improved robustness.
db916693bc6f0b858b290b5963c8f012f8e8bccd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Long-Range Arena (LRA) benchmark, which includes six tasks with sequence lengths from 1,024 to 16,000, to evaluate the performance of the proposed S4-PTD and S5-PTD models. The models will be compared against established baselines such as S4, S4D, S5, and Liquid-S4, using the same architectures and parameter counts for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy and robustness to input perturbations, particularly those in specific Fourier modes. Additional experiments will include ablation studies on the size of the perturbation matrix and sensitivity analyses using the sequential CIFAR-10 (sCIFAR) dataset, where robustness to Fourier-mode noise will be assessed.
db916693bc6f0b858b290b5963c8f012f8e8bccd.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a generic, backward-stable PTD methodology for approximately diagonalizing non-normal matrices in state-space models, addressing the ill-posedness of diagonalizing HiPPO and similar frameworks. This approach is theoretically grounded in pseudospectral theory and is adaptable to any initialization scheme, not limited to HiPPO. The resulting S4-PTD and S5-PTD models are claimed to achieve improved robustness to input perturbations, particularly in the frequency domain, and to match or exceed the accuracy of existing state-space models on long-range sequence tasks. The method also provides a principled way to optimize the trade-off between numerical stability and fidelity to the original initialization.

db9507cdd3e2d7d9c90ed185bd831e55c62dcec9.title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for On-Device LLM Compression and Acceleration
db9507cdd3e2d7d9c90ed185bd831e55c62dcec9.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be efficiently quantized for on-device deployment to reduce memory and computation requirements while maintaining high accuracy and generalization across diverse domains and modalities?
db9507cdd3e2d7d9c90ed185bd831e55c62dcec9.hypothesis: A small fraction of weights in LLMs are significantly more important than others, and identifying and protecting these salient weights using activation statistics—rather than weight magnitude—enables low-bit quantization with minimal accuracy loss. Furthermore, scaling these salient weight channels prior to quantization can reduce quantization error without the need for backpropagation or reconstruction, resulting in a hardware-friendly and generalizable quantization method.
db9507cdd3e2d7d9c90ed185bd831e55c62dcec9.proposed_method: The proposed method, Activation-aware Weight Quantization (AWQ), introduces a hardware-friendly, low-bit, weight-only quantization framework for LLMs. The approach begins by identifying salient weight channels based on activation distributions collected offline from a small calibration set, rather than relying on weight magnitude. To avoid hardware-inefficient mixed-precision quantization, a per-channel scaling transformation is applied to the salient weights, mathematically derived to minimize quantization error. The scaling factors are optimized via a grid search to balance protection of salient and non-salient channels, and weight clipping is used to further minimize mean squared quantization error. AWQ does not require any backpropagation or reconstruction, making it robust to overfitting and broadly applicable to different domains and modalities. Additionally, the method is implemented in an efficient inference framework, TinyChat, which leverages kernel fusion, platform-aware weight packing, and on-the-fly dequantization to maximize real-world speedup on edge devices.
db9507cdd3e2d7d9c90ed185bd831e55c62dcec9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of LLM architectures, including LLaMA, Llama-2, OPT, Mistral, Mixtral, and instruction-tuned models such as Vicuna, as well as multi-modal models like OpenFlamingo and VILA. Quantization will focus on INT3 and INT4 group-wise weight-only quantization with a group size of 128, using small calibration sets sampled from pre-training datasets (e.g., The Pile). Baselines for comparison include round-to-nearest quantization (RTN) and GPTQ (with and without reordering). Evaluation metrics will include perplexity on language modeling tasks (WikiText-2), accuracy on programming (MBPP) and math (GSM8K) benchmarks, as well as performance on visual-language tasks (COCO Captioning, VQA, GQA, and others). System-level benchmarks will measure inference speedup on edge devices (e.g., NVIDIA RTX 4090, Jetson Orin, Apple M1) using the TinyChat framework. Robustness to calibration set size and distribution will also be evaluated.
db9507cdd3e2d7d9c90ed185bd831e55c62dcec9.novelty_claims: The proposed method claims several key innovations: (1) a principled, activation-aware approach to identifying and protecting salient weights for quantization, (2) a mathematically derived per-channel scaling transformation that reduces quantization error without mixed-precision or backpropagation, (3) a hardware-friendly implementation that generalizes across domains and modalities, including instruction-tuned and multi-modal LLMs, (4) a highly data-efficient quantization process requiring minimal calibration data, and (5) a practical, open-source inference framework (TinyChat) that translates theoretical memory savings into measurable speedup on diverse edge platforms. AWQ is also claimed to be the first method to enable lossless low-bit quantization of multi-modal LLMs and to demonstrate robust generalization without overfitting to the calibration set.

dbb70b8f0f82056091f8670d8b2492088343d3ae.title: Gradient-based Explanations for Deep Learning Survival Models
dbb70b8f0f82056091f8670d8b2492088343d3ae.research_question: How can gradient-based explanation methods be systematically extended and adapted to provide accurate, time-dependent, and interpretable feature attributions for deep learning survival models, particularly in settings with multi-modal data such as medical images and tabular features?
dbb70b8f0f82056091f8670d8b2492088343d3ae.hypothesis: Gradient-based explanation methods, when formally extended to survival neural networks and adapted for time-dependent outcomes, will provide more accurate, efficient, and interpretable local and global feature attributions than existing model-agnostic approaches, enabling improved transparency and actionable insights for deep learning survival models.
dbb70b8f0f82056091f8670d8b2492088343d3ae.proposed_method: A formal framework will be developed to generalize gradient-based feature attribution methods—including Saliency (Grad), SmoothGrad, Gradient×Input, Integrated Gradients, and a novel GradSHAP(t)—to survival neural networks. These methods will be adapted to handle time-dependent prediction outcomes, enabling attribution computation at each discretized time point for functional outputs such as survival probability, hazard, or cumulative hazard. The approach will include the design of effective visualizations to capture the temporal dynamics of feature contributions and will address the challenge of selecting appropriate baselines for multi-modal data (e.g., tabular and image features). GradSHAP(t) will be introduced as a model-specific, gradient-based approximation of SHAP values, leveraging expectations over reference distributions to provide stable and unbiased attributions. The methodology will be implemented in a toolkit compatible with modern deep learning libraries and designed for practical use in medical and other high-stakes domains.
dbb70b8f0f82056091f8670d8b2492088343d3ae.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both simulated and real-world datasets. Synthetic data will be generated using standard survival models (e.g., Cox proportional hazards and Weibull models) with controlled time-independent and time-dependent feature effects, allowing for ground-truth comparison. Deep learning survival models such as DeepSurv, CoxTime, and DeepHit will be trained on these datasets. The proposed gradient-based methods will be compared to established baselines, including SurvSHAP(t) and SurvLIME, in terms of local accuracy (decomposition error), computational efficiency (runtime), and global feature importance rankings. Evaluation metrics will include normalized decomposition error, computation time as a function of feature dimensionality, and alignment with known feature effects. Additionally, the methods will be applied to a real multi-modal medical dataset (e.g., TCGA glioma survival data with tabular and histopathological image inputs), using a CNN-based DeepHit model, to demonstrate interpretability and visualization of temporal feature effects in a clinically relevant context.
dbb70b8f0f82056091f8670d8b2492088343d3ae.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to provide systematic, time-dependent gradient-based explanations for deep learning survival models, including those with multi-modal inputs such as images and tabular data. GradSHAP(t) introduces a novel, model-specific, and computationally efficient alternative to sample-based SHAP methods for survival analysis, offering improved scalability and accuracy. The approach enables detailed visualization of temporal dynamics in feature attributions, supporting both local (individual-level) and global (population-level) interpretability. The methodology is designed to bridge the gap between the predictive power of deep learning survival models and the need for transparency in high-stakes domains such as personalized medicine.

dc0c132b273456b288a785414db2fa72edf87b1a.title: BLIP-Diffusion: Pre-trained Subject Representation for Controllable Text-to-Image Generation and Editing
dc0c132b273456b288a785414db2fa72edf87b1a.research_question: How can subject-driven text-to-image generation and editing be made more controllable, efficient, and generalizable, enabling high-fidelity image synthesis from both subject images and text prompts with minimal fine-tuning or in zero-shot settings?
dc0c132b273456b288a785414db2fa72edf87b1a.hypothesis: A diffusion-based text-to-image generation model equipped with a pre-trained, generic, multimodal subject representation will enable efficient, high-fidelity, and controllable subject-driven image generation and editing, outperforming existing methods in both zero-shot and fine-tuning scenarios.
dc0c132b273456b288a785414db2fa72edf87b1a.proposed_method: A new framework is developed that integrates a pre-trained multimodal encoder (adapted from BLIP-2) with a latent diffusion model (e.g., Stable Diffusion). The method employs a two-stage pre-training strategy: first, multimodal representation learning aligns visual and textual features using large-scale image-text pairs and multiple vision-language objectives (contrastive, generation, and matching losses). Second, subject representation learning is performed by synthesizing training pairs where the subject is composited onto random backgrounds, encouraging the model to disentangle subject appearance from context. The multimodal encoder produces a subject representation from an input image and category text, which is then projected and appended to text prompt embeddings, guiding the diffusion model for subject-driven generation. The architecture supports both zero-shot generation and rapid fine-tuning for new subjects, and is designed to be compatible with structure-control and editing techniques such as ControlNet and prompt-to-prompt.
dc0c132b273456b288a785414db2fa72edf87b1a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using large-scale datasets for pre-training, including 129M image-text pairs (from LAION, COCO, Visual Genome, and Conceptual Captions) for multimodal representation learning, and 292K subject-centric images from OpenImage-V6 for subject representation learning, with 59K background images for synthetic composition. The model is evaluated on the DreamBooth dataset (30 subjects, 4-7 images each) and DreamBench, using metrics such as DINO and CLIP-I (for subject alignment) and CLIP-T (for image-text alignment). Baselines include Textual Inversion, DreamBooth, Re-Imagen, and InstructPix2Pix. Both zero-shot and fine-tuning scenarios are tested, with fine-tuning requiring only 40-120 steps (20-40 seconds on a single A100 GPU). Additional experiments demonstrate compatibility with ControlNet for structure-controlled generation and prompt-to-prompt for subject-driven editing. Ablation studies assess the impact of pre-training stages and architectural choices.
dc0c132b273456b288a785414db2fa72edf87b1a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first subject-driven text-to-image diffusion model with a pre-trained, generic, multimodal subject representation, enabling both zero-shot and highly efficient fine-tuning for new subjects. The two-stage pre-training strategy allows for disentanglement of subject and context, supporting faithful and flexible control via both images and text. The architecture maintains compatibility with advanced generative techniques (e.g., ControlNet, prompt-to-prompt) without additional training. Experimental results demonstrate up to 20x speedup in fine-tuning compared to prior methods, superior zero-shot generation, and strong subject fidelity and prompt relevance, establishing the method as a foundation for multimodal controllable image generation and editing.

dc0d5f7b8bb3860fb8254151f70f705e17429009.title: Evaluating LLM-Contaminated Crowdsourcing Data Without Ground Truth
dc0d5f7b8bb3860fb8254151f70f705e17429009.research_question: How can the quality of human-contributed crowdsourcing data be reliably evaluated and potential misuse of large language models (LLMs) by crowd workers be detected, especially in the absence of ground truth and in structured annotation tasks such as multiple-choice labeling?
dc0d5f7b8bb3860fb8254151f70f705e17429009.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a scoring mechanism based on conditional correlations between worker responses, while conditioning on LLM-generated labels available to the requester, can robustly distinguish between high-effort human responses and low-effort or LLM-assisted responses, even without access to ground truth.
dc0d5f7b8bb3860fb8254151f70f705e17429009.proposed_method: A novel, training-free scoring mechanism is proposed that extends the peer prediction framework to address LLM contamination in crowdsourcing annotation tasks. The method, termed the conditioned Correlated Agreement (CA) mechanism, scores each agent by measuring the correlation between their responses and those of their peers, conditioned on a set of LLM-generated labels (cheap signals) available to the requester. The approach involves estimating empirical conditioned joint distributions of agent responses, computing a delta tensor to capture deviations from independence, and defining a scoring function based on the sign of these deviations. Bonus and penalty scores are calculated by comparing agent agreement on pairs of questions with identical LLM-generated labels, and the final score is averaged across all such pairs and label conditions. Theoretical analysis establishes conditions under which the mechanism is information monotone, ensuring that truthful, high-effort reporting is incentivized and reliably detected.
dc0d5f7b8bb3860fb8254151f70f705e17429009.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using real-world crowdsourcing datasets, including a toxicity labeling dataset (with 3459 social media comments labeled by MTurk workers) and a preference alignment dataset (with over 10,000 LLM response comparisons labeled by crowd workers and experts). LLM-generated responses from multiple popular models (e.g., GPT-4) will be used to simulate cheap signals. The method's effectiveness will be evaluated by simulating mixed crowds with varying proportions of low-effort agents (LLM-reliant, random, and biased), and comparing the ability of the proposed mechanism to detect these agents against several baselines: Output Agreement, standard Correlated Agreement, Expectation-Maximization under the Dawid-Skene model, and a conditioned Output Agreement variant. The area under the ROC curve (AUC) will serve as the primary evaluation metric, and robustness will be assessed across different agent compositions and LLMs. Additional analyses will examine the impact of the number of LLM-labeled questions and uncertainty about which LLMs are used by agents.
dc0d5f7b8bb3860fb8254151f70f705e17429009.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a theoretically grounded, training-free scoring mechanism for evaluating crowdsourcing data quality in the presence of LLM contamination, specifically tailored for structured annotation tasks without ground truth. It generalizes existing peer prediction mechanisms by conditioning on observable LLM-generated signals, provides theoretical guarantees of information monotonicity under both general and practical (lazy-reporting) cheating strategies, and empirically demonstrates robust performance in detecting low-effort agents across diverse datasets and LLM scenarios. The approach is claimed to be more robust than traditional baselines, particularly as the proportion of LLM-reliant agents increases, and is adaptable to both categorical and, heuristically, open-ended textual data.

dc1f10d926b2f7fae5f7c643b2064de69711bd57.title: SurroundOcc: Multi-Camera 3D Occupancy Prediction for Autonomous Driving
dc1f10d926b2f7fae5f7c643b2064de69711bd57.research_question: How can dense and accurate 3D occupancy of real-world scenes be predicted using only multi-camera images, in a way that generalizes to arbitrary object shapes and classes for autonomous driving applications?
dc1f10d926b2f7fae5f7c643b2064de69711bd57.hypothesis: A multi-camera vision-based approach utilizing 2D-3D spatial attention and a novel dense occupancy ground truth generation pipeline can achieve superior 3D occupancy prediction performance compared to existing methods relying on sparse LiDAR supervision or BEV-based representations.
dc1f10d926b2f7fae5f7c643b2064de69711bd57.proposed_method: A new framework is developed for multi-camera 3D occupancy prediction. The approach begins by extracting multi-scale features from each camera image using a 2D backbone network (e.g., ResNet-101 or EfficientNetB7 with FPN). These features are lifted to 3D volumetric space using a 2D-3D spatial attention mechanism based on deformable attention, which projects 3D reference points into 2D views and aggregates information from relevant image regions. The resulting 3D volume features are progressively upsampled and fused via a 3D convolutional U-Net-like architecture, with multi-scale skip connections to preserve both high- and low-level details. Supervision is imposed at multiple levels using a decayed weighted loss. To enable dense occupancy prediction, a pipeline is designed to generate dense ground truth by fusing multi-frame LiDAR scans of dynamic objects and static scenes, applying Poisson surface reconstruction to fill holes, voxelizing the resulting mesh, and assigning semantic labels via nearest neighbor search.
dc1f10d926b2f7fae5f7c643b2064de69711bd57.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the nuScenes and SemanticKITTI datasets. For nuScenes, the model is trained and validated on the provided splits, with a 3D occupancy prediction range of [-50m, 50m] for X/Y and [-5m, 3m] for Z, and a voxel size of 0.5m (output shape: 200x200x16). For SemanticKITTI, the model is evaluated on the test set with a 256x256x32 grid and 0.2m voxel size. Baselines include MonoScene, Atlas, BEVFormer, TPVFormer, and state-of-the-art depth estimation and 3D reconstruction methods. Evaluation metrics include IoU and mIoU for semantic occupancy, as well as Chamfer Distance and F-score for 3D scene reconstruction. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of spatial attention, multi-scale structure, and dense supervision. Model efficiency (inference time and memory) is also benchmarked.
dc1f10d926b2f7fae5f7c643b2064de69711bd57.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel 2D-3D spatial attention mechanism for fusing multi-camera image features directly into 3D volumetric space, preserving geometric consistency and enabling prediction of occluded regions. A new pipeline for generating dense 3D occupancy ground truth from sparse LiDAR and existing annotations is developed, leveraging multi-frame fusion, Poisson reconstruction, and semantic label propagation. The approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on both multi-camera and monocular 3D semantic scene completion and reconstruction benchmarks, and demonstrates significant improvements in occupancy density and accuracy over prior methods. The framework is also efficient and extensible to downstream 3D tasks.

dc4c9ae8c0cfc08ff6392aff69b0fd170da398a4.title: FoundationPose: Unified 6D Pose Estimation and Tracking of Novel Objects
dc4c9ae8c0cfc08ff6392aff69b0fd170da398a4.research_question: How can a unified framework be developed for 6D object pose estimation and tracking that generalizes to novel objects in both model-based (CAD model available) and model-free (reference images available) scenarios, supporting efficient and accurate performance across diverse datasets and challenging real-world conditions?
dc4c9ae8c0cfc08ff6392aff69b0fd170da398a4.hypothesis: A unified neural implicit representation, trained on large-scale, LLM-aided synthetic data with transformer-based architectures and contrastive learning, will enable instant and robust 6D pose estimation and tracking of novel objects in both model-based and model-free setups, outperforming specialized state-of-the-art methods without requiring instance-level fine-tuning.
dc4c9ae8c0cfc08ff6392aff69b0fd170da398a4.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a unified framework for 6D pose estimation and tracking that supports both model-based (using a given CAD model) and model-free (using a small set of reference images) setups. The approach leverages a neural implicit object-centric representation based on signed distance fields (SDF) for efficient and high-quality novel view RGBD rendering, bridging the gap between the two setups. Large-scale synthetic training data is generated using a pipeline that combines 3D model databases, large language models (LLMs) for automatic prompt generation, and diffusion models for realistic texture augmentation. The pose estimation pipeline consists of global pose initialization (sampling and augmenting poses), a transformer-based pose refinement network that iteratively improves pose hypotheses, and a hierarchical pose selection module using a two-level transformer-based comparison and a pose-conditioned contrastive loss for robust hypothesis ranking. The same downstream modules are used for both estimation and tracking, with tracking leveraging temporal cues for efficiency.
dc4c9ae8c0cfc08ff6392aff69b0fd170da398a4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five public datasets: LINEMOD, Occluded-LINEMOD, YCB-Video, T-LESS, and YCBInEOAT, covering a range of object properties and scene complexities. Both model-based and model-free setups will be evaluated, with model-free using varying numbers of reference images and model-based using provided CAD models. Baselines will include state-of-the-art methods for each task, such as OnePose++, MegaPose, FS6D, and others, with comparisons made in terms of AUC of ADD and ADD-S, ADD-0.1d recall, and BOP challenge metrics (AR of VSD, MSSD, MSPD). The evaluation will consider both pose estimation and tracking tasks, including robustness to occlusion, textureless objects, and long-term tracking scenarios. Ablation studies will assess the impact of LLM-aided texture augmentation, transformer-based architectures, hierarchical comparison, and training data scale. Inference speed and scalability with respect to reference images and training data size will also be measured.
dc4c9ae8c0cfc08ff6392aff69b0fd170da398a4.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to unify 6D pose estimation and tracking for novel objects in both model-based and model-free scenarios using a single architecture. Key innovations include an object-centric neural implicit representation for efficient RGBD rendering, a scalable LLM-aided synthetic data generation pipeline with realistic texture augmentation, a novel transformer-based network architecture, and a hierarchical contrastive learning formulation for robust pose hypothesis ranking. The method claims strong generalization from synthetic data alone, outperforming specialized state-of-the-art methods across multiple benchmarks and achieving results comparable to instance-level approaches without requiring instance-specific training or fine-tuning.

dc8400e0b90d81438bef2c704785ceba13fc6809.title: Towards High-resolution 3D Anomaly Detection via Group-Level Feature Contrastive Learning
dc8400e0b90d81438bef2c704785ceba13fc6809.research_question: How can anomaly detection in high-resolution 3D point clouds be improved to achieve greater precision and robustness, particularly for industrial applications where anomalies are rare and spatially subtle?
dc8400e0b90d81438bef2c704785ceba13fc6809.hypothesis: Group-level contrastive learning, which simultaneously maximizes inter-cluster feature uniformity and minimizes intra-cluster feature dispersion, combined with adaptive group-center selection based on geometric cues, will significantly improve the accuracy and sensitivity of anomaly detection in high-resolution 3D point clouds.
dc8400e0b90d81438bef2c704785ceba13fc6809.proposed_method: A novel framework, Group3AD, will be developed for high-resolution 3D anomaly detection. The approach begins with group-level feature extraction from input point clouds, followed by clustering these features using K-means with the optimal number of clusters determined by the Elbow Method. The Intercluster Uniformity Network (IUN) will enforce dispersion between clusters in the feature space by maximizing the minimum distance between cluster centers, while the Intracluster Alignment Network (IAN) will minimize the maximum distance between points within each cluster, promoting compactness. During inference, Adaptive Group-Center Selection (AGCS) will be applied, leveraging Fast Point Feature Histogram (FPFH) descriptors to focus sampling density on regions with significant geometric variation, thereby increasing sensitivity to potential anomalies. The overall pipeline integrates these components with a memory bank for efficient anomaly scoring and localization.
dc8400e0b90d81438bef2c704785ceba13fc6809.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Real3D-AD dataset, which contains high-resolution multi-view 3D point clouds of various industrial objects. Evaluation will be performed at both object and point levels using AUROC (Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve) and AUPR (Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve) metrics. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including Reg3D-AD, CPMF, IMRNet, PatchCore, and BTF, under identical experimental settings. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the individual contributions of the IUN, IAN, and AGCS modules. Visualization of feature clustering and anomaly localization will be included to qualitatively validate the effectiveness of the approach.
dc8400e0b90d81438bef2c704785ceba13fc6809.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces group-level contrastive learning for 3D anomaly detection, which is unconstrained by point cloud resolution and enables efficient feature representation even with small sample sizes. The combination of Intercluster Uniformity and Intracluster Alignment networks is novel in enforcing both dispersion and compactness in feature space, directly addressing the anisotropic distribution problem of transformer-based encoders. The Adaptive Group-Center Selection mechanism, based on geometric descriptors, further enhances detection sensitivity by adaptively focusing on regions with potential anomalies. The framework is flexible, scalable, and can be integrated with other architectures, representing a significant advancement over existing high-resolution 3D anomaly detection methods.

dc85180153687539724d20a5927b2fbdf5f8e2a4.title: Fast-R2D2: A Pretrained Recursive Neural Network based on Pruned CKY for Grammar Induction and Text Representation
dc85180153687539724d20a5927b2fbdf5f8e2a4.research_question: How can hierarchical and recursive neural network architectures be efficiently scaled for unsupervised grammar induction and text representation, while improving inference speed and maintaining or improving performance on downstream NLP tasks?
dc85180153687539724d20a5927b2fbdf5f8e2a4.hypothesis: A recursive neural network architecture that leverages a fast, model-guided top-down parser for global pruning can significantly reduce inference time and memory complexity, while achieving competitive or superior results in grammar induction and downstream classification tasks compared to existing chart-based and sequential Transformer models.
dc85180153687539724d20a5927b2fbdf5f8e2a4.proposed_method: A unified recursive neural network architecture is proposed, combining a top-down unsupervised parser with a chart-based CKY encoder. The top-down parser scores all possible split points in a sentence using a bidirectional LSTM, enabling parallel computation of split scores. Parsing is cast as a split point scoring task, where the highest-scoring split recursively divides spans, and the reverse order of splits determines the merge order for CKY pruning. The parser is optimized by minimizing the Kullback–Leibler divergence between tree probabilities from the parser and the CKY encoder, using a Monte Carlo sampling approach inspired by URNNG. The pretraining objective combines bidirectional masked language modeling with KL divergence minimization, and the architecture supports both forced encoding and model-guided pruning for efficient parallel inference.
dc85180153687539724d20a5927b2fbdf5f8e2a4.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on large-scale English (WikiText103) and Chinese (Wikipedia, CTB 8.0) corpora for unsupervised grammar induction, with fine-tuning on the Penn Treebank (PTB) and Chinese Treebank (CTB) datasets. Baselines include StructFormer, Ordered Neurons, URNNG, DIORA, C-PCFG, and R2D2, with evaluations using sentence-level unlabeled F1 and constituent recall metrics. Downstream tasks are evaluated on GLUE benchmark datasets (SST-2, CoLA, QQP, MNLI), comparing against BERT models of similar parameter size. Inference speed is measured across varying sequence lengths, and ablation studies assess the impact of different components and training objectives. All models are trained and evaluated using standardized splits, with hyperparameters and batch sizes controlled for fair comparison.
dc85180153687539724d20a5927b2fbdf5f8e2a4.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a globally optimized, model-guided pruning strategy for recursive neural networks, enabling parallel encoding and significantly faster inference (30-50x speedup) compared to previous chart-based approaches. The architecture jointly pretrains a parser and encoder in linear memory cost, achieving superior or competitive results in grammar induction and downstream tasks relative to both recursive and sequential Transformer baselines. The approach provides interpretable intermediate representations and demonstrates higher parameter efficiency, offering a scalable and practical alternative to conventional sequential models for hierarchical text representation.

dcb051ce8825ae82bde44f43938c070d18394f1f.title: Think Twice before Driving: Towards Scalable Decoders for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
dcb051ce8825ae82bde44f43938c070d18394f1f.research_question: How can the capacity and effectiveness of decoders in end-to-end autonomous driving systems be improved to enhance planning, safety, and generalization, particularly in complex urban environments?
dcb051ce8825ae82bde44f43938c070d18394f1f.hypothesis: Increasing the capacity of the decoder in end-to-end autonomous driving models, by introducing spatial-temporal priors, dense supervision, and explicit future-conditioned reasoning, will lead to improved driving performance, safety, and generalization compared to existing approaches that primarily focus on encoder design.
dcb051ce8825ae82bde44f43938c070d18394f1f.proposed_method: A novel cascaded decoder paradigm is proposed for end-to-end autonomous driving, which operates in a coarse-to-fine manner. Initially, a coarse future trajectory and action for the ego vehicle are predicted using an MLP. Subsequently, a Look Module retrieves fine-grained features from the encoder around the predicted future locations, leveraging multi-scale deformable attention for camera inputs and voxel retrieval for LiDAR. A Prediction Module then anticipates the future scene conditioned on the predicted action and trajectory, using a spatial-GRU that is supervised via teacher-forcing with privileged BEV features from an expert RL agent. The outputs of the Look and Prediction Modules are fused in a Refinement Module, which predicts offsets to refine the initial trajectory and action. This refinement process can be stacked multiple times, enabling the decoder to iteratively improve predictions by incorporating spatial-temporal priors and dense supervision at each stage.
dcb051ce8825ae82bde44f43938c070d18394f1f.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the CARLA simulator using two closed-loop autonomous driving benchmarks: Town05Long and Longest6. The system is trained via imitation learning using data collected from multiple sensors (four cameras, one LiDAR, IMU, GPS, speedometer) and an RL-based expert agent (Roach) for privileged supervision. Baselines include state-of-the-art end-to-end driving models such as CILRS, LBC, Transfuser, Roach, LAV, TCP, MILE, and Interfuser. Evaluation metrics are Driving Score (DS), Route Completion (RC), and Infraction Score (IS), as defined by the CARLA Leaderboard. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of each module, supervision strategy, and model scaling approach. Additional experiments compare increasing encoder size, decoder depth/width, and the effect of stacking the proposed decoder modules.
dcb051ce8825ae82bde44f43938c070d18394f1f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first scalable decoder paradigm in end-to-end autonomous driving that emphasizes increasing decoder capacity through spatial-temporal priors and dense supervision. It presents a cascaded, coarse-to-fine decoder structure that explicitly leverages future-conditioned reasoning and critical region feature retrieval. The method integrates privileged feature distillation from expert agents for both current and predicted future scenes, and demonstrates that stacking such decoder modules leads to significant performance gains. The approach achieves state-of-the-art results on competitive closed-loop driving benchmarks and provides a systematic analysis of model scaling strategies for both encoder and decoder components.

dcc13e077dc301c15208402bfc2ac47bd70083e7.title: Improve Robustness of Reinforcement Learning against Observation Perturbations via l∞ Lipschitz Policy Networks
dcc13e077dc301c15208402bfc2ac47bd70083e7.research_question: How can the robustness of reinforcement learning policies be improved against observation perturbations, particularly in high-dimensional and safety-critical environments?
dcc13e077dc301c15208402bfc2ac47bd70083e7.hypothesis: Incorporating global Lipschitz continuity into the policy network architecture and optimizing the output margin will significantly enhance the robustness of reinforcement learning policies against bounded observation perturbations, without incurring substantial losses in nominal performance.
dcc13e077dc301c15208402bfc2ac47bd70083e7.proposed_method: A new robust reinforcement learning framework, SortRL, is proposed to improve policy robustness against observation perturbations by designing the policy network as an l-infinity Lipschitz Neural Network, referred to as SortNet. The architecture ensures that the policy output is globally 1-Lipschitz continuous with respect to the l-infinity norm, which allows for a convenient and computationally efficient estimation of the policy's robust radius via the output margin (the difference between the largest and second-largest action scores). The training framework employs policy distillation: a standard deep RL agent (teacher) is first trained in a clean environment, and then a student SortRL policy is trained to mimic the teacher's actions while explicitly optimizing the output margin to guarantee robustness. The loss function combines cross-entropy for imitation and a robust hinge loss to maximize the output margin, with a schedule to balance optimality and robustness during training.
dcc13e077dc301c15208402bfc2ac47bd70083e7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on classic control tasks (CartPole, Acrobot, MountainCar, LunarLander) and video game environments (Atari and ProcGen benchmarks) to evaluate robustness under various observation perturbation strengths. The evaluation will use teacher policies trained with standard RL algorithms (e.g., PPO, DQN) and adversarial perturbations generated by PGD and FGSM-based attacks with varying l-infinity bounds. Baseline comparisons will include standard RL algorithms, robust policy regularization methods, adversarial training, and certified robustness frameworks. Evaluation metrics will include episode reward under attack, Action Certification Rate (ACR), and normalized scores relative to human and nominal performance. Experiments will also assess performance under strong adversaries (e.g., ϵ > 5/255) and curriculum-based adversarial training setups. All policies will be trained with the AdamW optimizer and evaluated over multiple random seeds for statistical reliability.
dcc13e077dc301c15208402bfc2ac47bd70083e7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to address robustness to observation perturbations from the perspective of network architecture by employing a globally l-infinity Lipschitz policy network. The method introduces a practical and efficient way to estimate and optimize the robust radius of policies via the output margin, avoiding the computational overhead of adversarial training or complex regularization. The training framework based on policy distillation enables a principled trade-off between optimality and robustness, and the approach demonstrates state-of-the-art robustness across a range of control and video game tasks, especially under strong perturbations.

dcc390c48adf9943aa45be833f1e378699acd3ab.title: Generalization Analysis for Contrastive Representation Learning
dcc390c48adf9943aa45be833f1e378699acd3ab.research_question: How does the generalization behavior of contrastive representation learning (CRL) depend on the number of negative examples and the properties of the loss function, and how can generalization error bounds be improved for both linear and nonlinear (deep neural network) representations in unsupervised learning settings?
dcc390c48adf9943aa45be833f1e378699acd3ab.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by exploiting the Lipschitz continuity and self-bounding properties of loss functions, it is possible to derive generalization error bounds for contrastive learning that do not scale linearly with the number of negative examples, and that these bounds can be further improved for specific loss types and representation classes.
dcc390c48adf9943aa45be833f1e378699acd3ab.proposed_method: A novel theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the generalization properties of contrastive representation learning. The approach will involve deriving generalization error bounds for contrastive learning objectives by leveraging structural results on empirical covering numbers and Rademacher complexities, with a focus on the Lipschitz continuity of loss functions. The analysis will consider three types of loss functions: ℓ2-Lipschitz, ℓ∞-Lipschitz, and self-bounding Lipschitz losses. For ℓ2-Lipschitz losses, vector-contraction lemmas will be applied to obtain bounds with only square-root dependency on the number of negative examples. For ℓ∞-Lipschitz losses, the method will expand the dataset and approximate the arguments of the loss to remove explicit dependency on the number of negatives (up to logarithmic terms). For self-bounding losses, optimistic bounds will be developed that yield fast rates under low-noise conditions. The methodology will be applied to both linear representations (with p-norm and Schatten-norm regularization) and nonlinear representations via deep neural networks, with Rademacher complexity bounds tailored to each case.
dcc390c48adf9943aa45be833f1e378699acd3ab.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be validated through application to two main settings: (1) linear representation learning with different regularization schemes (p-norm and Schatten-norm), and (2) nonlinear representation learning using deep neural networks with positive-homogeneous, contractive activations (e.g., ReLU). For each setting, the derived generalization bounds will be compared to existing state-of-the-art theoretical results, particularly those with linear dependency on the number of negative examples. The evaluation will focus on the tightness of the bounds, their dependency on key parameters (number of negatives, feature dimension, network depth), and their implications for downstream supervised classification tasks. Empirical or synthetic datasets may be used to illustrate the practical impact of the improved bounds, but the primary focus will be on rigorous mathematical analysis and comparison.
dcc390c48adf9943aa45be833f1e378699acd3ab.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces generalization error bounds for contrastive representation learning that significantly reduce or eliminate the dependency on the number of negative examples, up to logarithmic terms, for various classes of loss functions. The framework leverages advanced Rademacher complexity analysis and preserves feature coupling, leading to tighter bounds than previous work. Optimistic bounds are provided for self-bounding Lipschitz losses, enabling fast rates under low-noise conditions. The approach is applicable to both linear and nonlinear (deep neural network) representations, and the resulting bounds outperform existing theoretical guarantees by factors of √k or k, depending on the loss function, thus providing a deeper theoretical understanding of the empirical success of contrastive learning.

dcd1a3f3adba5aba5fc3fabf435d62f0e97f0ed9.title: DreamCatalyst: Fast and High-Quality 3D Editing via Controlling Editability and Identity Preservation
dcd1a3f3adba5aba5fc3fabf435d62f0e97f0ed9.research_question: How can 3D scene editing be made both faster and higher in quality, while effectively balancing editability and identity preservation, across different 3D representations such as Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)?
dcd1a3f3adba5aba5fc3fabf435d62f0e97f0ed9.hypothesis: A novel objective function that explicitly reweights identity preservation and editability based on diffusion timestep dynamics, combined with an improved model architecture leveraging FreeU, will enable significantly faster and higher-quality 3D editing compared to existing methods, while maintaining strong identity preservation across diverse 3D representations.
dcd1a3f3adba5aba5fc3fabf435d62f0e97f0ed9.proposed_method: A new framework, DreamCatalyst, will be developed for text-driven 3D editing by formulating a diffusion-friendly objective function that explicitly balances identity preservation and editability according to the noise level (diffusion timestep). The method introduces a specialized loss function where the weights for identity preservation are emphasized at high noise levels (early timesteps), and reduced at low noise levels (late timesteps), thus aligning the optimization process with the reverse diffusion process. The architecture will integrate FreeU, a technique that amplifies low-frequency features and suppresses high-frequency features in the U-Net backbone, thereby enhancing editability without compromising identity preservation or incurring additional computational costs. The framework will support both NeRF and 3DGS, enabling model-agnostic 3D scene editing.
dcd1a3f3adba5aba5fc3fabf435d62f0e97f0ed9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on real 3D scenes using datasets from IN2N and PDS, covering a variety of scene types including people, faces, objects, and outdoor environments. The method will be evaluated against state-of-the-art baselines such as IN2N and PDS for NeRF, and PDS, GaussianEditor, and DGE for 3DGS. Both qualitative and quantitative comparisons will be made using metrics including CLIP directional similarity (for prompt alignment), CLIP image similarity (for identity preservation), and aesthetic score (for visual quality). Editing speed will be measured by total training time. User studies will be conducted via Amazon Mechanical Turk to assess human preference for prompt alignment, overall quality, and identity preservation. Ablation studies will further analyze the impact of FreeU and the loss weighting scheme.
dcd1a3f3adba5aba5fc3fabf435d62f0e97f0ed9.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a general and controllable formulation for 3D editing that explicitly reweights identity preservation and editability in alignment with diffusion process dynamics. It is the first to leverage FreeU for 3D editing, achieving enhanced editability without additional computational or memory overhead. DreamCatalyst establishes a model-agnostic framework applicable to both NeRF and 3DGS, and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in both speed and quality, surpassing existing methods in comprehensive quantitative and user study evaluations.

dcd9366596840fbaaf9a4f031efa93f33fcb15ef.title: NUDGE: Lightweight Non-Parametric Fine-Tuning of Embeddings for Retrieval
dcd9366596840fbaaf9a4f031efa93f33fcb15ef.research_question: How can the accuracy and efficiency of k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) retrieval using pre-trained embedding models be improved for text and image datasets, without requiring access to model parameters or incurring significant computational and deployment costs?
dcd9366596840fbaaf9a4f031efa93f33fcb15ef.hypothesis: Direct, non-parametric fine-tuning of data embeddings through constrained optimization can achieve higher retrieval accuracy and efficiency than traditional parametric fine-tuning or adaptor-based approaches, while maintaining generalization and minimizing semantic distortion.
dcd9366596840fbaaf9a4f031efa93f33fcb15ef.proposed_method: A new family of non-parametric embedding fine-tuning methods, termed NUDGE, will be developed to directly optimize the embeddings of data records for k-NN retrieval tasks. The approach treats the embeddings themselves as tunable parameters and formulates constrained optimization problems to maximize the similarity between training queries and their ground-truth answers. Two main variants are proposed: NUDGE-M, which constrains the magnitude of embedding changes, and NUDGE-N, which additionally enforces normalization of embeddings to lie on the unit ball. Closed-form solutions for these constrained problems will be derived, enabling efficient updates to embeddings without modifying the underlying model or requiring additional deployment overhead. The optimal constraint parameters will be selected via validation accuracy maximization, and the methods will be designed to avoid overfitting and preserve the semantics learned during pre-training.
dcd9366596840fbaaf9a4f031efa93f33fcb15ef.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of nine standard text and image retrieval datasets, including SciFacts, Fever, ArguAna, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, Natural Questions, NF-Corpus, COCO, and Flickr. Five different pre-trained embedding models will be evaluated: three for text (BGE-small, GTE-large, OpenAI's text-embedding-large-3) and two for images (CLIP ViT-B/32 and ViT-L/14). Baselines will include traditional fine-tuning of the pre-trained model (PTFT), training small adaptor models, and a no fine-tuning condition. Evaluation metrics will focus on Recall@k and NDCG@k (with k=10), as well as Recall@1. Experimental setups will include both in-distribution and out-of-distribution query splits, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of different constraints. Runtime and computational efficiency will be measured on both GPU and CPU platforms.
dcd9366596840fbaaf9a4f031efa93f33fcb15ef.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a non-parametric, model-agnostic framework for fine-tuning embeddings that does not require access to model parameters or additional deployment infrastructure. By directly optimizing data embeddings under carefully designed constraints, the method achieves significant improvements in retrieval accuracy and efficiency compared to both parametric fine-tuning and adaptor-based methods. Closed-form solutions for the constrained optimization problems enable rapid fine-tuning, and the approach maintains strong generalization, including on out-of-distribution queries. The method is applicable to any pre-trained embedding model, including closed-source models, and provides substantial accuracy boosts with minimal computational overhead.

dcf8ccfcbadcf6b4613dd1b89064f5e6146ae625.title: An Invitation to the Euler Characteristic Transform
dcf8ccfcbadcf6b4613dd1b89064f5e6146ae625.research_question: How can shape be quantitatively represented and compared in a way that is computationally efficient, mathematically robust, and broadly applicable across domains without requiring pre-annotated landmarks or explicit correspondences between shapes?
dcf8ccfcbadcf6b4613dd1b89064f5e6146ae625.hypothesis: A transform based on the Euler characteristic, applied over directional filtrations, provides a complete, injective, and computationally efficient representation of embedded shapes suitable for quantitative analysis and machine learning applications.
dcf8ccfcbadcf6b4613dd1b89064f5e6146ae625.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops the Euler Characteristic Transform (ECT) as a shape descriptor for embedded simplicial complexes in low-dimensional Euclidean spaces. For each input shape, a set of directions on the unit sphere is selected, and for each direction, a filtration is defined by sublevel sets of a height function aligned with that direction. The Euler characteristic is computed for each sublevel set, resulting in a piecewise constant curve (Euler Characteristic Curve, ECC) per direction. The collection of ECCs across all directions forms the ECT, which is stored as a matrix indexed by direction and threshold. Variants such as the Smooth Euler Characteristic Transform (SECT) are also proposed, replacing the step function with a continuous, integrated version to enable Hilbert space structure and improved statistical properties. The method is designed to be computationally efficient, requiring only simple counts of simplices per filtration step, and is amenable to further extensions for time-varying shapes and function-valued data.
dcf8ccfcbadcf6b4613dd1b89064f5e6146ae625.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, such as binarized images of leaves, 3D scans of biological specimens (e.g., barley seeds), and protein structures. Shapes will be preprocessed to ensure alignment (e.g., via PCA or Procrustes analysis) before ECT computation. The ECT representations will be evaluated for their ability to distinguish between different shapes and for their utility in downstream tasks such as classification, using machine learning models like support vector machines. Comparisons will be made against traditional shape analysis methods that require landmarks or explicit correspondences. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness to noise and alignment errors. Additional experiments will explore the impact of the number of directions and thresholds on injectivity and representation quality.
dcf8ccfcbadcf6b4613dd1b89064f5e6146ae625.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a landmark-free, correspondence-free, and injective topological transform for shape representation that is computationally efficient and broadly applicable. The ECT provides a complete encoding of shape, enabling both reconstruction and robust comparison. The SECT variant further enables statistical inference by endowing the representation with a Hilbert space structure. Extensions to time-varying shapes and function-valued data, as well as integration with machine learning pipelines, demonstrate the versatility and innovation of the approach.

dd0930318a3b908f4dee33179db65846822706f2.title: unMORE: Unsupervised Multi-Object Segmentation via Center-Boundary Reasoning
dd0930318a3b908f4dee33179db65846822706f2.research_question: How can unsupervised multi-object segmentation in single images be improved to accurately identify and delineate multiple complex objects in real-world scenes, without relying on human annotations or pretrained object grouping features?
dd0930318a3b908f4dee33179db65846822706f2.hypothesis: Explicitly learning multi-level object-centric representations (existence, center, and boundary) from single-object images, combined with a network-free multi-object reasoning module, enables superior unsupervised segmentation of multiple objects in complex real-world images.
dd0930318a3b908f4dee33179db65846822706f2.proposed_method: A two-stage framework is developed for unsupervised multi-object segmentation. In the first stage, an objectness network is trained on single-object images (e.g., from ImageNet) using rough object masks generated via self-supervised pretrained features and affinity-based clustering. This network learns three explicit object-centric representations: (1) a binary object existence score, (2) an object center field encoding unit vectors pointing to object centers, and (3) an object boundary distance field indicating signed distances to object boundaries. In the second stage, a network-free multi-object reasoning module is introduced. This module generates candidate bounding box proposals across the image, queries the pretrained objectness network for each proposal, and iteratively refines, splits, or discards proposals based on existence, center, and boundary cues. Kernel-based operations and connected-component analysis are used to split proposals containing multiple objects, enabling accurate discovery of individual objects without human labels.
dd0930318a3b908f4dee33179db65846822706f2.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on six real-world benchmark datasets, including the challenging COCO dataset, to evaluate unsupervised multi-object segmentation performance. The proposed method is compared against state-of-the-art unsupervised segmentation baselines, including slot-based models and self-supervised feature grouping methods such as SlotAtt, DINOSAUR, CutLER, and CuVLER. Evaluation metrics include segmentation accuracy, object discovery rate, and performance in crowded scenes. The experimental setup ensures fair comparison by using standard dataset splits and publicly available implementations for all baselines.
dd0930318a3b908f4dee33179db65846822706f2.novelty_claims: The framework introduces three explicit, parallel object-centric representations learned from single-object images, which are then leveraged by a fully network-free multi-object reasoning module for segmentation. The center-boundary-aware reasoning algorithm iteratively discovers and splits object proposals without any human supervision or additional pretrained grouping models. The method demonstrates significant improvements over existing unsupervised approaches, particularly in crowded and complex real-world images, and achieves state-of-the-art segmentation results on multiple challenging datasets.

dd18782960f9ee4c66b79e1518b342ad3f8d19e7.title: WizardMath: Empowering Mathematical Reasoning for Large Language Models via Reinforced Evol-Instruct
dd18782960f9ee4c66b79e1518b342ad3f8d19e7.research_question: How can large language models be enhanced to achieve superior mathematical reasoning abilities across a range of problem difficulties, without relying on external Python tools?
dd18782960f9ee4c66b79e1518b342ad3f8d19e7.hypothesis: Integrating a novel reinforcement learning framework that combines evolved mathematical instruction generation with step-level process supervision will significantly improve the mathematical reasoning performance of large language models compared to existing open-source and proprietary models.
dd18782960f9ee4c66b79e1518b342ad3f8d19e7.proposed_method: A new framework, Reinforcement Learning from Evol-Instruct Feedback (RLEIF), will be developed to enhance mathematical reasoning in large language models. The approach begins with Math Evol-Instruct, which generates diverse and complex mathematical instructions through iterative upward (increasing difficulty and complexity) and downward (simplifying or diversifying topics) evolution using LLMs such as GPT-4. Two reward models will be trained: an Instruction Reward Model (IRM) to assess the quality and clarity of evolved instructions, and a Process-supervised Reward Model (PRM) to evaluate the correctness of each reasoning step in model-generated solutions. Supervised fine-tuning will be performed on the evolved dataset, followed by step-by-step Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) reinforcement learning, where the final reward for each instruction-answer pair is computed as the product of IRM and PRM scores. The PRM will also be used as a verifier to aggregate and select the best reasoning paths among multiple candidates.
dd18782960f9ee4c66b79e1518b342ad3f8d19e7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two widely used mathematical reasoning benchmarks: GSM8k and MATH, covering problems from grade school to high school levels. The training data will consist of both original and evolved instructions, with a total of over 400k unique instructions after filtering for contamination. Reward models will be trained using additional evolved data, with step-level correctness labels and instruction rankings provided by GPT-4. The proposed method will be evaluated on multiple open-source model backbones (Llama-2, Mistral, GPT-2, Qwen, DeepSeek) at various parameter scales (from 0.1B to 70B), and compared against state-of-the-art open-source and proprietary LLMs. Evaluation metrics will include pass@1 accuracy on GSM8k and MATH, as well as out-of-domain generalization on additional math benchmarks (e.g., MWPBench, AGIEval, Gaokao, SAT). Ablation studies will assess the impact of data size, evolution rounds, and reward model components.
dd18782960f9ee4c66b79e1518b342ad3f8d19e7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a fully AI-powered, automatic reinforcement learning framework (RLEIF) that integrates both instruction evolution and step-level process supervision for mathematical reasoning. The Math Evol-Instruct paradigm enables scalable generation of diverse and complex math instructions without human annotation. The combination of IRM and PRM in the reinforcement learning loop is claimed to address both instruction quality and false-positive reasoning steps, leading to substantial improvements over previous SFT-only or outcome-supervised approaches. The approach demonstrates superior data efficiency and scalability across different model sizes and backbones, and achieves state-of-the-art results on both in-domain and out-of-domain mathematical reasoning benchmarks, surpassing top-tier open-source and proprietary LLMs.

dd2bfd2f46ebab5a64fab0c94afe56fa066e1137.title: The Devil is in the Points: Weakly Semi-Supervised Instance Segmentation via Point-Guided Mask Representation
dd2bfd2f46ebab5a64fab0c94afe56fa066e1137.research_question: How can instance segmentation be performed effectively and efficiently when only a small fraction of the training data is fully labeled, with the majority of data labeled using only point annotations?
dd2bfd2f46ebab5a64fab0c94afe56fa066e1137.hypothesis: Point labels, despite their minimal annotation cost, can serve as a powerful weak supervision signal for instance segmentation, enabling high-quality mask generation and reducing the performance gap between semi-supervised and fully-supervised approaches. Furthermore, refining rough pseudo-masks with a dedicated network can further boost segmentation quality, especially when fully labeled data is scarce.
dd2bfd2f46ebab5a64fab0c94afe56fa066e1137.proposed_method: A novel weakly semi-supervised instance segmentation (WSSIS) framework is developed that leverages a small set of fully labeled images and a large set of point-labeled images. The approach employs a two-stage training protocol: first, a teacher network is trained on the fully labeled data to learn robust mask representations; second, the teacher generates pseudo-labels for point-labeled images, filtering proposals using point annotations to retain only true-positive proposals. To address the challenge of selecting the appropriate feature pyramid level for each instance, an Adaptive Pyramid-Level Selection strategy is introduced, which chooses the feature map level with the highest confidence for each point. Additionally, a MaskRefineNet is proposed to refine rough or noisy pseudo-masks, using the input image, rough mask, and point heatmap as inputs. This network is trained post-hoc to correct errors and improve mask quality, particularly in low-data regimes.
dd2bfd2f46ebab5a64fab0c94afe56fa066e1137.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the COCO 2017 and BDD100K datasets. Various splits of the COCO training set are used, ranging from 1% to 50% fully labeled data, with the remainder point-labeled. The SOLOv2 architecture with a ResNet-101 backbone is used as the base segmentation network. Baselines include fully supervised training, semi-supervised training with pseudo-labels from unlabeled data, and other weakly supervised methods using image-level, box, or point labels. Evaluation metrics include Average Precision (AP), AP@50, AP@75, and Average Recall (AR). Ablation studies assess the impact of point label guidance, adaptive pyramid-level selection, MaskRefineNet, and iterative training strategies. Labeling budget calculations are provided to compare annotation efficiency across methods.
dd2bfd2f46ebab5a64fab0c94afe56fa066e1137.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a new weakly semi-supervised instance segmentation paradigm that utilizes point labels as an effective and budget-friendly weak supervision signal. The Adaptive Pyramid-Level Selection method enables optimal use of multi-scale features in the presence of point-only annotations. MaskRefineNet is a novel mask refinement network that significantly improves pseudo-label quality, especially under extremely limited fully labeled data. The approach achieves state-of-the-art results in the weakly and semi-supervised regime, demonstrating competitive performance with fully supervised models at a fraction of the annotation cost.

dd2c0317dfc32db963f0a14f93a98c771ef784cd.title: Efficient Methods for Non-stationary Online Learning
dd2c0317dfc32db963f0a14f93a98c771ef784cd.research_question: How can the computational efficiency of non-stationary online learning algorithms be improved, specifically in minimizing dynamic regret, adaptive regret, and interval dynamic regret, without sacrificing theoretical performance guarantees?
