dd2c0317dfc32db963f0a14f93a98c771ef784cd.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging a reduction mechanism inspired by parameter-free online learning, it is possible to design non-stationary online learning algorithms that require only a single projection onto the feasible domain per round, while maintaining optimal or near-optimal regret bounds for dynamic, adaptive, and interval dynamic regret.
dd2c0317dfc32db963f0a14f93a98c771ef784cd.proposed_method: A generic reduction mechanism will be developed to decrease the projection complexity of existing non-stationary online learning algorithms from O(log T) or O(log^2 T) to 1 per round. The approach involves transforming the original constrained optimization problem into a surrogate problem defined over a larger, simpler domain (such as a scaled Euclidean ball), where projections are computationally cheaper. A carefully constructed surrogate loss function will be used to ensure that the regret guarantees of the original problem are preserved. The method will require only one gradient query and one function evaluation per round. For algorithms that do not natively satisfy this requirement (such as those for small-loss adaptive regret), modifications will be made, including replacing the meta-algorithm with a second-order expert-tracking algorithm and introducing adaptive thresholds for geometric covering intervals, ensuring compatibility with the reduction and improved regret bounds.
dd2c0317dfc32db963f0a14f93a98c771ef784cd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark datasets relevant to online convex optimization, including applications in online stochastic control and online principal component analysis, where projection operations are notably expensive. The proposed methods will be compared against state-of-the-art two-layer ensemble algorithms that optimize dynamic, adaptive, and interval dynamic regret. Evaluation metrics will include the number of projections per round, gradient and function evaluation counts, and achieved regret (dynamic, adaptive, and interval dynamic). Both worst-case and small-loss regret scenarios will be tested, and the computational efficiency and theoretical guarantees of the proposed methods will be empirically validated.
dd2c0317dfc32db963f0a14f93a98c771ef784cd.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a general reduction mechanism that matches the projection complexity of stationary online learning methods for non-stationary settings, reducing the number of projections per round from O(log T) or O(log^2 T) to 1 without loss of regret optimality. The method is broadly applicable to a variety of non-stationary regret measures, including dynamic, adaptive, and interval dynamic regret, and can be instantiated for important applications such as online stochastic control and principal component analysis. Technical innovations include new algorithmic modifications to enable single-projection operation per round for small-loss adaptive regret, as well as improved regret bounds that recover or surpass the best known worst-case results. The approach substantially improves computational efficiency in complex domains while maintaining theoretical performance.

dd3367e8c6c98d0630eda10e1d0c7ced99a90969.title: G-Mixup: Graph Data Augmentation for Graph Classification
dd3367e8c6c98d0630eda10e1d0c7ced99a90969.research_question: How can the generalization and robustness of graph neural networks (GNNs) for graph classification be improved through novel data augmentation techniques that enable effective information exchange between different graph instances, despite the challenges posed by the irregular, unaligned, and non-Euclidean nature of graph data?
dd3367e8c6c98d0630eda10e1d0c7ced99a90969.hypothesis: Interpolating the underlying generative models (graphons) of graphs from different classes and generating synthetic graphs from these mixed graphons will produce augmented data that preserves key topological motifs from both source classes, thereby improving the generalization and robustness of GNNs for graph classification.
dd3367e8c6c98d0630eda10e1d0c7ced99a90969.proposed_method: A new data augmentation framework, termed G-Mixup, is proposed for graph classification tasks. The approach first estimates the graphon—a probabilistic generative function—for each class of graphs using step function approximations based on node-aligned adjacency matrices. Graphons from different classes are then linearly interpolated in Euclidean space, controlled by a mixing parameter λ, to create a mixed graphon that blends the structural properties of the source classes. Synthetic graphs are generated by sampling node positions uniformly and then sampling edges according to the probabilities defined by the mixed graphon. Node features for synthetic graphs are generated by pooling aligned features from the original graphs. The resulting synthetic graphs, along with mixed labels, are used as additional training data for GNNs.
dd3367e8c6c98d0630eda10e1d0c7ced99a90969.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple benchmark graph classification datasets, including IMDB-BINARY, IMDB-MULTI, REDDIT-BINARY, REDDIT-MULTI-5K, and REDDIT-MULTI-12K, as well as OGB datasets. Various GNN architectures (e.g., GCN, DiffPool, MinCutPool, GraphSAGE) will be used as backbones. Baseline comparisons will include standard data augmentation techniques such as DropEdge, DropNode, Subgraph sampling, and Manifold Mixup. Evaluation metrics will primarily be classification accuracy, with additional analysis of generalization (test loss curves), robustness to label noise and adversarial/topological perturbations, and training stability (variance across runs). Experiments will also investigate the impact of hyperparameters such as the number of nodes in synthetic graphs and GNN depth.
dd3367e8c6c98d0630eda10e1d0c7ced99a90969.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first class-level graph data augmentation approach that operates in the space of graphons, enabling the mixing of structural motifs from different graph classes in a principled and theoretically justified manner. Unlike existing graph augmentation strategies that perturb individual graphs, this approach leverages the regularity and alignment of graphons to create synthetic graphs that are true mixtures of source classes. Theoretical analysis guarantees that the generated graphs preserve discriminative motifs from both classes. Extensive experiments demonstrate substantial improvements in GNN performance, generalization, and robustness to both label and topological noise, outperforming existing augmentation baselines.

dd4cfde3e135f799a9a71b4f57e13a29de89f7e3.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
dd4cfde3e135f799a9a71b4f57e13a29de89f7e3.research_question: How can reinforcement learning be effectively scaled and made reproducible for large language models to elicit advanced reasoning abilities, particularly in complex mathematical tasks, using fully open-source methods and datasets?
dd4cfde3e135f799a9a71b4f57e13a29de89f7e3.hypothesis: A reinforcement learning system for large language models that incorporates decoupled clipping, dynamic sampling, token-level policy gradient loss, and overlong reward shaping will achieve superior reasoning performance and training stability compared to existing methods, while being fully reproducible and open-source.
dd4cfde3e135f799a9a71b4f57e13a29de89f7e3.proposed_method: A novel reinforcement learning algorithm, Decoupled Clip and Dynamic Sampling Policy Optimization (DAPO), will be developed for large language models. The method introduces four key techniques: (1) Clip-Higher, which decouples the lower and upper clipping thresholds in policy optimization to enhance exploration and prevent entropy collapse; (2) Dynamic Sampling, which filters out prompts with all-correct or all-incorrect responses to maintain effective gradient signals and consistent batch sizes; (3) Token-Level Policy Gradient Loss, which computes the policy gradient at the token level rather than the sample level, ensuring longer and more complex responses contribute proportionally to learning and penalizing undesirable patterns; and (4) Overlong Reward Shaping, which masks or softly penalizes truncated responses to reduce reward noise and stabilize training. The system will be implemented on top of the verl framework and will include open-sourced training code and a curated dataset.
dd4cfde3e135f799a9a71b4f57e13a29de89f7e3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Qwen2.5-32B pretrained language model, focusing on mathematical reasoning tasks such as the AIME 2024 benchmark. The primary dataset, DAPO-Math-17K, consists of 17,000 math prompts with integer answers, curated and transformed for robust reward modeling. Baseline comparisons will include naive Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B. Evaluation metrics will include avg@32 accuracy on AIME, training stability, entropy, and response length. Training will use the AdamW optimizer with a constant learning rate, prompt batch size of 512, and 16 responses per prompt. Key ablation studies will assess the impact of each proposed technique on performance and training dynamics.
dd4cfde3e135f799a9a71b4f57e13a29de89f7e3.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first fully open-source, large-scale reinforcement learning system for LLMs that achieves state-of-the-art results on competitive reasoning benchmarks. The DAPO algorithm is novel in its decoupling of clipping thresholds, dynamic batch sampling, token-level loss computation, and length-aware reward shaping. The open release of code, algorithmic details, and datasets addresses the reproducibility gap in LLM RL research and provides a foundation for future advancements in scalable reasoning LLMs.

dd85e6cab147d237a0b1ab6f674570d3efb4d4a0.title: QuaRot: Outlier-Free 4-Bit Inference in Rotated LLMs
dd85e6cab147d237a0b1ab6f674570d3efb4d4a0.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be quantized end-to-end to 4 bits—including all weights, activations, and KV cache—without sacrificing accuracy or requiring higher-precision outlier retention?
dd85e6cab147d237a0b1ab6f674570d3efb4d4a0.hypothesis: Applying randomized Hadamard-based rotations to LLM weights and activations will eliminate outlier features, thereby enabling effective 4-bit quantization of all model components without significant loss in accuracy or the need for higher-precision outlier handling.
dd85e6cab147d237a0b1ab6f674570d3efb4d4a0.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a two-stage quantization framework for LLMs. In the first stage, randomized Hadamard transformations are applied to the weight matrices and activations throughout the model, leveraging computational invariance to ensure that these rotations do not alter the model's outputs. These rotations are fused into the model's weights and applied online to activations, including within the feed-forward and attention modules, as well as to the KV cache. The approach includes fusing RMSNorm scaling into adjacent weights, inserting efficient Hadamard transforms before down-projection layers, and rotating both key and value projections in the attention mechanism. In the second stage, all weights are quantized using either GPTQ or a round-to-nearest (RTN) scheme, and activations are quantized online using symmetric per-token quantization. The method ensures that all matrix multiplications are performed in 4 bits, with no channels retained in higher precision.
dd85e6cab147d237a0b1ab6f674570d3efb4d4a0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the LLAMA-2 family of models (7B, 13B, 70B parameters) using both language generation (WikiText-2) and zero-shot evaluation tasks (PIQA, WinoGrande, HellaSwag, LAMBADA, Arc-Easy, Arc-Challenge). Baselines for comparison include SmoothQuant, OmniQuant, QUIK, and Atom, with both group-wise and per-channel quantization schemes. Evaluation metrics include perplexity for generation and accuracy for zero-shot tasks. The setup uses per-token symmetric quantization for activations, asymmetric group-wise quantization for KV cache, and both GPTQ and RTN for weights. Performance is measured on NVIDIA RTX 3090 and A100 GPUs, with custom CUDA kernels for 4-bit matrix multiplication and memory/speed benchmarks during prefill and decoding stages.
dd85e6cab147d237a0b1ab6f674570d3efb4d4a0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable end-to-end 4-bit quantization of LLMs, including all weights, activations, and KV cache, without retaining any higher-precision outlier channels. The method leverages randomized Hadamard rotations fused into model weights and activations, eliminating outlier features and making quantization straightforward and outlier-free. Unlike prior work, this approach does not require calibration data, additional hyperparameters, or mixed-precision computation, and achieves minimal accuracy loss while providing significant speed and memory improvements. The method is also extensible to lossless 6- and 8-bit quantization using simple round-to-nearest schemes.

ddbd8fe782ac98e9c64dd98710687a962195dd9b.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
ddbd8fe782ac98e9c64dd98710687a962195dd9b.research_question: How can large language models be enhanced to improve the factual accuracy, controllability, and versatility of their generated outputs, particularly in knowledge-intensive and open-ended tasks, through adaptive retrieval and self-reflection mechanisms?
ddbd8fe782ac98e9c64dd98710687a962195dd9b.hypothesis: Incorporating an adaptive retrieval mechanism and self-reflection via special tokens into large language models will significantly improve the factual accuracy, citation precision, and overall quality of generated outputs across diverse tasks, without sacrificing model versatility.
ddbd8fe782ac98e9c64dd98710687a962195dd9b.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed Self-Reflective Retrieval-Augmented Generation (SELF-RAG), is proposed to enable large language models (LLMs) to dynamically decide when to retrieve external knowledge and to critique their own outputs using reflection tokens. The approach involves training a generator LLM to produce both task outputs and special reflection tokens that signal the need for retrieval, assess the relevance of retrieved passages, evaluate the support provided by these passages, and judge the overall utility of the generated segment. Reflection tokens are inserted into training data offline using a critic model, which is itself trained on data labeled by prompting a strong LLM (e.g., GPT-4) for fine-grained feedback. During inference, the generator LLM adaptively retrieves passages as needed, processes multiple passages in parallel, and uses its own generated reflection tokens to guide segment selection through a customizable scoring mechanism that balances relevance, support, and utility. This enables both soft and hard constraints to be enforced at inference, allowing for task-specific customization without additional training.
ddbd8fe782ac98e9c64dd98710687a962195dd9b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six diverse tasks, including fact verification (PubHealth), multiple-choice reasoning (ARC-Challenge), open-domain question answering (PopQA, TriviaQA-unfiltered), biography generation, and long-form QA with citation requirements (ASQA). The evaluation will use metrics such as accuracy, FactScore for factuality, exact match and Rouge for correctness, MAUVE for fluency, and citation precision/recall for evidence attribution. Baselines will include strong pre-trained and instruction-tuned LLMs (e.g., Llama2, Alpaca, ChatGPT), standard retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approaches, and recent methods with iterative prompting or retrieval-based fine-tuning. The SELF-RAG models will be trained on 150k instruction-output pairs from diverse datasets, using Llama2 (7B and 13B) as the generator and critic base models, and Contriever-MSMARCO as the retriever. Inference will employ adaptive retrieval thresholds and segment-level beam search, with ablation studies to assess the contributions of retrieval, critique, and inference-time customization.
ddbd8fe782ac98e9c64dd98710687a962195dd9b.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified approach for LLMs to learn when and how to retrieve external knowledge, generate outputs, and self-critique their own generations using reflection tokens, all within a single model. Unlike conventional RAG methods that indiscriminately retrieve a fixed number of passages, SELF-RAG adaptively triggers retrieval only when beneficial, and further evaluates and selects outputs based on fine-grained self-reflection. The use of reflection tokens enables controllable and customizable inference-time behavior, allowing practitioners to balance factuality, completeness, and fluency without retraining. The method also reduces training overhead by distilling critique into the training corpus offline, eliminating the need for separate reward models or critics at inference. Empirical results demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art LLMs and retrieval-augmented models in factual accuracy, citation precision, and overall output quality across a broad range of tasks.

dddbff68c6c35ea9b4482779642683b0be7fc900.title: Knowledge Distillation of Uncertainty using Deep Latent Factor Model
dddbff68c6c35ea9b4482779642683b0be7fc900.research_question: How can the uncertainty quantification capabilities of deep ensembles be efficiently compressed into smaller, practical student models without significant loss of predictive uncertainty, particularly for on-device AI and resource-constrained applications?
dddbff68c6c35ea9b4482779642683b0be7fc900.hypothesis: A distribution distillation approach that models teacher ensemble members as realizations of a Gaussian process—parameterized by a deep latent factor (DLF) model and estimated via an expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm—will preserve predictive uncertainty more effectively than existing knowledge distillation techniques, while enabling efficient inference and reduced resource requirements.
dddbff68c6c35ea9b4482779642683b0be7fc900.proposed_method: The proposed method, termed Gaussian distillation, compresses a teacher deep ensemble into a student distribution by treating each ensemble member as an independent realization of a Gaussian process. The mean and covariance functions of this process are parameterized by a student deep neural network (DNN) within the Deep Latent Factor (DLF) model, which extends the standard linear factor model to allow both mean and factor loading to be learned by the DNN. The estimation of the DLF parameters is performed using an expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm, which alternates between inferring latent factors and optimizing the DNN parameters for maximum likelihood. For regression, the method also distills the noise variance by modeling it with an inverse gamma distribution; for classification, a multivariate DLF is used. Design points for training are selected from validation or representative data to ensure coverage of the input space, and a penalized log-likelihood with a maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) term is used to initialize the EM algorithm robustly.
dddbff68c6c35ea9b4482779642683b0be7fc900.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple benchmark datasets for both regression and classification tasks. For regression, six UCI datasets (Boston Housing, Concrete, Energy, Wine, Power Plant, Kin8nm) will be used, with 90/10 train/test splits and repeated random splits for robust evaluation. For classification, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 will be used, with additional experiments on language model fine-tuning (GLUE and SuperGLUE tasks: RTE, MRPC, WiC) using RoBERTa and DistilRoBERTa with LoRA adaptation. Baselines will include naive distillation (small-Ens), Hydra, Batch Ensemble (BE), Latent Batch Ensemble (LBE), Proxy–Dirichlet Distillation, and Ensemble Distillation via Flow Matching (EDFM). Evaluation metrics will include RMSE, NLL, CRPS, coverage probability for regression, and accuracy, negative log-likelihood (NLL), and expected calibration error (ECE) for classification. Additional experiments will assess performance under distribution shift (e.g., label-swapped CIFAR-10) and ablation studies will analyze sensitivity to design points, latent factor dimension, and student DNN architecture.
dddbff68c6c35ea9b4482779642683b0be7fc900.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a numerically stable and general distribution distillation framework based on a novel deep latent factor (DLF) model, enabling the preservation of both mean and covariance structure of teacher ensembles in a compact student model. Unlike prior methods, this approach supports both regression and classification, provides a principled EM-based estimation procedure, and demonstrates superior uncertainty quantification compared to one-to-one and Dirichlet distillation baselines. The method is further distinguished by its applicability to fine-tuning language models and adaptation to distribution shift scenarios, with empirical results indicating consistent improvements in predictive uncertainty and calibration.

dde7098fd218fbdad3579b52493bf0556fa29e19.title: RFM-Pose:Reinforcement-Guided Flow Matching for Fast Category-Level 6D Pose Estimation
dde7098fd218fbdad3579b52493bf0556fa29e19.research_question: How can category-level 6D object pose estimation be made both faster and more accurate, especially in the presence of multimodal uncertainty and rotational symmetry ambiguity, without relying on instance-level CAD models or computationally expensive generative sampling methods?
dde7098fd218fbdad3579b52493bf0556fa29e19.hypothesis: Integrating flow-matching generative modeling with reinforcement learning-based policy refinement and value-based hypothesis selection will significantly improve both the efficiency and accuracy of category-level 6D object pose estimation, outperforming existing diffusion-based and deterministic methods.
dde7098fd218fbdad3579b52493bf0556fa29e19.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that first trains a flow-matching generative model to efficiently sample pose candidates by learning a deterministic transport field from a simple Gaussian prior to the target pose distribution conditioned on partial point cloud observations. The generative sampling process is then reformulated as a Markov decision process (MDP), where each integration step is treated as a policy action, and the pretrained flow model serves as the initial policy. Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) is applied to fine-tune the policy, using a multi-critic value network to separately estimate rotation and translation rewards based on geometric accuracy. During inference, the refined policy generates multiple pose hypotheses, which are then ranked and aggregated using the learned value network, enabling principled selection of high-quality candidates and robust final pose estimation.
dde7098fd218fbdad3579b52493bf0556fa29e19.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the REAL275, CAMERA, and Omni6DPose benchmarks, covering both synthetic and real RGB-D data across multiple object categories. The evaluation uses standard metrics such as mean Average Precision (mAP) at several rotation and translation error thresholds (e.g., 5°2cm, 5°5cm, 10°2cm, 10°5cm). Baselines include both deterministic and probabilistic (diffusion-based) state-of-the-art methods, such as GenPose, CATRE, and others. The experimental setup includes training the flow-matching model with PointNet++ feature extraction, followed by PPO-based policy refinement, and value-guided aggregation. Ablation studies investigate the impact of sampling count, candidate selection ratio, ranking strategies, and the contribution of RL refinement and value-based aggregation. Evaluation includes both single-frame pose estimation and category-level pose tracking, with efficiency measured in frames per second (FPS) and accuracy assessed per-category and overall.
dde7098fd218fbdad3579b52493bf0556fa29e19.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first integration of flow-matching generative modeling with reinforcement learning for category-level 6D pose estimation, enabling an order-of-magnitude reduction in sampling steps compared to diffusion-based methods. The method uniquely formulates pose sampling as an MDP and applies PPO-based policy refinement with a multi-critic value network, replacing likelihood-based scoring with direct geometric feedback. This unified framework achieves superior speed-accuracy trade-offs, delivers state-of-the-art accuracy on multiple benchmarks, and naturally extends to pose tracking and generalizes to diverse object categories. The value-guided aggregation strategy further enhances robustness, particularly for objects with rotational symmetry.

ddf40a9248bcd3657a4d721aea58d0957b8bdace.title: Learning to Solve Combinatorial Graph Partitioning Problems via Efficient Exploration
ddf40a9248bcd3657a4d721aea58d0957b8bdace.research_question: How can combinatorial graph partitioning problems, such as Maximum Cut, be solved efficiently and scalably using reinforcement learning, while maintaining or improving solution quality on large graphs?
ddf40a9248bcd3657a4d721aea58d0957b8bdace.hypothesis: A reinforcement learning approach that restricts graph neural network computation to a single pre-processing step, followed by recurrent decoding with per-vertex and global observations, will achieve state-of-the-art performance and scalability on combinatorial graph partitioning problems, outperforming existing RL-GNN methods in both speed and solution quality, especially on large graphs.
ddf40a9248bcd3657a4d721aea58d0957b8bdace.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a reinforcement learning algorithm for combinatorial graph partitioning, specifically targeting the Maximum Cut problem. The approach formulates the problem as a Markov Decision Process where the state consists of the graph and a binary labelling of vertices, and actions correspond to flipping the label of a single vertex. A single gated graph convolution network (GNN) is applied as a pre-processing step to generate per-vertex embeddings based on the graph's structure. During the optimization trajectory, a recurrent neural network (RNN) maintains a hidden state representing the ongoing search history, and per-vertex and global observations (such as current labels, one-step look-ahead cut changes, and time since last flip) are concatenated with GNN embeddings to inform action selection. The Q-value for each possible action is predicted using a dueling architecture, and the agent is trained using Munchausen DQN, which encourages stochastic exploration and entropy maximization. Training employs truncated backpropagation through time to efficiently update the RNN parameters.
ddf40a9248bcd3657a4d721aea58d0957b8bdace.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmark datasets for the Maximum Cut problem, including Erdős-Rényi and Barabasi-Albert random graphs with up to 500 vertices, as well as the GSet collection containing graphs with up to 10,000 vertices. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art RL-GNN baselines (S2V-DQN and ECO-DQN) and strong heuristic baselines (MCA and MCA-soft). Evaluation metrics will include approximation ratio (solution quality relative to the best known cut), wall-clock time, memory usage, and scalability (throughput and parallelization capacity). Ablation studies will assess the impact of the GNN and RNN components, and the effect of stochastic versus deterministic policies will be analyzed. All experiments will be run on a consistent hardware platform with GPU acceleration, and results will be averaged over multiple random seeds.
ddf40a9248bcd3657a4d721aea58d0957b8bdace.novelty_claims: The proposed method claims several innovations: (1) introducing a framework that restricts GNN computation to a single pre-processing step, drastically reducing per-action computational and memory costs; (2) leveraging a recurrent unit to maintain a rich representation of the optimization trajectory, enabling informed and efficient exploration; (3) achieving state-of-the-art performance among RL-based methods on Maximum Cut, with orders-of-magnitude improvements in speed and scalability, scaling to graphs with up to 10,000 vertices; (4) demonstrating that suitably stochastic policies outperform deterministic ones in exploratory combinatorial optimization; and (5) providing empirical evidence that the method generalizes across graph types and sizes, and outperforms or matches existing RL-GNN and heuristic baselines.

ddf9a63c92778db8659366a22e25dbe6fa4f7ead.title: When Diffusion Models Memorize: Inductive Biases in Probability Flow of Minimum-Norm Shallow Neural Nets
ddf9a63c92778db8659366a22e25dbe6fa4f7ead.research_question: Under what conditions do diffusion models exhibit memorization of training samples versus generalization to novel points on the data manifold, and how do the inductive biases of minimum-norm shallow neural network denoisers influence the probability flow dynamics in these models?
ddf9a63c92778db8659366a22e25dbe6fa4f7ead.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the probability flow of diffusion models using minimum-norm shallow ReLU neural network denoisers will converge either to training samples, to sums of training points (virtual points), or to more general points on the data manifold, depending on the structure of the data and the scheduling of the diffusion process. Furthermore, memorization will decrease and generalization will increase as the number of training samples grows.
ddf9a63c92778db8659366a22e25dbe6fa4f7ead.proposed_method: The proposed method involves a theoretical and empirical investigation of the probability flow and score flow dynamics in diffusion models where the denoiser is a shallow ReLU neural network trained to interpolate noisy samples with minimal ℓ2 norm (minimum representation cost). The analysis will focus on the low-noise regime and will derive explicit solutions for the denoiser in analytically tractable cases, such as when training points are orthogonal or form an obtuse simplex. Theoretical results will characterize the convergence points of the probability and score flows, showing how the diffusion time scheduler (noise schedule) induces 'early stopping' and affects whether the flow converges to training points, virtual points (sums of training points), or boundary points on the data manifold. The method will also extend to simulations that empirically validate the theoretical predictions, using constrained optimization (e.g., augmented Lagrangian) to enforce near-exact interpolation in the denoiser.
ddf9a63c92778db8659366a22e25dbe6fa4f7ead.experiment_details: Experiments will train shallow ReLU denoisers on synthetic datasets with controlled geometric properties (e.g., orthogonal points in high-dimensional space, points forming a simplex), using a non-standard training protocol (augmented Lagrangian method) to ensure close-to-exact interpolation. The probability flow ODE and score flow ODE will be discretized and simulated with varying numbers of training samples (N), noise levels, and initializations. Evaluation metrics will include the percentage of generated samples converging to training points, virtual points, or boundary points (within a specified L-infinity distance), and the effect of training set size and data augmentation will be systematically studied. Comparisons will be made between standard and regularized training (e.g., with and without weight decay), as well as with dropout, to assess their impact on memorization and generalization behavior.
ddf9a63c92778db8659366a22e25dbe6fa4f7ead.novelty_claims: The proposal claims a novel theoretical characterization of the probability flow dynamics in diffusion models with minimum-norm shallow neural network denoisers, explicitly linking the structure of the data and the noise schedule to the emergence of memorization and generalization phenomena. It introduces the concept of virtual points (sums of training points) as stable convergence points, and demonstrates how early stopping induced by the diffusion scheduler enables sampling from more general points on the data manifold. The work provides both rigorous analysis and empirical validation in simplified yet insightful settings, offering new perspectives on the interplay between model inductive bias, data geometry, and generative behavior in diffusion models.

de0d20742bb37f866324fb6c1db9736a76ecdbec.title: Invisible Image Watermarks Are Provably Removable Using Generative AI
de0d20742bb37f866324fb6c1db9736a76ecdbec.research_question: Are invisible image watermarks fundamentally robust against removal attacks that preserve image quality, or is there an inherent trade-off between watermark invisibility and resilience to such attacks?
de0d20742bb37f866324fb6c1db9736a76ecdbec.hypothesis: There exists a fundamental vulnerability in pixel-level invisible watermarking schemes such that a class of regeneration attacks, leveraging generative models, can provably and effectively remove these watermarks while maintaining high image quality.
de0d20742bb37f866324fb6c1db9736a76ecdbec.proposed_method: A family of regeneration attacks will be developed to remove invisible watermarks from images. The approach first maps a watermarked image to a latent or embedding space using an embedding function (which may be the identity, a variational autoencoder, or a diffusion model encoder). Independent Gaussian noise is then added to this representation to destructively disrupt the watermark. Subsequently, a regeneration function—instantiated as a denoising algorithm or a generative model (such as a diffusion model or VAE)—is applied to reconstruct a clean image from the noisy embedding. The method is flexible, allowing instantiation with various traditional and deep learning-based denoising or generative models. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to provide formal guarantees on watermark removal and image quality preservation.
de0d20742bb37f866324fb6c1db9736a76ecdbec.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both real photographs (500 randomly selected images from the MS-COCO dataset) and AI-generated images (500 images generated by Stable Diffusion-v2.1 using prompts from the Stable Diffusion Prompt dataset). Four publicly available pixel-level watermarking methods will be evaluated: DwtDctSvd, RivaGAN, StegaStamp, and SSL watermark, with appropriate bit-length settings. The proposed regeneration attacks will be compared against a diverse set of baseline attacks, including geometric and quality distortions (brightness, contrast, JPEG compression, Gaussian noise, Gaussian blur). Evaluation metrics will include Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), and watermark detection rates (TPR@FPR=0.01). Multiple instantiations of the regeneration attack (using VAEs and diffusion models) will be tested, with varying noise levels and compression factors, and all experiments will be run on high-performance GPUs.
de0d20742bb37f866324fb6c1db9736a76ecdbec.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a provably effective family of regeneration attacks that leverage generative models to remove invisible watermarks, providing both theoretical guarantees and empirical validation. Unlike prior destructive or constructive attacks, this approach combines both by operating in latent space and reconstructing high-quality images. Theoretical analysis establishes that, for a broad class of pixel-level invisible watermarks, no detection algorithm can reliably distinguish between watermarked and clean images after the attack. Extensive experiments demonstrate that these attacks outperform existing removal techniques, achieving higher image quality and lower watermark detectability. The research also highlights the fundamental limitations of invisible watermarking and motivates a shift toward semantic-preserving watermarking as a more robust alternative.

de23d38bc2604dcf334dcc46aff217eb6bcd1fe1.title: Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective
de23d38bc2604dcf334dcc46aff217eb6bcd1fe1.research_question: How do the characteristics of base language models and reinforcement learning (RL) optimization algorithms affect the reasoning capabilities and efficiency of large language models (LLMs) when trained with R1-Zero-like paradigms, and how can biases in RL optimization be identified and mitigated to improve model performance?
de23d38bc2604dcf334dcc46aff217eb6bcd1fe1.hypothesis: 1) Pretraining characteristics and template usage significantly influence the RL trainability and reasoning performance of base LLMs. 2) Existing RL optimization algorithms such as GRPO introduce biases (e.g., response length and question difficulty) that can artificially inflate certain behaviors, and removing these biases will improve token efficiency without sacrificing reasoning accuracy. 3) Domain-specific pretraining raises the RL performance ceiling for weaker base models.
de23d38bc2604dcf334dcc46aff217eb6bcd1fe1.proposed_method: A comprehensive experimental framework will be developed to analyze the impact of base model pretraining and RL optimization on R1-Zero-like training. Various open-source base models, including Qwen2.5, Llama-3, and DeepSeek-V3, will be evaluated for their inherent reasoning and self-reflection capabilities, both with and without prompt templates. The study will systematically investigate the effects of template selection and question set coverage on RL improvement. To address optimization biases, a modified RL algorithm, Dr. GRPO, will be implemented by removing response length and per-question standard deviation normalization from the GRPO objective, thus aligning the optimization with unbiased PPO principles. The methodology will include continual pretraining of weaker models on domain-specific datasets to assess the impact on RL trainability and final performance.
de23d38bc2604dcf334dcc46aff217eb6bcd1fe1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a range of base models (Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B/7B, Llama-3.2-3B, DeepSeek-V3-Base) and multiple prompt templates (R1, Qwen-Math, No template). The models will be evaluated on standard mathematical reasoning benchmarks, including AIME2024, AMC, MATH500, Minerva Math, and OlympiadBench. RL training will be performed using both the original GRPO and the proposed Dr. GRPO algorithms, with reward signals provided by rule-based verifiers (e.g., Math-Verify). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, pass@8, response length, and token efficiency. The impact of template-question set combinations and domain-specific pretraining (e.g., FineMath, NuminaQA) will be systematically assessed, and all experiments will be run with controlled compute resources (e.g., 8 A100 GPUs for 27 hours for main RL runs). Baselines will include state-of-the-art RL-tuned models and open-source PPO implementations.
de23d38bc2604dcf334dcc46aff217eb6bcd1fe1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a critical analysis of both base model pretraining and RL optimization biases in R1-Zero-like training. It identifies and formally characterizes previously overlooked biases in GRPO and open-source PPO implementations, specifically response length and question difficulty normalization, and proposes Dr. GRPO as a simple, unbiased alternative. The methodology provides a minimalist yet effective RL recipe that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on challenging math benchmarks with efficient compute usage. The study also offers new insights into the interplay between templates, question set coverage, and domain-specific pretraining, guiding future RL-based LLM post-training strategies.

de32da8f5c6a50a6c311e9357ba16aa7d05a1bc9.title: What Can Transformers Learn In-Context? A Case Study of Simple Function Classes
de32da8f5c6a50a6c311e9357ba16aa7d05a1bc9.research_question: To what extent can Transformer models be trained to perform in-context learning of various function classes, and how does their in-context learning ability generalize across different distributions and function complexities?
de32da8f5c6a50a6c311e9357ba16aa7d05a1bc9.hypothesis: Transformer architectures can be trained from scratch to in-context learn a wide range of function classes—including linear, sparse linear, decision trees, and two-layer neural networks—achieving performance comparable to or exceeding traditional task-specific algorithms, and demonstrating robustness to distribution shifts in prompts and queries.
de32da8f5c6a50a6c311e9357ba16aa7d05a1bc9.proposed_method: A decoder-only Transformer model will be trained from scratch to perform in-context learning on synthetic tasks defined by well-specified function classes. For each training instance, a random function from the target class will be sampled, and a prompt will be constructed by generating a sequence of input-output pairs (in-context examples) and a query input, all drawn from specified distributions. The Transformer will receive these sequences as input and will be trained to predict the correct output for the query input, using a squared error loss. The model architecture will be based on a 12-layer, 8-head, 256-dimensional embedding Transformer (approximately 9.5M parameters), with learnable linear transformations mapping inputs and outputs into the embedding space and back to scalars. Curriculum learning will be employed, starting with simpler functions and gradually increasing complexity to facilitate efficient training.
de32da8f5c6a50a6c311e9357ba16aa7d05a1bc9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets generated from various function classes: (1) linear functions with weights and inputs drawn from isotropic or anisotropic Gaussian distributions, (2) sparse linear functions with randomly zeroed weight vectors, (3) decision trees of fixed depth with random structure and leaf values, and (4) two-layer ReLU neural networks with random parameters. Baselines will include the optimal least squares estimator, Lasso for sparse linear functions, greedy and boosted tree algorithms for decision trees, and gradient-based neural network training for neural networks. Evaluation metrics will primarily be normalized squared error, averaged over thousands of prompts. Robustness will be assessed by introducing distribution shifts, such as changes in input covariance, label noise, prompt scaling, and mismatches between in-context and query inputs. Model capacity and problem dimensionality will also be systematically varied to analyze their effects on in-context learning performance.
de32da8f5c6a50a6c311e9357ba16aa7d05a1bc9.novelty_claims: The proposed research will systematically investigate and demonstrate that Transformers can be trained to in-context learn not only linear functions but also more complex function classes, matching or exceeding the performance of specialized learning algorithms in a single forward pass. The approach will show that such models can generalize in-context learning abilities to out-of-distribution prompts and queries, revealing that Transformers can encode effective learning algorithms beyond memorization. The research will also provide insights into the role of model capacity and curriculum learning in scaling in-context learning to higher-dimensional and more complex tasks, and will highlight the potential for Transformers to implicitly discover sample-efficient algorithms for tasks where explicit efficient algorithms are not well understood.

de34832e7e706e8f54ddc8b4e2ad490a87d5b9ed.title: Logical Languages Accepted by Transformer Encoders with Hard Attention
de34832e7e706e8f54ddc8b4e2ad490a87d5b9ed.research_question: What are the classes of formal languages that can be recognized by transformer encoder architectures with hard attention mechanisms, and how do the properties of these mechanisms influence the expressive power of such models?
de34832e7e706e8f54ddc8b4e2ad490a87d5b9ed.hypothesis: Transformer encoders with unique hard attention (UHAT) can recognize all languages definable in first-order logic with arbitrary unary numerical predicates (FO(Mon)), while transformer encoders with average hard attention (AHAT) can recognize an even broader class, including languages with counting features beyond AC0.
de34832e7e706e8f54ddc8b4e2ad490a87d5b9ed.proposed_method: The proposed research will formally analyze the expressive power of transformer encoders equipped with two types of hard attention mechanisms: unique hard attention (UHAT) and average hard attention (AHAT). The approach will involve characterizing the sets of languages recognized by these models using tools from circuit complexity and descriptive logic. Specifically, the method will construct formal proofs to show that UHATs can recognize all languages definable in FO(Mon) by leveraging structural induction and translations between first-order logic and linear temporal logic (LTL) with unary numerical predicates. For AHATs, the method will define and utilize an extended logic (LTL(C,+)) that incorporates counting terms, and demonstrate that AHATs can recognize all languages expressible in this logic. Technical constructions will include the design of appropriate positional encodings, embedding functions, and the use of ReLU and affine transformations within the transformer layers to simulate logical operations.
de34832e7e706e8f54ddc8b4e2ad490a87d5b9ed.experiment_details: The research will involve theoretical constructions and proofs rather than empirical experiments. However, to validate the expressiveness claims, representative languages from various complexity classes (e.g., regular languages, majority, parity, Dyck languages) will be formally analyzed to determine their recognizability by UHAT and AHAT models. The evaluation will compare the recognized language classes to established circuit complexity classes (AC0, TC0) and logical definability (FO, FO(Mon), LTL(Mon), LTL(C,+)). Baselines for comparison will include known results about the expressive power of transformers with soft attention and standard automata-theoretic models. Theoretical results will be supported by explicit constructions of transformer encoders for key example languages.
de34832e7e706e8f54ddc8b4e2ad490a87d5b9ed.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a precise characterization of the expressive power of transformer encoders with hard attention, showing that UHATs recognize exactly all languages definable in FO(Mon), a rich fragment of AC0, and that AHATs extend this power to languages with counting features, including those outside AC0. The approach leverages new logical frameworks and technical constructions to bridge the gap between neural network architectures and formal language theory. The research provides new insights into the limitations and capabilities of transformer encoders, establishes connections to circuit complexity, and extends the understanding of how attention mechanisms affect computational expressiveness.

de374dc9bb0b443ef399fc36587aa1e192447466.title: DreamSim: Learning New Dimensions of Human Visual Similarity using Synthetic Data
de374dc9bb0b443ef399fc36587aa1e192447466.research_question: How can a perceptual image similarity metric be developed that better aligns with human judgments across a broad range of visual variations, including mid-level attributes such as pose, perspective, color, object count, and shape, rather than being limited to low-level or categorical differences?
de374dc9bb0b443ef399fc36587aa1e192447466.hypothesis: A perceptual similarity metric trained on a large, diverse dataset of human-judged synthetic image triplets—spanning mid-level visual variations—will more accurately reflect human visual similarity judgments than existing low-level, patch-based, or semantic embedding-based metrics, and will generalize effectively to real-world images and downstream tasks.
de374dc9bb0b443ef399fc36587aa1e192447466.proposed_method: A new dataset of synthetic image triplets will be generated using a state-of-the-art text-to-image diffusion model (Stable Diffusion v1.4), with each triplet consisting of a reference image and two perturbed versions along various mid-level visual dimensions. Human perceptual similarity judgments will be collected using a two-alternative forced choice (2AFC) protocol, ensuring cognitive impenetrability by filtering for unanimous votes and validating with just-noticeable-difference (JND) experiments. Multiple state-of-the-art vision model embeddings (e.g., DINO, CLIP, OpenCLIP, MAE) will be evaluated as feature extractors, and their representations will be fine-tuned on the new dataset using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for efficient parameter updates. An ensemble metric will be constructed by concatenating the best-performing features and further fine-tuning with LoRA, optimizing a hinge loss to maximize agreement with human judgments.
de374dc9bb0b443ef399fc36587aa1e192447466.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize the newly collected NIGHTS dataset, comprising over 20,000 synthetic image triplets with unanimous human similarity judgments, partitioned into training, validation, and test splits. Baseline comparisons will include classical metrics (PSNR, SSIM), learned perceptual metrics (LPIPS, DISTS), and embeddings from large vision models (DINO, CLIP, OpenCLIP, MAE). Evaluation will measure agreement with human judgments on both 2AFC and JND tasks, as well as generalization to out-of-domain datasets such as ImageNet-R and MS-COCO for image retrieval, and BAPPS, THINGS, TID2013, and KADID-10k for low- and high-level similarity. Additional analyses will assess sensitivity to image attribute ablations and alignment with semantic and low-level features. User studies will be conducted to compare retrieval results, and downstream applications such as feature inversion and k-NN classification will be evaluated.
de374dc9bb0b443ef399fc36587aa1e192447466.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a new large-scale, cognitively impenetrable dataset of human-judged synthetic image triplets spanning mid-level visual variations, filling a gap between low-level and high-level similarity benchmarks. The methodology leverages generative diffusion models for diverse, controlled data synthesis and employs a fine-tuned ensemble of state-of-the-art vision model embeddings, optimized for human alignment using efficient LoRA adaptation. The resulting metric is claimed to achieve substantially higher agreement with human similarity judgments (over 96%), outperform existing metrics on both synthetic and real-world tasks, and provide new insights into the visual attributes most salient to human perception.

de434991f06ee87ea2629378329ca41361bd2db6.title: Accelerated Training through Iterative Gradient Propagation Along the Residual Path
de434991f06ee87ea2629378329ca41361bd2db6.research_question: How can the training of deep sequential neural network models be accelerated by leveraging architectural features such as residual connections, while maintaining high model performance and scalability?
de434991f06ee87ea2629378329ca41361bd2db6.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that an iterative, parallelizable algorithm exploiting residual paths in deep neural architectures can approximate backpropagation with significantly reduced computational cost, achieving substantial training speedups with minimal degradation in model accuracy.
de434991f06ee87ea2629378329ca41361bd2db6.proposed_method: A novel iterative algorithm, termed Highway Backpropagation (Highway-BP), is proposed to approximate the standard backpropagation process in deep sequential models. The method decomposes the gradient computation into a sum over all possible paths through residual connections and blocks, and iteratively accumulates gradient estimates along these paths. At each iteration, the algorithm alternates between parallel backpropagation through computationally expensive blocks and efficient propagation along residual connections using prefix scan (CumSumProd) operations. The number of iterations, k, serves as a hyperparameter, enabling a trade-off between computational speed and the fidelity of the gradient approximation. The approach is designed to be architecture-aware, allowing adaptation to a wide range of models including ResNets, Transformers, and RNNs, and is compatible with both linear and nonlinear residual connections.
de434991f06ee87ea2629378329ca41361bd2db6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of deep learning models and tasks, including image classification (CIFAR10, ImageNet32) with ResNet variants, language modeling (Wikitext103) with GPT-2 and RoBERTa Transformers, and sequence modeling with RNNs (LSTM, GRU) on Wikitext103 and pixel-level CIFAR10. Baselines will include standard backpropagation and fixed-point iteration methods. Evaluation metrics will comprise classification accuracy for image and NLP tasks, and validation loss or perplexity for language modeling. The experimental setup will systematically vary the number of Highway-BP iterations to assess the trade-off between speedup and performance, and will analyze convergence properties, gradient similarity, and runtime speedup compared to baselines.
de434991f06ee87ea2629378329ca41361bd2db6.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a parallelizable, architecture-aware algorithm for approximating backpropagation in deep sequential models, leveraging residual connections to enable efficient gradient propagation. The approach provides an interpretable, iterative gradient approximation with a tunable trade-off between computational cost and accuracy. It generalizes previous scan-based parallelization techniques by exploiting the structure of modern neural architectures, resulting in significant training speedups with minimal performance loss. The method is broadly applicable across a variety of model types, including deep residual networks, transformers, and recurrent neural networks.

de5b72c3f8b0802fb860b4d3369dcfc864848944.title: Towards Scalable and Stable Parallelization of Nonlinear RNNs
de5b72c3f8b0802fb860b4d3369dcfc864848944.research_question: How can the evaluation of nonlinear recurrent neural networks (RNNs) be made scalable and numerically stable for parallel computation, enabling efficient use of modern hardware while maintaining accuracy and convergence properties?
de5b72c3f8b0802fb860b4d3369dcfc864848944.hypothesis: Quasi-Newton approximations and trust-region-based stabilization, when applied to the parallel evaluation of nonlinear RNNs, will significantly reduce computational and memory complexity and improve numerical stability, allowing for scalable and robust parallelization without sacrificing convergence or accuracy.
de5b72c3f8b0802fb860b4d3369dcfc864848944.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces two key innovations for parallel evaluation of nonlinear RNNs. First, quasi-Newton approximations are employed by replacing the full Jacobian matrices in Newton's method with diagonal (or otherwise structured) approximations, resulting in a method termed quasi-DEER. This reduces the computational complexity from cubic to linear in the state dimension and lowers memory requirements, while maintaining global convergence guarantees. Second, the method leverages a connection between the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm (a trust-region method for nonlinear least squares) and Kalman smoothing, resulting in the ELK algorithm. ELK stabilizes Newton's method by constraining update step sizes via a trust region, and computes updates efficiently using parallel Kalman smoothing or filtering. The combination of these approaches, termed quasi-ELK, yields an algorithm that is both scalable and numerically stable for parallel evaluation of nonlinear RNNs.
de5b72c3f8b0802fb860b4d3369dcfc864848944.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world tasks. For scalability and efficiency, untrained and trained GRUs (Gated Recurrent Units) of varying hidden state sizes and sequence lengths will be evaluated on modern GPUs (e.g., 16GB V100). Wall-clock time, memory usage, and convergence accuracy will be measured for sequential evaluation, DEER, quasi-DEER, ELK, and quasi-ELK. Additional experiments will involve training GRUs for time-series classification tasks (e.g., C. elegans phenotype classification), comparing validation accuracy, runtime per training step, and number of Newton iterations required. For stability assessment, autoregressive RNNs will be evaluated in regimes known to induce numerical instability, with metrics such as mean absolute discrepancy (MAD) and convergence speed. Hyperparameters for trust region size in ELK/quasi-ELK will be selected via sweeps over log-spaced values. Baselines will include sequential RNN evaluation and the original DEER method, with performance compared across all methods using consistent hardware and datasets.
de5b72c3f8b0802fb860b4d3369dcfc864848944.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first scalable and stable parallelization framework for nonlinear RNNs that combines quasi-Newton approximations with trust-region-based stabilization via Kalman smoothing. It provides new theoretical proofs of global convergence for both DEER and quasi-DEER, demonstrates that diagonal Jacobian approximations can drastically reduce computational and memory costs while retaining accuracy, and establishes a novel connection between Levenberg-Marquardt optimization and parallel Kalman smoothing for stability. The resulting algorithms (quasi-DEER, ELK, and quasi-ELK) enable parallel evaluation of nonlinear RNNs at scales previously infeasible, with improved stability and efficiency over prior methods.

de6d82d1969742028374c18fcfe3b0e2c26adcc8.title: PPI++: Efficient Prediction-Powered Inference
de6d82d1969742028374c18fcfe3b0e2c26adcc8.research_question: How can statistical inference be made more efficient and practical by leveraging a small labeled dataset together with a large set of machine learning predictions, while maintaining valid confidence intervals for parameters of arbitrary dimensionality?
de6d82d1969742028374c18fcfe3b0e2c26adcc8.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a computationally efficient framework can be developed to combine labeled data and machine learning predictions, automatically adapting to the quality of predictions, to yield confidence intervals that are never worse—and often better—than those obtained using only labeled data.
de6d82d1969742028374c18fcfe3b0e2c26adcc8.proposed_method: A new methodology, termed PPI++, will be developed to perform estimation and inference by combining a small labeled dataset with a much larger set of machine learning predictions. The approach will construct a convex-optimization-based estimator that minimizes a rectified loss function, which incorporates both the labeled and predicted data. The method will leverage the asymptotic normality of the estimator to construct confidence intervals, and will introduce a tuning parameter λ that interpolates between classical inference (using only labeled data) and prediction-powered inference (using both data sources). The optimal value of λ will be selected adaptively based on the data to maximize statistical power, a process referred to as power tuning. The methodology will be applicable to a wide class of estimands, including all generalized linear models and general M-estimators, and will provide efficient algorithms for constructing confidence intervals in high-dimensional settings.
de6d82d1969742028374c18fcfe3b0e2c26adcc8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both real and synthetic datasets to evaluate the performance of the proposed PPI++ methodology. The experimental setup will include scenarios with varying prediction accuracies and different ratios of labeled to unlabeled data. Baseline methods will include classical inference using only labeled data, the original prediction-powered inference (PPI), and, where appropriate, augmented inverse propensity weighting (AIPW) estimators. Evaluation metrics will focus on the coverage and width of confidence intervals, computational efficiency, and statistical power. The experiments will include applications to linear regression, logistic regression, Poisson regression, and multiclass logistic regression, with confidence intervals constructed for both individual coefficients and the full parameter vector.
de6d82d1969742028374c18fcfe3b0e2c26adcc8.novelty_claims: The proposed methodology claims several innovations: (1) a computationally efficient convex-optimization-based framework for prediction-powered inference applicable to high-dimensional estimands, (2) an adaptive power tuning mechanism that automatically selects the optimal weighting between labeled and predicted data, ensuring confidence intervals are never worse than classical intervals, (3) asymptotic equivalence to idealized confidence sets obtained via hypothesis testing, but with dramatically improved computational tractability, and (4) generalization to a broad class of loss functions, including all GLMs and general M-estimators, with practical algorithms for real-world scientific inference tasks.

de9402a5e259f2c5eb919914bc898a3ca9eccdef.title: Adaptive Slot Attention: Object Discovery with Dynamic Slot Number
de9402a5e259f2c5eb919914bc898a3ca9eccdef.research_question: How can object-centric learning models be enhanced to automatically and dynamically determine the optimal number of object slots for each instance, without requiring prior knowledge or dataset-specific hyperparameters, in order to improve object discovery and segmentation performance across diverse and complex visual scenes?
de9402a5e259f2c5eb919914bc898a3ca9eccdef.hypothesis: Allowing the number of object slots to be dynamically determined based on instance complexity, rather than fixed a priori, will improve object discovery and segmentation performance by better adapting to the inherent variability in object count and scene complexity across images.
de9402a5e259f2c5eb919914bc898a3ca9eccdef.proposed_method: A complexity-aware object auto-encoder framework is developed that introduces an adaptive slot attention (AdaSlot) mechanism. The method sets an upper bound K_max on the number of slots and employs a lightweight neural slot selection module to predict, for each instance, which slots to keep or drop. Slot selection is formulated as a differentiable binary selection problem using the mean-field approximation and Gumbel-Softmax sampling, enabling end-to-end training. During decoding, a masked slot decoder suppresses the influence of dropped slots by manipulating the alpha masks, ensuring only the selected slots contribute to reconstruction. A complexity-aware regularization term is incorporated into the loss function to encourage the model to use as few slots as necessary while maintaining reconstruction quality, balancing slot utilization with instance complexity.
de9402a5e259f2c5eb919914bc898a3ca9eccdef.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed on a variety of datasets, including the synthetic CLEVR10 (toy dataset), MOVi-C and MOVi-E (synthetic datasets with up to 10 and 23 objects per image, respectively), and the real-world MS COCO 2017 dataset. The evaluation will use multiple metrics: pair-counting (precision, recall, F1, ARI), matching-based (mBO, CorLoc, Purity), and information-theoretic (AMI, NMI), with a focus on both object grouping and localization. Baselines will include state-of-the-art fixed-slot models such as DINOSAUR and GENESIS-V2, with a range of slot numbers for comparison. Implementation will use a frozen DINO ViT/B-16 backbone for feature extraction, and a mixture decoder for slot-based reconstruction. Hyperparameters such as K_max and regularization strength will be tuned per dataset, and results will be averaged over multiple random seeds. Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of different decoder designs and regularization strengths.
de9402a5e259f2c5eb919914bc898a3ca9eccdef.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel adaptive slot attention mechanism that dynamically determines the number of slots per instance, overcoming the limitations of fixed-slot object-centric models. The method leverages a differentiable, efficient slot selection process using mean-field Gumbel-Softmax sampling, and a masked slot decoder to effectively suppress unselected slots. The framework incorporates a complexity-aware regularization term to balance reconstruction quality and slot usage. This is the first method to demonstrate instance-level adaptability in slot number selection for object-centric learning, achieving competitive or superior performance to state-of-the-art fixed-slot models and offering new insights for further research in adaptive object-centric representation learning.

ded6f6fc4a708d23cf1cc73296b4f501df3bf648.title: Iterative Foundation Model Fine-Tuning on Multiple Rewards
ded6f6fc4a708d23cf1cc73296b4f501df3bf648.research_question: How can foundation models be fine-tuned to optimize for multiple, potentially conflicting reward signals or objectives, in order to achieve balanced and high-quality outputs across diverse domains such as text generation, biological sequence generation, and drug discovery?
ded6f6fc4a708d23cf1cc73296b4f501df3bf648.hypothesis: Iteratively fine-tuning foundation models on multiple objectives, with periodic merging of expert policies, will result in improved average performance and consistency across objectives compared to existing single-reward or expert-merging approaches.
ded6f6fc4a708d23cf1cc73296b4f501df3bf648.proposed_method: A novel iterative multi-objective reinforcement learning algorithm, IterativeRS (Iterative Rewarded Soups), is proposed for fine-tuning foundation models. The method maintains a separate expert policy for each objective and alternates between objective-specific fine-tuning and periodic merging of expert policies into a shared parameter vector. At each merging step, a subset of objectives is selected, and their expert policies are merged via a weighted linear combination, with weights reflecting objective preferences. The merged policy is then used to reinitialize all expert policies for the next round of fine-tuning. This process is repeated for a set number of optimization steps, and the final policy is obtained by merging all expert policies. The approach generalizes both reward-combining and expert-merging baselines and is supported by a theoretical analysis of convergence properties.
ded6f6fc4a708d23cf1cc73296b4f501df3bf648.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three domains: small molecule generation, DNA sequence generation, and text summarization. For small molecule generation, a pre-trained MolGPT-2 model will be fine-tuned on the QM9 dataset using reward models predicting molecular properties, with evaluation based on Pareto-optimality and average rewards for objectives such as polarizability, HOMO-LUMO gap, and internal energy. DNA sequence generation will use a DNAGPT-2 model pre-trained on the MPRA dataset and evaluated using the Malinois model for regulatory activity in three cell lines. Text summarization experiments will fine-tune Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct on the RedditSummary dataset, with evaluation using multiple reward models (bart-faithful-summary, gpt2-reward-summary, deberta-v3) and standard metrics like ROUGE. Baselines will include MORLHF (reward-combining), Rewarded Soups (expert-merging), and Rewards-in-Context (supervised fine-tuning). Evaluation metrics will include average reward per objective, overall average reward, and an inverse coefficient of variation (ICV) score to assess performance consistency across objectives.
ded6f6fc4a708d23cf1cc73296b4f501df3bf648.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces an iterative fine-tuning and merging strategy that generalizes and improves upon both reward-combining and expert-merging approaches for multi-objective reinforcement learning. By alternating between objective-specific fine-tuning and periodic merging, the method enables learning of objective-specific skills while controlling variance among expert policies. Theoretical analysis provides new insights into convergence and the impact of hyperparameters. Empirical results across diverse domains demonstrate superior average rewards and consistency compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

dedfe929d182cc3537a9ed765d589b4735ce062a.title: On the Planning Abilities of Large Language Models - A Critical Investigation
dedfe929d182cc3537a9ed765d589b4735ce062a.research_question: How effective are large language models (LLMs) at generating valid plans for commonsense and classical planning tasks, and can LLMs provide useful heuristic guidance or plan suggestions to external automated planners and verifiers in structured planning domains?
dedfe929d182cc3537a9ed765d589b4735ce062a.hypothesis: LLMs, when used autonomously, are limited in their ability to generate valid and executable plans for classical planning problems, but their outputs can serve as useful heuristic seeds or idea generators for external planners and verifiers, potentially improving the efficiency and correctness of the planning process.
dedfe929d182cc3537a9ed765d589b4735ce062a.proposed_method: A systematic evaluation will be conducted of LLMs' planning abilities in two modes: (1) autonomous plan generation, where LLMs are prompted with domain and problem descriptions (in both natural language and PDDL) and asked to generate plans directly; and (2) LLM-Modulo mode, where LLM-generated plans are used as heuristic seeds for external planners (e.g., LPG) or are iteratively refined via feedback from automated verifiers (e.g., VAL). The prompt generation pipeline will create diverse planning instances based on standard domains (such as Blocksworld and Logistics), with various prompt configurations (zero-shot, one-shot, chain-of-thought, and obfuscated domains) to test robustness. For the LLM-Modulo setting, the impact of LLM-generated plans on planner search efficiency and correctness will be measured, and a back-prompting loop will be established where verifier feedback is used to iteratively improve LLM outputs.
dedfe929d182cc3537a9ed765d589b4735ce062a.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize benchmark domains inspired by the International Planning Competition, including Blocksworld, Logistics, and obfuscated variants (Mystery Blocksworld). LLMs to be evaluated include GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Instruct-GPT-3, and open-source models such as BLOOM. Baselines will include human performance (via IRB-approved user studies), empty or random seed plans for LPG, and plan validation using the VAL tool. Evaluation metrics will include plan executability, goal achievement, optimality, number of LPG search steps, Levenshtein edit distance between LLM and final plans, and rates of improvement via verifier-assisted back-prompting. The experimental setup will control for prompt format, number of examples, and domain obfuscation to assess generalization and robustness.
dedfe929d182cc3537a9ed765d589b4735ce062a.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a comprehensive and automated framework for evaluating LLMs' planning abilities in both autonomous and assistive roles, using rigorous, domain-independent benchmarks and external validation tools. The approach systematically distinguishes between LLMs' pattern-matching capabilities and true planning competence by employing obfuscated domains and relaxed executability criteria. Additionally, the integration of LLMs as heuristic generators for external planners and the use of verifier-assisted back-prompting represent novel methods for leveraging LLM outputs to enhance classical planning pipelines. The proposal also provides the first large-scale, quantitative comparison of LLM planning performance against both automated planners and human baselines in structured domains.

dee343cfff76e46a4b9845e765d13be28165df06.title: VectorMapNet: End-to-end Vectorized HD Map Learning
dee343cfff76e46a4b9845e765d13be28165df06.research_question: How can high-definition (HD) semantic maps for autonomous driving be learned in an end-to-end manner from onboard sensor data, producing vectorized map representations that are directly usable by downstream driving tasks?
dee343cfff76e46a4b9845e765d13be28165df06.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that representing map elements as polylines and formulating the map learning task as a set detection and sequence generation problem will enable the direct prediction of vectorized HD maps from onboard sensor observations, improving both scalability and downstream task compatibility compared to rasterized or post-processed approaches.
dee343cfff76e46a4b9845e765d13be28165df06.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces an end-to-end framework for HD map learning that predicts a sparse set of polylines representing map elements directly from onboard sensor data (cameras and LiDAR). The method first extracts Bird’s Eye View (BEV) features by fusing multi-modal sensor data using a combination of ResNet (for images) and PointPillars with dynamic voxelization (for LiDAR), followed by a two-layer convolutional network for feature aggregation. Map elements are detected using a transformer-based set prediction model with learnable element queries, which predict keypoints and class labels for each map element. A polyline generator, implemented as an autoregressive transformer, then generates ordered sequences of polyline vertices for each detected element, modeling the conditional distribution over discrete vertex coordinates and using a categorical distribution for each coordinate. The entire system is trained end-to-end with a combination of bipartite matching loss for element detection and negative log-likelihood for polyline generation, with teacher forcing and optional fine-tuning for improved performance.
dee343cfff76e46a4b9845e765d13be28165df06.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the nuScenes and Argoverse2 datasets, using both camera and LiDAR modalities as inputs, as well as sensor fusion. Baselines will include HDMapNet and STSU, with comparisons made using average precision (AP) metrics based on Chamfer and Fréchet distances for polyline matching. Ablation studies will be performed to evaluate different keypoint representations and modeling choices. The evaluation will also include qualitative analyses of map quality and compatibility with downstream tasks, such as motion forecasting, where predicted maps are used as input to a trajectory prediction model (mmTransformer) and compared against models using ground-truth or no map data. Key metrics for motion forecasting include minimum average displacement error (minADE), minimum final displacement error (minFDE), and miss rate (MR).
dee343cfff76e46a4b9845e765d13be28165df06.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to formulate HD semantic map learning as an end-to-end vectorized prediction problem, eliminating the need for rasterization and heuristic post-processing. It introduces the use of polylines as a unified, flexible primitive for representing diverse map elements, and leverages transformer-based set detection and sequence generation to jointly model topological and geometric relationships. The approach demonstrates significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in both quantitative and qualitative evaluations, and shows that the predicted vectorized maps are directly beneficial for downstream autonomous driving tasks.

df09bfc9cf53fb64c0894782073435b438bfc8db.title: Token Fusion: Bridging the Gap between Token Pruning and Token Merging
df09bfc9cf53fb64c0894782073435b438bfc8db.research_question: How can computational efficiency in Vision Transformers be improved without sacrificing model accuracy, particularly for deployment on resource-constrained devices, by leveraging token reduction techniques?
df09bfc9cf53fb64c0894782073435b438bfc8db.hypothesis: Combining token pruning and token merging in a dynamic, layer-adaptive manner, and employing a norm-preserving merging strategy, will yield superior trade-offs between computational efficiency and model accuracy compared to using either approach alone.
df09bfc9cf53fb64c0894782073435b438bfc8db.proposed_method: A novel framework, Token Fusion (ToFu), is proposed to unify token pruning and token merging within Vision Transformers. The method dynamically selects between pruning and merging at each layer based on the layer's functional linearity with respect to input interpolation, as measured by a proposed metric. Early layers with low functional linearity utilize similarity-based pruned merging, while deeper layers with higher linearity employ average or norm-preserving merging. The core mechanism leverages Bipartite Soft Matching (BSM) to identify similar token pairs, followed by either discarding redundant tokens (pruning) or fusing them using average or MLERP (Maximum Norm Linear Interpolation, a variant of SLERP) merging. MLERP ensures that the feature norm is preserved during merging, mitigating distributional shifts. The reduction operation is inserted before the MLP module in classification tasks and before the attention module in image generation tasks, with the transition point between pruning and merging controlled by a hyperparameter.
df09bfc9cf53fb64c0894782073435b438bfc8db.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on ImageNet-1K for classification using pretrained Vision Transformer models (e.g., ViT-B, ViT-L), with both MAE and AugReg pretraining. The method will be evaluated in terms of top-1 accuracy, inference throughput (images/sec), and FLOPs, and compared against baselines such as Token Merging (ToMe) and other state-of-the-art token reduction methods. For image generation, the Stable Diffusion model will be used, with ToFu integrated into the U-Net backbone. Evaluation metrics will include FID, LPIPS, and MS-SSIM to assess distributional alignment and perceptual similarity, as well as generation speed and memory usage. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of the hybrid merging strategy, the MLERP merging variant, and the choice of transition depth between pruning and merging.
df09bfc9cf53fb64c0894782073435b438bfc8db.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces Token Fusion, a unified and dynamic framework that adaptively combines token pruning and token merging within Vision Transformers, guided by a novel functional linearity metric. It further proposes MLERP, a norm-preserving merging technique that addresses the distributional shift caused by conventional average merging. The approach is compatible with pretrained models and does not require additional training or auxiliary modules. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy in both classification and image generation tasks, outperforming existing token reduction methods.

df0facd3274afe26cde9b326c28f7de47171464c.title: Distributional Offline Policy Evaluation with Predictive Error Guarantees
df0facd3274afe26cde9b326c28f7de47171464c.research_question: How can the full distribution of returns for a given policy be accurately estimated from offline data, especially in settings with high-dimensional, continuous state/action spaces and multi-dimensional rewards, with provable predictive error guarantees?
