df0facd3274afe26cde9b326c28f7de47171464c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a sequence of maximum likelihood estimations (MLE) using flexible generative models can accurately approximate the distribution of policy returns in offline settings, provided the offline data sufficiently covers the test policy's state-action distribution and the supervised learning procedure generalizes well.
df0facd3274afe26cde9b326c28f7de47171464c.proposed_method: A new algorithm, Fitted Likelihood Estimation (FLE), will be developed to estimate the distribution of returns for a target policy using only offline data. FLE decomposes the distributional offline policy evaluation problem into a sequence of supervised learning problems, each solved via maximum likelihood estimation. At each iteration, FLE fits a conditional generative model to approximate the distributional Bellman target, leveraging any probabilistic generative model trainable by MLE (e.g., Gaussian mixture models, diffusion models). The approach is applicable to both finite-horizon and infinite-horizon discounted Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), and supports multi-dimensional reward vectors. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to show that, under suitable data coverage and generalization conditions, the learned return distributions are close to the ground truth in total variation or Wasserstein distance.
df0facd3274afe26cde9b326c28f7de47171464c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a high-dimensional, continuous observation combination lock MDP, including both one-dimensional and multi-dimensional reward settings. Offline datasets will be generated uniformly, ensuring coverage of the test policy's state-action distribution. The proposed FLE algorithm will be instantiated with Gaussian mixture models and diffusion models as generative components. Baseline methods will include categorical distributional RL algorithms and quantile regression TD, with comparisons made using total variation and Wasserstein distances between the estimated and true return distributions. Evaluation will involve visualizations and quantitative metrics (e.g., approximated total variation distance) across multiple runs to assess predictive accuracy and the ability to capture complex return structures.
df0facd3274afe26cde9b326c28f7de47171464c.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to provide PAC-style predictive error guarantees for distributional offline policy evaluation with general function approximation and multi-dimensional rewards. FLE offers a modular reduction to supervised learning, enabling the integration of state-of-the-art generative models for flexible and scalable distribution estimation. Theoretical results establish strong error bounds under total variation and Wasserstein distances, and the approach is applicable to both finite- and infinite-horizon MDPs. Empirical results demonstrate the method's ability to accurately estimate complex, high-dimensional return distributions, outperforming existing baselines and overcoming the curse of dimensionality faced by discretization-based methods.

df29153629c3f00bdbbe1ea28f32ce379e35a144.title: Smoothing the Landscape Boosts the Signal for SGD: Optimal Sample Complexity for Learning Single Index Models
df29153629c3f00bdbbe1ea28f32ce379e35a144.research_question: What is the optimal sample complexity for learning single-index models with known link functions under isotropic Gaussian distributions, and how can modifications to the loss landscape improve the efficiency of gradient-based algorithms in this setting?
df29153629c3f00bdbbe1ea28f32ce379e35a144.hypothesis: Smoothing the empirical loss landscape in the context of online stochastic gradient descent (SGD) will increase the signal-to-noise ratio, allowing the recovery of the underlying direction in single-index models with a sample complexity that matches the correlation statistical query (CSQ) lower bound, specifically n ≳ d^{k*/2} for information exponent k*.
df29153629c3f00bdbbe1ea28f32ce379e35a144.proposed_method: A novel approach is proposed that applies online stochastic gradient descent to a smoothed version of the empirical loss for single-index models. The smoothing operator is defined intrinsically on the sphere, leveraging the Riemannian exponential map and averaging the loss over a local neighborhood determined by a smoothing parameter λ. The algorithm initializes the direction vector randomly on the unit sphere and, at each iteration, samples a fresh data point, computes the spherical gradient of the smoothed loss, and updates the direction using a learning rate and normalization step. The smoothing parameter and learning rate are scheduled in two phases: an initial phase with large smoothing to quickly escape regions of poor signal, followed by a phase with no smoothing and decaying learning rate to refine the solution. The method exploits the Hermite expansion of the link function to analyze and optimize the signal-to-noise ratio throughout the optimization trajectory.
df29153629c3f00bdbbe1ea28f32ce379e35a144.experiment_details: Experiments are designed to empirically verify the sample complexity scaling for various information exponents (k* = 3, 4, 5) and input dimensions (d = 2^8 to 2^13). The target function is set as the normalized k*-th Hermite polynomial, and a minibatch variant of the proposed algorithm is used with batch size and learning rate tuned according to theoretical scaling laws. The number of samples required to reach a specified correlation threshold is measured, and results are averaged over multiple random seeds. Baselines include the unsmoothed online SGD and theoretical lower bounds from the CSQ framework. Evaluation metrics include the number of samples to achieve a target alignment between the estimated and true direction vectors, and the empirical scaling exponent is compared to the predicted optimal rate.
df29153629c3f00bdbbe1ea28f32ce379e35a144.novelty_claims: The proposed method closes the gap between previously known upper and lower bounds for sample complexity in learning single-index models with gradient-based methods, achieving the optimal n ≳ d^{k*/2} rate for online SGD by smoothing the loss landscape. The approach provides a new theoretical and algorithmic connection between implicit regularization effects in minibatch SGD, smoothing techniques from tensor PCA, and optimal sample complexity in the CSQ framework. The analysis demonstrates how smoothing boosts the signal-to-noise ratio, enabling efficient escape from poor local minima and matching information-theoretic lower bounds for a broad class of link functions.

df298ef4717dadb23be3571852f6b522a7ab237a.title: Model-based Reinforcement Learning for Parameterized Action Spaces
df298ef4717dadb23be3571852f6b522a7ab237a.research_question: How can model-based reinforcement learning be effectively applied to environments with parameterized (discrete-continuous hybrid) action spaces to achieve high sample efficiency and strong asymptotic performance?
df298ef4717dadb23be3571852f6b522a7ab237a.hypothesis: Model-based reinforcement learning, when equipped with parameterized-action-conditioned dynamics models and tailored planning algorithms, can outperform existing model-free methods in parameterized action Markov decision processes (PAMDPs) in terms of sample efficiency and final performance.
df298ef4717dadb23be3571852f6b522a7ab237a.proposed_method: A new model-based reinforcement learning algorithm, Dynamics Learning and Predictive Control with Parameterized Actions (DLPA), is developed for PAMDPs. The method first learns a dynamics model conditioned on parameterized actions using neural networks, incorporating three distinct inference architectures (parallel, masking, and sequential) to handle the entangled discrete and continuous action components. The dynamics model is trained with an H-step prediction loss, enabling multi-step trajectory prediction and more effective credit assignment. Two separate reward predictors are learned, conditioned on whether the episode is continuing or terminating, to better capture the nuanced effects of actions. For planning, a modified Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control algorithm is used, maintaining separate distributions over continuous parameters for each discrete action and updating these distributions iteratively based on predicted returns from the learned model.
df298ef4717dadb23be3571852f6b522a7ab237a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on eight standard PAMDP benchmarks, including Platform, Goal, Catch Point, Hard Goal, and four variants of Hard Move with increasing action space dimensionality, as well as the Half-Field-Offense (HFO) domain. The proposed method is compared against five state-of-the-art PAMDP baselines: HyAR, P-DQN, PADDPG (with TD3), HPPO, and PATD3. Evaluation metrics include sample efficiency (learning speed) and asymptotic performance (final achieved reward). The experimental setup uses multi-layer perceptrons for all models, planning horizons between 5 and 10, top-trajectory selection during planning, and six planning iterations per step. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of planning algorithms, inference architectures, H-step prediction, reward predictor separation, and the MPPI modification.
df298ef4717dadb23be3571852f6b522a7ab237a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to successfully apply model-based reinforcement learning to parameterized action spaces (PAMDPs), introducing a tailored dynamics model with multi-step prediction loss and PAMDP-specific planning via MPPI. The method provides the first theoretical performance guarantees for model-based RL in PAMDPs, including bounds on trajectory regret via Lipschitz continuity. Empirical results demonstrate significant improvements in sample efficiency and asymptotic performance over all existing model-free PAMDP algorithms, especially in large action spaces where previous methods fail without complex action embeddings. The approach also introduces novel architectural components, including separate reward predictors and specialized inference structures for parameterized actions.

df602516e28a9ef0ef665ed0aef551984d8d770d.title: Recommendation as Language Processing (RLP): A Unified Pretrain, Personalized Prompt & Predict Paradigm (P5)
df602516e28a9ef0ef665ed0aef551984d8d770d.research_question: How can a unified language-based framework be developed to address a wide range of personalized recommendation tasks, enabling knowledge transfer, generalization, and zero-shot/few-shot learning across different recommendation scenarios?
df602516e28a9ef0ef665ed0aef551984d8d770d.hypothesis: A unified pretrain, personalized prompt, and predict paradigm that reformulates recommendation tasks as conditional natural language generation problems will enable effective multitask learning, improved generalization, and robust zero-shot performance across diverse recommendation tasks and domains.
df602516e28a9ef0ef665ed0aef551984d8d770d.proposed_method: A unified recommendation framework is proposed that formulates various recommendation tasks—such as rating prediction, sequential recommendation, explanation generation, review summarization, and direct recommendation—as text-to-text problems using personalized natural language prompts. The approach leverages an encoder–decoder Transformer architecture (e.g., T5) and pretrains it on a large, multitask collection of personalized prompts that encode user, item, and contextual information as natural language sequences. The model is trained with a shared language modeling objective, enabling it to learn from diverse recommendation tasks in a single framework. Personalized prompt templates are designed for each task family, and input–target pairs are constructed by substituting user/item fields and metadata into these templates. After pretraining, the model can perform zero-shot or few-shot prediction for new tasks, prompts, or domains without extensive fine-tuning.
df602516e28a9ef0ef665ed0aef551984d8d770d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple real-world datasets, including Amazon Sports, Beauty, Toys, and Yelp, covering a range of recommendation scenarios. The evaluation will span five task families: rating prediction, sequential recommendation, explanation generation, review summarization, and direct recommendation. Baseline comparisons will include traditional collaborative filtering (MF, MLP), state-of-the-art sequential models (SASRec, S3-Rec, BERT4Rec), text generation models (Attn2Seq, NRT, PETER, GPT-2, T0), and contrastive learning methods (SimpleX). Evaluation metrics will include RMSE and MAE for regression tasks, HR@k and NDCG@k for ranking tasks, and BLEU/ROUGE for text generation tasks. The experimental setup will involve multitask pretraining, zero-shot generalization to unseen prompts and domains, ablation studies on model size, number of tasks, and prompt scaling, as well as analysis of different personalization strategies.
df602516e28a9ef0ef665ed0aef551984d8d770d.novelty_claims: The proposed paradigm is the first to unify a broad spectrum of recommendation tasks within a single conditional language generation framework using personalized prompts. It enables seamless multitask learning, knowledge transfer, and robust zero-shot generalization across tasks and domains without task-specific architectures or objectives. The approach leverages the flexibility of natural language to encode diverse features and scenarios, eliminates the need for feature-specific encoders, and demonstrates strong performance even with smaller model sizes compared to large-scale language models. The method also introduces a comprehensive collection of personalized prompts, supports instruction-based recommendation, and provides a foundation for universal, instruction-driven recommendation engines.

df67a069d7425a2075f26681bc40c45901cfa67e.title: SlotDiffusion: Object-Centric Generative Modeling with Diffusion Models
df67a069d7425a2075f26681bc40c45901cfa67e.research_question: How can object-centric generative modeling be improved to enable high-quality, controllable image and video generation, while maintaining robust unsupervised object discovery and segmentation across both synthetic and real-world datasets?
df67a069d7425a2075f26681bc40c45901cfa67e.hypothesis: Integrating a latent diffusion model as the slot-to-image decoder within an object-centric framework will significantly enhance the generative quality and segmentation performance of unsupervised slot-based models, outperforming existing mixture-based and transformer-based decoders, and enabling better downstream utility for tasks such as video prediction and visual question answering.
df67a069d7425a2075f26681bc40c45901cfa67e.proposed_method: A novel object-centric generative modeling approach is proposed, where visual scenes are represented as sets of object-centric slots extracted via Slot Attention. These slots are used to condition a Latent Diffusion Model (LDM) that serves as the slot-to-image decoder. The LDM operates in a learned latent space produced by a pre-trained VQ-VAE, and denoises latent feature maps iteratively, guided by the object slots through cross-attention mechanisms at multiple U-Net layers. This conditioning preserves permutation equivariance and enables compositional generation by assembling slots from a learned visual concept library. The entire model is trained end-to-end with a slot-conditioned denoising loss over VQ-VAE feature maps, and can be extended to leverage self-supervised pre-trained encoders for real-world data.
df67a069d7425a2075f26681bc40c45901cfa67e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six datasets for unsupervised object discovery and slot-based visual generation: CLEVRTex and CelebA for images, MOVi-D/E/Solid/Tex for videos, and further downstream evaluation on Physion for video prediction and VQA. Scalability will be tested on PASCAL VOC 2012 and MS COCO 2017 for real-world segmentation. Baselines include Slot Attention, SLATE, SAVi, STEVE, and DINOSAUR, with consistent use of pre-trained encoders where applicable. Evaluation metrics include FG-ARI, mIoU, and mBO for segmentation; MSE and LPIPS for reconstruction; and FID/FVD for generative quality. Additional experiments will assess compositional generation, image editing, and integration with recent slot-based model improvements.
df67a069d7425a2075f26681bc40c45901cfa67e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first object-centric generative model that leverages a latent diffusion model as the slot decoder, enabling high-fidelity, controllable image and video generation from unsupervised slots. It demonstrates state-of-the-art segmentation and generation performance across diverse datasets, improves downstream temporal reasoning and video prediction via more informative slot representations, and scales to unconstrained real-world data when combined with self-supervised pre-trained encoders. The approach is modular and compatible with recent advances in slot-based learning, offering a significant step forward in object-centric generative modeling.

df8c3a325419d63366b9b347739fcbf3e2c4d22c.title: Self-Play Preference Optimization for Language Model Alignment
df8c3a325419d63366b9b347739fcbf3e2c4d22c.research_question: How can language model alignment be improved by directly optimizing for human preference probabilities, rather than relying on parametric reward models, and can a scalable, theoretically sound self-play framework be developed to efficiently achieve Nash equilibrium policies in large language models?
df8c3a325419d63366b9b347739fcbf3e2c4d22c.hypothesis: Directly optimizing language models using a self-play framework based on preference probabilities, rather than parametric reward models, will more accurately capture human preferences (including intransitivity and irrationality), leading to superior alignment and performance on alignment benchmarks without reliance on external supervision from stronger models.
df8c3a325419d63366b9b347739fcbf3e2c4d22c.proposed_method: A new algorithm, Self-Play Preference Optimization (SPPO), is developed to align large language models by treating the alignment problem as a constant-sum two-player game. The method iteratively updates the policy using multiplicative weights, where in each round, the model generates synthetic responses to prompts, and a preference model is used to annotate the win rates among these responses. The core optimization objective minimizes the squared difference between the log-probability ratio of the updated and current policies and the scaled empirical win rate, with a theoretically motivated constant baseline. This approach avoids reliance on pairwise loss functions and instead directly regresses the policy to match token-level win rates, providing a strong connection to policy gradient theory. The algorithm is designed to be scalable for large language models and provably converges to an approximate Nash equilibrium.
df8c3a325419d63366b9b347739fcbf3e2c4d22c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using 60,000 prompts from the UltraFeedback dataset, without using any response data or prompt augmentation. The preference model employed is PairRM with 0.4B parameters. The base language models include Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 and Llama-3-8B-Instruct. The proposed SPPO method will be compared against strong baselines such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and Identity Preference Optimization (IPO). Evaluation will be performed on multiple benchmarks, including AlpacaEval 2.0 (using length-controlled win-rate against GPT-4-Turbo), MT-Bench, Arena-Hard, and the Open LLM Leaderboard. Key metrics include win-rate against GPT-4-Turbo and performance consistency across diverse alignment tasks. No external supervision (e.g., responses or preferences from GPT-4 or other stronger models) will be used.
df8c3a325419d63366b9b347739fcbf3e2c4d22c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a theoretically grounded self-play framework for language model alignment that directly optimizes preference probabilities, rather than relying on parametric reward models. The SPPO algorithm offers provable convergence to Nash equilibrium and introduces a new, simple, and effective loss function that does not depend on pairwise comparisons. The approach is scalable to large language models and achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple alignment benchmarks without requiring external supervision from stronger models. The method also provides a deeper connection to policy gradient theory and enables consistent performance improvements across diverse evaluation settings.

dfa3013f9b9af4053e57d6250e0f2b7dc7ff6258.title: ALMTokenizer: A Low-bitrate and Semantic-rich Audio Codec Tokenizer for Audio Language Modeling
dfa3013f9b9af4053e57d6250e0f2b7dc7ff6258.research_question: What type of audio codec tokenizer is most suitable for audio language modeling, particularly in achieving low bitrate and high semantic richness for both speech and non-speech audio tasks?
dfa3013f9b9af4053e57d6250e0f2b7dc7ff6258.hypothesis: A query-based audio codec tokenizer that explicitly models context across audio frames, integrates semantic priors into vector quantization, and incorporates masked autoencoder and autoregressive prediction losses will yield a low-bitrate, semantically rich representation that improves audio language modeling performance over existing tokenizers.
dfa3013f9b9af4053e57d6250e0f2b7dc7ff6258.proposed_method: A novel audio codec tokenizer, ALMTokenizer, will be developed to convert audio signals into discrete tokens optimized for audio language modeling. The method introduces a query-based compression strategy, employing a set of learnable query tokens and transformer layers to capture holistic and contextual information across audio frames. Semantic richness is enhanced by integrating a masked autoencoder (MAE) loss, which encourages the model to capture global information, and by initializing the vector quantization (VQ) codebook with semantic priors derived from k-means clustering on pre-trained SSL model outputs (e.g., wav2vec2 and BEATs). Additionally, an autoregressive (AR) prediction loss is introduced to optimize the latent space for AR modeling, particularly improving token predictability in deeper VQ layers. The overall architecture includes Patchify and UnPatchify modules for audio framing, token interleaving and retrieval modules for sequence manipulation, and multi-scale residual vector quantization for compression.
dfa3013f9b9af4053e57d6250e0f2b7dc7ff6258.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on approximately 4,500 hours of audio data spanning speech (LibriTTS, MLS), sound (AudioSet), and music (Million Song Dataset) domains. The ALMTokenizer will be evaluated on standard benchmarks such as VCTK, AudioCaps, and MusicCaps for reconstruction and semantic performance. Baselines will include state-of-the-art audio tokenizers such as Encodec, DAC, Wavtokenizer, StableCodec, SpeechTokenizer, and MimiCodec. Evaluation metrics will cover objective reconstruction quality (UTMOS, DNS-MOS, PESQ, STOI, VISQOL, STFT loss, Mel loss), semantic information (ASR, emotion, sound, and music classification accuracy), and downstream audio language modeling tasks (text-to-speech, speech-to-text, audio captioning, text-to-sound, text-to-music, music captioning) using BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr-D, SPICE, SPIDEr, and other relevant metrics. Ablation studies will assess the impact of each component, including query-based compression, semantic priors, MAE loss, AR loss, and two-stage training strategies.
dfa3013f9b9af4053e57d6250e0f2b7dc7ff6258.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a query-based compression strategy for audio tokenization, enabling holistic context modeling across frames and dynamic bitrate control. It is the first to comprehensively integrate semantic priors into all VQ layers for both speech and general sound, rather than just the first layer or speech-only tasks. The combination of MAE loss and AR prediction loss in the training objective is novel for audio codec models, enhancing both semantic richness and autoregressive modeling suitability. The resulting tokenizer achieves superior performance in both reconstruction and semantic tasks at lower bitrates compared to previous state-of-the-art methods, and is validated across a wide range of audio understanding and generation tasks.

dfb8cf117dc2ccf1f326bb17b489547007fce85d.title: SE(3) Equivariant Augmented Coupling Flows
dfb8cf117dc2ccf1f326bb17b489547007fce85d.research_question: How can a normalizing flow architecture be developed that operates directly on the Cartesian coordinates of atoms, while preserving SE(3) (rotation and translation) and permutation equivariance, to enable fast and unbiased probabilistic modeling and sampling of physical systems such as molecules and particle systems?
dfb8cf117dc2ccf1f326bb17b489547007fce85d.hypothesis: A coupling flow architecture that augments the input space with auxiliary variables and applies projection-based transformations into SE(3)-invariant bases can achieve SE(3) and permutation equivariance, enabling efficient and unbiased modeling of the Boltzmann distribution over Cartesian coordinates, with fast sampling and density evaluation competitive with or superior to existing equivariant continuous normalizing flows and diffusion models.
dfb8cf117dc2ccf1f326bb17b489547007fce85d.proposed_method: A novel SE(3)×S_n equivariant augmented coupling flow will be constructed, operating on the zero-center-of-mass (CoM) subspace of Cartesian coordinates. The method introduces auxiliary augmented variables, which are acted upon jointly with the observed variables by SE(3) and permutation symmetries. Each coupling layer consists of (1) a shift-CoM transform to swap the center of mass between observed and augmented variables, and (2) a core transformation that projects atomic positions into a learned SE(3)-invariant basis using an equivariant neural network, applies a flexible normalizing flow transformation (such as monotonic rational-quadratic splines or affine mappings) in the invariant space, and then projects back to the original space. Multiple projection strategies (Cartesian, spherical, and vector-based) will be explored for the invariant basis construction. The base distribution is chosen to be SE(3) and permutation invariant, and training is performed either by maximum likelihood on samples or by energy-based objectives using annealed importance sampling (FAB) when only unnormalized densities are available.
dfb8cf117dc2ccf1f326bb17b489547007fce85d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the DW4 and LJ13 particle systems, as well as the QM9-positional and alanine dipeptide datasets. The proposed method (with all projection variants) will be compared against baselines including non-equivariant augmented flows (with data augmentation), SE(3)-equivariant continuous normalizing flows (CNFs) trained by maximum likelihood and flow matching, SE(3)-equivariant diffusion models, and flows operating on internal coordinates. Evaluation metrics will include negative log-likelihood (NLL), Kullback-Leibler divergence (KLD) of Ramachandran plots (for alanine dipeptide), and effective sample size (ESS) for both forward and reverse directions. Sampling and density evaluation speed will also be measured. Energy-based training will be performed using the FAB algorithm, with results compared in terms of ESS and NLL. All methods will be run for multiple seeds, and standard errors will be reported.
dfb8cf117dc2ccf1f326bb17b489547007fce85d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to achieve SE(3) and permutation equivariance in a coupling flow operating directly on Cartesian coordinates, enabling unbiased and efficient modeling of the Boltzmann distribution for molecules and particle systems. The method allows for fast sampling and density evaluation—over an order of magnitude faster than existing SE(3)-equivariant CNFs and diffusion models—while maintaining competitive or superior performance. It is also the first to learn the full Boltzmann distribution of alanine dipeptide using only Cartesian coordinates. The projection-based coupling transform provides a flexible and generalizable framework for incorporating physical symmetries into normalizing flows, and the approach is tractable for energy-based training where other methods are computationally infeasible.

e002b6ce5283d88ce0c21afbca27b3aea091e78f.title: Booster: Tackling Harmful Fine-tuning for Large Language Models via Attenuating Harmful Perturbation
e002b6ce5283d88ce0c21afbca27b3aea091e78f.research_question: Can information from harmful datasets be leveraged during the alignment stage to immunize large language models against harmful fine-tuning attacks, thereby improving robustness without sacrificing downstream task performance?
e002b6ce5283d88ce0c21afbca27b3aea091e78f.hypothesis: Introducing a regularizer during the alignment stage that attenuates the reduction of harmful loss after simulated harmful perturbation will enhance the robustness of large language models to harmful fine-tuning attacks while maintaining or improving downstream task accuracy.
e002b6ce5283d88ce0c21afbca27b3aea091e78f.proposed_method: A novel alignment-stage defense, termed Booster, is proposed to mitigate the impact of harmful fine-tuning attacks on large language models. The method augments the standard alignment loss with a regularizer that penalizes the reduction in harmful loss after a simulated gradient step in the direction of harmful data. Specifically, the optimization objective includes the original alignment loss and an additional term measuring the difference in harmful loss before and after a normalized gradient step on the harmful dataset. The approach is efficiently solved via an iterative gradient-based algorithm, requiring three forward/backward passes per optimization step: one for alignment data, one for harmful data, and one for the simulated post-perturbation harmful data. Hyperparameters such as the regularizer intensity and inner step size are tuned to balance defense strength and model performance.
e002b6ce5283d88ce0c21afbca27b3aea091e78f.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using Llama2-7B, Gemma2-9B, and Qwen2-7B models. The alignment and harmful datasets are derived from BeaverTails, with 5000 samples each for alignment and harmful data. Fine-tuning tasks include SST2, AGNEWS, GSM8K, and AlpacaEval, with varying proportions of harmful data mixed into the fine-tuning set to simulate attacks. Baselines include SFT (standard supervised fine-tuning), Lisa (a fine-tuning stage solution), and two alignment-stage defenses: Vaccine and RepNoise. Evaluation metrics are Finetune Accuracy (FA) on downstream tasks and Harmful Score (HS), which measures the proportion of unsafe outputs on malicious prompts. Training uses LoRA for efficient adaptation, AdamW optimizer, and consistent batch sizes and epochs across methods. System overhead (training time and GPU memory) is also measured.
e002b6ce5283d88ce0c21afbca27b3aea091e78f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of harmful perturbation as a root cause of alignment failure and is the first to directly minimize the harmful loss reduction rate via a regularizer in the alignment stage. The Booster algorithm simulates the effect of harmful fine-tuning during alignment, providing a proactive defense that is computationally efficient since it incurs overhead only once at alignment. Booster demonstrates superior robustness to harmful fine-tuning compared to existing alignment-stage and fine-tuning-stage defenses, with significant reductions in harmful score and maintenance or improvement of downstream accuracy. The method is generalizable across multiple model architectures and tasks, and can be combined with other defenses for further enhancement.

e01515c6138bc525f7aec30fc85f2adf028d4156.title: Principle-Driven Self-Alignment of Language Models from Scratch with Minimal Human Supervision
e01515c6138bc525f7aec30fc85f2adf028d4156.research_question: How can large language models be aligned with human values and intentions, such as helpfulness, ethical behavior, and reliability, using minimal human supervision and without reliance on extensive human-annotated datasets or pre-aligned teacher models?
e01515c6138bc525f7aec30fc85f2adf028d4156.hypothesis: A principle-driven self-alignment framework, leveraging a small set of human-defined principles and minimal annotated examples, can effectively align large language models from scratch to produce helpful, ethical, and reliable responses, achieving or surpassing the performance of models trained with extensive human supervision.
e01515c6138bc525f7aec30fc85f2adf028d4156.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a four-stage principle-driven self-alignment framework for large language models. First, a Topic-Guided Red-Teaming Self-Instruct process is used to generate a diverse set of synthetic instructions and prompts, starting from a small set of manually crafted seed prompts and topic-specific adversarial instructions. Second, Principle-Driven Self-Alignment is performed by defining a compact set of human-written alignment principles and providing a handful of in-context learning demonstrations, guiding the model to generate responses that adhere to these principles. Third, a Principle Engraving stage fine-tunes the base language model on self-generated, principle-aligned responses, effectively internalizing the alignment rules into the model parameters and removing the need for explicit principle prompts at inference. Finally, a Verbose Cloning step employs context distillation to further refine the model, encouraging the generation of more comprehensive and detailed responses by training on verbose outputs produced by the principle-engraved model. This process is designed to require fewer than 300 lines of human annotation in total.
e01515c6138bc525f7aec30fc85f2adf028d4156.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the LLaMA-65B base language model, with the aligned model (Dromedary) evaluated against several state-of-the-art baselines, including Text-Davinci-003, Alpaca, Vicuna, ChatGPT, and Anthropic-LM. Evaluation will utilize benchmark datasets such as TruthfulQA (for truthfulness in multiple-choice and generative tasks), BIG-bench HHH (for helpfulness, honesty, and harmlessness), and the Vicuna benchmark (with GPT-4 as an automated evaluator for response quality). Metrics will include accuracy on multiple-choice tasks, the fraction of truthful and informative answers, and GPT-4-judged win/tie/lose rates in open-ended conversations. The experimental setup will compare both the non-verbose and verbose (final) variants of the proposed model, using consistent decoding parameters and, where relevant, in-context learning prompts for fair comparison.
e01515c6138bc525f7aec30fc85f2adf028d4156.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables language model alignment from scratch with minimal human supervision, requiring orders of magnitude fewer human annotations than existing methods such as SFT+RLHF or knowledge distillation from pre-aligned teacher models. Unlike prior open-source models that inherit alignment from extensively supervised teacher models, this method is independent of pre-existing aligned LLMs and instead engraves alignment principles directly into the model. The framework introduces a principled, rule-based alignment process that is both efficient and effective, achieving state-of-the-art or highly competitive results on multiple alignment benchmarks while drastically reducing annotation costs. The approach also provides a new paradigm for alignment—prioritizing harmlessness and reliability before helpfulness—and demonstrates the feasibility of principle-driven, self-supervised alignment for large language models.

e023272ec3eabf4473f42b17f76d961b81e3e6f0.title: Transferable Boltzmann Generators
e023272ec3eabf4473f42b17f76d961b81e3e6f0.research_question: Can a generative machine learning framework be developed to enable transferable, zero-shot sampling from Boltzmann distributions of unseen molecular systems, thereby overcoming the need for system-specific retraining and improving the efficiency of equilibrium sampling in molecular simulations?
e023272ec3eabf4473f42b17f76d961b81e3e6f0.hypothesis: A continuous normalizing flow-based Boltzmann Generator, equipped with an equivariant graph neural network architecture that encodes molecular topology and sequence information, can generalize across chemical space and enable efficient, unbiased sampling from Boltzmann distributions of previously unseen molecules without retraining.
e023272ec3eabf4473f42b17f76d961b81e3e6f0.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a transferable Boltzmann Generator (TBG) based on continuous normalizing flows (CNFs), where the transformation from a simple prior (e.g., Gaussian) to the target Boltzmann distribution is parameterized by a vector field realized as an O(D)- and S(N)-equivariant graph neural network (EGNN). The architecture encodes each atom with a composite embedding that includes atom type, amino acid identity, and positional information within the peptide, ensuring transferability and symmetry invariance. Training employs flow matching, a simulation-free objective that directly matches the learned vector field to a conditional target, with normalization by atom count to accommodate variable system sizes. During inference, generated samples are post-processed to ensure correct molecular topology and chirality, using bond graph isomorphism checks and chirality validation, and only valid configurations are retained for reweighting to the target Boltzmann distribution.
e023272ec3eabf4473f42b17f76d961b81e3e6f0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on datasets of dipeptides and the alanine dipeptide system, using both classical and semi-empirical force fields. The TBG will be trained on a set of peptides and evaluated on unseen test peptides to assess zero-shot transferability. Baselines will include non-transferable Boltzmann Generators and the Timewarp method, which uses large time steps and Metropolis-Hastings acceptance. Evaluation metrics will include negative log-likelihood (NLL), effective sample size (ESS), the proportion of valid molecular configurations, and Wasserstein distance between generated and reference distributions (e.g., Ramachandran plots). Additional ablation studies will investigate the impact of training set size, data biasing, and architectural choices. Computational efficiency will be assessed in terms of energy evaluations and wall-clock time.
e023272ec3eabf4473f42b17f76d961b81e3e6f0.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first framework for transferable Boltzmann Generators capable of zero-shot generalization to unseen molecular systems without retraining. The method leverages a novel combination of continuous normalizing flows and a topology-aware, equivariant graph neural network architecture to encode molecular structure and sequence information. The approach enables efficient, unbiased sampling and reweighting for new molecules, demonstrating significant data efficiency and improved sampling quality over existing methods. Comprehensive ablation studies and comparisons with state-of-the-art baselines substantiate the claim of superior transferability and efficiency.

e023857638ba1a508711659cee20b6c248746afe.title: A Simple Framework for Open-Vocabulary Zero-Shot Segmentation
e023857638ba1a508711659cee20b6c248746afe.research_question: How can open-vocabulary zero-shot segmentation be achieved efficiently and effectively using only image-caption pair datasets, without requiring dense pixel-level annotations or closed-vocabulary constraints?
e023857638ba1a508711659cee20b6c248746afe.hypothesis: A framework that leverages frozen vision-only models with strong spatial awareness, combined with a text encoder aligned exclusively to the vision model and guided by linguistic concept extraction from captions, can enable efficient and accurate open-vocabulary zero-shot segmentation.
e023857638ba1a508711659cee20b6c248746afe.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a framework, SimZSS, that utilizes a pretrained and frozen vision transformer (ViT) as the visual backbone, ensuring strong spatial and semantic coherence in image representations. Only the text encoder is trained, and it is aligned to the frozen vision model using a cross-modality consistency objective. Semantic concepts are extracted from image captions using a part-of-speech tagger to identify noun phrases, which are filtered through a predefined concept bank. These text concepts are mapped to the visual space via a learned linear projection. For each concept, similarity-based pooling retrieves the corresponding visual concept representation from the dense vision features. Cross-entropy loss is used to enforce consistency between text and visual concepts at both the global (image-caption) and local (concept-level) scales, with a weighted sum of these objectives guiding training. The approach requires only image-caption pairs for training and is compatible with both small curated and large-scale noisy datasets.
e023857638ba1a508711659cee20b6c248746afe.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using two pretraining datasets: COCO Captions (600K curated image-caption pairs) and LAION-400M (400M noisy web-scale pairs). Vision backbones include ViT-S/14 and ViT-B/14 pretrained with DINOv2, and ViT-B/16 pretrained with AugReg. The text encoder architecture matches that of CLIP but is randomly initialized. Evaluation will be performed on standard zero-shot segmentation benchmarks, including Pascal VOC, Pascal Context, COCO-Stuff, Cityscapes, and ADE20K, using mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) as the primary metric. Baselines for comparison include LiT, CLIP, GroupViT, TCL, MaskCLIP, OVDiff, and others. Training will use large batch sizes, warm-up and cosine decay schedules, and concept extraction will be performed using SpaCy with a concept bank derived from multiple segmentation datasets. Both foreground-only and background-inclusive segmentation scenarios will be evaluated, and zero-shot classification performance will also be assessed across 38 datasets.
e023857638ba1a508711659cee20b6c248746afe.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is simple, with minimal hyperparameters, and is robust to different vision backbones and pretraining methods. It decouples visual representation learning from cross-modality alignment, enabling high computational and data efficiency. The method exploits the discrete nature of text and linguistic knowledge for local concept identification, and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on multiple zero-shot segmentation benchmarks with rapid training times. Unlike prior approaches, it requires only image-caption pairs and no dense pixel-level annotations, and generalizes well to both curated and large-scale noisy datasets.

e0271cb75087ccfd4a8c3351e0f5189a6de04c03.title: The Lazy Neuron Phenomenon: On Emergence of Activation Sparsity in Transformers
e0271cb75087ccfd4a8c3351e0f5189a6de04c03.research_question: Why do activation maps in Transformer-based deep neural networks exhibit high levels of sparsity after training, and what are the implications of this sparsity for model efficiency, robustness, and calibration across different tasks and architectures?
e0271cb75087ccfd4a8c3351e0f5189a6de04c03.hypothesis: The emergence of activation sparsity in trained Transformers is primarily a result of the training dynamics rather than specific properties of the data, labels, or over-parameterization, and enforcing explicit sparsity will improve computational efficiency, robustness to noise, and confidence calibration.
e0271cb75087ccfd4a8c3351e0f5189a6de04c03.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical and theoretical investigation will be conducted into the emergence and effects of activation sparsity in Transformer architectures. The study will measure the percentage of nonzero entries in the intermediate outputs of multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) after ReLU activation across various Transformer models, including T5 and Vision Transformer (ViT), under different training regimes and data conditions. Controlled experiments will be designed to manipulate model depth, width, data scale, label structure, and input randomness, as well as to test the effect of explicit sparsity enforcement via a Top-k thresholding operation applied to MLP activations. Theoretical analysis will be performed to understand the role of training dynamics in inducing sparsity, particularly through gradient behavior at initialization.
e0271cb75087ccfd4a8c3351e0f5189a6de04c03.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize standard Transformer models such as T5 (trained on the C4 dataset for span corruption tasks) and ViT (trained on ImageNet-21k and ImageNet-1k for image classification). Sparsity will be measured at each MLP layer for both training and evaluation data, across different model configurations (varying depth and width), and with alternative architectures (e.g., BERT, MLP-mixers). Additional experiments will involve training with random labels, random images, and infinite data to isolate the effects of data and label structure. Baselines will include standard Transformers without explicit sparsity enforcement. Evaluation metrics will include activation sparsity (percentage of nonzero activations), model accuracy, robustness to noisy labels and input corruptions, calibration of prediction confidence, FLOP counts, and inference latency (e.g., on TPUv4 hardware). Top-k Transformers will be compared to vanilla Transformers to assess trade-offs between enforced sparsity and model performance.
e0271cb75087ccfd4a8c3351e0f5189a6de04c03.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a systematic, multi-faceted investigation into the emergent phenomenon of activation sparsity in Transformers, demonstrating its prevalence across tasks, architectures, and training conditions. It provides new theoretical insights linking training dynamics to sparsity emergence, independent of data or label structure. The proposed Top-k thresholding mechanism offers a simple yet effective architectural modification to control and leverage sparsity, yielding significant improvements in computational efficiency, robustness to noise, and prediction calibration, with minimal loss in accuracy. The work also pioneers empirical evaluation of sparsity-induced efficiency gains on modern hardware and explores the broader implications for neural network design.

e04261cb963b620159f015ef80eabb4f93dac776.title: Linear combinations of latents in generative models: subspaces and beyond
e04261cb963b620159f015ef80eabb4f93dac776.research_question: How can linear combinations of latent variables in generative models be constructed to ensure that manipulated latents (for interpolation, centroid determination, and subspace construction) adhere to the statistical assumptions of the model's latent distribution, thereby enabling high-quality and reliable generation across different modalities and architectures?
e04261cb963b620159f015ef80eabb4f93dac776.hypothesis: Effective manipulation of latent variables in generative models requires that the resulting latent vectors match the full statistical characteristics of the model's latent distribution, not just individual statistics such as the norm. Ensuring this adherence will improve the quality and reliability of generated outputs for a broad range of latent manipulations.
e04261cb963b620159f015ef80eabb4f93dac776.proposed_method: A general-purpose framework, Latent Optimal Linear combinations (LOL), is developed to form linear combinations of latent variables such that the resulting vectors exactly match the statistical properties (e.g., mean and covariance) of the original latent distribution. For Gaussian latents, the method applies a closed-form transport map to any linear combination, ensuring the output remains distributed as N(μ, Σ) regardless of the weights or operation (interpolation, centroid, or subspace projection). The approach is extended to arbitrary latent distributions using optimal transport theory. Additionally, standard statistical distribution tests (e.g., Kolmogorov-Smirnov) are incorporated to assess whether seed latents (such as those obtained via inversion) are valid samples from the assumed latent distribution before manipulation, providing a diagnostic tool for identifying and correcting deficient latents.
e04261cb963b620159f015ef80eabb4f93dac776.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on popular generative models, including Stable Diffusion 2.1 (diffusion model), Stable Diffusion 3 (flow matching model), and the SLIDE diffusion model trained on ShapeNet for 3D design. The evaluation will include tasks such as interpolation, centroid determination, and construction of low-dimensional subspaces. Baselines for comparison will include linear interpolation (LERP), spherical interpolation (SLERP), and Norm-Aware Optimization (NAO). Performance will be measured using Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for visual quality, class prediction accuracy for semantic preservation, and computational efficiency (runtime). Additional qualitative analysis will be performed on generated samples and subspaces. Distribution tests will be applied to latent vectors obtained via inversion from ImageNet1k to assess their validity and impact on downstream manipulations.
e04261cb963b620159f015ef80eabb4f93dac776.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a closed-form, model- and modality-agnostic framework for constructing linear combinations of latents that guarantees adherence to the original latent distribution, enabling reliable manipulation beyond interpolation (e.g., subspace construction) without retraining or model-specific adaptations. The approach generalizes to arbitrary latent distributions and provides theoretical guarantees via optimal transport. The integration of statistical distribution testing for latent validity is novel in the context of generative model manipulation, offering a principled diagnostic tool for improving generation quality. The method is significantly more efficient than optimization-based alternatives and is broadly applicable to a wide range of generative models.

e04d5f333adf82a3e5fde1a7b47b1fc0963601ad.title: On the Generalization of Representations in Reinforcement Learning
e04d5f333adf82a3e5fde1a7b47b1fc0963601ad.research_question: How does the choice of state representation in reinforcement learning affect the generalization ability of value function approximators, and can this relationship be theoretically characterized and empirically validated across different environments and agent architectures?
e04d5f333adf82a3e5fde1a7b47b1fc0963601ad.hypothesis: The generalization capacity of a state representation in reinforcement learning is determined by its effective dimension, with lower effective dimension leading to better generalization, and this relationship can be quantified through theoretical bounds and validated empirically.
e04d5f333adf82a3e5fde1a7b47b1fc0963601ad.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to characterize the generalization error of value function approximators using a given state representation. This framework will introduce the concept of effective dimension, derived from the feature matrix's coherence, to quantify the sample complexity and generalization capacity of any state representation. Theoretical excess risk bounds will be derived for least-squares regression in the batch Monte Carlo policy evaluation setting, applicable to both classic and learned representations. The approach will be specialized to analyze representations constructed from the top singular vectors of the successor representation (SR), and the implications of transition structure on effective dimension and generalization will be analytically and empirically investigated. Additionally, an auxiliary loss function aimed at reducing effective dimension will be proposed and evaluated in deep RL settings.
e04d5f333adf82a3e5fde1a7b47b1fc0963601ad.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both synthetic and large-scale RL environments. In synthetic domains, such as the four-room domain and various graph-based MDPs (e.g., grid, torus, fully connected, star, and disconnected graphs), the singular value spectrum and effective dimension of proto-value functions (PVFs) and other representations (Krylov basis, bisimulation metric, random features) will be computed and compared. Monte Carlo policy evaluation will be performed with sampled rewards and states to measure empirical excess risk, and results will be compared to theoretical predictions. In large-scale experiments, the effective dimension of learned representations in deep RL agents (DQN, Rainbow, IQN, Munchausen-IQN) will be estimated using activations from hidden layers on the Arcade Learning Environment (Atari 2600, 60 games), with performance and effective dimension tracked over training. An auxiliary feature regularization loss will be evaluated in the offline RL setting on 17 Atari games, comparing performance and effective dimension to standard agents. Evaluation metrics include excess risk, effective dimension, and human-normalized scores, with statistical significance assessed via interquartile mean and bootstrap confidence intervals.
e04d5f333adf82a3e5fde1a7b47b1fc0963601ad.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a general theoretical bound on the generalization error for value function approximation in RL, applicable to any state representation and explicitly quantifying the role of effective dimension. The effective dimension is shown to capture the trade-off between approximation and generalization, and its dependence on environment transition structure is analyzed both theoretically and empirically. The relationship between effective dimension and empirical agent performance is established across a wide range of deep RL agents and environments. Furthermore, a novel auxiliary loss for reducing effective dimension is proposed and shown to improve generalization and performance in offline RL. The work provides new insights into the design and evaluation of representations in RL, bridging theoretical analysis and practical deep learning applications.

e06217b5d1c0bad7e67eb70094bd4a327359f6ef.title: Lisa: Lazy Safety Alignment for Large Language Models against Harmful Fine-tuning Attack
e06217b5d1c0bad7e67eb70094bd4a327359f6ef.research_question: Can a computationally efficient fine-tuning-stage mitigation strategy be developed to maintain safety alignment of large language models (LLMs) in the presence of harmful data mixed into user-provided fine-tuning datasets, while preserving model performance on downstream tasks?
e06217b5d1c0bad7e67eb70094bd4a327359f6ef.hypothesis: Introducing a proximal term to constrain model drift during alternating optimization over alignment and user fine-tuning datasets will improve safety alignment robustness against harmful fine-tuning attacks, without significantly sacrificing downstream task accuracy.
e06217b5d1c0bad7e67eb70094bd4a327359f6ef.proposed_method: A novel Lazy Safety Alignment (Lisa) framework is proposed, building on a Bi-State Optimization (BSO) paradigm. In this method, the fine-tuning stage is separated into two alternating states: one optimizing over a safety alignment dataset and the other over the user fine-tuning dataset. To address convergence instability and excess drift between these states, a proximal term is incorporated into the loss function of each state, penalizing the Euclidean distance between the current model weights and the previous state's checkpoint. The proximal intensity parameter controls the strength of this constraint, ensuring that the model does not drift excessively towards either task and maintains a balance between alignment and customization. Theoretical analysis is provided to guarantee convergence under appropriate proximal intensity settings.
e06217b5d1c0bad7e67eb70094bd4a327359f6ef.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple LLMs, including Llama2-7B, Opt-3.7B, and Mistral-7B. The alignment dataset is derived from BeaverTails, while user fine-tuning tasks include SST2, AGNEWS, GSM8K, and AlpacaEval, with a portion of harmful data injected at varying ratios (e.g., 5-40%). Baselines for comparison include standard supervised fine-tuning (SFT), NonAligned-SFT, Vaccine-SFT, EWC, and Vlguard. Evaluation metrics are Finetune Accuracy (Top-1 accuracy on downstream tasks) and Harmful Score (ratio of unsafe outputs flagged by a moderation model). The experimental setup utilizes LoRA-based efficient adaptation, fixed batch sizes, and controlled step allocations between alignment and fine-tuning states. Ablation studies and hyperparameter analyses (e.g., proximal intensity, step allocation) are also planned.
e06217b5d1c0bad7e67eb70094bd4a327359f6ef.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first Bi-State Optimization approach for user fine-tuning to mitigate harmful data attacks, and is the first to identify and address the excess drift phenomenon as a key cause of alignment degradation under asymmetric computation. The Lazy Safety Alignment (Lisa) method innovatively incorporates a proximal term to control drift between optimization states, theoretically guaranteeing convergence and empirically demonstrating superior alignment robustness with minimal computational overhead. Lisa is shown to outperform existing baselines in reducing harmful outputs while maintaining or improving downstream task accuracy, and can be flexibly combined with other defense mechanisms such as data filtering or alignment-stage enhancements.

e070ff286709db28312e08b52b05539debe88146.title: Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap in Language Models
e070ff286709db28312e08b52b05539debe88146.research_question: How can the compositional reasoning abilities of large language models be systematically measured and improved, particularly in tasks where solutions require composing answers to multiple sub-problems?
e070ff286709db28312e08b52b05539debe88146.hypothesis: Explicit decomposition of compositional questions into sub-questions, coupled with structured prompting and external knowledge retrieval, will significantly narrow the compositionality gap and improve language model performance on multi-hop reasoning tasks.
e070ff286709db28312e08b52b05539debe88146.proposed_method: A comprehensive methodology will be developed to quantify the compositional reasoning capabilities of language models using multi-hop question answering tasks. The approach introduces the 'compositionality gap' metric, defined as the proportion of cases where a model answers all sub-questions correctly but fails to answer the overall compositional question. To facilitate robust evaluation, new datasets will be constructed, including a large, automatically generated set (Compositional Celebrities) and a smaller, hand-crafted set (Bamboogle), both designed to require composition of facts unlikely to have co-occurred in training data. The method will further explore elicitive prompting strategies, such as chain-of-thought and a novel 'self-ask' prompting framework, where the model explicitly generates and answers follow-up sub-questions before producing a final answer. Additionally, the self-ask framework will be integrated with an internet search engine to answer sub-questions, enabling dynamic retrieval of up-to-date information and further enhancing compositional reasoning.
e070ff286709db28312e08b52b05539debe88146.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four datasets: Compositional Celebrities (CC), Bamboogle, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and Musique. The evaluation will use a range of GPT-3 model variants (including InstructGPT) of varying sizes, with few-shot prompting applied across all methods. Baselines will include direct prompting, chain-of-thought prompting, and search engine-based approaches. The primary evaluation metric will be exact match accuracy for compositional questions and their sub-questions, with the compositionality gap calculated for each model and prompting strategy. The impact of model scale, prompt structure, and integration with external search will be systematically assessed. Additional metrics such as speed (average tokens generated) and answer format consistency will be tracked. Experiments will also analyze the relationship between model confidence (perplexity) on sub-questions and compositional question accuracy.
e070ff286709db28312e08b52b05539debe88146.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the compositionality gap as a formal metric for evaluating compositional reasoning in language models, providing a systematic framework for disentangling memorization from reasoning. It presents two new datasets specifically designed to probe compositional abilities beyond rote recall. The self-ask prompting method is proposed as a novel approach to explicit question decomposition, outperforming prior elicitive prompting strategies. Furthermore, the integration of self-ask with real-time internet search is claimed to be a scalable, architecture-agnostic enhancement that further improves multi-hop reasoning performance. The research aims to demonstrate that these innovations collectively enable more accurate and interpretable compositional reasoning in large language models.

e085621bf6fa90a0437b3112b0408362e3bea7cc.title: A Theory of Non-Acyclic Generative Flow Networks
e085621bf6fa90a0437b3112b0408362e3bea7cc.research_question: How can the theoretical framework and training methodology of Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets) be extended to handle non-acyclic (cyclic) and continuous state spaces, and what stable loss functions can be designed to ensure effective training and sampling in such settings?
e085621bf6fa90a0437b3112b0408362e3bea7cc.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by generalizing the theory of GFlowNets to measurable spaces without acyclicity constraints and by designing new families of stable loss functions, it is possible to prevent pathological behaviors such as flow divergence in cycles, thereby enabling effective training and sampling in cyclic and continuous environments.
e085621bf6fa90a0437b3112b0408362e3bea7cc.proposed_method: A new theoretical framework will be developed to generalize GFlowNets from directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) to general measurable spaces, including those with cycles and continuous state spaces. The approach will formalize edge flows as measures on state transitions and introduce a generalized notion of cycles (0-flows) in this context. The stability of existing loss functions (Flow Matching, Detailed Balance, Trajectory Balance) will be analyzed, revealing their instability in the presence of cycles. A family of stable loss functions will be defined, based on divergence-like measures that are invariant to the addition of 0-flows, and regularization techniques will be proposed to further enhance stability. The method will include explicit mathematical conditions for loss stability and provide practical loss function instantiations for both discrete and continuous domains.
e085621bf6fa90a0437b3112b0408362e3bea7cc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several domains: (1) synthetic graph-based environments such as hypergrids and Cayley graphs, where cycles are intrinsic, and (2) continuous control tasks (e.g., Point-Robot-Sparse) with sparse rewards and cyclic trajectories. For each domain, models trained with proposed stable losses will be compared against those trained with standard (unstable) GFlowNet losses and relevant baselines such as Metropolis-Hastings MCMC and reinforcement learning algorithms (PPO, DDPG, SAC, TD3). Evaluation metrics will include convergence of the flow, expected reward, expected path length, number of valid-distinctive trajectories explored, and stability of training (e.g., variance in reward). Experimental setups will use adjacency matrices or neural parameterizations for edge flows, and in continuous settings, density-based flow representations. Hyperparameters for stable loss instantiations (e.g., exponents, regularization strengths) will be systematically explored.
e085621bf6fa90a0437b3112b0408362e3bea7cc.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a generalization of GFlowNets to measurable spaces without acyclicity constraints, enabling application to cyclic and continuous domains. It provides the first theoretical analysis of loss instability in the presence of cycles and formally defines stability for loss functions in this context. A novel family of stable loss functions and regularization strategies is proposed, with explicit mathematical conditions for stability. The approach is validated in both discrete and continuous settings, demonstrating robust training and effective sampling even in highly cyclic environments. This work advances the theoretical foundation of GFlowNets and broadens their applicability beyond DAGs.

e086a9009a857fbe26dd83a34854a4c317f575b8.title: One Step Diffusion via Shortcut Models
e086a9009a857fbe26dd83a34854a4c317f575b8.research_question: Can a generative modeling framework be developed that enables high-quality sample generation in a single or few steps, while retaining the benefits of diffusion-based training and avoiding the complexity and inefficiency of multi-stage or scheduled training procedures?
e086a9009a857fbe26dd83a34854a4c317f575b8.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that conditioning a generative model on both the current noise level and the desired step size, and training it with a self-consistency objective, will enable accurate and efficient one-step or few-step sample generation without sacrificing quality or requiring complex training schedules.
e086a9009a857fbe26dd83a34854a4c317f575b8.proposed_method: A novel family of generative models, termed shortcut models, will be developed to support variable-step denoising by conditioning the network on both the noise level and the desired step size. The model is trained end-to-end using a combined loss: for small step sizes, a flow-matching objective regresses onto empirical velocity samples; for larger step sizes, a self-consistency loss is used, where the model is trained to ensure that a shortcut of size 2d is consistent with two sequential shortcuts of size d. Training batches will be split between empirical (d=0) and self-consistency (d>0) targets, with the latter constructed recursively using the model's own predictions. The approach eliminates the need for separate pretraining, distillation, or scheduling, and requires only a single network and training phase. Additional techniques such as classifier-free guidance (for small steps), exponential moving average weights, and weight decay will be incorporated to enhance stability and sample quality.
e086a9009a857fbe26dd83a34854a4c317f575b8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation benchmarks, including CelebA-HQ-256 (unconditional) and ImageNet-256 (class-conditional), using the DiT-B diffusion transformer architecture and the sd-vae-ft-mse autoencoder latent space. The AdamW optimizer with a fixed learning rate and weight decay will be used. Shortcut models will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines: standard diffusion and flow-matching models, two-stage distillation methods (Reflow, Progressive Distillation, Consistency Distillation), and end-to-end methods (Consistency Training, LiveReflow). All methods will be trained from scratch using the same architecture and codebase, with equivalent or greater compute allocated to baselines. Evaluation will be performed using the FID-50k metric on samples generated with 128, 4, and 1 denoising steps. Additional experiments will assess model scaling effects, latent space interpolation, and generalization to non-image domains such as robotic control (Push-T and Transport tasks), comparing shortcut policies to iterative and one-step baselines.
e086a9009a857fbe26dd83a34854a4c317f575b8.novelty_claims: Shortcut models introduce a new, end-to-end trainable framework for generative modeling that supports high-quality one-step and few-step generation by conditioning on step size and leveraging a self-consistency loss. Unlike prior distillation or consistency-based methods, shortcut models require only a single training phase, avoid complex schedules, and provide flexibility in inference step budgets post-training. The method achieves competitive or superior sample quality compared to both two-stage and end-to-end baselines, drastically reduces inference cost, and generalizes to domains beyond image generation. The approach also demonstrates scalability with model size and provides a simple, practical recipe for fast, high-quality generative modeling.

e0b35be05aa8724aeb1f20ff4f28e4991086ae7d.title: Achieving Counterfactual Fairness for Anomaly Detection
e0b35be05aa8724aeb1f20ff4f28e4991086ae7d.research_question: How can anomaly detection models be designed to ensure fairness from a counterfactual perspective, such that detection outcomes for individuals remain consistent even if their sensitive attributes were different?
e0b35be05aa8724aeb1f20ff4f28e4991086ae7d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a two-phase framework combining counterfactual data generation via causal modeling and adversarially trained anomaly detection can achieve counterfactual fairness without sacrificing anomaly detection performance.
e0b35be05aa8724aeb1f20ff4f28e4991086ae7d.proposed_method: A novel two-phase framework for counterfactually fair anomaly detection is proposed. In the first phase, counterfactual data is generated by modeling the data generation process as a generalized linear structural causal model (SCM). A graph autoencoder is used to learn the causal structure and estimate the adjacency matrix, followed by a variable-wise decoder to reconstruct data and generate high-fidelity counterfactual samples via the Abduction-Action-Prediction process. In the second phase, a standard fully-connected autoencoder is pre-trained on factual normal data for anomaly detection, and then fine-tuned using adversarial training. The adversarial component ensures that the hidden representations of factual and counterfactual samples are indistinguishable to a discriminator, thereby removing sensitive attribute information and enforcing counterfactual fairness. Only non-sensitive features are used for final anomaly detection.
e0b35be05aa8724aeb1f20ff4f28e4991086ae7d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on one synthetic dataset (with known ground-truth counterfactuals) and two real-world datasets: Adult (with 'gender' as the sensitive attribute and 'income > 50k' as anomalies) and COMPAS (with 'race' as the sensitive attribute and 'recidivists' as anomalies). All continuous features will be normalized and categorical features binarized. Baselines for comparison include PCA, OC-SVM, Isolation Forest, Autoencoder (AE), Deep Clustering-based Fair Outlier Detection (DCFOD), and Fairness-aware Outlier Detection (FairOD). Evaluation metrics will include Area Under Precision-Recall Curve (AUC-PR), Area Under Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC-ROC), Macro-F1 for detection effectiveness, and a changing ratio metric to quantify counterfactual fairness. Thresholds for anomaly detection will be set based on the 0.95 quantile of reconstruction errors or analogous criteria for each method.
e0b35be05aa8724aeb1f20ff4f28e4991086ae7d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to address counterfactual fairness—a causation-based fairness notion—in anomaly detection. The framework introduces a novel counterfactual data generation method using a graph autoencoder with a variable-wise decoder for accurate causal modeling, and combines this with adversarially trained anomaly detection to ensure that sensitive attributes do not affect detection outcomes. This method is claimed to achieve both high anomaly detection performance and strong counterfactual fairness, outperforming existing association-based fairness approaches.

e0eac8c64be3313e581c28a495bec192e7e67284.title: Latte: Latent Diffusion Transformer for Video Generation
e0eac8c64be3313e581c28a495bec192e7e67284.research_question: Can Transformer-based latent diffusion models effectively enhance the generation of realistic and temporally coherent videos, and what are the optimal architectural and training practices for such models?
e0eac8c64be3313e581c28a495bec192e7e67284.hypothesis: Transformer-based latent diffusion models, when equipped with efficient spatio-temporal decomposition strategies and best-practice architectural components, can outperform existing state-of-the-art video generation methods in both unconditional and text-to-video tasks.
e0eac8c64be3313e581c28a495bec192e7e67284.proposed_method: A novel video generation framework, Latte, will be developed by integrating a Transformer backbone within a latent diffusion model. The approach begins by encoding input videos into a latent space using a pre-trained variational autoencoder, from which spatio-temporal tokens are extracted. Four model variants will be designed to efficiently decompose and capture spatial and temporal information, including interleaved and late fusion of Transformer blocks, as well as decomposed multi-head attention mechanisms. The framework will incorporate advanced design choices such as uniform frame patch embedding, scalable adaptive layer normalization (S-AdaLN) for timestep/class information injection, absolute temporal positional embeddings, and joint image-video training strategies. The method will also explore initialization from pre-trained image Transformers and employ a linear decoder for reconstructing video outputs from latent tokens.
e0eac8c64be3313e581c28a495bec192e7e67284.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four standard video generation datasets: FaceForensics, SkyTimelapse, UCF101, and Taichi-HD. The evaluation will use Fréchet Video Distance (FVD), Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), and Inception Score (IS) as primary metrics, with a focus on FVD for alignment with human judgment. The proposed method will be compared against recent baselines such as MoCoGAN, VideoGPT, DIGAN, StyleGAN-V, PVDM, MoStGAN-V, LVDM, VDT, and W.A.L.T. Ablation studies will systematically evaluate the impact of patch embedding strategies, model variants, timestep/class information injection, temporal positional embeddings, pre-training, and joint training. Implementation will use the AdamW optimizer, EMA model averaging, and training on 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs, with all models initialized using a pre-trained VAE from Stable Diffusion 1.4.
e0eac8c64be3313e581c28a495bec192e7e67284.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first comprehensive Transformer-based latent diffusion framework for video generation with four efficient spatio-temporal decomposition variants. It systematically investigates and establishes best practices for architectural design and training strategies specific to Transformer-based video diffusion models, including novel approaches for patch embedding, timestep/class information injection, and joint image-video training. The method claims to achieve state-of-the-art performance on multiple standard video generation benchmarks and demonstrates competitive results on text-to-video generation tasks, providing new insights into the integration of Transformers within diffusion models for video synthesis.

e0f08f6a3584efa08652ed61508dba020abdb2d4.title: Flexible Tails for Normalizing Flows
e0f08f6a3584efa08652ed61508dba020abdb2d4.research_question: How can normalizing flows be enhanced to more effectively model probability distributions with heavy tails, particularly in high-dimensional settings and for applications in density estimation and variational inference?
e0f08f6a3584efa08652ed61508dba020abdb2d4.hypothesis: Introducing a final non-Lipschitz transformation layer, specifically designed to produce heavy tails, to a normalizing flow with a Gaussian base distribution will enable the resulting model to flexibly and accurately capture heavy-tailed distributions, outperforming existing methods that rely on heavy-tailed base distributions or alternative tail modeling approaches.
e0f08f6a3584efa08652ed61508dba020abdb2d4.proposed_method: A new framework, termed Tail Transform Flow (TTF), is proposed for normalizing flows. The method retains a standard Gaussian base distribution and standard normalizing flow transformations for the body of the distribution, but appends a final transformation layer specifically designed to induce heavy tails. This final transformation is based on the complementary error function (erfc) and is parameterized to allow separate control over the upper and lower tail weights, as well as location and scale. The transformation is applied independently to each marginal in the multivariate case, with parameters either learned jointly with the flow or fixed in a two-stage procedure. The approach is theoretically justified to convert light-tailed (Gaussian) outputs of standard flows into heavy-tailed outputs with tunable tail weights, thus expanding the class of distributions that can be modeled without sacrificing universality.
e0f08f6a3584efa08652ed61508dba020abdb2d4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic data will be generated from models with known heavy-tailed marginals, allowing for controlled variation of dimensionality and tail weight. Real-world datasets will include applications from insurance, finance, and climate science, all exhibiting extreme values. The proposed TTF and its two-stage variant (TTFfix) will be compared against several baselines: standard normalizing flows with Gaussian, Student's T, Gaussian mixture, and generalized normal base distributions, as well as state-of-the-art methods such as Marginal Tail-Adaptive Flows (mTAF), Generalized Tail-Adaptive Flows (gTAF), and COMET flows. Evaluation metrics will include negative log-likelihood (for density estimation) and importance sampling diagnostics (ESS, k̂) for variational inference. Each experimental configuration will be repeated multiple times to assess stability, and hyperparameters such as learning rates and stopping criteria will be standardized across methods for fair comparison.
e0f08f6a3584efa08652ed61508dba020abdb2d4.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel, theoretically justified transformation that enables normalizing flows with Gaussian bases to flexibly model heavy-tailed distributions, overcoming the limitations of Lipschitz transformations. Unlike prior approaches that require heavy-tailed base distributions—often problematic for neural network optimization—the TTF framework models extremes in the final layer, improving both stability and expressiveness. The method provides tunable, asymmetric tail weights and preserves universality properties of normalizing flows. Empirical results demonstrate superior or competitive performance to existing methods, especially in high-dimensional or strongly heavy-tailed scenarios, for both density estimation and variational inference.

e0f12956ccfc1ed005b54cb876d9173c4a18dc75.title: The Disagreement Problem in Explainable Machine Learning: A Practitioner's Perspective
