e0f12956ccfc1ed005b54cb876d9173c4a18dc75.research_question: To what extent do post hoc explanation methods for machine learning models produce conflicting explanations, and how do practitioners perceive and resolve these disagreements in practical, high-stakes settings?
e0f12956ccfc1ed005b54cb876d9173c4a18dc75.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that state-of-the-art post hoc explanation methods frequently disagree in their outputs for the same model predictions, and that practitioners lack systematic strategies for resolving such disagreements, often relying on ad hoc heuristics.
e0f12956ccfc1ed005b54cb876d9173c4a18dc75.proposed_method: A mixed-methods approach will be employed to investigate the disagreement problem in explainable machine learning. First, semi-structured interviews with experienced data scientists will be conducted to characterize what constitutes disagreement between explanations and how often such disagreements are encountered in practice. Insights from these interviews will inform the formalization of explanation disagreement, leading to the development of a quantitative framework comprising six novel metrics: feature agreement, rank agreement, sign agreement, signed rank agreement, rank correlation, and pairwise rank agreement. These metrics will capture disagreement in terms of top-k feature overlap, ordering, directionality, and user-specified feature relationships. The framework will then be applied to systematically measure disagreement between pairs of explanations generated by multiple explanation methods across various models and data modalities.
e0f12956ccfc1ed005b54cb876d9173c4a18dc75.experiment_details: Empirical analysis will be conducted using four real-world datasets spanning tabular (COMPAS, German Credit), text (AG_News), and image (ImageNet with PASCAL VOC segmentation) modalities. Predictive models will include logistic regression, random forest, gradient-boosted trees, feed-forward neural networks for tabular data, LSTM-based classifiers for text, and pre-trained ResNet-18 for images. Six state-of-the-art post hoc explanation methods will be evaluated: LIME, KernelSHAP, Vanilla Gradient, Gradient times Input, Integrated Gradients, and SmoothGrad. Disagreement metrics will be computed for each pair of explanation methods on test data, with analysis stratified by model type, data modality, and feature set size (top-k). Additionally, an online user study with data scientists will present pairs of conflicting explanations to assess practitioner strategies for resolving disagreements and the rationale behind their choices. Evaluation will focus on the frequency, severity, and patterns of disagreement, as well as practitioner decision-making processes.
e0f12956ccfc1ed005b54cb876d9173c4a18dc75.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first practitioner-informed, formal quantitative framework for measuring disagreement between machine learning explanation methods. It systematically investigates the prevalence and nature of explanation disagreements across multiple data modalities, models, and explanation techniques. The work uniquely combines qualitative practitioner insights with rigorous empirical analysis and user studies, providing actionable understanding of how explanation disagreements are perceived and resolved in real-world settings. This approach highlights the critical need for principled evaluation and comparison frameworks for explainability tools in high-stakes applications.

e122a6d15e1730258d41487f59b9bc218dc6a9f1.title: Expandable Subspace Ensemble for Pre-Trained Model-Based Class-Incremental Learning
e122a6d15e1730258d41487f59b9bc218dc6a9f1.research_question: How can class-incremental learning systems based on pre-trained models continually learn new classes without catastrophic forgetting or excessive resource requirements, and without relying on exemplars from previous tasks?
e122a6d15e1730258d41487f59b9bc218dc6a9f1.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that constructing lightweight, task-specific subspaces using adapter modules for each incremental task, combined with a semantic-guided prototype completion strategy, will enable efficient and effective class-incremental learning with pre-trained models, mitigating forgetting and eliminating the need for exemplars.
e122a6d15e1730258d41487f59b9bc218dc6a9f1.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces an expandable subspace ensemble framework for class-incremental learning with pre-trained models. For each new incremental task, a distinct lightweight adapter module is trained and attached to the frozen pre-trained backbone, creating a task-specific subspace that encodes new class features without interfering with previously learned knowledge. The features from all adapters and the pre-trained model are concatenated to form a holistic, high-dimensional representation. To address the incompatibility between expanding feature spaces and existing classifiers, a semantic-guided prototype complement strategy is developed: class-wise similarities in a co-occurrence subspace are computed and used to synthesize old class prototypes in the new subspace, enabling classifier expansion without the need for any old class exemplars. During inference, predictions are reweighted based on the compatibility between features and prototypes, and an ensemble decision is made across all subspaces, with additional emphasis on the adapter corresponding to the current task.
e122a6d15e1730258d41487f59b9bc218dc6a9f1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven benchmark datasets, including CIFAR100, CUB200, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, ObjectNet, OmniBenchmark, and VTAB, covering both standard and out-of-distribution scenarios. The evaluation will follow exemplar-free settings, using pre-trained Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16-IN21K and ViT-B/16-IN1K) models as backbones. Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art prompt-based and adapter-based CIL methods (e.g., L2P, DualPrompt, CODA-Prompt, SimpleCIL, ADAM), as well as traditional exemplar-based methods (e.g., iCaRL, DER, FOSTER, MEMO) with and without exemplars. Performance will be measured using average and last-stage accuracy across incremental steps, and ablation studies will assess the contribution of each component. Additional analyses will investigate parameter robustness and alternative prototype completion strategies.
e122a6d15e1730258d41487f59b9bc218dc6a9f1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel expandable subspace ensemble framework that enables efficient, exemplar-free class-incremental learning with pre-trained models. Key innovations include the use of lightweight, task-specific adapters to create expandable subspaces without modifying the pre-trained backbone, and a semantic-guided prototype complement mechanism that synthesizes old class prototypes in new subspaces based on class-wise similarities, eliminating the need for stored exemplars. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse benchmarks while maintaining low memory and computational overhead, and demonstrates robustness to hyperparameter choices and superior performance compared to both prompt-based and traditional exemplar-based baselines.

e13ce1337159fff765e78ebe6d6f0accaf60850a.title: LatentEditor: Text Driven Local Editing of 3D Scenes
e13ce1337159fff765e78ebe6d6f0accaf60850a.research_question: How can efficient, precise, and locally controlled editing of 3D scenes represented by neural radiance fields be achieved using only text prompts, without requiring additional user guidance or pre-computed masks?
e13ce1337159fff765e78ebe6d6f0accaf60850a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that embedding 3D scenes into the latent space of a diffusion model and leveraging a novel delta scoring mechanism can enable fast, accurate, and spatially consistent local editing of neural fields based solely on text prompts.
e13ce1337159fff765e78ebe6d6f0accaf60850a.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a framework that embeds real-world 3D scenes into the latent space of a stable diffusion model, enabling direct NeRF training and editing in this compressed domain. A delta module is designed to compute pixel-level delta scores by contrasting conditional and unconditional noise predictions from InstructPix2Pix (IP2P), generating 2D masks in the latent space that guide local edits. The NeRF model is optimized to reconstruct latent features, and a refinement adapter with residual and self-attention mechanisms ensures consistency between rendered and original latents. During editing, text prompts are processed to generate editing masks, and the NeRF is iteratively updated using edited latents, confining changes to targeted regions while preserving the rest of the scene. Multi-attribute editing is supported by decomposing prompts using a large language model, allowing simultaneous application of multiple local edits.
e13ce1337159fff765e78ebe6d6f0accaf60850a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four benchmark 3D datasets: LLFF, IN2N, NeRFStudio, and NeRF-Art. The evaluation will compare the proposed method against state-of-the-art NeRF editing frameworks, including IN2N, NeRF-Art, Control-4D, and DreamEditor. Key evaluation metrics will include editing speed, output quality, spatial and semantic consistency, and the ability to perform multi-attribute and local edits. The experimental setup will involve initializing the NeRF in latent space for 30,000 iterations, followed by 2,000–4,000 editing iterations depending on the number of training views, with hyperparameters set according to prior work for fair comparison.
e13ce1337159fff765e78ebe6d6f0accaf60850a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables text-driven local editing of 3D NeRF scenes without the need for pre-computed masks, bounding boxes, or additional user guidance. A novel delta module leverages diffusion model noise predictions to generate precise editing masks in latent space, allowing for targeted modifications. The method operates directly in the latent space, significantly reducing computational costs and editing time compared to existing methods. A refinement adapter with residual and self-attention mechanisms ensures high consistency between edited and original scene representations. The framework supports multi-attribute editing through prompt decomposition, offering broader and more flexible editing capabilities than prior approaches.

e147cc46b7f441a68706ca53549d45e9a9843fb6.title: GraphPrompt: Unifying Pre-Training and Downstream Tasks for Graph Neural Networks
e147cc46b7f441a68706ca53549d45e9a9843fb6.research_question: How can pre-training and downstream tasks for graph neural networks be unified under a common framework to enable more effective knowledge transfer, particularly in few-shot learning scenarios, and how can task-specific adaptability be incorporated to suit diverse downstream objectives such as node and graph classification?
e147cc46b7f441a68706ca53549d45e9a9843fb6.hypothesis: A unified framework that formulates both pre-training and downstream tasks as subgraph similarity learning, combined with a learnable, task-specific prompt mechanism to guide aggregation, will enable more effective transfer of pre-trained knowledge to diverse downstream tasks and improve performance, especially in few-shot settings.
e147cc46b7f441a68706ca53549d45e9a9843fb6.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a framework, GraphPrompt, that unifies pre-training and downstream tasks for graph neural networks (GNNs) by representing both as subgraph similarity learning problems. During pre-training, a self-supervised link prediction task is used, where the model learns to distinguish between positive (linked) and negative (unlinked) node pairs based on the similarity of their contextual subgraphs. The subgraph representations are generated using a GNN encoder followed by a ReadOut operation, typically implemented as a sum pooling of node embeddings within the subgraph. For downstream tasks, such as node or graph classification, a learnable, task-specific prompt vector is introduced to modulate the ReadOut operation, enabling the aggregation function to adaptively emphasize features most relevant to the specific task. The prompt is optimized via prompt tuning, where only the prompt parameters are updated while the pre-trained GNN weights are kept frozen, ensuring parameter efficiency and reducing reliance on labeled data.
e147cc46b7f441a68706ca53549d45e9a9843fb6.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on five public benchmark datasets: Flickr, PROTEINS, COX2, ENZYMES, and BZR, covering both node and graph classification tasks. The evaluation focuses on few-shot learning settings, with k-shot classification tasks constructed for each dataset (e.g., 1-shot and 50-shot for node classification, 5-shot for graph classification). Baseline comparisons include end-to-end GNNs (GCN, GraphSAGE, GAT, GIN), graph pre-training models (DGI, InfoGraph, GraphCL), and a graph prompt model (GPPT). The primary evaluation metric is accuracy, and extensive ablation studies are performed to assess the contributions of the prompt mechanism and parameter efficiency. Hyperparameters for all models are tuned for optimal performance, and the same pre-trained model is used for both node and graph classification tasks on datasets where both tasks are applicable.
e147cc46b7f441a68706ca53549d45e9a9843fb6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach claims the first unified framework for pre-training and downstream tasks in GNNs based on subgraph similarity, applicable to both node and graph classification. It introduces a novel, learnable, task-specific prompt mechanism that guides the aggregation (ReadOut) operation in downstream tasks, enabling task adaptability without fine-tuning the entire GNN. This design achieves high parameter efficiency and strong performance in few-shot learning settings, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. The method also demonstrates that a single pre-trained model, when combined with task-specific prompts, can effectively generalize across different downstream objectives.

e151de8c75bebc628c0aab3056ff259d35c49773.title: AC-LoRA: (Almost) Training-Free Access Control-Aware Multi-Modal LLMs
e151de8c75bebc628c0aab3056ff259d35c49773.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs), including multi-modal variants, be deployed in organizational settings with strict access control requirements, ensuring information isolation and efficient knowledge retrieval without incurring prohibitive training or inference costs?
e151de8c75bebc628c0aab3056ff259d35c49773.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that maintaining separate fine-tuned LoRA adapters for distinct permissioned datasets, combined with a training-free, similarity-based retrieval and mixing mechanism, can provide strong access control guarantees, efficient information isolation, and high-quality responses in multi-modal LLMs, without the need for exponential model proliferation or additional training for LoRA routing.
e151de8c75bebc628c0aab3056ff259d35c49773.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces an end-to-end access control-aware inference system for LLMs, termed AC-LORA. This system maintains separate LoRA adapters, each fine-tuned on isolated datasets corresponding to specific permission zones (e.g., departments or projects). At inference, user queries are embedded and compared via cosine similarity to document embeddings associated with each LoRA. The system retrieves the top-k most relevant LoRAs, filters them according to the user's permission vector, and dynamically merges their outputs using a similarity-weighted, training-free mixing mechanism at each model layer. The architecture is designed to scale efficiently with the number of permission zones, supports efficient updates (add, remove, or modify datasets or permissions), and extends to multi-modal LLMs by applying the same access control and mixing principles to text, image, and text-image models.
e151de8c75bebc628c0aab3056ff259d35c49773.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple datasets and model architectures to validate the approach. For text-based evaluation, the RepLiQA dataset (covering 17 domains with human-evaluated Q&A pairs) and the FlanV2 dataset (10 task domains) will be used, with models such as LLAMA3.1-8B-INSTRUCT and LLAMA2/3. For multi-modal evaluation, the WikiArts dataset (27 image style domains) will be used with models like QWEN2-VL and STABLE-DIFFUSION-V1-4. Baselines will include state-of-the-art LoRA mixing techniques (e.g., LoRARetriever, MoLE, MoELoRA) and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy (e.g., ROUGE, BLEU, exact match), retrieval precision (correct LoRA retrieval), response quality (graded by external LLMs), latency (time-to-first-token), and memory usage. Experiments will also assess the ability to combine knowledge across LoRAs and the impact of access control on information leakage.
e151de8c75bebc628c0aab3056ff259d35c49773.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to provide an end-to-end, training-free, access control-aware inference system for both text and multi-modal LLMs. It introduces a dynamic, similarity-based LoRA retrieval and mixing mechanism that eliminates the need for exponential numbers of models or additional training for routing, while ensuring strict information isolation. The method supports efficient updates and arbitrary permission rules, and demonstrates that combining LoRAs can enhance information recall and response quality. The system is extensible to multi-modal scenarios and is designed for practical deployment in organizational settings with strong access control requirements.

e15900cf7c93d4b6e45a12fe3534840c910467e1.title: ELITE: Encoding Visual Concepts into Textual Embeddings for Customized Text-to-Image Generation
e15900cf7c93d4b6e45a12fe3534840c910467e1.research_question: How can customized visual concepts be efficiently and accurately encoded into textual embeddings for fast and editable text-to-image generation, overcoming the computational and memory burdens of existing optimization-based approaches?
e15900cf7c93d4b6e45a12fe3534840c910467e1.hypothesis: A learning-based encoder that utilizes both global and local mapping networks to encode hierarchical image features into textual embeddings will enable faster, more accurate, and more editable customized text-to-image generation compared to optimization-based methods.
e15900cf7c93d4b6e45a12fe3534840c910467e1.proposed_method: A novel learning-based encoder, termed ELITE, is proposed for encoding visual concepts into textual embeddings suitable for customized text-to-image generation. The method employs a pre-trained CLIP image encoder to extract hierarchical features from a user-provided image. A global mapping network projects these features into the textual word embedding space, learning a primary word for the main concept and auxiliary words for irrelevant disturbances. Simultaneously, a local mapping network encodes patch-level features into the textual feature space, which are injected into additional cross-attention layers of the diffusion model to provide fine-grained details without sacrificing editability. During generation, only the primary word embedding is used for guidance, ensuring robust editing capability while maintaining high fidelity to the input concept.
e15900cf7c93d4b6e45a12fe3534840c910467e1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Stable Diffusion model (v1-4) as the text-to-image backbone. The global and local mapping networks are trained on the OpenImages dataset, utilizing 125,000 images with 600 object classes, with object crops and masks extracted via bounding box and segmentation annotations. For evaluation, 20 user-defined concept images (e.g., dog, cat, toy) are used, and 25 editing prompts per subject are applied, generating 2,500 images in total. Baselines for comparison include Textual Inversion, DreamBooth, and Custom Diffusion, with official implementations and default hyperparameters. Evaluation metrics include CLIP-I (image-image similarity), CLIP-T (text-image similarity), DINO-I (visual similarity using ViT/DINO), and optimization time. Ablation studies will assess the impact of multi-layer features, local mapping, and fusion parameters. User studies will be conducted to assess text alignment, image alignment, and editing alignment.
e15900cf7c93d4b6e45a12fe3534840c910467e1.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a learning-based encoder that directly maps visual concepts into textual embeddings, significantly reducing computational and memory requirements compared to optimization-based approaches. The use of both global and local mapping networks enables the separation of primary concept and irrelevant disturbances, as well as the injection of fine-grained details without degrading editability. The method achieves near-instantaneous concept encoding (0.05s) and demonstrates superior or comparable performance in text alignment, image fidelity, and editing robustness. This approach enables practical, efficient, and flexible customization of text-to-image generation models.

e19b54ad4c1c8af045069e9cac350ffc2ce60e1a.title: No Language Left Behind: Scaling Human-Centered Machine Translation
e19b54ad4c1c8af045069e9cac350ffc2ce60e1a.research_question: How can high-quality, safe, and ethical machine translation be scaled to support over 200 languages, with a particular focus on low-resource languages, while addressing the needs and values of native speaker communities?
e19b54ad4c1c8af045069e9cac350ffc2ce60e1a.hypothesis: A human-centered approach that combines novel data mining techniques, large-scale multilingual datasets, advanced model architectures (such as sparsely gated mixture-of-experts), and comprehensive evaluation (including toxicity detection and human assessment) will significantly improve translation quality and safety for both low- and high-resource languages, enabling effective support for over 200 languages.
e19b54ad4c1c8af045069e9cac350ffc2ce60e1a.proposed_method: The proposed methodology begins with a human-centered design, incorporating exploratory interviews with native speakers of low-resource languages to inform ethical and practical requirements. Large-scale multilingual datasets will be created, including professionally translated benchmarks (e.g., Flores-200, NLLB-Seed) and mined bitexts using advanced language identification and sentence encoding techniques (such as LASER3). A conditional compute model based on a sparsely gated mixture-of-experts architecture will be trained on this data, with curriculum learning, self-supervised training on monolingual corpora, and data augmentation strategies to enhance generalization and prevent overfitting. The approach will also include the development of toxicity detection resources and benchmarks for all supported languages, ensuring translation safety.
e19b54ad4c1c8af045069e9cac350ffc2ce60e1a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on over 40,000 translation directions using the Flores-200 benchmark, which covers 204 languages, and additional seed and multi-domain datasets. Baseline comparisons will include previous state-of-the-art multilingual translation models, with evaluation metrics such as BLEU for automatic assessment and extensive human evaluation for qualitative analysis. A novel toxicity benchmark will be applied to all translation directions to assess and mitigate harmful outputs. The experimental setup will also include ablation studies on model architecture, data augmentation, and training strategies, as well as out-of-domain generalization tests and model distillation for efficiency.
e19b54ad4c1c8af045069e9cac350ffc2ce60e1a.novelty_claims: Key innovations include the creation of the largest human-translated multilingual benchmark (Flores-200), new techniques for mining and cleaning low-resource language data at scale, the application of a sparsely gated mixture-of-experts model to massively multilingual translation, and the integration of human-centered design principles throughout the process. The proposal also introduces a comprehensive toxicity detection benchmark for all supported languages and demonstrates significant improvements in translation quality—achieving a 44% BLEU increase over previous state-of-the-art results. All datasets, models, and tools will be open sourced to facilitate future research and practical deployment.

e1a1af352e80e870569ea5d3e3d4bf49eceeb978.title: Streaming Euclidean Max-Cut: Dimension vs Data Reduction
e1a1af352e80e870569ea5d3e3d4bf49eceeb978.research_question: How can the Max-Cut value be efficiently approximated for high-dimensional Euclidean datasets in the dynamic geometric streaming model, with space complexity that scales polynomially with the dimension and approximation parameter?
e1a1af352e80e870569ea5d3e3d4bf49eceeb978.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a data reduction approach based on importance sampling, combined with a geometric tree embedding, can achieve a (1+ε)-approximation to the Max-Cut value in high-dimensional Euclidean spaces using space poly(ε⁻¹ d logΔ), thereby overcoming the exponential dependence on ε⁻¹ found in previous dimension-reduction approaches.
e1a1af352e80e870569ea5d3e3d4bf49eceeb978.proposed_method: The proposed method constructs a streaming algorithm for the Euclidean Max-Cut problem by employing a data reduction technique based on importance sampling. The approach first defines a sampling distribution where each point is sampled with probability proportional to its total distance to all other points in the dataset, serving as a proxy for its contribution to the Max-Cut value. To implement this in the streaming setting, a randomly-shifted quadtree is constructed over the input domain, providing a tree embedding of the metric space. The algorithm samples points according to their tree-based importance, compensating for the embedding's distortion by increasing the sample size as needed. The sampled subset is re-weighted appropriately, and the Max-Cut value is estimated by solving the problem exactly on this reduced, weighted instance, which is feasible due to its small size.
e1a1af352e80e870569ea5d3e3d4bf49eceeb978.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and/or real datasets represented as point sets in [Δ]^d, with varying dimensionality d and domain size Δ. The streaming input will consist of dynamic sequences of point insertions and deletions. The proposed algorithm will be evaluated against prior approaches, particularly the dimension-reduction-based streaming algorithm, using space complexity, approximation ratio (1+ε), and success probability as primary metrics. Baseline comparisons will include existing (1+ε)-approximation algorithms with exponential space in d or ε⁻¹. The evaluation will also consider the impact of the quadtree embedding's distortion and the effectiveness of the importance sampling distribution.
e1a1af352e80e870569ea5d3e3d4bf49eceeb978.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first streaming algorithm for Euclidean Max-Cut in high dimensions that achieves a (1+ε)-approximation using space polynomial in the dimension, the inverse approximation parameter, and logΔ. The data reduction approach via importance sampling is novel in the context of Max-Cut for geometric streams, and the development of a geometric sampler based on a randomly-shifted quadtree is a new technical contribution. The method bypasses the limitations of dimension reduction, particularly the exponential dependence on ε⁻¹, and extends to all ℓ_p norms for p ≥ 1. The geometric sampling primitive developed may also be of independent interest for other streaming problems.

e1c4c02e22b2bb21cfe100667c3969a05e5fa6fe.title: How Effective Can Dropout Be in Multiple Instance Learning ?
e1c4c02e22b2bb21cfe100667c3969a05e5fa6fe.research_question: How can dropout techniques be effectively leveraged to improve the generalization and performance of multiple instance learning (MIL) models, particularly in weakly-supervised settings such as whole slide image (WSI) classification?
e1c4c02e22b2bb21cfe100667c3969a05e5fa6fe.hypothesis: Systematically dropping the top-k most important instances within a bag during MIL training will reduce overfitting, encourage the discovery of diverse and generalizable features, and improve both classification accuracy and robustness to noise, compared to standard random dropout or no dropout.
e1c4c02e22b2bb21cfe100667c3969a05e5fa6fe.proposed_method: A novel MIL-specific dropout method, termed MIL-Dropout, will be developed to systematically identify and drop the top-k most important instances in each bag during training. Instance importance will be determined using a non-parametric, averaging-based attention mechanism applied to the feature embeddings at each layer, followed by a sigmoid activation to generate importance weights. To further encourage diversity, a query-based mechanism will be used to select additional instances that are highly similar to the top-k, based on cosine similarity of their feature representations. The selected set of important and similar instances will be masked (zeroed out) in the feature map, with normalization to stabilize training. MIL-Dropout will be integrated into various MIL aggregator architectures without introducing additional learnable parameters and will only be applied during training.
e1c4c02e22b2bb21cfe100667c3969a05e5fa6fe.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five standard MIL benchmark datasets (MUSK1, MUSK2, FOX, TIGER, ELEPHANT) and two WSI datasets (CAMELYON16 and TCGA-NSCLC). For WSIs, patches will be extracted using both ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 and SimCLR-based self-supervised models. MIL-Dropout will be incorporated into several MIL aggregators, including ABMIL, ABMIL-Gated, DSMIL, TransMIL, and DTFD-MIL. Baselines will include mi-Net, MI-Net, MI-Net with DS/RC, GNN-MIL, DP-MINN, NLMIL, ANLMIL, and standard versions of the aforementioned aggregators. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, F1 score, and AUC, with results reported as mean and standard deviation over multiple runs and cross-validation folds. Additional analyses will include robustness to noise attacks, ablation studies on hyperparameters (top-k and similarity count), and qualitative assessment of attention maps for lesion localization.
e1c4c02e22b2bb21cfe100667c3969a05e5fa6fe.novelty_claims: The proposed MIL-Dropout introduces a principled, instance-level dropout mechanism specifically tailored for MIL, leveraging attention-based importance and similarity-driven selection rather than random dropout. This approach is claimed to improve generalization by encouraging the model to discover diverse positive instances, reduce gradient direction error, and converge to flatter minima. MIL-Dropout is designed to be computationally efficient, parameter-free (except for two interpretable hyperparameters), and easily integrable into existing MIL frameworks. Empirical and theoretical analyses support its effectiveness in boosting performance and robustness across a wide range of MIL tasks, including digital pathology and standard MIL benchmarks.

e1d83574867c501975507a26212f530135dea7b4.title: Hamiltonian variational ansatz without barren plateaus
e1d83574867c501975507a26212f530135dea7b4.research_question: How can the trainability of variational quantum algorithms (VQAs), specifically those based on the Hamiltonian variational ansatz (HVA), be improved to avoid barren plateaus and enable efficient optimization for quantum many-body problems as system size increases?
e1d83574867c501975507a26212f530135dea7b4.hypothesis: Constraining the parameter initialization and/or optimization trajectory of the HVA, such that the circuit approximates local Hamiltonian evolution with bounded total parameter norm, will prevent the onset of barren plateaus and maintain gradient magnitudes that scale at most polynomially with system size.
e1d83574867c501975507a26212f530135dea7b4.proposed_method: A new initialization scheme will be developed for the Hamiltonian variational ansatz (HVA) in which the sum of all variational parameters per layer is constrained to scale inversely with the number of qubits (e.g., T = c/N for some constant c). The method will leverage analytic results and the Floquet-Magnus expansion to show that, under this constraint, the HVA circuit closely approximates time evolution under a local Hamiltonian, thus preserving non-vanishing gradients. Additionally, a parameter-constrained ansatz will be constructed that enforces this constraint throughout the optimization process, ensuring that the circuit remains in a trainable regime. Theoretical bounds will be derived to rigorously guarantee the absence of barren plateaus under these conditions.
e1d83574867c501975507a26212f530135dea7b4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both one-dimensional and two-dimensional spin-1/2 Heisenberg-XYZ models using the HVA. Multiple initialization strategies will be compared: (1) fully random initialization, (2) constrained initialization with the total parameter sum per layer set to T = c/N, and (3) small constant initialization with parameters sampled from a narrow range. Gradient magnitudes will be measured as a function of system size (up to 28 qubits) and circuit depth, and the scaling of gradients will be analyzed. Full variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) simulations will be performed using the Adam optimizer, comparing convergence rates and final energies across initialization methods. Both exact gradients and gradients estimated with finite measurement shots will be evaluated. Evaluation metrics include the scaling of average gradient magnitude, convergence to ground state energy, and robustness to shot noise.
e1d83574867c501975507a26212f530135dea7b4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach provides the first rigorous analytic proof that the HVA, under a specific parameter constraint, is free from barren plateaus and maintains trainable gradients even for large system sizes. The initialization scheme requires no additional classical or quantum resources and is not based on heuristics, distinguishing it from prior methods. The parameter-constrained ansatz is expressive enough for variational time evolution while guaranteeing trainability. Extensive numerical results up to 28 qubits support the theoretical findings, and the method is shown to outperform existing initialization strategies in both gradient scaling and VQE performance.

e22c03e7ca21ee07e2253960dcd4670cf955a3de.title: GaussianPro: 3D Gaussian Splatting with Progressive Propagation
e22c03e7ca21ee07e2253960dcd4670cf955a3de.research_question: How can the densification and optimization of 3D Gaussian representations for neural rendering be improved to achieve higher quality and more efficient novel view synthesis, particularly in large-scale and texture-less scenes?
e22c03e7ca21ee07e2253960dcd4670cf955a3de.hypothesis: A progressive propagation strategy that leverages geometric priors and patch matching techniques can guide the densification of 3D Gaussians, resulting in more accurate, compact, and robust scene representations, thereby improving rendering quality and efficiency, especially in challenging regions such as texture-less surfaces.
e22c03e7ca21ee07e2253960dcd4670cf955a3de.proposed_method: A novel progressive propagation strategy will be developed to guide the densification of 3D Gaussians in both 3D world space and 2D image space. The method will begin by rendering depth and normal maps from the current set of 3D Gaussians using alpha-blending. Iterative propagation will be performed on these maps, where for each pixel, depth and normal values from neighboring pixels are considered as candidates, and classical patch matching techniques are used to select the best candidate based on multi-view photometric consistency. Pixels with significant discrepancies between propagated and rendered depth are identified, and their positions are back-projected into 3D to initialize new Gaussians. Additionally, a planar constraint will be incorporated, enforcing consistency between Gaussian normals and propagated normals, and regularizing Gaussian shapes towards planar surfaces using a combination of L1, angular, and scale losses.
e22c03e7ca21ee07e2253960dcd4670cf955a3de.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the large-scale Waymo dataset and the MipNeRF360 dataset, covering both urban and indoor scenes. The evaluation will use standard neural rendering metrics: PSNR (Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio), SSIM (Structural Similarity Index Measure), and LPIPS (Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity). Baselines for comparison will include Instant-NGP, Mip-NeRF360, Zip-NeRF, and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), with both original and retrained versions. The proposed method will be implemented on top of the open-source 3DGS codebase, following its training schedule and hyperparameters, and will activate the propagation strategy every 50 iterations. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of the propagation strategy and planar constraint, and robustness will be evaluated by varying the number of training images. Efficiency and scalability will be analyzed by comparing training time, number of Gaussians, and rendering speed under different initialization strategies.
e22c03e7ca21ee07e2253960dcd4670cf955a3de.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a progressive propagation strategy that explicitly leverages geometric priors from reconstructed scene geometries and patch matching to guide the densification of 3D Gaussians, particularly improving coverage and accuracy in texture-less regions. The method further incorporates a novel planar constraint in the optimization process, encouraging Gaussians to better fit real scene geometry and planar surfaces. This results in more compact and accurate Gaussian representations, improved rendering quality, and robustness to varying numbers of input images. The approach achieves state-of-the-art results on challenging large-scale datasets and demonstrates a favorable balance between rendering quality and computational efficiency.

e23c8c2e9145c5fba798d11c1bcd65586b4127ad.title: Boosting Adversarial Transferability with Spatial Adversarial Alignment
e23c8c2e9145c5fba798d11c1bcd65586b4127ad.research_question: How can the transferability of adversarial examples across different deep neural network architectures, particularly between convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers (ViTs), be significantly improved in black-box attack settings?
e23c8c2e9145c5fba798d11c1bcd65586b4127ad.hypothesis: Aligning both spatial and adversarial features between surrogate and witness models will enable the generation of adversarial examples with substantially higher transferability across diverse model architectures.
e23c8c2e9145c5fba798d11c1bcd65586b4127ad.proposed_method: A novel framework, Spatial Adversarial Alignment (SAA), will be developed to enhance adversarial transferability by aligning both spatial and adversarial features between a surrogate model and a witness model. The approach consists of two main components: spatial-aware alignment and adversarial-aware alignment. Spatial-aware alignment minimizes the divergence between global and local features of the surrogate and witness models, using KL divergence for global logits and cross-entropy loss for local feature regions, where pseudo-labels from the witness model supervise the surrogate's local features. Adversarial-aware alignment introduces a self-adversarial strategy, generating adversarial examples using gradients with respect to the witness model's features, and further aligning both global and local adversarial features. The overall optimization objective combines these losses, with hyperparameters balancing their contributions, and training is performed via stochastic gradient descent on the surrogate model.
e23c8c2e9145c5fba798d11c1bcd65586b4127ad.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet-compatible dataset, using 1,000 images from the ImageNet validation set, a standard benchmark in adversarial robustness research. Both CNNs (ResNet-18, ResNet-50, ResNet-101, VGG-19, DenseNet-121, Inception-v3) and ViTs (ViT-B, Swin-B, PVT-v2, MobileViT-s) will serve as target models. The main evaluation metric will be the average attack success rate (ASR) across all target models except the surrogate. Baselines will include standard transfer attacks (e.g., MI, NI, GI, DI, TI, SSA) and existing alignment methods (e.g., Model Alignment), with and without SAA integration. Additional experiments will assess transferability against adversarial defenses and ensemble attack settings, and ablation studies will isolate the contributions of global, local, and adversarial alignment modules. Hyperparameters such as perturbation magnitude, step size, and number of iterations will follow established standards from prior work.
e23c8c2e9145c5fba798d11c1bcd65586b4127ad.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to explicitly leverage both spatial and adversarial feature alignment for enhancing cross-architecture adversarial transferability. By introducing local region alignment and adversarial-aware alignment, the approach addresses limitations of prior methods that only consider global or clean feature alignment. SAA is designed to be compatible with existing transfer attack strategies and can be applied to both single-model and ensemble-based attacks. Empirical guidance for surrogate and witness model selection is also provided, and the method demonstrates state-of-the-art improvements in transferability, particularly in challenging CNN-to-ViT and ViT-to-CNN scenarios.

e26f7120b9a0698a9873db3cd653a16dcf0ed1e4.title: kNN-CLIP: Retrieval Enables Training-Free Segmentation on Continually Expanding Large Vocabularies
e26f7120b9a0698a9873db3cd653a16dcf0ed1e4.research_question: How can open-vocabulary segmentation models be efficiently adapted to continually expanding vocabularies, enabling accurate segmentation across large and dynamic sets of visual concepts without incurring catastrophic forgetting or significant computational and memory overhead?
e26f7120b9a0698a9873db3cd653a16dcf0ed1e4.hypothesis: A training-free retrieval-augmented framework that leverages a continually expanding database of instance embeddings can enable open-vocabulary segmentation models to adapt to new concepts with zero forgetting, minimal compute and memory costs, and improved segmentation accuracy across large and evolving vocabularies.
e26f7120b9a0698a9873db3cd653a16dcf0ed1e4.proposed_method: A novel training-free framework, kNN-CLIP, will be developed to augment open-vocabulary segmentation models with a dynamically growing database of instance embeddings. For each new image and its class-agnostic masks, features will be extracted using a pretrained vision encoder (e.g., DINOv2 ViT-Giant), and mask average pooling will be applied to obtain compact vector embeddings. These embeddings, along with their class labels, will be stored in a retrieval database using an efficient vector search library (e.g., FAISS). At inference, mask proposals from a segmentation model will be used to pool features and generate query embeddings, which will be matched against the database using k-nearest neighbor (kNN) search based on cosine similarity. The retrieved class labels and similarity scores will be aggregated into pseudo-logits, which are then fused with the original model's predictions using a confidence-based weighting scheme. The framework allows seamless addition of new classes and concepts to the database without any retraining, and supports both semantic and panoptic segmentation tasks.
e26f7120b9a0698a9873db3cd653a16dcf0ed1e4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of open-vocabulary semantic and panoptic segmentation benchmarks, including ADE20K, COCO Panoptic, A-847, PC-459, A-150, PC-59, and Pascal VOC-21. The proposed method will be integrated with the FC-CLIP segmentation model as the baseline. Comparisons will be made against state-of-the-art continual learning and retrieval-based segmentation methods such as Mask2Former, CoMFormer, ODISE, and Hummingbird. Evaluation metrics will include mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), Panoptic Quality (PQ), and Average Precision (AP). The database will be constructed using features from the training sets of each dataset, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of hyperparameters such as confidence thresholds, weighting factors, and the number of nearest neighbors retrieved. Both brute-force and approximate search strategies (e.g., HNSW) will be explored for retrieval efficiency.
e26f7120b9a0698a9873db3cd653a16dcf0ed1e4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully training-free, retrieval-augmented framework for continual open-vocabulary segmentation, enabling dynamic vocabulary expansion without catastrophic forgetting or retraining. The method achieves zero forgetting by relying solely on feature retrieval, supports efficient memory usage by storing only compact embeddings, and allows for rapid adaptation to new concepts and domains. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent and significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines across diverse and long-tailed segmentation datasets. The approach is robust to the number of incremental classes and outperforms prior retrieval-based methods by leveraging class-agnostic mask proposals and confidence-aware fusion of retrieval and model predictions.

e27c59ca5853172ce28b6a0e3967ec693611820b.title: DTFD-MIL: Double-Tier Feature Distillation Multiple Instance Learning for Histopathology Whole Slide Image Classification
e27c59ca5853172ce28b6a0e3967ec693611820b.research_question: How can the classification performance of histopathology whole slide images (WSIs) be improved under the multiple instance learning (MIL) paradigm, particularly when faced with small sample cohorts and limited slide-level annotations?
e27c59ca5853172ce28b6a0e3967ec693611820b.hypothesis: Introducing a double-tier MIL framework that leverages pseudo-bags and explicit instance probability derivation will improve the generalization and accuracy of WSI classification compared to existing MIL approaches, especially in scenarios with limited training samples and highly imbalanced positive instance distributions.
e27c59ca5853172ce28b6a0e3967ec693611820b.proposed_method: A novel double-tier feature distillation MIL (DTFD-MIL) framework will be developed for WSI classification. The method begins by randomly splitting the set of instances (patches) from each WSI (bag) into several smaller pseudo-bags, each inheriting the label of its parent slide. In the first tier, an attention-based MIL (AB-MIL) model is applied to each pseudo-bag, and instance probabilities are explicitly derived using a Grad-CAM-inspired mechanism, rather than relying solely on attention scores. Features are distilled from each pseudo-bag using one of several strategies (e.g., maximum probability, maximum/minimum, maximum attention, or aggregated features). These distilled features are then aggregated and input into a second-tier AB-MIL model, which predicts the parent bag's label. Both tiers are supervised by the ground-truth slide label, and the framework is trained end-to-end using cross-entropy loss.
e27c59ca5853172ce28b6a0e3967ec693611820b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two large public histopathology WSI datasets: CAMELYON-16 and TCGA lung cancer. Preprocessing includes tissue localization using OTSU thresholding and extraction of non-overlapping 256x256 patches at 20X magnification. The proposed method will be compared against several baselines, including mean/max pooling MIL, RNN-MIL, classic AB-MIL, DS-MIL, CLAM variants, and Trans-MIL. Evaluation metrics will include area under the ROC curve (AUC), accuracy, and F1 score, with results reported as means and confidence intervals or standard deviations. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of the number of pseudo-bags and feature distillation strategies. Model complexity and computational requirements will also be compared.
e27c59ca5853172ce28b6a0e3967ec693611820b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of pseudo-bags to virtually increase the number of training bags, addressing the challenge of small sample cohorts in WSI datasets. It provides a rigorous derivation of instance probabilities within the AB-MIL framework using a Grad-CAM-based approach, enabling more accurate identification of positive regions. The double-tier MIL architecture with feature distillation is a new approach that enhances representation learning and robustness to label noise. The method is claimed to outperform state-of-the-art MIL models on challenging WSI datasets and offers a generalizable framework for broader MIL applications.

e2947804451f8bd91ed3da1163b852c101424953.title: UniDetox: Universal Detoxification of Large Language Models via Dataset Distillation
e2947804451f8bd91ed3da1163b852c101424953.research_question: How can a universally applicable method be developed to mitigate toxicity in large language models (LLMs) without requiring model-specific tuning or architecture-dependent modifications?
e2947804451f8bd91ed3da1163b852c101424953.hypothesis: A dataset distillation technique leveraging contrastive decoding can generate synthetic detoxifying text that, when used for fine-tuning, universally reduces toxicity in diverse LLMs without the need for model-specific hyperparameter tuning or architecture-dependent adjustments.
e2947804451f8bd91ed3da1163b852c101424953.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a universal detoxification framework, UNIDETOX, that utilizes dataset distillation via contrastive decoding to generate detoxifying text. The process begins by creating a 'toxic model' through fine-tuning a base LLM on toxic text data. Contrastive decoding is then employed to distill detoxifying text by sampling sequences that maximize the difference in log probabilities between the base and toxic models, with an adaptive plausibility constraint to ensure text coherence and fluency. The distilled detoxifying text is subsequently used to fine-tune any target LLM, moving its parameters in the direction opposite to the 'toxicity vector' in parameter space. This method relies on a first-order Taylor approximation to theoretically justify the alignment of the detoxification gradient with the direction needed to reduce toxicity, and is designed to be computationally efficient and model-agnostic.
e2947804451f8bd91ed3da1163b852c101424953.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Dynamically Generated Hate Speech (DGHS) dataset to create toxic models and the ToxiGen dataset for evaluation, covering both in-distribution and out-of-distribution domains. Detoxifying text will be distilled from GPT-2 XL and used to fine-tune multiple models, including GPT-2 XL, OPT-6.7B, Falcon-7B, and LLaMA2-7B, with identical hyperparameter configurations. Baseline methods for comparison will include Safety Preprompt, LM-Steer, DEXPERTS, Task Arithmetic, and text sampled directly from GPT-2. Evaluation metrics will comprise Toxicity Probability (TP), Expected Maximum Toxicity (EMT) using Detoxify and PerspectiveAPI, language modeling perplexity (PPL), n-gram diversity (Dist-1/2/3), and downstream task accuracy (MMLU). Hyperparameter sensitivity and the generalizability of the distilled detoxifying text across models will also be assessed.
e2947804451f8bd91ed3da1163b852c101424953.novelty_claims: The proposed method offers a universally applicable detoxification technique for LLMs that eliminates the need for model-specific hyperparameter tuning and architecture-dependent modifications. It introduces an efficient dataset distillation approach based on contrastive decoding, enabling the generation of discrete, coherent detoxifying text suitable for fine-tuning any LLM. The approach is computationally scalable to large models and demonstrates strong generalizability, as detoxifying text distilled from one model can effectively detoxify others. Additionally, the method provides insights into the reduction of political bias in detoxifying text, contributing to a deeper understanding of effective detoxification attributes.

e2a6ffba64331989858e5078bfb8277343aa90bd.title: xLSTM: Extended Long Short-Term Memory
e2a6ffba64331989858e5078bfb8277343aa90bd.research_question: How can the limitations of traditional LSTM architectures in language modeling—such as inability to revise storage decisions, limited storage capacity, and lack of parallelizability—be overcome by scaling LSTMs to billions of parameters and integrating modern techniques, and how do such extended LSTM models compare to state-of-the-art Transformers and State Space Models in terms of performance and scaling?
e2a6ffba64331989858e5078bfb8277343aa90bd.hypothesis: Introducing exponential gating, advanced normalization and stabilization, and new memory structures (including scalar and matrix memories with novel update rules) into LSTM architectures will enable these models to overcome traditional LSTM limitations, resulting in improved language modeling performance, enhanced memory capacity, and better scalability compared to existing state-of-the-art architectures such as Transformers and State Space Models.
e2a6ffba64331989858e5078bfb8277343aa90bd.proposed_method: A novel family of Extended Long Short-Term Memory (xLSTM) models will be developed by introducing two key modifications to the standard LSTM: (1) exponential gating with appropriate normalization and stabilization to allow dynamic revision of storage decisions, and (2) new memory structures, including a scalar-memory sLSTM with advanced memory mixing and a matrix-memory mLSTM with a covariance-based update rule for enhanced storage capacity and parallelizability. The sLSTM will use exponential gates and a normalizer state to enable effective memory revision and mixing, while the mLSTM will replace the scalar memory with a matrix, using key-value pairs and a covariance update to store and retrieve information efficiently. Both variants will be integrated into residual block backbones, forming xLSTM blocks that are then residually stacked to build deep xLSTM architectures. Stabilization techniques will be applied to prevent numerical overflow in exponential gates, and both pre- and post-up-projection residual block designs will be explored to maximize representational power.
e2a6ffba64331989858e5078bfb8277343aa90bd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of tasks to evaluate the capabilities of xLSTM models. Synthetic tasks, such as formal language recognition and associative recall, will be used to test state tracking, memory revision, and storage capacity. Long context processing will be assessed using the Long Range Arena benchmark. For large-scale language modeling, models will be trained on 15B and 300B tokens from the SlimPajama dataset, with validation perplexity as the primary metric. Comparisons will be made against strong baselines, including Transformers (GPT-3, Llama), State Space Models (Mamba, H3), and other recurrent models (RWKV, HGRN, RetNet, Hyena, GLA). Ablation studies will isolate the impact of exponential gating, matrix memory, and various gating mechanisms. Additional evaluation will be performed on downstream tasks and the PALOMA language benchmark, covering 571 text domains. Model scaling behavior will be analyzed by training models of varying sizes and measuring performance trends.
e2a6ffba64331989858e5078bfb8277343aa90bd.novelty_claims: The proposed xLSTM framework introduces exponential gating with normalization and stabilization, enabling dynamic revision of memory and overcoming a key limitation of traditional LSTMs. The new memory structures, including the fully parallelizable matrix-memory mLSTM with a covariance update rule, significantly enhance storage capacity and allow for efficient large-scale training. Integration of these components into residual block architectures enables deep, scalable models that maintain linear computational complexity with respect to sequence length. The approach combines the strengths of LSTMs (such as state tracking and memory mixing) with modern deep learning techniques, resulting in models that outperform state-of-the-art Transformers and State Space Models on language modeling benchmarks and exhibit superior scaling behavior.

e2c8dcc5b91021470655aa7104608a01dbfc2bb4.title: Cluster-Adaptive Network A/B Testing: From Randomization to Estimation
e2c8dcc5b91021470655aa7104608a01dbfc2bb4.research_question: How can the estimation of average treatment effects (ATE) in A/B testing be improved in the presence of network interference and cluster effects among users in social networks?
e2c8dcc5b91021470655aa7104608a01dbfc2bb4.hypothesis: Utilizing a cluster-adaptive randomization procedure that balances cluster-level covariates, followed by a cluster-adjusted estimator, will yield more consistent and efficient estimates of the ATE in networked A/B testing settings compared to traditional randomization and estimation methods.
e2c8dcc5b91021470655aa7104608a01dbfc2bb4.proposed_method: A new cluster-adaptive network A/B testing framework will be developed, consisting of two main components: (1) a Cluster-Adaptive Randomization (CAR) procedure, and (2) a Cluster-Adjusted Estimator (CAE). The CAR procedure sequentially assigns clusters to treatment or control groups by minimizing the Mahalanobis distance of cluster-level covariates between groups, thus ensuring balanced covariate distributions. This is achieved by pairing clusters and probabilistically assigning them to treatment arms based on which assignment minimizes covariate imbalance, with a higher probability (e.g., q = 0.85) favoring the more balanced assignment. After randomization, the CAE computes the ATE using only 'uncontaminated' users (those not affected by network spillover from the opposite treatment), and further adjusts for cluster effects by averaging within clusters, thereby removing bias due to unequal cluster sizes and network interference. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish the consistency and efficiency of the proposed estimator under the CAR procedure.
e2c8dcc5b91021470655aa7104608a01dbfc2bb4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both simulated and real-world network data. The simulated network will be generated using the Watts-Strogatz small-world model, creating 500 independent clusters with varying sizes and controlled inter-cluster connections. Cluster-level covariates will include cluster size, internal and external edge counts, and density. The response model will incorporate both cluster effects and network spill-over effects. The real-world evaluation will use the MIT Phone Call Network, partitioned into clusters via label propagation. The proposed method will be compared to several baselines: classical user-level randomization with a classical estimator (CRU+CE), cluster randomization with a classical estimator (CRC+CE), and cluster randomization with the cluster-adjusted estimator (CRC+CAE). Evaluation metrics will include bias and standard deviation of the estimated ATE, as well as the percent reduction in variance (PRIV) relative to baselines. Multiple runs (e.g., 1000) will be performed to assess statistical properties under varying levels of network effect and cluster connectivity.
e2c8dcc5b91021470655aa7104608a01dbfc2bb4.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a novel cluster-adaptive randomization procedure that explicitly minimizes covariate imbalance at the cluster level in networked A/B testing, a feature not present in existing methods. The integration of this randomization with a cluster-adjusted estimator provides a consistent and efficient approach to estimating ATE in the presence of both cluster effects and network interference. Theoretical guarantees are established for both the balance and consistency properties of the method. Empirical results demonstrate substantial improvements in estimation efficiency (variance reduction exceeding 70-90%) and bias elimination compared to traditional and existing network A/B testing procedures.

e2c9a43281daed4543f299564fd46dde10b5e57c.title: ProxSkip: Yes! Local Gradient Steps Provably Lead to Communication Acceleration! Finally!
e2c9a43281daed4543f299564fd46dde10b5e57c.research_question: Can local gradient steps be leveraged to provably accelerate communication in distributed and federated optimization problems involving a smooth function and an expensive nonsmooth regularizer, without relying on data similarity or explicit acceleration mechanisms?
e2c9a43281daed4543f299564fd46dde10b5e57c.hypothesis: Local gradient steps, when combined with a randomized prox-skipping strategy and appropriate control variates, can achieve provable improvements in communication complexity over standard gradient descent and existing local-update methods, even in the presence of data heterogeneity.
e2c9a43281daed4543f299564fd46dde10b5e57c.proposed_method: A new algorithm, ProxSkip, is proposed for minimizing the sum of a smooth function and a proximable (but potentially expensive) nonsmooth function. The method introduces a randomized prox-skipping mechanism: in each iteration, a gradient-type step is performed, and the expensive proximal operator is only evaluated with a small probability p, allowing it to be skipped in most iterations. To ensure stability and convergence, a control variate is maintained and updated, correcting for the drift introduced by skipping the prox step. The approach is extended to distributed and federated learning settings, where the proximal operator corresponds to communication (e.g., model averaging), and to decentralized optimization over arbitrary communication graphs. Theoretical analysis establishes linear convergence rates and quantifies the trade-off between the number of local steps and communication rounds.
e2c9a43281daed4543f299564fd46dde10b5e57c.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on classical logistic regression tasks using the 'w8a' dataset from the LIBSVM library, simulating federated learning scenarios with heterogeneous data. The proposed method (Scaffnew, an instantiation of ProxSkip for federated learning) is compared against baselines such as LocalGD, Scaffold, S-Local-GD, and FedLin. Both deterministic and stochastic settings are evaluated, with communication rounds, number of local steps, and convergence to optimality as primary metrics. Hyperparameters are tested both with optimal tuning and with theoretically justified values. The experimental setup leverages parallelization and measures performance in terms of communication efficiency and convergence rate, including tests with varying numbers of clients and local steps.
e2c9a43281daed4543f299564fd46dde10b5e57c.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to provably achieve a communication complexity better than O(κ log(1/ε)) for local gradient-type methods in federated learning, without any data similarity or heterogeneity-bounding assumptions. The randomized prox-skipping mechanism, combined with control variates, enables significant reductions in the number of expensive proximal (communication) operations while maintaining optimal convergence rates. The approach is shown to be optimal with respect to known lower bounds for communication rounds in distributed optimization. Extensions are provided for stochastic gradients and decentralized communication, demonstrating the flexibility and broad applicability of the framework.

e2e52461194bc81351da7caa978ac42e9e9549cc.title: Fine-Grained Human Feedback Gives Better Rewards for Language Model Training
e2e52461194bc81351da7caa978ac42e9e9549cc.research_question: How can language model training be improved by leveraging more informative and granular human feedback, rather than relying solely on holistic, sequence-level preference judgments?
e2e52461194bc81351da7caa978ac42e9e9549cc.hypothesis: Utilizing fine-grained human feedback—both in terms of reward density (e.g., per sentence or sub-sentence) and error category (e.g., factuality, relevance, completeness)—to train multiple specialized reward models will provide more effective and controllable reinforcement learning signals, resulting in language models that produce less toxic, more relevant, factual, and complete outputs compared to models trained with holistic rewards.
e2e52461194bc81351da7caa978ac42e9e9549cc.proposed_method: A novel reinforcement learning framework, FINE-GRAINED RLHF, will be developed to incorporate fine-grained human feedback into language model training. The approach involves collecting human annotations that identify specific error types (such as irrelevance, factual inaccuracy, or information incompleteness) at various granularities (sub-sentence, sentence, or full sequence). Separate reward models will be trained for each error category and granularity, using architectures such as encoder-only transformers (e.g., Longformer) for classification or scoring. During RL training, these reward models will provide dense, segment-level reward signals, which are aggregated with adjustable weights and used to optimize the policy model via Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). The framework allows for flexible control over model behavior by tuning the contribution of each reward model.
e2e52461194bc81351da7caa978ac42e9e9549cc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two tasks: (1) Detoxification, using the REALTOXICITYPROMPTS dataset, where toxicity is measured at the sentence level with the PERSPECTIVE API as a reward model, and (2) Long-form Question Answering, using a newly constructed QA-FEEDBACK dataset based on ASQA, with human-annotated feedback for multiple error types. Baselines will include standard RLHF with holistic preference-based rewards, supervised fine-tuning, and state-of-the-art controlled generation methods (e.g., GeDi, DEXPERTS). Evaluation will involve both automatic metrics (toxicity scores, perplexity, n-gram diversity, RougeLSum, and reward model predictions) and human annotation of error spans and information completeness. The impact of varying reward model weights and ablation of individual reward models will also be analyzed to assess controllability and trade-offs.
e2e52461194bc81351da7caa978ac42e9e9549cc.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the use of multiple, fine-grained reward models trained on explicit human feedback for distinct error categories and at various granularities, enabling dense and informative reward signals during RL training. This approach allows for greater flexibility and controllability in shaping language model behavior, surpassing the limitations of traditional holistic, sequence-level reward models. The method also demonstrates the ability to customize model outputs to user needs by adjusting reward model weights, and provides empirical evidence of improved sample efficiency, factuality, relevance, and completeness in generated text.

e2f1eb1615d5bbf00aee17aa7806c68757ef1020.title: Synergy Between Sufficient Changes and Sparse Mixing Procedure for Disentangled Representation Learning
e2f1eb1615d5bbf00aee17aa7806c68757ef1020.research_question: How can disentangled representation learning achieve identifiability guarantees under milder and more realistic assumptions, particularly when neither sufficient distributional changes nor structural sparsity in the mixing procedure are fully satisfied in practice?
e2f1eb1615d5bbf00aee17aa7806c68757ef1020.hypothesis: The synergy between sufficient changes in the distribution of latent variables (as indicated by auxiliary variables) and structural sparsity in the mixing procedure enables identifiability of disentangled representations under weaker and more practical conditions than either assumption alone.
e2f1eb1615d5bbf00aee17aa7806c68757ef1020.proposed_method: A unified generative model framework will be developed that leverages both sufficient changes (via auxiliary variables) and sparse mixing constraints to achieve identifiability in disentangled representation learning. The framework incorporates a domain encoding neural network to model how auxiliary variables influence latent variable distributions, using normalizing flows to flexibly capture conditional dependencies. A sparse mixing constraint is imposed by penalizing the Jacobian of the mapping from latent to observed variables, encouraging conditional independence structures that reflect real-world sparsity. Two practical implementations will be constructed: CG-VAE, based on a variational autoencoder architecture, and CG-GAN, based on a generative adversarial network with domain-invariant and domain-specific latent partitions and a learnable mask for adaptive dimension selection. The total loss functions will combine reconstruction/generation objectives, KL divergence or adversarial losses, and the proposed sparsity penalties.
e2f1eb1615d5bbf00aee17aa7806c68757ef1020.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic datasets will be generated with varying numbers of domains and known latent structures, allowing precise evaluation of identifiability using metrics such as mean correlation coefficient (MCC), completeness, disentanglement score, informativeness, R2, and MSE. Real-world experiments will use multi-domain image generation tasks on CelebA (with domains defined by eyeglasses presence) and MNIST (with color domains), evaluating performance with Frechet Inception Distance (FID), Domain-Invariant Perceptual Distance (DIPD), and Joint-FID for paired data. Baselines will include β-VAE, FactorVAE, SlowVAE, iVAE, iMSDA, StyleGAN2-ADA, i-StyleGAN, and TGAN. The proposed methods will be compared under varying numbers of auxiliary variables and domain settings, with ablation studies to isolate the impact of sparsity constraints and domain encoding.
e2f1eb1615d5bbf00aee17aa7806c68757ef1020.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled identifiability theory that synergistically combines sufficient changes and sparse mixing constraints, reducing the need for strong assumptions on either auxiliary variable diversity or strict structural sparsity. The framework generalizes and subsumes prior identifiability results as special cases, and provides practical, scalable implementations for both VAE and GAN architectures. The approach enables identifiability and disentanglement even with limited domains or partially violated sparsity, enhancing applicability to real-world scenarios. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior disentanglement and identifiability compared to existing methods, especially under challenging conditions.

e2f4c1379e75977e89e9ce4969fe78c045c96c99.title: Geometric Algorithms for Neural Combinatorial Optimization with Constraints
e2f4c1379e75977e89e9ce4969fe78c045c96c99.research_question: How can neural networks be trained in a self-supervised, end-to-end differentiable manner to solve combinatorial optimization problems with discrete constraints, ensuring both constraint satisfaction and high-quality feasible solutions across a broad class of problems?
e2f4c1379e75977e89e9ce4969fe78c045c96c99.hypothesis: A geometric decomposition framework leveraging convex geometry and Carathéodory's theorem can enable neural networks to produce outputs that are efficiently and provably rounded to feasible solutions for discrete constrained combinatorial optimization, while supporting end-to-end differentiable training and outperforming existing neural and classical baselines.
e2f4c1379e75977e89e9ce4969fe78c045c96c99.proposed_method: A novel end-to-end differentiable framework will be developed for neural combinatorial optimization with discrete constraints. The approach will use a neural network encoder to map input instances to points in the convex hull of feasible solutions (the feasible set polytope). An iterative geometric decomposition algorithm, grounded in Carathéodory’s theorem and the GLS method, will decompose these outputs into sparse convex combinations of feasible sets, yielding a differentiable distribution over feasible solutions. The expected value of the discrete objective under this distribution will serve as the loss function, enabling gradient-based optimization. At inference, the decomposition provides a small support of candidate feasible solutions, from which the best can be selected with a rounding guarantee. The method will be instantiated for various constraint types, including cardinality, partition matroids, spanning trees, and independent sets, with specific projection or perturbation strategies to ensure neural outputs remain in the feasible polytope.
e2f4c1379e75977e89e9ce4969fe78c045c96c99.experiment_details: Experiments will focus on cardinality-constrained problems such as Maximum Coverage and Maximum Cut, using both synthetic and real-world datasets (e.g., random graphs, Twitch, Railway). The neural encoder will use a stack of GraphSage layers followed by a fully connected layer and a noise perturbation mechanism to ensure outputs lie in the hypersimplex. Baselines will include random selection, greedy algorithms, Gurobi MIP solvers, CardNN (with and without test-time optimization), UCOM2, and reinforcement learning approaches. Evaluation metrics will include objective value (solution quality) and inference time. Experiments will assess generalization by training on synthetic data and testing on real-world graphs, and will include ablation studies to isolate the effects of the decomposition algorithm and neural network parametrization.
e2f4c1379e75977e89e9ce4969fe78c045c96c99.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a general geometric decomposition framework for neural combinatorial optimization with constraints, enabling end-to-end differentiable training and inference with rounding guarantees. The approach generalizes prior work by supporting any constraint family whose feasible set polytope admits an efficient linear optimization oracle, and integrates loss function design and rounding in a unified, theoretically grounded manner. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior efficiency and solution quality compared to both neural and classical baselines, especially on large-scale instances. The framework is extensible to a wide range of combinatorial problems, including those with cardinality, matroid, and graph-based constraints.

e2ffc48a9cf1a43c546c66c3d5710262992885c4.title: Generalization Bounds using Data-Dependent Fractal Dimensions
e2ffc48a9cf1a43c546c66c3d5710262992885c4.research_question: How can generalization error bounds for modern neural networks be established using fractal geometry-based techniques without relying on restrictive Lipschitz continuity assumptions, and how can these bounds be made data-dependent and computationally tractable?
e2ffc48a9cf1a43c546c66c3d5710262992885c4.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that generalization error bounds for neural networks can be derived using a data-dependent fractal dimension, computed via a pseudo-metric induced by the loss function, without requiring any Lipschitz continuity assumptions. Furthermore, these bounds will provide improved interpretability and correlation with empirical generalization error compared to prior approaches.
e2ffc48a9cf1a43c546c66c3d5710262992885c4.proposed_method: A novel methodology will be developed that leverages a data-dependent pseudo-metric on the hypothesis set, defined by the average difference in loss values across the training dataset. The upper box-counting (fractal) dimension of the hypothesis set, with respect to this pseudo-metric, will be used as a complexity measure to bound the generalization error. The approach will extend classical covering arguments and Rademacher complexity techniques, and will introduce mutual information terms to capture the dependence between the data and the hypothesis set. To ensure computational tractability, the fractal dimension will be estimated using persistent homology tools from topological data analysis, allowing for efficient numerical computation even in high-dimensional settings. Additionally, a notion of geometric stability will be introduced to further interpret and control the mutual information terms in the bounds.
e2ffc48a9cf1a43c546c66c3d5710262992885c4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on various neural network architectures, including fully connected networks (FCN-5, FCN-7) and AlexNet, across datasets such as the California Housing Dataset (CHD), MNIST, and CIFAR-10. The hypothesis set will be constructed from SGD optimization trajectories near local minima. The proposed data-dependent fractal dimension will be computed using persistent homology software, replacing the Euclidean metric with the loss-based pseudo-metric. Correlations between the computed dimension and the generalization gap (difference between training and test accuracy) will be evaluated across a grid of hyperparameters (learning rates, batch sizes), and compared to existing dimension-based complexity measures. Evaluation metrics will include Spearman's rank correlation, Kendall's tau, and granulated Kendall's coefficient. Robustness of the dimension estimates will be assessed by subsampling the dataset used in the pseudo-metric computation.
e2ffc48a9cf1a43c546c66c3d5710262992885c4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach removes the need for Lipschitz continuity assumptions in fractal geometry-based generalization bounds, making the theory applicable to a broader class of neural networks. A data-dependent fractal dimension is introduced, which captures the intrinsic complexity of the hypothesis set with respect to the loss function and the data. The method enables efficient numerical computation of the dimension using persistent homology, and introduces a new notion of geometric stability to interpret and control mutual information terms in the bounds. Empirical results demonstrate that the proposed dimension correlates better with generalization error than previous Euclidean-based measures, especially in overparameterized and non-Lipschitz settings.

e3052ebca5eeae6a8a73e44517903d39746f5f3a.title: From Quantity to Quality: Boosting LLM Performance with Self-Guided Data Selection for Instruction Tuning
e3052ebca5eeae6a8a73e44517903d39746f5f3a.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) autonomously identify and select high-quality instruction data from large open-source datasets to improve instruction tuning efficiency and performance, while minimizing manual curation and resource usage?
e3052ebca5eeae6a8a73e44517903d39746f5f3a.hypothesis: LLMs equipped with a basic instruction-following capability can self-assess and select the most beneficial instruction samples from large datasets using a model-specific metric, leading to improved instruction tuning performance with significantly less data.
