e3052ebca5eeae6a8a73e44517903d39746f5f3a.proposed_method: A self-guided data selection framework is proposed for instruction tuning of LLMs, consisting of three phases: (1) Learning from Brief Experience, where the model is trained on a small, diverse subset of the target dataset to acquire basic instruction-following skills; (2) Evaluating Based on Experience, where a novel Instruction-Following Difficulty (IFD) score is computed for each sample by comparing the model's loss in generating responses with and without the instructional context, using the pre-experienced model; and (3) Retraining from Self-Guided Experience, where samples with high IFD scores (indicating greater instructional benefit) are selected as 'cherry data' for final model training. This process emphasizes data quality over quantity and is fully automated, requiring no external models for data curation.
e3052ebca5eeae6a8a73e44517903d39746f5f3a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Alpaca and WizardLM instruction-tuning datasets for training, with test evaluations on five diverse, human-curated instruction datasets: Vicuna, Koala, WizardLM, Self-instruct, and LIMA. Baseline comparisons will include models trained on full datasets, randomly selected subsets, diversity-based subsets, and subsets selected by alternative metrics such as Conditioned Answer Score. Evaluation will employ both automated LLM-based judges (GPT-4, ChatGPT) for pairwise response comparison and human evaluations on a random sample of instructions. Additional benchmarking will be performed on Huggingface OpenLLM Leaderboard and AlpacaEval Leaderboard using standard metrics (ARC, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA, and AlpacaEval). Ablation studies will test the impact of pre-experience sample size, data distribution, and selection strategy.
e3052ebca5eeae6a8a73e44517903d39746f5f3a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a model-specific, self-guided data selection approach for instruction tuning that eliminates the need for manual curation or external model scoring. The Instruction-Following Difficulty (IFD) metric is a novel, interpretable measure of how much instructional context aids response generation, enabling efficient identification of high-impact training samples. The method demonstrates that LLMs can achieve or surpass full-data performance using only a small fraction of carefully selected data, representing a significant advance in resource-efficient and scalable instruction tuning. The approach also provides new insights into the characteristics of high-value instruction data and offers a generalizable framework applicable to various LLM architectures.

e310707f28c60e1f56820ab12272affe71818d17.title: Generative Representational Instruction Tuning
e310707f28c60e1f56820ab12272affe71818d17.research_question: Can a single large language model be trained to achieve state-of-the-art performance on both text generation and text embedding tasks by unifying their training paradigms through instruction-based differentiation?
e310707f28c60e1f56820ab12272affe71818d17.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a unified instruction-tuned large language model can match or exceed the performance of models trained exclusively for either generative or embedding tasks, without incurring performance loss on either task type.
e310707f28c60e1f56820ab12272affe71818d17.proposed_method: A generative representational instruction tuning (GRIT) framework will be developed to unify generative and embedding tasks within a single large language model. The model will be finetuned on both generative instruction data and representational instruction data, using distinct instructions and loss functions to differentiate between the two task types. For embedding tasks, bidirectional attention will be applied over the input, with mean pooling over the final hidden states (excluding instruction and format tokens) to produce the representation, and a contrastive loss with in-batch negatives will be used. For generative tasks, causal attention will be used, and a language modeling head will predict the next tokens, with loss aggregated at the sample or token level, or a mixture of both. The objectives will be summed with tunable loss weights, and the architecture will support differing batch sizes for embedding and generative data to optimize performance and computational efficiency.
e310707f28c60e1f56820ab12272affe71818d17.experiment_details: The proposed models will be finetuned from pretrained LLMs such as Mistral 7B and Mixtral 8x7B using adapted datasets: E5 (with added scientific data) for embedding and filtered Tülu2 for generative tasks. Embedding performance will be evaluated on the 56 main datasets from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), using metrics such as accuracy, V-measure, average precision, MAP, nDCG, and Spearman correlation. Generative performance will be assessed on tasks including MMLU, GSM8K, BBH, TyDiQA, HumanEvalSynthesize, and AlpacaEval, using metrics like exact match, F1, pass@1, and win rate. Baselines will include embedding-only and generative-only variants, as well as other open and proprietary models (e.g., Llama2, GPT-J, BGELarge, InstructorXL). Ablation studies will be conducted on attention mechanisms, pooling strategies, batch sizes, loss aggregation, embedding head dimensionality, and training precision. Additional experiments will evaluate the impact of reranking, few-shot embedding, and alignment tuning (e.g., KTO) on model performance.
e310707f28c60e1f56820ab12272affe71818d17.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to unify state-of-the-art performance on both text embedding and generation tasks within a single open large language model, using instruction-based differentiation and dual-objective training. The method introduces novel architectural adaptations, such as bidirectional attention with mean pooling for embeddings and mixed sample/token-level loss aggregation for generation. Efficiency improvements are achieved by enabling a single model to replace separate embedding and generative models, significantly speeding up applications like Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and simplifying deployment infrastructure. Additional contributions include new techniques for memory reduction during embedding training and empirical findings on the ineffectiveness of few-shot embedding for LLMs.

e3160e5fa4cd8e5d3b0fc8e4c0c2032d68b58f34.title: Multi-Objective GFlowNets
e3160e5fa4cd8e5d3b0fc8e4c0c2032d68b58f34.research_question: How can diverse Pareto-optimal candidates be efficiently generated in multi-objective optimization problems, particularly in discrete and high-dimensional domains such as molecule and sequence design?
e3160e5fa4cd8e5d3b0fc8e4c0c2032d68b58f34.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging generative flow networks (GFlowNets), conditioned on preferences or acquisition functions, enables the generation of diverse sets of Pareto-optimal candidates that outperform existing methods in both Pareto performance and candidate diversity.
e3160e5fa4cd8e5d3b0fc8e4c0c2032d68b58f34.proposed_method: A novel framework, Multi-Objective GFlowNets (MOGFNs), will be developed to address the challenge of diverse candidate generation in multi-objective optimization. Two main variants will be introduced: (1) Preference-Conditional GFlowNets (MOGFN-PC), which utilize reward-conditional GFlowNets to model a family of independent sub-problems defined by scalarization functions and preference vectors, enabling the sampling of diverse candidates for each preference; and (2) MOGFN-AL, which integrates GFlowNets into a multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) loop, generating candidates by maximizing acquisition functions in an active learning setting. The methodology involves training conditional GFlowNet policies using the trajectory balance objective, with careful design of scalarization functions, preference sampling distributions, and reward exponents to control the trade-off between diversity and reward concentration. The approach is designed to efficiently amortize computation across sub-problems and exploit shared structure, enabling scalable and flexible candidate generation in discrete and combinatorial spaces.
e3160e5fa4cd8e5d3b0fc8e4c0c2032d68b58f34.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of synthetic and real-world benchmark tasks, including molecule generation (QM9 atom-based and fragment-based tasks), sequence design (n-gram synthetic tasks, DNA aptamer generation), and protein design (Proxy RFP task). Datasets such as QM9 and custom sequence datasets will be utilized, with objectives including chemical properties, synthetic accessibility, and sequence features. Baselines will include MOReinforce, Envelope-MOQ, MOSoftQL, MOA2C, MARS, NSGA-2, and model-based evolutionary algorithms. Evaluation metrics will comprise standard multi-objective optimization indicators such as hypervolume (HV), R2, generational distance (GD+), and diversity metrics (Top-K Diversity, Top-K Reward). Experimental protocols will involve sampling preferences, generating candidate sets per preference, and reporting mean and standard deviation of metrics over multiple seeds. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of preference distributions, scalarization functions, and reward exponents on performance and diversity.
e3160e5fa4cd8e5d3b0fc8e4c0c2032d68b58f34.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first framework for reward-conditional GFlowNets in multi-objective optimization, enabling the generation of diverse Pareto-optimal candidates in discrete and high-dimensional domains. The approach amortizes computation across sub-problems, exploits shared structure via conditional policies, and is empirically validated to outperform existing methods in both Pareto performance and candidate diversity. The integration of GFlowNets with active learning in MOBO settings (MOGFN-AL) is novel, providing significant improvements in sample efficiency and diversity in practical design tasks. The research also provides a thorough analysis of key design choices, such as preference sampling and scalarization, offering insights for future multi-objective generative modeling.

e33dd843f35ba929a3052bb752c1ec39b9a79617.title: BERT4ETH: A Pre-trained Transformer for Ethereum Fraud Detection
e33dd843f35ba929a3052bb752c1ec39b9a79617.research_question: How can fraud detection on the Ethereum blockchain be improved by leveraging advanced sequential modeling techniques, given the challenges of highly repetitive, skew-distributed, and heterogeneous transaction data?
e33dd843f35ba929a3052bb752c1ec39b9a79617.hypothesis: A universal pre-trained Transformer-based encoder, specifically adapted to the characteristics of Ethereum transaction data, will produce more robust and expressive account representations, leading to significantly improved performance in various Ethereum fraud detection tasks compared to existing graph-based and sequential learning methods.
e33dd843f35ba929a3052bb752c1ec39b9a79617.proposed_method: A pre-trained Transformer encoder, termed BERT4ETH, will be developed to serve as a universal account representation extractor for Ethereum fraud detection. The method will model transaction sequences for each externally owned account (EOA), encoding features such as address, timestamp, amount, account type, and in/out type using embedding layers. The architecture will incorporate three key strategies: (1) repetitiveness reduction via transaction de-duplication and high masking/dropout ratios during pre-training to prevent label leakage; (2) skew alleviation through frequency-aware negative sampling and intra-batch sharing to counteract the dominance of high-frequency addresses; and (3) modeling heterogeneity by separating in/out transaction sub-sequences and integrating ERC-20 token transfer logs using a gated encoder. Pre-training will use a Masked Address Prediction (MAP) task, where masked addresses in transaction sequences are predicted using contrastive loss with sampled negatives. The model will be designed to efficiently handle billions of unique addresses and capture multi-hop relational information.
e33dd843f35ba929a3052bb752c1ec39b9a79617.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two major Ethereum fraud detection tasks: phishing account detection (binary classification) and de-anonymization (identifying accounts controlled by the same user). Datasets will include labeled phishing accounts from Etherscan, ground-truth pairs from Ethereum Name Service (ENS), and Tornado Cash coin-mixer data, with millions of EOAs and tens of millions of transactions. Baselines will include DeepWalk-based methods (DeepWalk, Trans2Vec, Diff2Vec, Role2Vec), GNN-based methods (GCN, GraphSAGE, GAT), and ablated variants of the proposed method. Evaluation metrics will be F1 score, Precision, Recall for phishing detection, and HitRatio@k for de-anonymization. The experimental setup will include fixed-training and fine-tuning strategies, with hyperparameters such as Transformer layers, attention heads, sequence length, and negative-to-positive sampling ratio carefully tuned. Ablation studies will assess the impact of each proposed strategy.
e33dd843f35ba929a3052bb752c1ec39b9a79617.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first universal pre-trained Transformer encoder tailored for Ethereum fraud detection, addressing the unique challenges of transaction repetitiveness, skewed address distributions, and transactional heterogeneity. Key innovations include (1) a practical pre-training paradigm for large-scale blockchain data using high masking/dropout ratios and contrastive loss, (2) frequency-aware negative sampling and intra-batch sharing for effective skew alleviation, and (3) advanced modeling of transaction heterogeneity via in/out separation and ERC-20 log integration. The approach is expected to yield substantial improvements over state-of-the-art methods in both phishing detection and de-anonymization, and to generalize across multiple fraud detection tasks with minimal adaptation.

e3428dec9fad516a06def3e11dd77d79f7c32894.title: Homomorphism Counts as Structural Encodings for Graph Learning
e3428dec9fad516a06def3e11dd77d79f7c32894.research_question: How can structural encodings based on graph homomorphism counts be leveraged to enhance the expressive power and performance of graph neural networks, particularly Graph Transformers, across diverse graph learning tasks?
e3428dec9fad516a06def3e11dd77d79f7c32894.hypothesis: Structural encodings derived from motif-based homomorphism counts (MoSE) provide a more expressive and flexible graph inductive bias than existing positional and structural encodings, such as random-walk structural encoding (RWSE), leading to improved performance on a variety of graph learning benchmarks.
e3428dec9fad516a06def3e11dd77d79f7c32894.proposed_method: A novel structural encoding framework, termed Motif Structural Encoding (MoSE), will be developed by representing each node in a graph with a vector of homomorphism counts from a selected family of motif graphs. The encoding is parameterized by a finite set of pattern graphs and an optional node-weighting scheme, allowing for both unweighted and weighted homomorphism counts. For each node, the vector consists of rooted homomorphism counts from each motif to the graph, capturing rich local and global structural information. The method is designed to be isomorphism-invariant and highly flexible, with the choice of motifs and weighting functions tailored to the task and dataset. MoSE will be integrated into Graph Transformer architectures by concatenating or adding the encoding to node features, thereby providing a strong graph inductive bias without requiring explicit access to the adjacency matrix.
e3428dec9fad516a06def3e11dd77d79f7c32894.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of real-world and synthetic datasets, including molecular property prediction (ZINC-12K, PCQM4Mv2-subset, QM9), image classification (CIFAR10, MNIST), and a custom synthetic graph regression task (fractional domination number). Multiple Graph Transformer architectures (e.g., GPS, GRIT, GT-E) and MPNN baselines (e.g., GIN-E, GIN-E+VN) will be used for comparison. Baseline encodings will include Laplacian positional encoding (LapPE), random-walk structural encoding (RWSE), and other spectral and structural methods. Evaluation metrics will include mean absolute error (MAE) for regression tasks and classification accuracy for classification tasks. All models will be constrained to a comparable number of learnable parameters, and ablation studies will be performed to isolate the effect of the encoding. The impact of motif selection and node-weighting schemes will also be systematically explored.
e3428dec9fad516a06def3e11dd77d79f7c32894.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a general and flexible structural encoding framework for graphs based on motif homomorphism counts, which is theoretically shown to be strictly more expressive than random-walk structural encodings and not confined to a single level of the Weisfeiler-Lehman (WL) hierarchy. MoSE enables Graph Transformers to achieve or surpass state-of-the-art performance on several benchmarks, including molecular property prediction and challenging synthetic tasks, at a relatively low computational cost. The method provides a principled way to inject rich structural information into graph models, bridging the gap between theoretical expressivity and empirical performance, and offers new insights into the design of graph inductive biases.

e3622f469279f3884959957bcd7c7c80babfc138.title: Understanding the Gains from Repeated Self-Distillation
e3622f469279f3884959957bcd7c7c80babfc138.research_question: How much performance gain can be achieved by repeatedly applying self-distillation in machine learning models, specifically in the context of linear regression, and what are the theoretical and empirical limits of such gains?
e3622f469279f3884959957bcd7c7c80babfc138.hypothesis: Repeated self-distillation, when optimally tuned at each step, can achieve significantly lower excess risk than single-step self-distillation or standard ridge regression, with the potential for multiplicative improvements proportional to the input dimension or rank of the data matrix.
e3622f469279f3884959957bcd7c7c80babfc138.proposed_method: The proposed method investigates repeated self-distillation in the canonical setting of linear regression. A k-step self-distillation process is formulated, where at each step, a student model is trained using a convex combination of the ground-truth labels and the predictions from the previous student (acting as the teacher), controlled by a set of imitation parameters ξ. The method analytically derives the form of the estimator after k steps, showing that the estimator is a linear function of these parameters and the ridge regularization coefficient λ. Theoretical analysis is conducted to characterize the excess risk as a quadratic function of the reparameterized imitation parameters, and conditions are established under which r-step self-distillation (where r is the rank of the data matrix) achieves the fundamental lower bound on excess risk for any linear estimator of this form. A practical approach for hyperparameter selection is also developed, leveraging the quadratic form of the risk to efficiently estimate optimal ξ values using a small number of validation evaluations.
e3622f469279f3884959957bcd7c7c80babfc138.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world regression tasks. Synthetic experiments use fixed-design linear regression with controlled singular values and parameter alignments to validate theoretical predictions, including the necessity of certain assumptions for achieving maximal gain. Real-world experiments employ datasets from the UCI repository, where multi-step self-distillation (up to 2 steps) is compared against optimal ridge regression and single-step self-distillation. For each method, hyperparameters are selected using a validation set, with the excess risk or mean squared error (MSE) on a held-out test set serving as the primary evaluation metric. The proposed quadratic-based hyperparameter selection strategy is implemented to efficiently find optimal imitation parameters for each step.
e3622f469279f3884959957bcd7c7c80babfc138.novelty_claims: This proposal advances the theoretical understanding of repeated self-distillation by providing closed-form characterizations of the achievable excess risk and establishing that, under certain conditions, r-step self-distillation can reduce excess risk by a factor proportional to the rank or dimension of the input. The work introduces a practical and theoretically motivated approach for selecting imitation parameters in multi-step self-distillation, enabling efficient application to real-world datasets. The analysis demonstrates that the performance gains from repeated self-distillation are fundamentally linked to the spectral properties of the data and the alignment of the true parameter, offering new insights into when and why self-distillation is effective.

e3770567f3b0f00890ef419914beb3456d663303.title: Quantum data encoding: a comparative analysis of classical-to-quantum mapping techniques and their impact on machine learning accuracy
e3770567f3b0f00890ef419914beb3456d663303.research_question: How do different classical-to-quantum data encoding techniques impact the performance and computational efficiency of classical machine learning models when classical data is mapped into quantum representations?
e3770567f3b0f00890ef419914beb3456d663303.hypothesis: Quantum data encoding techniques, when applied to classical data and used as input to classical machine learning models, will enhance classification accuracy and F1 scores, particularly for models that benefit from richer feature representations, while introducing varying computational overhead depending on model complexity and encoding method.
e3770567f3b0f00890ef419914beb3456d663303.proposed_method: A systematic empirical study will be conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of several classical-to-quantum data encoding techniques—specifically, basis encoding, angle encoding, and amplitude encoding—when used to map classical datasets into quantum representations. Each encoding scheme will be rigorously defined and implemented using quantum circuit simulation frameworks, such as PennyLane, to ensure accurate translation of classical features into quantum states. The encoded data will then be used as input to a diverse set of classical machine learning algorithms, including Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machines, and ensemble methods (Random Forest, LightGBM, AdaBoost, CatBoost). Data preprocessing steps will include feature selection, one-hot encoding of categorical variables, and dimensionality reduction via principal component analysis to ensure consistency and manageability of input data. The methodology will maintain data consistency by applying identical datasets across all encoding and model combinations, isolating the effects of the encoding techniques on downstream model performance.
e3770567f3b0f00890ef419914beb3456d663303.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize a real-world customer churn classification dataset from the telecommunications sector, featuring 20 initial attributes (categorical and numeric) and a binary churn target, with preprocessing steps to remove highly correlated, multicollinear, or irrelevant features. The dataset will be balanced via undersampling, resulting in 3,738 records, and categorical features will be one-hot encoded, yielding 42 columns. Principal component analysis will be applied to reduce dimensionality, with the number of components determined by explained variance analysis (elbow point at 23 components). Each machine learning algorithm will be trained and evaluated using both the original classical data and the quantum-encoded variants, with an 80:20 train-test split. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, precision, recall (sensitivity), F1 score, ROC AUC, Cohen’s Kappa, and running time. Baseline comparisons will be made between models trained on classical data and those trained on each quantum encoding variant, across all algorithms.
e3770567f3b0f00890ef419914beb3456d663303.novelty_claims: The proposed research offers a comprehensive, systematic comparison of multiple classical-to-quantum data encoding techniques applied to a wide range of classical machine learning models. By maintaining strict data consistency and leveraging rigorous empirical evaluation, the study isolates the impact of quantum data encoding on model performance and computational cost. The work provides new insights into the practical benefits and trade-offs of quantum-inspired data representations for classical machine learning, particularly in real-world, imbalanced classification scenarios. The findings are expected to inform future research on optimizing quantum encoding processes and scaling quantum-classical integration for practical applications.

e387a975968cb201b6108d719eded30a8324e679.title: Semantic Probabilistic Layers for Neuro-Symbolic Learning
e387a975968cb201b6108d719eded30a8324e679.research_question: How can structured-output prediction tasks be addressed by neural networks in a way that guarantees predictions are always consistent with complex, predefined symbolic constraints, while retaining modularity, expressiveness, probabilistic semantics, and computational efficiency?
e387a975968cb201b6108d719eded30a8324e679.hypothesis: A predictive layer that combines exact probabilistic inference with logical reasoning, implemented via probabilistic and constraint circuits, can guarantee consistent, expressive, and efficient structured-output predictions in neural networks, outperforming existing neuro-symbolic approaches.
e387a975968cb201b6108d719eded30a8324e679.proposed_method: A new predictive layer, termed the Semantic Probabilistic Layer (SPL), will be developed to replace the final layer in any neural network for structured-output prediction. SPL will combine two main components: a probabilistic circuit that models expressive joint distributions over output labels, and a constraint circuit that encodes logical constraints as compact computational graphs. The SPL computes the product of these circuits, ensuring that only label configurations consistent with the constraints receive nonzero probability, and normalizes the result to maintain probabilistic semantics. Both circuits will be designed to be smooth, decomposable, and compatible, enabling efficient inference and gradient-based training. The approach supports both a two-circuit implementation (separate probabilistic and constraint circuits) and a single-circuit implementation (a parameterized constraint circuit), allowing flexibility in expressiveness and computational trade-offs.
e387a975968cb201b6108d719eded30a8324e679.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard neuro-symbolic structured-output prediction benchmarks, including simple path prediction (on 4x4 grids), preference learning (using sushi preference data), shortest pathfinding in Warcraft II terrain maps (12x12 grids), and hierarchical multi-label classification (HMLC) across twelve real-world datasets. Baseline methods will include fully independent layers (FIL), loss-based approaches such as Semantic Loss and Neuro-Symbolic Entropy, and state-of-the-art consistency layers like MultiplexNet and HMCNN. Neural architectures such as multi-layer perceptrons and ResNet-18 will be used as feature extractors. Evaluation metrics will include exact match (subset accuracy), Hamming score, and the percentage of constraint-consistent predictions. Logical constraints will be compiled into sentential decision diagrams (SDDs) or similar representations for use in SPL and baseline methods. Hyperparameters and architectural choices will be tuned via validation splits, and results will be averaged over multiple runs for statistical significance.
e387a975968cb201b6108d719eded30a8324e679.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to provide a modular, probabilistically sound, and computationally efficient predictive layer that guarantees consistency with arbitrary logical constraints in structured-output prediction tasks. SPL uniquely satisfies all six desiderata for neuro-symbolic SOP: probabilistic semantics, expressiveness, consistency, generality, modularity, and efficiency. Unlike prior methods, SPL can be plugged into any neural network, supports end-to-end learning, and leverages advances in tractable probabilistic circuits to enable exact inference and training. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior accuracy and perfect constraint satisfaction compared to state-of-the-art neuro-symbolic approaches.

e38a29f6463f38f43797b128673b9e44d18a991e.title: Whose Opinions Do Language Models Reflect?
e38a29f6463f38f43797b128673b9e44d18a991e.research_question: To what extent do language models reflect the opinions of various human demographic groups when responding to subjective queries, and how well can these models be steered to emulate the opinions of specific groups?
e38a29f6463f38f43797b128673b9e44d18a991e.hypothesis: Language models do not accurately reflect the diversity of opinions held by the general population or specific demographic groups, and even with targeted steering, significant misalignment persists.
e38a29f6463f38f43797b128673b9e44d18a991e.proposed_method: A quantitative framework will be developed to systematically evaluate the alignment between language model (LM) responses and human opinions across a wide range of subjective topics. This framework will leverage high-quality public opinion surveys, specifically multiple-choice questions from Pew Research’s American Trends Panel, to create a dataset (OpinionQA) that covers a broad spectrum of topics and includes responses from diverse demographic groups. LMs will be prompted with these survey questions, both in a default setting and with additional context designed to steer the model towards specific demographic personas (using QA, BIO, and PORTRAY prompting strategies). The distribution of LM responses will be extracted via next-token log probabilities for each answer choice, normalized to form an opinion distribution. Alignment between LM and human opinion distributions will be quantified using the 1-Wasserstein distance, which accounts for the ordinal structure of survey responses, and aggregated into alignment metrics across questions and groups.
e38a29f6463f38f43797b128673b9e44d18a991e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the OpinionQA dataset, which comprises 1,498 multiple-choice survey questions spanning 23 coarse and 40 fine-grained topics, with human responses from thousands of US participants across 60 demographic groups. Nine language models of varying sizes (350M to 178B parameters) and training regimes (base and human-feedback-tuned) from OpenAI and AI21 Labs will be evaluated. Baselines will include the alignment of demographic groups with the general population and with each other on contentious topics. Evaluation metrics will focus on representativeness (default alignment with the general population and demographic groups), steerability (improvement in alignment when prompted with group-specific context), and consistency (stability of alignment across topics). Robustness checks will include varying prompt templates and answer orderings.
e38a29f6463f38f43797b128673b9e44d18a991e.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a comprehensive, quantitative framework for evaluating the alignment of language model opinions with those of diverse human populations, leveraging large-scale, expert-curated public opinion surveys. A novel dataset, OpinionQA, will be constructed to enable systematic probing of LM opinions across a wide range of topics and demographic groups. The methodology incorporates new metrics for measuring opinion alignment that account for the ordinal structure of survey responses and distinguishes between default and steered model behaviors. This approach enables fine-grained analysis of representational gaps and steerability in LMs, providing actionable insights for both model developers and users regarding the societal impact and fairness of language models.

e3c1bb88b4b8299d331d83e4dce7837caa6db93d.title: GNNAutoScale: Scalable and Expressive Graph Neural Networks via Historical Embeddings
e3c1bb88b4b8299d331d83e4dce7837caa6db93d.research_question: How can arbitrary message-passing graph neural networks (GNNs) be scaled to very large graphs without sacrificing their expressive power or requiring sub-sampling of edges, and what are the theoretical and practical implications of such a scalable framework?
e3c1bb88b4b8299d331d83e4dce7837caa6db93d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging historical embeddings—node representations stored from previous training iterations—within a principled framework, it is possible to achieve scalable GNN training with constant GPU memory consumption, while maintaining the expressive power of the original GNN and achieving state-of-the-art performance on large-scale graphs.
e3c1bb88b4b8299d331d83e4dce7837caa6db93d.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a general framework, GNNAutoScale (GAS), that enables scalable training of arbitrary message-passing GNNs by utilizing historical embeddings. For each mini-batch, GAS prunes the computation graph such that only nodes in the current mini-batch and their direct 1-hop neighbors are retained, regardless of GNN depth. Embeddings for out-of-mini-batch nodes are approximated using their most recent historical embeddings, which are stored and updated in an offline storage (e.g., CPU memory). The framework provides theoretical error bounds for the approximation induced by historical embeddings, analyzes the impact of staleness and Lipschitz continuity, and proposes practical strategies to minimize approximation error, such as graph clustering for mini-batch selection and local Lipschitz regularization. The method is implemented as PyGAS, an extension for the PyTorch Geometric library, supporting easy conversion of existing GNN models to their scalable variants.
e3c1bb88b4b8299d331d83e4dce7837caa6db93d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of benchmark datasets, including small transductive graphs (e.g., CORA, CITESEER, PUBMED, COAUTHOR-CS, COAUTHOR-PHYSICS, AMAZON-COMPUTER, AMAZON-PHOTO, WIKI-CS) and large-scale graphs (e.g., ogbn-arxiv, ogbn-products, REDDIT, PPI, FLICKR, YELP). The proposed method will be evaluated using various GNN architectures, including GCN, GAT, APPNP, GCNII, and PNA, as well as deep and expressive models. Baselines for comparison will include full-batch GNNs, neighbor sampling methods (e.g., GraphSAGE, FastGCN, LADIES), subgraph sampling (Cluster-GCN), and other historical embedding-based approaches (VR-GCN, MVS-GNN). Evaluation metrics will primarily focus on node classification accuracy, GPU memory consumption, and runtime efficiency. Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of individual components such as clustering and regularization. All experiments will be run on single-GPU setups, with histories stored in CPU memory.
e3c1bb88b4b8299d331d83e4dce7837caa6db93d.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable scalable training of arbitrary message-passing GNNs without sub-sampling edges, while provably maintaining the expressive power of the original GNN. The method introduces a principled use of historical embeddings with theoretical error bounds, and demonstrates how to tighten these bounds in practice. The approach supports deep and expressive GNN architectures on large graphs, overcoming limitations of previous methods that either reduce expressiveness or are restricted to specific GNN operators. The practical implementation achieves constant GPU memory consumption with respect to input node size, and empirical results show that the method matches or exceeds the performance of full-batch training and state-of-the-art scalable GNN methods.

e3c8cb1e6a111442965bb7d469f5c0e6789f5c40.title: Flow Matching Guide and Code
e3c8cb1e6a111442965bb7d469f5c0e6789f5c40.research_question: How can a unified and extensible generative modeling framework be developed to efficiently map samples from a known source distribution to a complex target distribution across diverse data modalities and state spaces, including continuous, discrete, and manifold domains?
e3c8cb1e6a111442965bb7d469f5c0e6789f5c40.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by constructing an appropriate probability path between source and target distributions and training a neural network to parameterize the velocity or generator field governing this path, it is possible to achieve efficient, scalable, and high-quality generative modeling across a wide range of domains and data types.
e3c8cb1e6a111442965bb7d469f5c0e6789f5c40.proposed_method: The proposed method is based on the Flow Matching (FM) framework, which constructs a continuous probability path interpolating between a source distribution and a target data distribution. A neural network is used to parameterize a time-dependent velocity field (for flows) or generator (for more general Markov processes) that governs the transformation along this path. Training is performed via a regression objective that matches the neural network's output to the analytically derived velocity or generator field, using samples from the designed probability path at randomly sampled time points. The framework is extensible to a variety of state spaces, including Euclidean spaces, discrete spaces (via Continuous Time Markov Chains), and Riemannian manifolds, by adapting the definition of the probability path and the associated loss. Conditional and marginal probability paths, as well as optimal transport and manifold-aware extensions, are incorporated to address specific generative tasks and data structures.
e3c8cb1e6a111442965bb7d469f5c0e6789f5c40.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard generative modeling benchmarks across multiple domains, such as image generation (e.g., CIFAR-10, ImageNet), text generation, audio, speech, and biological structure datasets. Baseline comparisons will include diffusion models, continuous normalizing flows, and other state-of-the-art generative models relevant to each modality. Evaluation metrics will include sample quality scores (e.g., FID for images), likelihood estimation, and domain-specific measures. The experimental setup will leverage the provided PyTorch codebase, with ablation studies on probability path design, velocity field parameterization, and extensions to discrete and manifold domains.
e3c8cb1e6a111442965bb7d469f5c0e6789f5c40.novelty_claims: The proposed framework unifies a broad class of generative models, including flows, diffusion models, and Markov process-based models, under a single, extensible recipe. It introduces a general methodology for constructing probability paths and training generators or velocity fields for arbitrary state spaces, including non-Euclidean and discrete domains. The approach enables efficient, simulation-free training and sampling, supports conditional and guided generation, and provides a principled foundation for developing new generative models for any modality or data structure. The accompanying codebase facilitates rapid adoption and further research.

e3ddc2c05b031ec219d3fcca356edcf82736f305.title: Physics-informed Neural Motion Planning on Constraint Manifolds
e3ddc2c05b031ec219d3fcca356edcf82736f305.research_question: How can motion planning for robots be efficiently performed on kinematic constraint manifolds, without relying on expert demonstration data, while ensuring high computational efficiency and scalability to high-dimensional and real-world tasks?
e3ddc2c05b031ec219d3fcca356edcf82736f305.hypothesis: A physics-informed neural network framework that directly solves the Eikonal equation on constraint manifolds can enable efficient and accurate constrained motion planning without requiring expert demonstration data, outperforming existing optimization, sampling, and imitation learning-based methods in terms of computational speed, path quality, and success rate.
e3ddc2c05b031ec219d3fcca356edcf82736f305.proposed_method: A novel physics-informed neural motion planning framework is proposed that extends the Eikonal equation formulation to incorporate both collision avoidance and kinematic constraints, enabling learning directly on constraint manifolds. The method utilizes Task Space Regions (TSRs) to implicitly define kinematic constraints and samples robot configurations both on and near the constraint manifold using inverse kinematics and random perturbations. A neural architecture based on Fourier feature encoding and ResNet-style encoders is employed to predict a factorized arrival time field, which is used to compute speed and gradient fields for path generation. The speed model is designed as a negative exponential function of the distance to the collision-free constraint manifold, ensuring high speed on the manifold and low speed elsewhere. Training is performed using a progressive speed scheduling strategy and isotropic loss between predicted and ground truth speeds, with mini-batch sampling to improve efficiency. The planning procedure iteratively updates start and goal configurations along the tangential component of the learned gradient field to generate collision-free, constraint-adhering paths.
e3ddc2c05b031ec219d3fcca356edcf82736f305.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of scenarios, including 2D surface mesh manifolds (e.g., Bunny), 2D geometric constraint manifolds in 3D space (paraboloid and cylinder shapes), and high-dimensional 6-DOF robot manipulator tasks such as door opening and object manipulation under orientation constraints, both in simulation and real-world environments. Baseline methods for comparison include the Heat Method (HM), CBiRRT (projection-based sampling), CoMPNetX (imitation learning with informed sampling), and P-NTFields (physics-informed neural planning without manifold constraints). Evaluation metrics will include planning time, path length, margin to the manifold, and success rate. Data generation and training times for all learning-based methods will also be measured. All experiments will be run on a high-performance computing system with an RTX 3090 GPU, Core i7 CPU, and 128GB RAM.
e3ddc2c05b031ec219d3fcca356edcf82736f305.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to extend physics-informed neural motion planning to directly solve the Eikonal equation on kinematic constraint manifolds, eliminating the need for expert demonstration path datasets. The method introduces a new speed model tailored for constraint manifolds, enabling efficient learning and planning in high-dimensional and complex real-world environments. The framework achieves significantly faster planning times (up to 48× faster than classical methods and 15× faster than imitation learning-based methods) and reduces data generation time from hours to minutes, while maintaining or improving path quality and success rates compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

e3e68a4bd8b892321833c63a9607e406454dd4e8.title: Line Graph Neural Networks for Link Weight Prediction
e3e68a4bd8b892321833c63a9607e406454dd4e8.research_question: How can the prediction of link weights in complex networks be improved by leveraging deeper graph features, rather than relying solely on shallow topological characteristics?
e3e68a4bd8b892321833c63a9607e406454dd4e8.hypothesis: Utilizing a framework that combines enclosing subgraph extraction, weighted node labeling, line graph transformation, and graph convolutional neural networks will enable the learning of richer link features, thereby improving the accuracy and robustness of link weight prediction across diverse network types.
e3e68a4bd8b892321833c63a9607e406454dd4e8.proposed_method: The proposed approach begins by extracting a one-hop enclosing subgraph around each target link in the network, ensuring subgraph size uniformity by limiting the number of nodes. Nodes within the subgraph are then labeled using a weighted adaptation of the Weisfeiler-Lehman algorithm, which encodes both structural and weighted distance information. The labeled subgraph is transformed into its corresponding line graph, where each node represents a link from the original subgraph, and node attributes are generated by concatenating the attribute vectors of the link's endpoints. A Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) is applied to the line graph to learn node embeddings that capture complex structural and weight-related features. Finally, the embedding corresponding to the target link is input into a fully connected neural network with two layers to predict the link weight as a regression problem.
e3e68a4bd8b892321833c63a9607e406454dd4e8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six real-world weighted network datasets of varying sizes and domains, such as social, transportation, and biological networks. The datasets will be split into training and test sets by randomly dividing the set of link weights. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including shallow topological feature-based methods and other machine learning approaches for link weight prediction. Evaluation metrics will include root mean square error (RMSE) to assess regression performance. The experimental setup will ensure consistent subgraph sizes and normalization of link weights to the (0,1) interval for fair comparison.
e3e68a4bd8b892321833c63a9607e406454dd4e8.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel combination of line graph transformation and graph convolutional neural networks for direct link feature learning in the context of link weight prediction. Unlike prior approaches that rely on shallow node similarity metrics or simple feature concatenation, this framework enables the extraction of deeper, task-aware structural features. The approach is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art prediction accuracy and robustness across diverse network types and training set sizes.

e3e721fd51a5940273759c5058b2046740a54d5c.title: Pre-training Enhanced Spatial-temporal Graph Neural Network for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
e3e721fd51a5940273759c5058b2046740a54d5c.research_question: How can multivariate time series forecasting be improved by leveraging long-term historical dependencies and contextual information, beyond the limitations of current spatial-temporal graph neural networks that primarily focus on short-term data?
e3e721fd51a5940273759c5058b2046740a54d5c.hypothesis: Enhancing spatial-temporal graph neural networks with segment-level representations learned from a scalable, unsupervised pre-training model on very long-term historical time series will improve forecasting accuracy by providing richer temporal context and more robust dependency modeling.
e3e721fd51a5940273759c5058b2046740a54d5c.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that augments spatial-temporal graph neural networks (STGNNs) with a scalable pre-training model, termed STEP. The pre-training model, TSFormer, is based on Transformer blocks and is trained using a masked autoencoding strategy to efficiently learn temporal patterns from very long-term historical time series (e.g., up to several weeks). The time series are split into non-overlapping patches, and a high masking ratio (e.g., 75%) is used to force the model to learn high-level semantic representations at the segment level. The encoder processes only unmasked patches, while a lightweight decoder reconstructs the masked segments. The learned segment-level representations are then used to provide contextual information to downstream STGNNs. Additionally, a graph structure learner is designed to infer a discrete, sparse dependency graph using the representations from TSFormer, regularized by a k-nearest neighbor (kNN) graph computed from the learned features. The entire framework is modular and can be integrated with various STGNN architectures.
e3e721fd51a5940273759c5058b2046740a54d5c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three real-world multivariate time series datasets: METR-LA, PEMS-BAY, and PEMS04, each containing traffic data from hundreds of sensors over several months. For each dataset, the pre-training model is trained on long historical sequences (one to two weeks), and the enhanced STGNN is evaluated on forecasting the next 12 timesteps. Baseline comparisons will include traditional methods (HA, VAR, SVR), deep learning models (FC-LSTM, DCRNN, GraphWaveNet, ASTGCN, STSGCN), and recent state-of-the-art approaches (GMAN, MTGNN, GTS). Evaluation metrics will include Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). Ablation studies will assess the impact of the pre-training model, graph structure learning, and hyperparameters such as masking ratio and k in the kNN graph. Statistical significance will be tested using t-tests.
e3e721fd51a5940273759c5058b2046740a54d5c.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a scalable, unsupervised pre-training model for time series that can efficiently learn from very long-term historical data and generate segment-level representations, which is a significant departure from prior STGNNs limited to short-term windows. The integration of these representations into downstream STGNNs provides richer contextual information and enables more robust modeling of temporal and spatial dependencies. The graph structure learner leverages the pre-trained representations to infer a discrete, sparse dependency graph, addressing the common issue of incomplete or biased prior graphs. The approach is general and can be applied to a wide range of STGNN architectures, and experiments are designed to demonstrate consistent and significant improvements over existing baselines.

e3f80d950e6f841bd7eea4c24d4e1e5aa2bd85c7.title: SuGaR: Surface-Aligned Gaussian Splatting for Efficient 3D Mesh Reconstruction and High-Quality Mesh Rendering
e3f80d950e6f841bd7eea4c24d4e1e5aa2bd85c7.research_question: How can accurate, editable, and high-quality 3D meshes be efficiently extracted and rendered from unstructured 3D Gaussian Splatting representations, enabling fast mesh reconstruction and realistic rendering suitable for computer graphics applications?
e3f80d950e6f841bd7eea4c24d4e1e5aa2bd85c7.hypothesis: Introducing a regularization term that aligns 3D Gaussians with scene surfaces, combined with a scalable mesh extraction and refinement strategy, will enable rapid and high-fidelity mesh reconstruction and rendering from 3D Gaussian Splatting representations, outperforming existing methods in both speed and quality.
e3f80d950e6f841bd7eea4c24d4e1e5aa2bd85c7.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that first introduces a regularization term during 3D Gaussian Splatting optimization to encourage Gaussians to align with and be well distributed over the scene surface. This is achieved by deriving a surface-aligned density function and minimizing the difference between the ideal and actual signed distance functions (SDFs) at sampled points, using depth maps for efficient SDF estimation. Once the Gaussians are aligned, an efficient mesh extraction algorithm samples points on a chosen level set of the density function using depth maps, and reconstructs a triangle mesh via Poisson surface reconstruction. An optional refinement step binds new, flat Gaussians to mesh triangles and jointly optimizes both the mesh and the bound Gaussians using Gaussian Splatting rendering, enabling high-quality, editable, and relightable mesh representations. The method leverages GPU acceleration and is designed to complete mesh extraction and refinement within minutes.
e3f80d950e6f841bd7eea4c24d4e1e5aa2bd85c7.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on real 3D scenes from the Mip-NeRF360, DeepBlending, and Tanks & Temples datasets, following standard evaluation protocols for novel view synthesis and mesh reconstruction. The proposed method is compared against baselines including NeRF-based methods (Mip-NeRF360, Instant-NGP, Plenoxels), 3D Gaussian Splatting, and mesh-based approaches (Mobile-NeRF, NeRFMeshing, BakedSDF). Evaluation metrics include PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for rendering quality, and ablation studies assess the impact of different mesh extraction techniques (Marching Cubes, Poisson on Gaussian centers, and the proposed surface-aligned method) and mesh rendering strategies (surface-aligned Gaussians vs. traditional UV textures). The method is implemented on a single NVIDIA V100 GPU, with optimization and mesh extraction typically completed in 15-45 minutes per scene. Meshes are extracted using Poisson reconstruction at various density levels, and refinement is performed for up to 15,000 iterations.
e3f80d950e6f841bd7eea4c24d4e1e5aa2bd85c7.novelty_claims: The approach introduces a new regularization term that aligns 3D Gaussians with the scene surface, enabling accurate surface representation and efficient mesh extraction. A scalable mesh extraction algorithm is proposed that leverages surface-aligned Gaussians and Poisson reconstruction, outperforming traditional methods like Marching Cubes in speed and quality. The method enables joint optimization of meshes and surface-bound Gaussians for high-quality, editable, and relightable mesh rendering using Gaussian Splatting. The entire pipeline achieves mesh extraction and refinement within minutes on a single GPU, significantly reducing computation time compared to state-of-the-art neural SDF-based methods, and achieves superior rendering quality for mesh-based novel view synthesis.

e41482f4ee984f17382f6cdd900df094d928be06.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
e41482f4ee984f17382f6cdd900df094d928be06.research_question: How can a realistic, reproducible, and functionally diverse web environment be developed to enable the evaluation and advancement of autonomous agents that perform complex, high-level tasks via natural language commands?
e41482f4ee984f17382f6cdd900df094d928be06.hypothesis: Establishing a highly realistic, standalone web environment populated with authentic data and diverse, long-horizon tasks will reveal significant gaps in current autonomous agent capabilities and provide a robust testbed for measuring and improving agent performance on real-world web tasks.
e41482f4ee984f17382f6cdd900df094d928be06.proposed_method: A comprehensive web-based environment will be constructed by deploying fully functional, self-hosted websites from four major domains: e-commerce, social forums, collaborative software development, and content management. These sites will be built using open-source libraries and populated with data sampled from real-world counterparts to ensure authenticity. The environment will include utility tools (e.g., map, calculator, scratchpad) and external knowledge bases (e.g., Wikipedia, user manuals) as independent web resources. Agents will interact with this environment via a compound action space that emulates realistic keyboard and mouse operations, including multi-tab navigation and element selection through both coordinates and unique IDs. The observation space will support multiple modalities, such as raw HTML, screenshots, and accessibility trees, enabling flexible agent design and fair comparison.
e41482f4ee984f17382f6cdd900df094d928be06.experiment_details: A benchmark suite of 812 long-horizon, high-level natural language tasks will be curated, covering information-seeking, site navigation, and content/configuration operations. Each task will be annotated with programmatic validators to assess functional correctness, using a combination of exact match, must-include, and fuzzy-match metrics for textual answers, as well as direct inspection of web state changes for operational tasks. Baseline experiments will be conducted using large language models (GPT-4, GPT-3.5, PaLM-2/TEXT-BISON-001) with both direct and chain-of-thought prompting strategies, and with/without explicit hints for unachievable tasks. Human performance will be measured as an upper bound, and all agent performances will be compared using end-to-end task success rates and detailed error analysis.
e41482f4ee984f17382f6cdd900df094d928be06.novelty_claims: The proposed environment is the first to combine high realism, full reproducibility, and diverse, functionally correct web-based tasks in a standalone, self-hostable setup. It uniquely supports multi-tab interactions, integrates a wide range of authentic web domains and tools, and provides programmatic, outcome-based evaluation metrics that go beyond surface-form action matching. The benchmark exposes the limitations of current state-of-the-art language models in realistic web scenarios and establishes a new standard for evaluating and developing robust autonomous agents capable of handling complex, real-world web tasks.

e4148c7b73aeb7602070d605df13473c7748bc97.title: Uncovering Overfitting in Large Language Model Editing
e4148c7b73aeb7602070d605df13473c7748bc97.research_question: How can overfitting in large language model (LLM) knowledge editing be effectively identified, measured, and mitigated, particularly in complex reasoning scenarios such as multi-hop tasks?
e4148c7b73aeb7602070d605df13473c7748bc97.hypothesis: Editing overfit in LLMs arises from the prevailing editing paradigm that overemphasizes direct input-output correspondence, and introducing multi-stage inference constraints inspired by LLMs' natural reasoning mechanisms will mitigate overfitting while preserving edit success.
e4148c7b73aeb7602070d605df13473c7748bc97.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, EVOKE, will be constructed to systematically evaluate overfitting in LLM editing across a variety of tasks, including recall and overfit scenarios. Fine-grained evaluation metrics will be defined to quantify overfitting, such as Correct Answer Probability, Direct Probability, and a novel Editing Overfit Score. To address overfitting, a plug-and-play strategy named Learn the Inference (LTI) will be developed, introducing a Multi-stage Inference Constraint module. This module will impose constraints at different reasoning stages: aligning subject representations in shallow layers, regularizing output distributions in deeper layers, and enforcing new knowledge recall, all by matching the edited model’s behavior to that of an unedited model provided with the new knowledge in context. The approach will be designed to integrate seamlessly with existing editing methods (e.g., ROME, MEMIT) and can be jointly optimized with their objectives.
e4148c7b73aeb7602070d605df13473c7748bc97.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple LLMs, including GPT-J, GPT-2 XL, and Llama-2-7B, using the EVOKE benchmark, which comprises six tasks spanning recall and overfit scenarios (e.g., multi-hop reasoning, prefix distraction, subject and relation specificity). Baseline editing methods such as FT, FT-L, MEND, ROME, and MEMIT will be evaluated, both with and without the proposed LTI strategy. Evaluation metrics will include Correct Answer Probability, Direct Probability, Editing Overfit Score, and Answer Modify Score. Additional experiments will assess the effectiveness of general overfitting mitigation techniques (Norm Constraints, Batch Editing, Data Augmentation, Multi-layer Editing) and compare LTI to data augmentation strategies. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of different components of the Multi-stage Inference Constraints.
e4148c7b73aeb7602070d605df13473c7748bc97.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first dedicated benchmark (EVOKE) and fine-grained metrics for systematically evaluating overfitting in LLM editing. It identifies and formalizes the Editing Overfit phenomenon as a key limitation of current editing paradigms. The Learn the Inference (LTI) strategy is proposed as a novel, extensible, plug-and-play solution that leverages multi-stage inference constraints inspired by LLMs' natural knowledge recall mechanisms, enabling edited models to generalize new knowledge more robustly and reducing overfitting beyond what is achievable with existing mitigation strategies.

e43537515736fa087a85ba30b67ee44705a92b85.title: Accounting For Informative Sampling When Learning to Forecast Treatment Outcomes Over Time
e43537515736fa087a85ba30b67ee44705a92b85.research_question: How can accurate forecasting of treatment outcomes over time be achieved from observational data when the timing of observations is informative, i.e., dependent on patient characteristics, past outcomes, and administered treatments, rather than being random or regular?
e43537515736fa087a85ba30b67ee44705a92b85.hypothesis: Accounting for informative sampling in observational data using inverse intensity-weighting within a flexible machine learning framework will enable unbiased and more accurate forecasting of treatment outcomes over time, compared to existing methods that ignore the informativeness of the sampling process.
e43537515736fa087a85ba30b67ee44705a92b85.proposed_method: A general framework is developed for learning to forecast treatment outcomes in the presence of informative sampling by modeling the observation process as a covariate shift problem and applying inverse intensity-weighting. The method, TESAR-CDE, instantiates this framework using Neural Controlled Differential Equations (Neural CDEs). The approach involves encoding patient histories as continuous latent paths, forecasting future outcomes and observation intensities jointly, and optimizing a weighted loss function where the weights are the inverse of the estimated observation intensities. Two implementations are considered: a two-step procedure where observation intensities are estimated and then used to weight the outcome loss, and a multitask procedure where outcome and intensity prediction are learned jointly, but only the outcome loss is used to update the shared representation. The methodology assumes a 'sampling at random' (SAR) mechanism, where observation times depend on observed history but not on unobserved or future outcomes.
e43537515736fa087a85ba30b67ee44705a92b85.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in a simulation environment inspired by clinical use cases, specifically lung cancer treatment trials, where the informativeness of the observation process can be controlled. The simulation uses a pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic tumor growth model, with observation times determined by a patient-specific, history-dependent intensity process. Datasets are generated with varying levels of sampling informativeness and observation scarcity, and include both sequential and concurrent treatment regimes. The proposed methods are compared against a state-of-the-art baseline (TE-CDE) that does not account for informative sampling. Evaluation metrics include root mean squared error (RMSE) for forecasting tumor size over different prediction horizons. The experimental setup includes separate training, validation, and test sets, with test data providing complete information to assess unbiased forecasting performance.
e43537515736fa087a85ba30b67ee44705a92b85.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to formalize and address the challenge of informative sampling in the context of forecasting treatment outcomes over time using machine learning. The method introduces a general framework for correcting bias due to informative sampling via inverse intensity-weighting and presents TESAR-CDE, a novel instantiation using Neural CDEs. The work provides a new simulation environment for systematically studying the effects of informative sampling and demonstrates empirically that accounting for informative sampling leads to improved forecasting accuracy compared to existing methods.

e43f9e5479ff63a7445c6c133f9fbeac45167ebd.title: Ask a Strong LLM Judge when Your Reward Model is Uncertain
e43f9e5479ff63a7445c6c133f9fbeac45167ebd.research_question: How can reliable and cost-effective reward signals be provided for reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) in large language models (LLMs), especially when standard reward models are uncertain or face out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs?
e43f9e5479ff63a7445c6c133f9fbeac45167ebd.hypothesis: An uncertainty-based routing framework that combines a fast but less reliable reward model (RM) with a strong, costly LLM judge will improve the accuracy and generalization of preference predictions and downstream RLHF alignment, while maintaining affordable computational costs.
e43f9e5479ff63a7445c6c133f9fbeac45167ebd.proposed_method: A novel uncertainty-based routing framework is developed to complement a standard reward model (RM) with a strong but computationally expensive LLM judge. The approach begins by training a pairwise preference model (PM) using human preference data, employing a spectral-normalized Gaussian process (SNGP) head for principled uncertainty quantification. During inference, the uncertainty score for each response pair is computed; if the uncertainty is below a threshold, the PM's prediction is used, while pairs with high uncertainty are routed to the LLM judge for evaluation. The resulting preference predictions are used to estimate reward differences, which are then incorporated into policy gradient methods (such as RLOO and GRPO) for RLHF. The framework enables efficient allocation of LLM judge calls, focusing resources on the most uncertain and potentially OOD cases.
e43f9e5479ff63a7445c6c133f9fbeac45167ebd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as the base model for the PM and DeepSeek-R1 as the LLM judge. The HelpSteer2-Preference dataset will be used for PM training, while RewardBench and RM-Bench serve as evaluation benchmarks for reward model accuracy, focusing on both in-distribution and OOD data. For downstream RLHF alignment, a subset of the Ultrafeedback dataset will be used for training, and evaluation will be performed on Arena-Hard-v0.1, AlpacaEval2.0, and MT-Bench using standard win-rate and scoring metrics. Baselines will include a standard PM without uncertainty quantification and random routing strategies that match the number of LLM judge calls. The number of judge calls, inference time, and accuracy improvements will be systematically compared across routing strategies and thresholds.
e43f9e5479ff63a7445c6c133f9fbeac45167ebd.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a principled and efficient uncertainty-based routing mechanism that leverages SNGP-based uncertainty quantification for pairwise preference models in RLHF. This approach enables dynamic allocation of costly LLM judge resources, significantly improving OOD generalization and downstream alignment performance compared to both standard RMs and random routing. The method is the first to systematically integrate uncertainty quantification and routing for RLHF in LLMs, offering a practical solution to the trade-off between feedback quality and computational cost.

e4530cff25a23e5167997307aef50d3e83904d33.title: Grokking as a First Order Phase Transition in Two Layer Networks
e4530cff25a23e5167997307aef50d3e83904d33.research_question: How can the phenomenon of Grokking in deep neural networks be analytically characterized and predicted, and what is its relationship to phase transitions and feature learning in two-layer networks?
e4530cff25a23e5167997307aef50d3e83904d33.hypothesis: Grokking in two-layer deep neural networks corresponds to a first-order phase transition in the internal representations of the network, which can be analytically described using mean-field theory and adaptive kernel approaches, leading to distinct learning phases and altered sample complexity compared to Gaussian Process limits.
e4530cff25a23e5167997307aef50d3e83904d33.proposed_method: The proposed research will develop an analytical framework that maps Grokking in two-layer neural networks to first-order phase transitions, utilizing mean-field theory from statistical physics. The methodology will extend the adaptive kernel approach to analyze the posterior distribution of input layer weights, employing variational Gaussian mixture approximations to capture the emergence of new internal representations. Two teacher-student models will be studied: one with a cubic-polynomial teacher and another with a modular addition teacher, each trained with mean squared error loss and Langevin dynamics to equilibrium. The approach will derive self-consistency equations for the latent kernels and discrepancy modes, and employ saddle-point approximations to identify phase transitions in the weight distributions. Analytical predictions will be validated by scaling up network width, input dimension, and data size, and by comparing the resulting phases (GFL, GMFL-I, GMFL-II) to experimental outcomes.
e4530cff25a23e5167997307aef50d3e83904d33.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two settings: a non-linear teacher-student model with Gaussian inputs and a modular addition task with structured 'two-hot' vectors. Networks will be trained using Langevin dynamics to equilibrium, with careful scaling of width, input dimension, and data size according to specified laws. Ensembles of networks will be trained with varying random seeds and data draws to ensure statistical robustness. Key evaluation metrics will include the negative log posterior of weight projections, test accuracy, and root mean squared error (RMSE) on held-out data. Baselines will include the infinite-width Gaussian Process (GP) limit and standard neural network Gaussian Process (NNGP) kernels. The experiments will track the emergence of phase transitions by varying control parameters such as noise strength and sample size, and will compare empirical distributions of internal representations to theoretical predictions.
e4530cff25a23e5167997307aef50d3e83904d33.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a first-principles analytical mapping between Grokking and first-order phase transitions in representation learning for two-layer networks. It extends the adaptive kernel approach to Gaussian mixture approximations, enabling exact analytical predictions of feature learning phases. The framework provides a unified classification of learning phases (GFL, GMFL-I, GMFL-II), demonstrates that Grokking can reduce sample complexity compared to GP limits, and offers new insights into the internal state of networks post-Grokking. The approach is analytically tractable, generalizes to different architectures, and suggests novel directions for measuring, pruning, and regulating feature learning in deep networks.

e46a79cf7c2c9192639f9e1d12280650e06b9d56.title: Autoregressive Image Generation without Vector Quantization
e46a79cf7c2c9192639f9e1d12280650e06b9d56.research_question: Can autoregressive models for image generation operate effectively in continuous-valued token spaces without relying on vector quantization, and how can per-token probability distributions be modeled in such settings?
e46a79cf7c2c9192639f9e1d12280650e06b9d56.hypothesis: Autoregressive models for image generation do not require discrete, vector-quantized tokens; instead, modeling per-token probability distributions with a diffusion-based procedure in continuous-valued spaces will yield higher quality and more flexible image generation.
e46a79cf7c2c9192639f9e1d12280650e06b9d56.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed where autoregressive and masked autoregressive (MAR) models operate directly on continuous-valued tokens, eliminating the need for vector quantization. The per-token probability distribution is modeled using a denoising diffusion process: for each token, the autoregressive model predicts a conditioning vector z, which is then used by a small denoising MLP network to parameterize the diffusion process and model the conditional distribution p(x|z) of the token. The loss function, termed Diffusion Loss, is defined as a denoising criterion over noise-corrupted versions of the ground-truth token, and gradients are backpropagated through both the autoregressive model and the denoising network. At inference, samples are drawn from the modeled distribution via a reverse diffusion process, with temperature scaling available to control diversity. This approach is compatible with both causal and bidirectional attention mechanisms, and can be applied to standard AR and MAR variants.
e46a79cf7c2c9192639f9e1d12280650e06b9d56.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet dataset at 256x256 resolution. Both discrete (VQ-16) and continuous (KL-16, KL-8) tokenizers will be used for fair comparison, with public tokenizers from the LDM codebase and additional custom-trained variants. Baselines will include standard autoregressive models with cross-entropy loss on discrete tokens, as well as recent state-of-the-art models such as MaskGIT, MAGE, DiT, and others. Evaluation metrics will include FID, Inception Score (IS), Precision, and Recall. The experimental setup will involve training large-scale Transformer-based AR and MAR models (up to ~943M parameters), using both causal and bidirectional attention, and varying the number of autoregressive steps to study the speed/accuracy trade-off. Ablation studies will assess the impact of MLP size, diffusion steps, temperature, and tokenizer flexibility.
e46a79cf7c2c9192639f9e1d12280650e06b9d56.novelty_claims: The proposed approach removes the necessity for vector quantization in autoregressive image generation, enabling the use of continuous-valued tokens and thus higher-quality representations. Diffusion Loss provides a principled, flexible way to model per-token probability distributions in continuous spaces, and is compatible with a wide range of tokenizers and autoregressive model variants. The method unifies standard and masked autoregressive models under a generalized framework, supports both causal and bidirectional attention, and achieves state-of-the-art results on ImageNet in terms of FID and speed. The approach also demonstrates superior flexibility, efficiency, and scalability compared to existing token-based and latent diffusion models.

e48e4a32dc23b6615c6a2e21d52e5ffa8fb6bda7.title: Sampling, Diffusions, and Stochastic Localization
e48e4a32dc23b6615c6a2e21d52e5ffa8fb6bda7.research_question: How can sampling from high-dimensional probability distributions be unified and improved through the generalization and connection of diffusion-based and stochastic localization processes, and what new algorithmic frameworks can be developed from this unified perspective?
e48e4a32dc23b6615c6a2e21d52e5ffa8fb6bda7.hypothesis: A general framework that unifies diffusion-based sampling and stochastic localization processes will enable the development of new, broadly applicable, and potentially more efficient sampling algorithms for high-dimensional distributions, both in settings where the target distribution is known or only accessible via samples.
e48e4a32dc23b6615c6a2e21d52e5ffa8fb6bda7.proposed_method: A general class of sampling algorithms will be developed by constructing stochastic processes whose endpoints are samples from a target high-dimensional distribution. The approach will generalize both time-reversed diffusion processes (such as those based on Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics) and stochastic localization, where the process is defined in terms of increasingly informative noisy observations of the latent variable. The methodology will formalize observation processes as Markov chains and martingales in the space of probability measures, allowing for flexible choices of noise models, observation spaces, and update rules. Discretization schemes (e.g., Euler-Maruyama) will be used to approximate the continuous-time stochastic differential equations (SDEs) that govern these processes. The framework will be instantiated for various cases, including isotropic and anisotropic Gaussian processes, erasure processes, and discrete-valued processes, each with explicit update rules and transition kernels.
e48e4a32dc23b6615c6a2e21d52e5ffa8fb6bda7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world high-dimensional distributions. For known distributions, classical statistical mechanics models and Bayesian posteriors will be considered, with explicit forms for the target distribution. For unknown distributions, generative modeling benchmarks will be used, where only samples from the target are available. Baselines will include standard Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, existing diffusion-based samplers, and recent stochastic localization algorithms. Evaluation metrics will include sample quality (e.g., via Kullback-Leibler divergence, Wasserstein distance), mixing time, computational efficiency, and scalability. Experimental setups will involve varying the dimensionality, noise models, and observation process structures to assess the flexibility and performance of the proposed unified framework.
e48e4a32dc23b6615c6a2e21d52e5ffa8fb6bda7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified framework that generalizes and connects diffusion-based sampling and stochastic localization, providing a broad and flexible class of sampling algorithms for high-dimensional distributions. The approach allows for observation processes in spaces different from the latent variable, supports both continuous and discrete domains, and encompasses a wide range of noise models and update mechanisms. The framework clarifies the theoretical connections between time-reversal in diffusions and martingale-based localization, and enables the derivation of new sampling schemes and insights into existing ones. The methodology is broadly applicable to both explicitly known and sample-accessible distributions, and offers algorithmic generalizations that have not been previously exploited in the literature.

e4b73b4ea5b5afa4e2b583f8a38b08a5ec2d65c1.title: IDiff-Face: Synthetic-based Face Recognition through Fizzy Identity-Conditioned Diffusion Models
e4b73b4ea5b5afa4e2b583f8a38b08a5ec2d65c1.research_question: Can synthetic face datasets generated by identity-conditioned diffusion models provide a viable and privacy-preserving alternative to authentic data for training high-accuracy face recognition systems, while maintaining a realistic balance between identity discrimination and intra-class diversity?
e4b73b4ea5b5afa4e2b583f8a38b08a5ec2d65c1.hypothesis: Synthetic face images generated by identity-conditioned diffusion models, enhanced with mechanisms to control intra-class variation, can achieve face recognition performance comparable to models trained on authentic datasets, thus bridging the performance gap while addressing privacy and ethical concerns.
e4b73b4ea5b5afa4e2b583f8a38b08a5ec2d65c1.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed based on conditional latent diffusion models (LDMs) for generating synthetic face images. The method will condition a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) on identity representations extracted from a pre-trained face recognition model, injecting these features into the diffusion model via a cross-attention mechanism. Training will occur in the latent space of a pre-trained autoencoder (VQGAN), reducing computational complexity and improving sample quality.
