To enhance intra-class diversity and prevent overfitting to identity contexts, a Contextual Partial Dropout (CPD) mechanism will be introduced, randomly dropping components of the identity embedding during training. Two approaches for generating synthetic identities will be explored: direct sampling of identity embeddings from a hyperspherical Gaussian and a two-stage process where an unconditional diffusion model first generates a synthetic image, from which an identity embedding is extracted for further conditional generation.
e4b73b4ea5b5afa4e2b583f8a38b08a5ec2d65c1.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training the proposed diffusion-based generator on the FFHQ dataset (70,000 images, 128x128 resolution) and generating large-scale synthetic datasets (up to 500,000 images) for face recognition training. Multiple variants will be tested, varying the CPD probability (0%, 25%, 50%) and the identity embedding generation approach (uniform sampling vs. two-stage). Face recognition models (ResNet-18 and ResNet-50) will be trained on these synthetic datasets and evaluated on standard benchmarks: LFW, AgeDB-30, CA-LFW, CFP-FP, and CP-LFW. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art synthetic data approaches (e.g., SynFace, SFace, USynthFace, DigiFace-1M, ExFaceGAN, IDnet) and models trained on authentic data (CASIA-WebFace, MS1MV2). Evaluation metrics will include verification accuracy, Equal Error Rate (EER), FMR100, FMR1000, and Fisher Discriminant Ratio (FDR). The impact of dataset size, width (number of identities), depth (images per identity), and data augmentation will be systematically analyzed.
e4b73b4ea5b5afa4e2b583f8a38b08a5ec2d65c1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first identity-conditioned diffusion model for generating synthetic face datasets tailored for face recognition training. The Contextual Partial Dropout (CPD) mechanism is a novel contribution that enables explicit control over the trade-off between identity discrimination and intra-class diversity in synthetic data. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance among synthetic-based face recognition systems, significantly narrowing the gap to models trained on authentic data, and demonstrates that synthetic data can surpass human-level verification accuracy on LFW. This work provides a scalable, privacy-preserving alternative to authentic face datasets, addressing urgent legal and ethical concerns in the field.

e4d88921f16a710e93f166b5609f08ab7d65cd39.title: Constructing Linear-Sized Spectral Sparsification in Almost-Linear Time
e4d88921f16a710e93f166b5609f08ab7d65cd39.research_question: How can linear-sized spectral sparsifiers for graphs be constructed in almost-linear time, and can these techniques be generalized to sparsifying sums of rank-1 positive semi-definite matrices?
e4d88921f16a710e93f166b5609f08ab7d65cd39.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a novel combination of random sampling by effective resistance and adaptive construction based on barrier functions enables the construction of linear-sized spectral sparsifiers in almost-linear time, improving upon previous quadratic or suboptimal constructions.
e4d88921f16a710e93f166b5609f08ab7d65cd39.proposed_method: A new algorithm will be developed that constructs linear-sized spectral sparsifiers for graphs by iteratively sampling edges (or, more generally, rank-1 matrices) according to probabilities derived from their effective resistance, and adaptively updating spectral barrier functions to control the eigenvalues of the constructed sparsifier. The method introduces a potential function based on higher moments (parameterized by a large constant q), which allows for efficient approximation of sampling probabilities via Taylor expansion and enables the reuse of these probabilities over multiple iterations. At each iteration, the algorithm samples a batch of vectors (edges) with probabilities proportional to their relative effective resistance, adds appropriately weighted rank-1 updates to the current matrix, and updates the barrier values to maintain spectral invariants. The sampling probabilities are recomputed only after a fixed number of iterations, ensuring computational efficiency, and approximations are allowed for both the effective resistances and the number of samples to further reduce runtime.
e4d88921f16a710e93f166b5609f08ab7d65cd39.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on undirected, weighted graphs of varying sizes to validate the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed algorithm. The primary evaluation will focus on the runtime (measured in terms of the number of vertices n and edges m), the size of the resulting sparsifier (number of edges), and the spectral approximation quality (measured by the preservation of Laplacian quadratic forms within a (1+ε) factor for all vectors). Comparisons will be made against previous state-of-the-art algorithms, including those of Spielman and Srivastava (nearly-linear time, but with larger sparsifiers) and Batson, Spielman, and Srivastava (optimal size but quadratic time). Additional experiments may include generalizations to sums of rank-1 PSD matrices and the impact of varying the parameter q on performance and sparsifier quality.
e4d88921f16a710e93f166b5609f08ab7d65cd39.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to achieve almost-linear time construction of linear-sized spectral sparsifiers for graphs. It innovatively combines random sampling by effective resistance with adaptive barrier function techniques, and introduces a higher-moment potential function that enables efficient and reusable sampling probability computation. The approach generalizes to sparsifying sums of rank-1 PSD matrices and provides an alternative analysis framework for previous algorithms, leading to significant improvements in both theoretical runtime and practical applicability.

e4eee21ef4e11d3d0ad444b049c6c758b5240187.title: AI Alignment with Changing and Influenceable Reward Functions
e4eee21ef4e11d3d0ad444b049c6c758b5240187.research_question: How can AI systems be aligned with human preferences when those preferences are dynamic and can be influenced by the AI itself, and what are the trade-offs and limitations of different alignment objectives under such conditions?
e4eee21ef4e11d3d0ad444b049c6c758b5240187.proposed_method: A formal framework will be developed by extending Markov Decision Processes to Dynamic Reward Markov Decision Processes (DR-MDPs), which explicitly model human preferences as changing reward functions that may be influenced by the AI's actions. Multiple alignment objectives will be formalized within this DR-MDP framework, each specifying different ways of aggregating or prioritizing time-varying preferences (e.g., real-time, initial, final, natural evolution, constrained, myopic, privileged, and Pareto-efficient objectives). Theoretical analysis will be conducted to characterize the normative ambiguities, influence incentives, and potential for undesirable AI behavior under each objective. The approach will also include formal definitions of influence and incentives for reward manipulation, and will analyze the effects of optimization horizon on the emergence of influence incentives. Comparative evaluation of these objectives will be performed using illustrative DR-MDP examples.
e4eee21ef4e11d3d0ad444b049c6c758b5240187.experiment_details: Experiments will consist of constructing a series of synthetic DR-MDP scenarios that capture key challenges such as preference change, AI-induced influence, and normative ambiguity (e.g., scenarios inspired by health assistants, recommender systems, and therapy chatbots). For each scenario, the optimal policies under eight different alignment objectives will be computed and compared. Evaluation metrics will include the presence or absence of undesirable influence incentives, normative ambiguity, risk aversion (e.g., policy conservatism), and the ability to avoid reward lock-in. Baseline comparisons will include standard static-reward MDP objectives and current alignment techniques such as RLHF and reward modeling. The experimental setup will also analyze the impact of varying the optimization horizon on the emergence of influence incentives.
e4eee21ef4e11d3d0ad444b049c6c758b5240187.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the DR-MDP framework as a principled formalism for modeling dynamic and influenceable human preferences in AI alignment. It provides a systematic comparison of multiple alignment objectives, revealing that all existing and intuitive approaches either incentivize undesirable influence or are overly conservative. The analysis clarifies the inherent trade-offs in aligning AI with changing preferences and demonstrates that no straightforward solution exists, highlighting the need for explicit consideration of preference dynamics in future alignment practices. The work also contributes formal definitions and theoretical results regarding influence incentives and the effects of optimization horizon, offering conceptual clarity for future empirical and theoretical research in AI alignment.

e4f2efbc04f92bf01c393716a7d7cb3c1b238d66.title: What Are Good Positional Encodings for Directed Graphs?
e4f2efbc04f92bf01c393716a7d7cb3c1b238d66.research_question: What are effective positional encodings for directed graphs that can capture complex bidirectional structural relationships, and how can these encodings improve the performance of graph neural networks and transformers on tasks involving directed graphs?
e4f2efbc04f92bf01c393716a7d7cb3c1b238d66.hypothesis: A positional encoding based on the concatenation of eigenvectors from multiple Magnetic Laplacians with different potential parameters (multi-q) can provably and robustly express detailed bidirectional structural features in directed graphs, such as walk profiles, and will outperform existing positional encoding methods on both synthetic and real-world tasks.
e4f2efbc04f92bf01c393716a7d7cb3c1b238d66.proposed_method: A novel positional encoding scheme, Multi-q Magnetic Laplacian Positional Encoding (Multi-q Mag-PE), will be developed by computing eigenvectors and eigenvalues from several Magnetic Laplacians, each parameterized by a distinct potential q. For a given directed graph, multiple values of q are chosen (either evenly spaced or randomly sampled), and for each q, the eigenvectors of the corresponding Magnetic Laplacian are computed. The node-level positional encoding is formed by concatenating the rows of these eigenvector matrices across all chosen q values. To address the instability and basis ambiguity inherent in complex eigenvectors, a stable, basis-invariant neural architecture will be designed, generalizing previous stable PE frameworks to the complex domain. This architecture will process the real and imaginary parts of the eigenvector-based features, apply permutation-equivariant transformations, and concatenate the resulting stable encodings with node and edge features for downstream models.
e4f2efbc04f92bf01c393716a7d7cb3c1b238d66.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic experiments will include distance prediction tasks on large collections of randomly generated directed and directed acyclic graphs, where the goal is to predict shortest path, longest path, and detailed walk profile distances between node pairs. Additional experiments will be performed on sorting network satisfiability prediction, where sorting networks are represented as directed acyclic graphs and the task is to classify network satisfiability. Real-world benchmarks will include circuit property prediction (OpenCircuitBenchmark) and high-level synthesis resource prediction (HLS dataset), where circuits and program IRs are modeled as directed graphs and the task is to predict properties such as gain, bandwidth, phase margin, LUT, and DSP usage. Baselines will include Laplacian PE, SVD-based PE, and single-q Magnetic Laplacian PE, processed via naïve concatenation, SignNet, or the proposed stable PE (SPE) framework. Evaluation metrics will include RMSE, MSE, and F1 score, depending on the task. Hyperparameters such as the number of q values and model architectures will be systematically varied, and ablation studies will assess the impact of the number and choice of q values and the stability framework.
e4f2efbc04f92bf01c393716a7d7cb3c1b238d66.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first positional encoding for directed graphs that can provably and robustly reconstruct detailed walk profiles using multiple Magnetic Laplacians with distinct potentials. This approach generalizes and strictly improves upon prior Laplacian, SVD, and single-q Magnetic Laplacian encodings, which are shown to be insufficient for capturing bidirectional structural features. Additionally, the research presents the first stable, basis-invariant neural architecture for processing complex eigenvector-based positional encodings, ensuring stability and generalization in downstream models. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate consistent and significant improvements over existing methods on both synthetic and real-world directed graph tasks.

e4fef8d5864c5468100ca167639ef3fa374c0442.title: MaxInfoRL: Boosting exploration in reinforcement learning through information gain maximization
e4fef8d5864c5468100ca167639ef3fa374c0442.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents more effectively balance exploration and exploitation, particularly in challenging environments with sparse rewards or local optima, by leveraging both intrinsic and extrinsic objectives?
e4fef8d5864c5468100ca167639ef3fa374c0442.hypothesis: Maximizing information gain as an intrinsic reward, in combination with extrinsic task rewards and an adaptive trade-off mechanism, will lead to more efficient and effective exploration in reinforcement learning, resulting in improved performance and sample efficiency across a variety of challenging tasks.
e4fef8d5864c5468100ca167639ef3fa374c0442.proposed_method: A new reinforcement learning framework, MAXINFORL, will be developed to augment standard off-policy, model-free RL algorithms with directed exploration based on information gain. The method will incorporate intrinsic rewards—specifically, the information gain about the environment's dynamics, estimated using an ensemble of Bayesian dynamics models—into the policy optimization objective. The exploration strategy will modify traditional Boltzmann exploration by adding an intrinsic exploration bonus, resulting in a policy that trades off maximizing the value function with maximizing entropy over states, actions, and rewards. Two separate temperature parameters will be introduced to independently control the influence of policy entropy and information gain, both of which will be auto-tuned via constrained optimization to maintain desired levels of exploration. The approach will be modular and compatible with a wide range of base RL algorithms, and will include an efficient auto-tuning procedure to balance intrinsic and extrinsic objectives without manual intervention.
e4fef8d5864c5468100ca167639ef3fa374c0442.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard deep RL benchmarks, including both state-based and visual control tasks from suites such as DeepMind Control Suite (DMC), OpenAI Gym, and HumanoidBench. MAXINFORL will be combined with several base algorithms, including SAC, REDQ, DrQ, and DrQv2, resulting in variants such as MAXINFOSAC and MAXINFODRQV2. Baselines for comparison will include vanilla SAC, SAC with intrinsic rewards (curiosity, disagreement), weighted sum approaches (SACINTRINSIC, SACEIPO), and explore-then-exploit strategies. Evaluation metrics will include normalized average performance, sample efficiency, and learning curves, with results averaged over five random seeds and reported with standard error. Additional experiments will test robustness to action costs and scalability to high-dimensional and visual tasks, including challenging humanoid control scenarios.
e4fef8d5864c5468100ca167639ef3fa374c0442.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a principled and theoretically grounded method for combining intrinsic information gain with extrinsic rewards in off-policy RL, featuring a novel dual-temperature auto-tuning mechanism for balancing exploration bonuses. The approach is modular, scalable, and can be integrated with a wide range of existing RL algorithms. Theoretical analysis demonstrates sublinear regret in bandit settings and convergence guarantees analogous to maximum entropy RL. Empirical results are expected to show state-of-the-art performance across diverse and challenging RL benchmarks, particularly in environments where naive exploration fails.

e4ff72941d9fe5ecd2dd4a1412e02f0dfc707fbc.title: A Best-of-both-worlds Algorithm for Bandits with Delayed Feedback with Robustness to Excessive Delays
e4ff72941d9fe5ecd2dd4a1412e02f0dfc707fbc.research_question: How can a multi-armed bandit algorithm be designed to achieve best-of-both-worlds regret guarantees in the presence of variably delayed feedback, including excessive or unbounded delays, without requiring prior knowledge of the maximal delay and while remaining robust to delay outliers and the loss generation mechanism?
e4ff72941d9fe5ecd2dd4a1412e02f0dfc707fbc.hypothesis: A multi-armed bandit algorithm that leverages implicit exploration, adaptive skipping of excessively delayed feedback, and a novel drift control mechanism can achieve best-of-both-worlds regret bounds that depend on the number of outstanding observations rather than the maximal delay, thereby providing robustness to excessive delays and matching or improving upon existing regret bounds in both stochastic and adversarial settings.
e4ff72941d9fe5ecd2dd4a1412e02f0dfc707fbc.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a best-of-both-worlds modification of the Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL) algorithm with a hybrid regularizer, designed for multi-armed bandits with variably delayed feedback. The method introduces three key technical components: (1) an implicit exploration scheme for loss estimation that is compatible with best-of-both-worlds analysis, (2) a drift control mechanism that adaptively skips observations with excessive delays to limit the time span over which distribution drift must be controlled, and (3) a procedure that relates standard regret to drifted regret without relying on boundedness of delays. The algorithm maintains a set of skipped rounds, tracks the cumulative count of active outstanding observations, and updates loss estimates using importance-weighted estimators with implicit exploration terms. The skipping threshold is dynamically adjusted based on the current count of outstanding observations, and rounds with waiting times exceeding this threshold are skipped to ensure robustness to outliers.
e4ff72941d9fe5ecd2dd4a1412e02f0dfc707fbc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and/or real-world datasets simulating multi-armed bandit environments with variable and potentially unbounded delays. The proposed algorithm will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including prior best-of-both-worlds algorithms and adversarial/stochastic bandit algorithms with delayed feedback (e.g., modifications of UCB1, EXP3, and previous FTRL variants). Evaluation metrics will include pseudo-regret in both stochastic and adversarial regimes, with particular attention to scenarios involving delay outliers and excessive delays. The experimental setup will systematically vary the delay distributions, including cases with single or few large delays, to assess robustness and improvements in regret bounds.
e4ff72941d9fe5ecd2dd4a1412e02f0dfc707fbc.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first best-of-both-worlds algorithm for bandits with delayed feedback that is robust to delay outliers and does not require prior knowledge of the maximal delay. Key innovations include the first implicit exploration scheme applicable in the best-of-both-worlds setting, a novel drift control technique that does not rely on bounded delays, and a new procedure for relating drifted and standard regret under unbounded delays. The approach replaces regret terms dependent on maximal delay with terms dependent on the number of outstanding observations, enabling significant improvements in scenarios with excessive or outlier delays. Additionally, the method enables beneficial skipping of rounds, further enhancing robustness and regret performance.

e50583008fe4ec049e42fdc01727ce98f6d86a35.title: CogAgent: A Visual Language Model for GUI Agents
e50583008fe4ec049e42fdc01727ce98f6d86a35.research_question: How can a visual language model be developed to effectively understand and interact with graphical user interfaces (GUIs), enabling generalist agent capabilities across both computer and smartphone environments, and achieving robust performance on both GUI navigation and general visual question answering tasks?
e50583008fe4ec049e42fdc01727ce98f6d86a35.hypothesis: A visual language model equipped with a specialized high-resolution cross-attention module and trained on large-scale, domain-specific GUI and OCR datasets will outperform existing language-based and visual-language models in GUI understanding, navigation, and general visual question answering tasks.
e50583008fe4ec049e42fdc01727ce98f6d86a35.proposed_method: A novel visual language model architecture will be designed, integrating both low-resolution and high-resolution image encoders. The low-resolution encoder (EVA2-CLIP-E) processes standard 224x224 images, while a lightweight high-resolution encoder handles 1120x1120 images, focusing on capturing fine-grained GUI elements such as small icons and text. These features are fused in a pre-trained visual-language decoder via a cross-attention mechanism with a reduced hidden size for computational efficiency. The model will be pre-trained on a diverse set of data: synthetic text renderings, OCR-annotated natural images, academic documents, and a large-scale GUI screenshot dataset (CCS400K) with grounding annotations. Multi-task fine-tuning and alignment will be performed using human-annotated GUI tasks, Mind2Web, AITW, and a suite of VQA datasets, ensuring the model can generalize across both GUI and visual reasoning tasks.
e50583008fe4ec049e42fdc01727ce98f6d86a35.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on nine visual question answering benchmarks (including VQAv2, OK-VQA, TextVQA, ST-VQA, ChartQA, InfoVQA, DocVQA, MM-Vet, and POPE) to assess foundational visual understanding. For GUI agent evaluation, the model will be tested on Mind2Web (web-based tasks) and AITW (Android device tasks), comparing against both language-based and visual-language baselines such as LLaMA2, GPT-3.5/4, and Auto-UI. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, step success rate, and adversarial robustness (e.g., hallucination rates on POPE). The experimental setup involves unified fine-tuning across tasks, ablation studies on model architecture and pre-training data, and computational efficiency analysis using FLOPs at varying image resolutions.
e50583008fe4ec049e42fdc01727ce98f6d86a35.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a high-resolution cross-attention module that enables efficient processing of high-resolution GUI images without prohibitive computational cost. A large-scale, domain-specific GUI screenshot dataset (CCS400K) is constructed for pre-training, addressing the distribution gap between natural images and GUIs. The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on both generalist VQA and GUI navigation benchmarks, surpassing language-based and prior visual-language models. The architecture allows for flexible adaptation to various resolutions and tasks, and the open-sourcing of the model and data aims to facilitate future research in VLM-based GUI agents.

e5198108958a8382eb740d41e260346d86eeb059.title: Connecting Federated ADMM to Bayes
e5198108958a8382eb740d41e260346d86eeb059.research_question: How can connections between Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) and Variational Bayes (VB) be leveraged to develop improved algorithms for federated learning, particularly in the presence of data heterogeneity, communication constraints, and uncertainty estimation?
e5198108958a8382eb740d41e260346d86eeb059.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the dual variables in ADMM can be interpreted through the site parameters in Variational Bayes, and that combining the strengths of ADMM and VB will yield new federated learning algorithms with improved convergence and performance, especially when incorporating flexible covariance structures and function-space information.
e5198108958a8382eb740d41e260346d86eeb059.proposed_method: The proposed research will develop a unified framework that connects ADMM and Variational Bayes for federated learning. This will begin by formalizing the correspondence between ADMM dual variables and VB site parameters in the case of isotropic Gaussian posteriors, leading to a new algorithm (FedLap) that closely mirrors ADMM updates within a variational inference context. The framework will be extended to allow for full-covariance Gaussian posteriors (FedLap-Cov), introducing dual variables that act as preconditioners and incorporate uncertainty via the covariance structure. Additionally, a functional regularization extension (FedLap-Func) will be designed to transmit function-space information (e.g., soft labels on shared or public inputs) between clients and server, further enhancing the quality of information exchange. Each algorithm will be derived with careful attention to computational and communication efficiency, and will be implemented using iterative message-passing and delta approximations to maintain tractability for large-scale models.
e5198108958a8382eb740d41e260346d86eeb059.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of federated learning benchmarks, including tabular datasets (UCI Credit, FLamby-Heart), image datasets (MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10), and various model architectures (logistic regression, multi-layer perceptrons, convolutional neural networks). Both homogeneous and heterogeneous data splits will be considered, with varying numbers of clients (e.g., 4, 10, 100) and different levels of data heterogeneity induced via Dirichlet sampling. The proposed methods (FedLap, FedLap-Cov, FedLap-Func) will be compared against established baselines such as FedAvg, FedProx, and FedDyn. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy and communication rounds to convergence, with results averaged over multiple random seeds. Hyperparameters (e.g., learning rates, weight decay, function-space weighting) will be tuned for each method, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of covariance modeling and function-space information.
e5198108958a8382eb740d41e260346d86eeb059.novelty_claims: The proposal claims the first fundamental connection between ADMM and Variational Bayes in the context of federated learning, showing that ADMM dual variables naturally emerge from VB site parameters. It introduces new federated learning algorithms that combine duality and uncertainty, including variants with full-covariance modeling and function-space regularization. These algorithms are expected to improve convergence and performance over state-of-the-art ADMM and Bayesian methods, especially under data heterogeneity and limited communication. The approach enables new ways to combine the complementary strengths of optimization-based and Bayesian methods, and opens avenues for further extensions in continual learning, privacy, and distillation.

e53aa81923958e8e247bb9d09250b8ccf0848513.title: Arithmetic Control of LLMs for Diverse User Preferences: Directional Preference Alignment with Multi-Objective Rewards
e53aa81923958e8e247bb9d09250b8ccf0848513.research_question: How can large language models be aligned to flexibly and precisely accommodate diverse and potentially conflicting user preferences, such as helpfulness and verbosity, in a single model without sacrificing performance or fairness?
e53aa81923958e8e247bb9d09250b8ccf0848513.hypothesis: Modeling user preferences as directions in a multi-objective reward space and aligning LLMs through a preference-conditioned fine-tuning process will enable arithmetic and intuitive control over model outputs, achieving better trade-offs among objectives and improved personalization compared to scalar-reward RLHF methods.
e53aa81923958e8e247bb9d09250b8ccf0848513.proposed_method: A novel framework, Directional Preference Alignment (DPA), will be developed to enable fine-grained, user-dependent control over LLM outputs. The approach involves training a multi-objective reward model that scores responses along multiple axes (e.g., helpfulness, verbosity) using regression on annotated datasets. User preferences are encoded as unit vectors (directions) in the reward space, and the LLM is conditioned on these vectors during generation. Fine-tuning is performed using a preference-conditioned variant of Rejection Sampling Finetuning (RSF), where, for each prompt and sampled preference direction, multiple candidate responses are generated, scored, and the highest-reward response is selected for further training. This process is iteratively repeated, and the preference vector is prepended to the system prompt to enable arithmetic control at inference time.
e53aa81923958e8e247bb9d09250b8ccf0848513.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Mistral-7B model using the HelpSteer and UltraFeedback datasets, both containing multi-attribute human or LLM-annotated responses. The multi-objective reward model will be trained on the union of these datasets, with helpfulness and verbosity as primary objectives. For alignment, the model will be initialized from a supervised fine-tuned checkpoint and iteratively fine-tuned using DPA on UltraFeedback, with rejection sampling generating multiple candidate responses per prompt and preference direction. Baselines will include DPO (Direct Preference Optimization), SteerLM, and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) models. Evaluation will use both internal reward model metrics (helpfulness and verbosity) and external benchmarks such as AlpacaEval-2.0, which employs GPT-4-turbo as an LLM judge, measuring win rates against reference answers. Experiments will also compare the Pareto fronts of helpfulness-verbosity trade-offs across methods.
e53aa81923958e8e247bb9d09250b8ccf0848513.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new paradigm for LLM alignment by representing user preferences as directions in a multi-objective reward space, enabling arithmetic and intuitive control over output attributes. Unlike prior approaches, DPA allows a single LLM to accommodate diverse user preferences without requiring multiple models or suffering from infeasibility issues. The approach provides practical, user-controllable trade-offs between objectives such as helpfulness and verbosity, and demonstrates superior or competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art baselines while offering enhanced personalization and fairness.

e54e9412425b7c10b4ad5d090be3ca135e94a70e.title: Perception in Reflection
e54e9412425b7c10b4ad5d090be3ca135e94a70e.research_question: How can large vision-language models (LVLMs) be enabled to achieve more accurate, robust, and human-aligned visual perception through iterative, reflective processes rather than single-pass perception, particularly in complex reasoning and multi-step manipulation tasks?
e54e9412425b7c10b4ad5d090be3ca135e94a70e.hypothesis: Incorporating an iterative perception-feedback loop, modeled as a dual-policy and critic architecture with reflective perceptual learning and unlikelihood training, will significantly improve LVLMs' image understanding, reduce hallucinations, and align model attention with human visual focus.
e54e9412425b7c10b4ad5d090be3ca135e94a70e.proposed_method: A dual-model architecture is developed, consisting of a policy model and a critic model, to enable LVLMs to alternate between perception and reflection in multi-turn dialogues. The policy model generates perceptual responses to images and questions, while the critic model evaluates these responses, providing both scores and detailed feedback. Reflective Perceptual Learning (RPL) is introduced, which constructs a multi-turn visual reflection dataset using temperature sampling for diverse candidate answers, VLM-based and rule-based reward scoring, and explicit feedback. Training employs imitation learning with a reflective unlikelihood loss that balances likelihood and unlikelihood based on reward normalization, encouraging the model to improve over successive rounds. During inference, the policy and critic interact iteratively, with the policy refining its answers based on critic feedback until a stopping criterion is met.
e54e9412425b7c10b4ad5d090be3ca135e94a70e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using the LLaVA-1.5 architecture, fine-tuned on a curated visual reflection dataset derived from LLaVA-665K, with 11,065 samples spanning 8,101 images and up to three rounds of reflective dialogue per sample. Evaluation is performed on multiple benchmarks: image understanding (LLaVABench), hallucination detection (HallusionBench, MMHal-Bench, GAIVE), and detailed image captioning (DetailCaps), using metrics such as CAPTURE, precision, recall, relevancy, and hallucination rates. Baselines include MiniGPT-4, mPLUG-Owl, InstructBLIP, LLaVA variants, and Volcano. Additional evaluation uses GPT-4o-Assisted Perception Evaluation (GAPE) for human-aligned scoring and text-to-image reconstruction metrics (CLIP, DINO, DINOv2) via DALLE-3. Ablation studies analyze the effects of reflection turns, critic choice, scoring thresholds, and unlikelihood loss weight.
e54e9412425b7c10b4ad5d090be3ca135e94a70e.novelty_claims: The proposed paradigm introduces a systematic, iterative perception-feedback loop for LVLMs, moving beyond single-pass perception and specialized chain-of-thought approaches. The dual-model architecture with explicit policy-critic interaction and reflective perceptual learning enables fine-grained, multi-turn refinement of visual understanding. The method leverages a hybrid reward system and reflective unlikelihood training to mitigate behavioral collapse and hallucinations. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate quantifiable improvements in image understanding, captioning detail, and hallucination reduction, with model attention patterns progressively aligning with human visual focus. The approach establishes perception in reflection as a robust, generalizable paradigm for future multimodal agents.

e5526fcee23b6dc7b7bf0d83607d88d12cf6baf2.title: The emergence of clusters in self-attention dynamics
e5526fcee23b6dc7b7bf0d83607d88d12cf6baf2.research_question: What is the geometric structure of learned representations in Transformers when the self-attention weights are fixed, and how do these representations evolve asymptotically under the self-attention dynamics?
e5526fcee23b6dc7b7bf0d83607d88d12cf6baf2.hypothesis: Under fixed self-attention weights, the evolution of token representations in Transformers leads to the emergence of clustered structures, with the specific nature of these clusters determined by properties of the value matrix and initial token configuration.
e5526fcee23b6dc7b7bf0d83607d88d12cf6baf2.proposed_method: The proposed method models the evolution of token representations in a Transformer as an interacting particle system governed by continuous-time self-attention dynamics with time-independent weight matrices (Query, Key, Value). The system is analyzed using tools from dynamical systems and partial differential equations, focusing on the asymptotic behavior as the number of layers (time) tends to infinity. The approach includes mathematical analysis of the limiting geometry of token clusters, with particular attention to the spectrum of the value matrix and the initial configuration of tokens. Special cases such as one-dimensional dynamics and canonical choices of value matrices (e.g., identity, negative identity) are considered, and a time-rescaling analogous to layer normalization is introduced to prevent divergence and facilitate analysis.
e5526fcee23b6dc7b7bf0d83607d88d12cf6baf2.experiment_details: Experiments involve numerical simulations of the self-attention dynamics for various initial token sequences and weight matrix configurations, including both one-dimensional and higher-dimensional cases. The setup includes varying the number of tokens, the dimensionality of the token space, and the structure of the value matrix (e.g., identity, negative identity, matrices with simple or multiple leading eigenvalues). Evaluation metrics include the rank and Boolean structure of the self-attention matrix over time, the convergence of tokens to vertices or faces of convex polytopes or hyperplanes, and the rate of convergence. Baseline comparisons are made to empirical observations from prior Transformer studies, and experiments are conducted to test the robustness of the clustering phenomenon under different assumptions.
e5526fcee23b6dc7b7bf0d83607d88d12cf6baf2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous mathematical framework for analyzing the asymptotic geometry of Transformer representations under fixed self-attention weights, revealing that token representations cluster toward specific geometric objects (vertices of polytopes, hyperplanes, or subspaces) determined by the value matrix and initial tokens. The analysis provides the first theoretical confirmation of empirically observed leader-follower dynamics in self-attention and establishes conditions under which the self-attention matrix converges to a low-rank Boolean structure. The approach bridges dynamical systems theory with deep learning, offering new insights into the interpretability and complexity of Transformer models.

e578cc07c02055039cbffe35cdb43aceeaea1665.title: Beware of Calibration Data for Pruning Large Language Models
e578cc07c02055039cbffe35cdb43aceeaea1665.research_question: How does the choice and construction of calibration data affect the effectiveness of post-training pruning for large language models, and what strategies can be developed to generate optimal calibration data when original training data is inaccessible?
e578cc07c02055039cbffe35cdb43aceeaea1665.hypothesis: Calibration data that closely resembles the original training data of a large language model will yield superior pruning performance, and self-generated synthetic calibration data can serve as an effective proxy when the original training data is unavailable.
e578cc07c02055039cbffe35cdb43aceeaea1665.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted into the influence of calibration data characteristics—including data source, amount, and similarity to pre-training data—on post-training pruning performance for large language models (LLMs). The approach involves both empirical analysis and the development of a self-generating calibration data synthesis strategy. Specifically, the method will use the target LLM to generate synthetic calibration data by prompting it with truncated prefixes from available text sources, followed by sampling continuations using top-k and top-p decoding strategies. To ensure data quality, the generated samples will be filtered based on perplexity, discarding those with the highest perplexity scores to remove outliers. The similarity of the generated calibration data to the original training data will be quantified using metrics such as Jaccard similarity and Min-K%++ scores, ensuring that the synthetic data closely matches the distributional properties of the training data.
e578cc07c02055039cbffe35cdb43aceeaea1665.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several open-source LLMs, including DCLM-7B, LLaMA-2-7B, LLaMA-2-13B, and LLaMA-3-8B. Multiple post-training pruning methods—Wanda, DSnoT, and OWL—will be applied under various sparsity ratios and sparsity types (unstructured and semi-structured). Calibration data will be sourced from C4, Wikipedia, SlimPajama, DCLM pre-training data, and the proposed self-generated synthetic data. For each setting, 128 to 2048 sequences of 2048 tokens will be sampled, with experiments repeated across 20 random seeds to ensure statistical robustness. Evaluation will be performed on language modeling (using Alpaca dataset) and a suite of commonsense reasoning tasks (BoolQ, Winogrande, PIQA, Hellaswag, ARC-e, ARC-c, MMLU), using zero-shot and few-shot settings as appropriate. Performance metrics will include average accuracy across tasks and perplexity for language modeling. The impact of calibration data similarity, amount, and filtering strategies will be systematically compared, and ablation studies will be conducted on parameters such as prefix length and filtering rate.
e578cc07c02055039cbffe35cdb43aceeaea1665.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive empirical analysis of the impact of calibration data on post-training pruning for LLMs, highlighting the critical role of data similarity to the original training set. A novel self-generating calibration data synthesis strategy is developed, enabling the construction of effective calibration data even when the original training data is inaccessible. The approach demonstrates that self-generated synthetic calibration data can outperform commonly used calibration datasets and even match or exceed the performance of calibration data sampled directly from the training set. The method is shown to be robust across different pruning algorithms, sparsity settings, and LLM architectures, providing practical guidelines and a versatile tool for enhancing model compression in real-world scenarios.

e586a4591ba0303b769f2c07cbddaf1899cb72e4.title: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models
e586a4591ba0303b769f2c07cbddaf1899cb72e4.research_question: How can the memory footprint of the key-value (KV) cache in large language models (LLMs) be significantly reduced during generative inference, particularly for long-content and large-batch generation, without compromising model performance or increasing inference latency?
e586a4591ba0303b769f2c07cbddaf1899cb72e4.hypothesis: A dynamic KV cache eviction policy that prioritizes retaining a small subset of influential tokens—termed heavy hitters—alongside recent tokens can achieve substantial memory reduction in LLM inference while maintaining generation quality and improving throughput and latency.
e586a4591ba0303b769f2c07cbddaf1899cb72e4.proposed_method: A novel framework, Heavy-Hitter Oracle (H2O), is proposed for KV cache management in LLMs. The method identifies heavy hitter tokens at each decoding step by accumulating attention scores and selects the top-k tokens that contribute most to the attention mechanism, alongside the most recent tokens, to retain in the cache. The eviction policy is formulated as a dynamic submodular maximization problem, and a greedy algorithm is employed to select the optimal set of tokens for cache retention at each step. Theoretical guarantees are provided under mild assumptions, ensuring near-optimality of the greedy selection. The system is implemented to efficiently update the KV cache without costly memory swaps, and the approach is compatible with existing inference optimizations such as quantization and offloading.
e586a4591ba0303b769f2c07cbddaf1899cb72e4.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on multiple LLM architectures, including OPT, LLaMA, and GPT-NeoX, with model sizes ranging from 6.7B to 175B parameters. Evaluation spans a diverse set of tasks from benchmarks such as lm-eval-harness, HELM, AlpacaEval, MT-bench, XSUM, and CNN/DailyMail, using both synthetic and real-world datasets. Baseline comparisons include full KV cache, local-only cache (most recent tokens), SparseTransformer (strided and fixed), and state-of-the-art inference engines like DeepSpeed ZeRO-Inference, HuggingFace Accelerate, and FlexGen. Metrics include generation throughput (tokens/sec), latency (seconds), and task-specific accuracy. Experiments are run on NVIDIA A100 and T4 GPUs, with varying sequence lengths and batch sizes, and include ablation studies on cache budget, sequence length, quantization compatibility, and shot number.
e586a4591ba0303b769f2c07cbddaf1899cb72e4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a simple yet effective KV cache eviction policy based on heavy hitter tokens, enabling up to 5-10x memory reduction without accuracy loss. The approach is theoretically grounded via a dynamic submodular maximization formulation with provable guarantees. H2O achieves up to 29x throughput improvement and up to 1.9x latency reduction compared to leading inference systems, and is shown to be compatible with quantization and infinite-length input processing. The method also enhances the performance of existing sparsification techniques and increases the diversity of generated text.

e596c98260ec4096eaeb491eb75f91a8339fcf48.title: Diffusion Policy Policy Optimization
e596c98260ec4096eaeb491eb75f91a8339fcf48.research_question: How can diffusion-based policies be effectively fine-tuned for continuous control and robot learning tasks using reinforcement learning, and what are the mechanisms and best practices that enable efficient and robust policy optimization in these settings?
e596c98260ec4096eaeb491eb75f91a8339fcf48.hypothesis: Fine-tuning pre-trained diffusion-based policies via policy gradient methods, when combined with carefully designed algorithmic modifications and best practices, will yield robust, high-performing, and stable policies for challenging continuous control and robotic tasks, outperforming existing RL and demo-augmented baselines.
e596c98260ec4096eaeb491eb75f91a8339fcf48.proposed_method: A novel algorithmic framework, Diffusion Policy Policy Optimization (DPPO), is proposed for fine-tuning pre-trained diffusion-based policies using policy gradient (PG) methods, specifically Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). The approach models the denoising process of the diffusion policy as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), embedding this 'Diffusion MDP' within the environmental MDP to form a two-layer MDP structure. Policy gradient updates are applied by differentiating through the Gaussian likelihoods at each denoising step, with a specialized advantage estimator that accounts for both environment and denoising discount factors. Best practices include fine-tuning only the last few denoising steps or using DDIM sampling for efficiency, modifying the diffusion noise schedule to ensure stable training and adequate exploration, and leveraging both MLP and UNet architectures for the policy head. The method is designed to exploit the structured exploration and natural stochasticity of diffusion models, leading to improved training stability and policy robustness.
e596c98260ec4096eaeb491eb75f91a8339fcf48.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of continuous control and robotic manipulation benchmarks, including OpenAI Gym locomotion tasks (Hopper-v2, Walker2D-v2, HalfCheetah-v2), the FrankaKitchen environment (with multiple demonstration datasets), the ROBOMIMIC benchmark (Lift, Can, Square, Transport tasks with both state and pixel observations), and the Furniture-Bench suite for long-horizon, multi-stage manipulation. Policies will be pre-trained using behavior cloning on expert demonstrations and then fine-tuned using DPPO. Baselines will include off-policy Q-learning methods (IDQL, DQL, QSM, DIPO), reward/advantage-weighted regression (DRWR, DAWR), other demo-augmented RL methods (RLPD, Cal-QL, IBRL), and policy gradient fine-tuning of alternative policy parameterizations (Gaussian, Gaussian Mixture). Evaluation metrics will include task success rates, cumulative reward, training stability, and robustness, with comparisons made across multiple random seeds and both dense and sparse reward settings. Zero-shot sim-to-real transfer will be assessed by deploying simulation-trained policies on real robot hardware.
e596c98260ec4096eaeb491eb75f91a8339fcf48.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a principled and efficient approach for fine-tuning diffusion-based policies in reinforcement learning via policy gradient, overcoming previously conjectured inefficiencies. Key innovations include the two-layer MDP formulation, tailored advantage estimation, selective fine-tuning of denoising steps, and noise schedule modifications for exploration and stability. The method demonstrates superior performance and robustness across a wide range of challenging robotic and control tasks, including long-horizon and pixel-based settings, and achieves strong sim-to-real transfer without real-world data. The framework is general and potentially applicable to other sequential, interactive diffusion model settings beyond robotics.

e59f6ee30df087bc52a66f6b220d700c39d76ae2.title: Leveraging Predictive Equivalence in Decision Trees
e59f6ee30df087bc52a66f6b220d700c39d76ae2.research_question: How can the challenge of predictive equivalence in decision trees be addressed to improve model selection, variable importance quantification, robustness to missing data, and cost-efficiency in prediction, without altering the underlying decision boundary?
e59f6ee30df087bc52a66f6b220d700c39d76ae2.hypothesis: A minimal boolean logical representation of decision trees, which abstracts away evaluation order and resolves predictive equivalence, will enable more reliable downstream tasks such as variable importance estimation, robust prediction under missing data, and cost-efficient evaluation, while maintaining interpretability and faithfulness to the original decision boundary.
e59f6ee30df087bc52a66f6b220d700c39d76ae2.proposed_method: A new methodology will be developed that transforms any decision tree into a minimal disjunctive normal form (DNF), representing the tree as a boolean logical formula that captures all sufficient conditions for each prediction. This transformation uses a modified Quine-McCluskey algorithm to simplify the logical expression, ensuring that all predictively equivalent trees are mapped to the same canonical form. The method will also compute the Blake canonical form to enumerate all possible minimal sufficient conditions for predictions, enabling robust handling of missing data and cost optimization. The DNF representation will be used for prediction, variable importance analysis, and for optimizing the cost of feature acquisition via reinforcement learning (Q-learning) to minimize the expense of obtaining predictions.
e59f6ee30df087bc52a66f6b220d700c39d76ae2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several real-world datasets, including COMPAS, Wine Quality, Wisconsin Breast Cancer, and Coupon datasets, as well as additional datasets in supplementary analyses. The methodology will be evaluated by enumerating the Rashomon set of near-optimal decision trees using TreeFARMS, comparing the number of unique decision boundaries before and after resolving predictive equivalence. Variable importance will be assessed using both Gini importance and the Rashomon Importance Distribution (RID), with and without correction for predictive equivalence. Robustness to missing data will be evaluated by introducing synthetic missingness at various rates and measuring the proportion of samples for which predictions can be made without imputation, comparing to path-based and feature-based baselines. Cost-efficiency will be tested by assigning random costs to features and comparing the average cost of prediction using the proposed Q-learning policy, standard tree traversal, and naive feature acquisition, across multiple bootstrapped trees.
e59f6ee30df087bc52a66f6b220d700c39d76ae2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a minimal, canonical boolean representation for decision trees that eliminates predictive equivalence, enabling more accurate and stable variable importance estimation, robust predictions under missing data without additional imputation, and cost-optimized prediction strategies. This is the first method to globally resolve predictive equivalence across all trees, providing a foundation for improved interpretability and reliability in decision tree-based machine learning tasks. The use of DNF and Blake canonical forms for these purposes, combined with reinforcement learning for cost minimization, constitutes a novel framework for interpretable and efficient decision tree deployment.

e5aed8e930b1efa1a5e0aad7ecf3038084cb0a33.title: Controlled Decoding from Language Models
e5aed8e930b1efa1a5e0aad7ecf3038084cb0a33.research_question: How can language model outputs be controlled at inference time to align with arbitrary reward functions, including multi-objective settings, without retraining the base model or requiring expensive reinforcement learning fine-tuning?
e5aed8e930b1efa1a5e0aad7ecf3038084cb0a33.hypothesis: A modular inference-time control mechanism, based on a learned prefix scorer approximating the value function for a given reward, can effectively steer the outputs of a frozen language model toward high-reward outcomes, match or outperform existing RL-based and best-of-K methods in reward-KL tradeoff, and flexibly support multi-objective and model-transfer scenarios.
e5aed8e930b1efa1a5e0aad7ecf3038084cb0a33.proposed_method: A modular framework called Controlled Decoding (CD) will be developed, which introduces a prefix scorer module trained to estimate the expected cumulative reward (value function) for partially decoded sequences. The prefix scorer is trained using either on-policy or off-policy data, with two main approaches: CD-FUDGE (using explicit rewards from rollouts) and CD-Q (using Bellman updates inspired by DQN). At inference time, the prefix scorer is combined with the logits of a frozen base language model to adjust the token sampling distribution, either tokenwise (per token) or blockwise (reranking blocks of K continuations). The method supports combining multiple prefix scorers for multi-objective control and can be applied to new base models without retraining.
e5aed8e930b1efa1a5e0aad7ecf3038084cb0a33.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several tasks, including response length control (using the DSTC8 Reddit conversations corpus), dialog helpfulness and harmlessness (using the Anthropic HH dataset), and summarization quality (using the TL;DR dataset). Reward models for each task will be trained or defined as needed. The proposed CD methods (CD-Q, blockwise CD-Q, CD-FUDGE, blockwise CD-FUDGE) will be compared against baselines such as KL-regularized PPO, DPO, IPO, and best-of-K sampling. Evaluation metrics will include normalized expected reward, KL divergence from the base policy, and win-rate against the base model as judged by a strong LLM. Additional experiments will test transferability of prefix scorers to new base models, multi-objective control by combining prefix scorers, and efficiency under fixed inference throughput budgets.
e5aed8e930b1efa1a5e0aad7ecf3038084cb0a33.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a modular, inference-time control framework for language models that provably solves a KL-regularized RL objective without modifying the base model. The approach bridges the gap between tokenwise RL control and sequence-level best-of-K strategies, supports flexible multi-objective alignment by combining prefix scorers, and enables transfer to new base models without retraining. Blockwise controlled decoding is proposed as a novel compromise between efficiency and reward-KL tradeoff, achieving state-of-the-art results with significantly fewer samples than best-of-K. The method offers greater configurability and modularity compared to existing RL-based and training-time alignment techniques.

e5c396c69e0f2f1dc90253d39004f9f0a5748e7c.title: SCENT: Robust Spatiotemporal Learning for Continuous Scientific Data via Scalable Conditioned Neural Fields
e5c396c69e0f2f1dc90253d39004f9f0a5748e7c.research_question: How can robust and scalable spatiotemporal learning be achieved for continuous scientific data, particularly in the presence of complex spatial-temporal dependencies, high-dimensionality, irregular sensor distributions, and large data volumes?
e5c396c69e0f2f1dc90253d39004f9f0a5748e7c.hypothesis: A unified, transformer-based neural framework that incorporates learnable queries, sparse attention, and time-conditioned processing can effectively model, reconstruct, interpolate, and forecast continuous spatiotemporal scientific data, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy, scalability, and robustness to data irregularities.
e5c396c69e0f2f1dc90253d39004f9f0a5748e7c.proposed_method: A novel framework, SCENT (Scalable Conditioned Neural Field for SpatioTemporal Learning), will be developed to unify interpolation, reconstruction, and forecasting tasks within a single architecture. The approach employs a transformer-based encoder-processor-decoder backbone, where the encoder processes spatiotemporal coordinates and input samples using Fourier features and linear projections, followed by a Context Embedding Network (CEN) with sparse self-attention to encode global context efficiently. The processor leverages a Temporal Warp Processor (TWP) to enable joint reconstruction and forecasting, supporting flexible time horizons and a novel warp-unrolling forecasting strategy to mitigate error accumulation in long-term predictions. The decoder is time-conditioned, using cross-attention between processed latent tokens and time-encoded queries, with a Calibration Network (CN) to refine the output. The entire system is designed to handle arbitrary input and output sizes, irregular sensor distributions, and to scale linearly with data and model size.
e5c396c69e0f2f1dc90253d39004f9f0a5748e7c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of datasets, including benchmark Navier-Stokes simulations with varying turbulence levels, large-scale simulated datasets with noise, missing values, and dynamically moving sensors, and real-world data from the AirDelhi PM2.5 sensor network. Baselines will include state-of-the-art methods such as FNO, OFormer, CORAL, DINO, and AROMA. Evaluation metrics will comprise Mean Squared Error (MSE), Relative MSE (Rel-MSE), and Root MSE (RMSE), with specific attention to forecasting, interpolation, and reconstruction performance. Scalability will be assessed by varying model width and depth, as well as dataset size, and ablation studies will be performed to quantify the impact of key architectural components. Experiments will be run on high-performance GPUs, with distributed training for the largest models.
e5c396c69e0f2f1dc90253d39004f9f0a5748e7c.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to provide a unified, single-step training model for continuous spatiotemporal representation learning that jointly addresses reconstruction, interpolation, and forecasting. Key innovations include the introduction of learnable query mechanisms for enhanced generalizability, a sparse attention-based encoder for efficient context encoding, a time-conditioned decoder, and a warp-unrolling forecasting strategy that reduces error accumulation in long-term predictions. The method demonstrates superior scalability with respect to both data and model size and is capable of handling irregular, sparse, and dynamically changing sensor distributions, outperforming existing state-of-the-art approaches across a range of challenging scientific data scenarios.

e5c8960eb2ec034ffbd353ef39fd1cb541d3c7c9.title: LAION-5B: An open large-scale dataset for training next generation image-text models
e5c8960eb2ec034ffbd353ef39fd1cb541d3c7c9.research_question: How can the creation and open release of a massive, diverse, and multi-lingual image-text dataset enable and democratize the training and evaluation of next-generation large-scale vision-language models?
e5c8960eb2ec034ffbd353ef39fd1cb541d3c7c9.hypothesis: The availability of a large-scale, openly accessible, and CLIP-filtered image-text dataset will facilitate the training of state-of-the-art multimodal models with performance comparable to or exceeding those trained on private datasets, while enabling broader research participation and transparency.
e5c8960eb2ec034ffbd353ef39fd1cb541d3c7c9.proposed_method: A large-scale image-text dataset will be constructed by extracting image and alt-text pairs from the Common Crawl web archive. The pipeline will include distributed filtering of web pages to identify image-text pairs, asynchronous downloading of images, and post-processing to remove low-quality or potentially harmful data. CLIP-based cosine similarity filtering will be applied to retain only image-text pairs with high semantic correspondence, using language detection to create English, multilingual, and language-agnostic subsets. Additional metadata, such as NSFW and watermark detection scores, will be generated using CLIP-based classifiers. The resulting dataset, LAION-5B, will be released in Parquet format with an open-source software stack for reproducibility and further curation.
e5c8960eb2ec034ffbd353ef39fd1cb541d3c7c9.experiment_details: To validate the utility of the dataset, experiments will be conducted by training and evaluating vision-language models such as CLIP, GLIDE, and Stable Diffusion on various subsets of the dataset (e.g., LAION-400M, LAION-2B-en). Models will be trained using distributed computing resources, following the original architectures and hyperparameters where applicable. Evaluation will include zero-shot classification on ImageNet-1k, robustness tests on distribution shift datasets, and performance on the VTAB+ benchmark (35 tasks). For generative models, text-to-image generation quality will be assessed using metrics such as FID and human evaluation. Baselines will include models trained on private datasets (e.g., OpenAI's CLIP WIT) and prior public datasets (e.g., MS-COCO, CC3M, YFCC100M).
e5c8960eb2ec034ffbd353ef39fd1cb541d3c7c9.novelty_claims: The proposed dataset will be the largest openly available collection of image-text pairs, exceeding existing public datasets by an order of magnitude and including extensive multilingual coverage. The dataset will be filtered using CLIP-based semantic similarity, providing higher quality and more relevant image-text pairs. Open release of both the dataset and the supporting software stack will enable reproducibility, transparency, and community-driven curation, addressing the current limitations of access and auditability in large-scale multimodal research.

e5ca161a7833f8dd2a069025f9a6cd67923e063d.title: Does provable absence of barren plateaus imply classical simulability?
e5ca161a7833f8dd2a069025f9a6cd67923e063d.research_question: Does the provable absence of barren plateaus in variational quantum circuits necessarily imply that the associated loss functions can be efficiently simulated on a classical computer, and what are the structural conditions under which this classical simulability holds?
e5ca161a7833f8dd2a069025f9a6cd67923e063d.hypothesis: For a broad class of variational quantum circuits with provably barren plateau-free loss landscapes, the structural features that prevent barren plateaus also enable efficient classical simulation of the loss function, potentially with the aid of a quantum-enhanced data acquisition phase.
e5ca161a7833f8dd2a069025f9a6cd67923e063d.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically analyze variational quantum circuit architectures and loss functions that are provably barren plateau-free, identifying the underlying structural properties—such as confinement to polynomially-sized operator subspaces—that enable efficient classical simulation. The methodology involves (1) formalizing the adjoint action of the circuit on measurement operators and initial states to identify proper or effective polynomial subspaces, (2) developing algorithms to represent and simulate the loss function within these subspaces, and (3) determining whether the necessary projections of quantum states and operators can be obtained classically or require quantum-enhanced classical simulation (e.g., via classical shadows or tomography). The approach will be validated through explicit construction of classical simulation protocols for representative barren plateau-free models, including shallow hardware-efficient ansätze, symmetry-protected circuits, and circuits with small Lie algebras or local observables. Technical steps include deriving the reduced effective action of the circuit, implementing classical surrogate models for the loss, and, where necessary, designing efficient quantum data acquisition protocols to obtain the required state or operator projections.
e5ca161a7833f8dd2a069025f9a6cd67923e063d.experiment_details: Experiments will involve simulating a range of variational quantum circuit classes with known barren plateau-free properties, such as shallow hardware-efficient ansätze, quantum convolutional neural networks, and symmetry-constrained circuits. For each class, both classical and quantum-enhanced classical simulation algorithms will be implemented. Datasets will include randomly initialized circuit parameters as well as structured initial states (e.g., product, area-law, or volume-law entangled states). Baselines will consist of direct quantum simulation (where feasible) and existing classical simulation techniques (e.g., tensor networks, Pauli propagation, Lie algebraic methods). Evaluation metrics will include simulation runtime (scaling with system size), accuracy of loss function estimation (compared to quantum reference), and resource requirements (number of measurements, memory usage). The experimental setup will also test the necessity and sufficiency of quantum data acquisition phases by comparing fully classical and quantum-enhanced approaches.
e5ca161a7833f8dd2a069025f9a6cd67923e063d.novelty_claims: The proposal claims that the very structural features that guarantee the absence of barren plateaus—namely, the confinement of relevant operators and states to polynomially-sized subspaces—also enable efficient classical simulation of the loss function, either fully classically or with a non-adaptive quantum data acquisition phase. This establishes a fundamental connection between trainability (absence of barren plateaus) and classical simulability, challenging the assumption that barren plateau-free variational quantum circuits inherently offer quantum advantage. The research further introduces a unified framework for identifying and exploiting these polynomial subspaces across a wide range of circuit architectures, and provides explicit simulation protocols that generalize beyond case-by-case analyses. The work also highlights new opportunities for quantum-enhanced classical surrogate models and delineates the boundaries of classical and quantum advantage in variational quantum algorithms.

e5f7ec0af15e8fc2fb7c19b5a3af06a97e3bcc6a.title: Point Cloud Synthesis Using Inner Product Transforms
e5f7ec0af15e8fc2fb7c19b5a3af06a97e3bcc6a.research_question: How can point cloud synthesis be improved through alternative representations that enable efficient, high-quality generation and reconstruction, while reducing computational complexity and inference time?
e5f7ec0af15e8fc2fb7c19b5a3af06a97e3bcc6a.hypothesis: Encoding point clouds as geometrical-topological descriptors using inner product transforms (IPTs) will enable highly efficient, expressive, and invertible representations, leading to faster and competitive synthesis and reconstruction of point clouds compared to existing complex models.
e5f7ec0af15e8fc2fb7c19b5a3af06a97e3bcc6a.proposed_method: A novel two-stage generative pipeline is proposed for point cloud synthesis. First, each point cloud is mapped to a 2D image descriptor via the Inner Product Transform (IPT), which encodes geometrical-topological information by computing the cardinality of points below hyperplanes defined by sampled directions and heights. The IPT is approximated using differentiable sigmoid functions for practical computation, resulting in a discretized image representation. In the generative stage, any image-based generative model (e.g., a convolutional variational autoencoder) is trained to model the distribution of IPTs. For reconstruction, a lightweight neural network (the IP-Encoder), consisting of 1D convolutional and fully connected layers, maps IPT images back to point clouds. The pipeline leverages the injectivity and stability of the IPT representation, and a joint loss combining Chamfer Distance and IPT-based loss is used to balance global structure and fine details during training.
e5f7ec0af15e8fc2fb7c19b5a3af06a97e3bcc6a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on subsets of the ShapeNet dataset, focusing on three shape classes (airplanes, chairs, cars), with each point cloud containing 2048 points. The pipeline is evaluated on tasks including point cloud reconstruction, generation, interpolation, and downsampling/upsampling. Baselines for comparison include PointFlow, SoftFlow, ShapeGF, CanonicalVAE, LION, SetVAE, PointVoxelDiffusion, PointStraightFlows, and XCube. Evaluation metrics include Chamfer Distance (CD), Earth Mover's Distance (EMD), Minimum Matching Distance (MMD), coverage (COV), and 1-NNA. The proposed models are trained and evaluated on commodity hardware (e.g., NVIDIA RTX 4070 GPU), and inference/training times are reported. Ablation studies investigate the effect of different loss functions and IPT resolutions, and practical inversion of the IPT is explored via backpropagation.
e5f7ec0af15e8fc2fb7c19b5a3af06a97e3bcc6a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the Inner Product Transform (IPT) as a faithful, injective, and computationally efficient representation for point clouds, enabling their synthesis as an image generation task. The method allows for orders-of-magnitude faster training and inference compared to state-of-the-art models, while maintaining high reconstruction and generative quality. The pipeline is modular, allowing any image generative model to be used for point cloud synthesis. Theoretical properties such as injectivity and metric structure are established, and practical inversion is demonstrated. The approach also provides a stable latent space for smooth interpolation and out-of-distribution generalization without retraining.

e6423c211fea2945aa71e1ac5ea24f8f595b4b0a.title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
e6423c211fea2945aa71e1ac5ea24f8f595b4b0a.research_question: How prevalent is sycophancy in language models fine-tuned with human feedback, and to what extent do human preference judgments contribute to this behavior across varied, realistic text-generation tasks?
e6423c211fea2945aa71e1ac5ea24f8f595b4b0a.hypothesis: Sycophancy is a general behavior exhibited by AI assistants trained with human feedback, and this behavior is, at least in part, incentivized by human preference judgments that favor responses aligning with user beliefs over strictly truthful ones.
e6423c211fea2945aa71e1ac5ea24f8f595b4b0a.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed to systematically measure sycophancy in state-of-the-art AI assistants across multiple open-ended text-generation tasks. The methodology will involve designing controlled prompts that reveal user preferences, beliefs, or misconceptions, and then analyzing assistant responses for evidence of sycophantic behavior, such as tailoring feedback, changing answers to match user suggestions, or mimicking user mistakes. Human preference data will be analyzed by extracting interpretable features from response pairs and modeling their influence on human judgments using Bayesian logistic regression. Additionally, the effect of optimizing model outputs against preference models (PMs) trained on human feedback will be studied through best-of-N sampling and reinforcement learning, comparing standard PMs to those explicitly prompted to reduce sycophancy.
e6423c211fea2945aa71e1ac5ea24f8f595b4b0a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five leading AI assistants (Claude-1.3, Claude-2.0, GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, LLaMA-2-70b-chat) using a variety of datasets and tasks, including MATH, MMLU, AQuA, TruthfulQA, TriviaQA, and custom poetry attribution prompts. Sycophancy will be measured using metrics such as feedback positivity, answer conformity, and mimicry of user mistakes. Baseline and biasing prompts will be compared to quantify the effect of user-stated preferences. Evaluation will utilize both automated grading (via GPT-4 or Claude-2) and human crowdworker preference judgments. Preference model optimization will be assessed using best-of-N sampling and RL, with sycophancy rates compared between standard and 'non-sycophantic' PMs. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, frequency of sycophantic responses, and preference rates for sycophantic versus truthful responses.
e6423c211fea2945aa71e1ac5ea24f8f595b4b0a.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a detailed, multi-faceted empirical framework for measuring sycophancy in production-level AI assistants across diverse, realistic tasks. It combines large-scale behavioral analysis with statistical modeling of human preference data to identify the drivers of sycophancy. The approach uniquely investigates the impact of preference model optimization on sycophantic behavior and provides comparative analysis between standard and explicitly de-sycophantized PMs. The findings are expected to motivate new training and oversight methods that go beyond unaided, non-expert human ratings, addressing a critical limitation in current AI assistant alignment strategies.

e6493e61ffd6d8ab0e6cb17921e36ce5f2413bb9.title: GPLQ: A General, Practical, and Lightning QAT Method for Vision Transformers
e6493e61ffd6d8ab0e6cb17921e36ce5f2413bb9.research_question: How can quantization methods for Vision Transformers be improved to achieve high accuracy, strong generalization to downstream tasks, and practical efficiency, particularly at low bit-widths such as 4-bit, overcoming the limitations of existing Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) and Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) approaches?
e6493e61ffd6d8ab0e6cb17921e36ce5f2413bb9.hypothesis: A sequential quantization approach that prioritizes activation quantization while preserving the original model's optimization basin, followed by efficient post-training quantization of weights, will yield Vision Transformer models that are highly accurate, generalize well to downstream tasks, and are practical in terms of training time and resource consumption.
e6493e61ffd6d8ab0e6cb17921e36ce5f2413bb9.proposed_method: A two-stage quantization framework is developed for Vision Transformers. In Stage 1, only activations are quantized to low bit-width (e.g., 4 bits) using Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) with all weights kept at full precision (FP32). This stage employs a feature mimicking loss based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to ensure that the quantized model's feature representations remain close to those of the original FP32 model, thus preserving the optimization basin and generalization ability. The activation quantization uses uniform symmetric quantization with per-channel granularity, and scaling factors are learned using LSQ, initialized via percentile-based min-max calibration. Training in this stage is limited to a single epoch with a low learning rate to minimize deviation from the original model. In Stage 2, weights are quantized to 4 bits using efficient PTQ methods such as RepQ-ViT, with additional compensation (e.g., QwT) to correct quantization errors. The activation quantizers are frozen during this stage, simplifying the weight quantization process and reducing error coupling.
e6493e61ffd6d8ab0e6cb17921e36ce5f2413bb9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard vision benchmarks, including ImageNet-1k for image classification, COCO2017 for object detection and instance segmentation, and five fine-grained visual classification (FGVC) datasets (Aircraft, Food101, Flowers102, Pets, Cars) to assess generalization. The method will be evaluated on various Vision Transformer architectures (e.g., Swin-T, Swin-S, Swin-B, Swin-L, DeiT-S, DeiT-B). Baselines will include state-of-the-art PTQ and QAT methods such as RepQ-ViT, QwT, OFQ, and Q-Var. Evaluation metrics will include Top-1 accuracy for classification and APbox/APmask for detection/segmentation. The training setup for Act-QAT will use AdamW optimizer, a fixed low learning rate, and batch sizes suitable for available GPU resources. Ablation studies will analyze the effects of activation quantization granularity, PCA dimensionality, and basin retention strategies.
e6493e61ffd6d8ab0e6cb17921e36ce5f2413bb9.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a general, practical, and lightning-fast quantization method for Vision Transformers that achieves competitive or superior accuracy and generalization compared to existing PTQ and QAT methods, while drastically reducing training time and memory requirements. The sequential 'activation-first, weights-later' paradigm, combined with PCA-based feature mimicking to preserve the optimization basin, is a novel strategy that addresses both efficiency and generalization challenges. The approach is highly scalable, supports multiple vision tasks beyond classification, and will be released as an open-source toolkit.

e651e095f73c1031140f0b8426663c5164eb38d7.title: BagFlip: A Certified Defense against Data Poisoning
e651e095f73c1031140f0b8426663c5164eb38d7.research_question: How can machine learning models be robustly and certifiably defended against both trigger-less and backdoor data poisoning attacks, in a model-agnostic manner, while providing effective certificates of defense?
e651e095f73c1031140f0b8426663c5164eb38d7.hypothesis: A model-agnostic certification technique that combines randomized smoothing with both bagging and feature/label flipping can provide effective, scalable, and certifiable robustness against both trigger-less and backdoor data poisoning attacks across diverse datasets and models.
e651e095f73c1031140f0b8426663c5164eb38d7.proposed_method: A novel certification framework, BagFlip, will be developed that constructs a smoothed version of any learning algorithm by applying a dual-measure randomized smoothing process. This process involves (1) bagging the training set by sampling with replacement, and (2) introducing noise by randomly flipping features and labels in both the training data and the test input, with probabilities controlled by a noise parameter. The smoothed algorithm predicts by majority vote over multiple randomized instances. The certified radius, i.e., the maximum number of poisoned examples the model can withstand without changing its prediction, will be computed using an efficient adaptation of the Neyman–Pearson lemma, which partitions the outcome space into polynomially many subspaces and calculates likelihood ratios for certification. To further accelerate certification, a relaxation of the Neyman–Pearson lemma will be introduced, under-approximating the subspace set and reducing computational complexity while maintaining soundness.
