e651e095f73c1031140f0b8426663c5164eb38d7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification datasets (MNIST, CIFAR10) and malware detection datasets (EMBER, Contagio). The evaluation will include both trigger-less and backdoor poisoning scenarios. Neural networks will be used for image datasets and random forests for malware datasets. Baselines for comparison will include Bagging, LabelFlip, FeatFlip, and RAB, with all models trained using the same architectures, hyperparameters, and data augmentations as the baselines for fair comparison. Certified accuracy will be measured as the percentage of test inputs that are both correctly classified and have a certified radius greater than or equal to a specified poisoning amount. Monte Carlo sampling and Clopper-Pearson intervals will be used to estimate probabilities, and Bonferroni correction will be applied for multiple test inputs. Preparation and inference times will be measured and compared to baseline methods.
e651e095f73c1031140f0b8426663c5164eb38d7.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first model-agnostic certified defense that is effective against both trigger-less and backdoor data poisoning attacks, providing practical and scalable certificates of robustness. The dual-measure randomized smoothing framework, which combines bagging and feature/label flipping, is novel and enables certification for a broader class of poisoning attacks. The efficient computation of certified radii via a partitioned Neyman–Pearson approach and its relaxation substantially improves scalability compared to prior certified defenses. BagFlip is claimed to outperform or match state-of-the-art certified defenses on trigger-less attacks and to significantly outperform them on backdoor attacks, particularly in terms of certified accuracy and computational feasibility.

e6544820751a4aef15bffd540dce3d3f0d33063c.title: Think While You Generate: Discrete Diffusion with Planned Denoising
e6544820751a4aef15bffd540dce3d3f0d33063c.research_question: How can the generative process for discrete data be improved by decomposing it into separate planning and denoising components, and what impact does this have on efficiency and sample quality in discrete diffusion models across language and image generation tasks?
e6544820751a4aef15bffd540dce3d3f0d33063c.hypothesis: Decomposing the discrete generative process into distinct planning and denoising stages, and employing an adaptive sampling algorithm guided by a planner, will improve generative sample quality, robustness, and efficiency compared to traditional denoiser-only discrete diffusion models.
e6544820751a4aef15bffd540dce3d3f0d33063c.proposed_method: A novel framework, Discrete Diffusion with Planned Denoising (DDPD), is developed, which separates the generation process into two neural models: a planner and a denoiser. At each inference step, the planner examines the current noisy sequence to estimate the probability that each position is corrupted and selects the next position to denoise, prioritizing the most corrupted tokens. The denoiser then predicts the clean value for the selected position, conditioned on the current sequence. The generative process is simulated using an adaptive Gillespie-based sampler, which determines the holding time until the next denoising move and adaptively adjusts the timestep based on the planner's assessment of noise levels. The process continues iteratively, with the planner enabling error correction by revisiting and refining previously denoised positions as needed. Training objectives for the planner and denoiser are derived from the evidence lower bound (ELBO) of the discrete diffusion process, allowing for independent and efficient training of both components.
e6544820751a4aef15bffd540dce3d3f0d33063c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard language modeling benchmarks such as text8 and OpenWebText, as well as on token-based image generation using ImageNet 256×256. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art discrete diffusion models (e.g., DFM, SEDD), autoregressive models (e.g., GPT-2), and mask diffusion methods such as MaskGIT. Evaluation metrics will include negative log-likelihood (NLL) and entropy (for language), generative perplexity (measured by large language models like GPT-J and GPT-2-L), and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for images. Experimental setups will control for model size, number of training steps, and sampling step budgets. Ablations will examine the effects of planner and denoiser imperfections, the use of single versus separate networks, and the impact of adaptive versus fixed-step sampling. Additional studies will assess convergence speed, error correction, and the robustness of the proposed self-correction mechanism.
e6544820751a4aef15bffd540dce3d3f0d33063c.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a theoretically grounded decomposition of discrete diffusion generation into planning and denoising, enabling adaptive, planner-guided sampling that prioritizes correction of the most corrupted positions. The method leverages a Gillespie-based sampler for efficient, non-uniform timestep selection and incorporates a self-correction mechanism for continuous refinement. The approach allows for separate, simplified training of planner and denoiser networks, and demonstrates significant improvements in generative quality and efficiency over denoiser-only baselines, even when using weaker or smaller denoisers. The framework is generalizable to both language and image generation, and provides a principled way to leverage pretrained mask diffusion denoisers within a uniform diffusion setting.

e659a4ee6c13c60e21f66326df9d998735a30b7d.title: On the Foundations of Shortcut Learning
e659a4ee6c13c60e21f66326df9d998735a30b7d.research_question: How do the properties of feature predictivity and feature availability interact to influence which features deep learning models rely on, and under what conditions do models exhibit shortcut learning by favoring more available but less predictive features?
e659a4ee6c13c60e21f66326df9d998735a30b7d.hypothesis: Deep nonlinear models exhibit a systematic bias toward more available features, even when those features are less predictive, and this shortcut bias is amplified by model nonlinearity and depth. Linear models do not exhibit this bias.
e659a4ee6c13c60e21f66326df9d998735a30b7d.proposed_method: A generative framework will be developed to synthesize classification datasets with two latent features, each independently parameterized for predictivity (the statistical association with the label) and availability (the ease with which a model can extract the feature). Availability will be manipulated via two factors: amplification (scaling/redundancy) and nesting (nonlinearity of the embedding). Synthetic data will be generated by mapping latent features to high-dimensional input vectors, with explicit control over their predictivity and availability. Models of varying architectures (linear, shallow/deep MLPs with ReLU/Tanh activations, and vision models like ResNet-18) will be trained on these datasets. Shortcut bias will be quantified as the deviation in feature reliance between the trained model and the Bayes-optimal classifier, using a metric based on alignment with latent feature decision boundaries. Theoretical analysis will be conducted using Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) theory to characterize the inevitability and conditions of shortcut bias in nonlinear networks.
e659a4ee6c13c60e21f66326df9d998735a30b7d.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training models on synthetic datasets with controlled feature predictivity and availability, using class-balanced splits (e.g., 3200 train, 1000 validation, 900 probe instances) and high-dimensional input spaces (e.g., d=100). Model architectures will include linear classifiers, MLPs with varying depth and width, and nonlinear activations (ReLU, Tanh), as well as ResNet-18 for image-based experiments. Evaluation will focus on measuring shortcut bias as a function of feature predictivity and availability, with systematic variation of amplification and nesting parameters. Additional experiments will use synthetic images where feature availability is manipulated via pixel footprint (object size), and naturalistic datasets (Waterbirds, CelebA) to assess the impact of availability manipulations (e.g., background size, color, spatial frequency) on real-world models. Baselines will include the Bayes-optimal classifier (LDA) and comparisons across model architectures. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy on congruent/incongruent probes and quantitative shortcut bias scores.
e659a4ee6c13c60e21f66326df9d998735a30b7d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a minimal, explicit generative framework that allows independent and systematic manipulation of feature predictivity and availability, enabling controlled studies of shortcut learning. It provides quantitative measures of shortcut bias and theoretical analysis via NTK, revealing that shortcut bias is a fundamental property of deep nonlinear architectures but not linear ones. The approach demonstrates that availability can override predictivity in determining feature reliance, and identifies specific image properties (e.g., pixel footprint, background extent) that drive shortcut bias in practical vision models. The framework supports systematic investigation of architectural and data manipulations that influence shortcut learning, advancing understanding of the foundations of shortcut learning in deep models.

e65b346d442e9962a4276dc1c1af2956d9d5f1eb.title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
e65b346d442e9962a4276dc1c1af2956d9d5f1eb.research_question: How can the instruction-following capabilities of large pretrained language models be improved using minimal human-annotated data, and how can the diversity and quality of instruction data be increased to enhance generalization to novel tasks?
e65b346d442e9962a4276dc1c1af2956d9d5f1eb.hypothesis: A semi-automated, iterative framework that bootstraps instruction data from a language model's own generations can produce diverse, high-quality instruction datasets that, when used for finetuning, significantly improve the instruction-following abilities of pretrained language models, approaching or matching the performance of models trained with extensive human-annotated data.
e65b346d442e9962a4276dc1c1af2956d9d5f1eb.proposed_method: A novel framework, SELF-INSTRUCT, will be developed to automatically generate large-scale instruction datasets using a pretrained language model. The process begins with a small seed set of human-written tasks, which are used to prompt the model to generate new task instructions. For each new instruction, the framework determines whether it is a classification or non-classification task, then generates input-output instances using either an input-first or output-first approach. Heuristics and similarity-based filtering are applied to remove low-quality, repetitive, or invalid instructions and instances. The resulting synthetic instruction dataset is then used to finetune the original language model using supervised learning, with various prompt templates to increase robustness to input format variations.
e65b346d442e9962a4276dc1c1af2956d9d5f1eb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by applying the SELF-INSTRUCT pipeline to a large pretrained language model (e.g., GPT-3 'davinci' engine). The generated dataset will consist of tens of thousands of instructions and corresponding input-output instances. Evaluation will be performed on standard instruction-following benchmarks such as SUPER-NATURALINSTRUCTIONS (SUPERNI), as well as a newly curated set of expert-written, user-oriented instructions covering diverse domains. Baselines will include vanilla pretrained models, publicly available instruction-tuned models (e.g., T0, Tk-INSTRUCT), and models finetuned on public instruction datasets (PROMPTSOURCE, SUPERNI). Evaluation metrics will include ROUGE-L for automatic assessment and human expert ratings for qualitative evaluation. Experimental setups will control for data size, data quality, and instruction diversity, and ablation studies will examine the effect of dataset size and quality on model performance.
e65b346d442e9962a4276dc1c1af2956d9d5f1eb.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces an almost annotation-free, semi-automated method for generating diverse and creative instruction datasets by leveraging a language model's own generative capabilities. It enables the expansion of instruction data beyond typical NLP tasks, reduces dependence on costly human annotation, and provides a scalable means to improve instruction-following in language models. The approach demonstrates that models finetuned on self-generated instruction data can achieve performance close to or surpassing models trained on large-scale human-annotated datasets, and the resulting synthetic dataset will be released to facilitate future research.

e66d55565f6cd6336f92be01b4efc7e6a1eb2381.title: Optimistic Active Exploration of Dynamical Systems
e66d55565f6cd6336f92be01b4efc7e6a1eb2381.research_question: How can an unknown dynamical system be actively explored such that the learned model globally approximates the system's dynamics and enables efficient zero-shot solution of multiple downstream tasks?
e66d55565f6cd6336f92be01b4efc7e6a1eb2381.hypothesis: Active exploration guided by epistemic uncertainty, combined with optimistic planning, will result in more efficient and comprehensive learning of system dynamics, leading to improved generalization and zero-shot performance on unseen tasks compared to existing heuristic or random exploration approaches.
e66d55565f6cd6336f92be01b4efc7e6a1eb2381.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, Optimistic Active eXploration (OPAX), will be developed for active exploration of nonlinear, continuous-state dynamical systems. OPAX will employ well-calibrated probabilistic models (such as Gaussian Processes or Bayesian Neural Networks) to estimate both the mean and epistemic uncertainty of the system dynamics. At each episode, the method will formulate an optimal control problem that seeks exploration policies maximizing the expected information gain, operationalized as the reduction in epistemic uncertainty along planned trajectories. An optimistic planner will be used, which augments the dynamics model with an uncertainty-driven exploration term, effectively 'hallucinating' transitions that maximize information gain. The resulting policy will be deployed to collect new data, iteratively refining the model and reducing uncertainty across the reachable state-action space.
e66d55565f6cd6336f92be01b4efc7e6a1eb2381.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of simulated environments, including Pendulum-v1 and MountainCar from OpenAI Gym, Reacher, Swimmer, and Cheetah from the DeepMind Control Suite, and a high-dimensional (58D) robotic manipulation task (Fetch Pick & Place Construction). The proposed method will be compared against several baselines: random exploration, mean-based active exploration (MEAN-AE), trajectory sampling (PETS-AE), and a single-task model-based RL algorithm (H-UCRL), as well as CEE-US for high-dimensional tasks. Both Gaussian Processes and probabilistic ensembles will be used as dynamics models. Evaluation metrics will include reduction in maximum epistemic uncertainty, zero-shot performance on a variety of downstream control tasks, and success rates in complex manipulation scenarios. Experiments will be run with multiple random seeds, and both model-based planning (MPC with iCEM) and policy optimization (SAC) will be employed for downstream evaluation.
e66d55565f6cd6336f92be01b4efc7e6a1eb2381.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a theoretically grounded framework for active exploration in reinforcement learning, leveraging epistemic uncertainty as an intrinsic reward and employing an optimistic planner to maximize information gain. The method provides the first convergence and sample complexity guarantees for active exploration in a rich class of nonlinear dynamical systems, including those modeled with Gaussian Processes in RKHS. The approach is designed to be cost-agnostic and supports zero-shot planning for novel downstream tasks. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that the method achieves faster uncertainty reduction and superior generalization compared to existing baselines, including in high-dimensional and challenging environments.

e688203abeab59163578c8b4ff4bfd762ed72d03.title: COMET Flows: Towards Generative Modeling of Multivariate Extremes and Tail Dependence
e688203abeab59163578c8b4ff4bfd762ed72d03.research_question: How can generative models be developed to accurately represent multivariate extremes, particularly those characterized by heavy-tailed marginal distributions and asymmetric tail dependence, in real-world data?
e688203abeab59163578c8b4ff4bfd762ed72d03.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a generative modeling framework that explicitly decouples marginal distribution modeling from joint dependence structure—leveraging Extreme Value Theory for marginals and copula-based approaches for dependence—will more effectively capture heavy-tailedness and tail dependence in multivariate extremes than standard normalizing flows.
e688203abeab59163578c8b4ff4bfd762ed72d03.proposed_method: A novel generative modeling architecture, termed COMET (COpula Multivariate ExTreme) Flows, will be developed. The method decomposes the modeling of a joint distribution into two components: (1) a marginal transform that maps each marginal distribution to a uniform distribution using a semi-parametric mixture of a kernel density estimator for the central region and a generalized Pareto (GP) distribution for the tails, as motivated by Extreme Value Theory; and (2) a copula transform that models the dependence structure among the uniform marginals using a coupling layer-based normalizing flow (e.g., RealNVP), with a logit transform to ensure outputs remain in the unit hypercube. Tail dependence is addressed by conditioning the copula flow on noise levels during training, enabling the model to learn manifold structures induced by extreme co-occurrences. The marginal and copula components are composed to yield an invertible, tractable normalizing flow for both density estimation and sampling.
e688203abeab59163578c8b4ff4bfd762ed72d03.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets specifically designed to exhibit heavy tails and asymmetric tail dependence, as well as on real-world climate datasets (e.g., CLIMDEX indices) and standard benchmark datasets (POWER, GAS). Baseline models will include RealNVP, SoftFlow, Tail Adaptive Flows (TAF), and Copula Marginal Flows (CMF), with modifications as needed for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include average negative log-likelihood (NLL) on held-out test sets, as well as qualitative assessments of generated samples for capturing tail behavior and manifold structures. Hyperparameters such as tail quantile thresholds and GP parameters will be selected via validation, and models will be trained until validation loss ceases to improve.
e688203abeab59163578c8b4ff4bfd762ed72d03.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled decomposition of multivariate extreme modeling into marginal and copula components, with a semi-parametric tail modeling strategy for marginals and a noise-conditioned copula flow for capturing tail dependence as local manifold structures. This is the first framework to explicitly link manifold learning, normalizing flows, and tail dependencies in multivariate extremes. The method enables tractable, invertible transformations for both density estimation and sampling, and is empirically demonstrated to outperform existing state-of-the-art baselines in capturing both heavy-tailed marginals and asymmetric tail dependence.

e68ff850074c4891b08777bed900f3e923961ad0.title: Non-Vacuous Generalization Bounds for Large Language Models
e68ff850074c4891b08777bed900f3e923961ad0.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs) be mathematically guaranteed to generalize beyond their training data, and how can non-vacuous generalization bounds be constructed for LLMs with billions of parameters trained on next-token prediction tasks?
e68ff850074c4891b08777bed900f3e923961ad0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by developing new compression-based parameterizations and generalization bound techniques, it is possible to obtain non-vacuous generalization guarantees for large language models, even when trained with unbounded log-likelihood objectives and on massive datasets.
e68ff850074c4891b08777bed900f3e923961ad0.proposed_method: A novel methodology will be developed that constructs non-vacuous generalization bounds for large language models by leveraging a new nonlinear compression parameterization called SubLoRA. SubLoRA combines low-rank adaptation (LoRA) with subspace training to enable smooth and efficient compression of LLMs, allowing the model to maintain expressivity while significantly reducing the number of bits needed to specify its parameters. The approach will derive new PAC-Bayes-inspired bounds that are valid for the unbounded negative log-likelihood (bits-per-dimension) loss, using a prediction smoothing technique to control the worst-case behavior of the loss. Additionally, the methodology will include a subsampling-based extension, enabling the computation of generalization bounds using only a small subset of the training data, thus making the approach scalable to extremely large datasets.
e68ff850074c4891b08777bed900f3e923961ad0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by pretraining variants of the GPT-2 architecture (ranging from 124M to 849M parameters) on the OpenWebText dataset, which contains over 9 billion tokens. The proposed SubLoRA compression technique will be compared against LoRA-only and subspace-only baselines, as well as the original uncompressed model. Evaluation metrics will include bits-per-dimension (BPD), Top-1 error, and Top-100 error, with generalization bounds computed for each metric. The empirical risk will be estimated using a subsample of 10,000 documents from the training set, and arithmetic coding will be used to measure the compressed size of the models. The experiments will also investigate the impact of model size and data structure (e.g., permuted vs. regular text) on the tightness of the generalization bounds.
e68ff850074c4891b08777bed900f3e923961ad0.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first non-vacuous generalization bounds for large language models trained on next-token prediction, applicable to models with nearly a billion parameters. It develops a new nonlinear compression parameterization (SubLoRA) that enables tighter and scalable bounds compared to existing linear or low-rank approaches. The methodology extends PAC-Bayes theory to handle unbounded log-likelihood losses via prediction smoothing and provides a practical subsampling-based bound computation that accelerates evaluation by orders of magnitude. The research also empirically demonstrates that larger LLMs are more compressible and achieve better generalization bounds, challenging conventional expectations about model capacity and overfitting.

e6911819976aff6e2692d25e3b9b96872b004858.title: Spurious Correlations in High Dimensional Regression: The Roles of Regularization, Simplicity Bias and Over-Parameterization
e6911819976aff6e2692d25e3b9b96872b004858.research_question: How do regularization, simplicity bias, and over-parameterization influence the learning of spurious correlations in high-dimensional regression models, particularly when data contains both predictive core features and non-predictive spurious features?
e6911819976aff6e2692d25e3b9b96872b004858.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the strength of regularization, the simplicity of spurious features, and the degree of over-parameterization each play distinct and quantifiable roles in the extent to which regression models learn spurious correlations, and that there exists a trade-off between minimizing test loss and increasing reliance on spurious correlations.
e6911819976aff6e2692d25e3b9b96872b004858.proposed_method: A rigorous statistical framework will be developed to characterize the learning of spurious correlations in high-dimensional regression settings. The approach will model input data as comprising a core (predictive) feature and a spurious (non-predictive) feature, with the label dependent solely on the core feature. Linear regression with ridge (ℓ2) regularization will be analyzed, deriving explicit, non-asymptotic expressions for the spurious correlation as a function of data covariance and regularization strength. The simplicity of spurious features will be quantified via the spectrum of their covariance matrix, and their correlation with core features will be measured using the Schur complement of the full data covariance. Theoretical analysis will also extend to over-parameterized random features models, establishing their equivalence to regularized linear regression in terms of spurious correlation learning. Theoretical results will be supported by numerical experiments.
e6911819976aff6e2692d25e3b9b96872b004858.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic Gaussian data, as well as on real-world datasets such as Color-MNIST and CIFAR-10, where the core and spurious features can be explicitly controlled or identified (e.g., object vs. background in images, or digit vs. color in Color-MNIST). The experimental setup will involve training linear regression and random features models under varying regularization strengths and measuring both the in-distribution test loss and the degree of spurious correlation (as defined by the covariance between model output and label when core and spurious features are sampled independently). Baselines will include unregularized regression and models with varying levels of feature whitening to manipulate the simplicity of spurious features. Evaluation metrics will include test loss, spurious correlation magnitude, and the spectral properties of feature covariances. Key details such as sample size, feature dimensionality, and whitening procedures will be systematically varied to validate theoretical predictions.
e6911819976aff6e2692d25e3b9b96872b004858.novelty_claims: The proposed research offers a precise, non-asymptotic statistical characterization of spurious correlation learning in high-dimensional regression, explicitly linking regularization strength, feature simplicity, and over-parameterization to the extent of spurious correlation. The analysis introduces the use of the Schur complement and spectral properties of feature covariances to quantify simplicity bias and feature dependence. A novel trade-off is established between test loss minimization and spurious correlation increase, with theoretical bounds and empirical validation. Additionally, the equivalence between over-parameterized random features models and regularized linear regression is extended to the level of predictor behavior with respect to spurious correlations, rather than just training/test error.

e69a7c7028c9023aba468fb4c16d2cc62641cc1a.title: Split Conformal Prediction and Non-Exchangeable Data
e69a7c7028c9023aba468fb4c16d2cc62641cc1a.research_question: Can split conformal prediction methods provide valid uncertainty quantification and coverage guarantees for non-exchangeable data, such as time series, spatiotemporal, and dependent processes, without requiring new algorithmic modifications?
e69a7c7028c9023aba468fb4c16d2cc62641cc1a.hypothesis: Split conformal prediction retains valid marginal, empirical, and conditional coverage guarantees for a broad class of non-exchangeable data processes, with only a small additional coverage penalty determined by the dependence structure, and remains competitive with or superior to recent specialized conformal algorithms in terms of coverage, interval size, and computational efficiency.
e69a7c7028c9023aba468fb4c16d2cc62641cc1a.proposed_method: A novel theoretical framework will be developed to analyze split conformal prediction (CP) under non-exchangeable data by leveraging concentration inequalities and decoupling properties of the data-generating process. The approach will formalize conditions under which marginal, empirical, and conditional coverage guarantees can be extended to dependent data, such as stationary β-mixing processes, by introducing explicit error terms that account for the degree of dependence. The method will not require any algorithmic changes to the standard split CP procedure; instead, the theoretical analysis will yield finite-sample coverage bounds with an additional penalty term. Extensions to non-split CP methods and non-stationary data will also be considered by adapting the concentration and decoupling framework accordingly.
e69a7c7028c9023aba468fb4c16d2cc62641cc1a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both real and synthetic datasets. Real-world spatiotemporal climate data will be used to compare split CP's coverage and interval size against recent conformal algorithms specifically designed for non-exchangeable data. Synthetic datasets will be generated from stationary β-mixing processes, such as AR(1) time series and hidden Markov models, to benchmark empirical coverage and interval width. Additional experiments will include financial time series data to evaluate robustness under clear violations of exchangeability. Baselines will include recent conformal algorithms for non-exchangeable data (e.g., those by Barber et al., Gibbs and Candès, Xu and Xie), with evaluation metrics focusing on marginal and empirical coverage, interval size, and computational efficiency. Experimental setups will ensure fair comparison by using identical nonconformity scores (e.g., absolute residuals) and consistent calibration/test splits.
e69a7c7028c9023aba468fb4c16d2cc62641cc1a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework extends split conformal prediction's coverage guarantees to a broad class of dependent, non-exchangeable data processes without requiring any modifications to the algorithm or additional hyperparameters. The approach is based on new mathematical tools—concentration inequalities and decoupling arguments—that are not reliant on exchangeability. Explicit, finite-sample error bounds are provided for stationary β-mixing processes, and the method is shown to be computationally simple and orders of magnitude faster than recent alternatives. The framework also generalizes to non-split CP methods and non-stationary data, offering a unified and robust approach to uncertainty quantification in practical, real-world settings.

e69e44cb82d6e8595a20aa86923c4de9ff45096f.title: A Formal Framework for Understanding Length Generalization in Transformers
e69e44cb82d6e8595a20aa86923c4de9ff45096f.research_question: What are the theoretical principles that govern the ability of transformers to generalize to input sequences longer than those seen during training, particularly when using absolute positional encodings?
e69e44cb82d6e8595a20aa86923c4de9ff45096f.hypothesis: Length generalization in transformers can be rigorously characterized and predicted by whether the target function is expressible within a formal class of 'Limit Transformers' that satisfy specific constraints on the use of positional information, such as periodicity and locality.
e69e44cb82d6e8595a20aa86923c4de9ff45096f.proposed_method: A formal framework will be developed to analyze length generalization in causal transformers equipped with learnable absolute positional encodings (APE) or no positional encodings (NoPE). The methodology introduces the concept of 'Limit Transformers,' mathematical constructs that encapsulate the limiting behavior of a sequence of transformers as input length grows, while maintaining bounded width and precision. The inference procedure involves fitting a sequence of transformers to reproduce a target function on increasingly longer inputs, while minimizing a norm-based regularizer that penalizes model complexity and non-local attention. The expressivity of Limit Transformers will be characterized, and connections to a formal programming language (C-RASP) will be established to provide lower and upper bounds on the class of functions for which length generalization is possible. Communication complexity arguments will be used to identify functions that cannot be length-generalized by such transformers.
e69e44cb82d6e8595a20aa86923c4de9ff45096f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of algorithmic and formal language tasks, including benchmarks from prior work. Transformers with APE and NoPE will be trained on input sequences of lengths up to 50 and tested on much longer sequences (up to length 150), with random offsets to mimic real-world context placement. Evaluation will use accuracy as the metric, defined as the fraction of test sequences where predictions are correct at every step. Baselines will include random performance and existing empirical findings. Hyperparameters will be tuned to ensure strong performance on training and moderate test lengths, and results will be analyzed to assess whether empirical length generalization aligns with theoretical predictions based on C-RASP expressiveness and Limit Transformer representability.
e69e44cb82d6e8595a20aa86923c4de9ff45096f.novelty_claims: The proposed framework provides the first rigorous theoretical characterization of length generalization in transformers with absolute positional encodings, linking generalization guarantees to expressibility in a new class of Limit Transformers. The approach formalizes and extends the RASP-L Conjecture, offering both upper and lower bounds on generalization capabilities. The framework introduces a novel inference procedure and regularizer that capture implicit biases in standard training, and demonstrates predictive power across a wide range of tasks. The use of communication complexity to establish non-expressibility is also a new contribution, enabling the identification of tasks where length generalization is provably impossible for standard transformer architectures.

e69f8eb68686c451fe87cfbc0c40438201a68c21.title: RepoGraph: Enhancing AI Software Engineering with Repository-level Code Graph
e69f8eb68686c451fe87cfbc0c40438201a68c21.research_question: How can repository-level code structure and dependencies be effectively leveraged to enhance AI-driven software engineering tasks, particularly in complex, real-world codebases that require holistic understanding and navigation beyond function- or file-level approaches?
e69f8eb68686c451fe87cfbc0c40438201a68c21.hypothesis: Incorporating a fine-grained, repository-level code graph that encodes line-level dependencies and relationships will significantly improve the ability of large language models to localize, edit, and resolve issues in complex software repositories, outperforming existing file- or function-level context retrieval methods.
e69f8eb68686c451fe87cfbc0c40438201a68c21.proposed_method: A plug-in module, REPOGRAPH, will be developed to construct a repository-level code graph where each node represents a line of code and edges capture definition and reference dependencies. The construction process involves parsing the repository using an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) parser (e.g., tree-sitter) to identify relevant code elements, filtering out project-independent relations (such as standard library or third-party calls), and organizing the remaining code lines into a graph structure with meta-information. For downstream tasks, subgraph retrieval algorithms will be employed to extract k-hop ego-graphs centered on task-relevant keywords (e.g., functions or classes mentioned in an issue), providing targeted, context-rich subgraphs. These ego-graphs will be integrated into both procedural and agent-based LLM frameworks, either by flattening the subgraph into prompts or by introducing a new agent action for dynamic retrieval. Variants involving different hop distances and summarization strategies will be explored to balance context richness and token efficiency.
e69f8eb68686c451fe87cfbc0c40438201a68c21.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by integrating REPOGRAPH as a plug-in with four representative baseline frameworks (two procedural: RAG and Agentless; two agent-based: SWE-agent and AutoCodeRover) on the SWE-bench-Lite benchmark, which requires repository-level code modifications to resolve real-world GitHub issues. The same GPT-4 and GPT-4o LLMs as in the baselines will be used to ensure fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include resolve rate (percentage of issues fully fixed), patch application rate, average inference cost, and token usage. Additional analyses will measure localization accuracy at file, function, and line levels, and investigate the impact of different subgraph retrieval and integration strategies. Transferability will be tested on CrossCodeEval, a multilingual code completion benchmark emphasizing cross-file dependencies, using both GPT-4o and Deepseek-Coder as backbone models, with metrics such as exact match and identifier match (EM, ES, F1). All experiments will be performed in a containerized environment for reproducibility.
e69f8eb68686c451fe87cfbc0c40438201a68c21.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a repository-level, line-granular code graph that captures fine-grained dependencies across an entire codebase, surpassing prior methods limited to file- or function-level context. REPOGRAPH enables precise and contextually informed code localization and editing by leveraging subgraph retrieval, and is designed to be flexibly integrated into both procedural and agent-based LLM frameworks. The method demonstrates substantial improvements in issue resolution and localization accuracy on real-world benchmarks, achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source frameworks, and exhibits strong transferability to other repository-level coding tasks. The approach also provides a systematic analysis of subgraph retrieval and integration strategies, highlighting the trade-offs between context richness and efficiency.

e6a54f56883e009f09259d98010981d8cf0b80f3.title: Offline Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Implicit Global-to-Local Value Regularization
e6a54f56883e009f09259d98010981d8cf0b80f3.research_question: How can offline multi-agent reinforcement learning be improved to address the challenges posed by large joint state-action spaces, distributional shift, and the need for coordinated agent behavior, without relying on explicit knowledge of the behavior policy or out-of-distribution actions?
e6a54f56883e009f09259d98010981d8cf0b80f3.hypothesis: Introducing an implicit global-to-local value regularization framework, which rigorously derives local regularizations from global constraints under value decomposition, will enable more effective and stable offline multi-agent reinforcement learning by capturing global information and credit assignment, leading to improved joint policy optimality and performance.
e6a54f56883e009f09259d98010981d8cf0b80f3.proposed_method: A novel offline multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm, OMIGA, is proposed, which starts by imposing a global-level value regularization using a reverse KL divergence between the learned policy and the unknown behavior policy. Through theoretical analysis, this global regularization is shown to be decomposable into a set of implicit local value regularizations under a value decomposition scheme, provided the behavior policy is factorizable. The method leverages self-normalization constraints and convex optimization to learn local state-value functions, local action-value functions, and local policies, all in an in-sample manner using only offline data. The approach avoids explicit estimation of the behavior policy and does not require querying out-of-distribution actions, thus enhancing stability and scalability. The learning process involves three main supervised steps: (1) learning local state-value functions via a regularized objective, (2) jointly optimizing local Q-functions and value decomposition weights, and (3) learning local policies by minimizing the KL divergence to the derived optimal local policies, all while incorporating global information through the decomposition weights.
e6a54f56883e009f09259d98010981d8cf0b80f3.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two prominent offline multi-agent RL benchmarks: multi-agent MuJoCo (for continuous control tasks) and the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge (SMAC) for cooperative discrete-action tasks. Offline datasets are collected from strong online policies (e.g., HAPPO for MuJoCo, MAPPO for SMAC) and include various quality levels (good, medium, poor, and mixed). The proposed method is compared against four recent offline MARL baselines: BCQ-MA, CQL-MA, ICQ, and OMAR, all of which use value decomposition structures. Evaluation metrics include average episodic returns, measured over 32 independent episodes and 5 random seeds per task. Ablation studies are performed to analyze the impact of the global-to-local regularization, the regularization hyperparameter, and the incorporation of global information in local policy learning.
e6a54f56883e009f09259d98010981d8cf0b80f3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled and theoretically justified global-to-local value regularization framework for offline multi-agent RL, which bridges global regularization and local value decomposition in a way that captures both global information and multi-agent credit assignment. Unlike prior methods, the regularization is derived implicitly and does not require explicit knowledge or estimation of the behavior policy, nor does it rely on out-of-distribution actions. The method guarantees that learned local policies are jointly optimal at the global level and enables fully in-sample, stable learning. Empirical results demonstrate superior performance and convergence speed compared to state-of-the-art baselines across a wide range of challenging offline multi-agent tasks.

e6d36f474eed202bbc438f237f78f4d88686ced7.title: On the Diversity and Realism of Distilled Dataset: An Efficient Dataset Distillation Paradigm
e6d36f474eed202bbc438f237f78f4d88686ced7.research_question: How can dataset distillation be made more efficient, while simultaneously preserving both the diversity and realism of the distilled data, especially for large-scale and high-resolution datasets?
e6d36f474eed202bbc438f237f78f4d88686ced7.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a non-optimization-based, patch selection and recombination paradigm can achieve high efficiency, realism, and diversity in dataset distillation, outperforming existing optimization-based methods in both speed and generalization.
e6d36f474eed202bbc438f237f78f4d88686ced7.proposed_method: A novel two-stage, optimization-free dataset distillation paradigm is proposed, termed RDED (Realistic, Diverse, and Efficient Dataset Distillation). In the first stage, each image from the original dataset is cropped into patches, and a pre-trained observer model scores these patches for realism. The top-scoring patches are selected as 'key patches' for each class, and further pruned using a random uniform sampling strategy to maintain diversity. In the second stage, multiple key patches are stitched together to form new synthetic images, ensuring that each distilled image contains diverse and realistic content. These synthetic images are relabeled using soft labels generated by the observer model, capturing region-level information. The resulting distilled dataset is then used to train student models using a cross-entropy loss with the reconstructed soft labels.
e6d36f474eed202bbc438f237f78f4d88686ced7.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both low-resolution datasets (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100) and high-resolution, large-scale datasets (Tiny-ImageNet, ImageNet-1K, and several ImageNet-1K subsets such as ImageNet-100, ImageNette, and ImageWoof). Multiple neural architectures are used for both distillation and evaluation, including ConvNet, ResNet-18, ResNet-101, EfficientNet-B0, and MobileNet-V2. Baseline comparisons include state-of-the-art optimization-based dataset distillation methods such as MTT, IDM, TESLA, DATM, and SRe2L. Evaluation metrics include top-1 validation accuracy, cross-architecture generalization (training on one architecture, evaluating on another), synthesis time per image, and peak GPU memory usage. Ablation studies are performed to analyze the impact of key hyperparameters such as the size of the pre-selected subset and the number of patches per synthetic image.
e6d36f474eed202bbc438f237f78f4d88686ced7.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces an optimization-free, patch-based distillation paradigm that achieves a superior balance between realism and diversity in the distilled dataset. It is the first to demonstrate efficient dataset distillation on full ImageNet-1K at scale, achieving twice the accuracy of previous state-of-the-art methods while being over 50 times faster. The approach leverages V-information theory to explicitly define and maximize diversity and realism, and introduces a practical two-stage patch selection and recombination framework that is highly scalable and generalizes well across neural architectures.

e6d54edfd27593b6facbddf92aa2f4292d1d8d71.title: Incentivize without Bonus: Provably Efficient Model-based Online Multi-agent RL for Markov Games
e6d54edfd27593b6facbddf92aa2f4292d1d8d71.research_question: Can provably efficient algorithms be developed for online multi-agent reinforcement learning in general Markov games, with function approximation, that achieve near-optimal regret for finding Nash and coarse correlated equilibria, without relying on explicit uncertainty quantification or bonus-based exploration?
e6d54edfd27593b6facbddf92aa2f4292d1d8d71.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a model-based exploration strategy, which biases empirical model parameter estimates towards those with higher collective best-response values, can achieve near-optimal regret in online multi-agent Markov games under function approximation, matching the performance of approaches that require explicit uncertainty estimation.
e6d54edfd27593b6facbddf92aa2f4292d1d8d71.proposed_method: A model-based framework, termed VMG (Value-incentivized Markov Game solver), will be developed to solve online multi-agent Markov games with function approximation. The method incentivizes exploration by biasing the empirical model parameter estimates towards those that yield higher collective best-response values for all players, given the current policies of the other agents. At each iteration, the model parameters are updated via a regularized optimization that balances fitting the observed data (e.g., via least-squares or maximum likelihood) and maximizing the duality gap or best-response value, thus encouraging deviation from the current equilibrium for enhanced exploration. The approach is designed to be agnostic to the form of function approximation, allowing for simultaneous and uncoupled policy updates for all players, and does not require explicit construction of uncertainty sets or bonus functions. The framework is applicable to both two-player zero-sum and multi-player general-sum Markov games, and can be extended to infinite-horizon settings.
e6d54edfd27593b6facbddf92aa2f4292d1d8d71.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both two-player zero-sum matrix games and multi-player general-sum Markov games under linear function approximation. The evaluation will include online regret minimization tasks, where the goal is to find approximate Nash equilibria (NE) or coarse correlated equilibria (CCE) with minimal sample complexity. Datasets will be generated via stochastic oracles that provide noisy feedback for queried actions or transitions. Baseline comparisons will include existing model-based approaches that use explicit uncertainty quantification (e.g., UCB-based methods), as well as reward-biased maximum likelihood estimators in single-agent or bandit settings. Evaluation metrics will include cumulative regret, duality gap, and sample complexity required to reach ε-approximate equilibria. The experimental setup will also consider both finite-horizon and infinite-horizon variants, and may include ablation studies on the effect of regularization and function approximation choices.
e6d54edfd27593b6facbddf92aa2f4292d1d8d71.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a novel value-incentivized exploration strategy for multi-agent Markov games that does not rely on explicit uncertainty estimation or bonus-based exploration. It is the first to generalize reward-biased maximum likelihood estimation to the multi-player game-theoretic setting, enabling efficient and simultaneous policy updates for all agents under general function approximation. The method achieves near-optimal regret bounds for both Nash and coarse correlated equilibria in online settings, matching or improving upon the sample efficiency of prior approaches that require sophisticated uncertainty quantification. The unified framework also recovers and extends existing algorithms for special cases such as symmetric games, linear bandits, and single-agent RL, and provides new formulations that may be of independent interest.

e6ea9047000f899327397ffa2189c7ae696fa16d.title: Benign Overfitting without Linearity: Neural Network Classifiers Trained by Gradient Descent for Noisy Linear Data
e6ea9047000f899327397ffa2189c7ae696fa16d.research_question: Can neural network classifiers trained by gradient descent achieve benign overfitting—interpolating noisy training data while maintaining optimal generalization error—in high-dimensional, noisy linear data settings without relying on linearity or kernel-based approximations?
e6ea9047000f899327397ffa2189c7ae696fa16d.hypothesis: Neural network classifiers trained by gradient descent on noisy, high-dimensional linearly separable data can achieve zero training error (interpolating noisy labels) and simultaneously attain minimax optimal test error, even when the model and learning dynamics are fundamentally nonlinear.
e6ea9047000f899327397ffa2189c7ae696fa16d.proposed_method: A two-layer neural network with smoothed leaky ReLU activation functions will be employed, where the second layer weights are fixed and the first layer weights are initialized randomly. The network will be trained on data generated from a mixture of well-separated, high-dimensional, log-concave class-conditional distributions, with a constant fraction of training labels adversarially corrupted. Full-batch gradient descent will be used to minimize the logistic loss, with careful selection of step size and initialization variance to ensure the weights traverse far from their initial values. The analysis will focus on demonstrating that gradient descent dynamics allow the network to interpolate the noisy training data while maintaining a large normalized margin on clean examples, leveraging a 'loss ratio bound' to control the influence of noisy points throughout training.
e6ea9047000f899327397ffa2189c7ae696fa16d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets generated according to the specified mixture model, with parameters such as input dimension, mean separation, and noise rate varied systematically. The evaluation will compare the test error of the trained neural network to the minimax optimal error for the given noise rate, and will also assess the ability to drive the training loss to zero. Baselines will include linear and kernel-based classifiers, as well as maximum margin classifiers where appropriate. Key metrics will include training loss, test error, and normalized margin, with multiple random initializations and data draws to ensure statistical significance.
e6ea9047000f899327397ffa2189c7ae696fa16d.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides the first theoretical guarantee of benign overfitting for neural networks trained by gradient descent in a setting that is fundamentally nonlinear and does not rely on kernel or linear approximations. The analysis holds for finite-width networks, arbitrary training duration, and does not require the neural tangent kernel regime. The approach introduces a novel loss ratio bound to control the effect of noisy labels during training, enabling interpolation of noisy data without sacrificing generalization. This work extends benign overfitting theory to practical neural network settings beyond previously studied linear and kernel-based models.

e70d99795c4bdcfeca48eb979169a9e3f2c2eab4.title: FastJAM: a Fast Joint Alignment Model for Images
e70d99795c4bdcfeca48eb979169a9e3f2c2eab4.research_question: How can the computational efficiency and alignment quality of joint image alignment across collections be improved, particularly in terms of reducing runtime and memory requirements, while maintaining or enhancing alignment accuracy?
e70d99795c4bdcfeca48eb979169a9e3f2c2eab4.hypothesis: A graph-based framework that leverages sparse keypoint correspondences and a graph neural network for propagating alignment information can achieve faster and more scalable joint image alignment, with equal or superior accuracy compared to existing dense feature-based or atlas-based methods, and without the need for extensive regularization or hyperparameter tuning.
e70d99795c4bdcfeca48eb979169a9e3f2c2eab4.proposed_method: The proposed method, FastJAM, constructs a sparse graph over keypoints extracted from a collection of images using an off-the-shelf image matcher (such as RoMa). The graph encodes both intra-image spatial structure (via fully connected edges among keypoints within each image) and inter-image semantic correspondences (via edges between matched keypoints across images). Object-centric masks are extracted using a segmentation model (e.g., Grounded-SAM) to focus keypoint extraction on relevant regions. Redundant keypoints within each image are merged using a fast, nonparametric clustering algorithm (parallel DP-Means). The resulting graph is processed by a multi-layer GraphSAGE GNN, which propagates alignment cues and produces per-image embeddings via image-level pooling. These embeddings are projected to homography parameters (using a Lie-algebraic parameterization for stability), and an inverse-compositional geometric loss is computed over sparse keypoint correspondences, using a robust Geman-McClure loss function. The method eliminates the need for explicit regularization terms or reference images, enabling efficient, joint optimization over all images.
e70d99795c4bdcfeca48eb979169a9e3f2c2eab4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark datasets including SPair-71k (18 object categories, ~30 images per category) and CUB-200 (selected classes and subsets), using annotated keypoints and significant intra-class variation. The primary evaluation metric will be the Percentage of Correct Keypoints (PCK) at a normalized distance threshold (alpha=0.1), averaged across all keypoints and categories. The proposed method will be compared against several baselines: Neural Best Buddies (VGG/DINO+MLS), DINO-NN, GANgealing, Neural Congealing, ASIC, and SpaceJAM. All experiments will be run under a test-time optimization setting, with the model optimized independently for each image collection. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of key components (e.g., matcher choice, loss function, clustering, GNN backbone). Runtime and memory usage will be measured and compared to baselines, with all experiments conducted on a single high-end GPU (e.g., NVIDIA RTX4090).
e70d99795c4bdcfeca48eb979169a9e3f2c2eab4.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel graph-based joint alignment framework that processes the entire image collection simultaneously, unlike previous image-by-image or atlas-based approaches. It is the first to combine an inverse-compositional loss with a sparse keypoint representation, enabling regularization-free and highly efficient optimization. The use of a GNN for propagating alignment information across both intra- and inter-image keypoint relations is a key innovation, allowing for shared reasoning and improved alignment quality. The approach achieves state-of-the-art alignment accuracy while reducing computation time from hours or minutes to mere seconds, and significantly lowers memory requirements compared to dense feature-based methods.

e716e6e0b3dd5124268780dc9bed521a07f371b8.title: Contrastive Decoding Improves Reasoning in Large Language Models
e716e6e0b3dd5124268780dc9bed521a07f371b8.research_question: Can a contrastive decoding approach be used to improve reasoning abilities in large language models across a variety of tasks and model scales, and how does it compare to standard decoding and sampling methods?
e716e6e0b3dd5124268780dc9bed521a07f371b8.hypothesis: Contrastive decoding, which maximizes a weighted difference in likelihood between a strong expert model and a weaker amateur model, will enhance reasoning performance in large language models, particularly on chain-of-thought tasks, outperforming traditional greedy and sampling-based decoding methods.
e716e6e0b3dd5124268780dc9bed521a07f371b8.proposed_method: A contrastive decoding framework will be developed that generates text by maximizing a weighted difference in token likelihoods between an expert (large) language model and an amateur (smaller or less-trained) model. The method involves α-masking to restrict candidate tokens to those with sufficiently high expert likelihood, and a contrastive penalty parameter β to control the influence of the amateur model. The final token selection is determined by adjusting the expert logits with a scaled subtraction of the amateur logits, followed by normalization and sampling or greedy selection. The approach will be implemented efficiently to introduce minimal computational overhead, and will be evaluated with and without chain-of-thought prompting and self-consistency sampling. Hyperparameters such as α, β, and amateur model size will be systematically explored.
e716e6e0b3dd5124268780dc9bed521a07f371b8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using untuned LLaMA models of various sizes (7B, 13B, 30B, 65B) as experts, with a 1.5B parameter LLaMA model as the amateur, and additional studies using FLAN-T5 models. The method will be evaluated on a diverse set of reasoning benchmarks, including arithmetic word problems (AQuA, ASDiv, GSM8K, SVAMP, MATH), commonsense reasoning (CommonsenseQA, StrategyQA), and multiple-choice tasks (ARC-E, ARC-C, BoolQ, HellaSwag, PIQA, SIQA, WinoGrande, MMLU). Baselines will include greedy decoding, nucleus sampling, and self-consistency. Evaluation metrics will include exact match accuracy, multiple-choice accuracy, and error analysis on reasoning steps. Hyperparameter sweeps for α and β will be performed, and ablations will assess the impact of amateur model size, α-masking alone, and chain-of-thought prompting. FLOP efficiency and performance on factual recall tasks (OpenBookQA, TriviaQA) will also be measured.
e716e6e0b3dd5124268780dc9bed521a07f371b8.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a training-free, computationally efficient contrastive decoding method that unifies and improves text generation and reasoning in large language models. It claims to achieve state-of-the-art results on standard reasoning benchmarks without additional model training, outperforming larger or more heavily trained models. The approach is novel in its systematic exploration of hyperparameters, amateur model selection (including partially trained checkpoints), and its combination with chain-of-thought prompting and self-consistency. The method is also claimed to be more FLOP-efficient than other reasoning enhancement techniques and generalizable across different model families.

e7300d39b8eff54bd857083e6a95f6d6e32b18a0.title: Interpretable Generalized Additive Models for Datasets with Missing Values
e7300d39b8eff54bd857083e6a95f6d6e32b18a0.research_question: How can interpretable machine learning models be constructed to handle datasets with missing values, maintaining both predictive accuracy and model interpretability without relying on imputation or sacrificing sparsity?
e7300d39b8eff54bd857083e6a95f6d6e32b18a0.hypothesis: Explicitly incorporating missingness indicators and their interaction terms within a sparse generalized additive modeling framework will yield models that are as accurate or superior to impute-then-predict approaches, while significantly improving interpretability and sparsity.
e7300d39b8eff54bd857083e6a95f6d6e32b18a0.proposed_method: A new modeling framework, termed M-GAM (Missingness-aware Generalized Additive Model), will be developed to extend traditional Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) for datasets with missing values. The approach introduces two sets of Boolean variables for each feature: missingness indicators (identifying which features are missing) and missingness adjustment terms (modifying shape functions for other features when a given feature is missing). Interaction terms between missingness indicators and feature thresholds are included to capture dependencies between missingness and observed data. Sparsity is enforced via ℓ0 regularization, directly optimizing for a small number of nonzero coefficients, thus maintaining interpretability and reducing overfitting. The model is trained using exponential loss for efficient optimization, and all parameters (including main effects, missingness effects, and interactions) are jointly learned.
e7300d39b8eff54bd857083e6a95f6d6e32b18a0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several real-world datasets with naturally occurring missing values, including the FICO Explainable Machine Learning Challenge dataset, a breast cancer dataset, the MIMIC-III critical care dataset, and a pharyngitis prediction dataset. Additional synthetic missing-at-random (MAR) missingness will be introduced to evaluate performance under controlled conditions. The proposed M-GAM will be compared against multiple baselines: impute-then-predict models using multivariate imputation by chained equations (MICE), MIWAE, and MissForest, as well as tree-based models (e.g., XGBoost, scikit-learn decision trees) with and without explicit missingness handling. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy and AUC, with particular attention to model sparsity (number of nonzero coefficients) and runtime. Hyperparameters will be selected via cross-validation, and experiments will be repeated over multiple train-test splits to assess robustness.
e7300d39b8eff54bd857083e6a95f6d6e32b18a0.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a novel, sparse extension of generalized additive models that directly incorporates missingness indicators and their interactions, enabling interpretable reasoning in the presence of missing data. Unlike prior approaches, this method maintains global and local interpretability while controlling model complexity through ℓ0 regularization. The approach is claimed to provide comparable or superior predictive performance to impute-then-predict methods, achieve significantly greater sparsity, and offer substantial reductions in runtime. The method also supports explicit modeling of different reasons for missingness and is applicable to high-stakes domains where interpretability is critical.

e73d51188ca5d71e183be4a828796d0a98ff7520.title: Automatic Clipping: Differentially Private Deep Learning Made Easier and Stronger
e73d51188ca5d71e183be4a828796d0a98ff7520.research_question: How can the process of differentially private deep learning be simplified and strengthened by eliminating the need for tuning the per-example gradient clipping threshold, while maintaining or improving model utility and privacy guarantees across a variety of deep learning tasks?
e73d51188ca5d71e183be4a828796d0a98ff7520.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that an automatic clipping mechanism, which normalizes per-sample gradients with a stability constant and removes the need for a tunable clipping threshold, will enable differentially private optimizers to achieve equal or superior convergence rates and empirical performance compared to existing methods, while also simplifying the hyperparameter tuning process.
e73d51188ca5d71e183be4a828796d0a98ff7520.proposed_method: A novel automatic clipping framework will be developed, replacing the traditional per-example gradient clipping step in differentially private (DP) optimizers. Instead of clipping gradients using a tunable threshold R, each per-sample gradient will be normalized by its norm plus a small stability constant γ, resulting in a clipping function Clip_AUTO-S(g) = 1/(||g|| + γ). This approach removes the dependence on the clipping threshold and ensures that the magnitude information of gradients is preserved, addressing issues of scale invariance and convergence. The method will be implemented as a drop-in replacement for standard DP optimizers, including DP-SGD, DP-Adam, and others, and will require no DP-specific hyperparameters beyond those used in non-private training. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish convergence guarantees in non-convex settings, and privacy guarantees will be shown to match those of existing DP optimizers.
e73d51188ca5d71e183be4a828796d0a98ff7520.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of vision and language tasks, including image classification (MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR10, ImageNette, CelebA), sentence classification (MNLI, QQP, QNLI, SST2) with RoBERTa models, and table-to-text generation (E2E dataset) with GPT2 models of varying sizes. The proposed automatic clipping method will be compared against baselines such as Abadi's clipping, re-parameterized gradient perturbation, and other state-of-the-art DP fine-tuning strategies (e.g., LoRA, prefix-tuning, RGP). Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy for classification tasks and BLEU/ROUGE-L for generation tasks. All experiments will use the same hyperparameters as strong baselines to ensure fair comparison, and results will be averaged over multiple runs to assess stability and reproducibility. Privacy guarantees will be set to strong regimes (e.g., ε=3,8, δ=1e-5), and ablation studies will be performed to analyze the effect of the stability constant γ and learning rates.
e73d51188ca5d71e183be4a828796d0a98ff7520.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to eliminate the need for tuning the per-example gradient clipping threshold in DP deep learning, making DP training as straightforward as standard non-private training. The automatic clipping approach is theoretically proven to provide the same privacy guarantees as existing methods, while achieving convergence rates that match standard SGD in non-convex settings. Empirical results demonstrate that the method consistently matches or outperforms state-of-the-art DP optimizers across a variety of tasks and model sizes, with improved stability and reproducibility. The approach is general, computationally efficient, and can be integrated into existing codebases with minimal changes.

e788d5c6dc79f106296f8ad296bcbe512028d5f0.title: 3D-VLA: A 3D Vision-Language-Action Generative World Model
e788d5c6dc79f106296f8ad296bcbe512028d5f0.research_question: How can a unified generative world model be developed to seamlessly integrate 3D perception, reasoning, and action for embodied agents, enabling advanced multimodal understanding, planning, and goal imagination in complex physical environments?
e788d5c6dc79f106296f8ad296bcbe512028d5f0.hypothesis: Equipping embodied foundation models with a generative world model that incorporates 3D perception, multimodal goal imagination (images, depths, point clouds), and explicit interaction tokens will significantly enhance reasoning, planning, and action prediction capabilities in robotics and embodied tasks compared to models limited to 2D inputs or direct perception-to-action mapping.
e788d5c6dc79f106296f8ad296bcbe512028d5f0.proposed_method: A novel framework, 3D-VLA, will be developed that unifies 3D perception, language, and action through a generative world model. The backbone will be based on a large vision-language model (BLIP2-FlanT5), enhanced with Q-Former modules for multi-view 3D feature extraction. Specialized interaction tokens will be introduced to represent objects, locations, scenes, and robotic actions, enabling fine-grained grounding and manipulation within 3D environments. To endow the model with goal imagination capabilities, a suite of embodied diffusion models will be pretrained for RGBD-to-RGBD and point-to-point generation, conditioned on language and scene context. A transformer-based projector will align the LLM embedding space with the diffusion model decoders, facilitating seamless multi-modal goal generation. Training will leverage a curated large-scale 3D embodied instruction dataset, with LoRA-based fine-tuning to efficiently adapt the model while preventing catastrophic forgetting.
e788d5c6dc79f106296f8ad296bcbe512028d5f0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of real and synthetic robotics datasets, including 12 real-world robot datasets from Open-X, RLBench, CALVIN, and human-object interaction datasets such as Epic-Kitchens and HOI4D. The evaluation will cover a range of tasks: 3D reasoning and localization (using metrics like BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L, EM@1, IoU, and accuracy at thresholds), multimodal goal generation (evaluated with PSNR, CLIPSim, SSIM, FID for images, and P-FID, Chamfer-L for point clouds), and embodied action planning (measured by task completion rates on RLBench and CALVIN). Baselines will include state-of-the-art 2D and 3D vision-language models (e.g., BLIP2, OpenFlamingo, LLaVA, 3D-LLM), as well as specialized image/point cloud generation and action prediction methods. Both zero-shot and held-in (fine-tuned) settings will be explored, and ablation studies will assess the impact of interaction tokens and intermediate object localization.
e788d5c6dc79f106296f8ad296bcbe512028d5f0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to unify 3D perception, reasoning, and action within a generative world model for embodied agents, introducing interaction tokens for explicit 3D grounding and action representation. It pioneers the integration of pretrained diffusion models for multimodal goal imagination (images, depths, point clouds) aligned with a large language model. A large-scale 3D embodied instruction dataset will be curated to address the scarcity of 3D-annotated data for robotics. The framework enables advanced embodied tasks such as goal-based planning, what-if reasoning, and multimodal future state generation, demonstrating substantial improvements over existing 2D and 3D baselines in both reasoning and action planning benchmarks.

e7ad08848d5d7c5c47673ffe0da06af443643bda.title: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
e7ad08848d5d7c5c47673ffe0da06af443643bda.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs) be prompted in a zero-shot setting to perform complex multi-step reasoning across diverse tasks, without the need for task-specific few-shot exemplars or fine-tuning?
e7ad08848d5d7c5c47673ffe0da06af443643bda.hypothesis: A simple, task-agnostic prompt that encourages step-by-step reasoning (such as 'Let's think step by step') will enable large language models to perform effective multi-step reasoning in a zero-shot setting, substantially improving their accuracy on challenging reasoning tasks compared to standard zero-shot prompting.
e7ad08848d5d7c5c47673ffe0da06af443643bda.proposed_method: A novel zero-shot chain-of-thought (Zero-shot-CoT) prompting framework will be developed, in which a fixed, instructive trigger phrase (e.g., 'Let's think step by step.') is appended to each question to elicit step-by-step reasoning from LLMs. The methodology involves a two-stage prompting process: first, the model is prompted to generate a reasoning path by modifying the input question with the trigger phrase; second, the model is prompted again, using the generated reasoning text and an answer-extraction phrase, to produce the final answer in the required format. The approach is designed to be task-agnostic, requiring no hand-crafted few-shot examples or task-specific templates, and is applicable to a wide range of reasoning domains including arithmetic, symbolic, commonsense, and logical reasoning. Greedy decoding is used for answer generation, and an answer cleansing procedure is applied to extract the final prediction from the model's output.
e7ad08848d5d7c5c47673ffe0da06af443643bda.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 12 datasets spanning arithmetic (SingleEq, AddSub, MultiArith, AQUA-RAT, GSM8K, SVAMP), commonsense (CommonsenseQA, StrategyQA), symbolic (LastLetterConcatenation, CoinFlip), and logical reasoning tasks (DateUnderstanding, TrackingShuffledObjects from BIG-bench). Multiple LLMs will be evaluated, including InstructGPT-3 (text-davinci-002), original GPT-3 variants, and PaLM (8B, 62B, 540B), as well as other models for scaling studies (GPT-2, GPT-Neo, GPT-J, T0, OPT). Baselines will include standard zero-shot prompting, few-shot prompting, and few-shot chain-of-thought prompting, with accuracy as the primary evaluation metric. All methods will use greedy decoding, and experiments will control for answer format and prompt order to ensure fair comparisons. Robustness to different trigger templates and prompt variations will also be assessed.
e7ad08848d5d7c5c47673ffe0da06af443643bda.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first minimalist, task-agnostic zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting framework that elicits multi-step reasoning from LLMs across a broad range of tasks using a single fixed prompt. This approach eliminates the need for hand-crafted few-shot exemplars or task-specific prompt engineering, significantly improving zero-shot performance on challenging reasoning benchmarks. The method demonstrates that LLMs possess untapped, broad zero-shot reasoning capabilities that can be uncovered with simple prompting, and establishes a new strong zero-shot baseline for multi-step reasoning tasks.

e7c97e953849f1a8e5d85ceb4cfcc0a5d54d2365.title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations
e7c97e953849f1a8e5d85ceb4cfcc0a5d54d2365.research_question: How can large language models be enabled to generate text with accurate, verifiable citations, thereby improving factual correctness and trustworthiness in information-seeking applications?
e7c97e953849f1a8e5d85ceb4cfcc0a5d54d2365.hypothesis: Requiring large language models to generate text with explicit citations to retrieved supporting passages will improve the factual correctness and verifiability of their outputs, and automatic metrics can robustly evaluate these capabilities in a reproducible manner.
e7c97e953849f1a8e5d85ceb4cfcc0a5d54d2365.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, ALCE, will be developed to evaluate the ability of large language models (LLMs) to generate text with citations. The proposed approach will formalize the task as follows: given a natural language question and a large retrieval corpus, an end-to-end system will retrieve relevant passages, generate multi-sentence answers, and provide explicit citations for each statement. Multiple prompting strategies will be explored, including providing top-k passages as context (VANILLA), using summaries or snippets to fit more evidence in the context window, interactive prompting to allow the model to check full passages as needed, and enabling retrieval on-the-fly during generation. Automatic evaluation metrics will be designed to assess fluency (using MAUVE), correctness (using dataset-specific recall or claim-based NLI models), and citation quality (using NLI-based citation recall and precision). Human evaluation will be conducted to validate the correlation of these metrics with human judgment.
e7c97e953849f1a8e5d85ceb4cfcc0a5d54d2365.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three diverse QA datasets: ASQA and QAMPARI (factoid questions, using Wikipedia as the corpus), and ELI5 (open-ended questions, using the Sphere web corpus). For each dataset, 1,000 development examples will be selected. State-of-the-art LLMs (e.g., ChatGPT, GPT-4, LLaMA, Vicuna) will be evaluated using various prompting and retrieval strategies. Baselines will include closed-book models, retrieval-augmented models, and post-hoc citation assignment. Evaluation will use automatic metrics for fluency, correctness, and citation quality, and results will be compared to human annotations on a subset of examples. Additional ablations will examine the impact of retriever quality, context window size, reranking, and instruction tuning.
e7c97e953849f1a8e5d85ceb4cfcc0a5d54d2365.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces ALCE, the first reproducible, automatic benchmark for evaluating LLMs' ability to generate text with citations. It provides a unified framework for end-to-end retrieval, generation, and citation, along with robust automatic metrics for citation quality that correlate strongly with human judgment. The methodology supports multi-passage citation per statement and covers long-form, multi-aspect answers. The benchmark enables systematic comparison of prompting strategies, retrieval methods, and LLM architectures, highlighting key challenges and research directions for integrating retrieval and generation in LLMs.

e7d20783950d0d0f3c40e8e3d32ead57122bf826.title: Flash Communication: Reducing Tensor Parallelization Bottleneck for Fast Large Language Model Inference
e7d20783950d0d0f3c40e8e3d32ead57122bf826.research_question: How can communication bottlenecks in tensor parallelism be reduced to enable faster and more efficient large language model (LLM) inference on multi-GPU clusters, particularly under limited bandwidth conditions?
e7d20783950d0d0f3c40e8e3d32ead57122bf826.hypothesis: Applying fine-grained, low-bit quantization to activation tensors and redesigning the All-Reduce communication pattern will significantly reduce communication overhead in tensor parallelism for LLM inference, without substantial loss in model accuracy.
e7d20783950d0d0f3c40e8e3d32ead57122bf826.proposed_method: A novel communication mechanism, termed Flash Communication, will be developed to address the communication bottleneck in tensor parallelism. This method will employ fine-grained, low-bit quantization (e.g., INT4/INT6/INT8) of activation tensors prior to communication, and introduce a two-step All-Reduce strategy that minimizes the number of quantization/dequantization operations and communication hops. The approach will replace the traditional Ring All-Reduce with a combination of All2All and All-Gather primitives, reducing the number of sequential steps and leveraging fused CUDA kernels for efficient quantization, communication, and dequantization. The quantization granularity and bit-width will be adaptively chosen based on sensitivity analysis to balance accuracy and communication reduction. Fast packing and unpacking algorithms will be implemented to optimize memory and computational efficiency on GPU hardware.
