e7d20783950d0d0f3c40e8e3d32ead57122bf826.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on state-of-the-art LLMs such as LLaMA-2 and LLaMA-3 (with sizes ranging from 7B to 70B parameters), using both FP16 and INT8 quantized weights. Evaluations will be performed on NVIDIA L40 and A100 GPUs, with tensor parallelism degrees (TP) of 4 and 8, respectively. The experimental setup will include input token lengths of 1024 and output lengths of 64, with batch sizes varying from 8 to 64. Baseline comparisons will be made against standard FP16 communication and Ring All-Reduce implementations. Evaluation metrics will include time-to-first-token (TTFT), end-to-end latency, throughput, and model accuracy on benchmarks such as PIQA, ARC (Challenge and Easy), HellaSwag, WinoGrande, C4 perplexity, and WikiText-2. Ablation studies will explore the effects of quantization bit-width, granularity, and kernel design choices.
e7d20783950d0d0f3c40e8e3d32ead57122bf826.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a fine-grained, low-bit quantization strategy specifically for activation communication in tensor parallelism during LLM inference, which is not addressed by existing training-oriented quantization methods. The two-step All-Reduce algorithm reduces the number of quantization/dequantization and communication steps compared to traditional Ring All-Reduce, resulting in significant speedups (up to 2× TTFT reduction) with minimal accuracy loss. The approach is supported by a custom fused CUDA kernel for efficient execution, and extensive empirical analysis demonstrates its superiority over prior communication and quantization schemes in both accuracy and latency.

e7dad61b43b809517a73e497a76559992f2a130c.title: Controlling Moments with Kernel Stein Discrepancies
e7dad61b43b809517a73e497a76559992f2a130c.research_question: How can the kernel Stein discrepancy (KSD) be extended or modified to provide rigorous control over the convergence of moments (i.e., q-Wasserstein convergence) for probability distributions, particularly when the target distribution is defined by an unnormalized density and the integrands exhibit polynomial growth?
e7dad61b43b809517a73e497a76559992f2a130c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by selecting or designing alternative diffusion kernel Stein discrepancies with appropriate reproducing kernels and diffusion matrices, it is possible to control both weak convergence and moment convergence (q-Wasserstein convergence) for a broad class of target distributions, including those with heavy tails, thereby overcoming the limitations of standard KSDs.
e7dad61b43b809517a73e497a76559992f2a130c.proposed_method: The proposed approach will analyze and construct diffusion kernel Stein discrepancies (KSDs) by pairing general diffusion Stein operators with reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS) of vector-valued functions. The methodology will involve identifying sufficient conditions on the kernel and the diffusion matrix such that the resulting KSD controls both weak and moment convergence. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish equivalence between KSD convergence and q-Wasserstein convergence for all q > 0, including explicit bounds relating the KSD to integral probability metrics (IPMs) defined by pseudo-Lipschitz function classes. The method will also provide practical recommendations for kernel selection to ensure polynomial convergence control and will develop closed-form, computable expressions for the proposed KSDs suitable for empirical evaluation.
e7dad61b43b809517a73e497a76559992f2a130c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted to empirically validate the convergence control properties of the proposed diffusion KSDs. Datasets will include synthetic distributions such as Gaussian mixtures and heavy-tailed distributions (e.g., Student's t-distributions), as well as real-world Bayesian posterior distributions where the normalization constant is intractable. Baseline comparisons will be made against standard KSDs (e.g., those using the Langevin Stein operator with commonly used kernels) and possibly graph Stein discrepancies. Evaluation metrics will include the computed KSD values, empirical q-Wasserstein distances, and convergence rates of sample-based expectations for polynomially growing test functions. The experimental setup will involve both weighted and unweighted empirical measures generated by various Monte Carlo and variational inference methods.
e7dad61b43b809517a73e497a76559992f2a130c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces, for the first time, kernel Stein discrepancies that exactly characterize q-Wasserstein convergence for every q > 0, thereby enabling rigorous control of moment convergence in addition to weak convergence. It extends the applicability of KSDs to unbounded integrands of arbitrary polynomial growth and to heavy-tailed target distributions via the use of generalized diffusion Stein operators and specifically constructed kernels. The approach provides explicit, computable bounds and practical kernel choices for polynomial convergence control, filling a significant gap in the theoretical and practical understanding of Stein discrepancies for distributional approximation.

e80b885174c946932e54d9de54f2eff22771c4d2.title: ReDi: Rectified Discrete Flow
e80b885174c946932e54d9de54f2eff22771c4d2.research_question: How can the efficiency and quality of few-step and one-step generation in discrete flow-based generative models be improved without relying on complex distillation procedures or specialized training objectives?
e80b885174c946932e54d9de54f2eff22771c4d2.hypothesis: Iteratively rectifying the coupling between source and target distributions in discrete flow-based models will monotonically reduce factorization error, as measured by Conditional Total Correlation (TC), thereby enabling efficient few-step and one-step generation with high fidelity and diversity.
e80b885174c946932e54d9de54f2eff22771c4d2.proposed_method: A novel iterative framework, Rectified Discrete Flow (ReDi), will be developed to address the factorization error inherent in discrete flow-based models. The method begins with an initial coupling between source and target distributions and trains a discrete flow model (DFM) to model the conditional transition probability defined by this coupling. After training, the model generates paired samples, which are then used to define a new, rectified coupling with reduced factorization error. This rectification process is repeated for several iterations, each time training a new DFM on the updated coupling, guaranteeing a monotonic decrease in Conditional TC. Additionally, a perturbed rectification strategy will be introduced for high-dimensional data, where samples from the target distribution are perturbed and used to further reduce marginal approximation errors. The resulting rectified coupling is then used to train efficient one-step generative models.
e80b885174c946932e54d9de54f2eff22771c4d2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark datasets for discrete data synthesis, including ImageNet (for class-conditional image generation) and OpenWebText (for text generation). For image generation, images will be represented as vector-quantized tokens using a pretrained VQGAN, while text will be tokenized with a GPT-2 tokenizer. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as SDTT and Di4C, which employ distillation for few-step generation. Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), precision, recall, density, and coverage for images, and generative perplexity and 1-gram entropy for text. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the number of rectification iterations, sample pair size, and decoding strategies. Both few-step and one-step generation scenarios will be evaluated, with additional analysis on the reduction of Conditional TC across iterations.
e80b885174c946932e54d9de54f2eff22771c4d2.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a theoretically grounded, simple, and broadly applicable approach for reducing factorization error in discrete flow-based models by directly rectifying the coupling between source and target distributions. Unlike prior distillation-based methods, this framework requires neither specialized training objectives nor teacher-student architectures, reducing memory and implementation complexity. The iterative rectification process is proven to monotonically decrease Conditional TC, and the resulting rectified couplings are shown to be particularly effective for training highly efficient one-step generative models. The method is orthogonal to existing distillation techniques and can be combined with them for further performance gains, offering a new perspective on efficient discrete data synthesis.

e80f3559bbf308a989022a9bd9a266667a0f07d2.title: Post-hoc Reward Calibration: A Case Study on Length Bias
e80f3559bbf308a989022a9bd9a266667a0f07d2.research_question: How can biases in reward models used for aligning large language models, such as length bias, be mitigated in a post-hoc, training-free manner to improve the reliability of model evaluation and alignment without requiring additional data or retraining?
e80f3559bbf308a989022a9bd9a266667a0f07d2.hypothesis: It is possible to effectively mitigate biases in reward models, such as length bias, by applying post-hoc calibration techniques that estimate and remove the bias component from assigned rewards using only existing scored data, thereby improving the alignment of large language models with human preferences and enhancing evaluation reliability.
e80f3559bbf308a989022a9bd9a266667a0f07d2.proposed_method: A post-hoc reward calibration framework will be developed to mitigate biases in reward models without requiring additional data collection or retraining. The approach assumes that the biased reward can be decomposed into a true reward component and a bias term dependent on a measurable characteristic (e.g., output length). Two calibration strategies will be implemented: (1) a uniform averaging method that estimates the bias by computing local average rewards for outputs with similar characteristics and subtracts this estimate from the original reward, and (2) a more robust Locally Weighted Regression (LWR) approach, specifically using Robust Locally Estimated Scatterplot Smoothing (LOWESS), to dynamically estimate and remove the bias term by fitting a weighted local linear model over the characteristic-reward pairs. The method will be applied post-hoc to already-scored datasets, enabling seamless integration into existing RLHF pipelines and model evaluation settings.
e80f3559bbf308a989022a9bd9a266667a0f07d2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in three main settings: (1) Benchmarking reward models on the RewardBench dataset, using 2,985 prompts and 33 reward models, with calibration applied to 5,970 response pairs; (2) Evaluating the calibration's effect on model rankings using the AlpacaEval benchmark, which includes 184 LLMs and 805 instructions per model (151,000 samples), measuring agreement with GPT-4 and human preferences via Spearman correlation and gameability metrics; (3) Assessing the impact of calibrated rewards on LLM alignment by using the UltraFeedback dataset (60,000 instructions, 300,000 samples) to score responses, create preference pairs, and perform Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) tuning on two LLMs (Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct and gemma2-9b-it) with two reward models each. Baselines will include the original reward, a simple length penalty, and existing length-controlled calibration methods. Evaluation metrics will comprise accuracy on RewardBench, win rates and correlation with established leaderboards, gameability, and average performance on eight standard benchmarks (e.g., MMLU, GSM8K, ARC-challenge). Computational efficiency and generalization to other bias types (e.g., markdown features) will also be assessed.
e80f3559bbf308a989022a9bd9a266667a0f07d2.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a scalable, training-free post-hoc reward calibration framework that can be applied to any scored dataset, requiring no additional data annotation or reward model retraining. It is generalizable to multiple types of biases and reward model architectures, including BT-based, DPO-based, and LLM-as-judge models. The approach is computationally efficient, robust to hyperparameter choices, and minimally alters non-biased reward models while providing substantial improvements for strongly biased ones. The calibration effect is proportional to the degree of bias, and the method can be extended to multiple bias characteristics simultaneously. This framework offers a practical and effective solution for mitigating biases in reward models, thereby improving the alignment and evaluation of large language models.

e81c91cd71a3310e33e1bffc713aec4de608f40b.title: Revisiting Zeroth-Order Optimization for Memory-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning: A Benchmark
e81c91cd71a3310e33e1bffc713aec4de608f40b.research_question: Can a comprehensive benchmark be established for zeroth-order (ZO) optimization in large language model (LLM) fine-tuning, and can new optimization principles and techniques be identified to advance memory-efficient LLM fine-tuning across diverse models, tasks, and fine-tuning schemes?
e81c91cd71a3310e33e1bffc713aec4de608f40b.hypothesis: Zeroth-order optimization methods, when systematically benchmarked and enhanced with novel techniques such as block-wise descent, hybrid ZO-FO training, and gradient sparsity, can achieve competitive fine-tuning performance on LLMs while significantly reducing memory consumption compared to first-order methods.
e81c91cd71a3310e33e1bffc713aec4de608f40b.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark will be developed to evaluate a diverse set of zeroth-order optimization algorithms for LLM fine-tuning, including ZO-SGD, ZO-SGD-Sign, ZO-SGD-MMT, ZO-SGD-Cons, ZO-Adam, and Forward-Grad. The methodology will involve aligning downstream tasks with pre-training objectives using prompt engineering, and systematically applying both full-parameter and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) schemes such as LoRA, prefix-tuning, and prompt-tuning. Novel enhancements will be introduced: (1) block-wise ZO optimization, where gradients are estimated for parameter blocks to reduce variance; (2) hybrid ZO-FO fine-tuning, which applies ZO optimization to shallow layers and FO optimization to deep layers to balance memory and performance; and (3) sparsity-induced ZO optimization, where random or magnitude-based pruning is used to induce sparse gradient estimates and further reduce variance. Technical implementation will leverage half-precision and mixed-precision training to maximize memory efficiency.
e81c91cd71a3310e33e1bffc713aec4de608f40b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across five LLM families (Roberta, OPT, LLaMA, Vicuna, Mistral) on tasks of varying complexity, including SST2 (binary classification), COPA (question answering), WinoGrande (commonsense reasoning), and MultiRC (multi-sentence reading comprehension). Both full-parameter and PEFT schemes (LoRA, prefix-tuning, prompt-tuning) will be evaluated. Baselines will include standard first-order optimizers (SGD, Adam) and BP-free Forward-Grad. Evaluation metrics will encompass test accuracy, memory consumption (peak GB usage), GPU resource requirements, runtime per iteration, and query efficiency (number of function queries per gradient estimate). Ablation studies will assess the impact of query budget, block size, hybrid layer splits, and gradient sparsity ratios. Implementation will use both half-precision (F16) and mixed-precision (FP16) settings to assess practical memory savings.
e81c91cd71a3310e33e1bffc713aec4de608f40b.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first comprehensive benchmark for zeroth-order optimization in LLM fine-tuning, systematically evaluating a broad spectrum of ZO methods, model families, tasks, and fine-tuning schemes. It uncovers previously overlooked optimization principles, such as the critical role of task alignment and the potential of Forward-Grad as a BP-free baseline. The proposal advances the state of the art by developing and empirically validating novel techniques—block-wise ZO optimization, hybrid ZO-FO training, and sparsity-induced ZO gradients—that improve the accuracy and memory efficiency of ZO-based LLM fine-tuning. The work provides actionable insights and practical guidelines for achieving memory-efficient fine-tuning of large-scale language models.

e82e3f4347674b75c432cb80604d38ee630d4bf6.title: Transformers Learn Shortcuts to Automata
e82e3f4347674b75c432cb80604d38ee630d4bf6.research_question: How can shallow, non-recurrent Transformer architectures represent and learn the computations of finite-state automata and bounded-memory algorithms, and what are the properties, limitations, and robustness of these solutions compared to recurrent models?
e82e3f4347674b75c432cb80604d38ee630d4bf6.hypothesis: Shallow Transformer models can efficiently simulate the computations of any finite-state automaton by learning shortcut solutions that hierarchically reparameterize recurrent dynamics, but these solutions may exhibit statistical brittleness and limited generalization compared to recurrent neural networks.
e82e3f4347674b75c432cb80604d38ee630d4bf6.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to characterize the capacity of shallow Transformer architectures to simulate semiautomata (finite-state automata without output mappings) and their associated algorithms. The approach will involve constructing explicit Transformer architectures that leverage hierarchical composition of transition functions, enabling parallel computation of state transitions with depth logarithmic or even constant in the input sequence length. Theoretical results will be derived using tools from algebraic automata theory (notably the Krohn-Rhodes decomposition) and circuit complexity, establishing conditions under which shortcut solutions exist and their efficiency in terms of network depth, width, and parameter count. Empirical studies will train shallow Transformer models on a diverse set of automaton simulation tasks, analyzing their ability to learn shortcut solutions via standard gradient-based optimization, and probing the learned models for mechanistic interpretability and robustness.
e82e3f4347674b75c432cb80604d38ee630d4bf6.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training shallow Transformer models (e.g., GPT-2-like architectures) on sequence-to-sequence tasks derived from 19 different semiautomata, including both solvable and non-solvable groups, with randomly sampled input sequences of length T=100. Model depth will be varied from 1 to 16 layers, and performance will be evaluated on held-out sequences to assess generalization. Baselines will include recurrent neural networks (LSTMs) trained on the same tasks. Evaluation metrics will focus on in-distribution accuracy, out-of-distribution generalization (distribution shift, sequence length extrapolation), and robustness to partial or indirect supervision (e.g., latent-state prediction, incomplete state sequences). Additional analyses will visualize attention patterns and probe the internal representations of trained models.
e82e3f4347674b75c432cb80604d38ee630d4bf6.novelty_claims: The proposal claims several novel contributions: (1) a theoretical characterization showing that shallow Transformers can efficiently simulate any finite-state automaton with shortcut solutions of logarithmic or constant depth, leveraging algebraic decompositions; (2) identification and empirical demonstration that Transformers trained with standard methods reliably converge to these shortcut solutions across a wide variety of automata; (3) analysis revealing that such shortcut solutions are statistically brittle, exhibiting poor out-of-distribution and length generalization compared to recurrent models; and (4) proposals for mitigation strategies, such as recency-biased scratchpad training, to guide Transformers toward more robust, RNN-like iterative solutions.

e82e6b500308ef2f47512f1a3e02040d1ccdd054.title: Generalized Schrödinger Bridge Matching
e82e6b500308ef2f47512f1a3e02040d1ccdd054.research_question: How can distribution matching between two boundary distributions be generalized to account for task-specific optimality structures, particularly when the intermediate marginals are only implicitly defined by a task-specific objective function, and how can scalable, stable, and feasible algorithms be developed for solving such generalized distribution matching problems across diverse scientific and machine learning domains?
e82e6b500308ef2f47512f1a3e02040d1ccdd054.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a generalized matching algorithm, which formulates the distribution matching problem as a conditional stochastic optimal control problem and leverages efficient variational approximations (such as Gaussian path approximation and spline optimization), will achieve stable convergence, maintain feasible transport maps throughout training, and scale effectively to high-dimensional and complex tasks, outperforming existing methods in both feasibility and optimality.
e82e6b500308ef2f47512f1a3e02040d1ccdd054.proposed_method: A new algorithm, Generalized Schrödinger Bridge Matching (GSBM), is proposed to solve generalized distribution matching problems where the intermediate marginals are implicitly defined by a task-specific objective involving both kinetic energy and state-dependent costs. The approach alternates between two stages: (1) optimizing the drift of a stochastic differential equation (SDE) to match prescribed marginals using either implicit or explicit matching losses, and (2) solving a conditional stochastic optimal control (CondSOC) problem to update the marginals, where the solution is approximated using Gaussian probability paths parameterized by splines for computational efficiency. The method supports further debiasing via path integral theory, allowing for importance sampling-based resampling when the Gaussian approximation is insufficient. The algorithm is designed to be highly parallelizable, simulation-free, and requires only samples from the boundary distributions, making it suitable for high-dimensional applications.
e82e6b500308ef2f47512f1a3e02040d1ccdd054.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse suite of distribution matching tasks, including synthetic crowd navigation with mean-field and geometric state costs, navigation over LiDAR-derived manifolds, high-dimensional opinion depolarization, and unpaired image domain transfer (e.g., dog-to-cat translation using AFHQ). Baselines will include DeepGSB (a Sinkhorn-inspired method), DSBM (for the special case of zero state cost), and other recent matching algorithms. Evaluation metrics will include feasibility (measured by Wasserstein distance to the target distribution), optimality (objective value of the task-specific cost), and generative quality (e.g., FID for image tasks). Experimental setups will vary the state cost functions, noise levels in the SDE, and the use of path integral resampling, with ablation studies to assess computational efficiency and convergence properties. Both qualitative and quantitative results will be reported, including visualizations of transport maps and trajectories, as well as runtime and scalability analyses.
e82e6b500308ef2f47512f1a3e02040d1ccdd054.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a generalized matching algorithm that extends previous Schrödinger Bridge and diffusion model matching approaches to handle arbitrary, task-specific state costs within the transport objective. Unlike prior methods, GSBM maintains feasible solutions throughout training, supports high-dimensional and complex state costs via scalable variational approximations, and provides stable convergence guarantees. The approach unifies and generalizes existing matching algorithms as special cases, incorporates conditional stochastic optimal control into the distribution matching framework, and demonstrates improved scalability, stability, and interpretability across a broad range of scientific and machine learning tasks.

e82fde04494e15cb54df0c57d9c9d407525a7bcb.title: Elliptic Loss Regularization
e82fde04494e15cb54df0c57d9c9d407525a7bcb.research_question: How can neural network loss functions be regularized to improve generalization, particularly in regions of the input space that are underrepresented in the training data, and how does such regularization affect robustness to distribution shifts and data imbalance?
e82fde04494e15cb54df0c57d9c9d407525a7bcb.hypothesis: Imposing an elliptic partial differential equation (PDE) constraint on the loss landscape of neural networks will enforce a desirable level of smoothness, leading to improved generalization and robustness to distribution shifts and group imbalance compared to standard empirical risk minimization and existing regularization techniques.
e82fde04494e15cb54df0c57d9c9d407525a7bcb.proposed_method: A new regularization framework is developed in which the neural network loss landscape is required to satisfy an elliptic PDE over the data domain, with boundary conditions set by the loss values at training points. The method formulates a modified risk minimization objective that incorporates this PDE constraint, ensuring that the loss function exhibits controlled smoothness and regularity throughout the domain. Computationally, the solution to the elliptic PDE is approximated using a stochastic process representation via the Feynman-Kac formula, enabling scalable Monte Carlo estimation. In practice, Brownian bridge sampling is used to efficiently approximate the expected loss along paths between data points, with importance weighting introduced to further tailor the regularization to address data imbalance. The method is flexible, allowing for both second-order (diffusive) and lower-order (advection/drift) terms in the PDE, and can be implemented efficiently using pairwise distance computations and stochastic path sampling.
e82fde04494e15cb54df0c57d9c9d407525a7bcb.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a variety of standard and challenging machine learning benchmarks, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-Imagenet200 for classification, and Airfoil Self-Noise and NO2 for regression. Additional robustness evaluations are performed on datasets with group imbalance and distribution shifts, such as WaterBirds, CelebA, Camelyon17, SkillCraft, Crime, RCF-MNIST, and Med-MNIST. Baselines include empirical risk minimization (ERM), mixup, mixupE, c-mixup, Focal Loss, CVaR-DRO, DORO, JTT, and UMIX. Evaluation metrics include classification error rate, top-1 and top-5 accuracy, average and worst-group accuracy, and root mean squared error (RMSE) for regression. Experiments are repeated across multiple random seeds, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of different components of the method. The proposed regularization is shown to improve or match state-of-the-art results, particularly in scenarios with imbalanced data and distribution shifts.
e82fde04494e15cb54df0c57d9c9d407525a7bcb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled regularization technique for neural network loss landscapes based on elliptic PDE theory, enabling explicit control over loss smoothness and providing theoretical guarantees (such as the maximum principle) for loss behavior in unobserved regions. The method leverages a stochastic process (Feynman-Kac) representation for scalable computation and introduces a practical Brownian bridge-based implementation. The framework is general, applicable to both regression and classification, and can be adapted to address data imbalance via importance weighting. This represents a novel connection between PDE-based regularization and data augmentation, offering new insights and tools for robust machine learning under data shifts and imbalance.

e831d41650e4a724bdc58499c595378d41f3088f.title: Reverse Diffusion Monte Carlo
e831d41650e4a724bdc58499c595378d41f3088f.research_question: Can an efficient, general-purpose Monte Carlo sampling algorithm be developed based on the reverse diffusion process, which is capable of accurately sampling from complex, multi-modal, or heavy-tailed target distributions without relying on learned neural network score functions?
e831d41650e4a724bdc58499c595378d41f3088f.hypothesis: Transforming the score matching problem in reverse diffusion into a mean estimation problem for regularized posterior distributions enables the construction of a Monte Carlo sampling algorithm that achieves faster convergence and improved computational efficiency compared to classical MCMC methods, particularly for challenging distributions such as multi-modal or heavy-tailed targets.
e831d41650e4a724bdc58499c595378d41f3088f.proposed_method: A novel Monte Carlo sampling algorithm, termed Reverse Diffusion Monte Carlo (RDMC), will be developed by leveraging the explicit solutions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) process to reformulate the score function estimation as a mean estimation problem. The method will estimate the means of regularized posterior distributions at each step, avoiding the need for neural network-based score learning. Two main approaches for score estimation will be implemented: (1) importance sampling from a normal distribution determined by the OU transition kernel, with mean estimates weighted by the target density, and (2) an Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm (ULA) to sample from the product of the target and normal distributions, improving sample complexity in high dimensions. The reverse SDE will be discretized, and at each iteration, the score will be estimated using Monte Carlo samples from the appropriate posterior, followed by a reverse diffusion update. A hybrid approach combining importance sampling and ULA will be used to efficiently estimate the score across different regimes of the diffusion process.
e831d41650e4a724bdc58499c595378d41f3088f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of synthetic and benchmark distributions, including multi-modal Gaussian mixtures and heavy-tailed distributions, to evaluate the effectiveness of RDMC. Baseline comparisons will include classical MCMC methods such as Langevin Monte Carlo (LMC) and Underdamped LMC (ULMC). Evaluation metrics will include convergence in Total Variation (TV) distance and Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), as well as gradient complexity and mixing time. The experimental setup will involve varying the separation between modes and the tail behavior of the target distributions to assess performance under different levels of difficulty. The impact of RDMC's improved isoperimetric and dimension dependence will be quantitatively analyzed, and ablations will test the efficiency of the different score estimation strategies.
e831d41650e4a724bdc58499c595378d41f3088f.novelty_claims: The proposed RDMC algorithm introduces a non-parametric, neural network-free approach to score estimation in reverse diffusion, transforming the problem into mean estimation over regularized posteriors. This method provides explicit control over sample complexity and error tolerance, enabling approximate sampling to any desired accuracy. RDMC is theoretically and empirically demonstrated to outperform classical MCMC methods in scenarios with poor isoperimetric properties, such as multi-modal and heavy-tailed distributions, by reducing or eliminating exponential dependencies on problem parameters like mode separation or dimensionality. The approach offers a new perspective on diffusion-based sampling, providing convergence guarantees and complexity analyses that are independent of the log-Sobolev constant of the target distribution.

e85213146c7f50474c72116f33d36196c1c2e857.title: Masked Diffusion Models are Secretly Time-Agnostic Masked Models and Exploit Inaccurate Categorical Sampling
e85213146c7f50474c72116f33d36196c1c2e857.research_question: Can the theoretical and empirical properties of masked diffusion models (MDMs) for discrete generative modeling be fully understood and improved by reformulating their training and sampling processes, and how do these models compare to auto-regressive models (ARMs) in terms of efficiency, generation quality, and numerical stability?
e85213146c7f50474c72116f33d36196c1c2e857.hypothesis: Masked diffusion models are theoretically equivalent to time-agnostic masked models, and their perceived advantages over auto-regressive models in text generation are due to numerical artifacts in categorical sampling rather than inherent modeling superiority. Furthermore, a novel sampling approach can significantly improve the efficiency of MDMs without loss of generation quality.
e85213146c7f50474c72116f33d36196c1c2e857.proposed_method: The proposed research will rigorously analyze the training objective of MDMs, reformulating the evidence lower bound (ELBO) in terms of the number of masked tokens rather than a continuous time variable, thus demonstrating time-agnostic equivalence to masked models. A new sampling algorithm, the first-hitting sampler (FHS), will be developed, which analytically samples the first time a masked token is unmasked, reducing the computational cost of categorical sampling from O(NL|X|) to O(L|X|). The FHS will be extended to parallel and high-order variants for further efficiency gains. Additionally, the research will investigate the impact of floating-point precision and Gumbel-based categorical sampling on generation diversity and fairness of evaluation, providing a closed-form analysis of truncated Gumbel effects.
e85213146c7f50474c72116f33d36196c1c2e857.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using pretrained models (AR, SEDD Absorb, MDLM) with identical architectures and training configurations on the OpenWebText dataset. Evaluation will focus on generative perplexity and entropy, using both the original and proposed first-hitting samplers, under varying floating-point precisions (32-bit and 64-bit) to isolate numerical effects. Baseline comparisons will include ARMs and existing MDM sampling strategies, with additional ablations on temperature scaling and batch sizes. Wall-clock inference time and number of function evaluations (NFE) will be measured to quantify efficiency improvements.
e85213146c7f50474c72116f33d36196c1c2e857.novelty_claims: The research claims a theoretical unification of MDMs and masked models by reformulating the training objective, and introduces the first-hitting sampler, a novel, analytically justified, and highly efficient sampling algorithm for MDMs. The work identifies and provides a closed-form analysis of a previously unrecognized numerical issue in Gumbel-based categorical sampling under low-precision arithmetic, which has led to unfairly optimistic evaluations of MDMs. The proposed methodology enables up to 20× speedup in sampling without loss of generation quality, and establishes a fairer benchmark for comparing MDMs and ARMs in discrete generative modeling.

e86b047eeb9d2f4b9fa6b15f253dd08c18eae820.title: DiSK: Differentially Private Optimizer with Simplified Kalman Filter for Noise Reduction
e86b047eeb9d2f4b9fa6b15f253dd08c18eae820.research_question: How can the performance of differentially private (DP) optimizers be improved for large-scale machine learning tasks, particularly by reducing the negative impact of noise injection while maintaining strong privacy guarantees?
e86b047eeb9d2f4b9fa6b15f253dd08c18eae820.hypothesis: Incorporating a simplified Kalman filter into the gradient estimation process of DP optimizers will significantly reduce the variance introduced by DP noise, leading to improved model performance (accuracy and convergence) under the same privacy constraints, without incurring prohibitive computational or memory overhead.
e86b047eeb9d2f4b9fa6b15f253dd08c18eae820.proposed_method: A new framework, DiSK, is proposed to enhance DP optimizers by integrating a simplified Kalman filter for denoising privatized gradients. The method models the gradient update process as a linear dynamic system, where the true gradient is the latent state and the privatized (noisy) gradient is the observation. The Kalman filter is adapted to this setting, using finite-difference approximations for Hessian-vector products and simplifying the observation matrix to the identity, thereby reducing the complexity of matrix operations to efficient scalar-vector multiplications. Further, the filter gain is fixed to a constant, and the algorithm requires only one additional forward pass and two extra optimizer states compared to standard DP-SGD. The denoised gradient estimate is then used in the parameter update step of any base DP optimizer (e.g., DP-SGD, DP-Adam), making the approach broadly compatible and scalable.
e86b047eeb9d2f4b9fa6b15f253dd08c18eae820.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of computer vision and natural language processing tasks, including training from scratch and fine-tuning. Datasets include MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k for vision, and GLUE, E2E, and DART for language tasks. Models such as 5-layer CNNs, WideResNet, ViT, RoBERTa, and GPT-2 will be evaluated. Baselines will include standard DP-SGD, DP-Adam, and DP-AdamW, with and without the DiSK framework. Evaluation metrics will primarily be test accuracy and convergence speed under fixed privacy budgets (e.g., epsilon=8, delta=1/N^1.1). Hyperparameters will be tuned via grid search, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of key parameters. The experimental setup will ensure fair privacy comparisons and include both pre-training and fine-tuning scenarios.
e86b047eeb9d2f4b9fa6b15f253dd08c18eae820.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a memory- and computation-efficient Kalman filtering framework for denoising gradients in DP optimization, enabling practical application to large-scale models. The method provides theoretical guarantees on convergence and privacy-utility trade-offs, with provable improvements in iteration complexity over standard DP optimizers. Unlike prior filtering methods, it does not require strong assumptions about gradient frequency or additional memory overhead. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on several benchmarks under the same privacy constraints, outperforming existing DP optimizers.

e8815da26d4e6cac8b23b7e6aa75cec028cb66d2.title: Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data
e8815da26d4e6cac8b23b7e6aa75cec028cb66d2.research_question: What are the effects of accumulating both real and synthetic data, as opposed to replacing data, on the phenomenon of model collapse in generative models trained iteratively on their own outputs across various modalities and architectures?
e8815da26d4e6cac8b23b7e6aa75cec028cb66d2.hypothesis: Accumulating synthetic data alongside real data during iterative training of generative models prevents or significantly mitigates model collapse, resulting in bounded test error across iterations, whereas replacing data with synthetic data leads to unbounded error growth and degraded model performance.
e8815da26d4e6cac8b23b7e6aa75cec028cb66d2.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves empirically and theoretically investigating the effects of data accumulation versus data replacement in iterative training loops of generative models. Sequences of generative models—including transformer-based language models, diffusion models for molecular conformation, and variational autoencoders for image data—will be trained for multiple generations. In each generation, synthetic data will be generated by the current model and either replace the previous training set or be accumulated (concatenated) with all prior data, including the original real data. For theoretical analysis, a mathematically tractable framework based on sequences of linear models will be extended to precisely characterize test error dynamics under both accumulation and replacement regimes. Analytical results will be validated with numerical simulations.
e8815da26d4e6cac8b23b7e6aa75cec028cb66d2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three domains: (1) Language modeling using transformer architectures (GPT-2 and Llama2 at various scales) trained on the TinyStories dataset, with synthetic data generated at different sampling temperatures and either replaced or accumulated at each iteration; (2) Molecular conformation generation using the GeoDiff diffusion model on a downsampled GEOM-Drugs dataset, with iterative training and data handling as above; (3) Image generation using variational autoencoders trained on the CelebA dataset, with iterative synthetic data generation and accumulation or replacement. Baseline comparisons will include both the replace and accumulate regimes, as well as an ablation where the synthetic dataset size is matched to the accumulated regime. Evaluation metrics will include cross-entropy loss for language models, standard loss functions for diffusion and VAE models, and qualitative assessments of generated outputs. Theoretical predictions will be validated with numerical simulations in the linear model setting, measuring test mean squared error across iterations.
e8815da26d4e6cac8b23b7e6aa75cec028cb66d2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive empirical and theoretical investigation into the effects of accumulating versus replacing data in iterative generative model training, spanning multiple model architectures and data modalities. It claims to provide the first rigorous demonstration that data accumulation robustly prevents model collapse, with both empirical evidence across deep learning models and a new theoretical analysis showing test error remains bounded under accumulation. The work extends prior analytical frameworks to the accumulation regime and offers practical insights for future dataset curation and generative model training in real-world, web-scale environments.

e8df1cf6742b50a15500b8dd3dde3942e9c91418.title: Alphazero-like Tree-Search can Guide Large Language Model Decoding and Training
e8df1cf6742b50a15500b8dd3dde3942e9c91418.research_question: Can AlphaZero-like tree-search algorithms, equipped with a learned value function, be used to guide large language model (LLM) decoding and training across a diverse set of tasks and search depths, thereby improving reasoning, planning, alignment, and decision-making capabilities?
e8df1cf6742b50a15500b8dd3dde3942e9c91418.hypothesis: Integrating an AlphaZero-inspired tree-search framework with a learned value function into LLM inference and training will enable more effective multi-step reasoning and long-horizon planning, outperforming existing prompt-based and shallow tree-search approaches, and will generalize across models of varying sizes and task domains.
e8df1cf6742b50a15500b8dd3dde3942e9c91418.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed TS-LLM, will be developed that formulates language generation as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and applies AlphaZero-like tree-search algorithms to guide LLM decoding and training. The method will employ a learned value function and outcome reward model (ORM), both implemented as decoder-only transformers, to evaluate intermediate and final states during tree search. Tree-search variants such as MCTS-α (AlphaZero-style MCTS with value backup), MCTS-Rollout, BFS-V, and DFS-V will be explored, supporting both sentence-level and token-level action nodes to accommodate tasks with different granularity and planning horizons. During inference, tree search will generate improved trajectories, which will be used to augment the training set. Training will proceed iteratively: policy distillation will update the LLM based on tree-search-improved samples, and the value function and ORM will be refined using ground-truth rewards and TD/MC targets. Aggregation strategies such as majority vote and ORM-based selection will be used to combine multiple tree-search outputs.
e8df1cf6742b50a15500b8dd3dde3942e9c91418.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of tasks, including mathematical reasoning (GSM8k), mathematical planning (Game24), logical reasoning (PrOntoQA), RLHF alignment (using synthetic RLHF data), and chess endgame decision-making. Models of varying sizes (from 125M to 7B parameters) will be evaluated. Baselines will include prompt-based tree-search (e.g., ToT-GPT3.5), direct decoding (CoT-greedy), self-consistency (CoT-SC), and rejection sampling (RFT), as well as PPO for RLHF alignment. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, cumulative reward, and win rate, with careful control of computational budgets (e.g., equal-token comparisons) to ensure fair assessment. Tree-search hyperparameters such as tree width and depth will be systematically varied to assess scalability. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of data diversity and amount on value function learning, as well as the effect of search space parameters.
e8df1cf6742b50a15500b8dd3dde3942e9c91418.novelty_claims: The proposed TS-LLM framework introduces a generally applicable and scalable AlphaZero-like tree-search paradigm for LLMs, supporting both inference-time decoding and iterative training. Unlike prior methods that rely on prompt-based value estimation and are limited to shallow search, TS-LLM leverages a learned value function and ORM, enabling deep tree search (up to depth 64) and applicability to a wide range of tasks and model sizes. The framework supports both sentence-level and token-level action spaces, and provides a new training paradigm that iteratively improves policy and value networks through tree-search-guided data augmentation. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior performance over existing approaches in both shallow and deep search domains, as well as improved reliability and generalizability of the learned value function compared to prompt-based counterparts.

e8e035f9768a4d4e7fe9a2e167cd93d170407b1b.title: Aligning Language Models with Preferences through f-divergence Minimization
e8e035f9768a4d4e7fe9a2e167cd93d170407b1b.research_question: How can language models be effectively aligned with diverse human preferences by approximating target distributions, and what is the impact of different divergence objectives on alignment and diversity trade-offs?
e8e035f9768a4d4e7fe9a2e167cd93d170407b1b.hypothesis: Different choices of f-divergence objectives for aligning language models with target distributions will yield distinct trade-offs between alignment quality and output diversity, and there is no universally optimal divergence; however, certain divergences, such as Jensen-Shannon, may offer a superior balance across tasks.
e8e035f9768a4d4e7fe9a2e167cd93d170407b1b.proposed_method: A unified framework, termed f-DPG, will be developed to fine-tune language models by minimizing any f-divergence between a parametric model and a target distribution representing desired behaviors or preferences. The method generalizes and subsumes both Distributional Policy Gradient (DPG) and Reinforcement Learning with KL penalties (RLHF) by allowing the use of forward KL, reverse KL, Total Variation, Jensen-Shannon, or any other f-divergence as the optimization objective. The approach involves deriving a universal stochastic gradient estimator for any f-divergence, incorporating variance reduction techniques such as baselines, and supporting both unconditional and conditional (context-dependent) target distributions. The target distributions may be defined via binary, scalar, or distributional preferences, and normalization constants are estimated via importance sampling. The method is designed to be compatible with standard autoregressive language models and scalable to large parameter counts.
e8e035f9768a4d4e7fe9a2e167cd93d170407b1b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse array of thirteen language model alignment tasks, including imposing sentiment and lexical constraints, debiasing gender and religious regard, enforcing factual consistency in summarization, and ensuring code compilability. Target distributions will be modeled using binary, scalar, and distributional preferences. Four variants of f-DPG (KL, reverse KL, TV, JS) will be evaluated, with each variant minimizing a different f-divergence. Baselines will include prior approaches such as standard DPG (forward KL) and RLHF (reverse KL). Evaluation metrics will comprise multiple f-divergences (forward KL, reverse KL, TV, JS), alignment scores (e.g., feature moments, classifier scores), diversity (normalized entropy), and task-specific metrics (e.g., Rouge for summarization, success ratio for lexical constraints). Experiments will be run on pretrained GPT-2 models of varying sizes (117M to 1.5B parameters) to assess scaling trends, and ablation studies will examine the effects of parameter family capacity, training schemes, and variance reduction techniques.
e8e035f9768a4d4e7fe9a2e167cd93d170407b1b.novelty_claims: The proposed framework, f-DPG, unifies and generalizes previous approaches to language model alignment by enabling minimization of any f-divergence to any evaluable target distribution, including both explicit and implicit forms. It introduces a universal gradient estimator for f-divergence minimization, supports variance reduction and conditional distributions, and systematically explores the impact of divergence choice on alignment-diversity trade-offs. Empirical results demonstrate that different divergences yield distinct outcomes, with Jensen-Shannon divergence often providing the best balance between alignment and diversity, outperforming prior methods. The framework’s flexibility and scalability are validated across a wide range of tasks and model sizes, highlighting the critical importance of selecting appropriate divergence objectives for effective language model alignment.

e91d4c1ac468acb67aa1288f8734128647d20bed.title: RoSTE: An Efficient Quantization-Aware Supervised Fine-Tuning Approach for Large Language Models
e91d4c1ac468acb67aa1288f8734128647d20bed.research_question: How can quantization-aware supervised fine-tuning be improved to enable efficient and accurate low-bit quantized large language models for downstream tasks, while minimizing performance degradation and computational overhead?
e91d4c1ac468acb67aa1288f8734128647d20bed.hypothesis: Jointly optimizing quantized weights and adaptive rotation matrices during supervised fine-tuning, using a quantization-aware approach that reduces activation outliers, will produce low-bit quantized large language models that achieve higher accuracy and efficiency compared to conventional post-training quantization or standard quantization-aware training.
e91d4c1ac468acb67aa1288f8734128647d20bed.proposed_method: A novel quantization-aware supervised fine-tuning (QA-SFT) algorithm, termed Rotated Straight-Through-Estimator (RoSTE), is proposed. The method formulates the problem as a bilevel optimization, where the upper-level subproblem optimizes quantized weight matrices for the fine-tuning objective, and the lower-level subproblem adaptively selects rotation matrices (either identity or random Walsh-Hadamard) to minimize quantization error. The approach alternates between (i) a QAT subroutine using a rotation-enabled straight-through estimator (STE) for gradient updates, and (ii) a low-complexity heuristic search for optimal rotation configurations based on quantization error surrogates. The quantization scheme targets 4-bit quantization for weights, activations, and KV caches, and leverages group-wise scaling and shifting for practical efficiency. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the use of quantization error as a surrogate loss for rotation selection and to demonstrate the convergence properties of the STE-based training under this framework.
e91d4c1ac468acb67aa1288f8734128647d20bed.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple large language models, including Pythia (1B/6.9B), Qwen (0.5B/7B), and Llama (3.1 8B), fine-tuned on datasets such as Reddit TL;DR summarization and Tulu 3 SFT mixture. Evaluation will use standard downstream tasks and metrics, including ROUGE for summarization and benchmarks like TruthfulQA, MMLU-Pro, BigBenchHard, AGIEval, GSM8K, and MATH for general language understanding. Baselines will include post-training quantization methods (RTN, GPTQ, QuaRot, SpinQuant) and quantization-aware training with standard STE. The evaluation will compare accuracy, training time, and quantization error, with all experiments run on 8×NVIDIA A100 GPUs. The effect of rotation strategies and ablation studies on rotation adaptation will also be assessed.
e91d4c1ac468acb67aa1288f8734128647d20bed.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is among the first to jointly optimize quantized weights and adaptive rotation matrices within a single quantization-aware supervised fine-tuning process for large language models. The method introduces a bilevel optimization framework that explicitly leverages quantization error as a surrogate for rotation selection, and integrates efficient Walsh-Hadamard rotations to mitigate activation outliers. Theoretical insights are provided to justify the approach, and experimental results demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art post-training and quantization-aware baselines across various model architectures and tasks. The adaptive rotation strategy is shown to be critical for achieving high accuracy in low-bit quantized models.

e97addc2c9d137ca53a73d41ad59083c1a4cf214.title: Oobleck: Resilient Distributed Training of Large Models Using Pipeline Templates
e97addc2c9d137ca53a73d41ad59083c1a4cf214.research_question: How can distributed training of large deep neural network models be made resilient to failures while maximizing throughput and minimizing recovery overhead, particularly in hybrid-parallel training environments?
e97addc2c9d137ca53a73d41ad59083c1a4cf214.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that precomputing and utilizing a set of heterogeneous pipeline templates, combined with maintaining multiple logically equivalent pipeline replicas, can provide provable fault tolerance and high throughput for distributed training of large models, even under frequent failures.
e97addc2c9d137ca53a73d41ad59083c1a4cf214.proposed_method: A novel distributed training framework is proposed that leverages a planning-execution co-design. In the planning phase, a pipeline template generator creates a set of heterogeneous pipeline templates, each specifying the number of nodes, stage partitioning, and GPU-to-stage mapping for a given model. During execution, at least f+1 logically equivalent pipeline replicas are instantiated from these templates to tolerate up to f simultaneous failures. The execution engine dynamically reconfigures pipelines upon node failures by reinstantiating from precomputed templates, redistributing batch sizes to balance workload, and copying missing model states from surviving replicas. The method includes an integer optimization-based batch distribution mechanism and a divide-and-conquer algorithm for optimal pipeline partitioning, ensuring minimal iteration time and maximal resource utilization.
e97addc2c9d137ca53a73d41ad59083c1a4cf214.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on clusters of up to 30 NVIDIA A40 GPUs, evaluating models ranging from 340M to 6.7B parameters, including BERT-Large, GPT-2, and multiple GPT-3 variants. The evaluation will compare the proposed method against state-of-the-art baselines such as Bamboo and Varuna under various failure frequencies (from every 6 hours to every 10 minutes) and real-world spot instance preemption traces from AWS and GCP. Throughput (samples/sec) will be the primary metric, with additional analysis of recovery time, GPU utilization, and planning overhead. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by tuning batch sizes for each framework and using high-speed networking and storage to isolate the effects of the fault-tolerance mechanisms.
e97addc2c9d137ca53a73d41ad59083c1a4cf214.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of pipeline templates for hybrid-parallel training, enabling fast, restart-free recovery from failures and systematic resource utilization guarantees. Unlike prior work, the method provides provable fault tolerance for up to f simultaneous failures without checkpoint restarts, supports heterogeneous pipeline instantiation, and achieves high throughput even for large models and frequent failures. The framework also features a novel planning algorithm for generating pipeline templates and a dynamic execution engine for efficient, balanced batch distribution and rapid reconfiguration. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate significant throughput improvements over existing fault-tolerant training solutions.

e9ae8e12ba18430ab501c8b1f70ec5c66a92ba98.title: Data Scaling Laws in Imitation Learning for Robotic Manipulation
e9ae8e12ba18430ab501c8b1f70ec5c66a92ba98.research_question: Do data scaling laws exist in imitation learning for robotic manipulation, and can appropriate data scaling enable single-task robot policies to generalize to any object within the same category and any environment without fine-tuning?
e9ae8e12ba18430ab501c8b1f70ec5c66a92ba98.hypothesis: Scaling the diversity of environments and objects in imitation learning demonstrations will yield a power-law improvement in policy generalization, and there exists an efficient data collection strategy that enables strong zero-shot generalization to novel environments and objects.
e9ae8e12ba18430ab501c8b1f70ec5c66a92ba98.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical study will be conducted to investigate data scaling laws in imitation learning for robotic manipulation. Human demonstrations will be collected using a portable hand-held gripper (UMI) across a wide variety of real-world environments and objects within the same category. The collected data will be used to train single-task policies using a Diffusion Policy framework, employing a CNN-based U-Net as the noise prediction network, DDIM for inference acceleration, and a DINOv2 ViT-Large/14 visual encoder for enhanced spatial reasoning. A temporal ensemble strategy will be implemented to smooth action transitions. The study will systematically vary the number of training environments, objects, and demonstrations to analyze their effects on policy generalization, and will fit power-law models to the observed generalization performance.
e9ae8e12ba18430ab501c8b1f70ec5c66a92ba98.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on multiple robotic manipulation tasks, including Pour Water, Mouse Arrangement, Fold Towels, and Unplug Charger. For each task, demonstrations will be collected across up to 32 environments and 32 objects, with 50-120 demonstrations per environment-object pair, resulting in over 40,000 demonstrations and 15,000 real-world robot rollouts. Policies will be evaluated exclusively in unseen environments and with unseen objects, using a normalized score based on tester-assigned stage-wise criteria as the primary evaluation metric, alongside success rates. Baselines will include varying the number of environments, objects, and demonstrations, as well as ablations on model size and training strategies. Multiple policies will be evaluated in parallel under identical initial conditions to ensure fair comparison.
e9ae8e12ba18430ab501c8b1f70ec5c66a92ba98.novelty_claims: The proposed research will establish, for the first time, empirical data scaling laws for imitation learning in robotic manipulation, demonstrating a power-law relationship between policy generalization and the number of environments and objects. It will reveal that diversity of environments and objects is significantly more important than the absolute number of demonstrations per instance. An efficient data collection strategy will be derived and validated, enabling rapid training of highly generalizable single-task policies with modest data collection efforts. The study will also provide insights into the effects of model size and training strategy on generalization, and release code, data, and models to support further research.

e9b9a47cd81c66603c827f0f2bc4fba0d9ae77c4.title: A Continuous Time Framework for Discrete Denoising Models
e9b9a47cd81c66603c827f0f2bc4fba0d9ae77c4.research_question: How can a continuous time framework be developed for denoising diffusion models on discrete data, and does such a framework enable more flexible and higher-quality generative modeling compared to discrete time approaches?
e9b9a47cd81c66603c827f0f2bc4fba0d9ae77c4.hypothesis: A continuous time Markov chain (CTMC) formulation for discrete denoising diffusion models will enable more flexible training and sampling, allow for efficient simulation via tau-leaping, and yield higher-quality generative samples than existing discrete time methods.
e9b9a47cd81c66603c827f0f2bc4fba0d9ae77c4.proposed_method: A novel continuous time framework is proposed for discrete denoising diffusion models by formulating both the forward noising process and the reverse generative process as Continuous Time Markov Chains (CTMCs). The forward process is defined by a rate matrix that rapidly mixes the data distribution toward a simple stationary distribution, and the reverse process is parameterized by a neural denoising network that approximates the intractable reverse CTMC rates. Training is performed by minimizing a continuous time Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO), which is derived as an upper bound on the negative log-likelihood of the data under the model. For efficient sampling, tau-leaping is used to simulate the high-dimensional reverse CTMC, and a predictor-corrector scheme is introduced to further improve sample quality by bringing the sample marginals closer to the target distribution at each time step. The method also includes a theoretical analysis, providing a bound on the error between the generated sample distribution and the true data distribution.
e9b9a47cd81c66603c827f0f2bc4fba0d9ae77c4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world discrete data, including the CIFAR-10 image dataset (modeled in discrete space) and monophonic music sequences from the Lakh pianoroll dataset. The proposed method will be compared to state-of-the-art discrete time denoising diffusion models such as D3PM, as well as continuous state diffusion models for reference. Evaluation metrics will include Inception Score (IS), Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Hellinger distance between generated and true distributions, and the proportion of outlier samples. For image experiments, a U-net architecture will be used for the denoising network, and for music, a transformer-based model will be employed. The impact of tau-leaping step size and the number of corrector steps on sample quality and computational efficiency will be systematically studied.
e9b9a47cd81c66603c827f0f2bc4fba0d9ae77c4.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to provide a complete continuous time formulation for denoising diffusion models on discrete data. It introduces the use of CTMCs for both forward and reverse processes, a continuous time ELBO for efficient training, and adapts tau-leaping from chemical physics for high-dimensional generative sampling. The predictor-corrector scheme for discrete CTMCs is novel and demonstrably improves sample quality. Additionally, a new theoretical error bound is derived for the gap between the generated and true data distributions under tau-leaping, with explicit dependence on data dimensionality. Experimental results indicate that the method can outperform previous discrete time approaches on discrete data, narrowing the gap with continuous state models.

e9bf8602e26f50c4bd169e81a7b6e4c7a8d7ad25.title: Mastering Multiple-Expert Routing: Realizable H-Consistency and Strong Guarantees for Learning to Defer
e9bf8602e26f50c4bd169e81a7b6e4c7a8d7ad25.research_question: How can input instances be optimally assigned to the most suitable expert from a diverse set, balancing considerations of accuracy and computational cost, in both single-stage and two-stage learning-to-defer scenarios with multiple experts? What theoretical and practical guarantees can be established for such allocation strategies, particularly in terms of consistency properties of surrogate loss functions?
e9bf8602e26f50c4bd169e81a7b6e4c7a8d7ad25.hypothesis: Surrogate loss functions can be designed for both single-stage and two-stage multiple-expert deferral that achieve realizable H-consistency, H-consistency bounds, and Bayes-consistency, thereby enabling optimal and theoretically grounded allocation of instances to experts under various cost and noise assumptions.
e9bf8602e26f50c4bd169e81a7b6e4c7a8d7ad25.proposed_method: A new family of surrogate loss functions will be developed for both single-stage and two-stage learning-to-defer scenarios with multiple experts. For the single-stage case, the method will derive an alternative formulation of the deferral loss and replace indicator functions with smooth surrogate losses, such as comp-sum losses (including generalized cross-entropy and mean absolute error losses), parameterized by a function Ψ. The method will establish conditions under which these surrogate losses are realizable H-consistent and admit H-consistency bounds. For the two-stage case, margin-based surrogate losses will be constructed for both two-expert and general multiple-expert settings, using decreasing functions Φ or Ψ, and their consistency properties will be analyzed under natural cost and noise assumptions. Enhanced theoretical guarantees will be provided under low-noise (Tsybakov-type) assumptions, bridging the gap between realizable H-consistency and standard H-consistency bounds.
e9bf8602e26f50c4bd169e81a7b6e4c7a8d7ad25.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard datasets such as CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, and TinyImageNet, using ResNet-16 architectures for predictors and deferral models. Both single-stage and two-stage scenarios will be evaluated, with experts defined by domain-specific prediction ranges and cost functions based on classification error. Baseline methods will include previously proposed surrogate losses that are Bayes-consistent but not realizable H-consistent. Evaluation metrics will include system accuracy (average of 1 minus deferral loss on test data) and deferral ratios to each expert. Additional experiments will be performed on a synthetic, realizable Mixture-of-Gaussians dataset to assess performance in settings where realizable H-consistency is critical. Results will be averaged over multiple runs, and both accuracy and deferral behavior will be compared to state-of-the-art baselines.
e9bf8602e26f50c4bd169e81a7b6e4c7a8d7ad25.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first family of surrogate loss functions for multiple-expert deferral that simultaneously achieve realizable H-consistency, H-consistency bounds, and Bayes-consistency in both single-stage and two-stage settings. The method provides enhanced theoretical guarantees under low-noise assumptions, which interpolate between realizable and standard consistency bounds. Empirical results demonstrate that the new surrogate losses match or exceed the performance of existing baselines in both realizable and non-realizable scenarios, and uniquely guarantee near-zero error in realizable settings, which prior methods cannot achieve.

e9c5d9797ec6e577bd0d6a46a034786317dafdff.title: Localizing Memorization in SSL Vision Encoders
e9c5d9797ec6e577bd0d6a46a034786317dafdff.research_question: Where does memorization occur within self-supervised learning (SSL) vision encoders, and how can memorization be systematically localized at both the layer and unit (neuron/channel) level across different architectures and datasets?
e9c5d9797ec6e577bd0d6a46a034786317dafdff.hypothesis: Memorization in SSL vision encoders can be effectively localized to specific layers and individual units using metrics that do not require labels or downstream tasks, and such localization will reveal distinct patterns compared to supervised learning models, with practical implications for fine-tuning and pruning.
e9c5d9797ec6e577bd0d6a46a034786317dafdff.proposed_method: Two novel metrics, LayerMem and UnitMem, will be developed to localize memorization within SSL vision encoders. LayerMem will extend the SSLMem metric to measure memorization at each encoder layer by comparing the alignment of representations from two encoders trained with and without a specific data point, normalized for interpretability. UnitMem will quantify the sensitivity of individual units (neurons or channels) to specific training data points by measuring the difference between a unit's maximum activation for a data point and its mean activation for all other points, averaged over augmentations. Both metrics will be computed in a label-free, task-agnostic manner using only forward passes, enabling efficient analysis of large SSL models. The methodology will also include normalization steps and statistical analyses to ensure robustness and interpretability.
e9c5d9797ec6e577bd0d6a46a034786317dafdff.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of vision datasets, including CIFAR10, CIFAR100, SVHN, STL10, and ImageNet, using various SSL frameworks such as SimCLR, DINO, and MAE. Encoder architectures will include multiple ResNet variants (ResNet9, ResNet18, ResNet34, ResNet50) and Vision Transformers (ViT-Tiny, ViT-Base). Memorization will be localized and quantified at both the layer and unit level, with results compared across architectures, datasets, and SSL frameworks. Baseline comparisons will include supervised learning models and random or least-memorizing units/layers. Evaluation metrics will include the proposed LayerMem and UnitMem scores, linear probing accuracy after selective fine-tuning or pruning, and statistical measures such as Kendall's Tau for ranking consistency. Additional experiments will examine the impact of differential privacy and the relationship between data point and class memorization.
e9c5d9797ec6e577bd0d6a46a034786317dafdff.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first practical, label-agnostic metrics for localizing memorization in SSL vision encoders at both the layer and unit level. The approach enables fine-grained, efficient analysis of memorization patterns without reliance on downstream tasks or labels. The research will provide new insights into how memorization is distributed within SSL models, reveal differences from supervised learning, and demonstrate practical benefits for encoder fine-tuning and pruning strategies. The methods are broadly applicable across architectures and SSL frameworks, and the findings are expected to inform future SSL model design and privacy considerations.

e9c9ea9c463c3a4a0589b196a7ac708698723c9c.title: Efficient Test-Time Model Adaptation without Forgetting
e9c9ea9c463c3a4a0589b196a7ac708698723c9c.research_question: How can test-time adaptation methods be made more efficient and robust to distribution shifts, while avoiding catastrophic forgetting of in-distribution performance during adaptation?
e9c9ea9c463c3a4a0589b196a7ac708698723c9c.hypothesis: Selective adaptation using reliable and non-redundant test samples, combined with regularization of important model parameters, will improve the efficiency and robustness of test-time model adaptation and prevent catastrophic forgetting on in-distribution data.
e9c9ea9c463c3a4a0589b196a7ac708698723c9c.proposed_method: A novel test-time adaptation framework is developed that employs a sample-efficient entropy minimization strategy and an anti-forgetting regularizer. The method introduces an active sample selection criterion, where each incoming test sample is scored based on prediction entropy and output diversity; only samples with low entropy (reliable) and diverse outputs (non-redundant) are used for adaptation, thus reducing unnecessary backward computations. Adaptation is performed by minimizing the entropy loss over selected samples, updating only the affine parameters of batch normalization layers for efficiency. To address catastrophic forgetting, a Fisher information-based regularizer is incorporated, which penalizes changes to parameters deemed important for in-distribution performance; the Fisher information is estimated using pseudo-labeled in-distribution test samples. This dual strategy aims to balance adaptation to out-of-distribution data with retention of in-distribution accuracy.
e9c9ea9c463c3a4a0589b196a7ac708698723c9c.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed on standard robustness benchmarks including CIFAR-10-C, ImageNet-C, and ImageNet-R, using pre-trained ResNet architectures. The method will be compared against state-of-the-art test-time adaptation baselines such as TTT, Tent, MEMO, and batch norm adaptation. Evaluation metrics include out-of-distribution (OOD) accuracy/error, in-distribution (ID) accuracy/error after adaptation, and computational efficiency measured by the number of forward and backward passes required. The setup includes both batch and single-sample adaptation scenarios, as well as lifelong adaptation where model parameters are not reset between shifts. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of entropy thresholds, sample selection strategies, and the Fisher regularizer, and additional experiments will assess performance with varying numbers of test samples and network sizes.
e9c9ea9c463c3a4a0589b196a7ac708698723c9c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a sample-adaptive entropy minimization loss that selectively filters unreliable and redundant test samples, significantly improving adaptation efficiency. It extends Fisher-based regularization to the test-time adaptation setting using pseudo-labeled test data, effectively preventing catastrophic forgetting without access to original training data. The method achieves state-of-the-art robustness on multiple benchmarks, demonstrating both improved OOD performance and maintenance of ID accuracy, while reducing computational cost compared to existing methods.

e9efe9e01680c539ebf2581dc6cc8a10711df670.title: GIR: 3D Gaussian Inverse Rendering for Relightable Scene Factorization
e9efe9e01680c539ebf2581dc6cc8a10711df670.research_question: How can a unified, real-time inverse rendering framework be developed to accurately factorize scenes into geometry, material properties, and lighting from multi-view images, enabling high-quality relighting and material editing?
e9efe9e01680c539ebf2581dc6cc8a10711df670.hypothesis: A 3D Gaussian-based inverse rendering framework, equipped with explicit normal estimation, efficient indirect illumination tracing, and learnable high-resolution environmental lighting, will enable accurate, real-time scene factorization and outperform existing methods in relighting, novel view synthesis, and material editing tasks.
e9efe9e01680c539ebf2581dc6cc8a10711df670.proposed_method: A novel inverse rendering framework is proposed that represents scenes using explicit 3D Gaussians, each parameterized by position, anisotropic covariance, opacity, color (via spherical harmonics), albedo, roughness, and metallicity. Normals for each Gaussian are estimated using the shortest eigenvector of its covariance matrix, and a directional masking scheme is introduced to enforce correct normal orientation in a self-supervised manner. Direct illumination is modeled by a high-resolution environment map generated through a learnable low-resolution embedding and a fully convolutional network, which is pre-integrated for efficient physically-based rendering. Indirect illumination is approximated by tracing outgoing radiance using a voxelized grid of the scene, storing direction-aware information and leveraging trainable spherical harmonics to simulate multi-bounce light transport. The rendering pipeline employs a split-sum approximation for specular reflection and supports real-time performance.
e9efe9e01680c539ebf2581dc6cc8a10711df670.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several synthetic and real-world datasets, including TensoIR, Shiny Blender, Glossy Blender, and OWL, each providing multi-view images and ground truth for evaluation. The proposed method will be compared against baselines such as NeRFactor, NVDiffRec, NVDiffrecMC, InvRender, ENVIDR, NeRO, TensoIR, Gaussian Shader, GS-IR, and Relightable 3D Gaussian. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for novel view synthesis, relighting, and albedo estimation tasks. The experimental setup will adhere to standard training/testing splits, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of each module, including the FCN-based environment map, geometry and material regularization, indirect illumination, and directional masking. Rendering speed will be measured on both GPU inference and Unreal Engine integration to demonstrate real-time capabilities.
e9efe9e01680c539ebf2581dc6cc8a10711df670.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first unified, real-time inverse rendering approach based on 3D Gaussian splatting that enables explicit scene factorization into geometry, materials, and lighting. Key innovations include a self-supervised normal estimation method using the shortest eigenvector and directional masking, an efficient voxel-based indirect illumination tracing scheme, and a learnable, high-resolution environmental lighting model via a fully convolutional network. The method supports real-time rendering and interactive applications such as relighting and material editing, and achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks. Comprehensive ablation studies and comparisons demonstrate the effectiveness and broad applicability of the approach.

ea03e6469bf50eda150c7091022a8b03730a15be.title: Closed-Loop Long-Horizon Robotic Planning via Equilibrium Sequence Modeling
ea03e6469bf50eda150c7091022a8b03730a15be.research_question: How can long-horizon robotic planning be improved to translate high-level task descriptions into robust, closed-loop sequences of mid-level actions, especially when leveraging large language models (LLMs) that must incorporate environmental feedback and self-correct over extended planning horizons?
ea03e6469bf50eda150c7091022a8b03730a15be.hypothesis: A self-refining planning framework based on equilibrium sequence modeling, which iteratively refines draft plans until reaching an equilibrium point, will enable more effective closed-loop long-horizon robotic planning by allowing end-to-end supervised training, efficient incorporation of environmental feedback, and dynamic allocation of inference computation, outperforming existing LLM-based and tree-based planning methods.
ea03e6469bf50eda150c7091022a8b03730a15be.proposed_method: A novel equilibrium sequence modeling approach will be developed, framing robotic planning as a fixed-point optimization problem where a plan is iteratively refined until it becomes stable (the equilibrium). The method will leverage deep equilibrium models, enabling bidirectional dependency in plan generation and implicit self-correction without the need for additional verifiers or reward models.
