A nested equilibrium solving process will be introduced, with an inner loop for plan introspection and refinement using current feedback, and an outer loop for updating feedback through interaction with either the real environment or an internal world model. The planner will be trained end-to-end in a supervised fashion, utilizing an experience memory to cache equilibrium plans and a world model to simulate feedback, thus supporting efficient closed-loop planning and dynamic inference computation allocation.
ea03e6469bf50eda150c7091022a8b03730a15be.experiment_details: The proposed method will be evaluated on the VirtualHome-Env benchmark, which contains 1360 long-horizon tasks with ground truth action sequences and supports closed-loop feedback simulation. Experiments will include both settings without error correction and with up to 10 rounds of correction (self-correction based on feedback). Baselines will include Tree-Planner, SELF-REFINE, supervised finetuned planners, and several GPT-3.5-based planners. Evaluation metrics will be executability (Exec.), success rate (SR), and goal condition recall (GCR), with additional analysis of computational efficiency (TFLOPS) and scaling with inference computation. The experimental setup will involve finetuning Llama 3 8B models, using both real and simulated feedback, and ablation studies to assess the impact of feedback types, equilibrium reuse, and robustness to noisy feedback.
ea03e6469bf50eda150c7091022a8b03730a15be.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces equilibrium sequence modeling for self-refining LLM-based planners, enabling end-to-end supervised training without the need for reinforcement learning, curated verifiers, or reward models. The nested equilibrium process allows efficient closed-loop planning by incorporating both external and internal feedback, with dynamic computation allocation and reuse of previous equilibrium solutions. The method claims superior performance and scalability over existing prompting-based and tree-based planners, particularly in long-horizon and feedback-rich planning scenarios.

ea04174766c2cb2ab8a5ef3a424912a0dd0a4d51.title: Revisiting Discriminative vs. Generative Classifiers: Theory and Implications
ea04174766c2cb2ab8a5ef3a424912a0dd0a4d51.research_question: How do discriminative and generative linear classifiers compare in terms of sample efficiency and asymptotic error in multiclass settings, particularly when applied to deep representations extracted from pre-trained models? What are the theoretical and practical implications of using generative versus discriminative classifiers in linear evaluation for transfer learning?
ea04174766c2cb2ab8a5ef3a424912a0dd0a4d51.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under mild assumptions, multiclass naïve Bayes (a generative classifier) requires significantly fewer samples (O(log n), where n is feature dimension) to approach its asymptotic error compared to multiclass logistic regression (a discriminative classifier), which requires O(n) samples. Furthermore, naïve Bayes is expected to converge faster and perform better in few-shot scenarios, especially when applied to representations learned by supervised pre-training.
ea04174766c2cb2ab8a5ef3a424912a0dd0a4d51.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the sample complexity and convergence rates of multiclass generative (naïve Bayes) and discriminative (logistic regression) linear classifiers. The analysis will generalize classical binary results to the multiclass setting and will focus on surrogate loss functions, such as logistic loss, rather than the zero-one loss. A multiclass H-consistency bound framework will be introduced to relate the estimation error of surrogate losses to that of the zero-one loss, providing explicit and tight bounds for multiclass logistic regression. Theoretical results will be established under mild distributional assumptions, and explicit sample complexity bounds for both classifiers will be derived. The framework will be validated both analytically and empirically, considering the linear evaluation setting where pre-trained deep model representations are frozen and only the linear classifier is trained.
ea04174766c2cb2ab8a5ef3a424912a0dd0a4d51.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both synthetic data (e.g., mixtures of Gaussians) and real-world datasets such as CIFAR10 and CIFAR100. Various pre-trained deep vision models, including supervised (e.g., ResNet, ViT), self-supervised (e.g., MoCov2, SimCLR, MAE, SimMIM), and cross-modal (e.g., CLIP) models, will be used to extract features for linear evaluation. For each setting, the number of training samples will be varied, and the convergence of naïve Bayes and logistic regression to their respective asymptotic errors will be measured. Baselines will include standard logistic regression and naïve Bayes classifiers. Evaluation metrics will primarily be test error rates and convergence speed to asymptotic error. The occurrence of the 'two regimes' phenomenon (where naïve Bayes outperforms logistic regression in low-data regimes but is overtaken as sample size increases) will be systematically investigated. Empirical analysis will also assess the validity of theoretical assumptions on real data.
ea04174766c2cb2ab8a5ef3a424912a0dd0a4d51.novelty_claims: The proposed research generalizes the classical discriminative versus generative classifier comparison from binary to multiclass cases and replaces the impractical zero-one loss analysis with a rigorous surrogate loss (logistic loss) framework. A novel multiclass H-consistency bound is established, providing explicit and tight theoretical guarantees for the convergence of both naïve Bayes and logistic regression. The research claims that naïve Bayes achieves O(log n) sample complexity for approaching asymptotic error in multiclass settings, a result not previously established. Extensive empirical validation on deep representations from modern pre-trained models is proposed, revealing practical implications for transfer learning and highlighting differences between representations learned by supervised and self-supervised methods.

ea0e4a9778e33b7f8e7b3246d63071330950995a.title: Structure-Aware Transformer for Graph Representation Learning
ea0e4a9778e33b7f8e7b3246d63071330950995a.research_question: How can structural information be effectively encoded into Transformer architectures to improve graph representation learning, overcoming the limitations of current graph neural networks and position-aware Transformers?
ea0e4a9778e33b7f8e7b3246d63071330950995a.hypothesis: Incorporating explicit structural information into the self-attention mechanism of Transformers by leveraging subgraph-based representations will yield node and graph representations that are at least as expressive as those produced by state-of-the-art GNNs, and will improve performance on graph property prediction tasks.
ea0e4a9778e33b7f8e7b3246d63071330950995a.proposed_method: A novel Structure-Aware Transformer (SAT) framework will be developed, introducing a new self-attention mechanism that explicitly incorporates local graph structure. This is achieved by extracting a subgraph representation rooted at each node, using structure extractors such as k-hop subgraph GNNs or k-subtree GNNs, which generate node-level embeddings that encode both attribute and structural similarity. The self-attention kernel is reformulated to compare these subgraph representations, allowing the attention mechanism to be sensitive to both node features and their local graph topology. The architecture will support flexible integration of any GNN or differentiable graph kernel as the structure extractor, and will allow for the combination of structure-aware attention with absolute positional encodings (e.g., random walk or Laplacian positional encodings) for further representational power. The overall model will follow the standard Transformer stacking of multi-head self-attention, skip connections, feed-forward networks, and normalization, with graph-level representations obtained via pooling or [CLS] token strategies.
ea0e4a9778e33b7f8e7b3246d63071330950995a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five medium-to-large benchmark datasets for node and graph property prediction, including ZINC, CLUSTER, PATTERN, OGBG-PPA, and OGBG-CODE2. The SAT models will be evaluated using various structure extractors (e.g., GCN, GIN, GraphSAGE, PNA) and compared against state-of-the-art GNNs (such as GCN, GIN, PNA, DeeperGCN, ExpC) and graph Transformers (including vanilla Transformer with positional encoding, Graph Transformer, SAN, Graphormer, and GraphTrans). Evaluation metrics will include mean absolute error (MAE), accuracy, and F1 score, depending on the dataset. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of the size of the subgraph (k), the choice of absolute positional encoding, and the readout method. Model interpretability will be analyzed through attention visualization. All experiments will use consistent hyperparameter settings, with further details provided in supplementary material.
ea0e4a9778e33b7f8e7b3246d63071330950995a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a flexible structure-aware self-attention mechanism for Transformers that explicitly encodes local graph structure, overcoming the limitations of both message-passing GNNs (such as limited expressiveness, over-smoothing, and over-squashing) and position-aware Transformers (which lack structural similarity awareness). The framework allows for the integration of any GNN or graph kernel as a structure extractor, systematically enhancing the expressiveness of the base model. Theoretical analysis guarantees that the resulting node representations are at least as expressive as the underlying subgraph representations. Empirical results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on multiple graph prediction benchmarks, and the method provides improved interpretability over classic Transformers.

ea14465601f45bf50a148563c73c4d6e1971dcb1.title: Redeeming Intrinsic Rewards via Constrained Optimization
ea14465601f45bf50a148563c73c4d6e1971dcb1.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents automatically and dynamically balance intrinsic and extrinsic rewards to achieve consistent and superior performance across tasks with varying exploration difficulty, without requiring manual tuning of reward trade-off parameters?
ea14465601f45bf50a148563c73c4d6e1971dcb1.hypothesis: A constrained optimization approach that enforces an extrinsic optimality constraint—ensuring that the agent's policy achieves extrinsic rewards at least as high as the optimal extrinsic-only policy—will enable automatic and dynamic adjustment of the importance of intrinsic rewards, leading to consistent and improved performance across both easy and hard exploration tasks.
ea14465601f45bf50a148563c73c4d6e1971dcb1.proposed_method: A novel policy optimization algorithm, Extrinsic-Intrinsic Policy Optimization (EIPO), is developed to address the challenge of balancing intrinsic and extrinsic rewards in reinforcement learning. EIPO formulates the problem as a constrained optimization, where the agent maximizes a mixed reward objective (extrinsic plus intrinsic rewards) subject to an extrinsic optimality constraint that ensures the extrinsic return is not degraded relative to the optimal extrinsic-only policy. The constraint is handled via Lagrangian duality, resulting in an unconstrained min-max optimization problem over policy parameters and a Lagrange multiplier (alpha) that dynamically tunes the trade-off between exploration (intrinsic reward) and exploitation (extrinsic reward). The algorithm alternates between optimizing the mixed policy and the extrinsic-only policy, using shared neural network backbones with auxiliary objectives to prevent interference, and updates the Lagrange multiplier based on observed returns. This approach is agnostic to the choice of intrinsic reward function and can be integrated with any RL algorithm.
ea14465601f45bf50a148563c73c4d6e1971dcb1.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted primarily on the ATARI 2600 benchmark suite, encompassing 61 diverse games with varying exploration difficulty, as well as on a 2D navigation environment and the MuJoCo continuous control benchmark. The main intrinsic reward method used is Random Network Distillation (RND), with EIPO compared against several baselines: extrinsic-only (EO), RND with fixed and decayed intrinsic reward scaling, normalized extrinsic rewards (EN), and Decoupled-RND (DC) which regularizes policy similarity. All policies are trained using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Evaluation metrics include the median extrinsic return over the last 100 episodes, probability of improvement across games, and PPO-normalized scores with confidence intervals. Hyperparameter sweeps over the intrinsic reward scaling coefficient (lambda) are performed for RND to assess the necessity of dynamic tuning. Multiple random seeds are used for statistical robustness.
ea14465601f45bf50a148563c73c4d6e1971dcb1.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled, constrained optimization framework for redeeming intrinsic rewards in RL, eliminating the need for manual or per-task tuning of reward trade-offs. EIPO is the first to enforce an extrinsic optimality constraint, ensuring that exploration bonuses do not degrade task performance. The dynamic adjustment of the exploration-exploitation trade-off via a learned Lagrange multiplier is shown to outperform both fixed and decaying schedules. EIPO achieves consistent and superior performance across a wide range of tasks, including both easy and hard exploration settings, and can be used as a drop-in replacement in any RL pipeline, regardless of the intrinsic reward mechanism.

ea3448eb86a233189631d914721e587d45931b64.title: MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark
ea3448eb86a233189631d914721e587d45931b64.research_question: How can the temporal understanding capabilities of multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) be comprehensively evaluated, and what methods can be developed to improve their performance on temporally-sensitive video understanding tasks?
ea3448eb86a233189631d914721e587d45931b64.hypothesis: Current MLLMs are insufficient in temporal video understanding, and a benchmark specifically designed for temporal tasks, along with robust multi-modal instruction tuning, will reveal these limitations and enable the development of models with significantly improved temporal reasoning capabilities.
ea3448eb86a233189631d914721e587d45931b64.proposed_method: A comprehensive multi-modal video understanding benchmark, termed MVBench, will be constructed by systematically transforming static image-based tasks into dynamic, temporally-sensitive video tasks. This transformation employs a static-to-dynamic methodology, converting spatial tasks (e.g., object position, action recognition) into their temporal counterparts (e.g., moving direction, action sequence) that require reasoning over entire video clips. Multiple-choice QA pairs for each task will be automatically generated by leveraging public video annotations from 11 diverse datasets, with question and answer options created using large language models (LLMs) and template-based methods. To ensure fairness and reduce manual bias, all questions will be grounded in existing annotations, and a standardized evaluation protocol using detailed system and answer prompts will be established. Additionally, a robust video MLLM baseline (VideoChat2) will be developed using progressive multi-modal training, incorporating a large-scale, diverse instruction-tuning dataset that spans both image and video modalities.
ea3448eb86a233189631d914721e587d45931b64.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on MVBench, which comprises 20 temporally-sensitive tasks and 200 multiple-choice QA pairs per task, sourced from 11 public video datasets such as STAR, CLEVRER, Charades-STA, and TVQA. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art image and video MLLMs (e.g., LLaVA, VideoChat, VideoChatGPT, VideoLLaMA, BLIP2, Otter, InstructBLIP, GPT-4V), with all models evaluated under standardized input conditions (e.g., 16-frame videos at 224x224 resolution). Evaluation metrics will focus on accuracy in multiple-choice QA, with additional assessments on video conversation and zero-shot video QA benchmarks (e.g., MSVD-QA, MSRVTT-QA, ANet-QA). Ablation studies will analyze the impact of instruction data diversity, model architecture choices (visual encoder, LLM, QFormer), training strategies, and prompt design on temporal understanding performance.
ea3448eb86a233189631d914721e587d45931b64.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark, MVBench, uniquely covers a wide range of temporally-sensitive video understanding tasks that cannot be solved with single-frame analysis, enabling comprehensive evaluation of temporal reasoning in MLLMs. The static-to-dynamic task transformation and automatic QA generation pipeline allow efficient, large-scale benchmark construction with minimal manual intervention. The evaluation protocol ensures fairness and reproducibility by grounding all questions in public annotations and employing robust answer extraction prompts. The development of VideoChat2 introduces a new state-of-the-art video MLLM baseline, leveraging progressive multi-modal training and an enriched instruction-tuning dataset, which significantly outperforms existing models on temporal video understanding tasks.

ea44ca3dc7c0aa8d2c5bd3966ecfb56628662cd4.title: Recent Advances in Optimal Transport for Machine Learning
ea44ca3dc7c0aa8d2c5bd3966ecfb56628662cd4.research_question: How can recent advances in optimal transport theory and computational methods be leveraged to improve machine learning across supervised, unsupervised, transfer, and reinforcement learning tasks, particularly in terms of comparing and manipulating probability distributions?
ea44ca3dc7c0aa8d2c5bd3966ecfb56628662cd4.hypothesis: Optimal transport, with its extensions and computational innovations, provides a principled and effective framework for comparing, interpolating, and manipulating probability distributions, leading to improved performance and interpretability in a wide range of machine learning applications.
ea44ca3dc7c0aa8d2c5bd3966ecfb56628662cd4.proposed_method: The proposed research will develop and integrate advanced optimal transport (OT) frameworks—including Wasserstein distances, Sinkhorn divergence, sliced and structured OT, and neural network-based OT solvers—into machine learning pipelines for supervised, unsupervised, transfer, and reinforcement learning. The methodology will involve both the theoretical formulation of OT-based losses and regularizers, as well as the design of scalable computational algorithms (e.g., entropic regularization, mini-batch OT, and neural parameterizations of OT maps and plans). Extensions such as unbalanced, partial, and Gromov-Wasserstein OT will be incorporated to handle real-world data complexities like outliers, unequal mass, and incomparable spaces. The approach will also include learning or engineering ground cost functions, leveraging neural networks for flexible and data-adaptive OT metrics, and employing regularization techniques to ensure computational tractability and generalization.
ea44ca3dc7c0aa8d2c5bd3966ecfb56628662cd4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of benchmark datasets across different machine learning domains. For supervised learning, datasets such as CIFAR-10 will be used to evaluate OT-based loss functions in classification and fairness-aware learning. In unsupervised learning, generative modeling will be tested using image datasets (e.g., MNIST, CelebA) with GANs, VAEs, and normalizing flows, comparing OT-based objectives to standard divergences. Baselines will include traditional losses (cross-entropy, KL divergence, MMD) and state-of-the-art OT-based methods. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, generative sample quality (e.g., FID score), robustness to outliers, and fairness metrics. Experimental setups will explore the impact of entropic regularization, mini-batch strategies, and learned ground costs, as well as the computational efficiency and scalability of the proposed algorithms.
ea44ca3dc7c0aa8d2c5bd3966ecfb56628662cd4.novelty_claims: This research introduces a unified and comprehensive application of modern optimal transport theory to a broad spectrum of machine learning problems, leveraging recent computational advances such as entropic regularization, sliced and structured OT, and neural OT solvers. The proposal claims novelty in the integration of OT extensions (unbalanced, partial, Gromov-Wasserstein, neural OT) into practical ML workflows, the development of scalable and GPU-friendly algorithms, and the learning of adaptive ground costs for improved semantic alignment. The research also aims to bridge theoretical OT advances with empirical machine learning practice, providing new insights into the geometry of probability distributions and their impact on learning algorithms.

ea649172c0debf06beb4322f0befa35537973606.title: TorchOpt: An Efficient Library for Differentiable Optimization
ea649172c0debf06beb4322f0befa35537973606.research_question: How can the development and execution of differentiable optimization algorithms be made more efficient, scalable, and user-friendly, particularly for large-scale and distributed machine learning applications?
ea649172c0debf06beb4322f0befa35537973606.hypothesis: A unified, high-performance, and distributed library for differentiable optimization, supporting multiple differentiation modes and efficient resource utilization, will significantly accelerate algorithm development and training, while reducing computational overhead and complexity.
ea649172c0debf06beb4322f0befa35537973606.proposed_method: A new library, TorchOpt, will be developed as a PyTorch-based platform for efficient differentiable optimization. The library will provide a unified programming abstraction supporting explicit, implicit, and zero-order gradient computation, accessible via both high-level and low-level APIs. The system will feature CPU/GPU-accelerated optimizers, memory- and cache-efficient tree utilities (OpTree), and a distributed runtime leveraging RPC for parallel execution across multiple GPUs and CPUs. Technical innovations will include manual symbolic reduction in optimizer implementations, custom C++/CUDA bindings for performance-critical operations, and an auto-parallelization framework for distributing inner-loop optimization tasks. Additionally, advanced debugging and gradient visualization tools will be integrated to assist users in managing complex computational graphs.
ea649172c0debf06beb4322f0befa35537973606.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard meta-learning and differentiable optimization benchmarks, such as MAML with Omniglot and other representative tasks. Performance will be compared against existing libraries including PyTorch, Higher, learn2learn, JAXopt, and others, evaluating training time, optimizer forward/backward pass speed, and scalability across multiple CPUs/GPUs. Metrics will include wall-clock training time, speedup ratios, and model convergence, with experiments run on both single-node and distributed multi-GPU environments. Additional tests will assess memory efficiency and gradient computation correctness, and visualization tools will be validated for usability in debugging complex models.
ea649172c0debf06beb4322f0befa35537973606.novelty_claims: The proposed library introduces a unified abstraction supporting explicit, implicit, and zero-order differentiation within a single PyTorch-based framework, which is not fully supported by existing libraries. It features high-performance, CPU/GPU-accelerated optimizers and memory-efficient tree operations, enabling large-scale differentiable optimization. The distributed runtime supports automatic parallelization and execution of inner-loop optimization tasks across heterogeneous devices using RPC, achieving substantial speedups and scalability. Integrated debugging and gradient visualization tools further enhance usability, making the library a comprehensive and user-friendly solution for differentiable optimization research and applications.

ea68f9d9012106b050d72ec0a7a23c04779f6afe.title: SPOT: Self-Training with Patch-Order Permutation for Object-Centric Learning with Autoregressive Transformers
ea68f9d9012106b050d72ec0a7a23c04779f6afe.research_question: How can unsupervised object-centric learning in slot-based autoencoders be improved to achieve more accurate and robust object decomposition, especially in complex real-world images, using only visual cues?
ea68f9d9012106b050d72ec0a7a23c04779f6afe.hypothesis: Incorporating a self-training scheme that distills superior slot-attention masks from the decoder to the encoder, combined with a patch-order permutation strategy in autoregressive transformer decoders, will significantly enhance the precision and robustness of object-centric representations in slot-based autoencoders.
ea68f9d9012106b050d72ec0a7a23c04779f6afe.proposed_method: A novel two-stage training framework is developed for slot-based autoencoders. In the first stage, the model is trained with a reconstruction loss using a self-supervised pre-trained feature encoder (e.g., DINO ViT) to generate object-centric slots. In the second stage, a teacher-student self-training scheme is introduced, where attention masks generated by the teacher model's decoder are distilled to the student's encoder slot-attention module via a dedicated loss, improving the encoder's ability to generate object-specific slots. Additionally, the autoregressive transformer decoder is enhanced by introducing sequence permutations, altering the prediction order of image patches during decoding. This permutation strategy ensures that all patch positions rely more uniformly on slot vectors, mitigating overfitting to past tokens and strengthening the supervisory signal for object-centric learning. The method employs multiple patch-order permutations, each with a distinct [BOS] token, and randomly samples a permutation at each training step.
ea68f9d9012106b050d72ec0a7a23c04779f6afe.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on challenging real-world datasets such as MS COCO 2017 and PASCAL VOC 2012, as well as synthetic datasets MOVi-C and MOVi-E. The evaluation focuses on unsupervised object segmentation using metrics including Mean Best Overlap (MBO) at instance and class levels, Mean Intersection over Union (MIOU), and Foreground Adjusted Rand Index (FG-ARI). Baselines include prior slot-based autoencoder methods such as Slot Attention, SLATE, DINOSAUR, and SlotDiffusion, with both MLP and autoregressive transformer decoders. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of self-training, sequence permutation, and test-time ensembling. The models use a ViT-based encoder, a transformer decoder with 4 layers, and are trained with the Adam optimizer. Hyperparameters such as the number of slots, loss weights, and training epochs are systematically explored.
ea68f9d9012106b050d72ec0a7a23c04779f6afe.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces two key innovations: (1) an attention-based self-training scheme that distills superior slot-attention masks from the decoder to the encoder, enhancing object segmentation and enabling stable fine-tuning of pre-trained image encoders; and (2) a patch-order permutation strategy for autoregressive transformer decoders, which enforces a more uniform reliance on slot vectors across all patch positions, thereby improving the robustness and effectiveness of object-centric learning. The synergistic combination of these techniques achieves state-of-the-art performance in unsupervised object segmentation on complex real-world datasets, surpassing previous slot-based autoencoder methods.

ea693001245ba993cbd4387f21b41958a0948746.title: SaLoRA: Safety-Alignment Preserved Low-Rank Adaptation
ea693001245ba993cbd4387f21b41958a0948746.research_question: How can parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods for large language models be designed to preserve the original safety alignment of the model while enabling effective adaptation to downstream tasks?
ea693001245ba993cbd4387f21b41958a0948746.hypothesis: Introducing a fixed safety module based on safety data and a task-specific initialization for trainable parameters in low-rank adaptation will enable fine-tuned large language models to maintain their original safety alignment without sacrificing downstream task performance.
ea693001245ba993cbd4387f21b41958a0948746.proposed_method: A novel parameter-efficient fine-tuning framework, Safety-alignment preserved Low-Rank Adaptation (SaLoRA), is developed for large language models. SaLoRA introduces a fixed safety module, computed from a small set of pre-collected harmful prompts and their safe responses, which projects new features added by adapters into a subspace orthogonal to the original safety features, thereby preserving safety alignment. In addition, a task-specific initialization is proposed for the trainable adapter weights (A and B matrices), leveraging a subset of the fine-tuning data to locate task-relevant low-rank weight regions and initialize the adapters accordingly. During training, only the adapters are updated, while the safety module and the residual weights remain fixed. The method includes a preprocessing step to compute the safety module and adapter initialization, followed by standard fine-tuning on downstream data, and a simple merging step for adapter weights at inference.
ea693001245ba993cbd4387f21b41958a0948746.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on four widely used large language models (Llama-2-chat-7B, Llama-2-chat-13B, Llama-3.1-Instruct-8B, and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3), fine-tuned on the Alpaca dataset using SaLoRA and several baseline PEFT methods (LoRA, DoRA, PiSSA), as well as state-of-the-art post-hoc safety alignment methods (Self-Reminder, InferAligner, Vaccine, SafeLoRA). Safety alignment is evaluated using the harmful rate of model responses to unsafe prompts from the AdvBench dataset, measured by Llama-Guard-3-8B. Additional utility evaluations are performed on eight commonsense reasoning tasks (BoolQ, PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, OBQA) using the Commonsense-15k dataset, with prediction accuracy and harmful rate as metrics. The setup includes batch size 16, single NVIDIA A100-80GB GPU, and adapter rank settings of 16, 32, or 64. Further robustness is assessed under jailbreak attacks using the multiGCG method.
ea693001245ba993cbd4387f21b41958a0948746.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a fixed safety module, derived from a small set of safety data, that preserves the original safety features of the model during fine-tuning. It also presents a novel task-specific initialization for adapter weights, improving convergence and downstream performance. SaLoRA is claimed to be the first PEFT method that enables targeted adaptation without disrupting original safety alignment, outperforming both existing PEFT and post-hoc alignment methods in preserving safety while maintaining or improving task utility. The approach is computationally efficient, requiring only minor preprocessing overhead, and is compatible with standard inference pipelines.

ea6def1d770ef6fd8fca81d478f27b704b7fbd91.title: Historical Test-time Prompt Tuning for Vision Foundation Models
ea6def1d770ef6fd8fca81d478f27b704b7fbd91.research_question: How can test-time prompt tuning for vision foundation models be made more robust and effective, particularly in the presence of continuously changing test domains and without access to labeled data?
ea6def1d770ef6fd8fca81d478f27b704b7fbd91.hypothesis: Incorporating memory-based mechanisms that store and retrieve historical knowledge from previous test samples will mitigate the knowledge forgetting problem and enhance the robustness and performance of test-time prompt tuning across various visual recognition tasks and changing domains.
ea6def1d770ef6fd8fca81d478f27b704b7fbd91.proposed_method: A novel test-time prompt tuning framework is developed that integrates three distinct types of knowledge banks: a local knowledge bank, a hard-sample knowledge bank, and a global knowledge bank. The local knowledge bank buffers features from recent test samples to capture up-to-date distributional changes, operating as a FIFO queue. The hard-sample knowledge bank identifies and stores features of samples with high prediction entropy, focusing on difficult and rare cases, also using a FIFO mechanism. The global knowledge bank accumulates features from both local and hard-sample banks, maintaining a momentum-based prototype for comprehensive and representative memorization. An adaptive knowledge retrieval mechanism is introduced, which dynamically retrieves and weights information from the three banks for each test sample, regularizing predictions and guiding prompt optimization via a self-supervised loss. Prompt tokens are updated online with each incoming test sample, leveraging the retrieved knowledge to mitigate error accumulation and forgetting.
ea6def1d770ef6fd8fca81d478f27b704b7fbd91.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three major visual recognition tasks: semantic segmentation, image classification, and object detection. Multiple benchmark datasets will be used, including Cityscapes, BDD100K, Mapillary, ADE20K, Pascal Content, ACDC for segmentation and detection, and Flowers102, DTD, Oxford-Pets, StanfordCars, UCF101, Caltech101, Food101, SUN397, Aircraft, and EuroSAT for classification. Baseline comparisons will include existing test-time prompt tuning methods (such as TPT and DiffTPT), as well as memory-based learning approaches. Evaluation metrics will include mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) for segmentation, mean Average Precision (mAP) for detection, and top-1 classification accuracy for classification. The experimental setup will involve initializing prompts with a generic template, optimizing four learnable tokens per class, and using standard vision foundation models (e.g., CLIP, SEEM) with specified backbones and training hyperparameters. Ablation studies will assess the contribution of each knowledge bank and the adaptive retrieval mechanism.
ea6def1d770ef6fd8fca81d478f27b704b7fbd91.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to apply memory-based learning principles to test-time prompt tuning for vision foundation models. It introduces a comprehensive memorization strategy via three complementary knowledge banks and an adaptive retrieval mechanism, enabling robust online prompt optimization without labeled data. The method is generalizable across multiple vision tasks and is shown to be effective in scenarios with continuously changing test domains. Additionally, the approach is complementary to existing prompt learning methods and can be integrated as a plug-in to enhance their performance.

ea736025d29efdb92f40460c7d92453582872bab.title: A geometric framework for momentum-based optimizers for low-rank training
ea736025d29efdb92f40460c7d92453582872bab.research_question: How can momentum-based optimization methods be adapted to effectively and efficiently train low-rank parameterizations of large neural networks, while preserving the intrinsic geometry of the low-rank parameter space and achieving high compression rates without sacrificing model performance?
ea736025d29efdb92f40460c7d92453582872bab.hypothesis: Incorporating geometry-aware momentum-based optimization into dynamic low-rank training will enable stable and efficient convergence to low-rank optima, outperforming conventional low-rank optimizers in terms of both accuracy and compression, and matching or exceeding the performance of full-rank baselines under tight parameter budgets.
ea736025d29efdb92f40460c7d92453582872bab.proposed_method: A novel optimization framework will be developed that integrates adaptive momentum techniques, such as heavy ball and Adam, into the dynamic low-rank training (DLRT) paradigm. The method will explicitly account for the manifold geometry of the low-rank parameter space by projecting gradients and momentum updates onto the tangent space of the low-rank manifold. The algorithm will use orthonormal basis augmentation and rank-adaptive truncation to ensure numerical stability and efficient parameter updates. Both the weights and optimizer states (first and second moments) will be jointly compressed and updated using shared low-rank bases, with bias correction and adaptive step-size control incorporated for Adam-style updates. The approach will be extended to tensor-valued layers (e.g., convolutional and transformer architectures) using low-rank Tucker factorization, ensuring broad applicability.
ea736025d29efdb92f40460c7d92453582872bab.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of tasks, including low-rank transfer learning, fine-tuning, and pre-training, across diverse neural network architectures such as VGG11, VGG16, ViT-B.16, DeBERTaV3-base, Llama-2-7b-chat, and GPT-2. Datasets will include UCM, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, GLUE benchmark (SST-2, CoLA, QQP, QNLI, RTE, MRPC, STS-B), BoolQ, PIQA, and OpenWebText. Baselines will comprise full-rank training, standard DLRT without momentum projection, LoRA and its variants (including AdaLoRA, GeoLoRA, DoRA, LoRA+), and other adapter-based methods. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, validation loss, and compression ratio (percentage of parameter reduction), with computational efficiency and wall-clock time also reported. Each experiment will be repeated with multiple random seeds to assess robustness, and hyperparameters (such as rank) will be matched across methods to ensure fair comparison.
ea736025d29efdb92f40460c7d92453582872bab.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to provide a principled, geometry-aware momentum-based optimization method for low-rank training that is both rank-adaptive and jointly compresses weights, gradients, and optimizer states. The method provably approximates optimal gradient flows on the low-rank manifold, ensuring convergence to low-rank optima and robustness to ill-conditioning. It achieves state-of-the-art accuracy at high compression rates across a variety of tasks and architectures, surpassing existing low-rank and adapter-based methods. The approach is computationally and memory efficient, scalable to large models, and directly extendable to tensor-valued neural network layers, enabling broader deployment of deep learning on resource-constrained devices.

ea8575a032fe90b859bf3e19330f245e782090f7.title: Provable Stochastic Optimization for Global Contrastive Learning: Small Batch Does Not Harm Performance
ea8575a032fe90b859bf3e19330f245e782090f7.research_question: Can the performance limitations of contrastive learning methods due to large batch size or large negative sample dictionaries be overcome through a new stochastic optimization approach, and can this approach be generalized to other contrastive learning settings such as bimodal contrastive learning?
ea8575a032fe90b859bf3e19330f245e782090f7.hypothesis: A memory-efficient stochastic optimization algorithm can optimize a global contrastive learning objective without requiring large batch sizes or large dictionaries, achieving comparable or superior performance to existing methods under small batch regimes.
ea8575a032fe90b859bf3e19330f245e782090f7.proposed_method: A novel stochastic optimization algorithm, SogCLR, is proposed to solve the global contrastive learning objective efficiently. The method formulates a global contrastive loss that contrasts each positive pair against all possible negative pairs, and addresses the computational challenge by maintaining and updating a scalar tracking variable for each image to estimate the normalization term efficiently. The algorithm uses a moving average update for these scalars and computes stochastic gradient estimators using mini-batches, employing either momentum or Adam-style parameter updates. The approach is proven to have negligible optimization error under mild conditions and is further extended to handle two-way (bimodal) contrastive losses by maintaining separate tracking variables for each modality.
ea8575a032fe90b859bf3e19330f245e782090f7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet-1K and ImageNet-S datasets for self-supervised visual representation learning, using ResNet-50 as the backbone and standard data augmentations. SogCLR will be compared against SimCLR and other InfoNCE-based methods, with batch sizes ranging from 128 to 8192 and training epochs up to 800. Evaluation will be performed using top-1 linear evaluation accuracy on validation sets, with linear classifiers trained on the frozen encoder. Additional experiments will apply the method to a bimodal contrastive learning setting (CLIP-style) using image-text pairs constructed from ImageNet-S labels, comparing performance and convergence speed under small batch sizes.
ea8575a032fe90b859bf3e19330f245e782090f7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first provably convergent stochastic optimization algorithm for the global contrastive learning objective that does not require large batch sizes or dictionaries. The method provides a rigorous optimization perspective explaining the batch size sensitivity of SimCLR and overcomes this limitation with a memory-efficient algorithm. SogCLR achieves competitive or superior performance to state-of-the-art methods under small batch sizes and is shown to be generalizable to other contrastive loss settings, including bimodal contrastive learning. The algorithm is accompanied by theoretical convergence guarantees and practical empirical validation.

eaa7853facb9b49444b48a96192cb4be66b62671.title: Synapse: Trajectory-as-Exemplar Prompting with Memory for Computer Control
eaa7853facb9b49444b48a96192cb4be66b62671.research_question: How can large language model (LLM)-powered agents be improved to perform complex computer control tasks efficiently and generalize to novel scenarios, overcoming limitations of context length, exemplar structure, and task specificity?
eaa7853facb9b49444b48a96192cb4be66b62671.hypothesis: Introducing a framework that combines state abstraction, trajectory-as-exemplar prompting, and exemplar memory will enable LLM-based agents to perform more accurate, efficient, and generalizable computer control across diverse and complex tasks.
eaa7853facb9b49444b48a96192cb4be66b62671.proposed_method: A new agent framework is proposed, consisting of three main components: (i) state abstraction, which leverages few-shot learning with LLMs to filter raw computer states (such as HTML or screenshots) into concise, task-relevant observations, thus reducing input token length and enabling more exemplars within the LLM context window; (ii) trajectory-as-exemplar (TaE) prompting, where the LLM is prompted with complete successful trajectories (sequences of abstracted states and actions) rather than high-level plans or stepwise MCQs, enhancing multi-step decision-making and reducing error accumulation; (iii) exemplar memory, implemented as a vector database that stores embeddings of task metadata and associated exemplary trajectories, enabling similarity-based retrieval of relevant exemplars for new or unseen tasks. The agent retrieves the most relevant few-shot exemplars from memory for each task, processes raw states into clean observations, and iteratively generates actions until task completion.
eaa7853facb9b49444b48a96192cb4be66b62671.experiment_details: Experiments are planned on two benchmarks: MiniWoB++, a suite of 64 diverse computer control tasks, and Mind2Web, a real-world web navigation dataset with open-domain tasks. The agent will be evaluated using LLMs such as GPT-3.5-turbo and CodeLlama-7B, with state abstraction and trajectory prompting applied as described. Baselines will include state-of-the-art imitation learning (BC+RL), fine-tuned language models, and in-context learning agents such as RCI, AdaPlanner, and MindAct. Evaluation metrics will include average task success rate, step success rate, and element selection accuracy, with experiments run across standard, cross-task, cross-website, and cross-domain splits. Ablation studies will assess the contribution of each component (state abstraction, TaE prompting, and memory) to overall performance.
eaa7853facb9b49444b48a96192cb4be66b62671.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel trajectory-as-exemplar prompting scheme that leverages full successful trajectories as exemplars, overcoming the limitations of prior methods that use high-level plans or MCQs. The state abstraction mechanism enables the inclusion of more exemplars by reducing context length, while the exemplar memory module allows for automatic, similarity-based retrieval of relevant demonstrations, supporting generalization to unseen tasks. This combination is claimed to achieve human-level or superior performance on standard benchmarks without reliance on self-correction, and to significantly improve data efficiency and generalization compared to existing methods.

eabd80decd707ddc6d388f480667845094ac89b6.title: One Wave To Explain Them All: A Unifying Perspective On Feature Attribution
eabd80decd707ddc6d388f480667845094ac89b6.research_question: How can feature attribution for deep neural networks be unified across different data modalities (such as images, audio, and volumetric data) in a way that better captures the intrinsic structural properties of the data and provides more informative and faithful explanations of model decisions?
eabd80decd707ddc6d388f480667845094ac89b6.hypothesis: Feature attributions computed in the wavelet domain will yield more informative, faithful, and modality-agnostic explanations of deep neural network decisions compared to traditional pixel- or input-domain methods, due to the wavelet domain's ability to capture spatial and frequency-localized structures.
eabd80decd707ddc6d388f480667845094ac89b6.proposed_method: A novel feature attribution framework, the Wavelet Attribution Method (WAM), will be developed that computes attributions in the wavelet domain rather than the traditional pixel or input domain. The method will leverage the spatial and scale-localized properties of wavelet coefficients, enabling the decomposition of input signals (audio, images, or volumes) into components that retain both spatial and frequency information. WAM will generalize popular gradient-based attribution methods, such as SmoothGrad and Integrated Gradients, by applying them to the wavelet-transformed input. The approach will involve calculating the gradient of the model's prediction with respect to wavelet coefficients, optionally smoothing or integrating these gradients to improve explanation quality, and reconstructing interpretable attribution maps that highlight relevant features at multiple scales and orientations.
eabd80decd707ddc6d388f480667845094ac89b6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three data modalities: audio (ESC-50 dataset), images (ImageNet), and volumetric data (MedMNIST3D). For each modality, a representative deep learning model (e.g., ResNet for audio and images, 3DFormer for volumes) will be selected. The proposed WAM method will be compared against established feature attribution baselines, including Saliency, SmoothGrad, Integrated Gradients, and GradCAM. Evaluation will use quantitative faithfulness metrics, specifically the difference between insertion and deletion scores, to assess how well the attributions identify features critical to model predictions. Additional qualitative analyses will explore WAM's ability to disentangle multi-scale structures, assess model robustness, and provide post-hoc explanations for noisy or corrupted inputs.
eabd80decd707ddc6d388f480667845094ac89b6.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a unified, modality-agnostic framework for feature attribution that operates in the wavelet domain, enabling explanations that preserve both spatial and frequency information across audio, images, and volumes. WAM is the first approach to systematically extend and evaluate gradient-based attribution methods in the wavelet domain for multiple modalities, demonstrating superior or competitive performance compared to traditional methods. The method also offers new qualitative insights, such as multi-scale decomposition of attributions and connections to model robustness, that are not accessible with pixel-based approaches.

eb1f251d7f53f0be0236028315ad96744da6f846.title: GSPN-2: Efficient Parallel Sequence Modeling
eb1f251d7f53f0be0236028315ad96744da6f846.research_question: How can parallel sequence modeling for high-resolution images and long video data be made more computationally efficient and scalable, while maintaining or improving accuracy in vision applications such as image classification and text-to-image generation?
eb1f251d7f53f0be0236028315ad96744da6f846.hypothesis: A joint algorithmic and system-level redesign of spatial propagation networks—incorporating a unified CUDA kernel, channel-compressive propagation, and optimized memory access—will significantly improve computational efficiency and scalability for global spatial modeling in vision tasks, without sacrificing accuracy compared to transformer-based or prior efficient attention models.
eb1f251d7f53f0be0236028315ad96744da6f846.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces GSPN-2, an efficient parallel sequence modeling framework for vision applications. The approach consolidates all propagation steps into a single unified CUDA kernel, eliminating the overhead of thousands of micro-kernel launches and maximizing GPU hardware utilization. Channel-compressive propagation is implemented by projecting input features into a lower-dimensional proxy space, applying shared propagation matrices, and then restoring to the original channel space, thereby reducing parameter count and concurrency load. The CUDA execution pipeline is further optimized by leveraging 2D thread blocks, shared memory for hidden state caching, coalesced global memory access, and stream-based concurrency for multi-directional propagation. This system-level co-design ensures efficient on-chip memory reuse, high throughput, and near-constant runtime scaling even for large batch sizes and channel counts.
eb1f251d7f53f0be0236028315ad96744da6f846.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard vision benchmarks, including ImageNet-1K for image classification and the Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL) framework for text-to-image synthesis. The method will be compared against baselines such as GSPN-1, transformer models (e.g., DeiT, Swin), state-space models (e.g., Mamba, Vim), and convolutional networks (e.g., ConvNeXT). Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, inference runtime (forward and backward pass), memory throughput, and hardware utilization (SM occupancy, cache hit rates). Input configurations will span a range of image resolutions (up to 16K), batch sizes, and channel counts to assess scalability and efficiency. Profiling will isolate the impact of each kernel and algorithmic optimization, and qualitative results will be reported for high-resolution text-to-image generation.
eb1f251d7f53f0be0236028315ad96744da6f846.novelty_claims: The proposed method claims several innovations: (1) a unified single-kernel CUDA implementation for spatial propagation, drastically reducing kernel launch overhead; (2) a compact channel propagation strategy using proxy feature compression and channel-shared weights, enabling efficient scaling to large feature maps; (3) optimized CUDA execution with 2D thread blocks, shared memory caching, and coalesced memory access, achieving near-peak hardware utilization; and (4) demonstration of state-of-the-art efficiency and competitive accuracy across diverse vision tasks, establishing a new efficiency frontier for global spatial context modeling in high-resolution applications.

eb29a4b922196405e70767821ab38104f8c7c4ea.title: Learning to Maximize Mutual Information for Dynamic Feature Selection
eb29a4b922196405e70767821ab38104f8c7c4ea.research_question: How can dynamic feature selection be performed efficiently and accurately, enabling a model to sequentially select features based on currently available information in order to maximize predictive performance under a fixed feature acquisition budget?
eb29a4b922196405e70767821ab38104f8c7c4ea.hypothesis: A learning-based approach that directly predicts the optimal feature to select at each step, by maximizing conditional mutual information (CMI) with the response variable, will outperform both reinforcement learning-based and static feature selection methods in dynamic feature selection tasks.
eb29a4b922196405e70767821ab38104f8c7c4ea.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed for dynamic feature selection that leverages a variational perspective on greedy conditional mutual information (CMI) maximization. The method formulates the selection of each feature as an optimization problem, where at each step, a policy network predicts a distribution over the next feature to select based on the currently observed features. This policy network, along with a predictor network, is trained using amortized optimization with a continuous relaxation (Concrete distribution) to enable efficient gradient-based learning. The objective function directly minimizes the expected prediction loss after each feature selection, ensuring that the learned policy recovers the greedy CMI-based selection when trained to optimality. The approach avoids the need for generative modeling of the data distribution and instead focuses on directly learning the selection policy from labeled data.
eb29a4b922196405e70767821ab38104f8c7c4ea.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a diverse set of datasets, including three medical diagnosis tasks (bleeding risk, respiratory support, and fluid responsiveness), three public tabular datasets (spam classification, MiniBooNE, diabetes), and two image classification datasets (MNIST and CIFAR-10). The proposed method is compared against both static feature selection baselines (such as SAGE, permutation tests, DeepLift, Integrated Gradients, and Concrete Autoencoder) and dynamic baselines (including RL-based Opportunistic Learning and CMI estimation with generative models). Evaluation metrics include AUROC for classification tasks and top-1 accuracy for image datasets, with results averaged across multiple runs and feature budgets. Neural network architectures are used for all methods, and consistent experimental setups are maintained for fair comparison, including the use of dropout for regularization and pre-training of predictor networks.
eb29a4b922196405e70767821ab38104f8c7c4ea.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a practical and theoretically grounded method for dynamic feature selection by directly learning the greedy CMI policy via amortized optimization, bypassing the need for reinforcement learning or generative modeling. The method employs a continuous relaxation to enable efficient, architecture-agnostic gradient-based training. Empirical results demonstrate that this approach consistently outperforms both state-of-the-art static and dynamic feature selection methods across a variety of real-world and benchmark datasets, establishing it as a simple yet powerful solution for dynamic feature selection problems.

eb2c2330177f765038a2b17e2ee3498965865797.title: OmniQuant: Omnidirectionally Calibrated Quantization for Large Language Models
eb2c2330177f765038a2b17e2ee3498965865797.research_question: How can large language models be quantized to extremely low-bit formats while maintaining high performance and computational efficiency, especially in both weight-only and weight-activation quantization settings, without incurring the high resource costs of quantization-aware training?
eb2c2330177f765038a2b17e2ee3498965865797.hypothesis: Introducing learnable quantization parameters, specifically through learnable weight clipping and learnable equivalent transformation, enables large language models to achieve quantization performance comparable to quantization-aware training while retaining the efficiency of post-training quantization.
eb2c2330177f765038a2b17e2ee3498965865797.proposed_method: A novel quantization framework, OmniQuant, will be developed for large language models. The method will freeze original full-precision weights and introduce a small set of learnable quantization parameters, optimized using a differentiable, block-wise quantization error minimization framework. Two key components will be incorporated: Learnable Weight Clipping (LWC), which adaptively determines optimal clipping thresholds for weight distributions, and Learnable Equivalent Transformation (LET), which applies channel-wise scaling and shifting to activations and weights, making them more quantization-friendly. The optimization will be performed sequentially for each transformer block using stochastic gradient descent, and all learnable parameters will be fused into the quantized model post-optimization, incurring no additional inference cost.
eb2c2330177f765038a2b17e2ee3498965865797.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of large language models, including OPT (125M-66B), LLaMA (7B-65B), LLaMA-2 (7B-70B), Falcon-180B, and instruction-tuned LLaMA-2-chat, covering both weight-only and weight-activation quantization scenarios. Quantization configurations such as W4A4, W6A6, W4A16, W3A16, and W2A16 will be evaluated. Baseline comparisons will include RTN, GPTQ, AWQ for weight-only, and SmoothQuant, Outlier Suppression+, RPTQ, and LLM-QAT for weight-activation quantization. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity on WikiText2, PTB, and C4 datasets, as well as zero-shot accuracy on PIQA, ARC, BoolQ, and HellaSwag. Calibration will use 128 samples, with optimization performed on a single A100 GPU, and deployment feasibility will be assessed using MLC-LLM on real hardware.
eb2c2330177f765038a2b17e2ee3498965865797.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a differentiable, block-wise optimization framework for quantization parameters in large language models, enabling efficient integration of gradient-based updates into post-training quantization. The combination of learnable weight clipping and learnable equivalent transformation is novel in that it systematically addresses both weight and activation quantization challenges, particularly in low-bit regimes. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse quantization settings and model families, matches or exceeds quantization-aware training accuracy with the efficiency of post-training quantization, and ensures hardware compatibility by fusing all learnable parameters into the quantized model.

eb2cbd12f749f14716296f7f415e921562c9079b.title: LRM: Large Reconstruction Model for Single Image to 3D
eb2cbd12f749f14716296f7f415e921562c9079b.research_question: Can a large-scale, data-driven transformer-based model learn a generic 3D prior that enables high-quality, category-agnostic 3D object reconstruction from a single input image, using only multi-view 2D image supervision?
eb2cbd12f749f14716296f7f415e921562c9079b.hypothesis: A highly scalable transformer-based encoder-decoder architecture, trained end-to-end on a massive multi-view dataset, can learn expressive 3D priors that generalize to arbitrary objects and enable accurate, efficient 3D reconstruction from a single image without reliance on category-specific priors or per-shape optimization.
eb2cbd12f749f14716296f7f415e921562c9079b.proposed_method: A large reconstruction model (LRM) will be developed, consisting of a transformer-based encoder-decoder architecture with over 500 million parameters. The method will use a pre-trained visual transformer (DINO) as the image encoder to extract patch-wise features from the input image. These features, along with camera parameters, will be projected onto a 3D triplane representation using a transformer decoder with cross-attention and self-attention mechanisms. The triplane representation will serve as a compact, expressive 3D feature map, from which point features are queried and decoded via a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) to predict color and density for volumetric rendering using a neural radiance field (NeRF) formulation. The entire network will be trained end-to-end using simple image reconstruction losses between rendered and ground-truth images at novel views, without requiring complex 3D-aware regularization or extensive hyperparameter tuning.
eb2cbd12f749f14716296f7f415e921562c9079b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a large-scale dataset comprising approximately 1 million 3D objects, including synthetic renderings from Objaverse and real captures from MVImgNet. The model will be trained on 128 NVIDIA A100 GPUs with a batch size of 1024 for 30 epochs, utilizing both rendered images and video frames with background removal. Evaluation will involve reconstructing 3D shapes from single images drawn from diverse sources, including Objaverse, MVImgNet, ImageNet, Google Scanned Objects, Amazon Berkeley Objects, real-world captures, and images generated by Adobe Firefly. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art single-image-to-3D methods such as One-2-3-45. Evaluation metrics will include pixel-wise L2 loss, perceptual similarity (LPIPS), and qualitative assessments of fidelity, generalization, and reconstruction speed. Inference will be performed by extracting meshes from the triplane-NeRF using Marching Cubes, with the entire process taking less than 5 seconds per shape.
eb2cbd12f749f14716296f7f415e921562c9079b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first large-scale, transformer-based model for single-image-to-3D reconstruction, trained on an unprecedented scale of 3D data and leveraging a triplane NeRF representation for efficiency and scalability. Unlike prior methods, the model is fully data-driven, category-agnostic, and does not require guidance from pre-trained vision-language models or per-shape optimization. The method achieves high-quality, generalizable 3D reconstructions from a wide variety of input images, including real-world and generated images, and operates with high efficiency, producing reconstructions in seconds. The architecture and training paradigm are highly scalable, enabling future extensions to even larger models and datasets, as well as potential multimodal generative applications.

eb375712bd37250c350ecd3f559e1879e87eb3e5.title: Length-Controlled AlpacaEval: A Simple Way to Debias Automatic Evaluators
eb375712bd37250c350ecd3f559e1879e87eb3e5.research_question: How can automated evaluation metrics for large language models be debiased to reduce the influence of spurious correlates, such as output length, in order to better approximate human preferences in open-ended instruction-following tasks?
eb375712bd37250c350ecd3f559e1879e87eb3e5.hypothesis: Automated evaluation metrics for language models can be effectively debiased by applying regression-based causal inference techniques to control for confounding variables such as output length, resulting in metrics that are more robust to manipulation and more closely aligned with human judgments.
eb375712bd37250c350ecd3f559e1879e87eb3e5.proposed_method: A regression-based debiasing framework will be developed to adjust automated evaluation metrics, specifically targeting the length bias in LLM-based evaluators like AlpacaEval. The approach involves fitting a generalized linear model (GLM), such as logistic regression, to predict the auto-annotator's preference based on three main factors: model identity, output length difference (normalized and transformed via tanh), and instruction difficulty. The model is trained on a dataset of pairwise model comparisons, capturing the probability that an evaluated model's response is preferred over a baseline. To obtain length-controlled preferences, the regression model is used to predict preferences while conditioning on a zero length difference between model and baseline outputs, thus estimating the counterfactual win rate if both outputs had the same length. Regularization is applied to the length term to prevent adversarial exploitation, and instruction difficulty is estimated jointly across models for stability.
eb375712bd37250c350ecd3f559e1879e87eb3e5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the AlpacaEval benchmark, which consists of over 120 models evaluated on 805 diverse instructions, with pairwise comparisons generated by a GPT-4-turbo-based evaluator. The length-controlled metric will be compared against standard AlpacaEval, length-normalized, and length-balanced baselines. Evaluation metrics will include Spearman correlation with the LMSYS Chatbot Arena (a large-scale human evaluation platform), sensitivity to length manipulation (gameability), and robustness to adversarial attacks such as output truncation. Cross-validation and L2 regularization will be used to ensure model stability, and the impact of debiasing on leaderboard rankings and interpretability will be assessed.
eb375712bd37250c350ecd3f559e1879e87eb3e5.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple, interpretable regression-based approach for post-hoc debiasing of automated evaluation metrics, enabling control over specific confounders such as output length. This approach maintains desirable properties of win-rate metrics, is robust to adversarial manipulation, and achieves the highest reported correlation with human preferences on the Chatbot Arena benchmark. The method is generalizable to other biases by incorporating additional features into the regression model, and provides a principled, counterfactual interpretation of model win rates.

eb3e73a1a84e61646b577190dab2857a6e31e63b.title: No Token Left Behind: Efficient Vision Transformer via Dynamic Token Idling
eb3e73a1a84e61646b577190dab2857a6e31e63b.research_question: How can the computational complexity of Vision Transformers (ViTs) be reduced for deployment in resource-constrained environments without sacrificing significant model performance or losing critical image information during token reduction?
eb3e73a1a84e61646b577190dab2857a6e31e63b.hypothesis: A dynamic token idling strategy, which retains all tokens but selectively idles less informative ones at each layer, will enable ViTs to maintain high accuracy while significantly reducing computational complexity and mitigating the negative effects of early token pruning.
eb3e73a1a84e61646b577190dab2857a6e31e63b.proposed_method: A novel framework, IdleViT, will be developed to partition image tokens into Selected and Idle sets at each transformer layer. Only Selected tokens will participate in self-attention computations, while Idle tokens will bypass computation and be concatenated back at the layer's output, allowing for potential reselection in subsequent layers. Token selection will be based on class attention scores, with the top-k tokens chosen dynamically per layer. To enhance the semantic consistency of token partitioning, a token cut loss inspired by normalized graph cut theory will be introduced as a regularization term during finetuning. This loss will encourage strong intra-set attention among Selected tokens and weak inter-set attention between Selected and Idle tokens. The method will be designed to work with pretrained ViTs, requiring only a short finetuning phase and supporting integration with various token selection algorithms.
eb3e73a1a84e61646b577190dab2857a6e31e63b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet-1K dataset, utilizing representative ViT backbones such as DeiT-S and LV-ViT-S, and also extending to pyramid ViTs like Swin-Tiny. The models will be finetuned for 30 epochs using standard image augmentations and knowledge distillation from the full-size ViT as a teacher. Performance will be evaluated using top-1 and top-5 accuracy, computational complexity (GMACs), and inference speed (images/second). Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art dynamic token pruning methods such as DynamicViT, EViT, Evo-ViT, and ATS, with token reduction ratios matched for fair comparison. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the token cut loss and the token idle strategy on accuracy and attention map properties.
eb3e73a1a84e61646b577190dab2857a6e31e63b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of dynamic token idling, which differs fundamentally from prior token pruning methods by retaining all tokens and enabling reselection in later layers, thus preventing permanent information loss. The method also devises a novel token cut loss based on normalized graph cut theory to improve token selection regularity and semantic consistency. Additionally, the token idle strategy is shown to alleviate the oversmoothing problem in deep ViTs and is compatible with various ViT architectures, including pyramid structures. The approach achieves significant reductions in computational complexity and inference time with minimal or no loss in accuracy, outperforming existing dynamic token pruning baselines.

eb44ce1f7e1f4deac10f6e7009e2073f1eb0b3e4.title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis and the Geometry of Large Language Models
eb44ce1f7e1f4deac10f6e7009e2073f1eb0b3e4.research_question: Can high-level concepts in large language models be represented linearly in the model's representation space, and how can the geometry and inner product structure of these representations be formalized and leveraged for interpretation and control?
eb44ce1f7e1f4deac10f6e7009e2073f1eb0b3e4.hypothesis: High-level concepts in large language models are represented as linear directions in the representation space, and there exists a causal inner product that unifies different notions of linear representation, enabling meaningful geometric operations for interpretation and control.
eb44ce1f7e1f4deac10f6e7009e2073f1eb0b3e4.proposed_method: The proposed research will formalize the linear representation hypothesis by defining two types of linear representations: one in the output (unembedding) space and one in the input (embedding) space, both anchored in counterfactual pairs of words or contexts that differ only in the target concept. A causal inner product will be introduced, defined such that causally separable concepts are represented by orthogonal vectors. This inner product will be estimated empirically using the unembedding matrix of a large language model and the covariance structure of word vectors. The method will unify the subspace, measurement, and intervention notions of linear representation, and will provide explicit procedures for constructing concept directions and intervention vectors using counterfactual data.
eb44ce1f7e1f4deac10f6e7009e2073f1eb0b3e4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the LLaMA-2 language model with 7 billion parameters. A set of 27 concepts, including both linguistic and semantic categories, will be operationalized using counterfactual word pairs from resources such as BATS 3.0 and multilingual lexicons. The alignment of counterfactual differences with estimated concept directions will be measured using the proposed causal inner product, and the orthogonality of causally separable concepts will be validated. Additional experiments will test whether concept directions act as effective linear probes (measurement) and as intervention vectors (control) by manipulating model representations and observing changes in output probabilities. Evaluation metrics will include projection histograms, inner product heatmaps, and changes in output logits and token rankings.
eb44ce1f7e1f4deac10f6e7009e2073f1eb0b3e4.novelty_claims: This research formalizes the linear representation hypothesis in language models using counterfactual pairs and introduces the causal inner product as a principled geometric structure that respects semantic separability. It unifies previously distinct notions of subspace, measurement, and intervention representations, and provides explicit algorithms for estimating concept directions and inner products. The approach enables both interpretation (probing) and control (steering) of model behavior using linear algebraic operations, and demonstrates empirically that these structures exist and are meaningful in large language models.

eb87c11618e2de4f1287320c22cedcc9ad1af761.title: SparseLLM: Towards Global Pruning of Pre-trained Language Models
eb87c11618e2de4f1287320c22cedcc9ad1af761.research_question: How can global pruning of large pre-trained language models be achieved efficiently, overcoming the scalability limitations of traditional global pruning and the suboptimality of local pruning, while maintaining or improving model performance at high sparsity levels?
eb87c11618e2de4f1287320c22cedcc9ad1af761.hypothesis: A global pruning framework that decomposes the global pruning objective into coordinated, analytically solvable subproblems using auxiliary variables and modular decomposition will enable resource-efficient, globally optimal pruning of large language models, resulting in superior performance—especially at high sparsity—compared to existing local pruning methods.
eb87c11618e2de4f1287320c22cedcc9ad1af761.proposed_method: A novel pruning framework, SparseLLM, will be developed to enable global pruning of large pre-trained language models by reformulating the pruning objective as a composite function with auxiliary variables. The method decomposes the global pruning problem into multiple manageable subproblems, each corresponding to a model module (e.g., feed-forward networks and multi-head attention layers), and coordinates their solutions to approximate global optimality. Alternating optimization will be employed, leveraging closed-form solutions for each subproblem, which allows for efficient updates of pruning masks, weights, activations, and outputs. The approach prioritizes global pruning for the parameter-dense feed-forward network modules while applying local pruning to multi-head attention modules, balancing computational feasibility and pruning effectiveness. The framework is designed to be compatible with existing local pruning solvers, such as SparseGPT and Wanda, and can be flexibly configured to interpolate between local and global pruning regimes.
eb87c11618e2de4f1287320c22cedcc9ad1af761.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple large language model families, including OPT, LlaMA-2, and LlaMA-3, across a range of model sizes (from 1.3B to 66B parameters). The models will be pruned to various sparsity levels (70% to 90%, as well as structured 3:4 and 2:4 sparsity patterns). Calibration data will be drawn from 128 segments of 2048 tokens from the C4 dataset, with additional benchmarks using WikiText2 and Penn Treebank (PTB) for perplexity evaluation. Zero-shot accuracy will be assessed on tasks such as BoolQ, RTE, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, and OBQA using the EleutherAI-eval harness. Baselines for comparison will include magnitude-based local pruning, SparseGPT, and Wanda. Evaluation metrics will focus on perplexity and zero-shot accuracy, and experiments will be run on NVIDIA A100 GPUs. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by pruning the same set of layers and using consistent calibration sample sizes.
eb87c11618e2de4f1287320c22cedcc9ad1af761.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified, flexible formulation that enables global pruning of large language models with low memory overhead by decomposing the global objective into analytically solvable subproblems. This approach overcomes the scalability limitations of traditional global pruning and the suboptimality of local pruning, providing a resource-efficient method that achieves global optimality. The method is empirically shown to outperform state-of-the-art local pruning techniques, especially at high sparsity levels, and can be seamlessly integrated with existing pruning solvers. The framework's adaptability and closed-form optimization steps represent significant innovations in the field of model compression for large-scale language models.

eb8d97378c2aa78dc2ade95b6558dd8a388efb12.title: Watch Out Your Album! On the Inadvertent Privacy Memorization in Multi-Modal Large Language Models
eb8d97378c2aa78dc2ade95b6558dd8a388efb12.research_question: Do multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) inadvertently memorize private content that is entirely irrelevant to their training objectives, and how does the training process, particularly mini-batch dynamics, influence this memorization? How can such memorization be detected and measured, and what are the implications for privacy in MLLMs?
eb8d97378c2aa78dc2ade95b6558dd8a388efb12.hypothesis: MLLMs can inadvertently memorize task-irrelevant private content due to spurious correlations introduced by partial mini-batch training, even when this content has no direct relevance to the downstream tasks. Smaller batch sizes increase the likelihood of such memorization, and this memorization can be detected through probing methods even if it is not accessible via direct prompting.
eb8d97378c2aa78dc2ade95b6558dd8a388efb12.proposed_method: A probing framework will be developed to systematically evaluate whether MLLMs encode task-irrelevant private content during fine-tuning. The method involves generating two sets of synthetic, task-irrelevant private data (e.g., usernames and user IDs) and embedding them into the image regions of fine-tuning and probing datasets at varying probabilities. After fine-tuning MLLMs with these watermarked datasets, intermediate representations will be extracted from each model layer. Binary classifiers will be trained on these representations to distinguish between seen and unseen private content, thereby quantifying the extent of memorization. The approach also includes direct prompting and multi-hop reasoning queries to assess whether memorized content can be elicited via standard interaction, and gradient analysis to measure the impact of privacy embedding on training dynamics.
eb8d97378c2aa78dc2ade95b6558dd8a388efb12.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using popular MLLMs such as LLaVA-1.5 (Vicuna-1.5 7B) and Qwen-VL Chat (7B), fine-tuned with LoRA on standard VQA datasets including COCO, GQA, OCR-VQA, TextVQA, and VisualGenome. Privacy watermarks will be embedded at rates of 0%, 50%, and 100%. Downstream performance will be evaluated on ScienceQA and MME-Perception. Baselines will include original data, image transformations, and text transformations. Evaluation metrics will include probing classifier accuracy at each model layer, cosine similarity of training gradients, and membership inference attack (MIA) performance (AUCROC). Ablation studies will vary batch size and model scale to assess their effects on inadvertent memorization.
eb8d97378c2aa78dc2ade95b6558dd8a388efb12.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a systematic probing framework to detect and quantify the memorization of task-irrelevant private content in MLLMs, a dimension of privacy risk not addressed by prior work focused on task-relevant leakage.
