It demonstrates that MLLMs can encode spurious correlations from random, irrelevant data due to mini-batch training dynamics, even when such content does not affect downstream performance or is not extractable via direct prompting or standard MIAs. The work further reveals that smaller batch sizes and larger model scales exacerbate this inadvertent memorization, highlighting new risks and informing future privacy-preserving training strategies for multi-modal models.

eb923557d7d47b09cb80ed62ae10f9a6ad519a77.title: Deep Clustering With a Constraint for Topological Invariance Based on Symmetric InfoNCE
eb923557d7d47b09cb80ed62ae10f9a6ad519a77.research_question: How can deep clustering methods be improved to achieve robust performance across both non-complex and complex topology datasets, particularly in scenarios with limited prior knowledge and without domain-specific assumptions?
eb923557d7d47b09cb80ed62ae10f9a6ad519a77.hypothesis: Introducing a topological invariant constraint based on symmetric InfoNCE into deep clustering objectives will enhance clustering performance for both non-complex and complex topology datasets by enforcing local consistency in predicted cluster assignments.
eb923557d7d47b09cb80ed62ae10f9a6ad519a77.proposed_method: A novel constraint for topological invariance will be developed, leveraging symmetric InfoNCE as a regularization term within deep clustering objectives. For each pair of data points that are close in the input space (using Euclidean distance for non-complex topology or geodesic distance on a K-NN graph for complex topology), the method will maximize the similarity between their predicted cluster probability distributions produced by a neural network (MLP with softmax output). The constraint will be implemented by constructing positive pairs via two generative processes: one using Euclidean K-NN for non-complex datasets, and another using geodesic K-NN for complex datasets. The symmetric InfoNCE loss will be computed for these pairs, encouraging the model to assign similar cluster probabilities to topologically close samples. This constraint will be integrated into existing deep clustering frameworks, such as IMSAT, to form a new method (e.g., MIST), and theoretical analysis will be conducted to justify the approach.
eb923557d7d47b09cb80ed62ae10f9a6ad519a77.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of ten benchmark datasets, including both synthetic datasets with complex topology (e.g., Two-Moons, Two-Rings) and real-world datasets with non-complex topology (e.g., MNIST, STL, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, Omniglot, 20news, SVHN, Reuters10K). The proposed method will be compared against classical clustering algorithms (K-means, Spectral Clustering, GMMC) and state-of-the-art deep clustering baselines (DEC, SpectralNet, VaDE, IMSAT, IIC, CatGAN, SELA, SCAN). Evaluation metrics will include clustering accuracy, with results reported as mean and standard deviation over multiple trials. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by adapting baseline methods to the non-domain-specific scenario, and ablation studies will be performed to isolate the effect of the proposed constraint.
eb923557d7d47b09cb80ed62ae10f9a6ad519a77.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a topological invariant constraint for deep clustering based on symmetric InfoNCE, which has not previously been explored in this context. The method is designed to be effective for both non-complex and complex topology datasets without relying on domain-specific knowledge. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the use of symmetric InfoNCE and its advantages over existing constraints. The resulting method is expected to achieve state-of-the-art clustering accuracy across a diverse set of datasets, demonstrating superior versatility and robustness compared to existing deep clustering approaches.

eb95c327260725498404eb43ec370d419b8d92c7.title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
eb95c327260725498404eb43ec370d419b8d92c7.research_question: How can the execution of structured language model programs, which require multiple dependent generation calls, advanced prompting, control flow, and structured input/output, be made significantly more efficient in terms of throughput and latency across diverse LLM workloads and modalities?
eb95c327260725498404eb43ec370d419b8d92c7.hypothesis: Integrating a domain-specific programming language with a co-designed runtime that systematically exploits multi-call structures, enables KV cache reuse, accelerates constrained decoding, and supports speculative execution for API-only models will substantially improve the efficiency of structured language model program execution compared to existing systems.
eb95c327260725498404eb43ec370d419b8d92c7.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that combines a Python-embedded domain-specific language (DSL) for structured language model programming with an optimized runtime. The DSL will provide primitives for generation, parallelism, and multi-modal input handling, allowing users to compose complex LLM workflows with native Python syntax. The runtime will introduce RadixAttention, a tree-based LRU cache mechanism for automatic and systematic reuse of the key-value (KV) cache across multiple generation calls and program instances, managed via a radix tree structure and cache-aware scheduling. For structured output decoding, a compressed finite state machine (FSM) will be implemented to allow multi-token constrained decoding, accelerating output generation for regular-expression-constrained outputs. Additionally, speculative execution techniques will be incorporated to optimize multi-call programs for black-box API-only models, reducing redundant API calls and associated costs.
eb95c327260725498404eb43ec370d419b8d92c7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of LLM workloads, including agent control, logical reasoning, few-shot learning (MMLU, HellaSwag), JSON decoding, retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, multi-turn chat, and multi-modal tasks (image/video). The evaluation will utilize models such as Llama-7B/70B, Mixtral-8x7B, LLaVA-v1.5-7B (image), LLaVA-NeXT-34B (video), and OpenAI GPT-3.5/4, deployed on NVIDIA A10G and A100 GPUs. Baseline systems for comparison will include Guidance, vLLM, and LMQL, with performance measured in terms of throughput (programs per second) and latency (average per-instance latency). Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the impact of each optimization (RadixAttention, compressed FSM, speculative execution), and cache hit rates will be analyzed to correlate with performance improvements. Multi-modal and distributed settings will also be evaluated.
eb95c327260725498404eb43ec370d419b8d92c7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first systematic, tree-based LRU cache mechanism (RadixAttention) for multi-level KV cache sharing across arbitrary program structures and distributed settings, enabling cache-aware scheduling and frontend-runtime co-design. The compressed FSM for constrained decoding allows multi-token output in a single forward pass, significantly accelerating structured output generation. The integration of speculative execution for API-only models reduces redundant API calls and costs. The framework unifies these runtime optimizations with a flexible, Python-embedded DSL, supporting both open-weight and API-only models, and demonstrates substantial improvements in throughput and latency across a wide variety of LLM workloads and modalities.

eb984b142db9965b10a3b5ae5813eeb3e0f6e676.title: Sign and Basis Invariant Networks for Spectral Graph Representation Learning
eb984b142db9965b10a3b5ae5813eeb3e0f6e676.research_question: How can neural network architectures be designed to learn from eigenvectors in a manner that is invariant to sign flips and arbitrary basis choices, and does such invariance improve the expressiveness and performance of spectral graph representation learning and related tasks?
eb984b142db9965b10a3b5ae5813eeb3e0f6e676.hypothesis: Neural architectures that are explicitly invariant to eigenvector sign flips and basis changes will be more expressive and effective for spectral graph representation learning, outperforming existing methods that do not fully address these symmetries.
eb984b142db9965b10a3b5ae5813eeb3e0f6e676.proposed_method: A novel class of neural network architectures, SignNet and BasisNet, will be developed to process eigenvectors with explicit invariance to sign flips (for SignNet) and to general basis changes within eigenspaces (for BasisNet). For sign invariance, the architecture will parameterize functions as sums over neural network outputs evaluated at both v and -v for each eigenvector, ensuring invariance to sign flips. For basis invariance, the architecture will operate on orthogonal projectors (VV^T) of eigenspaces, using invariant graph networks (IGNs) to achieve invariance to basis changes and permutation equivariance. Both architectures will be extended to handle multiple eigenspaces by decomposing the invariance problem and aggregating over subspace-specific neural modules. The networks will be designed to be universal approximators for continuous functions of eigenvectors with the desired invariances, and practical variants will restrict to efficient operations (e.g., vectors and matrices) while a theoretical variant will allow higher-order tensors for maximal expressivity.
eb984b142db9965b10a3b5ae5813eeb3e0f6e676.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on tasks including molecular graph regression (using the ZINC and Alchemy datasets), substructure counting and property regression on synthetic graphs, and texture reconstruction on triangle meshes (using datasets such as those from Koestler et al.). Baseline methods will include standard GNNs with no positional encoding, Laplacian eigenvector-based positional encodings with random sign flipping, canonicalization, or absolute value, and other recent state-of-the-art positional encoding and spectral GNN approaches. Evaluation metrics will include mean absolute error (MAE) for regression tasks, as well as perceptual metrics such as PSNR, DSSIM, and LPIPS for texture reconstruction. The experimental setup will control for model parameter counts (e.g., 500k budget), and ablation studies will be performed to isolate the effects of sign and basis invariance. Additional experiments will assess computational efficiency and the ability to learn or approximate known spectral invariants and positional encodings.
eb984b142db9965b10a3b5ae5813eeb3e0f6e676.novelty_claims: The proposed architectures are the first to provide universal, learnable neural network models that are invariant to both sign flips and arbitrary basis choices in eigenvector inputs. These models strictly generalize spectral graph convolutions and can provably approximate a wide range of spectral invariants and existing graph positional encodings. The approach unifies and subsumes prior ad-hoc methods for handling eigenvector symmetries, and demonstrates both theoretical and empirical advances in expressiveness and performance on diverse graph learning tasks.

eb9a93acadbb8e2e1132a7415c81c5c2b32aeb80.title: Zero-sum Polymatrix Markov Games: Equilibrium Collapse and Efficient Computation of Nash Equilibria
eb9a93acadbb8e2e1132a7415c81c5c2b32aeb80.research_question: Can efficient computation of Nash equilibria be achieved in specific classes of multi-agent Markov games that involve both competition and coordination, and under what structural assumptions does this tractability hold?
eb9a93acadbb8e2e1132a7415c81c5c2b32aeb80.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that in zero-sum polymatrix Markov games with a switching controller per state, the set of coarse-correlated equilibria collapses to the set of Nash equilibria, enabling efficient computation of approximate Nash equilibria.
eb9a93acadbb8e2e1132a7415c81c5c2b32aeb80.proposed_method: A new class of zero-sum polymatrix Markov games is defined, where agents interact pairwise according to a state-dependent graph structure, and in each state, a single agent (the controller) determines the transition dynamics. The method generalizes equilibrium collapse results from normal-form games to Markov games by leveraging nonlinear programming formulations whose optima correspond to Nash equilibria. The approach demonstrates that, under the switching controller assumption, the marginals of any coarse-correlated equilibrium (CCE) policy form an approximate Nash equilibrium (NE). This is established by analyzing the structure of the reward and transition functions, and by showing that existing algorithms for computing approximate CCEs in Markov games can be repurposed to efficiently compute approximate NEs in this setting.
eb9a93acadbb8e2e1132a7415c81c5c2b32aeb80.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis is conducted to prove the equilibrium collapse phenomenon in both finite- and infinite-horizon settings. The computational complexity of finding an ε-approximate Nash equilibrium is characterized as polynomial in the number of agents, state and action space sizes, and 1/ε. The approach is compared conceptually to existing settings such as single-controller and two-player zero-sum Markov games, as well as zero-sum polymatrix normal-form games. Counterexamples are constructed to demonstrate that the equilibrium collapse does not occur when more than one controller per state is allowed, highlighting the necessity of the switching controller assumption. No empirical datasets or numerical experiments are specified; the evaluation is primarily theoretical and based on complexity analysis and counterexample construction.
eb9a93acadbb8e2e1132a7415c81c5c2b32aeb80.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first generalization of zero-sum polymatrix normal-form games to Markov games with dynamically changing interaction graphs and switching controllers. It establishes a new equilibrium collapse result, showing that in these games, every coarse-correlated equilibrium collapses to a Nash equilibrium, enabling efficient computation of approximate Nash equilibria. The approach unifies and extends previous tractability results for Nash equilibrium computation in multi-agent Markov games, and identifies precise structural conditions (switching controller per state) under which this tractability holds. Additionally, it provides theoretical insights into the limitations of equilibrium collapse in more general settings.

ebacf10f8881d58b61203742bde203ed3e5b0f09.title: ACCO: Accumulate While You Communicate for Communication-Overlapped Sharded LLM Training
ebacf10f8881d58b61203742bde203ed3e5b0f09.research_question: How can communication and memory bottlenecks in distributed training of large language models (LLMs) be mitigated, particularly in sharded optimizer settings and heterogeneous hardware environments, without degrading convergence or increasing memory overhead?
ebacf10f8881d58b61203742bde203ed3e5b0f09.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a memory-efficient optimization algorithm that overlaps gradient computation and communication, while compensating for delayed updates through a novel accumulation mechanism, can achieve convergence and training dynamics comparable to standard distributed optimizers, while significantly reducing communication overhead and supporting heterogeneous hardware.
ebacf10f8881d58b61203742bde203ed3e5b0f09.proposed_method: A new optimization algorithm, ACCO (Accumulate while you Communicate), is proposed for distributed LLM training. The method splits each mini-batch into two stages: the first half is used to estimate the parameters for the next step, while the second half is used to compute gradients with respect to the current parameters. These two streams—computation and communication—are run in parallel, enabling the overlap of gradient computation and parameter synchronization. A novel two-stage accumulation mechanism compensates for the delayed updates introduced by parallel execution, ensuring that the training dynamics remain aligned with those of standard distributed optimization (e.g., AdamW-DDP), without introducing additional hyperparameters or requiring a warmup phase. ACCO is designed to be compatible with sharded optimizer frameworks and supports both homogeneous and heterogeneous hardware environments.
ebacf10f8881d58b61203742bde203ed3e5b0f09.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale distributed GPU clusters, including both homogeneous and heterogeneous hardware setups. The evaluation will use a variety of LLM architectures, such as GPT-Neo (36M, 125M, and 2.7B parameters), and datasets including TinyStories, OpenWebText, and Alpaca. Baselines will include PyTorch DDP with ZeRO-1 sharding, Delayed Parameter Update (DPU), and Weight Prediction (WP) methods. Metrics for evaluation will include wall-clock training time, convergence speed, validation loss, and perplexity on benchmarks such as LAMBADA and OpenWebText. The experimental setup will utilize mixed-precision training, sharded optimizer states, and will profile parallelism using tools like NVIDIA Nsight Systems. Additional experiments will simulate hardware heterogeneity by artificially slowing down selected GPUs to assess the method's ability to mitigate straggler effects.
ebacf10f8881d58b61203742bde203ed3e5b0f09.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a memory-efficient optimization algorithm that enables full overlap of communication and computation in sharded LLM training, without requiring additional hyperparameters or warmup phases. A novel two-stage accumulation mechanism is developed to compensate for delayed updates, ensuring convergence rates and training dynamics equivalent to standard distributed optimizers. Unlike previous methods, ACCO is fully compatible with sharded optimizer frameworks and heterogeneous hardware, and eliminates the need for outer loops or increased memory overhead. Theoretical analysis guarantees standard convergence rates for both GD and SGD, and empirical results demonstrate substantial speedups and improved scalability compared to existing baselines.

ebb77213f63cda5612cc1bc48eb55c2b71a5cfd8.title: Towards image compression with perfect realism at ultra-low bitrates
ebb77213f63cda5612cc1bc48eb55c2b71a5cfd8.research_question: How can image compression at ultra-low bitrates achieve high perceptual realism, minimizing visible artifacts and decoupling visual quality from bitrate constraints?
ebb77213f63cda5612cc1bc48eb55c2b71a5cfd8.hypothesis: Conditioning a diffusion-based decoder on both vector-quantized local image representations and global semantic descriptions (e.g., image captions) enables the reconstruction of highly realistic images at ultra-low bitrates, outperforming existing codecs in perceptual quality metrics and reducing the dependency of realism on bitrate.
ebb77213f63cda5612cc1bc48eb55c2b71a5cfd8.proposed_method: A novel image compression framework, PerCo, will be developed, combining a VQ-VAE-like encoder with a conditional diffusion model as the decoder. The encoding process will generate two complementary representations: (1) a local, spatially quantized latent tensor using a hyper encoder and vector quantization, and (2) a global semantic context via automatically generated image captions (e.g., using BLIP-2), which are losslessly compressed. The decoder will reconstruct images by conditioning the diffusion process on both the quantized local features and the global semantic embedding, leveraging cross-attention and classifier-free guidance for improved realism. The latent diffusion model will operate in the autoencoder's latent space to reduce computational cost, and the entire system will be trained end-to-end, with the autoencoder weights frozen and only the hyper encoder and selected diffusion model layers finetuned.
ebb77213f63cda5612cc1bc48eb55c2b71a5cfd8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image datasets, including Kodak and MS-COCO 30k, at resolutions up to 512×512. The model will be evaluated at bitrates ranging from 0.1 down to 0.003 bits per pixel, significantly lower than most prior work. Baselines will include state-of-the-art hand-crafted codecs (e.g., VTM), neural codecs with adversarial losses (e.g., HiFiC, MS-ILLM), and recent diffusion-based approaches (e.g., Text-Sketch, DIRAC, HFD/DDPM). Evaluation metrics will focus on perceptual quality (FID, KID), semantic alignment (CLIP score, mIoU), and traditional distortion measures (LPIPS, MS-SSIM, PSNR), with emphasis on the stability of perceptual metrics across bitrates. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of local and global conditioning, classifier-free guidance, and quantization strategies.
ebb77213f63cda5612cc1bc48eb55c2b71a5cfd8.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a diffusion-based decoder for image compression conditioned on both vector-quantized local features and global semantic descriptions, enabling state-of-the-art perceptual quality at ultra-low bitrates. The method is the first to achieve high realism (as measured by FID and KID) at bitrates as low as 0.003 bpp for images up to 512×768, with realism metrics largely decoupled from bitrate. The use of textual or global image features as conditioning information for the diffusion decoder is a key innovation, and the framework advances the field towards the theoretical goal of perfect realism codecs.

ebd1c04c61f73f46def3305ca11d038c46665b65.title: Contrastive Preference Optimization: Pushing the Boundaries of LLM Performance in Machine Translation
ebd1c04c61f73f46def3305ca11d038c46665b65.research_question: How can the performance gap between moderate-sized large language models (LLMs) and state-of-the-art machine translation (MT) systems be bridged, particularly given the limitations of supervised fine-tuning and the quality issues of reference data in MT tasks?
ebd1c04c61f73f46def3305ca11d038c46665b65.hypothesis: Contrastive preference optimization (CPO), a preference-based training objective using high-quality triplet preference data, will enable moderate-sized LLMs to generate translations that match or surpass the quality of both gold references and outputs from state-of-the-art MT systems, including larger LLMs and WMT competition winners.
ebd1c04c61f73f46def3305ca11d038c46665b65.proposed_method: A novel training objective, Contrastive Preference Optimization (CPO), will be developed to directly optimize LLMs for generating superior translations and rejecting near-perfect but flawed outputs. Preference data will be constructed from triplets consisting of system outputs (from ALMA-13B-LoRA, GPT-4, and gold references) for each source sentence, with reference-free evaluation models (KIWI-XXL, XCOMET) used to determine the preferred and dis-preferred translations. The CPO loss will approximate Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) but with a uniform reference policy, resulting in a memory- and speed-efficient objective. An additional behavior cloning regularizer will be incorporated to ensure the model does not deviate significantly from the preferred data distribution. Training will update only a small fraction of model parameters (e.g., LoRA adapters), enabling efficient adaptation.
ebd1c04c61f73f46def3305ca11d038c46665b65.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 10 translation directions using high-quality parallel data from the FLORES-200 dataset, with a total of approximately 22K triplet samples for preference training. The main model, ALMA-13B-LoRA, will be fine-tuned using CPO, updating only 0.1% of parameters. Baselines will include supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on preferred data, DPO, and state-of-the-art systems such as GPT-4, WMT competition winners, and other LLM-based translators (e.g., TowerInstruct). Evaluation will primarily use reference-free metrics (KIWI-XXL, XCOMET, KIWI-22) to mitigate the influence of flawed references, and results will be reported on WMT’21, WMT’22, and WMT’23 test sets. Human evaluation will be conducted on sampled outputs to validate metric-based findings. Ablation studies will assess the impact of loss components and preference data composition.
ebd1c04c61f73f46def3305ca11d038c46665b65.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new, efficient preference-based optimization objective (CPO) for LLMs in MT, leveraging high-quality triplet preference data and reference-free evaluation. This method addresses the limitations of supervised fine-tuning and the quality ceiling imposed by gold references, enabling moderate-sized LLMs to achieve or exceed the performance of much larger models and competition-winning systems. The work also provides a new high-quality preference dataset for MT, demonstrates the importance of dis-preferred data quality, and offers a practical, low-cost adaptation strategy requiring minimal parameter updates.

ebdbded60f48131ed7ba73807c3c086993a96f89.title: WavTokenizer: an Efficient Acoustic Discrete Codec Tokenizer for Audio Language Modeling
ebdbded60f48131ed7ba73807c3c086993a96f89.research_question: How can an acoustic discrete codec tokenizer be designed to achieve extreme audio compression while maintaining high subjective reconstruction quality and rich semantic information for audio language modeling across speech, music, and general audio domains?
ebdbded60f48131ed7ba73807c3c086993a96f89.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a single-quantizer acoustic codec model, equipped with an expanded vector quantization (VQ) codebook space, advanced initialization and activation strategies, improved decoder architecture (including attention mechanisms and inverse Fourier transform upsampling), and multi-scale discriminators, can achieve state-of-the-art audio reconstruction quality and semantic richness at extremely low token rates.
ebdbded60f48131ed7ba73807c3c086993a96f89.proposed_method: The proposed method develops an acoustic discrete codec tokenizer based on a VQ-GAN framework, utilizing a full convolutional encoder to extract latent audio features, followed by a single quantizer with an expanded codebook (e.g., 4096 or 8192 entries) for discretization. K-means clustering is used to initialize the codebook, and a random awakening strategy ensures high codebook utilization. The decoder is enhanced with an attention module and ConvNeXt blocks, and employs an inverse Fourier transform for waveform upsampling, avoiding aliasing artifacts common in mirrored decoder structures. Multi-scale discriminators, including multi-period, multi-resolution, and complex STFT-based discriminators, are integrated to improve perceptual quality, and the model is trained end-to-end with a composite loss function comprising quantizer, mel-spectrum, adversarial, and feature-matching losses. The contextual modeling window is extended (e.g., to three seconds) to improve semantic capture during training.
ebdbded60f48131ed7ba73807c3c086993a96f89.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on approximately 8,000 hours of publicly available datasets spanning speech (LibriTTS, VCTK, CommonVoice), audio (AudioSet), and music (Jamendo, MusicDB). Evaluation will include both objective metrics (UTMOS, PESQ, STOI, V/UV F1) and subjective metrics (MUSHRA, CMOS) across clean, noisy, and out-of-domain environments. Baseline comparisons will be made against state-of-the-art codec models such as EnCodec, HiFi-Codec, Vocos, SpeechTokenizer, and DAC, using official model weights and configurations. Additional experiments will assess semantic representation quality on the ARCH benchmark and performance in downstream generative tasks (e.g., TTS with ParlerTTS), as well as comprehensive ablation studies to validate the contributions of each module (codebook size, contextual window, discriminator, attention, and decoder structure).
ebdbded60f48131ed7ba73807c3c086993a96f89.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first acoustic codec model to achieve effective audio reconstruction with a single quantizer at extremely low token rates (40 or 75 tokens per second), while maintaining or surpassing state-of-the-art subjective and objective quality metrics. Innovations include the expansion and efficient utilization of the VQ codebook space, integration of an attention-based decoder with inverse Fourier transform upsampling, and the use of multi-scale discriminators for perceptual quality. The method also demonstrates superior semantic representation and adaptability for downstream generative models, and provides extensive empirical validation and ablation confirming the necessity and effectiveness of each component.

ebe2a5a186fa08e4e1b5d225d7a253d444d2c396.title: ZoeDepth: Zero-shot Transfer by Combining Relative and Metric Depth
ebe2a5a186fa08e4e1b5d225d7a253d444d2c396.research_question: How can a single model be developed for monocular depth estimation that achieves both strong generalization across diverse domains and accurate metric depth prediction, overcoming the limitations of current approaches that focus on either relative or metric depth estimation?
ebe2a5a186fa08e4e1b5d225d7a253d444d2c396.hypothesis: A two-stage training framework that combines large-scale relative depth pre-training with domain-specific metric depth fine-tuning, utilizing a novel metric bins module and automatic domain routing, will enable a single model to achieve state-of-the-art metric depth estimation and unprecedented zero-shot generalization across both indoor and outdoor domains.
ebe2a5a186fa08e4e1b5d225d7a253d444d2c396.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a two-stage framework for monocular depth estimation. In the first stage, a transformer-based encoder-decoder network is pre-trained on a diverse mix of 12 datasets using a scale- and shift-invariant loss for relative depth estimation, leveraging the MiDaS training strategy and a DPT backbone with a BEiT-L encoder. In the second stage, lightweight metric heads—one per domain—are attached to the decoder, each employing a novel metric bins module that predicts per-pixel depth bins and refines them using attractor layers across decoder hierarchies. The metric bins module utilizes an ordering-aware log-binomial distribution to assign probabilities to depth bins, improving ordinal prediction. During inference, a latent classifier automatically routes each input image to the appropriate domain-specific metric head, enabling the model to adapt to diverse domains without manual intervention.
ebe2a5a186fa08e4e1b5d225d7a253d444d2c396.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pre-training the model on 12 diverse datasets for relative depth and fine-tuning on metric depth using NYU Depth v2 (indoor) and KITTI (outdoor) datasets, both individually and jointly. The evaluation will include zero-shot transfer to eight unseen datasets spanning both indoor and outdoor domains (e.g., SUN RGB-D, iBims-1, DIODE Indoor, HyperSim, DDAD, DIML Outdoor, DIODE Outdoor, Virtual KITTI2). Baselines will include state-of-the-art metric and relative depth models such as NeWCRFs, AdaBins, LocalBins, and DORN, with comparisons made under single- and multi-domain training regimes. Evaluation metrics will include absolute relative error (REL), root mean squared error (RMSE), average log10 error, and threshold accuracy at various levels. Ablation studies will assess the impact of backbone choice, metric bins module variants, and routing mechanisms.
ebe2a5a186fa08e4e1b5d225d7a253d444d2c396.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to combine large-scale relative depth pre-training with domain-specific metric fine-tuning in a unified model, enabling strong generalization and accurate metric depth estimation across domains. The metric bins module introduces attractor-based bin refinement and log-binomial probability assignment for improved ordinal prediction. The automatic domain routing mechanism allows seamless adaptation to diverse domains without manual labeling at inference. The approach demonstrates unprecedented zero-shot generalization to multiple unseen datasets and achieves significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods in both in-domain and cross-domain settings.

ebedc4d7a2356090904baba4104ef0832bc236df.title: A survey on multimodal large language models
ebedc4d7a2356090904baba4104ef0832bc236df.research_question: How can the next generation of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) be designed to achieve advanced multimodal reasoning, support a wider range of modalities, languages, and granularities, and address challenges such as multimodal hallucination and alignment with human preferences?
ebedc4d7a2356090904baba4104ef0832bc236df.hypothesis: Integrating large-scale pre-trained language models with advanced modality encoders and novel training strategies will enable MLLMs to achieve superior performance in multimodal understanding, reasoning, and generation tasks, while targeted alignment and instruction-tuning will mitigate issues such as hallucination and improve alignment with human intent.
ebedc4d7a2356090904baba4104ef0832bc236df.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed that combines pre-trained modality encoders (for images, audio, video, and potentially other modalities) with large language models (LLMs) via learnable connectors or expert model-based interfaces. The architecture will support both token-level and feature-level fusion to enable deep interaction between modalities. Training will proceed in three stages: (1) large-scale multimodal pre-training using both coarse- and fine-grained datasets to align modalities and impart world knowledge, (2) instruction-tuning with diverse, high-quality, and multi-turn instruction datasets (including self-instructed and adapted task-specific data) to enhance zero-shot and conversational capabilities, and (3) alignment tuning using human or AI-generated preference data and advanced optimization techniques such as RLHF and DPO to reduce hallucinations and align outputs with human values. The framework will be extensible to support additional modalities, languages, and finer input/output granularities, such as region- and pixel-level grounding.
ebedc4d7a2356090904baba4104ef0832bc236df.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a broad suite of benchmarks covering both closed-set and open-set multimodal tasks, including VQA, image captioning, video understanding, and domain-specific applications such as medical image analysis. Datasets for pre-training will include large-scale web-scraped image-text corpora (e.g., LAION-5B, CC-12M), fine-grained instruction datasets generated via GPT-4V, and domain-specific resources. Baselines will include prior MLLMs such as GPT-4V, LLaVA, and CLIP-based models. Evaluation metrics will span accuracy, CIDEr, BLEU, and human or GPT-4V-based preference scoring, with additional focus on hallucination rates and grounding precision. Ablation studies will assess the impact of encoder choice, connector type, instruction diversity, and alignment strategies. The experimental setup will also explore multilingual and multi-modal extensions, as well as the effect of scaling model and input sizes.
ebedc4d7a2356090904baba4104ef0832bc236df.novelty_claims: The proposed research aims to advance MLLMs by (1) systematically integrating high-resolution, multi-modal encoders with large language models using flexible connector strategies; (2) leveraging a multi-stage training pipeline that combines large-scale multimodal pre-training, diverse instruction-tuning, and targeted alignment optimization; (3) introducing extensible support for additional modalities, languages, and fine-grained input/output control; and (4) developing comprehensive evaluation protocols, including open-ended and human-preference-based assessments, to rigorously benchmark emergent capabilities and address multimodal hallucination. The approach is expected to set new standards in multimodal reasoning, generalization, and alignment with human intent.

ec072b1382e8da7480737a8cc5b9ca98dda30c9a.title: Machine Unlearning of Pre-trained Large Language Models
ec072b1382e8da7480737a8cc5b9ca98dda30c9a.research_question: How can machine unlearning be effectively and efficiently achieved for pre-trained large language models to support the removal of specific data, such as copyrighted or sensitive content, while maintaining model utility and computational feasibility?
ec072b1382e8da7480737a8cc5b9ca98dda30c9a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that approximate unlearning methods, particularly those combining gradient ascent on the forget set with gradient descent or KL-divergence constraints on the retain set, can achieve effective data removal from pre-trained LLMs with significantly lower computational cost than full retraining, while preserving model performance on retained and general tasks.
ec072b1382e8da7480737a8cc5b9ca98dda30c9a.proposed_method: A unified framework for machine unlearning in pre-trained large language models will be developed, consolidating and adapting seven distinct unlearning methodologies within the next-token prediction paradigm. The methods include gradient ascent on the forget set, fine-tuning with random labels, unlearning with adversarial samples, and hybrid strategies that combine gradient ascent with either gradient descent or KL-divergence constraints on the retain set, using both in-distribution and general data. The approach will formalize the unlearning objective to minimize the influence of designated forget sequences while preserving performance on the retained data. Approximate retraining will be introduced as a practical evaluation baseline, leveraging unseen, in-domain data to simulate the performance of a fully retrained model, thus circumventing the infeasibility of retraining large models from scratch. The methodology will also include comprehensive hyperparameter tuning guidelines to enhance robustness and efficiency.
ec072b1382e8da7480737a8cc5b9ca98dda30c9a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using an open-source 6B-parameter LLM (Yi-6B) across three domains: arXiv academic papers, GitHub code repositories, and books. For each domain, a forget set (e.g., 500 arXiv papers, 2,000 GitHub files, 100 books) will be sampled from the pre-training data, with corresponding retain and approximate sets constructed from unseen, in-domain data. The unlearning methods will be benchmarked against an approximate retraining baseline. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity and accuracy on the forget and retain sets, membership inference attack (MIA) AUC scores to assess privacy leakage, and performance on general downstream tasks (MMLU, ARC, HumanEval, GSM8K) to measure utility preservation. Computational efficiency will be quantified using FLOPs, and ablation studies will be performed to analyze the impact of learning rate and optimization steps on unlearning effectiveness and stability.
ec072b1382e8da7480737a8cc5b9ca98dda30c9a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first comprehensive framework for machine unlearning in pre-trained LLMs, addressing a critical gap in prior research which has largely focused on fine-tuned models or limited-scale settings. It adapts and unifies multiple unlearning strategies for generative language models, establishes a practical and reproducible approximate retraining baseline for evaluation, and provides open-source datasets sampled from real pre-training corpora. The approach claims over 100,000-fold improvement in computational efficiency compared to full retraining, and demonstrates that hybrid gradient ascent/descent methods offer superior hyperparameter robustness. Detailed hyperparameter tuning guidelines are also provided to facilitate practical deployment of unlearning in large-scale LLMs.

ec0b78cd2d2ddbe69f0b487049e1754c9350b2ea.title: QLASS: Boosting Language Agent Inference via Q-Guided Stepwise Search
ec0b78cd2d2ddbe69f0b487049e1754c9350b2ea.research_question: How can language agents be improved to make more effective stepwise decisions in complex interactive tasks, particularly in scenarios with limited annotated data and sparse outcome rewards?
ec0b78cd2d2ddbe69f0b487049e1754c9350b2ea.hypothesis: Incorporating stepwise Q-value estimation as process rewards and guiding inference-time generation with a learned Q-value model will enable language agents to make more effective decisions, improve performance on complex tasks, and maintain robustness even with reduced supervision.
ec0b78cd2d2ddbe69f0b487049e1754c9350b2ea.proposed_method: A novel framework, QLASS (Q-guided Language Agent Stepwise Search), will be developed to enhance language agent inference by modeling process rewards through stepwise Q-value estimation. The approach begins with supervised fine-tuning (behavior cloning) of a base language agent on expert-annotated trajectories. During self-generation, the agent constructs exploration trees for each task, where each node represents a state-action pair and is annotated with an estimated Q-value using the Bellman equation to propagate future rewards. A neural Q-network (QNet) is then trained in a supervised manner to predict Q-values for any partial trajectory, using the collected Q-value-labeled nodes as training data. For inference, a Q-guided generation strategy is employed: at each step, the agent samples several candidate actions and selects the one with the highest predicted Q-value from QNet, thus prioritizing actions that maximize long-term expected rewards.
ec0b78cd2d2ddbe69f0b487049e1754c9350b2ea.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three complex agent benchmarks: WebShop, ALFWorld, and SciWorld, each providing only sparse outcome rewards at the end of trajectories. The main evaluation metric will be the average reward achieved on test sets, with both seen and unseen cases considered. Baselines will include supervised fine-tuning (SFT), rejection sampling fine-tuning (RFT), preference-based optimization (ETO), reinforcement learning (PPO), and inference-time search methods such as Best-of-N sampling. Closed-source models like GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-4, and Reflexion will also be included for comparison. The impact of QLASS will be assessed under varying annotation budgets (e.g., with only half the expert data), and ablations will be performed to compare different process reward modeling strategies (Q-value, average reward, and outcome reward propagation). The experiments will ensure fair comparison by controlling for search budgets and model architectures.
ec0b78cd2d2ddbe69f0b487049e1754c9350b2ea.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a process reward modeling framework for language agents that leverages stepwise Q-value estimation from exploration trees, enabling effective intermediate guidance without requiring dense human annotation. The Q-guided generation strategy provides a principled way to steer agent inference towards actions with higher long-term value, outperforming both training-based and inference-based baselines, including those relying on proprietary models. The approach demonstrates strong robustness to limited supervision, achieving high performance even with reduced annotated data, and offers a scalable, efficient alternative to costly reinforcement learning or human-in-the-loop reward modeling.

ec29f2eecd1ae07a4318398fba1fd76e2828c1f0.title: Tensor Train Low-rank Approximation (TT-LoRA): Democratizing AI with Accelerated LLMs
ec29f2eecd1ae07a4318398fba1fd76e2828c1f0.research_question: How can the number of trainable parameters required for fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) be significantly reduced without compromising downstream task performance, thereby enabling efficient deployment on resource-constrained platforms?
ec29f2eecd1ae07a4318398fba1fd76e2828c1f0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that integrating optimized tensor train (TT) decomposition directly into the fine-tuning process of LLMs, while eliminating Adapters and traditional LoRA-based structures, will achieve greater model compression and reduced computational overhead without sacrificing accuracy on downstream tasks.
ec29f2eecd1ae07a4318398fba1fd76e2828c1f0.proposed_method: A novel parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) approach, Tensor Train Low-Rank Approximation (TT-LoRA), will be developed. This method will directly decompose the weight updating matrix into a series of low-rank, three-dimensional tensor cores using TT decomposition, bypassing the need for Adapters and LoRA-style matrix factorization. The pre-trained model weights will remain frozen, and only the TT-decomposed update tensors will be trained, substantially reducing the number of trainable parameters. A comprehensive hyperparameter search will be conducted to optimize tensor shapes, TT ranks, and scaling factors (alpha) for each model and task. The method will be applied to key weight matrices (e.g., Wq and Wv in Transformer layers) identified as most impactful for fine-tuning.
ec29f2eecd1ae07a4318398fba1fd76e2828c1f0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of LLMs, including BERT-based models (DeBERTa, RoBERTa) and larger models (LLaMA-2-7B, LLaMA-3-8B), using the GLUE and SuperGLUE benchmarks. Baseline comparisons will include full fine-tuning, Adapters, Prompt Tuning, Prefix Tuning, BitFit, LoRA, and LoRETTA. Evaluation metrics will include task-specific accuracies, F1 scores, Matthews correlation coefficient, and Spearman correlation. The experimental setup will leverage high-performance computing resources (NVIDIA H100 GPUs) and employ early stopping and HyperBand-based hyperparameter optimization. Detailed memory and storage analyses will be performed to quantify compression ratios, and exhaustive parameter searches will establish benchmarks for the trade-off between compression and performance.
ec29f2eecd1ae07a4318398fba1fd76e2828c1f0.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a direct integration of TT decomposition into the fine-tuning process, eliminating the need for Adapters and LoRA-based structures, which reduces inference latency and computational overhead. TT-LoRA achieves significantly higher compression ratios—up to several thousand-fold—compared to existing PEFT methods, while maintaining or improving downstream task performance. The approach enables fine-tuning of very large LLMs with minimal trainable parameters, facilitating deployment on resource-constrained hardware. An exhaustive parameter search provides new benchmarks for the compression-performance trade-off, offering practical guidance for future PEFT strategies.

ec2ce4e38af8bc82f1b8928ba51a84911bad0cc6.title: Gemma 2: Improving Open Language Models at a Practical Size
ec2ce4e38af8bc82f1b8928ba51a84911bad0cc6.research_question: How can the performance of open-source language models at practical sizes be significantly improved without solely increasing training data or model size, while maintaining safety, efficiency, and low memorization rates?
ec2ce4e38af8bc82f1b8928ba51a84911bad0cc6.hypothesis: Integrating knowledge distillation from larger teacher models, interleaving local-global attention mechanisms, and employing grouped-query attention in the Transformer architecture will yield smaller language models that achieve state-of-the-art performance relative to their size, with improved safety and reduced memorization compared to prior models.
ec2ce4e38af8bc82f1b8928ba51a84911bad0cc6.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves developing a family of decoder-only Transformer-based language models ranging from 2B to 27B parameters. Key architectural modifications include alternating local sliding window attention and global attention layers, employing Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) for efficient inference, and using pre-norm and post-norm RMSNorm for training stability. The 2B and 9B models are trained using knowledge distillation, where a large teacher model provides token-level probability distributions as targets, enabling richer gradients and effective learning beyond the compute-optimal token count. Additional techniques include logit soft-capping to control output distributions, use of a large multilingual vocabulary, and careful data filtering to reduce the risk of memorization and unsafe outputs. Post-training involves supervised fine-tuning on a mix of synthetic and human-generated prompt-response pairs, followed by reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) to further align the models with helpfulness and safety objectives.
ec2ce4e38af8bc82f1b8928ba51a84911bad0cc6.experiment_details: Experiments will train models of 2B, 9B, and 27B parameters on up to 13 trillion tokens of primarily English data, including web documents, code, and scientific articles. The 2B and 9B models will be trained with knowledge distillation from a larger teacher model, while the 27B model will be trained from scratch. Evaluation will be conducted on a wide range of academic and human-preference benchmarks, such as MMLU, GSM8K, ARC-c, HellaSwag, Winogrande, and others, comparing against state-of-the-art open models like LLaMA-3 and Qwen1.5. Human evaluations will include single-turn and multi-turn dialogue assessments, safety and instruction-following metrics, and Chatbot Arena Elo ratings. Memorization and privacy will be assessed using verbatim and approximate memorization rates, with additional checks for personal data leakage. Baselines will include prior Gemma models, Mistral, and LLaMA-3, with evaluation metrics such as accuracy, F1, pass@1, and human satisfaction scores.
ec2ce4e38af8bc82f1b8928ba51a84911bad0cc6.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a combination of knowledge distillation at scale, interleaved local-global attention, and grouped-query attention in practical-size open models, resulting in state-of-the-art performance for their parameter range. The approach demonstrates that small models can achieve competitive results with models 2-3 times larger, while maintaining low memorization rates and improved safety. Additional innovations include efficient training recipes, robust data filtering, and comprehensive post-training alignment strategies, establishing new benchmarks for open-source language models in both automated and human evaluations.

ec3d27dbfdd9431720c8a848b0ac33145dac58be.title: Scalable Discrete Diffusion Samplers: Combinatorial Optimization and Statistical Physics
ec3d27dbfdd9431720c8a848b0ac33145dac58be.research_question: How can scalable and memory-efficient discrete diffusion models be developed for sampling from complex unnormalized distributions in discrete domains, with applications to combinatorial optimization and statistical physics, while enabling both high-quality solution generation and unbiased sampling?
ec3d27dbfdd9431720c8a848b0ac33145dac58be.hypothesis: Employing novel training objectives for discrete diffusion models—specifically, a reverse KL divergence objective optimized via reinforcement learning and a forward KL divergence objective leveraging self-normalized neural importance sampling—will enable memory-efficient training with more diffusion steps, improve solution quality in unsupervised combinatorial optimization, and allow for unbiased sampling in scientific applications.
ec3d27dbfdd9431720c8a848b0ac33145dac58be.proposed_method: A scalable discrete diffusion sampler (SDDS) framework will be developed, introducing two alternative training objectives to address memory scaling limitations. The first method minimizes the reverse KL divergence using the policy gradient theorem, integrating reinforcement learning techniques such as Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to enable efficient optimization and sampling across diffusion steps. The second method adapts Self-Normalized Neural Importance Sampling (SN-NIS) to estimate unbiased gradients for the forward KL divergence, using Monte Carlo estimation to allow mini-batching over diffusion steps and reduce memory requirements. For unbiased sampling, SN-NIS and Neural Markov Chain Monte Carlo (NMCMC) will be extended to work with approximate likelihood models such as diffusion models, enabling unbiased computation of expectation values and partition functions even when exact likelihoods are unavailable.
ec3d27dbfdd9431720c8a848b0ac33145dac58be.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on unsupervised combinatorial optimization (UCO) benchmarks, covering Maximum Independent Set, Maximum Clique, Minimum Dominating Set, and Maximum Cut problems, using both small (200-300 nodes) and large (800-1200 nodes) graph datasets. Each dataset will be split into training, validation, and test sets, and models will be conditioned on problem instances via graph neural networks. Baselines will include autoregressive models, mean-field models, and classical solvers such as Gurobi. Evaluation metrics will include average solution quality, best-of-many sampling, and computational efficiency under fixed resource constraints. For unbiased sampling, experiments will use the 2D Ising model and the Edwards-Anderson model, comparing estimated free energy, internal energy, entropy, and effective sample size to theoretical values and autoregressive baselines. Diffusion models will be implemented with U-Net or GNN architectures, and the number of diffusion steps will be varied to assess scalability and performance.
ec3d27dbfdd9431720c8a848b0ac33145dac58be.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces two novel, memory-efficient training objectives for discrete diffusion models, enabling a significantly increased number of diffusion steps without linear memory scaling. It is the first to adapt SN-NIS and NMCMC for unbiased sampling with approximate likelihood models in discrete domains, overcoming a key limitation of prior approaches. The proposed methods are expected to achieve state-of-the-art results in unsupervised combinatorial optimization and enable unbiased sampling in scientific applications where only unnormalized distributions are available. This work opens new avenues for applying diffusion models to discrete scientific problems previously restricted to exact likelihood models.

ec4398c262169eb7c8bcec0ad9916dd898a9a5d1.title: Understanding and Mitigating Copying in Diffusion Models
ec4398c262169eb7c8bcec0ad9916dd898a9a5d1.research_question: What are the underlying causes of training data replication (copying) in text-to-image diffusion models, and how can this replication be effectively mitigated to reduce memorization and copying of training data in generated outputs?
ec4398c262169eb7c8bcec0ad9916dd898a9a5d1.hypothesis: Replication in diffusion models is not solely caused by duplicated images in the training set; the diversity and specificity of text conditioning (captions) play a critical role in memorization and copying behavior. Increasing caption diversity and randomizing text conditioning during training or inference will significantly reduce data replication, even in the presence of image duplication.
ec4398c262169eb7c8bcec0ad9916dd898a9a5d1.proposed_method: A comprehensive experimental framework will be developed to analyze the factors contributing to memorization in text-to-image diffusion models. The approach involves training and fine-tuning diffusion models (such as Stable Diffusion) on curated datasets with controlled levels of image and caption duplication. Various conditioning strategies will be systematically tested, including fixed captions, class-based captions, unique (BLIP-generated) captions, and random captions. Multiple mitigation strategies will be proposed and evaluated, including randomizing or augmenting image captions during training (e.g., generating multiple captions per image, adding random tokens or numbers, or introducing Gaussian noise to text embeddings), as well as inference-time interventions that alter prompt structure. The methodology will also include the identification and analysis of duplicated image clusters and caption clusters in large-scale datasets using similarity metrics.
ec4398c262169eb7c8bcec0ad9916dd898a9a5d1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using subsets of the LAION-2B dataset (e.g., LAION-10k, LAION-100k) and Imagenette, with both captioned and uncaptained data. Stable Diffusion v2.1 will serve as the primary model, with fine-tuning performed on the U-Net component for 100,000 iterations at a resolution of 256x256 and batch size 16. Baseline comparisons will include models trained with no duplication, full duplication (image and caption), and partial duplication (image only, with diverse captions). Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for image quality and diversity, SSCD similarity scores for measuring memorization (focusing on the top 5% of most similar generated images), and CLIP/ClipScore for semantic alignment. Additional analyses will assess the impact of training duration, dataset size, and image complexity (using histogram entropy and JPEG compressibility) on memorization. Both training-time and inference-time mitigation strategies will be quantitatively compared for their effectiveness in reducing copying behavior.
ec4398c262169eb7c8bcec0ad9916dd898a9a5d1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the insight that text conditioning, particularly caption diversity and specificity, is a fundamental driver of memorization and copying in diffusion models, beyond the previously emphasized role of image duplication. It proposes and systematically evaluates a suite of novel mitigation strategies that randomize or diversify text conditioning at both training and inference time, demonstrating that these approaches can substantially reduce replication even in large-scale, modern diffusion models. The work provides a detailed empirical analysis of the interplay between data duplication, caption diversity, training regimen, and image complexity, offering actionable recommendations for safer model training and deployment.

ec54ee7e6ee669dbead0db13f336042e6ccf18a1.title: Low-rank lottery tickets: finding efficient low-rank neural networks via matrix differential equations
ec54ee7e6ee669dbead0db13f336042e6ccf18a1.research_question: How can neural network architectures be made more efficient in terms of memory and computational demands, particularly by identifying and training low-rank subnetworks, while maintaining high predictive accuracy?
ec54ee7e6ee669dbead0db13f336042e6ccf18a1.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that constraining neural network weight matrices to low-rank manifolds and dynamically adapting their ranks during training will yield subnetworks that are significantly more efficient in terms of memory and computation, while achieving comparable accuracy to their full-rank counterparts.
ec54ee7e6ee669dbead0db13f336042e6ccf18a1.proposed_method: A novel training algorithm will be developed that constrains the weight matrices of neural networks to lie on low-rank manifolds throughout the training process. The method interprets neural network training as a continuous-time gradient flow and employs matrix differential equation techniques, specifically Dynamical Low-Rank Approximation (DLRA), to update low-rank factors (U, S, V) instead of the full weight matrices. The approach uses a rank-adaptive integrator based on the unconventional KLS method, allowing the ranks of the weight matrices to be dynamically adjusted according to the training dynamics. The algorithm alternates between updating the low-rank factors via coupled ODEs, orthonormalizing basis matrices, and truncating small singular values to maintain efficiency. Efficient gradient computation is achieved by taping gradients with respect to the low-rank factors, and the method supports both fixed and adaptive rank regimes.
ec54ee7e6ee669dbead0db13f336042e6ccf18a1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmarks, including MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet1K, using both fully-connected and convolutional architectures such as LeNet5, ResNet-50, VGG16, and AlexNet. The proposed method will be compared against full-rank baselines and state-of-the-art pruning and low-rank training techniques (e.g., SVDprune, LRNN, GAL, SSL, NISP). Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy, parameter count, compression ratio, and computational cost (training and inference time). Training will use optimizers such as SGD and Adam, with hyperparameters like learning rate and singular value threshold for rank adaptation. Both fixed-rank and adaptive-rank variants will be assessed, and robustness to small singular values will be analyzed. Experiments will be run on both CPU and GPU hardware, and results will be averaged over multiple runs to ensure statistical significance.
ec54ee7e6ee669dbead0db13f336042e6ccf18a1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a dynamic, rank-adaptive low-rank training paradigm for neural networks, enabling the discovery of highly efficient low-rank subnetworks directly during training. Unlike prior methods, the algorithm does not require pre-training or manual rank selection, and it provides theoretical guarantees of approximation accuracy and monotonic loss descent. The method is robust to small singular values and achieves significant reductions in memory and computational costs for both training and inference, while maintaining competitive accuracy. Automatic rank adaptation eliminates the need for hyperparameter grid search over ranks, and the approach offers a principled alternative to traditional pruning and fixed low-rank factorization techniques.

ec58a564fdda29e6a9a0a7bab5eeb4c290f716d7.title: ChatEval: Towards Better LLM-based Evaluators through Multi-Agent Debate
ec58a564fdda29e6a9a0a7bab5eeb4c290f716d7.research_question: How can the evaluation of generated text, particularly for open-ended questions and dialogue response generation, be improved to better align with human judgment and overcome the limitations of single-agent LLM-based evaluators?
ec58a564fdda29e6a9a0a7bab5eeb4c290f716d7.hypothesis: A multi-agent debate framework, where multiple LLMs with diverse role prompts autonomously discuss and evaluate generated responses using structured communication strategies, will yield evaluation results that are more accurate and better correlated with human assessments compared to single-agent LLM evaluators.
ec58a564fdda29e6a9a0a7bab5eeb4c290f716d7.proposed_method: A multi-agent debate framework will be developed, wherein each agent is instantiated as an LLM (e.g., GPT-4 or ChatGPT) assigned a unique role prompt to simulate diverse evaluative perspectives. The agents will autonomously engage in structured group discussions using one of several communication strategies: (1) one-by-one turn-taking, (2) simultaneous response generation, or (3) simultaneous response generation with an additional summarizer agent that distills the discussion at each round. The agents will exchange responses over multiple rounds, with chat histories maintained according to the chosen strategy. Final evaluation decisions will be derived either by majority vote (for categorical judgments) or by averaging scores (for numerical ratings), ensuring impartiality and robustness. The system will be implemented to allow composability and scalability, supporting easy experimentation with different agent configurations and communication protocols.
ec58a564fdda29e6a9a0a7bab5eeb4c290f716d7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two benchmark tasks: open-ended question answering (using the FairEval dataset) and dialogue response generation (using the Topical-Chat dataset). Human annotation results from prior studies will serve as ground truth for comparison. The proposed multi-agent framework will be evaluated against single-agent LLM evaluators, as well as established baselines such as FairEval (with Multiple Evidence Calibration and Balanced Position Calibration), G-EVAL, and traditional automatic metrics like ROUGE, BLEU, and BERTScore. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy and Kappa correlation for open-ended question answering, and turn-level Spearman and Kendall-Tau correlations for dialogue response generation. Experiments will systematically vary the number of agents, discussion turns, role prompt diversity, and communication strategies to analyze their impact on evaluation performance.
ec58a564fdda29e6a9a0a7bab5eeb4c290f716d7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a multi-agent debate framework for LLM-based text evaluation, moving beyond single-agent prompting by leveraging diverse role prompts and structured inter-agent communication. The method systematically investigates and demonstrates the necessity of role diversity and the impact of different communication strategies on evaluation quality. The framework is designed to be composable and scalable, enabling flexible experimentation with agent roles and debate protocols. Empirical results are expected to show superior alignment with human judgment compared to existing single-agent and automatic evaluation methods, and the approach offers a human-mimicking, interactive evaluation process that captures nuanced perspectives often missed by traditional metrics.

ec7e33597160535af56f046b8d6914ff49c66e1a.title: Gaussian Splatting SLAM
ec7e33597160535af56f046b8d6914ff49c66e1a.research_question: How can a unified, high-fidelity, and efficient 3D scene representation be developed for live monocular and RGB-D SLAM systems, enabling robust camera tracking, mapping, and novel view synthesis, including the reconstruction of challenging scene elements such as thin structures and transparent objects?
ec7e33597160535af56f046b8d6914ff49c66e1a.hypothesis: A dense 3D representation based solely on anisotropic Gaussians, combined with differentiable rasterisation and novel regularisation and optimisation techniques, will enable a live SLAM system to achieve state-of-the-art camera tracking accuracy, high-fidelity mapping, and efficient novel view synthesis, even in challenging monocular settings.
ec7e33597160535af56f046b8d6914ff49c66e1a.proposed_method: A new SLAM system will be developed that uses 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) as the sole scene representation. The method will incrementally construct and optimise a map of anisotropic 3D Gaussians, each parameterised by position, covariance (shape), colour, and opacity, directly from incoming RGB or RGB-D frames. Camera poses will be jointly optimised with the Gaussian parameters using direct photometric and, when available, geometric residuals, leveraging an analytically derived Jacobian on the Lie group SE(3) for efficient gradient-based optimisation. The system will employ differentiable rasterisation for rapid and scalable rendering and gradient computation, enabling efficient tracking and mapping loops. Additional innovations will include isotropic regularisation of Gaussian shapes to prevent degenerate geometry, geometric verification and pruning to maintain map consistency, and a keyframe management strategy based on occlusion-aware covisibility estimation.
ec7e33597160535af56f046b8d6914ff49c66e1a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both real-world and synthetic datasets, including the TUM RGB-D and Replica datasets, as well as self-captured sequences with challenging scene elements. The system will be evaluated in both monocular and RGB-D settings. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art direct and learning-based visual odometry methods (e.g., DSO, DROID-SLAM, DepthCov), as well as recent map-centric and neural implicit SLAM systems (e.g., iMAP, NICE-SLAM, Point-SLAM, ESLAM, Vox-Fusion). Evaluation metrics will comprise Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE) RMSE for camera tracking, and photometric rendering quality metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for map fidelity and novel view synthesis. Ablation studies will assess the impact of regularisation, geometric residuals, and keyframe selection. Additional analyses will include memory usage and convergence basin experiments to evaluate robustness and efficiency.
ec7e33597160535af56f046b8d6914ff49c66e1a.novelty_claims: The proposed system will be the first near real-time SLAM framework to use 3D Gaussian Splatting as the sole underlying scene representation, unifying tracking, mapping, and rendering. Key innovations include the derivation and integration of an analytic Jacobian for camera pose optimisation with respect to a 3D Gaussian map, isotropic regularisation to ensure geometric consistency, and a novel occlusion-aware keyframe management and Gaussian pruning strategy. The approach is expected to achieve state-of-the-art results in both camera tracking and novel view synthesis, with significant advances in the fidelity and diversity of scene elements captured, including thin and transparent objects, all while maintaining high computational efficiency suitable for live operation.

ec97a1565dff9d2fab1ef489e47296bbef68b680.title: Using Human Feedback to Fine-tune Diffusion Models without Any Reward Model
ec97a1565dff9d2fab1ef489e47296bbef68b680.research_question: How can diffusion models be fine-tuned to align with human preferences for tasks such as image quality, safety, and prompt-image alignment, without relying on the development or training of explicit reward models?
ec97a1565dff9d2fab1ef489e47296bbef68b680.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that diffusion models can be directly fine-tuned using human preference feedback, bypassing the need for a separate reward model, while achieving performance comparable to or better than methods that utilize explicit reward models.
ec97a1565dff9d2fab1ef489e47296bbef68b680.proposed_method: A novel method, Direct Preference for Denoising Diffusion Policy Optimization (D3PO), is proposed to fine-tune diffusion models directly from human feedback without training a reward model. The denoising process of the diffusion model is formulated as a multi-step Markov Decision Process (MDP), enabling the application of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) theory to update model parameters based on human preferences. At each training iteration, two images are generated from the same prompt and initial noise; human evaluators select the preferred image according to task-specific criteria (e.g., alignment, safety, aesthetics). The model parameters are updated using a DPO-style loss, which leverages the relative likelihoods of the preferred and non-preferred outputs at each denoising step, thus maximizing the probability of generating images that align with human preferences. This approach includes a KL-divergence regularization to prevent the fine-tuned policy from deviating excessively from the reference model, and utilizes all intermediate states in the denoising trajectory to maximize data efficiency.
ec97a1565dff9d2fab1ef489e47296bbef68b680.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of objectives, including quantifiable metrics (such as image compressibility and LAION aesthetic score) and challenging subjective tasks (such as reducing hand and body deformities, increasing image safety, and improving prompt-image alignment). Stable Diffusion v1.5 and the Anything v5 model will be used as base models for image generation. Human feedback will be collected for subjective tasks, while objective tasks will use measurable metrics as proxies for preference. Baselines will include DDPO, DPOK, and Reward Weighted methods, all of which require explicit reward models. Evaluation metrics will include normalcy and deformity rates, safety rates, CLIP and BLIP scores, ImageReward scores, and human preference rates. The experimental setup involves generating multiple images per prompt, collecting human or metric-based preferences, and tracking performance over training epochs.
ec97a1565dff9d2fab1ef489e47296bbef68b680.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to fine-tune diffusion models directly from human feedback without any reward model, significantly reducing computational overhead and annotation costs. By extending DPO theory to multi-step MDPs and leveraging all denoising steps for preference-based updates, the approach achieves efficient and effective alignment with human preferences. Theoretical analysis demonstrates equivalence to optimal reward-model-based policy updates, and empirical results are expected to show competitive or superior performance compared to state-of-the-art reward-model-based fine-tuning methods, especially in tasks lacking robust automated reward models.

ec9936ca344c640ef76ec551528512355a69cfc1.title: SmartRAG: Jointly Learn RAG-Related Tasks From the Environment Feedback
ec9936ca344c640ef76ec551528512355a69cfc1.research_question: How can retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems be holistically optimized to improve performance on knowledge-intensive tasks, minimizing retrieval cost and maximizing answer accuracy, by leveraging environment feedback rather than separate module supervision?
ec9936ca344c640ef76ec551528512355a69cfc1.hypothesis: Jointly optimizing all modules of a RAG system through reinforcement learning with environment-based feedback will result in superior performance and more efficient retrieval behavior compared to systems where modules are trained separately.
ec9936ca344c640ef76ec551528512355a69cfc1.proposed_method: A new framework, SmartRAG, is proposed that integrates a policy network and a retriever into a unified system. The policy network, implemented as a large language model (LLM), serves three roles: (1) decision maker to determine when to retrieve, (2) query rewriter to generate optimal search queries for the retriever, and (3) answer generator to produce the final response with or without retrieved observations. The system is first initialized via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on a constructed dataset to ensure correct output formatting and basic competency. Subsequently, the entire SmartRAG pipeline is jointly optimized using reinforcement learning, specifically Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), where the reward function is designed to encourage correct answers while penalizing unnecessary retrievals. The reward combines exact match, soft match (F1 score), and retrieval cost, allowing the policy network to learn optimal retrieval and answer strategies in an end-to-end manner.
ec9936ca344c640ef76ec551528512355a69cfc1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several open-domain QA benchmarks, including PopQA, AmbigNQ, and HotpotQA, as well as additional datasets such as TrivialQA, OpenBookQA, MedQA-cn, and ARC-c for broader analysis. The Bing search engine will serve as the retriever, returning the top K (typically K=4) snippets per query. Two base LLMs, Flan-T5-large and LlaMa2-7B, will be used for the policy network. Baselines for comparison include Vanilla RAG, SFT RAG, GPT4Rewriter+SFT RAG, Self-RAG, SKR, ReAct, IRCoT, and non-retrieval baselines (ICL, SFT). Evaluation metrics will include exact match (EM), F1 score, and a 'hit' metric indicating whether the retrieved observation contains the correct answer. Training involves an SFT warm-up (1 epoch, lr=3e-4, batch size 8) followed by PPO-based RL (trajectory length 5120, lr=2e-6, batch size 32, retrieval penalty alpha=0.2, retrieval quota N=1). Ablation studies will assess the impact of query rewriting and answer generation modules, and transfer experiments will evaluate generalization to unseen datasets.
ec9936ca344c640ef76ec551528512355a69cfc1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully end-to-end, jointly optimized RAG system where all modules (decision making, query rewriting, answer generation) are trained together using reinforcement learning from environment feedback, rather than relying on proxy supervision or separate module training. The policy network is capable of dynamically deciding when and what to retrieve, and how to generate answers, leading to improved efficiency and accuracy. Empirical results demonstrate superior performance over state-of-the-art baselines, reduced retrieval costs, and enhanced adaptability to both the knowledge base and the model's own capabilities. The method also shows improved transferability to new datasets, highlighting the benefits of holistic system optimization.

eca2914873cf7b88824af8a661aa087b57032b0f.title: Diffusion Recommender Model
eca2914873cf7b88824af8a661aa087b57032b0f.research_question: How can the generative process of user-item interactions in recommender systems be more accurately modeled to address the limitations of existing generative models, such as instability and restricted representation ability, especially in the presence of noisy data, large-scale item sets, and temporal shifts in user preferences?
eca2914873cf7b88824af8a661aa087b57032b0f.hypothesis: Diffusion models, when adapted for recommender systems, can more robustly and accurately capture the complex generative process of user interactions, outperforming traditional GAN- and VAE-based generative recommenders, particularly under noisy, large-scale, and temporally dynamic conditions.
eca2914873cf7b88824af8a661aa087b57032b0f.proposed_method: A novel diffusion-based framework for recommendation, termed DiffRec, is proposed to model the generative process of user-item interactions in a denoising manner. The method introduces a forward process that gradually corrupts user interaction histories with scheduled Gaussian noise, followed by a reverse process that iteratively denoises and reconstructs the original interactions via a parameterized neural network. To retain personalized information, the noise schedule is carefully controlled to avoid corrupting user histories into pure noise. Two key extensions are developed: L-DiffRec, which clusters items for dimension compression and performs diffusion in a latent space to reduce resource costs for large-scale item prediction; and T-DiffRec, which incorporates temporal information by reweighting user interactions based on timestamps, allowing the model to capture temporal shifts in user preference. Training is performed by maximizing a modified evidence lower bound (ELBO) tailored to the recommendation setting, with importance sampling to focus optimization on harder denoising steps.
eca2914873cf7b88824af8a661aa087b57032b0f.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three real-world datasets (Amazon-book, Yelp, and ML-1M), each split into clean, noisy (with natural and random noise), and temporal training settings. The proposed methods are compared against a range of strong baselines, including both generative (MultiVAE, MultiDAE, CODIGEM) and non-generative (MF, LightGCN) recommenders, as well as a state-of-the-art sequential model (ACVAE) for temporal modeling. Evaluation metrics include Recall@K and NDCG@K under a full-ranking protocol, with K set to 10 and 20. Extensive hyperparameter tuning is performed for all models, and resource costs (parameters and GPU memory) are reported for scalability analysis. Ablation studies examine the effects of noise scale, diffusion steps, importance sampling, and latent clustering.
eca2914873cf7b88824af8a661aa087b57032b0f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first diffusion-based paradigm for generative recommendation, leveraging the denoising process to better model noisy and complex user interaction generation. Key innovations include a personalized noise schedule for forward corruption, latent-space diffusion with item clustering for scalable large-scale prediction, and a simple yet effective temporal reweighting strategy for modeling user preference shifts. The method demonstrates superior accuracy and robustness over competitive baselines, especially under noisy and temporal settings, and achieves significant reductions in resource costs with the L-DiffRec extension, making it suitable for industrial-scale applications.
