eca8a3e6383e3618e0bc984382e08c09be3cca6c.title: TimeChat: A Time-sensitive Multimodal Large Language Model for Long Video Understanding
eca8a3e6383e3618e0bc984382e08c09be3cca6c.research_question: How can a multimodal large language model be developed to effectively understand, localize, and summarize events in long-form videos, including precise temporal associations between visual content and timestamps, to satisfy realistic user requirements across diverse video comprehension tasks?
eca8a3e6383e3618e0bc984382e08c09be3cca6c.hypothesis: Integrating a timestamp-aware frame encoder with a sliding video Q-Former into a multimodal large language model, and instruction-tuning it on a diverse, time-sensitive dataset, will significantly improve the model's ability to temporally localize, summarize, and interact with long-form videos compared to existing video-language models.
eca8a3e6383e3618e0bc984382e08c09be3cca6c.proposed_method: A novel multimodal large language model, named TimeChat, will be developed for long video understanding. The architecture will include a timestamp-aware frame encoder that binds visual tokens with their corresponding timestamp descriptions at the frame level, ensuring explicit time-vision associations. A sliding video Q-Former will be introduced to aggregate and compress frame-level visual tokens within a moving window, producing a variable-length sequence of video tokens adaptable to different video durations and preserving temporal semantics. These video tokens, along with optional transcribed speech and user instructions, will be concatenated and input to a large language model (e.g., LLaMA-2) for response generation. The model will be instruction-tuned using a newly constructed dataset, TimeIT, which covers a wide range of timestamp-related video tasks and domains.
eca8a3e6383e3618e0bc984382e08c09be3cca6c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three core long video understanding tasks: dense video captioning (YouCook2), temporal video grounding (Charades-STA), and video highlight detection (QVHighlights), all evaluated in zero-shot settings. The evaluation will use standard metrics such as SODA_c, CIDEr, F1 score for captioning, mAP and HIT@1 for highlight detection, and R@1 (IoU=0.5/0.7) for temporal grounding. Baselines will include both multi-model pipelines (e.g., InstructBLIP+ChatGPT, VideoChat-Text) and end-to-end video-language models (e.g., Video-LLaMA, VideoChat-Embed, Valley) with comparable model sizes. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of the timestamp-aware frame encoder and sliding video Q-Former. Additional experiments will test scalability with respect to input video length and generalization to new domains (e.g., movies, egocentric videos).
eca8a3e6383e3618e0bc984382e08c09be3cca6c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces two key innovations: (1) a timestamp-aware frame encoder that explicitly binds visual content to temporal information at the frame level, and (2) a sliding video Q-Former that enables adaptive, variable-length video token representation for long videos, preserving temporal semantics. The construction of the TimeIT dataset provides the first large-scale, instruction-tuning resource focused on time-sensitive video tasks, supporting diverse and realistic user instructions. The method unifies a broad range of time-sensitive video understanding tasks within a single LLM-based framework, achieving substantial improvements in temporal localization and generalization over prior video-language models.

ecb6a8003d4726cc1e9e9f3c2d8ff6c0627e4e95.title: Text2Reward: Reward Shaping with Language Models for Reinforcement Learning
ecb6a8003d4726cc1e9e9f3c2d8ff6c0627e4e95.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents be enabled to automatically generate and refine dense, interpretable reward functions for a wide range of tasks using natural language descriptions, without relying on expert knowledge or domain-specific data?
ecb6a8003d4726cc1e9e9f3c2d8ff6c0627e4e95.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that large language models, when provided with structured environment abstractions and natural language task descriptions, can generate executable, dense reward functions that are effective for reinforcement learning, and that iterative refinement with human feedback can further improve policy performance and resolve ambiguities.
ecb6a8003d4726cc1e9e9f3c2d8ff6c0627e4e95.proposed_method: A data-free framework is proposed that leverages large language models (LLMs) to automatically generate dense, shaped reward functions from natural language goal descriptions. The method grounds reward code generation in a compact, Pythonic abstraction of the environment, exposing relevant object states and callable functions to the LLM. The approach supports both zero-shot and few-shot reward generation, where few-shot involves retrieving similar instruction-code pairs from a growing library using sentence embeddings. Generated reward code is executed and iteratively refined based on code execution feedback to eliminate syntax and runtime errors. Additionally, after each reinforcement learning training cycle, human feedback is solicited based on policy rollout videos, and this feedback is incorporated into subsequent prompts to iteratively improve the reward code, allowing for better alignment with user intent and task requirements.
ecb6a8003d4726cc1e9e9f3c2d8ff6c0627e4e95.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two robotic manipulation benchmarks (MANISKILL2 and METAWORLD) and two locomotion environments from GymMUJOCO. For manipulation tasks, policies trained with generated reward codes will be compared against expert-written (oracle) reward functions and a baseline adapted from prior work using LLM-generated sparse rewards. Evaluation metrics include task success rate and convergence speed, measured over multiple random seeds. For locomotion, novel tasks will be defined and evaluated based on human judgment of policy rollouts. Real-world deployment will be demonstrated by transferring policies trained in simulation to a Franka Panda robot, using vision-based object pose estimation. Interactive experiments will assess the impact of iterative human feedback on reward code quality and policy performance.
ecb6a8003d4726cc1e9e9f3c2d8ff6c0627e4e95.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a data-free, language model-driven approach for generating dense, interpretable reward functions directly from natural language instructions, without requiring expert-crafted rewards or domain-specific data. It supports free-form, staged reward code that leverages existing programming packages and environment abstractions, enabling coverage of diverse and complex tasks. The method incorporates an interactive, human-in-the-loop refinement process, allowing non-experts to iteratively improve reward functions using natural language feedback. The approach demonstrates generalization to novel tasks, real-world transferability, and improved policy performance compared to both expert-written and prior LLM-generated reward baselines.

ecf1530ff9cc50058fb915329b59161e461c371c.title: Flow Matching for Scalable Simulation-Based Inference
ecf1530ff9cc50058fb915329b59161e461c371c.research_question: How can simulation-based Bayesian inference be made more scalable and flexible, particularly for high-dimensional and complex scientific data, while maintaining tractable posterior density evaluation and mass-covering properties?
ecf1530ff9cc50058fb915329b59161e461c371c.hypothesis: A continuous normalizing flow approach trained via flow matching, with unconstrained neural architectures and tailored loss weighting, will provide more scalable, flexible, and accurate posterior estimation for simulation-based inference tasks compared to discrete normalizing flows, while retaining tractable density evaluation and mass-covering guarantees.
ecf1530ff9cc50058fb915329b59161e461c371c.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces Flow-Matching Posterior Estimation (FMPE), which adapts flow matching—a technique from generative modeling based on continuous normalizing flows—to simulation-based Bayesian inference. FMPE parameterizes the conditional posterior distribution as a deterministic ordinary differential equation (ODE) driven by a neural vector field v_t,x, which is trained to match a target vector field u_t,x along sample-conditional probability paths. The training objective minimizes the mean squared error between the learned and target vector fields over samples drawn from the prior and simulated data, with an additional power-law reweighting of the time parameter to focus learning on more complex regions of the flow. The neural architecture is designed to flexibly map high-dimensional observations x to the vector field, using feature extractors and gated linear units for conditioning on parameters (θ) and time (t), allowing for scalability to large and complex data domains.
ecf1530ff9cc50058fb915329b59161e461c371c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of ten established simulation-based inference benchmarks, covering a range of parameter and observation dimensionalities (e.g., 2 to 100), with simulation budgets varying from 1,000 to 100,000. For each task, FMPE will be compared against a baseline neural posterior estimation (NPE) method using discrete normalizing flows, with models evaluated via metrics such as the C2ST score (classifier two-sample test) and maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) against reference posteriors. Additionally, FMPE will be applied to a challenging real-world problem: gravitational-wave parameter inference, using simulated and real LIGO data (e.g., GW150914), with performance assessed in terms of posterior accuracy (Jensen-Shannon divergence to reference), training time, and scalability. Both methods will use comparable neural architectures and training budgets, with careful control of validation and test splits.
ecf1530ff9cc50058fb915329b59161e461c371c.novelty_claims: The proposal claims several innovations: (1) the first adaptation of flow matching to Bayesian simulation-based inference, enabling the use of continuous normalizing flows with unconstrained neural architectures; (2) a new loss weighting scheme for time parameterization that improves learning in complex tasks; (3) theoretical and empirical analysis showing that FMPE encourages mass-covering posteriors, a property critical for scientific inference; (4) demonstration of superior scalability, training efficiency, and accuracy compared to discrete flow-based methods, especially in high-dimensional and real-world scientific applications such as gravitational-wave inference; and (5) the ability to maintain tractable density evaluation, facilitating downstream tasks like importance sampling and evidence computation.

ecf38d702bea560c1f9d372645e2be7661a71f37.title: MagicBrush: A Manually Annotated Dataset for Instruction-Guided Image Editing
ecf38d702bea560c1f9d372645e2be7661a71f37.research_question: How can a high-quality, large-scale, manually annotated dataset facilitate the development and evaluation of instruction-guided image editing models that address real-world editing needs across diverse scenarios, including single-turn, multi-turn, mask-provided, and mask-free editing?
ecf38d702bea560c1f9d372645e2be7661a71f37.hypothesis: A manually annotated, large-scale dataset of instruction-guided image editing triplets will enable the training and evaluation of models that better align with human preferences and real-world requirements, outperforming models trained on synthetic or automatically generated data.
ecf38d702bea560c1f9d372645e2be7661a71f37.proposed_method: A new dataset, MAGICBRUSH, will be constructed by collecting over 10,000 manually annotated triplets consisting of a source image, a natural language editing instruction, and a target image. The dataset will be built through a rigorous crowdsourcing pipeline, where qualified annotators interact with a text-guided image synthesis platform (DALL-E2) to iteratively generate high-quality edited images based on user-provided instructions and, where applicable, region masks. The dataset will support both single-turn and multi-turn editing sessions, and will include mask-provided and mask-free scenarios to comprehensively capture real-world editing tasks. Quality control will be enforced through multi-stage worker selection, ongoing spot-checks, and post-verification of image-instruction consistency and image quality. The resulting dataset will be used to train and fine-tune state-of-the-art instruction-guided image editing models, such as InstructPix2Pix and HIVE, and to benchmark a variety of existing baselines.
ecf38d702bea560c1f9d372645e2be7661a71f37.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training and evaluating multiple image editing models on the MAGICBRUSH dataset. The dataset will be split into training, development, and test sets, with over 5,000 edit sessions and more than 10,000 edit turns. Baseline methods will include both mask-free (e.g., Open-Edit, VQGAN-CLIP, SD-SDEdit, Text2LIVE, Null Text Inversion, InstructPix2Pix, HIVE) and mask-provided (e.g., GLIDE, Blended Diffusion) approaches. Evaluation metrics will include pixel-level differences (L1, L2), image similarity metrics (CLIP-I, DINO), and text-image alignment (CLIP-T). Both quantitative and qualitative analyses will be conducted, including human evaluations for consistency and image quality, multi-choice and one-on-one comparisons, and Likert-scale ratings. The impact of fine-tuning models on MAGICBRUSH will be systematically assessed, and the challenges of multi-turn editing and error accumulation will be analyzed.
ecf38d702bea560c1f9d372645e2be7661a71f37.novelty_claims: The proposed dataset is the first large-scale, manually annotated resource for instruction-guided real image editing that covers a wide range of scenarios, including single-turn, multi-turn, mask-provided, and mask-free editing. The annotation pipeline ensures high-quality, diverse, and realistic editing instructions and outcomes, surpassing the limitations of synthetic or domain-specific datasets. The dataset enables comprehensive benchmarking and reveals significant gaps between current model performance and real-world editing needs, thereby providing a foundation for future advancements in instruction-guided image editing and evaluation metrics aligned with human preferences.

ed219eb91a0d9d4501e312b64616ac68b91916d3.title: AutoAL: Automated Active Learning with Differentiable Query Strategy Search
ed219eb91a0d9d4501e312b64616ac68b91916d3.research_question: How can active learning strategies be automatically and efficiently selected and optimized for diverse deep learning tasks, in order to maximize data efficiency and model performance across varying datasets and domains?
ed219eb91a0d9d4501e312b64616ac68b91916d3.hypothesis: A differentiable, data-driven framework that jointly optimizes over a continuous space of candidate active learning strategies will enable more effective and adaptive sample selection, leading to improved model performance and reduced annotation costs compared to existing discrete or manually selected active learning methods.
ed219eb91a0d9d4501e312b64616ac68b91916d3.proposed_method: A novel automated active learning framework, AutoAL, will be developed to perform differentiable query strategy search. The method will integrate two neural networks: FitNet, which models the informativeness of each unlabeled sample based on labeled data, and SearchNet, which learns to select the optimal active learning (AL) strategy from a pool of candidates. These networks will be co-optimized in a bi-level optimization framework, where FitNet is trained on labeled data to guide the optimization of SearchNet. The search space of AL strategies will be relaxed from discrete to continuous using probabilistic modeling (e.g., Gaussian Mixture Models and Sigmoid-based mixing weights), enabling gradient-based optimization. The framework will incorporate a loss prediction module and regularization to control the number of selected samples, and will be designed to efficiently select the most informative samples for annotation in each AL iteration.
ed219eb91a0d9d4501e312b64616ac68b91916d3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven benchmark datasets, including natural image datasets (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, TinyImageNet) and medical image datasets (OrganCMNIST, PathMNIST, TissueMNIST from MedMNIST). The method will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines: classical AL strategies (Maximum Entropy, Margin Sampling, Least Confidence, KMeans, BALD, VarRatio, MeanSTD) and state-of-the-art deep AL methods (BADGE, LPL, VAAL, Core-set, ENSvarR, DDU, ALBL). All methods, including AutoAL, will use ResNet-18 as the backbone for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy versus labeled data budget, robustness (standard deviation across runs), and smoothness of performance curves. Ablation studies will analyze the contribution of key components (SearchNet architecture, candidate pool size) and the adaptive selection of AL strategies throughout the learning process. Each experiment will be repeated three times with different random seeds, and results will be reported as mean and standard deviation.
ed219eb91a0d9d4501e312b64616ac68b91916d3.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first differentiable, automated query strategy search method for active learning that can be trained end-to-end. It enables seamless, data-driven integration and optimization of multiple existing AL strategies within a continuous search space, allowing for efficient gradient-based updates. The bi-level optimization approach, combined with probabilistic modeling and a loss prediction module, provides a robust and adaptive mechanism for AL strategy selection. The method claims significant improvements in both performance and computational efficiency over traditional black-box or discrete AL strategy selection approaches, and demonstrates superior generalizability and robustness across diverse datasets and domains.

ed3fa74ebc0adcad4aee915c4625b384eaddbc91.title: AROMA: Preserving Spatial Structure for Latent PDE Modeling with Local Neural Fields
ed3fa74ebc0adcad4aee915c4625b384eaddbc91.research_question: How can the modeling of spatio-temporal dynamics governed by partial differential equations (PDEs) be improved to efficiently handle diverse and complex geometries, including irregular grids and point clouds, while maintaining stability and accuracy over long forecasting horizons?
ed3fa74ebc0adcad4aee915c4625b384eaddbc91.hypothesis: Encoding spatial information into a compact latent space using attention mechanisms and neural fields, and modeling temporal dynamics with a conditional diffusion-based transformer, will enable efficient and accurate surrogate modeling of PDEs across varied geometries, outperforming existing neural operator and neural field approaches in both accuracy and computational complexity.
ed3fa74ebc0adcad4aee915c4625b384eaddbc91.proposed_method: A flexible encode-process-decode framework is developed for surrogate modeling of time-dependent PDEs. The encoder maps arbitrary spatial observations (from grids, meshes, or point clouds) into a fixed-size set of latent tokens using a sequence of positional and value embeddings, geometry-aware cross-attention, and variational bottleneck regularization, resulting in a smooth, compact latent representation. Temporal dynamics are modeled in this latent space using a transformer architecture enhanced with a conditional diffusion process, which is trained to predict the evolution of latent tokens over time via a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) formulation. The decoder reconstructs the physical field at any spatial location by lifting the latent tokens, applying self- and cross-attention with query coordinates, and decoding with a local neural field (MLP), enabling continuous querying in the spatial domain. Training is performed in two stages: first, the encoder and decoder are jointly optimized as a variational autoencoder to reconstruct input fields; second, the latent refiner (diffusion transformer) is trained to model temporal transitions in the latent space.
ed3fa74ebc0adcad4aee915c4625b384eaddbc91.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a suite of representative PDE benchmarks, including 1D Burgers' equation, 2D Navier-Stokes equations (with varying viscosity), 3D Shallow-Water equations, and fluid dynamics around obstacles (CylinderFlow and AirfoilFlow) with both regular and irregular spatial discretizations. Datasets include thousands of trajectories with varying spatial resolutions and observation sparsity. Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art neural operators (Fourier Neural Operator, ResNet), transformer-based PDE solvers (OFormer, GNOT), and neural field models (DINO, CORAL). Evaluation metrics include relative L2 error and mean squared error (MSE) on both in-distribution (training horizon) and extrapolation (out-of-distribution) forecasting tasks, with additional analysis of long rollout stability and uncertainty quantification. Experimental setups include both fully observed and sparsely observed spatial domains, as well as generalization to unseen geometries.
ed3fa74ebc0adcad4aee915c4625b384eaddbc91.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first fully attention-based architecture for encoding domain geometries and unrolling spatio-temporal dynamics in a compact latent space, significantly reducing computational complexity compared to existing transformer-based PDE solvers. The method enables flexible processing of arbitrary input geometries without patching or prior feature engineering, and allows querying at any spatial location. The integration of a conditional diffusion process into the latent dynamics modeling enhances stability and supports longer rollouts. The framework demonstrates state-of-the-art or superior performance on diverse PDE benchmarks, particularly for complex and irregular geometries, and provides a principled approach to uncertainty quantification in surrogate PDE modeling.

ed44571dd9de3654b84ee1fea63015ecb67e6e63.title: LLaVA-Video: Video Instruction Tuning With Synthetic Data
ed44571dd9de3654b84ee1fea63015ecb67e6e63.research_question: How can high-quality, large-scale synthetic video instruction-following datasets be constructed to improve the performance of large multimodal models (LMMs) on video understanding tasks, and what are the effects of such data on the capabilities of video-language models across diverse benchmarks?
ed44571dd9de3654b84ee1fea63015ecb67e6e63.hypothesis: A synthetic, densely annotated, and diverse video instruction-following dataset, constructed with dynamic, untrimmed videos and detailed multi-level captions and question-answer pairs, will significantly enhance the performance of large multimodal models on a wide range of video understanding tasks compared to existing datasets that are more static or sparsely annotated.
ed44571dd9de3654b84ee1fea63015ecb67e6e63.proposed_method: A comprehensive synthetic video instruction-following dataset will be developed by aggregating videos from ten major, diverse sources, prioritizing untrimmed and dynamic content. The selection process will use automated scene detection and specific filtering criteria to ensure temporal richness and plot complexity. A three-level recurrent captioning pipeline will be constructed, where video frames are sampled at 1 FPS and captions are generated at 10-second (level-1), 30-second (level-2), and full-video (level-3) intervals, each conditioned on historical context to maintain narrative continuity. Additionally, 16 types of question-answer pairs, covering open-ended and multiple-choice formats, will be generated for each video using GPT-4o, with in-context prompting and automated filtering for quality control. The resulting dataset will be used to instruction-tune a large multimodal model, leveraging a novel video representation technique inspired by SlowFast, which optimally distributes visual tokens across frames to maximize temporal coverage within GPU memory constraints.
ed44571dd9de3654b84ee1fea63015ecb67e6e63.experiment_details: Experiments will involve fine-tuning a large multimodal model, initialized from a single-image instruction-tuned checkpoint, on the proposed synthetic video dataset combined with selected public video QA datasets and image-language pairs. The model will utilize a vision encoder (e.g., SigLIP) and a large language model (e.g., Qwen2), with video representations parameterized to balance frame count and token allocation. Evaluation will be conducted on 11 diverse video understanding benchmarks, including ActivityNet-QA, LongVideoBench, EgoSchema, MLVU, PerceptionTest, VideoMME, NExT-QA, VideoDetailCaption, Dream-1K, Video-ChatGPT, and TemporalBench, covering tasks such as detailed captioning, open-ended QA, and multiple-choice QA. Baselines will include leading open-source and proprietary video LMMs, and performance will be measured using accuracy and standardized metrics from LMMs-Eval. Ablation studies will assess the impact of dataset components and training strategies, with in-domain and zero-shot evaluations.
ed44571dd9de3654b84ee1fea63015ecb67e6e63.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a synthetic video instruction-following dataset that is significantly larger and more detailed than prior efforts, featuring dynamic, untrimmed videos, dense frame sampling, and multi-level recurrent captioning. The dataset covers a broader range of tasks and question types, and employs a novel recurrent annotation pipeline that maintains narrative context. The video representation method enables efficient utilization of GPU memory to incorporate more frames per video, enhancing temporal understanding. The approach is expected to set a new standard for open-source video-language instruction data and models, with comprehensive public release of data, code, and model checkpoints to support the community.

ed4a59cbb9ae22587d4d0a2bc9b400cd089437a4.title: Physics-based Deep Learning
ed4a59cbb9ae22587d4d0a2bc9b400cd089437a4.research_question: How can deep learning methods be systematically integrated with physical models and constraints to improve the accuracy, efficiency, and generalization of simulations, surrogate modeling, inverse problem solving, and generative modeling in scientific and engineering domains?
ed4a59cbb9ae22587d4d0a2bc9b400cd089437a4.hypothesis: Integrating physical knowledge, constraints, and differentiable simulation operators into deep learning architectures will yield models that are more accurate, data-efficient, and generalizable for forward and inverse problems, as well as for generative modeling of physical systems.
ed4a59cbb9ae22587d4d0a2bc9b400cd089437a4.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed that combines neural networks with physical models through several strategies: (1) incorporating physical loss terms and constraints into supervised and unsupervised learning; (2) leveraging differentiable physics operators to enable end-to-end gradient-based optimization and learning; (3) constructing neural surrogates and operators for fast approximation of complex simulations; (4) employing probabilistic generative models such as normalizing flows, diffusion models, and score-based methods, with physical guidance; and (5) integrating reinforcement learning and improved gradient schemes for control and inverse problems. The approach will support both structured and unstructured data, utilize advanced architectures (e.g., graph neural networks, transformers), and allow for the composition of neural and numerical solvers. Technical implementation will include differentiable solvers for PDEs, physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), and probabilistic inference pipelines.
ed4a59cbb9ae22587d4d0a2bc9b400cd089437a4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of benchmark physical systems, including Burgers' equation, Navier-Stokes equations, heat conduction, and turbulent flows around airfoils and wings. Datasets will be generated from high-fidelity numerical simulations and, where available, from real-world measurements. Baseline comparisons will include traditional numerical solvers, standard deep learning surrogates, and existing physics-informed neural networks. Evaluation metrics will encompass accuracy (e.g., L2 error, distributional accuracy), computational efficiency, generalization to out-of-distribution scenarios, and robustness to noise and data scarcity. Ablation studies will assess the impact of physical constraints, differentiable operators, and probabilistic modeling components.
ed4a59cbb9ae22587d4d0a2bc9b400cd089437a4.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified, modular framework for physics-based deep learning that systematically integrates physical models, differentiable simulation, and advanced generative and probabilistic methods. Key innovations include the use of differentiable physics operators for end-to-end learning, the combination of physical constraints with probabilistic generative models (e.g., diffusion and flow matching), the development of neural operators for unstructured and meshless domains, and new gradient schemes for inverse problems. The approach aims to bridge the gap between data-driven and physics-based modeling, enabling improved accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability in scientific machine learning.

ed5ea216dab687f71461b4e03fdb8e98c79652c1.title: Higher degree sum-of-squares relaxations robust against oblivious outliers
ed5ea216dab687f71461b4e03fdb8e98c79652c1.research_question: How can structured signals be efficiently and robustly recovered in high-dimensional estimation problems under symmetric, potentially heavy-tailed noise and in the presence of oblivious or adversarial outliers, across a wide range of models such as sparse linear regression, sparse principal component analysis (PCA), and tensor PCA?
ed5ea216dab687f71461b4e03fdb8e98c79652c1.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that for any estimation problem where a sum-of-squares (SoS) algorithm can recover the structured signal under Gaussian noise, a suitably constructed higher-degree SoS relaxation can also recover the signal under general symmetric noise, even with a small fraction of adversarially corrupted entries, and with error guarantees matching those for the Gaussian case.
ed5ea216dab687f71461b4e03fdb8e98c79652c1.proposed_method: A general framework will be developed based on higher-degree sum-of-squares (SoS) relaxations for signal recovery in structured estimation problems. The method constructs SoS relaxations that enforce polynomial constraints defining the structured signal set and leverages SoS proofs to certify upper bounds on the Gaussian complexity of the solution space. The approach involves bounding the covering numbers of sets of pseudo-expectations using SoS certificates, ensuring that feasible solutions are concentrated near the true signal. The framework is designed to be robust to symmetric, potentially heavy-tailed noise and an -fraction of adversarial corruptions, and does not require decomposable norm regularizers, thus extending applicability to challenging models such as tensor PCA and sparse PCA.
ed5ea216dab687f71461b4e03fdb8e98c79652c1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and possibly real datasets for tensor PCA and sparse PCA under various noise models, including symmetric heavy-tailed distributions (e.g., Cauchy noise) and Gaussian noise for comparison. The proposed SoS-based algorithms will be evaluated against state-of-the-art baselines, including convex relaxation and Huber loss-based estimators, in terms of signal recovery accuracy, robustness to outliers, and computational efficiency. Evaluation metrics will include correlation with the ground truth signal, error rates, and the fraction of adversarial corruptions tolerated. The experimental setup will systematically vary parameters such as signal-to-noise ratio, sparsity, and fraction of corrupted entries to assess the limits of recovery and computational trade-offs.
ed5ea216dab687f71461b4e03fdb8e98c79652c1.novelty_claims: The proposed framework generalizes sum-of-squares algorithms for Gaussian noise to arbitrary symmetric noise models, including those with unbounded or heavy-tailed distributions, and is robust to a small fraction of adversarial outliers. It extends the applicability of SoS relaxations to a broader class of structured estimation problems without requiring decomposable regularizers. The approach achieves error and robustness guarantees matching the best known results for Gaussian noise, and provides nearly optimal computational and statistical trade-offs. Additionally, the method introduces new techniques for bounding covering numbers of pseudo-expectation sets via SoS certificates, which may have further applications in high-dimensional statistics and optimization.

ed67f404a138f265d1b19044c91adea19f4bb4ec.title: PDE Generalization of In-Context Operator Networks: A Study on 1D Scalar Nonlinear Conservation Laws
ed67f404a138f265d1b19044c91adea19f4bb4ec.research_question: Can a single large neural network model be developed to solve a wide range of partial differential equation (PDE)-related scientific learning tasks, and can this model generalize to new PDEs, even of new forms, without any fine-tuning?
ed67f404a138f265d1b19044c91adea19f4bb4ec.hypothesis: A transformer-based in-context operator network (ICON) trained on a family of 1D scalar nonlinear conservation laws can generalize to solve PDEs with new forms and varying flux functions without requiring fine-tuning, by leveraging in-context operator learning from data prompts.
ed67f404a138f265d1b19044c91adea19f4bb4ec.proposed_method: The proposed approach utilizes a transformer-based in-context operator network (ICON) that accepts sequences of condition-quantity-of-interest (QoI) pairs as input, enabling the model to infer and apply the underlying operator to new conditions in a single forward pass. The ICON model is trained using a 'next function prediction' paradigm, analogous to next-token prediction in language models, where the loss is computed as the mean squared error between predicted and ground truth QoIs. Both forward and reverse operators are addressed: the forward operator predicts future states from initial conditions, while the reverse operator predicts possible previous states, with training losses including both standard L2 and a consistency loss that enforces operator invertibility. The model is designed to be flexible in handling varying temporal strides and can incorporate transformations (e.g., change of variables, stride scaling) to broaden its applicability to operators and functions outside its original training distribution.
ed67f404a138f265d1b19044c91adea19f4bb4ec.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on 1D scalar nonlinear conservation laws with periodic boundary conditions, where the training data is generated using the third-order Weighted Essentially Non-Oscillatory (WENO) scheme and the fourth-order Runge-Kutta method. The training set consists of conservation laws with cubic flux functions (parameters sampled from [-1,1]), and initial conditions are sampled from periodic Gaussian random fields. The ICON model is evaluated on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution operators, including flux functions of more general forms and varying time strides. Evaluation metrics include the average L1 distance (forward error) between predicted and true QoIs, and a reverse error metric that measures the reconstruction accuracy of the initial condition via the predicted reverse operator. Baselines include different training losses (L2 vs. consistency loss), and experiments are run with varying numbers of in-context examples and recursive prediction schemes for long time horizons.
ed67f404a138f265d1b19044c91adea19f4bb4ec.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a methodology for training a single ICON model capable of in-context operator learning across a diverse set of PDEs, including generalization to new PDE forms and flux functions without fine-tuning. The approach leverages flexible prompt construction, recursive prediction, and operator/function transformations to extend the model's applicability. The work claims significant progress toward a foundation model for PDE-related tasks, demonstrating, for the first time, generalization of in-context operator networks to previously unseen PDE forms in the context of nonlinear conservation laws.

ed81c644692ec88f59e287366c8cba619948295a.title: Direct Preference Optimization with an Offset
ed81c644692ec88f59e287366c8cba619948295a.research_question: How can language models be more effectively aligned with human preferences by incorporating not just the ordering of preferences, but also the degree to which one response is preferred over another, especially in scenarios where preference data includes graded or pointwise information?
ed81c644692ec88f59e287366c8cba619948295a.hypothesis: Incorporating the magnitude of preference between response pairs into the fine-tuning objective will result in language models that better align with human preferences and achieve superior performance on alignment tasks compared to methods that treat all preference pairs equally.
ed81c644692ec88f59e287366c8cba619948295a.proposed_method: A new fine-tuning strategy, termed Direct Preference Optimization with an Offset (ODPO), will be developed as a generalization of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). ODPO will introduce an offset into the loss function, requiring the model to increase the likelihood of the preferred response over the dispreferred response by an amount determined by the degree of preference. The offset will be modeled as a monotonic function (e.g., logarithmic scaling) of the difference in reward or quality scores between the two responses, allowing for stronger or weaker preferences to influence the optimization process accordingly. The method will maintain the simplicity of DPO by avoiding the need for a separate reward model or reinforcement learning, and will be compatible with both pointwise and pairwise human feedback data. Theoretical connections to the Bradley–Terry model and softmax-margin losses will be established to justify the approach.
ed81c644692ec88f59e287366c8cba619948295a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several alignment tasks, including sentiment control (using the IMDB dataset), toxicity control (using adversarial prompts from the RealToxicityPrompts dataset), and summarization (using Reddit TL;DR with Likert-scale human ratings). Language models such as GPT2-Large, GPT-Neo-2.7B, and GPT-J-6B will be fine-tuned using both DPO and ODPO for comparison. Preference datasets will be constructed either from classifier-based pointwise rewards or from human-annotated scores, with offsets computed accordingly. Evaluation will involve measuring the average reward (e.g., sentiment positivity, toxicity reduction, or summary quality) and the KL divergence from the supervised fine-tuned model, with Pareto frontier analysis to assess trade-offs. Baselines will include standard DPO and supervised fine-tuning, and additional comparisons will be made against human-written references using win-rate metrics judged by large language models (e.g., GPT-4). Ablation studies will explore the effect of different offset scaling functions and hyperparameters.
ed81c644692ec88f59e287366c8cba619948295a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled way to incorporate the strength of human preferences into the fine-tuning objective for language models, generalizing DPO to account for graded or pointwise preference information. This approach enables more nuanced alignment, particularly in cases where not all preference pairs are equally informative. ODPO is claimed to outperform DPO in terms of alignment with human preferences, especially when preference data is limited or when the degree of preference varies significantly. The method maintains the efficiency and simplicity of DPO, requiring no reward model or reinforcement learning, and provides theoretical connections to established probabilistic models and margin-based losses.

eda90d3d4f8515b778e8255399c1bd950009c1a0.title: ATLAS: Autoformalizing Theorems through Lifting, Augmentation, and Synthesis of Data
eda90d3d4f8515b778e8255399c1bd950009c1a0.research_question: How can large-scale, high-quality parallel corpora of mathematical theorem statements in natural language and formal language be efficiently generated to advance the automatic formalization (autoformalization) of mathematics?
eda90d3d4f8515b778e8255399c1bd950009c1a0.hypothesis: A data generation framework that leverages concept extraction from formal mathematical libraries, knowledge distillation, and innovative data augmentation strategies can produce high-quality, large-scale parallel corpora, leading to significant improvements in the autoformalization capabilities of large language models.
eda90d3d4f8515b778e8255399c1bd950009c1a0.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a three-stage data generation framework named ATLAS, consisting of Data Lifting, Data Synthesis, and Data Augmentation. Data Lifting begins by extracting mathematical concepts directly from a formal library (Mathlib), constructing a concept repository that ensures scalability and eliminates the need for extensive pre-processing. Data Synthesis employs a teacher-student paradigm with knowledge distillation: a teacher model generates diverse natural language (NL) theorem statements by sampling from the concept repository, and a student model translates these into formal language (FL) statements. The syntactic validity of FL statements is verified using the Lean compiler, and failed cases are revised iteratively using error feedback. Semantic alignment between NL and FL pairs is assessed, and only high-quality pairs are retained. Data Augmentation further expands the dataset by generating new FL statements via proof step extraction (using an automated prover and Lean Infoview) and by producing contrapositives of existing theorems. Augmented FL statements are translated back into NL to form additional parallel pairs. The entire process is executed iteratively, with expert iteration and knowledge distillation accelerating student model improvement.
eda90d3d4f8515b778e8255399c1bd950009c1a0.experiment_details: Experiments will involve constructing a large-scale dataset (ATLAS dataset) of undergraduate-level theorem statement pairs, targeting the Lean4 formal language. The student model (Llama3.1-8B-Instruct) is initialized with data from Mathlib and Lean Workbook, then iteratively fine-tuned using LoRA on synthetic and augmented data generated by the framework. Evaluation is conducted on multiple benchmarks, including ProofNet, PutnamBench, and the newly introduced MathQual dataset (graduate-level), using pass@k metrics (k=1,8,32) to measure the rate of successful formalization. Baselines for comparison include DeepSeek-V3, Herald Translator, Kimina-Autoformalizer, and initialization models. The evaluation pipeline involves translation, compilation, back-translation, and natural language inference checks to ensure both syntactic and semantic correctness. Ablation studies are performed to assess the contribution of each framework component, and additional experiments compare LoRA and full-parameter fine-tuning across different base models.
eda90d3d4f8515b778e8255399c1bd950009c1a0.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a novel data generation pipeline for autoformalization that starts from concept extraction (Data Lifting) rather than NL or FL statements, ensuring scalability and eliminating pre-processing bottlenecks. It innovates with two data augmentation strategies—proof step extraction and contraposition—leveraging the structure of formal languages and automated theorem proving tools. The resulting ATLAS dataset is among the largest of its kind, and the iterative expert distillation process enables efficient, autonomous improvement of the student model. The approach achieves statistically significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines on multiple benchmarks, with minimal human intervention and lower computational costs.

edb548fe7574d99454b352ffdb61bca93c3072ba.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
edb548fe7574d99454b352ffdb61bca93c3072ba.research_question: How can the internal representations of language models be decomposed into interpretable, monosemantic features, and can such decompositions improve our understanding and control of model behavior?
edb548fe7574d99454b352ffdb61bca93c3072ba.hypothesis: Sparse autoencoders can recover a set of features from language model activations that are more interpretable and causally meaningful than features obtained from standard neuron bases or other decomposition techniques.
edb548fe7574d99454b352ffdb61bca93c3072ba.proposed_method: A scalable, unsupervised approach will be developed using sparse autoencoders to learn a dictionary of features from internal activations of language models, such as the residual stream or MLP sublayers. The autoencoder will consist of a single hidden layer with ReLU activations and tied weights, trained to minimize a loss function combining reconstruction error and an L1 sparsity penalty on the hidden activations. The size of the feature dictionary will be controlled by a hyperparameter, allowing for overcomplete representations. The learned dictionary features will be interpreted using automated methods, such as autointerpretability scores generated by prompting large language models to describe and predict feature activations. Causal effects of features will be analyzed through targeted interventions and ablations.
edb548fe7574d99454b352ffdb61bca93c3072ba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on activations extracted from pretrained language models, specifically Pythia-70M and Pythia-410M, using datasets such as the Pile. The proposed sparse autoencoder method will be compared against baselines including the default neuron basis, random directions, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and Independent Component Analysis (ICA). Evaluation metrics will include automated interpretability scores (autointerpretability), reconstruction loss, and the ability to localize causally important features for specific behaviors, such as the Indirect Object Identification (IOI) task. Causal mediation analysis will be performed using activation patching and the Automated Circuit Discovery (ACDC) algorithm, measuring the number and magnitude of feature interventions required to achieve target changes in model output (e.g., KL divergence from a counterfactual target). Additional case studies will analyze the semantic coherence and causal effects of individual dictionary features.
edb548fe7574d99454b352ffdb61bca93c3072ba.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a scalable, unsupervised framework for extracting highly interpretable and monosemantic features from language model activations using sparse autoencoders. This approach enables finer-grained localization of causally important features for specific behaviors than previous decomposition techniques, such as PCA or ICA. Automated interpretability evaluation demonstrates that the learned features are significantly more interpretable than those obtained from standard neuron bases or other unsupervised methods. The method also facilitates targeted model editing and circuit discovery, providing a foundation for future mechanistic interpretability and model transparency efforts.

edc3948f91f3b22ada4b0dd2872106b2ac57d418.title: GraphGDP: Generative Diffusion Processes for Permutation Invariant Graph Generation
edc3948f91f3b22ada4b0dd2872106b2ac57d418.research_question: How can permutation invariant graph generative models be developed to efficiently and accurately capture the underlying distribution of discrete, high-dimensional graphs, overcoming the limitations of existing autoregressive and deep generative approaches?
edc3948f91f3b22ada4b0dd2872106b2ac57d418.hypothesis: A continuous-time generative diffusion process, specifically designed for graphs and leveraging permutation equivariant score networks with position-enhanced features, can generate high-fidelity, diverse, and permutation invariant graphs more efficiently and with higher quality than current state-of-the-art methods.
edc3948f91f3b22ada4b0dd2872106b2ac57d418.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a continuous-time generative diffusion process for graph generation, formulated as a stochastic differential equation (SDE) that perturbs graphs toward a known random graph distribution (e.g., Erdo˝s-Re´nyi). The forward diffusion process adds noise to the adjacency matrix elements, gradually erasing structural information, while the reverse-time SDE reconstructs graphs from noise by leveraging a neural score network. A novel position-enhanced graph score network (PGSN) is designed to estimate the gradient of the log-probability (score) at each diffusion step, using both perturbed continuous adjacency matrices and discrete, quantized graph states. The PGSN incorporates node and edge features, including random walk-based position encodings and shortest-path distances, within a multi-layer message passing architecture to capture evolving graph topology. Graph generation is performed by numerically solving the reverse-time SDE or its corresponding probability flow ODE, allowing for efficient sampling with a small number of function evaluations.
edc3948f91f3b22ada4b0dd2872106b2ac57d418.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four benchmark datasets: Community-small, Ego-small, Ego, and Enzymes, which vary in graph size and structural characteristics. The proposed method will be compared against leading baselines, including VGAE, GraphRNN, GRAN, BIGG, EDP-GNN, and Erdo˝s-Re´nyi models, with both order-dependent and order-independent settings. Evaluation metrics will include classical structure-based Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) metrics (degree distribution, clustering coefficient, Laplacian spectrum), as well as neural-network-based metrics (random GIN-based MMDRBF, F1PR, F1DC) to assess fidelity, diversity, and mode coverage. The experimental setup will involve training on 80% of each dataset, with validation and testing on the remaining splits, and generating either 1024 or a test-set-matched number of graphs for evaluation. Sampling efficiency will be measured by the number of function evaluations (NFE) and wall-clock time, using both SDE and ODE solvers, and ablation studies will analyze the impact of architectural choices in the score network.
edc3948f91f3b22ada4b0dd2872106b2ac57d418.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to introduce a continuous-time generative diffusion process specifically tailored for permutation invariant graph generation, leveraging both continuous and discrete representations of graphs. The position-enhanced graph score network uniquely integrates evolving structural and positional information from perturbed graphs, enabling accurate score estimation and efficient denoising. The method achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on multiple graph generation benchmarks, with significantly improved sampling speed (as few as 24 function evaluations) compared to autoregressive models. The approach also provides a principled and flexible way to model the discrete nature of graphs within the diffusion framework, addressing both permutation invariance and efficient sampling.

edd1dc1e8d7989f36c0e54f69f4aeb5e597edc8b.title: Steering Llama 2 via Contrastive Activation Addition
edd1dc1e8d7989f36c0e54f69f4aeb5e597edc8b.research_question: How can large language models be steered toward or away from specific high-level behaviors, such as alignment-relevant traits, through targeted interventions at the activation level, and how does such steering interact with existing alignment methods like finetuning and system prompting?
edd1dc1e8d7989f36c0e54f69f4aeb5e597edc8b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that constructing and applying steering vectors derived from contrastive activation differences between positive and negative behavioral examples can effectively and precisely modulate targeted behaviors in large language models, with minimal impact on general capabilities and compatibility with other alignment techniques.
edd1dc1e8d7989f36c0e54f69f4aeb5e597edc8b.proposed_method: The proposed method involves generating 'steering vectors' by averaging the difference in residual stream activations at a specific transformer layer between pairs of prompts that differ only in exhibiting a target behavior (positive) or its opposite (negative). These contrastive prompt pairs are constructed using multiple-choice questions with answer letters appended, isolating the behavioral variable of interest. The mean difference vector is computed over many such pairs to reduce noise and capture the desired behavioral direction. During inference, this steering vector is added to the residual stream activations at all token positions after the user's prompt, with a tunable multiplier to control the degree of behavioral modulation. The method is designed to be model-agnostic and applicable on top of existing finetuned or RLHF-aligned models.
edd1dc1e8d7989f36c0e54f69f4aeb5e597edc8b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on Llama 2 Chat models (7B and 13B parameters), primarily focusing on behaviors such as coordination with other AIs, corrigibility, hallucination, myopic reward, survival instinct, sycophancy, and refusal. Datasets are sourced from Anthropic’s 'Advanced AI Risk' evaluation set and custom GPT-4-generated contrastive datasets. The method will be evaluated on both held-out multiple-choice behavioral question datasets and open-ended generation tasks, with behavioral prevalence measured by GPT-4 ratings and token probabilities. Baselines will include system prompting, few-shot prompting, and supervised finetuning on the same datasets. Additional evaluations will assess the impact on general capabilities using the MMLU benchmark and TruthfulQA, as well as the interaction and transferability of steering vectors across layers and between base and chat models.
edd1dc1e8d7989f36c0e54f69f4aeb5e597edc8b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a scalable and generalizable method for steering language model behaviors via contrastive activation addition, leveraging averaged activation differences over large, diverse datasets to isolate behavioral directions. Unlike prior activation engineering methods, this approach aggregates over many prompt pairs, applies steering at all post-prompt token positions, and demonstrates compatibility with existing alignment techniques such as finetuning and system prompting. The method claims improved precision, robustness, and generalization to open-ended tasks, while providing new insights into the linear representation of high-level concepts within model activations.

edd705ebe3546272b7fe952e2ed6088200adad76.title: Retrieval Head Mechanistically Explains Long-Context Factuality
edd705ebe3546272b7fe952e2ed6088200adad76.research_question: What are the internal mechanisms that enable large language models (LLMs) with long-context capabilities to retrieve relevant information from arbitrary locations within their input, and how do these mechanisms impact factuality and reasoning in downstream tasks?
edd705ebe3546272b7fe952e2ed6088200adad76.hypothesis: A small, specialized subset of attention heads, termed retrieval heads, are primarily responsible for the retrieval of relevant information from long contexts in transformer-based LLMs. These retrieval heads are universal, sparse, intrinsic to pretrained models, dynamically activated based on context, and causally linked to the model's ability to maintain factuality and perform complex reasoning.
edd705ebe3546272b7fe952e2ed6088200adad76.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted to identify and characterize retrieval heads within transformer-based LLMs. The methodology involves defining a retrieval score for each attention head, quantifying the frequency of copy-paste behavior during autoregressive decoding in tasks that require information retrieval from the input context. Needle-in-a-Haystack tests will be used, where unique question-answer pairs (needles) are embedded at random positions within long contexts (haystacks), ensuring that correct answers must be copied from the context rather than generated from internal model knowledge. Retrieval scores will be computed for all attention heads across diverse input contexts and model variants, with heads exceeding a threshold considered retrieval heads. Additional analyses will examine the universality, sparsity, intrinsic nature, and dynamic activation of these heads across model families, scales, and fine-tuning types.
edd705ebe3546272b7fe952e2ed6088200adad76.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on a wide range of LLMs, including Llama-2, Yi, Qwen, Mistral, and Mixtral, covering different model scales (6B, 7B, 13B, 14B, 34B, 8x7B) and training regimes (base, chat, dense, MoE, continued pretraining, SFT, RLHF, sparse upcycling). The primary evaluation will use the Needle-in-a-Haystack benchmark, with approximately 600 retrieval test instances per model, varying context lengths from 1K to 50K tokens and multiple insertion depths. Baseline comparisons will include masking out top retrieval heads versus random non-retrieval heads, measuring the impact on retrieval accuracy and hallucination rates. Additional downstream tasks will include extractive QA (using a synthesized dataset from news articles and GPT-4-generated questions) and chain-of-thought reasoning (using MMLU, MuSiQue, and GSM8K), with performance measured by F1 score and accuracy. The effect of masking retrieval heads versus random heads will be systematically evaluated across these tasks.
edd705ebe3546272b7fe952e2ed6088200adad76.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of retrieval heads as a mechanistic explanation for long-context retrieval in LLMs, providing the first comprehensive identification and characterization of these specialized attention heads. It claims universality and sparsity of retrieval heads across diverse model families and scales, demonstrates their intrinsic nature in pretrained models, and establishes their causal role in factual information retrieval and reasoning. The findings offer mechanistic interpretability of LLMs, explain why certain context compression methods may fail, and suggest new directions for reducing hallucination, improving reasoning, and optimizing KV cache compression for efficient deployment of long-context models.

ededb7059f32807ef86f2795a6255c45121abfed.title: Almost-linear-time algorithms for Markov chains and new spectral primitives for directed graphs
ededb7059f32807ef86f2795a6255c45121abfed.research_question: Can efficient, almost-linear-time algorithms be developed for fundamental computational problems involving Markov chains and directed graphs, such as solving directed Laplacian systems, computing stationary distributions, and related spectral quantities, by introducing new spectral primitives and sparsification techniques tailored for directed graphs?
ededb7059f32807ef86f2795a6255c45121abfed.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by defining a suitable notion of spectral approximation for directed graphs and constructing efficient sparsifiers under this notion, it is possible to design almost-linear-time algorithms for solving directed Laplacian systems and related problems, thereby closing the algorithmic gap between undirected and directed spectral graph theory.
ededb7059f32807ef86f2795a6255c45121abfed.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed that introduces a well-behaved notion of spectral approximation specifically for directed graphs, overcoming the lack of symmetry and positive semidefiniteness present in undirected Laplacians. Under this notion, an algorithm will be constructed to compute sparsifiers for strongly-connected directed graphs, reducing the number of edges to O~(n/ε^2) while preserving key spectral properties. These sparsifiers will be used as preconditioners within an iterative scheme designed to solve linear systems involving directed Laplacians, particularly for Eulerian graphs. The iterative solver will address error accumulation due to asymmetry by employing a novel analysis and correction mechanism, enabling the solution of Lx = b in almost-linear time with respect to the number of edges.
ededb7059f32807ef86f2795a6255c45121abfed.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of synthetic and real-world directed graphs, focusing on tasks such as solving directed Laplacian systems, computing stationary distributions, personalized PageRank vectors, and commute/hitting times. The proposed algorithms will be evaluated against previous state-of-the-art methods with running times of O~(nm^{3/4} + n^{2/3}m), using metrics such as runtime, accuracy (measured in ℓ2 distance to ground truth solutions), and scalability with respect to graph size and sparsity. Baseline comparisons will include both general-purpose linear system solvers and prior specialized algorithms for directed Laplacians. The experimental setup will ensure that the dependence on condition number and accuracy parameter ε is thoroughly assessed, and the performance of the sparsification and solver routines will be profiled separately and in combination.
ededb7059f32807ef86f2795a6255c45121abfed.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first almost-linear-time algorithms for solving directed Laplacian systems and related Markov chain problems, enabled by a new notion of spectral approximation and sparsification for directed graphs. It establishes the existence and efficient construction of sparsifiers with o(n^2) edges for directed graphs under this new definition, a result not previously known even in non-algorithmic settings. The proposed iterative solver for directed Laplacians leverages these sparsifiers to achieve significant improvements in running time, matching the best known results for undirected graphs up to subpolynomial factors, and provides a general framework that can be extended to a range of spectral and combinatorial problems on directed graphs.

ee1fb6a0ea9ac58fdfd1bd7b5e3b71cb17c64f54.title: Amortized Inference for Causal Structure Learning
ee1fb6a0ea9ac58fdfd1bd7b5e3b71cb17c64f54.research_question: How can causal structure among a set of variables be efficiently inferred from observational and interventional data, particularly in complex and high-dimensional domains where traditional combinatorial search and score-based methods are computationally intractable or fail to encode appropriate inductive biases?
ee1fb6a0ea9ac58fdfd1bd7b5e3b71cb17c64f54.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a variational inference model, trained to directly predict causal structure from data generated by a domain-specific simulator, can efficiently and accurately infer causal graphs, generalize to out-of-distribution settings and larger problem instances, and provide well-calibrated uncertainty estimates, outperforming existing causal discovery algorithms.
ee1fb6a0ea9ac58fdfd1bd7b5e3b71cb17c64f54.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that amortizes causal structure learning by training a neural variational inference model to directly predict the posterior distribution over causal graphs from observational and interventional datasets. The inference model will be designed to encode permutation invariance across samples and permutation equivariance across variables, ensuring statistical efficiency and generalization to unseen problem sizes. The architecture will utilize multi-head self-attention layers alternating over sample and variable axes, followed by max-pooling and inner product-based edge probability estimation. The variational family will be factorized over edges, and an augmented Lagrangian dual optimization will be used to enforce acyclicity constraints when appropriate. Training will be performed on synthetic data generated from domain-specific simulators, allowing the model to acquire inductive biases relevant to the target application.
ee1fb6a0ea9ac58fdfd1bd7b5e3b71cb17c64f54.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three domains: linear and nonlinear structural causal models (SCMs) and semisynthetic gene regulatory network (GRN) data, using both in-distribution and out-of-distribution test sets to assess robustness to distributional shift. Datasets will be generated using a variety of random graph models (Erdős-Rényi, scale-free, Watts-Strogatz, stochastic block, geometric random graphs) and simulators for gene expression data, with both observational and interventional samples. Baseline methods for comparison will include PC, GES, LiNGAM, DAG-GNN, GraN-DAG, GIES, IGSP, DCDI, and DiBS, with hyperparameters tuned on held-out validation sets. Evaluation metrics will include structural Hamming distance (SHD), structural intervention distance (SID), edge precision, recall, F1 score, area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and expected calibration error (ECE) for uncertainty quantification. Experiments will also assess generalization to larger numbers of variables and samples, as well as ablations of model architecture components.
ee1fb6a0ea9ac58fdfd1bd7b5e3b71cb17c64f54.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces amortized variational inference for causal structure learning, bypassing the need for combinatorial graph search and hand-engineered score functions by leveraging domain simulators for training. The inference model is specifically designed to encode permutation symmetries, enabling generalization to larger and more complex problem instances than seen during training. The method provides well-calibrated uncertainty estimates for predicted causal edges and demonstrates robust generalization under significant distributional shifts, including unseen graph structures, mechanisms, and noise types. This approach is particularly effective in challenging domains such as genomics, where existing methods struggle to encode appropriate inductive biases or handle noisy data.

ee21089c6ef2a683b19407b76bf4ed631cb4633b.title: OctFormer: Octree-based Transformers for 3D Point Clouds
ee21089c6ef2a683b19407b76bf4ed631cb4633b.research_question: How can the computational efficiency and scalability of transformer-based models for 3D point cloud understanding be improved, while maintaining or surpassing state-of-the-art performance in segmentation and detection tasks?
ee21089c6ef2a683b19407b76bf4ed631cb4633b.hypothesis: Partitioning point clouds into local windows with a fixed number of points using octree-based grouping, rather than fixed-shape cubic windows, will enable more efficient and scalable transformer attention mechanisms for large-scale 3D point cloud tasks, without sacrificing model accuracy.
ee21089c6ef2a683b19407b76bf4ed631cb4633b.proposed_method: A novel octree-based transformer architecture, OctFormer, will be developed for 3D point cloud analysis. The core component is an octree attention mechanism that partitions point clouds into groups with a fixed number of points per window, regardless of window shape, by leveraging the sorted shuffled keys of octrees. This enables highly efficient, parallelizable attention computation using standard deep learning operators. A dilated variant of octree attention will be introduced to expand the receptive field. The network will employ a hierarchical structure with an embedding module, multiple OctFormer blocks (each containing octree attention, MLP, and LayerNorm), and downsampling modules, producing multiscale features suitable for segmentation, detection, and classification. Conditional positional encoding will be used to enhance spatial awareness without excessive parameter overhead.
ee21089c6ef2a683b19407b76bf4ed631cb4633b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale 3D point cloud benchmarks, including ScanNet and ScanNet200 for semantic segmentation, and SUNRGB-D for 3D object detection. OctFormer will be compared against state-of-the-art point-based, sparse-voxel-based CNNs, and transformer baselines such as Point Transformer V2, Stratified Transformer, and MinkowskiNet. Evaluation metrics will include mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) for segmentation and mean Average Precision (mAP) at various IoU thresholds for detection. Experimental setup will include ablation studies on model size, positional encoding, voxel size, point number per window, dilation, and data augmentation. Efficiency will be measured by forward pass runtime and GPU memory usage, with all models run on Nvidia 3090 GPUs.
ee21089c6ef2a683b19407b76bf4ed631cb4633b.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel octree attention mechanism for transformers that partitions point clouds into windows with a fixed number of points, enabling efficient and scalable attention computation. This approach eliminates the need for complex neighborhood search and custom GPU kernels, allowing implementation with standard deep learning libraries. The method achieves linear complexity with respect to point cloud size and can be implemented in as few as 10 lines of code. OctFormer sets new state-of-the-art results on multiple 3D segmentation and detection benchmarks, surpassing both previous point cloud transformers and highly optimized sparse-voxel-based CNNs in both accuracy and computational efficiency.

ee4014497ccf2f65d6e05d3956b0e6b0c7369bae.title: PiSSA: Principal Singular Values and Singular Vectors Adaptation of Large Language Models
ee4014497ccf2f65d6e05d3956b0e6b0c7369bae.research_question: How can parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models be improved to achieve faster convergence, better performance, and lower quantization error, while maintaining compatibility with existing low-rank adaptation architectures?
ee4014497ccf2f65d6e05d3956b0e6b0c7369bae.hypothesis: Initializing low-rank adapters for large language models using the principal singular values and singular vectors of the original weight matrices, while freezing the residual components, will enable faster convergence, improved downstream task performance, and reduced quantization error compared to standard random or zero-initialized low-rank adaptation methods.
ee4014497ccf2f65d6e05d3956b0e6b0c7369bae.proposed_method: The proposed method, Principal Singular Values and Singular Vectors Adaptation (PiSSA), applies singular value decomposition (SVD) to the weight matrices of pre-trained large language models. The top-r principal singular values and vectors are used to initialize low-rank adapter matrices A and B, such that A = U[:, :r] S[:r, :r]^{1/2} and B = S[:r, :r]^{1/2} V[:, :r]^T, where U, S, and V are from the SVD of the original matrix W. The remaining singular components form a residual matrix W_res = U[:, r:] S[r:, r:] V[:, r:]^T, which is kept frozen during fine-tuning. Only the principal component adapters (A, B) are updated during training, while the residual is quantized (in the QPiSSA variant) to further reduce memory usage. The method leverages a fast SVD algorithm for efficient initialization and is fully compatible with existing LoRA architectures and pipelines.
ee4014497ccf2f65d6e05d3956b0e6b0c7369bae.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of large language models (184M to 70B parameters), including LLaMA2-7B, Mistral-7B, Gemma-7B, LLaMA-3-8B/70B, Qwen1.5-7B, Yi-1.5-34B, DeepSeek-MoE-16B, and Mixtral-8x7B. Fine-tuning will be performed on both natural language generation (NLG) and understanding (NLU) tasks, such as GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, MBPP, MT-Bench, and the GLUE benchmark. Baselines will include full-parameter fine-tuning, LoRA (with Gaussian and Kaiming initializations), QLoRA, LoftQ, and other adapter-based PEFT methods. Evaluation metrics will include task-specific accuracy, training loss, convergence speed, and quantization error (measured by nuclear norm). Experiments will systematically vary the number of trainable parameters (adapter rank), quantization precision (4-bit NF4), and training data size, with results averaged over multiple runs.
ee4014497ccf2f65d6e05d3956b0e6b0c7369bae.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to leverage SVD of the original model weights to initialize low-rank adapters with principal singular values and vectors, rather than random or zero initialization. By updating only the principal components and freezing the residual, the approach enables faster and better convergence, as well as improved generalization. The method also introduces a quantized variant (QPiSSA) that significantly reduces quantization error compared to QLoRA and LoftQ, particularly at lower ranks. PiSSA maintains full compatibility with existing LoRA architectures, requires negligible additional initialization time, and can be seamlessly integrated into current PEFT pipelines. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines across models, tasks, and parameter budgets.

ee42f8a43bdf2cf1e39a0e08bd7b448034cb4a0d.title: Why neural networks find simple solutions: the many regularizers of geometric complexity
ee42f8a43bdf2cf1e39a0e08bd7b448034cb4a0d.research_question: What is an appropriate and tractable measure of model complexity for deep neural networks, and how do various explicit and implicit regularization techniques, initialization schemes, and training heuristics influence this complexity and the resulting generalization performance?
ee42f8a43bdf2cf1e39a0e08bd7b448034cb4a0d.hypothesis: Geometric complexity, defined as the discrete Dirichlet energy of the neural network's logit function over the dataset, serves as a unifying and effective measure of model complexity for deep neural networks. Common explicit and implicit regularization techniques, as well as initialization and training heuristics, act to control geometric complexity, thereby encouraging neural networks to find simpler, more generalizable solutions.
ee42f8a43bdf2cf1e39a0e08bd7b448034cb4a0d.proposed_method: A new measure of model complexity, termed Geometric Complexity (GC), will be developed based on the discrete Dirichlet energy of the neural network's logit function, computed as the average squared Frobenius norm of the Jacobian over the dataset. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to relate GC to existing notions such as parameter norm, spectral norm, Lipschitz smoothness, and flatness. Empirical studies will be designed to systematically investigate the impact of various explicit regularizers (e.g., L2, spectral norm, flatness, Jacobian regularization), implicit regularization via stochastic gradient descent (SGD) dynamics (e.g., learning rate, batch size), and initialization schemes on GC. The method will also explore how GC captures phenomena such as double descent and its correlation with generalization error.
ee42f8a43bdf2cf1e39a0e08bd7b448034cb4a0d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification datasets such as MNIST and CIFAR-10 using architectures including multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) and ResNet18. The impact of explicit regularization (L2, spectral norm, flatness, label noise, and Jacobian regularization) will be evaluated by varying regularization strengths and measuring GC at the point of maximum test accuracy. Implicit regularization effects will be studied by training models with varying learning rates and batch sizes, using SGD without momentum as the default optimizer, and observing the resulting GC and test accuracy. Double descent will be investigated by training models with increasing width and plotting GC against test loss. Baselines will include models trained without explicit regularization and with standard initialization schemes. Evaluation metrics will include geometric complexity, test accuracy, and test loss.
ee42f8a43bdf2cf1e39a0e08bd7b448034cb4a0d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces geometric complexity as a computationally tractable, data-dependent measure of neural network complexity that unifies and explains the effects of a wide range of explicit and implicit regularization techniques. It provides theoretical and empirical evidence that many common training heuristics act to control geometric complexity, offering a new perspective on why neural networks tend to find simple solutions. The approach also demonstrates that geometric complexity captures key phenomena such as double descent and correlates with generalization, providing a valuable tool for understanding and improving deep learning models.

ee49b5f62f51835e01533acae4bdb367c7fa97fd.title: Ross3D: Reconstructive Visual Instruction Tuning with 3D-Awareness
ee49b5f62f51835e01533acae4bdb367c7fa97fd.research_question: How can large multimodal models be enhanced to achieve comprehensive and spatially-aware understanding of 3D scenes, given the scarcity of large-scale 3D vision-language datasets?
ee49b5f62f51835e01533acae4bdb367c7fa97fd.hypothesis: Integrating 3D-aware visual supervision into the training of large multimodal models, specifically through reconstructive visual instruction tuning with cross-view and global-view reconstruction pretext tasks, will significantly improve the models' ability to understand 3D scenes in terms of spatial relationships and overall layout, even when only limited labeled 3D vision-language data is available.
ee49b5f62f51835e01533acae4bdb367c7fa97fd.proposed_method: A new framework, ROSS3D, will be developed to inject 3D-awareness into large multimodal models by incorporating two novel vision-centric pretext tasks during training. The first task, cross-view reconstruction, requires the model to reconstruct masked views of a 3D scene by aggregating overlapping information from other available views, thus modeling fine-grained spatial relationships between viewpoints. The second task, global-view reconstruction, tasks the model with synthesizing a comprehensive Bird’s-Eye-View (BEV) image of the entire scene by integrating information from all perspectives, enabling holistic scene layout understanding. Both tasks are implemented via a denoising network conditioned on the visual outputs of the multimodal model, with training objectives based on diffusion processes and KL-regularized VAE tokenization. The method also supports semi-supervised learning by applying these 3D-aware objectives to unlabeled 3D visual data, enabling effective utilization of large-scale vision-only datasets.
ee49b5f62f51835e01533acae4bdb367c7fa97fd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five representative 3D scene understanding benchmarks: SQA3D (situated reasoning), ScanQA (spatial QA), Scan2Cap (dense captioning), ScanRefer (single-target visual grounding), and Multi3DRefer (multi-target visual grounding), all derived from the ScanNet dataset. The proposed method will be compared against both expert task-specific models and state-of-the-art 2D/3D LMMs, including those using point cloud features, voxel aggregation, and video-based multi-view representations. Evaluation metrics will include EM, CIDEr, BLEU-4, METEOR, ROUGE, Acc@0.25/0.5, and F1@0.25/0.5, depending on the task.
