The training setup will use a LLaVA-Video-7B backbone, fine-tuned with a batch size of 256, 32 frames per scene, and BEV images rendered from point clouds. Ablation studies will assess the individual and combined effects of the cross-view and global-view pretext tasks, as well as the impact of semi-supervised learning using unlabeled 3D data.
ee49b5f62f51835e01533acae4bdb367c7fa97fd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first vision-centric 3D-aware supervision framework for large multimodal models, moving beyond prior input-level modifications by directly incorporating reconstructive pretext tasks tailored for 3D spatial understanding. The dual pretext task design—cross-view and global-view reconstruction—enables both fine-grained and holistic 3D scene comprehension. The method demonstrates substantial improvements over previous state-of-the-art models across multiple 3D benchmarks and, notably, enables effective semi-supervised learning from large-scale unlabeled 3D visual data, surpassing fully supervised baselines in certain scenarios. This work establishes a new paradigm for leveraging 3D-aware supervision in multimodal models and highlights the potential of vision-only 3D data for scalable 3D scene understanding.

ee5070fe52fd17da9a89d3f342fb07cc9ae51afe.title: DROID: A Large-Scale In-The-Wild Robot Manipulation Dataset
ee5070fe52fd17da9a89d3f342fb07cc9ae51afe.research_question: How can a large-scale, diverse, and in-the-wild robot manipulation dataset be constructed to enable the development of more generalizable and robust robotic manipulation policies across a wide range of real-world environments, tasks, and objects?
ee5070fe52fd17da9a89d3f342fb07cc9ae51afe.hypothesis: Training robot manipulation policies on a large, diverse, and high-quality dataset collected across numerous real-world scenes, tasks, and objects will result in policies with improved generalization, robustness, and performance compared to those trained on existing, less diverse datasets.
ee5070fe52fd17da9a89d3f342fb07cc9ae51afe.proposed_method: A comprehensive robot manipulation dataset will be collected using a standardized, portable hardware platform based on the Franka Emika Panda 7-DoF arm, equipped with synchronized multi-view RGB-D cameras and teleoperation via VR controllers. Data collection will be distributed across multiple institutions and geographic locations, with 50 data collectors gathering 76,000 demonstration trajectories spanning 564 unique scenes, 86 tasks, and 52 buildings. Each episode will include synchronized multi-view RGB streams, depth, camera calibration, robot state, and natural language instructions. A rigorous data collection protocol will be implemented to maximize scene, task, object, viewpoint, and interaction location diversity, including randomization of tasks, scene augmentations, and post-hoc camera calibration. All data will be labeled with natural language instructions using crowdsourcing, and comprehensive metadata will be maintained for reproducibility and analysis.
ee5070fe52fd17da9a89d3f342fb07cc9ae51afe.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training robot manipulation policies using state-of-the-art diffusion policy learning frameworks, conditioning on visual and language inputs. Policies will be evaluated across six representative tasks in four diverse environments (labs, offices, households), with both in-distribution and out-of-distribution (OOD) variants that introduce novel objects, distractors, or scene changes. Baseline comparisons will include policies trained solely on in-domain demonstrations, as well as co-training with existing large-scale datasets such as Open X-Embodiment (OXE). Evaluation metrics will focus on task success rate, robustness to distribution shifts, and qualitative assessment of policy smoothness and precision. Additional ablation studies will compare the impact of scene diversity by subsampling the dataset to control for the number of scenes while matching dataset size.
ee5070fe52fd17da9a89d3f342fb07cc9ae51afe.novelty_claims: The proposed dataset offers unprecedented diversity in scene types, tasks, objects, and viewpoints for robot manipulation, surpassing existing datasets by an order of magnitude in scene diversity. The standardized, portable hardware platform and unified data collection protocol enable consistent, reproducible, and scalable data gathering across multiple institutions. The inclusion of synchronized multi-view RGB-D data, comprehensive camera calibration, and natural language instructions supports a wide range of research in policy learning and 3D perception. Experiments are designed to demonstrate that training with this dataset leads to significantly improved policy generalization and robustness, establishing new benchmarks for in-the-wild robot manipulation.

ee57e4d7a125f4ca8916284a857c3760d7d378d3.title: Self-Supervised Learning from Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture
ee57e4d7a125f4ca8916284a857c3760d7d378d3.research_question: How can self-supervised learning from images be improved to produce highly semantic and generalizable visual representations without relying on hand-crafted data augmentations?
ee57e4d7a125f4ca8916284a857c3760d7d378d3.hypothesis: Learning to predict the representations of masked target blocks from a single context block within the same image, in representation space rather than pixel space, will result in more semantic, scalable, and generalizable image representations compared to existing generative or invariance-based self-supervised methods.
ee57e4d7a125f4ca8916284a857c3760d7d378d3.proposed_method: A novel self-supervised learning framework, termed Image-based Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (I-JEPA), will be developed. The method will use a Vision Transformer (ViT) as both context and target encoders, and a narrow predictor network. During pretraining, an image will be divided into non-overlapping patches; a large context block will be sampled and encoded, while several target blocks will be masked and their representations predicted by the predictor, conditioned on positional mask tokens. The target representations are computed by a target encoder, updated via exponential moving average of the context encoder weights. The loss will be the average L2 distance between predicted and actual target block representations, encouraging the model to learn semantic features. A multi-block masking strategy will be employed, ensuring that target blocks are sufficiently large and spatially distributed, while the context block is informative but sparse.
ee57e4d7a125f4ca8916284a857c3760d7d378d3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large-scale datasets such as ImageNet-1K and ImageNet-22K for pretraining. The proposed method will be evaluated on a variety of downstream tasks, including linear probing and fine-tuning for image classification (ImageNet-1K, CIFAR100, Places205, iNat18), as well as low-level tasks like object counting and depth prediction (Clevr/Count, Clevr/Dist). Baselines will include both generative (e.g., MAE, data2vec, CAE) and invariance-based (e.g., DINO, iBOT, MSN) self-supervised methods, with and without hand-crafted data augmentations. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy for classification tasks and task-specific metrics for low-level tasks. The experimental setup will also include ablations on masking strategies, prediction targets (representation vs. pixel space), model and dataset scaling, and computational efficiency measured in GPU hours.
ee57e4d7a125f4ca8916284a857c3760d7d378d3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach eliminates the need for hand-crafted data augmentations during pretraining, instead leveraging a predictive joint-embedding architecture that operates in representation space. The multi-block masking strategy is designed to guide the model toward learning semantic features, and the method is shown to be highly scalable and computationally efficient, converging faster and requiring less compute than prior approaches. The framework is applicable to a wide range of downstream tasks, demonstrating strong performance in both semantic and low-level vision tasks, and closes or surpasses the performance gap with state-of-the-art view-invariance-based methods. The use of prediction in representation space, rather than pixel space, is highlighted as a key innovation leading to improved semantic abstraction and transferability.

ee59c51ae8d654645150bd86780b3211cc4f4ba7.title: Universal Video Temporal Grounding with Generative Multi-modal Large Language Models
ee59c51ae8d654645150bd86780b3211cc4f4ba7.research_question: How can a universal computational model be developed to accurately localize temporal moments in videos based on natural language queries, regardless of video domain, genre, viewpoint, or duration?
ee59c51ae8d654645150bd86780b3211cc4f4ba7.hypothesis: A multi-modal large language model (MLLM) framework that interleaves explicit timestamp tokens with video tokens and employs adaptive frame scaling, combined with a coarse-to-fine, multi-stage inference strategy, will enable robust and precise temporal grounding across diverse video types and improve downstream video understanding tasks.
ee59c51ae8d654645150bd86780b3211cc4f4ba7.proposed_method: A novel universal video temporal grounding framework is proposed, leveraging generative multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) as the backbone. The method encodes temporal information by interleaving free-text timestamp tokens with visual tokens, allowing the model to associate visual content with precise temporal positions. Adaptive frame scaling dynamically adjusts spatial resolution and token allocation based on video duration, allocating higher resolution to short videos and lower resolution to long videos, thus optimizing the use of the model's context window and computational resources. For long videos, a hierarchical multi-stage inference strategy is employed: the video is partitioned into clips, segment retrieval is performed at a coarse level, and then fine-grained temporal localization is conducted within candidate segments. Training is made efficient by a video-centric paradigm, where all query-answer pairs for a video are processed in a single pass, reducing redundant computation and I/O bottlenecks.
ee59c51ae8d654645150bd86780b3211cc4f4ba7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of public temporal grounding benchmarks, including both short-video (Charades-STA, ActivityNet-Captions, QVHighlights) and long-video (Ego4D-NLQ, TaCoS) datasets, as well as downstream video question answering (VideoQA) tasks (QaEgo4D, CG-Bench, MLVU, LongVideoBench). Evaluation metrics for temporal grounding include Recall@1 at various intersection-over-union (IoU) thresholds and mean IoU (mIoU), while VideoQA tasks are evaluated with standard accuracy and grounding-specific metrics such as intersection-over-prediction (IoP). Baselines will include state-of-the-art discriminative, DETR-like, and MLLM-based models, as well as closed-source MLLMs. Ablation studies will assess the impact of adaptive frame scaling, multi-stage inference, and segment retrieval modules. Robustness will be tested by perturbing event positions and decomposing complex queries.
ee59c51ae8d654645150bd86780b3211cc4f4ba7.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces several key innovations: (1) explicit interleaving of timestamp tokens with video tokens for precise and generalizable temporal grounding; (2) adaptive frame scaling that dynamically adjusts spatial and temporal granularity based on video duration, enabling efficient handling of both short and long videos; (3) a hierarchical, coarse-to-fine multi-stage inference strategy for robust grounding in long videos; (4) a video-centric training paradigm that significantly improves training efficiency; and (5) a model-agnostic, plug-and-play design compatible with various MLLM architectures. The approach achieves state-of-the-art results across multiple benchmarks, demonstrates strong zero-shot and cross-domain generalization, and substantially enhances downstream video understanding tasks.

ee619d0e8455604a03ec4c78cc940c0a243feb77.title: Polynomial Semantics of Tractable Probabilistic Circuits
ee619d0e8455604a03ec4c78cc940c0a243feb77.research_question: What are the relationships between different polynomial semantics used in tractable probabilistic circuits for representing multivariate probability distributions, and how do these relationships impact the tractability and expressiveness of inference across various classes of distributions, including binary and categorical variables?
ee619d0e8455604a03ec4c78cc940c0a243feb77.hypothesis: For distributions over binary variables, all major polynomial semantics (likelihood, network, generating, and Fourier polynomials) are equivalent in expressive power up to a polynomial increase in circuit size, and all support tractable marginal inference. For categorical variables with four or more categories, tractable inference is not generally possible.
ee619d0e8455604a03ec4c78cc940c0a243feb77.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework will be developed to analyze and formally relate the major polynomial representations used in probabilistic circuits, including network polynomials, likelihood polynomials, generating functions, and Fourier transforms. The approach will involve constructing explicit polynomial-time circuit transformations between these semantics, leveraging results from circuit complexity (e.g., Strassen's division elimination and circuit homogenization). The methodology will extend to analyze the tractability of inference in these representations, both for binary and categorical random variables, and will include the development of new inference algorithms where existing ones are lacking (e.g., for likelihood polynomial circuits). For categorical variables, reductions from known #P-hard problems will be constructed to assess the hardness of inference.
ee619d0e8455604a03ec4c78cc940c0a243feb77.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be validated by constructing explicit circuit transformations and analyzing their size complexity, with polynomial bounds established for binary variables. The equivalence of tractability will be demonstrated by providing linear-time or polynomial-time inference algorithms for each polynomial semantics and by showing that circuits for one representation can be transformed into another with at most a polynomial increase in size. For categorical variables, hardness results will be established via reductions from the permanent computation problem, demonstrating #P-hardness for inference in categorical generating circuits with k ≥ 4 categories. Empirical experiments are not the focus, but illustrative circuit constructions and algorithmic steps will be provided.
ee619d0e8455604a03ec4c78cc940c0a243feb77.novelty_claims: The proposal establishes, for the first time, a unified theoretical framework connecting all major polynomial semantics for tractable probabilistic circuits, demonstrating their equivalence for binary variables up to polynomial circuit size. It introduces new polynomial-time circuit transformations, including from likelihood and generating polynomials to network polynomials, and provides the first linear-time inference algorithm for circuits representing likelihood polynomials. The work also extends the analysis to categorical variables, proving that inference in categorical generating circuits is #P-hard for k ≥ 4, thus delineating the boundary of tractability for these models.

ee6b02a348c920ec9ff09b081614cd24ca45feb4.title: Generalization in Kernel Regression Under Realistic Assumptions
ee6b02a348c920ec9ff09b081614cd24ca45feb4.research_question: How does kernel regression generalize under realistic and minimal assumptions, particularly in over-parameterized regimes, and what are the theoretical upper bounds on excess risk for a wide range of kernels, regularization strengths, noise levels, input dimensions, and sample sizes?
ee6b02a348c920ec9ff09b081614cd24ca45feb4.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that kernel regression exhibits a self-regularization phenomenon, whereby the structure of common kernels provides implicit regularization, enabling good generalization even in the absence of explicit regularization, across a variety of realistic settings.
ee6b02a348c920ec9ff09b081614cd24ca45feb4.proposed_method: A unified theoretical framework will be developed to rigorously upper bound the excess risk of kernel regression under minimal and realistic assumptions. The methodology will involve deriving relative perturbation bounds for the eigenvalues of kernel matrices, applicable to common kernels and for any amount of regularization, noise, input dimension, and sample size. The analysis will avoid restrictive assumptions such as sub-Gaussianity or i.i.d. features, instead introducing mild heavy-tailed conditions that are satisfied by many practical kernels. The approach will decompose the kernel matrix into low- and high-dimensional components, analyze their spectral properties, and leverage these to characterize the bias and variance components of the excess risk. The framework will also provide explicit concentration coefficients and effective rank measures to control the generalization error, and will be applicable to both regularized and unregularized (min-norm interpolator) kernel regression.
ee6b02a348c920ec9ff09b081614cd24ca45feb4.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be validated through experiments on synthetic datasets, such as learning a constant function with noise and inputs uniformly distributed on high-dimensional spheres. Common kernels including polynomial kernels and Neural Tangent Kernels (NTKs) corresponding to multi-layer fully-connected networks will be used. The experiments will measure the mean squared error (MSE) for various input dimensions, sample sizes, and noise levels, and will compare the empirical risk curves to the derived theoretical bounds. Baselines will include standard kernel regression setups under both regularized and unregularized regimes, and evaluation metrics will focus on excess risk and its bias-variance decomposition. The setup will also explore the phenomenon of benign overfitting and the behavior of the kernel matrix spectrum in high-dimensional regimes.
ee6b02a348c920ec9ff09b081614cd24ca45feb4.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified and rigorous theory for upper bounding the excess risk of kernel regression under minimal and realistic assumptions, applicable to a broad class of kernels and settings. Novel relative perturbation bounds for the eigenvalues of kernel matrices are developed, revealing an implicit self-regularization effect inherent to many kernels. The framework provides the first sharp upper bounds for both regularized and unregularized kernel regression in fixed and high-dimensional regimes, including explicit convergence rates for neural networks in the kernel regime. The analysis is broadly applicable, overcoming limitations of prior work that relied on unrealistic assumptions or narrow problem setups, and the eigenvalue perturbation results may be of independent interest for other applications.

ee71a4e9f01498b7061c506e6d42e887210a9e33.title: Beyond the Universal Law of Robustness: Sharper Laws for Random Features and Neural Tangent Kernels
ee71a4e9f01498b7061c506e6d42e887210a9e33.research_question: When does over-parameterization become a sufficient condition to achieve adversarial robustness in machine learning models, and how do different model architectures (specifically random features and neural tangent kernels) compare in their robustness properties under empirical risk minimization?
ee71a4e9f01498b7061c506e6d42e887210a9e33.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the sufficiency of over-parameterization for adversarial robustness depends on the specific model architecture. In particular, random features models may remain non-robust regardless of the degree of over-parameterization, while neural tangent kernel models with certain activation functions may achieve robustness once a necessary over-parameterization threshold is met.
ee71a4e9f01498b7061c506e6d42e887210a9e33.proposed_method: The proposed research will analyze adversarial robustness through a scale-invariant sensitivity measure based on the norm of the input gradient of the model output. The study will focus on empirical risk minimization (ERM) solutions in two settings: random features (RF) models and neural tangent kernel (NTK) models. For RF, the method involves deriving lower bounds on sensitivity by decomposing the solution into kernel and interaction matrix components, with detailed spectral analysis of these matrices. For NTK, the approach will investigate the effect of even activation functions on robustness, providing upper bounds on sensitivity that match known lower bounds. The methodology will include theoretical derivations under high-dimensional assumptions and rigorous probabilistic analysis, leveraging concentration inequalities and random matrix theory.
ee71a4e9f01498b7061c506e6d42e887210a9e33.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic datasets (e.g., Gaussian-distributed data with high input dimension) and standard image datasets such as MNIST and CIFAR-10. The empirical evaluation will measure sensitivity as a function of the number of parameters and activation function, comparing RF and NTK models. Baselines will include different activation functions (e.g., tanh, quadratic) to isolate the impact of activation symmetry. The evaluation metric will be the scale-invariant sensitivity measure, averaged over multiple independent trials, with confidence intervals reported. The experimental setup will ensure over-parameterized regimes and will validate theoretical predictions regarding robustness thresholds and the role of the interaction matrix.
ee71a4e9f01498b7061c506e6d42e887210a9e33.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a sharper, model-specific law of robustness that goes beyond the universal necessary condition, providing the first upper bounds on sensitivity for NTK models with even activations that match known lower bounds. A novel interaction matrix is defined and analyzed, revealing its central role in determining adversarial robustness and the impact of activation function symmetry. The research resolves open questions regarding the sufficiency of over-parameterization for robustness in random features models and addresses conjectures in the literature about NTK robustness. The approach offers new theoretical insights and is supported by empirical evidence on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

eecb45aa040064cbc0b37fd100706c02e7dc880e.title: Structured Prompting: Scaling In-Context Learning to 1, 000 Examples
eecb45aa040064cbc0b37fd100706c02e7dc880e.research_question: How can in-context learning in large language models be effectively scaled to utilize thousands of demonstration examples, overcoming context length and computational complexity limitations, while improving performance and stability across diverse NLP tasks?
eecb45aa040064cbc0b37fd100706c02e7dc880e.hypothesis: Structured prompting, which encodes demonstration examples in groups with right-aligned position embeddings and incorporates them into the test input via a rescaled attention mechanism, will enable in-context learning to scale to thousands of examples, leading to improved end-task performance and reduced evaluation variance compared to conventional in-context learning.
eecb45aa040064cbc0b37fd100706c02e7dc880e.proposed_method: A novel structured prompting framework is proposed to scale in-context learning to thousands of examples. The approach divides a large set of demonstration examples into multiple groups, each of which is independently encoded by the language model using right-aligned position embeddings to ensure consistent relative positioning with respect to the test input. The representations of these grouped exemplars are then incorporated into the test input through a rescaled attention mechanism, which normalizes attention scores by a scaling factor corresponding to the number of groups, preventing the model from over-attending to demonstrations as their number increases. This method reduces the computational complexity from quadratic to linear with respect to the number of exemplars and enables efficient utilization of long contexts. The approach is compatible with decoder-only Transformer architectures and does not require updating model parameters.
eecb45aa040064cbc0b37fd100706c02e7dc880e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a broad range of NLP tasks, including text classification (e.g., SST-2, SST-5, MR, Subj, DBPedia, AGNews, TREC, CB, RTE, BoolQ), multi-choice tasks (e.g., HellaSwag, StoryCloze, PIQA, OpenBookQA, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, COPA), and open-ended generation tasks (e.g., NaturalQS, WebQS, TriviaQA, SQuAD, SQuADv2). Multiple open-source GPT-like models of varying sizes (1.3B, 6.7B, 13B parameters) and the BLOOM-176B model will be used. Baselines will include conventional in-context learning with 0-shot and the maximum number of shots fitting the context window. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for classification and multi-choice tasks, exact-match accuracy for closed-book QA, and F1 score for extractive QA. Experiments will use multiple random seeds to assess stability, and ablation studies will examine the effects of prompt length, scaling factor, and alignment strategies.
eecb45aa040064cbc0b37fd100706c02e7dc880e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a structured prompting framework that enables in-context learning to scale to thousands of examples by reducing computational complexity from quadratic to linear. The approach incorporates a rescaled attention mechanism and right-aligned position embeddings, allowing efficient and stable encoding of large numbers of demonstrations. This method significantly improves both performance and stability of in-context learning across a variety of tasks and model sizes, overcoming the context window and memory limitations of conventional approaches. The framework is flexible, compatible with existing decoder-only language models, and can be extended to incorporate long documents or retrieved texts as context.

eee108b3e51e89d160d1116935e062c4d169b475.title: LayerSkip: Enabling Early Exit Inference and Self-Speculative Decoding
eee108b3e51e89d160d1116935e062c4d169b475.research_question: How can inference speed of large language models (LLMs) be improved by enabling early exit at intermediate layers, and can speculative decoding be achieved within a single model to further accelerate generation without significant accuracy loss?
eee108b3e51e89d160d1116935e062c4d169b475.hypothesis: Applying a training procedure that combines layer dropout (with higher dropout rates in later layers) and an early exit loss (using a shared LM head for all layers) will enable robust early exit inference in LLMs, allowing tokens to be predicted accurately at earlier layers. Furthermore, integrating a self-speculative decoding approach that reuses activations and cache within the same model will provide additional speedup with minimal memory overhead and without requiring auxiliary models.
eee108b3e51e89d160d1116935e062c4d169b475.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a novel training and inference framework for LLMs called LayerSkip. During training, layer dropout is applied with dropout rates increasing exponentially from early to late layers, making the model less reliant on later layers. Simultaneously, an early exit loss is imposed at each layer by connecting all transformer layers to a shared LM head, directly supervising lower layers for the language modeling task. The loss is weighted to penalize later layers more heavily, and a curriculum is used to control which layers receive early exit supervision at each iteration. During inference, the model can exit at any intermediate layer, skipping the remaining layers to the LM head for faster token prediction. For further acceleration, a self-speculative decoding algorithm is proposed: the model first drafts tokens by exiting early, then verifies and corrects them using the remaining layers, reusing the computed activations and key-value cache to minimize redundant computation and memory use.
eee108b3e51e89d160d1116935e062c4d169b475.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on various Llama model sizes (e.g., Llama2 7B, 13B, Llama3 8B, 1B) under different training regimes: pretraining from scratch, continual pretraining, finetuning on code data, and finetuning on a task-specific dataset (e.g., TOPv2 for semantic parsing). Evaluation will cover a diverse set of downstream tasks including summarization (CNN/DM), code generation (HumanEval, MBPP), and semantic parsing (TOPv2), as well as standard language modeling benchmarks (MMLU, ARC, BoolQ, etc.). Baselines will include standard Llama models trained without LayerSkip. Metrics will include task-specific accuracy, perplexity, and inference speedup (measured as wall-clock or layer-compute reduction). The experimental setup will compare early exit accuracy at different layers, last-layer accuracy, and end-to-end speedup, as well as memory footprint for speculative decoding approaches.
eee108b3e51e89d160d1116935e062c4d169b475.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to combine exponentially increasing layer dropout and a shared LM head with early exit loss for decoder-only LLMs, enabling robust early exit inference without auxiliary layers or additional models. The self-speculative decoding algorithm is novel in that it allows speculative decoding within a single model by reusing activations and cache, reducing both memory and compute overhead compared to traditional speculative decoding methods that require separate draft and main models. The method enables the creation of an ensemble of sub-models of varying depths within a single trained model, facilitating flexible and efficient inference.

eefbd8b384a58f464827b19e30a6920ba976def9.title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
eefbd8b384a58f464827b19e30a6920ba976def9.research_question: How can the process of discovering and isolating computational circuits responsible for specific behaviors in neural network models, particularly transformer-based language models, be automated to improve the scalability and rigor of mechanistic interpretability research?
eefbd8b384a58f464827b19e30a6920ba976def9.hypothesis: Automating the identification of subgraphs (circuits) within neural network computational graphs that are responsible for specific behaviors is feasible and can recover known circuits with high fidelity, reducing the need for manual inspection and enabling scalable interpretability.
eefbd8b384a58f464827b19e30a6920ba976def9.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, Automatic Circuit Discovery (ACDC), will be developed to automate the process of identifying relevant subgraphs (circuits) within a neural network's computational graph that are responsible for a specified behavior. The method will start by specifying a computational graph at a chosen level of granularity (e.g., attention heads, MLP layers), a dataset eliciting the target behavior, and a metric to quantify model performance on the behavior. ACDC will iteratively traverse the graph from outputs to inputs, recursively removing edges whose removal does not significantly degrade performance on the chosen metric, as measured by the KL divergence between the original and modified model outputs. The process will use activation patching, where activations are replaced with those from corrupted inputs to test the importance of connections. The method will be compared and extended with adaptations of Subnetwork Probing (SP) and Head Importance Score for Pruning (HISP), with all methods generalized to use corrupted activations rather than only zeroing out activations.
eefbd8b384a58f464827b19e30a6920ba976def9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of transformer models and tasks for which end-to-end circuits have been previously reverse-engineered, including GPT-2 Small on the IOI, Docstring, and Greater-Than tasks, as well as tiny transformers implementing known algorithms via tracr. Datasets will consist of curated prompts eliciting specific behaviors (e.g., year comparison, pronoun resolution), and corresponding corrupted datasets will be used for activation patching. Baselines will include SP and HISP, both adapted to the circuit discovery context. Evaluation metrics will include area under the ROC curve (AUC) for edge classification against canonical circuits, KL divergence between the original and subgraph outputs, and the number of edges in the recovered circuit. Extensive ablation studies will be performed to assess sensitivity to hyperparameters, metrics, and activation patching strategies.
eefbd8b384a58f464827b19e30a6920ba976def9.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a fully automated approach for discovering circuits in neural networks, reducing reliance on manual inspection and enabling scalable mechanistic interpretability. The ACDC algorithm systematically applies activation patching to prune irrelevant connections, directly reflecting the workflow used in manual circuit discovery but automating the process. The approach is validated on multiple tasks and models, demonstrating the ability to recover known circuits with high fidelity and to provide quantitative metrics for circuit extraction quality. The method is further distinguished by its generalization of existing pruning and probing techniques to the interpretability setting and its empirical analysis of limitations and robustness.

ef018d9fad6167cfddb7d6654c5422df1e953730.title: Self-Evaluation Guided Beam Search for Reasoning
ef018d9fad6167cfddb7d6654c5422df1e953730.research_question: How can uncertainty and error accumulation in multi-step reasoning with large language models be mitigated to improve the accuracy and robustness of final predictions across diverse reasoning tasks?
ef018d9fad6167cfddb7d6654c5422df1e953730.hypothesis: Incorporating a stepwise self-evaluation mechanism into the decoding process of large language models will guide and calibrate multi-step reasoning, reducing error accumulation and improving prediction quality compared to standard autoregressive or self-consistency-based methods.
ef018d9fad6167cfddb7d6654c5422df1e953730.proposed_method: A novel decoding algorithm is proposed that integrates stepwise self-evaluation guidance into stochastic beam search for multi-step reasoning tasks. The approach decomposes the reasoning process into discrete steps, with each step generating a semantically meaningful sequence of tokens. At each step, a constraint function combines the language model's generation probability with a correctness confidence score derived from self-evaluation prompts, forming a new decoding objective that balances both factors via a tunable parameter. Stochastic beam search is employed, where candidate reasoning chains are sampled and pruned based on their combined scores, with temperature-controlled randomness to balance exploration and exploitation. The self-evaluation is performed by prompting the same LLM (with different prompts) to assess the correctness of each reasoning step, using a multiple-choice format to calibrate the confidence score.
ef018d9fad6167cfddb7d6654c5422df1e953730.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of reasoning benchmarks, including arithmetic reasoning (GSM8K, AQuA, SVAMP, ASDiv, TabMWP), symbolic reasoning (BIG-Bench Date Understanding and Object Counting), and commonsense reasoning (CommonsenseQA, StrategyQA, Sports Understanding from BIG-Bench). Both closed-source (Codex) and open-source (Llama-2) LLMs will be used as backbones, with program-aided (PAL, PoT) and chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting schemes. Baselines will include standard CoT, PAL, PoT, and their self-consistency and diversity-augmented variants. Evaluation metrics will primarily be accuracy, with computational cost measured in generated tokens. The effect of hyperparameters such as beam size, generation and sampling temperatures, and the balance parameter for self-evaluation will be systematically analyzed. Cost-performance trade-offs will be assessed by matching computational budgets across methods.
ef018d9fad6167cfddb7d6654c5422df1e953730.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a unified framework that combines stepwise self-evaluation with stochastic beam search for multi-step reasoning, enabling fine-grained calibration and error control at each reasoning step. Unlike prior approaches that apply self-evaluation only at the instance level or rely on single-chain sampling, this method leverages stepwise correctness assessment to guide the search through the exponentially large reasoning space. The integration of temperature-controlled stochasticity into beam search allows for a principled trade-off between diversity and quality in candidate reasoning chains. The approach demonstrates substantial improvements in accuracy, especially on tasks requiring long and complex reasoning chains, and provides a generalizable mechanism applicable across arithmetic, symbolic, and commonsense reasoning domains.

ef0b411cb5117adc730dab9e9b89473e23f7af8d.title: vSHARP: variable Splitting Half-quadratic ADMM algorithm for Reconstruction of inverse-Problems
ef0b411cb5117adc730dab9e9b89473e23f7af8d.research_question: How can the reconstruction of ill-posed inverse problems in medical imaging, such as accelerated parallel static and dynamic MRI, be improved to achieve higher image quality and computational efficiency compared to existing methods?
ef0b411cb5117adc730dab9e9b89473e23f7af8d.hypothesis: Integrating a deep learning-based variable splitting half-quadratic ADMM framework, which unrolls the optimization process and incorporates neural network-based denoisers and Lagrange multiplier initialization, will lead to superior reconstruction quality and efficiency for inverse problems in medical imaging compared to current state-of-the-art approaches.
ef0b411cb5117adc730dab9e9b89473e23f7af8d.proposed_method: A novel deep learning-based framework, vSHARP, will be developed for solving ill-posed inverse problems in medical imaging. The method will leverage the Half-Quadratic Variable Splitting (HQVS) technique and the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), unrolling the optimization process into a trainable neural network architecture. At each iteration, a deep neural network denoiser (e.g., U-Net or variants) will be used for the z-step, while a differentiable gradient descent process will be unrolled for the x-step to ensure data consistency in the image domain. The initialization of Lagrange multipliers will be performed using a dedicated neural network employing dilated convolutions and replication padding. All penalty parameters and gradient descent step sizes will be learned end-to-end, and the framework will be adaptable to both 2D and 3D (dynamic) imaging scenarios.
ef0b411cb5117adc730dab9e9b89473e23f7af8d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple public MRI datasets, including the Calgary-Campinas brain dataset, fastMRI T2 prostate dataset, and the CMRxRecon cardiac cine dataset. The evaluation will cover both static and dynamic accelerated parallel MRI reconstruction tasks, using retrospectively undersampled k-space data with various acceleration factors (4x, 8x, 16x) and different undersampling patterns (e.g., Variable Density Poisson disk, equispaced masks). Baseline comparisons will include non-physics-based deep learning models (U-Net, Uformer) and state-of-the-art physics-based unrolled optimization networks (E2EVarNet, RVarNet). Evaluation metrics will comprise SSIM, pSNR, NMSE, and additional image/k-space domain losses (e.g., SSIMLoss, HFEN, NMSE, NMAE). Statistical significance testing will be performed to assess improvements over baselines.
ef0b411cb5117adc730dab9e9b89473e23f7af8d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a versatile deep learning-based variable splitting half-quadratic ADMM framework for inverse problem reconstruction, featuring: (1) end-to-end unrolling of HQVS-ADMM with trainable penalty and step size parameters, (2) integration of neural network-based denoisers and a learnable Lagrange multiplier initializer, (3) adaptability to both static and dynamic (3D) imaging tasks, and (4) comprehensive mathematical derivation and practical implementation for accelerated parallel MRI. The method claims to surpass current baselines in both reconstruction fidelity and computational efficiency.

ef146eec42d80f81354abdfeb803183ac6341279.title: Contexts can be Cheap: Solving Stochastic Contextual Bandits with Linear Bandit Algorithms
ef146eec42d80f81354abdfeb803183ac6341279.research_question: How can stochastic contextual linear bandit problems be efficiently solved, and is it possible to achieve regret bounds comparable to those in standard linear bandit settings, even when the context distribution is unknown? Additionally, can this approach be extended to settings with batch learning, model misspecification, adversarial corruption, and parameter sparsity?
ef146eec42d80f81354abdfeb803183ac6341279.hypothesis: Stochastic contextual linear bandit problems can be reduced to (possibly misspecified) linear bandit problems, enabling the use of linear bandit algorithms to achieve optimal or near-optimal regret bounds in a variety of settings, including cases with unknown context distributions, batch constraints, model misspecification, adversarial corruption, and sparse parameters.
ef146eec42d80f81354abdfeb803183ac6341279.proposed_method: A novel reduction framework will be developed to transform any stochastic contextual linear bandit instance into a linear bandit instance. When the context distribution is known, the reduction constructs a fixed action set by mapping each parameter to its expected optimal action under the context distribution, allowing any linear bandit algorithm to be applied directly. For unknown context distributions, the method divides the time horizon into batches and incrementally estimates the expected optimal actions using empirical data from previous batches, resulting in a sequence of misspecified linear bandit instances. The approach includes discretizing the parameter space to ensure coverage and bounding the misspecification error via concentration inequalities. Adaptations are proposed for batch learning (with O(loglogT) batches), misspecified models (with unknown or known deviation bounds), adversarial corruption (with bounded corruption), and sparse parameter regimes (with efficient discretization).
ef146eec42d80f81354abdfeb803183ac6341279.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and/or real-world datasets that simulate stochastic contextual linear bandit environments. The proposed reduction-based algorithms will be evaluated against state-of-the-art baselines for contextual linear bandits, linear bandits, and specialized settings such as batch learning, misspecified models, adversarial corruption, and sparsity. Evaluation metrics will include cumulative regret, regret bounds with high probability, and computational efficiency. Key experimental setups will involve varying the time horizon T, model dimension d, sparsity level s, misspecification parameter ǫ, and adversarial corruption budget C, with results reported for both infinite and finite action sets, as well as for different batch sizes.
ef146eec42d80f81354abdfeb803183ac6341279.novelty_claims: The proposed reduction framework establishes, for the first time, a constructive equivalence between stochastic contextual linear bandits and linear bandits, enabling the direct application of linear bandit algorithms to contextual settings without additional regret in the worst case. The method achieves improved or optimal high-probability regret bounds (e.g., O(d√T logT)) for a range of settings, including batch learning, misspecified models, adversarial corruption, and sparsity, often surpassing prior results by removing extra log factors or providing the first high-probability guarantees. The approach also introduces new algorithms for batch and sparse contextual bandits with tighter regret bounds and fewer batches, and provides a unified perspective that simplifies the analysis and design of contextual bandit algorithms.

ef2a4b5da1c58183b699861030b40face5587a30.title: BlockScan: Detecting Anomalies in Blockchain Transactions
ef2a4b5da1c58183b699861030b40face5587a30.research_question: How can anomalies in blockchain transactions be effectively detected, given the unique multi-modal and complex data structure of such transactions, in order to improve security in decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystems?
ef2a4b5da1c58183b699861030b40face5587a30.hypothesis: A customized Transformer-based model with a multi-modal tokenization scheme and masked language modeling can more accurately detect anomalous blockchain transactions than rule-based, traditional machine learning, or generic language model approaches.
ef2a4b5da1c58183b699861030b40face5587a30.proposed_method: A novel Transformer-based framework will be developed, leveraging a BERT-style architecture with masked language modeling (MLM) to learn robust representations of normal blockchain transaction patterns. The method will introduce a modularized, multi-modal tokenizer designed to handle blockchain-specific tokens (such as addresses and hashes), large numerical values (converted to hexadecimal for consistency), and textual log messages (using subword tokenization). The model will incorporate Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) and FlashAttention to efficiently process long transaction sequences. During pretraining, a proportion of transaction tokens will be masked and the model trained to reconstruct them, with reconstruction error serving as an anomaly score. Anomalous transactions will be identified by ranking transactions according to their reconstruction errors, with theoretical analysis provided to justify the approach.
ef2a4b5da1c58183b699861030b40face5587a30.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on real-world transaction datasets from Ethereum (October 2020 to April 2023) and Solana (September 2023 to December 2023), covering interactions with multiple DeFi applications. Benign transactions will be split into training (80%) and evaluation (20%) sets based on block timestamps to prevent data leakage, while malicious transactions will be sourced from verified vendors and manually validated. The evaluation will use metrics including False Positive Rate (FPR), Recall, and Precision, with top-k anomaly detection thresholds. Baselines for comparison will include BlockGPT (causal Transformer), Doc2Vec+GMM, GPT-4o, and heuristic-based methods. Ablation studies will assess the impact of core components such as the tokenizer, log message encoding, and positional embeddings, and hyperparameter sensitivity will be analyzed. Model architectures will include BERT-base for Ethereum and BERT-large for Solana, with sequence lengths and batch sizes tailored to dataset characteristics.
ef2a4b5da1c58183b699861030b40face5587a30.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first open-source, Transformer-based anomaly detection system for blockchain transactions with a theoretical guarantee on detection. Key innovations include a custom multi-modal tokenization strategy tailored for blockchain data, the integration of RoPE and FlashAttention for efficient handling of long sequences, and a simple yet effective post-training anomaly detection method based on reconstruction error. The method is claimed to outperform all existing baselines, especially on challenging datasets such as Solana, where previous methods fail to detect anomalies. The approach is robust to hyperparameter choices and model architecture, and the open-sourced code and datasets establish a new benchmark for future research in blockchain anomaly detection.

ef2a773c3c7848a6cc16b18164be5f8876a310af.title: Scaling Up Influence Functions
ef2a773c3c7848a6cc16b18164be5f8876a310af.research_question: How can influence functions be efficiently scaled to enable interpretation and debugging of predictions in deep neural networks with hundreds of millions of parameters and training examples, particularly for large-scale language and vision models?
ef2a773c3c7848a6cc16b18164be5f8876a310af.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging Arnoldi iteration to approximate the dominant eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Hessian, influence functions can be computed efficiently in both time and memory, making them practical for full-scale deep neural networks without sacrificing accuracy.
ef2a773c3c7848a6cc16b18164be5f8876a310af.proposed_method: A novel approach is proposed for efficient computation of influence functions by avoiding explicit storage and inversion of the full Hessian matrix. The method employs Arnoldi iteration to identify the dominant eigenvalues and corresponding orthonormal eigenvectors of the Hessian on a small random subset of the data. The Hessian is then diagonalized within this low-dimensional subspace, allowing for cheap inversion and efficient computation of Hessian-gradient products using forward-mode Jacobian-vector products. This approach eliminates the need for repeated, memory-intensive LISSA iterations and enables influence estimation using only scalar-gradient products, which do not require materialization of full gradients or Hessians. The method supports parallelization and is compatible with subsetting strategies for both data and parameters, further enhancing scalability.
ef2a773c3c7848a6cc16b18164be5f8876a310af.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both image classification and sequence-to-sequence tasks, using datasets such as MNIST (for small-scale benchmarking), ImageNet (14M examples), and Paracrawl (100M examples) for machine translation. Models evaluated will include small and large convolutional neural networks, ResNet50, and Vision Transformers with up to 300M parameters. Baseline methods for comparison will include LISSA-based influence functions, TracIn, RandProj, and RandSelect. Evaluation metrics will focus on retrieval of mislabeled or noisy examples using self-influence scores, with performance measured by area under the ROC curve (AUC) and average precision (AP). Additional experiments will assess the scalability of the method with respect to model and dataset size, as well as the impact of restricting influence computation to subsets of model parameters.
ef2a773c3c7848a6cc16b18164be5f8876a310af.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to enable practical, scalable computation of influence functions for full-size language and vision transformer models with hundreds of millions of parameters and training examples. By introducing Arnoldi iteration for Hessian approximation, the approach drastically reduces memory and computational requirements, achieving speedups of several orders of magnitude over existing methods such as LISSA and TracIn. The method allows influence-based data debugging and interpretability analyses at scales previously inaccessible, and provides a foundation for further research into influence-based model understanding and data quality assessment.

ef3bdb9e805887a1a14e1e4cdb27145135591305.title: RADAR: Robust AI-Text Detection via Adversarial Learning
ef3bdb9e805887a1a14e1e4cdb27145135591305.research_question: How can AI-generated text be reliably distinguished from human-written text, particularly in the presence of paraphrasing attacks that aim to evade detection?
ef3bdb9e805887a1a14e1e4cdb27145135591305.hypothesis: Joint adversarial training of a paraphraser and a detector will result in a more robust AI-text detector that maintains high detection performance even when faced with paraphrased AI-generated texts.
ef3bdb9e805887a1a14e1e4cdb27145135591305.proposed_method: A robust AI-text detection framework will be developed based on adversarial learning between two large language models: a paraphraser and a detector. The paraphraser will be trained to rewrite AI-generated text to evade detection, using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with an entropy penalty to encourage diverse paraphrasing strategies. The detector will be trained to distinguish between human-written text, original AI-generated text, and paraphrased AI-generated text using a reweighted logistic loss to address class imbalance. The training process will alternate between updating the paraphraser (to maximize evasion) and the detector (to maximize detection accuracy), continuing until validation loss stabilizes. The detector will then be deployed to predict the likelihood of any input text being AI-generated.
ef3bdb9e805887a1a14e1e4cdb27145135591305.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using eight different large language models (including Pythia, Dolly 2.0, Palmyra, Camel, GPT-J, Dolly 1.0, LLaMA, and Vicuna) as sources of AI-generated text. Four diverse human-text datasets will be used for evaluation: Xsum (news), SQuAD (academic), Reddit Writing Prompts (creative writing), and TOEFL (non-native English). The detection framework will be compared against six existing AI-text detection baselines, including statistical and classification-based methods, as well as DetectGPT and OpenAI's RoBERTa classifier. Evaluation metrics will primarily include the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), with experiments conducted both with and without paraphrasing, including both seen (trained) and unseen (external, e.g., GPT-3.5-Turbo) paraphrasers. Additional experiments will assess transferability of the detector across LLMs, robustness to multi-round paraphrasing, and the effect of hyperparameter tuning on detection performance.
ef3bdb9e805887a1a14e1e4cdb27145135591305.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to leverage adversarial learning between a paraphraser and a detector for robust AI-text detection. The method demonstrates superior robustness to paraphrasing attacks compared to existing detectors, maintaining high detection accuracy even against unseen paraphrasers. The approach also exhibits strong transferability, enabling detectors trained on one LLM to generalize effectively to texts generated by other LLMs, including state-of-the-art models like GPT-4. Additionally, the adversarial training process improves the quality and diversity of paraphrasing, and the framework allows for balancing detection performance between paraphrased and unperturbed text through hyperparameter tuning.

ef7993ab30d0a8afabb4ebab080e471c0d5c743c.title: Diffusion-based Time Series Imputation and Forecasting with Structured State Space Models
ef7993ab30d0a8afabb4ebab080e471c0d5c743c.research_question: How can time series imputation and forecasting be improved, particularly under diverse and challenging missingness scenarios, by leveraging advanced generative modeling and architectures capable of capturing long-term dependencies?
ef7993ab30d0a8afabb4ebab080e471c0d5c743c.hypothesis: Integrating conditional diffusion models with structured state space model (SSM) layers will enable more accurate and robust time series imputation and forecasting across a variety of missingness scenarios, including those where existing state-of-the-art methods fail, by effectively modeling long-term dependencies and providing probabilistic imputations.
ef7993ab30d0a8afabb4ebab080e471c0d5c743c.proposed_method: A novel framework, SSSDS4, will be developed that combines conditional diffusion models with structured state space model (S4) layers as the core architectural component. The diffusion process will be applied only to the regions of the time series that require imputation, as specified by binary masks, while conditioning on the observed portions of the data. The architecture will replace traditional dilated convolutions with S4 layers within each residual block and introduce an additional S4 layer after the conditional information is incorporated, enhancing the model's flexibility and ability to capture long-term temporal dependencies. The model will be trained using a weighted variational bound on the negative log-likelihood, focusing the loss on the imputed regions, and will support both unconditional and conditional diffusion setups. Additional architectural variants, such as SSSDSA (a non-autoregressive SaShiMi-based model) and CSDIS4 (a CSDI variant with S4 layers), will be explored to assess the impact of state space modeling in diffusion-based imputation.
ef7993ab30d0a8afabb4ebab080e471c0d5c743c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of benchmark datasets, including PTB-XL (ECG data), MuJoCo, Electricity, PEMS-Bay, and METR-LA, covering a range of missingness scenarios: random missing (RM), random block missing (RBM), blackout missing (BM), and time series forecasting (TF). The evaluation will use standard metrics such as MAE, RMSE, and MSE, and will include both deterministic and probabilistic baselines (e.g., LAMC, CSDI, DiffWave, SAITS, BRITS, GRIN, M-RNN, GP-VAE, NAOMI, NRTSI, NeuralCDE, Latent-ODE). For each dataset and scenario, models will be trained and evaluated under identical missingness ratios and patterns, with results averaged over multiple samples and trials. The robustness of the approach will be further assessed by varying missingness ratios (up to 90%) and testing on high-dimensional data (hundreds of channels), as well as by evaluating the impact of mismatches between training and test missingness patterns.
ef7993ab30d0a8afabb4ebab080e471c0d5c743c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first direct application of conditional diffusion models with structured state space layers for time series imputation and forecasting. Key innovations include the use of S4 layers as a replacement for convolutional or transformer layers within the diffusion process, the targeted application of noise to only the imputed regions, and architectural enhancements that improve flexibility and performance in capturing long-term dependencies. The methodology is demonstrated to outperform state-of-the-art probabilistic and deterministic imputers, especially in challenging blackout and forecasting scenarios where prior methods fail to produce meaningful results. The framework also provides a simple yet effective way to handle various missingness patterns and supports probabilistic imputation, offering samples of plausible imputations rather than single deterministic outputs.

ef8a8bd193b1a0a5e2c834a7a28869a2ec85bab7.title: s1: Simple test-time scaling
ef8a8bd193b1a0a5e2c834a7a28869a2ec85bab7.research_question: How can test-time compute be efficiently scaled to improve reasoning performance in language models, using minimal additional data and simple interventions?
ef8a8bd193b1a0a5e2c834a7a28869a2ec85bab7.hypothesis: A language model fine-tuned on a small, carefully curated set of high-quality, diverse, and difficult reasoning samples, when equipped with a simple test-time compute control mechanism, will exhibit strong reasoning performance and predictable scaling with increased test-time compute.
ef8a8bd193b1a0a5e2c834a7a28869a2ec85bab7.proposed_method: A new approach will be developed that first curates a dataset of 1,000 reasoning-intensive questions (s1K) selected from a large pool of 59,000 samples using three criteria: quality, difficulty, and diversity. Quality control involves filtering out low-quality or malformed samples; difficulty is assessed via model performance and reasoning trace length; diversity is ensured by sampling uniformly across domains classified by subject taxonomy. The selected 1,000 samples, each paired with detailed reasoning traces, are used to perform supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on a large pretrained language model (e.g., Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct). At test time, a decoding-time intervention called 'budget forcing' is introduced: the model's reasoning phase is forcibly lengthened or shortened by appending specific tokens (e.g., 'Wait') or delimiters, thereby controlling the amount of compute spent on each problem. This sequential scaling method enables the model to self-correct and refine its answers as more compute is allocated.
ef8a8bd193b1a0a5e2c834a7a28869a2ec85bab7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on challenging reasoning benchmarks, including AIME24 (30 problems from the 2024 American Invitational Mathematics Examination), MATH500 (500 competition math problems), and GPQA Diamond (198 PhD-level science questions). The fine-tuned model (s1-32B) will be evaluated under varying test-time compute budgets, using accuracy as the primary metric and additional metrics for controllability and scaling slope. Baselines will include conditional length-control methods (token/step/class-conditional), rejection sampling, and parallel scaling via majority voting and tree search (REBASE). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art closed and open models such as OpenAI o1-preview, DeepSeek-r1, QwQ-32B, and Gemini2.0. Ablation studies will assess the impact of data selection criteria and test-time scaling techniques.
ef8a8bd193b1a0a5e2c834a7a28869a2ec85bab7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a highly sample-efficient reasoning training methodology, achieving strong performance with only 1,000 fine-tuning samples. It presents a simple, transparent, and controllable test-time compute scaling technique ('budget forcing') that enables predictable and effective performance improvements. The approach establishes new benchmarks for sample efficiency and open-source reproducibility in reasoning models, and provides the first open reproduction of test-time scaling curves previously demonstrated only in closed-source models. The method also defines clear evaluation metrics for test-time scaling, facilitating future research in this area.

ef9e058d22d190fdd38ddee367cf6aa8d1a14bd5.title: Self-Play Fine-Tuning Converts Weak Language Models to Strong Language Models
ef9e058d22d190fdd38ddee367cf6aa8d1a14bd5.research_question: Can a weak large language model (LLM) be improved to reach or surpass the performance of stronger models without the need for additional human-annotated data or external preference feedback?
ef9e058d22d190fdd38ddee367cf6aa8d1a14bd5.hypothesis: A self-play fine-tuning mechanism, in which an LLM iteratively generates and learns from its own responses, can significantly enhance the capabilities of a weak LLM, potentially achieving or exceeding the performance of models trained with additional human or AI feedback.
ef9e058d22d190fdd38ddee367cf6aa8d1a14bd5.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces Self-Play fIne-tuNing (SPIN), a novel iterative fine-tuning approach for LLMs that eliminates the need for new human-annotated or preference data. Starting from a supervised fine-tuned model, the LLM engages in self-play by generating synthetic responses to prompts from its own previous iteration. At each iteration, the current model (main player) is trained to distinguish between human-annotated responses and those generated by the previous iteration (opponent player), using a loss function such as the logistic loss. The main player is optimized to prefer human-like responses, while the opponent player is updated to make its responses increasingly indistinguishable from human responses. This process is formalized as a two-player game, with a KL regularization term to stabilize training and prevent excessive deviation from the previous model. The procedure is repeated iteratively, with each new model becoming the opponent in the next round, until the LLM's output distribution aligns with the target data distribution.
ef9e058d22d190fdd38ddee367cf6aa8d1a14bd5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the zephyr-7b-sft-full model, a supervised fine-tuned variant of Mistral-7B, as the base LLM. The Ultrachat200k dataset, specifically a 50k prompt subset, will serve as the source of prompts for generating synthetic responses. At each iteration, the model will be fine-tuned for two epochs using both the original human-annotated data and the newly generated synthetic responses. Evaluation will be performed on multiple benchmarks, including the HuggingFace Open LLM Leaderboard (covering Arc, HellaSwag, Winogrande, MMLU, TruthfulQA, and GSM8k), MT-Bench, and selected Big-Bench datasets. Baselines for comparison will include continued supervised fine-tuning (SFT), direct preference optimization (DPO) with additional preference data, and ablations varying synthetic data size and number of training epochs. Performance will be measured using standard accuracy and leaderboard metrics for each benchmark.
ef9e058d22d190fdd38ddee367cf6aa8d1a14bd5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a self-play fine-tuning framework for LLMs that does not require any additional human-annotated or preference data beyond the initial supervised fine-tuning dataset. Unlike prior methods such as DPO or RLHF, which rely on external feedback or preference datasets, SPIN leverages only the model's own generations in an adversarial, iterative process. The method is theoretically grounded, with convergence guarantees showing that the LLM's distribution aligns with the target data distribution at global optimum. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that SPIN can break the performance plateau of standard SFT, achieve significant improvements across diverse benchmarks, and even outperform models trained with extra preference data. This establishes a new paradigm for efficiently converting weak LLMs into strong ones through self-improvement.

efa164de424f51168c0258ced4c93ab7f9ff6bea.title: Unconstrained Dynamic Regret via Sparse Coding
efa164de424f51168c0258ced4c93ab7f9ff6bea.research_question: How can online convex optimization algorithms be designed to achieve adaptive dynamic regret bounds in unconstrained, nonstationary environments, where the comparator sequence is arbitrarily time-varying and the domain is unbounded?
efa164de424f51168c0258ced4c93ab7f9ff6bea.hypothesis: Adaptive regret bounds can be achieved in unconstrained online convex optimization by leveraging sparse coding frameworks that measure comparator complexity via energy and sparsity on a user-specified dictionary, enabling improved performance over existing methods, especially in almost static or structured environments.
efa164de424f51168c0258ced4c93ab7f9ff6bea.proposed_method: A novel algorithmic framework will be developed that converts the unconstrained dynamic online convex optimization problem into a vector-output online linear regression (OLR) problem using a sparse coding approach. The method introduces a user-specified dictionary of orthogonal feature vectors (such as Haar wavelets or Fourier bases) spanning the sequence space, allowing the comparator sequence to be represented as a linear combination of these features. An unconstrained static OCO algorithm (e.g., FreeGrad) is applied in the transform domain to adaptively aggregate these features, with the regret bound depending on the energy and sparsity of the comparator's representation. The framework supports arbitrary dictionaries, enabling the incorporation of prior knowledge or learned representations, and allows for efficient computation by exploiting the local support of wavelet features.
efa164de424f51168c0258ced4c93ab7f9ff6bea.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both synthetic and real-world time series datasets, such as weather data, to evaluate the proposed algorithm. Baseline comparisons will include existing unconstrained dynamic regret algorithms, such as those from JC22, and meta-expert OGD (Ader). Evaluation metrics will focus on dynamic regret, measured against various comparator complexity statistics including energy, sparsity, path length, and number of switches. The experimental setup will test the algorithm's performance under different types of nonstationarity, such as persistent oscillations and local outliers, and will assess computational efficiency (e.g., O(d log T) per round for Haar wavelets).
efa164de424f51168c0258ced4c93ab7f9ff6bea.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a new class of unconstrained dynamic regret bounds that adapt to both the energy and sparsity of the comparator sequence on a flexible, user-chosen dictionary. This approach generalizes and improves upon prior results by decoupling function approximation from regret minimization and by enabling finer-grained adaptivity to comparator structure. The use of wavelet dictionaries, in particular, yields strictly improved regret rates in almost static environments and provides computational efficiency. The method establishes a novel connection between online learning, sparse signal representations, and adaptive regret, offering a versatile and theoretically justified approach for nonstationary online decision making.

efb4c44dc2aec86c25893660564c920895dfedea.title: PARS: Pseudo-Label Aware Robust Sample Selection for Learning with Noisy Labels
efb4c44dc2aec86c25893660564c920895dfedea.research_question: How can robust deep learning models be trained effectively when training data contains high levels of noisy or incorrect labels, especially in both standard and low-resource/semi-supervised scenarios?
efb4c44dc2aec86c25893660564c920895dfedea.hypothesis: A joint training framework that simultaneously leverages both original noisy labels and pseudo-labels, employs robust sample selection, and applies label-dependent noise-aware loss functions can significantly improve model robustness and accuracy in learning with noisy labels, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods, particularly under high noise and low-resource conditions.
efb4c44dc2aec86c25893660564c920895dfedea.proposed_method: The proposed method, PARS (Pseudo-Label Aware Robust Sample Selection), introduces a hybrid framework that integrates robust loss functions, sample selection, and pseudo-labeling in a unified training process. Initially, a robust warm-up phase is conducted using noise-robust loss functions (such as MAE, SCE, NCE, or APL) to stabilize early learning and produce reliable predictions. The entire dataset is then partitioned into ambiguous and noisy subsets based on a confidence threshold applied to model predictions, independent of the noisy labels. For ambiguous samples, robust learning losses are applied, while for noisy samples, negative learning losses are used to learn the complement of the noisy labels. Simultaneously, self-training is performed using pseudo-labels generated by the model, applying positive/negative learning to ambiguous/noisy pseudo-labels, respectively. A confidence penalty regularization is added to prevent degenerate solutions during self-training, and data augmentation (weak for raw labels, strong for pseudo-labels) is incorporated to further enhance generalization.
efb4c44dc2aec86c25893660564c920895dfedea.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on benchmark image classification datasets with synthetic and real-world noisy labels, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Clothing1M. Synthetic noise is injected into CIFAR datasets using both symmetric (random label flipping at rates of 20%, 50%, 80%, 90%) and asymmetric (class-conditional, 40%) noise protocols. In addition to standard supervised noisy label settings, a low-resource semi-supervised scenario is evaluated, where only a subset of data is weakly labeled and the rest is unlabeled. Baselines include state-of-the-art methods such as DivideMix, ELR+, Co-teaching+, Meta-Learning, and FixMatch. Evaluation metrics focus on test accuracy using the original clean labels. Ablation studies are performed to assess the contribution of each component (warm-up, pseudo-labeling, negative learning) to overall performance.
efb4c44dc2aec86c25893660564c920895dfedea.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is novel in jointly leveraging both original noisy labels and pseudo-labels throughout training, rather than discarding noisy labels or relying solely on sample selection. It introduces a unified framework that applies label-dependent noise-aware loss functions to both ambiguous and noisy samples, and integrates robust/negative learning with self-training and data augmentation. The method demonstrates significant improvements over existing techniques, particularly in high-noise and low-resource settings, and provides the first evidence that filtered noisy labels can be effectively exploited, rather than discarded, to boost model performance in learning with noisy labels.

efbe97d20c4ffe356e8826c01dc550bacc405add.title: Adding Conditional Control to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
efbe97d20c4ffe356e8826c01dc550bacc405add.research_question: How can spatially localized, task-specific conditional controls be effectively integrated into large pretrained text-to-image diffusion models to enable fine-grained, user-directed image generation beyond what is possible with text prompts alone?
efbe97d20c4ffe356e8826c01dc550bacc405add.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a neural network architecture that augments large pretrained text-to-image diffusion models with spatially localized conditional controls—while preserving the original model's parameters—will enable robust, fine-grained control over image generation using a variety of conditioning inputs (e.g., edges, poses, segmentation, depth) without degrading the model's generative quality or requiring extensive retraining.
efbe97d20c4ffe356e8826c01dc550bacc405add.proposed_method: A neural network architecture, termed ControlNet, will be developed to enhance large pretrained text-to-image diffusion models with additional conditional control. The approach involves creating a trainable copy of the encoding layers of the diffusion model (e.g., Stable Diffusion) while locking the original parameters. These two branches are connected via zero-initialized convolutional layers ('zero convolutions'), which ensure that no harmful noise is introduced at the start of training and that the pretrained backbone is preserved. The conditional input (such as an edge map, pose skeleton, or segmentation mask) is encoded into a feature vector using a small convolutional network and injected into the trainable copy at each encoder level. The architecture supports single or multiple conditioning inputs, and the design is computationally efficient as gradients are only computed for the trainable copy and zero convolution layers.
efbe97d20c4ffe356e8826c01dc550bacc405add.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Stable Diffusion as the base model, with ControlNet trained and evaluated on a variety of conditioning tasks including Canny edges, Hough lines, user scribbles, human keypoints, segmentation maps, shape normals, depth maps, and cartoon line drawings. Both small (<50k) and large (>1M) datasets will be utilized to test robustness and scalability. Baselines will include PITI, Sketch-Guided Diffusion, Taming Transformers, and variants of ControlNet with architectural ablations (e.g., without zero convolutions). Evaluation metrics will include user studies for result quality and condition fidelity, Intersection-over-Union (IoU) for segmentation reconstruction, Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for distributional similarity, and CLIP-based text-image alignment and aesthetic scores. Additional experiments will assess the ability to compose multiple conditions, interpret ambiguous inputs, and transfer pretrained ControlNets to community models.
efbe97d20c4ffe356e8826c01dc550bacc405add.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a neural architecture that enables spatially localized conditional control in large pretrained text-to-image diffusion models without altering the original model's parameters. The use of zero-initialized convolutional layers to connect a trainable copy to the locked backbone is novel, preventing harmful noise during training and preserving the pretrained model's capabilities. The approach supports robust, scalable training on both small and large datasets, allows for the composition of multiple conditioning signals, and can be directly transferred to various community diffusion models without retraining. Extensive experiments and ablation studies will demonstrate superior control, fidelity, and image quality compared to existing conditional generation baselines.

efc256781701fffc53b850fe77159e1f450023ad.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search with Boltzmann Exploration
efc256781701fffc53b850fe77159e1f450023ad.research_question: How can Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) algorithms be improved to efficiently balance exploration and exploitation, ensuring convergence to the optimal policy in planning problems, particularly in domains with sparse or dense rewards and large state spaces?
efc256781701fffc53b850fe77159e1f450023ad.hypothesis: Boltzmann-based search policies, when combined with Bellman backups or decaying entropy bonuses, will yield MCTS algorithms that are consistent, converge to the optimal reward-maximizing policy, and outperform existing methods such as UCT and MENTS across a variety of benchmark domains.
efc256781701fffc53b850fe77159e1f450023ad.proposed_method: A novel MCTS framework will be developed, introducing two algorithms: Boltzmann Tree Search (BTS) and Decaying Entropy Tree Search (DENTS). BTS will employ a Boltzmann (softmax) search policy for action selection, but will use Bellman value backups to ensure consistency with the standard reward maximization objective. DENTS will interpolate between maximum entropy and standard objectives by augmenting Bellman backups with an entropy-based exploration bonus, controlled by a decaying function β(N(s)) that decreases as nodes are visited more often. Both algorithms will leverage the Alias method for efficient stochastic action sampling, reducing computational complexity. Technical details include explicit formulations for action selection, value backups, and entropy calculations, as well as mechanisms for integrating neural network priors in complex domains such as Go.
efc256781701fffc53b850fe77159e1f450023ad.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark gridworld environments (such as FrozenLake for sparse rewards and the Sailing Problem for dense rewards) and the game of Go. Each algorithm will be evaluated using a fixed number of trials, with hyperparameters selected via search. Baselines will include UCT, MENTS, REN-TS, TENTS, and H-MCTS. Evaluation metrics will focus on the average return of the recommended policy (simple regret), convergence rate, and computational efficiency (e.g., trials per move). In Go, neural network value and policy priors will be used, and algorithms will be compared in a round-robin tournament under equal computational budgets. The Alias method will be used to measure improvements in sampling efficiency.
efc256781701fffc53b850fe77159e1f450023ad.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces consistent MCTS algorithms that use Boltzmann search policies without sacrificing convergence to the optimal reward-maximizing policy. Unlike prior maximum entropy methods, these algorithms are robust to parameter selection and avoid misalignment between entropy-augmented and standard objectives. The use of decaying entropy bonuses enables adaptive exploration, and the integration of the Alias method significantly improves sampling efficiency.
