Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior or comparable performance to state-of-the-art baselines across both sparse and dense reward domains, as well as in large-scale games like Go.

efcbc21d945651ed5248b6c51e1c065283d68c47.title: Multisample Flow Matching: Straightening Flows with Minibatch Couplings
efcbc21d945651ed5248b6c51e1c065283d68c47.research_question: How can continuous-time generative models be improved by leveraging non-trivial couplings between data and noise samples, rather than relying on independently sampled pairs, to construct more efficient and consistent probability paths for simulation-free training?
efcbc21d945651ed5248b6c51e1c065283d68c47.hypothesis: Utilizing minibatch-based optimal transport couplings to jointly sample data and noise will reduce gradient variance during training, produce straighter and more efficient flows, and yield higher quality samples with fewer function evaluations compared to independent sampling approaches.
efcbc21d945651ed5248b6c51e1c065283d68c47.proposed_method: A new framework, termed Multisample Flow Matching, will be developed to generalize simulation-free training of continuous normalizing flows by constructing joint distributions over data and noise samples that satisfy correct marginal constraints. The method will employ minibatch optimal transport (OT) solutions, such as BatchOT and BatchEOT, to define couplings within each minibatch, and use these couplings to sample pairs for training. The conditional vector field will be constructed so that each path connects the paired samples, ensuring all points arrive at the correct target at the final time. The training objective will be a joint conditional flow matching loss, which regresses the model vector field to the conditional vector field induced by the minibatch coupling. The approach will also allow for alternative couplings, such as stable matchings or heuristic approximations, to balance computational efficiency and optimality.
efcbc21d945651ed5248b6c51e1c065283d68c47.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic datasets (e.g., 2D and high-dimensional Gaussian mixtures) and high-dimensional image datasets such as ImageNet32x32 and ImageNet64x64. The proposed method will be compared against baselines including standard Flow Matching (with independent sampling), diffusion models (e.g., DDPM, ScoreSDE), and static OT-based mappings. Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for sample quality, negative log-likelihood (bits per dimension), consistency metrics for sample path stability, and the number of function evaluations (NFE) required for high-quality generation. The impact of different coupling strategies (BatchOT, BatchEOT, stable, heuristic) and batch sizes will be systematically studied, and ablation studies will assess the effect on gradient variance and flow straightness.
efcbc21d945651ed5248b6c51e1c065283d68c47.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable the use of minibatch optimal transport couplings for simulation-free training of continuous-time generative models while preserving correct marginal distributions. It introduces a tractable method to regularize towards optimal vector fields without adversarial or simulation-based training, and demonstrates improved sample efficiency, reduced gradient variance, and straighter flows. The method also provides a practical means to approximate optimal transport maps in high dimensions, even when the cost function is unknown and only batch-level couplings are available.

efde8940a0b924e93d35184c4a1e8f9670b94fe7.title: AutoML-Agent: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Full-Pipeline AutoML
efde8940a0b924e93d35184c4a1e8f9670b94fe7.research_question: How can a fully automated, end-to-end AutoML system be developed that is accessible to non-experts, minimizes human intervention, and efficiently covers the entire machine learning pipeline from data retrieval to model deployment across diverse tasks and data modalities?
efde8940a0b924e93d35184c4a1e8f9670b94fe7.hypothesis: A multi-agent framework leveraging large language models (LLMs), equipped with retrieval-augmented planning, role-specific plan decomposition, prompting-based execution, and multi-stage verification, will enable efficient, accurate, and user-friendly full-pipeline AutoML for a wide range of tasks and users, outperforming existing AutoML and LLM-based frameworks.
efde8940a0b924e93d35184c4a1e8f9670b94fe7.proposed_method: A novel multi-agent LLM framework, AutoML-Agent, is proposed for full-pipeline AutoML. The system consists of specialized LLM agents—Agent Manager, Prompt Agent, Data Agent, Model Agent, and Operation Agent—each responsible for distinct stages of the pipeline. The framework introduces a retrieval-augmented planning (RAP) strategy that generates multiple candidate plans for a user-specified task by leveraging both the LLM's internal knowledge and external resources (e.g., APIs, web search, scientific papers). Each plan is decomposed into sub-tasks tailored to the agent's expertise, enabling parallel and efficient execution via prompting without actual code execution until final selection. Multi-stage verification modules (request, execution, and implementation verification) ensure that user requirements are accurately captured, plans are feasible, and generated code is correct and deployable. The prompt parsing module standardizes user instructions into structured JSON, facilitating robust inter-agent communication and adaptive plan generation.
efde8940a0b924e93d35184c4a1e8f9670b94fe7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven downstream machine learning tasks spanning five data modalities (image, text, tabular, graph, and time series), using fourteen datasets sourced from public repositories. Both constraint-free and constraint-aware natural language task descriptions will be evaluated, with each method required to generate full-pipeline solutions from scratch. Baselines will include state-of-the-art AutoML systems (e.g., AutoGluon), LLM-based frameworks (e.g., DS-Agent, GPT-3.5, GPT-4), and manually designed pipelines by human experts. Evaluation metrics will include success rate (SR) of code generation, normalized performance score (NPS) of the resulting models, and a comprehensive score (CS) that combines both. Experiments will be run multiple times to ensure statistical reliability, and resource usage (time, monetary cost) will be tracked. Ablation studies will assess the contribution of each framework component, and robustness will be tested against noisy external knowledge and prompt variations.
efde8940a0b924e93d35184c4a1e8f9670b94fe7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first task-agnostic, multi-agent LLM framework for full-pipeline AutoML that covers the entire machine learning workflow from data retrieval to model deployment. Key innovations include retrieval-augmented planning for diverse and up-to-date plan generation, parallelizable role-specific plan decomposition, prompting-based execution for training-free search, and a multi-stage verification process to ensure accuracy and robustness. The framework is designed to be accessible to non-experts via natural language interfaces and demonstrates superior performance and efficiency compared to existing AutoML and LLM-based systems.

eff474d5ebc29644ecf016667f74424bacfa52bd.title: Adversarial Score identity Distillation: Rapidly Surpassing the Teacher in One Step
eff474d5ebc29644ecf016667f74424bacfa52bd.research_question: How can the distillation of diffusion models for image generation be improved to achieve higher sample quality and faster convergence, potentially surpassing the performance of the original teacher models, especially in single-step generation settings?
eff474d5ebc29644ecf016667f74424bacfa52bd.hypothesis: Integrating adversarial loss with score identity distillation, leveraging both real images and a shared encoder-discriminator architecture, will enable more effective alignment between generated and true data distributions, resulting in faster convergence and higher quality image generation than conventional score distillation methods or the original teacher diffusion models.
eff474d5ebc29644ecf016667f74424bacfa52bd.proposed_method: A novel framework, Adversarial Score Identity Distillation (SiDA), will be developed by augmenting score identity distillation (SiD) with an adversarial loss component. The method will utilize the encoder from the generator’s score network as a discriminator, enabling discrimination between real and generated images at various stages of the forward diffusion process. The adversarial loss will be batch-normalized per GPU and combined with the original SiD loss, incorporating the average 'fakeness' per GPU batch into the pixel-based SiD loss. This integration allows for the distillation of a single-step generator without introducing additional parameters, as the score network serves both denoising and discrimination roles. The training will alternate between updating the fake score network (for denoising and discrimination) and the generator, using both generator-synthesized data and real images, with losses constructed to balance pixel-level and latent-level objectives.
eff474d5ebc29644ecf016667f74424bacfa52bd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple datasets, including CIFAR-10 (unconditional and conditional), ImageNet 64x64, ImageNet 512x512, FFHQ 64x64, and AFHQ-v2 64x64. The method will distill pretrained EDM and EDM2 diffusion models of varying sizes, comparing against a wide range of baselines such as GANs, other diffusion models, and state-of-the-art distillation techniques (e.g., DMD, Diff-Instruct, GDD-I, sCD, sCT). Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), Precision, and Recall. Key experimental setups will involve both training from scratch and fine-tuning from pre-distilled SiD generators (SiD2A), with ablation studies on hyperparameters such as the gradient bias correction weight (alpha). Batch sizes, GPU pooling strategies, and loss weighting will be systematically explored to ensure fair and robust comparisons.
eff474d5ebc29644ecf016667f74424bacfa52bd.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a unified framework that combines score-based distillation with adversarial learning, enabling the distillation of single-step generators that rapidly surpass the teacher model's performance. The approach eliminates the need for additional discriminator parameters by reusing the score network's encoder, and incorporates a novel per-GPU batch normalization of adversarial loss to harmonize pixel-level and latent-level objectives. SiDA demonstrates an order-of-magnitude improvement in convergence speed and achieves state-of-the-art FID scores across multiple datasets and model sizes, outperforming both teacher models and existing distillation baselines. The method is the first to consistently surpass the performance of the largest teacher diffusion models in a single generation step without classifier-free guidance.

f00a2a2dbc7828b667b75b369317e4fbb20466f0.title: Fast training and sampling of Restricted Boltzmann Machines
f00a2a2dbc7828b667b75b369317e4fbb20466f0.research_question: How can the training, sampling, and evaluation of Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) be accelerated and made more reliable, especially for highly structured and clustered datasets, without sacrificing model interpretability and equilibrium properties?
f00a2a2dbc7828b667b75b369317e4fbb20466f0.hypothesis: Leveraging the stepwise encoding of data patterns into the singular vectors of the RBM coupling matrix, combined with a smooth annealing trajectory for training and a novel sampling strategy, will significantly reduce the computational cost and improve the reliability of training, sampling, and evaluation of RBMs on highly structured datasets.
f00a2a2dbc7828b667b75b369317e4fbb20466f0.proposed_method: The proposed methodology consists of three integrated components. First, a novel log-likelihood estimation method will be developed by exploiting the smoothness of the RBM training trajectory, enabling efficient online computation and offline reconstruction using trajectory annealing or parallel tempering. Second, a new sampling algorithm, Parallel Trajectory Tempering (PTT), will be introduced, where model parameters from different training stages are exchanged instead of temperatures, facilitating rapid mixing and improved sampling efficiency in multimodal distributions. Third, a pre-training phase will be implemented using a low-rank RBM framework, where the principal components of the data are encoded via convex optimization, initializing the model in a way that mitigates critical slowdown and enables efficient static Monte Carlo sampling. This pre-training is further refined by incorporating a trainable bias term, essential for image data, and by tuning the sampling process for equilibrium estimation.
f00a2a2dbc7828b667b75b369317e4fbb20466f0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of datasets with varying degrees of structure and clustering, including MNIST01 (digits 0 and 1), a synthetic 'Mickey' dataset, a Human Genome Dataset (HGD), equilibrium configurations from the 2D Ising model, and the CelebA image dataset (resized to 32x32 pixels, grayscale). The proposed methods will be compared against standard baselines such as Alternating Gibbs Sampling (AGS), Parallel Tempering (PT), Stacked Tempering, and Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS) for both training and sampling tasks. Evaluation metrics will include log-likelihood estimation accuracy (with exact partition function computation for small models), sample quality (via PCA projections and moment matching), mixing time (measured by mode-jumping statistics), and computational efficiency. Both online and offline estimation scenarios will be explored, and the impact of pre-training versus standard persistent contrastive divergence (PCD) will be systematically assessed.
f00a2a2dbc7828b667b75b369317e4fbb20466f0.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a trajectory-based annealing paradigm for both log-likelihood estimation and sampling, which circumvents the limitations of temperature-based methods in highly clustered datasets. The Parallel Trajectory Tempering (PTT) algorithm is a novel sampling strategy that leverages the training trajectory for efficient mixing and outperforms existing MCMC-based methods. The pre-training approach using a low-rank RBM with convex optimization and a trainable bias is an innovative initialization strategy that mitigates critical slowdown and improves model quality on structured datasets. Together, these contributions enable fast, reliable, and interpretable equilibrium RBM training and evaluation, particularly in challenging multimodal data regimes.

f02d9889bab24f0da4446db0288fe7dfcde1b630.title: How Transformers Learn Causal Structure with Gradient Descent
f02d9889bab24f0da4446db0288fe7dfcde1b630.research_question: How do transformer architectures learn and represent latent causal structures in sequential data when trained via gradient descent, particularly in the context of in-context learning tasks?
f02d9889bab24f0da4446db0288fe7dfcde1b630.hypothesis: Gradient descent training on appropriately designed in-context learning tasks enables transformer models to encode the underlying latent causal graph within their attention layers, with the attention matrix gradients reflecting mutual information between tokens and converging to the adjacency matrix of the true causal structure.
f02d9889bab24f0da4446db0288fe7dfcde1b630.proposed_method: A novel family of in-context learning tasks, termed 'random sequences with causal structure,' will be introduced, where each sequence is generated according to a latent, unknown causal graph. The experimental focus will be on training simplified two-layer, attention-only (disentangled) transformers using gradient descent on these tasks. The architecture will be designed such that the first attention layer is capable of encoding the adjacency matrix of the latent causal graph, while the second attention layer aggregates information according to the learned structure. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to prove that the gradient of the attention matrix in the first layer encodes the mutual information between tokens, and that, due to the data processing inequality, the largest entries of this gradient correspond to edges in the latent causal graph. Special cases, such as Markov chains and in-context function learning, will be analyzed to demonstrate the generality of the approach.
f02d9889bab24f0da4446db0288fe7dfcde1b630.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training two-layer disentangled transformers with one head per layer on the proposed in-context learning tasks, with varying latent causal graphs (including trees and more general DAGs). Sequences will be generated using Markov chains with transition matrices sampled from Dirichlet distributions, and the models will be trained using cross-entropy loss with cosine learning rate decay. Evaluation will focus on the ability of the trained models to recover the underlying causal structure, assessed by comparing the learned attention weights to the true adjacency matrix and by measuring prediction accuracy on held-out sequences. Baselines will include random and untrained models, and metrics will include adjacency matrix recovery accuracy and population loss.
f02d9889bab24f0da4446db0288fe7dfcde1b630.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a principled theoretical and empirical framework for understanding how transformers learn latent causal structure through gradient descent, going beyond prior work that focused on representational capacity rather than learning dynamics. The approach provides end-to-end guarantees for learning a wide variety of causal graphs, including trees and more complex structures, and establishes a direct link between attention gradients and mutual information. The method generalizes the induction head mechanism to arbitrary causal graphs and demonstrates that transformers can recover these structures without requiring large alphabet sizes or restrictive assumptions.

f02d9cd70f3e6d53796a47c0b4efefd0a81f826f.title: Demystifying Softmax Gating Function in Gaussian Mixture of Experts
f02d9cd70f3e6d53796a47c0b4efefd0a81f826f.research_question: What are the fundamental statistical properties and convergence rates of parameter estimation in softmax gating Gaussian mixture of experts models, especially under both exact-fitted and over-fitted settings, and how can these be theoretically characterized?
f02d9cd70f3e6d53796a47c0b4efefd0a81f826f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that novel loss functions based on Voronoi metrics can resolve the challenges of identifiability, parameter interaction, and complex dependencies in softmax gating Gaussian mixture of experts, enabling the establishment of precise convergence rates for maximum likelihood estimation under both exact-fitted and over-fitted regimes.
f02d9cd70f3e6d53796a47c0b4efefd0a81f826f.proposed_method: A new theoretical framework will be developed for analyzing parameter estimation in softmax gating Gaussian mixture of experts (GME) models. This framework will introduce two novel Voronoi-based loss functions to address the unique identifiability and interaction challenges posed by the softmax gating function. The approach will involve deriving lower bounds on the Hellinger distance between mixing densities in terms of these Voronoi metrics, which are designed to capture the translation invariance and parameter dependencies inherent in the model. The methodology will utilize Taylor expansions and partial differential equations to decompose the density discrepancies, and will relate convergence rates to the solvability of specific systems of polynomial equations, particularly in over-fitted settings. Theoretical analysis will be conducted for both exact-fitted (where the number of experts is known) and over-fitted (where the number is over-specified) scenarios.
f02d9cd70f3e6d53796a47c0b4efefd0a81f826f.experiment_details: Experiments will consist of simulation studies using synthetic datasets generated from softmax gating Gaussian mixture of experts models with varying numbers of components and covariate dimensions. Maximum likelihood estimation will be performed under both exact-fitted and over-fitted settings, and the proposed Voronoi loss functions will be used to evaluate convergence rates. Baseline comparisons will include standard loss functions such as Wasserstein distance and existing methods for mixture of experts with covariate-free gating. Evaluation metrics will focus on the Hellinger distance between estimated and true conditional densities, as well as the rates of parameter estimation for gating and expert parameters. The experimental setup will also investigate the computational efficiency of the proposed loss functions and the impact of over-specification on estimation rates.
f02d9cd70f3e6d53796a47c0b4efefd0a81f826f.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first comprehensive theoretical analysis of parameter estimation rates in softmax gating Gaussian mixture of experts, resolving longstanding open problems related to identifiability and parameter interaction. The work develops two novel Voronoi-based loss functions that account for translation invariance and complex parameter dependencies, and establishes convergence rates for maximum likelihood estimation in both exact-fitted and over-fitted regimes. The analysis reveals a new connection between estimation rates and the solvability of systems of polynomial equations, providing a richer understanding of over-fitted mixture models. Additionally, the proposed loss functions are computationally efficient and offer practical guidance for model selection and post-processing in mixture of experts frameworks.

f02ea7a18f00859d9ea1b321e3385ae7d0170639.title: VideoComposer: Compositional Video Synthesis with Motion Controllability
f02ea7a18f00859d9ea1b321e3385ae7d0170639.research_question: How can controllability in video synthesis be improved to allow flexible composition of videos with diverse spatial, textual, and temporal conditions, while maintaining high temporal consistency and motion controllability?
f02ea7a18f00859d9ea1b321e3385ae7d0170639.hypothesis: Incorporating explicit temporal control signals such as motion vectors, along with a unified spatio-temporal condition encoder, will enable more precise and flexible control over both spatial and temporal aspects of video synthesis, resulting in higher inter-frame consistency and improved motion controllability compared to existing methods.
f02ea7a18f00859d9ea1b321e3385ae7d0170639.proposed_method: A novel compositional video synthesis framework will be developed that decomposes video generation into three representative factors: textual conditions, spatial conditions, and temporal conditions. The method will introduce motion vectors extracted from compressed video as explicit temporal control signals, enabling direct guidance of temporal dynamics. A Spatio-Temporal Condition encoder (STC-encoder) will be designed to jointly model spatial and temporal dependencies of sequential input conditions using a combination of lightweight 2D convolutions, average pooling, and a temporal Transformer layer. The system will operate within a latent diffusion model architecture, where all condition embeddings are fused and used to guide the denoising process. Cross-attention mechanisms will be used to inject textual and stylistic guidance, and a two-stage training strategy will be adopted: first specializing in temporal modeling via text-to-video generation, then optimizing for compositional video synthesis with diverse conditions.
f02ea7a18f00859d9ea1b321e3385ae7d0170639.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large-scale datasets such as WebVid10M (video-caption pairs) and LAION-400M (image-caption pairs). The evaluation will include both qualitative and quantitative analysis, with metrics such as average CLIP cosine similarity between consecutive frames (for frame consistency) and end-point-error (for motion controllability, measuring the Euclidean distance between predicted and ground truth optical flow). Baselines will include ablations without the STC-encoder and without motion vector conditions, as well as comparisons to existing video synthesis models like CogVideo. The experimental setup will also involve compositional tasks such as image-to-video generation, video inpainting, sketch-to-video generation, and video-to-video translation, with various combinations of spatial and temporal conditions.
f02ea7a18f00859d9ea1b321e3385ae7d0170639.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the use of motion vectors from compressed video as explicit and efficient temporal control signals for video synthesis, which is seldom explored in prior work. The unified STC-encoder enables effective aggregation of spatial and temporal dependencies across diverse input conditions, facilitating higher inter-frame consistency. The compositional framework allows flexible integration of multiple condition types (text, image, sketch, depth, mask, motion) within a single model, supporting highly customizable and controllable video generation. The method demonstrates superior motion controllability and temporal consistency compared to existing baselines, and enables novel applications such as fine-grained motion control using hand-crafted strokes.

f03074286282431a5afa1927cc79792d51980cb7.title: ParetoFlow: Guided Flows in Multi-Objective Optimization
f03074286282431a5afa1927cc79792d51980cb7.research_question: How can generative modeling be leveraged to improve offline multi-objective optimization, enabling the effective approximation of the Pareto front across diverse and potentially non-convex objective spaces?
f03074286282431a5afa1927cc79792d51980cb7.hypothesis: A guided flow matching framework, incorporating multi-objective predictor guidance with uniform weight vectors and a neighboring evolution module, will enable more effective and diverse sampling of Pareto-optimal solutions in offline multi-objective optimization compared to existing evolutionary, Bayesian, and generative modeling approaches.
f03074286282431a5afa1927cc79792d51980cb7.proposed_method: A new framework, ParetoFlow, is proposed for offline multi-objective optimization by integrating advanced flow matching generative modeling with evolutionary algorithm-inspired guidance. The method begins by training objective predictors for each objective in a supervised manner on the offline dataset, followed by training a neural vector field using the flow matching loss to enable conditional sample generation. Uniform weight vectors are generated using the Das-Dennis method to ensure comprehensive coverage of the objective space; each sample is associated with a weight vector representing a weighted distribution over objectives. A multi-objective predictor guidance module directs the flow sampling process towards the Pareto front by incorporating these weight vectors into the conditional vector field, while a local filtering scheme confines sampling to hypercones aligned with the weight vectors, addressing non-convex Pareto fronts. Additionally, a neighboring evolution module is introduced, where offspring samples are generated from both a distribution and its K nearest neighbors in weight space, and the most promising offspring is selected for the next iteration, promoting knowledge sharing and diversity.
f03074286282431a5afa1927cc79792d51980cb7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on Off-MOO-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark suite encompassing synthetic functions, multi-objective neural architecture search (MO-NAS), multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL), scientific design (including molecular and protein design), and real-world engineering applications. Each task provides an offline dataset and a ground-truth oracle for evaluation. The proposed method will be compared against DNN-based surrogate models with evolutionary algorithms, GP-based Bayesian optimization methods, and state-of-the-art generative modeling baselines such as diffusion models, VAEs, and GFlowNets. Evaluation will follow the protocol of generating 256 candidate solutions per task, with performance measured using the hypervolume metric at both 100th and 50th percentiles after non-dominated sorting. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the multi-objective predictor guidance, local filtering, neighboring evolution, and Pareto set update modules. Key hyperparameters such as the number of neighbors and offspring will be systematically varied to assess sensitivity.
f03074286282431a5afa1927cc79792d51980cb7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to combine flow matching generative modeling with evolutionary algorithm-inspired multi-objective guidance for offline optimization. Novel contributions include the multi-objective predictor guidance module with uniform weight vectors for comprehensive Pareto front coverage, a local filtering scheme for handling non-convex fronts, and a neighboring evolution module for knowledge sharing among similar distributions. The method enables effective and diverse sampling of Pareto-optimal solutions, outperforming existing evolutionary, Bayesian, and generative modeling baselines across a wide range of tasks.

f0476cea3628818f7275ccb47e6ab7e92d9e83c3.title: CDFlow: Building Invertible Layers with Circulant and Diagonal Matrices
f0476cea3628818f7275ccb47e6ab7e92d9e83c3.research_question: How can invertible linear layers be designed for normalizing flow models to enhance expressiveness, reduce parameter and computational complexity, and enable efficient computation of Jacobian determinants and matrix inverses, particularly for high-dimensional data and data with periodic structures?
f0476cea3628818f7275ccb47e6ab7e92d9e83c3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that constructing invertible linear layers as products of circulant and diagonal matrices will significantly reduce parameter and computational complexity, while maintaining or improving the expressive power and efficiency of normalizing flow models for density estimation and generative modeling.
f0476cea3628818f7275ccb47e6ab7e92d9e83c3.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves designing invertible linear layers by decomposing the weight matrix into a sequence of alternating circulant and diagonal matrices. Each linear transformation is parameterized by m diagonal matrices and m-1 circulant matrices, where m is a tunable hyperparameter. The circulant matrices are implemented in the frequency domain using the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), enabling efficient computation of matrix-vector products, matrix inversion, and log-determinant calculations. The invertible linear layer is integrated into a normalizing flow model, termed Circulant-Diagonal Flow (CDFlow), which is structured as a multi-scale architecture with flow modules consisting of ActNorm, the proposed CD-Convolution layer, and coupling layers. The model is trained end-to-end for density estimation and generative tasks.
f0476cea3628818f7275ccb47e6ab7e92d9e83c3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image datasets such as CIFAR-10 and ImageNet 32x32, as well as on structured datasets exhibiting periodicity, such as the Galaxy dataset. The primary evaluation metric will be bits per dimension (BPD), a standard measure for generative modeling. Baseline comparisons will include models such as MAF, RealNVP, Glow, Emerging, i-ResNet, Woodbury, i-DenseNet, and ButterflyFlow, all configured with consistent backbone and multi-scale settings for fair comparison. Additional experiments will analyze runtime performance for forward, inverse, and log-determinant computations across varying channel and spatial dimensions, with all methods implemented in PyTorch and evaluated on high-performance GPUs. Hyperparameter ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of the number of circulant and diagonal matrices (m) on expressiveness, parameter count, and computational efficiency.
f0476cea3628818f7275ccb47e6ab7e92d9e83c3.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel invertible linear layer for flow-based generative models, constructed from products of circulant and diagonal matrices, resulting in linear storage complexity with respect to input dimension. The method leverages FFT to achieve efficient O(mn) log-determinant and O(mn log n) inversion computations, significantly reducing computational overhead compared to dense and other structured matrix approaches. The approach enables accurate approximation of arbitrary linear transformations with fewer parameters and faster runtime, and demonstrates superior performance in modeling both standard and periodic data distributions. The integration of these layers into a multi-scale normalizing flow framework represents a new direction for parameter- and computation-efficient deep generative modeling.

f05e84702562cb693dd68d3d1c88072519a7bd71.title: ∞Bench: Extending Long Context Evaluation Beyond 100K Tokens
f05e84702562cb693dd68d3d1c88072519a7bd71.research_question: How can the evaluation of large language models (LLMs) be extended to accurately assess their ability to process and reason over extremely long contexts, specifically those surpassing 100,000 tokens, across diverse domains and languages?
f05e84702562cb693dd68d3d1c88072519a7bd71.hypothesis: Current long-context LLMs, despite recent advances, are not yet capable of effectively processing and reasoning over contexts exceeding 100,000 tokens, and a comprehensive, multi-domain benchmark will reveal significant performance degradation and highlight areas for improvement.
f05e84702562cb693dd68d3d1c88072519a7bd71.proposed_method: A new benchmark, ∞BENCH, will be constructed to evaluate LLMs on their ability to process and reason over contexts averaging more than 100,000 tokens. The benchmark will include both synthetic and realistic tasks spanning multiple domains such as novels, code, math, and dialogue, and will be presented in both English and Chinese. Human-annotated and auto-generated tasks will be developed, with annotation pipelines ensuring high-quality examples that require long-range dependency reasoning. The benchmark will incorporate tasks that test retrieval, aggregation, filtering, state preservation, and sequential processing abilities, including challenging formats such as key-value retrieval in large JSON objects, multi-step code execution, and complex arithmetic over long sequences.
f05e84702562cb693dd68d3d1c88072519a7bd71.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by evaluating state-of-the-art proprietary and open-source LLMs (including GPT-4, Claude 2, Kimi-Chat, and YaRN-Mistral) on ∞BENCH. Tasks will cover 12 types across 5 domains, with approximately 4,000 examples and input lengths averaging around 200,000 tokens. Evaluation metrics will include ROUGE-L-Sum for summarization, exact match for retrieval and QA, and task-specific metrics for code and math. Baseline models will be compared on their ability to handle long contexts, with input truncation strategies applied as needed for models with context length limitations. Additional analyses will be performed, such as length ablation studies, answer position sensitivity, and the impact of prompting strategies (e.g., context recalling) on model performance.
f05e84702562cb693dd68d3d1c88072519a7bd71.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark is the first to feature average context lengths surpassing 100,000 tokens, covering a broader range of domains and languages than existing long-context benchmarks. It enables systematic evaluation of LLMs' long-context reasoning and processing abilities, reveals significant performance gaps in current models, and introduces new task formats and annotation pipelines for both realistic and synthetic scenarios. The benchmark also facilitates novel analyses of model behavior in extreme context settings, such as the absence of the 'lost in the middle' phenomenon and the effectiveness of context recalling prompting techniques.

f0676c081f12c9395cd0e920d137a90a9ceb2c4a.title: Privacy-Preserving In-Context Learning with Differentially Private Few-Shot Generation
f0676c081f12c9395cd0e920d137a90a9ceb2c4a.research_question: Can in-context learning (ICL) with large language models (LLMs) be performed effectively on private datasets while providing rigorous privacy guarantees for the prompt data, specifically using differential privacy (DP)?
f0676c081f12c9395cd0e920d137a90a9ceb2c4a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that synthetic few-shot demonstrations generated from private datasets under formal differential privacy guarantees can enable effective in-context learning with large language models, achieving competitive performance to non-private ICL while protecting the privacy of the underlying data.
f0676c081f12c9395cd0e920d137a90a9ceb2c4a.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed for privacy-preserving in-context learning that operates in two main steps. First, a differentially private (DP) algorithm generates synthetic few-shot examples from the private dataset. This is achieved by partitioning the dataset into disjoint subsets, constructing prompts with task-specific instructions and subset samples, and using a pre-trained LLM to generate next-token probabilities for each subset. These probabilities are then privately aggregated using either the Gaussian mechanism or the Report-Noisy-Max with Exponential mechanism, ensuring DP at each generation step. The vocabulary for generation can be restricted to the top-K tokens determined by public instructions to reduce noise. The synthetic few-shot demonstrations are then used as ICL prompts for downstream inference, leveraging the post-processing property of DP to allow an unbounded number of queries without incurring additional privacy loss.
f0676c081f12c9395cd0e920d137a90a9ceb2c4a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard NLP benchmarks, including AGNews (4-way news classification), TREC (6-way question classification), DBPedia (14-way topic classification), and MITMovies trivia10k13 (slot-filling for genre and director). The main LLM used is GPT-3 Babbage, with additional studies on Ada, Curie, and Davinci models. Baselines include non-private ICL (randomly selected real few-shot samples), zero-shot learning, and synthetic demonstrations generated without private data. Evaluation metrics are primarily classification accuracy, measured over multiple runs with different random seeds. The privacy parameter epsilon is varied (e.g., 1, 2, 4, 8) to assess the privacy-utility tradeoff, and ablation studies are performed on the number of shots, model size, and DP mechanism. Empirical privacy is further evaluated via membership inference attacks.
f0676c081f12c9395cd0e920d137a90a9ceb2c4a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new algorithm for generating synthetic few-shot demonstrations from private data with formal differential privacy guarantees, enabling effective in-context learning without any model fine-tuning. Unlike prior methods, the framework allows an unbounded number of ICL queries without additional privacy cost and does not require access to public data. The method extends beyond text classification to information extraction tasks, and demonstrates that privacy-preserving ICL can achieve competitive performance with non-private baselines. Additionally, the work highlights that for some tasks, LLMs can generate effective demonstrations without private data, suggesting privacy may be achievable at no cost in certain scenarios.

f08050068df877864ee10f62043e5ff2e27f8939.title: Neural Guided Diffusion Bridges
f08050068df877864ee10f62043e5ff2e27f8939.research_question: How can conditioned diffusion processes (diffusion bridges) in Euclidean spaces be efficiently simulated, particularly in scenarios involving rare events and multimodal distributions, without relying on computationally intensive MCMC methods or score modeling?
f08050068df877864ee10f62043e5ff2e27f8939.hypothesis: A variational approach that augments guided diffusion proposals with a neural network-based correction drift can approximate the true diffusion bridge path measure more efficiently and robustly than existing MCMC- or score-matching-based methods, especially in challenging conditioning scenarios.
f08050068df877864ee10f62043e5ff2e27f8939.proposed_method: A new simulation framework for diffusion bridges is developed by combining the guided proposal method with a learnable correction drift term parameterized by a neural network. The neural network is trained to minimize the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the law of the neural-guided process and the true conditioned process, using a variational loss derived from Girsanov's theorem. The method leverages the reparameterization trick to enable gradient-based optimization, allowing backpropagation through the SDE solver for efficient training. Once trained, the neural network enables fast and independent sampling of diffusion bridges at a computational cost comparable to simulating the unconditioned process. The approach is designed to learn directly from conditional samples, improving efficiency and accuracy in rare event and multimodal settings.
f08050068df877864ee10f62043e5ff2e27f8939.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of diffusion processes, including analytically tractable linear cases (Brownian motion and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes) and more complex nonlinear systems such as a cell differentiation model and the FitzHugh-Nagumo model. For linear processes, the method's accuracy will be benchmarked against known analytical solutions and lower bounds for the variational loss. For nonlinear and high-dimensional cases, qualitative and quantitative analyses will be performed, including scenarios with rare event conditioning and multimodal distributions. Baselines will include the guided proposal method, score-matching-based bridge simulation, and adjoint process-based methods. Evaluation metrics will include KL divergence to ground truth (when available), empirical marginal distributions, and qualitative trajectory comparisons. Experimental setups will involve both fully and partially observed conditioning, and computational efficiency will be assessed by comparing sampling costs and convergence behavior.
f08050068df877864ee10f62043e5ff2e27f8939.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a flexible variational family for diffusion bridge simulation that eliminates the need for score modeling or intensive MCMC/SMC sampling. It enables efficient, independent sampling after training and is robust to rare event conditioning and multimodal distributions. Unlike score-matching approaches, it learns directly from conditional samples, leading to greater training efficiency and improved accuracy in challenging scenarios. The approach is broadly applicable across a range of diffusion specifications and conditioning types, and demonstrates superior adaptability and computational efficiency compared to existing methods.

f0a69aea334b0ad41bf85ddb9d200a48d3c88842.title: BEER: Fast O(1/T) Rate for Decentralized Nonconvex Optimization with Communication Compression
f0a69aea334b0ad41bf85ddb9d200a48d3c88842.research_question: How can decentralized nonconvex optimization in multi-agent or federated learning environments be made more communication-efficient, particularly under high data heterogeneity and without strong bounded gradient or dissimilarity assumptions?
f0a69aea334b0ad41bf85ddb9d200a48d3c88842.hypothesis: A decentralized optimization algorithm that integrates communication compression with gradient tracking can achieve fast convergence rates, matching the best-known rates for uncompressed methods, even under arbitrary data heterogeneity and without requiring strong bounded gradient or bounded dissimilarity assumptions.
f0a69aea334b0ad41bf85ddb9d200a48d3c88842.proposed_method: A new decentralized optimization algorithm, BEER, is developed that combines communication compression with gradient tracking to address nonconvex optimization problems in multi-agent networks. Each client maintains local model and gradient estimates, as well as compressed surrogates of these quantities, which are updated by aggregating compressed messages from neighbors over a predefined network topology. The algorithm leverages a general class of biased compression operators and uses a mixing matrix to ensure consensus among clients. Gradient tracking is employed to accurately estimate global gradients and to implicitly handle compression errors, eliminating the need for explicit error feedback mechanisms. The method is designed to operate efficiently under arbitrary data heterogeneity and supports both full and stochastic gradient oracles.
f0a69aea334b0ad41bf85ddb9d200a48d3c88842.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on real-world datasets, including logistic regression with a nonconvex regularizer on the a9a dataset and training a one-hidden-layer neural network on the MNIST dataset. Data will be distributed in a highly heterogeneous manner across 10 clients connected in a ring topology, simulating non-i.i.d. data distributions. The performance of the proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as CHOCO-SGD (with compression), DSGD, and D2 (without compression), using metrics such as training gradient norm, testing accuracy, communication rounds, and total communication bits. The same initializations, learning rates, batch sizes, and compression operators will be used across all methods to ensure fair comparison.
f0a69aea334b0ad41bf85ddb9d200a48d3c88842.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to achieve an O(1/T) convergence rate for decentralized nonconvex optimization with communication compression, matching the rate of uncompressed algorithms even under arbitrary data heterogeneity. It removes the need for strong bounded gradient or bounded dissimilarity assumptions required by prior works. The method also supports linear convergence under the Polyak-Łojasiewicz condition and demonstrates superior empirical performance in highly heterogeneous data settings. The integration of gradient tracking with communication compression in a decentralized, nonconvex setting constitutes a significant innovation over existing methods.

f0c31511134abdd23f990310e8a2f2eb3a629b62.title: SpecInfer: Accelerating Large Language Model Serving with Tree-based Speculative Inference and Verification
f0c31511134abdd23f990310e8a2f2eb3a629b62.research_question: How can the end-to-end latency and computational efficiency of large language model (LLM) serving be improved without sacrificing generative performance, particularly for distributed and offloading-based inference scenarios?
f0c31511134abdd23f990310e8a2f2eb3a629b62.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging tree-based speculative inference and verification, which utilizes small speculative models (SSMs) to generate diverse candidate token sequences organized as a token tree and verifies them in parallel against the LLM, can significantly accelerate LLM serving while maintaining output quality.
f0c31511134abdd23f990310e8a2f2eb3a629b62.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a tree-based speculative inference and verification framework for LLM serving. Small speculative models (SSMs), which are distilled, quantized, or pruned variants of the target LLM, are used to generate a diverse set of candidate token sequences organized as a token tree. Two strategies are employed for token tree construction: expansion-based (using top-k outputs from SSMs at each step) and merge-based (aggregating outputs from multiple SSMs via adaptive boosting). The correctness of all candidate sequences in the token tree is verified in parallel using a novel tree-based parallel decoding mechanism, which generalizes the attention mechanism to tree structures and employs topology-aware causal masking to efficiently manage key-value caches. A multi-step speculative sampling algorithm is developed to ensure that the generative distribution matches that of standard incremental decoding, supporting both greedy and stochastic decoding modes.
f0c31511134abdd23f990310e8a2f2eb3a629b62.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using state-of-the-art LLMs such as LLaMA-7B and OPT-175B, with SSMs selected from smaller variants pre-trained on the same datasets. Evaluation will be performed on both distributed multi-GPU clusters and offloading-based single-GPU setups. Datasets will include a range of prompt datasets such as Alpaca, CP, WebQA, CIP, and PIQA to assess generality. Baselines will include existing incremental decoding and sequence-based speculative inference methods. Evaluation metrics will comprise end-to-end inference latency, throughput, memory overhead, and generative accuracy (measured by token-level alignment and output quality). The experimental setup will also analyze the impact of different token tree configurations and SSM ensemble strategies.
f0c31511134abdd23f990310e8a2f2eb3a629b62.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel tree-based speculative inference and verification system for LLM serving, which enables simultaneous consideration and verification of multiple candidate token sequences, rather than a single sequence as in prior speculative inference methods. Key innovations include the use of token trees to organize speculation, a tree-based parallel decoding mechanism that efficiently verifies all candidates in a single LLM pass, and a multi-step speculative sampling algorithm that provably preserves generative performance. The method claims substantial improvements in inference speed (1.5-3.5x over baselines) with negligible impact on output quality, and demonstrates scalability to both distributed and offloading-based inference scenarios.

f0ef0711262bf818d49c744f74a9ba3306313956.title: Efficient training of energy-based models using Jarzynski equality
f0ef0711262bf818d49c744f74a9ba3306313956.research_question: How can the training of energy-based models (EBMs) be made more efficient and accurate, particularly in learning the relative weights of modes in complex, high-dimensional, and multimodal data distributions, while minimizing biases and instabilities associated with existing training algorithms?
f0ef0711262bf818d49c744f74a9ba3306313956.hypothesis: Incorporating the Jarzynski equality from nonequilibrium thermodynamics into a sequential Monte Carlo framework, combined with weighted walkers and a modified unadjusted Langevin algorithm (ULA), will enable unbiased and efficient estimation of the cross-entropy gradient for EBM training, thereby overcoming the limitations of contrastive divergence-based methods and improving the recovery of mode weights in multimodal distributions.
f0ef0711262bf818d49c744f74a9ba3306313956.proposed_method: A novel training algorithm for energy-based models is proposed that leverages the Jarzynski equality to derive exact expressions for the cross-entropy and its gradient with respect to model parameters. The method utilizes a sequential Monte Carlo approach, where an ensemble of walkers is evolved using a modified unadjusted Langevin algorithm (ULA). Each walker is assigned a weight that evolves according to the Jarzynski correction, allowing for unbiased estimation of expectations over the model distribution at each optimization step. The algorithm includes a resampling procedure based on the effective sample size (ESS) to maintain diversity among walkers and prevent sample degeneracy. The approach supports mini-batch training and is compatible with standard optimizers such as Adam, and can be implemented with deep neural network energy functions.
f0ef0711262bf818d49c744f74a9ba3306313956.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic Gaussian mixture models, as well as real-world datasets including MNIST and CIFAR-10. For the Gaussian mixture experiments, the model will be initialized with parameters close to the true distribution, and the ability to recover both the locations and relative weights of modes will be evaluated, comparing against persistent contrastive divergence (PCD) and contrastive divergence (CD) baselines. On MNIST, experiments will focus on subsets with intentionally imbalanced class proportions to test the recovery of mode weights, using a convolutional neural network as the energy function and evaluating generated samples with a pre-trained classifier. For CIFAR-10, the method will be compared to PCD and PCD with data augmentation, using metrics such as Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS), with identical neural architectures and hyperparameters across methods. All experiments will monitor cross-entropy estimates, effective sample size, and qualitative sample quality.
f0ef0711262bf818d49c744f74a9ba3306313956.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a theoretically principled and practical method for unbiased cross-entropy minimization in EBM training by integrating the Jarzynski equality with sequential Monte Carlo sampling and weighted walkers. Unlike contrastive divergence and its variants, this method provides exact gradient estimates (up to sampling error), corrects for sampling biases due to slow mixing and discretization, and enables accurate recovery of mode weights in multimodal distributions. The method is computationally efficient, requires minimal additional cost compared to standard ULA-based training, and is the first to directly perform gradient descent on the cross-entropy objective for EBMs with provable bias correction. The approach also offers a mechanism for assessing sample quality and supports scalable training on complex, high-dimensional datasets.

f0f4801449505330ffdffb7b5f3813a1a11add31.title: CLIPLoss and Norm-Based Data Selection Methods for Multimodal Contrastive Learning
f0f4801449505330ffdffb7b5f3813a1a11add31.research_question: How can data selection strategies for large-scale multimodal contrastive learning models be improved to more effectively filter high-quality and task-relevant image-text pairs from noisy web-curated datasets, without relying on external models or retraining new embedding models?
f0f4801449505330ffdffb7b5f3813a1a11add31.hypothesis: Incorporating a surrogate CLIP training loss as a data quality metric and introducing a norm-based similarity metric between pretraining and target data will yield more accurate and effective data selection for multimodal contrastive learning, resulting in improved downstream performance compared to classical CLIPScore-based methods.
f0f4801449505330ffdffb7b5f3813a1a11add31.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces two novel data selection metrics for multimodal contrastive learning. First, a surrogate-CLIPLoss (s-CLIPLoss) is developed, inspired by the original CLIP training loss, which augments the traditional CLIPScore by adding a normalization term that accounts for the alignment between a sample and its contrastive pairs within a batch. This adjustment corrects for biases where generic or uninformative samples may receive artificially high CLIPScores. Second, a norm-based similarity metric (NormSim) is introduced, which measures the similarity between the vision embedding of a training sample and a set of target data (representing downstream tasks) using a p-norm (typically p=2 or p=∞) over the dot products between embeddings. NormSim can be computed using only visual embeddings, leveraging the stronger representation power of the image encoder. Both metrics are designed to be universally applicable to any CLIP-style embedding model and can be combined for joint filtering.
f0f4801449505330ffdffb7b5f3813a1a11add31.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the DataComp-medium benchmark, which consists of approximately 128 million web-curated image-text pairs. The filtered subsets will be used to train a fixed CLIP-B/32 model under a standardized training budget, ensuring fair comparison by repeating smaller subsets as needed. Evaluation will be performed on 38 downstream tasks, including ImageNet-1k, ImageNet distribution shifts, VTAB, WILDS, and several retrieval datasets (e.g., Flickr30k, MSCOCO, WinoGAViL). Baselines will include classical CLIPScore filtering, image-based filtering, D2Pruning, and state-of-the-art methods that utilize external models or retrained CLIP-style embeddings (e.g., DFN, HYPE, T-MARS, Devils, MLM). Performance will be measured by zero-shot accuracy and average performance across all downstream tasks. Ablation studies will explore the impact of different norm choices, teacher models (ViT-L/14, ViT-B/32, DFN-P), and the use of proxy target sets when downstream data is unavailable.
f0f4801449505330ffdffb7b5f3813a1a11add31.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a statistically interpretable surrogate-CLIPLoss metric that directly replaces CLIPScore for data quality assessment, requiring negligible additional computation and no external data. It also presents NormSim, a universal, vision-only similarity metric for aligning pretraining data with downstream tasks, which can be computed with any good image encoder. The combination of s-CLIPLoss and NormSim is claimed to outperform existing CLIPScore-based and external-resource-based filtering approaches, achieving state-of-the-art results on the DataComp-medium benchmark. Furthermore, these methods are compatible with and complementary to existing advanced data filtering techniques, enabling further performance improvements when integrated. The approach is efficient, model-agnostic, and does not require retraining or access to proprietary datasets.

f1173df25d83e5c6ff16e087f890993bccf355ed.title: Policy-labeled Preference Learning: Is Preference Enough for RLHF?
f1173df25d83e5c6ff16e087f890993bccf355ed.research_question: Can reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) be improved by explicitly incorporating information about the behavior policy that generated preference data, rather than relying solely on preference comparisons between trajectory pairs? Is preference data alone sufficient for effective policy learning in RLHF, especially in offline and heterogeneous settings?
f1173df25d83e5c6ff16e087f890993bccf355ed.hypothesis: Explicitly modeling human preferences with regret that incorporates behavior policy information, along with contrastive KL regularization, will resolve likelihood mismatch issues in RLHF and lead to more accurate policy learning and improved performance, particularly in offline and heterogeneous datasets.
f1173df25d83e5c6ff16e087f890993bccf355ed.proposed_method: A novel RLHF framework called Policy-labeled Preference Learning (PPL) will be developed, which models human preferences using regret—a metric that quantifies the difference between the expected return under the optimal policy and the achieved return under the behavior policy. Each trajectory segment in the dataset will be explicitly labeled with its generating policy (behavior policy). The method will use a regret-based score function to disentangle the effects of environmental stochasticity from policy suboptimality, addressing the likelihood mismatch that arises when all data is assumed to be generated by the optimal policy. Additionally, a contrastive KL regularization term will be introduced, aligning the learned policy with preferred segments while explicitly contrasting it against less preferred ones. Theoretical analysis will establish a bijective mapping between reward functions and optimal policies, and show that minimizing regret is equivalent to minimizing the sequential forward KL divergence between the learned and behavior policies.
f1173df25d83e5c6ff16e087f890993bccf355ed.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six high-dimensional continuous control tasks from the MetaWorld benchmark, using both homogeneous (single policy) and heterogeneous (multiple diverse policies) offline datasets. Preference labels will be generated using a pre-trained oracle critic, and both dense and sparse preference query settings will be evaluated. Baselines for comparison will include Contrastive Preference Learning (CPL), supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and Preference-based Implicit Q-Learning (P-IQL). Performance will be measured by success rates over multiple seeds and evaluation windows. Additional ablations will test the impact of policy labeling versus deterministic pseudo-labeling, and online RLHF experiments will be conducted to assess the method's effectiveness when policy labels are directly available.
f1173df25d83e5c6ff16e087f890993bccf355ed.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the explicit use of policy labels in preference-based RLHF, resolving the likelihood mismatch problem inherent in prior approaches that assume all data is generated by the optimal policy. It formulates a regret-based preference model that uniquely accounts for both policy suboptimality and environmental stochasticity, and introduces a contrastive KL regularization mechanism for sequential decision-making. Theoretical contributions include a bijection between reward functions and optimal policies within the MaxEnt framework and a demonstration that regret minimization is equivalent to forward KL-constrained RLHF. Empirical results claim significant improvements in offline RLHF performance, robustness to heterogeneous datasets, and efficiency in online RLHF settings.

f121117c8cf3dd9feb16e278915b7ddf658b1961.title: Lexico: Extreme KV Cache Compression via Sparse Coding over Universal Dictionaries
f121117c8cf3dd9feb16e278915b7ddf658b1961.research_question: Can key-value (KV) cache memory usage in large language models (LLMs) be significantly reduced while preserving model performance, by leveraging low-dimensional structures and universal sparse coding techniques across diverse tasks, inputs, and model architectures?
f121117c8cf3dd9feb16e278915b7ddf658b1961.hypothesis: The KV cache in modern LLMs can be accurately and efficiently approximated using sparse linear combinations from a small, input-agnostic universal dictionary, enabling substantial memory savings without significant loss in model performance.
f121117c8cf3dd9feb16e278915b7ddf658b1961.proposed_method: A novel KV cache compression framework, Lexico, is proposed that utilizes sparse coding over a universal, overcomplete dictionary. The method involves three main steps: (1) Pretraining layer-specific key and value dictionaries on a large, representative corpus (e.g., WikiText-103) using gradient-based optimization to minimize reconstruction error; (2) At inference, decomposing each key and value vector into a sparse linear combination of dictionary atoms using Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP), with direct control over sparsity to flexibly adjust compression ratios; (3) Further compressing the sparse coefficients by quantizing them to 8 bits, and storing the representations in a compact compressed sparse row (CSR) format. A small buffer retains the most recent tokens in full precision to preserve generative performance. During attention computation, the compressed and uncompressed caches are handled separately and efficiently, with the final attention weights produced by concatenating their respective contributions.
f121117c8cf3dd9feb16e278915b7ddf658b1961.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple LLM architectures, including Llama-3 (1B, 3B, 8B), Mistral-7B, and Qwen2.5-14B, using dictionaries trained on WikiText-103. Evaluation will cover a range of tasks: long-context understanding (LongBench), complex reasoning (GSM8K with 5-shot prompting), and challenging zero-shot tasks (MMLU-Pro Engineering/Law). Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art quantization-based methods (KIVI, ZipCache, per-token quantization) and eviction-based methods (PyramidKV, SnapKV). Key metrics will be accuracy, F1, ROUGE-L, and memory usage as a percentage of the original KV cache. Hyperparameters such as dictionary size (N=4096), buffer size (n=128), and sparsity level will be systematically varied to match or exceed baseline compression ratios, including regimes below 20% of the original KV cache size. Ablation studies will examine the impact of error thresholding, buffer size, and memory allocation between buffer and sparse representation.
f121117c8cf3dd9feb16e278915b7ddf658b1961.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a universal, input-agnostic dictionary for sparse coding of KV caches, enabling off-the-shelf, post-training compression that generalizes across tasks and users. Unlike prior methods, Lexico achieves compression rates beyond the limits of 2-bit quantization, supporting fine-grained control over memory usage and maintaining high performance even in extreme low-memory regimes. The approach leverages low-dimensional structures in KV vectors, is compatible with existing quantization and eviction strategies, and demonstrates robustness and universality across diverse models and datasets. The method also provides a practical, efficient implementation suitable for deployment in memory-constrained environments.

f1249e8a557ecded20cdaf25d8af51901736d5f1.title: Gap Preserving Distillation by Building Bidirectional Mappings with A Dynamic Teacher
f1249e8a557ecded20cdaf25d8af51901736d5f1.research_question: How can the knowledge distillation process be improved by adaptively controlling the performance gap between teacher and student models to enhance knowledge transfer, especially in scenarios where the teacher is significantly stronger than the student?
f1249e8a557ecded20cdaf25d8af51901736d5f1.hypothesis: Maintaining a dynamically controlled, moderate performance gap between teacher and student models throughout the distillation process, using a jointly trained dynamic teacher and parameter sharing strategies, will lead to more effective knowledge transfer and improved student model performance compared to traditional fixed-teacher distillation approaches.
f1249e8a557ecded20cdaf25d8af51901736d5f1.proposed_method: A Gap Preserving Distillation (GPD) framework will be developed, introducing a dynamic teacher model that is trained from scratch alongside the student model to maintain a suitable performance gap throughout training. The dynamic teacher will be constructed using Inverse Reparameterization (IR), which expands the student model along both channel and branch dimensions with an arbitrary expansion ratio, ensuring identical initial accuracy for both models. Parameter sharing will be enforced between the dynamic teacher and student, enabling direct inheritance of well-learned parameters. Bidirectional mappings between the dynamic teacher and student will be established via IR and a Channel-Branch Reparameterization (CBR) strategy, allowing for both hard and soft knowledge transfer. The CBR will enable the extraction of an effective student model from the dynamic teacher without any post-training, facilitating flexible model deployment.
f1249e8a557ecded20cdaf25d8af51901736d5f1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet dataset using a variety of convolutional neural networks (e.g., ResNet34→ResNet18, ResNet50→MobileNet) and transformer architectures (e.g., RVT-S→RVT-Ti). The proposed GPD method will be compared against a comprehensive set of state-of-the-art knowledge distillation baselines, including KD, AT, OFD, CRD, RKD, WSLD, SRRL, SimKD, DIST, NKD, CAT-KD, CTKD, MLKD, CKD, ReviewKD, and DKD. Evaluation metrics will primarily be top-1 classification accuracy. Experimental setups will include standard distillation with a static teacher, training from scratch without a pre-trained teacher, and fine-tuning scenarios. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of gap preservation, parameter sharing, and the individual effects of channel- and branch-level reparameterization. Hyperparameters such as branch number and channel expansion ratio will be systematically varied to analyze their impact on performance.
f1249e8a557ecded20cdaf25d8af51901736d5f1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a dynamic teacher model that is trained jointly with the student, maintaining an adaptive and moderate performance gap throughout distillation, which is fundamentally different from prior methods relying on fixed, pre-trained teachers. The Inverse Reparameterization (IR) technique enables lossless expansion of the student model to construct the dynamic teacher with identical initial accuracy, supporting arbitrary expansion ratios. The Channel-Branch Reparameterization (CBR) strategy allows for direct parameter inheritance and extraction of a compact student model from the dynamic teacher without post-training. The method supports both hard and soft knowledge transfer through parameter sharing and bidirectional mappings. The approach generalizes to scenarios without a pre-trained teacher, including training from scratch and fine-tuning, and demonstrates consistent improvements over state-of-the-art distillation methods across diverse architectures.

f1481b4eba72c1e1d355413af37352a0bcfc50e9.title: Knowledge Circuits in Pretrained Transformers
f1481b4eba72c1e1d355413af37352a0bcfc50e9.research_question: How is knowledge stored, represented, and utilized within pretrained Transformer-based language models, and how can the internal mechanisms responsible for knowledge expression, editing, and reasoning be systematically identified and interpreted?
f1481b4eba72c1e1d355413af37352a0bcfc50e9.hypothesis: Knowledge in Transformer-based language models is not confined to isolated components but is encoded through collaborative circuits involving attention heads, MLPs, and embeddings; identifying and analyzing these knowledge circuits will yield deeper insights into knowledge storage, facilitate more effective knowledge editing, and improve interpretability of complex model behaviors.
f1481b4eba72c1e1d355413af37352a0bcfc50e9.proposed_method: A novel methodology will be developed to discover and analyze 'knowledge circuits'—critical subgraphs within the computation graph of Transformer models—that are responsible for encoding and expressing specific knowledge. The approach involves systematically ablating edges and nodes (such as attention heads and MLPs) in the model’s computation graph and measuring the impact on factual recall tasks, using metrics such as MatchNLL loss to determine circuit criticality. Identified circuits will be further analyzed by mapping their outputs into the embedding space via layer normalization and unembedding transformations, enabling detailed inspection of information flow and the roles of special components (e.g., mover heads, relation heads). The method will also be extended to evaluate the effects of knowledge editing techniques (such as ROME and fine-tuning) on these circuits, as well as to interpret model behaviors like hallucination and in-context learning by tracing circuit activation and information transfer.
f1481b4eba72c1e1d355413af37352a0bcfc50e9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on Transformer-based language models, including GPT-2 (medium and large) and TinyLLAMA, using the Automated Circuit Discovery toolkit and transformer lens for analysis. The primary evaluation will use factual recall tasks drawn from the LRE dataset, covering linguistic, commonsense, factual, and bias knowledge domains. Circuits will be constructed from validation data and tested for completeness and generalization on held-out test sets, with Hit@10 used as the main evaluation metric. Baselines will include random subgraph circuits of equivalent size, and the effects of knowledge editing methods (e.g., ROME, FT-M) will be compared by analyzing changes in circuit structure and performance, including multi-hop reasoning and in-context learning scenarios. Additional ablation studies will assess the importance of newly activated attention heads in demonstration-based learning.
f1481b4eba72c1e1d355413af37352a0bcfc50e9.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the concept of 'knowledge circuits' as interconnected subgraphs within Transformer models that collaboratively encode and express knowledge, moving beyond prior approaches that treat knowledge storage as isolated to specific components. The methodology enables systematic identification and analysis of these circuits, providing new insights into the flow and aggregation of knowledge across layers and components. The approach also offers a principled framework for evaluating and interpreting the effects of knowledge editing techniques, as well as for understanding complex behaviors such as hallucination and in-context learning. This work is expected to advance mechanistic interpretability, inform safer and more effective knowledge editing, and guide the design of future language models.

f14bad17c837124ba380a69e5569c5c95fe5eb39.title: Geometry of the Loss Landscape in Overparameterized Neural Networks: Symmetries and Invariances
f14bad17c837124ba380a69e5569c5c95fe5eb39.research_question: How do permutation symmetries and other invariances shape the geometry and connectivity of the loss landscape in overparameterized multi-layer neural networks, particularly with respect to the structure and proliferation of global minima and symmetry-induced critical points?
f14bad17c837124ba380a69e5569c5c95fe5eb39.hypothesis: In overparameterized neural networks, permutation symmetries and related invariances lead to the emergence of connected manifolds of global minima, and the addition of extra neurons fundamentally alters the landscape by connecting previously isolated minima. Furthermore, the number and structure of symmetry-induced critical points scale in a predictable manner with network width.
f14bad17c837124ba380a69e5569c5c95fe5eb39.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and combinatorial analysis will be conducted to characterize the geometry of the loss landscape in overparameterized neural networks, focusing on the role of permutation symmetries and associated invariances. The approach will involve deriving closed-form expressions for the number and connectivity of affine subspaces corresponding to global minima and symmetry-induced critical points, using tools from group theory and combinatorics. Theoretical results will be established for both two-layer and multi-layer networks, with explicit construction of manifolds of global minima and identification of symmetry-induced saddle points. The analysis will also include the study of expansion manifolds generated by adding neurons to minimal-width networks and the classification of all zero-loss points under smooth activation functions.
f14bad17c837124ba380a69e5569c5c95fe5eb39.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on synthetic datasets generated by teacher networks of minimal width, with student networks of varying degrees of overparameterization. Networks will be trained with smooth activation functions (e.g., softplus variants) and the loss landscape will be explored using multiple random initializations to empirically verify the theoretical predictions regarding the connectivity and structure of global minima. The experiments will track the convergence behavior, the frequency of reaching global minima, and the classification of neurons into groups (e.g., copies of teacher neurons or zero-type neurons). Evaluation metrics will include the fraction of initializations reaching global minima, the empirical loss values, and the geometric classification of solution manifolds. Baselines will include both mildly and vastly overparameterized regimes to contrast the proliferation of saddles versus the dominance of connected global minima manifolds.
f14bad17c837124ba380a69e5569c5c95fe5eb39.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a precise combinatorial and geometric characterization of the loss landscape in overparameterized neural networks, providing closed-form formulas for the number and connectivity of global minima and symmetry-induced critical subspaces. It establishes, for the first time, the explicit connectivity of the global minima manifold for networks with continuously differentiable activation functions and demonstrates how adding a single neuron can connect previously isolated minima. The approach reveals a scaling law for the proliferation of symmetry-induced critical points versus global minima as a function of overparameterization, offering new theoretical insights into the optimization landscape of neural networks beyond previous work limited to specific activation functions or empirical observations.

f1567aba236bce3c4c9b2a8c9a3c3de5e5db95e9.title: Multiclass Online Learning and Uniform Convergence
f1567aba236bce3c4c9b2a8c9a3c3de5e5db95e9.research_question: What are the fundamental conditions for agnostic online learnability in multiclass classification, and how do these relate to combinatorial complexity parameters such as the Littlestone dimension and sequential graph dimension? Furthermore, how does online learnability relate to online uniform convergence in the multiclass setting, especially when the label space is unbounded?
f1567aba236bce3c4c9b2a8c9a3c3de5e5db95e9.hypothesis: Agnostic online learnability for multiclass concept classes is characterized by the finiteness of the Littlestone dimension, regardless of the size of the label space. Additionally, online learnability and online uniform convergence are not equivalent in the multiclass setting with unbounded label spaces.
f1567aba236bce3c4c9b2a8c9a3c3de5e5db95e9.proposed_method: A novel online learning algorithm will be developed for multiclass classification in the agnostic adversarial setting. The algorithm will utilize the multiplicative weights framework, with the set of experts defined by all possible executions of the Standard Optimal Algorithm (SOA) on subsequences of the data of size up to the Littlestone dimension. At each round, the algorithm will aggregate predictions from these experts using multiplicative weights, ensuring that at least one expert corresponds to the SOA run on a maximal realizable subsequence, thus guaranteeing a bounded regret relative to the best concept in the class. The regret analysis will leverage classical results from prediction with expert advice, and the approach will be fully general for arbitrary instance and label spaces.
f1567aba236bce3c4c9b2a8c9a3c3de5e5db95e9.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish regret bounds for the proposed algorithm, showing that the regret is upper bounded by O~(L(H)√T), where L(H) is the Littlestone dimension. Lower bounds will also be established to demonstrate the tightness of the result. Theoretical separation between online learnability and online uniform convergence will be demonstrated by constructing explicit concept classes with finite Littlestone dimension but infinite sequential graph dimension. Evaluation will be based on regret (expected number of mistakes minus the best in-class function), and the analysis will consider both finite and infinite label spaces. No empirical datasets or computational experiments are specified, as the focus is on theoretical guarantees and combinatorial constructions.
f1567aba236bce3c4c9b2a8c9a3c3de5e5db95e9.novelty_claims: The proposal establishes, for the first time, that agnostic online learnability in multiclass classification is characterized exactly by the finiteness of the Littlestone dimension, even when the label space is infinite.
