It introduces a new algorithmic framework for agnostic online multiclass learning that achieves optimal regret bounds independent of the number of labels. The work also identifies and formalizes the sequential graph dimension as the key parameter for online uniform convergence, and provides a separation between online learnability and online uniform convergence in the multiclass setting. These results resolve longstanding open problems in online multiclass learning theory.

f18439302485521d7439791b786b0e33319ad39b.title: Online Detection of LLM-Generated Texts via Sequential Hypothesis Testing by Betting
f18439302485521d7439791b786b0e33319ad39b.research_question: How can machine-generated texts from large language models (LLMs) be accurately and efficiently detected in an online, streaming setting, with strong statistical guarantees on error rates and detection time?
f18439302485521d7439791b786b0e33319ad39b.hypothesis: A sequential hypothesis testing framework based on betting, combined with online optimization and robust score functions, will enable rapid and statistically reliable detection of LLM-generated texts in streaming scenarios, with controlled false positive rates and bounded detection times.
f18439302485521d7439791b786b0e33319ad39b.proposed_method: A novel online detection algorithm will be developed, leveraging sequential hypothesis testing via betting strategies. At each time step, a text from an unknown source is observed and scored using a selected function (e.g., likelihood, entropy, or classifier-based scores). A reference human-written text is sampled from a curated dataset and scored similarly. The difference in scores is used to update a wealth variable through an Online Newton Step (ONS) optimization, ensuring the process forms a non-negative supermartingale. The detection decision is made when the wealth crosses a threshold determined by the significance level, providing anytime-valid statistical guarantees. The method supports both simple and composite hypotheses, allowing for small differences between human-written sources, and adapts to unknown score bounds by estimating them from initial samples.
f18439302485521d7439791b786b0e33319ad39b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a mix of real and LLM-generated news articles, including 500 authentic news pieces about the 2024 Olympics and an equal number of fake news items generated by models such as Gemini-1.5-Flash, Gemini-1.5-Pro, and PaLM2. Human-written reference texts will be sampled from the XSum dataset. Ten different score functions, including DetectGPT, Fast-DetectGPT, LRR, NPR, DNA-GPT, Likelihood, LogRank, Entropy, and RoBERTa-based classifiers, will be evaluated. Two scoring models, GPT-Neo-2.7B and Gemma-2B, will be used for black-box evaluation. Baselines will include batch-based permutation tests with both fixed and corrected significance levels. Performance will be assessed over 1000 runs per configuration, measuring false positive rates (FPR) under the null hypothesis and average detection time under the alternative, across a range of significance levels. Additional experiments will test robustness to parameter estimation and mixed-source scenarios.
f18439302485521d7439791b786b0e33319ad39b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first online detection framework for LLM-generated texts with provable anytime-valid statistical guarantees, including controlled type-I error and bounded expected detection time. Unlike prior offline or batch-based methods, this method operates in a streaming setting, does not require pre-tuned thresholds, and is non-parametric, making no distributional assumptions about the data. The algorithm flexibly accommodates both simple and composite hypotheses, adapts to unknown score bounds, and leverages a wide range of score functions. Empirical results demonstrate superior control of false positive rates and rapid detection compared to adapted offline baselines.

f18587247e4769ad0efd96a0286b012d856ba214.title: HIQL: Offline Goal-Conditioned RL with Latent States as Actions
f18587247e4769ad0efd96a0286b012d856ba214.research_question: How can offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (RL) be made more robust and effective, especially for long-horizon tasks and in the presence of noisy value functions, while leveraging large quantities of unlabeled or action-free data, including high-dimensional observations such as images?
f18587247e4769ad0efd96a0286b012d856ba214.hypothesis: A hierarchical policy extraction framework that decomposes goal-conditioned RL into high-level subgoal prediction and low-level action selection, both derived from a single value function with latent goal representations, will improve robustness to value function noise, enhance performance on long-horizon and high-dimensional tasks, and enable efficient utilization of action-free data.
f18587247e4769ad0efd96a0286b012d856ba214.proposed_method: The proposed method, Hierarchical Implicit Q-Learning (HIQL), introduces a two-level hierarchical policy structure for offline goal-conditioned RL. First, a goal-conditioned value function is trained using action-free implicit Q-learning (IQL), which enables learning from both action-labeled and action-free (state-only) trajectories. The high-level policy predicts intermediate subgoals as latent representations, extracted from an intermediate layer of the value function, rather than raw states, allowing scalability to high-dimensional observation spaces. The low-level policy then takes these latent subgoal representations as input and outputs primitive actions to reach the subgoal. Both policies are trained using advantage-weighted regression objectives, with the high-level policy leveraging action-free data and the low-level policy trained on action-labeled data. This approach enables the value function to provide clearer learning signals for both policy levels, improving robustness to noise and facilitating learning from diverse offline datasets.
f18587247e4769ad0efd96a0286b012d856ba214.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six benchmark environments, including both state-based (AntMaze, Kitchen, CALVIN) and pixel-based (Procgen Maze, VisualAntMaze, Roboverse) offline goal-conditioned RL tasks. Datasets will include both action-labeled and action-free trajectories, with some experiments using limited action-labeled data to test the method's ability to leverage passive data. Baselines for comparison will include flat and hierarchical behavioral cloning, flat and hierarchical offline RL methods (such as GC-IQL and GC-POR), and model-based approaches (Trajectory Transformer, TAP). Evaluation metrics will include average return, success rate, and policy accuracy, with statistical significance assessed using interquartile mean (IQM) and confidence intervals. Additional analyses will examine robustness to value function noise, generalization to unseen goals, and ablations on subgoal representations and hierarchy depth.
f18587247e4769ad0efd96a0286b012d856ba214.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a simple yet effective hierarchical policy extraction framework for offline goal-conditioned RL, where both high-level and low-level policies, as well as subgoal representations, are extracted from a single value function. Unlike prior hierarchical RL methods, this method does not require multiple value functions or complex planning procedures, and it enables the use of action-free data for both value function and high-level policy training. The use of latent subgoal representations learned end-to-end from the value function allows scalability to high-dimensional, image-based environments. The method claims improved robustness to value function noise, superior performance on long-horizon and high-dimensional tasks, and the ability to maintain performance with limited action-labeled data, outperforming previous state-of-the-art offline RL methods.

f197bf0fc2f228483f6af3285000d54d8d97f9eb.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
f197bf0fc2f228483f6af3285000d54d8d97f9eb.research_question: How can an embodied agent autonomously achieve open-ended, lifelong skill acquisition and exploration in a complex, open-world environment without human intervention?
f197bf0fc2f228483f6af3285000d54d8d97f9eb.hypothesis: An embodied agent powered by large language models, equipped with an automatic curriculum for exploration, a compositional skill library, and an iterative prompting mechanism that leverages environment feedback and self-verification, will outperform existing LLM-based agent baselines in lifelong learning, skill acquisition, and generalization to novel tasks in open-ended environments such as Minecraft.
f197bf0fc2f228483f6af3285000d54d8d97f9eb.proposed_method: A novel agent architecture is proposed that integrates three key components: (1) an automatic curriculum generator, leveraging GPT-4, which dynamically proposes new tasks based on the agent's current state and exploration progress to maximize open-ended discovery; (2) a skill library, where each skill is represented as executable code indexed by semantic embeddings, enabling the storage, retrieval, and composition of complex, temporally-extended behaviors; and (3) an iterative prompting mechanism that refines code generation through repeated cycles of execution, environment feedback, error analysis, and self-verification using LLMs. The agent interacts with the environment via high-level APIs, using code as the action space, and continuously expands its skill repertoire by committing successful programs to the library. Self-verification is performed by a separate LLM agent, which critiques task completion and suggests improvements, further enhancing the agent's autonomy and robustness.
f197bf0fc2f228483f6af3285000d54d8d97f9eb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in the MineDojo Minecraft simulation environment, utilizing the Mineflayer API for embodied control. The agent will use OpenAI's GPT-4 for code and curriculum generation, GPT-3.5 for auxiliary NLP tasks, and text-embedding-ada-002 for skill library indexing. Baselines will include LLM-based agents such as ReAct, Reflexion, and AutoGPT, re-implemented for the embodied setting. Evaluation metrics will include the number of unique items discovered, distance traversed, speed of tech tree mastery (measured by prompting iterations to unlock tool milestones), and zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks in new worlds. Ablation studies will assess the contribution of each component, and experiments will be repeated across multiple seeds for statistical robustness.
f197bf0fc2f228483f6af3285000d54d8d97f9eb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent capable of autonomous, open-ended exploration and skill acquisition in Minecraft. Key innovations include an automatic curriculum that adapts to the agent's state for curiosity-driven exploration, a compositional skill library of executable code enabling rapid accumulation and reuse of complex behaviors, and a novel iterative prompting mechanism that integrates environment feedback, execution errors, and self-verification for program improvement. The method demonstrates superior lifelong learning, exploration, and zero-shot generalization compared to prior LLM-based agents, and establishes a versatile framework for plug-and-play skill transfer in new environments.

f1a2ec7363fbdfff3e84a88d2401d1862e3ef146.title: Twice-ramanujan sparsifiers
f1a2ec7363fbdfff3e84a88d2401d1862e3ef146.research_question: Can every undirected, weighted graph be approximated by a much sparser graph that preserves its spectral properties within a tight multiplicative bound, and can such sparsifiers be constructed deterministically in polynomial time with a number of edges linear in the number of vertices?
f1a2ec7363fbdfff3e84a88d2401d1862e3ef146.hypothesis: For any d > 1, every undirected, weighted graph on n vertices admits a spectral sparsifier with at most d(n-1) edges, such that the Laplacian quadratic form of the sparsifier approximates that of the original graph within a factor matching or improving the Ramanujan expander bound.
f1a2ec7363fbdfff3e84a88d2401d1862e3ef146.proposed_method: A deterministic, polynomial-time algorithm will be developed to construct a spectral sparsifier for any given undirected, weighted graph. The approach is based on a novel linear algebraic theorem that ensures, for any set of vectors summing to the identity, a sparse weighted sum can be selected to tightly sandwich the identity operator between two scaled versions of the sum. The algorithm incrementally builds the sparsifier by greedily selecting edges (or, equivalently, rank-one updates to the Laplacian) while maintaining two moving spectral barriers, ensuring all eigenvalues of the constructed Laplacian remain within the desired range. The method leverages barrier potential functions and the Sherman-Morrison formula to control the spectrum at each step, and guarantees that the resulting sparsifier has at most d(n-1) edges with appropriately chosen weights.
f1a2ec7363fbdfff3e84a88d2401d1862e3ef146.experiment_details: The proposed algorithm will be evaluated on a variety of undirected, weighted graphs, including both synthetic graphs (such as complete graphs, random graphs, and graphs with known spectral properties) and real-world network datasets. The quality of the sparsifiers will be assessed by comparing the spectral approximation factor (the ratio between the largest and smallest nonzero eigenvalues of the Laplacian quadratic forms) to the theoretical bounds, particularly the Ramanujan expander bound. Baseline comparisons will include previous randomized constructions of spectral sparsifiers (such as those based on effective resistance sampling) and cut-sparsifiers. Evaluation metrics will include the number of edges in the sparsifier, the achieved spectral approximation factor, and the runtime of the algorithm. The experimental setup will ensure that the sparsifier's edge weights and structure are reported, and that the method's deterministic nature is verified.
f1a2ec7363fbdfff3e84a88d2401d1862e3ef146.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first deterministic polynomial-time algorithm to construct spectral sparsifiers with a number of edges linear in the number of vertices, matching the edge count of Ramanujan expanders for complete graphs and generalizing this property to arbitrary graphs. The approach achieves a spectral approximation factor at least as strong as that of Ramanujan graphs, and does so without relying on randomization or effective resistance sampling. The underlying linear algebraic result and barrier-based greedy construction are new, providing both theoretical guarantees and practical algorithms for spectral sparsification.

f1a9e0830bc36c048fa4659beaa62609869895b5.title: Break the Sequential Dependency of LLM Inference Using Lookahead Decoding
f1a9e0830bc36c048fa4659beaa62609869895b5.research_question: How can the sequential dependency in large language model (LLM) autoregressive decoding be broken to achieve lower inference latency and better utilization of modern parallel hardware, without requiring auxiliary models or datastores?
f1a9e0830bc36c048fa4659beaa62609869895b5.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by reformulating LLM decoding as a parallel process using a lookahead and verification mechanism, it is possible to significantly accelerate inference while maintaining exact output distributions and compatibility with existing memory-efficient attention mechanisms.
f1a9e0830bc36c048fa4659beaa62609869895b5.proposed_method: A novel, lossless parallel decoding algorithm called LOOKAHEAD DECODING will be developed to accelerate LLM inference without the need for auxiliary draft models or datastores. The method leverages the equivalence between autoregressive decoding and solving a non-linear system via fixed-point Jacobi iteration, enabling the generation of multiple disjoint n-grams in parallel within a single decoding step. The approach maintains a fixed-sized 2D window (with configurable lookahead and lookback parameters) to generate and cache n-grams, which are then verified in parallel by a dedicated verification branch to ensure the output distribution remains unchanged. The method integrates with advanced attention mechanisms such as FlashAttention and is designed for efficient parallelization across multiple GPUs, allowing for strong scaling with available compute resources.
f1a9e0830bc36c048fa4659beaa62609869895b5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on various LLMs, including LLaMA-2 and CodeLlama models (7B, 13B, 34B, 70B), using both single and multi-GPU setups (NVIDIA A100 and RTX 3090). The evaluation will cover a range of tasks and datasets, such as MT-Bench (multi-turn chat), HumanEval (code completion and infilling), MBPP, GSM8K (math), ClassEval, CNN/DailyMail, and XSum (summarization). Baselines will include standard autoregressive decoding (greedy search), speculative decoding, and state-of-the-art memory-efficient attention implementations (e.g., FlashAttention). Key metrics will be end-to-end throughput (tokens/sec), step compression ratio, speedup over baselines, and output quality (ROUGE scores for summarization, pass@k for code, etc.). The experimental setup will also include ablation studies on lookahead and verification branch configurations, and scaling analyses with increasing compute resources.
f1a9e0830bc36c048fa4659beaa62609869895b5.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first exact, parallel decoding algorithm for LLMs that does not require auxiliary draft models or datastores, breaking the traditional sequential dependency of autoregressive decoding. It enables linear reduction in decoding steps relative to per-step log(FLOPs), offers strong scaling with compute resources, and is compatible with modern memory-efficient attention mechanisms. The approach maintains output distribution fidelity across sampling methods and tasks, and demonstrates significant wall-clock speedups (up to 4x) in both single and multi-GPU settings. Additionally, the method is future-proof, allowing for flexible trade-offs between per-step compute and total decoding steps, and can be integrated with prompt-based speculation for further acceleration.

f1bd7ea3a63b78a60b5d90d91fdb4a1d7ac0de8e.title: CrossCodeEval: A Diverse and Multilingual Benchmark for Cross-File Code Completion
f1bd7ea3a63b78a60b5d90d91fdb4a1d7ac0de8e.research_question: How can code language models be effectively evaluated on their ability to perform code completion tasks that require understanding and leveraging cross-file context in realistic, multi-file, multilingual software repositories?
f1bd7ea3a63b78a60b5d90d91fdb4a1d7ac0de8e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that existing code language models, when evaluated on code completion tasks that strictly require cross-file context, will perform suboptimally with only in-file context, but their performance will significantly improve when relevant cross-file context is provided. Furthermore, even with access to cross-file context, current models and retrieval methods will not achieve perfect performance, indicating substantial room for improvement in both model design and context retrieval.
f1bd7ea3a63b78a60b5d90d91fdb4a1d7ac0de8e.proposed_method: A new benchmark, CROSSCODEEVAL, will be constructed to evaluate code language models on cross-file code completion tasks. The benchmark will be built from a diverse set of real-world, permissively-licensed open-source repositories in four programming languages: Python, Java, TypeScript, and C#. A static-analysis-based approach will be developed to automatically identify code fragments that require cross-file context for accurate completion. This involves replacing intra-project imports with empty class definitions and using static analysis tools (e.g., Pylint, javac, tsc, csc) to detect undefined names, which indicate dependencies on cross-file entities. The dataset will be curated through rule-based and model-based filters to ensure high quality, minimal data leakage, and that completions cannot be inferred from in-file context alone. Additional post-processing and human annotation will further enhance dataset quality.
f1bd7ea3a63b78a60b5d90d91fdb4a1d7ac0de8e.experiment_details: Experiments will benchmark several state-of-the-art code language models, including CodeGen (350M to 16B parameters), StarCoder (1B to 15.5B), and GPT-3.5-turbo, using the CROSSCODEEVAL dataset. The evaluation will be performed in a zero-shot setting, with models provided either only in-file context or augmented with retrieved cross-file context using a retrieve-and-generate (RG) framework. Retrieval methods will include sparse (BM25) and neural (UniXCoder, OpenAI ada embeddings) retrievers, with the top-5 most similar cross-file code snippets prepended to the prompt. Evaluation metrics will include code exact match (EM), edit similarity (ES), and identifier match (EM, F1). The experimental setup will control for prompt length, use consistent hyperparameters, and include both greedy and nucleus sampling. Additional analyses will investigate the impact of retrieval quality, identifier overlap, and file location on model performance.
f1bd7ea3a63b78a60b5d90d91fdb4a1d7ac0de8e.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces the first large-scale, multilingual, and diverse dataset specifically designed to evaluate cross-file code completion, strictly requiring cross-file context for accurate completion. The static-analysis-based method for identifying cross-file dependencies is efficient and generalizable across languages. The benchmark is constructed to minimize data leakage and memorization by excluding overlap with major pre-training datasets. CROSSCODEEVAL enables comprehensive evaluation of both code completion and code retrieval capabilities, filling a critical gap in current code LM evaluation and providing a resource for advancing research in repository-level code understanding.

f1ef2a0b1630b2e04a3a55d4bbe446fc9c1c7672.title: Understanding Generalization in Quantum Machine Learning with Margins
f1ef2a0b1630b2e04a3a55d4bbe446fc9c1c7672.research_question: How can generalization in quantum machine learning (QML) models be more accurately characterized and improved, particularly in comparison to traditional metrics such as parameter count, and what theoretical and empirical tools can provide reliable predictors of generalization performance in QML?
f1ef2a0b1630b2e04a3a55d4bbe446fc9c1c7672.hypothesis: Margin-based generalization bounds provide a more reliable and tighter measure of generalization performance in QML models than traditional uniform bounds or parameter-based metrics, and optimizing quantum embeddings to maximize class separability in the quantum feature space will enhance generalization.
f1ef2a0b1630b2e04a3a55d4bbe446fc9c1c7672.proposed_method: A novel margin-based generalization bound for quantum neural networks (QNNs) will be established by extending classical margin theory to the quantum domain. This involves interpreting quantum measurements as Lipschitz continuous nonlinear activations and applying matrix covering techniques to complex-valued spaces, accounting for the unitary constraints of quantum circuits and the normalization of quantum states. The method will analytically bound the Rademacher complexity of QNNs in terms of quantum channel components, leading to a generalization bound that depends on the margin distribution normalized by the spectral norms of the measurement operators. For projective measurements, the bound will further simplify, making the margin distribution alone sufficient for generalization assessment. Additionally, the connection between margin distributions and quantum state discrimination will be formalized, and classical-quantum hybrid embedding schemes will be explored to maximize margins when applying QML to classical data.
f1ef2a0b1630b2e04a3a55d4bbe446fc9c1c7672.experiment_details: Empirical studies will be conducted using Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks (QCNNs) on the Quantum Phase Recognition (QPR) dataset, a multiclass quantum classification task with varying degrees of label noise. Experiments will compare models with different numbers of layers, variational ansatzes, and quantum embedding strategies (fixed, trainable, and neural quantum embeddings). Margin-based metrics (lower quartile, median, mean) will be evaluated against parameter-based metrics (total and effective parameter count) for their ability to predict the generalization gap. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy, margin distribution statistics, mutual information, and Kendall rank correlation between metrics and generalization gap. Additional experiments will be performed on classical datasets (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, Kuzushiji-MNIST) embedded into quantum states, assessing the impact of quantum embedding schemes on margin distributions and generalization.
f1ef2a0b1630b2e04a3a55d4bbe446fc9c1c7672.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first margin-based generalization bound specifically tailored for multiclass QNNs, adapting and extending classical margin theory to the quantum setting. The approach demonstrates that margin-based metrics are superior predictors of generalization in QML compared to parameter-based metrics, even under randomized labels where traditional bounds fail. The work establishes a theoretical and empirical link between quantum state discrimination (trace distance) and margin-based generalization, providing a systematic pathway for optimizing QML models via quantum embeddings. The framework offers both theoretical insights and practical guidance for designing QML architectures that generalize well, advancing the understanding of generalization in quantum machine learning.

f1ef4b3463df9b9542773f7b7f6332359979dafe.title: Probing Equivariance and Symmetry Breaking in Convolutional Networks
f1ef4b3463df9b9542773f7b7f6332359979dafe.research_question: What are the impacts of varying degrees of group-equivariance constraints and symmetry-breaking mechanisms in convolutional neural networks on the expressivity, generalization, and empirical performance across diverse geometric learning tasks? Under what conditions do explicit structural priors, such as equivariance and symmetry-breaking, provide tangible benefits, and how do these compare to less constrained or non-equivariant models in terms of data efficiency, scalability, and task alignment?
f1ef4b3463df9b9542773f7b7f6332359979dafe.hypothesis: Explicit group-equivariant constraints and symmetry-breaking mechanisms, when aligned with the geometric structure of the task, enhance model expressivity, generalization, and data efficiency beyond what can be achieved by merely increasing representation capacity or training data in unconstrained models. Furthermore, incorporating geometric reference frames or controlled equivariance-breaking features can provide additional empirical benefits, particularly when such information is relevant to the task geometry.
f1ef4b3463df9b9542773f7b7f6332359979dafe.proposed_method: A unified, modular group convolutional architecture, termed Rapidash, will be developed to enable fine-grained control over equivariance constraints, input/output representations, and mechanisms for symmetry- and equivariance-breaking. The architecture will operate over the position-orientation space (R3 × S2), supporting both SE(3)- and T(3)-equivariant variants, and will be capable of incorporating geometric inputs such as global frames, normals, and velocities. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to formalize the expressivity and universal approximation properties of the architecture, including its equivalence to steerable tensor field networks via spherical harmonic decomposition. The empirical study will systematically compare model variants under matched capacity and training regimes, isolating the effects of kernel constraints, representation scaling, data scaling, and explicit symmetry-breaking via auxiliary geometric information.
f1ef4b3463df9b9542773f7b7f6332359979dafe.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of geometric learning tasks, including molecular property prediction and generation (using the QM9 dataset), 3D part segmentation and shape generation (using ShapeNet3D), and human motion prediction (using the CMU Motion Capture dataset). For each task, multiple model variants will be evaluated, including SE(3)- and T(3)-equivariant Rapidash models, with and without symmetry-breaking or equivariance-breaking inputs. Baselines will include state-of-the-art models such as EGNN, DimeNet++, SE(3)-Transformer, PointNeXt, DeltaConv, GeomGCNN, LION, and others. Evaluation metrics will include mean absolute error (MAE) for regression, mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) for segmentation, 1-Nearest Neighbor Accuracy for generation, and mean squared error (MSE) for motion prediction. Experiments will also assess the effects of scaling model capacity, varying dataset size, and introducing explicit geometric reference frames or input features that break equivariance.
f1ef4b3463df9b9542773f7b7f6332359979dafe.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified group convolutional architecture (Rapidash) that enables controlled, systematic comparison of equivariant and non-equivariant models across multiple tasks and symmetry settings. Theoretical contributions include formal analysis of expressivity, universal approximation, and the role of symmetry-breaking via auxiliary variables. Empirically, the research provides nuanced, task-specific insights into the benefits and limitations of equivariance and symmetry-breaking, demonstrating that explicit geometric priors and reference frames can yield state-of-the-art performance and improved data efficiency. The framework offers a principled basis for model selection and architectural design in geometric deep learning.

f208ea909fa7f54fea82def9a92fd81dfc758c39.title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions
f208ea909fa7f54fea82def9a92fd81dfc758c39.research_question: How can multi-step, knowledge-intensive open-domain question answering be improved by integrating external knowledge retrieval and reasoning in a more interactive and iterative manner, especially when the required knowledge is not fully contained within the language model's parameters?
f208ea909fa7f54fea82def9a92fd81dfc758c39.hypothesis: Interleaving retrieval with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, such that each reasoning step informs subsequent retrieval and vice versa, will lead to improved retrieval of relevant information, more accurate multi-step reasoning, and better question answering performance compared to standard one-step retrieval or retrieval-free approaches.
f208ea909fa7f54fea82def9a92fd81dfc758c39.proposed_method: A novel approach, IRCoT (Interleaving Retrieval guided by Chain-of-Thought Reasoning), is developed for multi-step open-domain question answering. The method begins by retrieving an initial set of paragraphs using the question as a query. It then alternates between two steps: (1) generating the next chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning step using the question, all previously retrieved paragraphs, and previously generated CoT sentences; and (2) using the most recent CoT sentence as a query to retrieve additional paragraphs from the knowledge source. This process is repeated iteratively until a termination criterion is met (such as the CoT indicating an answer or reaching a maximum number of steps). All retrieved paragraphs are then provided as context to a QA reader model, which produces the final answer using either direct prompting or CoT prompting. The approach is designed to be compatible with both large and smaller language models and does not require supervised training.
f208ea909fa7f54fea82def9a92fd81dfc758c39.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four multi-step open-domain QA datasets: HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC. For each dataset, a corpus is constructed, and 100 development and 500 test questions are sampled. The retrieval component uses BM25 as the base retriever, and both OpenAI GPT-3 and Flan-T5 models of various sizes are used for CoT generation and as QA readers. Baselines include one-step retrieval (using only the question as a query), retrieval-free QA (relying solely on model parameters), and the proposed IRCoT method. Evaluation metrics include recall of gold supporting paragraphs among retrieved documents and answer F1 score. Experiments also include out-of-distribution (OOD) settings, where prompt demonstrations from one dataset are used to evaluate on another, and ablation studies on model size and factual accuracy of generated CoTs.
f208ea909fa7f54fea82def9a92fd81dfc758c39.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel interleaving framework that tightly couples retrieval and reasoning, allowing each to inform the other at every step. This approach is claimed to substantially improve both retrieval recall and downstream QA performance over standard one-step retrieval, reduce factual errors in generated reasoning chains, and be effective across a range of language model sizes without additional training. The method also demonstrates strong generalization in out-of-distribution settings and achieves state-of-the-art results on several multi-step open-domain QA benchmarks.

f212ca51d941ee686341d43eb167fcbd7e78807c.title: AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Language Models
f212ca51d941ee686341d43eb167fcbd7e78807c.research_question: How can knowledge in large language models be efficiently and accurately updated while ensuring the preservation of existing knowledge, particularly in sequential editing scenarios, and without causing degradation in the model's general capabilities or inducing overfitting?
f212ca51d941ee686341d43eb167fcbd7e78807c.hypothesis: Projecting parameter perturbations onto the null space of preserved knowledge representations will enable targeted knowledge updates in large language models while maintaining the integrity of existing knowledge and preventing distributional shifts or model collapse, especially during sequential edits.
f212ca51d941ee686341d43eb167fcbd7e78807c.proposed_method: A novel model editing framework, AlphaEdit, will be developed to address the challenge of balancing knowledge update and preservation in large language models. The approach will first identify the parameters associated with the knowledge to be updated using a locate-then-edit paradigm. Instead of directly applying perturbations, the method will project these perturbations onto the null space of the matrix encoding preserved knowledge, ensuring that the key-value associations for preserved knowledge remain intact. This projection will be efficiently computed using the singular value decomposition (SVD) of the covariance matrix of preserved knowledge representations, allowing for computational tractability even with high-dimensional data. The final optimization objective will focus solely on minimizing the error for the updated knowledge, with regularization for stable convergence, and will be extended to sequential editing by including terms to protect previously updated knowledge.
f212ca51d941ee686341d43eb167fcbd7e78807c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple large language models, including GPT-2 XL (1.5B parameters), GPT-J (6B), and LLaMA3 (8B). The evaluation will utilize widely adopted benchmarks such as the Counterfact and ZsRE datasets for knowledge editing, with 2,000 samples randomly drawn for sequential updates (batch size of 100 per edit). Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art model editing methods such as Fine-Tuning, MEND, InstructEdit, ROME, MEMIT, PRUNE, and RECT. Evaluation metrics will comprise Efficacy, Generalization, Specificity, Fluency, and Consistency. Additional general capability tests will be performed using six tasks from the GLUE benchmark (SST, MRPC, MMLU, RTE, CoLA, NLI) to assess the impact on overall model performance. The experimental setup will also include ablation studies and integration of the proposed projection step into existing baselines to measure performance improvements.
f212ca51d941ee686341d43eb167fcbd7e78807c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a null-space projection mechanism for model editing that ensures preserved knowledge is unaffected by parameter updates, addressing the fundamental trade-off in current approaches. The projection is implemented with minimal computational overhead and can be integrated into existing editing algorithms with a single line of code. AlphaEdit is claimed to significantly improve both knowledge update efficacy and preservation, particularly in sequential editing scenarios, and to prevent overfitting and distributional shifts in hidden representations. The method demonstrates broad applicability and plug-and-play enhancement for a variety of model editing techniques, achieving substantial improvements in both editing and generalization performance.

f21a88af78583bd7959b121b800eed5c1f7b7b99.title: Self-Stabilization: The Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent at the Edge of Stability
f21a88af78583bd7959b121b800eed5c1f7b7b99.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms that govern the behavior of gradient descent when training neural networks at the edge of stability, particularly when the sharpness of the loss function approaches the instability threshold, and how can these dynamics be theoretically characterized and predicted?
f21a88af78583bd7959b121b800eed5c1f7b7b99.hypothesis: Gradient descent at the edge of stability exhibits a self-stabilization property, wherein the dynamics are governed by a negative feedback loop arising from higher-order terms in the loss function's Taylor expansion. This mechanism implicitly constrains the optimization trajectory to remain near the stability threshold, preventing divergence and enabling continued (though non-monotonic) decrease of the loss.
f21a88af78583bd7959b121b800eed5c1f7b7b99.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the dynamics of gradient descent at the edge of stability using a cubic Taylor expansion of the loss function. The method will derive and study a set of coupled dynamical equations that track the evolution of the optimization trajectory in the directions of the top Hessian eigenvector and the gradient of sharpness. The analysis will identify a negative feedback loop, termed self-stabilization, which regulates both the sharpness and the deviation in the unstable direction. The framework will further show that gradient descent implicitly follows a projected gradient descent (PGD) trajectory constrained by the sharpness threshold, and will provide explicit predictions for the loss, sharpness, and trajectory deviation throughout training. Theoretical results will be established under mild assumptions on the loss function, and the predictions will be validated both analytically and empirically.
f21a88af78583bd7959b121b800eed5c1f7b7b99.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard neural network architectures, such as multi-layer perceptrons, trained on benchmark datasets like CIFAR-10. Full-batch or large-batch gradient descent will be used with learning rates set near the theoretical instability threshold. The experiments will track the evolution of training loss, sharpness (largest Hessian eigenvalue), and the deviation from the predicted PGD trajectory over the course of training. Baselines will include classical gradient descent dynamics and prior theoretical predictions that do not account for self-stabilization. Evaluation metrics will include the accuracy of theoretical predictions for loss and sharpness, as well as empirical verification of the boundedness and oscillatory behavior at the edge of stability.
f21a88af78583bd7959b121b800eed5c1f7b7b99.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of self-stabilization as a general property of gradient descent at the edge of stability, providing a new theoretical explanation for the observed non-monotonic but stable loss decrease in modern neural network training. The analysis leverages a cubic Taylor expansion to reveal a negative feedback loop that implicitly enforces a sharpness constraint, offering a precise and predictive characterization of the optimization dynamics. The framework unifies and extends previous empirical observations by providing explicit, testable predictions for loss, sharpness, and trajectory deviation, and demonstrates that gradient descent effectively performs projected optimization under a sharpness constraint.

f2229c525fe2142538771750a2c9f180c978da52.title: Convergence and stability results for the particle system in the Stein gradient descent method
f2229c525fe2142538771750a2c9f180c978da52.research_question: What are the convergence and stability properties of the particle system in the Stein gradient descent method when sampling from complex probability distributions, and how do these properties scale with the number of particles and time?
f2229c525fe2142538771750a2c9f180c978da52.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the Stein gradient descent particle system exhibits improved stability and convergence properties over longer, algebraically-scaling time intervals (in terms of the number of particles N), as compared to previously established logarithmic time scales, provided the initial particle configuration is sufficiently close to the target distribution.
f2229c525fe2142538771750a2c9f180c978da52.proposed_method: A rigorous mathematical framework will be developed to analyze the convergence and stability of the Stein gradient descent particle system. The approach will involve formulating the particle dynamics as an ODE system that approximates the gradient flow of the Kullback-Leibler divergence, and connecting the empirical particle measure to the solution of a nonlocal PDE. The analysis will leverage duality methods and introduce a weighted bounded Lipschitz distance to quantify stability. A key technical innovation will be the construction of a functional invariant for the linearized dual equation, allowing for improved Grönwall-type estimates that avoid exponential growth in error bounds. The method will explicitly characterize the time scales over which the empirical measure remains close to the asymptotic state, with detailed assumptions on the kernel and potential functions.
f2229c525fe2142538771750a2c9f180c978da52.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be validated through mathematical proofs, with the primary 'experiments' consisting of deriving convergence and stability estimates under varying assumptions on the kernel K and potential V. The analysis will consider empirical measures generated by the particle system and compare them to the solution of the associated mean-field PDE, using metrics such as the Wasserstein distance and a weighted bounded Lipschitz norm. Theoretical baselines will include prior results that establish convergence only for logarithmic time scales in N. The setup will explore both the joint limit of large N and long time t, as well as the behavior for initial configurations close to the target distribution, with technical lemmas ensuring the well-posedness of the measure solutions.
f2229c525fe2142538771750a2c9f180c978da52.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces new stability estimates for the Stein gradient descent particle system that extend the practical time scale of stability from logarithmic to algebraic in the number of particles. The use of a functional invariant for the linearized dual equation, inspired by but distinct from techniques used in the analysis of the Vlasov equation, enables the elimination of exponential terms in error bounds. The approach generalizes previous methods to a broader class of non-Hamiltonian PDEs and provides the first rigorous analysis of long-time stability for deterministic sampling algorithms of this type.

f2231e6dbccced314f30a2fc926bc8a977904562.title: In Search of Robust Measures of Generalization
f2231e6dbccced314f30a2fc926bc8a977904562.research_question: How can robust empirical methodologies be developed to evaluate and compare generalization measures in deep learning, particularly in the presence of varying experimental settings and interventions?
f2231e6dbccced314f30a2fc926bc8a977904562.hypothesis: Generalization measures evaluated using a distributional robustness framework, rather than average-based metrics, will more accurately identify the limitations and strengths of these measures across a range of experimental environments.
f2231e6dbccced314f30a2fc926bc8a977904562.proposed_method: A new empirical methodology will be developed to evaluate generalization measures within the framework of distributional robustness. This approach will define families of environments by systematically varying hyperparameters such as learning rate, network width, depth, training set size, and dataset. For each environment, paired experiments will be conducted where only one hyperparameter is changed at a time. The method will employ a robust ranking evaluation, specifically focusing on the worst-case (robust) sign-error across environments, rather than average-case performance. The evaluation will use a weighted empirical sign-error metric that accounts for Monte Carlo variance, discarding comparisons where the difference in generalization error is below the noise threshold. This methodology will allow for the identification of both the strengths and the failure modes of various generalization measures.
f2231e6dbccced314f30a2fc926bc8a977904562.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale collections of deep learning models trained on CIFAR-10 and SVHN datasets, with thousands of runs varying key hyperparameters such as width, depth, learning rate, and training set size. Each environment will consist of paired experiments differing in a single hyperparameter, and the evaluation will be performed on over 1,600,000 pairs of experiments across 24 candidate generalization measures. The primary evaluation metric will be the robust sign-error, defined as the worst-case error in predicting the direction of change in generalization error across environments. Baselines will include existing complexity and generalization measures derived from the literature, such as norm-based, PAC-Bayes, and spectral measures. The evaluation will also consider average and 90th percentile sign-errors for comparison, but the focus will be on robustness to interventions.
f2231e6dbccced314f30a2fc926bc8a977904562.novelty_claims: The proposed methodology introduces a robust, distributional robustness-based evaluation framework for generalization measures, which contrasts with prior approaches that rely on average-case metrics. This approach is capable of uncovering failure modes and limitations of generalization measures that are obscured by averaging, providing a more scientifically rigorous and informative assessment. The methodology also enables the identification of subfamilies of environments where specific measures are robust, guiding the development of better theories and predictors of generalization in deep learning.

f229557011920c440b89f199d6fc334853092643.title: Multi-Task Learning as a Bargaining Game
f229557011920c440b89f199d6fc334853092643.research_question: How can multi-task learning optimization be improved to address the issue of conflicting task gradients and achieve balanced, state-of-the-art performance across diverse tasks and domains?
f229557011920c440b89f199d6fc334853092643.hypothesis: Formulating the gradient combination step in multi-task learning as a cooperative bargaining game and using the Nash Bargaining Solution will yield a principled, scale-invariant, and proportionally fair update direction that improves convergence and overall performance compared to existing heuristic or ad-hoc gradient aggregation methods.
f229557011920c440b89f199d6fc334853092643.proposed_method: A novel multi-task learning optimization procedure, Nash-MTL, is proposed, where the combination of per-task gradients at each optimization step is framed as a cooperative bargaining game. Each task is treated as a player whose utility is defined by the inner product of its gradient with the proposed update direction. The Nash Bargaining Solution is used to determine the optimal convex combination of gradients, ensuring Pareto optimality, symmetry, independence of irrelevant alternatives, and invariance to affine transformations. The solution involves solving a system where the Gram matrix of gradients and the vector of combination weights satisfy G^T G α = 1/α (element-wise reciprocal), which is efficiently approximated using a sequence of convex optimization problems and the concave-convex procedure. To address computational scalability, the method allows for less frequent updates of the combination weights, significantly reducing runtime while maintaining strong performance.
f229557011920c440b89f199d6fc334853092643.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of multi-task learning benchmarks spanning domains such as computer vision (NYUv2, Cityscapes), quantum chemistry (QM9), and reinforcement learning (Meta-World MT10). The method will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines, including single-task learning, linear scalarization, scale-invariant loss, dynamic and uncertainty-based weighting, multiple gradient descent algorithms, and recent fair or conflict-averse gradient aggregation methods. Evaluation metrics will include per-task standard metrics (e.g., mIoU, pixel accuracy, mean absolute error), as well as aggregate measures such as mean rank (MR) and average performance drop (Δm%) relative to single-task baselines. The experimental setup will involve training with state-of-the-art architectures (e.g., Multi-Task Attention Network, GNNs, SAC for RL), hyperparameter tuning via validation sets, and reporting results over multiple random seeds for statistical robustness. Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of update frequency for gradient weights on runtime and performance.
f229557011920c440b89f199d6fc334853092643.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled, axiomatic approach to gradient aggregation in multi-task learning by leveraging the Nash Bargaining Solution, ensuring scale-invariance and proportional fairness across tasks. The method provides theoretical convergence guarantees to Pareto stationary or optimal points in both convex and non-convex settings. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across diverse domains, outperforming existing heuristic and algorithmic baselines. The approach also addresses computational scalability, offering practical solutions for reducing runtime without significant loss in performance.

f22d71c7ce9720ba1f717a4f1181488200e78198.title: LLaVA-Med: Training a Large Language-and-Vision Assistant for Biomedicine in One Day
f22d71c7ce9720ba1f717a4f1181488200e78198.research_question: How can a large language-and-vision conversational assistant be efficiently adapted to the biomedical domain to enable open-ended, instruction-following interactions about biomedical images, and how does such a system perform compared to existing methods on standard biomedical visual question answering tasks?
f22d71c7ce9720ba1f717a4f1181488200e78198.hypothesis: A curriculum learning approach that first aligns a general-domain vision-language model to biomedical concepts using large-scale image-caption pairs, followed by fine-tuning with diverse, self-instructed biomedical instruction-following data, will enable the resulting assistant to outperform existing supervised and general-domain models on biomedical multimodal conversational and VQA tasks.
f22d71c7ce9720ba1f717a4f1181488200e78198.proposed_method: A two-stage curriculum learning framework will be developed to adapt a general-domain large language-and-vision model to the biomedical domain. In the first stage, the model will be fine-tuned for biomedical concept alignment using 600,000 image-caption pairs sampled from the PMC-15M dataset, where the model is trained to generate captions from images with simple descriptive instructions. During this stage, the vision encoder and language model weights are frozen, and only the projection matrix is updated to align biomedical image features with textual embeddings. In the second stage, the model will undergo end-to-end instruction-tuning using a diverse set of 60,000 instruction-following examples generated by prompting GPT-4 with biomedical image captions and contextual sentences, creating multi-round conversational data. Here, both the projection layer and language model weights are updated, while the vision encoder remains frozen. The approach will be implemented using a linear projection between the vision encoder and a 7B or 13B parameter language model, and will leverage both English and cross-lingual capabilities.
f22d71c7ce9720ba1f717a4f1181488200e78198.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three standard biomedical VQA datasets: VQA-RAD (radiology), SLAKE (multimodal radiology with knowledge graph), and PathVQA (pathology), covering a range of biomedical imaging modalities and question types. The evaluation will include both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings, with performance measured on closed-set questions (accuracy) and open-set questions (recall of ground-truth tokens in generated responses). Baselines will include the general-domain LLaVA model and state-of-the-art supervised biomedical VQA methods. Additional experiments will assess multimodal conversational ability using a custom evaluation set of 193 novel biomedical questions, scored by GPT-4 for helpfulness, relevance, accuracy, and detail. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of dataset size, inclusion of inline mentions, model initialization, and training duration. Training efficiency and serving cost will also be measured, with all experiments conducted on 8xA100 GPUs.
f22d71c7ce9720ba1f717a4f1181488200e78198.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first large-scale, self-instructed biomedical multimodal instruction-following dataset, generated automatically from PMC-15M image-caption pairs using GPT-4 without manual annotation. A novel curriculum learning strategy is developed for efficient domain adaptation of vision-language models to biomedicine, enabling end-to-end conversational capabilities in less than 15 hours of training. The resulting assistant demonstrates superior performance over prior supervised and general-domain models on multiple biomedical VQA benchmarks and exhibits strong multimodal conversational ability, including cross-lingual generalization. All datasets, code, and trained models will be released to facilitate further research in biomedical multimodal AI.

f23222ad51b9b1f4c1addcf848906db7698ccbff.title: Design-Bench: Benchmarks for Data-Driven Offline Model-Based Optimization
f23222ad51b9b1f4c1addcf848906db7698ccbff.research_question: How can standardized benchmarks be developed to enable rigorous, reproducible, and comprehensive evaluation of offline model-based optimization (MBO) algorithms across diverse, high-dimensional, and realistically challenging design tasks?
f23222ad51b9b1f4c1addcf848906db7698ccbff.hypothesis: Establishing a unified benchmark suite with diverse, high-dimensional, and challenging offline MBO tasks, along with standardized evaluation protocols and reference implementations, will facilitate more accurate tracking of algorithmic progress, enable fair comparisons, and accelerate the development of effective offline MBO methods.
f23222ad51b9b1f4c1addcf848906db7698ccbff.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark suite, named Design-Bench, will be constructed to evaluate offline model-based optimization algorithms. This suite will include a diverse set of tasks spanning multiple domains such as biology, materials science, and robotics, with both discrete and continuous design spaces and varying dimensionalities. Each task will provide a static dataset of design-objective pairs and a ground-truth oracle (either an expert model or simulation) for evaluation, but not for training or hyperparameter tuning. The benchmark will enforce a unified evaluation protocol, including standardized metrics (e.g., percentile of top-K candidate performance), and will supply reference implementations of recent offline MBO algorithms and baselines. The benchmark will also address challenges such as heavy-tailed objective distributions, high sensitivity of objective functions, and the need to balance exploration of the design space with adherence to the data manifold.
f23222ad51b9b1f4c1addcf848906db7698ccbff.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of eight tasks, including TFBind8/10 (DNA sequence optimization), NAS (neural architecture search), ChEMBL (molecule activity maximization), Superconductor (critical temperature maximization), AntMorphology and D’KittyMorphology (robot morphology optimization), and HopperController (robot controller optimization). Each task will provide a static dataset, and algorithms will be evaluated by generating K=128 candidate designs, with performance measured by the 100th percentile of objective values as assessed by the oracle. Baselines and state-of-the-art offline MBO algorithms such as CbAS, Auto-CbAS, MINs, COMs, CMA-ES, gradient ascent, and REINFORCE will be implemented and compared under identical conditions. Hyperparameter tuning will be strictly limited to offline procedures, with no access to the oracle during training or tuning. Results will be averaged over multiple independent runs, and additional metrics (e.g., median, IQM) will be reported for robustness.
f23222ad51b9b1f4c1addcf848906db7698ccbff.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark suite introduces the first standardized, diverse, and challenging set of tasks for offline model-based optimization, enabling rigorous and fair comparison of algorithms. It provides a unified evaluation protocol, reference implementations of recent methods, and tasks that reflect real-world challenges such as high dimensionality, heavy-tailed data, and sensitive objective landscapes. This benchmark is designed to catalyze progress in offline MBO by providing a reproducible and comprehensive testbed for future algorithm development and evaluation.

f23abc7a07d299fcc65f116c7702d7c01b8cbcdc.title: Deep Directly-Trained Spiking Neural Networks for Object Detection
f23abc7a07d299fcc65f116c7702d7c01b8cbcdc.research_question: How can directly-trained spiking neural networks (SNNs) be designed to efficiently and accurately perform object detection tasks, including both static and event-based data, while minimizing energy consumption and overcoming challenges related to deep network training?
f23abc7a07d299fcc65f116c7702d7c01b8cbcdc.hypothesis: A directly-trained, deep spiking neural network with a novel full-spike residual block and surrogate gradient optimization can achieve object detection performance comparable to conventional artificial neural networks (ANNs), while operating with significantly fewer time steps and lower energy consumption.
f23abc7a07d299fcc65f116c7702d7c01b8cbcdc.proposed_method: A new object detection framework, EMS-YOLO, will be developed based on the YOLO architecture but implemented as a directly-trained spiking neural network. The core innovation is the Energy-efficient Membrane-Shortcut ResNet (EMS-ResNet), a full-spike residual block that eliminates non-spike convolution operations on shortcut paths, thereby reducing redundant multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations and enhancing energy efficiency. Surrogate gradient methods will be used to enable direct training of the SNN, allowing for deep architectures without suffering from vanishing or exploding gradients. The model will process both static images and event-based data by converting inputs into spike trains and leveraging the temporal dynamics of spiking neurons, with the detection head adapted to output bounding box coordinates and class predictions from membrane potentials.
f23abc7a07d299fcc65f116c7702d7c01b8cbcdc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both the frame-based COCO2017 dataset and the event-based Gen1 Automotive Detection dataset. The models will be trained using SGD optimization, with data augmentation (e.g., Mosaic) applied to COCO. Baselines will include ANN-based YOLO and ResNet models, as well as state-of-the-art ANN-SNN conversion methods such as Spike-YOLO and Spike Calibration. Evaluation metrics will be mean Average Precision (mAP) at IOU=0.5 and mAP averaged over IOU thresholds (mAP@0.5:0.95). Energy consumption will be measured in terms of synaptic operations (SyOPs) and compared across models. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of different residual blocks, network depth, and time step size on both performance and energy efficiency.
f23abc7a07d299fcc65f116c7702d7c01b8cbcdc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to directly train a deep SNN for object detection using surrogate gradients, rather than relying on ANN-to-SNN conversion. The EMS-ResNet block enables full-spiking operation throughout the network, significantly reducing energy consumption by eliminating non-spike convolutions on shortcut paths. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the architecture avoids gradient vanishing and explosion, supporting deep SNN training. The method achieves comparable or superior detection accuracy to ANN-SNN conversion methods with drastically fewer time steps and demonstrates strong performance on both static and event-based datasets, paving the way for efficient neuromorphic deployment.

f23f624836db8b43953984d0832a0afd3bec6001.title: Differential Privacy Mechanisms in Neural Tangent Kernel Regression
f23f624836db8b43953984d0832a0afd3bec6001.research_question: How can differential privacy mechanisms be effectively integrated into neural tangent kernel (NTK) regression to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees while maintaining high utility in practical machine learning applications?
f23f624836db8b43953984d0832a0afd3bec6001.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by carefully designing and applying differential privacy mechanisms—specifically, the Gaussian Sampling Mechanism for kernel matrices and the truncated Laplace mechanism for kernel functions—NTK regression can achieve strong (ε, δ)-differential privacy guarantees without significant loss in predictive accuracy.
f23f624836db8b43953984d0832a0afd3bec6001.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a differentially private NTK regression framework by introducing two key privacy-preserving mechanisms. First, a Gaussian Sampling Mechanism is applied to the NTK kernel matrix to add a positive semi-definite noise matrix, ensuring that the privatized kernel matrix remains positive semi-definite, which is crucial for the stability and correctness of kernel regression. Second, the truncated Laplace mechanism is used to privatize the kernel function K(x, X), protecting sensitive information in the input data. The approach leverages the post-processing and composition lemmas of differential privacy to guarantee that the entire regression process, including the computation of regression coefficients and predictions, satisfies (ε, δ)-DP. Theoretical analysis is conducted to provide both privacy and utility guarantees, quantifying the trade-off between privacy budget and prediction accuracy.
f23f624836db8b43953984d0832a0afd3bec6001.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the CIFAR-10 image classification dataset, a standard benchmark in machine learning, to empirically validate the proposed differentially private NTK regression method. The experimental setup will involve training NTK regression models with and without privacy mechanisms, comparing their test accuracy under varying privacy budgets (values of ε and δ). Baseline comparisons will include non-private NTK regression and potentially other differentially private regression methods if available. Evaluation metrics will focus on classification accuracy and empirical privacy loss, with additional analysis of the utility-privacy trade-off as privacy parameters vary.
f23f624836db8b43953984d0832a0afd3bec6001.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first rigorous framework for achieving differential privacy in NTK regression, combining the Gaussian Sampling Mechanism for positive semi-definite kernel privatization and the truncated Laplace mechanism for kernel function privacy. The method provides formal, provable guarantees for both privacy and utility, bridging the gap between modern deep learning analysis frameworks and practical privacy-preserving machine learning. This approach enables NTK regression to be applied in sensitive domains where user data privacy is paramount, without incurring prohibitive accuracy losses.

f253aae5222d82297f8e274abdca48247abb89d9.title: Where We Are and What We're Looking At: Query Based Worldwide Image Geo-localization Using Hierarchies and Scenes
f253aae5222d82297f8e274abdca48247abb89d9.research_question: How can global image geo-localization be improved by leveraging hierarchical geographic structures and scene-specific visual cues, and how can evaluation datasets be designed to minimize landmark and social media biases?
f253aae5222d82297f8e274abdca48247abb89d9.hypothesis: Learning separate feature representations for different geographic hierarchies and scene types, using a transformer-based architecture with hierarchy- and scene-specific queries, will significantly improve the accuracy and robustness of worldwide image geo-localization, especially on unbiased, real-world datasets.
f253aae5222d82297f8e274abdca48247abb89d9.proposed_method: A novel end-to-end transformer-based framework will be developed for global image geo-localization. The method will segment the Earth's surface into hierarchical S2 cells, each representing a class at a specific geographic granularity. For each input image, a Swin Transformer encoder will extract patch features, which will then be processed by a two-stage decoder: a hierarchy-independent decoder followed by a hierarchy-dependent decoder. Learned latent queries will be initialized for each combination of geographic hierarchy and scene type, with scene labels derived from a pre-trained Places2 classifier. Cross-attention mechanisms will be used to allow these queries to extract features relevant to their assigned hierarchy and scene, and separate feed-forward networks will be used for each hierarchy in the hierarchy-dependent decoder. During inference, the scene with the highest confidence will be selected, and the corresponding queries will be used to predict class probabilities at each hierarchy, which are then combined multiplicatively to produce a final location estimate.
f253aae5222d82297f8e274abdca48247abb89d9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the MediaEval Placing Task 2016 (MP-16) dataset for training, which consists of 4.72 million geo-tagged images from YFCC100M. Evaluation will be performed on five datasets: Im2GPS, Im2GPS3k, YFCC26k, YFCC4k, and a newly proposed Google-World-Streets-15k dataset designed to reduce landmark and social media biases by sampling images from Google Streetview across 193 countries. Baselines will include prior state-of-the-art methods such as PlaNet, CPlaNet, ISNs, and TransLocator. Evaluation metrics will include geo-localization accuracy at multiple distance thresholds (1km, 25km, 200km, 750km, 2500km). Ablation studies will be conducted on decoder depth, encoder type, scene prediction strategy, and the number of hierarchy-dependent layers. TenCrop augmentation will be used during evaluation to improve robustness.
f253aae5222d82297f8e274abdca48247abb89d9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first transformer decoder architecture for worldwide image geo-localization that produces multiple sets of features per image, tailored to both geographic hierarchy and scene type, without requiring separate networks for each scene. The method leverages hierarchical cross-attention and hierarchy-dependent decoding to learn specialized features for each hierarchy and scene. A new, globally distributed testing dataset (Google-World-Streets-15k) is introduced to address biases present in existing benchmarks. The approach claims significant improvements over previous state-of-the-art methods across multiple datasets and provides qualitative analysis demonstrating the interpretability and specificity of learned features.

f29f8b8aa2b7e608199b65d3cf751969d4024132.title: Physics of Language Models: Part 3.1, Knowledge Storage and Extraction
f29f8b8aa2b7e608199b65d3cf751969d4024132.research_question: How do large language models store and extract factual knowledge from training data, and what factors in pretraining data influence their ability to answer knowledge-based questions accurately and robustly?
f29f8b8aa2b7e608199b65d3cf751969d4024132.hypothesis: Knowledge stored in language models during pretraining is only reliably extractable via question answering if the pretraining data is sufficiently augmented with diverse representations (e.g., paraphrasing, sentence shuffling, translations); otherwise, knowledge may be memorized but not accessible for extraction, regardless of subsequent instruction fine-tuning.
f29f8b8aa2b7e608199b65d3cf751969d4024132.proposed_method: A controlled experimental framework will be developed using large-scale synthetic and near-real biography datasets, each containing multiple factual attributes per individual. Language models based on autoregressive transformer architectures (e.g., GPT2, Llama) will be pretrained on these datasets under varying conditions of knowledge augmentation, such as multiplicity (multiple paraphrased entries per individual), sentence permutation, and pronoun replacement with full names. After pretraining, models will be fine-tuned on question-answer (QA) pairs for a subset of individuals and evaluated on their ability to answer out-of-distribution QAs for unseen individuals. Probing techniques, including (nearly) linear probing, will be employed to analyze how knowledge is encoded in model embeddings and to correlate encoding structure with extractability. Comparative experiments will also be conducted with encoder-only (BERT-like) models to assess architectural differences in knowledge extraction.
f29f8b8aa2b7e608199b65d3cf751969d4024132.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize two primary datasets: a synthetic biography dataset (bioS) with 100,000 individuals and a near-real dataset (bioR) generated by prompting Llama to create diverse biographies. Each biography encodes six factual attributes, and various augmentations (multiplicity, permutation, fullname replacement) will be systematically applied. Models will be evaluated using QA accuracy, defined as the proportion of exact matches between generated answers and ground-truth attributes, with a focus on out-of-distribution generalization (i.e., answering questions about individuals whose QAs were not seen during fine-tuning). Baselines will include majority guessing and models trained without augmentation. Both full and LoRA-based fine-tuning will be tested, and results will be compared across different model sizes and architectures (GPT2, Llama, BERT). Additional analyses will include the effect of augmenting only a subset of the data (e.g., 'celebrity' individuals) and the impact of introducing QA-like data during pretraining versus only at fine-tuning.
f29f8b8aa2b7e608199b65d3cf751969d4024132.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a rigorous, controlled experimental setup to disentangle memorization from true knowledge extraction in language models, leveraging synthetic data to eliminate confounding data contamination effects. It systematically demonstrates the necessity and effectiveness of knowledge augmentation (e.g., paraphrasing, permutation, translation) for enabling robust knowledge extraction, and provides mechanistic insight via probing techniques that reveal how augmentation influences the linear encoding of knowledge in model embeddings. The proposal also highlights practical recommendations for industrial-scale LLM pretraining, including the use of auxiliary models for data rewriting and the early incorporation of instruction-finetuning data, which have not been previously formalized or empirically validated at this scale.

f2b0017ddd77fa38760a18145e63553105a1a236.title: The Flan Collection: Designing Data and Methods for Effective Instruction Tuning
f2b0017ddd77fa38760a18145e63553105a1a236.research_question: How can the design of data collections and instruction tuning methods be optimized to improve the generalization and efficiency of large language models across a wide range of NLP tasks?
f2b0017ddd77fa38760a18145e63553105a1a236.hypothesis: Incorporating a diverse and balanced mixture of prompt types (zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought), scaling the number and diversity of tasks, enriching tasks via input inversion, and carefully balancing data sources during instruction tuning will significantly enhance the performance and efficiency of large language models on both seen and unseen tasks.
f2b0017ddd77fa38760a18145e63553105a1a236.proposed_method: A comprehensive instruction tuning framework will be developed that integrates a large, diverse collection of NLP tasks, combining datasets such as Flan2021, P3++, Super-Natural Instructions, and additional reasoning, dialog, and program synthesis datasets. The method will employ a mixture of prompt types—zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought—during training, with systematic ablation studies to determine the optimal mixture ratios. Task enrichment will be achieved by inverting input-output pairs to generate new task variants, thereby increasing data diversity. Mixture balancing techniques will be applied to ensure that no single data source dominates, optimizing the weighting of different task sources. The approach will be implemented using a consistent model architecture (e.g., T5-XL) to enable fair comparisons and controlled ablations.
f2b0017ddd77fa38760a18145e63553105a1a236.experiment_details: Experiments will involve fine-tuning T5-XL (3B parameters) language models on the proposed instruction tuning collection, with controlled ablations to isolate the effects of mixed prompt settings, input inversion, and mixture balancing. Evaluation will be conducted on a suite of 'Held-In' tasks (included in training), 'Held-Out' tasks (such as MMLU and BIG-Bench Hard), and chain-of-thought benchmarks, using metrics like accuracy across zero-shot and few-shot settings. Baselines will include models trained on previous instruction tuning collections (Flan2021, P3++, Super-Natural Instructions, OPT-IML) and non-instruction-tuned models. Additional experiments will assess the efficiency and convergence speed of instruction-tuned models as starting points for single-task fine-tuning, comparing against conventional fine-tuning from pretrained checkpoints.
f2b0017ddd77fa38760a18145e63553105a1a236.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified, extensible collection of instruction tuning datasets, templates, and methods, with systematic analysis of design decisions such as prompt mixture, task scaling, input inversion, and data source balancing. The approach demonstrates that training with mixed prompt types yields superior performance across all evaluation settings, and that task enrichment and mixture balancing are critical yet underexplored factors. The resulting instruction-tuned models are shown to outperform prior public collections and serve as more computationally efficient starting points for downstream applications. All resources, including data generation code and templates, will be made publicly available to accelerate open research in instruction tuning.

f2d0f3d47ae850f49a58f4977393bd0025af4bec.title: HybridFlow: A Flexible and Efficient RLHF Framework
f2d0f3d47ae850f49a58f4977393bd0025af4bec.research_question: How can reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) workflows for large language model (LLM) alignment be represented and executed in a manner that is both flexible and efficient, accommodating diverse RLHF algorithms, heterogeneous model workloads, and scalable distributed computation?
f2d0f3d47ae850f49a58f4977393bd0025af4bec.hypothesis: A hybrid framework that combines single-controller and multi-controller paradigms, together with hierarchical APIs and optimized model/data placement, will enable more flexible, modular, and efficient RLHF workflows than existing systems, reducing overhead and improving throughput across a range of RLHF algorithms and cluster configurations.
f2d0f3d47ae850f49a58f4977393bd0025af4bec.proposed_method: A hierarchical hybrid programming model will be developed, combining a single-controller paradigm for inter-node coordination and a multi-controller paradigm for intra-node distributed computation. This model will provide modular APIs that encapsulate distributed computation, data dependencies, and parallelism strategies for each model (actor, critic, reference, reward) in the RLHF dataflow. A set of transfer protocols will be designed to abstract and automate data resharding between models with differing parallelism configurations. A 3D-HybridEngine will be implemented to enable efficient, zero-redundancy model resharding between actor training and generation phases, minimizing memory and communication overhead. An auto-mapping algorithm will be created to optimize device placement and parallelism strategies for each model, maximizing resource utilization and throughput.
f2d0f3d47ae850f49a58f4977393bd0025af4bec.experiment_details: Extensive experiments will be conducted comparing the proposed framework against state-of-the-art RLHF systems such as DeepSpeed-Chat, OpenRLHF, and NeMo-Aligner. The evaluation will cover a range of RLHF algorithms (e.g., PPO, Safe-RLHF, ReMax), model sizes (from 7B to 70B parameters), and cluster scales. Datasets will include standard RLHF benchmarks and human preference datasets. Baselines will be evaluated under equivalent hardware and parallelism settings. Key metrics will include throughput (samples/sec), memory usage, communication overhead, and flexibility in supporting diverse RLHF workflows and model placements. The experimental setup will also assess the ease of implementing new RLHF algorithms and the impact of the auto-mapping algorithm on device utilization.
f2d0f3d47ae850f49a58f4977393bd0025af4bec.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a hybrid programming model that decouples intra-node distributed computation from inter-node data transfer, enabling flexible and modular RLHF workflow construction. The 3D-HybridEngine provides zero-redundancy, efficient model resharding between training and generation, a capability not present in existing RLHF systems. The auto-mapping algorithm automates optimal device placement and parallelism configuration for heterogeneous RLHF workloads. The framework supports a broader range of RLHF algorithms and parallelism strategies than prior art, with demonstrated improvements in throughput (up to 20.57x) and resource efficiency.

f2d952a183dfb0a1e031b8a3f535d9f8423d7a6e.title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models
