f2d952a183dfb0a1e031b8a3f535d9f8423d7a6e.research_question: How can a single reinforcement learning algorithm be developed to robustly master a wide variety of tasks across diverse domains, without the need for domain-specific tuning or human-provided data?
f2d952a183dfb0a1e031b8a3f535d9f8423d7a6e.hypothesis: A reinforcement learning agent equipped with a learned world model, combined with robust normalization, balancing, and transformation techniques, can achieve state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of domains using a single configuration, even in environments with sparse rewards and high diversity.
f2d952a183dfb0a1e031b8a3f535d9f8423d7a6e.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a general reinforcement learning framework based on world models, specifically utilizing a Recurrent State-Space Model (RSSM) to encode sensory inputs into compact, stochastic representations. The world model predicts future representations, rewards, and episode continuation flags, enabling the agent to plan by imagining future scenarios. The approach employs three neural networks: a world model for environment prediction, a critic for value estimation, and an actor for policy optimization. Robustness across domains is achieved through techniques such as symlog transformations for input normalization, symlog squared error and symexp twohot losses for stable prediction of targets of varying magnitudes, and free bits for loss balancing. The actor and critic are trained on imagined trajectories generated by the world model, with return normalization and entropy regularization to ensure effective exploration and exploitation across tasks with varying reward structures.
f2d952a183dfb0a1e031b8a3f535d9f8423d7a6e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across eight diverse domains encompassing over 150 tasks, including benchmarks such as Atari (57 games, 200M steps), ProcGen (16 games, 50M steps), DMLab (30 tasks, 100M steps), Minecraft (1 task, 100M steps), Atari100k (26 games, 400K steps), Proprio Control (18 tasks, 500K steps), Visual Control (20 tasks, 1M steps), and BSuite (23 environments, 468 configurations). The method will be evaluated against specialized expert algorithms and strong baselines such as PPO, MuZero, Rainbow, IMPALA, R2D2+, D4PG, DMPO, MPO, DrQ-v2, CURL, Boot DQN, and others, using fixed hyperparameters across all domains. Evaluation metrics will include average return, data efficiency, and the fraction of agents achieving key milestones (e.g., diamond collection in Minecraft). Ablation studies will assess the contribution of individual robustness techniques and learning signals, while scaling experiments will investigate the impact of model size and replay ratio on performance and data efficiency.
f2d952a183dfb0a1e031b8a3f535d9f8423d7a6e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach claims to be the first general reinforcement learning algorithm to achieve state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of domains with a single configuration, eliminating the need for domain-specific tuning. It introduces robust normalization and loss balancing techniques that enable stable learning across tasks with vastly different input and reward scales. The method demonstrates, for the first time, the ability to solve the challenging Minecraft diamond collection task from scratch without human data or curricula. Additionally, the approach provides predictable scaling of performance with increased model size and computational resources, making reinforcement learning broadly applicable and reproducible.

f2d95572cde472fedeaaae78c27b51304fe19ef2.title: R.I.P.: Better Models by Survival of the Fittest Prompts
f2d95572cde472fedeaaae78c27b51304fe19ef2.research_question: How can the quality of training prompts for large language models be automatically evaluated and filtered to improve model performance and alignment, particularly in instruction-following and preference optimization settings?
f2d95572cde472fedeaaae78c27b51304fe19ef2.hypothesis: 1) Low-quality prompts are likely to produce low-quality responses, as measured by the quality and length of rejected responses in preference pairs. 2) Low-quality prompts are likely to produce responses with higher variance, leading to larger reward gaps between chosen and rejected responses.
f2d95572cde472fedeaaae78c27b51304fe19ef2.proposed_method: A novel data filtering framework, Rejecting Instruction Preferences (RIP), is proposed for curating high-quality prompts in instruction fine-tuning via preference optimization. The approach operates by analyzing preference pairs consisting of prompts and their chosen and rejected responses, utilizing three key metrics: the reward of the rejected response, the length of the rejected response, and the reward gap between chosen and rejected responses. Thresholds for each metric are selected (e.g., lower-bound for reward and length, upper-bound for reward gap) to filter out prompts associated with low-quality or high-variance responses. The method is also extended to generate synthetic data (Self-RIP) by using RIP-filtered prompts as seeds for few-shot prompt generation, followed by an additional round of RIP filtering on the generated synthetic prompts. The filtered prompts, whether human-written or synthetic, are then used to fine-tune language models using preference optimization algorithms such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO).
f2d95572cde472fedeaaae78c27b51304fe19ef2.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using Llama 3.1-8B-Instruct and Llama 3.3-70B-Instruct models, fine-tuned on both human-written (WildChat, HelpSteer2) and synthetic datasets. The filtering effectiveness of RIP is compared against various baselines, including prompt-based (InsTag Complexity/Diversity, LLM-as-Prompt-Judge), prompt-and-chosen-response-based (Instruction-Following Difficulty, Perplexity), and chosen-and-rejected-response-based (Jaccard Similarity) methods. Evaluation is performed on standard instruction-following benchmarks: AlpacaEval2 (LC Win Rate), Arena-Hard (Win Score), and WildBench (Score), using both model-based and human-based reward annotations. The impact of filtering thresholds, model scale, and weak-to-strong generalizability (using smaller models for filtering larger models' data) is systematically assessed. Ablation studies examine the contributions of seed selection and post-filtering in Self-RIP. Safety and prompt quality are further analyzed using GPT-4 and Llama3.1-405B-Instruct as external judges.
f2d95572cde472fedeaaae78c27b51304fe19ef2.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a prompt-response-pair-based filtering mechanism that leverages rejected response quality and reward gap as indicators of prompt quality, a perspective not previously explored in depth for preference optimization datasets. The approach demonstrates substantial improvements over existing filtering heuristics and model-based quality classifiers, achieving state-of-the-art results on multiple instruction-following benchmarks. The Self-RIP extension enables the creation of high-quality synthetic datasets that outperform both unfiltered and standard self-instructed data. The methodology is shown to be effective across different model sizes and in weak-to-strong generalization settings, and provides a principled, scalable solution for data curation in LLM training pipelines.

f2ef514a1815764ab289b7d64e33039a5e7a0297.title: FD-CAM: Improving Faithfulness and Discriminability of Visual Explanation for CNNs
f2ef514a1815764ab289b7d64e33039a5e7a0297.research_question: How can the faithfulness and discriminability of visual explanations for convolutional neural networks (CNNs) be simultaneously improved in class activation map (CAM)-based techniques?
f2ef514a1815764ab289b7d64e33039a5e7a0297.hypothesis: A novel CAM weighting scheme that combines grouped channel switching-based score perturbations with gradient-based weights will yield more faithful and discriminative visual explanations for CNNs than existing gradient- or score-based CAM methods.
f2ef514a1815764ab289b7d64e33039a5e7a0297.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a new CAM weighting scheme, termed FD-CAM, that integrates both gradient-based and score-based weighting strategies to enhance the quality of visual explanations. First, the method computes similarity groups for each channel in the target convolutional layer using cosine similarity, identifying channels with highly similar features. A grouped channel switching operation is then performed: for each channel, all channels in its similarity group are switched on or off together, and the resulting change in the class prediction score is recorded as the score-based weight. Both switch-on and switch-off operations are averaged to provide a robust importance estimate for each channel. These improved score-based weights are then combined with conventional gradient-based weights (from Grad-CAM), using a min-max normalization and an exponential scaling function with a bias term, to form the final channel weights. The final CAM is generated by linearly combining the upsampled activation maps with these composite weights and applying a ReLU activation.
f2ef514a1815764ab289b7d64e33039a5e7a0297.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using pre-trained VGG16 models on the ILSVRC2015 validation set (2,000 images) for qualitative and quantitative evaluation, and the VOC2007 validation set for discriminability assessment. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art CAM-based visual explanation techniques, including gradient-based (Grad-CAM, Grad-CAM++, XGrad-CAM), score-based (Score-CAM, Ablation-CAM), and region-based (XRAI, Integrated Gradients) baselines. Evaluation metrics will include the area under the curve (AUC) for deletion and insertion tests (measuring faithfulness), and the pointing game accuracy (measuring discriminability) across all classes. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of grouped channel switching, switch-on/off strategies, and different weight combination schemes. All experiments will be implemented in PyTorch and run on an NVIDIA TITAN RTX GPU.
f2ef514a1815764ab289b7d64e33039a5e7a0297.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel grouped channel switching operation for CAM weighting, which perturbs groups of similar channels rather than individual ones to yield more faithful and discriminative score-based weights. It further innovates by combining these enhanced score-based weights with traditional gradient-based weights through a new normalization and exponential scaling scheme, resulting in improved visual explanations. The method claims to outperform existing CAM techniques in both faithfulness and discriminability, as demonstrated by comprehensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations and ablation studies.

f32502fa8147320b48be351360de43dd22b0006f.title: Mixture of Experts Meets Prompt-Based Continual Learning
f32502fa8147320b48be351360de43dd22b0006f.research_question: How can continual learning in deep neural networks be improved to prevent catastrophic forgetting, particularly in prompt-based approaches, while maintaining parameter efficiency and strong within-task prediction accuracy?
f32502fa8147320b48be351360de43dd22b0006f.hypothesis: Incorporating a non-linear residual gating mechanism into the prompt-based continual learning framework will enhance sample efficiency, improve within-task prediction, and achieve superior continual learning performance compared to existing linear gating prompt-based methods.
f32502fa8147320b48be351360de43dd22b0006f.proposed_method: A novel gating mechanism, termed Non-linear Residual Gates (NoRGa), will be integrated into the prompt-based continual learning paradigm, specifically within the prefix-tuning approach for Vision Transformers. NoRGa modifies the gating score functions of newly introduced task-specific experts by adding a non-linear activation (such as tanh, sigmoid, or GELU) and a residual connection to the original linear gating. The score function for each prefix expert will thus be a sum of the linear component and a scaled non-linear transformation of the same input, with learnable scalar factors controlling the contribution of the non-linear term. This modification is designed to accelerate parameter estimation and improve sample efficiency without increasing the number of learnable parameters per task. The method will be implemented by directly modifying the attention matrices in the multi-head self-attention layers to include the NoRGa gating for prompt vectors.
f32502fa8147320b48be351360de43dd22b0006f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on widely used class-incremental learning benchmarks, including Split CIFAR-100, Split ImageNet-R, Split CUB-200, and 5-Datasets, to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Multiple pre-trained Vision Transformer models will be used as backbones, including supervised (Sup-21K) and self-supervised (iBOT-21K, iBOT-1K, DINO-1K, MoCo-1K) pretraining paradigms. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art prompt-based continual learning baselines such as L2P, DualPrompt, S-Prompt, CODA-Prompt, and HiDe-Prompt, as well as parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods like LoRA and Adapters. Evaluation metrics will include Final Average Accuracy (FA), Cumulative Average Accuracy (CA), and Average Forgetting Measure (FM), with emphasis on FA and CA. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of different non-linear activation functions within NoRGa.
f32502fa8147320b48be351360de43dd22b0006f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new theoretical perspective connecting self-attention and mixture of experts, reframing prefix-tuning as the addition of new experts to a pre-trained mixture of experts model. Building on this insight, the Non-linear Residual Gates (NoRGa) mechanism is proposed to address the sample efficiency limitations of existing linear gating prompt-based methods. NoRGa is claimed to enhance continual learning performance while preserving parameter efficiency, and theoretical analysis is provided to justify its statistical advantages. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks and pretraining settings, with robustness to the choice of non-linear activation function.

f32bcc2155997110a7905da050df4c8404867b24.title: Improve Mathematical Reasoning in Language Models by Automated Process Supervision
f32bcc2155997110a7905da050df4c8404867b24.research_question: How can the mathematical reasoning abilities of large language models be improved through scalable, automated process supervision, particularly for complex multi-step problems?
f32bcc2155997110a7905da050df4c8404867b24.hypothesis: Automated, high-quality process supervision data collected via a novel divide-and-conquer Monte Carlo Tree Search algorithm will enable the training of more effective Process Reward Models, thereby significantly enhancing the mathematical reasoning performance of large language models without requiring human annotation.
f32bcc2155997110a7905da050df4c8404867b24.proposed_method: A new divide-and-conquer Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) algorithm, OmegaPRM, will be developed to efficiently generate process supervision data for mathematical reasoning tasks. The method constructs a state-action tree for each question, where nodes represent partial chain-of-thought solutions and edges represent reasoning steps. Binary search is used within the tree to rapidly locate the first error in a reasoning chain, reducing the time complexity of error localization from O(kM) to O(k log M), where M is the number of steps. All rollouts and intermediate states are stored, enabling the reuse of rollouts for multiple training examples and prioritizing high-value rollouts during tree traversal. The resulting process annotations are used to train Process Reward Models (PRMs) with pointwise soft labels, hard labels, or pairwise preference objectives.
f32bcc2155997110a7905da050df4c8404867b24.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the MATH dataset, using the established train/test splits (12K training, 500 test problems). The OmegaPRM algorithm will be used to generate over 1.5 million process supervision annotations without human intervention. Instruction-tuned Gemini Pro and pretrained Gemma2 27B models will serve as the base LLMs, with PRMs trained from their respective checkpoints. Evaluation will be performed on MATH500 and GSM8K benchmarks, using PRM-weighted majority voting as the main metric. Baselines will include PRM800K (human-annotated), Math-Shepherd (automatic, brute-force), and majority vote approaches. Hyperparameters for tree search, rollout sampling (k=8), and PRM training will be systematically set and reported. Performance will be measured as the percentage of problems solved.
f32bcc2155997110a7905da050df4c8404867b24.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully automated, scalable process supervision pipeline for training Process Reward Models, eliminating the need for costly human annotation. The OmegaPRM algorithm leverages a divide-and-conquer MCTS strategy with binary search to efficiently and accurately locate reasoning errors, enabling the creation of the largest and highest-quality process supervision dataset to date. The method demonstrates superior performance over both human-annotated and prior automated baselines, and is cost-effective in terms of both computation and annotation. The approach also introduces a flexible step division strategy for process annotation and explores multiple PRM training objectives.

f3460dc3ae5cfd41099d576a3bb77411e1fc2e3f.title: A General Theoretical Paradigm to Understand Learning from Human Preferences
f3460dc3ae5cfd41099d576a3bb77411e1fc2e3f.research_question: How can a general theoretical framework be developed to better understand and improve learning from human preferences, particularly in reinforcement learning settings, while addressing the limitations of current practical algorithms such as RLHF and DPO?
f3460dc3ae5cfd41099d576a3bb77411e1fc2e3f.hypothesis: A general objective for learning from human preferences, expressed directly in terms of pairwise preferences and parameterized by a non-decreasing mapping, will provide a more robust and theoretically grounded approach than existing methods, overcoming issues such as overfitting and weak regularization present in RLHF and DPO.
f3460dc3ae5cfd41099d576a3bb77411e1fc2e3f.proposed_method: A new general objective, termed Ψ-preference optimisation (ΨPO), will be formulated for learning from human preferences. This objective will maximize a non-linear function of pairwise preference probabilities, balanced by a KL-regularization term to maintain proximity to a reference policy. Special cases of ΨPO, including RLHF and DPO, will be analyzed to identify their theoretical limitations, particularly regarding overfitting and regularization failure. A specific instantiation, Identity-PO (IPO), will be developed by setting the non-decreasing mapping Ψ to the identity function, resulting in a bounded and convex objective that avoids the problematic assumptions of the Bradley-Terry model and enables direct optimization from empirical preference data. An efficient optimization procedure will be derived for IPO, including a sampled loss function suitable for practical implementation without explicit reward modeling.
f3460dc3ae5cfd41099d576a3bb77411e1fc2e3f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in simplified contextual bandit and bandit settings, using synthetic datasets where contexts and actions are finite and preferences are either deterministic or sampled. The proposed IPO method will be compared to DPO by optimizing policies over preference datasets constructed from pairwise comparisons. Evaluation will focus on the stability and regularization behavior of the learned policies, particularly under varying regularization strengths (τ) and dataset regimes (e.g., when some actions are rarely or never preferred). Metrics will include convergence of action probabilities, policy divergence from the reference policy, and robustness to overfitting. Multiple random seeds and repeated trials will be used to ensure statistical validity, and experiments will be implemented in JAX/Flax with optimization via Adam.
f3460dc3ae5cfd41099d576a3bb77411e1fc2e3f.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified theoretical objective (ΨPO) that generalizes and subsumes RLHF and DPO as special cases, providing a new lens for analyzing and improving preference-based learning algorithms. The IPO variant offers a practical, theoretically justified method that directly optimizes from pairwise preferences without relying on reward modeling or the Bradley-Terry assumption, thereby mitigating overfitting and weak regularization issues. The work also derives a novel, efficient sampled loss function for IPO, enabling empirical optimization and demonstrating superior stability and regularization compared to DPO in illustrative examples. These contributions bridge the gap between theory and practice in learning from human preferences and lay the groundwork for scalable application to more complex domains.

f349e5e8f0d18c948c1ffd92d3791db2b0ba2e55.title: Data Filtering Networks
f349e5e8f0d18c948c1ffd92d3791db2b0ba2e55.research_question: How can the process of filtering large, uncurated image-text datasets be improved to construct higher-quality training sets that enable more effective and efficient training of large-scale multimodal models?
f349e5e8f0d18c948c1ffd92d3791db2b0ba2e55.hypothesis: Training data filtering networks (DFNs) on high-quality, human-verified image-text pairs and leveraging contrastive learning techniques will result in filtering models that induce superior large-scale datasets, which in turn enable the training of state-of-the-art multimodal models with improved accuracy and efficiency compared to existing heuristic or model-based filtering approaches.
f349e5e8f0d18c948c1ffd92d3791db2b0ba2e55.proposed_method: A novel data filtering network (DFN) will be developed by training a contrastive image-text model, such as a CLIP variant, on a large, high-quality dataset of human-verified image-text pairs (e.g., HQITP-350M). The DFN will be fine-tuned on additional curated datasets (e.g., MS COCO, Flickr30k, ImageNet with templated captions) using data augmentation and weight ensembling to enhance generalization and robustness. The trained DFN will then be applied pointwise to a massive uncurated image-text pool (such as DataComp's 12.8B CommonPool or an expanded 42B pool), filtering the top percentile of samples based on the model's alignment score. The resulting induced datasets (e.g., DFN-2B, DFN-5B) will serve as training data for large-scale multimodal models (e.g., CLIP ViT-L/14, ViT-H/14), with the filtering process and model training conducted in a scalable, parallelizable pipeline.
f349e5e8f0d18c948c1ffd92d3791db2b0ba2e55.experiment_details: Experiments will involve filtering large-scale candidate pools (DataComp medium: 128M, large: 1.28B, xlarge: 12.8B, and extended pools up to 42B samples) using the proposed DFN, and then training CLIP models of various sizes (ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, ViT-L/14, ViT-H/14) on the induced datasets. Baselines will include datasets filtered by existing methods such as LAION-2B, DataComp-1B, OpenAI WIT-400M, and MetaCLIP. Evaluation will be conducted using the DataComp benchmark suite, which includes 38 zero-shot classification and retrieval tasks (e.g., ImageNet, ImageNet distribution shifts, VTAB, COCO, Flickr, WinoGAViL). Metrics will include zero-shot transfer accuracy (e.g., ImageNet top-1), average performance across tasks, and compute efficiency (accuracy vs. training cost). Additional ablations will examine the impact of DFN training data quality, model architecture, fine-tuning, and augmentation strategies.
f349e5e8f0d18c948c1ffd92d3791db2b0ba2e55.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified, scalable, and model-driven approach to dataset filtering using data filtering networks trained on high-quality data, moving beyond heuristic or fixed-model filtering pipelines. It demonstrates that filtering network quality is distinct from standard downstream task accuracy, and that even smaller models trained on high-quality data can outperform larger, widely-used models as filters. The method enables the construction of billion-scale, state-of-the-art image-text datasets that yield superior multimodal models in terms of both accuracy and compute efficiency. The approach also simplifies the dataset construction pipeline, reduces computational costs, and provides a reproducible recipe for democratizing access to high-quality training data by leveraging only publicly available datasets.

f3632a7f829a9686c6f6b57131d2d1e62f798dac.title: Fast Axiomatic Attribution for Neural Networks
f3632a7f829a9686c6f6b57131d2d1e62f798dac.research_question: How can high-quality, axiomatic feature attributions be computed efficiently for deep neural networks, enabling practical and effective use of attribution priors during training to mitigate dependence on spurious correlations and unwanted features?
f3632a7f829a9686c6f6b57131d2d1e62f798dac.hypothesis: Nonnegatively homogeneous deep neural networks (DNNs) can be constructed such that they admit closed-form, axiomatic feature attributions that are both computationally efficient and of high quality, thereby enabling effective training with attribution priors without significant loss in predictive accuracy.
f3632a7f829a9686c6f6b57131d2d1e62f798dac.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed that focuses on a special class of deep neural networks, termed nonnegatively homogeneous DNNs (X-DNNs), which are constructed by removing the bias term from each layer of regular DNN architectures. The proposed method leverages the mathematical property of nonnegative homogeneity to derive a closed-form solution for Integrated Gradients, allowing the computation of axiomatic feature attributions with only a single forward and backward pass. The resulting attribution method, called X-Gradient, is formally proven to satisfy all desirable axioms for feature attribution, including sensitivity, implementation invariance, completeness, linearity, symmetry preservation, and nonnegative homogeneity. The approach is compatible with a wide range of popular architectures (e.g., AlexNet, VGGNet, ResNet, MLPs with ReLU activations) by simply omitting bias terms, and is designed to be easily integrated into existing training pipelines for efficient inclusion of attribution priors.
f3632a7f829a9686c6f6b57131d2d1e62f798dac.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both image classification and tabular data domains. For image classification, models such as AlexNet, VGG16, and ResNet-50 (and their X-DNN variants) will be trained and evaluated on the ImageNet dataset, with top-5 accuracy and attribution quality metrics (e.g., Keep Positive Mask, Keep Negative Mask, Keep Absolute Mask, Remove Absolute Mask) adapted from Lundberg et al. to assess attribution effectiveness. Attribution methods to be compared include Integrated Gradients, Expected Gradients (with varying numbers of reference samples), Input Gradient, and the proposed X-Gradient. For tabular data, the NHANES I dataset will be used with MLPs to benchmark the effectiveness of attribution priors in producing sparser, more generalizable models, using ROC-AUC as the primary evaluation metric. Computational efficiency will be measured in terms of gradient calls and training time, and qualitative robustness to input contrast changes will be assessed for vision models.
f3632a7f829a9686c6f6b57131d2d1e62f798dac.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a theoretically grounded and computationally efficient approach for computing high-quality, axiomatic feature attributions in DNNs by leveraging nonnegative homogeneity. It establishes a new theoretical connection between Input Gradient and Integrated Gradients for this class of networks, and demonstrates that bias removal is a simple yet effective architectural modification with minimal impact on predictive accuracy. The X-Gradient method matches or exceeds the attribution quality of state-of-the-art methods while reducing computational cost by one to two orders of magnitude, enabling practical training with attribution priors. The approach is broadly applicable to many popular DNN architectures and provides improved robustness to input contrast changes, supporting more reliable and interpretable model behavior.

f36b09be6b05286e86ae06b2bc4e013848210947.title: Estimation error analysis of deep learning on the regression problem on the variable exponent Besov space
f36b09be6b05286e86ae06b2bc4e013848210947.research_question: How can the generalization and estimation error of deep learning methods be theoretically characterized for nonparametric regression problems where the target function resides in a variable exponent Besov space, and how does this compare to linear estimators?
f36b09be6b05286e86ae06b2bc4e013848210947.hypothesis: Deep learning methods, due to their adaptive approximation capabilities, will achieve improved estimation and approximation error rates over linear estimators when the underlying function class exhibits spatially inhomogeneous smoothness, as modeled by variable exponent Besov spaces.
f36b09be6b05286e86ae06b2bc4e013848210947.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the approximation and estimation errors of deep neural networks, specifically ReLU networks, when applied to regression problems where the target function belongs to a variable exponent Besov space. The approach will first establish new approximation theory results for variable exponent Besov spaces using B-spline basis expansions, deriving both lower and upper bounds for the approximation error. The analysis will then extend to the estimation error of deep learning by leveraging empirical risk minimization and covering number arguments, balancing model complexity and approximation error. The adaptivity of deep learning will be quantified by examining how the error rates depend on the spatial distribution of smoothness, particularly when regions of low smoothness are small and the ambient dimension is high.
f36b09be6b05286e86ae06b2bc4e013848210947.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be validated through rigorous mathematical analysis rather than empirical experiments. Error rates will be derived in terms of the number of neural network units (N), sample size (n), smoothness parameters, and domain dimension (d). Comparisons will be made to established minimax rates for both adaptive (deep learning) and non-adaptive (linear) estimators, including least squares, Nadaraya-Watson, and kernel ridge regression. The evaluation metric will be the worst-case estimation error measured in the L2 norm over the probability distribution of the inputs, with explicit convergence rates and poly-logarithmic factors analyzed.
f36b09be6b05286e86ae06b2bc4e013848210947.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first comprehensive approximation theory for variable exponent Besov spaces using B-spline bases, establishing both lower and upper bounds for approximation errors in this setting. It further derives new upper bounds for the estimation error of deep neural networks on these spaces, explicitly quantifying the benefits of adaptivity in deep learning. The analysis demonstrates that deep learning achieves superior convergence rates compared to linear estimators, especially when the region of low smoothness is small and the dimension is large. These results provide new theoretical insights into the adaptivity and generalization capabilities of deep learning in highly inhomogeneous function spaces.

f374c4d9407566e349ab861c5d51720b211e37f9.title: DreamVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model Dreamed with Comprehensive World Knowledge
f374c4d9407566e349ab861c5d51720b211e37f9.research_question: How can the integration of comprehensive world knowledge forecasting, including dynamic, spatial, and semantic information, improve the generalization, reasoning, and performance of vision-language-action models for robotic manipulation tasks?
f374c4d9407566e349ab861c5d51720b211e37f9.hypothesis: Incorporating explicit predictions of dynamic regions, depth maps, and high-level semantic features as intermediate world knowledge will provide more concise and relevant look-ahead cues for action planning, resulting in improved multi-step reasoning, generalization, and task success rates in both simulated and real-world robotic manipulation settings.
f374c4d9407566e349ab861c5d51720b211e37f9.proposed_method: A novel vision-language-action (VLA) framework will be developed that recasts the VLA paradigm as a perception–prediction–action loop. The method will encode multimodal inputs—natural language instructions, visual observations, and proprioceptive states—using modality-specific encoders (e.g., CLIP for text, Masked Autoencoder for vision, and convolutional/FC layers for state). Special learnable <dream> queries will be appended to the embeddings, each dedicated to predicting a specific aspect of world knowledge: dynamic regions (via optical flow-based masks), depth (via monocular depth estimation or teacher supervision), and high-level semantics (via DINOv2/SAM features). A large language model backbone (GPT-2-based) will integrate these modalities using a block-wise structured attention mechanism that masks mutual attention between knowledge types, ensuring disentangled and clean representations. During training, lightweight decoders will supervise the prediction of each world knowledge type, while a denoising diffusion transformer will be used to generate action sequences from the latent action embedding, conditioned on the predicted world knowledge.
f374c4d9407566e349ab861c5d51720b211e37f9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks. The CALVIN ABC-D and LIBERO benchmarks will be used for simulation, covering long-horizon, language-conditioned manipulation with diverse environments and tasks. Real-world experiments will utilize a Franka Panda robot with dual RGB cameras and a suite of pick, place, and drawer manipulation tasks. Baselines will include state-of-the-art VLA models, models employing copilot image/video generation, and models with direct pixel-level forecasting. Evaluation metrics will include average task success rate, average consecutive task length, and per-task performance. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each knowledge type, the effect of structured attention, and the impact of query count per modality. Hyperparameters such as learning rates, batch size, and loss weights will be tuned, and models will be trained with AdamW optimizer and cosine learning rate schedules.
f374c4d9407566e349ab861c5d51720b211e37f9.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a comprehensive world knowledge forecasting mechanism that explicitly predicts dynamic regions, depth, and semantic features as intermediate reasoning steps, rather than relying on dense pixel-level forecasting or redundant frame generation. The use of block-wise structured attention ensures disentangled representations, preventing information leakage between knowledge types. The integration of a denoising diffusion transformer for action sequence generation from world knowledge embeddings further enhances multi-step reasoning and diversity in action planning. This approach is claimed to set new state-of-the-art results on established benchmarks, demonstrating superior generalization, robustness, and efficiency in both simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks.

f393aff1593c2d370ec0ae004910d18e40524967.title: Resurrecting Recurrent Neural Networks for Long Sequences
f393aff1593c2d370ec0ae004910d18e40524967.research_question: Can deep recurrent neural networks (RNNs) be designed to match the performance and computational efficiency of deep state-space models (SSMs) on long-range sequence modeling tasks?
f393aff1593c2d370ec0ae004910d18e40524967.hypothesis: With appropriate modifications to architecture, parameterization, initialization, and normalization, deep RNNs can achieve performance and efficiency comparable to state-of-the-art deep SSMs on long sequence modeling benchmarks.
f393aff1593c2d370ec0ae004910d18e40524967.proposed_method: A novel RNN architecture, termed the Linear Recurrent Unit (LRU), will be developed by systematically modifying standard deep RNNs. The approach involves removing nonlinearities from the recurrence, resulting in linear RNN layers, and interleaving these with nonlinear MLP or GLU blocks to maintain expressivity. The recurrent matrices will be reparameterized as complex-valued diagonal matrices, initialized to match the spectral properties of standard dense RNNs, and further parameterized using a stable exponential form to enforce stability and facilitate long-range reasoning. An adaptive normalization scheme will be introduced for the hidden activations, using trainable scaling factors to prevent forward-pass blow-up, especially when eigenvalues are initialized close to the unit circle. For very long sequences, the initialization of eigenvalue phases will be restricted to a small range to avoid spurious oscillatory behavior and improve generalization.
f393aff1593c2d370ec0ae004910d18e40524967.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Long Range Arena (LRA) benchmark, which includes tasks such as sequential CIFAR-10 classification, ListOps, Text, Retrieval, Pathfinder, and PathX, all designed to test long-range sequence modeling capabilities. The proposed LRU-based architecture will be compared against deep SSMs (e.g., S4, S4D, S5) and standard RNN variants (tanh, ReLU, linear) using accuracy as the primary evaluation metric. All models will be trained with 6-layer networks, residual connections, and layer/batch normalization, using the AdamW optimizer with tuned hyperparameters. Each experiment will be repeated three times to report mean and standard error. Training and inference speed, as well as the impact of each architectural modification, will be carefully ablated and analyzed.
f393aff1593c2d370ec0ae004910d18e40524967.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a principled methodology for transforming standard deep RNNs into highly performant and efficient models for long-range sequence tasks, matching the capabilities of deep SSMs. Key innovations include the use of linear recurrences with interleaved nonlinear blocks, complex diagonal parameterization with stable exponential initialization, and a novel normalization scheme for hidden activations. The work provides new theoretical and empirical insights into the origins of SSM performance, demonstrates that RNNs can achieve similar results with proper design, and offers practical guidelines for future architecture development.

f3a9437383b9de53b54069e37422256deb5f584f.title: Token Perturbation Guidance for Diffusion Models
f3a9437383b9de53b54069e37422256deb5f584f.research_question: How can diffusion models be guided to improve both unconditional and conditional generation quality and semantic alignment without requiring additional training or architectural modifications?
f3a9437383b9de53b54069e37422256deb5f584f.hypothesis: Applying norm-preserving perturbations, specifically token shuffling, directly to intermediate token representations within diffusion models can provide effective, stable, and training-free guidance signals that improve generation quality and prompt alignment for both conditional and unconditional tasks.
f3a9437383b9de53b54069e37422256deb5f584f.proposed_method: A novel guidance technique, Token Perturbation Guidance (TPG), will be developed to operate directly on the intermediate token representations in the denoiser network of diffusion models during inference. TPG introduces a norm-preserving shuffling operation, implemented as an orthonormal matrix multiplication along the token dimension, which disrupts local structure while preserving global statistics of the token features. At each denoising step, two forward passes are performed: one standard and one with token perturbation applied at selected layers using unique shuffling matrices per layer and timestep. The outputs from these passes are linearly combined, with a guidance scale parameter, to steer the denoising trajectory. This method is designed to be plug-and-play, requiring no retraining or changes to the underlying model architecture, and is applicable to both conditional and unconditional generation.
f3a9437383b9de53b54069e37422256deb5f584f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using official implementations and pre-trained checkpoints of Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL) and Stable Diffusion 2.1 as primary baselines. The evaluation will include both unconditional and conditional image generation tasks, with 30,000 samples generated per method unless otherwise specified. Baseline comparisons will include vanilla SDXL, PAG, SEG, and CFG, with all methods evaluated using their default configurations and guidance scales (TPG guidance scale fixed at 3.0). Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), sFID, Inception Score, Aesthetic Score, and CLIPScore, measured on the MS-COCO 2014 validation set. Additional ablation studies will compare different norm-preserving perturbation strategies (e.g., Sign Flip, Hadamard, Haar) to assess the effectiveness of token shuffling.
f3a9437383b9de53b54069e37422256deb5f584f.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a training-free, condition-agnostic guidance mechanism for diffusion models that operates by perturbing intermediate token representations via norm-preserving shuffling. Unlike prior approaches, TPG does not require model retraining or architectural changes and is applicable to both conditional and unconditional generation. The approach claims to bridge the gap between the effectiveness of classifier-free guidance (CFG) and existing training-free methods, achieving significant improvements in generation quality and prompt alignment. The method is also claimed to be simple to implement as a plug-and-play module and to exhibit guidance behavior closely resembling CFG in both direction and frequency content.

f3bf096ccda887b5e0a0980a74b8aee36fd7bc1b.title: Into the LAIONs Den: Investigating Hate in Multimodal Datasets
f3bf096ccda887b5e0a0980a74b8aee36fd7bc1b.research_question: How does the scale of large multimodal vision-language datasets impact the prevalence of hateful, targeted, and aggressive content, and to what extent do current filtering mechanisms effectively mitigate such harmful content in both image and text modalities?
f3bf096ccda887b5e0a0980a74b8aee36fd7bc1b.hypothesis: Increasing the scale of multimodal vision-language datasets leads to a higher prevalence of hateful, targeted, and aggressive content in the text modality, and existing image-based filtering mechanisms (such as NSFW classifiers) are insufficient to comprehensively remove harmful content present in associated alt-text descriptions.
f3bf096ccda887b5e0a0980a74b8aee36fd7bc1b.proposed_method: A comprehensive audit will be conducted on two large-scale open-source vision-language datasets of different sizes, specifically LAION-400M and LAION-2B-en, focusing on the alt-text associated with image-text pairs. The methodology involves sub-sampling a large number of image-text pairs from each dataset and analyzing the alt-text using a state-of-the-art open-source NLP toolkit (e.g., pysentimiento) to assign probabilistic scores for hateful, targeted, and aggressive speech. Two main metrics will be defined: Hate Content Rate (HCR) for each category, and an 'Any-of-the-three' HCR that flags a sample if any of the three scores exceed a defined threshold. Additionally, the relationship between text-based harmful content and image-based NSFW scores will be examined to assess the effectiveness of current filtering approaches. Statistical analyses, including confidence intervals and t-tests, will be used to compare the prevalence of harmful content across dataset scales and file shards.
f3bf096ccda887b5e0a0980a74b8aee36fd7bc1b.experiment_details: Experiments will involve sub-sampling 100,000 image-text pairs from each constituent file (parquet shard) of both LAION-400M and LAION-2B-en datasets, yielding millions of samples for analysis. The alt-texts will be processed using pysentimiento to extract probability scores for hateful, targeted, and aggressive speech, and HCR metrics will be computed at both dataset and file levels. The effectiveness of image-based NSFW filtering will be evaluated by comparing NSFW classifier outputs (using a threshold of 0.5) with the presence of harmful content in the corresponding alt-texts. Statistical significance of differences in HCR across datasets and shards will be tested using Welch's t-test, and correlations between NSFW scores and text-based toxicity will be calculated using Pearson correlation coefficients. Evaluation will focus on the prevalence of harmful content, the impact of dataset scaling, and the residual toxicity after filtering.
f3bf096ccda887b5e0a0980a74b8aee36fd7bc1b.novelty_claims: The proposed study introduces a systematic, large-scale audit of hateful, targeted, and aggressive content in the alt-text of major open-source multimodal datasets, directly quantifying the impact of dataset scaling on the prevalence of such content. It establishes and formalizes new metrics (HCR and 'Any-of-the-three' HCR) for evaluating harmful content in text, and rigorously compares the effectiveness of current image-based filtering mechanisms against text-based toxicity detection. The approach provides empirical evidence that dataset scaling exacerbates the presence of harmful content, and demonstrates that relying solely on image-based NSFW filtering is insufficient for comprehensive dataset sanitization. The findings are intended to inform best practices for dataset curation, filtering, and auditing in the development of equitable and responsible AI systems.

f3d64e57043f855f6b7b5bf83358ffe77b6ab4e7.title: Batched Multi-armed Bandits Problem
f3d64e57043f855f6b7b5bf83358ffe77b6ab4e7.research_question: How does the number of batches and the adaptivity of batch sizes affect the regret in multi-armed bandit problems, and what are the optimal strategies for minimizing regret in batched settings with multiple arms?
f3d64e57043f855f6b7b5bf83358ffe77b6ab4e7.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a carefully designed batched policy, such as a batched version of successive elimination, can achieve near-optimal minimax and problem-dependent regret rates (within logarithmic factors) for multi-armed bandits, regardless of whether batch sizes are chosen statically or adaptively.
f3d64e57043f855f6b7b5bf83358ffe77b6ab4e7.proposed_method: A novel batched policy, termed Batched Successive Elimination (BaSE), will be developed for the multi-armed bandit problem under batch constraints. The BaSE policy operates by dividing the time horizon into M batches, either with a static or adaptive grid. In each of the first M-1 batches, all active arms are pulled an equal number of times, and arms that are statistically inferior are eliminated based on upper confidence bounds. In the final batch, the algorithm commits to the arm with the highest empirical mean among those remaining. Two specific grid choices will be considered: a minimax grid for minimax regret and a geometric grid for problem-dependent regret, with grid parameters chosen to optimize the respective regret bounds. The policy is designed to ensure that all arms are evaluated fairly and that elimination decisions are robust to batch-induced sampling constraints.
f3d64e57043f855f6b7b5bf83358ffe77b6ab4e7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic multi-armed bandit problems with varying numbers of arms (K), batches (M), and time horizons (T). The reward distributions will be Gaussian, with the optimal arm having a higher mean than the others. The BaSE policy will be evaluated under different grid choices (minimax, geometric, arithmetic), and compared to the centralized UCB1 algorithm (without batch constraints) and the Explore-Then-Commit (ETC) algorithm for the two-arm case. Evaluation metrics will include average cumulative regret over multiple runs. The impact of the number of batches, arms, and time horizon on regret will be systematically analyzed, and empirical results will be visualized to demonstrate the approach to centralized performance as M increases.
f3d64e57043f855f6b7b5bf83358ffe77b6ab4e7.novelty_claims: The proposed research will provide the first comprehensive characterization of minimax and problem-dependent regret for batched multi-armed bandit problems with multiple arms, including both static and adaptive batch size settings. The BaSE policy is a novel adaptation of successive elimination to the batched regime, achieving rate-optimal regret within logarithmic factors. Matching lower bounds will be established for both static and adaptive grids, demonstrating that adaptive batch sizing does not offer significant improvement over static grids in terms of regret. Theoretical techniques for proving lower bounds in adaptive settings are also expected to contribute new insights to the literature on learning with limited rounds of adaptivity.

f3f23f7f9f5369aade19f20bc5d028cce7b9c9aa.title: AutoDAN: Generating Stealthy Jailbreak Prompts on Aligned Large Language Models
f3f23f7f9f5369aade19f20bc5d028cce7b9c9aa.research_question: Can an automated approach be developed to generate stealthy jailbreak prompts that effectively bypass safety mechanisms in aligned large language models, while maintaining semantic meaningfulness and scalability?
f3f23f7f9f5369aade19f20bc5d028cce7b9c9aa.hypothesis: Automatically generating jailbreak prompts using a hierarchical genetic algorithm initialized with handcrafted prototypes will yield prompts that are both semantically meaningful (stealthy) and highly effective at bypassing alignment safeguards in LLMs, outperforming existing token-level or manual approaches in terms of attack success, transferability, and resistance to perplexity-based defenses.
f3f23f7f9f5369aade19f20bc5d028cce7b9c9aa.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces AutoDAN, a hierarchical genetic algorithm specifically designed for generating stealthy jailbreak prompts targeting aligned LLMs. The process begins by initializing a population of candidate prompts using diversified versions of effective handcrafted jailbreak prompts, ensuring both semantic coherence and diversity. Fitness evaluation is performed using a log-likelihood-based loss function that measures the likelihood of eliciting non-refusal, harmful responses from the target LLM. The genetic algorithm operates at two levels: sentence-level (word choice optimization using a momentum-based word scoring system) and paragraph-level (sentence combination and crossover), employing multi-point crossover and LLM-based mutation to preserve meaning and introduce diversity. The algorithm iterates until either a maximum number of generations is reached or no refusal keywords are detected in the LLM’s responses, returning the highest-fitness prompt as the optimal jailbreak.
f3f23f7f9f5369aade19f20bc5d028cce7b9c9aa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the AdvBench Harmful Behaviors dataset, which contains 520 malicious requests spanning various categories such as profanity, misinformation, and dangerous suggestions. The method will be evaluated against baselines including the GCG attack (a token-level, gradient-based automatic method) and handcrafted DAN prompts. Evaluation metrics will include attack success rate (ASR) based on keyword detection, a GPT-based recheck metric to assess whether the response answers the malicious query, and sentence perplexity (PPL) for stealthiness, measured by GPT-2. The approach will be tested on multiple open-source LLMs (Vicuna-7b, Guanaco-7b, Llama2-7b-chat) and proprietary models (GPT-3.5-turbo), with additional experiments assessing cross-model transferability, cross-sample universality, and robustness against perplexity-based and other defenses. Ablation studies will be performed to quantify the contributions of initialization, mutation, and hierarchical design components.
f3f23f7f9f5369aade19f20bc5d028cce7b9c9aa.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to automatically generate semantically meaningful (stealthy) jailbreak prompts using a hierarchical genetic algorithm tailored for structured discrete text data. Unlike prior token-level or manual methods, this framework combines the scalability and automation of evolutionary algorithms with the stealthiness of human-crafted prompts, enabling effective bypass of perplexity-based and other simple defenses. The method demonstrates superior attack success, transferability across models, and universality across malicious queries, while maintaining low perplexity scores comparable to benign text. Key innovations include LLM-based population initialization, momentum-based word scoring for mutation, and a two-level genetic optimization process for prompt generation.

f3fbaceeff1aad6883b8ca20f43e031440467416.title: Safe-Sora: Safe Text-to-Video Generation via Graphical Watermarking
f3fbaceeff1aad6883b8ca20f43e031440467416.research_question: How can graphical watermarks be robustly and invisibly embedded into AI-generated videos during the text-to-video generation process to enable reliable copyright protection and ownership verification?
f3fbaceeff1aad6883b8ca20f43e031440467416.hypothesis: Embedding graphical watermarks directly into the video generation process using a hierarchical adaptive matching strategy and a state space model-based architecture will improve watermark fidelity, video quality, robustness to distortions, and temporal consistency compared to existing watermarking methods.
f3fbaceeff1aad6883b8ca20f43e031440467416.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that embeds graphical watermarks into the video generation pipeline by partitioning the watermark image into patches and adaptively matching each patch to the most visually similar video frame and spatial region using a hierarchical coarse-to-fine matching mechanism. Each patch is assigned to a frame and region based on feature similarity computed in the latent space, with position information encoded for robust recovery. The watermark feature map is then fused with multi-scale video features using a UNet with 2D Spatial-Frequency Mamba (SFMamba) blocks, followed by a series of 3D SFMamba blocks that implement a spatiotemporal local scanning strategy. The 3D SFMamba architecture leverages 3D wavelet transforms and a custom scanning order to model long-range dependencies across both spatial and temporal dimensions, facilitating effective watermark embedding and extraction. The extraction process uses a dedicated network with a distortion simulation layer, 3D SFMamba blocks, and position recovery to reconstruct the watermark from the generated video.
f3fbaceeff1aad6883b8ca20f43e031440467416.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using the Panda-70M dataset (10,000 videos, 8 frames per video, 320x512 resolution) for video content and the Logo-2K+ dataset (167,140 watermark images, 256x256 resolution) for graphical watermarks. For text-to-video evaluation, prompts are sampled from the VidProm dataset. The proposed method is implemented with VideoCrafter2 as the backbone and compared against five state-of-the-art baselines from three paradigms: post-processed image watermarking (Balujanet, UDH, PUSNet), generative image watermarking (Safe-SD), and video steganography (Wengnet). All baselines are retrained on the same data for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics include PSNR, MAE, RMSE, SSIM, LPIPS for both watermark and video quality, as well as tLP and Fréchet Video Distance (FVD) for temporal consistency. Robustness is assessed under various distortions such as random erasing, Gaussian blur, noise, rotation, and H.264 compression. Ablation studies are performed to analyze the impact of key components.
f3fbaceeff1aad6883b8ca20f43e031440467416.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to embed graphical watermarks directly into generative video models, addressing the need for copyright protection in AI-generated videos. A hierarchical coarse-to-fine adaptive matching mechanism is introduced to strategically embed watermark patches into visually similar frames and regions, enhancing both invisibility and robustness. The method pioneers the use of state space models for watermarking by developing a 3D wavelet transform-enhanced Mamba architecture with a novel spatiotemporal local scanning strategy, enabling efficient and robust watermark fusion and extraction across space and time. Experimental results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in video quality, watermark fidelity, robustness to distortions, and temporal consistency, establishing a new foundation for copyright protection in generative video.

f406aceba4f29cc7cfbe7edb2f52f01374486589.title: The Internal State of an LLM Knows When its Lying
f406aceba4f29cc7cfbe7edb2f52f01374486589.research_question: Can the internal hidden states of large language models (LLMs) be leveraged to reliably detect the truthfulness of statements, independent of explicit model outputs or sentence probabilities, across a range of topics and both externally provided and self-generated statements?
f406aceba4f29cc7cfbe7edb2f52f01374486589.hypothesis: The hidden layer activations of an LLM encode information about the model's internal belief regarding the truth or falsehood of a statement, enabling a classifier trained on these activations to distinguish true from false statements, even on topics not seen during training.
f406aceba4f29cc7cfbe7edb2f52f01374486589.proposed_method: A method is proposed in which a feedforward neural network classifier is trained to predict the truthfulness of statements based solely on the hidden layer activations of a large language model (LLM) as it processes each statement. The classifier receives as input the activations from selected layers (e.g., last, 28th, 24th, 20th, and middle layers) of the LLM, with each layer comprising thousands of units. The classifier consists of three hidden layers with decreasing sizes (256, 128, 64 units) and ReLU activations, followed by a sigmoid output. Training is performed on a dataset of true and false statements spanning multiple disjoint topics, ensuring that the classifier is evaluated on held-out topics to test generalization. The approach is designed to operate without fine-tuning the LLM itself and can be applied alongside any LLM to provide real-time truthfulness assessment of generated or input statements.
f406aceba4f29cc7cfbe7edb2f52f01374486589.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize a newly constructed true-false dataset comprising over 6,000 statements from six distinct topics (Cities, Inventions, Chemical Elements, Animals, Companies, Scientific Facts), with balanced true and false labels. The classifier will be trained on all but one topic and tested on the held-out topic, rotating through all topics to assess generalization. Two LLMs (OPT-6.7b and LLAMA2-7b) will be used as the base models for extracting activations. Baselines for comparison include a BERT-based classifier, few-shot prompting with the LLM, and sentence-level probability-based methods. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy and AUC, with additional experiments conducted on LLM self-generated statements, which are fact-checked and labeled by human annotators. Threshold optimization and analysis of layer-wise performance will also be performed.
f406aceba4f29cc7cfbe7edb2f52f01374486589.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel method for detecting the truthfulness of statements by leveraging the internal hidden states of LLMs, rather than relying on explicit outputs or sentence probabilities. This method demonstrates generalization across topics and can detect truthfulness in both externally provided and LLM-generated statements without requiring LLM fine-tuning. The research also releases a new multi-topic true-false dataset and provides evidence that LLMs possess internal representations of factuality that can be extracted for practical use in real-time content filtering or user-facing applications.

f40f6da0678a80706dd76a1254dab200ee2d8e9f.title: End-to-End User Behavior Retrieval in Click-Through RatePrediction Model
f40f6da0678a80706dd76a1254dab200ee2d8e9f.research_question: How can click-through rate (CTR) prediction models in recommender systems effectively utilize long-term user behavior sequences in an end-to-end manner while meeting strict inference time constraints in real-world large-scale systems?
f40f6da0678a80706dd76a1254dab200ee2d8e9f.hypothesis: Integrating an end-to-end, locality-sensitive hashing-based retrieval mechanism with target attention into CTR prediction models will enable efficient and effective utilization of long-term user behavior sequences, leading to improved prediction accuracy and online performance compared to existing two-stage or pooling-based methods.
f40f6da0678a80706dd76a1254dab200ee2d8e9f.proposed_method: A novel CTR prediction framework, ETA (End-to-End Target Attention), is proposed that incorporates a SimHash-based locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) mechanism for efficient retrieval of relevant user behaviors from long-term sequences. Each item in a user's behavior history is embedded and then hashed into a compact binary signature using SimHash, preserving similarity in the Hamming space. During both training and inference, the target item is also hashed, and the top-k most similar behaviors are selected in real time based on Hamming distance, significantly reducing retrieval complexity. These selected behaviors are then processed with a multi-head target attention mechanism, allowing the model to focus on the most relevant historical actions for each candidate item. The entire system is trained end-to-end, ensuring that retrieval and prediction objectives are aligned and embeddings remain up-to-date.
f40f6da0678a80706dd76a1254dab200ee2d8e9f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both a public dataset (Taobao) and a large-scale industrial dataset from a real-world e-commerce platform. The industrial dataset includes over 142 billion instances with long user behavior sequences (average length 938). Baseline methods will include average pooling DNN, DIN (Deep Interest Network), DIN with long sequences, SIM (hard), UBR4CTR, and their variants with time information. Models will be evaluated using AUC (area under the ROC curve) for offline experiments, and CTR/GMV (gross merchandise value) for online A/B tests. Inference time will be measured by deploying models in a controlled online environment. Ablation studies will assess the impact of sequence length, retrieval method (SimHash vs. inner product), and bit-length of hash signatures on both accuracy and latency.
f40f6da0678a80706dd76a1254dab200ee2d8e9f.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to enable end-to-end modeling of long-term user behavior sequences in CTR prediction without relying on offline auxiliary retrieval models or outdated embeddings. The integration of SimHash-based retrieval reduces complexity from O(L*B*d) to O(L*B), making real-time retrieval feasible for large-scale systems. The approach aligns retrieval and prediction objectives by sharing embeddings and enabling joint optimization, leading to significant improvements in prediction accuracy and online business metrics (e.g., 3.1% GMV gain over state-of-the-art baselines). The framework is also extensible to other domains requiring efficient handling of extremely long sequences.

f4186a28f6b33057cdb1a45eb7cb4a4eb3e21d73.title: Generalized Strategic Classification and the Case of Aligned Incentives
f4186a28f6b33057cdb1a45eb7cb4a4eb3e21d73.research_question: How can classification models be designed to robustly and flexibly account for a wide range of strategic user behaviors, particularly in settings where user incentives may be aligned with those of the system, and what are the implications for learning, generalization, and practical deployment?
f4186a28f6b33057cdb1a45eb7cb4a4eb3e21d73.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a generalized strategic classification framework, which models diverse user objectives and side information, can yield practical and theoretically sound learning algorithms. In particular, when user and system incentives are aligned, appropriately designed proxy losses (such as a generalized strategic hinge loss) will enable improved generalization and empirical performance compared to naive adaptations of standard classification methods.
f4186a28f6b33057cdb1a45eb7cb4a4eb3e21d73.proposed_method: A flexible framework for generalized strategic classification (GSC) will be developed, allowing users to modify their features based on private side information and diverse objectives, subsuming existing models and introducing new settings such as incentive-aligned strategic classification (IASC). The method will formalize user responses as utility-maximizing updates, parameterized by what users know, want, and how they act, leading to a general response mapping. For learning, a novel strategic hinge loss (s-hinge) will be introduced, adapting the notion of margin to strategic settings by measuring distances and correctness with respect to strategically modified inputs and individualized reference points. This approach will be extended to a generalized strategic hinge (gs-hinge) loss, applicable to any subclass of GSC, and will be optimized using gradient-based methods. Theoretical analysis will provide generalization bounds based on Rademacher complexity, demonstrating that the gs-hinge enjoys favorable statistical properties akin to standard hinge loss in non-strategic settings.
f4186a28f6b33057cdb1a45eb7cb4a4eb3e21d73.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both synthetic and real-world environments. Synthetic experiments will evaluate generalization behavior of the gs-hinge loss versus naive hinge adaptations and standard hinge loss across multiple strategic settings, including noisy labels, standard strategic classification, and adversarial user types. Metrics will include classification accuracy and convergence rates as a function of training sample size, with statistical significance assessed over multiple random splits. For real-world evaluation, a personalized previous experiences (PPE) setting will be implemented using the CoatsShopping dataset, where users' private side information consists of past item interactions. The system will employ bi-linear classifiers and compare the gs-hinge approach to standard hinge loss, varying the amount and type of user side information. Performance will be measured by prediction accuracy, and the impact of matching proxy losses between users and the system will be analyzed. Optimization challenges, such as triple-nested objectives in PPE, will be addressed by leveraging tractable proxy losses.
f4186a28f6b33057cdb1a45eb7cb4a4eb3e21d73.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive and flexible framework for strategic classification that generalizes prior models and incorporates richer forms of user knowledge, objectives, and actions. It identifies and formalizes the setting of incentive-aligned strategic classification, revealing that standard max-margin losses are ill-suited for strategic inputs and proposing a novel strategic hinge loss that corrects these deficiencies. The approach provides tractable, differentiable proxy losses that can be optimized end-to-end, and establishes new generalization bounds closely matching non-strategic cases. The framework enables principled reasoning about the effects of general strategic interactions on learning, and demonstrates both theoretically and empirically that properly designed losses can harness strategic behavior for collective improvement, especially when incentives are aligned.

f421b314aaff48e463507034691cfdd3f93cd4c2.title: Emergent Correspondence from Image Diffusion
f421b314aaff48e463507034691cfdd3f93cd4c2.research_question: Can accurate visual correspondences between images—including semantic, geometric, and temporal correspondences—be learned and extracted from large-scale image diffusion models without any explicit supervision or fine-tuning?
f421b314aaff48e463507034691cfdd3f93cd4c2.hypothesis: Image diffusion models, when trained for generative tasks, implicitly learn representations that encode rich correspondence information, enabling the extraction of robust and accurate visual correspondences across images, categories, and domains without explicit supervision.
f421b314aaff48e463507034691cfdd3f93cd4c2.proposed_method: A novel approach is proposed to extract dense image features from pre-trained diffusion models, termed DIffusion FeaTures (DIFT), for the purpose of establishing correspondences between real images. The method involves simulating the forward diffusion process by adding noise to real images at a chosen timestep, then passing these noisy images through the U-Net backbone of a pre-trained diffusion model to obtain intermediate layer activations as feature maps. Pixel correspondences are determined by performing nearest neighbor matching in the feature space using cosine distance. To improve robustness, features are averaged over multiple noise samples. A grid search is conducted to select optimal timesteps and network layers for different correspondence tasks, balancing semantic and low-level information as needed.
f421b314aaff48e463507034691cfdd3f93cd4c2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of visual correspondence tasks: semantic correspondence (using SPair-71k, PF-WILLOW, and CUB-200-2011 datasets), geometric correspondence (using the HPatches benchmark for homography estimation), and temporal correspondence (using DAVIS-2017 for video segmentation and JHMDB for pose tracking). DIFT features extracted from two diffusion models (Stable Diffusion and Ablated Diffusion Model) will be compared against state-of-the-art supervised, weakly-supervised, and self-supervised baselines, including DINO and OpenCLIP. Evaluation metrics include Percentage of Correct Keypoints (PCK), homography estimation accuracy at various pixel thresholds, region-based similarity (J), contour-based accuracy (F), and PCK for pose tracking. Hyperparameters such as noise timestep and feature extraction layer will be tuned via grid search, and feature matching will be performed without any fine-tuning or additional supervision.
f421b314aaff48e463507034691cfdd3f93cd4c2.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to directly demonstrate and systematically evaluate the emergence of visual correspondence in pre-trained diffusion models across semantic, geometric, and temporal tasks. DIFT enables accurate correspondence extraction without any explicit supervision or fine-tuning, outperforming both weakly-supervised and self-supervised baselines, and achieving competitive or superior results compared to state-of-the-art supervised methods on several benchmarks. The approach is simple, generalizable across tasks and domains, and reveals new insights into the self-supervised learning capabilities of diffusion models.

f42881b52212860263a162cf83a718bb44ba15cd.title: MACE: Mass Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models
f42881b52212860263a162cf83a718bb44ba15cd.research_question: How can a text-to-image diffusion model be fine-tuned to effectively and efficiently erase a large number of unwanted concepts, such as objects, celebrities, explicit content, or artistic styles, while maintaining a balance between erasure efficacy, generality (removal of synonyms), and specificity (preservation of unrelated concepts)?
f42881b52212860263a162cf83a718bb44ba15cd.hypothesis: A fine-tuning framework that combines closed-form cross-attention refinement with concept-specific LoRA modules, together with a novel fusion and importance sampling strategy, will enable scalable and effective mass concept erasure in diffusion models, achieving superior balance between generality and specificity compared to existing methods.
f42881b52212860263a162cf83a718bb44ba15cd.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a two-stage fine-tuning framework for mass concept erasure in pretrained text-to-image diffusion models. First, a closed-form cross-attention refinement is applied to the model's cross-attention layers, discouraging the embedding of residual information about target concepts in co-occurring words within the prompt. This is achieved by optimizing the projection matrices so that the 'Keys' and 'Values' of words co-occurring with the target phrase are mapped to those of a generic or super-category concept, using a closed-form solution. Second, for each target concept, a distinct LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) module is trained to erase the intrinsic information of that concept by minimizing the activation in attention maps corresponding to the target phrase, with the help of segmentation masks. To maintain specificity, a concept-focal importance sampling strategy is employed, focusing LoRA training on critical diffusion timesteps. Finally, a closed-form fusion technique is introduced to integrate multiple LoRA modules without mutual interference, ensuring that the model can forget a large set of concepts without catastrophic forgetting or performance degradation.
f42881b52212860263a162cf83a718bb44ba15cd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on Stable Diffusion v1.4, targeting four tasks: object erasure (using CIFAR-10 classes), celebrity erasure (using a curated set of 200 celebrities with GIPHY Celebrity Detector for evaluation), explicit content erasure (using the I2P benchmark and NudeNet detector), and artistic style erasure (using the Image Synthesis Style Studies Database). For each task, models will be fine-tuned to erase varying numbers of concepts (up to 100), and compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as ESD-u, ESD-x, FMN, SLD-M, UCE, and AC. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy for erased and retained concepts (efficacy and specificity), accuracy on synonyms (generality), harmonic mean of these metrics for overall erasure capability, FID and CLIP scores for image quality and semantic alignment, and the ratio of facial images for conceptual integrity. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of key components, and qualitative results will be provided for further analysis.
f42881b52212860263a162cf83a718bb44ba15cd.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to scale concept erasure up to 100 concepts in diffusion models while maintaining a strong balance between generality and specificity. It introduces a closed-form cross-attention refinement to eliminate residual concept information, a concept-focal importance sampling strategy for targeted LoRA training, and a novel closed-form fusion of multiple LoRA modules to prevent mutual interference and catastrophic forgetting. Unlike prior methods, the approach does not require synonyms or original training data for erasure, and demonstrates superior performance across multiple erasure tasks and evaluation metrics.

f43b56501d9d11195bbdd6d81bc65d92765b2837.title: Evaluating Neuron Explanations: A Unified Framework with Sanity Checks
f43b56501d9d11195bbdd6d81bc65d92765b2837.research_question: How can the evaluation of individual neuron explanations in neural networks be standardized and improved to ensure reliability and faithfulness across different domains and explanation types?
f43b56501d9d11195bbdd6d81bc65d92765b2837.hypothesis: A unified mathematical framework for evaluating neuron explanations, combined with rigorous sanity checks, will enable the identification of reliable evaluation metrics and expose weaknesses in commonly used metrics.
f43b56501d9d11195bbdd6d81bc65d92765b2837.proposed_method: A unified evaluation framework, termed NeuronEval, will be developed to formalize and encompass a wide range of existing neuron explanation evaluation metrics under a single mathematical notation. This framework will represent evaluation as a function of neuron activation vectors and concept activation vectors, allowing for the systematic comparison and analysis of 18+ metrics, including Recall, Precision, F1-score, IoU, Correlation, AUPRC, and others. Two novel sanity checks, the Missing Labels Test and Extra Labels Test, will be introduced to assess whether evaluation metrics can distinguish between explanations that are too specific or too generic, respectively. Both theoretical and empirical analyses will be conducted, including the derivation of analytical expectations and the implementation of these tests on real and synthetic neuron/concept pairs. The approach will also include meta-evaluation by measuring how well each metric separates correct from incorrect explanations using area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) across multiple datasets and domains.
f43b56501d9d11195bbdd6d81bc65d92765b2837.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of neural network models, including vision models (evaluated on ImageNet, Places365, and CUB200 datasets) and language models (evaluated on OpenWebText). Both final layer and hidden layer neurons, as well as CBM neurons and linear probe outputs, will be included. Evaluation metrics will be tested using both ground truth and pseudo-labels as concept sources. For each metric, the Missing Labels and Extra Labels sanity checks will be applied, and DecreaseAcc (the proportion of neurons where the metric decreases as expected) will be reported. Additionally, meta-evaluation will be performed by computing the AUPRC for each metric's ability to rank correct explanations above incorrect ones for neurons with known ground truth concepts. Hyperparameters for metrics will be selected using a validation split, and results will be averaged across multiple experimental setups. Ablation studies and sensitivity analyses will be included to ensure robustness.
f43b56501d9d11195bbdd6d81bc65d92765b2837.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first unified mathematical framework (NeuronEval) that encompasses nearly all existing neuron explanation evaluation metrics, enabling direct comparison and systematic analysis. Two new sanity checks (Missing Labels Test and Extra Labels Test) are proposed to rigorously assess the reliability of evaluation metrics, revealing that many widely used metrics fail at least one of these basic tests. The research identifies a set of reliable metrics (Correlation, Cosine Similarity, F1-score, IoU, AUPRC) and provides clear guidelines for future evaluation practices. The approach also connects common explanation failure modes to the proposed tests, offering a principled foundation for trustworthy neuron explanation evaluation.

f45f85fa1beaa795c24c4ff86f1f2deece72252f.title: A decoder-only foundation model for time-series forecasting
