f45f85fa1beaa795c24c4ff86f1f2deece72252f.research_question: Can a single, general-purpose, decoder-only foundation model, pretrained on large-scale real-world and synthetic time-series data, achieve strong zero-shot forecasting performance across a wide variety of previously unseen datasets, domains, forecasting horizons, and temporal granularities?
f45f85fa1beaa795c24c4ff86f1f2deece72252f.hypothesis: A decoder-only attention-based foundation model, pretrained on a diverse and massive corpus of real and synthetic time-series data using input patching and patch masking, will achieve zero-shot forecasting accuracy that is comparable to or surpasses state-of-the-art supervised models trained individually on each target dataset.
f45f85fa1beaa795c24c4ff86f1f2deece72252f.proposed_method: A foundation model for time-series forecasting will be developed using a decoder-only transformer architecture with input patching and patch masking. The model will process time-series data by segmenting it into contiguous, non-overlapping patches, each encoded via a residual MLP block and positional encoding. The transformer stack will use causal multi-head self-attention to encode temporal dependencies, with masking strategies to support variable context lengths and ensure the model learns across all possible context sizes. Output patches may be longer than input patches, enabling efficient forecasting over long horizons with fewer autoregressive steps. The model will be trained using a point forecasting loss (Mean Squared Error) in a decoder-only fashion, with random patch masking to expose the model to varying context lengths during training.
f45f85fa1beaa795c24c4ff86f1f2deece72252f.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the zero-shot forecasting performance of the pretrained model on three groups of public benchmark datasets intentionally held out from pretraining: Monash (18 datasets across various domains and granularities), Darts (8 univariate datasets with diverse seasonalities and trends), and Informer/ETT (electricity transformer temperature datasets with long forecasting horizons). Baselines will include both classical statistical methods (e.g., ARIMA, Exponential Smoothing), supervised deep learning models (e.g., DeepAR, N-BEATS, PatchTST), and zero-shot large language model-based approaches (e.g., GPT-3-based llmtime). Evaluation metrics will primarily be Mean Absolute Error (MAE), often scaled by a naive baseline, with results aggregated using geometric or arithmetic means as appropriate. The experimental setup will ensure consistent context and horizon lengths across methods, and ablation studies will be conducted to analyze the impact of model size, patch lengths, synthetic data inclusion, and decoding strategies.
f45f85fa1beaa795c24c4ff86f1f2deece72252f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a single, decoder-only, attention-based foundation model for time-series forecasting that is pretrained exclusively on time-series data (both real and synthetic) at large scale. Unlike prior work, this model is designed for strong zero-shot performance across a wide range of unseen datasets, domains, and temporal granularities, without any dataset-specific fine-tuning or covariate information. Key innovations include the use of input and output patching with flexible patch lengths, a tailored patch masking strategy for variable context exposure, and a training corpus that combines diverse real-world and synthetic time-series data to enhance generalization. The method claims to achieve zero-shot accuracy close to or exceeding that of supervised models, while being significantly smaller and more efficient than large language models repurposed for time-series forecasting.

f483c00cc45dd387364dc485794c27afae9289bb.title: The mechanistic basis of data dependence and abrupt learning in an in-context classification task
f483c00cc45dd387364dc485794c27afae9289bb.research_question: What are the mechanistic and data distributional factors that determine the emergence and dynamics of in-context learning versus in-weights learning in attention-based neural networks, and how do architectural and data properties influence abrupt transitions in learning behavior?
f483c00cc45dd387364dc485794c27afae9289bb.hypothesis: The abrupt emergence of in-context learning in attention-based networks is driven by the formation of induction heads, which are facilitated by specific data distributional properties and a sequence of nested nonlinear operations across multiple layers.
f483c00cc45dd387364dc485794c27afae9289bb.proposed_method: A minimal attention-only neural network will be constructed, consisting of two attention layers (each with a single head and causal mask) followed by a three-layer multilayer perceptron classifier. The network will be trained on a synthetic in-context classification task, where sequences of item-label pairs are presented, and the model must predict the label of a target item. The data distribution will be parameterized by the number of classes, burstiness (frequency of repeated classes), within-class variability, and rank-frequency distribution, allowing systematic manipulation of these properties. Progress measures will be defined to track the development of in-context and in-weights learning, and targeted ablation experiments will be designed to test causal hypotheses about the emergence of induction heads and abrupt transitions. Additionally, a minimal phenomenological model of the induction head and its loss landscape will be developed to analyze the sequential learning dynamics and abrupt transitions.
f483c00cc45dd387364dc485794c27afae9289bb.experiment_details: Experiments will use both synthetic datasets (Gaussian mixture models for item classes) and controlled manipulations of data distribution parameters such as number of classes (K), burstiness (B), within-class variability (ε), and rank-frequency exponent (α). The primary evaluation metrics will be in-context accuracy (on novel classes) and in-weights accuracy (on seen classes), along with progress measures quantifying attention and association patterns in the network. Baselines will include varying the fraction of bursty sequences, the number of contextual labels, and ablation of key parameters in the minimal model. All experiments will be repeated with multiple random seeds, and training will use vanilla SGD with a fixed learning rate and batch size. Additional analysis will include visualization of attention maps, alignment of progress measures, and simulation of learning trajectories on the analytically derived loss landscape.
f483c00cc45dd387364dc485794c27afae9289bb.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a mechanistic framework that links abrupt transitions in in-context learning to the formation of induction heads and the sequential learning of nested logits in multi-layer attention networks. It develops a minimal, analytically tractable model that captures the essential dynamics of induction head formation and explains the observed abruptness in learning. The approach systematically connects data distributional properties to the trade-off and coexistence of in-context and in-weights learning, providing new insights into the emergence of zero-shot learning abilities in attention-based models. The methodology enables causal testing of hypotheses about learning dynamics and offers a generalizable explanation for abrupt phase transitions in neural network training.

f4a0c4154203808f362e4678f3741b3d317fdc82.title: The Hedgehog & the Porcupine: Expressive Linear Attentions with Softmax Mimicry
f4a0c4154203808f362e4678f3741b3d317fdc82.research_question: Can a learnable linear attention mechanism be developed that matches the expressivity and performance of softmax attention while maintaining linear time and space complexity, thereby enabling efficient training and conversion of Transformers for various tasks and settings?
f4a0c4154203808f362e4678f3741b3d317fdc82.hypothesis: A trainable linear attention mechanism that explicitly mimics the spiky (low-entropy) and monotonic properties of softmax attention can close the performance gap between linear and standard softmax attention, achieving comparable modeling quality with linear complexity.
f4a0c4154203808f362e4678f3741b3d317fdc82.proposed_method: A new linear attention mechanism, termed Hedgehog, will be developed using trainable single-layer MLPs as feature maps applied to queries and keys within Transformer attention layers. These MLPs will be trained to mimic softmax attention weights by minimizing a cross-entropy distillation loss between the linear attention weights and the corresponding softmax attention weights. The feature map will use an element-wise exponential activation to induce spikiness, and the architecture will ensure monotonicity with respect to query-key dot products. Each attention head and layer will have its own trainable MLP, and the method will maintain O(nd^2) time and space complexity, where n is the sequence length and d is the head dimension. The approach will be validated both for training models from scratch and for converting pretrained or finetuned Transformers into efficient linear attention variants.
f4a0c4154203808f362e4678f3741b3d317fdc82.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in three regimes: training-from-scratch, finetuned-conversion, and pretrained-conversion. For training-from-scratch, Hedgehog Transformers will be evaluated on the Long Range Arena (LRA) benchmark for sequence classification and WikiText-103 for language modeling, comparing accuracy and perplexity against standard Transformers and prior linear attention methods. In the finetuned-conversion setting, BERT-base models finetuned on GLUE tasks and ViT-B/16 models on ImageNet-1K will have their attention layers swapped with Hedgehog and then be finetuned, with performance recovery measured against the original models. For pretrained-conversion, pretrained GPT-2 and Llama-2 7B models will be converted to Hedgehog attention and evaluated on WikiText-103 and SAMSum summarization, respectively, using perplexity and ROUGE metrics. Baselines will include standard softmax attention, Performer, Reformer, cosFormer, and other recent linear and subquadratic attention models. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, perplexity, ROUGE, and KL divergence between attention weights.
f4a0c4154203808f362e4678f3741b3d317fdc82.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a learnable linear attention mechanism that directly mimics softmax attention, recovering both spiky and monotonic properties critical for high modeling quality. Unlike prior linear attentions that use fixed feature maps, Hedgehog employs trainable MLPs optimized via attention weight distillation, enabling near-perfect recovery of softmax performance in both training-from-scratch and conversion scenarios. The approach achieves linear complexity without sacrificing expressivity, generalizes across tasks and sequence lengths, and demonstrates state-of-the-art results for linearized Transformers, including large language models.

f4a86daae3233d4e92a11aa4998c239217d929bf.title: Learning mirror maps in policy mirror descent
f4a86daae3233d4e92a11aa4998c239217d929bf.research_question: Does the choice of mirror map in Policy Mirror Descent (PMD) significantly impact the effectiveness of reinforcement learning algorithms, and can mirror maps be learned to outperform conventional choices such as negative entropy across a range of environments?
f4a86daae3233d4e92a11aa4998c239217d929bf.hypothesis: The choice of mirror map in PMD has a substantial effect on both convergence speed and final policy performance, and mirror maps learned through optimization can consistently outperform the standard negative entropy mirror map in both tabular and non-tabular reinforcement learning environments.
f4a86daae3233d4e92a11aa4998c239217d929bf.proposed_method: A framework will be developed to automatically learn mirror maps within the PMD and Approximate Mirror Policy Optimization (AMPO) algorithms. Mirror maps will be parameterized using neural networks or piecewise-linear functions, depending on the environment's complexity and computational constraints. Evolutionary strategies, such as OpenAI-ES and sep-CMA-ES, will be employed to optimize the mirror map parameters by maximizing the expected return of the final policy over a fixed time horizon. The method will support both tabular and deep RL settings, enabling the search for ω-potential mirror maps that generalize across tasks. The fitness of candidate mirror maps will be evaluated by the performance of PMD or AMPO using those maps, and the approach will include mechanisms to ensure monotonicity and coverage of standard mirror maps (e.g., negative entropy, ℓ2-norm).
f4a86daae3233d4e92a11aa4998c239217d929bf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a variety of RL environments, including tabular Grid-Worlds, the Basic Control Suite (BCS), MinAtar (discrete-action Atari-like environments), and continuous control tasks in MuJoCo simulated via Brax. In the tabular setting, the learned mirror maps will be compared to negative entropy and ℓ2-norm baselines, with hyperparameters tuned for fairness. Theoretical quantities such as estimation error and policy update distance will be tracked to relate empirical findings to existing convergence guarantees. In non-tabular and continuous control settings, mirror maps will be learned separately for each environment, and their generalization will be tested by applying them across different tasks. Evaluation metrics will include final policy value averaged over multiple runs, convergence speed, and robustness across held-out and random environment configurations. All experiments will use standardized implementations and sufficient computational resources (e.g., multi-GPU setups) to ensure reproducibility and scalability.
f4a86daae3233d4e92a11aa4998c239217d929bf.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic framework for learning mirror maps in PMD and AMPO, moving beyond the conventional use of negative entropy. It demonstrates empirically that learned mirror maps can significantly outperform standard choices across diverse RL environments and that the impact of the mirror map is much greater than suggested by existing theoretical upper bounds. The methodology provides evidence that small policy updates induced by certain mirror maps lead to smoother and more reliable policy improvement. Furthermore, the learned mirror maps exhibit strong generalization across tasks, suggesting practical utility for broad RL applications. The work also highlights a gap between theoretical guarantees and empirical performance, motivating new directions for theory and practice in RL regularization.

f4ac1508877f4d0ff8c9245d9099b4516610815c.title: $R^{2}$ Former: Unified Retrieval and Reranking Transformer for Place Recognition
f4ac1508877f4d0ff8c9245d9099b4516610815c.research_question: How can a unified, transformer-based framework be developed to improve both retrieval and reranking efficiency and accuracy for large-scale visual place recognition, while reducing computational cost and memory footprint?
f4ac1508877f4d0ff8c9245d9099b4516610815c.hypothesis: A unified transformer-based architecture that jointly handles both global retrieval and reranking, leveraging feature correlation, attention values, and spatial coordinates, will outperform existing CNN-based and RANSAC-based pipelines in terms of accuracy, inference speed, and memory efficiency for visual place recognition tasks.
f4ac1508877f4d0ff8c9245d9099b4516610815c.proposed_method: A novel unified framework will be developed that employs vision transformers for both global retrieval and reranking in visual place recognition. The approach will extract global features using the class token and local features using patch tokens from a shared transformer backbone. For reranking, a transformer-based module will be designed to take as input a correlation matrix encoding feature similarity, attention values, and xy coordinates for local feature pairs between query and reference images. The reranking module will select the most informative local features based on transformer attention maps, reducing the number of features to a fixed, memory-efficient set. The entire pipeline will be end-to-end trainable, with the reranking module formulated as a binary classification problem to predict whether image pairs depict the same location. Dimension reduction will be applied to both global and local features to further minimize computational and memory requirements.
f4ac1508877f4d0ff8c9245d9099b4516610815c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on major visual place recognition datasets, including MSLS (Mapillary Street-Level Sequences), Pitts30k, Tokyo 24/7, R-SF, and St Lucia. The model will be trained on MSLS and optionally fine-tuned on Pitts30k for urban scenarios. Evaluation metrics will include recall@k (k=1,5,10), inference latency, feature dimension, GFLOPs, and memory footprint. Baselines for comparison will include NetVLAD, Patch-NetVLAD, TransVPR, SFRS, SP-SuperGlue, and other state-of-the-art retrieval and reranking methods. The reranking module will be evaluated both as part of the unified transformer framework and as a plug-in for CNN backbones. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of various architectural and training choices, and scalability will be tested on datasets with over 1M reference images.
f4ac1508877f4d0ff8c9245d9099b4516610815c.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to unify retrieval and reranking for place recognition using only transformers, demonstrating that vision transformer tokens can match or exceed the performance of CNN local features for reranking. The reranking module introduces a novel use of feature correlation, attention, and spatial information within a transformer, enabling efficient, parallel reranking of candidate image pairs. The approach achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on multiple benchmarks while drastically reducing inference time and memory consumption, making it suitable for real-world, large-scale applications. The reranking module is generic and can be integrated with either CNN or transformer backbones.

f4af14fd6ec535900d8009985699e0953c97df85.title: Neural signature kernels as infinite-width-depth-limits of controlled ResNets
f4af14fd6ec535900d8009985699e0953c97df85.research_question: What are the limiting behaviors and associated kernel functions of randomly initialized controlled ResNets, particularly in the infinite-width and infinite-depth regimes, and how do these limits depend on network architecture, activation function, and weight-sharing schemes?
f4af14fd6ec535900d8009985699e0953c97df85.hypothesis: Randomly initialized controlled ResNets, when taken to their infinite-width and infinite-depth limits under appropriate scaling, converge to Gaussian processes indexed by continuous paths, with limiting kernels characterized by solutions to certain partial differential equations that depend on the network's architecture and activation function.
f4af14fd6ec535900d8009985699e0953c97df85.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves a rigorous mathematical analysis of controlled ResNets, which are defined as Euler discretizations of neural controlled differential equations (Neural CDEs). The study will consider both homogeneous (weight-sharing) and inhomogeneous (no weight-sharing) variants, with random Gaussian initialization of weights and biases. The approach will analyze the weak convergence of these architectures, first in the infinite-width-then-depth regime and then in the infinite-depth-then-width regime, using tools from stochastic analysis, rough path theory, and Gaussian process theory. The limiting behavior will be characterized by deriving and solving partial differential equations (PDEs) for the kernels, with special attention to the case where the activation function is linear (identity), leading to explicit connections with signature kernels. Additionally, the methodology will include the analysis of the finite-width, infinite-depth regime, showing convergence to Neural CDEs with random vector fields.
f4af14fd6ec535900d8009985699e0953c97df85.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by simulating controlled ResNets with varying widths and depths, using both synthetic and real-valued continuous path data. The primary datasets will consist of multivariate time series or continuous paths sampled from Gaussian processes with specified kernels (e.g., RBF). Baseline comparisons will include empirical estimators of the limiting kernels and Gaussian process predictions. Evaluation metrics will focus on convergence rates (e.g., mean squared error between empirical and theoretical kernel values), distributional agreement (e.g., quantile-quantile plots), and computational efficiency for kernel computation. Numerical experiments will also explore the scalability of the approach, leveraging GPU-based solvers and structured random matrices, and will empirically validate theoretical convergence rates and the distinctiveness of neural signature kernels for different activation functions.
f4af14fd6ec535900d8009985699e0953c97df85.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel family of neural signature kernels as the infinite-width-depth limits of controlled ResNets, rigorously characterizing their behavior via PDEs that generalize the classical signature kernel. It establishes, for the first time, the commutativity of width and depth limits for controlled ResNets in both homogeneous and inhomogeneous settings, and provides explicit convergence rates in the linear case. The work extends previous results by handling architectures with weight-sharing and non-linear activation functions, and by connecting the limiting kernels to well-studied objects in rough path theory. Additionally, the proposal outlines new scalable computational approaches for signature kernels via wide and deep ResNets, and suggests future directions for analyzing the functional analytic properties and expressivity of the resulting reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces.

f4e768015fc9b32c3319339865b3f1d83f9a1411.title: AdaNPC: Exploring Non-Parametric Classifier for Test-Time Adaptation
f4e768015fc9b32c3319339865b3f1d83f9a1411.research_question: How can test-time adaptation for domain generalization be improved to achieve robust performance on unseen distributions, while minimizing computational overhead and avoiding catastrophic forgetting of source domain knowledge?
f4e768015fc9b32c3319339865b3f1d83f9a1411.hypothesis: A non-parametric classifier, specifically a K-nearest neighbor (KNN) based approach that incrementally augments its memory with test-time samples and predictions, will enable effective test-time adaptation, reduce domain divergence, and maintain or improve generalization performance across both source and target domains without requiring model parameter updates.
f4e768015fc9b32c3319339865b3f1d83f9a1411.proposed_method: The proposed method, AdaNPC, utilizes a non-parametric KNN classifier for test-time adaptation. During training, the model is optimized using a KNN-based loss rather than the standard cross-entropy loss, encouraging robust feature representations less sensitive to outliers. A memory bank is constructed to store feature-label pairs from the training domains. At inference, each incoming test sample is embedded, and its prediction is determined by a weighted vote among the k nearest neighbors in the memory bank. If the prediction confidence exceeds a threshold, the test feature and its predicted label are added to the memory, allowing the memory distribution to gradually shift toward the test domain. The method is designed to be parameter-free at test time, requiring no gradient-based updates, and can optionally retrain only the batch normalization layer for further adaptation.
f4e768015fc9b32c3319339865b3f1d83f9a1411.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on five popular out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization benchmarks: Rotated MNIST, PACS, VLCS, TerraIncognita, and DomainNet, using multiple backbones including ResNet18, ResNet50, and ViT-B16. AdaNPC is compared against a comprehensive set of domain generalization and test-time adaptation baselines, such as ERM, IRM, CORAL, DANN, Fishr, Tent, and T3A. Evaluation metrics include average accuracy across all domains, with additional analysis on adaptation to a series of domains (successive adaptation), catastrophic forgetting, and robustness to corruptions (CIFAR-10-C and ImageNet-C). Experiments also measure inference time and memory usage, and ablation studies are performed on the effect of KNN loss, memory size, and the choice of k.
f4e768015fc9b32c3319339865b3f1d83f9a1411.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a non-parametric, memory-augmented KNN classifier for test-time adaptation that requires no model parameter updates, thus avoiding catastrophic forgetting and enabling strong knowledge expandability. The method is theoretically justified to reduce domain divergence and tighten target error bounds under both covariate and posterior shift settings. AdaNPC achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple OOD benchmarks, demonstrates superior performance in successive domain adaptation scenarios, and offers interpretability by exposing the decision process through memory retrieval. Furthermore, the approach is computationally efficient, scalable to large datasets, and effective even without fine-tuning on source domains.

f4eabf08e63ba55380b4685a468ce4399813422e.title: Inference-Aware Fine-Tuning for Best-of-N Sampling in Large Language Models
f4eabf08e63ba55380b4685a468ce4399813422e.research_question: How can fine-tuning large language models be made aware of inference-time strategies, specifically Best-of-N (BoN) sampling, to improve performance and efficiency across diverse reasoning and generation tasks?
f4eabf08e63ba55380b4685a468ce4399813422e.hypothesis: Incorporating inference-time strategies, such as BoN sampling, directly into the fine-tuning process of large language models will lead to improved performance and more efficient use of inference-time compute, compared to traditional fine-tuning methods that are agnostic to these strategies.
f4eabf08e63ba55380b4685a468ce4399813422e.proposed_method: A novel inference-aware fine-tuning paradigm will be developed that explicitly optimizes model parameters for the BoN inference strategy. This involves both supervised imitation learning and reinforcement learning (RL) approaches that account for the non-differentiable argmax operation inherent in BoN sampling. The supervised BoN-aware fine-tuning (BoN-SFT) method aligns the model's output distribution with the BoN policy by maximizing a variational approximation of the BoN likelihood, incorporating a win-rate regularizer to encourage exploration. The RL-based BoN-aware methods (BoN-RL, BoN-RLB, BoN-RLB(P)) optimize the expected environment reward under the BoN policy, with specialized estimators for binary reward scenarios that enable efficient and scalable training. Both approaches leverage a verifier to select the best response from N samples, and parameter co-scaling (temperature and sample size) is analyzed to balance exploration and exploitation.
f4eabf08e63ba55380b4685a468ce4399813422e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Gemma 2B and 9B language models on mathematical problem-solving (Hendrycks MATH, Functional MATH, MathOdyssey) and code generation (MBPP, HumanEval) benchmarks. Evaluation metrics include BoN accuracy (using a learned verifier) and pass@N accuracy (using ground-truth reward), with systematic variation of BoN sample size (N) and temperature (T) to analyze co-scaling effects. Baselines will include standard supervised fine-tuning, RL with and without verifier feedback, self-training over correct responses (STaR), and the pre-trained base model. Both offline (supervised) and on-policy (RL) BoN-aware fine-tuning methods will be compared, with detailed ablations on the effect of N and T during training and evaluation.
f4eabf08e63ba55380b4685a468ce4399813422e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first formal framework and algorithms for inference-aware fine-tuning of large language models under the BoN sampling strategy, bridging the gap between training and inference-time procedures. It provides new variational and RL-based methods that directly optimize for BoN performance, including efficient closed-form solutions for binary reward settings. The approach enables explicit control over the exploration-exploitation trade-off during fine-tuning, and demonstrates substantial improvements in BoN and pass@N accuracy over existing baselines. The work also presents a detailed analysis of parameter co-scaling, offering practical guidelines for optimizing inference-time compute.

f4f154892800008894ebbf57add31fcaac4f27ca.title: SeeGULL: A Stereotype Benchmark with Broad Geo-Cultural Coverage Leveraging Generative Models
f4f154892800008894ebbf57add31fcaac4f27ca.research_question: How can a comprehensive, globally representative benchmark for detecting and evaluating social stereotypes in NLP models be constructed to address limitations of existing datasets in terms of size, geo-cultural coverage, and contextual sensitivity?
f4f154892800008894ebbf57add31fcaac4f27ca.hypothesis: Leveraging large language models (LLMs) in conjunction with geographically and culturally diverse human validation will enable the creation of a stereotype benchmark that is broader in coverage, more contextually sensitive, and more effective at uncovering stereotyping harms in NLP models than existing resources.
f4f154892800008894ebbf57add31fcaac4f27ca.proposed_method: A novel LLM-human partnership framework will be developed to generate and validate a large-scale stereotype benchmark. First, seed sets of stereotypes will be curated for both global (country/region-level) and local (state-level within the US and India) axes, using existing sources and manual selection. Few-shot prompting will be employed with generative LLMs (PaLM, GPT-3, T0) to produce candidate stereotypes by associating identity groups with descriptive attributes. Post-processing will extract and normalize candidate tuples, and a salience score (modified tf-idf) will be computed to prioritize unique and representative associations. The top candidates per region will be selected for human validation, where a geographically diverse pool of annotators will label the prevalence and offensiveness of stereotypes, with special attention to in-region versus out-region perceptions. Offensiveness will be rated on a Likert scale and mapped to stereotypes for further analysis.
f4f154892800008894ebbf57add31fcaac4f27ca.experiment_details: Experiments will involve constructing the SeeGULL dataset, containing 7,750 validated stereotypes across 179 identity groups from 178 countries and 8 geo-political regions, as well as state-level identities in the US and India. The annotation process will use 89 annotators from 16 countries, ensuring both in-region and out-region perspectives. The benchmark's utility will be evaluated by measuring stereotyping harms in natural language inference (NLI) models (ELMo, XLNet, ELECTRA), using SeeGULL alongside existing benchmarks (StereoSet, CrowS-Pairs) and a neutral baseline. Evaluation metrics will include mean entailment and percentage of entailed stereotypes, with experiments designed to compare coverage and sensitivity across regions and models. Offensiveness ratings will be aggregated and analyzed by region and identity group.
f4f154892800008894ebbf57add31fcaac4f27ca.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable LLM-human partnership for stereotype benchmark creation, enabling unprecedented geo-cultural breadth and contextual sensitivity. SeeGULL is the first resource to provide both global and local (state-level) stereotype coverage, fine-grained offensiveness ratings, and comparative in-region versus out-region annotations. The methodology allows for extensibility to other dimensions (e.g., religion, race, gender) and languages. Experiments demonstrate that the benchmark uncovers significantly more embedded stereotype harms in NLP models, especially for underrepresented regions, than existing datasets.

f50d219534c592ca4ba471d3389fc9dc2d8f3def.title: Annealed adaptive importance sampling method in PINNs for solving high dimensional partial differential equations
f50d219534c592ca4ba471d3389fc9dc2d8f3def.research_question: How can the efficiency and accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) be improved for solving high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs), particularly in cases with singularities and multi-modal loss landscapes?
f50d219534c592ca4ba471d3389fc9dc2d8f3def.hypothesis: Integrating an annealed adaptive importance sampling (AAIS) strategy into the training of PINNs will lead to more effective sampling in regions of high residual, thereby improving solution accuracy and efficiency, especially for high-dimensional and singular PDEs.
f50d219534c592ca4ba471d3389fc9dc2d8f3def.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces an adaptive sampling framework for PINNs based on Annealed Adaptive Importance Sampling (AAIS). This approach leverages the Expectation Maximization (EM) algorithm to construct a finite mixture model (either Gaussian or Student's t-distributions) that approximates the distribution of PDE residuals. During training, the AAIS algorithm iteratively refines the proposal distribution by adding, updating, or deleting mixture components based on effective sample size (ESS) criteria, and employs an annealing schedule to smoothly transition from an initial guess to the target residual distribution. The resampling strategy maintains a fixed training dataset size by combining newly sampled points (from high-residual regions identified by AAIS) with existing points, ensuring that the neural network focuses on challenging areas of the solution space. The AAIS framework is designed to be modular and can be integrated with various PINN architectures.
f50d219534c592ca4ba471d3389fc9dc2d8f3def.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of PDE problems, including two-dimensional and high-dimensional Poisson equations with single and multiple peaks, as well as other benchmark equations such as Burgers', Allen-Cahn, and KdV equations. The proposed AAIS-PINN approach (with both Gaussian and Student's t-mixture variants) will be compared against uniform sampling (Uni) and the Residual-based Adaptive Distribution (RAD) method. Evaluation metrics include L2 relative error and L-infinity error on test datasets, with neural networks configured with 7 hidden layers and 20 neurons per layer, using tanh activations and Adam/lbfgs optimizers. The effectiveness of adaptive sampling will be analyzed in terms of error decay, residual distribution, and node clustering, with particular attention to performance in high-dimensional settings and under limited computational resources.
f50d219534c592ca4ba471d3389fc9dc2d8f3def.novelty_claims: The proposed AAIS-PINN framework is the first to apply annealed adaptive importance sampling, guided by EM-based mixture models, to the adaptive sampling of PINNs for high-dimensional and singular PDEs. The method introduces a robust, modular resampling strategy that maintains dataset size while adaptively focusing on regions of high residual, overcoming limitations of previous Monte Carlo-based adaptive methods in high dimensions. The framework supports both Gaussian and heavy-tailed Student's t-mixtures, enhancing flexibility and performance. Empirical results indicate significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency, especially in challenging high-dimensional scenarios where existing methods struggle.

f52293edcaccf33cc16c372175a69ffa63cf3460.title: Towards Open Vocabulary Learning: A Survey
f52293edcaccf33cc16c372175a69ffa63cf3460.research_question: How can open vocabulary learning be systematically advanced to enable visual scene understanding models to recognize and localize categories beyond the pre-defined label space, leveraging large-scale vision-language pre-training and language supervision?
f52293edcaccf33cc16c372175a69ffa63cf3460.hypothesis: Integrating large-scale vision-language models and language-augmented supervision into detection and segmentation frameworks will enable models to generalize to novel, previously unseen categories, surpassing the limitations of close-set and zero-shot learning.
f52293edcaccf33cc16c372175a69ffa63cf3460.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed that transforms conventional close-set detectors and segmenters into open vocabulary models by replacing fixed classifier weights with text embeddings derived from large-scale vision-language models (VLMs) such as CLIP or ALIGN. The approach will incorporate knowledge distillation techniques to transfer semantic alignment from VLMs to downstream detectors, and will leverage region-text pre-training using web-scale image-caption pairs to align visual regions with language concepts. Additional modules will be designed for global and relational knowledge distillation, and the system will support both two-stage and transformer-based query detection architectures. The framework will also explore the use of language-augmented supervision, such as image captions and attribute phrases, to further enhance generalization to novel classes.
f52293edcaccf33cc16c372175a69ffa63cf3460.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard detection and segmentation benchmarks, including COCO, LVIS, ADE20k, and v3Det, evaluating performance on both base (seen) and novel (unseen) categories. Baseline comparisons will include traditional close-set detectors, zero-shot learning models, and recent open vocabulary approaches. Evaluation metrics will comprise mean average precision (mAP) for detection, mean intersection over union (mIoU) for segmentation, and panoptic quality (PQ) for panoptic segmentation. The experimental setup will involve both supervised and weakly supervised settings, with ablation studies on language supervision sources, distillation strategies, and the impact of different VLMs.
f52293edcaccf33cc16c372175a69ffa63cf3460.novelty_claims: The proposed research will introduce a unified and extensible framework for open vocabulary learning that systematically integrates vision-language pre-training, language-augmented supervision, and knowledge distillation. It will provide a detailed taxonomy and comparative analysis of methods across detection, segmentation, video, and 3D scene understanding tasks, and will pioneer the use of large-scale language data and VLMs to bridge the gap between close-set and open-set recognition. The approach will offer practical solutions for scalable, generalizable scene understanding in real-world applications and establish new benchmarks for open vocabulary evaluation.

f5241abdad7e43606f1c79fc71273d43de3f31c5.title: ButterflyFlow: Building Invertible Layers with Butterfly Matrices
f5241abdad7e43606f1c79fc71273d43de3f31c5.research_question: How can invertible linear layers with high representational power and computational efficiency be designed to improve the expressivity and performance of normalizing flow-based generative models, particularly for data with complex or structured linear relationships such as permutations and periodicity?
f5241abdad7e43606f1c79fc71273d43de3f31c5.hypothesis: Invertible linear layers constructed from butterfly matrices, due to their theoretical ability to efficiently represent complex structured linear transformations (including permutations and periodicity), will enhance the expressivity and efficiency of normalizing flow models, leading to improved density estimation and generative performance, especially on datasets with underlying structured regularities.
f5241abdad7e43606f1c79fc71273d43de3f31c5.proposed_method: A new class of invertible linear layers will be developed based on butterfly matrices, which are constructed as products of sparse butterfly factors. These layers are designed to efficiently compute both forward and inverse transformations, as well as tractable Jacobian determinants, making them suitable for use in normalizing flows. The method will introduce both standard and block-wise invertible butterfly layers, the latter allowing for flexible grouping of input dimensions and further generalizing existing invertible linear layers such as 1x1 convolutions. The butterfly layers will be integrated as architectural primitives within a flow-based generative model, termed ButterflyFlow, which will also incorporate standard components such as coupling layers, actnorm layers, and squeeze/split operations. The architecture will be modular, stacking multiple levels of flow modules, each containing a butterfly layer, actnorm, and coupling layer, to maximize expressivity and efficiency.
f5241abdad7e43606f1c79fc71273d43de3f31c5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image datasets (MNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet-32x32) to benchmark density estimation and generative performance, using uniform dequantization and standard data augmentation. Baselines will include state-of-the-art flow-based models such as Glow, Emerging convolutions, Woodbury flows, and i-ResNet, all using comparable architectural backbones. Additional experiments will target datasets with known or induced structure, such as permuted image datasets (where a fixed random permutation is applied to all images), galaxy images (exhibiting periodicity), and the MIMIC-III patient waveform dataset (with periodic temporal structure). Evaluation metrics will include bits per dimension (BPD) for density estimation and negative log-likelihood per dimension, as well as qualitative assessment of generated samples. Model efficiency will be assessed via parameter count and wall-clock runtime comparisons for forward and inverse passes.
f5241abdad7e43606f1c79fc71273d43de3f31c5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a theoretically grounded and computationally efficient family of invertible linear layers based on butterfly matrices, capable of representing a broad class of structured linear transformations (including all permutations and periodic convolutions). These layers are shown to be more expressive and efficient than existing invertible linear layers, such as 1x1 convolutions, and can be flexibly parameterized via block-wise constructions. The integration of these layers into flow-based generative models (ButterflyFlow) is claimed to yield superior performance on both standard and structured datasets, while also reducing model size and computational cost. The method is novel in its ability to efficiently capture global regularities in data that are not easily modeled by conventional flow architectures.

f5275c61736781d236abe6700b822f1ea62f982e.title: Diffusion Model Alignment Using Direct Preference Optimization
f5275c61736781d236abe6700b822f1ea62f982e.research_question: How can text-to-image diffusion models be aligned with human preferences in an open-vocabulary setting using direct optimization on human comparison data, and how does this approach compare to existing alignment and fine-tuning methods?
f5275c61736781d236abe6700b822f1ea62f982e.hypothesis: Directly optimizing diffusion models on human preference data using a reformulated Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) objective will yield models that generate images with higher visual appeal and better prompt alignment, outperforming both base and refinement pipelines of state-of-the-art diffusion models, and can be effectively scaled using AI-generated feedback.
f5275c61736781d236abe6700b822f1ea62f982e.proposed_method: A novel method, Diffusion-DPO, is developed by adapting Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to the diffusion model setting. The approach reformulates the DPO objective to account for the likelihood structure of diffusion models, utilizing the evidence lower bound (ELBO) to derive a differentiable loss function. The method directly optimizes the model on human comparison data, where each data point consists of a prompt and a pair of images with a human-annotated preference. The loss encourages the model to improve denoising performance on preferred samples while penalizing less preferred ones, and incorporates a KL-regularization term to maintain proximity to a reference model. The method also supports learning from AI-generated feedback by using scoring networks to generate pseudo-preference labels, enabling scalable alignment.
f5275c61736781d236abe6700b822f1ea62f982e.experiment_details: Experiments involve fine-tuning state-of-the-art text-to-image diffusion models, specifically Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL)-1.0 and SD1.5, using the Diffusion-DPO objective. The primary training dataset is Pick-a-Pic v2, containing 851,293 pairs of images with human preference annotations across 58,960 unique prompts. Baselines include the SDXL base model, the SDXL base plus refinement pipeline, and models fine-tuned with supervised learning or reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). Evaluation is conducted using human labelers on Amazon Mechanical Turk, assessing general preference, visual appeal, and prompt alignment on the PartiPrompts and HPSv2 benchmarks, as well as automated metrics such as PickScore, CLIP, and Aesthetic Predictor. Additional experiments test image-to-image editing (using SDEdit on TEdBench) and the effectiveness of learning from AI feedback. Hyperparameters are tuned for stability and performance, with large-scale distributed training employed.
f5275c61736781d236abe6700b822f1ea62f982e.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to enable direct alignment of text-to-image diffusion models with human preferences in an open-vocabulary setting using a DPO-based objective. Diffusion-DPO introduces a theoretically justified, efficient, and stable loss formulation for preference optimization in diffusion models, outperforming existing RL-based and supervised fine-tuning approaches. The method demonstrates superior human preference alignment, visual appeal, and prompt fidelity compared to both base and refinement pipelines, and is the first to show that scalable alignment with AI-generated feedback is feasible for diffusion models. The approach also implicitly learns a reward model, matching or exceeding the expressivity of explicit reward modeling architectures.

f52af2c0cf521b48edd50670e9ba9cd02646d2b4.title: MoMask: Generative Masked Modeling of 3D Human Motions
f52af2c0cf521b48edd50670e9ba9cd02646d2b4.research_question: How can high-quality, efficient, and controllable 3D human motion sequences be generated from natural language descriptions, and how can such a system support related tasks such as temporal inpainting without requiring model fine-tuning?
f52af2c0cf521b48edd50670e9ba9cd02646d2b4.hypothesis: A hierarchical residual vector quantization combined with generative masked modeling using bidirectional transformers will enable more precise, diverse, and controllable 3D human motion generation from text, outperforming existing unidirectional and single-layer quantization approaches in both quality and efficiency.
f52af2c0cf521b48edd50670e9ba9cd02646d2b4.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that represents 3D human motion as a hierarchy of discrete motion tokens using residual vector quantization (RVQ). The process begins by encoding motion sequences into latent vectors, which are then quantized in multiple layers: the base layer captures the primary motion information, and subsequent layers iteratively quantize residuals to reduce reconstruction error. A Masked Transformer, conditioned on text embeddings (e.g., from CLIP), will be trained to predict randomly masked base-layer motion tokens in parallel, using a variable masking ratio schedule. During inference, the Masked Transformer iteratively fills in masked tokens, starting from a fully masked sequence. Once the base layer is generated, a Residual Transformer will progressively predict the tokens for each residual quantization layer, conditioned on the tokens from previous layers. The entire token sequence is then decoded to reconstruct the full 3D motion sequence. Quantization dropout and remasking strategies will be incorporated to enhance learning and generalization.
f52af2c0cf521b48edd50670e9ba9cd02646d2b4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the HumanML3D and KIT-ML datasets, both of which provide paired motion and text data with diverse actions and language descriptions. The proposed method will be evaluated against state-of-the-art baselines including VAE-based, diffusion-based, and autoregressive models such as T2M, TM2T, MDM, MLD, T2M-GPT, and ReMoDiffuse. Standard evaluation metrics will include Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for motion quality, R-Precision and multimodal distance for text-motion alignment, and Multimodality for diversity. The experimental setup will use consistent pose representations, data augmentation, and standardized train/val/test splits. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of hierarchical quantization, quantization dropout, and remasking. Inference efficiency and user preference will be assessed through timing benchmarks and user studies. Additional experiments will demonstrate the method's ability to perform temporal inpainting without further fine-tuning.
f52af2c0cf521b48edd50670e9ba9cd02646d2b4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first generative masked modeling framework for text-to-motion generation using hierarchical residual vector quantization, enabling high-fidelity, multi-layer discrete motion token representations. The combination of a bidirectional masked transformer for base-layer token generation and a residual transformer for progressive refinement allows for efficient, parallel, and globally conditioned motion synthesis. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks, supports related tasks such as temporal inpainting without retraining, and demonstrates superior efficiency compared to autoregressive and diffusion-based baselines. Key innovations include the hierarchical RVQ design, scheduled variable masking, quantization dropout, and a unified framework for both generation and inpainting.

f52be2741418df216561bd4436da302ece39d9e2.title: Foundations & Trends in Multimodal Machine Learning: Principles, Challenges, and Open Questions
f52be2741418df216561bd4436da302ece39d9e2.research_question: What are the foundational principles, technical challenges, and open questions in multimodal machine learning, and how can a systematic taxonomy be developed to guide future research in this field?
f52be2741418df216561bd4436da302ece39d9e2.proposed_method: A comprehensive taxonomy will be developed to categorize and analyze the core challenges in multimodal machine learning, focusing on six key areas: representation, alignment, reasoning, generation, transference, and quantification. Each challenge will be systematically examined through a review of historical and recent literature, identifying subchallenges, methodological approaches, and representative techniques. The approach will emphasize the foundational principles of modality heterogeneity, connections, and interactions, and will propose a structured framework to map out the relationships and gaps across the field. The taxonomy will be illustrated with detailed examples and technical descriptions, including mathematical formulations for representation fusion, coordination, and fission, as well as alignment and reasoning mechanisms.
f52be2741418df216561bd4436da302ece39d9e2.experiment_details: The proposal involves an extensive survey and synthesis of existing multimodal machine learning research, drawing from a wide range of application domains such as computer vision, natural language processing, robotics, and healthcare. Key representative datasets and benchmarks from these domains will be cataloged and analyzed in relation to the proposed taxonomy. Baseline methods from unimodal and multimodal learning will be compared to highlight the unique challenges and solutions in each core area. Evaluation will be based on coverage of technical approaches, clarity in categorization, and the identification of open questions and future research directions.
f52be2741418df216561bd4436da302ece39d9e2.novelty_claims: The proposed taxonomy introduces a unified and principled framework for understanding and organizing the core challenges in multimodal machine learning. By synthesizing a broad spectrum of theoretical and computational perspectives, the taxonomy provides a comprehensive map of the field, facilitating the identification of common themes, methodological gaps, and open research questions. The explicit articulation of foundational principles and the systematic breakdown of subchallenges and approaches represent significant contributions toward advancing the theoretical and practical understanding of multimodal machine learning.

f56ad6a6a588945c4ee9ddd7b0d1efef2f2f3f31.title: DiLoCo: Distributed Low-Communication Training of Language Models
f56ad6a6a588945c4ee9ddd7b0d1efef2f2f3f31.research_question: How can large language models be effectively trained across multiple, poorly connected clusters of accelerators while minimizing communication overhead and maintaining or improving model performance and robustness?
f56ad6a6a588945c4ee9ddd7b0d1efef2f2f3f31.hypothesis: A distributed optimization algorithm that significantly reduces inter-cluster communication frequency, while leveraging advanced local and global optimization strategies, can match or exceed the performance of fully synchronous training for large language models, even in heterogeneous and unreliable computing environments.
f56ad6a6a588945c4ee9ddd7b0d1efef2f2f3f31.proposed_method: A novel distributed training framework, DiLoCo (Distributed Low-Communication), is introduced for large language models. The method partitions the training process across k worker clusters (islands), each hosting a replica of the model and a shard of the dataset. Training proceeds in two nested loops: an inner loop where each worker independently performs H steps of local optimization using AdamW on its data shard, and an outer loop where model updates from all workers are aggregated and applied using a Nesterov momentum optimizer. Communication between clusters is required only once every H inner steps, drastically reducing bandwidth requirements. The approach supports both i.i.d. and non-i.i.d. data distributions, is robust to resource availability changes, and can be initialized from scratch or a pretrained model.
f56ad6a6a588945c4ee9ddd7b0d1efef2f2f3f31.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the C4 dataset for language modeling, using decoder-only transformer architectures (Chinchilla-style) with model sizes of 60M, 150M, and 400M parameters. The evaluation metric is validation perplexity. DiLoCo is compared against several baselines: standard large-batch training with data parallelism, microbatching, and increased update frequency, as well as fully synchronous training. Ablations investigate the impact of communication frequency (H), number of worker clusters, model size, pretraining steps, and data distribution (i.i.d. vs non-i.i.d.). Robustness is further tested under varying compute availability and simulated communication failures (dropped updates). Hyperparameters are tuned for the outer optimizer, and experiments include both starting from scratch and from pretrained checkpoints.
f56ad6a6a588945c4ee9ddd7b0d1efef2f2f3f31.novelty_claims: The proposed framework enables efficient distributed training of large language models across loosely connected clusters, reducing inter-cluster communication by up to 500x compared to fully synchronous methods while maintaining or improving generalization performance. The method demonstrates robustness to heterogeneous data distributions, dynamic resource availability, and communication failures. Unlike prior large-scale federated or local SGD approaches, this method leverages advanced optimizers (AdamW locally, Nesterov globally) and operates effectively at scale (up to 400M parameters and 64 clusters), with minimal performance degradation even in challenging non-i.i.d. or asynchronous settings.

f56d363635bc378a196bae6d886ddd2d2899a220.title: Relative representations enable zero-shot latent space communication
f56d363635bc378a196bae6d886ddd2d2899a220.research_question: How can neural network latent representations be made invariant to stochastic factors in training, such that components trained independently can be reused, compared, or composed in a zero-shot manner across different architectures, datasets, or modalities?
f56d363635bc378a196bae6d886ddd2d2899a220.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that constructing relative representations based on the similarity of each sample to a fixed set of anchor samples will yield latent representations that are invariant to isometric transformations and rescalings induced by stochastic training factors, thereby enabling zero-shot interoperability and compositionality between independently trained neural network components.
f56d363635bc378a196bae6d886ddd2d2899a220.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed wherein each data sample's latent representation is expressed as a vector of similarities (e.g., cosine similarity) to a fixed set of anchor samples selected from the training data or external sources. The method involves first training standard neural encoders to produce absolute latent embeddings, then computing relative representations by measuring the similarity between each embedding and the anchors. This approach ensures invariance to angle-preserving transformations (rotations, reflections, rescalings) in the latent space, as the relative representation depends only on the angles between embeddings. The choice and composition of anchors will be explored, including in-domain, out-of-domain, and parallel anchors for cross-domain tasks. The framework will be implemented as a modular layer compatible with existing neural architectures and will support both post-hoc conversion of embeddings and end-to-end training using relative representations.
f56d363635bc378a196bae6d886ddd2d2899a220.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across multiple modalities and tasks, including image classification (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet1k), graph node classification (Cora, CiteSeer, PubMed), and text classification (TREC, DBpedia, Amazon Reviews in multiple languages). Baselines will include models using absolute latent representations and existing stitching or alignment methods. Evaluation metrics will comprise classification accuracy, weighted F1 score, mean squared error (for reconstructions), mean absolute error, Jaccard similarity, mean reciprocal rank, and cosine similarity between embeddings. Experimental setups will include zero-shot model stitching (combining encoders and decoders trained independently), cross-lingual and cross-architecture transfer, and ablation studies on anchor selection and dimensionality. Extensive comparisons will be made between relative and absolute representations in terms of performance, invariance, and interoperability.
f56d363635bc378a196bae6d886ddd2d2899a220.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of relative representations for neural network latent spaces, enabling invariance to stochastic training factors without additional training or learnable parameters. For the first time, zero-shot model stitching is demonstrated across independently trained neural components, architectures, and domains. The method provides a differentiable, label-free quantitative measure of model performance correlated with standard metrics. The framework is general, applicable to images, text, and graphs, and supports both in-domain and cross-domain tasks using flexible anchor selection strategies.

f574f4e4f94c0268014d8c10dd85d5df34a46561.title: The Tunnel Effect: Building Data Representations in Deep Neural Networks
f574f4e4f94c0268014d8c10dd85d5df34a46561.research_question: How do data representations in deep neural networks depend on the depth of a layer, and what are the implications of this dependence for generalization, out-of-distribution robustness, and continual learning?
f574f4e4f94c0268014d8c10dd85d5df34a46561.hypothesis: Sufficiently large neural networks develop a configuration in which network layers split into two distinct groups: an extractor that builds linearly-separable representations and a tunnel that compresses these representations, with the tunnel hindering out-of-distribution generalization and influencing continual learning dynamics.
f574f4e4f94c0268014d8c10dd85d5df34a46561.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically investigate the structure and dynamics of data representations across layers in overparameterized deep neural networks. Multiple families of architectures, including MLPs, VGGs, and ResNets, will be trained on supervised image classification tasks. Layer-wise analysis will be performed using linear probing to assess the linear separability of representations, spectral analysis to compute the numerical rank of layer activations, and CKA similarity to quantify representational similarity between layers. The evolution of these metrics will be tracked throughout training to identify the emergence of distinct network regions (extractor and tunnel) and to analyze their impact on generalization and transferability. Additional experiments will manipulate network depth, width, and dataset complexity to study their effects on the formation and properties of these regions.
f574f4e4f94c0268014d8c10dd85d5df34a46561.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training MLPs, VGGs, and ResNets of varying depths and widths on standard image classification datasets such as CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and CINIC-10. Linear probes will be attached to each layer to measure classification accuracy, and numerical rank will be computed via singular value decomposition of sample covariance matrices. CKA similarity and intra/inter-class variance will be used to further characterize representations. Out-of-distribution generalization will be tested by training on one dataset (e.g., CIFAR-10) and probing on another (e.g., a subset of CIFAR-100). Continual learning scenarios will be simulated by sequentially training on disjoint class subsets and measuring catastrophic forgetting and task transfer, including experiments with mixed extractor/tunnel combinations and retraining of classification heads. Baselines will include varying network capacities and dataset complexities, with evaluation metrics such as linear probe accuracy, numerical rank, CKA similarity, and forgetting rates.
f574f4e4f94c0268014d8c10dd85d5df34a46561.novelty_claims: The research introduces the tunnel effect, a novel conceptualization of deep neural network structure in which layers naturally split into extractor and tunnel regions with distinct functional roles. It provides empirical evidence that the tunnel emerges early in training, persists throughout optimization, and is prevalent across architectures and datasets. The work demonstrates that the tunnel compresses representations, leading to degraded out-of-distribution generalization and increased catastrophic forgetting in continual learning. The findings establish new links between network capacity, task complexity, and the structure of learned representations, offering actionable recommendations for model design, transfer learning, and efficient inference.

f57749e893c9d532e5b65845cea7adacedc0a4aa.title: Generalizing Nonlinear ICA Beyond Structural Sparsity
f57749e893c9d532e5b65845cea7adacedc0a4aa.research_question: How can the identifiability of nonlinear independent component analysis (ICA) be generalized to settings where structural sparsity, bijectivity, and source independence assumptions are partially or wholly violated, including cases with undercompleteness, partial sparsity, source dependence, and flexible grouping structures?
f57749e893c9d532e5b65845cea7adacedc0a4aa.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that identifiability of latent sources in nonlinear ICA can be achieved under weaker and more general conditions than previously established, specifically when structural sparsity holds only for a subset of sources, when the number of observed variables exceeds the number of sources (undercompleteness), and when some sources are dependent or grouped in flexible structures.
f57749e893c9d532e5b65845cea7adacedc0a4aa.proposed_method: A new theoretical framework will be developed to establish identifiability results for nonlinear ICA under relaxed assumptions. The approach will formalize the data-generating process as a smooth, possibly non-bijective nonlinear mixing function from latent sources to observed variables, allowing for undercomplete scenarios (more observed variables than sources). The method will introduce and leverage the concept of structural sparsity on the Jacobian of the mixing function, but only require it to hold for subsets of sources (partial sparsity). Additionally, the framework will accommodate partial source dependence by partitioning sources into independent and dependent subsets, and will extend to cases with flexible grouping structures, such as independent subspaces of varying dimensions. Theoretical proofs will be constructed to show identifiability up to permissible indeterminacies (e.g., element-wise or subspace-wise invertible transformations and permutations) under these generalized settings.
f57749e893c9d532e5b65845cea7adacedc0a4aa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets to empirically validate the proposed identifiability results. Synthetic datasets will be generated under controlled conditions to satisfy or violate specific assumptions (e.g., structural sparsity, undercompleteness, source dependence), and ablation studies will be performed to assess the necessity of each assumption. Real-world datasets, such as the Triangles dataset (synthetic images with known generative factors) and EMNIST (handwritten digits), will be used to test the practical applicability of the theory. The estimation procedure will employ flow-based generative models (e.g., General Incompressible-flow Network) with sparsity regularization on the Jacobian, using a regularized maximum-likelihood objective. Evaluation metrics will include the mean correlation coefficient (MCC) between true and estimated sources, and the percentage of random structures satisfying structural sparsity as a function of undercompleteness. Multiple trials with random seeds will ensure statistical robustness.
f57749e893c9d532e5b65845cea7adacedc0a4aa.novelty_claims: The proposed research establishes, for the first time, identifiability results for nonlinear ICA in settings with undercompleteness, partial sparsity, and partial source dependence, without requiring bijectivity or universal independence of sources. The framework further generalizes identifiability to cases with flexible grouping structures, such as mixtures of independent subspaces of varying dimensions. These results significantly broaden the applicability of nonlinear ICA to real-world scenarios where previous theoretical guarantees did not hold, and provide partial identifiability even when key assumptions are only partially satisfied. Theoretical advancements are complemented by empirical validation on both synthetic and real-world data.

f5789596531fad358c3166fdb5bd72d8e661c32c.title: Small-scale proxies for large-scale Transformer training instabilities
f5789596531fad358c3166fdb5bd72d8e661c32c.research_question: How can training instabilities observed in large-scale Transformer models be systematically reproduced, studied, and mitigated at small scale, and what methodologies allow for predicting and preventing such instabilities across model and optimizer configurations?
f5789596531fad358c3166fdb5bd72d8e661c32c.hypothesis: Training instabilities characteristic of large-scale Transformer models, such as attention logit growth and output logit divergence, can be reliably reproduced at small scale by manipulating hyperparameters (e.g., learning rate), and mitigations effective at large scale will also be effective in small-scale regimes. Furthermore, scaling trends of model characteristics can be used to predict and preemptively address emerging instabilities.
f5789596531fad358c3166fdb5bd72d8e661c32c.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves training small-scale Transformer models using a controlled experimental setup that mirrors large-scale configurations, including decoder-only architectures, auto-regressive loss, and standardized hyperparameters (e.g., AdamW optimizer, cosine learning rate decay, rotary positional embeddings, and C4 dataset). Systematic sweeps over learning rates and other hyperparameters will be conducted to elicit known instabilities, such as attention logit growth and output logit divergence. Key interventions, including qk-layernorm and z-loss regularization, will be applied to assess their effectiveness in stabilizing training across a wide range of learning rates. Additional optimizer and model interventions—such as warm-up schedules, independent weight decay, µParam parameterization, and scaling of width versus depth—will be evaluated for their impact on training stability and learning rate sensitivity. The methodology also includes tracking and analyzing scaling trends of model characteristics (e.g., activation and gradient norms) to predict the onset of new or undocumented instabilities before they manifest.
f5789596531fad358c3166fdb5bd72d8e661c32c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on small-scale Transformer models trained on the C4 dataset, using a setup similar to GPT-2 with Flax and JAX on TPUs in bfloat16 precision. Model parameters, including embedding size, depth, and number of heads, will be scaled jointly and independently to study their effects. Learning rates will be swept across several orders of magnitude, and learning rate sensitivity will be quantified as the deviation from optimal validation loss across this range. Baseline configurations will include standard AdamW optimizer settings, with ablations on warm-up length, weight decay (independent and coupled), and batch size. Interventions such as qk-layernorm, z-loss, and µParam will be systematically applied and compared. Evaluation metrics will include validation loss, learning rate sensitivity, maximum attention logit values, and gradient root mean square (RMS) across layers. Additional experiments will extrapolate scaling trends to predict instability thresholds and validate predictions by training larger models at critical hyperparameter values.
f5789596531fad358c3166fdb5bd72d8e661c32c.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a systematic framework for reproducing and studying large-scale Transformer training instabilities at small scale, enabling resource-efficient investigation of failure modes. It establishes that interventions effective at large scale are also effective in small models, and proposes learning rate sensitivity as a practical metric for summarizing stability across hyperparameter sweeps. The methodology enables prediction of instabilities before they emerge by analyzing scaling trends of model characteristics, and identifies optimizer hyperparameters (such as AdamW epsilon) as critical factors in stability at scale. The approach also provides insights into the relative effects of scaling width versus depth and evaluates the practical impact of advanced parameterizations like µParam in stabilizing training dynamics.

f57edfe71eb044da97b56cf39157002174644352.title: FedBiOT: LLM Local Fine-tuning in Federated Learning without Full Model
f57edfe71eb044da97b56cf39157002174644352.research_question: How can large language models be collaboratively fine-tuned in a federated learning setting when clients lack access to the full model, while also minimizing computation and communication overhead and preserving data privacy?
f57edfe71eb044da97b56cf39157002174644352.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by compressing large language models into an emulator-adapter architecture and formulating the training as a bi-level optimization problem, it is possible to enable effective federated fine-tuning without requiring clients to access the full model, thereby reducing resource consumption and maintaining competitive task performance.
f57edfe71eb044da97b56cf39157002174644352.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a resource-efficient federated learning framework for large language models (LLMs) called FedBiOT. The method begins by compressing the LLM on the server using uniform layer dropout and partitioning it into two components: an emulator (a sub-model simulating the original model's behavior) and an adapter (a lightweight, trainable module for domain-specific adaptation). LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) modules are incorporated into both emulator and adapter to further reduce trainable parameters. The server aligns the emulator to the original model using knowledge distillation on a public dataset, minimizing both representation and output distribution discrepancies. During federated training, clients only fine-tune the adapter locally using their private data, while the server aggregates adapter updates and periodically re-aligns the emulator using public data, all formulated as a bi-level optimization problem to address data distribution shifts between server and clients.
f57edfe71eb044da97b56cf39157002174644352.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using the LLaMA-2-7B model as the base LLM. Three domain-specific NLP tasks are evaluated: math problem-solving (GSM-8K), code generation (Rosetta and HumanEvalX), and question answering (Dolly-15K and HELM). Data is partitioned across clients either i.i.d. or non-i.i.d., depending on the task. The Alpaca dataset serves as the public dataset for server-side emulator alignment. Baselines include Offsite-tuning and FedOT, both enhanced with LoRA for parameter efficiency. Evaluation metrics include task-specific accuracy (e.g., Pass@1, Pass@10 for code, Top-1 accuracy for QA), and resource usage is measured in terms of trainable parameters, FLOPs per token, and communication cost per round. Hyperparameters such as dropout rates, adapter sizes, and learning rates are tuned via grid search, and results are averaged over multiple random seeds.
f57edfe71eb044da97b56cf39157002174644352.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to address both the lack of full model access and the need for resource-efficient federated fine-tuning of LLMs. By introducing a bi-level optimization formulation and a modular emulator-adapter architecture, the method enables clients to fine-tune LLMs without loading the full model or sharing private data. The approach significantly reduces computation and communication overhead compared to existing methods, while maintaining or improving task performance. The design also naturally accommodates data distribution shifts between server and clients, and the use of LoRA modules further enhances scalability and efficiency.

f5a0c57f90c6abe31482e9f320ccac5ee789b135.title: Align Your Latents: High-Resolution Video Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
f5a0c57f90c6abe31482e9f320ccac5ee789b135.research_question: How can high-resolution, temporally consistent, and long-duration video synthesis be achieved efficiently using generative models, particularly in resource-intensive domains such as real-world driving scenes and creative text-to-video content generation?
f5a0c57f90c6abe31482e9f320ccac5ee789b135.hypothesis: Introducing temporal alignment layers into pre-trained latent diffusion models (LDMs) will enable efficient, high-resolution, and temporally coherent video generation by leveraging large-scale image datasets for spatial modeling and focused video data for temporal consistency, while maintaining computational and memory efficiency.
f5a0c57f90c6abe31482e9f320ccac5ee789b135.proposed_method: The proposed method builds upon latent diffusion models (LDMs) pre-trained on large-scale image datasets. Temporal neural network layers are introduced and interleaved with the existing spatial layers of the LDM, enabling the model to learn temporal alignment and consistency across video frames. During training, the spatial (image) layers are kept fixed, and only the temporal layers are fine-tuned using encoded video sequences in latent space, ensuring efficient use of limited video data. To further enhance spatial and temporal resolution, the approach includes temporally fine-tuned diffusion model upsamplers, which are trained either in pixel or latent space to produce temporally consistent super-resolved videos. For long video generation and high frame rates, prediction and interpolation models are trained using masking strategies, allowing the model to generate or interpolate frames conditioned on context frames. The methodology also supports personalized text-to-video generation by transferring trained temporal layers to fine-tuned image LDMs.
f5a0c57f90c6abe31482e9f320ccac5ee789b135.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple datasets, including a large-scale real driving scene (RDS) video dataset (683,060 videos at 512×1024 resolution), the WebVid-10M dataset for text-to-video tasks, and additional datasets such as Mountain Biking and UCF-101 for benchmarking. Baselines will include state-of-the-art video GANs (e.g., Long Video GAN), previous diffusion-based video models, and independent frame-wise upsampling methods. Evaluation metrics will comprise frame-wise Frechet Inception Distance (FID), Frechet Video Distance (FVD), CLIP similarity, Inception Score (IS), and human preference studies. The experimental setup will involve training the spatial LDM backbone on image data, followed by temporal fine-tuning on video data, and training/updating super-resolution upsamplers for high-resolution outputs. Ablation studies will assess the impact of temporal layers, context guidance, and decoder fine-tuning on video quality and temporal consistency.
f5a0c57f90c6abe31482e9f320ccac5ee789b135.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel framework for turning pre-trained image LDMs into efficient, high-resolution video generators by inserting and fine-tuning temporal alignment layers in latent space. It claims the ability to leverage large-scale image datasets for spatial modeling while requiring only limited video data for temporal consistency, resulting in computational and memory efficiency. The approach enables state-of-the-art performance in high-resolution, long-duration video synthesis, supports temporally consistent super-resolution, and is the first to demonstrate personalized text-to-video generation by transferring temporal layers to fine-tuned image LDMs. The method is also extensible to various domains, including autonomous driving simulation and creative content generation.

f5a6363a39bb4a7a3ea9e17e95f43ce7cc5ca23a.title: CoSy: Evaluating Textual Explanations of Neurons
f5a6363a39bb4a7a3ea9e17e95f43ce7cc5ca23a.research_question: How can the quality of textual explanations for neurons in deep neural networks be quantitatively and automatically evaluated in a unified, architecture-agnostic manner, particularly for open-vocabulary explanations in computer vision models?
