f5a6363a39bb4a7a3ea9e17e95f43ce7cc5ca23a.hypothesis: A generative-model-based evaluation framework that synthesizes visual representations from textual neuron explanations and quantitatively compares neuron activations on these versus control images can provide a reliable, general-purpose measure of explanation quality, enabling robust benchmarking across explanation methods and model architectures.
f5a6363a39bb4a7a3ea9e17e95f43ce7cc5ca23a.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces an automatic evaluation framework (COSY) for textual explanations of neurons. The approach consists of three main steps: (1) For each neuron and its associated textual explanation, a generative text-to-image model is used to synthesize a set of images representing the explanation. (2) The neuron’s activations are collected for both the synthetic images and a control dataset of natural images unrelated to the explanation. (3) The quality of the explanation is quantified by comparing the distributions of neuron activations on the synthetic and control images using metrics such as Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) and Mean Activation Difference (MAD). The method is architecture-agnostic and can be applied to any computer vision model and explanation method, leveraging recent advances in generative AI to bridge the gap between textual and visual domains.
f5a6363a39bb4a7a3ea9e17e95f43ce7cc5ca23a.experiment_details: Experiments will involve evaluating the proposed framework on a variety of pre-trained computer vision models, such as ResNet18, ResNet50, DenseNet161, GoogleNet, and ViT-B/16, using datasets including ImageNet and Places365. The evaluation will benchmark several state-of-the-art neuron explanation methods (e.g., MILAN, INVERT, CLIP-Dissect, FALCON) across different layers and neuron types. Synthetic images will be generated using open-source text-to-image models (e.g., Stable Diffusion XL, Stable Cascade) with carefully designed prompts. The framework’s reliability will be validated through sanity checks, including similarity analyses between synthetic and natural images, assessment of model responses to both image types, and comparison of scores for true versus random explanations. Evaluation metrics will include AUC and MAD, and results will be compared across methods and layers to assess explanation quality.
f5a6363a39bb4a7a3ea9e17e95f43ce7cc5ca23a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first general-purpose, quantitative, and architecture-agnostic method for evaluating textual explanations of neurons, enabling direct benchmarking across different explanation methods and models. It leverages generative models to synthesize visual representations from open-vocabulary textual explanations, facilitating a unified evaluation approach that does not require human annotation or ground truth labels for latent neurons. The framework provides new insights into the reliability and limitations of existing neuron explanation methods, particularly highlighting the challenges in explaining lower-layer neurons and the variability in explanation quality across methods.

f5afaccfe90268485a9961c5771ec5e71e9b806c.title: Extending Context Window of Large Language Models via Positional Interpolation
f5afaccfe90268485a9961c5771ec5e71e9b806c.research_question: How can the context window of pre-trained large language models, particularly those using RoPE-based positional encodings, be efficiently and stably extended to handle much longer input sequences while preserving model quality on both long and original context window tasks?
f5afaccfe90268485a9961c5771ec5e71e9b806c.hypothesis: Position Interpolation, which linearly rescales input position indices to fit within the original pre-trained context window range, enables stable and effective extension of context windows in RoPE-based LLMs with minimal fine-tuning, outperforming direct extrapolation or fine-tuning approaches in both stability and empirical performance.
f5afaccfe90268485a9961c5771ec5e71e9b806c.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces Position Interpolation (PI), a technique that extends the context window of RoPE-based large language models by linearly down-scaling position indices so that the maximum index matches the original pre-trained context window limit. Instead of extrapolating positional encodings beyond the trained range, which can destabilize attention computations, PI interpolates position encodings at non-integer positions, leveraging the smoothness of the trigonometric basis in RoPE. This transformation is applied by modifying the positional encoding function such that for a new context window L', the position index m is mapped as m * L / L', where L is the original context window. The model architecture and weights remain unchanged, and only the position encoding computation is altered. Fine-tuning is performed on the extended context window using next-token prediction on a large-scale corpus, allowing the model to adapt to the new positional encoding distribution efficiently.
f5afaccfe90268485a9961c5771ec5e71e9b806c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by extending pre-trained LLaMA models (7B, 13B, 33B, 65B) from their original 2048-token context window up to 32768 tokens using Position Interpolation. Fine-tuning will be performed for 1000 steps on large-scale datasets such as the Pile and RedPajama, using next-token prediction as the objective. Baselines will include direct fine-tuning with longer context windows and evaluation without any adaptation. Evaluation will cover multiple tasks: (1) language modeling on PG-19 and Arxiv Math Proof-pile datasets, measuring perplexity at various context window lengths; (2) passkey retrieval tasks to assess effective context window size; (3) standard LLaMA benchmarks (BoolQ, PIQA, Race, WinoGrande) within the original context window; and (4) long document summarization on the GovReport dataset, using ROUGE scores. Model performance will be compared in terms of perplexity, retrieval accuracy, and benchmark scores, with detailed tracking of degradation or improvement as context windows are extended.
f5afaccfe90268485a9961c5771ec5e71e9b806c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a simple yet theoretically grounded method for extending the context window of RoPE-based LLMs without modifying model architecture or weights. Position Interpolation is claimed to be significantly more stable than extrapolation, with theoretical analysis showing the upper bound on attention score errors is at least 600x smaller. The method enables efficient adaptation to much longer context windows with minimal fine-tuning, preserves model quality on original tasks, and allows seamless reuse of existing model infrastructure. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate strong performance on long-context tasks and competitive results on standard benchmarks, establishing Position Interpolation as a practical and effective solution for context window extension.

f5b3cb14e0947c62b470d2072483481f14258738.title: A Solvable Model of Neural Scaling Laws
f5b3cb14e0947c62b470d2072483481f14258738.research_question: What are the fundamental statistical properties of datasets and model architectures that give rise to neural scaling laws in large-scale machine learning, and under what conditions do these scaling laws arise or break down?
f5b3cb14e0947c62b470d2072483481f14258738.hypothesis: Neural scaling laws emerge when datasets possess specific power-law spectral properties and when models employ nonlinear feature maps that extend these power laws, resulting in predictable power-law scaling of test loss with respect to both model size and dataset size, until limited by resource bottlenecks or the intrinsic dimensionality of the data.
f5b3cb14e0947c62b470d2072483481f14258738.proposed_method: A joint statistical model will be developed, combining a generative data model with a random feature model to analytically capture the emergence of neural scaling laws. The approach involves constructing datasets with controlled spectral properties, specifically power-law spectra, and applying nonlinear random feature maps to these data representations. The model will be solved in the dual limit of large dataset size and large model parameter count, using tools from random matrix theory, including a diagrammatic approach to efficiently compute expectations relevant to test loss. Analytical expressions for test loss as a function of both dataset size and model size will be derived, and the effects of varying the latent space dimensionality and feature map nonlinearity will be systematically explored.
f5b3cb14e0947c62b470d2072483481f14258738.experiment_details: Experiments will involve generating synthetic datasets with tunable spectral properties, such as power-law and Marchenko-Pastur spectra, and evaluating generalized linear models and random feature models trained on these datasets. Test loss will be measured as a function of both training set size and number of model parameters, with and without regularization. Baseline comparisons will include linear models on Gaussian data and models without feature mapping. Evaluation metrics will focus on test loss scaling behavior, plateau effects, and the breakdown of scaling laws as resource bottlenecks or latent space limits are approached. Analytical results will be validated against numerical simulations.
f5b3cb14e0947c62b470d2072483481f14258738.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a solvable theoretical framework that jointly models data generation and feature mapping to explain neural scaling laws, extending beyond previous empirical and partial theoretical results. It identifies precise statistical prerequisites in data and model architecture for scaling laws to arise, provides a mechanism for the extension and breakdown of power-law scaling, and offers new analytical tools—such as a diagrammatic random matrix theory approach—for tractable analysis in the large-scale regime. The research also clarifies the optimality of equiparameterization and predicts new regimes where scaling laws fail, offering insights not previously observed in empirical studies.

f5c73d9e6641b018b633690102121f5605d34fb0.title: Editing Large Language Models: Problems, Methods, and Opportunities
f5c73d9e6641b018b633690102121f5605d34fb0.research_question: How can large language models be efficiently and reliably edited to update, correct, or remove specific knowledge or behaviors, while minimizing negative side effects and ensuring robust generalization and efficiency across different model architectures and scales?
f5c73d9e6641b018b633690102121f5605d34fb0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a systematic evaluation and comparison of existing model editing techniques, combined with the development of new benchmarks and comprehensive metrics, will reveal the strengths and limitations of current approaches and highlight opportunities for more effective, robust, and efficient model editing methods for large language models.
f5c73d9e6641b018b633690102121f5605d34fb0.proposed_method: A comprehensive research program is proposed to systematically evaluate, compare, and advance methods for editing large language models (LLMs). The methodology will include: (1) formalizing the problem definition of model editing, including the concepts of reliability, generalization, and locality; (2) categorizing and implementing representative editing techniques, such as memory-based retrieval, additional parameter injection, meta-learning, and direct parameter modification (e.g., ROME, MEMIT, SERAC, T-Patcher, IKE, MEND); (3) developing and releasing new benchmark datasets and evaluation protocols that assess not only single-edit cases but also batch and sequential edits, as well as robust generalization (portability), side effects (locality), and computational efficiency; (4) conducting controlled experiments on a range of LLM architectures and sizes, including both encoder-decoder and decoder-only models, to assess scalability and transferability; and (5) analyzing the results to identify bottlenecks, failure modes, and promising directions for future model editing research.
f5c73d9e6641b018b633690102121f5605d34fb0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using established factual knowledge editing datasets such as ZsRE and COUNTERFACT, as well as newly constructed benchmarks to assess portability (robust generalization), locality (side effects), and efficiency (time and memory usage). The evaluation will be performed on multiple model architectures, including T5-XL (3B), GPT-J (6B), OPT-13B, and GPT-NEOX-20B, covering both encoder-decoder and decoder-only paradigms. Baselines will include fine-tuning selected layers (FT-L), memory-based approaches (SERAC, IKE), parameter modification methods (ROME, MEMIT), and meta-learning approaches (MEND, KE), among others. Metrics for evaluation will include reliability (accuracy on edited facts), generalization (accuracy on paraphrased or related facts), locality (preservation of unrelated outputs), portability (transfer of edits to related contexts), and computational efficiency (wall-clock time and GPU memory usage). Batch and sequential editing scenarios will be tested to assess scalability and cumulative side effects.
f5c73d9e6641b018b633690102121f5605d34fb0.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a comprehensive framework for evaluating and comparing model editing techniques for LLMs, including the development of new benchmarks and metrics that go beyond existing evaluations. The approach systematically examines not only the direct effects of edits but also their generalization, side effects, and computational efficiency across a range of model architectures and sizes. The research will provide the first in-depth empirical analysis of editing methods on large-scale generative models, identify critical limitations of current techniques (such as poor portability and locality), and offer actionable insights and resources to guide future research and practical deployment of model editing in LLMs.

f5dd35ddea0c96db92d748798fb802168135b1e7.title: Constrained Posterior Sampling: Time Series Generation with Hard Constraints
f5dd35ddea0c96db92d748798fb802168135b1e7.research_question: How can realistic time series data be generated such that samples strictly satisfy a wide variety of hard, domain-specific constraints, while maintaining high sample quality and scalability to many constraints, without requiring additional training or hyperparameter tuning?
f5dd35ddea0c96db92d748798fb802168135b1e7.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a diffusion-based sampling algorithm that projects the posterior mean estimate onto the constraint set after each denoising update can efficiently generate high-quality time series samples that satisfy a large number of hard constraints, without the need for retraining or external realism enforcers.
f5dd35ddea0c96db92d748798fb802168135b1e7.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, Constrained Posterior Sampling (CPS), is developed for diffusion-based time series generation under hard constraints. The approach alternates between standard denoising steps of a pre-trained diffusion model (such as DDIM) and a projection step, where the posterior mean estimate is projected onto the constraint set using off-the-shelf optimization solvers. The projection is formulated as an unconstrained minimization of a convex objective that penalizes constraint violations, with a time-varying penalty coefficient that increases as denoising progresses, ensuring that constraints are enforced more strictly in later steps. The method does not require additional training, hyperparameter tuning, or external models to enforce realism, as subsequent denoising steps naturally correct any artifacts introduced by projection. The approach is designed to handle both linear and certain classes of non-linear constraints, and theoretical analysis provides convergence guarantees under mild assumptions.
f5dd35ddea0c96db92d748798fb802168135b1e7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six real-world and simulated datasets from finance (Stocks), environmental monitoring (Air Quality), and transportation (Traffic), including both unconditional and conditional generation settings. The evaluation will compare CPS against state-of-the-art baselines such as COP, COP-FT, GuidedDiffTime, Diffusion-TS, Projected Diffusion Models (PDM), and PRODIGY, using a common denoiser backbone for fairness. Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Time Series Distance (FTSD), Joint-FTSD, Train-on-Synthetic-Test-on-Real (TSTR), Discriminative Score (DS), Dynamic Time Warping (DTW), and average constraint violation magnitude. Constraints will be extracted from test samples and include statistical features such as means, extrema, OHLC constraints for stocks, and autocorrelation. The experimental protocol will assess both distributional similarity and per-sample fidelity, as well as scalability to a large number of constraints.
f5dd35ddea0c96db92d748798fb802168135b1e7.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a training-free, hyperparameter-free, and scalable framework for constrained time series generation using diffusion models. CPS uniquely projects the posterior mean estimate (rather than noisy latents) onto the constraint set after each denoising step, allowing for efficient satisfaction of up to 100 constraints without retraining. The approach eliminates the need for external realism enforcers and mitigates the adverse effects of projection through subsequent denoising. Theoretical contributions include convergence guarantees for linear constraint sets and insights into penalty scheduling. Empirical results demonstrate substantial improvements in sample quality, similarity to real data, and constraint satisfaction over existing methods, with up to 70% and 22% improvements in sample quality and similarity, respectively, on real-world datasets.

f5e1993f3f505e8fbb9cac9231285c8c9f1712a7.title: Cal-QL: Calibrated Offline RL Pre-Training for Efficient Online Fine-Tuning
f5e1993f3f505e8fbb9cac9231285c8c9f1712a7.research_question: How can offline reinforcement learning be leveraged to obtain policy initializations that enable efficient and effective online fine-tuning with limited interaction, while avoiding performance degradation or slow improvement during the fine-tuning phase?
f5e1993f3f505e8fbb9cac9231285c8c9f1712a7.hypothesis: Calibrating the value function learned during conservative offline RL pre-training, such that it lower-bounds the value of the learned policy and upper-bounds the value of a reference policy (e.g., the behavior policy), will enable faster and more stable online fine-tuning by preventing initial unlearning and improving cumulative regret.
f5e1993f3f505e8fbb9cac9231285c8c9f1712a7.proposed_method: A new approach, Calibrated Q-Learning (Cal-QL), is developed to learn a conservative yet calibrated value function from offline data. Cal-QL extends the conservative Q-learning (CQL) framework by modifying the regularizer: it constrains the learned Q-function to produce Q-values that are no smaller than the Q-value of a reference policy, typically the behavior policy from the offline dataset. This is achieved by masking the regularizer's push-down on out-of-distribution actions if the learned Q-value is already below the reference value, ensuring calibration as defined by a lower bound on the learned policy and an upper bound on the reference policy. The method can be implemented as a simple modification to CQL, requiring no additional hyperparameters, and supports both tabular and function approximation settings. During fine-tuning, the method continues to train on a mixture of offline and online data, maintaining the calibration constraint to facilitate rapid and stable improvement.
f5e1993f3f505e8fbb9cac9231285c8c9f1712a7.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a diverse set of benchmark tasks, including AntMaze and Franka Kitchen domains from D4RL, Adroit dexterous manipulation tasks, and a vision-based robotic manipulation task. The evaluation protocol compares Cal-QL to several state-of-the-art baselines: online SAC from scratch, offline RL methods fine-tuned online (CQL, IQL, AWAC), and hybrid approaches (O3F, ODT, HybridRL, CQL+SAC, SAC+offlinedata, RLPD). Performance is measured both before and after fine-tuning using normalized return scores, as well as cumulative regret over the course of online fine-tuning. Additional ablation studies examine the effect of dataset composition (narrow vs. diverse coverage), the impact of errors in reference value function estimation, and the influence of high update-to-data (UTD) ratios. All methods are evaluated using consistent protocols and multiple random seeds.
f5e1993f3f505e8fbb9cac9231285c8c9f1712a7.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the concept of calibration for conservative offline RL, formally defining and enforcing a value function constraint that prevents initial unlearning during online fine-tuning. Cal-QL is the first method to combine conservative value estimation with explicit calibration against a reference policy, resulting in improved cumulative regret and faster performance improvement across a wide range of tasks. The approach is simple to implement as a modification to existing CQL algorithms and does not require additional hyperparameters. Theoretical analysis provides new regret bounds that improve upon prior work, and empirical results demonstrate consistent state-of-the-art performance in both asymptotic return and sample efficiency.

f5e9337477d7a9eb6267d0310549fdefafbb7fe2.title: Transformers learn to implement preconditioned gradient descent for in-context learning
f5e9337477d7a9eb6267d0310549fdefafbb7fe2.research_question: Can transformer architectures learn to implement gradient-based optimization algorithms, such as preconditioned gradient descent, through training on random instances of linear regression, and what is the structure of the loss landscape that enables such algorithmic learning in the context of in-context learning?
f5e9337477d7a9eb6267d0310549fdefafbb7fe2.hypothesis: Transformers trained on random instances of linear regression will learn to implement gradient-based optimization algorithms, specifically preconditioned gradient descent, and the loss landscape of such training objectives will contain global minima or critical points corresponding to these algorithms.
f5e9337477d7a9eb6267d0310549fdefafbb7fe2.proposed_method: The proposed research will analyze transformer architectures, specifically linear transformers without softmax, trained on random linear regression tasks. The architecture will consist of L stacked linear self-attention layers, each parameterized by matrices that may be constrained to enforce sparsity or symmetry, or left unconstrained for more generality. The training objective will be the in-context loss, which measures the squared error between the transformer's prediction and the true label for a held-out example, averaged over randomly generated linear regression problems. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to characterize the global minima and critical points of the loss landscape for various settings (single-layer, multi-layer, with/without parameter constraints), and to interpret these points as implementations of gradient-based algorithms such as preconditioned gradient descent or more general adaptive methods. Empirical experiments will be performed to validate the theoretical findings and to observe the convergence of trained parameters to the theoretically predicted structures.
f5e9337477d7a9eb6267d0310549fdefafbb7fe2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets generated as random instances of linear regression, where covariates x(i) are sampled from multivariate Gaussian distributions (with isotropic or non-isotropic covariance), and regression weights w are also sampled from appropriate Gaussian distributions. The transformer models will be trained using optimizers such as ADAM or L-BFGS, with minibatch sizes and gradient clipping as needed. Baselines will include standard gradient descent and adaptive methods such as Adagrad. Evaluation metrics will focus on the in-context loss (mean squared error on held-out predictions), as well as the convergence of learned parameter matrices to theoretically optimal forms (measured via normalized Frobenius norm distances to identity or covariance-inverse matrices). Additional analyses will visualize the learned weights and track their evolution during training to confirm alignment with theoretical predictions.
f5e9337477d7a9eb6267d0310549fdefafbb7fe2.novelty_claims: The research proposes the first theoretical characterization of how transformers can learn to implement gradient-based optimization algorithms, such as preconditioned gradient descent, through training on random problem instances, rather than by explicit parameter construction. It demonstrates that the global minimum of the in-context loss for a single-layer transformer corresponds to a step of preconditioned gradient descent, with the preconditioning matrix adapting to both data distribution and sample variance. For multi-layer transformers, the research identifies critical points corresponding to multiple iterations of such algorithms, and extends the analysis to more general parameterizations that go beyond standard optimization methods. The work establishes a theoretical and empirical foundation for understanding algorithmic learning in transformers, particularly in the context of in-context learning.

f65335ed3d20c041e226e959ba73c28336392ab7.title: video-SALMONN-o1: Reasoning-enhanced Audio-visual Large Language Model
f65335ed3d20c041e226e959ba73c28336392ab7.research_question: How can the reasoning abilities of large language models be enhanced for general video understanding tasks that involve complex audio-visual information and require step-by-step logical inference?
f65335ed3d20c041e226e959ba73c28336392ab7.hypothesis: Incorporating reasoning-intensive training data and developing a process-level preference optimization method tailored for multimodal inputs will significantly improve the reasoning capabilities and overall performance of audio-visual large language models on general video understanding tasks.
f65335ed3d20c041e226e959ba73c28336392ab7.proposed_method: A novel audio-visual large language model, video-SALMONN-o1, will be developed with a modular architecture that processes video inputs through separate visual and audio encoders, followed by modality aligners and an interleaved synchronization module to produce joint audio-visual token sequences for a language model backbone. The model will be trained in multiple stages, starting with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on a newly constructed, reasoning-intensive dataset featuring challenging audio-visual questions and step-by-step solutions. To further enhance reasoning, a process direct preference optimization (pDPO) algorithm will be introduced, which leverages contrastive step selection to efficiently model step-level pairwise rewards for multimodal reasoning paths. The pDPO method focuses on the most error-prone reasoning steps, identified via input perturbation and KL-divergence analysis, and applies pairwise rollouts to optimize the model's ability to select better reasoning steps without requiring external reward models or two-pass pipelines.
f65335ed3d20c041e226e959ba73c28336392ab7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmarks, including the newly proposed RivaBench (over 4,000 expert-curated question-answer pairs across academic presentations, standup comedy, and synthetic video detection), as well as established datasets such as VideoMME and NExT-QA. Baselines will include state-of-the-art open-source and proprietary audio-visual LLMs (e.g., LLaVA-OneVision, Video-LLaMA2, Gemini-1.5-pro, GPT-4o). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy and F1-score, with specific attention to step-by-step reasoning performance and zero-shot synthetic video detection capabilities. The experimental setup involves training on high-quality audio-visual QA pairs, using SFT and pDPO, and comparing models trained with different reward modeling strategies (ORM, PRM, pDPO) and data partitions (reasoning-intensive vs. general SFT data). Ablation studies will analyze the impact of reasoning-intensive data, the number of steps used in pDPO, and the effectiveness of contrastive step selection.
f65335ed3d20c041e226e959ba73c28336392ab7.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first open-source reasoning-enhanced audio-visual LLM designed specifically for general video understanding tasks. It pioneers the use of RL-based reasoning optimization for multimodal LLMs in this domain, with the development of the pDPO algorithm for efficient, step-level reward modeling tailored to audio-visual reasoning. The creation of RivaBench establishes the first reasoning-intensive benchmark for video understanding with expert annotations. The approach demonstrates consistent and significant improvements over strong baselines in accuracy and interpretability, and exhibits emergent zero-shot synthetic video detection abilities not seen in prior models.

f653569b131176dfed8842694b5ad2ead5e4b923.title: Tree-Ring Watermarks: Fingerprints for Diffusion Images that are Invisible and Robust
f653569b131176dfed8842694b5ad2ead5e4b923.research_question: How can diffusion model outputs be robustly watermarked with invisible fingerprints that survive common image manipulations and enable reliable detection, without degrading image quality or requiring model retraining?
f653569b131176dfed8842694b5ad2ead5e4b923.hypothesis: Embedding a carefully constructed pattern in the Fourier space of the initial noise vector used by diffusion models will produce watermarks that are invisible to humans, robust to common image transformations, and reliably detectable by inverting the diffusion process, all without significant impact on image quality.
f653569b131176dfed8842694b5ad2ead5e4b923.proposed_method: A new watermarking framework is developed that embeds a 'key' pattern into the Fourier transform of the initial Gaussian noise vector used in diffusion model sampling. The key is structured using circular or ring-shaped masks in Fourier space, designed to be invariant to transformations such as rotations, crops, dilations, flips, and color jitter. During image generation, the diffusion process proceeds unmodified except for the altered initial noise, ensuring no visible artifacts are introduced. For detection, the diffusion process is inverted (using DDIM inversion) to recover the approximate initial noise vector from a suspect image, and the presence of the key is tested by measuring the distance in Fourier space between the recovered noise and the embedded key. Statistical hypothesis testing is used to assign a p-value to each detection, allowing for interpretable and tunable false positive rates.
f653569b131176dfed8842694b5ad2ead5e4b923.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two diffusion models: Stable Diffusion-v2 (a state-of-the-art text-to-image model) and a 256x256 ImageNet diffusion model. The evaluation will use 1,000 watermarked and 1,000 unwatermarked images per run, with FID (Frechet Inception Distance) and CLIPScore used to assess image quality, and ROC AUC and TPR@1%FPR to measure watermark detection accuracy. Robustness will be tested under a battery of common image manipulations, including rotations, JPEG compression, cropping and scaling, blurring, Gaussian noise, and color jitter. Baseline comparisons will be made against DwtDct, DwtDctSvd, and RivaGAN watermarking methods. Ablation studies will examine the effect of key type, watermark radius, and number of inference steps on detection performance.
f653569b131176dfed8842694b5ad2ead5e4b923.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to embed watermarks in the initial noise distribution of diffusion models rather than via post-hoc image modification, resulting in truly invisible watermarks. The method is training-free, requires no model retraining or fine-tuning, and is compatible with arbitrary diffusion models. The watermark is robust to a wide range of image transformations and manipulations, and detection is statistically principled with interpretable p-values. The technique achieves high detection accuracy with negligible impact on image quality, outperforming existing watermarking baselines in both robustness and invisibility.

f665c60dcd51d06d9705a4ed5d176f794ce08c87.title: A Geometric Framework for Understanding Memorization in Generative Models
f665c60dcd51d06d9705a4ed5d176f794ce08c87.research_question: How can memorization in deep generative models be systematically understood, detected, and mitigated using a geometric framework that relates the dimensionality of learned and ground truth data manifolds?
f665c60dcd51d06d9705a4ed5d176f794ce08c87.hypothesis: Memorization in generative models occurs when the local intrinsic dimension (LID) of the model's learned manifold at a data point is lower than that of the ground truth data manifold at the same point, and that controlling or estimating LID enables systematic detection and mitigation of memorization.
f665c60dcd51d06d9705a4ed5d176f794ce08c87.proposed_method: A geometric framework, termed the Manifold Memorization Hypothesis (MMH), will be developed to analyze memorization in generative models by comparing the local intrinsic dimensions (LID) of the ground truth data manifold and the model's learned manifold at each data point. The approach distinguishes between overfitting-driven memorization (OD-Mem), where the model's LID is lower than the ground truth, and data-driven memorization (DD-Mem), where the ground truth itself has low LID. The methodology involves estimating LID using scalable estimators such as FLIPD and the normal bundle (NB) method for diffusion models, and Jacobian rank or LPCA for GANs. The framework will be extended to practical tools for detecting memorized samples and for mitigating memorization during sampling by manipulating LID through prompt engineering or sampling procedures.
f665c60dcd51d06d9705a4ed5d176f794ce08c87.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets (e.g., mixtures of von Mises distributions and point masses), CIFAR10 with pretrained diffusion models (iDDPM) and GANs (StyleGAN2-ADA), and large-scale image datasets such as LAION and COCO using Stable Diffusion v1.5. Memorization will be assessed by retrieving generated samples similar to training data using SSCD and calibrated L2 distances, followed by manual labeling. LID will be estimated for both generated and training samples, and the relationship between LID and memorization will be analyzed. Additional experiments will evaluate mitigation strategies by altering text prompts to increase LID or reduce memorization metrics such as the CFG vector norm or FLIPD-based metrics, with evaluation using CLIP scores and SSCD similarity. Baselines will include random prompt modification and existing memorization detection methods.
f665c60dcd51d06d9705a4ed5d176f794ce08c87.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified geometric framework (MMH) for understanding and categorizing memorization in generative models based on manifold dimensionality, providing a principled explanation for both exact and reconstructive memorization. It develops scalable, model-agnostic estimators for LID to detect memorization at scale, including for high-dimensional data and large models. The work proposes new sample-time mitigation strategies based on LID control and offers differentiable metrics for prompt attribution and modification to reduce memorization. The approach enables detection and mitigation of memorization without requiring access to the full training dataset or large-scale retrieval, addressing practical limitations of prior methods.

f66b6049946a10080d1f2a7ee6a40e5cca3ee6a0.title: Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling
f66b6049946a10080d1f2a7ee6a40e5cca3ee6a0.research_question: How can scaling inference compute, specifically through repeated sampling of large language models, improve problem-solving performance across diverse reasoning tasks, and what are the limitations imposed by verification methods?
f66b6049946a10080d1f2a7ee6a40e5cca3ee6a0.hypothesis: Increasing the number of independent samples generated by large language models during inference will significantly improve the fraction of problems solved (coverage) across various tasks, and this improvement can be systematically characterized, but the realized performance gains are constrained by the effectiveness of available verification methods.
f66b6049946a10080d1f2a7ee6a40e5cca3ee6a0.proposed_method: A framework will be developed that scales inference compute by repeatedly sampling candidate solutions from large language models (LLMs) for each problem instance. For each task, a large number (up to 10,000) of independent samples will be generated per problem using LLMs with positive temperature settings. Where available, domain-specific automatic verifiers (such as unit tests for code, proof checkers for formal proofs) will be used to select correct solutions from the sample pool. In domains lacking automatic verifiers, alternative selection strategies—including majority voting and reward model-based scoring—will be evaluated. The relationship between coverage (fraction of problems solved by any sample) and the number of samples will be modeled, with particular attention to the emergence of scaling laws at inference time.
f66b6049946a10080d1f2a7ee6a40e5cca3ee6a0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five benchmark tasks: GSM8K (grade-school math word problems), MATH (advanced math word problems), MiniF2F-MATH (formalized math proofs in Lean4), CodeContests (competitive programming problems with hidden test cases), and SWE-bench Lite (real-world GitHub issues requiring code edits). Multiple LLMs of varying sizes and families (Llama 3, Gemma, Pythia, DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) will be evaluated. For each task, up to 10,000 samples per problem will be generated, and coverage (pass@k) will be measured as a function of sample count. Where possible, automatic verifiers will be used; otherwise, majority voting and reward models will be applied. Baselines will include single-sample performance of strong models and state-of-the-art results. Evaluation metrics will include coverage (pass@k), precision (ability to select correct samples), and cost-effectiveness (measured in FLOPs and API pricing).
f66b6049946a10080d1f2a7ee6a40e5cca3ee6a0.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces inference-time scaling as a new axis for improving LLM performance, demonstrating that repeated sampling can amplify weaker models to outperform single-sample state-of-the-art results from stronger models. It systematically characterizes the relationship between coverage and sample count, revealing that coverage often follows an exponentiated power law, analogous to training scaling laws. The work also highlights the limitations of current verification strategies in domains without automatic verifiers, showing that majority voting and reward models fail to fully exploit increased sample budgets. Additionally, the proposal explores the trade-offs between model size, sample count, and cost, offering new insights into optimizing inference compute for both performance and efficiency.

f67b4718b8425aff8c4156757ec0d9c9958ab7d0.title: Learning Multi-Level Features with Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoders
f67b4718b8425aff8c4156757ec0d9c9958ab7d0.research_question: How can sparse autoencoders be designed to learn interpretable, multi-level features from neural network activations without suffering from pathological issues such as feature absorption, splitting, and composition, especially as the size of the feature dictionary increases?
f67b4718b8425aff8c4156757ec0d9c9958ab7d0.hypothesis: Training sparse autoencoders with a hierarchical, nested structure that enforces reconstruction at multiple dictionary sizes will mitigate feature absorption, splitting, and composition, resulting in more interpretable and disentangled feature representations across scales, even as the dictionary size increases.
f67b4718b8425aff8c4156757ec0d9c9958ab7d0.proposed_method: A novel sparse autoencoder architecture, termed Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoder (Matryoshka SAE), is proposed. This method simultaneously trains multiple nested autoencoders of increasing dictionary sizes, where each sub-autoencoder is constrained to reconstruct the input using only a prefix (subset) of the total latent features. The training objective enforces accurate reconstruction at each nested level, compelling early latents to capture general, high-level features while later latents specialize in more specific concepts. The BatchTopK activation function is employed to maintain a fixed average sparsity across the batch, and during inference, a global threshold is calibrated for consistent sparsity. The approach is implemented efficiently, with only a modest increase in training time relative to standard SAEs, and supports both random and fixed prefix nesting strategies.
f67b4718b8425aff8c4156757ec0d9c9958ab7d0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three settings: (1) a synthetic toy model with hierarchical binary features to directly test feature absorption and disentanglement, (2) a small 4-layer Transformer trained on the TinyStories dataset to qualitatively and quantitatively analyze feature evolution and absorption as dictionary size increases, and (3) large-scale validation on the Gemma-2-2B language model using residual stream activations from layer 12, trained on 500M tokens from The Pile dataset. Baselines will include standard sparse autoencoders (Vanilla SAE, BatchTopK SAE) and recent architectural variants. Evaluation metrics will cover reconstruction quality (variance explained), downstream language model cross-entropy loss, feature absorption and splitting (via first-letter classification probes), feature composition (cosine similarity between decoder vectors), sparse probing accuracy (across 35 binary tasks), targeted concept erasure (SCR and TPP metrics), and automated interpretability (LLM-based scoring). Multiple dictionary sizes and sparsity levels will be tested to assess scalability and robustness.
f67b4718b8425aff8c4156757ec0d9c9958ab7d0.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a hierarchical, multi-level sparse autoencoder framework that enforces feature disentanglement and interpretability across scales by training with multiple nested reconstruction objectives. This approach is claimed to significantly reduce feature absorption, splitting, and composition compared to existing SAEs, enabling the extraction of both general and specific concepts within a single model. The method is efficient to train, scales well with increasing dictionary size, and achieves superior performance on probing, concept erasure, and interpretability benchmarks, while maintaining competitive reconstruction and downstream task performance.

f680d47a51a0e470fcb228bf0110c026535ead1b.title: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability
f680d47a51a0e470fcb228bf0110c026535ead1b.research_question: How can continuous progress measures be defined and used to understand the training dynamics and emergent behavior, such as grokking, in neural networks trained on algorithmic tasks?
f680d47a51a0e470fcb228bf0110c026535ead1b.hypothesis: Continuous progress measures derived from mechanistic interpretability can reveal underlying smooth dynamics that precede and explain seemingly abrupt emergent behaviors, such as grokking, in neural network training.
f680d47a51a0e470fcb228bf0110c026535ead1b.proposed_method: The proposed research will develop a mechanistic interpretability framework to reverse-engineer the internal mechanisms of neural networks trained on modular arithmetic tasks, specifically modular addition. The approach involves analyzing the learned representations, weights, and activations of small transformer models to identify the algorithmic components and their evolution during training. By leveraging tools such as Fourier analysis and trigonometric decomposition, the method will isolate key frequencies and mechanisms used by the network. Based on this mechanistic understanding, new progress measures will be defined by selectively ablating or preserving specific components in the Fourier domain, allowing for the tracking of the network's transition from memorization to generalization.
f680d47a51a0e470fcb228bf0110c026535ead1b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using one-layer ReLU transformer models with 128-dimensional embeddings, 4 attention heads, and 512-unit MLPs, trained on modular addition tasks with prime modulus (e.g., P=113). The training data will consist of a subset (e.g., 30%) of all possible input pairs, with evaluation on the remaining pairs. Full batch gradient descent with AdamW optimizer and weight decay will be used, and training will span up to 40,000 epochs. Baseline comparisons will include models with and without regularization, as well as ablation studies targeting specific Fourier components. Evaluation metrics will include standard train/test accuracy and loss, as well as the newly defined restricted and excluded loss progress measures, Gini coefficients of Fourier component norms, and sum of squared weights. Additional experiments will test robustness across different architectures, data splits, and prime moduli.
f680d47a51a0e470fcb228bf0110c026535ead1b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel approach for defining and empirically validating continuous progress measures for neural network training, grounded in mechanistic interpretability. It claims innovation in fully reverse-engineering the learned algorithm of small transformers on modular addition, revealing the use of discrete Fourier transforms and trigonometric identities. The research will establish new metrics—restricted and excluded loss—that provide early and smooth indicators of emergent generalization, enabling the decomposition of training into distinct phases. This work aims to demonstrate that emergent behaviors like grokking are underpinned by gradual, interpretable changes in network mechanisms, rather than abrupt, inexplicable shifts.

f68f6f2a057c4e6e5a3c91fc8563533d9bf6e560.title: ShareGPT4V: Improving Large Multi-Modal Models with Better Captions
f68f6f2a057c4e6e5a3c91fc8563533d9bf6e560.research_question: How can the quality of image-text captions be improved to enhance the modality alignment and performance of large multi-modal models (LMMs) across a variety of vision-language tasks?
f68f6f2a057c4e6e5a3c91fc8563533d9bf6e560.hypothesis: Incorporating high-quality, highly descriptive image-text captions into both the pre-training and supervised fine-tuning stages of LMMs will significantly improve modality alignment and overall model performance compared to using existing lower-quality caption datasets.
f68f6f2a057c4e6e5a3c91fc8563533d9bf6e560.proposed_method: A large-scale dataset of highly descriptive image-text pairs, ShareGPT4V, will be constructed in two phases. First, 100K high-quality captions will be generated using advanced GPT4-Vision with carefully designed, data-specific prompts across diverse image sources. These captions will cover world knowledge, object properties, spatial relationships, and aesthetic evaluations. Second, a general caption model (Share-Captioner) will be trained on this seed set and used to generate an additional 1.2M captions for large-scale pre-training. The resulting dataset will be used to pre-train a multi-modal model based on a CLIP-Large vision encoder and a Vicuna-7B language model, with a two-layer MLP projector for modality alignment. During pre-training, the vision encoder, projector, and language model will be jointly fine-tuned, particularly unlocking the latter half of the vision encoder's transformer blocks to maximize alignment. In supervised fine-tuning, a portion of standard instruction-tuning data will be replaced with high-quality ShareGPT4V captions, and only the projector and language model will be fine-tuned for efficiency.
f68f6f2a057c4e6e5a3c91fc8563533d9bf6e560.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of multi-modal benchmarks, including LLaVA-Bench, MME (Perception and Cognition), MMBench (English and Chinese), SEED, MM-Vet, QBench, ScienceQA-IMG, VQA-v2, and VizWiz. Baselines will include state-of-the-art LMMs such as LLaVA-1.5, Qwen-VL-Chat, InstructBLIP, BLIP-2, and others, with comparisons made at similar parameter scales (7B) and with larger models. Evaluation metrics will include benchmark-specific accuracy and total scores. Ablation studies will assess the impact of caption quality, number of captions used in pre-training, and the number of learnable blocks in the vision encoder. Human evaluations will compare the quality of captions generated by GPT4-Vision and Share-Captioner. All experiments will use public datasets for fair comparison, and training will be performed with controlled hyperparameters (e.g., learning rate 2e-5, batch sizes 128-256, 4700-5200 steps).
f68f6f2a057c4e6e5a3c91fc8563533d9bf6e560.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first large-scale, highly descriptive image-text dataset (ShareGPT4V) generated via advanced LMMs and a scalable captioning model, covering a broader range of semantic, relational, and aesthetic information than existing datasets. The method demonstrates that high-quality captions, even at a fraction of the data scale, can yield significant improvements in modality alignment and downstream performance for LMMs. The approach also establishes that fine-tuning the vision encoder with high-quality captions is beneficial, challenging the prevailing practice of freezing it during pre-training. The resulting model achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive results across a wide spectrum of benchmarks, despite using fewer parameters and less data than many competitors.

f69f95835deec7748a688675721b6d581b60d42b.title: LIV: Language-Image Representations and Rewards for Robotic Control
f69f95835deec7748a688675721b6d581b60d42b.research_question: How can a unified vision-language representation and reward learning framework be developed to enable robots to learn and perform a wide range of tasks specified by language or image goals, including in unseen environments and with minimal domain-specific data?
f69f95835deec7748a688675721b6d581b60d42b.hypothesis: A multi-modal representation and reward learning objective that jointly encodes vision and language modalities, trained via a unified contrastive and value-based approach on large-scale action-free, text-annotated video datasets, will enable effective zero-shot and fine-tuned language-conditioned robotic control, outperforming existing unimodal or contrastive-only methods.
f69f95835deec7748a688675721b6d581b60d42b.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, Language-Image Value Learning (LIV), will be developed to jointly pre-train and fine-tune multi-modal vision-language representations and reward functions from large-scale, action-free, text-annotated videos. The approach combines a goal-conditioned value learning objective (VIP) with a mutual-information-based contrastive learning objective (CLIP/InfoNCE), resulting in a unified loss that aligns both temporal and semantic information across modalities. The method will utilize a shared embedding space for both vision and language encoders, enabling dense, potential-based reward assignment to video frames based on either image or language goals. The framework will support both extensive domain-generic pre-training on human activity datasets and efficient domain-specific fine-tuning on small robot datasets, facilitating robust transfer and grounding of language in new contexts.
f69f95835deec7748a688675721b6d581b60d42b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple simulated and real-world robotic manipulation environments, including MetaWorld, FrankaKitchen, and a real Franka-based tabletop setup, with tasks specified via natural language. The LIV model will be pre-trained on large-scale human video datasets such as EpicKitchen, and fine-tuned with domain-specific data where available. Baselines will include state-of-the-art vision-language models (CLIP), visual representations (R3M, VIP), and language-conditioned reward models (LOREL), with appropriate adaptations for multi-modal input. Evaluation will cover zero-shot reward assignment, policy learning via language-conditioned behavior cloning, and model-based planning using learned reward functions. Metrics will include task success rates, reward alignment curves, and qualitative analysis of learned representations, with ablations on pre-training, fine-tuning, and reward specification strategies.
f69f95835deec7748a688675721b6d581b60d42b.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to unify vision-language representation and reward learning for control in a single objective that supports both pre-training and fine-tuning. It introduces a principled combination of temporal value learning and semantic contrastive alignment, enabling dense, multi-modal reward assignment from action-free, text-annotated videos. The method enables effective zero-shot transfer and domain-specific adaptation for robotic control, outperforming existing unimodal and contrastive methods in both representation learning and reward specification. The approach also demonstrates the ability to generalize to real-world robotic tasks and supports flexible policy synthesis via both imitation and reinforcement learning.

f6a3593463aa771694973e6afd8419c0b988b496.title: No Need to Talk: Asynchronous Mixture of Language Models
f6a3593463aa771694973e6afd8419c0b988b496.research_question: How can large language models be trained and deployed efficiently in distributed environments with minimal communication overhead, while maintaining or improving model performance on language modeling and downstream tasks?
f6a3593463aa771694973e6afd8419c0b988b496.hypothesis: A mixture of independently trained language models, each specializing in distinct parts of the data distribution and routed via lightweight prefix-based language model routers, can achieve lower perplexity and better downstream task performance than dense baselines, while significantly reducing communication and computational costs during both training and inference.
f6a3593463aa771694973e6afd8419c0b988b496.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops an asynchronous mixture of language models (SMALLTALK LM), where each expert model is trained independently on a partition of the data determined by lightweight router language models. The routers, which are orders of magnitude smaller than the experts, assign sequences to experts based on the log-likelihood of a short prefix, enabling efficient routing even with limited context. Training proceeds in two stages: (1) routers are trained using an EM-like procedure to optimize data assignments, ensuring balanced partitioning across experts, and (2) experts are trained independently on their assigned data segments. During inference, a lightweight router selects the most appropriate expert for each input sequence using only a short prefix, activating only a fraction of the total model parameters. The method is designed for minimal communication, with only small score matrices exchanged during balanced assignment, and is highly parallelizable.
f6a3593463aa771694973e6afd8419c0b988b496.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the RedPajama-V2 dataset, a large-scale web text corpus. Both experts and routers will use Transformer architectures with rotary positional encoding, and models will be trained with the AdamW optimizer and standard hyperparameters. Model sizes will include 335M and 1.3B parameter experts, with routers as small as 4.4M parameters. The mixture models will be evaluated against dense baselines matched for total training FLOPs and inference cost. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity on held-out test sets and accuracy on downstream NLP tasks such as ARC Challenge, ARC Easy, HellaSwag, SciQ, and MMLU, using zero-shot evaluation protocols. Additional analyses will assess the impact of router size, prefix length, and routing strategies (including comparisons to TF-IDF-based clustering). Communication overhead and computational efficiency will be measured and reported.
f6a3593463aa771694973e6afd8419c0b988b496.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a practical, asynchronous mixture of language models framework that enables independent training of experts with minimal communication, leveraging lightweight language model routers for efficient prefix-based routing. Unlike prior asynchronous MoE methods, the approach does not require full corpus clustering or metadata, making it suitable for real-world applications with short input contexts. The method achieves significant improvements in perplexity and downstream task accuracy over dense baselines at matched computational budgets, and demonstrates that very small routers suffice for effective expert assignment. The framework also ensures balanced expert utilization and is highly scalable and parallelizable, offering a new direction for efficient large language model training and inference.

f6c05626d3f94ccf0935ad1e9c144d1f41ae8135.title: Understanding Edge-of-Stability Training Dynamics with a Minimalist Example
f6c05626d3f94ccf0935ad1e9c144d1f41ae8135.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms that govern the edge-of-stability (EoS) training dynamics in deep neural networks, and how do these mechanisms relate to network depth and sharpness adaptivity/concentration during gradient descent optimization?
f6c05626d3f94ccf0935ad1e9c144d1f41ae8135.hypothesis: A minimalist, higher-degree (degree-4) scalar network model can capture and explain the sharpness adaptivity and sharpness concentration phenomena observed in deep neural network training at the edge of stability, distinguishing it from lower-degree models such as matrix factorization or two-layer networks.
f6c05626d3f94ccf0935ad1e9c144d1f41ae8135.proposed_method: A minimalist objective function, specifically a 4-layer scalar network with coupled entries, is constructed to emulate the EoS behavior observed in deep neural networks. The training dynamics of this function under gradient descent with fixed step size are rigorously analyzed, both locally and globally, using reparameterization techniques to reduce the problem to two dimensions. The method involves deriving closed-form expressions for the EoS minima, characterizing the sharpness of converging points, and analyzing the two-step update dynamics via both discrete and continuous approximations (ODEs). The approach is extended to a rank-1 matrix factorization problem to demonstrate generality, and comparisons are made with degree-2 models to highlight the role of higher-order terms in producing sharpness adaptivity and concentration.
f6c05626d3f94ccf0935ad1e9c144d1f41ae8135.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by running gradient descent with various learning rates and initializations on three models: a 5-layer fully connected ReLU network, a 2-layer linear network, and the proposed 4-layer scalar network. The evolution of training loss, sharpness (maximum Hessian eigenvalue), and parameter trajectories will be tracked. For the scalar and matrix factorization models, a dense grid of initializations will be used to empirically verify sharpness concentration and adaptivity. Baselines will include degree-2 models (matrix factorization, two-layer networks) for direct comparison. Evaluation metrics include convergence of loss, proximity of sharpness to the EoS threshold (2/η), and the geometric properties of the parameter trajectories (e.g., parabolic vs. elliptical). Additional experiments will be performed on real-world datasets (e.g., CIFAR-10) using over-parameterized deep networks to compare observed dynamics with those of the minimalist model.
f6c05626d3f94ccf0935ad1e9c144d1f41ae8135.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a simple, analytically tractable degree-4 scalar model that rigorously captures both sharpness adaptivity and sharpness concentration phenomena at the edge of stability, which are empirically observed in deep neural networks but not in shallower or lower-degree models. The analysis provides new theoretical insights into why higher-degree models exhibit EoS convergence with sharpness near the stability threshold, while lower-degree models do not. The work also demonstrates that the local training dynamics of over-parameterized deep networks on real data can be well-approximated by the parabolic trajectories of the minimalist model, establishing a concrete link between simple theoretical models and complex real-world neural network training behavior.

f6c8e59d1b1de55a5a7aa67d228eabf742121cbb.title: Learning 3D Perception from Others' Predictions
f6c8e59d1b1de55a5a7aa67d228eabf742121cbb.research_question: How can a 3D object detector for an autonomous agent be trained in a label-efficient, sensor-agnostic, and communication-efficient manner by leveraging predictions from nearby agents equipped with accurate detectors, despite challenges such as viewpoint mismatch and localization errors?
f6c8e59d1b1de55a5a7aa67d228eabf742121cbb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a 3D object detector can be effectively trained for a new agent using only a small amount of annotated data, by refining and filtering the predictions of nearby reference agents through a combination of box refinement modules and distance-based curriculum self-training, thereby overcoming the challenges of noisy pseudo-labels caused by viewpoint mismatch and localization errors.
f6c8e59d1b1de55a5a7aa67d228eabf742121cbb.proposed_method: A novel learning pipeline, R&B-POP, is proposed to enable 3D object detector training using predictions from nearby reference agents. The method first receives 3D bounding box predictions from a reference agent and transforms them into the ego agent’s coordinate frame. To address mislocalization, a box refinement module is introduced, which leverages a neural ranker (trained with a handful of annotated frames or simulation data) to select and adjust among noisy candidate boxes sampled around each initial prediction. A coarse-to-fine (C2F) sampling strategy is employed to efficiently cover both large and small localization errors. For the challenge of viewpoint mismatch, a distance-based curriculum is implemented: the ego agent first learns from high-confidence pseudo-labels generated when the reference and ego agents are close, then iteratively expands training to more challenging frames using self-training, where the detector’s own predictions are filtered by a distance-adaptive confidence threshold. This pipeline iteratively improves pseudo-label quality and detector performance while minimizing the need for human annotation.
f6c8e59d1b1de55a5a7aa67d228eabf742121cbb.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted primarily on the V2V4Real dataset, which contains LiDAR point clouds and 3D bounding box annotations from two vehicles driving together. The dataset is re-split to simulate the proposed learning scenario, with one vehicle serving as the reference agent and the other as the ego agent. The main detector backbone is PointPillars, and additional experiments use SECOND. Baselines include naive pseudo-labeling, heuristic-based box refinement, and standard self-training. Evaluation metrics are average precision (AP) at IoU thresholds of 0.5 and 0.7, reported over various depth ranges. The box ranker is trained with as few as 40 annotated frames (<1% of the data), and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of ranker training data, inference strategies, and curriculum design. Additional experiments test the method’s robustness to different sensors (varying LiDAR beam counts), detector architectures, and domain adaptation scenarios using simulated data.
f6c8e59d1b1de55a5a7aa67d228eabf742121cbb.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new research problem of learning 3D perception from others’ predictions in a collaborative, label-efficient setting. Key innovations include a label-efficient box refinement module using a neural ranker trained with minimal annotation, a coarse-to-fine candidate sampling strategy for robust localization correction, and a distance-based curriculum for self-training that exploits the correlation between viewpoint quality and agent proximity. The method is claimed to be sensor- and detector-agnostic, requiring only a small amount of annotated data or simulation data for effective training, and demonstrates near-upper-bound performance compared to fully supervised training. The approach is validated across different sensors, detector architectures, and domains, highlighting its flexibility and general applicability.

f6fecdb9f4fc8798ff47c983653cc3e3f21b7320.title: Online Linear Regression in Dynamic Environments via Discounting
f6fecdb9f4fc8798ff47c983653cc3e3f21b7320.research_question: How can online linear regression algorithms be designed to achieve optimal static and dynamic regret guarantees in fully dynamic, non-stationary environments without any prior knowledge or boundedness assumptions on the data or comparator sequence?
f6fecdb9f4fc8798ff47c983653cc3e3f21b7320.hypothesis: It is possible to construct online linear regression algorithms, based on a discounted variant of the Vovk-Azoury-Warmuth (VAW) forecaster, that achieve optimal dynamic regret bounds—matching lower bounds up to logarithmic factors—even in the complete absence of prior knowledge about the data stream, and that these algorithms can adaptively learn the optimal discount factor on-the-fly.
f6fecdb9f4fc8798ff47c983653cc3e3f21b7320.proposed_method: A new approach will be developed using a discounted variant of the Vovk-Azoury-Warmuth (VAW) forecaster for online linear regression. The method incorporates a discount factor into the forecaster's statistics, allowing recent data to be weighted more heavily and enabling adaptation to non-stationary environments. The discount factor is not fixed in advance but is learned dynamically, either by running multiple instances of the forecaster with different discount rates and combining their predictions via an expert/meta-algorithm, or by optimizing the discount factor online based on observed losses. The algorithm operates without any boundedness assumptions on the features, targets, or comparator sequence, and does not require any prior knowledge of the data-generating process or hyperparameter tuning. Furthermore, the method is extended to provide strongly-adaptive guarantees, ensuring optimal regret bounds over every sub-interval of the time horizon.
f6fecdb9f4fc8798ff47c983653cc3e3f21b7320.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both synthetic and real-world streaming datasets that exhibit varying degrees of non-stationarity and dynamic changes in the underlying data distribution. The proposed algorithms will be compared against established baselines, including the standard (undiscounted) VAW forecaster, static regret minimization algorithms, and recent adaptive online regression methods that require boundedness or prior knowledge. Evaluation metrics will include static and dynamic regret, as well as small-loss bounds and strongly-adaptive regret over sub-intervals. The experimental setup will ensure that no prior knowledge or boundedness assumptions are provided to any method, and the impact of learning the discount factor on-the-fly will be systematically assessed.
f6fecdb9f4fc8798ff47c983653cc3e3f21b7320.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first algorithms for online linear regression that achieve optimal dynamic and strongly-adaptive regret guarantees without any prior knowledge or boundedness assumptions. The analysis establishes a novel regret bound of the form O(d log T + d P_γ(u, T)), where P_γ(u, T) is a measure of comparator sequence variability, and proves that this is optimal via a matching lower bound. The method also demonstrates that the discount factor required for optimal performance can be learned adaptively online, eliminating the need for oracle knowledge or hyperparameter tuning. Additionally, the approach generalizes to provide strongly-adaptive guarantees over all sub-intervals, and the regret bounds adapt to the difficulty of the data sequence, including small-loss scenarios.

f719d0ba9ba035e2511d0c1a5448db755502df92.title: MBR and QE Finetuning: Training-time Distillation of the Best and Most Expensive Decoding Methods
f719d0ba9ba035e2511d0c1a5448db755502df92.research_question: How can the quality gains of advanced but computationally expensive decoding methods for natural language generation, such as Minimum Bayes Risk (MBR) decoding and Quality Estimation (QE) reranking, be distilled into neural machine translation models at training time to enable efficient and high-quality inference using standard decoding algorithms?
f719d0ba9ba035e2511d0c1a5448db755502df92.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that finetuning neural machine translation models on outputs generated by MBR decoding or QE reranking—using either self-generated or teacher-generated data—can transfer the quality improvements of these advanced decoding methods to the model itself, allowing efficient decoding at inference time without sacrificing translation quality.
f719d0ba9ba035e2511d0c1a5448db755502df92.proposed_method: A novel finetuning framework is proposed that leverages MBR and QE decoding strategies during training to distill their quality benefits into neural machine translation (NMT) models. The method consists of generating candidate translations for source sentences using epsilon sampling, followed by selecting the best candidate either via MBR scoring with a neural utility metric (e.g., BLEURT) or QE reranking with a reference-free metric (e.g., MetricX-XXL-QE). These selected translations are then used as pseudo-targets to finetune the student NMT model. The approach supports both self-training (student as its own teacher) and distillation from a stronger external teacher model, such as a large language model (LLM). At inference time, the finetuned model is decoded using efficient algorithms like beam search or greedy decoding, thus avoiding the computational overhead of MBR or QE at deployment.
f719d0ba9ba035e2511d0c1a5448db755502df92.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two language pairs: English-German (high-resource) and English-Japanese (medium-resource). Base models are trained on WMT parallel corpora, with finetuning performed on WMT test sets, MBR-decoded outputs, QE-reranked outputs, and translations generated from large-scale monolingual data (Common Crawl). Both self-training and teacher-student setups are explored, with PaLM-2 Bison serving as an external LLM teacher. Baselines include beam search decoding, beam-finetuned models, and reference-finetuned models. Evaluation is carried out using a suite of automatic metrics (BLEURT, MetricX-XXL, MetricX-23-c, chrF, Comet20, Comet22) and human evaluation via MQM. The main evaluation set is WMT2022, with newstest2021 used for development. Ablation studies investigate the impact of decoding strategies and data sources.
f719d0ba9ba035e2511d0c1a5448db755502df92.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces training-time distillation of MBR and QE decoding quality into NMT models, enabling efficient inference without loss of translation quality. This is the first systematic exploration of using MBR and QE outputs as finetuning data, including both self-training and distillation from a strong external LLM teacher. The method demonstrates that monolingual data can be effectively leveraged for substantial quality gains, often surpassing improvements from human-curated parallel data. Additionally, the approach provides a practical pathway for deploying high-quality NMT systems without the computational burden of advanced decoding methods at inference.

f7274310391c50eb319d5fbe7f4f557c124fffd7.title: Addressing Order Sensitivity of In-Context Demonstration Examples in Causal Language Models
f7274310391c50eb319d5fbe7f4f557c124fffd7.research_question: How can the order sensitivity of in-context demonstration examples in causal language models be mitigated to improve predictive consistency and generalizability across different tasks and settings?
f7274310391c50eb319d5fbe7f4f557c124fffd7.hypothesis: Causal language models exhibit heightened sensitivity to the order of in-context demonstration examples due to their auto-regressive attention masks, and this sensitivity can be significantly reduced by aligning representations across permutations and enhancing consistency through unsupervised fine-tuning objectives.
f7274310391c50eb319d5fbe7f4f557c124fffd7.proposed_method: A novel unsupervised fine-tuning approach, termed Information-Augmented and Consistency-Enhanced (InfoAC), is proposed to address order sensitivity in causal language models (CausalLMs). The method consists of two main components: (1) Information Augmentation, which employs contrastive learning to align the representations of in-context examples across different positions with those at the end of the demonstration, ensuring that each example encapsulates the full spectrum of information regardless of its position. This is achieved by using a reference model to generate target representations and optimizing the model to match these via a contrastive loss. (2) Consistency Enhancement, which introduces a consistency loss to enforce similarity among the hidden representations preceding the classification head across different permutations of in-context examples, thereby promoting consistent predictions. The approach leverages Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for efficient fine-tuning, keeping most model parameters fixed and only updating select attention matrices.
f7274310391c50eb319d5fbe7f4f557c124fffd7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five benchmarks spanning text classification, textual entailment, and mathematical reasoning: SST-5, SST-2, QQP, Sequence Next Term, and Round Number. Multiple CausalLMs (Llama-7B, Llama-13B, Vicuna-7B, Vicuna-13B) will be evaluated, with PrefixLMs (e.g., Flan-T5) serving as baselines for comparative analysis. Evaluation metrics include Majority Voting Accuracy, Partial Correct Ratio, and Entropy, which collectively measure the model's sensitivity to order, prediction consistency, and output diversity. The experimental setup includes random and advanced (KNN, One-Shot) in-context example selection, cross-pool and cross-count generalizability tests (varying the number and source of in-context examples), and ablation studies on the proposed method's components. Each experiment involves sampling multiple permutations of in-context examples per test case to robustly assess order sensitivity and the effectiveness of the proposed mitigation strategies.
f7274310391c50eb319d5fbe7f4f557c124fffd7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to directly address the root cause of order sensitivity in CausalLMs by aligning token representations across permutations and enforcing consistency through unsupervised objectives, rather than merely searching for optimal demonstration orders. The method is simple, architecture-agnostic, and leverages efficient fine-tuning via LoRA. It demonstrates robust generalizability across different candidate pools and varying numbers of in-context examples, significantly reducing order sensitivity and improving prediction consistency on a wide range of benchmarks. The approach also provides new insights into the representational dynamics underlying order effects in CausalLMs.

f72be31de9f9a09d4410fd38bc717efe43444827.title: SALMONN: Towards Generic Hearing Abilities for Large Language Models
f72be31de9f9a09d4410fd38bc717efe43444827.research_question: Can a single large language model be developed to achieve generic hearing abilities, enabling the perception and understanding of general auditory information—including speech, audio events, and music—across a wide range of tasks, including both trained and untrained cross-modal reasoning tasks?
f72be31de9f9a09d4410fd38bc717efe43444827.hypothesis: A multimodal large language model, equipped with dual auditory encoders and an efficient cross-modal alignment mechanism, can achieve competitive performance on a broad spectrum of auditory tasks and demonstrate emergent abilities on tasks not seen during training, provided that overfitting to trained tasks is mitigated through targeted activation tuning.
f72be31de9f9a09d4410fd38bc717efe43444827.proposed_method: A new multimodal framework will be constructed by integrating a pre-trained text-based large language model (Vicuna) with two complementary auditory encoders: the Whisper speech encoder and the BEATs audio encoder. These encoders' outputs will be concatenated frame-wise and processed through a window-level Q-Former module, which converts variable-length audio features into a variable number of augmented audio tokens aligned with the LLM input space. The LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) technique will be applied as a cross-modal adaptor to efficiently align the LLM’s augmented input space with its output space, updating only a small subset of parameters. Training will proceed in three stages: (1) cross-modal pre-training on speech recognition and audio captioning to establish high-quality alignment, (2) instruction tuning on a diverse set of supervised audio, speech, and music tasks, and (3) a novel activation tuning stage using few-shot, self-supervised fine-tuning with long and diverse responses (such as storytelling) to restore and enhance cross-modal emergent abilities lost during instruction tuning.
f72be31de9f9a09d4410fd38bc717efe43444827.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a comprehensive suite of 15 tasks spanning three levels: (1) tasks used in instruction tuning (e.g., ASR, speech translation, audio captioning, phone recognition, emotion recognition, music captioning, speaker verification, and question answering), (2) untrained speech-based NLP tasks (e.g., keyword extraction, spoken-query QA, slot filling, and translation to untrained languages), and (3) novel cross-modal reasoning tasks (audio-based storytelling and speech-audio co-reasoning). Datasets include LibriSpeech, GigaSpeech, WavCaps, AudioCaps, Clotho, CoVoST2, IEMOCAP, MusicCaps, LibriMix, VoxCeleb1, SLURP, WikiQA, and in-house data for novel tasks. Baselines will include state-of-the-art models such as Whisper and Whisper+Vicuna pipelines. Evaluation metrics will be task-specific, including WER, BLEU4, METEOR, SPIDEr, PER, accuracy, RougeL, diversity, and following rate (FR) for instruction adherence. The experimental setup will ensure only the Q-Former and LoRA modules are updated during training, with the rest of the model frozen.
f72be31de9f9a09d4410fd38bc717efe43444827.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first end-to-end multimodal large language model capable of perceiving and understanding general audio—including speech, audio events, and music—within a single unified architecture.
