A dual-encoder structure is leveraged for comprehensive auditory representation, and a window-level Q-Former is adapted for efficient variable-length audio-to-text alignment. A novel activation tuning stage is proposed to recover and enhance cross-modal emergent abilities lost during instruction tuning, enabling the model to perform open-ended and previously unseen cross-modal reasoning tasks. Two new benchmark tasks, audio-based storytelling and speech-audio co-reasoning, are also introduced to evaluate generic hearing abilities.

f7310dac21abc6ba357bcd5e75fb2e6957a97303.title: MobileLLM: Optimizing Sub-billion Parameter Language Models for On-Device Use Cases
f7310dac21abc6ba357bcd5e75fb2e6957a97303.research_question: How can language models with fewer than one billion parameters be optimized for high performance in on-device use cases, considering the unique constraints of mobile hardware and the need for efficient inference?
f7310dac21abc6ba357bcd5e75fb2e6957a97303.hypothesis: For sub-billion parameter language models, architectural innovations—particularly increasing model depth over width and employing advanced weight-sharing techniques—can yield significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency, surpassing the impact of merely increasing data or parameter count.
f7310dac21abc6ba357bcd5e75fb2e6957a97303.proposed_method: A new family of sub-billion parameter language models, termed MobileLLM, will be developed by systematically exploring and integrating several architectural strategies tailored for mobile deployment. The approach will prioritize deep-and-thin transformer architectures, replacing standard feed-forward networks with SwiGLU activation for improved reasoning performance. Input-output embedding sharing will be revisited to reduce parameter redundancy, and grouped query attention will be employed to maximize weight utilization and minimize key-value cache size. Additionally, an immediate block-wise weight-sharing mechanism will be introduced, allowing adjacent transformer blocks to share weights, thereby increasing effective depth without increasing model size or incurring substantial latency overhead. The resulting models will be trained from scratch and further fine-tuned for downstream tasks.
f7310dac21abc6ba357bcd5e75fb2e6957a97303.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large-scale pretraining on 1T tokens with 480k iterations, utilizing 32 A100 GPUs and the Adam optimizer, followed by fine-tuning for downstream tasks. Evaluation will occur on a comprehensive suite of zero-shot commonsense reasoning tasks (ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, BoolQ, PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, OBQA, WinoGrande), as well as question answering and reading comprehension benchmarks (TQA, RACE). Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art sub-billion parameter models such as OPT, GPT-Neo, BLOOM, Pythia, and RWKV, using open-source checkpoints for consistent evaluation. Metrics will include accuracy, F1 score, and win rate on chat and API calling tasks (AlpacaEval, MT-Bench), as well as latency and memory profiling on real mobile hardware. Ablation studies will assess the impact of depth, width, embedding sharing, attention head configuration, and layer-sharing strategies.
f7310dac21abc6ba357bcd5e75fb2e6957a97303.novelty_claims: The proposed work challenges prevailing scaling laws by demonstrating that for small-scale LLMs, depth is more critical than width for performance. The method introduces a novel immediate block-wise weight-sharing strategy that enhances effective model depth without increasing storage requirements or significantly impacting latency. The integration of embedding sharing and grouped query attention is optimized specifically for sub-billion parameter regimes. The resulting MobileLLM models are claimed to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy on a wide range of reasoning and comprehension tasks, outperforming prior models of similar or larger size, and demonstrate competitive performance in real-world on-device scenarios such as chat and API calling. Compatibility with quantization and efficient hardware execution is also established, supporting practical deployment.

f733a8280d5da71f7046460e7e6b9eae863376ac.title: Guiding a Diffusion Model with a Bad Version of Itself
f733a8280d5da71f7046460e7e6b9eae863376ac.research_question: How can image quality and sample diversity in diffusion models be disentangled and improved, particularly in both conditional and unconditional image generation, without sacrificing variation or requiring external guidance models?
f733a8280d5da71f7046460e7e6b9eae863376ac.hypothesis: Guiding a high-quality diffusion model with a deliberately degraded, smaller, or less-trained version of itself (with matched conditioning) will improve image quality and sample alignment with the data distribution, without reducing diversity, and will outperform existing classifier-free guidance approaches.
f733a8280d5da71f7046460e7e6b9eae863376ac.proposed_method: A novel guidance technique, termed 'autoguidance,' is proposed, in which a primary (main) diffusion model is guided during sampling by a secondary, inferior version of itself. The guiding model is constructed by reducing model capacity (e.g., using a smaller network architecture) and/or limiting training time (e.g., fewer training iterations), but is trained on the same data and with the same conditioning as the main model. During sampling, the denoising trajectory is modified by extrapolating between the outputs of the main and guiding models, similar to the mechanism in classifier-free guidance, but both models share the same conditioning. The guidance weight is a tunable parameter controlling the influence of the guiding model. The method is applicable to both conditional and unconditional diffusion models, and does not require any changes to the training data or conditioning strategy.
f733a8280d5da71f7046460e7e6b9eae863376ac.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted primarily on the ImageNet dataset at two resolutions: 512x512 and 64x64. Both latent diffusion and pixel-space diffusion models (EDM2-S and EDM2-XXL) will be used as baselines. The guiding models will be created by reducing either the training time, model capacity, or both, relative to the main model. Performance will be evaluated using FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) and FD (Fréchet Distance using DINOv2 embeddings) metrics. Comparisons will be made against standard classifier-free guidance, guidance interval methods, and ablations will be performed to assess the impact of different degradation strategies and hyperparameters (such as guidance weight and EMA length). Additional experiments will include synthetic degradations and applications to unconditional generation and large-scale text-to-image models (e.g., DeepFloyd IF).
f733a8280d5da71f7046460e7e6b9eae863376ac.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new form of guidance for diffusion models that uses a degraded version of the model itself, rather than an unconditional model, to achieve disentangled control over image quality and diversity. This approach enables significant improvements in image quality (as measured by FID and FD), sets new state-of-the-art results on ImageNet-64 and ImageNet-512, and is applicable to both conditional and unconditional generation. The method does not require changes to the conditioning mechanism and avoids the task discrepancy issues inherent in classifier-free guidance. Furthermore, it provides a practical and efficient way to improve diffusion model sampling with minimal additional training cost.

f743464f22136d5b845483c5fd1597cb5809ddad.title: Mr.Steve: Instruction-Following Agents in Minecraft with What-Where-When Memory
f743464f22136d5b845483c5fd1597cb5809ddad.research_question: How can embodied AI agents in complex, open-ended environments such as Minecraft be enhanced to efficiently solve long-horizon, instruction-following tasks, particularly when task-relevant resources are sparsely distributed and require episodic memory for effective exploration and task completion?
f743464f22136d5b845483c5fd1597cb5809ddad.hypothesis: Integrating a hierarchical episodic memory system that captures what, where, and when information about events and locations will significantly improve the efficiency and success rate of low-level instruction-following agents in sparse, long-horizon sequential tasks compared to existing short-term memory-based controllers.
f743464f22136d5b845483c5fd1597cb5809ddad.proposed_method: A novel low-level controller, termed MrSteve, will be developed, incorporating a Place Event Memory (PEM) module that hierarchically organizes and stores spatial and event-based information from the agent's experiences. The PEM will cluster agent trajectories into place clusters and further subdivide them into event clusters using video embeddings and DP-Means clustering, ensuring distinct events are efficiently stored and retrievable even under limited memory capacity. A Mode Selector module will determine whether the agent should explore or execute a task based on the presence of task-relevant information in memory, leveraging a hierarchical memory read operation for computational efficiency. Exploration will be guided by a count-based high-level goal selector and a fine-tuned, goal-conditioned VPT-Nav policy for low-level navigation, enabling the agent to efficiently cover new areas and revisit previously seen resources as needed.
f743464f22136d5b845483c5fd1597cb5809ddad.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in Minecraft environments, including both 100x100 and 200x200 block maps with complex terrain. Tasks will include ABA-Sparse sequential tasks, memory-constrained navigation challenges (e.g., Find Water, Find Zombies’ Death Spot, Find First-Visited House), and long-horizon task sequences. Baselines will include Steve-1 (short-term memory controller), Plan4MC (hierarchical RNN+DQN), and MrSteve variants with FIFO, event-only, and place-only memory. Evaluation metrics will comprise map coverage, revisit count, task success rate, and task duration. Memory capacity constraints and generalization to long-horizon tasks will be explicitly tested.
f743464f22136d5b845483c5fd1597cb5809ddad.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces Place Event Memory, a hierarchical episodic memory system for low-level controllers that organizes both spatial and event-based experiences, enabling efficient recall and navigation in long-horizon, sparse environments. The approach uniquely combines hierarchical memory clustering, event distinctiveness, and a memory-augmented exploration and task-solving framework, addressing limitations of both transformer-based short-term memory and high-level skill libraries. The method claims to significantly improve exploration efficiency, task-solving speed, and robustness under memory constraints, outperforming existing baselines in both sequential and long-horizon tasks.

f765e1a0b18b21b1534caeb7416909f107f78fb2.title: Stochastic Approximation with Biased MCMC for Expectation Maximization
f765e1a0b18b21b1534caeb7416909f107f78fb2.research_question: How can stochastic approximation expectation maximization (SAEM) algorithms be theoretically and practically extended to accommodate biased Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) steps, and what are the implications for empirical Bayes inference in latent variable models?
f765e1a0b18b21b1534caeb7416909f107f78fb2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that SAEM algorithms incorporating asymptotically biased MCMC steps can achieve stable and efficient convergence under certain regularity conditions, and that the trade-off between bias and mixing rate can be theoretically characterized and practically advantageous in high-dimensional or poorly conditioned settings.
f765e1a0b18b21b1534caeb7416909f107f78fb2.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the asymptotic and non-asymptotic convergence properties of SAEM algorithms when the E-step is approximated using biased MCMC kernels, such as the unadjusted Langevin algorithm (ULA). The analysis will generalize existing stochastic approximation theory to account for the presence of asymptotic bias in the Markov chain, providing explicit bounds on convergence rates and stationary points as a function of the bias and problem smoothness. The methodology will include the derivation of high-probability non-asymptotic bounds, leveraging Lyapunov functions and Poisson equation techniques to control Markovian noise and bias. Additionally, practical algorithms will be instantiated using both asymptotically unbiased (e.g., MALA) and biased (e.g., ULA) MCMC kernels within the SAEM framework, with stepsizes and preconditioning strategies tailored to the statistical model and data.
f765e1a0b18b21b1534caeb7416909f107f78fb2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including high-dimensional logistic regression, pharmacokinetic nonlinear mixed-effects models, robust Poisson regression, and logistic regression with automatic relevance determination (ARD). For each setting, the proposed biased and unbiased MCMC-SAEM variants will be compared in terms of convergence speed, stability with respect to stepsize, and marginal log-likelihood or predictive density on held-out data. Baselines will include MALA-based SAEM (asymptotically unbiased) and ULA-based SAEM (asymptotically biased), with stepsizes systematically varied to assess robustness. Evaluation metrics will include convergence to stationary points, test log-predictive density, and computational efficiency. Multiple random train-test splits and bootstrap confidence intervals will be used to ensure statistical reliability of results.
f765e1a0b18b21b1534caeb7416909f107f78fb2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first comprehensive theoretical analysis of SAEM with asymptotically biased MCMC steps, providing both asymptotic and high-probability non-asymptotic guarantees that explicitly account for the bias-variance trade-off. The framework generalizes prior results by quantifying the impact of MCMC bias on convergence and stationary points, and demonstrates that biased MCMC methods such as ULA can offer practical advantages in terms of stability and speed, especially in high-dimensional or non-smooth settings. The empirical evaluation establishes new evidence that approximate MCMC can outperform exact MCMC in SAEM, challenging conventional wisdom and expanding the toolkit for scalable empirical Bayes inference.

f76ae83c992356e972665e1d35bc38b34eee7647.title: UniScene: Unified Occupancy-centric Driving Scene Generation
f76ae83c992356e972665e1d35bc38b34eee7647.research_question: How can a unified framework be developed to generate high-fidelity, controllable, and annotated multi-modal driving scene data—including semantic occupancy, video, and LiDAR point clouds—from structured scene layouts, in order to support diverse downstream autonomous driving tasks?
f76ae83c992356e972665e1d35bc38b34eee7647.hypothesis: Decomposing the driving scene generation process into a hierarchical, occupancy-centric paradigm—where semantic occupancy is first generated from scene layouts and subsequently used as conditional guidance for video and LiDAR generation—will enable more accurate, controllable, and versatile data synthesis across modalities, outperforming single-step or single-modality approaches.
f76ae83c992356e972665e1d35bc38b34eee7647.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a unified, occupancy-centric generative framework for driving scenes, structured as a two-stage hierarchy. First, a controllable semantic occupancy sequence is generated from multi-frame BEV (Bird's Eye View) layouts using an Occupancy Diffusion Transformer (DiT) and a continuous latent-space VAE, ensuring spatial-temporal consistency and efficient compression. This semantic occupancy serves as an intermediate representation rich in geometry and semantics. In the second stage, two novel transfer strategies are employed: (1) Gaussian-based joint rendering converts occupancy into multi-view semantic and depth maps, which, together with text prompts, condition a video diffusion model (based on Stable Video Diffusion) for multi-view video generation; (2) a prior-guided sparse modeling scheme encodes occupancy into sparse voxel features and uses occupancy-based priors to efficiently sample and generate LiDAR point clouds, incorporating ray-based rendering, intensity, and ray-dropping heads for realism. The framework supports controllable editing via BEV layout manipulation and enables attribute customization through text prompts.
f76ae83c992356e972665e1d35bc38b34eee7647.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the NuScenes benchmark, including the NuScenes-Occupancy dataset with interpolated annotations for higher frame rates. The framework will be evaluated on three generation tasks: semantic occupancy, multi-view video, and LiDAR point cloud synthesis. Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art methods for each modality (e.g., OccWorld, OccSora for occupancy; MagicDrive, Vista for video; LiDARDM, Open3D for LiDAR). Evaluation metrics will include mIoU and IoU for occupancy, FID and FVD for video, and MMD and JSD for LiDAR, as well as inference speed and memory consumption. Downstream task performance will also be assessed by augmenting training data for semantic occupancy prediction, BEV segmentation, and 3D object detection, using standard models (e.g., CONet, CVT, BEVFusion) and measuring improvements. Ablation studies will isolate the impact of architectural components such as temporal/spatial attention, occupancy-based conditional guidance, and sparse modeling.
f76ae83c992356e972665e1d35bc38b34eee7647.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to unify the generation of semantic occupancy, multi-view video, and LiDAR point clouds in driving scenes using an occupancy-centric, hierarchical paradigm. Key innovations include: (1) decomposing scene generation into controllable semantic occupancy followed by modality-specific generation, (2) introducing Gaussian-based joint rendering for bridging occupancy and video, (3) developing a prior-guided sparse modeling approach for efficient and realistic LiDAR synthesis, and (4) enabling fine-grained control and editing via BEV layouts and text prompts. The approach claims substantial improvements over state-of-the-art methods in all evaluated modalities and demonstrates significant benefits for downstream perception tasks.

f773ceb43ffc7f9cd685250c4919924ec0bc85c7.title: RoboCasa: Large-Scale Simulation of Everyday Tasks for Generalist Robots
f773ceb43ffc7f9cd685250c4919924ec0bc85c7.research_question: How can large-scale, realistic simulation environments be leveraged to advance the training and generalization capabilities of generalist robots for everyday tasks, particularly in complex home environments?
f773ceb43ffc7f9cd685250c4919924ec0bc85c7.hypothesis: Scaling up the diversity and realism of simulated environments, tasks, and datasets—augmented by generative AI tools—will enable the development of generalist robot agents that can learn robust, transferable skills and outperform those trained on limited real-world data alone.
f773ceb43ffc7f9cd685250c4919924ec0bc85c7.proposed_method: A comprehensive simulation framework, RoboCasa, will be developed to support the training of generalist robot agents in diverse and realistic kitchen environments. The framework will include 120 kitchen scenes, over 2,500 high-quality 3D objects across 153 categories, and support for multiple robot embodiments (mobile manipulators, humanoids, quadrupeds). Generative AI tools will be used to create both 3D assets (via text-to-3D models) and environment textures (via text-to-image models), as well as to generate a diverse set of 100 tasks (25 atomic and 75 composite) with the guidance of large language models. Human demonstrations will be collected for all tasks, and automated trajectory generation (MimicGen) will be employed to synthesize over 100,000 additional trajectories, enabling large-scale behavioral cloning and imitation learning. The simulation will be built on RoboSuite and extended for room-scale, photorealistic scenes and cross-embodiment support.
f773ceb43ffc7f9cd685250c4919924ec0bc85c7.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training visuomotor policies using behavioral cloning on both human and machine-generated datasets, with varying dataset sizes (e.g., 50, 100, 300, 3,000 demonstrations per task). Evaluation will be conducted on 25 atomic and 75 composite tasks, using a Franka Panda robot with an Omron mobile base in both simulated and real-world kitchen environments. Policies will be tested for generalization across unseen scenes, styles, and object instances, with success rates measured over multiple trials per task. Baselines will include policies trained solely on human data, solely on machine-generated data, and co-training with both. Additional real-world transfer experiments will be conducted by co-training on simulated and real robot demonstrations, with success rates compared for seen and unseen objects. Evaluation metrics will primarily be task success rates, with qualitative analysis of policy robustness and failure modes.
f773ceb43ffc7f9cd685250c4919924ec0bc85c7.novelty_claims: The proposed framework uniquely combines large-scale, photorealistic, and highly diverse simulation environments with AI-generated assets and tasks, supporting cross-embodiment robot training. It is the first to integrate generative AI for both asset and task creation at this scale, and to provide a massive, multi-task dataset with over 100,000 trajectories for imitation learning. The approach demonstrates clear scaling trends in policy performance with increased synthetic data and shows that simulation-trained policies can significantly improve real-world task success. The framework enables systematic benchmarking of generalist robot agents and paves the way for scalable, reproducible research in robot learning.

f7749635a5fc0492ef4705bee963ffa887bb2865.title: Fine-Tuning Large Vision-Language Models as Decision-Making Agents via Reinforcement Learning
f7749635a5fc0492ef4705bee963ffa887bb2865.research_question: How can large vision-language models be effectively fine-tuned to serve as decision-making agents in interactive, multi-step, goal-directed environments that require both visual recognition and language reasoning?
f7749635a5fc0492ef4705bee963ffa887bb2865.hypothesis: Fine-tuning large vision-language models using reinforcement learning, with explicit chain-of-thought reasoning in the output, will significantly improve their decision-making performance in complex, interactive tasks compared to supervised instruction tuning or RL methods without chain-of-thought reasoning.
f7749635a5fc0492ef4705bee963ffa887bb2865.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed to fine-tune large vision-language models (VLMs) as decision-making agents via reinforcement learning (RL). At each time step, the VLM receives a visual observation and a task-specific prompt, and generates an open-ended textual output containing both chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning and a text-based action. A post-processing function parses the output to extract a legal action, which is executed in the environment to obtain a reward and the next state. The RL training loop is implemented using a policy gradient method (e.g., PPO), with a custom likelihood computation that balances the influence of CoT and action tokens via a scaling factor. The entire VLM is fine-tuned end-to-end, leveraging both vision and language modalities for policy learning.
f7749635a5fc0492ef4705bee963ffa887bb2865.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two domains: (1) a custom 'gym_cards' suite of four tasks (NumberLine, EZPoints, Points24, Blackjack) designed to test fine-grained visual recognition and arithmetic reasoning, and (2) the ALFWorld embodied AI environment, which requires visual semantic understanding and state-dependent action selection. The backbone VLM will be a 7B-parameter model (e.g., LLaVA-v1.6-mistral-7b), with comparisons against commercial models (GPT-4V, Gemini), a supervised fine-tuned baseline, and a CNN-based RL agent. Evaluation metrics will include episode success rates and learning curves over environment steps, with ablations to assess the impact of CoT reasoning and the scaling factor. Experiments will use up to 15k steps for gym_cards and 5k steps for ALFWorld, with equal or weighted averages for multi-task domains.
f7749635a5fc0492ef4705bee963ffa887bb2865.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to directly fine-tune large vision-language models end-to-end with reinforcement learning for multi-step, goal-directed decision-making tasks requiring both vision and language understanding. The method uniquely integrates chain-of-thought reasoning into the RL fine-tuning process, demonstrating that CoT is a crucial component for performance gains. The framework enables 7B VLMs to outperform commercial models on a range of tasks, and provides new insights into the role of intermediate reasoning in RL-based policy learning for multimodal agents.

f79d9763e2ede46600b1a3e48c0c2033d3eef532.title: Asymptotically Optimal Strategies For Combinatorial Semi-Bandits in Polynomial Time
f79d9763e2ede46600b1a3e48c0c2033d3eef532.research_question: How can asymptotically optimal strategies for combinatorial semi-bandits with uncorrelated Gaussian rewards be implemented in polynomial time for a broad class of combinatorial structures?
f79d9763e2ede46600b1a3e48c0c2033d3eef532.hypothesis: It is possible to design an algorithm that computes the solution to the Graves-Lai optimization problem in polynomial time for many combinatorial structures, thereby enabling the implementation of asymptotically optimal algorithms for combinatorial semi-bandits within polynomial time complexity.
f79d9763e2ede46600b1a3e48c0c2033d3eef532.proposed_method: A new algorithm, termed Graves-Lai Projected Gradient (GLPG), will be developed to solve the Graves-Lai optimization problem efficiently for combinatorial semi-bandits. The method leverages a dimensionality reduction that reformulates the original high-dimensional optimization into a lower-dimensional problem, focusing on the number of samples required for accurate estimation of unknown reward parameters. The approach assumes the combinatorial decision set admits a compact convex hull representation and that certain combinatorial optimization subproblems (such as linear maximization and budgeted linear maximization) can be solved exactly or approximately in polynomial time. The GLPG algorithm iteratively updates candidate solutions using projected gradient steps, with projections performed onto the feasible set defined by the combinatorial structure, and guarantees convergence to an optimal or near-optimal solution up to any desired accuracy. The method is designed to be compatible with a wide range of combinatorial structures, including m-sets, spanning trees, matroids, paths, matchings, and intersections of matroids.
f79d9763e2ede46600b1a3e48c0c2033d3eef532.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard combinatorial semi-bandit benchmarks, encompassing a variety of combinatorial structures such as m-sets, spanning trees, matroids, source-destination paths, matchings, and intersections of matroids. The performance of the proposed GLPG-based asymptotically optimal algorithm will be evaluated against established baselines, including CUCB, ESCB, AESCB, TS, and OSSB. Evaluation metrics will include cumulative regret and computational complexity (runtime per decision step), with particular attention paid to the scalability of the approach as the dimension and complexity of the combinatorial set increase. Datasets will be generated according to the uncorrelated Gaussian reward model, and experiments will systematically vary problem parameters such as the size of the decision set, reward gaps, and time horizon to assess robustness and efficiency.
f79d9763e2ede46600b1a3e48c0c2033d3eef532.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first method capable of solving the Graves-Lai optimization problem in polynomial time for a broad class of combinatorial structures, thereby enabling the first polynomial-time implementation of asymptotically optimal algorithms for combinatorial semi-bandits. The approach generalizes beyond previously studied special cases (such as m-sets and matroids), and provides both exact and approximate solutions depending on the tractability of underlying combinatorial optimization subproblems. The dimensionality reduction and projected gradient framework represent significant algorithmic innovations, and the method is broadly applicable to many real-world combinatorial optimization problems.

f7b4211d53a05737b5efc161da69c78e2e7b8850.title: Consistent Diffusion Meets Tweedie: Training Exact Ambient Diffusion Models with Noisy Data
f7b4211d53a05737b5efc161da69c78e2e7b8850.research_question: How can diffusion models be trained to generate samples from an uncorrupted data distribution when only noisy or corrupted training data is available, and can this approach mitigate memorization and data replication in large-scale generative models?
f7b4211d53a05737b5efc161da69c78e2e7b8850.hypothesis: It is possible to develop an exact framework for training diffusion models using only noisy or corrupted data such that the resulting models can sample from the uncorrupted data distribution, while reducing memorization of the training set and maintaining competitive generative performance.
f7b4211d53a05737b5efc161da69c78e2e7b8850.proposed_method: A novel training framework is proposed that enables exact learning of diffusion models from noisy or corrupted data. The method consists of two main components: (1) a double application of Tweedie’s formula to learn optimal denoisers for all noise levels above the observed data noise, and (2) a consistency loss function that enforces the learned denoisers to be consistent across noise levels, allowing learning for noise levels below the observed data noise. The training objective combines an ambient score matching term for noise levels above the training noise and a consistency loss for all pairs of time steps, ensuring the denoiser is optimal and consistent. The approach is designed to be computationally efficient, avoiding expensive divergence terms, and can be applied to both standard and variance-preserving diffusion processes. The framework is implemented to fine-tune large diffusion models, such as Stable Diffusion XL, using only noisy samples, with or without text guidance.
f7b4211d53a05737b5efc161da69c78e2e7b8850.experiment_details: Experiments involve fine-tuning Stable Diffusion XL on datasets such as FFHQ (1024x1024 resolution), subsets of LAION, and chest x-ray images, using various levels of added Gaussian noise to simulate corruption. Models are trained with the proposed ambient denoising score matching loss, both with and without the consistency term. Evaluation includes measuring denoising performance (latent and pixel MSE), unconditional image generation quality (FID scores on 50,000 samples), and visual fidelity of generated samples. Memorization and data replication are assessed using similarity metrics in the DINOv2 embedding space, comparing generated samples to training data and benchmarking against previous methods for detecting replication. Baselines include models trained with clean data and prior SURE-based or Noise2Noise approaches.
f7b4211d53a05737b5efc161da69c78e2e7b8850.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable exact training of diffusion models from only noisy or corrupted data, allowing sampling from the true uncorrupted distribution. The method introduces a computationally efficient objective based on a double application of Tweedie’s formula and a consistency loss, overcoming limitations of prior approximation-based methods. The approach is shown to reduce memorization and replication of training data compared to traditional training on clean data, and it maintains competitive generative performance even at high corruption levels. The framework is generalizable to various data domains and noise models, and code is open-sourced to facilitate further research.

f7daa82747a13314c42a1df0c8eb2d4958ac27d6.title: Tackling Prevalent Conditions in Unsupervised Combinatorial Optimization: Cardinality, Minimum, Covering, and More
f7daa82747a13314c42a1df0c8eb2d4958ac27d6.research_question: How can unsupervised learning methods for combinatorial optimization be systematically extended to handle prevalent conditions such as cardinality constraints, minimum objectives, and covering constraints, in a way that improves both optimization quality and computational efficiency across a range of combinatorial optimization problems?
f7daa82747a13314c42a1df0c8eb2d4958ac27d6.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by concretizing the targets for probabilistic objective construction and derandomization, and by deriving non-trivial objectives and efficient derandomization schemes for prevalent combinatorial conditions, it is possible to achieve superior optimization quality and speed compared to existing unsupervised learning for combinatorial optimization (UL4CO) methods.
f7daa82747a13314c42a1df0c8eb2d4958ac27d6.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework, UCOM2 (Unsupervised Combinatorial Optimization Under Commonly-involved Conditions), will be developed to address prevalent conditions in combinatorial optimization. The approach begins by formalizing desirable properties for probabilistic objectives and derandomization, providing theoretical justification for these targets. For each prevalent condition (such as cardinality, minimum, covering, and clique constraints), tight upper bounds (TUBs) are derived and used to construct probabilistic objectives as expectations over discrete functions. Efficient, incremental greedy derandomization algorithms are then proposed, leveraging entry-wise concavity and local decomposability to ensure both quality guarantees and computational tractability. The methodology is modular, allowing for the combination of derived objectives and derandomization schemes to address complex, multi-condition problems.
f7daa82747a13314c42a1df0c8eb2d4958ac27d6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world graph datasets across several benchmark combinatorial optimization problems, including facility location, maximum coverage, and robust coloring. The proposed method will be compared against a suite of baselines, including random selection, greedy heuristics, commercial solvers (Gurobi, SCIP), state-of-the-art UL4CO methods (such as CardNN and EGN), and reinforcement learning approaches. Evaluation metrics will include optimization objective value (quality) and running time (speed), with results averaged over multiple trials and datasets. Additional ablation studies will analyze the impact of individual components, such as the choice of probabilistic objective and derandomization strategy, on overall performance.
f7daa82747a13314c42a1df0c8eb2d4958ac27d6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled and theoretically justified framework for constructing probabilistic objectives and efficient derandomization schemes tailored to prevalent combinatorial conditions, many of which have not been systematically addressed in prior UL4CO literature. The method provides stronger quality guarantees and faster derandomization compared to existing random sampling and naive rounding approaches. The incremental and modular design enables broad applicability to a variety of combinatorial optimization problems, and empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior trade-offs between optimization quality and computational speed.

f7e93c8adec97784ec0e18d4fd56d982a8922e0d.title: Linear Convergence of Natural Policy Gradient Methods with Log-Linear Policies
f7e93c8adec97784ec0e18d4fd56d982a8922e0d.research_question: Can natural policy gradient (NPG) and Q-NPG methods achieve linear convergence rates and favorable sample complexity guarantees when applied to infinite-horizon discounted Markov decision processes with log-linear policy parameterizations, without relying on strong convex regularization?
f7e93c8adec97784ec0e18d4fd56d982a8922e0d.hypothesis: Natural policy gradient and Q-NPG methods, when formulated with log-linear policies and compatible function approximation, will achieve linear convergence rates and near-optimal sample complexity using simple, non-adaptive geometrically increasing step sizes, even in the absence of entropy or other strongly convex regularization.
f7e93c8adec97784ec0e18d4fd56d982a8922e0d.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops and analyzes natural policy gradient (NPG) and Q-NPG algorithms for infinite-horizon discounted Markov decision processes, focusing on policies parameterized by log-linear models. Both methods are formulated within the compatible function approximation framework, allowing the policy update to be expressed as an inexact policy mirror descent (PMD) step. The NPG update is computed by solving a regression problem that approximates the advantage function using the gradient of the log-policy, while Q-NPG uses the Q-function as the regression target. Both algorithms employ a simple, geometrically increasing step size schedule and do not require entropy or other strongly convex regularization. Theoretical analysis is conducted under assumptions of bounded statistical and approximation (or transfer) errors, as well as reasonable distribution mismatch and concentrability coefficients.
f7e93c8adec97784ec0e18d4fd56d982a8922e0d.experiment_details: The experimental plan involves theoretical analysis and empirical validation of the convergence rates and sample complexities of NPG and Q-NPG with log-linear policies. Experiments will be conducted on standard infinite-horizon discounted MDP benchmarks, using both synthetic and real-world datasets where applicable. Baseline comparisons will include tabular NPG, entropy-regularized NPG, and other policy gradient methods with and without function approximation. Evaluation metrics will focus on convergence rate (linear vs. sublinear), sample complexity (number of samples required to achieve a given error), and final policy performance (expected cost or reward). Key experimental setup details include varying the step size schedule, the quality of function approximation, and the initial state-action distributions to test robustness and generality.
f7e93c8adec97784ec0e18d4fd56d982a8922e0d.novelty_claims: The proposed research establishes, for the first time, non-asymptotic linear convergence rates and near-optimal sample complexity bounds for both NPG and Q-NPG methods with log-linear policy parameterizations in the function approximation regime, without requiring entropy or other strongly convex regularization. The approach leverages a novel connection to inexact policy mirror descent, employs a simple geometrically increasing step size, and provides sharper theoretical guarantees than prior work, which was limited to the tabular setting or required additional regularization. The analysis also clarifies the roles of distribution mismatch and concentrability coefficients, and corrects errors in previous sample complexity results.

f7f1b23797c4886fcf7be184201d0a7d47baa40c.title: ZipIt! Merging Models from Different Tasks without Training
f7f1b23797c4886fcf7be184201d0a7d47baa40c.research_question: How can models trained on entirely different tasks, with different initializations and potentially disjoint datasets and label sets, be merged into a single multi-task model without any additional training?
f7f1b23797c4886fcf7be184201d0a7d47baa40c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by generalizing the model merging process to allow merging both across and within models' feature spaces, and by supporting partial merging up to specified layers (creating multi-head architectures), it is possible to effectively combine models trained on disjoint tasks into a single model that retains strong performance on all original tasks without retraining.
f7f1b23797c4886fcf7be184201d0a7d47baa40c.proposed_method: A novel framework, ZipIt!, is proposed for merging multiple neural network models of the same architecture, each trained on different tasks, into a single multi-task model without any retraining. The method introduces a 'zip' operation that merges features both across models and within the same model by identifying and averaging highly correlated features, as determined by activation correlations over a small set of unlabeled images. This is accomplished by constructing a merge matrix for each layer, which allows for flexible pairing and averaging of features, and an unmerge matrix to maintain compatibility with subsequent layers. The framework also supports partial zipping, where only a subset of layers are merged, resulting in a multi-head model that can handle multiple tasks. The merging process is performed greedily for computational efficiency, and propagation rules are defined to handle various network modules, including skip connections and non-linearities.
f7f1b23797c4886fcf7be184201d0a7d47baa40c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several challenging settings: (1) merging models trained on disjoint class splits of the same dataset (e.g., CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100), (2) merging models trained on completely different datasets (e.g., Stanford Dogs, Oxford Pets, CUB200, NABirds), and (3) merging models across modalities (e.g., combining a semantic segmentation model with an image classification model). Datasets such as CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k, and various fine-grained classification datasets will be used. Baselines for comparison include weight averaging, permutation-based merging (e.g., GitRe-Basin), and ensembles (as an upper bound). Evaluation metrics include joint accuracy (across all classes) and per-task accuracy. Experimental setups involve training models from scratch with different initializations, using a portion of the training set to compute feature correlations, and resetting batch normalization statistics for fair comparison. Ablation studies will be performed to analyze the effects of merging within models, model scale, and matching algorithms.
f7f1b23797c4886fcf7be184201d0a7d47baa40c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first general method to merge models trained on entirely disjoint tasks without any additional training. Key innovations include the introduction of within-model feature merging, a general graph-based matching algorithm for flexible feature pairing, and the concept of partial zipping to create multi-head models. The method generalizes and outperforms prior permutation-based merging approaches, achieving significant improvements (20-60%) in accuracy on challenging multi-task merging scenarios. The framework is also extensible to merging more than two models and supports merging across different modalities.

f8034b8bed96179b261c47db2ec75292cef92627.title: LOTUS: Continual Imitation Learning for Robot Manipulation Through Unsupervised Skill Discovery
f8034b8bed96179b261c47db2ec75292cef92627.research_question: How can a robot continually and efficiently learn to solve new manipulation tasks throughout its lifespan, using a small number of human demonstrations, while avoiding catastrophic forgetting and enabling effective knowledge transfer in vision-based manipulation domains?
f8034b8bed96179b261c47db2ec75292cef92627.hypothesis: A hierarchical imitation learning framework that continually discovers and composes reusable sensorimotor skills from unsegmented human demonstrations, leveraging open-world vision models and incremental clustering, will enable robots to efficiently learn new manipulation tasks, transfer knowledge forward and backward, and avoid catastrophic forgetting.
f8034b8bed96179b261c47db2ec75292cef92627.proposed_method: A novel continual imitation learning algorithm is proposed that builds an ever-growing library of sensorimotor skills from sequential human demonstrations. The method begins with a continual skill discovery process using an open-vocabulary vision model (such as DINOv2) to extract recurring patterns as skills from unsegmented demonstrations. Temporal segments are identified via hierarchical clustering on semantic features, and incremental clustering is used to assign segments to existing or new skill partitions based on similarity metrics and Silhouette analysis. Each skill is modeled as a goal-conditioned visuomotor policy operating on raw images, and a meta-controller is trained to flexibly compose these skills by predicting skill indices and subgoals using a transformer-based architecture. Experience Replay is incorporated to retain exemplar demonstrations and enable both forward and backward knowledge transfer, mitigating catastrophic forgetting.
f8034b8bed96179b261c47db2ec75292cef92627.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in both simulated and real-world environments. Simulation benchmarks include the LIBERO-OBJECT, LIBERO-GOAL, and LIBERO-50 task suites, which collectively cover a range of object concepts and manipulation motions. Each base task is provided with a set number of demonstrations, and lifelong learning stages introduce new tasks with fewer demonstrations per task. Baselines for comparison include sequential fine-tuning, Experience Replay (ER), and hierarchical skill discovery methods adapted for continual learning. Evaluation metrics include Forward Transfer (FWT), Negative Backward Transfer (NBT), and Area Under the Success Rate Curve (AUC), all computed in terms of task success rates. Real-robot experiments are performed on the MUTEX suite, with similar lifelong learning protocols and demonstration counts. Ablation studies assess the impact of skill library growth and the choice of vision models for skill discovery.
f8034b8bed96179b261c47db2ec75292cef92627.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a hierarchical imitation learning algorithm that continually discovers and composes skills from a stream of new tasks, using open-world vision models for unsupervised skill discovery. The method incrementally grows and updates the skill library, enabling both forward and backward transfer in lifelong learning settings. A meta-controller is designed to handle a variable number of skills and compose them adaptively. The approach demonstrates superior knowledge transfer, data efficiency, and robustness to non-stationary task distributions compared to state-of-the-art baselines, and is validated in both simulation and real-robot settings.

f81a1b4510631d14b5b565c4701ee056f8d5c72f.title: CodePlan: Repository-Level Coding using LLMs and Planning
f81a1b4510631d14b5b565c4701ee056f8d5c72f.research_question: How can repository-level coding tasks, which require pervasive and interdependent edits across an entire codebase, be automated using large language models (LLMs) in a scalable and systematic manner?
f81a1b4510631d14b5b565c4701ee056f8d5c72f.hypothesis: Repository-level coding tasks can be effectively automated by framing them as planning problems, where a combination of static dependency analysis, change impact analysis, and adaptive planning enables LLMs to generate and propagate interdependent code edits across large codebases, resulting in higher correctness and repository validity compared to oracle-guided or non-planning baselines.
f81a1b4510631d14b5b565c4701ee056f8d5c72f.proposed_method: A task-agnostic framework, CodePlan, is developed to automate repository-level coding tasks by synthesizing a multi-step plan of code edits. The method begins by constructing a dependency graph representing syntactic and semantic relationships among code blocks in the repository. Seed edit specifications, derived from task instructions, are used to initialize a plan graph, where each node represents a code edit obligation. For each pending obligation, CodePlan extracts the relevant code fragment, gathers spatial and temporal context using static analysis and the plan graph, and constructs a prompt for the LLM to generate the required code edit. The edited code is merged back into the repository, and the dependency graph is updated. Change impact analysis is then used to identify and propagate new edit obligations to dependent code blocks, iteratively extending the plan until the repository passes a correctness oracle (e.g., build, static analysis, or tests). This process continues until all obligations are resolved and the repository is validated.
f81a1b4510631d14b5b565c4701ee056f8d5c72f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two repository-level coding tasks: package migration for C# repositories and temporal code edits for Python repositories. Each task will be evaluated on multiple real-world code repositories, with the number of affected files ranging from 2 to 97 per repository. The evaluation will use the gpt-4-32k model as the LLM, and correctness oracles such as build systems (for C#) and static type checkers (for Python) to validate repository states. Baselines will include iterative oracle-guided repair approaches that use the same contextual information as CodePlan but do not employ planning. Evaluation metrics will include ground truth match rates and the number of repositories passing validity checks (e.g., building without errors and making correct code edits). Data and evaluation scripts, except for proprietary repositories, will be released for reproducibility.
f81a1b4510631d14b5b565c4701ee056f8d5c72f.novelty_claims: The proposal formalizes and addresses the previously unsolved problem of automating repository-level coding tasks with LLMs by systematically analyzing and propagating the effects of code edits across entire repositories. CodePlan introduces a novel integration of incremental dependency analysis, change may-impact analysis, and adaptive planning to synthesize interdependent chains of code edits. Unlike existing methods, which rely on developer-specified edit locations or oracle-guided repair, CodePlan autonomously infers and propagates edit obligations, providing both spatial and temporal context to the LLM. This unified framework enables scalable automation of complex, interdependent coding tasks that have not been previously automated using LLMs.

f849b873e94f28e1f2a3e1dc4d7bef17eb64adab.title: Towards Stable Test-Time Adaptation in Dynamic Wild World
f849b873e94f28e1f2a3e1dc4d7bef17eb64adab.research_question: How can test-time adaptation (TTA) methods be made stable and effective in real-world scenarios characterized by mixed distribution shifts, small test batch sizes, and online imbalanced label distribution shifts?
f849b873e94f28e1f2a3e1dc4d7bef17eb64adab.hypothesis: Batch-agnostic normalization layers (such as group or layer normalization) improve the stability of TTA under wild test settings, but further stabilization can be achieved by filtering out unreliable samples and encouraging model weights to converge to flat minima via sharpness-aware entropy minimization.
f849b873e94f28e1f2a3e1dc4d7bef17eb64adab.proposed_method: A novel test-time adaptation framework is proposed that leverages batch-agnostic normalization layers (group or layer norm) to improve stability under dynamic, real-world shifts. The method, termed Sharpness-Aware and Reliable entropy minimization (SAR), operates in two main stages: (1) unreliable test samples are filtered out based on their entropy, removing those likely to produce large, noisy gradients that destabilize adaptation; (2) for the remaining samples, a sharpness-aware optimization is performed by jointly minimizing the entropy and the sharpness of the entropy loss, encouraging the model to converge to flat minima that are robust to noisy updates. The sharpness is quantified by the maximal change in entropy under small perturbations of model weights, and optimization is performed efficiently using a first-order approximation. Additionally, a model recovery scheme is introduced, resetting model parameters if collapse is detected, further enhancing robustness.
f849b873e94f28e1f2a3e1dc4d7bef17eb64adab.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the ImageNet-C benchmark, which includes 15 corruption types across four main categories (noise, blur, weather, digital) and five severity levels, as well as on the VisDA-2021 dataset. The proposed method is evaluated using pre-trained ResNet50 models with batch norm (BN) and group norm (GN), and VitBase models with layer norm (LN). Baselines include state-of-the-art TTA methods such as Tent, EATA, MEMO, and DDA. Evaluation metrics focus on classification accuracy under various wild test settings: mixed distribution shifts, small batch sizes (including batch size = 1), and online imbalanced label distributions. Computational efficiency is also assessed by measuring GPU time for processing large test sets. Ablation studies are performed to analyze the contributions of each component of the SAR method.
f849b873e94f28e1f2a3e1dc4d7bef17eb64adab.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a sharpness-aware and reliable entropy minimization framework that stabilizes TTA under challenging real-world conditions by filtering unreliable samples and optimizing for flat minima. It demonstrates that batch-agnostic normalization layers are more suitable for stable TTA than batch norm, and that the combination of entropy filtering and sharpness-aware optimization significantly reduces failure cases such as model collapse. The approach achieves state-of-the-art performance and efficiency compared to existing TTA methods, especially in scenarios with mixed shifts, small batches, and label imbalance, without requiring access to source data or extensive pre-collection of in-distribution samples.

f8790bfd44bb6386b00189333ddcdb6d9d20a089.title: Layer-Adaptive State Pruning for Deep State Space Models
f8790bfd44bb6386b00189333ddcdb6d9d20a089.research_question: How can the state dimension of deep state space models be adaptively reduced to improve computational efficiency and memory usage, while maintaining model performance and stability across various sequential tasks?
f8790bfd44bb6386b00189333ddcdb6d9d20a089.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a layer-adaptive, structured pruning method based on frequency-domain energy loss minimization can identify and remove insignificant states in deep state space models, resulting in substantial model compression with minimal loss in accuracy and without requiring retraining.
f8790bfd44bb6386b00189333ddcdb6d9d20a089.proposed_method: A novel structured pruning framework, termed Layer-Adaptive State Pruning (LAST), will be developed for deep state space models (SSMs). The method will compute importance scores for each state in every layer, based on the H-infinity norm of the corresponding subsystem, which quantifies the maximum frequency-domain gain. These scores will be normalized layer-wise to enable cross-layer comparison, allowing for global, layer-adaptive pruning decisions. The pruning process will iteratively remove states with the lowest normalized scores, targeting a desired overall compression ratio, while bounding the model-level output energy loss. The approach will be applicable to both multi-SISO and MIMO SSM architectures and will leverage the guaranteed stability of diagonal SSM parameterizations.
f8790bfd44bb6386b00189333ddcdb6d9d20a089.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of long-range sequence modeling benchmarks, including the Long Range Arena (LRA), Speech Commands, and pixel-level image classification datasets such as MNIST and CIFAR10. Both multi-SISO (e.g., S4D) and MIMO (e.g., S5) SSM models will be evaluated. Baseline methods will include uniform local pruning and global pruning without energy normalization, as well as random pruning for ablation. Evaluation metrics will focus on classification accuracy and the achieved compression ratio, with models assessed in a one-shot pruning setting (no retraining). The experimental setup will ensure reproducibility using fixed seeds and standardized configurations, and the effect of pruning will be measured by the accuracy loss at various pruning ratios.
f8790bfd44bb6386b00189333ddcdb6d9d20a089.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first global, layer-adaptive pruning criterion for deep state space models, leveraging H-infinity norm-based energy normalization to enable cross-layer comparison of state importance. Unlike traditional model order reduction methods, which are limited to single linear systems, this method extends to multi-system, nonlinear, and deep architectures. The approach provides a principled, non-magnitude-based pruning criterion specifically tailored for SSMs, and demonstrates that significant model compression can be achieved without retraining and with minimal accuracy loss. Additionally, the method offers new insights into the compressibility and redundancy of state spaces in modern SSMs.

f87ce4d2786cd7b40f6ef0e891181fe9464a4baf.title: Adversarial Unlearning of Backdoors via Implicit Hypergradient
f87ce4d2786cd7b40f6ef0e891181fe9464a4baf.research_question: How can backdoors be effectively removed from a poisoned machine learning model using only a small set of clean data, while maintaining model accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency across a wide range of attack settings and trigger types?
f87ce4d2786cd7b40f6ef0e891181fe9464a4baf.hypothesis: A minimax optimization framework, solved via implicit hypergradients, can enable effective and generalizable removal of backdoors from poisoned models using limited clean data, outperforming or matching state-of-the-art defenses in robustness, accuracy, and efficiency, even under challenging attack scenarios.
f87ce4d2786cd7b40f6ef0e891181fe9464a4baf.proposed_method: A minimax optimization formulation will be developed for backdoor removal, where the outer minimization seeks model parameters that are robust to backdoor triggers, and the inner maximization seeks universal perturbations (triggers) that maximize prediction loss on clean data. The proposed approach will utilize an Implicit Backdoor Adversarial Unlearning (I-BAU) algorithm, which leverages implicit hypergradients to capture the interdependence between the inner and outer optimization problems. The method will compute the gradient of the objective with respect to model parameters by combining direct gradients and an efficiently approximated response Jacobian, using iterative solvers and reverse-mode automatic differentiation. The algorithm will be implemented to support norm-bounded triggers and will be designed to be memory- and computation-efficient, allowing for effective operation even with a small clean dataset.
f87ce4d2786cd7b40f6ef0e891181fe9464a4baf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a simplified VGG neural network architecture on the CIFAR-10 and GTSRB datasets. The evaluation will cover eleven backdoor attack types, including both additive and non-additive triggers, in multiple attack settings: one-trigger-one-target, one-trigger-all-to-all, and multi-trigger-multi-target. The proposed method will be compared against six state-of-the-art backdoor defenses: Neural Cleanse, DeepInspect, TABOR, Fine-pruning, Neural Attention Distillation, and Differential Privacy training. Evaluation metrics will include attack success rate (ASR), clean accuracy (ACC), computational runtime, and sensitivity to poison ratio and clean data size. The experiments will further analyze stability across runs, robustness to trigger and attack variations, and performance in extreme cases with as few as 100 clean samples.
f87ce4d2786cd7b40f6ef0e891181fe9464a4baf.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified minimax formulation for backdoor removal that does not require assumptions about the number or type of triggers, encompassing and generalizing prior trigger synthesis-based and fine-tuning defenses. The use of implicit hypergradients to solve the minimax problem accounts for the interdependence between inner and outer optimization, overcoming the instability and inefficiency of previous methods. The algorithm achieves state-of-the-art or superior robustness and accuracy across diverse attack scenarios, is significantly more computationally efficient (over 13× faster than the most efficient baseline in some settings), and remains effective even with extremely limited clean data, where all baselines fail.

f87d1379fdca3c2af8239f441f21a6e2ff90bf45.title: Moderately Distributional Exploration for Domain Generalization
f87d1379fdca3c2af8239f441f21a6e2ff90bf45.research_question: How can domain generalization be improved by mitigating the negative effects of distributional shift between training and unknown target domains, particularly when generating new domains for training?
f87d1379fdca3c2af8239f441f21a6e2ff90bf45.hypothesis: Restricting distributional exploration to an uncertainty subset that shares semantic factors with the training domains, rather than exploring the full uncertainty set, will improve generalization to unknown target domains by reducing low-confidence predictions and distribution discrepancy.
f87d1379fdca3c2af8239f441f21a6e2ff90bf45.proposed_method: A novel approach called Moderately Distributional Exploration (MODE) is proposed for domain generalization. MODE restricts distributional exploration to a subset of the uncertainty set that preserves the semantic factors of the training domains, thereby avoiding exploration into semantically unrelated domains. The method is grounded in a causal assumption where observed data are generated by a mechanism involving both semantic and non-semantic factors, with only the semantic factors influencing the label. MODE operationalizes this by generating new domains through controlled perturbations of non-semantic factors (e.g., style) while keeping semantic content fixed, using techniques such as Fourier-based amplitude mixing or AdaIN-based feature statistics manipulation. Theoretical analysis provides generalization and risk bounds, showing that MODE can achieve provable generalization performance under mild assumptions.
f87d1379fdca3c2af8239f441f21a6e2ff90bf45.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard domain generalization benchmarks including PACS, Office-Home, and Digit-DG. The evaluation will follow a leave-one-domain-out protocol, training on all but one domain and testing on the held-out domain. Baseline methods will include state-of-the-art domain generalization approaches such as DeepAll, Jigen, MMD-AAE, CrossGrad, DDAIG, L2A-OT, MixStyle, FACT, CIRL, and GroupDRO. Evaluation metrics will be classification accuracy on the target domain. Experimental setup will involve using pre-trained backbones (e.g., ResNet-18), standard data augmentations, and hyperparameter sweeps for key method parameters (e.g., trade-off coefficients, number of style providers, inner optimization steps). Ablation studies will examine the effects of uncertainty subset size, trade-off parameters, and style manipulation strategies.
f87d1379fdca3c2af8239f441f21a6e2ff90bf45.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled restriction of distributional exploration to semantically consistent uncertainty subsets, addressing the low-confidence issue of traditional distributionally robust optimization in domain generalization. Theoretical contributions include new generalization and risk bounds for domain generalization under the proposed framework. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate competitive or superior performance to state-of-the-art baselines, particularly in challenging settings with large domain shifts. The method is also flexible, allowing instantiation with various style transfer and feature manipulation techniques.

f8a2dca1e8fe56e698984c077f7ff58d8ca867e9.title: Large Language Models as Optimizers
f8a2dca1e8fe56e698984c077f7ff58d8ca867e9.research_question: Can large language models be leveraged as general-purpose optimizers for a variety of optimization tasks, including mathematical and prompt optimization, when the optimization problem is described in natural language?
f8a2dca1e8fe56e698984c077f7ff58d8ca867e9.hypothesis: Large language models, when prompted with a meta-prompt containing natural language problem descriptions and optimization trajectories, can iteratively generate improved solutions to optimization problems, potentially matching or surpassing hand-designed heuristics and human-crafted prompts in certain domains.
f8a2dca1e8fe56e698984c077f7ff58d8ca867e9.proposed_method: A novel optimization framework, Optimization by PROmpting (OPRO), is developed to utilize large language models (LLMs) as optimizers. The optimization process is driven by a meta-prompt that includes a natural language description of the optimization task, a trajectory of previously generated solutions and their scores, and meta-instructions specifying the desired output format. At each optimization step, the LLM generates multiple new candidate solutions based on the meta-prompt. These candidates are then evaluated using an objective function (which may itself be implemented by an LLM), and the best-performing solutions are appended to the meta-prompt for subsequent steps. The process iterates until convergence or a maximum number of steps is reached, with temperature and sampling strategies tuned to balance exploration and exploitation.
f8a2dca1e8fe56e698984c077f7ff58d8ca867e9.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both mathematical optimization tasks (linear regression and the Traveling Salesman Problem) and prompt optimization for natural language tasks. For mathematical optimization, synthetic datasets are generated for linear regression (with randomly sampled coefficients and Gaussian noise) and TSP (with random node coordinates), and performance is compared against classical heuristics such as Nearest Neighbor and Farthest Insertion. For prompt optimization, benchmarks include GSM8K (grade-school math word problems) and Big-Bench Hard (BBH), with small training subsets (e.g., 3.5% for GSM8K) used for optimization and full test sets for evaluation. Multiple LLMs (PaLM 2-L, PaLM 2-L-IT, text-bison, gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4) are evaluated as both optimizers and scorers. Evaluation metrics include optimization trajectory (steps to convergence), accuracy (for prompt optimization), and optimality gap (for TSP). Baselines include human-designed prompts and standard heuristics.
f8a2dca1e8fe56e698984c077f7ff58d8ca867e9.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to systematically leverage large language models as general-purpose optimizers through iterative prompting, using natural language descriptions and optimization trajectories. OPRO demonstrates that LLMs can perform black-box optimization without explicit gradient information, and can optimize both continuous and discrete objectives. In prompt optimization, OPRO-optimized instructions outperform human-designed prompts by up to 8% on GSM8K and up to 50% on BBH tasks. The framework is model-agnostic, requires only API access, and enables rapid adaptation to new tasks by changing the problem description in the prompt.

f8aed7062dd4689d6c489d884c989a86b7ef5bee.title: MAGNET: A Multi-agent Framework for Finding Audio-Visual Needles by Reasoning over Multi-Video Haystacks
f8aed7062dd4689d6c489d884c989a86b7ef5bee.research_question: How can large multimodal models be effectively evaluated and enhanced for complex audio-visual reasoning and retrieval tasks that require identifying and integrating salient segments across multiple videos in response to a query?
f8aed7062dd4689d6c489d884c989a86b7ef5bee.hypothesis: A model-agnostic, multi-agent retrieval-augmented framework that leverages specialized audio-visual encoders, dynamic agentic reasoning, and adaptive salient frame selection will significantly improve multi-video audio-visual retrieval, temporal grounding, and answer generation compared to existing baselines.
f8aed7062dd4689d6c489d884c989a86b7ef5bee.proposed_method: A novel multi-agent framework, MAGNET, will be developed for large-scale audio-visual retrieval and reasoning across multiple videos. The approach begins with a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline that computes similarity between a query and a large collection of videos using fused audio-visual features and generated captions, both encoded with a multimodal encoder (e.g., IMAGEBIND). An adaptive Salient Frame Selector (SFS) module will be introduced to identify visually and semantically important frames, ensuring efficient localization of key events within long videos. For each shortlisted video, a dedicated audio-visual large language model (AVLLM) agent (e.g., Qwen2.5Omni) will process the content independently, predicting relevant temporal segments and partial answers. These outputs will be aggregated by a meta-agent (e.g., GPT-4o), which synthesizes a coherent, contextually grounded final answer. The framework will be model-agnostic, allowing integration with various AVLLMs, and will include new metrics for robust evaluation of temporal grounding and step-wise reasoning.
f8aed7062dd4689d6c489d884c989a86b7ef5bee.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the newly curated AVHaystacks benchmark, which contains 3100 annotated audio-visual QA pairs requiring evidence from at least two distinct videos, drawn from a pool of 500 YouTube videos across diverse domains. The dataset will be split into training and testing sets (2k/1k), with a smaller AVHaystacks-50 subset for baseline comparisons. Baseline methods will include state-of-the-art audio-visual models such as VideoRAG, Video-RAG, Qwen2.5Omni, UnifiedIO2, and Video-SALMONN, with adaptations for multi-video retrieval and reasoning. Evaluation metrics will comprise BLEU@4, CIDEr, cosine similarity of sentence embeddings, GPT-based scoring, human evaluation, recall at top-k (R@1, R@3, R@5), the Matched Temporal Grounding Score (MTGS) for segment-level grounding, and the Step-wise Error Metric (STEM) for procedural alignment. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of modality combinations, sampling strategies, and penalty hyperparameters.
f8aed7062dd4689d6c489d884c989a86b7ef5bee.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new benchmark (AVHaystacks) specifically designed for multi-video, audio-visual retrieval and reasoning, addressing a gap in existing evaluation datasets. The MAGNET framework is novel in its use of a model-agnostic, multi-agent architecture that tightly integrates retrieval, adaptive frame selection, and agentic reasoning for large-scale, cross-video audio-visual QA. Two new evaluation metrics, STEM and MTGS, are proposed for balanced and interpretable assessment of temporal grounding and step-wise reasoning. The approach claims substantial improvements over existing baselines in retrieval accuracy, temporal grounding, and answer generation, as demonstrated by both automated and human-centric metrics.

f8c6d738617c10f9598037c20cee6ebffd855597.title: Controlling Continuous Relaxation for Combinatorial Optimization
f8c6d738617c10f9598037c20cee6ebffd855597.research_question: How can unsupervised learning-based neural network solvers for combinatorial optimization be improved to address optimization challenges and eliminate the need for artificial rounding when mapping continuous relaxations back to discrete solutions?
f8c6d738617c10f9598037c20cee6ebffd855597.hypothesis: Introducing a continuous relaxation annealing strategy with a dynamically controlled penalty term will enable unsupervised learning-based solvers to escape local optima and achieve discrete solutions without artificial rounding, thereby improving solution quality and robustness for combinatorial optimization problems.
f8c6d738617c10f9598037c20cee6ebffd855597.proposed_method: A novel continuous relaxation annealing (CRA) method will be developed for unsupervised learning-based combinatorial optimization solvers. The approach augments the loss function with a penalty term parameterized by gamma (γ), which controls the trade-off between continuous and discrete solutions. Initially, γ is set to a negative value to smooth the non-convexity of the objective and facilitate exploration, then gradually annealed to a positive value to enforce discreteness in the solution space. The penalty term is designed to ensure gradients remain bounded and to eliminate stationary points that cause optimization plateaus. An early stopping criterion will be employed, halting training when the penalty term approaches zero, ensuring that the final solution is inherently discrete and robust to thresholding.
f8c6d738617c10f9598037c20cee6ebffd855597.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark combinatorial optimization problems, including Maximum Independent Set (MIS), MaxCut, and Diverse Bipartite Matching (DBM), across graphs of varying sizes and degrees. The proposed CRA-PI-GNN solver will be compared against baselines such as the original PI-GNN solver, random greedy algorithm (RGA), degree-based greedy algorithm (DGA), EGN, Meta-EGN, RUN-CSP, SDP-based methods, and other classical and learning-based solvers. Evaluation metrics will include approximation ratio (ApR), independent set density, and cut ratio, with optimal or theoretical values used for normalization. The experiments will utilize standard neural network architectures (e.g., GraphSAGE, GCN), the AdamW optimizer, and early stopping based on loss and penalty convergence. Computational scaling and learning speed will also be analyzed.
f8c6d738617c10f9598037c20cee6ebffd855597.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a rounding-free unsupervised learning framework for combinatorial optimization by dynamically controlling the discreteness of relaxed variables through annealing. This method eliminates the need for artificial post-training rounding, directly outputs discrete solutions, and addresses local optima entrapment by smoothing the optimization landscape. The approach is generalizable to various combinatorial optimization problems and demonstrates superior performance and scalability compared to existing unsupervised learning and heuristic baselines, while also accelerating the learning process.

f8cea2c1638c75ad1bf196ff66e7753120d2c54b.title: Generalization on the Unseen, Logic Reasoning and Degree Curriculum
f8cea2c1638c75ad1bf196ff66e7753120d2c54b.research_question: How do neural network architectures generalize to unseen domains in logical (Boolean) reasoning tasks, particularly under strong out-of-distribution (OOD) settings, and what are the underlying implicit biases that govern their extrapolation behavior?
f8cea2c1638c75ad1bf196ff66e7753120d2c54b.hypothesis: Neural network architectures trained by (stochastic) gradient descent on sparse Boolean functions in the generalization-on-the-unseen (GOTU) setting will converge to interpolators that minimize the degree-profile (min-degree interpolators) of the Fourier-Walsh expansion, exhibiting a min-degree bias on the unseen domain. This bias can be leveraged or mitigated through curriculum learning or regularization.
f8cea2c1638c75ad1bf196ff66e7753120d2c54b.proposed_method: The proposed approach will systematically study the generalization behavior of various neural network architectures—including random features models, linear neural networks (both diagonal and fully connected), and encoder-only Transformers—when trained on Boolean reasoning tasks with a holdout (unseen) domain. The methodology involves both theoretical analysis and empirical evaluation. Theoretical work will characterize the implicit bias of these architectures in the GOTU setting, using tools from Boolean Fourier analysis and algebraic geometry (vanishing ideals), to prove that min-degree interpolators are favored. Empirical work will involve training these models using (S)GD with zero training error on the seen domain and evaluating their extrapolation on the unseen domain. Additionally, a curriculum learning algorithm, 'Degree-Curriculum', will be developed to incrementally increase input complexity (e.g., via Hamming weight) to accelerate the learning of monomial supports. The method will also explore the impact of architectural choices (such as attention masks in Transformers) and propose symmetry-based regularization to mitigate min-degree bias when undesirable.
f8cea2c1638c75ad1bf196ff66e7753120d2c54b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and benchmark datasets relevant to logical and arithmetic reasoning, such as synthetic Boolean function tasks, arithmetic/algebra datasets, and possibly visual or algorithmic reasoning benchmarks (e.g., CLEVR, CLRS). The experimental setup will include training neural networks on a subset of the input space (the seen domain) and evaluating generalization on the strictly held-out unseen domain (GOTU metric). Baselines will include standard neural network architectures (random features models, linear networks, Transformers) and possibly models with and without curriculum learning or regularization. Evaluation metrics will focus on test accuracy or loss on the unseen domain, degree-profile of the learned interpolator, and Fourier mass distribution. Additional experiments will probe the effect of sparsity, input dimension, and architectural modifications (e.g., causal attention masks).
f8cea2c1638c75ad1bf196ff66e7753120d2c54b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous framework for studying generalization on the unseen (GOTU) as a strong OOD setting for reasoning tasks, providing both theoretical and empirical evidence of a min-degree implicit bias in neural networks trained by (S)GD. It establishes new theoretical results for random features models and linear networks, characterizes the solutions learned on the unseen domain, and connects these findings to the length generalization problem. The Degree-Curriculum algorithm is proposed as a novel curriculum learning strategy for efficient monomial learning. The work also explores the mitigation of min-degree bias via symmetry-based regularization, offering new insights into the controllability of implicit biases in neural networks for reasoning tasks.

f8d357d38bbcdd93889fe71762eb57842b2ab063.title: Simple and Effective Masked Diffusion Language Models
f8d357d38bbcdd93889fe71762eb57842b2ab063.research_question: Can a simplified, masked diffusion-based framework for language modeling close the performance gap with autoregressive models, and can such a framework be extended to enable efficient, generative, and representation learning capabilities for both language and biological sequence data?
f8d357d38bbcdd93889fe71762eb57842b2ab063.hypothesis: A masked diffusion language modeling framework, when combined with a well-engineered training recipe and a simplified Rao-Blackwellized objective, will achieve state-of-the-art performance among diffusion models on language modeling benchmarks, approach the perplexity of autoregressive models, and provide strong generative and representation learning capabilities across domains.
f8d357d38bbcdd93889fe71762eb57842b2ab063.proposed_method: A masked diffusion language modeling (MDLM) framework will be developed, focusing on a forward process that applies masking (absorbing state) noise to discrete tokens.
