The reverse process will be parameterized using a substitution-based (SUBS) approach, enforcing two key properties: zero probability for masked tokens and carry-over for unmasked tokens. The training objective will be a simplified, continuous-time Rao-Blackwellized variational lower bound (ELBO), which analytically reduces variance and tightens the bound by leveraging the properties of the masking process. The denoising network will be implemented as a diffusion transformer (DiT), incorporating timestep conditioning and rotary positional embeddings, and will be trained using a weighted average of masked language modeling losses. Efficient samplers will be designed to support both ancestral and semi-autoregressive (SAR) generation, allowing generation of arbitrary-length sequences and enabling BERT-style encoder-only models to perform principled text generation.
f8d357d38bbcdd93889fe71762eb57842b2ab063.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard language modeling datasets, including One Billion Words (LM1B) and OpenWebText (OWT), using established tokenizers (bert-base-uncased for LM1B, GPT2 tokenizer for OWT) and context sizes (128 for LM1B, 1024 for OWT). Models will be trained for up to 327B tokens, and compared against autoregressive (AR) baselines, prior diffusion models (D3PM, SEDD, DiffusionBERT), and other relevant approaches. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity (PPL) for generative modeling and downstream performance on the GLUE benchmark for representation learning. Additional experiments will extend the framework to DNA sequence modeling using the Caduceus model and Genomics Benchmarks, assessing both generative and classification performance. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of key components (continuous time, carry-over, zero masking) on performance. Semi-autoregressive generation speed and quality will be compared to SSD-LM using long-sequence generation tasks.
f8d357d38bbcdd93889fe71762eb57842b2ab063.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a principled and simplified masked diffusion objective that analytically tightens the ELBO and reduces training variance, outperforming all existing diffusion models on language modeling benchmarks and approaching autoregressive model performance. The method provides a direct connection between generative diffusion models and encoder-only BERT-style models, enabling efficient, principled generation from BERT-like architectures. The approach also supports fast semi-autoregressive decoding for arbitrary-length sequences and extends effectively to non-language domains such as biological sequence modeling, achieving strong generative and downstream task performance. The well-engineered implementation and training recipes significantly improve the performance of both the proposed method and previously discounted baselines, establishing new strong baselines for discrete diffusion modeling.

f8d75c913a4811fe9f2030ca8d965c3a6d49b423.title: GraphRouter: A Graph-based Router for LLM Selections
f8d75c913a4811fe9f2030ca8d965c3a6d49b423.research_question: How can the selection of large language models (LLMs) for diverse user queries and tasks be improved to balance performance and computational cost, while enabling generalization to new LLMs and tasks without retraining?
f8d75c913a4811fe9f2030ca8d965c3a6d49b423.hypothesis: A graph-based inductive framework that models contextual interactions among tasks, queries, and LLMs will enable more effective, adaptive, and generalizable LLM selection, outperforming existing transductive and embedding-based routers in both standard and new LLM scenarios.
f8d75c913a4811fe9f2030ca8d965c3a6d49b423.proposed_method: The proposed approach constructs a heterogeneous graph where nodes represent tasks, queries, and LLMs, and edges encode contextual interaction data such as performance and cost of LLM responses to queries. Initial node embeddings are generated using descriptive text for tasks and LLMs (produced by a generative LLM like GPT-4o and encoded with a moderate-sized pre-trained language model such as BERT), and queries are similarly embedded. Edge features between queries and LLMs are initialized by concatenating observed performance and cost metrics. A heterogeneous graph neural network (GNN) is employed to iteratively aggregate information across node and edge types, learning expressive representations that capture the contextual relationships. The LLM selection task is formulated as an edge prediction problem, where the model predicts the optimal LLM for a given query-task pair by computing edge logits and selecting the LLM node with the highest score. The framework is designed to generalize to new LLMs by generating inductive embeddings from textual descriptions, enabling few-shot adaptation without retraining.
f8d75c913a4811fe9f2030ca8d965c3a6d49b423.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a multi-task interaction dataset constructed from four benchmark tasks: Alpaca (hybrid QA), GSM8K (mathematical reasoning), SQUAD (reading comprehension), and Multi-News (multi-document summarization), each with 600 queries and responses from 10 LLMs of varying sizes and costs. The evaluation will use metrics for performance (task-specific, e.g., F1, accuracy), cost (LLM inference cost), and a composite reward metric balancing performance and cost under three user preference scenarios (performance-first, balanced, cost-first). Baselines for comparison include rule-based (always largest/smallest LLM), prompt-based, and state-of-the-art routers (HybridLLM, FrugalGPT, C2MAB-V), as well as an oracle upper bound. The dataset will be split into training, validation, and test sets, with additional few-shot auxiliary data for new LLM generalization experiments. The GNN will be implemented as a two-layer graph attention network with a 32-dimensional hidden size, trained using Adam optimizer and evaluated on both standard and new LLM settings.
f8d75c913a4811fe9f2030ca8d965c3a6d49b423.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first graph-based inductive framework for LLM selection, fully leveraging contextual information among tasks, queries, and LLMs to enable generalization to new LLMs and tasks without retraining. By reframing LLM selection as an edge prediction task in a heterogeneous graph, the approach captures richer interaction patterns than existing embedding- or index-based routers. The method demonstrates substantial improvements in reward (at least 12.3%) and generalization (at least 9.5% boost in effect and significant reduction in computational demands) over strong baselines, and achieves near-oracle performance while supporting efficient adaptation to new LLMs in few-shot settings.

f90595f99a0c66d2bb6d0f230f17c7cd8c58f44d.title: Qwen-Audio: Advancing Universal Audio Understanding via Unified Large-Scale Audio-Language Models
f90595f99a0c66d2bb6d0f230f17c7cd8c58f44d.research_question: How can a unified large-scale audio-language model be developed to enable universal audio understanding across diverse audio types, languages, and tasks, while overcoming interference issues inherent in multi-task and multi-dataset training?
f90595f99a0c66d2bb6d0f230f17c7cd8c58f44d.hypothesis: A multi-task training framework that conditions the decoder on a sequence of hierarchical tags, combined with large-scale pre-training across diverse audio types and tasks, will enable a single audio-language model to achieve universal audio understanding and outperform existing models without task-specific fine-tuning.
f90595f99a0c66d2bb6d0f230f17c7cd8c58f44d.proposed_method: A unified audio-language model will be constructed by integrating a single audio encoder, initialized from a large pre-trained model (e.g., Whisper-large-v2), with a large language model backbone (e.g., Qwen-7B). The model will be trained on paired audio-text data spanning over 30 tasks, eight languages, and various audio types including speech, natural sounds, and music. To address interference from heterogeneous datasets and tasks, a multi-task training framework will be designed, conditioning the decoder on a sequence of hierarchical tags: transcription tag, audio language tag, task tag, text language tag, timestamps tag, and output instruction. This tag-based conditioning will maximize knowledge sharing among similar tasks while distinguishing different tasks and output formats, thus mitigating one-to-many mapping issues. Additionally, the training will incorporate a speech recognition with word-level timestamps (SRWT) task to improve alignment and grounding capabilities. Supervised instruction fine-tuning will further enable flexible multi-turn audio-text dialogue capabilities.
f90595f99a0c66d2bb6d0f230f17c7cd8c58f44d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a comprehensive suite of 12 benchmark datasets covering tasks such as Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech-to-Text Translation (S2TT), Automatic Audio Captioning (AAC), Acoustic Scene Classification (ASC), Speech Emotion Recognition (SER), Audio Question Answering (AQA), Vocal Sound Classification (VSC), and Music Note Analysis (MNA). Datasets include Aishell1, Aishell2, Librispeech, CoVoST2, Clotho, CochlScene, TUT2017, Meld, ClothoAQA, VocalSound, and NSynth. Evaluation metrics will include Word Error Rate (WER) for ASR, BLEU for translation, CIDEr/SPICE/SPIDEr for captioning, accuracy for classification tasks, and mean average precision (MAP) for music analysis. Baselines will include state-of-the-art models such as SpeechT5, SpeechNet, SpeechLLaMA, SALMONN, Pengi, WavLM, and CLAP. The evaluation will be performed without any task-specific fine-tuning, and training/test splits will be strictly separated to avoid data leakage.
f90595f99a0c66d2bb6d0f230f17c7cd8c58f44d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a universal, large-scale audio-language model capable of handling over 30 tasks, eight languages, and diverse audio types within a single framework. The multi-task training format with hierarchical tag conditioning is claimed to effectively mitigate interference between heterogeneous datasets and tasks, enabling knowledge sharing and avoiding one-to-many mapping problems. Incorporation of the SRWT task is highlighted as a novel addition that enhances grounding and alignment for both speech and non-speech audio tasks. The resulting model is expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of benchmarks without the need for task-specific fine-tuning, and to support flexible, multi-turn audio-text dialogue scenarios.

f9570989919338079088270a9cf1a7afc8db8093.title: DataComp: In search of the next generation of multimodal datasets
f9570989919338079088270a9cf1a7afc8db8093.research_question: How can the design, filtering, and curation of large-scale multimodal (image-text) datasets be systematically benchmarked and improved to enable the development of more effective and generalizable multimodal models?
f9570989919338079088270a9cf1a7afc8db8093.hypothesis: Systematic benchmarking and rigorous filtering or curation of large-scale image-text datasets will yield training sets that enable multimodal models to achieve higher accuracy and generalization on diverse downstream tasks, compared to models trained on unfiltered or less carefully curated data.
f9570989919338079088270a9cf1a7afc8db8093.proposed_method: A new benchmark, DATACOMP, will be established to facilitate controlled, data-centric experimentation on multimodal dataset design. The methodology involves constructing a massive candidate pool (COMMONPOOL) of 12.8 billion image-text pairs from Common Crawl, with extensive safety preprocessing, deduplication, and privacy protection (e.g., NSFW filtering, face blurring). Two experimental tracks are proposed: (1) a filtering track, where participants select or filter subsets from COMMONPOOL using various algorithms and criteria, and (2) a Bring Your Own Data (BYOD) track, where participants curate datasets from any non-overlapping sources. All submitted datasets will be used to train CLIP models from scratch using a fixed architecture and standardized hyperparameters, ensuring comparability. The training follows a contrastive learning objective, maximizing similarity between paired image and text representations.
f9570989919338079088270a9cf1a7afc8db8093.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted at four compute scales (small, medium, large, xlarge), each defined by a fixed number of training samples and corresponding model architectures (e.g., ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, ViT-L/14). Each dataset submission will be evaluated by training a CLIP model using the OpenCLIP codebase and then testing the resulting model on a suite of 38 downstream image classification and retrieval tasks, including ImageNet, ImageNet-V2, DTD, EuroSAT, SUN-397, MSCOCO, and others. Zero-shot evaluation protocols will be used to assess model generalization without further fine-tuning. Baselines will include unfiltered data, random subsets, basic filtering (e.g., language, caption length, image size), CLIP score filtering, text-based filtering, and image-based filtering. Additional experiments will examine the impact of combining external datasets in the BYOD track. Evaluation metrics include zero-shot accuracy on ImageNet, average performance across all tasks, and robustness/fairness analyses.
f9570989919338079088270a9cf1a7afc8db8093.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces the largest public candidate pool for multimodal dataset curation (12.8B image-text pairs) and establishes a standardized, controlled environment for dataset-centric research. By decoupling dataset design from model and training algorithm changes, the benchmark enables rigorous, fair comparison of dataset curation methods. The infrastructure supports multi-scale experimentation, making large-scale data-centric research accessible to a wide range of researchers. The methodology demonstrates that carefully filtered and curated datasets can yield models that outperform those trained on larger, less curated datasets, and provides open-source tools, code, and data for reproducible research in multimodal dataset design.

f9927b2c7ecce6e67d20e6c8a078670765e7885c.title: Graph Neural Network Generalization With Gaussian Mixture Model Based Augmentation
f9927b2c7ecce6e67d20e6c8a078670765e7885c.research_question: How can the generalization and robustness of graph neural networks (GNNs) be improved, particularly in scenarios with limited, diverse, or out-of-distribution graph data, through theoretically informed data augmentation strategies?
f9927b2c7ecce6e67d20e6c8a078670765e7885c.hypothesis: Applying a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM)-based augmentation technique at the level of graph hidden representations will improve the generalization and robustness of GNNs compared to existing graph data augmentation methods, by effectively enriching the training data distribution and controlling generalization error bounds.
f9927b2c7ecce6e67d20e6c8a078670765e7885c.proposed_method: A novel graph data augmentation framework, termed GRATIN, will be developed to enhance GNN generalization. The method first trains a standard GNN on the original graph classification task to obtain hidden graph representations via the READOUT function. These representations are then partitioned by class, and for each class, a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) is fitted using the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm to approximate the empirical distribution of graph embeddings. New synthetic graph representations are generated by sampling from the fitted GMMs, inheriting class labels accordingly. The post-readout neural network (typically a linear layer and Softmax) is then fine-tuned using both the original and augmented representations. Theoretical analysis using Rademacher complexity and influence functions will guide the augmentation and filtering process, ensuring that only augmentations with positive influence on generalization are retained.
f9927b2c7ecce6e67d20e6c8a078670765e7885c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on widely used graph classification benchmarks such as IMDB-BIN, IMDB-MUL, MUTAG, PROTEINS, and DD. Both GCN and GIN backbones will be evaluated. Baseline augmentation methods for comparison will include DropEdge, DropNode, SubMix, G-Mixup, and GeoMix. Evaluation metrics will primarily be classification accuracy and robustness to structural corruption (e.g., random edge removal/addition at 10% and 20% noise budgets). The experimental setup will ensure consistent train/validation/test splits, architectures, and hyperparameters across methods. Influence function analysis will be used to filter augmented samples, and time complexity of augmentation and training will be measured and compared.
f9927b2c7ecce6e67d20e6c8a078670765e7885c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a theoretically grounded framework for graph data augmentation based on Rademacher complexity and influence functions, providing new insights into the mechanisms by which augmentation improves GNN generalization. GRATIN leverages GMMs as universal approximators for efficient and scalable augmentation at the hidden representation level, rather than directly on graph structures. The method offers improved computational efficiency and robustness, and incorporates influence-function-based filtering to select augmentations that positively impact generalization. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior or highly competitive performance and robustness compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

f9a4ed62ea6da274c1c81748b2bca240655b7c29.title: Transformers as Support Vector Machines
f9a4ed62ea6da274c1c81748b2bca240655b7c29.research_question: Can the optimization landscape and implicit bias of transformer attention layers be rigorously characterized, and how do these properties relate to classical max-margin learning frameworks such as support vector machines (SVMs)? What are the conditions under which gradient descent on transformer attention parameters converges to globally or locally optimal solutions, and how does over-parameterization affect these dynamics?
f9a4ed62ea6da274c1c81748b2bca240655b7c29.hypothesis: The optimization of transformer attention layers via gradient descent exhibits an implicit max-margin bias analogous to SVMs, with the specific nature of the bias (e.g., Frobenius norm vs. nuclear norm) depending on the parameterization (direct W vs. factored K, Q). Over-parameterization facilitates global convergence to max-margin solutions, and the equivalence can be extended to nonlinear prediction heads.
f9a4ed62ea6da274c1c81748b2bca240655b7c29.proposed_method: A formal equivalence will be established between the optimization geometry of transformer self-attention layers and hard-margin SVM problems that separate optimal input tokens from non-optimal tokens using linear constraints on token pair outer products. The study will analyze both direct parameterization of attention weights (W) and factored parameterization (K, Q), characterizing their respective implicit biases via Frobenius and nuclear norm objectives. Gradient descent dynamics will be investigated theoretically and empirically, focusing on convergence to globally or locally optimal SVM solutions under varying initialization and over-parameterization regimes. The approach will be extended to attention layers with nonlinear prediction heads, proposing a generalized SVM equivalence that predicts implicit bias in broader settings.
f9a4ed62ea6da274c1c81748b2bca240655b7c29.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and general datasets, where input sequences and token embeddings are randomly generated or sampled from specified distributions. Both self-attention and cross-attention settings will be evaluated. Baselines will include different parameterizations (W vs. K, Q), and the effect of over-parameterization (varying embedding dimension d, number of tokens T, and number of sequences n) will be systematically studied. Evaluation metrics will include convergence type (global, local, not local), alignment with SVM solutions (measured by correlation coefficients and softmax probabilities), and rank properties of learned attention matrices. Extensive numerical experiments will validate theoretical predictions regarding convergence, implicit bias, and the effect of nonlinear heads.
f9a4ed62ea6da274c1c81748b2bca240655b7c29.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first formal and comprehensive equivalence between transformer attention optimization and hard-margin SVMs, distinguishing the implicit bias of different parameterizations (Frobenius vs. nuclear norm). It provides new theoretical guarantees for global and local convergence of gradient descent in attention layers, identifies geometric and over-parameterization conditions that ensure benign optimization landscapes, and extends the SVM equivalence to nonlinear prediction heads. The findings offer a new perspective on transformers as hierarchical max-margin token selection mechanisms and lay the groundwork for future studies on their optimization and generalization dynamics.

f9b39a6a7e40986b46f7796f3a805d70d7e3931a.title: SeeClick: Harnessing GUI Grounding for Advanced Visual GUI Agents
f9b39a6a7e40986b46f7796f3a805d70d7e3931a.research_question: How can visual GUI agents be developed to automate complex tasks on diverse digital platforms using only interface screenshots, and what techniques can improve their ability to accurately locate and interact with GUI elements based on natural language instructions?
f9b39a6a7e40986b46f7796f3a805d70d7e3931a.hypothesis: Enhancing large vision-language models (LVLMs) with GUI grounding pre-training and curated GUI grounding data will significantly improve the accuracy and generalization of visual GUI agents in locating actionable elements from screenshots, leading to superior performance in downstream GUI automation tasks across mobile, desktop, and web environments.
f9b39a6a7e40986b46f7796f3a805d70d7e3931a.proposed_method: A novel visual GUI agent, SeeClick, will be developed to perform low-level actions such as clicking and typing by interpreting screenshots of user interfaces in response to natural language instructions. The approach will enhance an existing LVLM (e.g., Qwen-VL) with a GUI grounding pre-training strategy, enabling the model to predict the location of actionable elements (text, widgets, icons) directly from screenshots and instructions. Data for pre-training will be curated automatically from web and mobile sources, including element descriptions and their coordinates, as well as tasks like web OCR and widget captioning. The model will be trained using a mixture of web UI data, reorganized mobile UI datasets, and general vision-language instruction-following data, with prompts crafted for each GUI task. Fine-tuning will be performed using LoRA to adapt both the vision encoder and language model components.
f9b39a6a7e40986b46f7796f3a805d70d7e3931a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the newly created ScreenSpot benchmark, which contains over 600 screenshots and 1200+ instructions spanning iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, and web platforms, with a focus on both text and icon/widget elements. The evaluation will compare SeeClick to generalist LVLMs (e.g., MiniGPT-v2, Qwen-VL, GPT-4V) and GUI-specific models (e.g., CogAgent, Fuyu) using click accuracy as the main metric, defined by whether the predicted location falls within the ground-truth bounding box. Additional experiments will adapt SeeClick to downstream agent tasks, including MiniWob (web automation), AITW (Android automation), and Mind2Web (real-world web navigation), using their respective training/test splits and reporting metrics such as success rate, operation F1, and step success rate. Baselines will include both text-based and vision-based models, and ablation studies will analyze the impact of GUI grounding pre-training.
f9b39a6a7e40986b46f7796f3a805d70d7e3931a.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first universal visual GUI agent that relies solely on screenshots for task automation across diverse platforms, eliminating the need for structured metadata. A new GUI grounding pre-training strategy is devised to enhance LVLMs' ability to localize actionable elements in complex GUI contexts. The work also presents ScreenSpot, the first realistic and comprehensive GUI grounding benchmark covering mobile, desktop, and web environments with a variety of element types. The approach demonstrates that improvements in GUI grounding directly correlate with enhanced performance in downstream GUI agent tasks, and achieves state-of-the-art results among vision-based agents with substantially less training data.

f9bcec8ae8d511163a13429a0916acd8bd72a69f.title: Offline RL by Reward-Weighted Fine-Tuning for Conversation Optimization
f9bcec8ae8d511163a13429a0916acd8bd72a69f.research_question: How can offline reinforcement learning be effectively applied to optimize multi-turn conversational policies in large language models, particularly for question answering and clarifying question tasks, using only previously collected datasets of trajectories and rewards?
f9bcec8ae8d511163a13429a0916acd8bd72a69f.hypothesis: Reward-weighted fine-tuning and its standardized variant will enable more stable and effective offline reinforcement learning for conversational optimization in large language models, leading to improved reward maximization and language quality compared to existing supervised fine-tuning and direct preference optimization baselines.
f9bcec8ae8d511163a13429a0916acd8bd72a69f.proposed_method: A novel offline reinforcement learning framework is developed that recasts policy optimization as reward-weighted fine-tuning, allowing the use of standard supervised fine-tuning (SFT) primitives with minimal modification. The key algorithm, Refit, maximizes a lower bound on the expected reward by weighting the log-probabilities of actions in logged trajectories according to their trajectory-level rewards, thus directly optimizing for reward without requiring token-level propensity score ratios. An extension, Swift, further standardizes trajectory rewards within each context to reduce variance in policy optimization, using the mean and standard deviation of rewards over multiple sampled trajectories. Both methods are implemented as iterative gradient ascent procedures over a dataset of logged conversations, and can be efficiently realized by modifying the weighting of examples in SFT pipelines.
f9bcec8ae8d511163a13429a0916acd8bd72a69f.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on six diverse datasets, including OpenBookQA, ARC, SciQA, MMLU, CoSQL, and MathDial, covering open-domain, scientific, text-to-SQL, and mathematical dialogue tasks. For each dataset, 500 multi-turn conversational tasks are generated, with both reasoning and clarifying-question modes evaluated. The agent is instantiated as Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, with conversations simulated using varying temperatures. Baselines include two variants of supervised fine-tuning (SFT), two variants of direct preference optimization (DPO), and the original policy. Evaluation metrics include accuracy, reasoning ability, pedagogical value, comprehensiveness, confidence calibration, and overall reward, with conversation quality judged by GPT-4o and Claude 4 Opus. Ablation studies vary conversation length and dataset size to assess robustness.
f9bcec8ae8d511163a13429a0916acd8bd72a69f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a generic offline RL objective for conversation optimization that does not require token-level propensity score ratios, leading to greater stability and practicality in large language models. The reward-weighted fine-tuning framework is directly compatible with standard SFT infrastructure, requiring only minor modifications. The standardized reward variant further reduces variance and improves statistical efficiency. Empirical results demonstrate substantial gains in both reward optimization and language quality over state-of-the-art SFT and DPO baselines, with improvements observed across multiple datasets and evaluation metrics.

f9c3e82436f284d59d9d37d84f9021b76b0c5a56.title: A Hitchhiker's Guide to Scaling Law Estimation
f9c3e82436f284d59d9d37d84f9021b76b0c5a56.research_question: How can scaling laws for language models be estimated most reliably and efficiently, given limited computational resources and data availability, across diverse model architectures and training regimes?
f9c3e82436f284d59d9d37d84f9021b76b0c5a56.hypothesis: Scaling law estimation can be significantly improved by leveraging intermediate checkpoints from training runs, using multiple small models rather than a few large ones, and by pooling information across similar model families. Furthermore, the functional form of scaling laws may be simpler than previously assumed, with fewer degrees of freedom.
f9c3e82436f284d59d9d37d84f9021b76b0c5a56.proposed_method: A comprehensive meta-analysis will be conducted using a large-scale, publicly released dataset aggregating training losses and downstream evaluations from 485 pretrained language models spanning over 40 model families. The methodology will involve fitting parametric scaling laws to subsets of models differing in size, number of training tokens, and training checkpoints, using nonlinear regression (e.g., curve_fit in scikit-learn) to minimize squared error between predicted and empirical losses. The approach will systematically evaluate the impact of using intermediate checkpoints versus final losses, the number and size of models included in the estimation, and the transferability of scaling law parameters across model families. Principal component analysis will be applied to the learned scaling law parameters to investigate potential redundancy and propose simplified functional forms.
f9c3e82436f284d59d9d37d84f9021b76b0c5a56.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize the compiled dataset, which includes 1.9 million training steps and loss/perplexity evaluations for models such as Pythia, OPT, OLMO, Amber, K2, Mamba, RedPajama, ModuleFormer, Llama, Bloom, T5-Pile, and others. Scaling laws will be fit to various subsets of each model family, controlling for number of models, model sizes, and training data fractions. Baseline comparisons will include naive extrapolation from the best-performing small model and from the most-trained model in each family. Evaluation metrics will focus on absolute relative error (ARE) between predicted and actual losses, with additional analysis of variance due to random seeds and the effect of discarding early training checkpoints. The robustness of scaling law predictions will be tested both within and across model families.
f9c3e82436f284d59d9d37d84f9021b76b0c5a56.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first large-scale, systematic study of scaling law estimation across diverse language model families, leveraging a uniquely comprehensive dataset of training trajectories and downstream evaluations. Key innovations include the demonstration that intermediate checkpoints substantially improve scaling law accuracy, the finding that training multiple small models can outperform a single large model for estimation, and the identification of potential simplifications in the functional form of scaling laws. The work also provides actionable guidelines for practitioners on cost-effective experimental design for scaling law estimation.

f9da7cfe8d403f66ab844b08577deeff6d1b1170.title: AgentSquare: Automatic LLM Agent Search in Modular Design Space
f9da7cfe8d403f66ab844b08577deeff6d1b1170.research_question: How can the design and optimization of large language model (LLM) agents be automated in a modular design space to improve adaptability and performance across diverse tasks, while leveraging prior successful agentic modules?
f9da7cfe8d403f66ab844b08577deeff6d1b1170.hypothesis: A modular design space for LLM agents, combined with automated search mechanisms for module evolution and recombination, will enable the discovery of novel agent architectures that outperform manually designed agents and existing search methods across a variety of complex tasks.
f9da7cfe8d403f66ab844b08577deeff6d1b1170.proposed_method: A modular design space will be constructed, abstracting LLM agent architectures into four standardized modules: Planning, Reasoning, Tool Use, and Memory, each with uniform input-output interfaces. The proposed AgentSquare framework will perform automatic agent search within this space using two core mechanisms: module evolution and module recombination. Module evolution employs an evolutionary meta-prompt to generate new module variants through program-level optimization, informed by task descriptions and historical performance data. Module recombination leverages LLMs to strategically propose and assemble promising combinations of existing modules based on accumulated experience. To reduce computational costs, a performance predictor—a surrogate LLM model—will be introduced to efficiently estimate the performance of candidate agents, allowing for the rapid exclusion of unpromising designs and acceleration of the search process.
f9da7cfe8d403f66ab844b08577deeff6d1b1170.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six representative benchmarks spanning web, embodied, tool-use, and game domains, including tasks such as Webshop, ALFWorld, SciWorld, M3Tool, TravelPlanner, and PDDL. The evaluation will compare the best agents discovered by AgentSquare against hand-crafted agents, module-level search (e.g., Bayesian search), prompt-level search (e.g., OPRO), and agent-level search (e.g., ADAS). Both GPT-3.5-turbo-0125 and GPT-4o will be used as the underlying LLMs. Metrics will include task-specific success or accuracy rates and API cost efficiency. The search process will be initialized with a diverse pool of well-designed seed agents, and experiments will be run for a fixed number of iterations or until convergence, ensuring fair comparison by maintaining equal search budgets across methods.
f9da7cfe8d403f66ab844b08577deeff6d1b1170.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a standardized, extensible modular design space for LLM agents, enabling systematic reuse and recombination of successful agentic modules from prior work. The AgentSquare framework pioneers the integration of both module evolution (for generating new module variants) and module recombination (for assembling novel agent architectures) within this modular space. The inclusion of a performance predictor as an in-context surrogate model for agent evaluation significantly reduces search costs and enables scalable optimization. The approach claims to generate interpretable design insights, facilitate community-driven agent development, and achieve superior performance and efficiency compared to existing hand-crafted and automated agent design methods.

fa018aa098c28bd694b316ddf7e213641e7f86ad.title: Aligning LLM Agents by Learning Latent Preference from User Edits
fa018aa098c28bd694b316ddf7e213641e7f86ad.research_question: How can large language model (LLM) agents be interactively aligned to individual users' latent preferences using naturally occurring user edits, without incurring the cost and risks of model fine-tuning?
fa018aa098c28bd694b316ddf7e213641e7f86ad.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that user edits to LLM-generated outputs encode latent, context-dependent user preferences, and that learning to infer and utilize these preferences from edit histories can significantly reduce user editing effort and improve agent alignment, while maintaining computational efficiency and interpretability.
fa018aa098c28bd694b316ddf7e213641e7f86ad.proposed_method: A learning framework, PRELUDE, will be developed to infer descriptive, context-dependent user preferences from historical user edits. The core algorithm, CIPHER, will represent each context using a vector embedding (e.g., via MPNET or BERT), and maintain a history of inferred preferences paired with their context representations. For each new context, the k most similar past contexts will be retrieved using cosine similarity, and their associated preferences will be aggregated (using the LLM) to form a prompt for response generation. If the user subsequently makes significant edits (as measured by token-level Levenshtein distance), the LLM will be queried to induce a new preference that explains the edits, and this will be added to the history. The agent will use these inferred preferences as prompt augmentations, avoiding any model fine-tuning.
fa018aa098c28bd694b316ddf7e213641e7f86ad.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in two interactive environments: document summarization and email writing, using documents from diverse sources such as news articles, Reddit posts, Wikipedia pages, and scientific abstracts. A simulated user based on GPT-4 will generate edits according to predefined, context-dependent latent preferences. Baselines will include agents with no learning, context-agnostic preference learning, in-context learning with edit retrieval, and chain-of-thought preference inference. Evaluation metrics will include cumulative user edit cost (token-level Levenshtein distance), preference classification accuracy (using BERTScore to compare inferred and ground-truth preferences), and total LLM token expense. Human evaluations will further assess output quality and edit effort.
fa018aa098c28bd694b316ddf7e213641e7f86ad.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable, interpretable, and efficient framework for aligning LLM agents to user preferences using only naturally occurring user edits, without any model fine-tuning. The CIPHER algorithm leverages retrieval and aggregation of inferred preferences, enabling context-dependent adaptation and interpretability. This method reduces user editing effort, achieves higher alignment accuracy, and incurs lower computational costs compared to existing baselines. The approach also provides interpretable preference descriptions that can be viewed and modified by users, enhancing transparency and user control.

fa0c7c850b6298fa49518e42e9f9e492dd4c5541.title: MVSplat: Efficient 3D Gaussian Splatting from Sparse Multi-View Images
fa0c7c850b6298fa49518e42e9f9e492dd4c5541.research_question: How can efficient and high-quality 3D scene reconstruction and novel view synthesis be achieved from sparse multi-view images using a feed-forward approach?
fa0c7c850b6298fa49518e42e9f9e492dd4c5541.hypothesis: Incorporating a cost volume representation based on multi-view feature matching into a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework will enable more accurate geometry estimation, resulting in improved appearance and geometry quality, faster inference, and better generalization compared to existing methods.
fa0c7c850b6298fa49518e42e9f9e492dd4c5541.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a feed-forward model, MVSplat, that reconstructs 3D scenes from sparse multi-view images by predicting 3D Gaussian primitives. Multi-view image features are first extracted using a combination of a shallow CNN and a multi-view Transformer with self- and cross-attention layers to encode cross-view information. For each input view, a cost volume is constructed via plane sweeping, where features from other views are warped and correlated at multiple depth candidates, capturing feature matching information crucial for geometry estimation. These cost volumes are refined using a 2D U-Net with cross-view attention to handle ambiguities and texture-less regions, followed by softmax-based depth estimation and an additional lightweight U-Net for depth refinement. The resulting depth maps are unprojected to 3D space to define Gaussian centers, while other Gaussian parameters (opacity, covariance, color) are predicted in parallel from the matching confidence and feature representations. The entire model is trained end-to-end using only photometric loss between rendered and ground truth images, enabling efficient and scalable learning.
fa0c7c850b6298fa49518e42e9f9e492dd4c5541.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the large-scale RealEstate10K and ACID datasets, both providing diverse real-world scenes with estimated camera parameters. The model will be evaluated by taking two input views per scene and rendering three novel views, with performance assessed using standard image quality metrics: PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS. Inference time and model parameter count will be reported to compare efficiency. Baselines will include state-of-the-art feed-forward NeRF-based models (pixelNeRF, MuRF), Light Field Network-based methods (GPNR, AttnRend), and the latest 3D Gaussian Splatting model (pixelSplat). Additional cross-dataset generalization tests will be performed on the DTU dataset. All experiments will use 256x256 image resolution, and models will be trained for 300,000 iterations with the Adam optimizer on a single A100 GPU.
fa0c7c850b6298fa49518e42e9f9e492dd4c5541.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a cost volume-based feature matching mechanism for feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting, enabling accurate geometry estimation from sparse views without requiring ground truth depth supervision. The method achieves state-of-the-art visual quality and geometry reconstruction with significantly fewer parameters and faster inference than prior methods, particularly surpassing pixelSplat by using 10× fewer parameters and more than 2× faster inference. The model is fully differentiable, scalable to in-the-wild scenarios, and demonstrates superior cross-dataset generalization. The design leverages efficient 2D convolutions and attention mechanisms, avoiding computationally expensive 3D convolutions or per-scene optimization.

fa29841d8e97b84414588806483221fd885e0c2a.title: Classifier Clustering and Feature Alignment for Federated Learning under Distributed Concept Drift
fa29841d8e97b84414588806483221fd885e0c2a.research_question: How can federated learning systems effectively adapt to distributed concept drift and data heterogeneity, particularly when the conditional distribution P(Y|X) varies across clients and over time?
fa29841d8e97b84414588806483221fd885e0c2a.hypothesis: A federated learning framework that integrates class-level classifier clustering and adaptive feature alignment based on clustered feature anchors can significantly improve generalization and adaptability under distributed concept drift and data heterogeneity compared to existing single-model, personalized, and clustered federated learning methods.
fa29841d8e97b84414588806483221fd885e0c2a.proposed_method: The proposed approach, termed FedCCFA, decouples the federated model into a shared feature extractor and client-specific classifiers. Initially, each client trains a balanced classifier using a small, class-balanced batch to mitigate class imbalance and initialization variance, and these balanced classifiers are used for class-level clustering via DBSCAN based on cosine similarity of classifier weights. For each class, clients with similar conditional distributions are grouped, and their class-specific classifiers are aggregated within clusters. To address feature space inconsistency, the method computes clustered feature anchors by averaging local feature centroids within each cluster, and clients align their feature spaces to these anchors using a contrastive-guided loss. The alignment weight is adaptively scaled according to the entropy of the client’s label distribution, reducing the impact of severe data heterogeneity on main task learning.
fa29841d8e97b84414588806483221fd885e0c2a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three image classification datasets: Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CINIC-10, using convolutional neural network models tailored to each dataset. The federated setting involves both 20-client full participation and 100-client partial participation scenarios, with non-IID data partitioned via Dirichlet distribution (varying α for heterogeneity). Distributed concept drift is simulated by label-swapping schemes across clients and over time, including sudden, incremental, and reoccurring drift patterns. The proposed method will be compared against single-model (FedAvg, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, FedFM, AdapFedAvg, Flash), personalized (pFedMe, Ditto, FedRep, FedBABU, FedPAC), and clustered (IFCA, FedDrift) baselines. Evaluation metrics include average test accuracy across clients, with additional ablation studies on classifier clustering inputs, feature alignment strategies, and adaptive alignment weights. Hyperparameters such as learning rates, batch sizes, and clustering thresholds will be tuned as per standard practice, and experiments will be repeated for statistical robustness.
fa29841d8e97b84414588806483221fd885e0c2a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a novel class-level classifier clustering mechanism for federated learning under distributed concept drift, enabling fine-grained collaboration among clients with similar conditional distributions. It further innovates by employing clustered feature anchors for feature alignment, which are robust to both concept drift and data heterogeneity. The adaptive alignment weight, determined by the entropy of the label distribution, allows dynamic balancing between main task learning and feature alignment, particularly under severe heterogeneity. These contributions collectively enable more effective adaptation and generalization in federated learning environments where both data heterogeneity and distributed concept drift are present.

fa2d16678b65017f8883cc73c0c1b085bad8b57e.title: Language-guided Skill Learning with Temporal Variational Inference
fa2d16678b65017f8883cc73c0c1b085bad8b57e.research_question: How can reusable and semantically meaningful skills be autonomously discovered from expert demonstrations to accelerate learning and improve generalization in long-horizon reinforcement learning tasks, particularly in complex, multimodal environments?
fa2d16678b65017f8883cc73c0c1b085bad8b57e.hypothesis: Incorporating language-guided initial segmentation from large language models, followed by a hierarchical temporal variational inference framework augmented with a minimum description length objective, will enable the discovery of reusable skills that improve learning efficiency and generalization to new tasks compared to existing skill discovery methods.
fa2d16678b65017f8883cc73c0c1b085bad8b57e.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that begins by using a large language model (LLM) to generate an initial segmentation of expert demonstration trajectories, producing short, semantically annotated sub-sequences. These initial segments are then refined through a hierarchical temporal variational inference process, which merges sub-sequences into longer, reusable skills by modeling the joint distribution over skill assignments and skill-switching variables. The inference process is guided by an auxiliary objective based on the Minimum Description Length (MDL) principle, which encourages compression by minimizing the number of skills needed to reconstruct the demonstrations while preserving reusability. The model architecture employs multi-modal transformers to encode observations, actions, and language annotations, and learns both low-level skill-conditioned policies and high-level policies over skills. The final skill library is pruned to retain only frequently used skills, and online hierarchical reinforcement learning is performed using the discovered skills as temporally extended actions.
fa2d16678b65017f8883cc73c0c1b085bad8b57e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in two challenging domains: BabyAI, a gridworld navigation environment with symbolic state and action spaces, and ALFRED, a photorealistic household simulation environment with high-dimensional visual observations and diverse action/object spaces. The method will be trained on a small subset of expert demonstrations sampled from multiple tasks, using GPT-4 for initial segmentation and pretrained encoders for multimodal inputs. Baselines for comparison will include Behavior Cloning (BC), LOVE (a state-of-the-art skill discovery method without language), LISA (a language-based skill learning method), and other relevant approaches, all implemented with comparable neural architectures. Evaluation metrics will include zero-shot task success rates on new tasks, downstream learning efficiency (success rate vs. training steps), and qualitative analysis of the semantic coherence and reusability of the discovered skills. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each component, including the initial segmentation, language annotations, and the MDL objective.
fa2d16678b65017f8883cc73c0c1b085bad8b57e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new framework that leverages LLM-generated initial segmentation to drastically reduce the search space for skill discovery, integrates language supervision into temporal variational inference for skill merging, and augments the process with a novel MDL-based auxiliary objective for optimal compression and reusability. Unlike prior methods, the framework does not restrict skill representations to language alone, nor does it require pre-specified skill sets or domain models. The approach is designed to autonomously discover transferable, semantically meaningful skills from unparsed demonstrations, enabling efficient hierarchical reinforcement learning in complex, long-horizon, multimodal environments.

fa4da39036c5e33157d19ed2def5e2ee41be8ec3.title: Incorporating Arbitrary Matrix Group Equivariance into KANs
fa4da39036c5e33157d19ed2def5e2ee41be8ec3.research_question: How can arbitrary matrix group equivariance be incorporated into Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) to improve their performance and generalization on tasks with known symmetries across scientific and non-scientific domains?
fa4da39036c5e33157d19ed2def5e2ee41be8ec3.hypothesis: Embedding arbitrary matrix group equivariance into KANs will enable these networks to better respect task-specific symmetries, leading to improved accuracy and generalization, particularly on tasks where symmetry is crucial, and will outperform both standard KANs and existing equivariant neural architectures, especially with smaller datasets or fewer parameters.
fa4da39036c5e33157d19ed2def5e2ee41be8ec3.proposed_method: A new architecture, Equivariant Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (EKAN), will be developed to incorporate arbitrary matrix group equivariance into KANs. The method will construct gated spline basis functions for each layer, combining them with equivariant linear weights to form the EKAN layer. A lift layer will be introduced at the network input to align the input space with the dataset's feature space, ensuring the correct group action is embedded from the outset. The architecture will define and enforce equivariance constraints by solving for the appropriate linear weights using group representation theory, ensuring that both the non-linear spline activations and the linear transformations respect the specified symmetry group. The final network will consist of stacked EKAN layers, with gating mechanisms applied to both input and output spaces to facilitate equivariant non-linearities.
fa4da39036c5e33157d19ed2def5e2ee41be8ec3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on tasks with known matrix group symmetries, including particle scattering (O(1,3) Lorentz invariance), the three-body problem (O(2) rotational/reflectional equivariance), and top quark tagging (O(1,3) invariance with partial observation). Synthetic and real-world datasets will be used, with training set sizes and model parameter counts systematically varied to evaluate sample efficiency and scalability. Baseline comparisons will include Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs), standard KANs, data-augmented versions of both, and state-of-the-art equivariant neural architectures such as EMLP and CGENN. Evaluation metrics will include test mean squared error (MSE) for regression tasks and test accuracy for classification, with additional analysis of equivariant error and parameter efficiency. All experiments will be repeated with multiple random seeds to ensure statistical robustness.
fa4da39036c5e33157d19ed2def5e2ee41be8ec3.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first general framework for embedding arbitrary matrix group equivariance into Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, unifying the strengths of KANs' learnable spline activations with the principled handling of symmetry via group representations. The method is the first to combine equivariant gating mechanisms with spline-based architectures, enabling KANs to be applied to a broader range of symmetry-aware tasks. The approach theoretically guarantees equivariance at both the non-linear and linear stages of each layer, and demonstrates significant empirical improvements over both standard KANs and existing equivariant neural networks, especially in terms of accuracy with limited data and parameter efficiency.

fa5b841a69a1262aaf4ca346989368526c90f2bd.title: ElasticDiffusion: Training-Free Arbitrary Size Image Generation Through Global-Local Content Separation
fa5b841a69a1262aaf4ca346989368526c90f2bd.research_question: How can pretrained text-to-image diffusion models be adapted to generate high-quality images at arbitrary sizes and aspect ratios during inference, without additional training or increased memory requirements?
fa5b841a69a1262aaf4ca346989368526c90f2bd.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that separating global and local content signals during the diffusion process enables pretrained diffusion models, originally limited to a fixed training resolution, to generate coherent and high-quality images at arbitrary resolutions and aspect ratios without retraining or increasing memory usage.
fa5b841a69a1262aaf4ca346989368526c90f2bd.proposed_method: A novel decoding framework is introduced that decouples the generation of global and local content within a pretrained diffusion model. The local signal, responsible for fine-grained pixel details, is estimated on local patches using an efficient patch fusion strategy that incorporates contextual information from adjacent patches, thereby avoiding boundary discontinuities and reducing computational overhead. The global signal, which maintains overall image structure and semantic coherence, is estimated by downsampling the current latent to the model's training resolution, computing the class-direction score, and upsampling it to the target resolution. An iterative resampling technique is applied to refine the global signal, enhancing detail and coherence. The method further integrates a Reduced-Resolution Guidance (RRG) mechanism, which aligns the generated latent with a downsampled reference at each diffusion step to minimize artifacts, using a scheduled guidance weight. The entire process operates at a constant memory footprint and does not require any fine-tuning or retraining of the base diffusion model.
fa5b841a69a1262aaf4ca346989368526c90f2bd.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the CelebA-HQ (faces) and LAION-COCO (objects, indoor, outdoor scenes) datasets, evaluating image generation at multiple resolutions and aspect ratios. The method is compared against baselines including Stable Diffusion (SD), MultiDiffusion (MD), and Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL), with all models using consistent seeds, captions, and DDIM sampling with 50 steps. Evaluation metrics include Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for realism and diversity, and CLIP-score for prompt-image alignment, computed on 10,000 generated images per setting. The number of diffusion model calls and memory usage are also reported to assess computational efficiency. Ablation studies are performed to evaluate the contributions of patch fusion, resampling, and RRG components.
fa5b841a69a1262aaf4ca346989368526c90f2bd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables training-free, arbitrary-size image generation from pretrained diffusion models with a constant memory footprint. Key innovations include the explicit separation and independent estimation of global and local content signals, an efficient patch fusion strategy for local detail synthesis, a novel iterative resampling technique for refining global guidance, and the introduction of Reduced-Resolution Guidance to suppress artifacts. The method achieves superior or comparable image quality and semantic alignment to state-of-the-art baselines across a wide range of resolutions and aspect ratios, without requiring additional training or increased computational resources.

fa61bfc90e60f5bf05f9c9374279898808de348a.title: Composition of Differential Privacy & Privacy Amplification by Subsampling
fa61bfc90e60f5bf05f9c9374279898808de348a.research_question: How can the composition properties of differential privacy and privacy amplification by subsampling be formally characterized and leveraged to design complex, multi-stage privacy-preserving data analysis systems with quantifiable privacy guarantees?
fa61bfc90e60f5bf05f9c9374279898808de348a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that advanced composition theorems and privacy amplification techniques, particularly those based on privacy loss distributions and subsampling, can provide tighter, more practical privacy guarantees than basic composition, enabling better privacy-utility tradeoffs in real-world systems.
fa61bfc90e60f5bf05f9c9374279898808de348a.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework will be developed to analyze and improve the composition properties of differential privacy. The approach will begin with formal proofs of basic and advanced composition theorems for both pure and approximate differential privacy, utilizing privacy loss distributions as a central analytical tool. The method will extend to the study of concentrated and Rényi differential privacy, providing explicit characterizations of privacy loss under Gaussian and Laplace mechanisms. Privacy amplification by subsampling will be rigorously analyzed, including Poisson and uniform subsampling, with analytic bounds derived for privacy parameters. The framework will also address adaptive composition and postprocessing, ensuring the results are applicable to practical, iterative data analysis workflows.
fa61bfc90e60f5bf05f9c9374279898808de348a.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be validated through simulation experiments using synthetic datasets where privacy mechanisms (Laplace, Gaussian, and subsampling-based) are applied to queries of varying sensitivity and composition depth. Empirical privacy loss distributions will be measured and compared to theoretical bounds under different composition and subsampling strategies. Baselines will include basic composition, advanced composition, and privacy amplification bounds from existing literature. Evaluation metrics will focus on empirical privacy loss, probability of privacy breach (δ), and utility loss (e.g., mean squared error of released statistics). Experimental setups will vary the number of compositions, privacy parameters (ε, δ), and subsampling rates to assess the tightness and practical impact of the proposed theoretical results.
fa61bfc90e60f5bf05f9c9374279898808de348a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified and rigorous analysis of differential privacy composition and privacy amplification by subsampling, leveraging privacy loss distributions as a foundational tool. Novel contributions include optimality proofs for basic composition, new analytic bounds for privacy amplification under Poisson subsampling in the Rényi differential privacy framework, and practical guidelines for privacy accounting in complex systems. The approach bridges gaps between pure, approximate, and concentrated differential privacy, providing actionable insights for system designers to achieve better privacy-utility tradeoffs in multi-stage, real-world data analysis pipelines.

fa65e367e9f56268b0a9aa500a18f042559d6d8a.title: PAC-Bayesian Generalization Bounds for Adversarial Generative Models
fa65e367e9f56268b0a9aa500a18f042559d6d8a.research_question: How can PAC-Bayesian theory be extended to provide generalization guarantees for adversarial generative models, particularly those based on the Wasserstein and total variation distances, and what are the implications for the statistical reliability of such models in practical settings?
fa65e367e9f56268b0a9aa500a18f042559d6d8a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that PAC-Bayesian generalization bounds can be derived for adversarial generative models, such as Wasserstein GANs and Energy-Based GANs, without requiring restrictive assumptions on the data distribution or the complexity of the critic family, and that these bounds can yield non-vacuous risk certificates and new training objectives that improve statistical guarantees.
fa65e367e9f56268b0a9aa500a18f042559d6d8a.proposed_method: A novel extension of PAC-Bayesian theory will be developed to derive generalization bounds for adversarial generative models, focusing on metrics such as the Wasserstein distance and total variation distance. The approach will formulate the generalization error as the discrepancy between empirical and population risks, leveraging the integral probability metric (IPM) framework to encompass Wasserstein and total variation distances. The methodology will include the derivation of bounds that depend on either the diameter of the instance space or the intrinsic dimension of the data manifold, using pushforward measures to model generative processes. The bounds will be constructed to apply systematically to any critic family, including neural networks, and will be adaptable to both aggregate and individual generators, with technical innovations allowing for risk certificates that do not require density or smoothness assumptions on the data distribution.
fa65e367e9f56268b0a9aa500a18f042559d6d8a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic datasets will include mixtures of Gaussians arranged in ring and grid structures, with the instance space bounded to ensure theoretical assumptions hold. The proposed PAC-Bayesian training objectives will be optimized using probabilistic neural networks with Gaussian priors and posteriors, and the empirical and population risks will be estimated by averaging over multiple sampled generators. Baselines will include standard Wasserstein GANs and Energy-Based GANs trained with conventional objectives. Evaluation metrics will comprise the negative critic loss, risk certificates derived from the proposed bounds, and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for real-world datasets such as MNIST. Additional experimental setup details include the use of orthonormalization techniques to enforce Lipschitz continuity in the critic and hyperparameter sweeps to study the impact of prior variance on generalization.
fa65e367e9f56268b0a9aa500a18f042559d6d8a.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first PAC-Bayesian generalization bounds specifically tailored for adversarial generative models, including Wasserstein GANs and Energy-Based GANs. The bounds are novel in that they do not require assumptions on the complexity or smoothness of the critic family, nor on the density of the data distribution, and they provide new training objectives that can be directly optimized to yield statistical risk certificates. The methodology further innovates by enabling bounds that depend on the intrinsic dimension of the data manifold, rather than the ambient dimension, and by offering a framework that is broadly applicable to neural network-based generative models. Numerical experiments are designed to demonstrate the practicality and non-vacuity of the proposed risk certificates.

fa7bbb1ca4b39f732fdc7cf3d0a45878fb07eaf4.title: OccAM's Laser: Occlusion-based Attribution Maps for 3D Object Detectors on LiDAR Data
fa7bbb1ca4b39f732fdc7cf3d0a45878fb07eaf4.research_question: How can the decision-making process of 3D object detectors operating on LiDAR point cloud data be made more interpretable and explainable, especially in black-box settings where model internals are inaccessible?
fa7bbb1ca4b39f732fdc7cf3d0a45878fb07eaf4.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that an occlusion-based, perturbation-driven approach can generate meaningful and interpretable attribution maps for 3D object detectors on LiDAR data, even when the models are treated as black boxes.
fa7bbb1ca4b39f732fdc7cf3d0a45878fb07eaf4.proposed_method: A novel occlusion-based attribution mapping framework, OccAM, will be developed to estimate the importance of each 3D point in a LiDAR point cloud for the predictions of black-box 3D object detectors. The method systematically generates random binary masks to sub-sample the input point cloud by removing or retaining points within spatially defined voxels, where the probability of retaining points is adapted according to the depth-dependent density of LiDAR data. For each detected object, the model is probed with thousands of such sub-sampled point clouds, and the impact of each point on the detection output is quantified using a similarity metric tailored for 3D bounding boxes, evaluating translation, rotation, and scale separately. The expected contribution of each point is then aggregated across all perturbations to form an attribution map, with normalization to account for the number of times each point is sampled.
fa7bbb1ca4b39f732fdc7cf3d0a45878fb07eaf4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using several state-of-the-art 3D object detectors, including PointPillars, SECOND, and PV-RCNN, trained and evaluated on the KITTI and Waymo Open Dataset (WOD) benchmarks. The OpenPCDet toolbox will be used for model training and inference. Attribution maps will be generated for both true and false positive detections, and qualitative interpretability will be assessed by visualizing the maps. Quantitative evaluation will be performed using a point-dropping protocol, where points are removed in order of their attributed importance and the resulting degradation in detection performance (measured by IoU and confidence score) is compared to random and least-important point removal baselines. The effect of density-aware sampling versus fixed-probability sampling will also be analyzed by plotting similarity scores as a function of object distance from the sensor.
fa7bbb1ca4b39f732fdc7cf3d0a45878fb07eaf4.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to generate point-level attribution maps for black-box 3D object detectors on real LiDAR point clouds, requiring no access to model internals such as gradients or parameters. The approach introduces a voxel-based, density-aware sub-sampling strategy specifically tailored to the unstructured and depth-varying nature of LiDAR data, and a similarity metric that evaluates 3D bounding box properties individually. The method enables universal applicability across different detector architectures and datasets, and provides new insights into both correct and erroneous model behaviors.

fa85633fb74d071911fe64d952afe47adc9928d6.title: CoTracker: It is Better to Track Together
fa85633fb74d071911fe64d952afe47adc9928d6.research_question: How can the accuracy and robustness of 2D point tracking in videos be improved, particularly for long-term tracking in the presence of occlusions and when points leave the camera view?
fa85633fb74d071911fe64d952afe47adc9928d6.hypothesis: Jointly tracking multiple points by exploiting their statistical dependencies, rather than treating them independently, will significantly improve tracking accuracy and robustness, especially under challenging conditions such as occlusions and points leaving the field of view.
fa85633fb74d071911fe64d952afe47adc9928d6.proposed_method: A transformer-based model is developed to perform joint tracking of a large number of 2D points in video sequences. The method encodes tracks as tokens in a two-dimensional grid (across time and points), and processes them using a transformer with specialized attention layers that alternate between time and track dimensions. To address computational and memory efficiency, the method introduces proxy tokens, which act as learnable proxies for groups of tracks, enabling efficient cross-attention and reducing the cost from quadratic to linear in the number of tracks. The model operates in a sliding window fashion, with overlapping windows processed recurrently; predictions from previous windows are used to initialize subsequent windows, enabling long-term tracking. Track features are initialized from convolutional image features sampled at starting locations, and are iteratively refined through multiple transformer passes. The method also proposes the use of additional support points (not explicitly requested by the user) to provide contextual information and further improve tracking performance.
fa85633fb74d071911fe64d952afe47adc9928d6.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several standard tracking benchmarks. The model is trained on the synthetic TAP-Vid-Kubric dataset, which contains 24-frame sequences of 3D objects with occlusions and background clutter. Evaluation is performed on TAP-Vid-DAVIS (real videos), TAP-Vid-RGB-Stacking (synthetic robot-manipulated objects), PointOdyssey (long-term synthetic tracking), and DynamicReplica (synthetic 3D articulated models). Metrics include Occlusion Accuracy (OA), fraction of visible points tracked within various pixel thresholds (δvis), Average Jaccard (AJ), and survival rate (average frames until failure). Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art trackers such as TAPIR and PIPs++. The experimental setup involves both causal and bidirectional tracking protocols, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of joint tracking, proxy tokens, and support points.
fa85633fb74d071911fe64d952afe47adc9928d6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of joint point tracking using a transformer architecture that shares information between tracked points via attention mechanisms. It presents the use of proxy tokens to dramatically improve memory and computational efficiency, enabling the simultaneous tracking of up to 70,000 points on a single GPU. The method incorporates an unrolled, recurrent training strategy for long-term and occlusion-robust tracking. The use of additional support points for contextual enhancement is also proposed. Collectively, these innovations enable state-of-the-art performance on multiple challenging tracking benchmarks, particularly in long-term and occlusion-heavy scenarios.

fa96417f8766568ba570088513940bbf14e3b356.title: WorkArena: How Capable Are Web Agents at Solving Common Knowledge Work Tasks?
fa96417f8766568ba570088513940bbf14e3b356.research_question: How capable are large language model-based web agents at solving common knowledge work tasks in real-world enterprise software environments, and what are the key challenges and limitations faced by such agents when interacting with complex, dynamic user interfaces?
fa96417f8766568ba570088513940bbf14e3b356.hypothesis: Large language model-based web agents, when provided with rich multimodal observations and advanced action spaces, can achieve meaningful automation of enterprise knowledge work tasks, but will face significant performance limitations due to complex, non-standard UIs and long-context requirements. Closed-source LLMs will outperform open-source models, but both will struggle with certain classes of tasks.
fa96417f8766568ba570088513940bbf14e3b356.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, WorkArena, will be developed to evaluate web agents on 33 representative enterprise tasks (e.g., filtering lists, filling forms, searching knowledge bases, navigating menus) within the ServiceNow platform. Each task will be specified through natural language goals and validated with automated oracle functions and real-time feedback mechanisms. A new environment, BrowserGym, will be created to support agent development and evaluation, providing multimodal observations (HTML, accessibility tree, screenshots), a broad set of actions (Python code, high-level primitives, coordinate-based actions), and chat-based interaction. Agents will be implemented using state-of-the-art LLMs (both closed- and open-source), equipped with features such as chain-of-thought prompting, memory through action and error histories, and flexible observation/action spaces. The methodology will include ablation studies to assess the impact of different environment features and agent configurations.
fa96417f8766568ba570088513940bbf14e3b356.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on WorkArena, as well as on established benchmarks such as MiniWoB and WebArena, using BrowserGym as a unified evaluation platform. Multiple LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Llama3-70B) will be tested, with agent configurations tuned via random search. Evaluation will use success rate as the primary metric, with stratified bootstrap to estimate standard error. Each agent will be run with multiple seeds per task to ensure statistical robustness. Baselines will include both zero-shot and vision-augmented agents, and ablation studies will systematically vary features such as chain-of-thought, memory, multimodal inputs, and action space granularity to quantify their effects on performance. The experiments will also analyze performance gaps between open- and closed-source LLMs, and between different task categories.
fa96417f8766568ba570088513940bbf14e3b356.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces WorkArena, the first realistic benchmark focused on enterprise knowledge work tasks for web agents, featuring nearly 20,000 unique task instances with automated validation and oracle solutions. BrowserGym is presented as a novel, extensible environment supporting multimodal observations, rich action spaces, and chat-based interaction, compatible with multiple benchmarks. The research will provide the first comprehensive empirical evaluation of LLM-based web agents on realistic enterprise tasks, uncovering key limitations and performance gaps, especially between open- and closed-source models. The benchmark and environment are open-source, designed to catalyze further research in web automation and LLM-based agents.

fa984cd8632af37ee6a587043619a688ad5c354d.title: PFNs4BO: In-Context Learning for Bayesian Optimization
fa984cd8632af37ee6a587043619a688ad5c354d.research_question: Can flexible neural surrogate models, trained via in-context learning on arbitrary priors, serve as effective and extensible replacements for traditional Gaussian processes in Bayesian Optimization, particularly for hyperparameter optimization and other black-box optimization tasks?
fa984cd8632af37ee6a587043619a688ad5c354d.hypothesis: Neural surrogates trained to approximate posterior predictive distributions for arbitrary priors can match or exceed the performance of Gaussian processes in Bayesian Optimization, while also enabling principled incorporation of user priors, handling of irrelevant dimensions, and non-myopic acquisition strategies.
fa984cd8632af37ee6a587043619a688ad5c354d.proposed_method: A neural surrogate model, specifically a Prior-data Fitted Network (PFN), will be trained offline to approximate the posterior predictive distribution (PPD) for a chosen prior distribution over functions (e.g., GP, BNN, or custom priors). The PFN leverages a Transformer architecture to encode variable-length datasets and queries, using in-context learning to perform Bayesian inference in a single forward pass. The training procedure involves sampling synthetic datasets from the prior, conditioning on subsets of data, and minimizing cross-entropy loss on held-out examples to learn the PPD approximation. During Bayesian Optimization, the trained PFN replaces the traditional surrogate, providing predictive distributions for acquisition function computation (e.g., EI, PI, UCB), and supports gradient-based optimization for acquisition maximization and input warping. Extensions include incorporating user-specified priors (e.g., intervals where optima are likely), handling spurious dimensions by augmenting priors with irrelevant features, and learning non-myopic acquisition functions directly.
fa984cd8632af37ee6a587043619a688ad5c354d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of benchmarks, including artificial GP samples and three real-world hyperparameter optimization testbeds: HPO-B (discrete, tree-based models), Bayesmark (continuous, scikit-learn models), and PD1 (large neural network tuning). The PFN-based approach will be compared against baselines such as Random Search, standard Gaussian Processes (with Empirical Bayes), DNGO, Deep Kernel GPs, HEBO, HyperOpt, PySOT, and Optformer. Evaluation metrics will include average rank, average regret, and accuracy across multiple seeds and tasks. Ablation studies will assess the impact of input warping, handling of spurious features, user priors, and different acquisition functions. The experimental setup includes up to 50 function evaluations per task, use of both discrete and continuous search spaces, and systematic comparison of PFN priors (GP, HEBO-inspired, BNN) against established methods.
fa984cd8632af37ee6a587043619a688ad5c354d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables the use of neural surrogates trained on arbitrary priors for Bayesian Optimization, overcoming limitations of Gaussian processes related to prior expressivity, scalability, and handling of non-standard data types. The method allows principled integration of user beliefs about optima, direct modeling of spurious dimensions, and learning of non-myopic acquisition functions, all within a single, reusable neural network. The PFN framework supports efficient offline training and fast inference, generalizes across search space dimensionalities, and demonstrates strong empirical performance on diverse benchmarks, including large-scale hyperparameter optimization tasks.

faa76d61e9e8e7b247d1632e76bb2138693bb67a.title: Enhancing Cognition and Explainability of Multimodal Foundation Models with Self-Synthesized Data
faa76d61e9e8e7b247d1632e76bb2138693bb67a.research_question: How can the cognitive abilities and explainability of large multimodal models (LMMs) be improved for fine-grained, domain-specific visual classification tasks, particularly in settings lacking image-specific expert annotations?
faa76d61e9e8e7b247d1632e76bb2138693bb67a.hypothesis: Iterative fine-tuning of LMMs using self-synthesized, interpretable explanations that are grounded in expert-defined, image-level visual concepts will significantly enhance both classification accuracy and the quality of model explanations, without requiring extensive manual annotation.
faa76d61e9e8e7b247d1632e76bb2138693bb67a.proposed_method: A novel visual rejection sampling framework will be developed to iteratively fine-tune LMMs using synthetic, interpretable answers. The process begins by generating image descriptions via the LMM's captioning abilities, which are then used to identify relevant visual features based on an expert-defined concept set for each class. An information bottleneck-based selection method is applied to extract the most informative, non-redundant image-level concepts, which are then rewritten into textual explanations. These explanations, paired with images and queries, form the initial fine-tuning dataset.
