After each round of fine-tuning, the model generates new candidate answers, which are filtered using a reward model-free rejection sampling mechanism that selects the answer best aligned with the previously selected concepts, as measured by InfoNCE scores. This iterative process continues for multiple rounds, progressively improving the model’s ability to generate accurate, human-verifiable explanations.
faa76d61e9e8e7b247d1632e76bb2138693bb67a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse range of datasets, including fine-grained classification (CUB-200, Stanford Dogs, FGVC-Aircraft), medical imaging (HAM10000, Chest X-Ray for Pneumonia), and plant disease datasets. The base model will be LLaVA-1.5-7B, with LoRA-based fine-tuning applied to all linear layers, and E5 as the embedding model for concept and explanation alignment. Baselines will include zero-shot base LMMs, naive label-only fine-tuning, and label-plus-general-explanation synthesis using language-only models. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, explanation existence (EE), cognition score (CS), fluency score (FS), and general ability (MMMU). Additional human expert annotation and precision analysis will be performed for concept selection, and qualitative analysis will include heatmap visualizations of model attention.
faa76d61e9e8e7b247d1632e76bb2138693bb67a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a self-synthesizing, interpretable data generation process for LMM fine-tuning that does not require image-specific manual annotation. It leverages an information-theoretic approach for selecting image-level visual concepts and a reward model-free rejection sampling method for high-quality explanation filtering. The iterative synthesis and fine-tuning process is claimed to improve both the cognitive and explainability aspects of LMMs, outperforming existing baselines in accuracy and explanation quality across multiple domains. The approach is theoretically justified via mutual information maximization and empirically validated on diverse, challenging datasets.

faab24bc6cd4a4dea6e82420d145f08445c05fc7.title: Outlier Weighed Layerwise Sparsity (OWL): A Missing Secret Sauce for Pruning LLMs to High Sparsity
faab24bc6cd4a4dea6e82420d145f08445c05fc7.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be pruned to achieve high sparsity levels without significant loss in performance, and what is the optimal layerwise sparsity allocation strategy for such pruning?
faab24bc6cd4a4dea6e82420d145f08445c05fc7.hypothesis: Aligning the layerwise sparsity ratios in LLM pruning with the non-uniform distribution of outlier features within each layer will result in better preservation of model performance at high sparsity levels compared to uniform sparsity or other existing strategies.
faab24bc6cd4a4dea6e82420d145f08445c05fc7.proposed_method: A novel pruning methodology, Outlier Weighed Layerwise Sparsity (OWL), will be developed to assign non-uniform sparsity ratios to each layer of an LLM based on the prevalence of outlier features in that layer. The method first computes the Layerwise Outlier Distribution (LOD) by quantifying the proportion of weights in each layer whose outlier scores (derived from input activation norms and weight magnitudes) exceed a threshold multiple of the mean. Layers with higher outlier ratios are assigned lower sparsity (i.e., more weights retained), while layers with fewer outliers are pruned more aggressively. A hyperparameter is introduced to constrain the layerwise sparsity ratios within a bounded range around the global target sparsity, preventing excessive variation and ensuring stability. The OWL strategy can be integrated with existing pruning metrics, such as those used in Wanda or SparseGPT, by replacing their uniform sparsity allocation with OWL's outlier-informed ratios.
faab24bc6cd4a4dea6e82420d145f08445c05fc7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of LLMs, including the LLaMA-V1 family (7B, 13B, 30B, 65B parameters), OPT-6.7B, as well as advanced models like LLaMA-V2-7B, Vicuna-7B, and Mistral-7B. The primary evaluation dataset for language modeling will be WikiText, with perplexity as the main metric. Zero-shot downstream task performance will be assessed on benchmarks such as BoolQ, RTE, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, and OpenbookQA, using accuracy as the metric. Baselines for comparison will include magnitude pruning, Wanda, and SparseGPT, all using uniform layerwise sparsity. The proposed OWL method will be integrated with both Wanda and SparseGPT to create OWLw.Wanda and OWLw.SparseGPT variants. Experiments will focus on high sparsity regimes (50%-90%), and inference speedup will be measured using the DeepSparse engine on CPUs. Additional experiments will include fine-tuning with LoRA, analysis of pruning time overhead, and exploration of OWL's applicability to low-rank approximations and other practical compression scenarios.
faab24bc6cd4a4dea6e82420d145f08445c05fc7.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first systematic approach to non-uniform layerwise sparsity allocation for LLM pruning, guided by the empirical distribution of outlier features in each layer. OWL is claimed to significantly outperform state-of-the-art pruning methods (Wanda, SparseGPT) at high sparsity levels, achieving substantial reductions in perplexity and notable inference speedups, while incurring negligible computational overhead. The method is general, applicable across different pruning metrics, model architectures, and practical deployment scenarios, and provides new insights into the critical role of outlier preservation in LLM compression.

faba2be59dbef9e6dcea551d64601ec4c9b7470a.title: Optimal or Greedy Decision Trees? Revisiting their Objectives, Tuning, and Performance
faba2be59dbef9e6dcea551d64601ec4c9b7470a.research_question: What are the effects of different objective functions and tuning strategies on the performance of optimal and greedy decision tree methods, and how do these approaches compare in terms of accuracy, interpretability, and robustness across diverse datasets?
faba2be59dbef9e6dcea551d64601ec4c9b7470a.hypothesis: Optimal decision trees trained with appropriately chosen objective functions and tuning methods can outperform or match greedy decision trees in terms of out-of-sample accuracy and interpretability, and the choice of objective function (especially concavity) and tuning strategy significantly affects the performance and robustness of both approaches.
faba2be59dbef9e6dcea551d64601ec4c9b7470a.proposed_method: A comprehensive experimental framework will be developed to systematically compare optimal and greedy decision tree methods. The study will implement and evaluate 11 objective functions, including traditional concave criteria (such as Gini impurity and entropy) and newly proposed non-concave objectives (M-loss and L-loss), within both greedy (top-down induction) and optimal (global optimization) tree learning paradigms. Six complexity tuning approaches will be incorporated, including four established and two novel methods, to assess their impact on model selection and performance. The methodology will involve transforming existing greedy splitting criteria into global objectives suitable for optimal tree training, and empirically analyzing the behavior of these objectives under various training regimes, including the presence of noise and varying dataset sizes. All methods will be implemented in a scalable dynamic programming-based optimal decision tree solver with standardized binarization procedures for fair comparison.
faba2be59dbef9e6dcea551d64601ec4c9b7470a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a large benchmark of 180 real-world and synthetic binary classification datasets sourced from OpenML, filtered for manageable feature and instance counts. Each dataset will be split into five folds for cross-validation, ensuring robust evaluation of generalization performance. Both optimal and greedy decision trees will be trained up to a fixed maximum depth (e.g., depth four), with hyperparameters such as tree size tuned via cross-validation. Synthetic datasets will be generated to systematically vary feature and class noise, as well as sample size, enabling controlled analysis of robustness. Baselines will include standard greedy methods (e.g., CART with various splitting criteria) and optimal tree methods with different objectives. Evaluation metrics will focus on out-of-sample accuracy, average rank across datasets, tree size (number of leaf nodes), and computational efficiency. Statistical tests (such as the Nemenyi critical distance test) will be used to assess the significance of observed differences.
faba2be59dbef9e6dcea551d64601ec4c9b7470a.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces two novel non-concave objective functions for optimal decision tree training and systematically analyzes their impact compared to traditional concave objectives. It provides the most extensive empirical evaluation to date of both optimal and greedy decision tree methods across a wide range of objectives, tuning strategies, and datasets. The study offers new insights into the interplay between objective function concavity and tree learning paradigm, demonstrates the critical role of tuning in optimal decision trees, and establishes best practices for benchmarking and comparing decision tree algorithms. The findings are expected to clarify conflicting claims in the literature and provide actionable recommendations for practitioners and researchers.

fabf58a766313f3f7088e95c53233a1e3fd0ef6f.title: Momentum Tracking: Momentum Acceleration for Decentralized Deep Learning on Heterogeneous Data
fabf58a766313f3f7088e95c53233a1e3fd0ef6f.research_question: How can decentralized deep learning algorithms be made robust to data heterogeneity while leveraging momentum acceleration, particularly in non-convex optimization settings with stochastic gradients?
fabf58a766313f3f7088e95c53233a1e3fd0ef6f.hypothesis: A decentralized learning algorithm that combines momentum with gradient tracking can achieve convergence rates that are independent of data heterogeneity, even when the objective function is non-convex and only stochastic gradients are available.
fabf58a766313f3f7088e95c53233a1e3fd0ef6f.proposed_method: A new decentralized learning algorithm, termed Momentum Tracking, is developed by integrating momentum acceleration with gradient tracking. Each node maintains local model parameters, a momentum term, and a correction variable. At each iteration, the local momentum is updated as a moving average of stochastic gradients, and the model parameters are updated using a combination of local and neighbor information weighted by a mixing matrix. The correction variable tracks the global momentum by aggregating local momentum updates across the network, ensuring that parameter drift due to data heterogeneity is mitigated. The method is theoretically analyzed, with convergence rates derived under standard assumptions for decentralized learning, showing independence from data heterogeneity for any momentum coefficient β in [0,1).
fabf58a766313f3f7088e95c53233a1e3fd0ef6f.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three image classification benchmarks: FashionMNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR-10, using neural network architectures including LeNet, VGG-11, and ResNet-34. Data heterogeneity is simulated by distributing data such that each node receives samples from a subset of classes (k-class partitioning, with smaller k indicating higher heterogeneity). Baseline algorithms include DSGD, DSGDm, QG-DSGDm, DecentLaM, and Gradient Tracking. Evaluation metrics focus on test accuracy and convergence speed, with experiments run on a ring network of eight nodes (N=8) and repeated with three random seeds. Hyperparameters, including step size and momentum coefficient (β=0.9), are tuned individually for each method.
fabf58a766313f3f7088e95c53233a1e3fd0ef6f.novelty_claims: The proposed Momentum Tracking algorithm is the first decentralized learning method with momentum whose convergence rate is theoretically proven to be independent of data heterogeneity in the non-convex, stochastic gradient setting. Unlike previous momentum-based decentralized methods, which suffer degraded performance as data heterogeneity increases, this approach maintains robust convergence and outperforms existing baselines across a range of heterogeneous data distributions and neural network architectures. The method also achieves linear speedup with respect to the number of nodes and demonstrates stable convergence behavior even in highly heterogeneous scenarios.

face928230ea69c69e92f3f451a014f4304f2ef1.title: Bigger, Regularized, Categorical: High-Capacity Value Functions are Efficient Multi-Task Learners
face928230ea69c69e92f3f451a014f4304f2ef1.research_question: How can value-based reinforcement learning agents be scaled to efficiently learn and generalize across a large number of diverse tasks in an online, multi-task setting, and what design choices enable robust, sample-efficient transfer to new tasks?
face928230ea69c69e92f3f451a014f4304f2ef1.hypothesis: Scaling value-based reinforcement learning agents using high-capacity, regularized architectures trained with cross-entropy loss and conditioned on learnable task embeddings will enable stable, efficient multi-task learning and improve transferability to new tasks, outperforming existing single-task and multi-task baselines.
face928230ea69c69e92f3f451a014f4304f2ef1.proposed_method: A new approach is developed that combines three key components: (1) a scaled and regularized residual network architecture (BroNet) to represent Q-values, (2) a cross-entropy loss via categorical Q-learning to stabilize learning across tasks with heterogeneous reward scales, and (3) learnable task embeddings that condition the value function on task identity, learned online by backpropagating the temporal difference loss. The method normalizes rewards per task to ensure consistent learning signals and uses a unified model for all tasks, avoiding separate network heads. The approach is applied to both continuous and discrete control problems by integrating with Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) and DrQ-ϵ algorithms, respectively, and is designed to function with a single set of hyperparameters across all tasks and domains.
face928230ea69c69e92f3f451a014f4304f2ef1.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on 283 tasks from five major RL benchmarks: DeepMind Control Suite (DMC), MetaWorld (MW), HumanoidBench (HB), ShadowHand (SH), and Atari, covering diverse domains such as high- and low-degree-of-freedom locomotion, manipulation, and vision-based discrete control. Multi-task configurations include up to 85 tasks per benchmark, with agents trained for up to 2 million environment steps per task. The proposed method is compared against a comprehensive set of state-of-the-art baselines, including both single-task and multi-task algorithms (e.g., TD-MPC2, DreamerV3, BRO, SimBa, PCGrad, PaCo, CTPG, GAMT, DDPG+HER, DrQ-ϵ, SPR, SimPLe, DER). Evaluation metrics include normalized returns and success rates, with normalization procedures adapted to each environment. Transfer learning experiments evaluate model transfer, embedding-tuning transfer, and data transfer protocols on held-out tasks, assessing both sample efficiency and final performance. All experiments use a fixed set of hyperparameters, and multi-task agents interact with all tasks in parallel, maintaining a fixed updates-per-data ratio.
face928230ea69c69e92f3f451a014f4304f2ef1.novelty_claims: The proposed method demonstrates, for the first time, that online temporal-difference learning with high-capacity value models can scale to the billion-parameter range and hundreds of tasks without relying on offline data or expert demonstrations. Key innovations include the synergistic combination of scaled residual Q-value architectures, cross-entropy loss for stable multi-task learning, and learnable task embeddings for efficient task conditioning. The approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in both single-task and multi-task settings, significantly improves sample and compute efficiency (up to 40× fewer gradient updates), and enables robust, sample-efficient transfer to new tasks. The method also shows that increasing model and data scale leads to improved generalization and transfer, challenging the prevailing paradigm of 'one agent per task' in value-based RL.

facf11419e149a03bd4a9bffdda2ebb433a59d85.title: Equivariant and Stable Positional Encoding for More Powerful Graph Neural Networks
facf11419e149a03bd4a9bffdda2ebb433a59d85.research_question: How can graph neural networks be enhanced to achieve better generalization and stability, particularly for tasks involving sets of nodes such as link prediction, by leveraging positional encoding while maintaining permutation equivariance and computational efficiency?
facf11419e149a03bd4a9bffdda2ebb433a59d85.hypothesis: A graph neural network architecture that updates node features and positional features through separate channels, imposing permutation equivariance on node features and orthogonal group equivariance on positional features, will yield more stable and generalizable representations, outperforming existing approaches in node-set-based tasks such as link prediction.
facf11419e149a03bd4a9bffdda2ebb433a59d85.proposed_method: A novel GNN layer, termed PEG, is developed to process both original node features and positional features obtained from positional encoding (PE) techniques such as Laplacian Eigenmaps or DeepWalk. The architecture maintains two separate update channels: one for node features, which enforces permutation equivariance, and one for positional features, which enforces O(p) (orthogonal group) equivariance, where p is the dimension of the positional features. The PEG layer is mathematically designed so that the sensitivity of node representations depends only on the eigengap between the p-th and (p+1)-th eigenvalues of the graph Laplacian, ensuring stability even under graph perturbations. The method is generalizable to other matrix-factorization-based PE techniques and can be integrated with various GNN backbones, such as GCN or GraphSAGE, by modulating edge weights based on distances in the positional feature space.
facf11419e149a03bd4a9bffdda2ebb433a59d85.experiment_details: Experiments will focus on link prediction tasks across eight real-world networks, including citation networks (Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed), user-interaction networks (Twitch-RU, Twitch-PT, Chameleon), and large-scale OGB datasets (ogbl-ddi, ogbl-collab). Both traditional link prediction (training and testing on the same graph) and domain-shift link prediction (training and testing on different graphs) will be evaluated. Baselines for comparison include VGAE, P-GNN, SEAL, GNN-Trans, LE, DeepWalk, and variants of GraphSAGE. Evaluation metrics will include ROC-AUC and Hits@K, with experiments repeated 10 times for statistical robustness. Implementation details include careful partitioning of training and validation links to avoid overfitting positional features, and computational complexity will be measured in both training and inference phases.
facf11419e149a03bd4a9bffdda2ebb433a59d85.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled framework for incorporating positional encodings into GNNs that guarantees both permutation equivariance and stability with respect to graph perturbations. The PEG layer achieves O(p) equivariance for positional features, addressing the instability and non-generalizability issues of prior PE-based GNNs. The method is provably stable, with sensitivity controlled by the eigengap between specific Laplacian eigenvalues, and is applicable to a broad class of PE techniques. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior generalization, scalability, and computational efficiency compared to state-of-the-art baselines, especially in domain-shift scenarios.

fae41e2dded7f20f110a57c61dd0d1dbdd4c6a24.title: Estimating average causal effects from patient trajectories
fae41e2dded7f20f110a57c61dd0d1dbdd4c6a24.research_question: How can average causal effects (ACEs) of time-varying treatments on patient outcomes be accurately estimated from longitudinal observational data, such as electronic health records, in the presence of time-varying confounders?
fae41e2dded7f20f110a57c61dd0d1dbdd4c6a24.hypothesis: An end-to-end deep learning framework that jointly models the sequence of conditional expectations and incorporates a sequential targeting procedure will yield more accurate, doubly robust, and asymptotically efficient estimates of time-varying average causal effects from patient trajectories than existing methods.
fae41e2dded7f20f110a57c61dd0d1dbdd4c6a24.proposed_method: A novel end-to-end deep learning model, DeepACE, is proposed to estimate time-varying ACEs from longitudinal observational data. DeepACE integrates a recurrent neural network (specifically, an LSTM) to process patient trajectories and treatments over time, capturing complex nonlinear dependencies. The model implements a G-computation layer that learns conditional expectations for both factual and counterfactual outcomes, using both observed and hypothetical interventions. To address time-varying confounding, DeepACE leverages the iterative G-computation formula, enabling joint learning of all conditional expectations rather than training separate models for each time step. Additionally, a sequential targeting layer is introduced, which perturbs the model outputs using estimated propensity scores and a targeted regularization loss, ensuring that the final estimator satisfies a semi-parametric efficient estimating equation and achieves double robustness.
fae41e2dded7f20f110a57c61dd0d1dbdd4c6a24.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic, semi-synthetic, and real-world datasets. Synthetic datasets will be generated to provide known ground-truth ACEs, allowing for benchmarking of estimation accuracy across different treatment regimes and time lags. Semi-synthetic data will be created using real patient records (e.g., from the MIMIC-III database) with simulated interventions, again enabling ground-truth comparisons. Real-world evaluation will use a clinical dataset of patients with low back pain, examining the effect of physical labor on pain intensity across patient subgroups. Baselines will include state-of-the-art methods for time-varying ACE estimation (such as marginal structural models, iterative G-computation, parametric G-formula, structural nested models, LTMLE with GLM and super learner), as well as deep learning models for individualized treatment effect estimation (e.g., RMSNs, CRN, G-Net). Evaluation metrics will focus on absolute error between estimated and true ACEs (when available), and model performance will be assessed across multiple runs and intervention scenarios.
fae41e2dded7f20f110a57c61dd0d1dbdd4c6a24.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first end-to-end neural network specifically designed for estimating time-varying average causal effects from longitudinal observational data. Unlike existing methods, DeepACE jointly learns all conditional expectations and incorporates a novel sequential targeting procedure within the model training process, rather than as a post-hoc step. This enables the estimator to be both doubly robust and asymptotically efficient. The method is claimed to outperform state-of-the-art baselines in terms of estimation accuracy, particularly in settings with complex, nonlinear dependencies and long-range temporal relationships. Furthermore, the approach provides meaningful and actionable findings in real-world clinical applications.

faffd56c4024f552335a76639526d5d60e7a278b.title: EMOS: Embodiment-aware Heterogeneous Multi-robot Operating System with LLM Agents
faffd56c4024f552335a76639526d5d60e7a278b.research_question: How can heterogeneous multi-robot systems achieve effective, fully automated collaboration in complex real-world environments by leveraging large language model-based multi-agent systems that are aware of each robot's physical embodiment and capabilities?
faffd56c4024f552335a76639526d5d60e7a278b.hypothesis: A multi-agent system that incorporates embodiment-aware reasoning—where each agent autonomously understands and communicates its robot's physical capabilities through self-generated 'robot resumes'—will enable more effective task planning, assignment, and execution in heterogeneous multi-robot systems compared to systems relying on human-assigned roles or lacking embodiment awareness.
faffd56c4024f552335a76639526d5d60e7a278b.proposed_method: A general framework will be developed for operating heterogeneous multi-robot systems using large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems. Each robot will be paired with an LLM agent that generates a 'robot resume' by parsing the robot's URDF file and using both LLM summarization and forward kinematics tools to extract and describe mobility, perception, and manipulation capabilities in both natural language and numerical form. The system will operate in a hierarchical fashion: first, a centralized group discussion phase will allow agents to collectively plan and assign tasks based on the scene context and robot resumes; then, a decentralized action execution phase will have each agent independently execute its assigned sub-tasks, using its robot's skill libraries and maintaining a history of actions and outcomes. Scene context will be constructed bottom-up from geometric and semantic representations, transformed into textual descriptions for LLM processing. The approach emphasizes asynchronous, parallel execution and embodiment-aware task decomposition.
faffd56c4024f552335a76639526d5d60e7a278b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Habitat-MAS benchmark, a simulated environment built on top of the Habitat platform and featuring multi-floor real and synthetic indoor scenes from Matterport3D and HSSD datasets. The benchmark includes four types of robots (Fetch, Stretch, Drone, Spot) and four tasks designed to test navigation, perception, manipulation, and comprehensive multi-agent rearrangement. Evaluation metrics will include overall task success rate, sub-goal success rate, token usage (as a measure of LLM communication efficiency), and simulation steps (reflecting operational efficiency). Baseline comparisons will include ablations such as removing numerical reasoning, removing robot resumes (replacing with human-authored roles), and removing group discussion. The experiments will use the GPT-4o API for LLM agents, and all robot control will be performed via standardized APIs for navigation and manipulation.
faffd56c4024f552335a76639526d5d60e7a278b.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the concept of 'robot resumes'—self-generated, embodiment-aware capability descriptions—enabling LLM agents to reason about and communicate each robot's unique physical abilities without relying on human-assigned roles. This is the first system to integrate such embodiment-aware reasoning into LLM-based multi-agent task planning and execution for heterogeneous multi-robot systems. The Habitat-MAS benchmark is also novel, providing the first simulated environment specifically designed to evaluate multi-agent systems' understanding of physical embodiment across a diverse set of robots and scenes. The hierarchical, discussion-based planning and decentralized execution pipeline, combined with numerical and textual reasoning about robot capabilities, represents a significant advancement toward fully automated, generalizable heterogeneous multi-robot collaboration.

fb00c87e7d91205310ab673ed7d96b4b83e80181.title: Controllable Mesh Generation Through Sparse Latent Point Diffusion Models
fb00c87e7d91205310ab673ed7d96b4b83e80181.research_question: How can 3D mesh generation be made more efficient, controllable, and of higher quality, given the challenges of irregular data structures and varying topology in meshes?
fb00c87e7d91205310ab673ed7d96b4b83e80181.hypothesis: Encoding 3D meshes as sparse latent point clouds with semantic features, and modeling their distributions using diffusion models in this latent space, will enable faster, higher-quality, and more controllable mesh generation compared to existing methods that operate directly on dense point clouds or mesh templates.
fb00c87e7d91205310ab673ed7d96b4b83e80181.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that reformulates mesh generation as a two-stage process: first, generating point clouds as an intermediate representation, and second, reconstructing meshes from these point clouds. Dense point clouds sampled from meshes are further encoded into a sparse set of latent points using farthest point sampling (FPS), with each point assigned a semantically meaningful feature via a neural encoder. Two denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) are trained in this sparse latent space: one models the distribution of the positions of the latent points, and the other models the distribution of their features conditioned on the positions. A neural decoder then reconstructs dense point clouds from the sparse latent points and their features, and a differentiable surface reconstruction technique (such as Shape as Points, SAP) is used to generate the final mesh. This approach enables explicit control over both global and local mesh structures by manipulating the sparse latent points and their features.
fb00c87e7d91205310ab673ed7d96b4b83e80181.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the ShapeNet dataset, using five categories (airplane, cabinet, car, chair, lamp). The proposed method is compared against several baselines, including TreeGAN, SPGAN, ShapeGF, PVD, and DPM, with all baselines trained using their public codebases. Evaluation metrics include 1-NN, Minimum Matching Distance (MMD), Coverage (COV), Chamfer Distance (CD), Earth Mover Distance (EMD), and normal consistency loss, computed on both generated point clouds and reconstructed meshes. The experimental setup also measures generation efficiency (inference time per sample) and includes ablation studies on the number and sampling strategy of sparse latent points. Qualitative and quantitative results are provided, demonstrating visual quality, diversity, and controllability of generated meshes.
fb00c87e7d91205310ab673ed7d96b4b83e80181.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a sparse latent point diffusion model (SLIDE) for mesh generation, which encodes dense point clouds into a compact set of semantic latent points and models their distributions using DDPMs. This enables significantly faster sampling compared to direct dense point cloud diffusion, and allows explicit, fine-grained control over mesh structure and details without requiring part annotations. The method is claimed to outperform existing point cloud and mesh generative models in both quality and efficiency, and supports new capabilities such as global/local interpolation, shape combination, and user-guided controllable generation via manipulation of sparse latent points.

fb09b581589e1195ff018179c6a11668587c6d64.title: Vision-Language Models are Zero-Shot Reward Models for Reinforcement Learning
fb09b581589e1195ff018179c6a11668587c6d64.research_question: Can large pretrained vision-language models serve as effective zero-shot reward models for reinforcement learning agents, enabling task specification via natural language prompts without manual reward engineering or extensive human feedback?
fb09b581589e1195ff018179c6a11668587c6d64.hypothesis: Pretrained vision-language models, when used as zero-shot reward models, can provide sufficiently informative and robust reward signals from simple natural language prompts to enable reinforcement learning agents to learn complex tasks, with performance scaling positively with model size and environment realism.
fb09b581589e1195ff018179c6a11668587c6d64.proposed_method: A framework is developed in which pretrained vision-language models (VLMs), specifically CLIP, are used as zero-shot reward models (VLM-RMs) for reinforcement learning tasks. The reward for each state is computed as the cosine similarity between the CLIP-encoded image of the current environment state and the CLIP-encoded text prompt describing the desired task. An optional goal-baseline regularization technique is introduced, where a 'baseline' prompt describing a neutral state is also encoded, and the state embedding is projected onto the line between the baseline and goal embeddings, with a tunable regularization parameter. This approach is integrated into standard RL algorithms (DQN and SAC) by replacing the environment's reward function with the VLM-RM output, and rewards are computed in batches during training. The method is designed to require minimal prompt engineering and no fine-tuning of the VLM.
fb09b581589e1195ff018179c6a11668587c6d64.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on classic RL benchmarks (CartPole and MountainCar) and a suite of complex tasks in the MuJoCo Humanoid-v4 environment. For the classic benchmarks, both ground truth rewards and VLM-RM rewards are compared, and the effect of environment realism (e.g., adding textures) is tested. In the humanoid environment, tasks such as kneeling, sitting in lotus position, doing the splits, and others are specified via single-sentence prompts, with human evaluation used for tasks lacking ground truth rewards. Baselines include standard RL with ground truth rewards and ablations on regularization strength and environment modifications. Evaluation metrics include policy success rate (human-labeled for humanoid tasks), correlation with ground truth rewards, and EPIC distance between reward functions. The scaling behavior of reward model quality is assessed by varying the size of the CLIP model.
fb09b581589e1195ff018179c6a11668587c6d64.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a general, learning-free method for using pretrained vision-language models as zero-shot reward models for RL, enabling task specification via natural language without manual reward engineering or human feedback collection. The method demonstrates that simple cosine similarity-based reward computation, optionally regularized with a baseline prompt, is sufficient for a range of tasks. The approach is shown to scale with VLM size and environment realism, and is validated on both standard benchmarks and complex humanoid tasks, achieving high success rates with minimal prompt engineering. This work provides evidence that future, larger VLMs will further expand the applicability of zero-shot reward modeling in RL.

fb30199d753b923d880746f998d19704afcc77d1.title: Estimating and Controlling for Equalized Odds via Sensitive Attribute Predictors
fb30199d753b923d880746f998d19704afcc77d1.research_question: How can fairness violations, specifically regarding equalized odds, be estimated and controlled in machine learning classifiers when sensitive attribute data is unavailable during model development and deployment?
fb30199d753b923d880746f998d19704afcc77d1.hypothesis: It is possible to provide tight, computable upper bounds on equalized odds violations and to control worst-case fairness violations using proxy sensitive attribute predictors, even when true sensitive attribute data is not jointly observed with labels.
fb30199d753b923d880746f998d19704afcc77d1.proposed_method: A framework is developed for auditing and controlling equalized odds (EOD) fairness violations in binary classifiers when sensitive attributes are unobserved. The approach involves training a sensitive attribute predictor on a dataset containing features and sensitive attributes, and then using this predictor to estimate sensitive attributes on a separate dataset containing features and labels. The method derives tight, computable upper bounds on the worst-case EOD violation of a classifier, based on the performance of the sensitive attribute predictor and the classifier's group-conditional error rates. A post-processing correction technique is formulated as a linear program, which adjusts the classifier's predictions to minimize worst-case EOD violations while maintaining predictive accuracy, even in the absence of true sensitive attribute labels. The method also characterizes when correcting for fairness with respect to proxy attributes is optimal and when it is suboptimal, depending on the error distribution of the sensitive attribute predictor.
fb30199d753b923d880746f998d19704afcc77d1.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. In the synthetic setting, data is generated with controlled fairness violations and varying error distributions in the sensitive attribute predictor, allowing for systematic evaluation of the proposed bounds and correction method. For real-world evaluation, the CheXpert medical imaging dataset is used, where a DenseNet121 neural network is trained both as a sensitive attribute (sex) predictor and as a disease classifier. The sensitive attribute predictor is trained on a subset of the data, and its predictions are used to estimate fairness violations and apply the post-processing correction on the classifier. Baseline comparisons include naïve equalized odds post-processing using proxy attributes and uncorrected classifiers. Evaluation metrics include true and worst-case fairness violations (differences in TPR and FPR across groups), as well as expected classification loss. Bootstrap sampling is used to assess the stability of results.
fb30199d753b923d880746f998d19704afcc77d1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach provides the first tight and computable upper bounds on equalized odds violations in the absence of jointly observed sensitive attribute and label data. It introduces a practical post-processing correction method that provably minimizes worst-case fairness violations with respect to unobserved sensitive attributes, under mild and verifiable assumptions. The method explicitly characterizes when fairness correction with proxy attributes is optimal and when it is not, and offers actionable guarantees for fairness auditing and mitigation in demographically scarce regimes. The approach is demonstrated to be effective on both synthetic and real-world high-stakes datasets.

fb3dc5e20e0a71134ca916f0d6d8d41f01225b4b.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
fb3dc5e20e0a71134ca916f0d6d8d41f01225b4b.research_question: How does overoptimization against learned reward models in reinforcement learning from human feedback scale with model and data size, optimization method, and policy size, and what functional relationships govern the degradation of ground-truth performance as optimization increases?
fb3dc5e20e0a71134ca916f0d6d8d41f01225b4b.hypothesis: Overoptimization effects in reward models follow predictable scaling laws that depend on the method of optimization, the number of reward model parameters, the size of the training dataset, and the policy size. These scaling laws can be empirically characterized and used to predict the onset and extent of overoptimization.
fb3dc5e20e0a71134ca916f0d6d8d41f01225b4b.proposed_method: A synthetic experimental setup will be constructed where a fixed, high-capacity 'gold-standard' reward model serves as a proxy for human feedback, providing deterministic preference labels for policy outputs. Proxy reward models of varying sizes will be trained on these synthetic preference datasets, and policies will be optimized against these proxies using two methods: reinforcement learning (PPO) and best-of-n sampling (BoN). The relationship between the ground-truth (gold) reward and the proxy reward will be systematically measured as optimization progresses, quantified by the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the initial and optimized policies. Functional forms relating gold reward to KL divergence will be fitted for both optimization methods, and the dependence of these forms' coefficients on reward model size, data size, and policy size will be analyzed. Additional experiments will vary the KL penalty in RL and recalibrate reward model outputs for comparability.
fb3dc5e20e0a71134ca916f0d6d8d41f01225b4b.experiment_details: Experiments will use pretrained GPT-3 series language models as initial policies, fine-tuned on human demonstration data. The gold reward model will be a large (6B parameter) GPT-3 model, while proxy reward models will range from 3M to 3B parameters. Synthetic datasets of 100,000 preference comparisons will be generated and split into training and validation sets. Optimization will be performed using PPO (with and without KL penalty) and BoN sampling, with KL divergence tracked throughout. Evaluation metrics include the ground-truth (gold) reward score, proxy reward score, and the gap between them, as well as the KL divergence at which peak gold reward is achieved. Baselines include varying reward model and policy sizes, and dataset sizes. All experiments will be repeated across different seeds for robustness, and recalibration of reward model outputs will be performed to ensure comparability.
fb3dc5e20e0a71134ca916f0d6d8d41f01225b4b.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces empirically validated scaling laws for overoptimization in reward models, distinguishing the functional forms for different optimization methods (RL vs BoN) and demonstrating smooth, predictable scaling of overoptimization coefficients with reward model size and data. The synthetic gold-standard setup enables precise measurement of overoptimization effects without the prohibitive cost of human labeling. The work provides actionable insights for AI alignment, including implications for iterative RLHF and the limits of KL divergence as a universal metric for optimization. The findings offer a framework for predicting and mitigating Goodhart-like failures in large-scale reinforcement learning from human feedback.

fb6d7bbc20a68ad51a7821b044ca58ef311e58c0.title: Learning with little mixing
fb6d7bbc20a68ad51a7821b044ca58ef311e58c0.research_question: How can learning algorithms achieve minimax optimal risk rates in time-series regression with dependent data, particularly under weak mixing or long-range correlations, and what are the minimal conditions under which the least-squares estimator's performance matches that of the i.i.d. setting after a finite burn-in period?
fb6d7bbc20a68ad51a7821b044ca58ef311e58c0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under a trajectory hypercontractivity condition and mild ergodicity assumptions, the excess risk of the least-squares estimator in time-series regression with dependent data will match the minimax optimal rate of the i.i.d. case after a finite burn-in time, regardless of the mixing time of the underlying process.
fb6d7bbc20a68ad51a7821b044ca58ef311e58c0.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the least-squares estimator (LSE) in a general time-series regression model with martingale difference noise. The approach will rely on two main conditions: (1) a trajectory hypercontractivity condition on the function class and covariate process, which generalizes moment equivalence assumptions from i.i.d. learning to dependent data, and (2) a mild ergodicity condition quantified via the dependency matrix, which measures the temporal dependence of the covariate process. The methodology will establish a lower isometry property for the empirical risk, leveraging concentration inequalities for dependent sequences, and will characterize the excess risk of the LSE using a martingale offset complexity term. The analysis will avoid the traditional blocking technique and instead directly relate the dependency structure to the burn-in time required for optimal learning rates.
fb6d7bbc20a68ad51a7821b044ca58ef311e58c0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and real-world time-series data, including stable linear dynamical systems (LDS) and systems with generalized linear model (GLM) transitions. The performance of the LSE will be evaluated in terms of excess risk, comparing the empirical results to the theoretical predictions, particularly the rate at which the risk matches the i.i.d. benchmark after the burn-in period. Baselines will include standard LSE under i.i.d. assumptions and existing methods for dependent data that incorporate mixing-time corrections. Evaluation metrics will focus on excess risk, parameter recovery error, and convergence rates as a function of sample size and dependency structure.
fb6d7bbc20a68ad51a7821b044ca58ef311e58c0.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a new theoretical regime, termed 'learning with little mixing,' where the effects of temporal dependence in time-series data are confined to a finite burn-in period, after which the excess risk of the LSE matches the i.i.d. rate. This framework applies to a broad class of function spaces, including infinite-dimensional ellipsoids, and to processes with long-range correlations that are substantially weaker than geometric ergodicity. The approach generalizes existing results by providing sufficient conditions for minimax optimal risk rates without sample size deflation due to mixing time, and establishes the sharpest known excess risk bounds for certain classes of dynamical systems, including GLMs, in the stable case.

fb6ecf67c275fe775a12ad4ddf2c8dc7cfad1348.title: Unifying Grokking and Double Descent
fb6ecf67c275fe775a12ad4ddf2c8dc7cfad1348.research_question: Can a unified conceptual and mathematical framework explain both grokking and double descent phenomena in neural network training dynamics, and does this framework generalize across both training time and model capacity?
fb6ecf67c275fe775a12ad4ddf2c8dc7cfad1348.hypothesis: Grokking and double descent are manifestations of the same underlying learning dynamics, where neural networks learn patterns at different speeds, and inductive biases ultimately favor slow-to-learn, well-generalizing patterns. These dynamics occur both as a function of training time (epoch-wise) and model size (model-wise).
fb6ecf67c275fe775a12ad4ddf2c8dc7cfad1348.proposed_method: A mathematical model of neural network training will be developed based on the notion that networks learn multiple distinct patterns at different rates, each with its own generalization ability and learning speed. The model will formalize the probability of correct classification for each pattern as a sigmoid function over time, parameterized by maximum predictiveness, inflection point, and learning speed. The overall training and test accuracy will be computed as probabilistic unions of these patterns, with test accuracy weighted by per-pattern generalization parameters and a mechanism for inductive bias via 'preferred' patterns. This framework will be used to simulate and analyze both epoch-wise and model-wise learning dynamics, interpolating between grokking and double descent by modulating pattern properties.
fb6ecf67c275fe775a12ad4ddf2c8dc7cfad1348.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by training decoder-only transformer models with causal attention masking on a modular division task (e.g., division mod 97), encoding each residue as a symbol. The effect of model complexity will be explored by varying the parameter count, specifically the embedding dimension, and observing both training and test loss/accuracy across optimization steps and model sizes. Baselines will include standard training curves for grokking and double descent, with evaluation metrics such as loss and accuracy on both training and held-out test sets. The experimental setup will use 2-layer networks of width 128, a single attention head, AdamW optimizer, a learning rate of 1e-3, weight decay of 1e-5, and typically 400,000 optimization steps. Additional analyses will investigate the emergence of specific pattern types and their correspondence to phases of generalization.
fb6ecf67c275fe775a12ad4ddf2c8dc7cfad1348.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified conceptual and mathematical framework that explains both grokking and double descent as instances of the same pattern learning dynamics. It provides the first demonstration of model-wise grokking, showing that delayed generalization and double descent can occur as a function of model size, not just training time. The model distinguishes itself by allowing per-pattern generalization parameters, separating maximum predictiveness from learning speed, and formalizing the influence of inductive bias through preferred patterns. This approach aims to bridge previously isolated observations in deep learning generalization.

fb71a64159ce408f9ee47091c53d6c0b2282e466.title: NFIG: Multi-Scale Autoregressive Image Generation via Frequency Ordering
fb71a64159ce408f9ee47091c53d6c0b2282e466.research_question: How can autoregressive image generation models be improved to better capture the hierarchical structure of images and enhance both generation quality and computational efficiency?
fb71a64159ce408f9ee47091c53d6c0b2282e466.hypothesis: Decomposing the image generation process into frequency-guided stages, where low-frequency components are generated first to capture global structure and higher-frequency details are progressively added, will improve image quality and reduce inference cost compared to conventional spatially-ordered autoregressive models.
fb71a64159ce408f9ee47091c53d6c0b2282e466.proposed_method: A novel multi-scale autoregressive image generation framework is proposed that operates via frequency ordering, termed Next-Frequency Image Generation (NFIG). The method begins by encoding images using a Frequency-guided Residual-quantized VAE (FR-VAE), which decomposes the image into multiple frequency bands using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and frequency masks. Low-frequency components, representing global structure, are generated first using fewer tokens, followed by the progressive synthesis of higher-frequency components that add local details. Each frequency band is quantized into discrete tokens via a vector quantization process, and a decoder-only transformer with block-wise causal attention autoregressively predicts token sequences for each frequency band in a coarse-to-fine manner. The frequency bands are merged using a frequency-guided composer to reconstruct the final image, ensuring information preservation and efficient hierarchical synthesis.
fb71a64159ce408f9ee47091c53d6c0b2282e466.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ILSVRC2012 ImageNet dataset, focusing on 256x256 image generation. The evaluation will use Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), Precision, and Recall as metrics. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art generative models, including GANs (e.g., BigGAN, StyleGAN-XL), diffusion models (e.g., DiT-L/2, LDM-4-G), mask-based models (e.g., MaskGIT, RCG), and autoregressive models (e.g., VAR, ViTVQ, XQGAN). The FR-VAE employs a VQGAN architecture with a DINO discriminator, and the transformer backbone is based on VAR with a depth of 16. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of frequency-guided quantization, discriminator choice, and sampling strategies. Models will be trained for up to 350 epochs, and inference speed as well as parameter efficiency will be benchmarked.
fb71a64159ce408f9ee47091c53d6c0b2282e466.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to incorporate explicit frequency analysis into autoregressive image generation, aligning the generation sequence with the natural spectral hierarchy of images. The introduction of the Frequency-guided Residual-quantized VAE enables efficient and information-preserving decomposition and quantization of image frequency components. The frequency-aware autoregressive generation paradigm improves both image quality and computational efficiency, achieving state-of-the-art results among autoregressive models and competitive performance across all generative model families. The approach also demonstrates superior parameter efficiency and faster inference compared to strong baselines.

fb76edcbfe53f0cbafa9502c7282d93c6a075a15.title: Learning Single-Index Models with Shallow Neural Networks
fb76edcbfe53f0cbafa9502c7282d93c6a075a15.research_question: Can shallow neural networks with frozen random biases efficiently learn single-index models in high-dimensional settings, achieving both computational and statistical guarantees comparable to specialized semi-parametric methods?
fb76edcbfe53f0cbafa9502c7282d93c6a075a15.hypothesis: Shallow neural networks with frozen random biases, trained via gradient flow, can recover the relevant one-dimensional subspace and approximate the unknown univariate link function in single-index models with near-optimal sample complexity, even in high-dimensional regimes.
fb76edcbfe53f0cbafa9502c7282d93c6a075a15.proposed_method: A shallow neural network architecture will be constructed where the biases of the neurons are initialized randomly and then frozen throughout training, while the weights are trained using gradient flow (continuous-time gradient descent). The network will use ReLU activation functions and random features, with the output modeled as a linear combination of these features. The empirical risk minimization will be performed using mean-squared error loss with Tikhonov (L2) regularization. Theoretical analysis will focus on the optimization landscape, leveraging Hermite polynomial decompositions for Gaussian input data, and will establish conditions under which the network can recover the hidden direction and approximate the link function. The method will analyze both the population and empirical loss landscapes, ensuring that the optimization remains tractable and generalizes well.
fb76edcbfe53f0cbafa9502c7282d93c6a075a15.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets generated according to the single-index model, with high-dimensional Gaussian input distributions. The network's performance will be compared to kernel methods and other semi-parametric baselines. Evaluation metrics will include mean-squared error on held-out test data, recovery accuracy of the hidden direction, and sample complexity required for successful learning. The experimental setup will vary the network width, regularization parameter, and the smoothness/information exponent of the link function to assess robustness and scalability. Additional ablation studies will examine the effect of the number of random features and the choice of activation function.
fb76edcbfe53f0cbafa9502c7282d93c6a075a15.novelty_claims: The proposed approach demonstrates that shallow neural networks with frozen random biases can achieve generalization and optimization guarantees for single-index models that match the near-optimal sample complexity of dedicated semi-parametric algorithms. The analysis provides new theoretical insights into the benign optimization landscape of such networks, even in the presence of non-smooth activations like ReLU, and shows that joint optimization of both layers leads to improved learning rates over previous one-step or kernel-based methods. This framework extends positive learning guarantees to a broader class of link functions characterized by arbitrary information exponents, and establishes the robustness of shallow neural networks as adaptive learners in high-dimensional settings.

fb79e0c6d26e1b6811ebda18c1c1da1227a74f62.title: Model Steering: Learning with a Reference Model Improves Generalization Bounds and Scaling Laws
fb79e0c6d26e1b6811ebda18c1c1da1227a74f62.research_question: How can leveraging a trained reference model guide and enhance the training of a target model to improve generalization, data efficiency, and scaling behavior in machine learning, particularly in large-scale multimodal pretraining?
fb79e0c6d26e1b6811ebda18c1c1da1227a74f62.hypothesis: Incorporating a reference model into the training process via a principled, theory-driven framework will improve generalization bounds, reduce sample complexity, and yield superior scaling laws compared to training without a reference model or using heuristic data selection approaches.
fb79e0c6d26e1b6811ebda18c1c1da1227a74f62.proposed_method: A novel framework for model steering is developed, wherein a trained reference model is used to guide the training of a target model through strategic data selection, sampling, or weighting. The approach is formalized via Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) applied to a shifted loss, termed the RHO loss, defined as the difference between the target and reference model losses on each data point. This leads to the minimization of a DRRho risk, for which new generalization bounds are derived, showing improved variance properties and sample efficiency. The method is instantiated for contrastive language-image pretraining (CLIP) by integrating the DRRho risk into the contrastive loss, resulting in the DRRho-CLIP algorithm. The optimization is performed using a stochastic algorithm (SogCLR) that efficiently tracks the required statistics and gradients, with pre-computed reference model embeddings to reduce computational overhead.
fb79e0c6d26e1b6811ebda18c1c1da1227a74f62.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on large-scale multimodal datasets, including CC12M, DFN-192M, and DFN-12M, with target models such as ViT-B/16 and ViT-B/32 trained from scratch. Reference models include OpenAI CLIP (ViT-B/32), ViT-B/16, and ViT-L/14, pretrained on various datasets. Baselines for comparison include standard CLIP training (OpenCLIP, FastCLIP), heuristic RHO-loss-based data selection methods (JEST, JEST Top-k), and knowledge distillation approaches (MobileCLIP, FastCLIP with distillation). Evaluation metrics include zero-shot classification accuracy on ImageNet-1K and average performance across 38 Datacomp benchmark tasks. Experiments systematically vary the amount of training data and reference model strength, and analyze scaling laws by fitting error rates versus compute. Variance of loss terms is empirically measured to verify theoretical predictions.
fb79e0c6d26e1b6811ebda18c1c1da1227a74f62.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to provide a theoretical foundation for model steering with a reference model, deriving generalization bounds and demonstrating reduced sample complexity. The DRRho-CLIP method introduces a principled, DRO-based approach to integrating reference models into contrastive pretraining, outperforming heuristic data selection and knowledge distillation baselines. The method achieves superior scaling laws and demonstrates the ability to surpass the reference model's performance, even with reduced training data. Extensive empirical results validate both the theoretical insights and practical advantages of the approach.

fb970ce4383a78ad52c641bc38815d78ad737aad.title: ReSearch: Learning to Reason with Search for LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
fb970ce4383a78ad52c641bc38815d78ad737aad.research_question: How can large language models be trained to effectively integrate external search operations into their reasoning processes, particularly for complex multi-hop question answering tasks, without relying on supervised data for reasoning steps?
fb970ce4383a78ad52c641bc38815d78ad737aad.hypothesis: Training large language models with reinforcement learning, where search operations are treated as integral components of the reasoning chain and guided by text-based thinking, will enable these models to autonomously learn effective multi-step reasoning with search, resulting in improved performance and generalizability on complex multi-hop question answering benchmarks.
fb970ce4383a78ad52c641bc38815d78ad737aad.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed in which large language models (LLMs) are trained to reason with search via reinforcement learning, specifically using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) as the learning algorithm. The reasoning process will be structured as an alternating sequence of text-based thinking, search queries, and retrieval results, with special tags (<think>, <search>, <result>, <answer>) guiding the model's output format. During training, the model will iteratively generate reasoning steps, invoke search operations when necessary, and incorporate retrieved factual information into subsequent reasoning. Retrieval results will be masked during loss calculation to prevent bias, and the model will be trained from scratch without any supervised data on reasoning chains. Reward modeling will be based on the correctness of the final answer (using F1 score) and adherence to the prescribed output format.
fb970ce4383a78ad52c641bc38815d78ad737aad.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multi-hop question answering benchmarks including HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, and Bamboogle. The models will be trained only on the training set of MuSiQue and evaluated on the full development or test sets of all benchmarks, discarding context documents and using only question-answer pairs. An open-ended retrieval environment based on Wikipedia (December 2018 snapshot) and FlashRAG toolkit will be used, with E5-base-v2 as the retriever and top-5 results retrieved per query. Baselines for comparison will include NoRAG (direct generation), NaiveRAG (retrieval-augmented generation), Iter-RetGen (iterative retrieval-generation), and IRCoT (interleaved retrieval and chain-of-thought). Evaluation metrics will include Exact Match (EM) and LLM-as-a-judge (LJ) using GPT-4o-mini for automatic answer scoring. Training will be performed on Qwen2.5-7B(-Instruct) and Qwen2.5-32B(-Instruct) models for two epochs.
fb970ce4383a78ad52c641bc38815d78ad737aad.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a reinforcement learning approach that enables LLMs to learn to reason with search from scratch, without any supervised data on reasoning steps. By integrating search operations as explicit components of the reasoning chain and using a structured output format, the method elicits advanced reasoning capabilities such as reflection and self-correction without pre-defined heuristics. The approach demonstrates strong generalizability across diverse benchmarks despite being trained on a single dataset, and achieves significant improvements over existing retrieval-augmented and multi-step reasoning baselines.

fb9f9e98d35340875905730e1a80221fec818944.title: Revisiting Neural Scaling Laws in Language and Vision
fb9f9e98d35340875905730e1a80221fec818944.research_question: How can neural scaling laws be estimated and validated more rigorously across language and vision domains, and what methodologies enable more accurate extrapolation of learning curves for deep learning models?
fb9f9e98d35340875905730e1a80221fec818944.hypothesis: A novel estimator for scaling laws, based on extrapolation error rather than interpolation fit, will yield more accurate predictions of model performance at larger scales across diverse architectures and domains.
fb9f9e98d35340875905730e1a80221fec818944.proposed_method: A new scaling law estimator will be developed, formulated as a parameterized function that generalizes existing power law models and incorporates a sigmoid-like transition to handle deviations from pure power law behavior. The estimator will model the learning curve as a convex combination of limiting performance and random-guessing performance, with learnable parameters for the transition, scaling exponent, and offset. Parameters will be fitted by minimizing a square-log loss between predicted and observed performance, using block coordinate descent and closed-form least squares where possible, with remaining parameters optimized via gradient descent. The methodology will explicitly validate scaling law parameters based on their extrapolation error—how well they predict performance on unseen, larger-scale data—rather than solely on interpolation fit to observed data.
fb9f9e98d35340875905730e1a80221fec818944.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across multiple domains: image classification (using BiT, ViT, and MLP-Mixer architectures pretrained on JFT-300M and evaluated on downstream datasets such as ImageNet, Birds200, CIFAR100, and Caltech101), neural machine translation (using encoder-decoder transformers and other architectures on standard NMT datasets), language modeling (using LaMDA models of varying sizes), and language tasks from the BIG-Bench benchmark. For each task, learning curves will be split into training and evaluation segments, with extrapolation error measured as the root mean square error (RMSE) of the log-loss between predicted and actual performance on held-out, larger-scale data. Baseline scaling law estimators (including standard power law and its variants) will be implemented for comparison. All experiments will be run on TPUs, and a benchmark dataset of 90 evaluation tasks will be released to facilitate reproducibility and further research.
fb9f9e98d35340875905730e1a80221fec818944.novelty_claims: The proposed estimator introduces a principled approach to scaling law validation based on extrapolation error, addressing the limitations of prior methods that rely on interpolation fit. The method generalizes existing scaling law models, enabling robust estimation even when learning curves deviate from pure power law behavior. Empirical results across diverse domains and architectures demonstrate that the new estimator consistently outperforms previous approaches in extrapolation accuracy. Additionally, the release of a comprehensive benchmark dataset supports future research in neural scaling laws.

fbadf4807040858a3112f337fdcc51890b75a7c4.title: BaB-ND: Long-Horizon Motion Planning with Branch-and-Bound and Neural Dynamics
fbadf4807040858a3112f337fdcc51890b75a7c4.research_question: How can long-horizon motion planning in robotic manipulation tasks be made more effective and scalable when using highly non-linear, neural-network-based dynamics models, especially in scenarios involving complex contact events, non-convex feasible regions, and diverse object interactions?
fbadf4807040858a3112f337fdcc51890b75a7c4.hypothesis: A branch-and-bound framework, combined with specialized branching heuristics and neural network-inspired bounding procedures, will enable more efficient and effective long-horizon motion planning over neural dynamics models than current sampling-based and MIP-based approaches.
fbadf4807040858a3112f337fdcc51890b75a7c4.proposed_method: A GPU-accelerated branch-and-bound (BaB) framework, termed BaB-ND, will be developed for trajectory optimization in manipulation tasks using neural dynamics models. The method will partition the high-dimensional action space into subdomains using novel branching heuristics that prioritize promising regions based on both objective values and sample distributions. For each subdomain, a modified bound propagation procedure, inspired by neural network verification techniques such as α,β-CROWN, will be used to efficiently estimate lower bounds of the objective, allowing for strategic pruning of unpromising regions. The search component will employ sampling-based optimizers (e.g., CEM), integrated with the bounding process, to find high-quality feasible action sequences. The framework will be designed to support various neural network architectures, including multilayer perceptrons and graph neural networks, and will leverage GPU parallelism for scalability.
fbadf4807040858a3112f337fdcc51890b75a7c4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of complex robotic manipulation tasks, including non-prehensile planar pushing with obstacles, object merging, rope routing, and object sorting, in both simulated and real-world settings. Neural dynamics models of varying architectures (MLP, GNN) will be trained for each scenario. Baseline comparisons will include sampling-based methods such as Cross-Entropy Method (CEM), Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI), and projected gradient descent (GD), as well as MIP-based approaches where tractable. Evaluation metrics will include the best objective value found in open-loop planning (simulation) and closed-loop execution performance (final cost or success rate) in real-world trials. Additional synthetic high-dimensional optimization problems will be used to assess scalability and optimality.
fbadf4807040858a3112f337fdcc51890b75a7c4.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a general and scalable branch-and-bound approach for long-horizon planning over neural dynamics models, featuring novel branching heuristics and a specialized bounding procedure adapted from neural network verification but tailored for planning objectives. The method systematically explores the action space, enabling superior performance and scalability compared to existing sampling-based and MIP-based methods. It is broadly applicable across manipulation tasks with diverse neural network architectures and demonstrates the ability to handle complex, contact-rich, and deformable-object scenarios.

fbc34d83068505fb0a0df59bde1ea26f17ba90b4.title: Embeddings as Epistemic States: Limitations on the Use of Pooling Operators for Accumulating Knowledge
fbc34d83068505fb0a0df59bde1ea26f17ba90b4.research_question: Under what conditions can standard pooling operators used in neural network architectures faithfully aggregate knowledge represented as epistemic states in vector embeddings, and what are the implications for reasoning tasks, especially those involving propositional logic and non-monotonic inference?
fbc34d83068505fb0a0df59bde1ea26f17ba90b4.hypothesis: Standard pooling operators can satisfy the epistemic pooling principle only under specific constraints on embedding dimensionality and structure, and these constraints fundamentally limit the ability of neural network models to perform certain types of logical reasoning using pooled embeddings.
fbc34d83068505fb0a0df59bde1ea26f17ba90b4.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to formalize the notion of embeddings as epistemic states, where each embedding encodes a set of properties or possible worlds. The epistemic pooling principle will be defined, requiring that pooling embeddings corresponds to the union of their encoded knowledge. Several standard pooling operators—average, summation, max-pooling, and Hadamard (component-wise product)—will be analyzed to determine under what constraints (e.g., embedding dimensionality, non-negativity, boundedness) they can satisfy this principle. Both strict and weak semantic variants of the principle will be considered, and the realizability of the principle will be characterized for each operator. The analysis will extend to weighted epistemic states to address non-monotonic reasoning, identifying suitable pooling operators for such settings.
fbc34d83068505fb0a0df59bde1ea26f17ba90b4.experiment_details: Experiments will involve both theoretical analysis and illustrative toy examples, such as message-passing in Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) on graphs representing relationships among research topics, articles, researchers, and committees. Embeddings will be constructed to represent sets of properties or possible worlds, and pooling will be performed using the operators under study. The ability to verify propositional formulas using linear scoring functions on pooled embeddings will be evaluated. Scenarios with background knowledge and non-monotonic reasoning will be included, using weighted embeddings and possibilistic logic. Evaluation metrics will include the faithfulness of knowledge aggregation (i.e., satisfaction of the epistemic pooling principle) and the ability to perform logical inference via linear classifiers. Baselines will include standard GNN pooling strategies and neuro-symbolic reasoning approaches.
fbc34d83068505fb0a0df59bde1ea26f17ba90b4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal analysis of the epistemic pooling principle for standard pooling operators, revealing necessary conditions on embedding dimensionality and structure for faithful knowledge aggregation. It establishes new theoretical limitations on the use of pooling in neural architectures for reasoning tasks, particularly highlighting why certain pooling choices (e.g., averaging, summation) are fundamentally incompatible with linear reasoning over propositional formulas. The work identifies max-pooling (with bounded embeddings) and Hadamard pooling (with non-negative embeddings) as uniquely suitable for some reasoning tasks, and extends the analysis to weighted epistemic states for non-monotonic reasoning, where max-pooling emerges as the preferred operator. These insights clarify the empirical underperformance of GNNs in reasoning tasks and provide guidance for the design of neural-symbolic models.

fbebb1a5d72aec2a6b13fc909f781f6ba9b04925.title: Diffusion Self-Guidance for Controllable Image Generation
fbebb1a5d72aec2a6b13fc909f781f6ba9b04925.research_question: How can more granular and disentangled control over the properties of objects and concepts in images generated by large-scale text-to-image diffusion models be achieved, beyond what is possible through text prompts alone?
fbebb1a5d72aec2a6b13fc909f781f6ba9b04925.hypothesis: It is possible to achieve fine-grained, zero-shot control over the position, size, shape, and appearance of objects and concepts in generated images by leveraging and guiding the internal attention maps and activations of pretrained diffusion models, without requiring auxiliary models or additional training.
fbebb1a5d72aec2a6b13fc909f781f6ba9b04925.proposed_method: A novel self-guidance framework will be developed that steers the sampling process of pretrained text-to-image diffusion models by imposing constraints on their internal representations—specifically, attention maps and intermediate activations. Key object properties such as position, size, shape, and appearance will be extracted from the model's attention channels and activation tensors, and differentiable energy functions will be formulated to guide these properties toward user-specified or reference-derived targets during sampling. The method will allow for both absolute and relative manipulations, such as moving or resizing objects, and will support the composition of properties from multiple images, enabling complex edits like merging appearances or layouts. The approach will also be extended to enable editing of real images by running them through the diffusion model's denoising process to extract and manipulate their internal representations.
fbebb1a5d72aec2a6b13fc909f781f6ba9b04925.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Imagen diffusion model, generating 1024×1024 images. The method will be evaluated on a variety of challenging image manipulation tasks, including moving, resizing, and restyling objects, transferring appearance or layout between images, and compositional generation from multiple sources. Baselines will include prior state-of-the-art methods such as ControlNet and Prompt-to-Prompt, with comparisons focusing on the fidelity and disentanglement of object control. Evaluation metrics will include qualitative visual assessment, user studies, and, where applicable, quantitative measures of edit accuracy (e.g., spatial alignment, appearance similarity). Additional experiments will demonstrate the method's ability to reconstruct and edit real images, and to manipulate non-object concepts such as adjectives and verbs.
fbebb1a5d72aec2a6b13fc909f781f6ba9b04925.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a zero-shot, training-free approach for controllable image generation by directly leveraging the internal representations of pretrained diffusion models. It enables disentangled and granular manipulation of object properties—including position, size, shape, and appearance—without auxiliary models, fine-tuning, or paired data. The framework supports compositional editing, appearance transfer from real images, and manipulation of arbitrary concepts named in the prompt, significantly expanding the controllability and flexibility of diffusion-based image generation.

fc13fa57b21fa9882b821cbb5fa910451f35be7e.title: Mechanism Design for Collaborative Normal Mean Estimation
fc13fa57b21fa9882b821cbb5fa910451f35be7e.research_question: How can mechanisms be designed to incentivize strategic agents to collaboratively estimate the mean of a normal distribution, ensuring truthful data sharing and sufficient data collection, while minimizing the combined estimation error and data collection costs?
fc13fa57b21fa9882b821cbb5fa910451f35be7e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a mechanism can be constructed which is Nash incentive compatible, individually rational, and achieves a social penalty (sum of estimation errors and data collection costs) within a constant factor of the global minimum, even in the presence of strategic agents who may under-collect or fabricate data.
fc13fa57b21fa9882b821cbb5fa910451f35be7e.proposed_method: A novel mechanism, termed C3D (Cross-Check and Corrupt based on Difference), will be developed for collaborative normal mean estimation among m agents. Each agent collects and submits a dataset, which may be fabricated or altered. The mechanism pools the data from other agents and splits it into two subsets: one is returned as is, while the other is corrupted by adding Gaussian noise proportional to the difference between the agent's submitted data and the pooled data. The allocation to each agent consists of the clean subset, the corrupted subset, and the variance of the added noise. Agents are recommended to truthfully submit their collected data and use a weighted average estimator, where weights are determined by the inverse variances of the data sources (including the added corruption). The mechanism is designed so that the optimal strategy for each agent, given the strategies of others, is to collect a sufficient amount of data and report it truthfully, as deviation leads to increased corruption and higher penalty.
fc13fa57b21fa9882b821cbb5fa910451f35be7e.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis will be conducted to prove Nash incentive compatibility, individual rationality, and efficiency (bounded price of stability) of the proposed mechanism. The mechanism's performance will be evaluated in both the standard normal mean estimation setting and in high-dimensional, bounded-variance, non-Gaussian settings. Comparisons will be made to baseline mechanisms such as naive pooling (with and without minimum data requirements) and mechanisms that do not account for data fabrication. Evaluation metrics include the social penalty (sum of estimation errors and data collection costs), Nash equilibrium properties, and the efficiency ratio relative to the global minimum. Special cases with restricted agent strategy spaces (no fabrication, or forced estimator deployment) will also be analyzed to demonstrate the mechanism's robustness and optimality under various constraints.
fc13fa57b21fa9882b821cbb5fa910451f35be7e.novelty_claims: The proposed mechanism introduces a new corruption-based approach to deter free-riding and data fabrication in collaborative estimation, using a corruption level that is adaptively set based on the agent's deviation from the collective data. The design of a minimax optimal estimator for the corrupted data is novel and essential for achieving incentive compatibility. The mechanism achieves Nash equilibrium, individual rationality, and a social penalty within a factor of two of the global minimum, even when agents can fabricate data.
