Extensions to high-dimensional and non-Gaussian settings retain these properties with only minor losses in guarantees. The approach provides the first mechanism for this setting that is robust to both under-collection and data fabrication by strategic agents, and demonstrates that near-optimal collaboration is possible without monetary payments.

fc4c380102d6f72657d1ab54dffd6be536bb01c7.title: A Survey on Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
fc4c380102d6f72657d1ab54dffd6be536bb01c7.research_question: How can hallucinations in large vision-language models (LVLMs) be systematically evaluated, analyzed, and mitigated to improve the factual alignment between visual content and generated textual outputs across diverse tasks and modalities?
fc4c380102d6f72657d1ab54dffd6be536bb01c7.hypothesis: Hallucinations in LVLMs can be significantly reduced through targeted improvements in data quality, model architecture (including vision encoders and modality alignment modules), training objectives, and post-processing strategies, leading to more faithful and reliable multimodal systems.
fc4c380102d6f72657d1ab54dffd6be536bb01c7.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to investigate, evaluate, and mitigate hallucinations in LVLMs. The approach will begin by defining and categorizing hallucination types (e.g., object, attribute, relation, judgment, and description errors) and identifying their unique challenges in multimodal contexts. A suite of evaluation methodologies will be constructed, including both generative and discriminative benchmarks, leveraging handcrafted pipelines (e.g., object comparison, atomic fact extraction) and model-based end-to-end assessments (e.g., LLM-based scoring, hallucination detection datasets). Root causes of hallucination will be systematically analyzed by probing the effects of training data biases, vision encoder limitations (such as low resolution and lack of fine-grained semantics), modality misalignment, and language model decoding strategies. Based on this analysis, targeted mitigation strategies will be proposed, including data balancing and enrichment, scaling up vision resolution, enhancing connection modules, optimizing alignment training, decoding strategies, and post-processing correction modules.
fc4c380102d6f72657d1ab54dffd6be536bb01c7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a diverse set of LVLMs and a variety of publicly available and custom-built benchmarks, such as POPE, NOPE, CIEM, M-HalDetect, GAVIE, FAITHScore, HaELM, MMHal-Bench, and AMBER. Datasets will include large-scale image-text pairs with detailed annotations for objects, attributes, and relations, as well as instruction-following and negative sample sets. Baseline models will include state-of-the-art LVLMs (e.g., LLaVA, MiniGPT-4, BLIP-2, InternVL) and existing hallucination mitigation techniques. Evaluation metrics will cover accuracy, relevancy, faithfulness scores, and human preference alignment. Experimental setups will compare the effectiveness of different mitigation strategies (e.g., data augmentation, vision encoder scaling, alignment training, post-processing) in reducing hallucination rates and improving factual consistency.
fc4c380102d6f72657d1ab54dffd6be536bb01c7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified and systematic framework for evaluating, analyzing, and mitigating hallucinations in LVLMs, encompassing both cognitive (judgment/description) and semantic (object/attribute/relation) perspectives. It advances the field by integrating diverse evaluation methodologies, constructing comprehensive benchmarks, and providing a taxonomy of root causes specific to multimodal hallucinations. The proposed mitigation strategies are tailored to the unique challenges of LVLMs, including vision-language alignment, high-resolution visual processing, and context-aware decoding. The research aims to bridge the gap between current LVLM capabilities and the need for reliable, faithful multimodal AI systems.

fc5e3cc10ee2f901150210e533adc9255e1f0cca.title: Improving the Privacy and Practicality of Objective Perturbation for Differentially Private Linear Learners
fc5e3cc10ee2f901150210e533adc9255e1f0cca.research_question: How can the privacy and computational practicality of objective perturbation mechanisms for differentially private linear learners be improved to make them competitive with or superior to differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD) in unconstrained convex generalized linear model (GLM) settings?
fc5e3cc10ee2f901150210e533adc9255e1f0cca.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by developing tighter privacy analyses and novel computational tools, objective perturbation mechanisms can achieve privacy-utility trade-offs and computational efficiency that are competitive with or superior to DP-SGD, particularly when accounting for the privacy cost of hyperparameter tuning.
fc5e3cc10ee2f901150210e533adc9255e1f0cca.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a revamped objective perturbation mechanism for differentially private empirical risk minimization in unconstrained convex GLMs. The approach leverages modern privacy accounting tools, including privacy profiles for (ϵ,δ)-DP and Rényi Differential Privacy (RDP), to provide tighter privacy guarantees. A novel extension of the Approximate Minima Perturbation (AMP) framework is developed, enabling the mechanism to handle loss functions with unbounded gradients by incorporating gradient clipping and blackbox optimization. The algorithm perturbs the objective function with Gaussian noise, solves for an approximate minimizer using efficient convex optimization (e.g., L-BFGS or SAG), and releases the result with an additional output perturbation step to ensure privacy. The method achieves improved computational complexity, reducing the number of gradient evaluations to O(n log n), and allows hyperparameter tuning of the optimizer without additional privacy cost, provided these parameters are independent of the privacy guarantee.
fc5e3cc10ee2f901150210e533adc9255e1f0cca.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on binary classification tasks using datasets such as Adult, Synthetic-L, Synthetic-H, and Gisette, with features preprocessed to have unit ℓ2-norm. The proposed algorithm (Algorithm 1) will be compared against two baselines: 'dishonest' DP-SGD (which ignores the privacy cost of hyperparameter tuning) and 'honest' DP-SGD (which accounts for this cost using private selection algorithms and RDP bounds). Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy across varying privacy budgets (ϵ ∈ {0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0}) with δ fixed at 10⁻⁵. Hyperparameters such as learning rate, batch size, and optimizer type will be systematically varied, with special attention to ensuring fair comparison by isolating the effect of hyperparameter tuning. Results will be averaged over multiple trials, and statistical significance will be assessed using standard error bars.
fc5e3cc10ee2f901150210e533adc9255e1f0cca.novelty_claims: The proposal claims several innovations: (1) the introduction of improved (ϵ,δ)-DP bounds for objective perturbation using privacy profiles and dominating pairs of distributions, enabling tight composition and amplification by subsampling; (2) a novel RDP analysis for objective perturbation, facilitating fair empirical comparison with DP-SGD under honest hyperparameter tuning; (3) correction of a long-standing oversight in the privacy analysis of objective perturbation, particularly regarding the dependence between the noise vector and the private minimizer; (4) extension of the AMP framework to handle loss functions with unbounded gradients via algorithmic gradient clipping; and (5) a computational guarantee that achieves optimal excess risk bounds in O(n log n) time, improving upon the O(n²) complexity of DP-SGD.

fc690dd28d9a08614e7170fe4979e094710116bc.title: Diffusion-TS: Interpretable Diffusion for General Time Series Generation
fc690dd28d9a08614e7170fe4979e094710116bc.research_question: How can high-quality, interpretable, and flexible generative models for multivariate time series be developed to address both unconditional and conditional generation tasks, such as imputation and forecasting, across diverse and potentially irregular real-world datasets?
fc690dd28d9a08614e7170fe4979e094710116bc.hypothesis: A diffusion-based generative framework that explicitly disentangles temporal components (trend, seasonality, and noise) using a transformer-based encoder-decoder architecture, combined with a Fourier-based training objective, will yield interpretable and realistic time series samples, and can be flexibly adapted to conditional tasks without architectural modifications.
fc690dd28d9a08614e7170fe4979e094710116bc.proposed_method: A novel generative framework, Diffusion-TS, will be developed based on denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) for time series data. The core architecture will utilize an encoder-decoder transformer, where the decoder is designed as a deep decomposition network with interpretable layers that separately model trend (via polynomial regression), seasonality (via Fourier synthetic layers selecting top-K frequency bases), and residual error. During the reverse diffusion process, the model will be trained to reconstruct the clean time series sample directly at each step, rather than the noise, using a composite loss that includes both time-domain and frequency-domain (Fourier-based) terms. For conditional generation (e.g., imputation, forecasting), a reconstruction-based sampling strategy will be incorporated, leveraging gradients from a classifier to guide the diffusion process towards samples consistent with observed or target values, without requiring any change to the model parameters.
fc690dd28d9a08614e7170fe4979e094710116bc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four real-world datasets (Stocks, ETTh, Energy, fMRI) and two simulated datasets (Sines, MuJoCo), covering a range of domains and time series characteristics. The evaluation will include both unconditional generation (synthesizing new time series) and conditional tasks (imputation and forecasting under various missing data regimes). Baselines for comparison will include TimeVAE, Diffwave, TimeGAN, Cot-GAN, DiffTime, CSDI, SSSD, and TLAE. Metrics will include Discriminative Score, Predictive Score, Context-FID, and Correlational Score, assessing distributional similarity, temporal/feature dependency, and downstream predictive utility. Additional experiments will test robustness under data scarcity (cold start) and irregular settings, and ablation studies will isolate the contributions of the Fourier loss, interpretability, and transformer components.
fc690dd28d9a08614e7170fe4979e094710116bc.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces interpretable seasonal-trend decomposition directly into the diffusion model architecture for time series, enabling explicit disentanglement of temporal components. The use of a Fourier-based loss in the diffusion training objective is novel for improving both reconstruction accuracy and interpretability. The method supports plug-and-play conditional generation (imputation, forecasting) without architectural changes, and demonstrates robustness to long-term, high-dimensional, and irregular time series settings. The approach achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks and provides explainable outputs, addressing key limitations of prior diffusion-based and autoregressive models.

fc6a2f7478f68adefd69e2071f27e38aa1647f2f.title: Qwen-VL: A Versatile Vision-Language Model for Understanding, Localization, Text Reading, and Beyond
fc6a2f7478f68adefd69e2071f27e38aa1647f2f.research_question: How can a large-scale vision-language model be developed to achieve versatile and fine-grained understanding, localization, text reading, and instruction-following across multiple languages and diverse multimodal tasks?
fc6a2f7478f68adefd69e2071f27e38aa1647f2f.hypothesis: A vision-language model built upon a strong language model foundation, equipped with a carefully designed visual encoder, position-aware adapter, and trained on a large, multilingual, and multimodal corpus with a multi-stage training pipeline, will achieve state-of-the-art performance on a broad range of vision-language tasks, including fine-grained localization and text reading.
fc6a2f7478f68adefd69e2071f27e38aa1647f2f.proposed_method: A vision-language model will be constructed by augmenting a pre-trained large language model (Qwen-7B) with a visual processing branch. The visual encoder will utilize a Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture, initialized from OpenCLIP, to extract image features, which are then compressed via a position-aware vision-language adapter using a cross-attention mechanism with trainable query embeddings and 2D positional encodings. The model will process interleaved image-text sequences, with special tokens marking image and bounding box regions, enabling both global and fine-grained visual understanding. Training will proceed in three stages: (1) pre-training the vision encoder and adapter on a large, cleaned, multilingual image-text corpus while freezing the language model, (2) multi-task pre-training on high-quality annotated datasets for captioning, VQA, grounding, OCR, and autoregressive text, and (3) supervised instruction fine-tuning for enhanced dialogue and instruction-following capabilities, including multi-image and localization tasks. The final model will support both English and Chinese, handle multiple images, and output fine-grained region descriptions and bounding boxes.
fc6a2f7478f68adefd69e2071f27e38aa1647f2f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a comprehensive suite of vision-language benchmarks. Datasets for training include LAION-en, LAION-zh, DataComp, Coyo, CC12M, CC3M, SBU, COCOCaption, GQA, VGQA, VQAv2, DVQA, OCR-VQA, DocVQA, GRIT, Visual Genome, RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg, and synthetic OCR data. Evaluation will cover image captioning (Nocaps, Flickr30K), general VQA (VQAv2, OKVQA, GQA, ScienceQA-Img, VizWiz), text-oriented VQA (TextVQA, DocVQA, ChartQA, AI2Diagram, OCR-VQA), referring expression comprehension (RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg, GRIT), and instruction-following (TouchStone, SEED-Bench, MME). Metrics include CIDEr for captioning, accuracy for VQA and text tasks, and benchmark-specific scores for instruction-following. Baselines will include both generalist and specialist models such as Flamingo, BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, Shikra, Unified-IO, mPLUG-DocOwl, and others. Both zero-shot and few-shot settings will be evaluated, with ablations on input resolution, adapter query count, and attention mechanisms.
fc6a2f7478f68adefd69e2071f27e38aa1647f2f.novelty_claims: The proposed model introduces a concise yet effective architecture that tightly integrates a language-aligned visual encoder and a position-aware adapter with a large language model, enabling fine-grained visual grounding and text reading. The multi-stage training pipeline leverages a vast, cleaned, multilingual multimodal corpus and diverse high-quality annotations, supporting instruction-following, multi-image input, and multilingual dialogue. The model achieves state-of-the-art or top-tier results across a wide range of vision-language benchmarks and settings, surpassing previous open-source generalist models in both accuracy and versatility, and is released to facilitate further research in the community.

fc7c347df3b1988228ab8180be6de98e82ba598f.title: Towards Memorization-Free Diffusion Models
fc7c347df3b1988228ab8180be6de98e82ba598f.research_question: How can diffusion models be guided to prevent memorization of training data during inference, thereby mitigating privacy and copyright risks, while preserving high image quality and text alignment across a variety of generation tasks?
fc7c347df3b1988228ab8180be6de98e82ba598f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a unified framework employing targeted guidance strategies, each addressing distinct causes of memorization, combined with an automatic detection mechanism for memorization during inference, can effectively eliminate memorization in diffusion models without significant loss in image quality or text alignment.
fc7c347df3b1988228ab8180be6de98e82ba598f.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces Anti-Memorization Guidance (AMG), a comprehensive framework for diffusion models that integrates three specialized guidance strategies: despecification guidance, caption deduplication guidance, and dissimilarity guidance. Despecification guidance adaptively reduces the specificity of user prompts during inference, steering generations away from outputs that are overly similar to memorized training data. Caption deduplication guidance leverages the identification of duplicated captions in the training set to guide the model away from generating images that match these memorized pairs. Dissimilarity guidance operates by directly minimizing the similarity (measured via pixel-level or object-level metrics) between generated images and their nearest training samples, using gradient-based updates in the diffusion process. An automatic detection system continuously monitors similarity scores during each inference step, activating the appropriate guidance only when the risk of memorization is detected, and employing a dynamic (parabolic) threshold to balance intervention with preservation of output utility.
fc7c347df3b1988228ab8180be6de98e82ba598f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on pretrained Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM) and Stable Diffusion across various generation tasks, including unconditional, class-conditional, and text-conditional image synthesis. Datasets such as CIFAR-10 and LAION5B will be used, with memorization measured via pixel-level normalized L2 distance and object-level SSCD embedding similarity. Baselines for comparison include existing memorization mitigation techniques (e.g., concept ablation, randomization, deduplication, and differential privacy approaches). Evaluation metrics will include the proportion of generated images exceeding memorization thresholds, FID for image quality, and CLIP score for text-image alignment. Experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by reimplementing baselines under consistent conditions, and ablation studies will assess the contribution of each guidance component and the effect of dynamic versus constant guidance scheduling.
fc7c347df3b1988228ab8180be6de98e82ba598f.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to unify and automate multiple targeted guidance strategies for eliminating memorization in diffusion models, addressing image duplication, caption duplication, and prompt specificity. It introduces an automatic, step-wise detection and selective guidance mechanism that applies interventions only when necessary, preserving the original sampling process and maximizing output utility. The method is model-agnostic, requiring no retraining or fine-tuning, and is compatible with both conditional and unconditional diffusion models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this approach achieves complete eradication of memorization with minimal or no degradation in image quality or text alignment, outperforming prior methods in both privacy and utility.

fc7ee1828030a818f52518022a39f6a3ada60222.title: Scalable Extraction of Training Data from (Production) Language Models
fc7ee1828030a818f52518022a39f6a3ada60222.research_question: How much training data can be efficiently extracted from large language models by adversaries without prior knowledge of the training dataset, and how does this extractability scale across open-source, semi-open, and production models?
fc7ee1828030a818f52518022a39f6a3ada60222.hypothesis: Large language models, including those with alignment and RLHF, retain substantial amounts of extractable memorized training data that can be recovered at scale by adversaries using efficient prompting strategies, even when the training data is not publicly available.
fc7ee1828030a818f52518022a39f6a3ada60222.proposed_method: A scalable extraction methodology will be developed to measure and maximize the amount of training data that can be extracted from language models through black-box querying. The approach will involve generating a large number of prompts, including both random sequences and specially designed divergence prompts, to elicit verbatim outputs from the model. Outputs will be matched against a massive auxiliary dataset constructed from the union of several public web-scale corpora (e.g., The Pile, RedPajama, RefinedWeb, Dolma) using efficient data structures such as suffix arrays to identify memorized sequences. For models with dialog alignment, specialized prompting strategies will be devised to bypass alignment and trigger the model to revert to pre-training-like generation, thus increasing the likelihood of extracting memorized data. The methodology will also include statistical extrapolation techniques (e.g., Good-Turing estimator) to estimate the total quantity of extractable memorization beyond the observed samples.
fc7ee1828030a818f52518022a39f6a3ada60222.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of language models, including open-source models (e.g., Pythia, GPT-Neo, RedPajama), semi-open models (e.g., LLaMA, Falcon, Mistral, OPT), and production models (e.g., ChatGPT/gpt-3.5-turbo). For open and semi-open models, 1 billion tokens will be generated per model, and outputs will be matched against their known or reconstructed training datasets to identify unique memorized 50-token sequences. For closed models, a large auxiliary dataset will serve as a proxy for the unknown training set. Baseline attacks (random prompting) and advanced divergence attacks (for aligned models) will be compared. Evaluation metrics include the rate of memorized token emission, the number of unique memorized sequences, and extrapolated total memorization. The setup will involve large-scale distributed querying and high-throughput matching, with careful annotation of personally identifiable information (PII) and qualitative analysis of extracted content.
fc7ee1828030a818f52518022a39f6a3ada60222.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a scalable, automated framework for training data extraction that operates at terabyte-scale and can be applied to both open and closed language models. It demonstrates that current alignment and RLHF techniques do not eliminate extractable memorization and reveals that practical attacks can recover orders of magnitude more training data than previously reported. The methodology unifies and advances prior approaches by enabling efficient, large-scale evaluation of extractable memorization, and provides the first evidence that production models like ChatGPT can emit gigabytes of training data, including PII, through efficient prompting strategies.

fc8fb7812154bca2114eca48eadcdc1cd78a7d24.title: Staggered Environment Resets Improve Massively Parallel On-Policy Reinforcement Learning
fc8fb7812154bca2114eca48eadcdc1cd78a7d24.research_question: How can the stability, sample efficiency, and scalability of massively parallel on-policy reinforcement learning be improved, particularly when using short rollouts in environments with long task horizons?
fc8fb7812154bca2114eca48eadcdc1cd78a7d24.hypothesis: Introducing staggered resets—where parallel environments are initialized and reset at diverse points within the task horizon—will mitigate cyclical nonstationarity in training batches, leading to more stable learning, improved sample efficiency, faster convergence, and better scalability compared to standard synchronous resets.
fc8fb7812154bca2114eca48eadcdc1cd78a7d24.proposed_method: A novel environment interaction protocol is proposed for massively parallel on-policy reinforcement learning, termed staggered resets. Before training, each parallel environment is independently advanced by a specific offset, sampled from a set of discrete intervals spanning the task horizon, so that environments begin at different effective timesteps. This can be implemented by dividing environments into groups and assigning each group a unique offset, typically in multiples of the rollout length K, ensuring broad temporal coverage. During training, environments proceed synchronously for K steps per rollout, but due to their staggered starting points, the aggregated batch contains transitions from a wide range of episode segments. Resets are managed in a batched manner: environments are reset either at the end of their horizon or upon early termination, but always in alignment with their group’s reset schedule to maintain temporal diversity and minimize computational overhead. Policy and value function updates are performed using these temporally diverse batches, promoting a more stationary and representative data distribution.
fc8fb7812154bca2114eca48eadcdc1cd78a7d24.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both illustrative toy environments and high-dimensional robotics tasks. Toy environments will allow controlled variation of factors such as task horizon, reset stochasticity, and skill gating, enabling detailed analysis of when staggered resets are most beneficial. High-dimensional experiments will utilize GPU-accelerated robotics benchmarks from ManiSkill3 (e.g., StackCube-v1, PushT, TwoRobotPushCube, Unitree Transport Box, Anymal Reach C, and MS-HumanoidWalk) and AllegroKuka manipulation tasks. Baselines will include standard synchronous reset protocols with both long and short rollouts, and experiments will be run using state-of-the-art on-policy algorithms such as Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Split and Aggregate Policy Gradients (SAPG). Evaluation metrics will include sample efficiency, wall-clock convergence time, final policy performance (success rate or reward), and training stability, with results averaged over multiple random seeds. Additional analyses will visualize state visitation distributions and assess scalability as the number of parallel environments increases.
fc8fb7812154bca2114eca48eadcdc1cd78a7d24.novelty_claims: The proposed approach precisely identifies and formulates the problem of cyclical batch nonstationarity arising from synchronous resets and short rollouts in massively parallel RL. Staggered resets are introduced as a simple, algorithm-agnostic, and easily implementable mechanism that ensures temporal diversity within training batches, directly addressing this nonstationarity. The method is empirically shown to significantly improve sample efficiency, convergence speed, final performance, and scalability with increasing parallelism, and is validated across both PPO and SAPG, confirming its generality. The work provides a thorough characterization of environmental conditions where staggered resets are most effective and demonstrates robust improvements over existing data collection protocols.

fc90e6147b7184dc4ce9784dfd219fb3413e6b3a.title: Random features models: a way to study the success of naive imputation
fc90e6147b7184dc4ce9784dfd219fb3413e6b3a.research_question: How does naive (constant) imputation, particularly zero-imputation, impact the predictive performance of linear models in the presence of missing data across varying input dimensions, and under different missing data mechanisms?
fc90e6147b7184dc4ce9784dfd219fb3413e6b3a.hypothesis: Naive imputation, such as zero-imputation, induces negligible bias in both very low and high-dimensional linear models, especially under missing completely at random (MCAR) scenarios, and remains competitive with more sophisticated imputation strategies even in certain non-MCAR settings.
fc90e6147b7184dc4ce9784dfd219fb3413e6b3a.proposed_method: A rigorous theoretical framework will be developed using random features models, where input data are generated as random projections from a latent space of arbitrary (possibly infinite) dimension. The output variable will be modeled as a linear function of the latent variable plus Gaussian noise. Missing data will be introduced under the MCAR assumption, with each input feature observed independently with probability ρ. Missing entries will be imputed by zero (or the mean for non-centered data), and the predictive performance of linear models trained on these imputed datasets will be analyzed. Theoretical analysis will include deriving Bayes risks for complete, missing, and zero-imputed data, as well as finite-sample generalization bounds for stochastic gradient descent (SGD) applied to imputed data. Extensions will be considered for more complex missing data mechanisms (e.g., MNAR) and infinite-dimensional latent spaces.
fc90e6147b7184dc4ce9784dfd219fb3413e6b3a.experiment_details: Experiments will involve both theoretical derivations and empirical simulations. Synthetic datasets will be generated according to the random features model, with varying numbers of observed features (d), latent dimensions (p), and missingness rates (ρ). Baseline comparisons will include the Bayes optimal predictor (with complete data), predictors trained on missing data without imputation, and those using zero-imputation. Evaluation metrics will focus on the excess risk (difference in prediction error relative to the Bayes risk) and generalization bounds. The SGD algorithm will be implemented with Polyak-Ruppert averaging, and its performance will be assessed in both low- and high-dimensional regimes, as well as under different missing data mechanisms.
fc90e6147b7184dc4ce9784dfd219fb3413e6b3a.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides the first comprehensive theoretical characterization of the bias and risk induced by naive imputation in linear models with random features, across both low- and high-dimensional regimes. It establishes finite-sample generalization bounds for SGD on zero-imputed data and demonstrates that naive imputation remains competitive not only in high dimensions but also in very low-dimensional settings. The framework extends previous results by moving beyond low-rank input structures to arbitrary and infinite-dimensional latent spaces, and by relaxing the MCAR assumption to more general missing data scenarios. These contributions offer new insights into when and why simple imputation strategies can be effective for predictive modeling.

fcb6397d3ee54160901787e21adbf30158ed83f3.title: EDiT: A Local-SGD-Based Efficient Distributed Training Method for Large Language Models
fcb6397d3ee54160901787e21adbf30158ed83f3.research_question: How can distributed training of large language models be made more efficient, stable, and scalable in the presence of communication bottlenecks, stragglers, and heterogeneous or elastic computational environments?
fcb6397d3ee54160901787e21adbf30158ed83f3.hypothesis: Integrating a tailored Local SGD approach with model sharding and introducing a pseudo gradient penalty strategy will significantly improve the efficiency, stability, and scalability of distributed large language model training, outperforming existing synchronous and Local SGD-based methods, especially in heterogeneous and large-scale settings.
fcb6397d3ee54160901787e21adbf30158ed83f3.proposed_method: A novel distributed training framework, EDiT, is proposed, which combines Local SGD with model sharding on a two-dimensional device mesh. Model parameters are fully sharded along one dimension and synchronized along another, with layer-wise parameter synchronization performed during the forward pass. A prefetch strategy is employed to overlap communication and computation, reducing both communication and memory overhead. To address instability from noisy or low-quality data, a pseudo gradient penalty strategy is introduced, consisting of anomaly elimination (using EMA z-scores), weighted averaging of pseudo-gradients based on their norms, and gradient clipping. An asynchronous variant, A-EDiT, is also developed, where synchronization is triggered by a fixed time interval rather than fixed steps, allowing faster workers to proceed independently and addressing the issue of consistent stragglers in heterogeneous clusters.
fcb6397d3ee54160901787e21adbf30158ed83f3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Llama models of various scales (350M, 1B, 3B, 7B) on both the public FineWeb-Edu dataset and a diverse in-house pre-training dataset. Baselines will include standard mini-batch training, Post Local SGD, DiLoCo, and CO2/CO2* methods. Evaluation metrics will include training loss, validation perplexity (PPL), throughput (tokens/sec), TFLOPS, and performance on public benchmarks such as MMLU, ARC-E, ARC-C, HellaSwag, PIQA, CommonSense-QA, OpenBookQA, and WinoGrande. Experiments will be performed on clusters with up to 64 Nvidia A100 GPUs arranged in an 8x8 device mesh. Additional experiments will simulate straggler scenarios, bandwidth constraints, and elastic training by dynamically varying the number of workers, with ablation studies to assess the impact of each component of the pseudo gradient penalty strategy.
fcb6397d3ee54160901787e21adbf30158ed83f3.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a hierarchical device mesh-based distributed training strategy that integrates Local SGD with model sharding, enabling efficient large-scale LLM training. Layer-wise parameter synchronization during the forward pass with prefetching allows overlapping of communication and computation, reducing overhead. The pseudo gradient penalty strategy addresses training instability from noisy data and improves convergence and generalization. The asynchronous A-EDiT variant provides robust handling of consistent stragglers in heterogeneous environments. The approach demonstrates superior scalability, stability, and speed compared to state-of-the-art baselines, and offers practical insights for elastic and asynchronous distributed LLM training.

fcd0de4066d93fa3822a14898008fa2dd99f7be6.title: SyncDreamer: Generating Multiview-consistent Images from a Single-view Image
fcd0de4066d93fa3822a14898008fa2dd99f7be6.research_question: How can multiview-consistent images of arbitrary objects be generated from a single-view image, ensuring consistency in geometry and appearance across views, and enabling high-quality 3D reconstruction from diverse input styles?
fcd0de4066d93fa3822a14898008fa2dd99f7be6.hypothesis: Modeling the joint probability distribution of multiview images using a synchronized multiview diffusion model with 3D-aware feature attention will significantly improve multiview consistency and 3D reconstruction quality compared to existing methods.
fcd0de4066d93fa3822a14898008fa2dd99f7be6.proposed_method: A synchronized multiview diffusion model is developed to generate N images from a single input view, modeling the joint distribution of multiview images. The method constructs N shared noise predictors, each responsible for generating one target view, and synchronizes their intermediate states at every denoising step via a 3D-aware feature attention mechanism. This mechanism builds a spatial feature volume from all noisy target views, projects features into view frustums aligned with each target view, and applies depth-wise attention layers within a shared UNet backbone to correlate features across views. The backbone UNet is initialized from a pretrained Zero123 model, with the UNet and text attention layers typically frozen during training to leverage strong 3D priors. The training process involves adding noise to N images of the same object, randomly selecting a view, and minimizing the L2 loss between sampled and predicted noise for that view, ensuring cross-view consistency through shared conditioning.
fcd0de4066d93fa3822a14898008fa2dd99f7be6.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the Google Scanned Object (GSO) dataset, with additional qualitative tests on Internet images and hand-drawn designs to evaluate generalization. Baseline methods include Zero123, RealFusion, Magic123, One-2-3-45, Point-E, and Shap-E. Evaluation metrics for novel view synthesis include PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and the number of reconstructed points using COLMAP to assess multiview consistency. For single-view 3D reconstruction, Chamfer Distance and Volume IoU are reported between reconstructed and ground-truth shapes. Ablation studies examine the impact of 3D-aware attention, backbone initialization, and UNet training strategies. The method is also tested for its ability to generate multiple plausible object instances from the same input using different random seeds.
fcd0de4066d93fa3822a14898008fa2dd99f7be6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a synchronized multiview diffusion framework that models the joint probability of multiview images, enabling simultaneous generation of consistent views in a single reverse diffusion process. A novel 3D-aware feature attention mechanism is integrated, correlating features across views via spatial volumes and depth-wise attention, which enforces both global and local geometric consistency. The method leverages pretrained 2D diffusion models for strong generalization and supports diverse input styles, including hand-drawn images. Compared to prior methods, this approach achieves superior multiview consistency, improved 3D reconstruction quality, and greater diversity in generated outputs.

fceb6d9646a64e59708946c4ca9d01bb0b4d4e5d.title: An Introduction to Neural Data Compression
fceb6d9646a64e59708946c4ca9d01bb0b4d4e5d.research_question: How can neural networks and modern machine learning techniques be leveraged to improve both lossless and lossy data compression across various data types, including images and videos, and what are the fundamental connections between generative modeling and data compression?
fceb6d9646a64e59708946c4ca9d01bb0b4d4e5d.hypothesis: Neural networks and deep generative models can be trained end-to-end to learn efficient data representations that enable superior compression rates and reconstruction quality compared to traditional, hand-engineered codecs, while also providing adaptability to new or domain-specific data types.
fceb6d9646a64e59708946c4ca9d01bb0b4d4e5d.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed that utilizes deep generative models—including variational autoencoders (VAEs), normalizing flows, autoregressive models, and diffusion probabilistic models—for both lossless and lossy data compression. For lossless compression, probabilistic models will be trained to estimate the data distribution, which will then be combined with entropy coding schemes to achieve efficient bit allocation. For lossy compression, neural networks will be employed as encoder-decoder pairs, with quantization and learned entropy models enabling end-to-end optimization of the rate-distortion trade-off. The approach will further explore advanced techniques such as learned quantization, perceptual loss functions, and task-oriented compression, as well as extensions to temporally correlated data (e.g., video) and emerging data types (e.g., point clouds, neural radiance fields).
fceb6d9646a64e59708946c4ca9d01bb0b4d4e5d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image and video compression benchmarks such as Kodak, CLIC, and Vimeo-90k, as well as on domain-specific datasets like point clouds and neural radiance fields. Baseline comparisons will include traditional codecs (e.g., JPEG, JPEG2000, H.264/AVC) and recent neural compression models. Evaluation metrics will cover bit-rate (bits per pixel or bits per second), distortion (PSNR, SSIM), perceptual quality (LPIPS, FID), and, for task-oriented compression, downstream task performance. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of different generative model architectures, quantization schemes, and perceptual loss functions.
fceb6d9646a64e59708946c4ca9d01bb0b4d4e5d.novelty_claims: The proposed research aims to unify and extend neural compression by systematically leveraging deep generative models for both lossless and lossy compression, introducing end-to-end learned entropy models, and incorporating perceptual and task-oriented objectives. The framework is designed to be data-agnostic and adaptable to new data modalities, addressing open challenges in domain-specific compression and bridging the gap between generative modeling and practical data compression. Additional innovations include the exploration of compression without explicit quantization and the integration of adversarial critics to enhance perceptual quality.

fd016671555b3eb1e417f0a645e1268922e3c081.title: DeepACO: Neural-enhanced Ant Systems for Combinatorial Optimization
fd016671555b3eb1e417f0a645e1268922e3c081.research_question: How can the process of designing effective heuristics for Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithms be automated and generalized to a wide range of combinatorial optimization problems, reducing the need for expert-driven, problem-specific customization?
fd016671555b3eb1e417f0a645e1268922e3c081.hypothesis: A neural-enhanced ACO framework, which leverages deep reinforcement learning to learn heuristic measures across combinatorial optimization problems, can consistently outperform traditional ACO algorithms with expert-designed heuristics and achieve competitive or superior results compared to state-of-the-art neural combinatorial optimization methods.
fd016671555b3eb1e417f0a645e1268922e3c081.proposed_method: A generic neural-enhanced ACO meta-heuristic is proposed, in which a graph neural network (GNN) is trained to map instances of combinatorial optimization problems (COPs) to heuristic measures for solution components. The method involves two learning stages: first, the GNN-based heuristic learner is trained across a distribution of COP instances to predict effective heuristic measures; second, these learned measures are incorporated into the ACO solution construction and pheromone update process, biasing the search towards promising regions. The framework supports optional local search (LS) interleaved with neural-guided perturbation, where LS is used to refine solutions and neural-guided moves help escape local optima. Three extended designs are introduced to balance exploration and exploitation: a multihead decoder for diverse heuristics, a top-k entropy loss for encouraging diversity among top choices, and an imitation loss to leverage available expert heuristics.
fd016671555b3eb1e417f0a645e1268922e3c081.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on eight representative COPs, including routing (TSP, CVRP, OP, PCTSP, SOP), scheduling (SMTWTP, RCPSP), and subset selection (MKP) problems. The approach is evaluated using 100 held-out test instances per benchmark, with comparisons against fundamental and advanced ACO algorithms (Ant System, Elitist Ant System, MAX-MIN Ant System, Adaptive Elitist Ant System) as well as state-of-the-art neural combinatorial optimization baselines. Evaluation metrics include objective value (gap to optimum or best-known), robustness to hyperparameter choices, and execution time. Additional experiments assess generalization to real-world instances (TSPLIB), robustness across pheromone models, and the impact of the proposed exploration-enhancing extensions. Ablation studies are performed to isolate the effects of neural-guided perturbation and training strategies.
fd016671555b3eb1e417f0a645e1268922e3c081.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to exploit deep reinforcement learning for automating heuristic design in ACO, enabling strong neural enhancement across a broad range of COPs using a single neural architecture and hyperparameter set. The method dispenses with the need for expert-driven, problem-specific heuristic engineering and demonstrates superior flexibility and generalizability compared to prior neural combinatorial optimization approaches, which are often limited to specific problem types. The introduction of multihead decoding, top-k entropy loss, and imitation loss provides novel mechanisms for balancing exploration and exploitation in neural-guided meta-heuristics. The framework is shown to be robust to hyperparameter choices and adaptable to different pheromone models and ACO variants.

fd1cf28a2b8caf2fe29af5e7fa9191cecfedf84d.title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale
fd1cf28a2b8caf2fe29af5e7fa9191cecfedf84d.research_question: Can a single, large-scale, language-conditioned robotic policy be trained to perform a wide variety of real-world manipulation tasks, generalize to new instructions, objects, and environments, and robustly operate in the presence of distractors and distribution shifts?
fd1cf28a2b8caf2fe29af5e7fa9191cecfedf84d.hypothesis: A high-capacity Transformer-based model, trained on a large, diverse, task-agnostic dataset of real-world robotic demonstrations and conditioned on natural language, will be able to generalize to unseen tasks, objects, and environments, and achieve robust real-time control performance superior to existing baselines.
fd1cf28a2b8caf2fe29af5e7fa9191cecfedf84d.proposed_method: A novel architecture, Robotics Transformer 1 (RT-1), will be developed to process sequences of images and natural language instructions and output discretized robot actions in real time. The method will employ an EfficientNet-B3 pretrained on ImageNet, conditioned via FiLM layers on Universal Sentence Encoder embeddings of instructions, to extract vision-language tokens from image sequences. These tokens will be compressed using a TokenLearner module to reduce computational load, and then fed into a decoder-only Transformer with self-attention layers to produce action tokens. Actions will be discretized into 256 bins per dimension for both arm and base control, as well as a mode switch for arm, base, or episode termination. The entire system will be trained using behavioral cloning on a large dataset of successful human demonstrations, optimizing a categorical cross-entropy loss with causal masking for sequence modeling.
fd1cf28a2b8caf2fe29af5e7fa9191cecfedf84d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a fleet of 13 mobile manipulators in three kitchen-based environments: a training environment and two distinct real-world office kitchens. The dataset will consist of approximately 130,000 episodes covering over 700 distinct task instructions and a wide variety of objects. Evaluation will include over 3,000 real-world trials, measuring success rates on seen and unseen instructions, robustness to distractors and background changes, and performance on long-horizon, multi-stage tasks. Baselines for comparison will include Gato (Transformer-based), BC-Z (ResNet-based), and a scaled-up BC-Z XL, all trained on the same dataset. Metrics will include task success rate, generalization to novel instructions, and robustness to environmental changes. Additional ablations will examine the effects of model components, dataset diversity, and incorporation of heterogeneous data sources such as simulation and different robot types.
fd1cf28a2b8caf2fe29af5e7fa9191cecfedf84d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable, efficient Transformer-based architecture for real-time, language-conditioned robotic control that can absorb large-scale, diverse real-world data. The method claims significant improvements in generalization to unseen tasks, objects, and environments, as well as robustness to distractors and distribution shifts, compared to prior state-of-the-art methods. The approach also demonstrates the ability to incorporate heterogeneous data sources, such as simulation and different robot morphologies, without sacrificing performance. The scale of the dataset, the breadth of tasks, and the real-world evaluation represent a substantial advance in multi-task robotic learning.

fd27c08b7105da3412f3b285ea23b3a6dd92409b.title: XTab: Cross-table Pretraining for Tabular Transformers
fd27c08b7105da3412f3b285ea23b3a6dd92409b.research_question: How can pretraining methods for tabular transformers be designed to enable effective cross-table knowledge transfer and improve generalization, learning speed, and performance on diverse tabular prediction tasks from various domains?
fd27c08b7105da3412f3b285ea23b3a6dd92409b.hypothesis: Cross-table pretraining of tabular transformers using federated learning and data-specific featurizers will enable the learning of generalizable representations, thereby improving generalization, learning speed, and predictive performance on new, previously unseen tabular datasets compared to models trained from scratch or with domain-specific pretraining.
fd27c08b7105da3412f3b285ea23b3a6dd92409b.proposed_method: A novel cross-table pretraining framework, XTab, is developed for tabular transformers. The method decomposes the model into data-specific featurizers and projection heads, and a shared transformer backbone. Each table, potentially with a different number and type of columns, is processed by its own featurizer to produce token embeddings, which are then passed through the shared transformer backbone. The projection heads are also data-specific and are used to reconstruct the original table (reconstruction loss), perform contrastive learning, or predict supervised targets, depending on the pretraining objective. Pretraining is conducted in a federated learning setting, where each client (table) maintains its own featurizer and projection head, while the shared transformer backbone is updated through federated averaging across clients. After pretraining, only the shared backbone is retained and fine-tuned on new downstream tasks with randomly initialized featurizers and projection heads.
fd27c08b7105da3412f3b285ea23b3a6dd92409b.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the OpenML-AutoML Benchmark (AMLB), which includes 104 tabular datasets spanning regression, binary, and multiclass classification tasks. 52 datasets are used for pretraining and 52 for finetuning and evaluation, with 5-fold cross-validation on each task. Baselines include tree-based models (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost), neural networks (AutoGluon NN, FastAI), and transformer-based models (FT-Transformer, TransTab) with and without pretraining. Evaluation metrics are RMSE for regression, AUC for binary classification, and logloss for multiclass classification. Both light (fixed epochs) and heavy (early stopping) finetuning regimes are tested. Ablation studies investigate the impact of different pretraining objectives (reconstruction, contrastive, supervised), backbone architectures (FT-Transformer, Fastformer, Saint-v), number of pretraining tasks, and federated learning parameters.
fd27c08b7105da3412f3b285ea23b3a6dd92409b.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable effective cross-table pretraining for tabular transformers, addressing the challenge of varying column types and numbers across tables. By leveraging federated learning, the method allows scalable and distributed pretraining across a large collection of heterogeneous tabular datasets. The approach demonstrates that cross-table pretraining can significantly boost generalizability, learning speed, and downstream performance of tabular transformers, outperforming both randomly initialized deep models and other state-of-the-art tabular deep learning methods. The method is flexible to different transformer architectures and pretraining objectives, and is shown to be widely applicable without case-by-case tuning.

fd3882f15203254805f440e62d6f81636153e194.title: Certified Robustness to Data Poisoning in Gradient-Based Training
fd3882f15203254805f440e62d6f81636153e194.research_question: How can provable, general guarantees be established for the robustness of machine learning models trained with gradient-based methods against a wide range of data poisoning and backdoor attacks, without modifying the underlying model or training algorithm?
fd3882f15203254805f440e62d6f81636153e194.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging convex relaxations and interval bound propagation techniques, it is possible to compute sound, non-vacuous parameter-space bounds that certify the robustness of any gradient-based learning algorithm to both bounded and unbounded data poisoning and backdoor attacks.
fd3882f15203254805f440e62d6f81636153e194.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed to certify robustness to data poisoning in gradient-based training by computing parameter-space bounds that encapsulate all possible model parameterizations resulting from adversarially manipulated training data. The approach will formalize poisoning attacks as constraints over an adversary’s perturbation budget in both input and label spaces, encompassing bounded and unbounded adversaries. Abstract Gradient Training (AGT) will be introduced to iteratively propagate interval bounds over model parameters during training, using convex relaxations and explicit CROWN-style bound propagation for both the forward and backward passes of neural networks. The method will efficiently over-approximate the set of all possible parameter updates under a given threat model, allowing for the computation of worst-case model behavior bounds, including performance degradation and backdoor success rates. Gradient clipping and interval arithmetic will be incorporated to tighten bounds and ensure computational tractability.
fd3882f15203254805f440e62d6f81636153e194.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple real-world datasets, including the UCI Household Power Consumption dataset (regression), MNIST (multi-class classification with label-flipping attacks), MedMNIST/OCTMNIST (medical image classification and fine-tuning), and the Udacity self-driving car dataset (autonomous driving regression and backdoor attacks). The proposed method will be evaluated by certifying model robustness under varying strengths and types of poisoning attacks (feature, label, and combined), both in bounded and unbounded settings. Baselines will include nominal (unpoisoned) model performance and, where applicable, existing heuristic poisoning attacks. Evaluation metrics will include certified accuracy, mean squared error bounds, and certified backdoor success rates, with ablation studies on model architecture, batch size, learning rate, and adversary strength. Both CROWN and interval bound propagation (IBP) will be used to compute the tightest possible bounds.
fd3882f15203254805f440e62d6f81636153e194.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first general framework for certifying robustness to data poisoning attacks for any model trained with first-order optimization methods, without requiring modifications to the model or training algorithm. The approach supports both bounded and unbounded adversaries, as well as untargeted, targeted, and backdoor attacks. A novel parameter-space bound propagation strategy is developed, including an explicit extension of CROWN-style bounds to interval parameters and a general algorithm for abstract gradient training. The method provides formal, sound certificates of poisoning robustness and is empirically validated on diverse, real-world tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness and generality.

fd59c78825ae11c117b57e08e8003250343362a3.title: Safe LoRA: the Silver Lining of Reducing Safety Risks when Fine-tuning Large Language Models
fd59c78825ae11c117b57e08e8003250343362a3.research_question: How can the safety alignment of large language models (LLMs) be preserved during parameter-efficient fine-tuning, such as with LoRA, without requiring additional training data or significant computational resources?
fd59c78825ae11c117b57e08e8003250343362a3.hypothesis: Projecting LoRA weight updates onto a safety-aligned subspace, derived from the difference between aligned and unaligned LLM weights, will mitigate safety risks introduced during fine-tuning while maintaining model utility.
fd59c78825ae11c117b57e08e8003250343362a3.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a post-hoc projection mechanism for LoRA-based fine-tuning of LLMs, termed SafeLoRA. First, an alignment matrix is constructed for each layer by subtracting the weights of an unaligned model (e.g., base model) from an aligned model (e.g., chat/instruct model). A projection matrix is then derived from this alignment matrix, either using a full-rank or a computationally efficient approximation. After LoRA fine-tuning, the LoRA weight updates for each layer are projected onto the alignment subspace if their similarity to the alignment direction falls below a predefined threshold. This selective projection is determined by computing the Frobenius inner product between the original and projected LoRA weights, ensuring only layers most at risk for safety degradation are modified. The approach is data-free and training-free, requiring only access to the weights of the base and aligned models.
fd59c78825ae11c117b57e08e8003250343362a3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on Llama-2-7B-Chat and Llama-3-8B-Instruct models, using fine-tuning datasets such as PureBad (malicious data), DialogSummary (benign and mixed with harmful samples), and Alpaca (benign data). Baselines for comparison include standard LoRA, SafeInstr (safety-tuned instructions), and Backdoor Enhanced Alignment (BEA). Evaluation metrics will include harmfulness scores (1-5, judged by GPT-4), utility (Rouge-1 F1 for summaries, MT-Bench for general performance), and attack success rate (ASR). Fine-tuning will be performed using official scripts, with LoRA applied to selected attention layers and hyperparameters tailored per dataset. The impact of the number of projected layers and similarity thresholds will be analyzed, and ablation studies will be conducted to assess the trade-off between safety and utility.
fd59c78825ae11c117b57e08e8003250343362a3.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a data-free, training-free, and model-agnostic patch for LoRA-based fine-tuning that selectively projects parameter updates onto a safety-aligned subspace, preserving alignment without additional supervision. The approach leverages the availability of both base and aligned model weights to construct the alignment matrix, enabling practical deployment for open-source LLMs. Unlike prior defenses that require extra safety data or backdoor triggers, the method operates post-hoc and maintains competitive utility. The proposal also provides insights into the relationship between the number of projected layers and model alignment strength, and demonstrates applicability to both parameter-efficient and full fine-tuning regimes.

fd5e0543531f95f6b8d64abf78cdd038d0c769a1.title: OpenBox: Annotate Any Bounding Boxes in 3D
fd5e0543531f95f6b8d64abf78cdd038d0c769a1.research_question: How can high-quality, open-vocabulary 3D bounding box annotations be automatically generated for objects in autonomous driving scenarios using only synchronized images and LiDAR point clouds, while reducing annotation costs and improving scalability and recognition of unseen objects?
fd5e0543531f95f6b8d64abf78cdd038d0c769a1.hypothesis: Leveraging 2D vision foundation models for instance-level semantic cues, combined with cross-modal alignment and adaptive, physically-informed 3D bounding box generation, will enable automatic, high-quality 3D annotations across diverse object categories, outperforming existing unsupervised and multi-modal annotation methods without requiring iterative self-training.
fd5e0543531f95f6b8d64abf78cdd038d0c769a1.proposed_method: A two-stage automatic annotation pipeline is developed. In the first stage, cross-modal instance alignment associates instance-level cues from 2D images, extracted using vision foundation models (e.g., GroundingDINO and SAM2), with corresponding 3D point clouds via unprojection and context-aware refinement. This process fuses coarse LiDAR-based clusters (using HDBSCAN after ground removal) with 2D-derived instance masks, applying adaptive erosion and majority voting to reduce noise and improve instance localization. In the second stage, adaptive 3D bounding box generation is performed: instances are categorized by physical type (static rigid, dynamic rigid, or deformable) using semantic class and motion cues (e.g., PPscore), then bounding boxes are generated using class-specific size statistics, mesh reconstruction (via Signed Distance Function) for static objects, and closeness-to-edge algorithms for deformable objects. Refinement steps include surface-aware filtering, 3D-2D IoU alignment, and visibility-based box extension to ensure accurate localization and sizing.
fd5e0543531f95f6b8d64abf78cdd038d0c769a1.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the Waymo Open Dataset (WOD), Lyft Level 5 Perception dataset, and nuScenes dataset. The annotation pipeline is evaluated by training standard 3D object detectors (Voxel R-CNN, PointRCNN, CenterPoint) on the automatically generated annotations and comparing detection performance against human-annotated validation sets. Baseline methods include CPD, MODEST, OYSTER, LiSe, and UNION, representing both LiDAR-only and multi-modal annotation strategies. Evaluation metrics include 3D Average Precision (AP) at various IoU thresholds, both class-specific and class-agnostic, as well as BEV AP for different distance ranges. Additional experiments directly compare the automatic annotations to human annotations and include ablation studies to assess the contribution of each refinement and alignment module.
fd5e0543531f95f6b8d64abf78cdd038d0c769a1.novelty_claims: The proposed pipeline introduces a fully automatic, open-vocabulary 3D annotation method that requires only synchronized images and LiDAR point clouds, eliminating the need for iterative self-training. It uniquely leverages 2D vision foundation models for semantic guidance, incorporates context-aware and surface-aware refinement for high-quality instance point clouds, and adaptively generates bounding boxes based on physical object properties. The method achieves superior annotation quality and detection performance compared to state-of-the-art baselines, especially in challenging scenarios and for previously unseen object categories.

fd75311ac92e21fdae7dacefcec936332648cd94.title: Limiting Over-Smoothing and Over-Squashing of Graph Message Passing by Deep Scattering Transforms
fd75311ac92e21fdae7dacefcec936332648cd94.research_question: How can the fundamental limitations of graph neural networks, specifically over-smoothing, over-squashing, and instability, be addressed to improve the effectiveness of message passing on graph-structured data?
fd75311ac92e21fdae7dacefcec936332648cd94.hypothesis: A message passing framework that operates in the spectral domain and leverages deep scattering transforms can mitigate over-smoothing, over-squashing, and instability in graph neural networks, leading to more robust and expressive graph representations.
fd75311ac92e21fdae7dacefcec936332648cd94.proposed_method: A novel Deep Scattering Message Passing (DSMP) neural network will be developed, integrating spectral graph theory and wavelet-based scattering transforms into the message passing paradigm. The method will use framelet-based multi-scale graph signal decomposition, where both low-pass and high-pass framelet coefficients are computed recursively using Chebyshev polynomial approximations for efficient spectral filtering. The scattering transform will be cascaded across multiple layers, each comprising spectral filtering, pointwise nonlinearity (modulus), and aggregation, to capture both local and global graph signal patterns. The resulting multi-scale coefficients will be processed by a message passing neural network, such as a Graph Attention Network (GAT), followed by multi-layer perceptrons with nonlinear activations to enhance expressive power. The architecture is designed to inherit the energy-preserving and stability properties of scattering transforms, while explicitly addressing the information bottleneck and smoothing issues inherent to deep GNNs.
fd75311ac92e21fdae7dacefcec936332648cd94.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmark datasets for graph classification and node classification tasks, including datasets with varying graph sizes and topologies. Baseline methods for comparison will include traditional message passing neural networks such as GCN, GAT, and GIN, as well as spectral and wavelet-based GNN variants. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, measures of over-smoothing (e.g., Dirichlet energy evolution), and sensitivity to over-squashing (e.g., analysis of the Jacobian of node features and spectral gap/Cheeger constant proxies). Additional experiments will assess the stability of the proposed method under noisy or perturbed graph signals and analyze computational cost. Experimental protocols will ensure fair comparison through consistent data splits and hyperparameter tuning.
fd75311ac92e21fdae7dacefcec936332648cd94.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a discriminatively trained, multi-layer deep scattering transform within the message passing framework, enabling effective aggregation of both local and global information in graphs. The method provides theoretical guarantees and empirical validation for mitigating over-smoothing and over-squashing, and inherits stability properties from the scattering transform. The integration of framelet-based spectral filtering with efficient Chebyshev polynomial approximations and a layered scattering architecture is claimed as a key innovation, offering improved robustness and expressivity over existing GNN models.

fdaa21fce5ee5aadf1bb8c55d5f7c3155b905846.title: Faster Segment Anything: Towards Lightweight SAM for Mobile Applications
fdaa21fce5ee5aadf1bb8c55d5f7c3155b905846.research_question: How can a high-performing, prompt-guided segmentation model be adapted to run efficiently on resource-constrained mobile devices without significant loss in segmentation accuracy or versatility?
fdaa21fce5ee5aadf1bb8c55d5f7c3155b905846.hypothesis: A decoupled distillation approach, where knowledge from a large, high-capacity image encoder is transferred to a lightweight encoder while maintaining compatibility with the original mask decoder, will enable the creation of a mobile-friendly segmentation model that achieves performance comparable to the original model but with significantly reduced computational and memory requirements.
fdaa21fce5ee5aadf1bb8c55d5f7c3155b905846.proposed_method: A lightweight segmentation model, termed MobileSAM, will be developed by replacing the heavyweight image encoder in the original segmentation pipeline with a compact transformer-based encoder (e.g., TinyViT). The method involves a decoupled distillation process: first, the lightweight encoder is trained to mimic the image embeddings produced by the original large encoder using mean squared error loss, independent of the mask decoder. The original prompt-guided mask decoder is retained without modification, leveraging the alignment of the distilled encoder's output with the original encoder. Optionally, the mask decoder may be fine-tuned on the outputs of the new encoder to further improve alignment and performance. The training process is designed to be efficient, requiring only a small fraction of the original dataset and minimal computational resources (e.g., a single GPU for less than a day).
fdaa21fce5ee5aadf1bb8c55d5f7c3155b905846.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a subset (1%) of the SA-1B segmentation dataset for training, with the original SAM model's outputs serving as the distillation target. The lightweight encoder (TinyViT) will be trained for 8 epochs on a single GPU, with precomputed teacher embeddings to accelerate training. Evaluation will focus on mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) between masks predicted by MobileSAM and the original SAM, using both point and box prompts. Baseline comparisons will include the original SAM (with ViT-H and ViT-B encoders) and FastSAM, a concurrent lightweight segmentation model. Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of batch size and training iterations on performance. Inference speed and model size will be measured on a single GPU, and qualitative results will be provided for both 'segment anything' and 'segment everything' tasks.
fdaa21fce5ee5aadf1bb8c55d5f7c3155b905846.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a decoupled distillation strategy that enables efficient knowledge transfer from a large image encoder to a lightweight one, significantly reducing training cost and computational requirements. MobileSAM achieves a more than 60-fold reduction in model size and is up to 5 times faster and 7 times smaller than competing lightweight models such as FastSAM, while maintaining segmentation performance on par with the original SAM. The method preserves the plug-and-play compatibility of the original segmentation pipeline, facilitating seamless integration into existing applications for mobile and edge devices.

fdaacabb69ca054d1d9acf2f1409c083672adc4a.title: Exploring Vision-Language Models for Imbalanced Learning
fdaacabb69ca054d1d9acf2f1409c083672adc4a.research_question: How can the performance of vision-language models (VLMs) be improved for imbalanced classification tasks, particularly in scenarios where class distributions are highly skewed and tail classes are underrepresented?
fdaacabb69ca054d1d9acf2f1409c083672adc4a.hypothesis: Incorporating a lightweight decoder and established imbalanced learning algorithms into VLMs will significantly enhance their performance on imbalanced datasets, especially for minority (tail) classes, compared to zero-shot, prompt tuning, and standard fine-tuning approaches.
fdaacabb69ca054d1d9acf2f1409c083672adc4a.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that augments pre-trained vision-language models (such as CLIP) with a lightweight decoder module positioned after the frozen image encoder. This decoder, composed of multiple transformer blocks, will be trained to generate enriched representations that better capture nuanced features of minority classes. The approach will further integrate a suite of imbalanced learning algorithms, including loss function engineering (e.g., Focal Loss, Balanced Softmax, LDAM, LADE), class-balanced weighting, and two-stage classifier adjustment methods (e.g., CRT, LWS, DisAlign, MARC). The training procedure will involve freezing the backbone VLM, training the decoder and classifier with imbalanced loss functions, and optionally employing two-stage retraining to recalibrate classifier heads for balanced predictions. Both linear probing and full fine-tuning will be compared, but the focus will be on the effectiveness of the decoder and imbalanced algorithms in addressing class imbalance.
fdaacabb69ca054d1d9acf2f1409c083672adc4a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three widely-used long-tailed benchmarks: ImageNet-LT, iNaturalist18, and Places-LT, each featuring highly imbalanced class distributions. The evaluation protocol will include splitting classes into many-shot, medium-shot, and few-shot groups, and assessing performance using overall accuracy, as well as precision, recall, and F1 scores for each group. Baselines will include zero-shot VLM prediction, prompt tuning (e.g., CoOp), linear probing, and full fine-tuning. The proposed method will be compared against these baselines, as well as against the same VLMs enhanced with various imbalanced learning algorithms. Multiple VLM backbones (e.g., CLIP-ViT-B16, CLIP-ViT-L14, Laion-CLIP, CLIP-ResNet101) will be tested to assess generalizability. Training will use standard optimization techniques, with detailed hyperparameters specified for reproducibility.
fdaacabb69ca054d1d9acf2f1409c083672adc4a.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first comprehensive exploration of integrating vision-language models with a broad range of imbalanced classification algorithms, including the addition of a lightweight decoder to address memory and feature representation challenges in long-tailed settings. The approach enables VLMs to achieve substantial improvements in accuracy for minority classes, outperforming zero-shot, prompt tuning, and conventional fine-tuning methods. The framework is designed to be scalable to datasets with thousands of classes and is compatible with various VLM backbones, providing a unified and extensible solution for imbalanced visual recognition tasks.

fdb9e9ca290d79aa9051292e0bb060c1bfd5febb.title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Regret for Linearly Parameterized Bandits
fdb9e9ca290d79aa9051292e0bb060c1bfd5febb.research_question: What are the fundamental minimax regret limits for the linear contextual bandit problem with finite action sets, and can an algorithm be designed to achieve regret matching these limits up to iterated logarithmic factors?
fdb9e9ca290d79aa9051292e0bb060c1bfd5febb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the minimax expected regret for linear contextual bandits with finite action sets scales as Omega(sqrt(d T (log T)(log n))) and that a carefully designed algorithm can achieve an upper bound matching this lower bound up to iterated logarithmic factors.
fdb9e9ca290d79aa9051292e0bb060c1bfd5febb.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, Variable-Confidence-Level (VCL) SupLinUCB, will be developed as a variant of the classical SupLinUCB algorithm. This method will employ variable confidence levels that adapt over time, allowing the failure probability in confidence intervals to increase as the algorithm progresses, thereby reducing unnecessary logarithmic factors in the regret bound. The algorithm will utilize layered data partitioning, where data is divided into exponentially increasing layers, and ordinary least squares (OLS) estimates are computed separately within each layer to decouple statistical dependencies. At each round, the algorithm will sequentially refine the set of candidate actions by eliminating suboptimal ones based on OLS estimates and dynamically adjusted confidence intervals, selecting actions according to the most refined layer where a confident choice can be made.
fdb9e9ca290d79aa9051292e0bb060c1bfd5febb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic linear contextual bandit environments, where the dimension d, time horizon T, and number of actions per round n are systematically varied. The proposed VCL-SupLinUCB algorithm will be compared against established baselines such as classical SupLinUCB, SupLinRel, and algorithms from Dani et al. and Abbasi-Yadkori et al. Evaluation will focus on cumulative regret, with particular attention to the scaling of regret with respect to d, T, and n. The experimental setup will include adversarially chosen action sets and regression parameters to test worst-case performance, and results will be analyzed to verify whether the observed regret matches the theoretical upper and lower bounds up to iterated logarithmic factors.
fdb9e9ca290d79aa9051292e0bb060c1bfd5febb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces variable confidence levels into the SupLinUCB framework for the first time in the contextual bandit setting, allowing for the removal of two extraneous log T factors from previous analyses. The method also provides a tighter information-theoretic lower bound, improving previous results by one log T factor and revealing a fundamentally different regret scaling compared to classical multi-armed bandits. The proof techniques, including the refined analysis of layer sizes and the construction of tight adversarial sequences, establish nearly matching upper and lower bounds for minimax regret, marking a significant advancement in the theoretical understanding of linearly parameterized bandits.

fdc04fe7c4a3fb4038d1bbd5f4e2fdf2599566e3.title: Ambient Diffusion: Learning Clean Distributions from Corrupted Data
fdc04fe7c4a3fb4038d1bbd5f4e2fdf2599566e3.research_question: Is it possible to learn the underlying clean data distribution using only highly corrupted samples, particularly in scenarios where access to uncorrupted data is impossible or undesirable? How can generative models be trained to avoid memorizing individual training samples while still capturing the true data distribution from corrupted observations?
fdc04fe7c4a3fb4038d1bbd5f4e2fdf2599566e3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a diffusion-based generative modeling framework, augmented with additional measurement corruption during training, can learn the conditional expectation of the clean data distribution from only highly corrupted samples. This approach will enable the generation of new, non-memorized samples from the clean distribution, even when no uncorrupted training data is available.
fdc04fe7c4a3fb4038d1bbd5f4e2fdf2599566e3.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a novel training framework for diffusion models that operates solely on highly corrupted data. The core idea is to apply an additional, randomized corruption (e.g., further inpainting or measurement deletion) to already corrupted training samples, and require the model to predict the original corrupted image from this further corrupted version. The model is trained by minimizing a loss that penalizes errors only on pixels or measurements that are known (i.e., not missing due to the original corruption). This setup ensures the model cannot distinguish whether a missing entry is due to the original or further corruption, compelling it to learn the conditional expectation of the clean data. The approach generalizes to a wide family of corruption processes, including random inpainting, block inpainting, and Gaussian measurement matrices. Sampling from the learned model is performed using a modified diffusion process that leverages the trained conditional expectation, with optional reconstruction guidance to improve consistency and sample quality.
fdc04fe7c4a3fb4038d1bbd5f4e2fdf2599566e3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation benchmarks such as CelebA-HQ, CIFAR-10, and AFHQ, with training data subjected to varying levels of corruption (e.g., up to 90% missing pixels via random inpainting). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines including AmbientGAN, DDRM, and DPS, as well as diffusion models trained without the further corruption mechanism. Evaluation metrics will include FID (Fréchet Inception Distance), Inception Score, LPIPS, and PSNR, with additional analysis of memorization by measuring similarity between generated samples and training data using DINO-v2 embeddings. Experiments will also include fine-tuning of large foundation diffusion models (e.g., Deepfloyd IF) on small, highly corrupted datasets (e.g., MRI scans with block corruptions), and assessment of sample diversity and memorization trade-offs as a function of corruption level.
fdc04fe7c4a3fb4038d1bbd5f4e2fdf2599566e3.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first diffusion-based approach capable of learning clean data distributions from only highly corrupted samples, without ever accessing uncorrupted data. It provides theoretical guarantees for recovering the conditional expectation under broad corruption models, and empirically demonstrates the ability to generate high-quality, non-memorized samples even with extreme corruption levels. The method outperforms prior state-of-the-art generative models trained on corrupted data (such as AmbientGAN), and achieves comparable or superior results to diffusion-based inverse problem solvers while requiring only a single prediction step.
