Additionally, the approach enables practical fine-tuning of foundation models on limited, corrupted datasets, mitigating memorization and privacy risks.

fdc261abb778093e07f8c3184f3cc05c4539e81c.title: Learning Sparse Graphon Mean Field Games
fdc261abb778093e07f8c3184f3cc05c4539e81c.research_question: How can scalable and mathematically rigorous learning methods be developed for mean field games on large, sparse, and realistic networks, particularly those exhibiting power law degree distributions, to efficiently approximate equilibria in multi-agent reinforcement learning problems?
fdc261abb778093e07f8c3184f3cc05c4539e81c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging Lp graphons as a mathematical framework for sparse graphs, combined with adapted learning algorithms such as Online Mirror Descent, will enable efficient and accurate approximation of equilibria in mean field games on sparse networks, including those with power law degree distributions, thereby overcoming the limitations of standard dense graphon approaches.
fdc261abb778093e07f8c3184f3cc05c4539e81c.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that formulates mean field games (MFGs) on sparse graphs using Lp graphons, termed LPGMFGs. This approach generalizes the classical dense graphon MFGs to accommodate sparse and power law networks by representing agent interactions through Lp graphons, which can capture the topology of large, sparse graphs. The methodology includes the derivation of theoretical existence and convergence guarantees for equilibria in LPGMFGs. To enable scalable learning, the Online Mirror Descent (OMD) algorithm is extended to the LPGMFG setting, incorporating a new concept of smoothed step graphons to facilitate theoretical analysis and accelerate convergence. The approach discretizes the agent space into equivalence classes, enabling efficient computation of approximate equilibria for large-scale systems.
fdc261abb778093e07f8c3184f3cc05c4539e81c.experiment_details: Experiments are designed to evaluate the proposed LPGMFG framework and the adapted OMD algorithm on several benchmark problems, including a cyber security scenario (where malware spreads in a computer network) and the Beach Bar process (a spatial coordination game). Networks are generated using power law Lp graphons to reflect realistic sparse connectivity. The agent space is discretized (e.g., into 25 subintervals for the cyber security problem and 10 for the Beach Bar problem), and OMD is run with specified hyperparameters (such as step size gamma=1). Baselines include standard dense graphon MFGs, which are shown to be inadequate for sparse networks. Evaluation metrics include exploitability (measuring sub-optimality of learned policies), convergence of empirical distributions to mean field limits (using L1 error), and qualitative analysis of equilibrium policies. Experiments are conducted for both homogeneous and heterogeneous agent classes, and results are averaged over multiple random graph samples to assess robustness.
fdc261abb778093e07f8c3184f3cc05c4539e81c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first general framework for learning mean field games on sparse graphs using Lp graphons, enabling the modeling and analysis of systems with power law degree distributions that cannot be captured by standard graphon methods. It provides rigorous theoretical results, including existence and convergence guarantees for equilibria in LPGMFGs, and extends the Online Mirror Descent algorithm to this new setting with a novel smoothing technique for step graphons. The approach is empirically validated on realistic multi-agent problems, demonstrating scalability and accuracy for large numbers of agents, and offers a mathematically principled solution to previously intractable MARL problems on sparse networks.

fdc53c2c10742464087c0525f77e32604827a21d.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
fdc53c2c10742464087c0525f77e32604827a21d.research_question: How can large language models be efficiently deployed in streaming applications to handle input sequences of arbitrary length without degradation in performance or excessive memory usage?
fdc53c2c10742464087c0525f77e32604827a21d.hypothesis: Preserving a small set of initial tokens as 'attention sinks' in the key-value cache, or introducing a dedicated sink token during pre-training, will stabilize attention distributions and enable language models trained with finite attention windows to generalize to infinite-length input streams efficiently and without loss of performance.
fdc53c2c10742464087c0525f77e32604827a21d.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed StreamingLLM, is proposed to enable efficient streaming inference for large language models. The method maintains a rolling cache of the most recent tokens' key-value (KV) states, supplemented by a small fixed number of initial tokens (attention sinks) retained throughout the sequence. This approach leverages the observation that initial tokens act as sinks for excess attention due to the softmax normalization in transformer attention layers. For models with relative positional encoding (e.g., RoPE or ALiBi), the method reassigns positions within the cache at each decoding step to ensure correct positional information. Additionally, a variant of the method involves pre-training language models with a dedicated, learnable sink token prepended to every training sample, allowing the model to offload unnecessary attention to this token and further improve streaming performance.
fdc53c2c10742464087c0525f77e32604827a21d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across multiple open-source LLM families, including Llama-2, MPT, Falcon, and Pythia, covering a range of model sizes. Evaluation will use the concatenated PG19 dataset (containing long books) for language modeling perplexity, with cache sizes set to fractions of the pre-training window for clarity. Baselines will include dense attention, window attention, and sliding window with re-computation. Additional experiments will assess zero-shot accuracy on seven NLP benchmarks (ARC-Challenge, ARC-Easy, HellaSwag, LAMBADA, OpenbookQA, PIQA, Winogrande), as well as streaming question answering using concatenated ARC datasets and a custom StreamEval benchmark. Metrics will include perplexity, accuracy, decoding latency, and memory usage. Ablation studies will investigate the number of attention sink tokens and cache size effects.
fdc53c2c10742464087c0525f77e32604827a21d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to decouple the pre-training attention window size from the effective inference context length, enabling LLMs to process input streams of arbitrary length without fine-tuning. The method introduces the concept of attention sinks and demonstrates their critical role in stabilizing attention distributions for streaming. Pre-training with a dedicated sink token is shown to further improve streaming performance and efficiency. StreamingLLM achieves up to 22.2× speedup over the best quality baseline while maintaining stable perplexity on multi-million-token sequences, and is compatible with existing context extension techniques.

fdd7d5b0f6b8641c356e170fd264cd11f70ba657.title: Planning-oriented Autonomous Driving
fdd7d5b0f6b8641c356e170fd264cd11f70ba657.research_question: How can an autonomous driving system be designed to effectively coordinate perception, prediction, and planning tasks in a unified, planning-oriented framework to improve safety and robustness in complex driving scenarios?
fdd7d5b0f6b8641c356e170fd264cd11f70ba657.hypothesis: A planning-oriented, unified framework that jointly optimizes perception, prediction, and planning tasks using a query-based transformer architecture will reduce error accumulation, improve task coordination, and achieve superior safety and performance compared to standalone or naive multi-task learning approaches.
fdd7d5b0f6b8641c356e170fd264cd11f70ba657.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a comprehensive end-to-end autonomous driving framework, termed UniAD, which integrates five essential driving tasks—3D object detection, multi-object tracking, online mapping, motion forecasting, and occupancy prediction—within a single transformer-based architecture. Each module is implemented as a transformer decoder, and unified task queries serve as interfaces to enable information exchange and interaction across tasks. Multi-camera images are processed into a bird’s-eye-view (BEV) representation, which is then used by task-specific queries (e.g., track queries for detection and tracking, map queries for road semantics, motion queries for forecasting, and occupancy queries for future scene occupancy). The planner module utilizes an expressive ego-vehicle query, enriched by upstream modules, to predict future waypoints while explicitly avoiding predicted occupied regions using a collision-aware cost function. The system leverages non-linear optimization and attention-based mechanisms to refine predictions and ensure physically feasible, safe planning outcomes.
fdd7d5b0f6b8641c356e170fd264cd11f70ba657.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the challenging nuScenes benchmark, using its multi-modal data for training and evaluation. The framework will be evaluated on all five tasks, with comparisons to state-of-the-art baselines for each module, including both vision-based and LiDAR-based methods. Evaluation metrics will include AMOTA, AMOTP, IDS for tracking; IoU for mapping and occupancy; minADE, minFDE, MR for motion forecasting; and L2 error and collision rate for planning. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each module and design choice, such as query types, attention mechanisms, and non-linear optimization. The experimental setup includes joint and modular training, two-stage learning (perception modules first, then end-to-end), and extensive qualitative and quantitative analysis.
fdd7d5b0f6b8641c356e170fd264cd11f70ba657.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first comprehensive, planning-oriented autonomous driving framework that jointly optimizes perception, prediction, and planning in a unified transformer-based architecture. Key innovations include the use of unified task queries for cross-module interaction, a scene-centric approach to motion and occupancy prediction, and a collision-aware planner that leverages upstream uncertainty. The method claims to outperform both standalone and naive multi-task learning approaches, achieving state-of-the-art results across all tasks without sacrificing perceptual performance, and demonstrates the necessity and effectiveness of coordinated task design for safe autonomous driving.

fddaaaead704e8eb1fce7a7fc07a5441cc4375b7.title: Generalization in VAE and Diffusion Models: A Unified Information-Theoretic Analysis
fddaaaead704e8eb1fce7a7fc07a5441cc4375b7.research_question: How can the generalization properties of encoder-generator-based generative models, specifically Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) and Diffusion Models (DMs), be theoretically characterized and bounded in a unified manner? What are the algorithm- and data-dependent factors that influence generalization in these models, and how can these insights guide practical model selection and optimization?
fddaaaead704e8eb1fce7a7fc07a5441cc4375b7.hypothesis: A unified information-theoretic framework can yield meaningful, computable, and tighter generalization bounds for both the encoder and generator components of VAEs and DMs, revealing explicit trade-offs (e.g., with respect to diffusion time in DMs) and providing practical guidance for model selection and optimization.
fddaaaead704e8eb1fce7a7fc07a5441cc4375b7.proposed_method: A novel information-theoretic framework will be developed to analyze the generalization of encoder-generator-based generative models by modeling both encoder and generator as randomized mappings. The approach will derive algorithm- and data-dependent upper bounds on the generalization gap using mutual information and divergence measures under the sub-Gaussian assumption. For VAEs, the method will provide refined bounds that account for both encoder and generator generalization, directly bounding the generation error using empirical reconstruction loss and mutual information terms. For DMs, the framework will treat the model as a sequence of encoder-generator pairs (or as time-dependent stochastic processes), enabling the derivation of computable upper bounds on the divergence between generated and original data distributions as a function of diffusion time. These bounds will be designed to be estimable using only training data, facilitating their integration into model selection and optimization procedures.
fddaaaead704e8eb1fce7a7fc07a5441cc4375b7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real datasets, including the Swiss Roll (synthetic), MNIST, and CIFAR-10 datasets. For DMs, models will be trained with varying diffusion times and dataset sizes, and the proposed generalization bounds will be estimated using only training data. The bounds' tightness and practical relevance will be validated by comparing them to empirical KL-divergence and log-likelihood (bits per dimension) on held-out test data. For VAEs, experiments will compare the proposed bounds to previous PAC-Bayes-based bounds, analyzing the impact of including generator mutual information terms. Evaluation metrics will include KL-divergence, Wasserstein distance, empirical reconstruction error, and mutual information, with additional qualitative assessment of generated samples. Baselines will include existing generalization bounds for VAEs and DMs, as well as standard score-matching and reconstruction-based objectives.
fddaaaead704e8eb1fce7a7fc07a5441cc4375b7.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first unified information-theoretic generalization framework for both VAEs and DMs, treating encoder and generator as randomized mappings and deriving algorithm- and data-dependent bounds. It provides the first explicit theoretical formulation of the trade-off in generalization terms for DMs as a function of diffusion time, and it is the first to offer computable, non-vacuous upper bounds for DMs that can be estimated solely from training data. The method yields tighter and more comprehensive bounds for VAEs by accounting for both encoder and generator generalization, surpassing prior work that only considered fixed generators or reconstruction loss. The framework also enables practical model selection and regularization strategies based on theoretically grounded generalization estimates.

fde266447d68b2728752a7835e8c97e1af316ac4.title: JARVIS-1: Open-World Multi-Task Agents With Memory-Augmented Multimodal Language Models
fde266447d68b2728752a7835e8c97e1af316ac4.research_question: How can an autonomous agent be developed to robustly perform a wide range of open-world, long-horizon tasks in complex, multimodal environments, such as Minecraft, using human-like planning and control with continual self-improvement?
fde266447d68b2728752a7835e8c97e1af316ac4.hypothesis: Augmenting a multimodal language model-based agent with a retrieval-augmented multimodal memory and self-instruct mechanisms will enable robust, situation-aware, and life-long learning capabilities, resulting in superior performance on diverse and long-horizon open-world tasks compared to existing baselines.
fde266447d68b2728752a7835e8c97e1af316ac4.proposed_method: A memory-augmented multimodal language model (MLM) agent will be developed, capable of perceiving both visual observations and textual instructions. The agent will employ a hierarchical architecture: a high-level interactive planner based on MLM generates situation-aware plans by translating multimodal observations into text and retrieving relevant experiences from a multimodal memory. This memory stores key-value pairs of past task-observation-plan tuples, allowing the agent to perform retrieval-augmented planning using both pretrained knowledge and accumulated in-game experiences. The planner will utilize self-check and self-explain mechanisms to proactively verify and refine plans, leveraging environmental feedback to recover from errors. The agent will be empowered with self-instruct capabilities, autonomously proposing and executing new tasks to expand its memory and continually improve planning skills in a distributed, life-long learning setup.
fde266447d68b2728752a7835e8c97e1af316ac4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in the Minecraft environment using the Minecraft Universe Benchmark, encompassing over 200 tasks across 11 categories, ranging from short-horizon (e.g., chopping trees) to long-horizon (e.g., obtaining a diamond pickaxe) objectives. The agent will interact with the native human interface (mouse and keyboard) at 20 frames per second, starting in survival mode with an empty inventory. Evaluation will be based on average success rate over at least 30 runs per task with varying seeds, with additional reporting of mean and variance for each task group. Baseline comparisons will include LLM-based multi-task agents such as Instruct GPT, ReAct, Inner Monologue, and DEPS, all adapted to the Minecraft setting. Ablation studies will assess the impact of memory, interactive planning, and self-instruct mechanisms. Exploratory experiments will evaluate the agent's life-long learning and self-improvement capabilities as game time progresses.
fde266447d68b2728752a7835e8c97e1af316ac4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a memory-augmented multimodal language model agent capable of situation-aware, interactive planning and life-long learning in open-world environments. Key innovations include the integration of retrieval-augmented multimodal memory for in-context planning, a self-instruct mechanism for autonomous curriculum generation and exploration, and a composable MLM-based planner with self-check and self-explain capabilities. The agent is designed to operate with human-like observation and action spaces, demonstrating unprecedented generality and robustness across a wide spectrum of open-world tasks, with continuous self-improvement and no need for gradient-based updates during life-long learning.

fdeb7beaa031ac77e41ef1571387b4c3dca0bfca.title: Neural Algorithmic Reasoning Without Intermediate Supervision
fdeb7beaa031ac77e41ef1571387b4c3dca0bfca.research_question: Can neural networks be trained to perform algorithmic reasoning tasks and generalize to out-of-distribution inputs, particularly larger input sizes, using only input-output supervision without relying on intermediate step (hint) supervision?
fdeb7beaa031ac77e41ef1571387b4c3dca0bfca.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that neural networks can achieve competitive or superior performance on algorithmic reasoning tasks, including strong out-of-distribution generalization, by leveraging architectural modifications and self-supervised regularization based solely on input-output pairs, without requiring intermediate supervision.
fdeb7beaa031ac77e41ef1571387b4c3dca0bfca.proposed_method: A neural network framework will be developed for algorithmic reasoning tasks, trained exclusively on input-output pairs, omitting explicit supervision of intermediate algorithmic steps (hints). The method introduces architectural modifications to the standard encode-process-decode paradigm: intermediate representations (analogous to hints) are computed and fed back into the processor at each step, but are not supervised, allowing the model to construct useful latent representations that inform subsequent steps. Additionally, a self-supervised contrastive regularization objective is incorporated, which enforces similarity of intermediate representations for inputs that share the same algorithmic execution trajectory (i.e., belong to the same equivalence class under the algorithm). This regularization is implemented by augmenting data to preserve relevant structural properties (such as relative order in sorting) and applying a contrastive loss to node representations at each step, encouraging invariance to irrelevant input changes. The approach is designed to reduce reliance on human-crafted hints, allow for parallel computation, and potentially discover novel solution strategies.
fdeb7beaa031ac77e41ef1571387b4c3dca0bfca.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the CLRS Algorithmic Reasoning Benchmark, which comprises 30 diverse algorithmic tasks, including sorting, shortest paths, minimum spanning tree, and others. The proposed method will be compared against several baselines: standard hint-supervised models, no-hint models, and advanced hint-based regularization methods such as Hint-ReLIC. All models will use the Triplet-GMPNN architecture, with training performed using the Adam optimizer and early stopping based on validation performance. Evaluation will focus on out-of-distribution generalization by training on small input sizes and testing on significantly larger ones (e.g., train sizes 4-16, test size 64). Metrics such as micro-F1 score will be reported, and experiments will include ablations on the number of processor steps and the effect of the contrastive regularization term. Data augmentations will be constructed to generate equivalent inputs for contrastive learning, preserving key algorithmic properties.
fdeb7beaa031ac77e41ef1571387b4c3dca0bfca.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel approach to neural algorithmic reasoning that eliminates the need for intermediate (hint) supervision, instead relying solely on input-output pairs. Key innovations include an architectural modification that enables the model to leverage intermediate latent representations without explicit supervision, and a self-supervised contrastive regularization objective that enforces invariance for inputs with equivalent algorithmic trajectories. This approach is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art results on several algorithmic tasks, particularly sorting, and demonstrates that competitive or superior performance is possible without access to intermediate supervision. The method also provides new insights into the potential for parallel computation and alternative solution strategies in neural algorithmic reasoners.

fe1163c28bf09cd05bcb93a57a85bf6d03fc0d0e.title: Real3D-AD: A Dataset of Point Cloud Anomaly Detection
fe1163c28bf09cd05bcb93a57a85bf6d03fc0d0e.research_question: How can high-precision, full-coverage point cloud datasets and novel detection methods advance the state of 3D anomaly detection for industrial applications, particularly in scenarios with limited training data and challenging real-world conditions?
fe1163c28bf09cd05bcb93a57a85bf6d03fc0d0e.hypothesis: A high-resolution, multi-view, real-world point cloud dataset combined with a registration-based anomaly detection method that leverages both local and global feature memory banks will significantly improve the accuracy and robustness of 3D anomaly detection in industrial settings, especially under few-shot training conditions.
fe1163c28bf09cd05bcb93a57a85bf6d03fc0d0e.proposed_method: A new high-precision, multi-category 3D point cloud anomaly detection dataset will be constructed by scanning real-world industrial toy objects using a high-resolution binocular 3D scanner (PMAX-S130), capturing all object views to eliminate blind spots. Each object will be scanned in multiple orientations and stitched into complete prototypes, with anomalies (incompleteness and redundancy) manually annotated at the point level. To benchmark methods, a systematic evaluation framework (ADBENCH-3D) will be established, including data preprocessing, evaluation scripts, and visualization tools. For anomaly detection, a registration-based approach (Reg3D-AD) will be developed, aligning test objects to prototypes using RANSAC, extracting both local (coordinate-based) and global (PointMAE-based) features, and comparing these to a memory bank constructed from training prototypes using Coreset sampling. Anomaly scores will be computed by measuring distances between test features and memory bank entries, with reweighting for robustness, and final scores will combine local and global assessments.
fe1163c28bf09cd05bcb93a57a85bf6d03fc0d0e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the newly created Real3D-AD dataset, which contains 1,254 high-resolution point clouds across 12 categories, with each category having four training prototypes and approximately 100 test samples (normal and abnormal). The evaluation will use object-level AUROC and AUPR/AP as primary metrics. Baseline comparisons will include eight state-of-the-art 3D anomaly detection algorithms (e.g., BTF, M3DM, PatchCore variants), all implemented within the ADBENCH-3D benchmark. The experimental setup will simulate real-world constraints by limiting training data and using single-view test scans, reflecting practical industrial inspection scenarios. Comprehensive ablation and comparison studies will be performed to assess the effectiveness of the proposed Reg3D-AD method relative to existing approaches.
fe1163c28bf09cd05bcb93a57a85bf6d03fc0d0e.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first high-resolution, full-coverage, real-world 3D point cloud anomaly detection dataset tailored for industrial applications, overcoming limitations of prior datasets in terms of precision, authenticity, and blind spot elimination. A comprehensive, open-source benchmarking framework is provided, supporting reproducible and systematic evaluation of 3D anomaly detection methods. The registration-based Reg3D-AD method is proposed to address the few-shot, high-precision anomaly detection challenge by coupling local and global feature representations within a memory bank, leading to significant performance improvements over existing techniques.

fe1250c8af48711a38e3b998a952ff228df829ee.title: Craftium: Bridging Flexibility and Efficiency for Rich 3D Single- and Multi-Agent Environments
fe1250c8af48711a38e3b998a952ff228df829ee.research_question: How can a flexible, efficient, and highly customizable platform be developed to enable the creation of rich 3D single- and multi-agent environments for autonomous agent research, overcoming the limitations of existing tools in terms of computational efficiency, customizability, and multi-agent support?
fe1250c8af48711a38e3b998a952ff228df829ee.hypothesis: A platform based on a modified open-source voxel game engine, equipped with a powerful scripting API and designed for seamless integration with standard RL interfaces, will enable the creation of diverse, rich, and computationally efficient 3D environments that support both single- and multi-agent scenarios, facilitating large-scale and advanced research in reinforcement learning and related fields.
fe1250c8af48711a38e3b998a952ff228df829ee.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed by modifying an open-source voxel game engine (Luanti) to support efficient, real-time communication with agents via a Python interface. The platform will expose a comprehensive scripting API using Lua, enabling fine-grained, programmatic customization of environment logic, reward functions, and procedural world generation. The architecture will support both single- and multi-agent environments, allowing for asynchronous parallel execution to maximize computational throughput. Standardized interfaces (Gymnasium for single-agent and PettingZoo for multi-agent) will be implemented to ensure compatibility with existing RL libraries and workflows. Extensive documentation, example environments, and integration with a vibrant modding community will be provided to lower the barrier for custom scenario development.
fe1250c8af48711a38e3b998a952ff228df829ee.experiment_details: Experiments will benchmark the platform's computational efficiency against leading alternatives such as MineDojo and VizDoom, measuring steps per second across a variety of environments on standardized hardware (e.g., NVIDIA A5000 GPU, Intel Xeon CPU). A suite of single- and multi-agent RL tasks of varying complexity will be implemented, including procedurally generated dungeons, open-world exploration, and competitive multi-agent combat. Agents will be trained using established RL algorithms (e.g., PPO, PPO+LSTM), and performance will be evaluated using episodic return and task completion metrics. Baselines will include both from-scratch and transfer learning agents, and the ability to support large-scale parallel experiments will be assessed. Additional experiments will demonstrate compatibility with large multimodal models and the ease of integrating community-created mods.
fe1250c8af48711a38e3b998a952ff228df829ee.novelty_claims: The proposed platform is the first to combine high computational efficiency, rich 3D voxel-based environments, and extensive customizability via a general-purpose scripting API, all within an open-source framework. It uniquely supports both single- and multi-agent scenarios, including vast open-worlds, and achieves significantly higher simulation throughput than comparably rich alternatives (e.g., over 2,000 steps per second more than Minecraft-based frameworks). The platform’s architecture enables rapid development of new environments, seamless integration with standard RL tools, and supports research lines previously limited by computational or flexibility constraints, such as continual RL, unsupervised environment design, and open-ended agents.

fe2673a2b6bac27d7a7ca5b6261fb5bb23943095.title: Adapters for Altering LLM Vocabularies: What Languages Benefit the Most?
fe2673a2b6bac27d7a7ca5b6261fb5bb23943095.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be efficiently adapted to new vocabularies to support additional languages and reduce token over-fragmentation, and which languages benefit most from such adaptation?
fe2673a2b6bac27d7a7ca5b6261fb5bb23943095.hypothesis: Learning optimal linear combinations of existing embeddings through adapter modules, while keeping the original model weights fixed, enables effective vocabulary adaptation for LLMs without reliance on heuristics or external resources, and this approach will yield the greatest benefits for languages with Latin scripts or those experiencing severe token fragmentation.
fe2673a2b6bac27d7a7ca5b6261fb5bb23943095.proposed_method: A vocabulary adaptation framework, VocADT, will be developed using adapter modules inserted between the new vocabulary and the original embedding matrix of a pre-trained LLM. The adapters, represented as learnable matrices, will be trained to produce new embeddings as linear combinations of the original embeddings, with all other model weights kept fixed. Initialization of the adapter will be handled by copying over embeddings for overlapping tokens, averaging embeddings for tokens whose partitions are present in the original vocabulary, and using normalized random initialization for all others. An auxiliary loss will be added to encourage the adapter entries for overlapping tokens to remain close to their initial values. After adapter training, the adapters and original embeddings will be merged to form the new embedding matrix, and the adapted model will optionally undergo further full-weight fine-tuning for downstream tasks such as machine translation.
fe2673a2b6bac27d7a7ca5b6261fb5bb23943095.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Mistral-7B language model, adapting its vocabulary to cover 11 languages with diverse scripts and resource levels. SentencePiece tokenizers will be trained on up to 2 million tokens per language to create new vocabularies of 50k tokens for both monolingual and multilingual settings. Adapter training will use 0.5B monolingual tokens per language (2.5B total for multilingual groups) from the MADLAD-400 corpus, with evaluation on multilingual benchmarks including FLORES (MT), XNLI (NLI), XCOPA (reasoning), Belebele, and MMMLU (QA). Baselines will include ZeTT, FOCUS, and OFA, with comparisons made on both monolingual and multilingual vocabulary adaptation strategies. Evaluation metrics will include xCOMET-XL for MT (range 0-1) and accuracy for classification tasks, with both five-shot and zero-shot prompting. Further, the impact of vocabulary adaptation after full-weight fine-tuning (ALMA recipe) will be assessed using monolingual and parallel corpora.
fe2673a2b6bac27d7a7ca5b6261fb5bb23943095.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a scalable and flexible vocabulary adaptation technique for LLMs that does not require external embeddings, heuristics, or language-specific constraints. By learning the optimal linear combinations of existing embeddings through adapter modules, the approach enables efficient adaptation to new vocabularies while keeping the original model weights fixed. The method is empirically validated across a wide range of languages, scripts, and tasks, demonstrating superior or competitive performance compared to strong baselines. Additionally, the research provides new insights into which languages benefit most from vocabulary adaptation and explores the effects of script consistency in multilingual vocabulary grouping.

fe303bbaae47b1b08d0641b41d3288fcd74a3a80.title: Steering Language Models With Activation Engineering
fe303bbaae47b1b08d0641b41d3288fcd74a3a80.research_question: How can language model outputs be more reliably and flexibly steered towards desired properties or behaviors at inference time, without retraining or prompt engineering?
fe303bbaae47b1b08d0641b41d3288fcd74a3a80.hypothesis: Modifying intermediate activations of language models at inference time, by adding steering vectors derived from contrasting prompt pairs, enables effective and targeted control over high-level output properties (such as sentiment or topic) while preserving general model capabilities.
fe303bbaae47b1b08d0641b41d3288fcd74a3a80.proposed_method: A novel activation engineering technique, Activation Addition (ActAdd), will be developed to steer language model outputs by manipulating intermediate activations during inference. The approach involves selecting a pair of natural language prompts that differ along a target property (e.g., 'Love' vs. 'Hate'), running forward passes to extract their activation vectors at a specified layer, and computing the difference to form a steering vector. This steering vector is then scaled by an injection coefficient and added to the model's residual stream at a chosen layer and sequence position during inference on new user prompts. Hyperparameters such as the injection coefficient, target layer, and alignment position will be tuned for optimal effect. The method requires no gradient-based optimization or retraining, and only minimal data (a single prompt pair) to construct each steering vector.
fe303bbaae47b1b08d0641b41d3288fcd74a3a80.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several large language models, including GPT-2-XL, OPT (6.7B), and LLaMA-3 (8B), across multiple tasks. For topic steering, the OpenWebText corpus will be used to evaluate perplexity and token probability shifts when steering towards topics such as 'weddings.' For toxicity reduction, the RealToxicityPrompts dataset will be used, with toxicity measured by the Perspective API and compared against baselines such as prompting, FUDGE, PREADD, and Air-Decoding. Sentiment control will be evaluated using the Stanford IMDb dataset, with sentiment classification performed by a fine-tuned SiEBERT model, and fluency and relevance measured by conditional perplexity and cosine similarity, respectively. General knowledge retention will be assessed using the ConceptNet subset of the LAMA benchmark, measuring P@K for factual completions. All experiments will include appropriate baselines and statistical significance testing where applicable.
fe303bbaae47b1b08d0641b41d3288fcd74a3a80.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a lightweight, optimization-free method for inference-time steering of language models by directly modifying activations, rather than relying on prompt engineering, fine-tuning, or gradient-based search. Activation Addition enables rapid, flexible, and targeted control over output properties using only a single pair of contrasting prompts, and achieves state-of-the-art results on sentiment shift and toxicity reduction tasks while preserving off-target model capabilities. The method demonstrates the practical utility and interpretability of activation engineering, providing experimental evidence for linear feature representations in LLMs and offering a promising direction for controllable and aligned language model behavior.

fe39ff332885c161e441a2beb5c7b66694c5511f.title: Data Taggants: Dataset Ownership Verification via Harmless Targeted Data Poisoning
fe39ff332885c161e441a2beb5c7b66694c5511f.research_question: How can dataset owners reliably verify whether their data has been used to train a machine learning model, particularly in black-box scenarios, without compromising model performance or introducing detectable artifacts?
fe39ff332885c161e441a2beb5c7b66694c5511f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a clean-label, targeted data poisoning approach using out-of-distribution key samples and random labels can enable robust, stealthy, and statistically certifiable dataset ownership verification, even with only black-box access to the suspect model.
fe39ff332885c161e441a2beb5c7b66694c5511f.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed for dataset ownership verification based on 'data taggants,' which are imperceptible modifications applied to a small subset of the dataset. The method involves generating a set of secret key pairs, each consisting of an out-of-distribution (OOD) image and a randomly assigned label. Using a clean-label targeted data poisoning technique, specifically gradient matching, the method perturbs selected images in the dataset such that models trained on this dataset will predict the key label for the corresponding OOD key image. The perturbations are constrained to be visually imperceptible, with a perceptual loss (LPIPS) term included in the optimization to enhance stealthiness. The approach is designed to be robust to various model architectures and training recipes, and detection is performed via a statistical test on the model's top-k predictions for the secret keys, requiring only black-box access.
fe39ff332885c161e441a2beb5c7b66694c5511f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet1k dataset using both Vision Transformer (DeIT) and ResNet architectures of varying sizes, employing state-of-the-art training recipes and data augmentation techniques (e.g., ThreeAugment, SimpleAugment). The method will be evaluated against several baselines, including backdoor watermarking (e.g., SleeperAgent, BadNets), data isotopes, naive canary insertion, and transparency-based approaches. Detection performance will be measured using true positive rate (TPR), false positive rate (FPR), and statistical significance (log p-value) of the binomial test, while model performance will be assessed via validation accuracy and stealthiness via PSNR and resistance to data poisoning and anomaly detection defenses. Robustness will be tested under various conditions, including changes in model architecture, data augmentation, and dataset composition (subsets/supersets).
fe39ff332885c161e441a2beb5c7b66694c5511f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a non-backdoor, clean-label data poisoning technique for dataset ownership verification that operates with only black-box access to the model and provides strong statistical guarantees against false positives. The method leverages out-of-distribution key samples and random labeling to avoid inducing errors on natural data, and incorporates a perceptual loss to ensure stealthiness. It demonstrates robustness across different model architectures and training recipes, achieves high detection confidence with negligible impact on model performance, and is resistant to standard data poisoning and anomaly detection defenses.

fe4f76d46e5506eb59a441bc8be482e7b2dd322e.title: Bounce: Reliable High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization for Combinatorial and Mixed Spaces
fe4f76d46e5506eb59a441bc8be482e7b2dd322e.research_question: How can high-dimensional black-box optimization be made more reliable and efficient for combinatorial, continuous, and mixed-variable input spaces, especially when the structure of the global optimum is unknown or arbitrary?
fe4f76d46e5506eb59a441bc8be482e7b2dd322e.hypothesis: A Bayesian optimization framework that employs nested embeddings of increasing dimensionality, combined with dynamic trust region management and batch parallelism, will achieve robust and state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of high-dimensional combinatorial and mixed-variable optimization problems, regardless of the underlying structure of the optimum.
fe4f76d46e5506eb59a441bc8be482e7b2dd322e.proposed_method: A novel Bayesian optimization algorithm, Bounce, is developed to address high-dimensional optimization in combinatorial, continuous, and mixed spaces. The method constructs a sequence of nested subspace embeddings by partitioning input variables of the same type (continuous, categorical, ordinal, binary) into bins, each representing a lower-dimensional target space. Bounce iteratively refines the embedding by splitting bins, thereby increasing the dimensionality and granularity of the search as needed. A Gaussian process surrogate model with a composite kernel (CoCaBo kernel) is used to model the objective, and trust region management is dynamically adapted to the current subspace and evaluation budget, enabling efficient batch parallelism. The acquisition function is optimized using gradient-based methods for continuous variables, local search for combinatorial variables, and an interleaved approach for mixed spaces. Batch acquisition is supported via q-expected improvement, and the algorithm dynamically adjusts trust region sizes to maximize sample efficiency within the allotted budget.
fe4f76d46e5506eb59a441bc8be482e7b2dd322e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a suite of seven established benchmarks, including combinatorial, continuous, and mixed-variable problems: 53D SVM, 50D LABS, 125D ClusterExpansion, 60D MaxSAT60, 25D PestControl, 53D Ackley53, and 25D Contamination. Each method is initialized with five initial points and evaluated for up to 200 function evaluations (500 for LABS and MaxSat125), with results averaged over 50 repetitions (20 for BODi due to memory constraints). Baselines include state-of-the-art algorithms BODi, Casmopolitan, COMBO, SMAC, RDUCB, and Random Search, with COMBO evaluated both in its original and bug-fixed forms. Evaluation metrics include the best objective value found over iterations, and sensitivity analyses are performed by randomizing the location of the optimum to assess robustness. Batch sizes from 1 to 20 are tested to evaluate parallelism efficiency, and all algorithms use common random seeds for fair comparison.
fe4f76d46e5506eb59a441bc8be482e7b2dd322e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a reliable and scalable Bayesian optimization algorithm for high-dimensional combinatorial and mixed spaces, overcoming the sensitivity and structural limitations of previous methods. Key innovations include a nested embedding strategy that allows for dynamic refinement of the search space, a novel trust region management system tailored for batch parallelism and evaluation budget adherence, and a flexible embedding scheme that accommodates variables of varying types and cardinalities. The method is demonstrated to be robust to the structure and location of the global optimum, achieving or surpassing state-of-the-art performance across diverse benchmarks and supporting efficient parallel evaluations.

fe56f4fc2bc24cb2b2eaf439454cc7253bbef6f3.title: Compressed Chain of Thought: Efficient Reasoning Through Dense Representations
fe56f4fc2bc24cb2b2eaf439454cc7253bbef6f3.research_question: How can reasoning efficiency and accuracy in large language models be improved by leveraging compressed, dense representations of reasoning chains, rather than explicit, token-level chain-of-thought decoding?
fe56f4fc2bc24cb2b2eaf439454cc7253bbef6f3.hypothesis: Compressed, contentful, and continuous contemplation tokens—learned as dense representations of reasoning chains—can enable large language models to achieve similar or better reasoning accuracy as explicit chain-of-thought prompting, while significantly reducing inference latency and computational cost.
fe56f4fc2bc24cb2b2eaf439454cc7253bbef6f3.proposed_method: A novel framework, Compressed Chain-of-Thought (CCOT), is proposed to generate variable-length, contentful, and continuous contemplation tokens that serve as compressed representations of explicit reasoning chains. The approach involves two main modules: CCOT, which is fine-tuned to generate compressed contemplation tokens by approximating a subset of hidden states from full reasoning traces, and DECODE, which is trained to decode answers conditioned on the query and these contemplation tokens. The CCOT module uses a learned scorer to select a subset of hidden states from the full reasoning chain, and then trains to generate these states autoregressively, using intermediate hidden layers as input for subsequent token generation. The DECODE module is trained with cross-entropy loss to generate the final answer, conditioned on both the query and the generated contemplation tokens. The framework is designed to be adaptable to off-the-shelf decoder-only language models, using LoRA for efficient fine-tuning, and supports variable compression ratios to trade off between reasoning accuracy and inference efficiency.
fe56f4fc2bc24cb2b2eaf439454cc7253bbef6f3.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the GSM8K math word problem dataset, using the reasoning chains provided with the dataset (with calculator annotations removed) as supervision for training. The proposed method is evaluated using LLAMA2-7B-CHAT as the base model, with LoRA fine-tuning applied to both the CCOT and DECODE modules. Multiple compression ratios (e.g., r = 0.05, 0.10) are tested to assess the trade-off between accuracy and efficiency. Baselines include models with no contemplation tokens, full explicit chain-of-thought, and non-contentful contemplation tokens (e.g., PAUSE tokens). Evaluation metrics include exact match accuracy on the test set and average decoding time per answer, measured on a single Nvidia A100 GPU. Additional ablations are performed to assess the impact of the autoregressive layer choice and subset selection strategies.
fe56f4fc2bc24cb2b2eaf439454cc7253bbef6f3.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the concept of contentful, continuous, and variable-length contemplation tokens as compressed representations of reasoning chains, enabling efficient and adaptive reasoning in language models. Unlike prior work, CCOT allows for post-hoc inspection of compressed reasoning, scales to larger models with greater data efficiency, and supports an adaptive trade-off between performance and efficiency via the compression ratio. The method is compatible with off-the-shelf models and does not require access to intermediate hidden states during inference. Theoretical analysis extends prior results by showing that autoregressively decoded contemplation tokens increase the computational expressivity of transformers, enabling them to solve a broader class of reasoning tasks.

fea848dfcf44e67fe149bbcebcb52c92fba40f28.title: BOND: Benchmarking Unsupervised Outlier Node Detection on Static Attributed Graphs
fea848dfcf44e67fe149bbcebcb52c92fba40f28.research_question: How can a comprehensive, extensible benchmark be established to systematically evaluate unsupervised outlier node detection methods on static attributed graphs, considering both detection effectiveness (across diverse outlier types and datasets) and computational efficiency?
fea848dfcf44e67fe149bbcebcb52c92fba40f28.hypothesis: A unified, extensible benchmarking framework that includes a diverse set of algorithms, datasets, and outlier types will reveal critical strengths and weaknesses of existing unsupervised outlier node detection methods, and will facilitate fair, reproducible, and insightful comparisons that can guide future research and algorithm development.
fea848dfcf44e67fe149bbcebcb52c92fba40f28.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmarking suite will be developed for unsupervised outlier node detection (OND) on static attributed graphs. The suite will incorporate a diverse set of 14 representative algorithms, spanning classical, non-graph, and deep graph-based methods, with unified APIs and optimized implementations. The benchmark will utilize nine real-world datasets (with both organic and synthetic outliers), as well as synthetically generated graphs of varying sizes, to systematically evaluate detection performance and computational efficiency. Synthetic outliers will be injected using controlled procedures to create both structural (densely connected) and contextual (attribute-dissimilar) outlier nodes, while organic outliers will be evaluated where available. The benchmarking system will be implemented as an open-source, extensible Python library (PyGOD), designed to facilitate future extensions and reproducibility.
fea848dfcf44e67fe149bbcebcb52c92fba40f28.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on nine real-world datasets, including Cora, Amazon, Flickr (with synthetic outliers), and Weibo, Reddit, Disney, Books, Enron, DGraph (with organic outliers), as well as on randomly generated synthetic graphs. Detection performance will be evaluated using ROC-AUC, Average Precision, and Recall@k metrics. Computational efficiency will be measured by wall-clock running time and GPU memory consumption. All algorithms will be evaluated under the same hyperparameter grids for fairness, and both detection quality and efficiency will be systematically compared across methods and datasets. Baselines will include both non-graph and graph-based methods, as well as classical and deep learning approaches.
fea848dfcf44e67fe149bbcebcb52c92fba40f28.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark constitutes the first comprehensive, extensible, and reproducible evaluation framework specifically for unsupervised outlier node detection on static attributed graphs. It introduces a consolidated taxonomy of outlier node types (structural and contextual), evaluates a uniquely broad set of algorithms and datasets, and systematically assesses both detection quality and computational efficiency. The open-source implementation enables easy extension and fair comparison for future research. The benchmark also reveals systematic performance gaps and stability issues in current methods, highlighting new research directions and open challenges.

fee99505eddb66b815320a48314875265ed6230a.title: Autoformulation of Mathematical Optimization Models Using LLMs
fee99505eddb66b815320a48314875265ed6230a.research_question: How can the process of translating natural language problem descriptions into solver-ready mathematical optimization models be automated, enabling efficient and accurate model formulation across diverse domains without requiring specialized optimization expertise?
fee99505eddb66b815320a48314875265ed6230a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a hierarchical search framework leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) in conjunction with Monte-Carlo Tree Search (MCTS), symbolic pruning, and LLM-based evaluation can systematically and efficiently generate correct and diverse mathematical optimization models from natural language descriptions, outperforming existing approaches in both accuracy and search efficiency.
fee99505eddb66b815320a48314875265ed6230a.proposed_method: A novel autoformulation framework is proposed that decomposes the optimization modeling process into four hierarchical components: parameters and decision variables, objective function, equality constraints, and inequality constraints. The method employs Monte-Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to systematically explore the space of possible formulations, with LLMs acting as conditional hypothesis generators at each stage to propose candidate formulations based on the current partial model and problem description. To improve search efficiency, symbolic pruning using Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) solvers is introduced to eliminate functionally equivalent but syntactically different formulations, while LLM-based evaluators assess the correctness and alignment of partial and complete formulations with the original problem requirements. A deterministic parser is used to convert mathematical models into solver-ready computational code, ensuring compatibility with commercial optimization solvers.
fee99505eddb66b815320a48314875265ed6230a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four real-world benchmarks: NLP4OPT, IndustryOR, ComplexOR, and the ComplexLP subset of MAMO, covering linear, integer, and mixed-integer programming problems of varying complexity. The proposed method will be compared against several baselines, including zero-shot prompting, multi-agent LLM frameworks (Chain-of-Experts, OptiMUS), and a finetuned Llama3-based model (ORLM). Evaluation metrics will include formulation correctness (measured by the proportion of problems yielding optimal objective values), search efficiency (unique formulations generated per search budget), and component-level error analysis. Experiments will use GPT-4 as the underlying LLM, and ablation studies will assess the impact of hierarchical decomposition, symbolic pruning, and LLM-based evaluation on performance.
fee99505eddb66b815320a48314875265ed6230a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a hierarchical decomposition of the optimization modeling process, enabling systematic exploration of the formulation space via MCTS rather than generating complete models in a single step. The integration of symbolic pruning with SMT solvers to eliminate redundant search paths represents a significant innovation, as does the use of LLM-based comparative evaluation for both partial and complete formulations. The approach is claimed to achieve superior accuracy and search efficiency compared to state-of-the-art baselines, with substantial reductions in redundant exploration and improved discovery of correct formulations. The framework is designed to be extensible to more complex problem types and adaptable to future advances in LLM capabilities.

feeb9bfbd2f64444d5320d2ca45ce11b1998e776.title: Evaluating and Incentivizing Diverse Data Contributions in Collaborative Learning
feeb9bfbd2f64444d5320d2ca45ce11b1998e776.research_question: How can collaborative learning systems be designed to incentivize diverse and representative data contributions from autonomous agents, balancing local agent interests with global model performance in federated learning settings?
feeb9bfbd2f64444d5320d2ca45ce11b1998e776.hypothesis: Strategically designed mechanisms that account for both data diversity and agent incentives can align individual agent behavior with global data representativeness and maximize information gain in collaborative learning systems.
feeb9bfbd2f64444d5320d2ca45ce11b1998e776.proposed_method: A principal-agent game-theoretic framework is proposed, where the federated learning platform (principal) interacts with multiple self-interested agents (data contributors) who each control data collection over their own sub-populations. The method formalizes the interaction as a multi-agent optimal experiment design problem, quantifying data diversity using the Fisher information matrix and evaluating statistical efficiency through various optimality criteria (e.g., D-, E-, A-, G-, V-criteria). Mechanisms are developed to allocate model accuracy or data contributions to agents, including a novel information-maximizing mechanism that penalizes agents for under-contribution via a simple scalar scaling of their data. The approach includes the design of mechanisms that guarantee incentive-compatible Nash equilibria, ensuring agents contribute data in a way that maximizes global information while respecting local costs and interests.
feeb9bfbd2f64444d5320d2ca45ce11b1998e776.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed using both theoretical analysis and simulation on toy datasets to examine agent behavior and system efficiency under different mechanisms. The experimental setup includes defining design spaces for agents, simulating data collection costs, and comparing the standard federated learning mechanism with the proposed information-maximizing mechanism. Evaluation metrics include total information (log-determinant of the Fisher information matrix), data contribution levels, and fairness among agents. Baselines for comparison include standard federated learning (where all data is pooled) and scenarios with varying agent costs and data diversity. The impact of mechanisms on free-riding, efficiency, and information maximization will be assessed.
feeb9bfbd2f64444d5320d2ca45ce11b1998e776.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal principal-agent game-theoretic model for collaborative experiment design in federated learning, explicitly accounting for both data diversity and strategic agent behavior. It identifies the D-criterion as uniquely supporting incentive-compatible efficiency in multi-agent systems and develops a simple, theoretically grounded mechanism that provably elicits maximal information contributions from agents. The work bridges optimal experiment design, federated learning, and economic incentives, offering new insights and practical mechanisms to mitigate free-riding and promote data diversity.

ff0baeb316df06d017f381c80a2c3aa6399fe938.title: 4D-fy: Text-to-4D Generation Using Hybrid Score Distillation Sampling
ff0baeb316df06d017f381c80a2c3aa6399fe938.research_question: How can high-quality dynamic 3D (4D) scenes be generated from text prompts, achieving a balance between realistic appearance, accurate 3D structure, and compelling motion?
ff0baeb316df06d017f381c80a2c3aa6399fe938.hypothesis: A hybrid score distillation sampling approach that blends supervisory signals from multiple pre-trained diffusion models (text-to-image, 3D-aware text-to-image, and text-to-video) will alleviate the tradeoff between appearance, 3D structure, and motion in text-to-4D scene generation, resulting in state-of-the-art quality across all three aspects.
ff0baeb316df06d017f381c80a2c3aa6399fe938.proposed_method: A novel hybrid score distillation sampling (SDS) framework will be developed for text-to-4D generation. The method employs a neural representation that disentangles static and dynamic scene components using multi-resolution hash encodings and MLPs. The optimization proceeds in three stages: (1) initialization of a static 3D scene using a 3D-aware text-to-image diffusion model to avoid multi-face (Janus) artifacts, (2) alternating supervision with variational SDS and a standard text-to-image model to enhance appearance, and (3) blending in video SDS using a text-to-video model to introduce motion. At each stage, gradient updates from the relevant diffusion models are alternated or blended according to a probabilistic schedule, and the dynamic/static components of the neural representation are selectively updated. The approach leverages open-source models such as MVDream (3D-aware T2I), Stable Diffusion (T2I), and Zeroscope (T2V), and is implemented within a neural volumetric rendering pipeline.
ff0baeb316df06d017f381c80a2c3aa6399fe938.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a set of 28 text prompts, with a subset of 5 prompts used for ablation studies due to computational constraints. The method will be compared against MAV3D, a recent state-of-the-art text-to-4D baseline, as well as several ablations (removing individual supervisory signals or using alternative neural representations such as HexPlane). Evaluation will include both quantitative metrics (CLIP Score, measuring text-image alignment) and qualitative user studies assessing appearance quality, 3D structure, motion quality, text alignment, and overall preference. The neural representation will be optimized using a staged training schedule, with hyperparameters and learning rates carefully tuned for each stage. Rendering resolutions and upsampling procedures will be matched to the native resolutions of the respective diffusion models.
ff0baeb316df06d017f381c80a2c3aa6399fe938.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces hybrid score distillation sampling, a technique that blends gradients from multiple pre-trained diffusion models in an alternating optimization scheme, effectively alleviating the tradeoff between appearance, 3D structure, and motion in text-to-4D generation. The method is the first to achieve state-of-the-art results for text-to-4D generation using only open-source pretrained models, and it provides both a quantitative and qualitative evaluation of the three-way tradeoff. The approach also includes a comprehensive ablation study and will make code and evaluation procedures publicly available to facilitate future research.

ff2a0fb125e7f03428420230c6ecbeafd4cf07a8.title: Can We Edit Factual Knowledge by In-Context Learning?
ff2a0fb125e7f03428420230c6ecbeafd4cf07a8.research_question: Can factual knowledge stored in large language models be edited effectively through in-context learning, achieving both generalization to various prompt formulations and specificity to avoid unintended changes to unrelated facts, without modifying model parameters?
ff2a0fb125e7f03428420230c6ecbeafd4cf07a8.hypothesis: In-context learning, through carefully designed demonstration formatting and organization, can enable effective and specific factual knowledge editing in large language models without requiring any parameter updates, and can scale to very large models with fewer side effects than gradient-based methods.
ff2a0fb125e7f03428420230c6ecbeafd4cf07a8.proposed_method: A novel in-context knowledge editing (IKE) framework will be developed that leverages in-context learning to edit factual knowledge in large language models (LLMs) without parameter updates. The method constructs demonstration contexts composed of three types of demonstrations: (i) copy (to inject new facts), (ii) update (to generalize the new fact to various prompt formulations), and (iii) retain (to preserve unrelated facts). Demonstrations are retrieved from a training corpus using a pretrained sentence encoder and cosine similarity to select and order the most relevant examples. The context is formatted using natural language templates that specify the new fact, the probing prompt, and the desired answer. The approach maximizes the probability of the new answer for in-scope prompts while minimizing changes to out-of-scope prompts, thus balancing generalization and specificity.
ff2a0fb125e7f03428420230c6ecbeafd4cf07a8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple GPT-style autoregressive transformer models ranging from 1.5B to 175B parameters (including GPT-2XL, GPT-NEO, GPT-J, GPT-NEOX, and OPT-175B). The primary evaluation will use the COUNTERFACT benchmark, which contains challenging knowledge editing tasks with paraphrased and neighborhood prompts to test both generalization and specificity. Baselines will include fine-tuning, MEND, ROME, and prompt-based approaches. Evaluation metrics will cover efficacy (editing success on target prompts), generalization (performance on paraphrased in-scope prompts), and specificity (preservation of out-of-scope facts), as well as side effect analysis such as over-editing and knowledge forgetting. Ablation studies will examine the impact of demonstration number, selection, ordering, and formatting.
ff2a0fb125e7f03428420230c6ecbeafd4cf07a8.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first systematic exploration of in-context learning for factual knowledge editing in LLMs, eliminating the need for parameter updates and enabling scalability to very large models. The method achieves competitive or superior editing efficacy and specificity compared to gradient-based approaches, with significantly reduced computational overhead and fewer side effects such as over-editing and knowledge forgetting. The approach provides an interpretable and efficient framework for real-world knowledge editing scenarios.

ff3525bd3b48c325ef3177eb5797cce176357910.title: Relaxed Recursive Transformers: Effective Parameter Sharing with Layer-wise LoRA
ff3525bd3b48c325ef3177eb5797cce176357910.research_question: Can parameter sharing techniques, specifically recursive layer tying and its relaxed variants, be leveraged to significantly reduce the parameter count and computational cost of large language models (LLMs) while maintaining competitive performance? Additionally, can novel batching and inference strategies further improve the efficiency of such compact models?
ff3525bd3b48c325ef3177eb5797cce176357910.hypothesis: Recursive parameter sharing, when combined with effective initialization and relaxation via low-rank adaptation modules, can produce compact LLMs that achieve performance comparable to much larger, non-shared models. Furthermore, the recursive structure will enable new batching strategies that yield substantial inference throughput gains.
ff3525bd3b48c325ef3177eb5797cce176357910.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves converting existing pretrained Transformer-based LLMs into Recursive Transformers by replacing the standard stack of unique layers with a single block of K shared layers, repeated in a loop to match the original depth. Several novel initialization strategies are developed for the shared layers, including Stepwise (selecting layers at intervals), Average (averaging weights), and Lower (using the first K layers). To address the limitations of strict parameter sharing, Relaxed Recursive Transformers are introduced, augmenting each shared layer with layer-specific low-rank adaptation (LoRA) modules whose parameters are initialized via truncated Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) on the residuals between original and shared weights. The LoRA rank is treated as a hyperparameter, allowing interpolation between fully shared and fully unique architectures. All model parameters, including LoRA modules, are jointly uptrained for a limited number of steps to recover performance.
ff3525bd3b48c325ef3177eb5797cce176357910.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several popular LLMs, including Gemma 2B, TinyLlama 1.1B, and Pythia 1B, using their available pretrained checkpoints. After conversion to recursive or relaxed recursive architectures, models will be uptrained on the SlimPajama dataset for up to 60 billion tokens. Evaluation will utilize the Language Model Evaluation Harness to measure few-shot accuracy on seven benchmarks (LAMBADA, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, OpenBookQA) and perplexity on SlimPajama, RedPajama, and PG19. Baselines will include full-size models, reduced-size models pretrained from scratch, and knowledge-distilled models. Ablation studies will compare different initialization methods, LoRA ranks, and the impact of knowledge distillation. Inference efficiency will be evaluated via simulation of the proposed Continuous Depth-wise Batching strategy, with and without early exiting, to measure potential throughput improvements.
ff3525bd3b48c325ef3177eb5797cce176357910.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel framework for converting pretrained LLMs into compact Recursive Transformers using advanced initialization strategies for shared layers. It further innovates by relaxing strict parameter sharing via layer-wise LoRA modules, initialized through SVD on residuals, enabling fine-grained control over the trade-off between model size and performance. The approach is the first to demonstrate that such recursive and relaxed recursive architectures can match or exceed the performance of equivalently sized non-recursive and knowledge-distilled models, and even recover most of the performance of full-size models. Additionally, the recursive structure enables a new inference paradigm, Continuous Depth-wise Batching, which, especially when combined with early exiting, can theoretically yield 2-3× improvements in inference throughput.

ff3e4f7c2481fb6df539f02be5945235101cbc19.title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
ff3e4f7c2481fb6df539f02be5945235101cbc19.research_question: How can the development and evaluation of multimodal agents for open-ended computer tasks in real operating system environments be advanced to better reflect the diversity and complexity of real-world computer use?
ff3e4f7c2481fb6df539f02be5945235101cbc19.hypothesis: A scalable, real computer environment supporting multimodal agent interaction, task setup, and execution-based evaluation across multiple operating systems will enable more comprehensive benchmarking and foster the development of generalist agents capable of handling complex, open-ended computer tasks.
ff3e4f7c2481fb6df539f02be5945235101cbc19.proposed_method: A unified, executable environment will be constructed using virtual machines to simulate real operating systems (Ubuntu, Windows, macOS), supporting raw mouse and keyboard control for arbitrary applications. The environment will allow for detailed initial state configuration, including file preparation and application setup, and will provide rich multimodal observations such as desktop screenshots and accessibility trees. Agents will interact with the environment by generating executable actions in the form of Python code (using pyautogui), and the environment will execute these actions, updating the state accordingly. Each task will be annotated with a natural language instruction, a reproducible initial state setup, and a custom execution-based evaluation script to assess task completion, enabling reliable and reproducible evaluation. The infrastructure will support parallel execution of virtual machines for scalable training and evaluation.
ff3e4f7c2481fb6df539f02be5945235101cbc19.experiment_details: A benchmark suite of 369 real-world computer tasks will be created, covering a wide range of applications (e.g., Chrome, VLC, Thunderbird, VSCode, LibreOffice, GIMP) and workflows, including both single-app and cross-app scenarios. Each task will have a detailed setup and a custom evaluation script, with 134 unique evaluation functions implemented. State-of-the-art LLM and VLM agent baselines (e.g., GPT-4V, Gemini, Claude-3 Opus, Qwen-Max, Mixtral, Llama-3, CogAgent) will be evaluated under different input modalities (screenshot, accessibility tree, or both), using a maximum of 15 steps per task. Evaluation metrics will include success rate (task completion), with human performance measured for comparison. The experimental setup will ensure reproducibility and allow for detailed analysis of agent capabilities and failure modes.
ff3e4f7c2481fb6df539f02be5945235101cbc19.novelty_claims: The proposed environment is the first scalable, real computer environment for benchmarking multimodal agents on open-ended tasks across multiple operating systems, supporting arbitrary applications and workflows. The benchmark features a diverse set of real-world tasks with reproducible initial states and execution-based evaluation scripts, far exceeding prior work in complexity, diversity, and evaluation rigor. The infrastructure enables parallelized, safe, and realistic agent training and evaluation, and supports both GUI and CLI interactions. The approach provides new insights into the limitations of current LLM/VLM-based agents and sets a foundation for the development of generalist digital agents capable of robust, real-world computer assistance.

ff4ac308b02331c75c431b4bf01c0485b91761c8.title: An Entropy-based Text Watermarking Detection Method
ff4ac308b02331c75c431b4bf01c0485b91761c8.research_question: How can the detection of text watermarks in machine-generated texts, particularly in low-entropy scenarios, be improved to reliably distinguish watermarked outputs from human-written content across varying entropy distributions?
ff4ac308b02331c75c431b4bf01c0485b91761c8.hypothesis: Incorporating token-level entropy as a weighting factor in the watermark detection process will improve the detection accuracy of watermarked texts, especially in low-entropy scenarios, without sacrificing performance in high-entropy cases.
ff4ac308b02331c75c431b4bf01c0485b91761c8.proposed_method: A novel detection algorithm, Entropy-based Text Watermarking Detection (EWD), will be developed to assign influence weights to each token in a text based on its entropy, as computed from the language model's logits during generation. The method will utilize a monotonically increasing and continuous function (such as linear, sigmoid, or exponential) to map token entropy to detection weights, ensuring that high-entropy tokens contribute more to the watermark detection score. The detection process will involve calculating token entropies, assigning weights, identifying green-list tokens using a detection key and context window, and computing a weighted z-score to determine if a text is watermarked. The approach will be fully automated, training-free, and independent of manual thresholding or human datasets.
ff4ac308b02331c75c431b4bf01c0485b91761c8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both low-entropy (code generation) and high-entropy (news and data-to-text generation) tasks. For low-entropy evaluation, datasets such as HumanEval and MBPP will be used with StarCoder as the generation model, while high-entropy tasks will use the C4 and Rotowire datasets with OPT-1.3B and fine-tuned T5-small models, respectively. All watermarked texts will be generated using the KGW watermarking algorithm with fixed hyperparameters. Baseline detectors will include the standard KGW and SWEET methods. Evaluation metrics will be True Positive Rate (TPR), F1 score, and False Positive Rate (FPR), with a focus on maintaining FPR below 5%. Additional experiments will assess robustness to prompt availability, detection speed, and resilience against back-translation attacks.
ff4ac308b02331c75c431b4bf01c0485b91761c8.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a fully automated, entropy-aware detection framework that customizes token influence based on entropy, addressing the underexplored challenge of watermark detection in low-entropy texts. Unlike prior approaches, it eliminates the need for manual entropy thresholding and human-coded datasets, and is applicable across texts with diverse entropy distributions. The method demonstrates significant improvements in detection accuracy for low-entropy scenarios, matches state-of-the-art performance in high-entropy cases, and maintains efficiency and robustness against common watermark removal attacks.

ff9ab30cf541dec4ad7e135c603994ba33caca28.title: Beyond ELBOs: A Large-Scale Evaluation of Variational Methods for Sampling
ff9ab30cf541dec4ad7e135c603994ba33caca28.research_question: How can variational and Monte Carlo-based sampling methods be systematically evaluated and compared across a diverse set of tasks using standardized performance criteria, including the ability to avoid mode collapse?
ff9ab30cf541dec4ad7e135c603994ba33caca28.hypothesis: A unified benchmarking framework with comprehensive evaluation metrics, including novel criteria for mode collapse, will reveal strengths and weaknesses of current variational and Monte Carlo sampling methods and guide the development of more effective sampling algorithms.
ff9ab30cf541dec4ad7e135c603994ba33caca28.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmarking suite will be developed to evaluate variational, Monte Carlo, and hybrid sampling methods on a standardized set of synthetic and real-world target distributions. The methodology will include the implementation of a broad range of performance criteria, such as density-ratio-based metrics (e.g., ELBO, EUBO), integral probability metrics (e.g., Wasserstein distance, MMD), and novel metrics specifically designed to quantify mode collapse, such as Entropic Mode Coverage (EMC). The benchmark will partition the evaluation into tractable density models, sequential importance sampling methods, and diffusion-based methods, each assessed using both traditional and newly proposed metrics. Mode descriptors will be constructed for multimodal targets to facilitate the computation of EMC, and both forward and reverse criteria will be systematically applied. Hyperparameter tuning and experimental protocols will be standardized to ensure fair and robust comparisons.
ff9ab30cf541dec4ad7e135c603994ba33caca28.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse suite of target densities, including synthetic distributions (e.g., funnel, mixtures of Gaussians/Student-t, downsampled MNIST and FashionMNIST), Bayesian logistic regression tasks, time series models, and spatial statistics models. Each method will be evaluated using multiple runs with different random seeds, and performance will be measured using metrics such as ELBO, EUBO, partition function estimation error (forward and reverse), Wasserstein distance, MMD, and EMC. Baselines will include mean-field VI, Gaussian mixture VI, normalizing flows, sequential Monte Carlo, annealed importance sampling, and a range of diffusion-based samplers. Evaluation will include both quantitative and qualitative analyses (e.g., sample visualizations), and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of key hyperparameters and algorithmic choices. Hyperparameter tuning will be performed via grid search, and sample efficiency will be tracked.
ff9ab30cf541dec4ad7e135c603994ba33caca28.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified, large-scale benchmarking framework for variational and Monte Carlo sampling methods, addressing the lack of standardized evaluation protocols in the field. A novel metric, Entropic Mode Coverage (EMC), is proposed to heuristically quantify mode collapse using mode descriptors, enabling more sensitive detection of mode-seeking behavior. The benchmark systematically compares a wide array of state-of-the-art methods across diverse tasks and evaluation criteria, providing new insights into the exploration-exploitation trade-offs and sample efficiency of modern samplers. The framework is designed to serve as a reference for future development and evaluation of probabilistic sampling algorithms.

ff9f08b0046105c6ffee62348ec478f3a6186b5e.title: Adaptivity and Non-stationarity: Problem-dependent Dynamic Regret for Online Convex Optimization
ff9f08b0046105c6ffee62348ec478f3a6186b5e.research_question: How can online convex optimization algorithms be designed to achieve dynamic regret bounds that are adaptive to the intrinsic difficulty and non-stationarity of the problem, particularly by leveraging problem-dependent quantities rather than worst-case parameters?
ff9f08b0046105c6ffee62348ec478f3a6186b5e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by exploiting smoothness and problem-dependent quantities such as gradient variation and cumulative comparator loss, online convex optimization algorithms can achieve dynamic regret bounds that are tighter than minimax rates in benign environments, while maintaining worst-case guarantees.
ff9f08b0046105c6ffee62348ec478f3a6186b5e.proposed_method: A novel collaborative online ensemble framework will be developed for online convex optimization in non-stationary environments.
