The approach will employ a two-layer ensemble structure, with a meta-algorithm coordinating a set of base learners. Optimistic online mirror descent (OMD) will be used as a modular building block at both meta and base levels, incorporating predictive gradient information (optimistic vectors) to enhance adaptivity. Crucial correction terms will be introduced to facilitate effective collaboration between the meta and base layers, enabling the algorithm to exploit negative terms in the regret analysis for achieving problem-dependent dynamic regret bounds. Two specific algorithms, Sword and Sword++, will be constructed: Sword for multi-gradient feedback (multiple gradient queries per round), and Sword++ for the more challenging one-gradient feedback model (only one gradient per round), ensuring computational efficiency and broad applicability.
ff9f08b0046105c6ffee62348ec478f3a6186b5e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard online convex optimization benchmarks, including both synthetic and real-world datasets that exhibit varying degrees of non-stationarity and smoothness. The proposed algorithms will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, such as online gradient descent with optimal step size tuning and other recent dynamic regret minimization methods. Evaluation metrics will focus on dynamic regret, particularly measuring performance in terms of path length, gradient variation, and cumulative comparator loss. Both multi-gradient and one-gradient feedback settings will be tested, and the gradient query complexity per iteration will be reported to assess computational efficiency.
ff9f08b0046105c6ffee62348ec478f3a6186b5e.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a collaborative online ensemble framework that achieves problem-dependent dynamic regret bounds, replacing the dependence on the time horizon with quantities such as gradient variation and cumulative comparator loss. The approach is adaptive to the intrinsic difficulty of the problem, yielding tighter bounds in easy instances while safeguarding minimax rates in the worst case. The Sword++ algorithm is particularly novel in attaining these guarantees with only one gradient query per iteration, matching the efficiency of static regret minimization methods. The framework's modularity and correction mechanisms for meta-base collaboration represent significant innovations, with potential applicability to a broad range of non-stationary online learning problems.

ffb5d0aa78c28753d133b7b2ed9bccb3e8eb41b4.title: Approximating the Shapley Value without Marginal Contributions
ffb5d0aa78c28753d133b7b2ed9bccb3e8eb41b4.research_question: How can the Shapley value be efficiently approximated in cooperative games, especially in contexts where marginal contributions are expensive or infeasible to compute, and under a fixed budget of value function evaluations?
ffb5d0aa78c28753d133b7b2ed9bccb3e8eb41b4.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the Shapley value can be accurately and efficiently approximated without relying on marginal contributions by leveraging alternative representations and stratified sampling techniques, resulting in improved theoretical and empirical performance over existing methods.
ffb5d0aa78c28753d133b7b2ed9bccb3e8eb41b4.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed for Shapley value approximation that does not require the computation of marginal contributions. The first algorithm, SVARM (Shapley Value Approximation without Requesting Marginals), utilizes a representation of the Shapley value as the difference between two weighted averages of coalition values (with and without a given player), and alternates sampling from two carefully constructed distributions over coalitions. This allows for simultaneous updates of multiple players' Shapley value estimates with each value function evaluation, maximizing sample reuse. The second algorithm, StratifiedSVARM, further refines this approach by stratifying coalitions according to their size, enabling an even more granular update mechanism where all players' estimates are updated with each sampled coalition. Both algorithms are parameter-free, domain-independent, incremental (anytime), and unbiased, and do not require prior knowledge of the value function.
ffb5d0aa78c28753d133b7b2ed9bccb3e8eb41b4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic cooperative games (such as the Airport game, Shoe game, and randomly generated Sum of Unanimity Games) and real-world explainable AI scenarios (including NLP sentiment analysis, image classification, and tabular data classification tasks). For each setting, the true Shapley values will be computed either analytically or exhaustively. The proposed algorithms will be compared against established baselines such as ApproShapley, KernelSHAP, and other sample-mean-based approaches. Evaluation will focus on mean squared error (MSE) of the Shapley value estimates as a function of the number of value function evaluations (budget T), with results averaged over multiple runs and players. Additional analysis will include variance and probabilistic error bounds, as well as the impact of stratification and sampling strategies.
ffb5d0aa78c28753d133b7b2ed9bccb3e8eb41b4.novelty_claims: The proposed algorithms introduce a new, parameter-free, and domain-independent approach to Shapley value approximation that completely avoids marginal contributions, instead leveraging direct coalition value sampling and stratification. Theoretical analysis provides unmatched guarantees, including logarithmic dependence on the number of players for variance and MSE, which is a significant improvement over the linear dependence in prior methods. The algorithms maximize sample reuse, are unbiased, incremental, and possess anytime properties. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior approximation quality, particularly for the stratified variant, and establish the first sample-mean-based method to rival state-of-the-art approaches in practical explainability tasks.

ffd91f85d6d19e75309ececfd190afa6bb562284.title: Spikformer: When Spiking Neural Network Meets Transformer
ffd91f85d6d19e75309ececfd190afa6bb562284.research_question: Can a novel integration of self-attention mechanisms and spiking neural networks (SNNs) enable efficient, high-performing deep learning models suitable for both static and neuromorphic datasets?
ffd91f85d6d19e75309ececfd190afa6bb562284.hypothesis: Incorporating a spike-form self-attention mechanism into SNNs will result in a transformer-like architecture that achieves superior accuracy and energy efficiency compared to existing SNN frameworks on image classification tasks.
ffd91f85d6d19e75309ececfd190afa6bb562284.proposed_method: A new framework, SpikingTransformer (Spikformer), will be developed by introducing a Spiking Self-Attention (SSA) mechanism tailored for SNNs. The SSA module replaces the standard softmax-based attention with a spike-form Query, Key, and Value system, where all elements are binary (0 or 1), and the attention computation is performed using logical AND and summation operations, thus avoiding multiplications and softmax normalization. The architecture will include a Spiking Patch Splitting (SPS) module for patch extraction and embedding, a stack of Spikformer encoder blocks (each with SSA and an MLP block), and a classification head. Batch normalization will be used in place of layer normalization, and spike-form relative position embeddings will be generated using a convolutional module followed by a spiking neuron layer. The SSA mechanism is decomposable, allowing for flexible computation order and reduced complexity when the sequence length exceeds the embedding dimension.
ffd91f85d6d19e75309ececfd190afa6bb562284.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both static datasets (ImageNet, CIFAR10, CIFAR100) and neuromorphic datasets (CIFAR10-DVS, DVS128Gesture). The models will be trained from scratch using the AdamW optimizer, with standard data augmentation techniques (random augmentation, mixup, cutmix) applied. Various Spikformer configurations will be evaluated by varying the number of encoder blocks and embedding dimensions. Baselines will include state-of-the-art SNN models (e.g., SEW-ResNet, TET, DSR) and ANN-based transformers. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 classification accuracy, number of parameters, synaptic operations (SOPs), floating-point operations (FLOPs), and theoretical energy consumption. Ablation studies will assess the impact of SSA versus vanilla self-attention and other attention variants, as well as the effect of different simulation time steps.
ffd91f85d6d19e75309ececfd190afa6bb562284.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first spike-form self-attention mechanism (SSA) specifically designed for SNNs, enabling efficient attention computation without multiplications or softmax normalization. Spikformer represents the first directly-trained transformer-like architecture in SNNs, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy and energy efficiency on both static and neuromorphic image classification tasks. The SSA mechanism is biologically plausible, computationally efficient, and decomposable, offering significant improvements in both performance and resource consumption compared to prior SNN frameworks.

ffdad9a5493e8d4c6c529b7b6f85eee91ca0bb79.title: SuS-X: Training-Free Name-Only Transfer of Vision-Language Models
ffdad9a5493e8d4c6c529b7b6f85eee91ca0bb79.research_question: How can vision-language models be adapted to new classification tasks in a training-free, name-only transfer regime, where only the names of target categories are available and no images from the target task distribution are accessible?
ffdad9a5493e8d4c6c529b7b6f85eee91ca0bb79.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that constructing a curated support set using only target category names, combined with a novel training-free inference method that leverages inter-modal similarities, can significantly improve the zero-shot and few-shot classification performance of vision-language models without requiring any training or access to target task data.
ffdad9a5493e8d4c6c529b7b6f85eee91ca0bb79.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces SuS-X, a framework for training-free, name-only transfer of vision-language models (VLMs) such as CLIP, BLIP, and TCL. The method consists of two main components: (1) SuS (Support Set) construction, which creates a pseudo few-shot dataset for each target category by either generating images using text-to-image models like Stable Diffusion or retrieving relevant images from large-scale vision-language datasets such as LAION-5B, based solely on category names; and (2) TIP-X, a novel inference algorithm that computes inter-modal (image-text) similarities between the support set and test images, using KL-divergence between their class probability distributions as attention weights for classification. TIP-X addresses calibration issues in prior methods by operating in the image-text space rather than the image-image space, and blends these affinity-based logits with the original zero-shot logits for robust prediction. The framework is fully training-free and does not require any samples from the target task distribution.
ffdad9a5493e8d4c6c529b7b6f85eee91ca0bb79.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 19 diverse benchmark datasets, including ImageNet, Stanford Cars, UCF101, Caltech101/256, Flowers102, OxfordPets, Food101, SUN397, DTD, EuroSAT, FGVCAircraft, Country211, CIFAR-10/100, Birdsnap, CUB, ImageNet-Sketch, and ImageNet-R. The evaluation will use multiple VLMs (CLIP, BLIP, TCL) and various visual backbones (ResNet, ViT). Baselines will include zero-shot CLIP, prompt engineering methods (CuPL, VisDesc), distribution normalization (CLIP+DN), and parameter-free attention (CALIP), as well as few-shot adaptation methods (TIP-Adapter). Metrics will focus on top-1 classification accuracy. Hyperparameter sweeps and ablations will be performed to assess the impact of support set size, prompting strategies, and blending parameters. The method will be evaluated in both zero-shot (name-only) and few-shot regimes, with support sets constructed without access to target data.
ffdad9a5493e8d4c6c529b7b6f85eee91ca0bb79.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable training-free, name-only transfer for vision-language models using only category names and no target task images. It introduces a dynamic support set construction strategy that leverages either generative models or large-scale retrieval, and a novel inference method (TIP-X) that uses inter-modal KL-divergence for robust classification. The approach outperforms previous state-of-the-art training-free and zero-shot adaptation methods across a wide range of datasets and VLM architectures, and generalizes to both zero-shot and few-shot settings without requiring any model training or access to target distribution samples.

fff3bec525f79f2dcc433a275b234e3550534d21.title: Co-PatcheR: Collaborative Software Patching with Component(s)-specific Small Reasoning Models
fff3bec525f79f2dcc433a275b234e3550534d21.research_question: How can collaborative, component-specific small reasoning models be leveraged to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of automated software patching systems, compared to monolithic or general-purpose large language models?
fff3bec525f79f2dcc433a275b234e3550534d21.hypothesis: Collaborative use of small, component-specific reasoning models for different stages of the software patching pipeline (localization, generation, validation) will achieve higher patch resolution rates and greater efficiency (in terms of data, parameters, and compute) than monolithic models or general-purpose LLMs.
fff3bec525f79f2dcc433a275b234e3550534d21.proposed_method: A novel collaborative patching system will be developed, employing three specialized small reasoning models: one for both localization and patch generation (Loc-Gen model), and two for patch validation (Val-assert and Val-no-assert models). The Loc-Gen model will use a two-step localization process (file then line) and integrate patch critique with generation, enabling self-refinement. The validation models will generate diverse proof-of-concept (PoC) test cases with and without assertions, and judge patch correctness based on dynamic test outcomes. All models will be fine-tuned via supervised distillation from larger teacher models using carefully constructed reasoning data, with rigorous filtering to ensure correctness and manageable reasoning chain length. The system will combine outputs through majority voting and dynamic testing to select the final patch.
fff3bec525f79f2dcc433a275b234e3550534d21.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the SWE-bench-Verified dataset, a benchmark of real-world GitHub issues in Python. The base model for all components will be Qwen-2.5-Coder-14B, with training data selected from the SWE-bench training set and SWE-Gym, ensuring diversity and no data leakage. The training set will be limited to 2,000 issues for efficiency, with additional filtering for correctness and reasoning quality. Baselines will include both commercial LLM agents (e.g., Claude, GPT-4o) and specialized open-source patching models (e.g., SWE-RL, SWE-Fixer). Evaluation metrics will include resolved rate (percentage of issues correctly patched), localization accuracy (file and line level), and validation effectiveness. Ablation studies will assess the impact of data size, model size, reasoning data filtering, critique training, and validation workflow components.
fff3bec525f79f2dcc433a275b234e3550534d21.novelty_claims: The proposed system introduces the first collaborative patching framework with component-specific small reasoning models, achieving state-of-the-art performance among specialized models with significantly reduced data and parameter requirements. Key innovations include a unified Loc-Gen model for both localization and generation, integration of patch critique into generation, dual validation models for diverse PoC generation, and a data-efficient distillation and filtering recipe tailored for patching tasks. The approach demonstrates that small, specialized models, when properly trained and orchestrated, can match or surpass much larger models in software patching, setting new benchmarks for efficiency and effectiveness.

fff81378762c5cbf7de9a56c9c8ab1092644b33e.title: Transformers Learn to Achieve Second-Order Convergence Rates for In-Context Linear Regression
fff81378762c5cbf7de9a56c9c8ab1092644b33e.research_question: What convergence rates can be achieved by deep Transformer architectures when performing in-context learning for linear regression, and how do these rates compare to those of established first-order and second-order optimization methods?
fff81378762c5cbf7de9a56c9c8ab1092644b33e.hypothesis: Transformers trained for in-context linear regression learn to internally implement algorithms with convergence rates comparable to second-order optimization methods, such as Iterative Newton's Method, rather than first-order methods like Gradient Descent.
fff81378762c5cbf7de9a56c9c8ab1092644b33e.proposed_method: A deep Transformer model will be trained to perform in-context linear regression, where the model receives a sequence of input-output pairs as context and predicts the output for a new query input. The architecture will use causal attention to ensure each prediction only depends on previous context, and the model will be trained end-to-end to minimize prediction error. To analyze the internal algorithmic behavior, the model's predictions at each layer will be extracted by retraining the readout head for each layer, allowing for a layer-wise comparison of convergence behavior. Two similarity metrics will be developed: one comparing the residual errors of the Transformer to those of standard iterative algorithms, and another comparing the induced weight vectors by fitting a linear model to the predictions. These metrics will be used to quantitatively assess the correspondence between Transformer layers and iterations of classical optimization algorithms.
fff81378762c5cbf7de9a56c9c8ab1092644b33e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic linear regression tasks where data is generated from a known distribution over positive semi-definite covariance matrices, with both well-conditioned (identity covariance) and ill-conditioned (high condition number) settings. The primary model will be a 12-layer, 8-head GPT-2 style Transformer, with additional experiments using alternative layer/head configurations. Baselines will include Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Gradient Descent (GD), Online Gradient Descent (OGD), Iterative Newton's Method, and LSTMs. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE), cosine similarity of residual errors, and cosine similarity of induced weights. For each Transformer layer, the readout head will be retrained to assess progressive improvement, and best-matching steps between Transformer layers and iterative algorithm steps will be identified using heatmaps of similarity metrics. Experiments will also test robustness to ill-conditioning and compare convergence rates across all methods.
fff81378762c5cbf7de9a56c9c8ab1092644b33e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a mechanistic investigation into the internal optimization algorithms learned by Transformers in the context of linear regression, providing both empirical and theoretical evidence that deep Transformers can approximate second-order optimization methods and achieve superlinear convergence rates. Unlike prior work that suggests Transformers implement first-order methods such as Gradient Descent, this approach demonstrates that Transformers can match the convergence behavior of Iterative Newton's Method, even under ill-conditioned data. The methodology includes novel metrics for algorithmic similarity and a layer-wise analysis framework, offering new insights into why Transformers are particularly effective at in-context learning compared to other architectures.

zswylB4Wnt.title: RAST: Reasoning Activation in LLMs via Small-model Transfer
zswylB4Wnt.research_question: How can reinforcement learning-induced reasoning improvements in small language models be efficiently transferred to larger base models to enhance their reasoning capabilities without expensive RL training at scale?
zswylB4Wnt.hypothesis: RL activates latent reasoning capabilities in LLMs by selectively adjusting probabilities of a small subset of tokens related to key reasoning behaviors, and these RL-induced output distribution shifts are largely model-size invariant and transferable from small RL-trained models to larger base models.
zswylB4Wnt.proposed_method: RAST, a decoding-time method that transfers logit-level adjustments (delta logits) from a small RL-tuned model to a larger base model by adding the difference in logits between the RL-trained small model and its base counterpart to the logits of the large base model during decoding, controlled by a scaling factor λ, thereby activating reasoning capabilities without retraining.
zswylB4Wnt.experiment_details: Preliminary token-level analysis measuring Path Coverage Rate (PCR) between base and RL models; evaluation of RAST on multiple benchmarks with pass@k accuracy and recovery rate metrics; token-level analysis of reasoning behaviors (branching, backtracking, self-verification) via curated tokens; efficiency analysis comparing GPU memory and inference speed with direct RL training; generalization tests on different models and tasks; conducted over multiple runs with temperature and nucleus sampling decoding configurations.
zswylB4Wnt.novelty_claims: RAST enables scalable reasoning enhancement by transferring RL-induced reasoning signals from small to large models without retraining; achieves comparable or better performance than direct RL training with significantly lower computational cost; increases reasoning diversity and pass@k performance beyond RL-trained models; provides empirical evidence of localized token-level reasoning activation transferable across model scales; demonstrates broad applicability across architectures, scales, and reasoning domains; offers practical insights and strategies for efficient RL-driven reasoning activation in LLMs.
